69				"reads there is not what shipped, and Reset puts the built-in back.\n\n" +
70				"This is the long one, so the two run buttons mean different things here. ⏸ " +
71				"parks it between requests and ▶ carries on from the same frame; ⏹ ends it, " +
72				"and if the describing had started the next ▶ describes the session from the " +
73				"beginning. Edit a prompt and it is ⏹ you want — a resumed run would describe " +
74				"the rest of the footage under the new wording and leave the first half " +
75				"under the old."},
76		{"cut", "Cut", "edit-cut-symbolic", "Choose the clips the video is made of",
77			"Add footage on the Prepare step first — the cut is laid out from the recordings",
78			"The footage over the session timeline, with everything the cut keeps tinted " +
79				"green over it, and a waveform lane per sound below. The row above the pictures " +
80				"is the cut in bars: a green bar per kept stretch, the one the red line is in " +
81				"drawn tall with handles on its ends and an ✕ that drops it — ⌦ does the " +
82				"same to whatever is in hand, which is how the cards and the sounds go. A " +
83				"selection is OF what it was drawn on: dragged across the pictures it is " +
84				"footage, dragged across a waveform it is that recording's sound, and the " +
85				"verbs read that. Which rows a SCENE is made of is said on the scene itself " +
86				"— take one in hand and every row shows a mark at its left edge: a lens on " +
87				"each camera row, lit on the one the scene is shown from, and a speaker on " +
88				"each sound row, lit where the scene hears it. Press a lens to show that " +
89				"scene from that camera, a speaker to switch that sound off for it. The rule " +
90				"the inserts follow is that an insert replaces what it brings and nothing " +
91				"else: laid over footage a clip takes the frames, and its form asks what " +
92				"happens to the sound — its own, or the session's carrying on underneath. " +
93				"Spliced in it replaces nothing at all, because it is time added to the " +
94				"session rather than a stretch of it. ▶ below asks " +
95				"the model to fill the ▶ target length from what Describe found; from then " +
96				"on the cut is yours — drag to select, add, remove, and Revert goes back to " +
97				"the suggestion. Once you have edited by hand ▶ says so rather than throwing " +
98				"the edits away — Revert first if you want a fresh suggestion. The scroll " +
99				"wheel zooms around the cursor.\n\nA left click " +
100				"drops the red playhead; the clock under the transport buttons is where it " +
101				"landed, in mm:ss.d of session time, and hovering it says which recording " +
102				"that is, which frame, and whether the cut keeps it; the ⟦ in and out ⟧ marks " +
103				"print their times the same way, in small type under their own buttons. Over " +
104				"the picture and the toolbar the wheel steps frames instead of zooming — a " +

107				"edges are trimmed rather than re-selected, and that is two buttons: the " +
108				"right one picks a green border up — it turns white — and does nothing else, " +
109				"so the choice keeps while your hand moves. Then move it, either by dragging " +
110				"the white bar with the left button or a frame at a time with ‹f and f› (the " +

125				"nudge either of them and it lands on the frame you left it on.\n\nA source on Inputs that is not marked as footage gets its own " +
126				"lanes under the cut, in blue, one per channel — left and right apart, because " +
127				"they are often separate things, a mic on one and the game on the other. A " +

136				"each is decoded once and kept.\n\n" +
137				"The prompts this step sends — the cut, then the captions, the speed and " +
138				"the effects, clip by clip — are on Prepare, in the box that holds every " +
139				"prompt in the app. There is one wording each and it assumes nothing about " +

147				"⧉ Insert drops a file into the cut at the playhead — a title card, a still, an " +

149				"the track, the preview shows it while the red line is inside it — animated cards " +

170				"around it, and never narrower than a marker you can hit. Its name and length " +

172				"than dragged. Right-click a card to hold it and ⧉ Insert becomes ✎ Edit: the " +
173				"same form again, for what the card says, which mode it is in, and how long it " +
174				"runs. Switching modes moves the footage back or out of the way to match.\n\n" +
175				"A card that animates itself is rendered frame by frame, written either " +

180				"The project's assets folder starts with cards this app draws itself: tier.svg is " +
181				"the S/A/B/C/D/F board, and s.svg, a.svg, b.svg, c.svg, d.svg, f.svg are single " +

183				"which is the one thing a still cannot show you and is what Just added below does. " +

188				"\"Dust II|logos/dust2.png\" is the name under the logo. A tier holds six; a " +
189				"seventh is not drawn and the log says so. The last line, Just " +

196				"pace, as it always did. What you type is kept on the end of the path " +
197				"(tier.svg?S=Dust II, Mirage&A=Nuke), so the same file is " +
198				"a different board every time you place it and the cut says which. tier.svg is also " +
199				"the file it is drawn from, and it is a board when you open it: every row and all " +
200				"six places in it are written out with their own coordinates, and the {{holes}} in " +
201				"them are what you typed and the timings the arrivals get — restyle that file and " +
202				"every board drawn from it comes out restyled. " +
203				"Your own SVG can " +
204				"do the same: put {{name}} or {{name|default}} in it and Insert asks for each one, " +
205				"and add <!-- Input: name | Label | what it is --> beside it to have the form ask " +
206				"in your words rather than in the placeholder's. assets/CARDS.md is written into " +
207				"the folder with the cards and says all of it — the canvas, the placeholders, and " +
208				"how an animated one has to be written — for whoever, or whatever, writes the next one.\n\n" +
209				"The aspect dropdown beside those buttons is for a video that is not the footage's " +
210				"shape — 9:16 for a short, 1:1, 4:5 — and \"source\" is the absence of the choice: " +
211				"nothing below applies until it is changed, and a cut that never touches it renders " +
212				"exactly as it always did. With one chosen, the height set on Produce names the " +
213				"output's height and the aspect names its width, and the video starts on the whole " +
214				"frame, black either side, because throwing footage away is a choice you make, not " +
215				"one made for you — until the first view: the moment one exists, the video is " +
216				"framed on it from the very start, wherever on the timeline it was placed.\n\n" +
217				"The four effects live in the ✚ Effect dropdown beside the aspect. " +
218				"▭ View is that choice: jump anywhere, pick it, and draw on " +
219				"the picture itself the region to show from there on. The rectangle keeps the cut's " +
220				"aspect while you drag, snaps flush when you reach the full width or height of the " +
221				"frame, and may be smaller — a crop, zoomed in — or larger, the frame with more " +
222				"black around it. The form then asks the one number: 0 switches the camera at " +
223				"that instant, seconds glide it over. Views chain — each one starts from wherever " +
224				"the camera is at that moment, mid-glide included — and the camera stays until the " +
225				"next one. ⊕ Zoom is a free drawing with a return ticket: any rectangle, not bound " +
226				"to the aspect — the camera closes in on the smallest output-shaped window that " +
227				"holds it — in over its own glide, held for its length, and back out over a separate " +
228				"glide to wherever the views say the camera belongs. " +
229				"⏩ Speed needs no drawing: it puts the seconds marked with in and out on a clock " +
230				"of their own — type the rate, a fifth for slow motion or up to 100× to run " +
231				"through the dead air of a long recording, the sound stretched or squeezed with " +
232				"the picture and the pitch kept. ⏸ Stop holds the frame under " +
233				"the playhead still for a time you type, which plays like a spliced card the " +

235				"flags for views, teal brackets for zooms, rose bands for speed, rose also washed " +
236				"over the footage that is off its own clock — and the marks answer to the timeline's own " +

241				"its rectangle on the picture: draw beside it to re-frame it, or grab inside it " +

245				"except on the first view, which has none to ask. Paused, the preview draws " +
246				"the camera as an outline over the full frame rather than cropping the picture — " +

251		{"narrate", "Narrate", "audio-input-microphone-symbolic", "The narration, and the voice it is spoken in",
252			"Finish Cut first — narration is written for the cut's clips",
253			"▶ below is the initial fill: it writes the narration once (again only if the " +
254				"cut moves) and speaks every line not cached yet. After that the lines are " +
255				"yours: each box is \"[emotion] words\" with its start time beside it — edit " +
256				"the words, the delivery, or when the line begins — a time inside another " +
257				"clip moves the line to that clip, and one outside the cut is refused with " +
258				"the line left where it was. ＋ beside the transport " +
259				"adds a line at the paused second, 🗑 removes one, and an edited line is " +
260				"simply re-spoken the first time it plays. The voice is cloned from a " +
261				"sample, picked under the video; the slider and the picture play the cut, speaking each " +
262				"line where it was placed, with the blue row following along. The bar is " +
263				"the cut end to end — what the edit removed takes up no room on it, so " +
264				"every point on it is video you keep, and the time beside it reads " +
265				"\"session clock · how far into the finished video\". The cut is " +
266				"the master: once it is rolling it keeps rolling, clip after clip, and " +
267				"nothing moves the picture but you. Picking a line — clicking its row, or " +
268				"its ▶ — starts three seconds before that line so you can watch it land, " +
269				"and then the preview simply carries on down the cut. A clip the narration " +
270				"left alone keeps its row and its ▶ too: that one plays the clip from the " +
271				"top on its own audio, which is how you decide whether it wants a line. " +
272				"A line whose time you retype into another clip leaves that row behind it, " +
273				"empty. ⏪ and ⏩ " +
274				"jump three seconds; stopped, the wheel over the slider steps one frame " +
275				"at a time, which is the resolution a line's placement is judged at. The " +
276				"playhead only lands on material the cut kept: dropped into a gap it " +
277				"carries on the way it was going, to the head of the next clip or back " +
278				"to the tail of the one behind.\n\nA take " +
279				"is stable: the same words, delivery and voice always come back as the " +
280				"same performance, so nothing you have approved changes behind you. " +
281				"When a delivery is wrong rather than the words, the row's ↻ re-rolls " +
282				"it — same line, a new draw — and plays the result.\n\nThe TTS blends eight base emotions — " +
283				"happy, angry, sad, afraid, disgusted, melancholic, surprised, calm — " +
284				"and maps whatever is in the [brackets] onto them. One or two of those " +
285				"words work best; \"loud\" or \"fast\" is not an emotion and only dilutes " +
286				"the match (anger already shouts, calm is already slow). Length lives in " +
287				"the words themselves: more short exclamations, not stretched letters, " +
288				"which get spelled out.\n\nPlain words are read by a small judge model, " +
289				"which is forgiving but approximate. Write a weight and it is skipped, " +
290				"the mix going to the engine exactly as asked: \"[angry=1]\" is pure " +
291				"anger at full force, \"[happy=0.8, surprised=0.4]\" a blend you chose. " +
292				"Weights run 0 to 1, and the difference is audible: \"[surprised]\" " +
293				"is the judge's reading of the word, \"[surprised=1]\" the axis " +
294				"itself at full force.\n\nBeside the eight there are named mixes of " +
295				"them, which take a weight the same way: excited, ecstatic, playful, " +
296				"proud, relieved, hopeful, tender, nostalgic, solemn, awed, alarmed, " +
297				"horrified, desperate, confused, frustrated, bitter, contemptuous, " +
298				"dismayed, heartbroken, ominous, tense. \"[excited=1]\" is happiness " +
299				"with surprise mixed into it, which is what excitement sounds like " +
300				"and what plain happiness does not. Any name none of these knows sends the " +
301				"line back to the judge rather than guessing at an axis."},
302		{"produce", "Produce", "applications-multimedia-symbolic", "Write the upload text, draw the thumbnail and render the video",
303			"Finish Cut first — there is no cut to produce a video from",
304			"Everything the upload needs, from one ▶: the first press writes the " +
305				"title, the thumbnail instruction and the description; every press " +
306				"draws the thumbnail; and then the final video is rendered — every " +
307				"clip cut from its own recording, the narration laid over ducked game " +
308				"audio, the whole thing loudness-normalized to -14 LUFS for YouTube. " +
309				"Lines that have not been synthesized yet are spoken first.\n\nThe " +
310				"model is not asked for the text again after the first run, however " +
311				"much you edit the boxes: rewording the edit instruction or swapping " +
312				"the images costs GPU time and no thinking. Deleting the publish folder " +
313				"is what starts the text over; Suggest again, beside the title, " +
314				"rewrites it without redrawing or rendering.\n\nThe thumbnail is " +
315				"usually an edit of one of your own frames, which is what keeps it " +
316				"recognizably this video rather than a stock illustration of the " +
317				"genre. The first image in the row is the picture being edited; the " +
318				"others are references the instruction can name by position — \"put " +
319				"the ship from the second image behind them\" — and Make base " +
320				"promotes one to the front. Empty the row and it is drawn from the " +
321				"instruction alone. Write the instruction as instructions, not as a " +
322				"description of a picture: say what to change, and everything you do " +
323				"not mention stays as it is. The title is lettered into the picture " +
324				"by the image model — four or five words survive being shrunk to a " +
325				"phone's sidebar, and an empty title means no lettering.\n\nA " +
326				"session's separate recordings are in the sound as well as in the " +
327				"picture: whatever was running while a clip was running is mixed into " +
328				"it, from the second of that recording the clip actually falls on — " +
329				"the same placement the blue lanes on Cut are drawn from, with the " +
330				"footage as the master. It joins the game audio rather than the " +
331				"narration, so \"Game audio under voice\" ducks both together and " +
332				"the spoken lines still sit on top. Cards are left silent: a card is " +
333				"time added to the cut, not a moment of the session, so there is " +
334				"nothing that was said under it."},
335	}

337	// stepLocked reports whether a tab's prerequisites are missing. Prepare
338	// never is -- it is where the sources are added, so a project with nothing in
339	// it still has to be able to open it -- and an unknown name (there is none, but
340	// the lookup can fail) counts as open rather than as locked: refusing to show a
341	// page is the worse mistake.
342	func (a *App) stepLocked(i int) bool {
343		if i < 0 || i >= len(steps) {
344			return false
345		}
346		switch steps[i].name {
347		case "cut":
348			return a.cutLocked
349		case "narrate":
350			// choosing a voice lives on this tab and therefore waits for a cut,
351			// which it does not need. That is deliberate: it belongs beside the lines
352			// it will speak, and hearing a sample before there is anything to narrate
353			// decides nothing you cannot decide again afterwards.
354			return a.narrateLocked
355		case "produce":
356			return a.produceLocked
357		}
358		return false
359	}
360	
361	func stepIndex(name string) int {
362		for i, s := range steps {
363			if s.name == name {
364				return i
365			}
366		}
367		return -1
368	}
369	
370	// showStep moves to a page without going through the tab's click handler --
371	// for the bounce off a locked tab, and for sending a page whose prerequisites
372	// vanished back to the start.
373	func (a *App) showStep(name string) {
374		// whatever was half-typed on the page being left is on disk before it is
375		// left: the narration boxes write on a beat after the typing stops, and
376		// clicking a tab is exactly the moment that beat has not come yet
377		a.narr.flushSave()
378		a.tabGuard = true
379		for i, s := range steps {
380			a.tabs[i].SetActive(s.name == name)
381		}
382		a.tabGuard = false
383		a.stack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
384		// the two groups on the shared bar are this page's
385		a.inStack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
386		a.outStack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
387		a.updateRunControls() // ▶ ⏹ belong to the new page's playback now
388		a.syncHelp()          // and so does the ⓘ
389		// ...and so does ▶ itself, when the ticks beside it name one step: the tab
390		// you walk to is the step you mean (followChainTick)
391		a.followChainTick(name)
392		// Cut's Inputs row lists what Suggest will be sent, and one of those things
393		// is the context box on Describe -- the page you have usually just come
394		// from. Refreshed on arrival rather than on every keystroke over there,
395		// which would re-read the session timeline as you type.
396		// ...and the tracks themselves, when the last run (or another project) moved
397		// what they are drawn from. Only then: a rebuild probes every recording and
398		// drops the undo history, which is not what a tab click should cost.
399		if name == "cut" && a.ed != nil {
400			if a.ed.stale || len(a.ed.vids) == 0 {
401				a.updateCutInfo() // which does updateInputs itself
402			} else {
403				a.ed.updateInputs()
404			}
405		}
406		// Narrate's row says the same thing about the narration, and one of the
407		// things it counts is the cut -- which is the page you have just come from
408		// and the one thing most likely to have changed under it.
409		if name == "narrate" && a.narr != nil {
410			a.narr.refit() // a clip dragged wider over there moves its line's slot here
411			a.narr.updateInputs()
412			a.narr.updateOut()
413		}
414		// ...and Produce reads both of those, plus the synthesis cache and the file
415		// it wrote last time. It is the end of the chain, so everything upstream is
416		// something that may have moved since it was last looked at.
417		if name == "produce" {
418			a.updateProduceInfo()
419			// ...and the thumbnail half reads the folder it wrote into last time,
420			// since the picture on the page is the file on disk rather than
421			// something remembered
422			if a.pub != nil {
423				a.pub.refresh()
424			}
425		}
426	}
427	
428	// syncHelp points the header ⓘ tooltip at the open page's help. Called from
429	// showStep, including the bounce off a locked tab.
430	func (a *App) syncHelp() {
431		if a.helpInfo == nil {
432			return
433		}
434		i := stepIndex(a.stack.VisibleChildName())
435		if i < 0 {
436			return
437		}
438		a.helpInfo.SetTooltipText(steps[i].label + "\n\n" + steps[i].help)
439	}

554		// several subprocesses can be live at once.

582		selTracks map[string][]int

658	
659	// The frame slider snaps to these stops; a linear 0.1..5 s scale would cram
660	// all the useful low end into the first pixel. Index 0 keeps every frame.
661	var frameStops = []float64{0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
662	var frameStopLabels = []string{"each", "0.1", "0.2", "0.5", "1s", "2s", "3s", "4s", "5s"}
663	
664	// where a session with nobody's opinion on it starts: one frame a second. Named
665	// rather than typed twice, since a new project has to land on the same stop the
666	// stepper builds itself at -- and index 0 is not it (that is every frame, which
667	// is gigabytes).
668	const defFrameStop = 4
669	
670	// Frame size presets, no-resize first because that is the default and picking a
671	// size is the exception. Name is the identity and Label is only what the drop
672	// down shows: the name goes into the project file AND into the stamp that
673	// decides whether frames must be extracted again, so it has to stay put even
674	// when the wording moves. 896w is the width the vision model gets fed.
675	var scalePresets = []struct{ Name, Label, VF string }{
676		// the label said "Resize", which on the closed button read as the
677		// control's caption and in the open list as a nonsense first choice
678		{"original", "Original", ""},
679		{"896w (LLM)", "896w (LLM)", "scale=896:-2"},
680		{"480p", "480p", "scale=-2:480"},
681		{"720p", "720p", "scale=-2:720"},
682		{"1080p", "1080p", "scale=-2:1080"},
683	}
684	
685	func (a *App) frameScale() (name, vf string) {
686		i := int(a.scalePick.Selected())
687		if i < 0 || i >= len(scalePresets) {
688			i = 0
689		}
690		return scalePresets[i].Name, scalePresets[i].VF
691	}
692	
693	func (a *App) setFrameScale(name string) {
694		for i, p := range scalePresets {
695			if p.Name == name || p.Label == name {
696				a.scalePick.SetSelected(uint(i))
697				return
698			}
699		}
700	}
701	
702	// defLanguage is what a session is assumed to be in when nobody says. It was a
703	// setting on this machine (llm.conf) and is now a field on the project, for the
704	// reason setup.go's header gives: the stack is the same every night, the
705	// footage is not.
706	const defLanguage = "en"
707	
708	// projectLanguage is the box's text as the project file stores it: what was
709	// typed, trimmed, and "" when nothing was -- an empty box means the default,
710	// and writing "en" into every project would freeze today's default into files
711	// that never asked for it (same rule as an unedited prompt).
712	func (a *App) projectLanguage() string {
713		a.promptMu.Lock()
714		defer a.promptMu.Unlock()
715		return strings.TrimSpace(a.langTxt)
716	}
717	
718	// asrLanguage is the same value with the default filled in: what Prepare puts in
719	// the request. Callable from a runner's goroutine, which is the whole reason
720	// the string is cached beside the widget rather than read off it -- the box is
721	// the GUI thread's (same rule as sessionCtx).
722	func (a *App) asrLanguage() string {
723		if s := a.projectLanguage(); s != "" {
724			return s
725		}
726		return defLanguage
727	}
728	
729	func (a *App) setLanguage(s string) {
730		a.promptMu.Lock()
731		a.langTxt = s
732		a.promptMu.Unlock()
733		// the subtitle translations are offered in every language but this one,
734		// and this is where it changes (syncLangs)
735		a.syncSubLangs()
736	}
737	
738	// applyLanguage loads a project's language into the box as well as the cache.
739	// GUI thread only, like applySessionCtx and for the same reason.
740	func (a *App) applyLanguage(s string) {
741		a.setLanguage(s)
742		if a.langEntry != nil {
743			a.langEntry.SetText(s)
744		}
745	}
746	
747	func (a *App) frameInterval() float64 { return frameStops[a.interval.i] }
748	
749	func (a *App) setFrameInterval(v float64) { a.interval.set(nearestStop(v)) }
750	
751	// nearestStop maps seconds onto the stop table -- a project may store a value
752	// from a build whose table was different, and typing is free-form.
753	func nearestStop(v float64) int {
754		best, bd := 4, math.MaxFloat64 // default 1 s
755		for i, s := range frameStops {
756			if d := math.Abs(s - v); d < bd {
757				best, bd = i, d
758			}
759		}
760		return best
761	}
762	
763	// freqPick is the frame-frequency stepper: one stop visible at a time, - / +
764	// walking the table, and the text editable by hand. Hand-rolled rather than a
765	// GtkSpinButton because the spin button re-reads its own display as a plain
766	// number before every step -- and "each" and "1s" are not numbers, so every
767	// click first corrupted the value it was about to step.
768	type freqPick struct {
769		box   *gtk.Box
770		entry *gtk.Entry
771		i     int
772	}
773	
774	func newFreqPick() *freqPick {
775		f := &freqPick{}
776		f.entry = gtk.NewEntry()
777		f.entry.SetWidthChars(4)
778		f.entry.SetMaxWidthChars(4)
779		f.entry.SetAlignment(0.5)
780		f.entry.SetTooltipText("Seconds between frames — type 0.1 to 5, or 'each' for every frame")
781		f.entry.ConnectActivate(f.parse)
782		// clicking elsewhere commits like Enter does: a half-typed value silently
783		// kept on screen would not be the value a run then uses
784		fc := gtk.NewEventControllerFocus()
785		fc.ConnectLeave(f.parse)
786		f.entry.AddController(fc)
787	
788		minus := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-remove-symbolic")
789		minus.ConnectClicked(func() { f.set(f.i - 1) })
790		plus := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-add-symbolic")
791		plus.ConnectClicked(func() { f.set(f.i + 1) })
792	
793		f.box = gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 0)
794		f.box.AddCSSClass("linked") // one control, three parts
795		f.box.Append(f.entry)
796		f.box.Append(minus)
797		f.box.Append(plus)
798		f.set(defFrameStop)
799		return f
800	}
801	
802	// set clamps to the table -- past either end the buttons simply stop moving.
803	func (f *freqPick) set(i int) {
804		if i < 0 {
805			i = 0
806		}
807		if i >= len(frameStops) {
808			i = len(frameStops) - 1
809		}
810		f.i = i
811		f.entry.SetText(frameStopLabels[i])
812	}
813	
814	// parse commits a typed value: seconds with or without the s, or "each"/"0"
815	// for every frame, landing on the nearest stop. Anything unreadable snaps the
816	// display back to the value still in force.
817	func (f *freqPick) parse() {
818		t := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.entry.Text())), "s")
819		if t == "each" {
820			f.set(0)
821			return
822		}
823		v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(t, 64)
824		if err != nil || v < 0 {
825			f.set(f.i)
826			return
827		}
828		f.set(nearestStop(v))
829	}
830	
831	// Where each step writes: folders named for their steps (step1/..step6/ once;
832	// migrateFolders moves them). Prepare's three jobs are under its name --
833	// prepare/inputs/, prepare/describe/, prepare/transcript/.
834	func (a *App) prepareDir() string    { return filepath.Join(a.outDir, "prepare") }
835	func (a *App) inputsDir() string     { return filepath.Join(a.prepareDir(), "inputs") }
836	func (a *App) describeDir() string   { return filepath.Join(a.prepareDir(), "describe") }
837	func (a *App) transcriptDir() string { return filepath.Join(a.prepareDir(), "transcript") }
838	func (a *App) narrateDir() string    { return filepath.Join(a.outDir, "narrate") }
839	func (a *App) produceDir() string    { return filepath.Join(a.outDir, "produce") }
840	
841	// framesDir is where the first half of Prepare leaves one video's frames:
842	// the describer reads them and the Cut page waits for them, so the path is
843	// named once.
844	func (a *App) framesDir(base string) string {
845		return filepath.Join(a.inputsDir(), "frames", base)
846	}
847	
848	// canCut is what the Cut page needs: frames out of a source marked as footage
849	// -- not session.tsv. A silent capture or a session nobody wants described is
850	// cut by hand; what Describe adds is text ON the timeline, and having none is
851	// an empty track, not a locked page.
852	// canCut is whether there is anything to lay on the tracks: one source marked
853	// as footage, and nothing more.
854	//
855	// It used to be "somebody has extracted frames", which locked the page until
856	// Prepare had run. But a recording is a lane before it is a transcript: its
857	// length, its shape and its sound are in the file itself, and laying the
858	// session out -- seeing where the takes fall against each other, shifting one
859	// by hand, hearing it -- is work that comes BEFORE describing anything. The
860	// frames are the pictures drawn on the lane, and a lane without them is a lane
861	// with no pictures on it, not a page that cannot be opened.
862	//
863	// What still needs Prepare is the SUGGESTION, and suggestClicked says so in
864	// the one place it is true: "run Describe first -- the suggestion reads the
865	// session timeline, and there is none".
866	func (a *App) canCut() bool {
867		vids, _ := a.snapSources()
868		return len(vids) > 0
869	}
870	
871	func main() {
872		a := &App{curCmds: map[*exec.Cmd]bool{}}
873		wd, _ := os.Getwd()
874		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(wd, "input_video")); err != nil {
875			// started elsewhere: the binary lives in <root>/gui
876			exe, _ := os.Executable()
877			wd = filepath.Dir(filepath.Dir(exe))
878		}
879		a.root = wd
880		a.vidDir = filepath.Join(wd, "input_video")
881		a.audDir = filepath.Join(wd, "input_audio")
882		// A session always has a file, before anyone saves one (see projExt). Set
883		// here rather than through setProject, which refreshes pages that do not
884		// exist yet; from build() on, setProject is the only thing that moves it.
885		a.projPath = filepath.Join(wd, workName)
886		a.outDir = dataDir(a.projPath)
887	
888		// HandlesOpen is the double-click. Without the flag gio treats a file
889		// argument as an error and refuses to start; with it, the desktop's "open
890		// with Naivepost" arrives at ConnectOpen and a bare launch still goes to
891		// ConnectActivate. GApplication is single-instance, so a double-click while
892		// a window is up is forwarded to this same process rather than starting a
893		// second one -- which is why open loads into the window that exists instead
894		// of building another.
895		app := gtk.NewApplication(appID, gio.ApplicationHandlesOpen)
896		app.ConnectActivate(func() {
897			a.build(app)
898			a.startHangWatch() // a stuck main loop writes its own stacks (hangwatch.go)
899		})
900		app.ConnectOpen(func(files []gio.Filer, _ string) {
901			var path string
902			if len(files) > 0 {
903				path = files[0].Path() // one window, one project: the rest are ignored
904			}
905			if a.win == nil {
906				a.openPath = path
907				a.build(app)
908				return
909			}
910			if path != "" {
911				a.loadProjectFrom(path)
912			}
913			a.win.Present()
914		})
915		os.Exit(app.Run(os.Args))
916	}
917	
918	// ---- state -----------------------------------------------------------------
919	
920	// loadMeta reads inputs/meta.env: the primary video and recording of the last
921	// run, and the frame settings it ran with. Its existence is also the marker
922	// that Prepare has run at all -- either of the two files may be missing from a
923	// legitimate session, so the keys are not that marker.
924	func (a *App) loadMeta() map[string]string {
925		m := map[string]string{}
926		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(a.outDir, "inputs", "meta.env"))
927		if err != nil {
928			return m
929		}
930		for _, line := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
931			if k, v, ok := strings.Cut(line, "="); ok {
932				m[k] = v
933			}
934		}
935		return m
936	}
937	
938	// snapSources caches the session's sources for background runners, which must
939	// never touch the list widget. Split by role: the footage, then everything
940	// else; every source is in exactly one of the two.
941	func (a *App) snapSources() (vids, auds []string) {

948	// snapItems takes one list of sources as the run's snapshot and hands back the
949	// two path lists the pipeline works from. It goes through a sourceList of its
950	// own rather than reading the fields: what counts as footage and who holds a
951	// narrator slot are that type's rules, and the run must not answer either
952	// question differently from the page.
953	func (a *App) snapItems(items []sourceItem) (vids, auds []string) {
954		l := sourceList{items: items} // the rules, without the widget
955		vids, auds = l.split()
956		var narr [narratorSlots]string
957		for n := 1; n <= narratorSlots; n++ {
958			narr[n-1] = l.narratorPath(n)
959		}
960		// only the rows that answered, so the map is empty for every session that
961		// has no multi-track file in it and nothing downstream has to tell "the
962		// first track" from "no answer" a second time
963		tracks := map[string][]int{}
964		for _, it := range items {
965			if len(it.tracks) > 0 {
966				tracks[it.path] = append([]int(nil), it.tracks...)
967			}
968		}
969		a.srcMu.Lock()
970		a.selItems, a.selVid, a.selAud, a.selNarr, a.selTracks = items, vids, auds, narr, tracks
971		a.srcMu.Unlock()
972		return
973	}
974

978	func (a *App) snappedTracks() map[string][]int {
979		a.srcMu.Lock()
980		defer a.srcMu.Unlock()
981		return a.selTracks
982	}

1466		}
1467		buf := a.log.Buffer()

1469		buf.Insert(end, fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)+"\n")
1470		mark := buf.CreateMark("", buf.EndIter(), false)

1472		buf.DeleteMark(mark)

1479	// A watchdog for the GTK thread: a heartbeat on the main loop, watched by its
1480	// own goroutine. When the beat is hangStall late, every goroutine's stack goes
1481	// to hang-<time>.txt beside the settings and to stderr -- the Go frames above
1482	// the blocked C call say which seek or state change never came back. One dump
1483	// per hang.
1484	
1485	const (
1486		hangBeat  = 200 * time.Millisecond // how often the main loop says it is alive
1487		hangStall = 3 * time.Second        // how late a beat has to be to count as a hang
1488	)
1489	
1490	// startHangWatch installs the heartbeat and the watcher. Called once the main
1491	// loop exists; harmless before the window does.
1492	func (a *App) startHangWatch() {
1493		var last atomic.Int64
1494		last.Store(time.Now().UnixNano())
1495		glib.TimeoutAdd(uint(hangBeat/time.Millisecond), func() bool {
1496			last.Store(time.Now().UnixNano())
1497			return true
1498		})
1499		go func() {
1500			dumped := false
1501			for range time.Tick(hangBeat) {
1502				late := time.Since(time.Unix(0, last.Load()))
1503				if late < hangStall {
1504					dumped = false
1505					continue
1506				}
1507				if dumped {
1508					continue
1509				}
1510				dumped = true
1511				a.dumpHang(late)
1512			}
1513		}()
1514	}
1515	
1516	// dumpHang writes every goroutine's stack. Not through the log: the log is a
1517	// widget on the thread that is stuck.
1518	func (a *App) dumpHang(late time.Duration) {
1519		buf := make([]byte, 1<<20)
1520		n := runtime.Stack(buf, true)
1521		head := fmt.Sprintf("naivepost: the GTK thread has not answered for %s -- every goroutine's stack follows\n\n", late.Round(100*time.Millisecond))
1522		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, head)
1523		os.Stderr.Write(buf[:n])
1524		dir := configDir()
1525		if dir == "" {
1526			return
1527		}
1528		p := filepath.Join(dir, "hang-"+time.Now().Format("0102-150405")+".txt")
1529		os.WriteFile(p, append([]byte(head), buf[:n]...), 0o600)
1530		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nnaivepost: written to %s\n", p)
1531	}

18	// starts what the page does and then pauses and resumes it, ⏹ ends it. Without

1	package main
2	
3	// Running the whole pipeline in one press.
4	//
5	// Each step is its own goroutine that ends on the GUI thread through endRun,
6	// so a chain is a LIST that endRun advances: the step that finished says what
7	// became of it, and the next is started or the chain is abandoned. Nothing
8	// about a step has to know it is in one.
9	//
10	// The steps are the pages, in the order the pipeline runs them, because that
11	// is the only order that makes sense: the cut reads what Prepare wrote, the
12	// narration is written over the cut, and the render needs both.
13	
14	import (
15		"fmt"
16		"strings"
17		"time"
18	
19		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gtk/v4"
20	)
21	
22	// the steps a chain can hold, in pipeline order: the page each runs on, and
23	// what to call it in the menu.
24	var chainSteps = []struct{ page, name string }{
25		{"prep", "Prepare"},
26		{"cut", "Cut"},
27		{"narrate", "Narrate"},
28		{"produce", "Produce"},
29	}
30	
31	// chainRun starts a chain: the ticked steps, in order, from the first one on.
32	func (a *App) chainRun() {
33		if a.busy() {
34			return
35		}
36		want := a.chainPicked()
37		if len(want) == 0 {
38			a.setStatus("nothing ticked beside ▶ — tick the steps to run")
39			return
40		}
41		a.chain = want
42		a.chainFrom, a.chainAt = time.Now(), time.Now()
43		a.chainRan = nil
44		a.logf(">>> run: %s", strings.Join(a.chainNames(want), " → "))
45		a.chainNext()
46	}
47	
48	// chainTime is a stretch of a run said the way a person would: under a minute
49	// in seconds, over it in minutes and seconds. Not mmss -- "3:04" beside a step
50	// name reads as a timestamp in the session rather than as how long the step
51	// took, and this is the one number on the page that is a duration.
52	func chainTime(d time.Duration) string {
53		s := d.Seconds()
54		if s < 60 {
55			return fmt.Sprintf("%.0fs", s)
56		}
57		return fmt.Sprintf("%dm %02ds", int(s)/60, int(s)%60)
58	}
59	
60	// chainNext takes the next step off the chain and runs it, on the page it
61	// belongs to: a step's own ▶ works on the widgets of its page, and a page that
62	// was never shown has none.
63	func (a *App) chainNext() {
64		for len(a.chain) > 0 {
65			page := a.chain[0]
66			a.chain = a.chain[1:]
67			if page == "narrate" && a.narrOff {
68				a.logf(">>> run: Narrate skipped — this video has no narration")
69				continue
70			}
71			// Cut refuses over hand edits, and in a chain that refusal would be a
72			// halt nobody asked for: the edits are the answer, so the step has
73			// nothing to do and the rest of the chain still does.
74			if page == "cut" && a.ed != nil && len(a.ed.segs) > 0 && !sameCut(a.ed.segs, a.ed.base.segs) {
75				a.logf(">>> run: Cut skipped — the cut has hand edits, which are kept")
76				continue
77			}
78			// showStep, not the stack: moving a page is more than showing it. It
79			// swaps the tab row and the two bars, and -- the half that matters
80			// here -- it REBUILDS the cut's tracks when a run has moved what they
81			// are drawn from, synchronously, before anything presses that page's
82			// button. Setting the stack's child alone left the cut asking about a
83			// session it had not loaded: Prepare finished, the chain reached Cut
84			// with an editor that still had no recordings in it, and the step
85			// came to nothing.
86			a.chainMoving = true
87			a.showStep(page)
88			a.chainMoving = false
89			a.logf(">>> run: %s", a.pageName(page))
90			a.chainStep, a.chainAt = page, time.Now()
91			a.runPageNow(page)
92			if !a.running {
93				// the step declined -- nothing to do, or it refused -- so the
94				// chain has to carry itself rather than wait for an endRun that
95				// is not coming. Its clock goes with it: a step that never ran
96				// has no duration, and leaving the marker set would put the next
97				// press on a page of its own into this chain's tally.
98				a.chainStep = ""
99				continue
100			}
101			return
102		}
103		a.chainEnd("done")
104	}
105	
106	// chainDone is endRun's half: the step that just finished either hands the
107	// chain on or ends it. Stopped or failed, the rest is abandoned -- a chain
108	// exists to save presses, not to carry on past the answer going wrong.
109	func (a *App) chainDone() {
110		if a.chainStep == "" {
111			return // no chain under way: a step pressed on its own page
112		}
113		// how long that step took, kept for the line at the end. Timed here rather
114		// than by each step, because what a chain is about is the WAIT -- the
115		// whole press, not the part of it any one page is responsible for.
116		a.chainRan = append(a.chainRan, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s",
117			a.pageName(a.chainStep), chainTime(time.Since(a.chainAt))))
118		a.chainStep = ""
119		if a.stopFlag.Load() {
120			a.chainEnd("stopped")
121			return
122		}
123		if len(a.chain) == 0 {
124			a.chainEnd("done")
125			return
126		}
127		a.chainNext()
128	}
129	
130	// chainEnd says what the whole press cost, and what it did not get to. Only
131	// worth a line for a chain of more than one: a single step already says what
132	// it did, and "Prepare 9m 12s — total 9m 12s" is the same number twice.
133	func (a *App) chainEnd(how string) {
134		left := len(a.chain)
135		a.chain, a.chainStep = nil, ""
136		if len(a.chainRan) == 0 {
137			return
138		}
139		total := chainTime(time.Since(a.chainFrom))
140		if len(a.chainRan) == 1 && left == 0 {
141			a.chainRan = nil
142			return
143		}
144		switch {
145		case how == "stopped":
146			a.logf(">>> run: stopped after %s — %s — %d step(s) left undone",
147				total, strings.Join(a.chainRan, ", "), left)
148			a.setStatus("stopped after " + total)
149		case left > 0:
150			a.logf(">>> run: %s — %s — %d step(s) left undone",
151				total, strings.Join(a.chainRan, ", "), left)
152			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("ran %s, %d left undone", total, left))
153		default:
154			a.logf(">>> run: all done in %s — %s", total, strings.Join(a.chainRan, ", "))
155			a.setStatus("all done in " + total)
156		}
157		a.chainRan = nil
158	}
159	
160	func (a *App) pageName(page string) string {
161		for _, s := range chainSteps {
162			if s.page == page {
163				return s.name
164			}
165		}
166		return page
167	}
168	
169	func (a *App) chainNames(pages []string) []string {
170		var out []string
171		for _, p := range pages {
172			out = append(out, a.pageName(p))
173		}
174		return out
175	}
176	
177	// chainPicked is the steps ticked, in pipeline order.
178	func (a *App) chainPicked() []string {
179		var out []string
180		for _, s := range chainSteps {
181			if t := a.chainTicks[s.page]; t != nil && t.Active() {
182				out = append(out, s.page)
183			}
184		}
185		return out
186	}
187	
188	// buildChainMenu is the ticks beside ▶ and the button that runs them. A menu
189	// rather than a second ▶: which steps is a standing answer, not a choice made
190	// on every press, and the button says which are on with the menu shut.
191	func (a *App) buildChainMenu() *gtk.Box {
192		pop := gtk.NewPopover()
193		list := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
194		list.SetMarginTop(6)
195		list.SetMarginBottom(6)
196		list.SetMarginStart(10)
197		list.SetMarginEnd(10)
198		a.chainTicks = map[string]*gtk.CheckButton{}
199		for _, s := range chainSteps {
200			s := s
201			c := gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel(s.name)
202			// Prepare alone to begin with: it is the one step a fresh project can
203			// run, and the only one whose inputs are on disk before anything else
204			// has happened. The rest are a tick away, and the answer is kept with
205			// the project.
206			c.SetActive(s.page == chainSteps[0].page)
207			c.ConnectToggled(func() {
208				a.syncChain()
209				if !a.chainQuiet {
210					a.saveProjectNow()
211				}
212			})
213			a.chainTicks[s.page] = c
214			list.Append(c)
215		}
216		pop.SetChild(list)
217	
218		a.chainPick = gtk.NewMenuButton()
219		a.chainPick.SetPopover(pop)
220		a.chainPick.SetTooltipText("Which steps ▶ runs, in this order. Narrate skips itself " +
221			"when the video has no narration, and Cut skips itself when the cut has hand edits.")
222		// one control in two halves, the split button's shape: press ▶ for the
223		// thing, press the arrow for which thing. GTK4 has no AdwSplitButton
224		// without libadwaita, and does not need one -- a linked box of a button
225		// and a menu button IS that control, and is what the tab row and the
226		// stepper on this window are already made of (widgets.go).
227		//
228		// ▶ itself is the left half: there is one thing to press on this bar, and
229		// two play buttons beside each other -- one for this page, one for
230		// several -- was one too many.
231		box := linked(a.playBtn, a.chainPick)
232		a.syncChain()
233		return box
234	}
235	
236	// followChainTick moves a lone tick to the page just opened.
237	//
238	// The ticks are a standing answer -- which steps ▶ runs -- and most of the time
239	// there is exactly one, the step being worked on. Walking to another tab is
240	// then the whole of "I am working on that one now", and having to open the menu
241	// to say it again is a second answer to the same question: press ▶ on Cut with
242	// Prepare ticked and Prepare runs, which is never what the press meant.
243	//
244	// Only when exactly ONE is ticked. Several ticked is a chain somebody built on
245	// purpose -- Prepare → Cut → Produce -- and a tab click must not rewrite it.
246	//
247	// A run does not stop it. It used to: the chain moves the pages itself
248	// (chainNext), and switching this off for the whole run was the blunt way of
249	// keeping it from retargeting the ticks as the chain walked them. The cost was
250	// that walking to another tab while a step ran did nothing, which is exactly
251	// when you do it -- Prepare takes an hour and you go and look at Cut. So the
252	// guard is now the chain's own move rather than the run: chainMoving is set
253	// only around the page changes chainNext makes.
254	func (a *App) followChainTick(page string) {
255		if a.chainTicks == nil || a.chainMoving {
256			return
257		}
258		if a.chainTicks[page] == nil {
259			return // a page the chain has no step for
260		}
261		picked := a.chainPicked()
262		if len(picked) != 1 || picked[0] == page {
263			return
264		}
265		// quietly, then one save: two toggles through the handler would be two
266		// writes of the project for one gesture
267		a.chainQuiet = true
268		a.chainTicks[picked[0]].SetActive(false)
269		a.chainTicks[page].SetActive(true)
270		a.chainQuiet = false
271		a.syncChain()
272		a.saveProjectNow()
273	}
274	
275	// syncChain puts the answer on the button.
276	func (a *App) syncChain() {
277		if a.chainPick == nil {
278			return
279		}
280		n := len(a.chainPicked())
281		switch n {
282		case 0:
283			a.chainPick.SetLabel("none")
284		case len(chainSteps):
285			a.chainPick.SetLabel("all")
286		default:
287			a.chainPick.SetLabel(fmt.Sprintf("%d steps", n))
288		}
289	}
290	
291	// applyChain is a project's answer, put on the ticks without saving it back. A
292	// project written before this has none, and gets the first step alone -- the
293	// same as a new one.
294	func (a *App) applyChain(pages []string) {
295		if a.chainTicks == nil {
296			a.chainSteps = pages
297			return
298		}
299		a.chainQuiet = true
300		if pages == nil {
301			for page, t := range a.chainTicks {
302				t.SetActive(page == chainSteps[0].page)
303			}
304		} else {
305			on := map[string]bool{}
306			for _, p := range pages {
307				on[p] = true
308			}
309			for page, t := range a.chainTicks {
310				t.SetActive(on[page])
311			}
312		}
313		a.chainQuiet = false
314		a.syncChain()
315	}

3	// The run queue: what one press of ▶ turned into, in order. A job fills it as
4	// work is found, the runner picks tasks off the front, and the bar says one
5	// short line: which job, which of the run's jobs, what the head task is doing,
6	// how far down the queue. Filenames belong in the log. The bar's FRACTION is
7	// not the queue's length -- the queue grows as it is opened, and a total that
8	// grows under a fraction drags the bar backwards -- but the weighted tracks
9	// (prog).
10

20	// The two tracks are the two halves of the bar. They are concurrent in Prepare
21	// (speech recognition on the GPU, frame extraction on the CPU) and sequential
22	// on Describe + Transcript, but the arithmetic is the same either way: each
23	// track reports its own absolute contribution and the bar shows the sum.
24	// Letting either write a raw fraction would make the bar bounce between them.
25	const (
26		trackSTT    = 0
27		trackFrames = 1
28		// the same two tracks under the names the Describe + Transcript step uses
29		// them for: its two jobs run one after the other, but each still owns half
30		// the bar and its own line
31		trackDescribe = trackSTT
32		trackFix      = trackFrames
33	)

35	// qTrack is one half of the bar: the job on it, the work it has left, and what
36	// the task at the head of the queue is doing this second.
37	type qTrack struct {
38		job        string // "describe", "speech", "narrate" — what this half is
39		phase, of  int    // ...and which of the run's jobs it is, when there are two
40		queued     int    // tasks known about, including the ones already taken
41		taken      int    // how many have been picked up: the head's position
42		what       string // what the head is doing, in two or three words
43		kind       string // what a task of this queue is, when nothing else is said
44		doneJob    bool   // the job finished; the other track may still be going
45		everFilled bool   // a queue that was filled and emptied is not an unfilled one
46	}
47	
48	// line is a track's whole contribution to the bar:
49	//
50	//	describe 1/2: chunk 4/12
51	//	transcript 2/2: fixing block 3/7
52	//	speech: recognising 2/3
53	//
54	// Every piece is dropped when it has nothing to say, so a job with one task and
55	// no phases is simply "thumbnail: drawing".
56	func (t qTrack) line() string {
57		if t.doneJob {
58			if t.job == "" {
59				return ""
60			}
61			return t.job + " done"
62		}
63		head := t.job
64		if t.of > 1 {
65			head += fmt.Sprintf(" %d/%d", t.phase, t.of)
66		}
67		what := t.what
68		if what == "" {
69			what = t.kind
70		}
71		if t.everFilled && t.taken > 0 {
72			pos := fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", t.taken, max(t.queued, t.taken))
73			if what == "" {
74				what = pos
75			} else {
76				what += " " + pos
77			}
78		}
79		switch {
80		case head == "":
81			return what
82		case what == "":
83			return head
84		}
85		return head + ": " + what
86	}

89	
90	// qReset empties both halves. A run starts here: the tracks are summed, so last
91	// run's leftovers would be added to every reading this one takes. It also gives
92	// the bar back to whatever runs next, whole (see qPhase).
93	func (a *App) qReset() {
94		// the exchange page belongs to the run, and this is the one call every run
95		// makes at its start: closing the old page here means the next LLM call
96		// opens a new one, named for whichever step makes it (llmlog.go)
97		a.llmMu.Lock()
98		a.runName, a.runSecs, a.runN = "", nil, 0
99		a.llmMu.Unlock()
100		a.progMu.Lock()
101		a.progParts = [2]float64{}
102		a.progQ = [2]qTrack{}
103		a.progBase, a.progShare = 0, 0
104		a.progMu.Unlock()
105		a.showProg()
106	}
107	
108	// qPhase says where in the bar the jobs that come next are drawn (base, share)
109	// and clears the queue for them. A single-step press never calls it; Prepare's
110	// ▶ is two steps back to back, each reporting its own whole bar, and the
111	// scaling happens here rather than in every place that moves the needle. A
112	// phase that has reported nothing stands where the one before it finished.
113	func (a *App) qPhase(base, share float64) {
114		a.progMu.Lock()
115		a.progBase, a.progShare = base, share
116		a.progQ = [2]qTrack{}
117		a.progParts = [2]float64{base / 2, base / 2}
118		a.progMu.Unlock()
119		a.showProg()
120	}
121	
122	// scaled maps a track's own fraction into the phase's slice of the bar. Share 0
123	// means no phase was set, which is the whole bar -- that is every step but
124	// Prepare, and it is also the headless App the tests build. Called with
125	// progMu held.
126	func (a *App) scaled(f float64) float64 {
127		if a.progShare == 0 {
128			return f
129		}
130		return a.progBase/2 + f*a.progShare
131	}
132	
133	// qJob says which job now owns a track, and which of the run's jobs it is --
134	// "describe 1/2", then "transcript 2/2". Pass of = 0 for a run that is one job,
135	// or whose jobs are concurrent and named rather than numbered.
136	func (a *App) qJob(track int, job string, phase, of int) {
137		a.progMu.Lock()
138		a.progQ[track] = qTrack{job: job, phase: phase, of: of}
139		a.progMu.Unlock()
140		a.showProg()
141	}

143	// qPush queues n more tasks of one kind. Called again whenever more work is
144	// found: a run that could count all of its work in advance would not need a
145	// queue.
146	func (a *App) qPush(track, n int, kind string) {
147		if n <= 0 {
148			return
149		}
150		a.progMu.Lock()
151		t := &a.progQ[track]
152		t.queued += n
153		t.everFilled = true
154		if kind != "" {
155			t.kind = kind
156		}
157		a.progMu.Unlock()
158		a.showProg()
159	}

161	// qTake picks the next task up. It is called once per task whatever becomes of
162	// it -- work already on disk from an earlier run is a task this run is done
163	// with, and a queue that skipped those would stall at the position where the
164	// resume started.
165	func (a *App) qTake(track int) {
166		a.progMu.Lock()
167		t := &a.progQ[track]
168		t.taken++
169		t.what = ""
170		a.progMu.Unlock()
171		a.showProg()
172	}

210		// Before the model unload below, which is housekeeping: the next step

214		// server is memory nothing is waiting on any more (freeAudioModels). Off
215		// the GUI thread, because it is a request over the network and the window
216		// has to come back to life now, not when the server answers.
217		go a.freeAudioModels()

221	// is the track's absolute contribution; the text is two or three words, no
222	// filename, no count (the queue counts, the log names). An empty format falls
223	// back to the task's kind ("chunk 4/12").
224	func (a *App) prog(track int, f float64, format string, args ...any) {
225		txt := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
226		a.progMu.Lock()
227		a.progParts[track] = a.scaled(f)
228		a.progQ[track].what = txt
229		a.progMu.Unlock()
230		a.showProg()
231	}

233	// pulseUntilCounted keeps the bar moving while a model thinks. The LLM calls
234	// have nothing countable in them, so the bar pulses until something with real
235	// news -- the thumbnail's first drawing fraction -- takes the needle. What
236	// stops it is that fraction rather than a flag set from the goroutine: Pulse
237	// and SetFraction drive the same needle, so the one that lasts has to be the
238	// one with news -- and reading progParts under its mutex is also the only way
239	// to ask this question from the GUI thread without racing the runner.
240	func (a *App) pulseUntilCounted() {
241		glib.TimeoutAdd(150, func() bool {
242			if !a.running {
243				return false
244			}
245			a.progMu.Lock()
246			counted := a.progParts[trackSTT] > 0
247			a.progMu.Unlock()
248			if counted {
249				return false
250			}
251			a.progress.Pulse()
252			return true
253		})
254	}

256	// showProg puts the two halves on the bar: the fractions summed, the lines
257	// joined. Callers are worker goroutines, so the widget is touched on the GUI
258	// thread and nowhere else.
259	func (a *App) showProg() {
260		a.progMu.Lock()
261		total := math.Max(0, math.Min(1, a.progParts[0]+a.progParts[1]))
262		text, tip := progLine(a.progQ)
263		a.progMu.Unlock()
264		if a.progress == nil {
265			return // a headless App under the tests
266		}
267		glib.IdleAdd(func() {
268			a.progress.SetFraction(total)
269			a.setStatus(text) // the bar is a fraction; the words are the status line's
270			if tip != "" {
271				// a run with nothing queued yet leaves the standing tooltip -- the
272				// one that says how to read the bar -- rather than blanking it
273				a.progress.SetTooltipText(tip)
274			}
275		})
276	}
277	
278	// progLine is the bar's text and its tooltip. The text is the short one: at
279	// most two jobs, joined, each of them a few words. The tooltip is where the
280	// counting is spelled out, for the one moment anyone wants it.
281	func progLine(q [2]qTrack) (text, tip string) {
282		var lines, tips []string
283		for _, t := range q {
284			if s := t.line(); s != "" {
285				lines = append(lines, s)
286			}
287			if t.job == "" || !t.everFilled {
288				continue
289			}
290			switch left := max(t.queued, t.taken) - t.taken; {
291			case t.doneJob:
292				tips = append(tips, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %d task(s), all done", t.job, t.taken))
293			case left == 0:
294				tips = append(tips, fmt.Sprintf("%s: task %d of %d, none waiting",
295					t.job, t.taken, max(t.queued, t.taken)))
296			default:
297				tips = append(tips, fmt.Sprintf("%s: task %d of %d, %d waiting",
298					t.job, t.taken, t.queued, left))
299			}
300		}
301		return strings.Join(lines, "  ·  "), strings.Join(tips, "\n")
302	}

33	// diarWins is the window lengths diarization is tried at, longest first.
34	//
35	// Sortformer refuses a request past its encoder position table -- measured, 90 s
36	// passes and 150 s does not -- so 90 is the most it can be ASKED. What the
37	// table cannot say is whether the MACHINE can find the memory for it: the
38	// backend allocates one contiguous buffer per request and it grows with the
39	// window, 2.9 GB at 90 s. Measured on this box with an LLM's weights pinned
40	// beside it: 90 s failed to allocate, 45 s answered in 400 ms, 5 s likewise.
41	// So the window is a preference rather than a constant -- the pass runs at the
42	// first length the server can actually hold, and a diarization at 25 s is a
43	// slower diarization rather than none.
44	var diarWins = []float64{diarWin, 45, 25}
45	
46	var errStopped = errors.New("stopped by user")

48	// Where the local audio.cpp stack lives, what it runs on and what language it
49	// expects are settings now, not constants -- see appConf in setup.go. What
50	// stays here is what is measured rather than chosen: change these and the
51	// models misbehave, which is not a preference anyone can hold.
52	const (
53		sampleRate = 16000 // what the ASR and diarization models are trained on
54	
55		// Sortformer refuses requests past its encoder position table (measured:
56		// 90 s passes, 150 s does not), and its slot names mean nothing across
57		// requests. Every window therefore carries the same short anchor clip of
58		// known voices in front; whichever slot owns an anchor block IS that voice.
59		diarWin   = 90.0 // the longest window, and the first one tried (diarWins)
60		anchorPer = 12.0 // seconds of each voice in the anchor, at diarWin
61		// shortTake is the length under which a recording is a start/stop rather
62		// than a take: the recorder was opened and closed again. Such a file
63		// carries no speech, no anchor for a voice, and not even one whole frame
64		// interval; it is written up as silence and the run carries on.
65		shortTake = 2.0
66		// anchorCut is the shortest stretch of one voice worth cutting into the
67		// anchor; anything under it cannot carry a voice
68		anchorCut   = 0.3
69		anchorMin   = 4.0 // speech that makes a slot count as a voice
70		minAnchorOv = 0.5 // anchor-block overlap to claim a slot
71		diarTurnGap = 0.5 // merge same-speaker turns closer than this
72		// pass 1's stride as a share of the window: it only has to see each voice
73		// once, so it steps two thirds of a window and overlaps the rest.
74		diarHopShare = 2.0 / 3.0
75	
76		// The ASR encoders have a position table a session is far past (Nemotron
77		// refuses well before 12 minutes; others run full context over the whole
78		// recording). Long audio goes in as chunks, cut where nobody is talking.
79		asrChunkMax  = 300.0 // longest audio in one ASR request
80		asrChunkQwen = 60.0  // ...and for a model that allocates by the second (asrChunk)
81		// and the shortest it is worth halving to. Under this the chunk edges
82		// outnumber the sentences: every edge costs the decoder its context, and a
83		// transcript cut into ten-second pieces is a worse answer than no answer,
84		// which at least says so.
85		asrChunkMin = 20.0
86		asrCutSeek  = 20.0 // how far from an even cut a silence is worth taking
87		asrQuietDB  = -35  // what counts as quiet, in dBFS
88		asrQuietMin = 0.4  // and for how long

102	// ---- run control -----------------------------------------------------------
103	
104	// checkpoint is where pause and stop take effect: between subprocesses, never
105	// inside one -- a GPU job cannot be meaningfully frozen halfway.
106	func (a *App) checkpoint() error {
107		for {
108			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
109				return errStopped
110			}
111			if !a.pauseFlag.Load() {
112				return nil
113			}
114			time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
115		}
116	}

118	// ---- process plumbing ------------------------------------------------------
119	
120	// runCmd runs a subprocess and remembers it, so the stop button can kill it.
121	// A kill while stopFlag is set reports as errStopped, not as a failure.
122	//
123	// The command goes in the log BEFORE it runs, every time. Every subprocess this
124	// app starts is an ffmpeg, and what it is asked to do is the whole of what
125	// comes out: a flag in the wrong place is a video that plays two frames out of
126	// sync in one player and fine in another, and the answer to "what did it
127	// actually run" should not be reading the source. Written as a shell would
128	// take it, so it can be pasted, edited and run by hand.
129	func (a *App) runCmd(name string, args ...string) error {
130		a.logCmd(name, args)
131		cmd := exec.Command(name, args...)
132		var out bytes.Buffer
133		cmd.Stdout = &out
134		cmd.Stderr = &out
135		a.ctlMu.Lock()
136		a.curCmds[cmd] = true
137		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
138		err := cmd.Run()
139		a.ctlMu.Lock()
140		delete(a.curCmds, cmd)
141		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
142		if err != nil {
143			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
144				return errStopped
145			}
146			tail := out.String()
147			if len(tail) > 400 {
148				tail = tail[len(tail)-400:]
149			}
150			// the whole command in the error as well as in the log: an error is
151			// read where it lands -- a status line, a FAILED line at the end of a
152			// run -- and hunting back up the log for the line that goes with it is
153			// the part nobody does
154			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w\n%s\n%s", name, err, cmdLine(name, args), tail)
155		}
156		return nil
157	}
158	
159	// logCmd puts one command in the log, at the detail indent the steps use for
160	// what they are doing rather than what they decided.
161	func (a *App) logCmd(name string, args []string) {
162		a.logfIdle("    $ %s", cmdLine(name, args))
163	}
164	
165	// cmdLine is a command as a shell would take it: every argument that needs
166	// quoting quoted, and the rest left alone. The paths in this app have spaces in
167	// them ("2026-09-10 15-04-39.mkv"), so a line printed with bare %v is a line
168	// that looks runnable and is not.
169	func cmdLine(name string, args []string) string {
170		out := make([]string, 0, len(args)+1)
171		out = append(out, shellArg(name))
172		for _, a := range args {
173			out = append(out, shellArg(a))
174		}
175		return strings.Join(out, " ")
176	}
177	
178	// shellArg quotes one argument the way sh wants it: single quotes, with any
179	// single quote inside closed, escaped and reopened.
180	func shellArg(s string) string {
181		if s != "" && !strings.ContainsFunc(s, needsQuote) {
182			return s
183		}
184		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"
185	}
186	
187	func needsQuote(r rune) bool {
188		switch {
189		case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':
190			return false
191		}
192		return !strings.ContainsRune("_@%+=:,./-", r)
193	}

195	// ffmpegProgress runs ffmpeg reporting completion against a known duration,
196	// for the long single-invocation phases (frame extraction).
197	func (a *App) ffmpegProgress(dur float64, cb func(float64), args ...string) error {
198		full := append([]string{"-progress", "pipe:1", "-nostats"}, args...)
199		a.logCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), full)
200		cmd := exec.Command(ffTool("ffmpeg"), full...)
201		var errBuf bytes.Buffer
202		cmd.Stderr = &errBuf
203		out, err := cmd.StdoutPipe()
204		if err != nil {
205			return err
206		}
207		a.ctlMu.Lock()
208		a.curCmds[cmd] = true
209		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
210		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
211			a.ctlMu.Lock()
212			delete(a.curCmds, cmd)
213			a.ctlMu.Unlock()
214			return err
215		}
216		sc := bufio.NewScanner(out)
217		for sc.Scan() {
218			if v, ok := strings.CutPrefix(sc.Text(), "out_time_us="); ok {
219				var us float64
220				fmt.Sscanf(v, "%f", &us)
221				if dur > 0 {
222					cb(us / 1e6 / dur)
223				}
224			}
225		}
226		err = cmd.Wait()
227		a.ctlMu.Lock()
228		delete(a.curCmds, cmd)
229		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
230		if err != nil {
231			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
232				return errStopped
233			}
234			tail := errBuf.String()
235			if len(tail) > 400 {
236				tail = tail[len(tail)-400:]
237			}
238			return fmt.Errorf("ffmpeg: %w\n%s", err, tail)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}

243	func ffprobeDur(f string) (float64, error) {
244		// the one probe every caller shares (ffprobe.go): asked once per file and
245		// remembered, because the Cut page asks four of these about every
246		// recording in the session and used to start a process for each
247		if v := ffprobeInfo(f).dur; v > 0 {
248			return v, nil
249		}
250		d := ""
251		{
252			// stream-to-disk recorders never finalize the header; decode and count
253			out, err := exec.Command("bash", "-c",
254				fmt.Sprintf(`ffmpeg -v error -progress /dev/stdout -i %q -f null - 2>/dev/null | awk -F= '/^out_time_us/ { t = $2 } END { printf "%%.2f", t / 1e6 }'`, f)).Output()
255			if err != nil {
256				return 0, fmt.Errorf("duration of %s: %w", f, err)
257			}
258			d = strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
259		}
260		var v float64
261		fmt.Sscanf(d, "%f", &v)
262		if v <= 0 {
263			return 0, fmt.Errorf("cannot determine duration of %s", f)
264		}
265		return v, nil
266	}

268	// ffprobeSize is a still's pixel size. The thumbnail stage needs it because the
269	// title is drawn at a fraction of the picture's height, and the picture's
270	// height is the image server's decision, not ours: it is asked for 1280x720
271	// and a model with a fixed latent size may hand back something else.
272	func ffprobeSize(f string) (w, h int, err error) {
273		info := ffprobeInfo(f)
274		if info.w <= 0 || info.h <= 0 {
275			return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("cannot read the size of %s -- no video stream", f)
276		}
277		return info.w, info.h, nil
278	}

280	// walk any decoded JSON, visiting every object -- survives the CLI and server
281	// wrapping payloads differently
282	func walkObjects(v any, fn func(map[string]any)) {
283		switch t := v.(type) {
284		case map[string]any:
285			fn(t)
286			for _, vv := range t {
287				walkObjects(vv, fn)
288			}
289		case []any:
290			for _, vv := range t {
291				walkObjects(vv, fn)
292			}
293		}
294	}

296	func loadJSON(path string) (any, error) {
297		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
298		if err != nil {
299			return nil, err
300		}
301		var v any
302		return v, json.Unmarshal(b, &v)
303	}

305	// spans from a diarization JSON: sample counts -> seconds
306	func loadSpans(path string) ([]span, error) {
307		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
308		if err != nil {
309			return nil, err
310		}
311		return spansFrom(b)
312	}
313	
314	// spansFrom is the same for an answer that never reached disk -- which is what
315	// a window of the diarization scan is.
316	func spansFrom(b []byte) ([]span, error) {
317		var v any
318		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &v); err != nil {
319			return nil, err
320		}
321		var out []span
322		walkObjects(v, func(m map[string]any) {
323			slot, ok := m["speaker_id"].(string)
324			if !ok {
325				slot, ok = m["speaker"].(string)
326			}
327			ss, okS := m["start_sample"].(float64)
328			es, okE := m["end_sample"].(float64)
329			if ok && okS && okE {
330				out = append(out, span{ss / sampleRate, es / sampleRate, slot})
331			}
332		})
333		return out, nil
334	}

336	// ---- the transcripts and the frames -----------------------------------------
337	
338	// ingest is the first half of Prepare: every source transcribed, and a
339	// frame out of the footage every few seconds. It is called by prepare
340	// (prep.go), which owns the goroutine, the run controls, the preflight on the
341	// server's models and the log lines for both halves -- this is only the work.
342	
343	func (a *App) ingest(videos, audios []string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF string) error {
344		inDir := a.inputsDir()
345		if err := os.MkdirAll(inDir, 0o755); err != nil {
346			return err
347		}
348		// progress plan: half the bar each. Speech recognition (GPU, server) and
349		// frame extraction (CPU ffmpeg) do not contend, so they run as parallel
350		// tracks; weighting by file count let one job take most of the bar and then
351		// sit still. Each queues a task per file, and the speech side queues more as
352		// it goes.
353		inputs := append(append([]string{}, videos...), audios...)
354		a.qJob(trackSTT, "speech", 0, 0)
355		a.qPush(trackSTT, len(inputs), "recording")
356		a.qJob(trackFrames, "frames", 0, 0)
357		a.qPush(trackFrames, len(videos), "video")
358		var unit, funit float64
359		if len(inputs) > 0 {
360			unit = 0.5 / float64(len(inputs))
361		} else {
362			a.qDone(trackSTT, 0.5) // a job with nothing to do is done, or its
363		}
364		if len(videos) > 0 {
365			funit = 0.5 / float64(len(videos))
366		} else {
367			a.qDone(trackFrames, 0.5) // half would never fill and neither would the bar
368		}
369	
370		var wg sync.WaitGroup
371		var framesErr error
372		wg.Add(1)
373		go func() {
374			defer wg.Done()
375			if len(videos) == 0 {
376				return
377			}
378			fb := 0.0
379			for _, v := range videos {
380				if framesErr = a.checkpoint(); framesErr != nil {
381					return
382				}
383				a.qTake(trackFrames)
384				if framesErr = a.extractFrames(v, interval, scaleName, scaleVF, inDir, fb, funit); framesErr != nil {
385					return
386				}
387				fb += funit
388			}
389			a.qDone(trackFrames, fb)
390		}()
391	
392		var sttErr error
393		base := 0.0
394		for _, in := range inputs {
395			if sttErr = a.checkpoint(); sttErr != nil {
396				break
397			}
398			a.qTake(trackSTT)
399			if sttErr = a.transcribe(in, inDir, base, unit); sttErr != nil {
400				if !errors.Is(sttErr, errStopped) {
401					sttErr = fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", filepath.Base(in), sttErr)
402				}
403				break
404			}
405			base += unit
406		}
407		if sttErr == nil {
408			a.qDone(trackSTT, base)
409		}
410		wg.Wait()
411	
412		// one stop is one stop, not two errors; otherwise report whatever failed
413		if errors.Is(sttErr, errStopped) && errors.Is(framesErr, errStopped) {
414			return errStopped
415		}
416		if err := errors.Join(sttErr, framesErr); err != nil {
417			return err
418		}
419	
420		// primary pair for the single-source consumers (review page, align); the
421		// full ordered lists live in project.json. Either half can be absent now:
422		// a session may be one screen recording that is both, or recordings with no
423		// footage at all. So each is written only if there is one -- and what says
424		// "the sources have been read" is that this file exists, not what is in it.
425		var lines []string
426		if len(videos) > 0 {
427			lines = append(lines, "VIDEO_FILE="+videos[0], "VIDEO_BASE="+baseName(videos[0]))
428		}
429		// the narrator, not the first recording: that tag is who this session speaks
430		// as, and untagged it falls back to exactly the file audios[0] used to be
431		if voice := a.narratorSource(1); voice != "" {
432			lines = append(lines, "AUDIO_FILE="+voice, "AUDIO_BASE="+baseName(voice))
433		}
434		lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("INTERVAL=%g", interval), "SCALE="+scaleName)
435		return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(inDir, "meta.env"),
436			[]byte(strings.Join(lines, "\n")+"\n"), 0o644)
437	}

439	// baseName is what a file is called with the folders and the extension taken
440	// off -- the name a source, a lane, a frame folder and a logo are all known by.
441	func baseName(p string) string {
442		b := filepath.Base(p)
443		return strings.TrimSuffix(b, filepath.Ext(b))
444	}
445	
446	func exists(p string) bool { _, err := os.Stat(p); return err == nil }
