448	// ---- one input: 16 kHz -> ASR -> diarization -> segments -------------------
449	
450	func (a *App) transcribe(input, inDir string, base, unit float64) error {
451		name := baseName(input)
452		out := filepath.Join(inDir, name)
453		if err := os.MkdirAll(out, 0o755); err != nil {
454			return err
455		}
456	
457		wav := filepath.Join(out, "voice16k.wav")
458		if !exists(wav) {
459			a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.01*unit, "extracting audio")
460			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", input,
461				"-vn", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", wav); err != nil {
462				return err
463			}
464		}
465		dur, err := ffprobeDur(wav)
466		if err != nil {
467			return err
468		}
469		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] %.1f s of audio", name, dur)
470		if dur < shortTake {
471			// a start/stop, not a take: the same files an empty recording gets,
472			// without asking three servers about %.1f s of nothing
473			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] %.1f s long -- a start/stop, not a take: written up as silence", name, dur)
474			if err := writeSilence(out); err != nil {
475				return err
476			}
477			return a.mergeSegments(out)
478		}
479	
480		if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
481			return err
482		}
483		if !exists(filepath.Join(out, "words.json")) {
484			a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.05*unit, "recognising speech")
485			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] ASR (%s)", name, a.readConf().ASRModel)
486			body, text, pieces, err := a.asrLong(wav, dur, name, base, unit)
487			if err != nil {
488				return fmt.Errorf("ASR: %w", err)
489			}
490			if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
491				// a real case, not an error: a screen capture with no mic behind
492				// it. The empty transcript is written and the step carries on
493				a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] no speech found -- an empty transcript", name)
494			}
495			if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.txt"),
496				[]byte(strings.TrimRight(text, "\n")+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
497				return err
498			}
499			// which seconds each request covered and what came back for them --
500			// written before words.json, because words.json is the resume marker
501			// and nothing may exist after it that the marker does not stand for
502			if err := saveASRPieces(out, pieces); err != nil {
503				return err
504			}
505			// words.json last, and whole: it is this stage's resume marker, so it
506			// must not exist until the answer it stands for is on disk
507			if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "words.json"), body, 0o644); err != nil {
508				return err
509			}
510		} else {
511			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] ASR already done", name)
512		}
513	
514		// ...and when it was said, which is a different question and a better
515		// answer (align.go). It runs here because the segments below are built
516		// from word times: an ASR that returns none -- the best of the three does
517		// -- has no transcript at all without this.
518		if models := a.alignModels(); len(models) > 0 {
519			if !exists(alignedWords(out)) {
520				a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.9*unit, "timing the words")
521				a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] aligning (%s)", name, a.alignModel())
522			}
523			if err := a.alignInput(out, wav, models); err != nil {
524				// what a failure costs depends on what the ASR gave. With its own
525				// word times, alignment is an improvement and losing it is a
526				// warning: the times stand where they stood before this existed.
527				//
528				// With none -- which is what the best transcriber answers -- it is
529				// the only source of times there is, and the transcript below is
530				// built from times. Failing here with the aligner's own words beats
531				// failing two steps later with a sentence about a missing aligner
532				// that is plainly registered.
533				if len(wordTimes(out)) > 0 {
534					a.logfIdle("!!! [%s] align: %v -- the ASR's own times stand", name, err)
535				} else if strings.TrimSpace(readFileString(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.txt"))) != "" {
536					return fmt.Errorf("align: %w\n\n%s answers with no word times of its own, so the "+
537						"aligner is the only thing that can time them and this recording cannot be "+
538						"transcribed without it", err, a.readConf().ASRModel)
539				}
540			}
541		}
542	
543		if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
544			return err
545		}
546		if !exists(filepath.Join(out, "turns.json")) {
547			// and when it fails, the step fails. There is no "skip it" answer: a
548			// window the machine cannot hold is walked down until one fits
549			// (diarWins), and what is left after that is a server that cannot do
550			// the job -- which a run should say rather than carry on past.
551			if err := a.diarize(out, dur, name, base, unit); err != nil {
552				if errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
553					return err
554				}
555				return fmt.Errorf("diarization: %w", err)
556			}
557		} else {
558			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] diarization already done", name)
559		}
560	
561		a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.98*unit, "building segments")
562		if err := a.mergeSegments(out); err != nil {
563			return fmt.Errorf("merge: %w", err)
564		}
565		return nil
566	}
567	
568	// writeSilence writes what a recording without speech leaves behind: an empty
569	// transcript, a words.json with no words (the stage's resume marker, in the
570	// shape the server answers) and no turns. No ASR pieces file: none is what a
571	// recording transcribed in one request leaves, and the aligner takes that.
572	func writeSilence(out string) error {
573		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.txt"), []byte("\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
574			return err
575		}
576		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "words.json"), []byte("{\"text\":\"\"}\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
577			return err
578		}
579		return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "turns.json"), []byte("[]\n"), 0o644)
580	}
581	
582	// asrLong is one recording through the ASR in as many requests as its length
583	// needs. A recording that fits goes in whole and words.json stays the server's
584	// own document; a long one is cut into pieces, stitched back into one answer
585	// of the same shape. The cuts slide to the middle of a silence, where a
586	// decoder losing its context costs nothing.
587	func (a *App) asrLong(wav string, dur float64, name string, base, unit float64) ([]byte, string, []asrPiece, error) {
588		limit := a.asrChunk()
589		// Down the same ladder diarization walks, and for the same failure: the
590		// model's own position table says how much audio it will READ, and the
591		// machine says how much of a graph it can find room for. Halving is not
592		// free here -- a chunk edge is a place the decoder loses its context, so
593		// the text at a join is the worst text in the file -- which is why this
594		// starts at what the model allows and shortens only when told to, rather
595		// than being set small to be safe.
596		for {
597			b, text, pieces, err := a.asrLongAt(wav, dur, name, base, unit, limit)
598			if err == nil || !noRoom(err) || limit <= asrChunkMin {
599				return b, text, pieces, err
600			}
601			limit = math.Max(asrChunkMin, math.Floor(limit/2))
602			a.logfIdle("!!! [%s] ASR: no room for that much audio (%v) -- trying %.0f s at a time",
603				name, err, limit)
604		}
605	}
606	
607	func (a *App) asrLongAt(wav string, dur float64, name string, base, unit, limit float64) ([]byte, string, []asrPiece, error) {
608		if dur <= limit {
609			b, text, err := a.asrJSON(wav)
610			if err != nil {
611				return nil, "", nil, err
612			}
613			// one request is one piece, and the aligner wants the same shape
614			// whether the recording was cut up or not
615			return b, text, []asrPiece{{S: 0, E: dur, Text: text}}, nil
616		}
617		seek := math.Min(asrCutSeek, limit/3)
618		edges := append(append([]float64{0}, asrCuts(dur, a.quietSpots(wav), limit, seek)...), dur)
619		n := len(edges) - 1
620		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] too long for one request -- %d ASR chunks", name, n)
621	
622		dir := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(wav), "asr")
623		os.RemoveAll(dir)
624		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
625			return nil, "", nil, err
626		}
627		// the chunks are scratch and go when the answer is stitched -- but only
628		// then. A failed run keeps them, because the one thing worth having after
629		// "the server could not open c00.wav" is c00.wav.
630		done := false
631		defer func() {
632			if done {
633				os.RemoveAll(dir)
634			}
635		}()
636	
637		var words []any
638		var texts []string
639		var pieces []asrPiece
640		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
641			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
642				return nil, "", nil, err
643			}
644			a.prog(trackSTT, base+(0.05+0.45*float64(i)/float64(n))*unit,
645				"recognising speech %d/%d", i+1, n)
646			part := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("c%02d.wav", i))
647			// -ss ahead of -i seeks the input, which on the pcm this stage wrote
648			// is exact rather than a keyframe away
649			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
650				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(edges[i]), "-t", fmt.Sprint(edges[i+1]-edges[i]),
651				"-i", wav, "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", part); err != nil {
652				return nil, "", nil, err
653			}
654			body, text, err := a.asrJSON(part)
655			if err != nil {
656				return nil, "", nil, err
657			}
658			words = append(words, shiftWords(body, edges[i])...)
659			t := strings.TrimSpace(text)
660			if t != "" {
661				texts = append(texts, t)
662			}
663			// what this request covered and what it heard there, kept together.
664			// Joining the texts and dropping the seconds is what used to leave the
665			// aligner guessing how many words belong in a window (alignInput).
666			pieces = append(pieces, asrPiece{S: edges[i], E: edges[i+1], Text: t})
667		}
668		text := strings.Join(texts, " ")
669		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(map[string]any{"text": text, "words": words}, "", "  ")
670		if err != nil {
671			return nil, "", nil, err
672		}
673		done = true
674		return append(b, '\n'), text, pieces, nil
675	}
676	
677	// asrChunk is how much audio one ASR request may hold, which is not one number
678	// for every model.
679	//
680	// The encoders differ in what they accept, and on a shared GPU in what they can
681	// GET: Qwen3-ASR allocates a classification graph sized by the clip in front of
682	// it -- about 1.5 GB per 20 s, measured here -- so a 96 s take asks for seven
683	// gigabytes in one piece and dies with "failed to allocate Qwen3 ASR thinker
684	// classification graph", on a machine where Nemotron reads the same take whole.
685	// The model that will do the reading decides how much it is handed.
686	func (a *App) asrChunk() float64 {
687		c := a.readConf()
688		if cat, err := audioCatalog(a.audioURL(), c.TTSKey); err == nil {
689			if strings.HasPrefix(cat[c.ASRModel].Family, "qwen3") {
690				return asrChunkQwen
691			}
692		}
693		return asrChunkMax
694	}
695	
696	// asrCuts divides dur into pieces and returns the times between them. Even
697	// pieces, not full ones with a runt. Each cut slides up to seek seconds to the
698	// nearest silence, and the pieces are sized so two cuts sliding apart cannot
699	// push the piece between them past max.
700	func asrCuts(dur float64, quiet []span, max, seek float64) []float64 {
701		if dur <= max || max <= 0 {
702			return nil
703		}
704		if seek < 0 || 2*seek >= max {
705			seek = 0
706		}
707		// the pieces are sized so two cuts sliding apart cannot overflow, which
708		// means a generous seek buys its room out of the piece: 20 s of reach
709		// against a 60 s ceiling was making 19 s pieces, three times the requests
710		// and three times the places the decoder loses its context. A sixth of the
711		// ceiling leaves every piece at least two thirds of what the model allows.
712		if seek > max/6 {
713			seek = max / 6
714		}
715		n := int(math.Ceil(dur / (max - 2*seek)))
716		step := dur / float64(n)
717		if lim := step / 3; seek > lim {
718			seek = lim // cuts stay in order, and each stays inside its own piece
719		}
720		var out []float64
721		for i := 1; i < n; i++ {
722			want, at, best := step*float64(i), step*float64(i), seek
723			for _, q := range quiet {
724				if mid := (q.s + q.e) / 2; math.Abs(mid-want) < best {
725					at, best = mid, math.Abs(mid-want)
726				}
727			}
728			out = append(out, at)
729		}
730		return out
731	}
732	
733	// shiftWords moves one chunk's words to where the chunk was in the recording,
734	// rewriting only the two sample counts so whatever else a word carries rides
735	// along. A word whose times cannot be read travels unshifted -- the merge is
736	// what has to notice an unknown shape.
737	func shiftWords(body []byte, off float64) []any {
738		var v any
739		if json.Unmarshal(body, &v) != nil {
740			return nil
741		}
742		var out []any
743		walkObjects(v, func(m map[string]any) {
744			if _, ok := m["word"].(string); !ok {
745				return
746			}
747			for _, k := range []string{"start_sample", "end_sample"} {
748				if n, ok := m[k].(float64); ok {
749					m[k] = n + off*sampleRate
750				}
751			}
752			out = append(out, m)
753		})
754		return out
755	}
756	
757	// quietSpots asks ffmpeg where the recording goes quiet. Best effort: finding
758	// none, or ffmpeg refusing the file, means the cuts land on the clock, which
759	// is a worse place to cut but never a reason to fail the step.
760	func (a *App) quietSpots(wav string) []span {
761		cmd := exec.Command(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "info", "-nostats", "-i", wav,
762			"-af", fmt.Sprintf("silencedetect=n=%ddB:d=%g", asrQuietDB, asrQuietMin),
763			"-f", "null", "-")
764		var buf bytes.Buffer
765		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &buf, &buf
766		a.ctlMu.Lock()
767		a.curCmds[cmd] = true
768		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
769		err := cmd.Run()
770		a.ctlMu.Lock()
771		delete(a.curCmds, cmd)
772		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
773		if err != nil {
774			return nil
775		}
776		return parseSilence(buf.String())
777	}
778	
779	// parseSilence reads the report silencedetect writes to stderr:
780	//
781	//	[silencedetect @ 0x..] silence_start: 12.345
782	//	[silencedetect @ 0x..] silence_end: 15.678 | silence_duration: 3.333
783	//
784	// A silence still open when the file ends has no end line and is dropped: the
785	// end of the recording is not a place anything needs to be cut.
786	func parseSilence(report string) []span {
787		var out []span
788		from, open := 0.0, false
789		for _, ln := range strings.Split(report, "\n") {
790			if i := strings.Index(ln, "silence_start:"); i >= 0 {
791				v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(ln[i+len("silence_start:"):]), 64)
792				from, open = v, err == nil
793				continue
794			}
795			i := strings.Index(ln, "silence_end:")
796			if i < 0 || !open {
797				continue
798			}
799			f := strings.TrimSpace(ln[i+len("silence_end:"):])
800			if j := strings.Index(f, "|"); j >= 0 {
801				f = strings.TrimSpace(f[:j])
802			}
803			if v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(f, 64); err == nil && v > from {
804				out = append(out, span{s: from, e: v})
805			}
806			open = false
807		}
808		return out
809	}
810	
811	// concatLine is one row of an ffmpeg concat list. The quoting is the reason it
812	// is a function: the demuxer reads 'file' arguments as single-quoted, so a path
813	// with an apostrophe in it -- a project called "tom's cut", which names the
814	// whole data folder -- ends the quote early and the rest of the list is read as
815	// something else. ffmpeg spells an escaped quote the shell way: close, a
816	// backslashed quote, open again.
817	func concatLine(path string) string {
818		return "file '" + strings.ReplaceAll(path, "'", `'\''`) + "'\n"
819	}
820	
821	func (a *App) diarize(out string, dur float64, name string, base, unit float64) error {
822		var err error
823		for i, win := range diarWins {
824			if err = a.diarizeAt(out, dur, name, base, unit, win); err == nil || !noRoom(err) {
825				return err
826			}
827			// the server has the model and refused the buffer, not the audio: the
828			// next window down is the same pass over more, smaller requests
829			if i+1 < len(diarWins) {
830				a.logfIdle("!!! [%s] diarization: no room for a %.0f s window (%v) -- trying %.0f s",
831					name, win, err, diarWins[i+1])
832			}
833		}
834		return err
835	}
836	
837	// anchorPiece is one stretch of one voice cut into the anchor.
838	type anchorPiece struct {
839		src, len float64
840		slot     string
841	}
842	
843	// anchorPieces takes up to per seconds of each voice from rows, which are in
844	// slot order and then time order, skipping any stretch under anchorCut.
845	func anchorPieces(rows []span, per float64) []anchorPiece {
846		var pieces []anchorPiece
847		acc := map[string]float64{}
848		for _, r := range rows {
849			if acc[r.slot] >= per {
850				continue
851			}
852			d := r.e - r.s
853			if d > per-acc[r.slot] {
854				d = per - acc[r.slot]
855			}
856			if d < anchorCut {
857				continue
858			}
859			acc[r.slot] += d
860			pieces = append(pieces, anchorPiece{r.s, d, r.slot})
861		}
862		return pieces
863	}
864	
865	// noRoom is whether the server refused for want of memory rather than for
866	// anything about the request. Its own words, because the failure arrives as a
867	// 500 with a message and nothing else to go on. Both the passes that hand it a
868	// stretch of audio ask this: what they choose is how much, and that is the
869	// only thing either can do about the answer.
870	func noRoom(err error) bool {
871		if err == nil {
872			return false
873		}
874		s := strings.ToLower(err.Error())
875		return strings.Contains(s, "failed to allocate") || strings.Contains(s, "out of memory") ||
876			strings.Contains(s, "alloc_tensor_range") || strings.Contains(s, "cudamalloc")
877	}
878	
879	// diarizeAt is the pass at one window length.
880	func (a *App) diarizeAt(out string, dur float64, name string, base, unit, win float64) error {
881		// the anchor is a share of the window, not a fixed dozen seconds: four
882		// voices at 12 s each is 48 s of anchor, which leaves a 45 s window no
883		// room for any new audio at all. A quarter of the window per voice keeps
884		// the same shape at every rung of the ladder.
885		per := math.Min(anchorPer, win/4)
886		dir := filepath.Join(out, "diar")
887		os.RemoveAll(dir)
888		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
889			return err
890		}
891		defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
892		turnsPath := filepath.Join(out, "turns.json")
893	
894		// -- pass 1: where are the voices? --------------------------------------
895		scanHop := math.Max(10, math.Floor(win*diarHopShare))
896		nwin := int(math.Ceil(dur / scanHop))
897		scan := map[int][]span{}
898		for i := 0; i < nwin; i++ {
899			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
900				return err
901			}
902			a.prog(trackSTT, base+(0.55+0.20*float64(i)/float64(nwin))*unit,
903				"finding voices %d/%d", i+1, nwin)
904			start := float64(i) * scanHop
905			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
906				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(start), "-t", fmt.Sprint(win),
907				"-i", filepath.Join(out, "voice16k.wav"),
908				"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", filepath.Join(dir, "s.wav")); err != nil {
909				return err
910			}
911			spans, err := a.diarSpans(filepath.Join(dir, "s.wav"))
912			if err != nil {
913				return err
914			}
915			for _, sp := range spans {
916				scan[i] = append(scan[i], span{sp.s + start, sp.e + start, sp.slot})
917			}
918		}
919		if len(scan) == 0 {
920			return os.WriteFile(turnsPath, []byte("[]\n"), 0o644)
921		}
922	
923		// -- pick the anchor window ---------------------------------------------
924		// Most distinct voices; on a tie, the window whose QUIETEST voice is best
925		// represented -- ranking by total speech picks whoever talks most and
926		// leaves the other voice too thin to anchor.
927		best, bestN, bestLo := -1, 0, 0.0
928		for w, spans := range scan {
929			durBy := map[string]float64{}
930			for _, sp := range spans {
931				durBy[sp.slot] += sp.e - sp.s
932			}
933			n, lo := 0, math.MaxFloat64
934			for _, d := range durBy {
935				if d >= anchorMin {
936					n++
937					if d < lo {
938						lo = d
939					}
940				}
941			}
942			if n > bestN || (n == bestN && n > 0 && lo > bestLo) {
943				best, bestN, bestLo = w, n, lo
944			}
945		}
946		if best < 0 {
947			for w := range scan {
948				if best < 0 || w < best {
949					best = w
950				}
951			}
952		}
953	
954		// -- build the anchor: up to anchorPer seconds of each voice ------------
955		rows := append([]span(nil), scan[best]...)
956		sort.Slice(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
957			if rows[i].slot != rows[j].slot {
958				return rows[i].slot < rows[j].slot
959			}
960			return rows[i].s < rows[j].s
961		})
962		pieces := anchorPieces(rows, per)
963		if len(pieces) == 0 {
964			// voices were heard but none for long enough to anchor -- a snippet
965			// under a second. Nothing to tell apart: no turns, same as no voices,
966			// and not an empty concat list for ffmpeg to refuse.
967			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] diarization: no voice long enough to anchor -- no turns", name)
968			return os.WriteFile(turnsPath, []byte("[]\n"), 0o644)
969		}
970		var list strings.Builder
971		for i, p := range pieces {
972			f := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("a%02d.wav", i))
973			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
974				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(p.src), "-t", fmt.Sprint(p.len),
975				"-i", filepath.Join(out, "voice16k.wav"),
976				"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", f); err != nil {
977				return err
978			}
979			list.WriteString(concatLine(f))
980		}
981		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "anchor.list"), []byte(list.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
982			return err
983		}
984		if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0",
985			"-i", filepath.Join(dir, "anchor.list"),
986			"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", filepath.Join(dir, "anchor.wav")); err != nil {
987			return err
988		}
989		// block b of the anchor is voice b: [bs, be) in anchor-local seconds
990		type block struct{ s, e float64 }
991		var blocks []block
992		t := 0.0
993		for i, p := range pieces {
994			if i == 0 || p.slot != pieces[i-1].slot {
995				blocks = append(blocks, block{t, t})
996			}
997			t += p.len
998			blocks[len(blocks)-1].e = t
999		}
1000		alen := t
1001		hop := math.Floor(win - alen - 1)
1002		if hop < 15 {
1003			return fmt.Errorf("anchor too long (%.1f s of %.0f s window)", alen, win)
1004		}
1005		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] anchor: %d voice(s) in %.1f s of a %.0f s window -- %.0f s of new audio each",
1006			name, len(blocks), alen, win, hop)
1007	
1008		// -- pass 2: every window carries the anchor ----------------------------
1009		nwin = int(math.Ceil(dur / hop))
1010		all := map[int][]span{}
1011		for i := 0; i < nwin; i++ {
1012			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
1013				return err
1014			}
1015			a.prog(trackSTT, base+(0.75+0.22*float64(i)/float64(nwin))*unit,
1016				"placing speakers %d/%d", i+1, nwin)
1017			start := float64(i) * hop
1018			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
1019				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(start), "-t", fmt.Sprint(hop),
1020				"-i", filepath.Join(out, "voice16k.wav"),
1021				"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", filepath.Join(dir, "seg.wav")); err != nil {
1022				return err
1023			}
1024			cc := concatLine(filepath.Join(dir, "anchor.wav")) +
1025				concatLine(filepath.Join(dir, "seg.wav"))
1026			if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "cc.list"), []byte(cc), 0o644); err != nil {
1027				return err
1028			}
1029			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0",

1298	// extractFrames dumps one video's frames into inputs/frames/<basename>/.
1299	// A marker file records interval + size, so re-runs skip until either changes.
1300	// frameChunk is one worker's share of a frame extraction: frames first..
1301	// first+n-1, from start for dur seconds.
1302	type frameChunk struct {
1303		start, dur float64
1304		first, n   int
1305	}

1307	// frameChunks splits total frames at one every interval over workers, in
1308	// chunks whose lengths are whole intervals so frame n is always t=(n-1)*interval.
1309	// The tail is never a single frame: the count is a rounding of the file's
1310	// length, and a lone last frame that turns out not to exist would leave that

1312	// the chunk before it, the same missing frame costs nothing -- ffmpeg stops at
1313	// the end of the file one frame short of its cap, and says nothing.
1314	func frameChunks(total, workers int, interval float64) []frameChunk {
1315		per := (total + workers - 1) / workers
1316		var chunks []frameChunk
1317		for k := 0; k < workers; k++ {
1318			n := min(per, total-k*per)
1319			if n <= 0 {
1320				break
1321			}
1322			chunks = append(chunks, frameChunk{float64(k*per) * interval, float64(n) * interval, k*per + 1, n})
1323		}
1324		if l := len(chunks); l >= 2 && chunks[l-1].n == 1 {
1325			chunks[l-2].n++
1326			chunks[l-2].dur += interval
1327			chunks = chunks[:l-1]
1328		}
1329		return chunks
1330	}

1337		if interval > 0 && dur < interval {

1340		return vf, false
1341	}

1343	func (a *App) extractFrames(video string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF, inDir string, base, unit float64) error {
1344		name := baseName(video)

1373		}
1374		if scaleVF != "" {
1375			filters = append(filters, scaleVF)
1376		}

1387		// Extraction is decode-bound: to keep one frame per second the decoder

1398			// count one too high sends the last worker after a frame that is not

1400			totalFrames = int(math.Round(dur / interval))

1404		} else {

1406		}
1407	
1408		if workers == 1 {

1412			}
1413			if oneFrame {

1415			}
1416			args = append(args, "-q:v", "4", "-start_number", "1", pattern)

1479	// stampFrames renames ffmpeg's numbering into the wall-clock second each frame
1480	// was shot in (several in one second get -1, -2). The name comes from the
1481	// frame NUMBER, never the sorted position, so t = (n-1) * interval survives a
1482	// gap. start is the session's placement of this video, passed in by the caller
1483	// who holds the whole source list. Nothing numbered left means nothing to do,
1484	// which is also what renames a folder extracted before stamping existed.
1485	func stampFrames(fdir, video string, start, interval float64) (int, error) {
1486		ents, err := os.ReadDir(fdir)
1487		if err != nil {
1488			return 0, err
1489		}
1490		type frame struct {
1491			n    int
1492			name string
1493		}
1494		var fs []frame
1495		for _, e := range ents {
1496			n, ok := frameNum(e.Name())
1497			if e.IsDir() || !ok {
1498				continue
1499			}
1500			fs = append(fs, frame{n, e.Name()})
1501		}
1502		if len(fs) == 0 {
1503			return 0, nil
1504		}
1505		if interval <= 0 {
1506			// every-frame mode: the spacing is the video's own. Without a frame rate
1507			// there is no time to name a frame after, so it keeps its number.
1508			fps := ffprobeFPS(video)
1509			if fps <= 0 {
1510				return 0, nil
1511			}
1512			interval = 1 / fps
1513		}
1514		sort.Slice(fs, func(i, j int) bool { return fs[i].n < fs[j].n })
1515		var seq stampSeq
1516		for _, f := range fs {
1517			to := seq.name(start+float64(f.n-1)*interval, ".jpg")
1518			if err := os.Rename(filepath.Join(fdir, f.name), filepath.Join(fdir, to)); err != nil {
1519				return 0, err
1520			}
1521		}
1522		return len(fs), nil
1523	}
1524	
1525	// frameNum reads ffmpeg's f000001.jpg back. Frames are renamed the moment they
1526	// are extracted, so this only ever sees a folder mid-extraction -- or one made
1527	// before the frames carried their timestamp.
1528	func frameNum(name string) (int, bool) {
1529		if !strings.HasPrefix(name, "f") || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".jpg") {
1530			return 0, false
1531		}
1532		n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSuffix(name[1:], ".jpg"))
1533		return n, err == nil && n >= 1
1534	}

func (a *App) buildPrep() gtk.Widgetter {

	a.inStack.AddNamed(p.inputs, "prep")

	// Files left, context and prompts right (prepedit.go), a handle between
	// opening at the middle; both sides resize with the window and stand six
	// off the handle like every other divider in the app.
	bench := a.prepEditor()
	gtk.BaseWidget(bench).SetMarginStart(6)
	sources := a.buildSources()
	sources.SetMarginEnd(6)

	outer := gtk.NewPaned(gtk.OrientationHorizontal)
	outer.SetStartChild(sources)
	outer.SetEndChild(bench)
	outer.SetResizeStartChild(true)
	outer.SetResizeEndChild(true)
	openAtHalf(outer)
	// Shrink off on both ends: shrink means a child may be allocated less than
	// it needs, and what these two need includes a heading row and a button
	// row. With it off, GtkPaned clamps the handle to what both children need,
	// so a shorter window moves the handle instead of hiding half a column.
	outer.SetShrinkStartChild(false)
	outer.SetShrinkEndChild(false)
	outer.SetVExpand(true)
	// 12 from the window's edges, like the columns on Cut and Narrate, so the
	// boxes line up with the Inputs row above them and with the same boxes one
	// tab over.
	outer.SetMarginStart(12)
	outer.SetMarginEnd(12)
	// and 8 off the tabs above and the shared bar below, so the Freq row and
	// the editor frame do not sit on the transport buttons -- the breathing
	// room every other edge of every page has
	outer.SetMarginTop(8)
	outer.SetMarginBottom(8)

	// One open-folder button for prepare/ with how much is in it; the three
	// subfolders are the folder's business. Rides the shared bottom bar
	// (outStack in main.go).
	outRow := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
	outBtn := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("folder-open-symbolic")
	outBtn.SetTooltipText("prepare/ — this step's three folders:\n" +
		"inputs/ — the frames, the per-source transcripts and who spoke when\n" +
		"describe/ — the event logs, one per video\n" +
		"transcript/ — the fixed transcripts, the subtitles and the session timeline")
	outBtn.ConnectClicked(func() { a.openFolder(a.prepareDir()) })
	p.prepOut = gtk.NewLabel("")
	outRow.Append(outBtn)
	outRow.Append(gtk.NewLabel("Prepare:"))
	outRow.Append(p.prepOut)
	a.outStack.AddNamed(outRow, "prep")

	// The work, and nothing above it -- no prompt row at the bottom any more,
	// because this page's prompts live in the right-hand box now, behind its
	// menu, and no Inputs row at the top: what this step reads and what it has
	// written are the two groups on the shared bar below all of it.
	page := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
	page.Append(outer)

	p.refresh()
	return page
}

func (a *App) buildSources() *gtk.Box {
	// every edit to the list changes what a run would see and who the narration
	// would be spoken by, so the snapshot and the voice picker are refreshed
	// from here rather than from each of the six things that can edit a row
	a.srcList = newSourceList(func() {
		a.snapSources()
		if a.voicePick != nil {
			a.voicePick.refreshNarrators()
		}
		a.prep.refresh()
		a.refreshCut() // the tracks ARE this list: a row added or unmarked changes them
	})

	// the frame controls: how often, then how big. A stepper over the same
	// discrete stops the slider had, each..5s, typable by hand.
	a.interval = newFreqPick()

	labels := make([]string, len(scalePresets))
	for i, p := range scalePresets {
		labels[i] = p.Label
	}
	a.scalePick = gtk.NewDropDownFromStrings(labels)
	a.scalePick.SetTooltipText("Frame size — Original keeps the video's own size")
	a.setFrameScale("original")
	a.scalePick.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)

	// The language, on the page whose run listens -- in Settings it was a property
	// of the machine, three tabs from the sources it was wrong about. Free text:
	// the code is the server's to interpret.
	a.langEntry = gtk.NewEntry()
	a.langEntry.SetWidthChars(4)
	a.langEntry.SetMaxWidthChars(6)
	a.langEntry.SetPlaceholderText(defLanguage)
	a.langEntry.SetTooltipText("Language of this session's speech, as the ASR model spells it (en, de, …) — " +
		"the wrong one transcribes into gibberish. Empty means " + defLanguage)
	a.langEntry.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
	// the cache follows every keystroke rather than a commit: unlike the frame
	// stepper there is nothing to parse, and a value that only counts once you
	// tab away is a value the next run silently disagrees with
	a.langEntry.ConnectChanged(func() { a.setLanguage(a.langEntry.Text()) })

	// One list, the width of the page; each row says what its file is for. The
	// buttons say "source" so the list needs no heading.
	addBtn := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Add source files…")
	addBtn.SetTooltipText("Add recordings or footage — several at once")
	addBtn.ConnectClicked(a.addFilesDialog)
	// "Add source folder…" was beside it. Nobody used it -- a session's
	// recordings are picked by name -- and files picked by name are the one
	// shape that works everywhere, a Flatpak's portal file chooser included,
	// where a folder handed over whole is a different and weaker grant.
	// The legend was here: the four row icons with their words, once, along
	// the top of the list. It cost a line of the page permanently to answer a
	// question asked twice -- and it answered it a hand's width away from the
	// buttons it was about, which is the one place the eye is not while it is
	// deciding what a symbol does. The words are on the buttons themselves
	// now: every one of them ends its tooltip with the whole row (srcRowKey),
	// so hovering any symbol says what all four are.

	// Where an added file goes, decided once and remembered with the project
	// rather than asked on every Add: into the project folder, or left where
	// it is. Copy is the default -- a project is one folder that can be moved
	// or zipped, and a session whose footage is on the card it was recorded on
	// is not one thing -- and the tick comes off for the machine that recorded
	// the footage, where 20 GB of capture does not want a twin.
	a.copyTick = gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel("copy into project")
	a.copyTick.SetActive(true)
	a.copyTick.SetTooltipText("Ticked, an added file is copied into the project's sources/ folder, " +
		"so the project holds everything it needs. Unticked, the file is referenced where it is: " +
		"nothing is duplicated, and the session breaks if it moves.")
	a.copyTick.ConnectToggled(func() {
		if a.refQuiet {
			return
		}
		a.refSources = !a.copyTick.Active()
		a.saveProjectNow()
	})

	addRow := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
	addRow.Append(addBtn)
	addRow.Append(a.copyTick)

	listScroll := gtk.NewScrolledWindow()
	listScroll.SetChild(a.srcList.box)
	listScroll.SetVExpand(true)
	// what the heading used to say, kept on the thing it was about
	listScroll.SetTooltipText("Every file here is transcribed, and placed on the session clock by the timestamp in its name")
	// this row is this side's heading, and it joins the size group every
	// editor's heading is in (editorBody): the two sides of the divider are
	// read against each other, so a button row a few px taller than the label
	// row opposite it starts the list a few px above the box it is beside.
	// The same group is why the Publish page's fields line up with the prompts
	// (publisher.heading).
	if a.headGroup == nil {
		a.headGroup = gtk.NewSizeGroup(gtk.SizeGroupVertical)
	}
	a.headGroup.AddWidget(addRow)

	sources := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
	sources.SetVExpand(true)
	// the same 4 px the editor's own box stands off the top with, so the two
	// frames begin on one line (editorFrame)
	sources.SetMarginTop(4)
	sources.Append(addRow)
	sources.Append(listScroll)

	// The bottom line, one line: how the frames are taken, and what language
	// they are spoken in. Where it all lands used to be chosen here too; it is
	// the project file's own folder now (project.go), so there is nothing to
	// choose, and what has been written into it is counted along the bottom of
	// the page where the other two folders this step writes are.
	bottom := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
	bottom.Append(gtk.NewLabel("Freq:"))
	bottom.Append(a.interval.box)
	bottom.Append(a.scalePick)
	bottom.Append(gtk.NewLabel("Language:"))
	bottom.Append(a.langEntry)
	// What kind of video this is, mechanically: a read to camera is edited as
	// text and its picture is never described; a session is described and
	// its moments picked. Not a wording -- the old Style dropdown below was
	// one, and went to the context box -- but which PIPELINE runs, and that
	// is this page's to say, since it is this page's ▶ that runs it.
	a.stylePick = gtk.NewDropDownFromStrings(styleLabels)
	a.stylePick.SetTooltipText("Lecture: a read to camera -- the speech is the video, cut by removing " +
		"the words said twice and the false starts. Gaming: a session -- the cut picks the " +
		"moments worth keeping. Both describe the picture; only what the cut is chosen from differs.")
	a.stylePick.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
	a.stylePick.NotifyProperty("selected", func() {
		// the cache first, then the save: the runner reads the cache, and a
		// project written from the widget would be one from the OLD cache
		a.setVideoStyle(styleOf(a.stylePick.Selected()))
		if !a.styleQuiet {
			a.saveProjectNow()
		}
	})
	bottom.Append(gtk.NewLabel("Style:"))
	bottom.Append(a.stylePick)
	// The Style dropdown was here, after Language: which kind of video ▶
	// Suggest built -- highlights, a rating, a Short -- turning every prompt
	// at once to a wording of that name. It is gone. What kind of video this
	// is, is a fact about the session like everything else on this page, and
	// the box beside these controls is where the session's facts go: said
	// there it reaches every step, it outranks the wordings (ctxRule), and
	// there is one place to say it instead of two that can disagree.

	// No margins of its own: it is one side of the page's divider now, and the
	// page keeps its columns 12 from the window's edges as Cut and Narrate do.
	box := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 12)
	box.SetVExpand(true)
	box.Append(sources)
	box.Append(bottom) // how the frames are taken, under the list they come from
	return box
}

// ---- what will be sent -------------------------------------------------------

// refresh re-reads everything on the page that is derived from the sources or
// from the output folder: what a run would send, and how much of it is already
// there. Safe on a page that has not been built -- it is called from the
// project loader and from the rescan, both of which can run first.
func (p *preproc) refresh() {
	if p == nil || p.inputs == nil {
		return
	}
	line, detail := p.a.inputsSummary()
	p.inputs.SetText(line)
	p.inputs.SetTooltipText(detail) // the per-file arithmetic, on hover
	setOutCount(p.prepOut, p.a.prepareDir())

}

// setOutCount fills one of the three output readings: how many files on the
// row, when the newest was written on hover. Three of the one-line form side by
// side is a paragraph across the bottom of the page, and the question the row
// is asked is how much is there.
func setOutCount(l *gtk.Label, dir string) {
	if l == nil {
		return
	}
	n, newest, size := countOutputs(dir)
	if n == 0 {
		l.SetText("nothing yet")
		l.SetTooltipText("")
		return
	}
	l.SetText(fmt.Sprintf("%d files, %s", n, humanSize(size)))
	l.SetTooltipText("newest " + humanAgo(newest))
}

// inputsSummary walks the session's sources once: line is what the page shows
// (files in, requests they become), detail the same per file for the tooltip
// and the log. One walk, because it reads every video's frame directory on
// every edit. framesPerReq and fixBlock are visible only here.
func (a *App) inputsSummary() (line, detail string) {
	if a.srcList == nil {
		return "", ""
	}
	vids, auds := a.srcList.split()
	if len(vids)+len(auds) == 0 {
		return "no input files — add some above", "(no sources)"
	}
	var b strings.Builder
	frames, vision, lines, fixes := 0, 0, 0, 0
	descDir := a.describeDir()
	count := func(base string) {
		n := len(loadSeg4(a.transcriptPath(base)))
		lines += n
		fixes += (n + fixBlock - 1) / fixBlock
	}
	for _, v := range vids {
		base := baseName(v)
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n", base)
		if p, err := a.planVideo(v, descDir); err != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  frames: %v\n", err)
		} else {
			scale := p.scale
			if scale == "" {
				scale = "original"
			}
			frames += len(p.frames)
			vision += p.chunks
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %d frames @ %gs (%s)  ->  %d vision requests\n",
				len(p.frames), p.interval, scale, p.chunks)
		}
		count(base)
		b.WriteString(fixerLine(a.transcriptPath(base)))
	}
	for _, aud := range auds {
		base := baseName(aud)
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n", base)
		count(base)
		b.WriteString(fixerLine(a.transcriptPath(base)))
	}
	// Names and counts, nothing else: the per-file arithmetic is the detail
	// beside this line -- the tooltip ON it (refresh), and the log when ▶
	// starts (prepRun) -- and a row that spells out what each number is FOR is
	// a paragraph wearing a row's clothes. Nobody reads it twice.
	// no count of the files: the list of them is directly under this row, with
	// what each one is for on its own button (srcRowKey). A row that counts
	// what the page below it shows is a row saying nothing.
	line = fmt.Sprintf("%d frames → %d vision · %d lines → %d fixer", frames, vision, lines, fixes)
	return line, strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
}

// inputsLabel is the line every step wears on the shared bottom bar: what the
// step reads, whole on hover. Ellipsized and capped so it cannot push the run
// bar's controls off the window.
func inputsLabel() *gtk.Label {
	l := gtk.NewLabel("")
	l.SetXAlign(0)
	l.SetEllipsize(pango.EllipsizeEnd)
	l.SetMaxWidthChars(60)
	return l
}

// plural is "1 clip" and "2 clips": the Inputs rows are read at a glance and
// "1 clip(s)" is a word nobody says out loud. Only the plural-by-s cases are
// on those rows, so this is the whole of the grammar needed.
func plural(n int, one string) string {
	if n == 1 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", n, one)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d %ss", n, one)
}

func (a *App) transcriptPath(base string) string {
	return filepath.Join(a.inputsDir(), base, "transcript.tsv")
}

func fixerLine(path string) string {
	if !exists(path) {
		return "  transcript.tsv: missing -- not transcribed yet\n"
	}
	n := len(loadSeg4(path))
	return fmt.Sprintf("  transcript.tsv, %d lines  ->  %d fixer requests\n",
		n, (n+fixBlock-1)/fixBlock)
}

// ---- run --------------------------------------------------------------------

// prepRun validates the sources and starts the whole step: transcripts and
// frames, then describing and fixing, in one press. No describe-only or
// fix-only run: describe resumes per chunk, and half of what the fixer is for
// is the events the describer just wrote.
func (a *App) prepRun() {
	if a.running {
		return
	}
	// one source is enough: a session can be a single screen recording that is
	// both the footage and every voice on it, and it can equally be a recording
	// with no footage at all
	vids, auds := a.snapSources()
	if len(vids)+len(auds) == 0 {
		a.setStatus("add at least one source")
		return
	}
	// two sources of the same name would write into one folder under inputs/,
	// and the second would quietly overwrite the first's transcript
	if x, y := a.srcList.clash(); x != "" {
		a.logf("!!! %s and %s are both inputs/%s -- rename one", x, y, baseName(x))
		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s and %s have the same name — rename one",
			filepath.Base(x), filepath.Base(y)))
		return
	}
	// The working copy always reflects what actually ran -- and so does the
	// named project, since saveProjectNow writes every target. It used to be
	// saveProjectTo(project.json), which also RENAMED the open project to the
	// working copy: running the step quietly stopped the autosave following the
	// file you had opened, and the header bar changed under you to say so.
	a.saveProjectNow()
	// ⏹ then ▶ is "do it again", not "carry on" -- and this is the moment to
	// act on that rather than the stop itself: pressing ⏹ has to be safe to do
	// at the end of the day, with the half-run still on disk in the morning.
	// It is the press that starts the work over that throws the work away.
	if err := a.undFreshStart(); err != nil {
		// nothing here is worth refusing to run over: say what could not be
		// cleared, and let the run pick up from what is still on disk
		a.logf(">>> could not clear the last run (%v) -- resuming it", err)
	}
	scaleName, scaleVF := a.frameScale()
	a.startPrep(vids, auds, a.frameInterval(), scaleName, scaleVF)
}

// undFreshStart is the difference between ⏸ and ⏹: paused resumes, stopped
// restarts the describing from the beginning, dropping the event logs it
// resumes from. Transcripts and frames are per-file on disk and untouched; the
// fixer never resumed anyway. Only armed by a ⏹ that had reached the
// describing.
func (a *App) undFreshStart() error {
	if !a.undRestart {
		return nil
	}
	a.undRestart = false
	return a.resetDescribe()
}

func (a *App) startPrep(videos, audios []string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF string) {
	a.startRun()
	a.prog(trackSTT, 0, "preparing")
	a.logExp.SetExpanded(true)
	// what went in, by name -- the page has room for a count and nothing more
	a.logf(">>> prepare: %d input files", len(videos)+len(audios))
	for _, f := range append(append([]string{}, videos...), audios...) {
		a.logf("    %s", f)
	}
	if _, detail := a.inputsSummary(); detail != "" {
		a.logf("%s", detail)
	}
	a.logCtx("prepare")
	go func() {
		described, err := a.prepare(videos, audios, interval, scaleName, scaleVF)
		glib.IdleAdd(func() {
			a.endRun()
			switch {
			case errors.Is(err, errStopped):
				// the work stays on disk until the next ▶, which is the press
				// that decides it was not wanted (undFreshStart) -- and only
				// the describing is thrown away, so a stop during the
				// transcribing arms nothing
				a.undRestart = described
				a.setStatus("stopped — finished work is kept")
			case err != nil:
				a.logf("prepare FAILED: %v", err)
				a.setStatus("prepare failed — see log")
			default:
				a.progress.SetFraction(1)
				a.logf(">>> prepare wrote:")
				n := a.logOutputs("inputs", a.inputsDir()) +
					a.logOutputs("describe", a.describeDir()) +
					a.logOutputs("transcript", a.transcriptDir())
				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("prepared — %d files", n))
			}
			a.prep.refresh()
			a.updateGates()
			// the frames and the session timeline the Cut page draws are what
			// this run just wrote -- including the first time, where the tab it
			// unlocks would otherwise open on nothing
			a.refreshCut()
		})
	}()
}

// prepInputsShare is how much of the progress bar the first half gets. The two
// halves are weighted by how long they TAKE, as the tracks inside each of them
// are: transcribing an hour of audio and pulling a frame out of it every couple
// of seconds is minutes, and describing those frames is a model call per
// handful of them and is the longest wait in the app. A third to the front is
// a rule of thumb from real sessions, and being roughly right is the whole
// requirement -- what a progress bar owes you is a direction, not an ETA.
const prepInputsShare = 0.3

// prepSepShare is the slice of that first third the voice splitting takes when
// there is any to do. A third of it: the separation is one model pass over the
// audio and the transcripts are two, over the same audio, plus every frame.
const prepSepShare = 0.1

// prepare is the whole press: the transcripts and the frames, then the
// describing and the fixing. It reports whether the second half had begun,
// which is what a ⏹ needs to know -- that is the half a restart throws away.
//
// Neither half knows the other exists: each still divides its own work into two
// tracks that add up to a whole bar. qPhase is what puts each of them in its
// own slice of it, so the needle crosses the middle once and never goes back.
func (a *App) prepare(videos, audios []string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF string) (bool, error) {
	// the models are the server's to load, but that it HAS them is worth
	// finding out now rather than after the frame extraction -- and before the
	// separation too, since that is the phase this step now opens with and the
	// one asking for the model a server is least likely to have.
	sep := len(a.sepWanted()) > 0
	if err := a.ensureAudioModels(sep); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	// the splitting goes first, because it changes what the rest of this is OF:
	// a recording being split is not the file the frames come out of or the
	// transcript is of -- the two files it becomes are. With nothing flagged
	// this phase costs nothing and the two below are the two there always were.
	sepAt := 0.0
	if sep {
		a.qPhase(0, prepSepShare)
		var err error
		if videos, audios, err = a.separateVoices(videos, audios); err != nil {
			return false, err
		}
		sepAt = prepSepShare
	}
	a.qPhase(sepAt, prepInputsShare-sepAt)
	if err := a.ingest(videos, audios, interval, scaleName, scaleVF); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	a.qPhase(prepInputsShare, 1-prepInputsShare)
	return true, a.understand(videos, audios)
}

func (a *App) understand(videos, audios []string) error {
	// Every style is described, Lecture included. Its CUT does not need the
	// picture -- the words are the video (textedit.go) -- and this step used
	// to skip it on that ground, which was half the story: Publish picks the
	// thumbnail by what is ON a frame, and a frame nobody described is a
	// frame nothing can find. A lecture's title slide is the thumbnail.
	//
	// two jobs, one after the other, and the bar says which of the two it is
	// on: this page's ▶ is the longest press in the app, and "1/2" is the
	// difference between halfway through and nearly done.
	a.qJob(trackDescribe, "describe", 1, 2)
	if err := a.describeAll(videos, audios, 0.5); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	a.qJob(trackFix, "transcript", 2, 2)
	return a.fixTranscripts(videos, audios, 0.5)
}

// openAtHalf opens a pane's handle at the middle of the window (unset, a
// GtkPaned gives each child what its widest content wants). It waits for the
// widget to be measured; Map fires on every show, hence the once guard, and
// after the first placement the handle is the user's.
func openAtHalf(p *gtk.Paned) {
	split := false
	p.ConnectMap(func() {
		if split {
			return
		}
		split = true
		glib.IdleAdd(func() { p.SetPosition(p.AllocatedWidth() / 2) })
	})
}

// videoStyleName is the style, callable from a runner's goroutine.
//
// A cached string and not the dropdown, for the same reason sessionCtx and
// asrLanguage are: the widget belongs to the GUI thread, and this is read by
// findMarks in the middle of Prepare -- which is a runner. It used to read
// stylePick.Selected() directly, a GTK call off the main thread that happened
// to work. The dropdown writes the cache on every change (prep.go) and the
// project writes it on load (applyStyle), so the two never disagree.
func (a *App) videoStyleName() string {
	a.promptMu.Lock()
	defer a.promptMu.Unlock()
	return a.videoStyle
}

func (a *App) setVideoStyle(name string) {
	a.promptMu.Lock()
	a.videoStyle = name
	a.promptMu.Unlock()
}

// applyStyle is the project's answer, put on the page without saving it back.
func (a *App) applyStyle(name string) {
	a.setVideoStyle(name)
	if a.stylePick == nil {
		return
	}
	a.styleQuiet = true
	a.stylePick.SetSelected(styleIndex(name))
	a.styleQuiet = false
}
