26	
27	type Project struct {
28		// the session's files in order, each with what it is for; paths relative to
29		// root where they can be
30		Sources []ProjectSource `json:"sources,omitempty"`
31		// videos/audios are read, never written: membership used to be a folder and
32		// a checkbox, one list per folder. A project written back then loads as
33		// sources -- its videos as footage, its first recording as narrator 1 --
34		// and the keys go away with the next save. See projectSources.
35		Videos     []string `json:"videos,omitempty"`
36		Audios     []string `json:"audios,omitempty"`
37		Interval   float64  `json:"interval"` // seconds between frames; 0 = every frame
38		FrameScale string   `json:"frame_scale,omitempty"`
39		// which pipeline the session runs through (textedit.go): "read" for a
40		// read to camera, edited as text with the picture never described; blank
41		// for a session, described and its moments picked -- so every project
42		// written before this reads as the latter.
43		Style string `json:"style,omitempty"`
44		// which steps the ▶▶ beside the play button runs, in pipeline order
45		// (runchain.go). Absent -- every project written before this -- means all
46		// of them, which is what "run it all" is for.
47		RunSteps []string `json:"run_steps,omitempty"`
48		// what the ASR model is told this session is spoken in. It was a setting --
49		// one language for the machine, however many languages its sessions were in
50		// -- and it is a property of the footage, so it belongs to the project that
51		// names that footage. Absent means defLanguage, the same deal a prompt gets.
52		Language string `json:"language,omitempty"`
53		// this video has no narration at all: no lines written, none spoken, and
54		// nothing in Produce that exists to carry one. Off is the ordinary answer
55		// and every project written before this reads as off, so an old project
56		// still narrates. See App.narrOff.
57		NoNarration bool `json:"no_narration,omitempty"`
58		// the sources are referenced where they are rather than copied into the
59		// project when added. Off -- copy -- is the ordinary answer, so a project
60		// is one folder that holds what it needs; on is for the machine that
61		// recorded the footage, where 20 GB of capture does not want a twin.
62		// Stored the wrong way round so every project written before this copies.
63		RefSources bool   `json:"reference_sources,omitempty"`
64		VidDir     string `json:"vid_dir,omitempty"` // where the choosers open, each
65		AudDir     string `json:"aud_dir,omitempty"` // stored the way every path is (storePath)
66		// in_dir is read, never written: there was one input folder, which had to
67		// hold input_video/ and input_audio/. A project written back then names it
68		// here, and those two subfolders are where the two folders above start.
69		InDir string `json:"in_dir,omitempty"`
70		// out_dir is read, never written: the output folder used to be chosen and
71		// stored, and is now derived from the project file's own name (see projExt).
72		// It is read only to say, once, where an older project's work was left.
73		OutDir string `json:"out_dir,omitempty"`
74		// these four are read, never written: the pages they belonged to had a notes
75		// box beside the system prompt, which the runner glued onto the prompt just
76		// before sending. One box per step now, so a project written by an older
77		// build has its notes folded into the prompt on load (migrateHints) and the
78		// keys go away with the next save.
79		DescribeHints   string `json:"describe_hints,omitempty"`
80		TranscriptHints string `json:"transcript_hints,omitempty"`
81		CutHints        string `json:"cut_hints,omitempty"`
82		NarrateHints    string `json:"narrate_hints,omitempty"`
83		// "pitch" used to live here too -- the output-pitch slider. It is gone; a
84		// project written back then still loads, the key is simply ignored.
85	
86		// what the editor typed about this session on the Describe page. Stored in
87		// full, unlike a prompt: there is no built-in wording for it to differ from
88		// (see context.go).
89		Context string `json:"context,omitempty"`
90	
91		// Read, never written: the prompts live on the machine now (promptstore in
92		// prompts.go). A project still carrying them is adopted once for whichever
93		// jobs this machine has nothing of its own for (applyPromptStyles); the
94		// file itself is left as it was.
95		Prompts map[string]string `json:"prompts,omitempty"`
96	
97		Produce *prodSettings `json:"produce,omitempty"`
98		// the thumbnail and the upload text. Absent until the thumbnail half of
99		// Produce has something on it, so an older project -- or a session that stops at the
100		// rendered video -- stays as short a file as it was.
101		Publish *pubSettings `json:"publish,omitempty"`
102	}
103	
104	// ProjectSource is one source as a project stores it. The roles are omitted
105	// when unset so the common row -- a recording nobody narrates as -- is one
106	// line, and so a project file stays something you can read and fix by hand.
107	type ProjectSource struct {
108		Path     string `json:"path"`
109		Footage  bool   `json:"footage,omitempty"`
110		Narrator int    `json:"narrator,omitempty"`
111		// the wish, not the result: it is saved because a project closed before ▶
112		// has to open with the same rows still flagged, and it is cleared by the
113		// run that grants it, so a finished project stores nothing here
114		SepVoice bool `json:"sepvoice,omitempty"`
115		// which audio tracks of a multi-track file this session uses (a:N indices).
116		// Omitted for the ordinary answer -- the first track alone -- so a project
117		// written before multi-track files were reachable already says the right
118		// thing by saying nothing, and no migration was needed (wantTracks).
119		Tracks []int `json:"tracks,omitempty"`
120	}
121	
122	// relToRoot stores a folder the way a project file wants it: relative when it
123	// lives inside root, so moving the naivepost directory moves it too; absolute
124	// when it does not, because then there is nothing to be relative to.
125	func (a *App) relToRoot(dir string) string {
126		if rel, err := filepath.Rel(a.root, dir); err == nil && !strings.HasPrefix(rel, "..") {
127			return rel
128		}
129		return dir
130	}
131	
132	// projPrefix marks a path stored relative to the PROJECT rather than to the
133	// root. Sources can live inside the project folder -- the voice-split step
134	// writes its stems there, and Add can copy footage in (project_import.go) --
135	// and a project is a folder you are meant to be able to rename, move or zip.
136	// Stored absolute, every one of those breaks the session silently: the file is
137	// not where the project says, the row is pruned, and the autosave then writes
138	// the pruned list back.
139	const projPrefix = "project:"
140	
141	// projRel is a path as the project folder sees it, and whether it is in there
142	// at all. Slash-separated, because a stored path is read on whatever machine
143	// the folder is opened on.
144	func (a *App) projRel(p string) (string, bool) {
145		if a.outDir == "" {
146			return p, false
147		}
148		rel, err := filepath.Rel(a.outDir, p)
149		if err != nil || rel == ".." || strings.HasPrefix(rel, ".."+string(filepath.Separator)) {
150			return p, false
151		}
152		return filepath.ToSlash(rel), true
153	}
154	
155	// storePath is how ANY file path goes into a project's files -- naivepost.json,
156	// cut.json, the publish record: relative to the project when it is inside it,
157	// relative to the root when it is under that, and absolute otherwise. Every
158	// writer goes through here, because a path stored the other way is a file the
159	// project loses the moment the folder is renamed or moved.
160	func (a *App) storePath(p string) string {
161		if rel, ok := a.projRel(p); ok {
162			return projPrefix + rel
163		}
164		return a.relToRoot(p)
165	}
166	
167	// loadPath is its inverse, and the one reader: a project written before this
168	// stores those same files relative to the root, which is what the last two
169	// cases are. An empty value means the root itself.
170	func (a *App) loadPath(p string) string {
171		switch {
172		case p == "":
173			return a.root
174		case strings.HasPrefix(p, projPrefix):
175			return filepath.Join(a.outDir, filepath.FromSlash(strings.TrimPrefix(p, projPrefix)))
176		case filepath.IsAbs(p):
177			return p
178		default:
179			return filepath.Join(a.root, p)
180		}
181	}
182	
183	// A project is a FOLDER: /mnt/rec/tom.naivepost, with naivepost.json in it and
184	// every step's work beside it. One thing to copy, back up, hand over or zip;
185	// nothing stores where the work goes, so nothing can disagree about it. The
186	// unsaved session is root/session.naivepost, and Save renames the folder.
187	// Projects from earlier builds (a file beside a .data folder) are adopted on
188	// open (adoptLegacy).
189	const projExt = ".naivepost"
190	
191	// projMain is the project's own file inside its folder. Named rather than
192	// spelled out because the folder IS the project everywhere else in the app,
193	// and this is the one place that cares which file in it carries the JSON.
194	//
195	// naivepost.json rather than main.json: opened on its own -- in an editor, in a
196	// diff, out of a zip somebody sent -- "main.json" is a file that could belong
197	// to anything.
198	const projMain = "naivepost.json"
199	
200	// projFile is where a project folder keeps its JSON.
201	func projFile(dir string) string { return filepath.Join(dir, projMain) }
202	
203	// workName is the working copy inside the naivepost root: what the first launch
204	// starts as, and what New Project goes back to.
205	const workName = "session" + projExt
206	
207	// dataDir is a project's output folder, which is the project (see projExt).
208	// Kept as a name because every step, every page and the Save that moves the
209	// folder go through it, and "the project" and "where it writes" are worth
210	// being able to tell apart in the reading even when they are one path.
211	func dataDir(proj string) string { return proj }
212	
213	// withProjExt is what Save actually writes, whatever was typed in the name box.
214	// The extension is not decoration: it is what the desktop matches to open a
215	// file with Naivepost (icon.go), and it is what .data hangs off, so "tom" and
216	// "tom.naivepost" would otherwise be two projects sharing neither name nor work.
217	func withProjExt(p string) string {
218		if strings.EqualFold(filepath.Ext(p), projExt) {
219			return p
220		}
221		return p + projExt
222	}
223	
224	func (a *App) currentProject() Project {
225		scaleName, _ := a.frameScale()
226		var prod *prodSettings
227		if a.prod != nil {
228			st := a.prodSettings()
229			// the destination is not stored: it is produce/final with the
230			// container's extension, worked out from where the project is
231			// (setOut, followOutDir), so a project that moves takes its video's
232			// folder with it and a project file cannot disagree with the page
233			st.OutFile = ""
234			prod = &st
235		}
236		var srcs []ProjectSource
237		for _, it := range a.srcList.items {
238			srcs = append(srcs, ProjectSource{
239				Path: a.storePath(it.path), Footage: it.footage, Narrator: it.narrator,
240				SepVoice: it.sepVoice, Tracks: it.tracks,
241			})
242		}
243		return Project{
244			Sources:    srcs,
245			Interval:   a.frameInterval(),
246			FrameScale: scaleName,
247			Style:      a.videoStyleName(),
248			RunSteps:   a.chainPicked(),
249			Language:   a.projectLanguage(),
250			// the cut's wording IS the style: the dropdown lists that job's
251			// wordings and every other job followed it. Written even
252			// when it is the shipped default, so that "this project is General"
253			// and "this project predates the field" stay different answers -- the
254			// first has to be able to switch a machine back off Showcase.
255			VidDir:      a.storePath(a.vidDir),
256			AudDir:      a.storePath(a.audDir),
257			Context:     a.sessionCtx(),
258			NoNarration: a.narrOff,
259			RefSources:  a.refSources,
260			Produce:     prod,
261			Publish:     a.currentPublish(),
262		}
263	}
264	
265	// projectSources is a stored project as a list of sources, migrating one
266	// written before the two lists became one.
267	//
268	// The migration has to preserve what the old project meant, which was: these
269	// videos are the footage, these recordings are the voices, and the first
270	// recording is the one Narrate clones. That last part was a convention nothing
271	// stated -- ownVoiceFile took audios[0] -- so it becomes the narrator 1 tag,
272	// which is the same choice said out loud.
273	//
274	// Legacy paths are resolved through the folder, not through root: a project
275	// from before the folders were settable stores input_video/x.mkv, which is
276	// relative to a root that may no longer be this one.
277	func (a *App) projectSources(p Project) []sourceItem {
278		if len(p.Sources) > 0 {
279			var out []sourceItem
280			for _, s := range p.Sources {
281				out = append(out, sourceItem{
282					path: a.loadPath(s.Path), footage: s.Footage, narrator: s.Narrator,
283					sepVoice: s.SepVoice, tracks: s.Tracks,
284				})
285			}
286			return out
287		}
288		var out []sourceItem
289		for _, l := range []struct {
290			dir     string
291			files   []string
292			footage bool
293		}{{a.vidDir, p.Videos, true}, {a.audDir, p.Audios, false}} {
294			for i, f := range l.files {
295				path := a.loadPath(f)
296				if inDir := filepath.Join(l.dir, filepath.Base(f)); !exists(path) && exists(inDir) {
297					path = inDir
298				}
299				it := sourceItem{path: path, footage: l.footage}
300				if !l.footage && i == 0 {
301					it.narrator = 1 // what "my own voice" used to mean
302				}
303				out = append(out, it)
304			}
305		}
306		return out
307	}
308	
309	// ---- saving, and then saving itself -----------------------------------------
310	
311	// projectJSON is the project as it would be written right now. It is also how
312	// the autosave decides there is anything to write: the bytes are the state, so
313	// comparing them catches every field of every page without a single page
314	// having to remember to say it changed. Nothing else could -- the settings are
315	// spread over five pages, two text buffers, a list and a dozen widgets, and a
316	// notify-me hook on each of them is a hook somebody will forget on the next
317	// one, silently, with the symptom appearing a session later as lost work.
318	func (a *App) projectJSON() []byte {
319		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(a.currentProject(), "", "  ")
320		if err != nil {
321			return nil // cannot happen with these types; not worth a wrong write
322		}
323		return append(b, '\n')
324	}
325	
326	// writeProject writes the JSON into the project folder, making it if this is
327	// the first write -- a project that has never been saved is a folder that does
328	// not exist yet, and the autosave is what brings it into being.
329	func (a *App) writeProject(path string, b []byte) error {
330		if err := os.MkdirAll(path, 0o755); err != nil {
331			return err
332		}
333		return os.WriteFile(projFile(path), b, 0o644)
334	}
335	
336	// projNameChars is how much of the project's name the header bar shows before
337	// it ellipsizes. Wide enough for the names people actually type ("before the
338	// recut.json"), narrow enough that it cannot walk the centered tabs sideways
339	// on a small window.
340	const projNameChars = 28
341	
342	// projLabelText is what the header bar can say about a project path: the file's
343	// name, the whole path, and the tooltip behind whichever of the two is on
344	// screen. Which one is shown is a question of width and belongs to fitHeader;
345	// this is only the wording, including the one for a session that has never been
346	// saved -- a blank space where a file name goes reads as a bug rather than as
347	// "nothing has been written yet". That case has no path to offer, so it gives
348	// the same words twice and the bar is free to pick either.
349	func projLabelText(p string) (name, full, tip string) {
350		if strings.TrimSpace(p) == "" {
351			none := "no project file"
352			return none, none, "this session has not been saved to a project file yet"
353		}
354		return filepath.Base(p), p, p
355	}
356	
357	// showProject puts the open project in the header bar. Called from both places
358	// that assign projPath, so the bar can never name a file the autosave has
359	// stopped following. The name first and then the fit, because the fit is what
360	// decides between the name and the path and it declines to answer at all
361	// before the bar has been laid out -- at which point the name is the right
362	// thing to be showing.
363	func (a *App) showProject() {
364		if a.projLabel == nil {
365			return // headless (tests)
366		}
367		name, _, tip := projLabelText(a.projPath)
368		a.projLabel.SetText(name)
369		a.projLabel.SetTooltipText(tip)
370		a.fitHeader()
371	}
372	
373	// setProject points the session at a project file: the file the autosave
374	// follows, and the folder beside it that every step writes into. The two are
375	// one decision (see projExt), so they are made in one place, and everything on
376	// screen that was read out of the old folder is re-read here.
377	func (a *App) setProject(path string) {
378		a.projPath = path
379		a.outDir = dataDir(path)
380		a.migrateFolders()
381		a.showProject()
382		a.followOutDir()
383		// the voice belongs to the project, not to the session: drop the cached id,
384		// pitch and hand-picked takes so all three are re-read from the folder we
385		// just moved to
386		a.voiceMu.Lock()
387		a.voiceSel = ""
388		a.takesRead, a.takesMap = false, nil
389		a.pitchRead = false
390		a.voiceMu.Unlock()
391		if a.voicePick != nil {
392			a.voicePick.syncSelection()
393		}
394		// The narration lives in the output folder, and this is the only thing that
395		// re-reads it: the page is built once at startup, against the empty
396		// session's folder, so without this a saved narration would never load for
397		// any project at all -- it looked like narration was never saved.
398		if a.narr != nil {
399			a.narr.load()
400			a.narr.rebuildRows()
401		}
402		// every page shows state derived from the output folder -- refresh all.
403		// The Cut page included: its tracks were just drawn from the folder of the
404		// project we are leaving.
405		a.prep.refresh()
406		a.updateProduceInfo()
407		a.pub.refresh()
408		a.refreshCut()
409		a.updateGates()
410	}
411	
412	// saveProjectNow writes every target and remembers what it wrote. Quiet: it is
413	// what the ticker and the step runners call, and a status line per autosave
414	// would push the message the user is actually waiting on off the bar.
415	func (a *App) saveProjectNow() {
416		b := a.projectJSON()
417		if b == nil {
418			return
419		}
420		// before the writes, not after: a target that cannot be written must not be
421		// retried every tick for the rest of the session, and the log line below
422		// says it once per change either way.
423		a.projSaved = b
424		// One file: the open one. It used to be two -- the named file and a working
425		// copy the next launch opened -- and the working copy is now simply the
426		// project that is open when nobody has named one, so there is nothing left
427		// to keep in step with anything.
428		if err := a.writeProject(a.projPath, b); err != nil {
429			a.logf("save project: %v", err)
430		}
431	}
432	
433	// adoptLegacy turns an older build's project -- the file tom.naivepost beside
434	// tom.naivepost.data -- into the folder this build opens, via a staging name so
435	// the file is never in the way of its own new name: rename .data aside, write
436	// naivepost.json into it, remove the file, rename into place. Interrupted, it
437	// leaves the file plus <name>.adopting and refuses next time rather than
438	// guessing. A folder is returned untouched.
439	func (a *App) adoptLegacy(path string) (string, error) {
440		if fi, err := os.Stat(path); err == nil && fi.IsDir() {
441			return path, nil
442		}
443		// the naivepost.json a file manager or an old recents list can point at
444		if strings.EqualFold(filepath.Base(path), projMain) {
445			return filepath.Dir(path), nil
446		}
447		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
448		if err != nil {
449			return "", fmt.Errorf("open %s: %w", path, err)
450		}
451		dir := withProjExt(path)
452		// root/project.json was never a name anybody chose -- it was the working
453		// copy, before a project was something you could double-click -- and the
454		// working copy has a name of its own now
455		if path == filepath.Join(a.root, "project.json") {
456			dir = filepath.Join(a.root, workName)
457		}
458		if dir != path && exists(dir) {
459			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s was written by an older build and %s already exists: "+
460				"move one of them aside", filepath.Base(path), filepath.Base(dir))
461		}
462		tmp := dir + ".adopting"
463		if exists(tmp) {
464			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s is left over from an interrupted open: move it aside, "+
465				"or rename it to %s", filepath.Base(tmp), filepath.Base(dir))
466		}
467		if old := path + ".data"; exists(old) {
468			if err := os.Rename(old, tmp); err != nil {
469				return "", fmt.Errorf("moving %s aside: %w", filepath.Base(old), err)
470			}
471		} else if err := os.MkdirAll(tmp, 0o755); err != nil {
472			return "", fmt.Errorf("making %s: %w", tmp, err)
473		}
474		// ...and the paths inside it that pointed into the folder being renamed.
475		// The stems the voice split writes live in there, and so does anything Add
476		// copied in: left absolute they would name a folder that no longer exists,
477		// the rows would be pruned on the next open, and the autosave would write
478		// the pruned list back. Stored project-relative they cannot come apart
479		// again (storePath).
480		b = []byte(strings.ReplaceAll(string(b), `"`+path+".data"+string(filepath.Separator), `"`+projPrefix))
481		if err := os.WriteFile(projFile(tmp), b, 0o644); err != nil {
482			return "", fmt.Errorf("writing %s: %w", projFile(tmp), err)
483		}
484		if err := os.Remove(path); err != nil {
485			return "", fmt.Errorf("removing %s, whose contents are now in %s: %w",
486				filepath.Base(path), filepath.Base(tmp), err)
487		}
488		if err := os.Rename(tmp, dir); err != nil {
489			return "", fmt.Errorf("naming %s: %w", filepath.Base(dir), err)
490		}
491		a.logf(">>> %s is a folder now, with the project inside it as %s — everything this "+
492			"session writes is in there", filepath.Base(dir), projMain)
493		return dir, nil
494	}
495	
496	// migrateFolders moves a project's data through the two renames there have
497	// been: step1/..step6/ into folders named for their steps, then inputs/ and
498	// understand/{describe,transcript} under prepare/. Once, on the open that
499	// finds them; a folder already under its new name is left alone. Logged.
500	func (a *App) migrateFolders() {
501		if a.outDir == "" {
502			return
503		}
504		for _, m := range [][2]string{
505			{"step1", "inputs"}, {"step2", "understand"}, {"step3", "cut"},
506			{"step4", "narrate"}, {"step5", "produce"}, {"step6", "publish"},
507		} {
508			from, to := filepath.Join(a.outDir, m[0]), filepath.Join(a.outDir, m[1])
509			if !exists(from) || exists(to) {
510				continue
511			}
512			if err := os.Rename(from, to); err != nil {
513				a.logf("!!! could not move %s/ to %s/: %v -- the files are still under the old name", m[0], m[1], err)
514				continue
515			}
516			a.logf(">>> moved %s/ to %s/ -- the folders are named for their steps now", m[0], m[1])
517		}
518		// ...and the three folders the FIRST step fills into one folder of its
519		// own. inputs/ sat beside understand/, and understand/ held the other
520		// two, so one step was two places on disk -- and its page carried three
521		// output buttons where every other step has one.
522		for _, m := range [][2]string{
523			{"inputs", filepath.Join("prepare", "inputs")},
524			{filepath.Join("understand", "describe"), filepath.Join("prepare", "describe")},
525			{filepath.Join("understand", "transcript"), filepath.Join("prepare", "transcript")},
526		} {
527			from, to := filepath.Join(a.outDir, m[0]), filepath.Join(a.outDir, m[1])
528			if !exists(from) || exists(to) {
529				continue
530			}
531			if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(to), 0o755); err != nil {
532				a.logf("!!! could not make %s/: %v -- %s/ is still where it was", filepath.Dir(m[1]), err, m[0])
533				continue
534			}
535			if err := os.Rename(from, to); err != nil {
536				a.logf("!!! could not move %s/ to %s/: %v -- the files are still under the old name", m[0], m[1], err)
537				continue
538			}
539			a.logf(">>> moved %s/ to %s/ -- Prepare's work is under its own name now", m[0], m[1])
540		}
541		// what is left of understand/ once its two are out: nothing, and an empty
542		// folder beside the named ones is a step somebody will go looking for.
543		// Remove, not RemoveAll -- anything still in there is not ours to throw
544		// away, and the call simply fails.
545		os.Remove(filepath.Join(a.outDir, "understand"))
546	}
547	
548	// saveProjectTo is the explicit save behind the button: it names the file the
549	// autosave follows from here on, and says so.
550	//
551	// The work follows the name. Transcripts, frames and renders live in a folder
552	// derived from the file name (see projExt), so a Save As without the move would
553	// leave a project whose every output is filed under the name it used to have,
554	// and which reads, on every page, as one that has never been run.
555	func (a *App) saveProjectTo(path string) {
556		path = withProjExt(path)
557		if path != a.projPath {
558			a.moveOutputs(a.outDir, dataDir(path))
559			a.setProject(path)
560		}
561		a.rememberProject(path)
562		a.saveProjectNow()
563		a.setStatus("project saved")
564	}
565	
566	// moveOutputs takes one project's output folder to another's name. A rename is
567	// instant on one filesystem and cannot half-happen, which is why it is a rename
568	// and not a copy: nobody presses Save expecting gigabytes of frames to be
569	// duplicated. It is also the whole check -- a rename onto a folder that already
570	// has work in it fails, and onto one that is empty succeeds, which is exactly
571	// the answer wanted in both cases. When it will not go through, across
572	// filesystems or into a name in use, the files stay where they are and the log
573	// says where, because a Save that silently moved work would be worse than one
574	// that did not.
575	//
576	// Silent when there is nothing to move, which is the ordinary case: a project
577	// saved before it has been run has an empty folder or none at all.
578	func (a *App) moveOutputs(from, to string) {
579		n, _, _ := countOutputs(from)
580		if n == 0 {
581			return
582		}
583		if err := os.Rename(from, to); err != nil {
584			a.logf("!!! could not move the output folder to %s: %v -- the %d file(s) are still in %s",
585				to, err, n, from)
586			return
587		}
588		a.logf(">>> moved the output folder to %s", to)
589	}
590	
591	// autosaveTick is how often the project is compared with what is on disk.
592	// Long enough that typing a prompt is not a write per keystroke, short enough
593	// that closing the window after a change loses nothing anyone would notice.
594	const autosaveTick = 2000
595	
596	// startAutosave keeps the file up to date without a button. Save Project stays
597	// -- it is how a variant gets a name -- but it stopped being the thing that
598	// decides whether tonight's work exists in the morning.
599	//
600	// A ticker rather than a debounce on every setter, for the reason projectJSON
601	// gives. The tick costs one marshal of a few kB, and closing the window
602	// flushes whatever the last tick has not seen yet.
603	func (a *App) startAutosave() {
604		a.projSaved = a.projectJSON() // what the startup load already put in memory
605		glib.TimeoutAdd(autosaveTick, func() bool {
606			a.flushProject()
607			a.flushPrompts() // the prompts are the machine's, not the project's, and
608			return true      // are written on the same tick for the same reason
609		})
610		// the tick leaves a gap of up to autosaveTick between a change and the
611		// file, and the change most likely to land in it is the LAST one -- you
612		// click it, you see it happen, you close the window. That gap is what made
613		// a narrator tag come back after it was taken off: the tick that caught
614		// the tagging ran, the one that would have caught the untagging never did.
615		if a.win != nil {
616			a.win.ConnectCloseRequest(func() bool {
617				a.narr.flushSave() // ...and the same for the last line typed
618				if a.ed != nil {
619					a.ed.flushLine() // the red line, as it stood when the window closed (cut_line.go)
620				}
621				a.flushProject()
622				a.flushPrompts()
623				return false // false lets the window close; this only writes
624			})
625		}
626	}
627	
628	// flushProject writes the project if it differs from what is on disk. The
629	// compare is what makes a tick free in practice: a session spends most of its
630	// time not changing anything, and an unchanged project writes nothing at all.
631	func (a *App) flushProject() {
632		if b := a.projectJSON(); b != nil && !bytes.Equal(b, a.projSaved) {
633			a.saveProjectNow()
634		}
635	}
636	
637	func (a *App) loadProjectFrom(path string) {
638		path, err := a.adoptLegacy(path)
639		if err != nil {
640			a.logf("!!! %v", err)
641			a.setStatus("could not open that project — see log")
642			return
643		}
644		b, err := os.ReadFile(projFile(path))
645		if err != nil {
646			a.logf("load project: %v", err)
647			return
648		}
649		var p Project
650		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &p); err != nil {
651			a.logf("load project: %v", err)
652			return
653		}
654		// The folder BEFORE the pages: a source that lives inside the project is
655		// stored relative to it (storePath), and applyProject is what resolves
656		// those. Read with the last project's folder still set, they would resolve
657		// into the last project's folder, not be there, and be pruned -- which is
658		// how a session loses the sources it was cut from.
659		a.projPath, a.outDir = path, dataDir(path)
660		a.applyProject(p)
661		// ...and then the rest of what opening a project means: the pages that
662		// read the folder, the voice, the autosave's target.
663		a.setProject(path)
664		if p.OutDir != "" && a.loadPath(p.OutDir) != a.outDir {
665			a.logf("!!! this project used to write into %s and now writes into %s -- "+
666				"the old folder is untouched", a.loadPath(p.OutDir), a.outDir)
667		}
668		a.rememberProject(a.projPath)
669		a.projSaved = a.projectJSON()
670	}
671	
672	// applyProject puts a project on screen -- every page of it. Split out of
673	// loadProjectFrom because New Project needs exactly this and nothing else:
674	// handed a blank project it walks the same list and each page comes back to its
675	// default, which is a reset that cannot forget a page. A newProject() that
676	// cleared what it could remember to clear would leave the last session's
677	// narration settings, or its thumbnail, in a project claiming to be new -- the
678	// invisible kind of bug applyPromptStyles's comment is about.
679	func (a *App) applyProject(p Project) {
680		// the folders first: they are where the file choosers open, and where a
681		// pre-merge project's half-relative source names are resolved from
682		vid, aud := srcDirs(p)
683		a.vidDir, a.audDir = a.loadPath(vid), a.loadPath(aud)
684		items := a.projectSources(p)
685		// a project entry whose file vanished (renamed, moved) must be LOUD: a
686		// silently-dropped source once cost half a debugging session
687		for _, it := range items {
688			if !exists(it.path) {
689				a.logf("!!! %s is not there any more -- dropped from the session", it.path)
690			}
691		}
692		a.srcList.load(items)
693		a.srcList.prune()
694		a.setFrameInterval(p.Interval)
695		if p.FrameScale != "" {
696			a.setFrameScale(p.FrameScale)
697		}
698		a.applyStyle(p.Style)
699		a.applyChain(p.RunSteps)
700		a.applyLanguage(p.Language)
701		a.adoptProjectPrompts(p.Prompts)
702		a.applySessionCtx(p.Context)
703		a.applyNarrOff(p.NoNarration)
704		a.applyRefSources(p.RefSources)
705		a.migrateHints(p)
706		a.applyProdSettings(p.Produce)
707		a.applyPublish(p.Publish)
708		// Every page except the ones drawn from the output folder -- the Cut page,
709		// the counts, the narration. The stored out_dir is deliberately not read:
710		// the folder is derived from the file's own name (see projExt), and the
711		// caller sets both with setProject, which is what redraws those pages.
712	}
713	
714	// blankProject is what New Project starts from. Interval and Produce are
715	// stated because their zero values are real and wrong (0 seconds is EVERY
716	// frame; a zeroed produce block is a 0-CRF, 0-fps render). The output folder
717	// is not a setting: it follows the project file.
718	func blankProject() Project {
719		prod := defaultProdSettings()
720		return Project{
721			Interval:   frameStops[defFrameStop],
722			FrameScale: scalePresets[0].Name,
723			Produce:    &prod,
724		}
725	}
726	
727	// newProject empties the session into a project of its own at path. The
728	// project that was open is not deleted and not written over: it stays on disk
729	// exactly as it was, with everything it has written, and going back to it is
730	// Load, not undo.
731	func (a *App) newProject(path string) {
732		a.applyProject(blankProject())
733		// where the project was put is where its footage almost certainly is, so
734		// that is where Add opens -- not input_video/ under the folder naivepost was
735		// started from, which for a session on a card or a scratch disk is a folder
736		// with nothing in it. The working copy keeps those defaults: nobody chose
737		// where it went.
738		if dir := filepath.Dir(path); dir != a.root {
739			a.vidDir, a.audDir = dir, dir
740		}
741		a.setProject(path)
742		// the new project is now the open one, and that is a decision, not an
743		// absence: without this the next launch reopens the project this was meant
744		// to get away from (see rememberProject)
745		a.rememberProject(a.projPath)
746		a.saveProjectNow()
747		a.setStatus("new project — " + filepath.Base(path))
748		a.logf(">>> new project %s -- the session is empty; outputs on disk are untouched", path)
749	}
750	
751	// newProjectAt is the answer to that dialog: the folder is made and the empty
752	// session moves into it.
753	//
754	// A name that is already a project is refused rather than started over. The
755	// blank session would be written into it within the second (saveProjectNow),
756	// on top of a project whose frames, cut and narration are all still in that
757	// folder and would then belong to a session that knows nothing about them.
758	func (a *App) newProjectAt(path string) {
759		path = withProjExt(path)
760		if exists(projFile(path)) {
761			a.setStatus(filepath.Base(path) + " is a project already — open it, or pick another name")
762			a.logf("!!! new project: %s is a project already -- nothing was changed", path)
763			return
764		}
765		a.newProject(path)
766	}
767	
768	// askNewProject asks what to call it and where to put it.
769	//
770	// New used to make session.naivepost in the folder naivepost was started from,
771	// which is the one folder a session's own footage is never in: every project
772	// began in the checkout and had to be moved by a Save As afterwards. A project
773	// is a folder you name and place (projExt), and this is where that happens.
774	//
775	// It opens beside the open project, which is where saveProjectDialog opens and
776	// for the same reason -- the last project is nearly always beside the footage
777	// this one is about.
778	func (a *App) askNewProject() {
779		dir := filepath.Dir(a.projPath)
780		a.saveAs("New project", dir, freeProjName(dir), nil, a.newProjectAt)
781	}
782	
783	// freeProjName is what the name box starts with: today's date, which is how the
784	// recorders name their own files, and a number after it when a project of that
785	// name is already there -- a second session in one day is not a mistake worth
786	// a refusal.
787	func freeProjName(dir string) string {
788		day := time.Now().Format("2006-01-02")
789		name := day + projExt
790		for i := 2; exists(filepath.Join(dir, name)); i++ {
791			name = fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d%s", day, i, projExt)
792		}
793		return name
794	}
795	
796	// newProjectDialog asks first, and then asks where (askNewProject). The
797	// session is not a file until Save names one, so New on a session nobody saved
798	// throws away work that exists nowhere else -- and it is one click from Load
799	// and Save in the header bar, which are the two buttons a hand reaching for it
800	// is aiming between.
801	//
802	// Nothing to lose, no question: an empty session being emptied is not a
803	// decision worth interrupting anyone for. The name dialog still comes.
804	func (a *App) newProjectDialog() {
805		if a.running {
806			a.setStatus("stop the run first — a new project would pull its inputs out from under it")
807			return
808		}
809		if len(a.srcList.items) == 0 && a.sessionCtx() == "" {
810			a.askNewProject()
811			return
812		}
813		detail := "The sources, the session context and every prompt edit go back to empty. " +
814			"Files already written to the output folder are left alone."
815		if filepath.Base(a.projPath) != workName {
816			detail += "\n\n" + filepath.Base(a.projPath) + " stays on disk as it is, " +
817				"with everything it has written -- this session simply stops being it."
818		} else {
819			detail += "\n\nThis session has never been saved under a name of its own, " +
820				"so there is nothing to come back to."
821		}
822		// the ellipsis is the promise that the press is not the last word: what
823		// follows is the box that names the new project and puts it somewhere
824		a.confirm("Start a new project?", detail, "Start new…", a.askNewProject)
825	}
826	
827	// confirm is a modal yes/no with the red button: what the left button does
828	// cannot be undone. Cancel has the focus, so a blind Enter does nothing.
829	func (a *App) confirm(question, detail, okLabel string, ok func()) {
830		var win *gtk.Window
831		go1 := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel(okLabel)
832		go1.AddCSSClass("destructive-action")
833		go1.ConnectClicked(func() { win.Close(); ok() })
834		cancel := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Cancel")
835		win = a.modal(question, detail, 420, nil, cancel, go1)
836		cancel.ConnectClicked(func() { win.Close() })
837		cancel.GrabFocus()
838		win.SetVisible(true)
839	}
840	
841	// migrateHints folds a pre-merge project's notes into the prompts they used to
842	// be appended to. The runners did that concatenation at request time, using
843	// exactly these lead-ins, so folding them in preserves what the model saw;
844	// dropping them would silently change what a reloaded project sends. Must run
845	// after applyPromptStyles, which is what puts the prompt in the box in the first
846	// place.
847	func (a *App) migrateHints(p Project) {
848		fold := func(key, notes, lead string) {
849			notes = strings.TrimSpace(notes)
850			if notes == "" {
851				return
852			}
853			cur := a.prompt(key)
854			if strings.Contains(cur, notes) {
855				return // already folded in, by this load or an earlier one
856			}
857			merged := cur + "\n" + lead + "\n" + notes
858			a.setPrompt(key, merged)
859			if tv := a.promptViews[key]; tv != nil {
860				tv.Buffer().SetText(merged)
861			}
862			if a.log != nil { // not during tests, which have no window
863				a.logf(">>> moved this project's notes into the %q prompt", key)
864			}
865		}
866		fold("describe", p.DescribeHints, "Editor's notes about this footage -- trust them:")
867		fold("fix", p.TranscriptHints, "Editor's notes -- trust them:")
868		fold("cut", p.CutHints, "Editor's notes about this session -- trust them and let them guide what matters:")
869		fold("narrate", p.NarrateHints, "Editor's goals and context -- honor them:")
870	}
871	
872	// srcDirs says where a project's two source folders are, still relative to root
873	// where it stored them that way. A project written before the split names one
874	// folder that had to hold input_video/ and input_audio/, and those two
875	// subfolders are exactly the folders it meant -- so an old project keeps
876	// pointing at the same files instead of opening on two empty lists.
877	func srcDirs(p Project) (vid, aud string) {
878		vid, aud = p.VidDir, p.AudDir
879		if vid == "" {
880			vid = filepath.Join(p.InDir, "input_video")
881		}
882		if aud == "" {
883			aud = filepath.Join(p.InDir, "input_audio")
884		}
885		return vid, aud
886	}
887	
888	// addFilesDialog adds files to the session, several at a time -- a card holds
889	// one take per angle and picking them one dialog at a time is not a workflow.
890	func (a *App) addFilesDialog() {
891		exts := make([]string, 0, len(mediaExt))
892		for e := range mediaExt {
893			exts = append(exts, e)
894		}
895		a.pickFiles("Add sources", a.vidDir, extFilter("Audio and video", exts...), a.askImport)
896	}
897	
898	// addSources puts files in the list and remembers where they came from, so the
899	// next chooser opens where the last one did. The two folders are no longer what
900	// the list is made of -- they are only where it starts looking.
901	func (a *App) addSources(paths ...string) {
902		n := a.srcList.add(paths...)
903		for _, p := range paths {
904			if isVideo(p) {
905				a.vidDir = filepath.Dir(p)
906			} else {
907				a.audDir = filepath.Dir(p)
908			}
909		}
910		switch {
911		case n == 0:
912			a.setStatus("already in the session — nothing added")
913		case n == len(paths):
914			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("added %d source(s)", n))
915		default:
916			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("added %d of %d — the rest were already in", n, len(paths)))
917		}
918	}
919	
920	// saveProjectDialog names the project. It opens beside the open project rather
921	// than in the root, because Save As on /mnt/rec/tom.json.naivepost is nearly
922	// always another name in /mnt/rec -- that is where the footage is.
923	//
924	// Not during a run: the save moves the output folder the run is writing into.
925	func (a *App) saveProjectDialog() {
926		if a.running {
927			a.setStatus("stop the run first — saving under a new name moves the folder it is writing into")
928			return
929		}
930		// Save, not SelectFolder: a name is typed here, and the name is what the
931		// folder will be called (withProjExt). A folder chooser can only pick one
932		// that exists.
933		a.saveAs("Save the project", filepath.Dir(a.projPath), filepath.Base(a.projPath), nil, a.saveProjectTo)
934	}
935	
936	// loadProjectDialog picks a project FOLDER -- which is what a project is
937	// (projExt). A project from an older build is a file and cannot be picked
938	// here; it is opened by double-clicking it, from the recents list, or from the
939	// command line, and adopted into a folder on the way in (adoptLegacy).
940	func (a *App) loadProjectDialog() {
941		a.pickFolder("Open a project", filepath.Dir(a.projPath), a.loadProjectFrom)
942	}
943	
944	// openFolder shows a directory in the user's file manager -- via the desktop
945	// portal (works on any DE, unlike bare xdg-open from an app context), falling
946	// back to xdg-open. The directory is created first: launching a missing path
947	// silently does nothing, which reads as a dead button.
948	func (a *App) openFolder(dir string) {
949		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
950			a.logf("open folder: %v", err)
951			return
952		}
953		l := gtk.NewFileLauncher(gio.NewFileForPath(dir))
954		l.Launch(context.Background(), &a.win.Window, func(res gio.AsyncResulter) {
955			if err := l.LaunchFinish(res); err != nil {
956				a.logf("portal launch failed (%v), trying xdg-open", err)
957				if err := exec.Command("xdg-open", dir).Start(); err != nil {
958					a.logf("xdg-open: %v", err)
959				}
960			}
961		})
962	}
963	
964	// ---- output inspection ------------------------------------------------------
965	
966	// summarizeOutputs is the one-line answer: how many files are under dir, and
967	// how long ago the newest was written. Recursive, because Prepare's output is
968	// mostly frames in subdirectories -- a top-level count would say "3 entries"
969	// about four thousand files. The age is what tells a finished step from a
970	// stale one at a glance.
971	func summarizeOutputs(dir string) string {
972		n, _, size := countOutputs(dir)
973		if n == 0 {
974			return "nothing yet"
975		}
976		// how many and how big, and nothing else. It used to end on "newest 12 min
977		// ago", which is a fact about the last run rather than about what is on
978		// disk -- and the run that wrote it finished in front of you.
979		return fmt.Sprintf("%s, %s", plural(n, "file"), humanSize(size))
980	}
981	
982	// countOutputs is the same walk with the two halves kept apart. Prepare
983	// shows three of these at once and puts the age on hover: three sentences of
984	// the form above, side by side, is a paragraph across the bottom of a page.
985	func countOutputs(dir string) (n int, newest time.Time, size int64) {
986		filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(_ string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
987			if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
988				return nil // an unreadable subtree is not worth a whole error line here
989			}
990			n++
991			if fi, err := d.Info(); err == nil {
992				size += fi.Size()
993				if fi.ModTime().After(newest) {
994					newest = fi.ModTime()
995				}
996			}
997			return nil
998		})
999		return n, newest, size
1000	}
1001	
1002	func humanAgo(t time.Time) string {
1003		d := time.Since(t)
1004		switch {
1005		case d < time.Minute:
1006			return "just now"
1007		case d < time.Hour:
1008			return fmt.Sprintf("%d min ago", int(d.Minutes()))
1009		case d < 24*time.Hour:
1010			return fmt.Sprintf("%d h ago", int(d.Hours()))
1011		case d < 48*time.Hour:
1012			return "yesterday"
1013		default:
1014			return fmt.Sprintf("%d days ago", int(d.Hours()/24))
1015		}
1016	}
1017	
1018	// logListMax is how many files a directory gets to name before it becomes a
1019	// count. Prepare writes one frame per second of footage; a log carrying four
1020	// thousand f000123.jpg lines is a log nobody scrolls, and the run's own
1021	// messages would be buried in it.
1022	const logListMax = 12
1023	
1024	// logOutputs names what a step actually wrote, in the log, and returns the file
1025	// count for the status line. The page shows the count; the names live here,
1026	// because that is the place you can scroll back through after a run.
1027	// GUI thread only -- callers are completion handlers.
1028	func (a *App) logOutputs(label, dir string) int {
1029		n := a.logTree(dir, label) // label leads every path, so the log says which step
1030		if n == 0 {
1031			a.logf("    %s/: nothing written", label)
1032		}
1033		return n
1034	}
1035	
1036	func (a *App) logTree(dir, rel string) int {
1037		ents, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
1038		if err != nil {
1039			return 0
1040		}

func (a *App) adoptProjectPrompts(legacy map[string]string) {

func sameStrings(model *gtk.StringList, want []string) bool {

func (a *App) askName(question, detail string, ok func(string)) {
	var win *gtk.Window

	done := func() {
		if name := strings.TrimSpace(entry.Text()); name != "" {
			win.Close()
			ok(name)
		}
	}
	entry.ConnectActivate(done)
	save := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Save")
	save.AddCSSClass("suggested-action")
	save.ConnectClicked(done)
	cancel := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Cancel")
	win = a.modal(question, detail, 380, entry, cancel, save)
	cancel.ConnectClicked(func() { win.Close() })
	entry.GrabFocus()

// editorBody is the one shape a text box on a step page has: a heading row,
// then a framed, scrolling box floored at four lines. Every heading row on
// every page joins one size group, so a row with a button and a row with a
// bare label are the same height and the boxes under them start at the same
// y. The four-line floor is the one number that can push things off a short
// window; 240 once did.
func (a *App) editorBody(head *gtk.Box, tv *gtk.TextView) *gtk.Box {
	if a.headGroup == nil {
		a.headGroup = gtk.NewSizeGroup(gtk.SizeGroupVertical)
	}
	a.headGroup.AddWidget(head)
	return editorFrame(head, tv)
}

// editorFrame is editorBody without the shared heading height: the same box, for
// somewhere there is nothing beside it to line up with. That is where every
// prompt is shown now -- one at a time, in the picker's window or in the Cut
// page's form column (promptpick.go) -- and a size group is worse than useless
// there, since it goes on measuring rows belonging to windows that have closed.
func editorFrame(head *gtk.Box, tv *gtk.TextView) *gtk.Box {
	// vexpand is what makes a taller window a taller box. Without it the box
	// stops at the height of its text and the window's extra height piles up as
	// blank page below it -- growing the window then bought nothing on the one
	// page whose whole content is text. It propagates up through what this
	// returns, so a page only has to put the box somewhere that can grow.
	scroll := gtk.NewScrolledWindow()
	scroll.SetChild(tv)
	scroll.SetPropagateNaturalHeight(true)
	scroll.SetPolicy(gtk.PolicyNever, gtk.PolicyAutomatic) // wrapped text has no width to scroll
	scroll.SetSizeRequest(-1, 72)
	scroll.SetVExpand(true)
	scroll.AddCSSClass("frame")

	body := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
	body.SetMarginTop(4)
	body.Append(head)
	body.Append(scroll)
	return body
}

// Edited prompts live in ~/.config/naivepost/prompts/<job>.txt, beside the
// settings that are also this machine's. Files, not project JSON: a prompt is
// how you like to be edited for, the same across sessions, and prose that
// gets diffed and grepped. Only what differs is written, so Reset is a delete
// and a newer build's wording reaches an untouched machine.

// promptsDir is the folder, or "" when there is nowhere to put it. Same answer
// as configDir, and for the same reason: nowhere to write is not an error, it
// is a launch where the prompts are whatever the binary ships.
func promptsDir() string {
	d := configDir()
	if d == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return filepath.Join(d, "prompts")
}

const promptExt = ".txt"

// promptPath is where a job's wording is kept, or "" with nowhere to put it:
// prompts/cut.txt, one file per job (it was a folder per job with a file per
// wording, back when styles existed).
func promptPath(key string) string {

	if d == "" || key == "" {
		return ""
	}
	return filepath.Join(d, key+promptExt)
}

// oldPromptNames are the file names the folder-per-job era wrote a job's
// DEFAULT wording under. Anything else in that folder was a wording for a
// style, and the styles no longer exist -- the file is left where it is, and
// what is worth keeping out of it goes in the box or the user context by hand.
var oldPromptNames = []string{"General" + promptExt, "Default" + promptExt}

// loadGlobalPrompts is the startup read: whatever this machine has of its own
// for each job. Called once, before the first project is opened, so that what
// the boxes show is this machine's answer rather than the last project's.
func (a *App) loadGlobalPrompts() {
	txt, disk := map[string]string{}, map[string]string{}
	for _, d := range promptDefs {
		text, from := a.readPrompt(d.key)
		if text == "" {
			continue
		}

			// for it is what makes the next flush write it where it belongs

	a.promptTxt = txt
	a.promptMu.Unlock()
	a.promptDisk = disk

		a.showPrompt(d.key)
	}

// readPrompt is one job's stored wording and the file it came from: its own
// file, or -- for a machine that last ran a build with styles -- the default
// wording out of the old folder.
//
// An empty file is a wording that says nothing, which would send the model no
// system prompt at all: treated as absent, here as before.
func (a *App) readPrompt(key string) (text, from string) {
	try := []string{promptPath(key)}
	if d := promptsDir(); d != "" {
		for _, n := range oldPromptNames {
			try = append(try, filepath.Join(d, key, n))
		}
	}
	for _, p := range try {
		if p == "" {
			continue
		}
		b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
		if err != nil {
			if !os.IsNotExist(err) {
				a.logf("!!! could not read the %s prompt: %v", key, err)
			}
			continue
		}
		if s := strings.TrimSpace(string(b)); s != "" {
			return s, p
		}
	}
	return "", ""
}

// flushPrompts writes what changed since the last flush, on the autosave tick
// (startAutosave). promptDisk is what is believed on disk; a failed write is
// logged and treated as done (the next edit retries). A job back on its
// shipped wording has its file REMOVED. GUI thread only, like flushProject.
func (a *App) flushPrompts() {
	if promptsDir() == "" {
		return
	}
	cur := map[string]string{}
	for _, d := range promptDefs {
		if a.promptOwned(d.key) {
			cur[d.key] = a.prompt(d.key)
		}
	}
	for key, text := range cur {
		if a.promptDisk[key] == text {
			continue
		}
		if err := os.MkdirAll(promptsDir(), 0o700); err != nil {
			a.logf("!!! could not keep the %s prompt: %v", key, err)
			continue
		}
		if err := os.WriteFile(promptPath(key), []byte(text+"\n"), 0o600); err != nil {
			a.logf("!!! could not keep the %s prompt: %v", key, err)
		}
	}
	for key := range a.promptDisk {
		if _, ok := cur[key]; ok {
			continue
		}
		if err := os.Remove(promptPath(key)); err != nil && !os.IsNotExist(err) {
			a.logf("!!! could not drop the %s prompt: %v", key, err)
		}
	}
	a.promptDisk = cur
}

// The user context: what the editor knows that the material does not say --
// who is in the session, what they were doing, what to call things. One box,
// the first row of the bench on Prepare, carried by every request. Prompts say
// HOW to work; this says WHAT this session was, which is why it is stored in
// full and a prompt only when it differs from the built-in.

// sessionCtx is the box's text, callable from a runner's goroutine.
func (a *App) sessionCtx() string {
	a.promptMu.Lock()
	defer a.promptMu.Unlock()
	return strings.TrimSpace(a.ctxTxt)
}

func (a *App) setSessionCtx(s string) {
	a.promptMu.Lock()
	a.ctxTxt = s
	a.promptMu.Unlock()
}

// applySessionCtx loads a project's context into the box and the cache. GUI
// thread only (a GtkTextBuffer). No box is the ordinary case: the bench shows
// one row at a time, and the box fills from the cache when switched back to.
func (a *App) applySessionCtx(s string) {
	a.setSessionCtx(s)
	if a.ctxView != nil {
		a.ctxView.Buffer().SetText(s)
	}
}

// ctxBlock is the context as a request carries it, or nothing when the box is
// empty (an empty heading invites invention). Headed USER CONTEXT, which is
// what downstream prompts call it. It goes in the USER message ahead of the
// material, never the system prompt: the prompt boxes stay what the user
// wrote, and a job's rules stay separable from a session's facts.
func (a *App) ctxBlock() string { return a.ctxBlockFor("cut") }

// ctxBlockFor is the block as one job carries it. The speech rule under it is
// about what to DO with spoken lines -- keep them, caption them, cut on them
// -- and only the jobs that decide that get it: the cut and the narration. The frame describer, the transcript fixer and the upload text
// are told the context and nothing about a decision they never make.
func (a *App) ctxBlockFor(key string) string {
	s := a.sessionCtx()
	if s == "" {
		return ""
	}
	b := "USER CONTEXT -- written by the person who made this recording and " +
		"is editing it. It outranks anything you infer from the material, and it " +
		"outranks the rules of the job you were given wherever the two disagree; " +
		"only the mechanics of the answer -- its shape, its clock, what may be " +
		"invented -- are not its to change:\n" + s + "\n\n"
	switch key {
	case "cut", "narrate":
		b += ctxSpeech + "\n\n"
	}
	return b
}

// ctxSpeech rides under the user context, and only under it: how the context
// bears on the spoken lines. Sent exactly when there is a context to be about.
// Read the wrong way it is the worst answer this app gives -- an aside to the
// editor captioned into the video, or the video thrown away as asides.
const ctxSpeech = `The speech is content unless the user context above says otherwise: the speakers are in the video, and what they say is why a moment is worth keeping. Where the user context calls it directions ("this part is boring", "speed this up"), do what a direction asks at the second it asks and keep its words out of the video -- never caption them, and never keep a stretch just because it was spoken over. An instruction about a kind of stretch -- speed the dull parts up and show them instead of cutting them, caption each thing as it is named -- holds wherever such a stretch occurs. It decides segments too: a stretch to be shown fast has to be in the cut, with a speed effect over it, or there is nothing left to speed up.`

// logCtx says, in the log, that this step's requests carried the context. A
// second input that changes the result and appears nowhere in the run is how
// an editor ends up baffled by their own note from three sessions ago; naming
// the step matters, because the log is read long after the run.
func (a *App) logCtx(step string) {
	if c := a.sessionCtx(); c != "" {
		a.logfIdle(">>> %s: sending the session context from Prepare (%d characters)", step, len(c))
	}
}

111				out = append(out, to)
112			}
113			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
114				a.endRun()
115				a.progress.SetFraction(0)
116				a.addSources(out...)
117				a.saveProjectNow()
118			})
119		}()
120	}
121	
122	// progIdle moves the run bar from a worker goroutine.
123	func (a *App) progIdle(f float64, format string, args ...any) {
124		s := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)
125		glib.IdleAdd(func() {
126			a.progress.SetFraction(f)
127			a.setStatus(s)
128		})
129	}
130	
131	// copyFile writes src to the exact path out, through the same .part-and-rename
132	// copyInto uses: a copy interrupted by a pulled drive or a full disk must not
133	// look like a finished file.
134	func copyFile(src, out string) error {
135		in, err := os.Open(src)
136		if err != nil {
137			return err
138		}
139		defer in.Close()
140		part := out + ".part"
141		f, err := os.Create(part)
142		if err != nil {
143			return err
144		}
145		if _, err := io.Copy(f, in); err != nil {
146			f.Close()
147			os.Remove(part)
148			return err
149		}
150		if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
151			os.Remove(part)
152			return err
153		}
154		return os.Rename(part, out)
155	}
156	
157	// copyMeter counts the bytes of one copy into a bar over all of them, and tells
158	// the bar only when the needle would visibly move: a Write per 32 kB block is
159	// hundreds of thousands of GUI round trips on a large file.
160	type copyMeter struct {
161		total, done int64
162		last        float64
163		tick        func(float64)
164	}
165	
166	func (m *copyMeter) Write(b []byte) (int, error) {
167		m.done += int64(len(b))
168		if m.total > 0 {
169			if f := float64(m.done) / float64(m.total); f-m.last >= 0.005 {
170				m.last = f
171				m.tick(f)
172			}
173		}
174		return len(b), nil
175	}
176	
177	// copyInto copies one file into dir and answers with its new path. The copy is
178	// written to a .part and renamed, so an interrupted copy cannot be mistaken
179	// for a source: a half file that plays for ten seconds and stops is the worst
180	// way to find out a drive was pulled. meter, when given, sees every byte.
181	func copyInto(dir, src string, meter io.Writer) (string, error) {
182		fi, err := os.Stat(src)
183		if err != nil {
184			return "", err
185		}
186		dst := filepath.Join(dir, filepath.Base(src))
187		if d, err := os.Stat(dst); err == nil && d.Size() == fi.Size() {
188			return dst, nil // already here, same size: the same file
189		}
190		in, err := os.Open(src)
191		if err != nil {
192			return "", err
193		}
194		defer in.Close()
195		part := dst + ".part"
196		out, err := os.Create(part)
197		if err != nil {
198			return "", err
199		}
200		var w io.Writer = out
201		if meter != nil {
202			w = io.MultiWriter(out, meter)
203		}
204		if _, err := io.Copy(w, in); err != nil {
205			out.Close()
206			os.Remove(part)
207			return "", err
208		}
209		if err := out.Close(); err != nil {
210			os.Remove(part)
211			return "", err
212		}
213		return dst, os.Rename(part, dst)
214	}

// The prompt bench: one box on Prepare holding everything the models are told,
// in the order the pipeline sends it, behind one menu. The context is the
// first row and is not a prompt: what the editor knows about THIS session,

// prepRow is one row of the menu: what it is called, which store it reads and
// writes (key "" is the session context), and the detail that would otherwise
// make the name a sentence.
type prepRow struct{ menu, key, tip string }

// title is what the heading says while the row is shown. The menu names the
// job; the heading says which of the two kinds of text this is, because "Cut"
// on its own over a box of rules reads like the cut itself.
func (r prepRow) title() string {
	if r.key == "" {
		return r.menu
	}
	return r.menu + " prompt"
}

// were free to change at runtime.

			"describer, the transcript fixer, the cut and its three passes, the " +
			"narration, the upload text — and it outranks the prompts below, which are " +
