package main

// Splitting the voice off a recording: the audio server decomposes a mixture
// into the voice AND everything else (the stems add back up). The result is
// two ordinary files and the session's row becomes two ordinary rows -- itself
// without the voice, and the voice -- so no reader downstream is taught about
// stems. A flag on the row, not a button: the work is minutes of GPU, spent
// by ▶.

import (
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"os/exec"
	"path/filepath"
	"strings"

	"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/glib/v2"
)

const (
	// the same shape as the ASR chunking, and for the same reason: one request
	// per five minutes rather than one per recording. The answer here is the
	// audio itself, base64 in a JSON body -- a whole session in one reply is
	// hundreds of megabytes of it -- so the ceiling matters more, not less.
	sepChunkMax = 300.0
	sepCutSeek  = 20.0
	// what goes up. The separation models are music models: 44.1 kHz stereo is
	// what they were trained on, and handing them the 16 kHz mono the ASR uses
	// would be asking them to separate something they have never heard.
	sepRate     = "44100"
	sepChannels = "2"
)

// sepDir is where the halves are kept. Beside the steps rather than inside
// one: they are sources now, and a source has to survive the step that made it
// being re-run.
func (a *App) sepDir() string { return filepath.Join(a.outDir, "stems") }

// sepNames are the two files a source becomes. The name keeps the original's,
// timestamp and all, because that stamp is how every source is placed on the
// session clock -- a split recording has to land exactly where it did.
//
// The voiceless half of a video is matroska: it carries the original picture
// stream copied, untouched, beside an audio codec of its own choosing, so
// giving a recording a new soundtrack never costs it a re-encode.
func sepNames(dir, src string) (rest, voice string) {
	base := baseName(src)
	rest = filepath.Join(dir, base+".split-novoice.wav")
	if isVideo(src) {
		rest = filepath.Join(dir, base+".split-novoice.mkv")
	}
	return rest, filepath.Join(dir, base+".split-voice.wav")
}

// splitProduct is whether a path is one half of a split: the name says so,
// and the name is the only thing a stem carries (see the file header). It is
// what keeps the scissors off a row that is already a half -- splitting the
// voice off a voice is a wish that produces x.split-voice.split-voice.wav.
// The old spellings are read too, for a project split before they changed.
func splitProduct(path string) bool {
	b := baseName(path)
	for _, s := range []string{".split-novoice", ".split-voice", ".novoice", ".voice"} {
		if strings.HasSuffix(b, s) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// sepResult is one granted wish: the row that asked, and the two files it is
// now.
type sepResult struct{ src, rest, voice string }

// sepApply rewrites a source list for what the separation produced: the row
// points at itself-without-voice and the voice follows as its own row. Pure,
// and the one place the rule lives (run snapshot and page list both go through
// it). The voice inherits the narrator tag; the wish is cleared by granting it.
func sepApply(items []sourceItem, res []sepResult) []sourceItem {
	by := map[string]sepResult{}
	for _, r := range res {
		by[r.src] = r
	}
	out := make([]sourceItem, 0, len(items)+len(res))
	for _, it := range items {
		r, ok := by[it.path]
		if !ok {
			out = append(out, it)
			continue
		}
		out = append(out,
			sourceItem{path: r.rest, footage: it.footage},
			sourceItem{path: r.voice, narrator: it.narrator})
	}
	return out
}

// ---- what the server sends back ---------------------------------------------

// sepStem is one stem of the answer: a whole wav, base64, under the name the
// model gave it.
type sepStem struct {
	ID    string `json:"id"`
	Audio string `json:"audio"`
}

// sepStems reads the stems out of a separation answer. The field is the
// server's own named_audio_outputs, which is how it returns any task with more
// than one sound in the result.
func sepStems(body []byte) ([]sepStem, error) {
	var out struct {
		Stems []sepStem `json:"named_audio_outputs"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(body, &out); err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("unreadable answer: %w", err)
	}
	if len(out.Stems) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no stems in the answer: %.200s", strings.TrimSpace(string(body)))
	}
	return out.Stems, nil
}

// sepPick decides which stem is the voice and which are everything else.
// RoFormers give "vocals" and "instrumental"; HTDemucs gives four instruments,
// where the rest is the other three. Both required: a model that gave neither
// fails here, not at the render.
func sepPick(ids []string) (voice string, rest []string, err error) {
	for _, id := range ids {
		if strings.EqualFold(id, "vocals") || strings.EqualFold(id, "voice") {
			voice = id
			break
		}
	}
	if voice == "" {
		return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("stems %s -- none of them is the voice",
			strings.Join(ids, ", "))
	}
	for _, id := range ids {
		if strings.EqualFold(id, "instrumental") {
			return voice, []string{id}, nil
		}
	}
	for _, id := range ids {
		if id != voice {
			rest = append(rest, id)
		}
	}
	if len(rest) == 0 {
		return "", nil, fmt.Errorf("only %q came back -- the recording without the voice "+
			"is the other half of this, and there is no other half", voice)
	}
	return voice, rest, nil
}

// ---- the run ----------------------------------------------------------------

// separateVoices grants the session's split wishes and hands back the source
// lists as they are once it has. It runs before anything else on ▶: its files
// are what the frames and transcripts come from. The snapshot is rewritten in
// place; the page is told separately.
func (a *App) separateVoices(videos, audios []string) ([]string, []string, error) {
	want := a.sepWanted()
	if len(want) == 0 {
		return videos, audios, nil
	}
	a.qJob(trackSTT, "voice split", 0, 0)
	a.qPush(trackSTT, len(want), "recording")
	a.qDone(trackFrames, 0.5) // one job in this phase, and it is not this half's

	unit := 0.5 / float64(len(want))
	var res []sepResult
	for i, src := range want {
		if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
			return nil, nil, err
		}
		a.qTake(trackSTT)
		r, err := a.separateOne(src, float64(i)*unit, unit)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("splitting the voice off %s: %w", filepath.Base(src), err)
		}
		res = append(res, r)
	}
	a.qDone(trackSTT, 0.5)

	items := sepApply(a.snappedItems(), res)
	vids, auds := a.snapItems(items)
	// the page catches up when it can, and saves: the session is two rows
	// bigger than the project on disk says it is until it does
	glib.IdleAdd(func() {
		if a.srcList == nil {
			return
		}
		a.srcList.items = sepApply(a.srcList.items, res)
		a.srcList.changed()
		a.saveProjectNow()
	})
	return vids, auds, nil
}

// separateOne is one recording. Resumable like every other minute this step
// spends: both halves already on disk is the work already done, and a re-run
// after a stop picks up at the recording it did not reach.
func (a *App) separateOne(src string, base, unit float64) (sepResult, error) {
	dir := a.sepDir()
	rest, voice := sepNames(dir, src)
	name := filepath.Base(src)
	if exists(rest) && exists(voice) {
		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] already split", baseName(src))
		return sepResult{src, rest, voice}, nil
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return sepResult{}, err
	}
	work := filepath.Join(dir, baseName(src)+".work")
	os.RemoveAll(work) // a half-finished attempt is not a resume point
	if err := os.MkdirAll(work, 0o755); err != nil {
		return sepResult{}, err
	}
	// the chunks and stems go when the two halves are written -- but only then.
	// What is worth having after "the server refused c02.wav" is c02.wav.
	done := false
	defer func() {
		if done {
			os.RemoveAll(work)
		}
	}()

	a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.02*unit, "reading %s", name)
	mix := filepath.Join(work, "mix.wav")
	if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", src,
		"-vn", "-ac", sepChannels, "-ar", sepRate, "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", mix); err != nil {
		return sepResult{}, err
	}
	dur, err := ffprobeDur(mix)
	if err != nil {
		return sepResult{}, err
	}
	edges := []float64{0, dur}
	if dur > sepChunkMax {
		edges = append(append([]float64{0},
			asrCuts(dur, a.quietSpots(mix), sepChunkMax, sepCutSeek)...), dur)
	}
	n := len(edges) - 1
	a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] splitting the voice off %.1f s in %d part(s) (%s)",
		baseName(src), dur, n, a.readConf().SepModel)

	var voiceParts, restParts []string
	for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
		if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
			return sepResult{}, err
		}
		a.prog(trackSTT, base+(0.05+0.8*float64(i)/float64(n))*unit,
			"splitting %s %d/%d", name, i+1, n)
		part := mix
		if n > 1 {
			part = filepath.Join(work, fmt.Sprintf("c%02d.wav", i))
			// -ss ahead of -i seeks the input, which on the pcm just written is
			// exact rather than a keyframe away
			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(edges[i]), "-t", fmt.Sprint(edges[i+1]-edges[i]),
				"-i", mix, "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", part); err != nil {
				return sepResult{}, err
			}
		}
		v, r, err := a.sepChunk(part, work, i)
		if err != nil {
			return sepResult{}, err
		}
		voiceParts, restParts = append(voiceParts, v), append(restParts, r)
	}

	a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.9*unit, "writing the two halves of %s", name)
	if err := a.sepJoin(voiceParts, voice); err != nil {
		return sepResult{}, err
	}
	restWav := rest
	if isVideo(src) {
		restWav = filepath.Join(work, "rest.wav")
	}
	if err := a.sepJoin(restParts, restWav); err != nil {
		return sepResult{}, err
	}
	if isVideo(src) {
		// the picture is copied, never re-encoded: this file exists to carry a
		// different soundtrack, and re-compressing the frames to do it would
		// cost the session a generation of quality for nothing
		if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", src, "-i", restWav,
			"-map", "0:v:0", "-map", "1:a:0", "-c:v", "copy", "-c:a", "flac",
			"-shortest", rest); err != nil {
			return sepResult{}, err
		}
	}
	done = true
	a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] split into %s and %s", baseName(src),
		filepath.Base(rest), filepath.Base(voice))
	// and how the sound fell between them, said now: a residual 13 dB under
	// the mix is a recording the model heard as voice from end to end --
	// other players talking in game chat, say -- and the half named for the
	// room then has next to nothing in it. Found by ear a day later, that
	// reads as "the footage is silent", and it is not the footage.
	if m, v, r := sepLoudness(mix), sepLoudness(voice), sepLoudness(restWav); m != "" {
		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] the mix averaged %s: the voice half %s, the rest %s%s",
			baseName(src), m, v, r, sepLopsided(mix, restWav))
	}
	return sepResult{src, rest, voice}, nil
}

// sepLoudness is a file's mean level, as ffmpeg's volumedetect reports it, or
// "" when it cannot be measured -- a line of the log, not a step of the run.
func sepLoudness(path string) string {
	out, err := exec.Command(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "info", "-t", "600", "-i", path, "-vn",
		"-af", "volumedetect", "-f", "null", "-").CombinedOutput()
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}
	for _, l := range strings.Split(string(out), "\n") {
		if i := strings.Index(l, "mean_volume:"); i >= 0 {
			return strings.TrimSpace(l[i+len("mean_volume:"):])
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// sepLopsided is the note for a rest that is sepLopsidedDB or more under the
// mix: what it means, and what to do about it.
func sepLopsided(mix, rest string) string {
	m, r := sepMeanDB(sepLoudness(mix)), sepMeanDB(sepLoudness(rest))
	if m == 0 && r == 0 || m-r < sepLopsidedDB {
		return ""
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf(" -- the rest is %.0f dB under the mix: the model heard this recording as "+
		"voice nearly throughout, so the half named for the room has little in it. Hear the voice "+
		"half where the game is wanted, or cut from the original instead of the split.", m-r)
}

// sepLopsidedDB is how far under the mix the rest has to fall before the log
// says so. 10 dB is a third of the loudness: past it the rest is a residue.
const sepLopsidedDB = 10.0

// sepMeanDB reads volumedetect's "-49.3 dB" back as a number; 0 for "".
func sepMeanDB(s string) float64 {
	var v float64
	fmt.Sscanf(strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(s), " dB"), "%g", &v)
	return v
}

// sepChunk runs one piece through the model and writes its two halves, giving
// back the paths. Everything the model may have called its stems is resolved
// here, so the caller only ever handles a voice file and a rest file.
func (a *App) sepChunk(part, work string, i int) (voice, rest string, err error) {
	up, err := a.serverFile(part)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	body, err := a.audioRun(a.readConf().SepModel, map[string]any{"audio": up})
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	stems, err := sepStems(body)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	wav := map[string][]byte{}
	var ids []string
	for _, s := range stems {
		b, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(s.Audio)
		if err != nil {
			return "", "", fmt.Errorf("stem %q is not audio: %w", s.ID, err)
		}
		wav[s.ID], ids = b, append(ids, s.ID)
	}
	vID, restIDs, err := sepPick(ids)
	if err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	voice = filepath.Join(work, fmt.Sprintf("v%02d.wav", i))
	if err := os.WriteFile(voice, wav[vID], 0o644); err != nil {
		return "", "", err
	}
	rest = filepath.Join(work, fmt.Sprintf("r%02d.wav", i))
	if len(restIDs) == 1 {
		return voice, rest, os.WriteFile(rest, wav[restIDs[0]], 0o644)
	}
	// more than one stem is not the voice, which is the four-instrument
	// models: everything that is not the voice IS the recording without it, so
	// they go back together rather than the caller picking one to keep
	args := []string{"-v", "error", "-y"}
	for j, id := range restIDs {
		p := filepath.Join(work, fmt.Sprintf("r%02d_%d.wav", i, j))
		if err := os.WriteFile(p, wav[id], 0o644); err != nil {
			return "", "", err
		}
		args = append(args, "-i", p)
	}
	// normalize=0: these stems were one recording a moment ago and summing them
	// has to give that recording back, not an eighth of it
	args = append(args, "-filter_complex",
		fmt.Sprintf("amix=inputs=%d:normalize=0", len(restIDs)),
		"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", rest)
	return voice, rest, a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), args...)
}

// sepJoin puts the pieces back in order. One piece is the whole thing and is
// simply moved: a rename is not worth a decode.
func (a *App) sepJoin(parts []string, dst string) error {
	if len(parts) == 1 {
		return os.Rename(parts[0], dst)
	}
	lf := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(parts[0]), "join_"+filepath.Base(dst)+".txt")
	var b strings.Builder
	for _, p := range parts {
		b.WriteString(concatLine(p))
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(lf, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
		"-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", lf, "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", dst)
}

1	package main
2	
3	// Every LLM exchange as a self-contained HTML page under the output folder's
4	// llm/: system prompt, user text, every image as sent (data URLs inline), the
5	// reply with thinking folded away, the error if any. The log gets a short
6	// preview and the clickable path. The page is written when the request goes
7	// out, appended to as a streamed reply arrives, and rewritten whole at the end.
8	
9	import (
10		"context"
11		"fmt"
12		"html"
13		"os"
14		"os/exec"
15		"path/filepath"
16		"strings"
17		"time"
18	
19		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gio/v2"
20		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/glib/v2"
21		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gtk/v4"
22		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/pango"
23	)
24	
25	// llmDir is where the exchanges land. One folder for the whole project, not
26	// one per step: a session's calls read as one conversation with the model,
27	// and the step is right there in each file's name.
28	func (a *App) llmDir() string { return filepath.Join(a.outDir, "llm") }
29	
30	// ---- one page per run --------------------------------------------------------
31	//
32	// A run's calls (cut, captions, effects) share one page: each call appends a
33	// section, the link in the log stays the same all run, and a refresh mid-call
34	// shows the reply arriving under everything before it. Finished sections are
35	// kept in memory; the file is rewritten whole after every call.
36	
37	// beginRun starts a page, named for the step whose first call opened it. Every
38	// step's runner calls qReset at its start, which clears the page so the next
39	// call opens a fresh one -- so a run is exactly the calls between two qResets,
40	// and no step has to name itself twice.
41	func (a *App) beginRun(step string) {
42		if a.outDir == "" {
43			return
44		}
45		a.llmMu.Lock()
46		defer a.llmMu.Unlock()
47		a.runName = fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s.html", time.Now().Format("0102-150405"), step)
48		a.runSecs = nil
49		a.runN = 0
50	}
51	
52	// runPagePath is the file, or "" when no run has begun (a call outside a run,
53	// or a headless one).
54	func (a *App) runPagePath() string {
55		if a.outDir == "" || a.runName == "" {
56			return ""
57		}
58		return filepath.Join(a.llmDir(), a.runName)
59	}
60	
61	// writeRunPage puts the page down as it stands: every finished call, then the
62	// one in flight if there is one. tail is left unclosed for the streaming
63	// reply to be appended to, exactly as the single-call page always did.
64	func (a *App) writeRunPage(tail string, open bool) *os.File {
65		path := a.runPagePath()
66		if path == "" {
67			return nil
68		}
69		if err := os.MkdirAll(a.llmDir(), 0o755); err != nil {
70			a.logfIdle(">>>   could not keep the exchange: %v", err)
71			return nil
72		}
73		var b strings.Builder
74		b.WriteString(runPageHead(a.runName))
75		a.llmMu.Lock()
76		for _, sec := range a.runSecs {
77			b.WriteString(sec)
78		}
79		a.llmMu.Unlock()
80		b.WriteString(tail)
81		if !open {
82			b.WriteString("</body></html>\n")
83			if err := os.WriteFile(path, []byte(b.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
84				a.logfIdle(">>>   could not keep the exchange: %v", err)
85			}
86			return nil
87		}
88		f, err := os.Create(path)
89		if err != nil {
90			a.logfIdle(">>>   could not keep the exchange: %v", err)
91			return nil
92		}
93		if _, err := f.WriteString(b.String()); err != nil {
94			f.Close()
95			return nil
96		}
97		return f
98	}
99	
100	func runPageHead(name string) string {
101		return fmt.Sprintf("<!doctype html>\n<html><head><meta charset=\"utf-8\">"+
102			"<title>%s -- Naivepost run</title>\n<style>%s</style></head><body>\n",
103			html.EscapeString(name), chatCSS)
104	}
105	
106	// chatRec is one exchange being recorded: opened by recordChatStart when the
107	// request goes out, grown by stream while the reply arrives, completed by
108	// done. A nil recorder is valid and inert -- headless callers get one, and
109	// every method on it does nothing.
110	type chatRec struct {
111		a        *App
112		step     string
113		thinking bool
114		msgs     []map[string]any
115		name     string
116		n        int      // which call of the run this is
117		f        *os.File // the page, held open so the reply can be appended live
118		streamed int      // how much of the reply is already on the page
119	}
120	
121	// recordChatStart files the request half of an exchange and puts what was
122	// sent -- sizes and the clickable page -- in the log, before the model has
123	// said a word. It never fails the call it records: observability must not
124	// break the work, so every problem here becomes a log line and nothing more.
125	// Called from llmChatOn on whatever goroutine the step runs on; the log lines
126	// go through the idle queue and the sequence counter is the only shared state.
127	func (a *App) recordChatStart(step string, thinking bool, msgs []map[string]any) *chatRec {
128		if a.outDir == "" {
129			return nil // headless (tests): nowhere agreed to hold the files
130		}
131		if a.runName == "" {
132			a.beginRun(step) // a call outside any run still gets a page of its own
133		}
134		a.llmMu.Lock()
135		a.llmSeq++
136		a.runN++
137		n := a.runN
138		name := a.runName
139		a.llmMu.Unlock()
140		c := &chatRec{a: a, step: step, thinking: thinking, msgs: msgs, name: name, n: n}
141		text, imgs := chatSent(msgs)
142		a.logfIdle(">>> %s: %s of text and %d image(s) went to the LLM", step, sizeOf(text), imgs)
143		// the section is written now and the file held open: everything sent, then
144		// an open assistant block that stream appends the reply into as it
145		// arrives. Any failure here just loses the live page -- done rewrites the
146		// whole file, and the disk may be kinder then.
147		c.f = a.writeRunPage(chatSection(n, step, a.readConf().Model, thinking, msgs, "", "", 0, nil, true), true)
148		if c.f != nil && n == 1 {
149			path := a.runPagePath()
150			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
151				a.logPath(">>>   this run's exchanges, images included: ", filepath.Join("llm", name), path)
152			})
153		}
154		return c
155	}
156	
157	// stream appends what is new of the reply to the page. The streaming callback
158	// hands over everything said so far, not the latest piece, so the page holds
159	// a suffix count and writes only what it has not seen. One failed write ends
160	// the live page quietly -- done still rewrites the whole thing.
161	func (c *chatRec) stream(sofar string) {
162		if c == nil || c.f == nil || len(sofar) <= c.streamed {
163			return
164		}
165		if _, err := c.f.WriteString(html.EscapeString(sofar[c.streamed:])); err != nil {
166			c.f.Close()
167			c.f = nil
168			return
169		}
170		c.streamed = len(sofar)
171	}
172	
173	// splitThink is the reply in its two halves: what the model told itself, tags
174	// and all, and the answer after it. Both spellings of thinking end up marked
175	// the same way by the time anything here sees a reply -- inline from the model,
176	// or wrapped by chatReply.recorded when the server sent it in a field of its
177	// own -- so this is the one place that knows the marker.
178	func splitThink(reply string) (think, answer string) {
179		if i := strings.LastIndex(reply, "</think>"); i >= 0 {
180			return reply[:i+len("</think>")], reply[i+len("</think>"):]
181		}
182		return "", reply
183	}
184	
185	// done completes the record: the page rewritten whole with the reply or the
186	// error, and the verdict in the log. The verdict measures the ANSWER and names
187	// the thinking separately -- "31 kB came back" for four minutes of reasoning
188	// and no words sends the reader hunting a parser bug.
189	func (c *chatRec) done(reply, stop string, took time.Duration, callErr error) {
190		if c == nil {
191			return
192		}
193		if c.f != nil {
194			c.f.Close() // the live page is done growing; the rewrite replaces it
195			c.f = nil
196		}
197		think, answer := splitThink(reply)
198		verdict := fmt.Sprintf("%s came back in %s", sizeOf(len(answer)), durOf(took))
199		if think != "" {
200			verdict += fmt.Sprintf(", after %s of thinking", sizeOf(len(think)))
201		}
202		switch {
203		case callErr != nil:
204		case stop == "length":
205			// the server stopped it, not the model: whichever half it was writing
206			// ends mid-word, and everything downstream would report the answer as
207			// a parse error and the reasoning as a model that gave up
208			verdict += " — cut off at the model's token limit"
209		case strings.TrimSpace(answer) == "":
210			verdict += " — the model answered nothing at all"
211		}
212		if callErr != nil {
213			verdict = fmt.Sprintf("the call failed after %s: %v", durOf(took), callErr)
214		}
215		c.a.logfIdle(">>> %s: %s", c.step, verdict)
216		if p := chatPreview(reply); p != "" {
217			c.a.logfIdle(">>>   the reply begins: %s", p)
218		}
219		sec := chatSection(c.n, c.step, c.a.readConf().Model, c.thinking, c.msgs, reply, stop, took, callErr, false)
220		c.a.llmMu.Lock()
221		c.a.runSecs = append(c.a.runSecs, sec)
222		c.a.llmMu.Unlock()
223		c.a.writeRunPage("", false)
224	}
225	
226	// chatSent measures a request the way the preview reports it: how much text,
227	// how many images. Content is either a plain string or the parts list that
228	// txtPart/imgPart build; an image's bytes are counted as a picture, not text,
229	// because "1.8 MB of text" would be a lie about a request with two frames.
230	func chatSent(msgs []map[string]any) (text, imgs int) {
231		for _, m := range msgs {
232			switch c := m["content"].(type) {
233			case string:
234				text += len(c)
235			case []any:
236				for _, p := range c {
237					part, _ := p.(map[string]any)
238					if s, _ := part["text"].(string); s != "" {
239						text += len(s)
240					}
241					if part["type"] == "image_url" {
242						imgs++
243					}
244				}
245			}
246		}
247		return
248	}
249	
250	// chatPreview is the first words of the answer itself. Everything up to the
251	// last </think> is the model talking to itself, and quoting that would make
252	// every preview open the same way; the whole of it is in the page.
253	func chatPreview(reply string) string {
254		s := reply
255		if i := strings.LastIndex(s, "</think>"); i >= 0 {
256			s = s[i+len("</think>"):]
257		}
258		s = strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), " ")
259		if r := []rune(s); len(r) > 110 {
260			s = string(r[:110]) + "…"
261		}
262		return s
263	}
264	
265	// sizeOf writes a byte count the way a person reads one.
266	func sizeOf(n int) string {
267		if n < 1024 {
268			return fmt.Sprintf("%d B", n)
269		}
270		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f kB", float64(n)/1024)
271	}
272	
273	// durOf keeps a duration readable: seconds once it has any, otherwise as is.
274	func durOf(d time.Duration) string {
275		if d >= time.Second {
276			d = d.Round(time.Second)
277		} else {
278			d = d.Round(time.Millisecond)
279		}
280		return d.String()
281	}
282	
283	const chatCSS = `body{font-family:sans-serif;max-width:60em;margin:2em auto;padding:0 1em;color:#222}
284	pre{white-space:pre-wrap;background:#f6f6f6;border:1px solid #ddd;border-radius:6px;padding:.8em}
285	img{max-width:24em;margin:.3em .3em 0 0;border:1px solid #ccc;border-radius:4px;vertical-align:top}
286	h1{font-size:1.4em}
287	h2{margin-top:1.5em;font-size:.9em;color:#666;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.05em}
288	.meta{color:#666}
289	.err{color:#b00;font-weight:bold}
290	details summary{color:#666;cursor:pointer}
291	`
292	
293	// chatHTML renders the exchange as one page that needs nothing else: the
294	// images ride along as the data URLs they were sent as, and the thinking sits
295	// behind a fold so the answer is what the eye lands on.
296	func chatHTML(step, model string, thinking bool, msgs []map[string]any, reply, stop string, took time.Duration, callErr error, pending bool) []byte {
297		return []byte(runPageHead(step) +
298			chatSection(1, step, model, thinking, msgs, reply, stop, took, callErr, pending))
299	}
300	
301	// chatSection is one call on the run's page: what was sent, then what came
302	// back. The page is the sections in order under one header (writeRunPage), and
303	// a pending section is left unclosed so the streaming reply appends into it.
304	func chatSection(n int, step, model string, thinking bool, msgs []map[string]any, reply, stop string, took time.Duration, callErr error, pending bool) string {
305		esc := html.EscapeString
306		var b strings.Builder
307		mode := "execute"
308		if thinking {
309			mode = "thinking"
310		}
311		status := "took " + durOf(took)
312		if pending {
313			status = "reply pending"
314		}
315		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "<hr><h1>%d. %s</h1>\n<p class=\"meta\">%s · model %s · %s mode · %s</p>\n",
316			n, esc(step), time.Now().Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"), esc(model), mode, status)
317		if callErr != nil {
318			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "<p class=\"err\">the call failed: %s</p>\n", esc(callErr.Error()))
319		}
320		for _, m := range msgs {
321			role, _ := m["role"].(string)
322			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "<h2>%s</h2>\n", esc(role))
323			switch c := m["content"].(type) {
324			case string:
325				b.WriteString("<pre>" + esc(c) + "</pre>\n")
326			case []any:
327				for _, p := range c {
328					part, _ := p.(map[string]any)
329					if s, _ := part["text"].(string); s != "" {
330						b.WriteString("<pre>" + esc(s) + "</pre>\n")
331					}
332					if iu, _ := part["image_url"].(map[string]any); iu != nil {
333						// the data URL is base64 and punctuation: nothing to escape
334						if url, _ := iu["url"].(string); strings.HasPrefix(url, "data:image/") {
335							b.WriteString("<img src=\"" + url + "\">\n")
336						}
337					}
338				}
339			}
340		}
341		b.WriteString("<h2>assistant</h2>\n")
342		if pending {
343			// left open on purpose: this is the live page, and stream appends the
344			// reply right here as it arrives. Browsers render the unclosed tags
345			// fine, and the finished page replaces the whole file anyway.
346			b.WriteString("<pre>")
347			return b.String()
348		}
349		think, answer := splitThink(reply)
350		if think != "" {
351			b.WriteString("<details><summary>thinking</summary><pre>" +
352				esc(think) + "</pre></details>\n")
353		}
354		if strings.TrimSpace(answer) != "" {
355			b.WriteString("<pre>" + esc(answer) + "</pre>\n")
356			if stop == "length" {
357				// the answer above ends mid-word, and nothing in the text says so:
358				// every reader downstream sees a parse error and goes looking for
359				// a fault in an answer the server stopped before it was finished
360				b.WriteString("<p class=\"err\">the reply was cut off at the model's " +
361					"token limit — the answer above is unfinished</p>\n")
362			}
363		} else if callErr == nil {
364			// the page has to say WHICH nothing this is. An empty answer under a
365			// fold full of reasoning is a model that thought and never wrote; an
366			// empty page with nothing behind it is a server that sent nothing.
367			msg := "(empty reply)"
368			switch {
369			case stop == "length":
370				// the budget ran out inside the reasoning: the fold above ends
371				// mid-sentence and there was never going to be an answer after it
372				msg = "(no answer — the reasoning above ran into the model's token limit and stopped there)"
373			case think != "":
374				msg = "(no answer — the model spent the call thinking; the reasoning is folded above)"
375			}
376			b.WriteString("<p class=\"meta\">" + msg + "</p>\n")
377		}
378		return b.String()
379	}
380	
381	// logPath is logf with a tail that opens. The path is drawn like a link and a
382	// click on it launches whatever opens the file -- the browser, for the llm/
383	// pages. display is the short form shown in the log; full is where the file
384	// really is, kept aside because a path pretty enough to read is relative and
385	// a path that opens is not.
386	func (a *App) logPath(prefix, display, full string) {
387		if a.log == nil {
388			a.logf("%s%s", prefix, full) // stderr only: the real path, nothing to click
389			return
390		}
391		if a.linkTag == nil {
392			a.linkTag = gtk.NewTextTag("link")
393			a.linkTag.SetObjectProperty("foreground", "#1a5fb4")
394			a.linkTag.SetObjectProperty("underline", int(pango.UnderlineSingle))
395			a.log.Buffer().TagTable().Add(a.linkTag)
396			a.linkPaths = map[string]string{}
397			click := gtk.NewGestureClick()
398			click.ConnectReleased(func(n int, x, y float64) { a.openLogLink(x, y) })
399			a.log.AddController(click)
400		}
401		a.linkPaths[display] = full
402		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "%s%s\n", prefix, full)
403		buf := a.log.Buffer()
404		buf.Insert(buf.EndIter(), prefix)
405		from := buf.EndIter().Offset()
406		buf.Insert(buf.EndIter(), display)
407		buf.ApplyTag(a.linkTag, buf.IterAtOffset(from), buf.EndIter())
408		buf.Insert(buf.EndIter(), "\n")
409		mark := buf.CreateMark("", buf.EndIter(), false)
410		a.log.ScrollToMark(mark, 0, false, 0, 1)
411		buf.DeleteMark(mark)
412	}
413	
414	// openLogLink resolves a click on the log to the tagged path under it, if any,
415	// and opens it the way openFolder opens folders: the portal first, xdg-open
416	// when the portal will not.
417	func (a *App) openLogLink(x, y float64) {
418		if a.linkTag == nil {
419			return
420		}
421		bx, by := a.log.WindowToBufferCoords(gtk.TextWindowText, int(x), int(y))
422		it, ok := a.log.IterAtLocation(bx, by)
423		if !ok || !it.HasTag(a.linkTag) {
424			return
425		}
426		start := it.Copy()
427		if !start.TogglesTag(a.linkTag) {
428			start.BackwardToTagToggle(a.linkTag)
429		}
430		end := it.Copy()
431		end.ForwardToTagToggle(a.linkTag)
432		full := a.linkPaths[a.log.Buffer().Text(start, end, false)]
433		if full == "" {
434			return
435		}
436		l := gtk.NewFileLauncher(gio.NewFileForPath(full))
437		l.Launch(context.Background(), &a.win.Window, func(res gio.AsyncResulter) {
438			if err := l.LaunchFinish(res); err != nil {
439				a.logf("portal launch failed (%v), trying xdg-open", err)
440				if err := exec.Command("xdg-open", full).Start(); err != nil {
441					a.logf("xdg-open: %v", err)
442				}
443			}
444		})
445	}

package main

// Retakes: the stretches you said, stopped, and said again.
//
// A session recorded off a script is full of them -- a sentence trails off, the
// camera is stopped, the next take starts the sentence again, sometimes a
// sentence or two further back. Both attempts are in the transcript and both
// are in the footage, so unless something says otherwise the finished video
// says everything twice, with the breath between.
//
// The cut pass was the wrong place to ask. It reads the timeline to choose
// MOMENTS -- what is worth keeping -- and it read a doubled sentence as
// content: one run's reasoning says "slight repetition, acceptable" in as many
// words. It is not a judgment about the video at all; it is a fact about what
// was said, true whoever cuts it and true before anyone does.
//
// So it is settled here, at the end of Prepare, and only here. That is the
// earliest point where it can be RIGHT, which is two conditions:
//
//   - the whole session is one stream. An attempt and its replacement are
//     usually in two different recordings -- stop, start again -- and anything
//     working per source (the ASR, the fixer's blocks) sees one half of the
//     pattern it is looking for.
//   - the text is already fixed. Two attempts at one sentence have to LOOK
//     alike to be read as one sentence twice, and raw ASR gives two different
//     manglings of it.
//
// What comes out is a marking, never a deletion: these seconds were abandoned,
// and this is where they were said again. The transcript keeps every word. The
// cut brief folds a marked stretch into one line so the model never chooses it,
// the toolbar can skip it, and a mark you disagree with costs you a glance.

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"unicode"
)

8	// The header bar re-fits itself on width: path and tab words, then file name
9	// and words, then name and icons. The tabs keep their words longest (the most
10	// pressed control); the project label gives up its directories first (the
11	// whole path is one hover away).
12	
13	// tabGap is the space between a tab's icon and its word. Here rather than at
14	// the gtk.NewBox call because fitHeader has to price the word AND the gap that
15	// disappears with it, and two constants that must agree is one too many.
16	const tabGap = 6
17	
18	// headSlack is what the bar spends on what we do not measure: its own padding,
19	// the gaps around the centered title widget, and the window controls the
20	// desktop draws at the right end -- one button under GNOME, up to three
21	// elsewhere, and not ours to ask about. Deliberately generous: guessing high
22	// costs the bar a word it could have shown, guessing low clips one it showed.
23	const headSlack = 90
24	
25	// headFit is what a bar with avail pixels left over can afford, given what the
26	// tab words, the project's file name and its whole path would each take. Split
27	// out from the measuring so the ladder above can be read -- and tested --
28	// without a display attached.
29	func headFit(avail, words, name, path int) (showWords, showPath bool) {
30		switch {
31		case avail >= words+path:
32			return true, true
33		case avail >= words+name:
34			return true, false
35		}
36		return false, false
37	}
38	
39	// textWidth is how wide s would draw in w's font. Asking Pango rather than
40	// measuring the widget: the label we are pricing is ellipsized and capped, so
41	// its own measurement answers "how wide are you allowed to be", which is the
42	// question we are trying to decide.
43	func textWidth(w gtk.Widgetter, s string) int {
44		px, _ := gtk.BaseWidget(w).CreatePangoLayout(s).PixelSize()
45		return px
46	}
47	
48	// fitHeader prices the bar as it stands and applies headFit's answer.
49	func (a *App) fitHeader() {
50		if a.head == nil || a.projLabel == nil || a.tabRow == nil {
51			return // headless (tests), or called while the bar is still being built
52		}
53		avail := a.head.Width()
54		if avail <= 0 {
55			return // not laid out yet; the first resize brings us straight back
56		}
57		for _, b := range a.headBtns {
58			_, nat, _, _ := gtk.BaseWidget(b).Measure(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, -1)
59			avail -= nat
60		}
61		// What the words cost, and what the tab row costs without them. Measuring
62		// the row as it stands and subtracting the words we know are in it prices
63		// both states from either one, and needs no guess at a button's padding.
64		// The gap goes with the word: GTK only spaces visible children.
65		words := 0
66		for i, w := range a.tabWords {
67			words += textWidth(w, steps[i].label) + tabGap
68		}
69		_, tabs, _, _ := a.tabRow.Measure(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, -1)
70		if a.tabWordsOn {
71			tabs -= words
72		}
73		name, path, _ := projLabelText(a.projPath)
74		showWords, showPath := headFit(avail-tabs-headSlack, words,
75			textWidth(a.projLabel, name), textWidth(a.projLabel, path))
76	
77		if showWords != a.tabWordsOn {
78			a.tabWordsOn = showWords
79			for _, w := range a.tabWords {
80				w.SetVisible(showWords)
81			}
82		}
83		if showPath {
84			// measured to fit before it was set, so there is nothing to cap
85			a.projLabel.SetMaxWidthChars(-1)
86			a.projLabel.SetText(path)
87			return
88		}
89		// the cap is the backstop for the rung below the last one: a file name too
90		// long even for a bar showing icons ends in "…" rather than pushing the
91		// tabs off center
92		a.projLabel.SetMaxWidthChars(projNameChars)
93		a.projLabel.SetText(name)
94	}
95	
96	// fitHeaderIdle re-fits once the resize that asked for it has finished.
97	// Straight from the notify handler would mean measuring widgets and changing
98	// their visibility from inside GTK's own allocation pass, which is how a
99	// layout loop starts.
100	func (a *App) fitHeaderIdle() {
101		if a.headFitQ {
102			return // one queued fit answers any number of width changes
103		}
104		a.headFitQ = true
105		glib.IdleAdd(func() {
106			a.headFitQ = false
107			a.fitHeader()
108		})
109	}
110	
111	// watchHeadWidth re-fits the bar whenever the window's width changes.
112	//
113	// The window's own default-width property is not the one to watch: it holds
114	// the size the window would have if it were not maximized, so maximizing --
115	// the one resize that hands the bar a lot of room at once -- would not report.
116	// The surface under the window carries the width actually being drawn, and it
117	// exists only once the window is realized, which is why this waits.
118	func (a *App) watchHeadWidth() {
119		a.win.ConnectRealize(func() {
120			if a.headWatch {
121				return // a window can be realized again; the handler must not stack
122			}
123			n := gtk.BaseWidget(a.win).Native()
124			if n == nil {
125				return
126			}
127			s := n.Surface()
128			if s == nil {
129				return
130			}
131			a.headWatch = true
132			s.NotifyProperty("width", a.fitHeaderIdle)
133		})
134	}

38	// backend allocates one contiguous buffer per request and it grows with the
39	// window, 2.9 GB at 90 s. Measured on this box with an LLM's weights pinned
40	// beside it: 90 s failed to allocate, 45 s answered in 400 ms, 5 s likewise.

102	// ---- run control -----------------------------------------------------------
103	
104	// checkpoint is where pause and stop take effect: between subprocesses, never
105	// inside one -- a GPU job cannot be meaningfully frozen halfway.
106	func (a *App) checkpoint() error {
107		for {
108			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
109				return errStopped
110			}
111			if !a.pauseFlag.Load() {
112				return nil
113			}
114			time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
115		}
116	}
117	
118	// ---- process plumbing ------------------------------------------------------
119	
120	// runCmd runs a subprocess and remembers it, so the stop button can kill it.
121	// A kill while stopFlag is set reports as errStopped, not as a failure.
122	//
123	// The command goes in the log BEFORE it runs, every time. Every subprocess this
124	// app starts is an ffmpeg, and what it is asked to do is the whole of what
125	// comes out: a flag in the wrong place is a video that plays two frames out of
126	// sync in one player and fine in another, and the answer to "what did it
127	// actually run" should not be reading the source. Written as a shell would
128	// take it, so it can be pasted, edited and run by hand.
129	func (a *App) runCmd(name string, args ...string) error {
130		a.logCmd(name, args)
131		cmd := exec.Command(name, args...)
132		var out bytes.Buffer
133		cmd.Stdout = &out
134		cmd.Stderr = &out
135		a.ctlMu.Lock()
136		a.curCmds[cmd] = true
137		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
138		err := cmd.Run()
139		a.ctlMu.Lock()
140		delete(a.curCmds, cmd)
141		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
142		if err != nil {
143			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
144				return errStopped
145			}
146			tail := out.String()
147			if len(tail) > 400 {
148				tail = tail[len(tail)-400:]
149			}
150			// the whole command in the error as well as in the log: an error is
151			// read where it lands -- a status line, a FAILED line at the end of a
152			// run -- and hunting back up the log for the line that goes with it is
153			// the part nobody does
154			return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w\n%s\n%s", name, err, cmdLine(name, args), tail)
155		}
156		return nil
157	}
158	
159	// logCmd puts one command in the log, at the detail indent the steps use for
160	// what they are doing rather than what they decided.
161	func (a *App) logCmd(name string, args []string) {
162		a.logfIdle("    $ %s", cmdLine(name, args))
163	}
164	
165	// cmdLine is a command as a shell would take it: every argument that needs
166	// quoting quoted, and the rest left alone. The paths in this app have spaces in
167	// them ("2026-09-10 15-04-39.mkv"), so a line printed with bare %v is a line
168	// that looks runnable and is not.
169	func cmdLine(name string, args []string) string {
170		out := make([]string, 0, len(args)+1)
171		out = append(out, shellArg(name))
172		for _, a := range args {
173			out = append(out, shellArg(a))
174		}
175		return strings.Join(out, " ")
176	}
177	
178	// shellArg quotes one argument the way sh wants it: single quotes, with any
179	// single quote inside closed, escaped and reopened.
180	func shellArg(s string) string {
181		if s != "" && !strings.ContainsFunc(s, needsQuote) {
182			return s
183		}
184		return "'" + strings.ReplaceAll(s, "'", `'\''`) + "'"
185	}

187	func needsQuote(r rune) bool {
188		switch {
189		case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':
190			return false
191		}
192		return !strings.ContainsRune("_@%+=:,./-", r)
193	}

195	// ffmpegProgress runs ffmpeg reporting completion against a known duration,
196	// for the long single-invocation phases (frame extraction).
197	func (a *App) ffmpegProgress(dur float64, cb func(float64), args ...string) error {
198		full := append([]string{"-progress", "pipe:1", "-nostats"}, args...)
199		a.logCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), full)
200		cmd := exec.Command(ffTool("ffmpeg"), full...)
201		var errBuf bytes.Buffer
202		cmd.Stderr = &errBuf
203		out, err := cmd.StdoutPipe()
204		if err != nil {
205			return err
206		}
207		a.ctlMu.Lock()
208		a.curCmds[cmd] = true
209		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
210		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
211			a.ctlMu.Lock()
212			delete(a.curCmds, cmd)
213			a.ctlMu.Unlock()
214			return err
215		}
216		sc := bufio.NewScanner(out)
217		for sc.Scan() {
218			if v, ok := strings.CutPrefix(sc.Text(), "out_time_us="); ok {
219				var us float64
220				fmt.Sscanf(v, "%f", &us)
221				if dur > 0 {
222					cb(us / 1e6 / dur)
223				}
224			}
225		}
226		err = cmd.Wait()
227		a.ctlMu.Lock()
228		delete(a.curCmds, cmd)
229		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
230		if err != nil {
231			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
232				return errStopped
233			}
234			tail := errBuf.String()
235			if len(tail) > 400 {
236				tail = tail[len(tail)-400:]
237			}
238			return fmt.Errorf("ffmpeg: %w\n%s", err, tail)
239		}
240		return nil
241	}

243	func ffprobeDur(f string) (float64, error) {
244		// the one probe every caller shares (ffprobe.go): asked once per file and
245		// remembered, because the Cut page asks four of these about every
246		// recording in the session and used to start a process for each
247		if v := ffprobeInfo(f).dur; v > 0 {
248			return v, nil
249		}
250		d := ""
251		{
252			// stream-to-disk recorders never finalize the header; decode and count
253			out, err := exec.Command("bash", "-c",
254				fmt.Sprintf(`ffmpeg -v error -progress /dev/stdout -i %q -f null - 2>/dev/null | awk -F= '/^out_time_us/ { t = $2 } END { printf "%%.2f", t / 1e6 }'`, f)).Output()
255			if err != nil {
256				return 0, fmt.Errorf("duration of %s: %w", f, err)
257			}
258			d = strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
259		}
260		var v float64
261		fmt.Sscanf(d, "%f", &v)
262		if v <= 0 {
263			return 0, fmt.Errorf("cannot determine duration of %s", f)
264		}
265		return v, nil
266	}

269	// title is drawn at a fraction of the picture's height, and the picture's
270	// height is the image server's decision, not ours: it is asked for 1280x720
271	// and a model with a fixed latent size may hand back something else.
272	func ffprobeSize(f string) (w, h int, err error) {
273		info := ffprobeInfo(f)
274		if info.w <= 0 || info.h <= 0 {
275			return 0, 0, fmt.Errorf("cannot read the size of %s -- no video stream", f)
276		}

282	func walkObjects(v any, fn func(map[string]any)) {
283		switch t := v.(type) {
284		case map[string]any:
285			fn(t)
286			for _, vv := range t {
287				walkObjects(vv, fn)
288			}
289		case []any:

318		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &v); err != nil {
319			return nil, err

327			ss, okS := m["start_sample"].(float64)
328			es, okE := m["end_sample"].(float64)
329			if ok && okS && okE {
330				out = append(out, span{ss / sampleRate, es / sampleRate, slot})
