377			}
378			fb := 0.0
379			for _, v := range videos {
380				if framesErr = a.checkpoint(); framesErr != nil {
381					return
382				}
383				a.qTake(trackFrames)
384				if framesErr = a.extractFrames(v, interval, scaleName, scaleVF, inDir, fb, funit); framesErr != nil {
385					return
386				}
387				fb += funit
388			}
389			a.qDone(trackFrames, fb)
390		}()
391	
392		var sttErr error
393		base := 0.0
394		for _, in := range inputs {
395			if sttErr = a.checkpoint(); sttErr != nil {
396				break
397			}
398			a.qTake(trackSTT)
399			if sttErr = a.transcribe(in, inDir, base, unit); sttErr != nil {
400				if !errors.Is(sttErr, errStopped) {
401					sttErr = fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", filepath.Base(in), sttErr)
402				}
403				break
404			}
405			base += unit
406		}
407		if sttErr == nil {
408			a.qDone(trackSTT, base)
409		}
410		wg.Wait()
411	
412		// one stop is one stop, not two errors; otherwise report whatever failed
413		if errors.Is(sttErr, errStopped) && errors.Is(framesErr, errStopped) {
414			return errStopped
415		}
416		if err := errors.Join(sttErr, framesErr); err != nil {
417			return err
418		}
419	
420		// primary pair for the single-source consumers (review page, align); the
421		// full ordered lists live in project.json. Either half can be absent now:
422		// a session may be one screen recording that is both, or recordings with no
423		// footage at all. So each is written only if there is one -- and what says
424		// "the sources have been read" is that this file exists, not what is in it.
425		var lines []string
426		if len(videos) > 0 {
427			lines = append(lines, "VIDEO_FILE="+videos[0], "VIDEO_BASE="+baseName(videos[0]))
428		}
429		// the narrator, not the first recording: that tag is who this session speaks
430		// as, and untagged it falls back to exactly the file audios[0] used to be
431		if voice := a.narratorSource(1); voice != "" {
432			lines = append(lines, "AUDIO_FILE="+voice, "AUDIO_BASE="+baseName(voice))
433		}
434		lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("INTERVAL=%g", interval), "SCALE="+scaleName)
435		return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(inDir, "meta.env"),
436			[]byte(strings.Join(lines, "\n")+"\n"), 0o644)
437	}
438	
439	// baseName is what a file is called with the folders and the extension taken
440	// off -- the name a source, a lane, a frame folder and a logo are all known by.
441	func baseName(p string) string {
442		b := filepath.Base(p)
443		return strings.TrimSuffix(b, filepath.Ext(b))
444	}
445	
446	func exists(p string) bool { _, err := os.Stat(p); return err == nil }
447	
448	// ---- one input: 16 kHz -> ASR -> diarization -> segments -------------------
449	
450	func (a *App) transcribe(input, inDir string, base, unit float64) error {
451		name := baseName(input)
452		out := filepath.Join(inDir, name)
453		if err := os.MkdirAll(out, 0o755); err != nil {
454			return err
455		}
456	
457		wav := filepath.Join(out, "voice16k.wav")
458		if !exists(wav) {
459			a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.01*unit, "extracting audio")
460			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", input,
461				"-vn", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", wav); err != nil {
462				return err
463			}
464		}
465		dur, err := ffprobeDur(wav)
466		if err != nil {
467			return err
468		}
469		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] %.1f s of audio", name, dur)
470		if dur < shortTake {
471			// a start/stop, not a take: the same files an empty recording gets,
472			// without asking three servers about %.1f s of nothing
473			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] %.1f s long -- a start/stop, not a take: written up as silence", name, dur)
474			if err := writeSilence(out); err != nil {
475				return err
476			}
477			return a.mergeSegments(out)
478		}
479	
480		if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
481			return err
482		}
483		if !exists(filepath.Join(out, "words.json")) {
484			a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.05*unit, "recognising speech")
485			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] ASR (%s)", name, a.readConf().ASRModel)
486			body, text, pieces, err := a.asrLong(wav, dur, name, base, unit)
487			if err != nil {
488				return fmt.Errorf("ASR: %w", err)
489			}
490			if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" {
491				// a real case, not an error: a screen capture with no mic behind
492				// it. The empty transcript is written and the step carries on
493				a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] no speech found -- an empty transcript", name)
494			}
495			if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.txt"),
496				[]byte(strings.TrimRight(text, "\n")+"\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
497				return err
498			}
499			// which seconds each request covered and what came back for them --
500			// written before words.json, because words.json is the resume marker
501			// and nothing may exist after it that the marker does not stand for
502			if err := saveASRPieces(out, pieces); err != nil {
503				return err
504			}
505			// words.json last, and whole: it is this stage's resume marker, so it
506			// must not exist until the answer it stands for is on disk
507			if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "words.json"), body, 0o644); err != nil {
508				return err
509			}
510		} else {
511			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] ASR already done", name)
512		}
513	
514		// ...and when it was said, which is a different question and a better
515		// answer (align.go). It runs here because the segments below are built
516		// from word times: an ASR that returns none -- the best of the three does
517		// -- has no transcript at all without this.
518		if models := a.alignModels(); len(models) > 0 {
519			if !exists(alignedWords(out)) {
520				a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.9*unit, "timing the words")
521				a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] aligning (%s)", name, a.alignModel())
522			}
523			if err := a.alignInput(out, wav, models); err != nil {
524				// what a failure costs depends on what the ASR gave. With its own
525				// word times, alignment is an improvement and losing it is a
526				// warning: the times stand where they stood before this existed.
527				//
528				// With none -- which is what the best transcriber answers -- it is
529				// the only source of times there is, and the transcript below is
530				// built from times. Failing here with the aligner's own words beats
531				// failing two steps later with a sentence about a missing aligner
532				// that is plainly registered.
533				if len(wordTimes(out)) > 0 {
534					a.logfIdle("!!! [%s] align: %v -- the ASR's own times stand", name, err)
535				} else if strings.TrimSpace(readFileString(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.txt"))) != "" {
536					return fmt.Errorf("align: %w\n\n%s answers with no word times of its own, so the "+
537						"aligner is the only thing that can time them and this recording cannot be "+
538						"transcribed without it", err, a.readConf().ASRModel)
539				}
540			}
541		}
542	
543		if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
544			return err
545		}
546		if !exists(filepath.Join(out, "turns.json")) {
547			// and when it fails, the step fails. There is no "skip it" answer: a
548			// window the machine cannot hold is walked down until one fits
549			// (diarWins), and what is left after that is a server that cannot do
550			// the job -- which a run should say rather than carry on past.
551			if err := a.diarize(out, dur, name, base, unit); err != nil {
552				if errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
553					return err
554				}
555				return fmt.Errorf("diarization: %w", err)
556			}
557		} else {
558			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] diarization already done", name)
559		}
560	
561		a.prog(trackSTT, base+0.98*unit, "building segments")
562		if err := a.mergeSegments(out); err != nil {
563			return fmt.Errorf("merge: %w", err)
564		}
565		return nil
566	}
567	
568	// writeSilence writes what a recording without speech leaves behind: an empty
569	// transcript, a words.json with no words (the stage's resume marker, in the
570	// shape the server answers) and no turns. No ASR pieces file: none is what a
571	// recording transcribed in one request leaves, and the aligner takes that.
572	func writeSilence(out string) error {
573		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.txt"), []byte("\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
574			return err
575		}
576		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "words.json"), []byte("{\"text\":\"\"}\n"), 0o644); err != nil {
577			return err
578		}
579		return os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "turns.json"), []byte("[]\n"), 0o644)
580	}
581	
582	// asrLong is one recording through the ASR in as many requests as its length
583	// needs. A recording that fits goes in whole and words.json stays the server's
584	// own document; a long one is cut into pieces, stitched back into one answer
585	// of the same shape. The cuts slide to the middle of a silence, where a
586	// decoder losing its context costs nothing.
587	func (a *App) asrLong(wav string, dur float64, name string, base, unit float64) ([]byte, string, []asrPiece, error) {
588		limit := a.asrChunk()
589		// Down the same ladder diarization walks, and for the same failure: the
590		// model's own position table says how much audio it will READ, and the
591		// machine says how much of a graph it can find room for. Halving is not
592		// free here -- a chunk edge is a place the decoder loses its context, so
593		// the text at a join is the worst text in the file -- which is why this
594		// starts at what the model allows and shortens only when told to, rather
595		// than being set small to be safe.
596		for {
597			b, text, pieces, err := a.asrLongAt(wav, dur, name, base, unit, limit)
598			if err == nil || !noRoom(err) || limit <= asrChunkMin {
599				return b, text, pieces, err
600			}
601			limit = math.Max(asrChunkMin, math.Floor(limit/2))
602			a.logfIdle("!!! [%s] ASR: no room for that much audio (%v) -- trying %.0f s at a time",
603				name, err, limit)
604		}
605	}
606	
607	func (a *App) asrLongAt(wav string, dur float64, name string, base, unit, limit float64) ([]byte, string, []asrPiece, error) {
608		if dur <= limit {
609			b, text, err := a.asrJSON(wav)
610			if err != nil {
611				return nil, "", nil, err
612			}
613			// one request is one piece, and the aligner wants the same shape
614			// whether the recording was cut up or not
615			return b, text, []asrPiece{{S: 0, E: dur, Text: text}}, nil
616		}
617		seek := math.Min(asrCutSeek, limit/3)
618		edges := append(append([]float64{0}, asrCuts(dur, a.quietSpots(wav), limit, seek)...), dur)
619		n := len(edges) - 1
620		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] too long for one request -- %d ASR chunks", name, n)
621	
622		dir := filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(wav), "asr")
623		os.RemoveAll(dir)
624		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
625			return nil, "", nil, err
626		}
627		// the chunks are scratch and go when the answer is stitched -- but only
628		// then. A failed run keeps them, because the one thing worth having after
629		// "the server could not open c00.wav" is c00.wav.
630		done := false
631		defer func() {
632			if done {
633				os.RemoveAll(dir)
634			}
635		}()
636	
637		var words []any
638		var texts []string
639		var pieces []asrPiece
640		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
641			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
642				return nil, "", nil, err
643			}
644			a.prog(trackSTT, base+(0.05+0.45*float64(i)/float64(n))*unit,
645				"recognising speech %d/%d", i+1, n)
646			part := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("c%02d.wav", i))
647			// -ss ahead of -i seeks the input, which on the pcm this stage wrote
648			// is exact rather than a keyframe away
649			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
650				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(edges[i]), "-t", fmt.Sprint(edges[i+1]-edges[i]),
651				"-i", wav, "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", part); err != nil {
652				return nil, "", nil, err
653			}
654			body, text, err := a.asrJSON(part)
655			if err != nil {
656				return nil, "", nil, err
657			}
658			words = append(words, shiftWords(body, edges[i])...)
659			t := strings.TrimSpace(text)
660			if t != "" {
661				texts = append(texts, t)
662			}
663			// what this request covered and what it heard there, kept together.
664			// Joining the texts and dropping the seconds is what used to leave the
665			// aligner guessing how many words belong in a window (alignInput).
666			pieces = append(pieces, asrPiece{S: edges[i], E: edges[i+1], Text: t})
667		}
668		text := strings.Join(texts, " ")
669		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(map[string]any{"text": text, "words": words}, "", "  ")
670		if err != nil {
671			return nil, "", nil, err
672		}
673		done = true
674		return append(b, '\n'), text, pieces, nil
675	}
676	
677	// asrChunk is how much audio one ASR request may hold, which is not one number
678	// for every model.
679	//
680	// The encoders differ in what they accept, and on a shared GPU in what they can
681	// GET: Qwen3-ASR allocates a classification graph sized by the clip in front of
682	// it -- about 1.5 GB per 20 s, measured here -- so a 96 s take asks for seven
683	// gigabytes in one piece and dies with "failed to allocate Qwen3 ASR thinker
684	// classification graph", on a machine where Nemotron reads the same take whole.
685	// The model that will do the reading decides how much it is handed.
686	func (a *App) asrChunk() float64 {
687		c := a.readConf()
688		if cat, err := audioCatalog(a.audioURL(), c.TTSKey); err == nil {
689			if strings.HasPrefix(cat[c.ASRModel].Family, "qwen3") {
690				return asrChunkQwen
691			}
692		}
693		return asrChunkMax
694	}
695	
696	// asrCuts divides dur into pieces and returns the times between them. Even
697	// pieces, not full ones with a runt. Each cut slides up to seek seconds to the
698	// nearest silence, and the pieces are sized so two cuts sliding apart cannot
699	// push the piece between them past max.
700	func asrCuts(dur float64, quiet []span, max, seek float64) []float64 {
701		if dur <= max || max <= 0 {
702			return nil
703		}
704		if seek < 0 || 2*seek >= max {
705			seek = 0
706		}
707		// the pieces are sized so two cuts sliding apart cannot overflow, which
708		// means a generous seek buys its room out of the piece: 20 s of reach
709		// against a 60 s ceiling was making 19 s pieces, three times the requests
710		// and three times the places the decoder loses its context. A sixth of the
711		// ceiling leaves every piece at least two thirds of what the model allows.
712		if seek > max/6 {
713			seek = max / 6
714		}
715		n := int(math.Ceil(dur / (max - 2*seek)))
716		step := dur / float64(n)
717		if lim := step / 3; seek > lim {
718			seek = lim // cuts stay in order, and each stays inside its own piece
719		}
720		var out []float64
721		for i := 1; i < n; i++ {
722			want, at, best := step*float64(i), step*float64(i), seek
723			for _, q := range quiet {
724				if mid := (q.s + q.e) / 2; math.Abs(mid-want) < best {
725					at, best = mid, math.Abs(mid-want)
726				}
727			}
728			out = append(out, at)
729		}
730		return out
731	}
732	
733	// shiftWords moves one chunk's words to where the chunk was in the recording,
734	// rewriting only the two sample counts so whatever else a word carries rides
735	// along. A word whose times cannot be read travels unshifted -- the merge is
736	// what has to notice an unknown shape.
737	func shiftWords(body []byte, off float64) []any {
738		var v any
739		if json.Unmarshal(body, &v) != nil {
740			return nil
741		}
742		var out []any
743		walkObjects(v, func(m map[string]any) {
744			if _, ok := m["word"].(string); !ok {
745				return
746			}
747			for _, k := range []string{"start_sample", "end_sample"} {
748				if n, ok := m[k].(float64); ok {
749					m[k] = n + off*sampleRate
750				}
751			}
752			out = append(out, m)
753		})
754		return out
755	}
756	
757	// quietSpots asks ffmpeg where the recording goes quiet. Best effort: finding
758	// none, or ffmpeg refusing the file, means the cuts land on the clock, which
759	// is a worse place to cut but never a reason to fail the step.
760	func (a *App) quietSpots(wav string) []span {
761		cmd := exec.Command(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "info", "-nostats", "-i", wav,
762			"-af", fmt.Sprintf("silencedetect=n=%ddB:d=%g", asrQuietDB, asrQuietMin),
763			"-f", "null", "-")
764		var buf bytes.Buffer
765		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &buf, &buf
766		a.ctlMu.Lock()
767		a.curCmds[cmd] = true
768		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
769		err := cmd.Run()
770		a.ctlMu.Lock()
771		delete(a.curCmds, cmd)
772		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
773		if err != nil {
774			return nil
775		}
776		return parseSilence(buf.String())
777	}
778	
779	// parseSilence reads the report silencedetect writes to stderr:
780	//
781	//	[silencedetect @ 0x..] silence_start: 12.345
782	//	[silencedetect @ 0x..] silence_end: 15.678 | silence_duration: 3.333
783	//
784	// A silence still open when the file ends has no end line and is dropped: the
785	// end of the recording is not a place anything needs to be cut.
786	func parseSilence(report string) []span {
787		var out []span
788		from, open := 0.0, false
789		for _, ln := range strings.Split(report, "\n") {
790			if i := strings.Index(ln, "silence_start:"); i >= 0 {
791				v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(ln[i+len("silence_start:"):]), 64)
792				from, open = v, err == nil
793				continue
794			}
795			i := strings.Index(ln, "silence_end:")
796			if i < 0 || !open {
797				continue
798			}
799			f := strings.TrimSpace(ln[i+len("silence_end:"):])
800			if j := strings.Index(f, "|"); j >= 0 {
801				f = strings.TrimSpace(f[:j])
802			}
803			if v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(f, 64); err == nil && v > from {
804				out = append(out, span{s: from, e: v})
805			}
806			open = false
807		}
808		return out
809	}
810	
811	// concatLine is one row of an ffmpeg concat list. The quoting is the reason it
812	// is a function: the demuxer reads 'file' arguments as single-quoted, so a path
813	// with an apostrophe in it -- a project called "tom's cut", which names the
814	// whole data folder -- ends the quote early and the rest of the list is read as
815	// something else. ffmpeg spells an escaped quote the shell way: close, a
816	// backslashed quote, open again.
817	func concatLine(path string) string {
818		return "file '" + strings.ReplaceAll(path, "'", `'\''`) + "'\n"
819	}
820	
821	func (a *App) diarize(out string, dur float64, name string, base, unit float64) error {
822		var err error
823		for i, win := range diarWins {
824			if err = a.diarizeAt(out, dur, name, base, unit, win); err == nil || !noRoom(err) {
825				return err
826			}
827			// the server has the model and refused the buffer, not the audio: the
828			// next window down is the same pass over more, smaller requests
829			if i+1 < len(diarWins) {
830				a.logfIdle("!!! [%s] diarization: no room for a %.0f s window (%v) -- trying %.0f s",
831					name, win, err, diarWins[i+1])
832			}
833		}
834		return err
835	}
836	
837	// anchorPiece is one stretch of one voice cut into the anchor.
838	type anchorPiece struct {
839		src, len float64
840		slot     string
841	}
842	
843	// anchorPieces takes up to per seconds of each voice from rows, which are in
844	// slot order and then time order, skipping any stretch under anchorCut.
845	func anchorPieces(rows []span, per float64) []anchorPiece {
846		var pieces []anchorPiece
847		acc := map[string]float64{}
848		for _, r := range rows {
849			if acc[r.slot] >= per {
850				continue
851			}
852			d := r.e - r.s
853			if d > per-acc[r.slot] {
854				d = per - acc[r.slot]
855			}
856			if d < anchorCut {
857				continue
858			}
859			acc[r.slot] += d
860			pieces = append(pieces, anchorPiece{r.s, d, r.slot})
861		}
862		return pieces
863	}
864	
865	// noRoom is whether the server refused for want of memory rather than for
866	// anything about the request. Its own words, because the failure arrives as a
867	// 500 with a message and nothing else to go on. Both the passes that hand it a
868	// stretch of audio ask this: what they choose is how much, and that is the
869	// only thing either can do about the answer.
870	func noRoom(err error) bool {
871		if err == nil {
872			return false
873		}
874		s := strings.ToLower(err.Error())
875		return strings.Contains(s, "failed to allocate") || strings.Contains(s, "out of memory") ||
876			strings.Contains(s, "alloc_tensor_range") || strings.Contains(s, "cudamalloc")
877	}
878	
879	// diarizeAt is the pass at one window length.
880	func (a *App) diarizeAt(out string, dur float64, name string, base, unit, win float64) error {
881		// the anchor is a share of the window, not a fixed dozen seconds: four
882		// voices at 12 s each is 48 s of anchor, which leaves a 45 s window no
883		// room for any new audio at all. A quarter of the window per voice keeps
884		// the same shape at every rung of the ladder.
885		per := math.Min(anchorPer, win/4)
886		dir := filepath.Join(out, "diar")
887		os.RemoveAll(dir)
888		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
889			return err
890		}
891		defer os.RemoveAll(dir)
892		turnsPath := filepath.Join(out, "turns.json")
893	
894		// -- pass 1: where are the voices? --------------------------------------
895		scanHop := math.Max(10, math.Floor(win*diarHopShare))
896		nwin := int(math.Ceil(dur / scanHop))
897		scan := map[int][]span{}
898		for i := 0; i < nwin; i++ {
899			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
900				return err
901			}
902			a.prog(trackSTT, base+(0.55+0.20*float64(i)/float64(nwin))*unit,
903				"finding voices %d/%d", i+1, nwin)
904			start := float64(i) * scanHop
905			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
906				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(start), "-t", fmt.Sprint(win),
907				"-i", filepath.Join(out, "voice16k.wav"),
908				"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", filepath.Join(dir, "s.wav")); err != nil {
909				return err
910			}
911			spans, err := a.diarSpans(filepath.Join(dir, "s.wav"))
912			if err != nil {
913				return err
914			}
915			for _, sp := range spans {
916				scan[i] = append(scan[i], span{sp.s + start, sp.e + start, sp.slot})
917			}
918		}
919		if len(scan) == 0 {
920			return os.WriteFile(turnsPath, []byte("[]\n"), 0o644)
921		}
922	
923		// -- pick the anchor window ---------------------------------------------
924		// Most distinct voices; on a tie, the window whose QUIETEST voice is best
925		// represented -- ranking by total speech picks whoever talks most and
926		// leaves the other voice too thin to anchor.
927		best, bestN, bestLo := -1, 0, 0.0
928		for w, spans := range scan {
929			durBy := map[string]float64{}
930			for _, sp := range spans {
931				durBy[sp.slot] += sp.e - sp.s
932			}
933			n, lo := 0, math.MaxFloat64
934			for _, d := range durBy {
935				if d >= anchorMin {
936					n++
937					if d < lo {
938						lo = d
939					}
940				}
941			}
942			if n > bestN || (n == bestN && n > 0 && lo > bestLo) {
943				best, bestN, bestLo = w, n, lo
944			}
945		}
946		if best < 0 {
947			for w := range scan {
948				if best < 0 || w < best {
949					best = w
950				}
951			}
952		}
953	
954		// -- build the anchor: up to anchorPer seconds of each voice ------------
955		rows := append([]span(nil), scan[best]...)
956		sort.Slice(rows, func(i, j int) bool {
957			if rows[i].slot != rows[j].slot {
958				return rows[i].slot < rows[j].slot
959			}
960			return rows[i].s < rows[j].s
961		})
962		pieces := anchorPieces(rows, per)
963		if len(pieces) == 0 {
964			// voices were heard but none for long enough to anchor -- a snippet
965			// under a second. Nothing to tell apart: no turns, same as no voices,
966			// and not an empty concat list for ffmpeg to refuse.
967			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] diarization: no voice long enough to anchor -- no turns", name)
968			return os.WriteFile(turnsPath, []byte("[]\n"), 0o644)
969		}
970		var list strings.Builder
971		for i, p := range pieces {
972			f := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf("a%02d.wav", i))
973			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
974				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(p.src), "-t", fmt.Sprint(p.len),
975				"-i", filepath.Join(out, "voice16k.wav"),
976				"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", f); err != nil {
977				return err
978			}
979			list.WriteString(concatLine(f))
980		}
981		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "anchor.list"), []byte(list.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
982			return err
983		}
984		if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0",
985			"-i", filepath.Join(dir, "anchor.list"),
986			"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", filepath.Join(dir, "anchor.wav")); err != nil {
987			return err
988		}
989		// block b of the anchor is voice b: [bs, be) in anchor-local seconds
990		type block struct{ s, e float64 }
991		var blocks []block
992		t := 0.0
993		for i, p := range pieces {
994			if i == 0 || p.slot != pieces[i-1].slot {
995				blocks = append(blocks, block{t, t})
996			}
997			t += p.len
998			blocks[len(blocks)-1].e = t
999		}
1000		alen := t
1001		hop := math.Floor(win - alen - 1)
1002		if hop < 15 {
1003			return fmt.Errorf("anchor too long (%.1f s of %.0f s window)", alen, win)
1004		}
1005		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] anchor: %d voice(s) in %.1f s of a %.0f s window -- %.0f s of new audio each",
1006			name, len(blocks), alen, win, hop)
1007	
1008		// -- pass 2: every window carries the anchor ----------------------------
1009		nwin = int(math.Ceil(dur / hop))
1010		all := map[int][]span{}
1011		for i := 0; i < nwin; i++ {
1012			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
1013				return err
1014			}
1015			a.prog(trackSTT, base+(0.75+0.22*float64(i)/float64(nwin))*unit,
1016				"placing speakers %d/%d", i+1, nwin)
1017			start := float64(i) * hop
1018			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
1019				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(start), "-t", fmt.Sprint(hop),
1020				"-i", filepath.Join(out, "voice16k.wav"),
1021				"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", filepath.Join(dir, "seg.wav")); err != nil {
1022				return err
1023			}
1024			cc := concatLine(filepath.Join(dir, "anchor.wav")) +
1025				concatLine(filepath.Join(dir, "seg.wav"))
1026			if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "cc.list"), []byte(cc), 0o644); err != nil {
1027				return err
1028			}
1029			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0",
1030				"-i", filepath.Join(dir, "cc.list"),
1031				"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", filepath.Join(dir, "win.wav")); err != nil {
1032				return err
1033			}
1034			spans, err := a.diarSpans(filepath.Join(dir, "win.wav"))
1035			if err != nil {
1036				return err
1037			}
1038			all[i] = spans
1039		}
1040	
1041		// -- resolve slots against the anchor, one-to-one per window ------------
1042		// Strongest claim first, each block claimed once: independent argmax per
1043		// slot would let two slots claim the same voice. A slot silent throughout
1044		// the anchor is a voice the anchor does not carry -- it gets its own id
1045		// rather than a guess, and surfaces as an extra speaker.
1046		type gspan struct {
1047			s, e float64
1048			g    int
1049		}
1050		var glob []gspan
1051		nunk := 0
1052		for w := 0; w < nwin; w++ {
1053			spans := all[w]
1054			if len(spans) == 0 {
1055				continue
1056			}
1057			var slots []string
1058			ov := map[string][]float64{}
1059			for _, sp := range spans {
1060				if _, seen := ov[sp.slot]; !seen {
1061					ov[sp.slot] = make([]float64, len(blocks))
1062					slots = append(slots, sp.slot)
1063				}
1064				for b, bl := range blocks {
1065					o := math.Min(sp.e, bl.e) - math.Max(sp.s, bl.s)
1066					if o > 0 {
1067						ov[sp.slot][b] += o
1068					}
1069				}
1070			}
1071			gid := map[string]int{}
1072			tookSlot := map[string]bool{}
1073			tookBlock := make([]bool, len(blocks))
1074			for {
1075				bo, bs, bb := minAnchorOv, "", -1
1076				for _, sl := range slots {
1077					if tookSlot[sl] {
1078						continue
1079					}
1080					for b := range blocks {
1081						if !tookBlock[b] {
1082							if ov[sl][b] > bo {
1083								bo, bs, bb = ov[sl][b], sl, b
1084							}
1085						}
1086					}
1087				}
1088				if bb < 0 {
1089					break
1090				}
1091				gid[bs] = bb
1092				tookSlot[bs] = true
1093				tookBlock[bb] = true
1094			}
1095			for _, sl := range slots {
1096				if !tookSlot[sl] {
1097					gid[sl] = len(blocks) + nunk
1098					nunk++
1099				}
1100			}
1101			for _, sp := range spans {
1102				if sp.s < alen { // the anchor itself, not content
1103					continue
1104				}
1105				glob = append(glob, gspan{
1106					float64(w)*hop + sp.s - alen,
1107					float64(w)*hop + sp.e - alen,
1108					gid[sp.slot]})
1109			}
1110		}
1111		sort.Slice(glob, func(i, j int) bool { return glob[i].s < glob[j].s })
1112	
1113		// glue same-speaker runs: sortformer reports frame-level bursts
1114		var outSpans []gspan
1115		for _, g := range glob {
1116			n := len(outSpans)
1117			if n > 0 && outSpans[n-1].g == g.g && g.s-outSpans[n-1].e <= diarTurnGap {
1118				if g.e > outSpans[n-1].e {
1119					outSpans[n-1].e = g.e
1120				}
1121				continue
1122			}
1123			outSpans = append(outSpans, g)
1124		}
1125		var sb strings.Builder
1126		sb.WriteString("[")
1127		for i, g := range outSpans {
1128			if i > 0 {
1129				sb.WriteString(",")
1130			}
1131			fmt.Fprintf(&sb, `{"start_sample":%d,"end_sample":%d,"speaker_id":"SPEAKER_%02d"}`,
1132				int64(g.s*sampleRate), int64(g.e*sampleRate), g.g)
1133		}
1134		sb.WriteString("]\n")
1135		unident := ""
1136		if nunk > 0 {
1137			unident = fmt.Sprintf(" (%d slot(s) the anchor could not identify)", nunk)
1138		}
1139		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] %d speaker(s), %d turns%s", name, len(blocks)+nunk, len(outSpans), unident)
1140		return os.WriteFile(turnsPath, []byte(sb.String()), 0o644)
1141	}
1142	
1143	// ---- words + turns -> speaker-tagged segments ------------------------------
1144	
1145	func (a *App) mergeSegments(out string) error {
1146		type word struct {
1147			s, e float64
1148			w    string
1149		}
1150		var words []word
1151		seen := 0
1152		for _, w := range wordTimes(out) {
1153			seen++
1154			if w.End > w.Start {
1155				words = append(words, word{float64(w.Start) / sampleRate, float64(w.End) / sampleRate, w.Word})
1156			}
1157		}
1158		// no words at all is silence, which becomes an empty transcript below; words
1159		// whose times cannot be read is an answer changing shape, which has to stop
1160		// here rather than quietly emptying every transcript after it
1161		if len(words) == 0 && seen > 0 {
1162			return fmt.Errorf("%d words carry no usable start_sample/end_sample -- the answer changed shape", seen)
1163		}
1164		// ...and no words where there IS speech is the case this used to make
1165		// impossible: an ASR that answers with text alone (Qwen3-ASR) and no
1166		// aligner registered to time it. Said plainly, because every transcript
1167		// after it would otherwise come out empty for no visible reason.
1168		if len(words) == 0 {
1169			if b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.txt")); err == nil && strings.TrimSpace(string(b)) != "" {
1170				how := "no aligner is registered to time them -- register one (task \"align\")"
1171				if len(a.alignModels()) > 0 {
1172					how = "and the aligner left no times either, which the line above this one says why"
1173				}
1174				return fmt.Errorf("%s transcribed this recording but timed no words, %s -- or use an "+
1175					"ASR that answers with word timings", a.readConf().ASRModel, how)
1176			}
1177		}
1178	
1179		turns, _ := loadSpans(filepath.Join(out, "turns.json"))
1180		// glue same-speaker turns (idempotent over what diarize wrote)
1181		var ts []span
1182		for _, t := range turns {
1183			n := len(ts)
1184			if n > 0 && ts[n-1].slot == t.slot && t.s-ts[n-1].e <= diarTurnGap {
1185				if t.e > ts[n-1].e {
1186					ts[n-1].e = t.e
1187				}
1188				continue
1189			}
1190			ts = append(ts, t)
1191		}
1192	
1193		// speaker whose turn shares the most time with the word; else the nearest
1194		// turn within mergeNear -- diarization edges are not exact
1195		who := func(ws, we float64) string {
1196			best, bi := 0.0, -1
1197			for i, t := range ts {
1198				o := math.Min(we, t.e) - math.Max(ws, t.s)
1199				if o > best {
1200					best, bi = o, i
1201				}
1202			}
1203			if bi >= 0 {
1204				return ts[bi].slot
1205			}
1206			bd := mergeNear
1207			for i, t := range ts {
1208				d := 0.0
1209				if t.s > we {
1210					d = t.s - we
1211				} else if t.e < ws {
1212					d = ws - t.e
1213				}
1214				if d < bd {
1215					bd, bi = d, i
1216				}
1217			}
1218			if bi >= 0 {
1219				return ts[bi].slot
1220			}
1221			// no turns at all is a recording diarization found no voices in -- it
1222			// writes "[]" for one -- whose ASR nevertheless heard words. One
1223			// voice, named as a diarized session would name it. "?" is for a word
1224			// BETWEEN turns, which the loop below hands to the running speaker;
1225			// with no turns there is none to run, and "?" would reach the timeline
1226			// as a speaker's name.
1227			if len(ts) == 0 {
1228				return "SPEAKER_00"
1229			}
1230			return "?"
1231		}
1232	
1233		type seg struct {
1234			s, e float64
1235			spk  string
1236			text string
1237		}
1238		var segs []seg
1239		var cur *seg
1240		prev := 0.0
1241		for _, w := range words {
1242			ws := w.s
1243			we := math.Min(w.e, ws+mergeMaxWord) // see mergeMaxWord
1244			spk := who(ws, we)
1245			if spk == "?" && cur != nil {
1246				spk = cur.spk // unknown keeps the running speaker
1247			}
1248			if cur != nil && (spk != cur.spk || ws-prev > mergeGap || we-cur.s > mergeMaxLen) {
1249				segs = append(segs, *cur)
1250				cur = nil
1251			}
1252			if cur == nil {
1253				cur = &seg{s: ws, spk: spk, text: w.w}
1254			} else {
1255				if cur.spk == "?" && spk != "?" {
1256					cur.spk = spk // upgrade once identified
1257				}
1258				cur.text += " " + w.w
1259			}
1260			cur.e = we
1261			prev = we
1262		}
1263		if cur != nil {
1264			segs = append(segs, *cur)
1265		}
1266	
1267		srt := func(t float64) string {
1268			if t < 0 {
1269				t = 0
1270			}
1271			h := int(t) / 3600
1272			m := (int(t) % 3600) / 60
1273			s := int(t) % 60
1274			ms := int((t-math.Floor(t))*1000 + 0.5)
1275			return fmt.Sprintf("%02d:%02d:%02d,%03d", h, m, s, ms)
1276		}
1277		var tsv, srtb strings.Builder
1278		for i, g := range segs {
1279			fmt.Fprintf(&tsv, "%.2f\t%.2f\t%s\t%s\n", g.s, g.e, g.spk, g.text)
1280			tag := ""
1281			if g.spk != "?" {
1282				tag = "[" + g.spk + "] "
1283			}
1284			fmt.Fprintf(&srtb, "%d\n%s --> %s\n%s%s\n\n", i+1, srt(g.s), srt(g.e), tag, g.text)
1285		}
1286		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.tsv"), []byte(tsv.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
1287			return err
1288		}
1289		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(out, "transcript.srt"), []byte(srtb.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
1290			return err
1291		}
1292		a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] %d segments", filepath.Base(out), len(segs))
1293		return nil
1294	}
1295	
1296	// ---- frames ----------------------------------------------------------------
1297	
1298	// extractFrames dumps one video's frames into inputs/frames/<basename>/.
1299	// A marker file records interval + size, so re-runs skip until either changes.
1300	// frameChunk is one worker's share of a frame extraction: frames first..
1301	// first+n-1, from start for dur seconds.
1302	type frameChunk struct {
1303		start, dur float64
1304		first, n   int
1305	}
1306	
1307	// frameChunks splits total frames at one every interval over workers, in
1308	// chunks whose lengths are whole intervals so frame n is always t=(n-1)*interval.
1309	// The tail is never a single frame: the count is a rounding of the file's
1310	// length, and a lone last frame that turns out not to exist would leave that
1311	// worker with nothing written, which ffmpeg reports as an error. Folded into
1312	// the chunk before it, the same missing frame costs nothing -- ffmpeg stops at
1313	// the end of the file one frame short of its cap, and says nothing.
1314	func frameChunks(total, workers int, interval float64) []frameChunk {
1315		per := (total + workers - 1) / workers
1316		var chunks []frameChunk
1317		for k := 0; k < workers; k++ {
1318			n := min(per, total-k*per)
1319			if n <= 0 {
1320				break
1321			}
1322			chunks = append(chunks, frameChunk{float64(k*per) * interval, float64(n) * interval, k*per + 1, n})
1323		}
1324		if l := len(chunks); l >= 2 && chunks[l-1].n == 1 {
1325			chunks[l-2].n++
1326			chunks[l-2].dur += interval
1327			chunks = chunks[:l-1]
1328		}
1329		return chunks
1330	}
1331	
1332	// frameFilter is the filter graph for a take of dur seconds sampled every
1333	// interval: the graph as built, or -- for a take shorter than one interval,
1334	// where fps would emit nothing -- the scale alone and the word to stop after
1335	// the first frame. With interval 0 every frame is wanted and nothing changes.
1336	func frameFilter(vf, scaleVF string, dur, interval float64) (string, bool) {
1337		if interval > 0 && dur < interval {
1338			return scaleVF, true
1339		}
1340		return vf, false
1341	}
1342	
1343	func (a *App) extractFrames(video string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF, inDir string, base, unit float64) error {
1344		name := baseName(video)
1345		fdir := filepath.Join(inDir, "frames", name)
1346		marker := filepath.Join(fdir, ".interval")
1347		want := fmt.Sprintf("%g|%s", interval, scaleName)
1348		if b, err := os.ReadFile(marker); err == nil && strings.TrimSpace(string(b)) == want {
1349			// the pixels are already right; only a folder extracted before frames
1350			// were named for their second has anything left to do, and that is a
1351			// rename rather than the minutes of decoding a re-extract would cost
1352			if n, err := stampFrames(fdir, video, a.sourceStart(video), interval); err != nil {
1353				return err
1354			} else if n > 0 {
1355				a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] %d frames renamed to the second they were shot in", name, n)
1356			}
1357			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] frames already extracted (%gs, %s), skipping", name, interval, scaleName)
1358			a.prog(trackFrames, base+unit, "already extracted")
1359			return nil
1360		}
1361		if interval == 0 {
1362			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] extracting EVERY frame -- gigabytes", name)
1363		} else {
1364			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] extracting a frame every %gs at %s", name, interval, scaleName)
1365		}
1366		os.RemoveAll(fdir)
1367		if err := os.MkdirAll(fdir, 0o755); err != nil {
1368			return err
1369		}
1370		var filters []string
1371		if interval > 0 {
1372			filters = append(filters, fmt.Sprintf("fps=%f", 1/interval))
1373		}
1374		if scaleVF != "" {
1375			filters = append(filters, scaleVF)
1376		}
1377		vf := strings.Join(filters, ",")
1378		pattern := filepath.Join(fdir, "f%06d.jpg")
1379		dur, err := ffprobeDur(video)
1380		if err != nil {
1381			return err
1382		}
1383		// shorter than one interval, the fps filter emits nothing and ffmpeg
1384		// fails for having written no file; the first frame is the whole take
1385		vf, oneFrame := frameFilter(vf, scaleVF, dur, interval)
1386	
1387		// Extraction is decode-bound: to keep one frame per second the decoder
1388		// still chews through every source frame. Splitting the timeline into
1389		// chunks and running one ffmpeg per chunk spreads that over the cores;
1390		// chunk lengths are multiples of the interval so the global mapping
1391		// frame n <-> t=(n-1)*interval stays exact across chunk borders.
1392		workers := runtime.NumCPU() / 4
1393		workers = max(2, min(8, workers))
1394		totalFrames := 0
1395		if interval > 0 {
1396			// what the fps filter emits over the whole file: the slot count rounded,
1397			// not rounded up -- measured, and a 49.25 s file at 1 s is 49 frames. A
1398			// count one too high sends the last worker after a frame that is not
1399			// there, and a chunk that yields nothing is an ffmpeg error.
1400			totalFrames = int(math.Round(dur / interval))
1401			if totalFrames < workers*4 {
1402				workers = 1
1403			}
1404		} else {
1405			workers = 1 // every-frame mode: frame count per chunk is not knowable
1406		}
1407	
1408		if workers == 1 {
1409			args := []string{"-v", "error", "-y", "-i", video}
1410			if vf != "" { // "-vf" with an empty graph is an ffmpeg error
1411				args = append(args, "-vf", vf)
1412			}
1413			if oneFrame {
1414				args = append(args, "-frames:v", "1")
1415			}
1416			args = append(args, "-q:v", "4", "-start_number", "1", pattern)
1417			if err := a.ffmpegProgress(dur, func(f float64) {
1418				a.prog(trackFrames, base+f*unit, "extracting %.0f%%", f*100)
1419			}, args...); err != nil {
1420				return err
1421			}
1422		} else {
1423			chunks := frameChunks(totalFrames, workers, interval)
1424			var mu sync.Mutex

1426			report := func() {

1428				sum := 0.0
1429				for _, f := range fracs {
1430					sum += f

1437			for k, c := range chunks {

1442					errs[k] = a.ffmpegProgress(c.dur, func(f float64) {

1445						mu.Unlock()
1446						report()
1447					}, "-v", "error", "-y",

1459					stopped = true
1460				} else if e != nil {
1461					return e
1462				}
1463			}

1479	// stampFrames renames ffmpeg's numbering into the wall-clock second each frame
1480	// was shot in (several in one second get -1, -2). The name comes from the
1481	// frame NUMBER, never the sorted position, so t = (n-1) * interval survives a
1482	// gap. start is the session's placement of this video, passed in by the caller
1483	// who holds the whole source list. Nothing numbered left means nothing to do,
1484	// which is also what renames a folder extracted before stamping existed.
1485	func stampFrames(fdir, video string, start, interval float64) (int, error) {
1486		ents, err := os.ReadDir(fdir)
1487		if err != nil {
1488			return 0, err
1489		}
1490		type frame struct {
1491			n    int
1492			name string
1493		}
1494		var fs []frame
1495		for _, e := range ents {
1496			n, ok := frameNum(e.Name())
1497			if e.IsDir() || !ok {
1498				continue
1499			}
1500			fs = append(fs, frame{n, e.Name()})
1501		}
1502		if len(fs) == 0 {
1503			return 0, nil
1504		}
1505		if interval <= 0 {
1506			// every-frame mode: the spacing is the video's own. Without a frame rate
1507			// there is no time to name a frame after, so it keeps its number.
1508			fps := ffprobeFPS(video)
1509			if fps <= 0 {
1510				return 0, nil
1511			}
1512			interval = 1 / fps
1513		}
1514		sort.Slice(fs, func(i, j int) bool { return fs[i].n < fs[j].n })
1515		var seq stampSeq
1516		for _, f := range fs {
1517			to := seq.name(start+float64(f.n-1)*interval, ".jpg")
1518			if err := os.Rename(filepath.Join(fdir, f.name), filepath.Join(fdir, to)); err != nil {
1519				return 0, err
1520			}
1521		}
1522		return len(fs), nil
1523	}
1524	
1525	// frameNum reads ffmpeg's f000001.jpg back. Frames are renamed the moment they
1526	// are extracted, so this only ever sees a folder mid-extraction -- or one made
1527	// before the frames carried their timestamp.
1528	func frameNum(name string) (int, bool) {
1529		if !strings.HasPrefix(name, "f") || !strings.HasSuffix(name, ".jpg") {
1530			return 0, false
1531		}
1532		n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSuffix(name[1:], ".jpg"))
1533		return n, err == nil && n >= 1
1534	}

3	// What ffprobe knows about a file, asked once.
4	//
5	// Every probe here used to be its own ffprobe process, and the page that opens
6	// the Cut step asks four things about every recording: how long it runs, how
7	// big its picture is, how fast it plays, how many tracks it has. A session of
8	// thirty-one takes is a hundred processes started one after another on the GUI
9	// thread, and the thread that starts them is the thread that draws -- so the
10	// window stops answering and the hang watch writes a stack (main.go,
11	// startHangWatch). Measured: 45 ms a probe, 93 probes, four and a bit seconds
12	// against a three-second watchdog.
13	//
14	// So: one call per file, answering everything, and the answer kept under the
15	// file's identity -- its path, size and modification time (fileMark). A
16	// recording still being written to disk changes size and is asked again; one
17	// that has not moved is never asked twice, and walking back to the Cut tab
18	// costs nothing at all.
19	
20	import (
21		"encoding/json"
22		"fmt"
23		"os/exec"
24		"strconv"
25		"strings"
26		"sync"
27	)
28	
29	// probeInfo is one file as ffprobe describes it. Zero values are "not known":
30	// a file with no video stream has no size and no frame rate, which is a real
31	// answer about a microphone recording rather than a failure.
32	type probeInfo struct {
33		dur    float64
34		w, h   int
35		fps    float64
36		tracks []audTrack
37		// whether ffprobe answered at all. Not the same as an empty answer: a
38		// silent capture HAS no audio stream and its no tracks is the truth,
39		// where a file ffprobe could not open says nothing about anything and
40		// the callers fall back to what they always did.
41		ok bool
42	}
43	
44	var (
45		probeMu    sync.Mutex
46		probeCache = map[string]probeInfo{}
47	)
48	
49	// ffprobeInfo is everything about one file, from one process, remembered.
50	func ffprobeInfo(path string) probeInfo {
51		key := path + " " + fileMark(path)
52		probeMu.Lock()
53		got, ok := probeCache[key]
54		probeMu.Unlock()
55		if ok {
56			return got
57		}
58		info := probeFile(path)
59		probeMu.Lock()
60		probeCache[key] = info
61		probeMu.Unlock()
62		return info
63	}
64	
65	// probeFile is the process itself. JSON rather than csv: this asks about the
66	// format and about every stream at once, and the shape of a csv answer depends
67	// on which of them a file happens to have.
68	func probeFile(path string) probeInfo {
69		out, err := exec.Command(ffTool("ffprobe"), "-v", "error",
70			"-show_entries", "format=duration:stream=codec_type,width,height,avg_frame_rate,channels:stream_tags=title",
71			"-of", "json", path).Output()
72		if err != nil {
73			return probeInfo{}
74		}
75		var got struct {
76			Format struct {
77				Duration string `json:"duration"`
78			} `json:"format"`
79			Streams []struct {
80				CodecType string `json:"codec_type"`
81				Width     int    `json:"width"`
82				Height    int    `json:"height"`
83				AvgRate   string `json:"avg_frame_rate"`
84				Channels  int    `json:"channels"`
85				Tags      struct {
86					Title string `json:"title"`
87				} `json:"tags"`
88			} `json:"streams"`
89		}
90		if json.Unmarshal(out, &got) != nil {
91			return probeInfo{}
92		}
93		info := probeInfo{ok: true}
94		fmt.Sscanf(strings.TrimSpace(got.Format.Duration), "%f", &info.dur)
95		for _, s := range got.Streams {
96			switch s.CodecType {
97			case "video":
98				if info.w == 0 && s.Width > 0 && s.Height > 0 {
99					info.w, info.h = s.Width, s.Height
100					info.fps = rateOf(s.AvgRate)
101				}
102			case "audio":
103				n := s.Channels
104				if n < 1 {
105					n = 1 // a stream ffprobe would not count is still a stream
106				}
107				info.tracks = append(info.tracks, audTrack{chans: min(2, n), title: strings.TrimSpace(s.Tags.Title)})
108			}
109		}
110		return info
111	}
112	
113	// rateOf reads ffprobe's "30000/1001" into frames a second, or 0 for an answer
114	// no picture has: 0/0 for a stream that never moved, a rate no camera shoots.
115	func rateOf(s string) float64 {
116		num, den, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(s), "/")
117		if !ok {
118			return 0
119		}
120		n, err1 := strconv.ParseFloat(num, 64)
121		d, err2 := strconv.ParseFloat(den, 64)
122		if err1 != nil || err2 != nil || d <= 0 {
123			return 0
124		}
125		if r := n / d; r >= 1 && r <= 240 {
126			return r
127		}
128		return 0
129	}
130

Terminal:
```
### Cut

The session on a timeline: thumbnails per camera row, a waveform lane per sound
below, everything the cut keeps tinted green. Time nobody filmed takes no width
at all, so two recordings meet with a striped amber border each.

The page opens as soon as there is footage — you can lay the session out, see
where takes fall against each other, shift a recording by hand and listen,
before anything has been transcribed.

▶ asks the model for a cut. The toolbar has three ▶s of its own: plain ▶ plays
the recording, every second of it; ▶✂ plays the cut, removed stretches skipped,
with the clock on the finished video's time; ▶✂✂ reviews the cuts — ten seconds
of the finished video before each join and ten after it, one join after the
other, stopping after the last — so every splice is heard in one sitting
without watching the minutes between them.

From then on the cut is yours: drag to select, ＋ Add,
✕ to drop, ⌦ for whatever is in hand, Revert to go back to the suggestion.
**Trim a clip edge by dragging it** — with either button, on the pictures or on
the green bar above them — or ‹f and f› a frame at a time once it is in hand.
Wherever the pointer turns into a resize arrow, a drag there resizes: that is the
whole rule. The right button is for *moving* things instead, a scene along its
recording or a recording along the clock. Everything snaps to word edges,
silences and visual cuts, with the pointer showing what a press would grab.

You can also splice in cards, stills and sounds, switch which camera a scene is
shown from, silence a lane for one scene, and add effects — zoom, hold, speed,
volume, captions, drawings — each proposed by its own model pass after the cut
and each editable by hand.

### Narrate

An editable line per clip: what is said over it, in which voice, with what
emotion. ▶ writes the lines the cut does not have and speaks the ones not
already in the cache. A clip grows, or the speech speeds up, when a line does
```

187	//
188	// One paragraph or bullet per line, unwrapped: see describeSystem.
189	const captionSystem = `You put words on screen over a cut that has already been chosen. You are given a few clips, each with the lines spoken over it stamped in seconds from that clip's start. The clips are not yours to change.
190	
191	Whether there are captions at all is the USER CONTEXT's call, and it is the only thing that decides it. Said nothing about them, caption nothing: answer with an empty list. Where it asks -- every spoken line, only the verdicts, only what is named on screen, one line per clip -- write exactly that and no more.
192	
193	- A caption starts when its line starts and ends when it ends, in seconds from the clip's own start, and stays inside the clip: a line running past the end is captioned up to the end.
194	- Clean the words as a subtitler would: no ehm, no ehh, no stutters ("I I" is "I"), no repeated words, sentence case, the swearing kept. The speaker's own words otherwise, never a paraphrase.
195	- A line that is not about the video -- an aside to the editor, "cut this part" -- is never captioned. The user context says which lines are directions.
196	
197	Answer with CAPTIONS.`
198	
199	// cutReply is the end of every cut wording: where a segment may start and end,
200	// the length arithmetic, the reply shape (read by suggestParse, so spelled here
201	// only) and the check to run before answering. The tolerance it asks for is
202	// tighter than the one the run accepts (suggestWindow).
203	const cutReply = `
204	
205	A segment ends on the payoff, never just before it, and a moment that only makes sense because of an earlier one takes that one too or neither. Segments run from about 8 seconds to a minute, longer where a stretch has to be shown but not watched -- keep such a stretch whole, as ONE segment: it is played fast afterwards, not cut into pieces with the dull seconds left out.
206	
207	Answer with SEGMENTS, and nothing else in the reply. How fast each plays, what is captioned over it and what is drawn on it are asked for afterwards, clip by clip, once the cut stands.
208	
209	Check before you answer: every segment has an EVENT line inside it, every start is later than the end before it, everything the user context names is in, and -- if you were given a range -- the footage they come to, end minus start added up, lands in it. Anywhere inside it is right; do not trim towards its middle. Given no range, there is nothing to add up: keep what is worth keeping and stop.`
210	
211	// cutSeg is one piece of the finished video: a stretch of session S..E, or an
212	// insert (Ins) that plays in that slot. An overwriting insert costs the session
213	// seconds it covers; a spliced one sits at a point (S == E) and runs for Dur.
214	// length() is the one place the two spellings meet; splitSpliced is what the
215	// render walks. coalesce never merges an insert and keepFilmed never drops one.
216	type cutSeg struct {
217		S float64 `json:"s"`
218		E float64 `json:"e"`
219		// the asset, absolute or relative to the project root. Empty for footage,
220		// which is nearly every segment, so an ordinary cut.json is unchanged.
221		Ins string `json:"ins,omitempty"`
222		// how long a SPLICED insert runs. Only a spliced one has it -- an insert
223		// that replaces footage runs for exactly the footage it replaces -- so an
224		// ordinary cut.json is unchanged by this too.
225		Dur float64 `json:"dur,omitempty"`
226		// playback rate for footage: 0.5 is half speed. 0 or 1 is normal, so an
227		// ordinary cut.json is unchanged by this as well. Only produceSegs writes
228		// rates -- the editor's own segments never carry one.
229		Rate float64 `json:"rate,omitempty"`
230		// where an inserted SOUND starts inside its file. Nought for a file
231		// chosen from disk, which plays from its own beginning, and the copied
232		// second for a stretch of a lane copied out of the session -- which is
233		// the whole of what makes a copy of sound different from a file.
234		Ss float64 `json:"ss,omitempty"`
235		// this insert brings no sound of its own (askInsertParams). Read by mode:
236		// SPLICED, the insert plays silent; OVERWRITING, the footage underneath keeps
237		// being heard and only the picture is replaced.
238		Mute bool `json:"mute,omitempty"`
239		// which row of the picture band this scene's PICTURE comes from. Nought on a
240		// one-camera session. The row, not the file: a row is a camera and a camera is
241		// several files; which FILE is a question about a second (pickVideoOn).
242		Cam int `json:"cam,omitempty"`
243		// for a sound laid over the footage: which recording it was put in place
244		// OF. Empty is the answer a selection scoped to picture-and-sound gives --
245		// the file stands in for everything audible, which is what overwriting the
246		// sound has always meant. Named -- the selection was drawn in that lane --
247		// it stands in for that one recording
248		// and the rest keep playing under it. Meaningless on anything but a sound
249		// insert, and an ordinary cut.json is unchanged by it.
250		Lane string `json:"lane,omitempty"`
251		// which lanes this scene does NOT hear, by the name every audio row on the
252		// page already carries: a camera's own sound is its recording's name, a
253		// separate recording is its file's. Both kinds go in one list because the
254		// page shows them as one kind of thing -- a row with a waveform -- and a
255		// scene that is "my voice only" has to be able to say so about both.
256		//
257		// The SILENT ones rather than the audible ones, for two reasons. A cut
258		// written before this, and a scene nobody has touched, both come out as the
259		// empty list, which is every lane playing -- what the render has always
260		// done. And a lane that appears later (another source split) arrives
261		// audible everywhere rather than silent everywhere, which is the answer
262		// that can be heard and corrected rather than the one that is missed.
263		Quiet []string `json:"quiet,omitempty"`
264		// this clip STARTS at a border somebody made on purpose: | Split put it
265		// there (cut_split.go). Two clips of one camera that touch are otherwise
266		// one clip, and coalesce joins them the moment anything rearranges the
267		// list -- which is right for two selections that turned out to meet, and
268		// wrong for a border drawn deliberately to give a stretch its own camera,
269		// its own sound or its own place in the order. The flag is what tells the
270		// two apart. Nothing else sets it, so an ordinary cut.json is unchanged.
271		Split bool `json:"split,omitempty"`
272		// which SCENE this piece came from, stamped by the render's planning
273		// (produceSegs), never stored. One scene becomes several pieces (splices, rate
274		// boundaries), and only the sound asks whether two are the same scene
275		// (cut_fxsound.go).
276		Scene int `json:"-"`
277	}
278	
279	// laneQuiet is the one reading of that list, so the page, the preview and the
280	// render cannot disagree about what a scene hears.
281	func laneQuiet(quiet []string, base string) bool {
282		for _, q := range quiet {
283			if q == base {
284				return true
285			}
286		}
287		return false
288	}
289	
290	// hears is the question every caller actually asks.
291	func (s cutSeg) hears(base string) bool { return !laneQuiet(s.Quiet, base) }
292	
293	func (s cutSeg) isInsert() bool { return s.Ins != "" }
294	
295	// spliced is "the footage is not replaced here, it is cut open and continues
296	// after the card". Dur rather than S == E as the test: a footage segment can be
297	// squeezed to nothing by an edit and would then answer yes to the other one.
298	func (s cutSeg) spliced() bool { return s.Ins != "" && s.Dur > 0 }
299	
300	// length is how long this clip runs in the finished video: a spliced card
301	// runs for its own Dur, slowed footage runs longer than the footage it shows.
302	func (s cutSeg) length() float64 {
303		if s.Dur > 0 {
304			return s.Dur
305		}
306		if s.Rate > 0 {
307			return (s.E - s.S) / s.Rate
308		}
309		return s.E - s.S
310	}
311	
312	type tlVideo struct {
313		base     string
314		path     string
315		start    float64 // session time of this video's t=0
316		wall     float64 // the same instant on the wall clock, for naming outputs
317		dur      float64
318		interval float64
319		fps      float64
320		frames   []string
321		w, h     int     // pixel size, for the framing overlay's arithmetic
322		pxOrigin float64 // display x of the video's left edge (at current zoom)
323		lane     int     // which row of the picture band this one is drawn on
324		// the second of the FILE this row starts at. Nought for a recording, which
325		// is shown whole from its first frame; a cut lane is a window on a file and
326		// may open partway into it (cut_lane.go).
327		off float64
328	}
329	
330	// at is the second of v's file that session-second t shows, and it is the
331	// question every -ss and every seek on this page is asking. Two things stand
332	// between the two clocks: where the recording sits in the session (start), and,
333	// on a lane the cut put there, how far into the file the row begins (off).
334	func (v *tlVideo) at(t float64) float64 { return t - v.start + v.off }
335	
336	// sessionAt is the same sum read the other way: the session second at which this
337	// file's second local is on screen.
338	func (v *tlVideo) sessionAt(local float64) float64 { return v.start + local - v.off }
339	
340	// ffprobeFPS reads the average frame rate; r_frame_rate lies on VFR captures.
341	func ffprobeFPS(path string) float64 {
342		if r := ffprobeInfo(path).fps; r > 0 {
343			return r
344		}
345		return 30
346	}
347

5	// The seam between the pipeline and the pages.
6	//
7	// Twenty-odd files in this package run the pipeline -- transcribe, align,
8	// describe, fix, translate, the LLM client, the image server -- and none of
9	// them touches a widget. They are still methods on *App, in the same package
10	// as the buttons, so nothing said what they were allowed to take from it.
11	// This is that list.
12	//
13	// runner is everything a pipeline file may ask the application for. *App
14	// satisfies it (the assertion below is checked by the compiler), and the fence
15	// test (seam_test.go) reads the pipeline files and refuses any use of *App
16	// that is not here, not a field named beside it, and not another pipeline
17	// file's own method. Adding to the seam is allowed; it is meant to be a
18	// deliberate line in a diff rather than something a helper call grew by
19	// accident.
20	//
21	// The shape is the interface a separate package would take, if the split is
22	// ever made: what is here is what would have to cross it.

3	// Retakes: the stretches you said, stopped, and said again.
4	//
5	// A session recorded off a script is full of them -- a sentence trails off, the
6	// camera is stopped, the next take starts the sentence again, sometimes a
7	// sentence or two further back. Both attempts are in the transcript and both
8	// are in the footage, so unless something says otherwise the finished video
9	// says everything twice, with the breath between.
10	//
11	// The cut pass was the wrong place to ask. It reads the timeline to choose
12	// MOMENTS -- what is worth keeping -- and it read a doubled sentence as
13	// content: one run's reasoning says "slight repetition, acceptable" in as many
14	// words. It is not a judgment about the video at all; it is a fact about what
15	// was said, true whoever cuts it and true before anyone does.
16	//
17	// So it is settled here, at the end of Prepare, and only here. That is the
18	// earliest point where it can be RIGHT, which is two conditions:
19	//
20	//   - the whole session is one stream. An attempt and its replacement are
21	//     usually in two different recordings -- stop, start again -- and anything
22	//     working per source (the ASR, the fixer's blocks) sees one half of the
23	//     pattern it is looking for.
24	//   - the text is already fixed. Two attempts at one sentence have to LOOK
25	//     alike to be read as one sentence twice, and raw ASR gives two different
26	//     manglings of it.
27	//
28	// What comes out is a marking, never a deletion: these seconds were abandoned,
29	// and this is where they were said again. The transcript keeps every word. The
30	// cut brief folds a marked stretch into one line so the model never chooses it,
31	// the toolbar can skip it, and a mark you disagree with costs you a glance.
32	
33	import (
34		"encoding/json"
35		"fmt"
36		"math"
37		"os"
38		"path/filepath"
39		"sort"
40		"strconv"
41		"strings"
42		"unicode"
43	)
44	
45	// retakeSystem is the pass's wording. One narrow job, said as a procedure:
46	// what a take is, which half of a doubled sentence goes, and the four things
47	// that look like a retake and are not.
48	//
49	// One paragraph or bullet per line, unwrapped: see describeSystem.
50	const retakeSystem = `You find the stretches a speaker said, broke off, and said again.
51	
52	You are given every spoken line of one session, numbered, each with its own seconds, the pause in front of it, and the seams where one recording stops and the next begins. A session recorded off a script is made of takes: a sentence trails off or comes out wrong, the recording stops, and the next take says it again -- sometimes starting a sentence or two further back than where it went wrong.
53	
54	Mark the ABANDONED attempt and never the one that was kept. The abandoned one is earlier, the kept one later. When a take starts further back than the mistake, everything it says again is abandoned: mark from the first line the later take repeats, not from the line that went wrong.
55	
56	Mark the line even when only its LAST FEW WORDS are said again. A take often breaks off part-way through a line: ten seconds of new material and then two words that the next take starts over with. That line is abandoned from those two words on, and marking it is right -- the editor trims the mark down to exactly the words that are said again, and keeps everything before them. Two takes that end and begin on the same word or two are the commonest retake there is, and the easiest to read past.
57	
58	These are NOT retakes, and marking one is worse than missing a real one:
59	- a sentence said twice on purpose, with no pause and no seam before it
60	- a phrase repeated inside one flowing sentence, with no pause and no seam in the middle of it
61	- anything said once
62	- anything not in the script. Going off script is the person talking, not a mistake, and it stays
63	
64	The user context may carry the script. Where it does it says what was MEANT to be said, and it is a hint rather than the truth: it writes 42 where the speaker says "forty two", and a line matching nothing in it is improvisation and stays. Where there is no script, the pauses, the seams and the words themselves are the whole of the evidence.
65	
66	A few words broken off and never picked up again is abandoned with nothing to point at: give "again": 0.
67	
68	Answer with line NUMBERS, never with times.`
69	
70	// retake is one abandoned stretch of the session: the seconds it covers, and
71	// where the good attempt starts (0 when it was simply broken off and never
72	// picked up again).
73	type retake struct {
74		S, E  float64 // the abandoned words, first to last
75		Again float64 // where the attempt that was kept begins, 0 for none
76		// where what the cut REMOVES ends. E when the words are all that goes;
77		// the retake's own onset when everything up to it goes with them -- the
78		// camera stop, the breath, the run-up (placeEdges).
79		To   float64

81	}

88		// middle, so a cut ON the edge clips it. Small, because what is on the
89		// other side of it is the breath this is here to take out.
90		wordPad = 0.08

100		retakeReach = 180.0

118	// retakeFile is where the marks are kept: beside the transcript they are about,
119	// so they travel with the project and are re-read rather than re-asked.
120	func (a *App) retakeFile() string { return filepath.Join(a.transcriptDir(), "retakes.tsv") }
121	
122	// findRetakes is the pass. It runs on the merged timeline, writes the marks and
123	// returns them; a session with nothing to mark writes an empty file, which is
124	// the answer "asked, and there are none" rather than "never asked".
125	func (a *App) findRetakes(rows []tsvRow) ([]retake, error) {
126		spoken := speechOnly(rows)
127		if len(spoken) < 4 {
128			return nil, a.writeRetakes(nil)
129		}
130		brief := retakeBrief(spoken, a.narratorMic())
131		user := a.ctxBlockFor("retake") + fmt.Sprintf("WHAT WAS SAID, line by line:\n%s", brief)
132		system := a.sysPrompt("retake")
133		msgs := []map[string]any{msg("system", system), msg("user", user)}
134		// Asked MORE THAN ONCE, and every answer pooled. The call is sampled, and
135		// one run's answer drifts against the next -- twelve marks, then ten, one
136		// of them inverted -- so a retake missed is a retake missed by luck. It is
137		// a short call, and every mark it names is verified below before it
138		// counts (trimToRepeat), so pooling the runs costs seconds and risks
139		// nothing: a wrong mark is refused whichever run it came from.
140		var found []struct{ From, To, Again int }
141		seen := map[[3]int]bool{}
142		cached := 0
143		for run := 0; run < retakeRuns; run++ {
144			var out struct {
145				Abandoned []struct {
146					From, To, Again int
147				} `json:"abandoned"`
148			}
149			// the same session asked the same way: the same pool (llmcache.go).
150			// The RUN NUMBER is in the key, which is the whole point -- these
151			// requests are deliberately identical and their answers are meant to
152			// differ, so one slot per run replays the pool a re-run would
153			// otherwise pay for again, and never collapses three answers into one.
154			ask := askKey(system, user, run)
155			reply, hit := a.cachedReply("retake", ask)
156			var err error
157			if hit {
158				cached++
159			} else {
160				reply, err = a.llmChatRetry("retake", msgs, false)
161			}
162			if err != nil {
163				if run == 0 {
164					return nil, err
165				}
166				a.logfIdle("!!! retakes: run %d: %v -- going on with %d", run+1, err, run)
167				break
168			}
169			if p := jsonReply(reply, &out); p != "" {
170				a.logfIdle("!!! retakes: run %d: %s -- its answer is set aside", run+1, p)
171				continue
172			}
173			// kept only once it parsed, like every other cached answer: a reply
174			// that was set aside is one the next run has to ask about again
175			if !hit {
176				a.keepReply("retake", ask, reply)
177			}
178			for _, x := range out.Abandoned {
179				if k := [3]int{x.From, x.To, x.Again}; !seen[k] {
180					seen[k] = true
181					found = append(found, x)
182				}
183			}
184		}
185		if cached > 0 {
186			a.logfIdle(">>> retakes: %d of %d run(s) answered from the cache", cached, retakeRuns)
187		}
188		marks, notes := keepRetakes(spoken, found)
189		// ...and then the half the model cannot be taken at its word on: a retake
190		// is usually the tail of a line, and dropping the whole line takes content
191		// with it (trimToRepeat).
192		vids, auds := a.snapSources()
193		paths := append(vids, auds...)
194		words := a.sessionWords(paths)
195		trimmed, refused, more := trimToRepeat(marks, words, spoken)
196		marks, notes = trimmed, append(notes, more...)
197		// a second hearing for the ones the words refused: the transcript was
198		// taken off a whole recording, and a short clip of the two attempts alone
199		// often comes back as the same words twice (reHear)
200		if len(refused) > 0 {
201			heard, hn := a.reHear(refused, paths, spoken)
202			marks, notes = append(marks, heard...), append(notes, hn...)
203			sort.Slice(marks, func(i, j int) bool { return marks[i].S < marks[j].S })
204		}
205		// and then the gap between the attempt and the retake, which is not worth
206		// a frame: the camera stop, the breath, the run-up. There are no words in
207		// it to place a boundary by, so the sound places it (retake_edge.go) --
208		// between the words on either side of it, and never across one.
209		marks, more = a.placeEdges(marks, paths, spoken, words)
210		notes = append(notes, more...)
211		// three runs name the same stretch three ways -- one line, two lines, the
212		// line and a half before it -- and after trimming they are one mark, or
213		// two that overlap. One mark per stretch (mergeMarks).
214		marks = mergeMarks(marks)
215		for _, n := range notes {

217		}

223		}
224		if len(marks) > 0 {

233	// keepRetakes turns the reply's line numbers into marks, and drops the ones
234	// that cannot be true. The model names lines and never times, so a wrong answer
235	// is a wrong line rather than a second somewhere in the session -- and every
236	// line it names is checked back against the transcript here.
237	func keepRetakes(spoken []tsvRow, in []struct{ From, To, Again int }) ([]retake, []string) {
238		var out []retake
239		var notes []string
240		// Overlaps are allowed through here. The answers of several runs are
241		// pooled (findRetakes), and three runs name one stretch three ways; each
242		// is verified on its own below and the survivors are folded into one
243		// afterwards (mergeMarks). Refusing the later ones used to leave the
244		// pool with nothing: one run's marks set a cursor at the last line of
245		// the session, and every mark of every other run then read as overlap.
246		for _, r := range in {
247			f, t := r.From-1, r.To-1 // the brief numbers from 1
248			if f < 0 || t < f || t >= len(spoken) {
249				notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("lines %d-%d are not lines of this timeline", r.From, r.To))
250				continue
251			}
252			m := retake{S: spoken[f].s, E: spoken[t].e, To: spoken[t].e, Text: spoken[f].text}
253			if g := r.Again - 1; g >= 0 {
254				if g <= t {
255					// the retake INSIDE the stretch it replaces. One run answers
256					// every mark this way -- "again" set to the mark's own last
257					// line -- and read as "never picked up" that is a claim the
258					// model did not make, which then fails for the wrong reason
259					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("lines %d-%d say they are said again at line %d, which is inside them -- not a mark",
260						r.From, r.To, r.Again))
261					continue
262				}
263				if g >= len(spoken) {
264					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("lines %d-%d are said again at line %d, which is not a line", r.From, r.To, r.Again))
265					continue
266				}
267				// the replacement has to follow the thing it replaces, and follow
268				// it soon: a sentence said again three minutes later is a callback
269				if spoken[g].s-m.E > retakeReach {
270					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("lines %d-%d are said again %s later, too far to be a retake",
271						r.From, r.To, mmss(spoken[g].s-m.E)))
272					continue
273				}
274				m.Again = spoken[g].s
275			}
276			out = append(out, m)
277		}
278		return out, notes
279	}
280	
281	// retakeBrief is what the pass reads: every spoken line numbered, with its own
282	// seconds, the pause in front of it, and the seam where one recording ends and
283	// the next begins.
284	//
285	// Those three are the whole of the signal. An attempt that trails off, a gap,
286	// a new take, the same sentence again -- said in the text, so the model reads
287	// a shape rather than inferring one from prose. The pauses come from the lines'
288	// own times and cost nothing: there is no need to look at the audio to know
289	// that nobody spoke for two seconds.
290	func retakeBrief(spoken []tsvRow, narr string) string {
291		var b strings.Builder
292		for i, r := range spoken {
293			if i > 0 {
294				if gap := r.s - spoken[i-1].e; gap >= retakePause {
295					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "        (%.1fs pause)\n", gap)
296				}
297				if r.src != spoken[i-1].src {
298					fmt.Fprintf(&b, "        --- the recording stops here; the next one begins ---\n")
299				}
300			}
301			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%4d  [%s-%s] %s: %s\n", i+1, mmssT(r.s), mmssT(r.e), tlLabel(r, narr), r.text)
302		}
303		return b.String()
304	}
305	
306	// mmssT is a stamp with a tenth on it. The cut works in whole seconds because
307	// it chooses moments; this pass points at lines, and the tenth is there for the
308	// person reading the brief back against the waveform.
309	func mmssT(t float64) string {
310		return fmt.Sprintf("%02d:%04.1f", int(t)/60, math.Mod(t, 60))
311	}
312	
313	func speechOnly(rows []tsvRow) []tsvRow {
314		var out []tsvRow
315		for _, r := range rows {
316			if r.spk != "EVENT" && strings.TrimSpace(r.text) != "" {
317				out = append(out, r)
318			}
319		}
320		return out
321	}
