323	// tooMuch is whether an answer has stopped being a list of retakes and become
324	// a proposal to halve the session. A pass that wants most of the speech gone
325	// has not found attempts, it has lost its place in the numbering -- and one
326	// wrong line number early can carry every later one with it, so the whole
327	// answer is refused rather than argued with line by line.
328	func tooMuch(marks []retake, spoken []tsvRow) bool {
329		said := speechSecs(spoken)
330		return said > 0 && retakeSecs(marks) > said*retakeCeil
331	}
332	
333	func retakeSecs(marks []retake) float64 {
334		t := 0.0
335		for _, m := range marks {
336			t += m.E - m.S
337		}
338		return t
339	}
340	
341	func speechSecs(rows []tsvRow) float64 {
342		t := 0.0
343		for _, r := range rows {
344			t += r.e - r.s
345		}
346		return t
347	}
348	
349	// writeRetakes stores the marks, and an empty file when there are none: the
350	// difference between "asked, none found" and "never asked" is what stops a
351	// reload from silently reading a stale answer from a run that predates this.
352	func (a *App) writeRetakes(marks []retake) error {
353		var b strings.Builder
354		for _, m := range marks {
355			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%.2f\t%.2f\t%.2f\t%.2f\t%s\n", m.S, m.E, m.Again, m.To, m.Text)
356		}
357		if err := os.MkdirAll(a.transcriptDir(), 0o755); err != nil {
358			return err
359		}
360		return os.WriteFile(a.retakeFile(), []byte(b.String()), 0o644)
361	}
362	
363	// loadRetakes reads them back. Missing is not an error: a project prepared
364	// before this existed has no file, and no marks is what it means.
365	func (a *App) loadRetakes() []retake {
366		b, err := os.ReadFile(a.retakeFile())
367		if err != nil {
368			return nil
369		}
370		var out []retake
371		for _, ln := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
372			f := strings.Split(ln, "\t")
373			if len(f) < 3 {
374				continue
375			}
376			s, e1 := strconv.ParseFloat(f[0], 64)
377			e, e2 := strconv.ParseFloat(f[1], 64)
378			ag, e3 := strconv.ParseFloat(f[2], 64)
379			if e1 != nil || e2 != nil || e3 != nil {
380				continue
381			}
382			m := retake{S: s, E: e, Again: ag, To: e}
383			// a fifth column is where the removal ends; a file with four was
384			// written before the edges were placed, and removes the words alone
385			if len(f) > 4 {
386				if to, err := strconv.ParseFloat(f[3], 64); err == nil && to > 0 {
387					m.To = to
388				}
389				m.Text = f[4]
390			} else if len(f) > 3 {
391				m.Text = f[3]
392			}
393			out = append(out, m)
394		}
395		return out
396	}
397	
398	// retakeAt is which marked stretch a line lies in, or -1.
399	func retakeAt(marks []retake, r tsvRow) int {
400		mid := (r.s + r.e) / 2
401		for i, m := range marks {
402			if mid >= m.S && mid <= m.E {
403				return i
404			}
405		}
406		return -1
407	}
408	
409	// retakeJSON is what a marked answer looks like, for the log and the tests.
410	func retakeJSON(marks []retake) string {
411		b, _ := json.Marshal(marks)
412		return string(b)
413	}
414	
415	// ---- what was actually said again -------------------------------------------
416	//
417	// The pass answers in whole LINES, and a retake is rarely a whole line. You
418	// stop in the middle of a sentence and pick it up from the last few words, so
419	// the line the model marks holds both the words that were said again and the
420	// words that were not -- and dropping all of it takes real content out of the
421	// video, silently, in the middle of a sentence the cut keeps both sides of.
422	//
423	// One run marked eleven stretches. Five were clean, five held content that was
424	// never repeated, and one was not a retake at all: the sentence ran across a
425	// seam and only the word "which" was said twice.
426	//
427	// So the claim is checked against the words. What survives is the SUFFIX of the
428	// marked stretch that the later take says again -- the stutter and nothing else
429	// -- and a stretch with no repeated tail is not marked at all. The words are the
430	// ASR's own (words.json), which is where the times come from too, so this can
431	// be exact where the lines cannot: it cuts inside a line, at a word boundary.
432	
433	// srcWord is one word of the session, on the session clock.
434	type srcWord struct {
435		s, e float64
436		w    string
437		// the word as it is WRITTEN, case and punctuation kept: w is bared and
438		// lowercased for matching, and matching is not reading. The subtitles are
439		// built from these (wordCues), so they have to say "Eastern University"
440		// and not "eastern university".
441		raw string
442		src string // the recording it was said in (baseName), for the seams
443	}
444	
445	// againReach is how much of the later take is read for the repeat: a retake
446	// says the sentence again at its start, not a minute into it.
447	const againReach = 25.0
448	
449	// trimToRepeat shrinks every mark to the words the later take repeats, and
450	// drops the ones it does not repeat at all. Marks with no replacement to check
451	// against (the model said it was broken off and never picked up) are left as
452	// they are: there is nothing to compare them with.
453	func trimToRepeat(marks []retake, words []srcWord, spoken []tsvRow) (out, refused []retake, notes []string) {
454		for _, m := range marks {
455			if goesWith(m, spoken) < retakeMin {
456				notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s is too short to be an attempt at anything", mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E)))
457				continue
458			}
459			if len(words) == 0 {
460				out = append(out, m) // nothing to check it against; the answer stands
461				continue
462			}
463			if m.Again <= 0 {
464				// the pass says it was broken off and never picked up, and there is
465				// nothing to verify that against. The shape has to carry it alone,
466				// and the only shape that does is a take that holds nothing else
467				// (wholeTake): a stretch with the rest of its take around it, or one
468				// that runs across a seam, is part of something that was said once.
469				if wholeTake(m, spoken) {
470					out = append(out, m)
471					continue
472				}
473				notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s is said to be broken off, but its take holds more than it -- left in",
474					mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E)))
475				continue
476			}
477			said := wordsIn(words, m.S, m.E)
478			again := wordsIn(words, m.Again, m.Again+againReach)
479			if len(said) == 0 || len(again) == 0 {
480				out = append(out, m)
481				continue
482			}
483			k := repeatFrom(said, again)
484			if k < 0 {
485				// not said again -- so the pass was wrong about where, and the
486				// question becomes whether it was right about the stretch at all.
487				//
488				// A take that consists of NOTHING BUT this stretch is a take that
489				// failed: you started, it came out wrong, you stopped. That is a
490				// false start whatever the next take goes on to say, and it is the
491				// one shape of abandonment there is nothing to compare against.
492				//
493				// A stretch with the rest of its take still around it is a
494				// different thing: usually a sentence carried across the seam,
495				// where dropping it takes a sentence out of the video that was
496				// only ever said once.
497				if wholeTake(m, spoken) {
498					m.Again = 0
499					out = append(out, m)
500					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s is the whole of its take and is not said again -- a false start (%q)",
501						mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E), shortWords(said)))
502					continue
503				}
504				// ...or a REPHRASE: the retake says the same thing in other
505				// words, so nothing repeats and there is no word to trim to. What
506				// there is instead is the shape of the stop: the mark ends in
507				// fragments -- a line or two too short to be anything but broken
508				// off -- and the take ends right after them. Those go; the full
509				// lines the model swept up in front of them stay (tailFragments).
510				// "...they forked, the project." and then thirty seconds of
511				// silence is this, and it went into the video three runs running.
512				if s := tailFragments(m, spoken); s >= 0 {
513					if s > m.S {
514						notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s trimmed to %s: not said again, but that is where it breaks off",
515							mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E), mmss(s)))
516						m.S = s
517					}
518					if goesWith(m, spoken) < retakeMin {
519						continue
520					}
521					out = append(out, m)
522					continue
523				}
524				notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s is not said again at %s -- left in (%q)",
525					mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E), mmss(m.Again), shortWords(said)))
526				refused = append(refused, m)
527				continue
528			}
529			if k > 0 {
530				notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s trimmed to %s: only %q is said again",
531					mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E), mmss(said[k].s), shortWords(said[k:])))
532				m.S = said[k].s
533			}
534			// ...and the floor again, on what the trim left. A stutter of one
535			// clipped word is a tenth of a second, and taking a tenth of a second
536			// out of the middle of a sentence is a click rather than an edit: the
537			// doubled word is less audible than the splice that would remove it.
538			if goesWith(m, spoken) < retakeMin {
539				notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s is all that is said again -- too short to cut cleanly, left in",
540					mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E)))
541				continue
542			}
543			out = append(out, m)
544		}
545		return out, refused, notes
546	}
547	
548	// wholeTake is whether a marked stretch is all the speech its recording holds.
549	//
550	// Nothing was said in that take but this, so the take is the attempt: it began,
551	// it went wrong, it stopped. The seam either side is what makes it readable as
552	// one -- a stretch with more of its own take around it is part of something,
553	// and what it is part of was said once.
554	// mergeMarks folds marks that overlap into one: the earliest start, the latest
555	// end, and the retake the later of them points at. Sorted on the way.
556	func mergeMarks(marks []retake) []retake {
557		sort.Slice(marks, func(i, j int) bool { return marks[i].S < marks[j].S })
558		var out []retake
559		for _, m := range marks {
560			if n := len(out); n > 0 && m.S <= math.Max(out[n-1].E, out[n-1].To)+0.01 {
561				p := &out[n-1]
562				p.E = math.Max(p.E, m.E)
563				p.To = math.Max(p.To, m.To)
564				if m.Again > p.Again {
565					p.Again = m.Again
566				}
567				if p.Text == "" {
568					p.Text = m.Text
569				}
570				continue
571			}
572			out = append(out, m)
573		}
574		return out
575	}
576	
577	// tailFragments is where a mark's broken-off tail begins, or -1 when it has
578	// none: the mark has to END its take -- that is the stop -- and the lines at
579	// the end of it have to be fragments (retakeFrag). Walked back from the end,
580	// so a full line the model marked in front of the fragments is not one.
581	func tailFragments(m retake, spoken []tsvRow) float64 {
582		var in []tsvRow
583		for _, r := range spoken {
584			if mid := (r.s + r.e) / 2; mid >= m.S && mid <= m.E {
585				in = append(in, r)
586			}
587		}
588		if len(in) == 0 || !endsTake(in[len(in)-1], spoken) {
589			return -1
590		}
591		i := len(in)
592		for i > 0 && in[i-1].e-in[i-1].s < retakeFrag {
593			i--
594		}
595		if i == len(in) {
596			return -1 // the last thing said is a whole line, not a fragment
597		}
598		return in[i].s
599	}
600	
601	// endsTake is whether r is the last thing said in its recording.
602	func endsTake(r tsvRow, spoken []tsvRow) bool {
603		for _, o := range spoken {
604			if o.src == r.src && o.s > r.s {
605				return false
606			}
607		}
608		return true
609	}
610	
611	func wholeTake(m retake, spoken []tsvRow) bool {
612		src, n, in := "", 0, 0
613		for _, r := range spoken {
614			mid := (r.s + r.e) / 2
615			if mid < m.S || mid > m.E {
616				continue
617			}
618			if src == "" {
619				src = r.src
620			} else if r.src != src {
621				return false // it spans two recordings: not one take's failure
622			}
623			in++
624		}
625		if src == "" {
626			return false
627		}
628		for _, r := range spoken {
629			if r.src == src {
630				n++
631			}
632		}
633		return in == n
634	}
635	
636	// repeatFrom is where the repeated tail of said begins: the earliest word from
637	// which what follows is said again in again. -1 when none of it is.
638	//
639	// Earliest, not longest: the whole stutter goes, not the part of it that
640	// matches best.
641	//
642	// Anchored, then tolerant. The tail is looked for anywhere in the later take --
643	// a retake does not always resume at its first word -- and once a run is going,
644	// a word that does not match is stepped over rather than ending it. Both are
645	// needed and neither alone is enough: without the anchor a repeat that starts
646	// three words in is never found, and without the tolerance one word ends the
647	// match.
648	//
649	// It has to be tolerant because the two attempts are never the same text. These
650	// are raw ASR words, and the same phrase came back as "and the tor project keep
651	// hearing" one time and "and the tour project kept hearing" the next -- two
652	// words, one edit each, in a phrase of six. sameWord is what forgives that.
653	func repeatFrom(said, again []srcWord) int {
654		for k := range said {
655			left := said[k:]
656			for a := range again {
657				if sameWord(left[0].w, again[a].w) && runFrom(left, again, a) >= int(math.Ceil(0.7*float64(len(left)))) {
658					return k
659				}
660			}
661		}
662		return -1
663	}
664	
665	// runFrom counts how much of left turns up in again, in order, starting at a.
666	// A word that is not there is stepped over: the next one may still be, and one
667	// word heard differently must not end the match.
668	func runFrom(left, again []srcWord, a int) int {
669		j, hit := a, 0
670		for _, w := range left {
671			for d := 0; d <= repeatSkip; d++ {
672				if j+d < len(again) && sameWord(w.w, again[j+d].w) {
673					hit, j = hit+1, j+d+1
674					break
675				}
676			}
677		}
678		return hit
679	}
680	
681	// repeatSkip is how many words of the later take may be stepped over to find
682	// the next one. Enough for a word or two said differently; not enough to walk
683	// the rest of the take looking for a common word.
684	const repeatSkip = 3
685	
686	// sameWord is whether two heard words are the same word.
687	//
688	// The same, one a prefix of the other -- which is what an attempt broken off
689	// mid-word looks like beside the one that finishes it, "sub" against "subject"
690	// -- or one edit apart, which is what one microphone and one model make of the
691	// same sound twice: "tor" and "tour", "keep" and "kept". Short words are
692	// compared exactly: at two letters every rule above matches half the language.
693	// bareWord is a word with the punctuation around it taken off, lowercased, so
694	// that "again," and "Again" are the same word.
695	//
696	// Every letter, not the ASCII ones: the test used to be a-z A-Z 0-9, which
697	// TrimFunc applies to BOTH ENDS, so a word beginning with an umlaut lost it.
698	// "über" came back as "ber" and "Übung" as "bung" -- while an umlaut in the
699	// middle survived, because the trim never reached it. That is not a cosmetic
700	// fault. Every word comparison in the app goes through here, and the one that
701	// lines the aligner's words up against the transcript's (redress) could not
702	// match "über" to "Über-Datum.", so it folded the two into one and left the
703	// word after them with no written form at all. Sixty-four words of one German
704	// lecture were folded that way.
705	func bareWord(s string) string {
706		return strings.ToLower(strings.TrimFunc(s, func(r rune) bool {
707			return !unicode.IsLetter(r) && !unicode.IsDigit(r) && r != '\''
708		}))
709	}
710	
711	func sameWord(a, b string) bool {
712		if a == b {
713			return true
714		}
715		if len(a) < 3 || len(b) < 3 {
716			return false
717		}
718		if strings.HasPrefix(a, b) || strings.HasPrefix(b, a) {
719			return true
720		}
721		return oneEdit(a, b)
722	}
723	
724	// oneEdit is whether a and b are at most one insertion, deletion or
725	// substitution apart.
726	func oneEdit(a, b string) bool {
727		if len(a) < len(b) {
728			a, b = b, a
729		}
730		if len(a)-len(b) > 1 {
731			return false
732		}
733		i, j, seen := 0, 0, false
734		for i < len(a) && j < len(b) {
735			if a[i] == b[j] {
736				i, j = i+1, j+1
737				continue
738			}
739			if seen {
740				return false
741			}
742			seen = true
743			if len(a) > len(b) {
744				i++
745			} else {
746				i, j = i+1, j+1
747			}
748		}
749		return !(seen && (len(a)-i > 0 || len(b)-j > 0))
750	}
751	
752	func wordsIn(words []srcWord, t0, t1 float64) []srcWord {
753		var out []srcWord
754		for _, w := range words {
755			if w.s >= t0-0.01 && w.e <= t1+0.01 {
756				out = append(out, w)
757			}
758		}
759		return out
760	}
761	
762	func shortWords(ws []srcWord) string {
763		var b []string
764		for _, w := range ws {
765			b = append(b, w.w)
766		}
767		s := strings.Join(b, " ")
768		if len(s) > 60 {
769			s = s[:57] + "..."
770		}
771		return s
772	}
773	
774	// ---- the words themselves ----------------------------------------------------
775	
776	// sessionWords is every word the ASR heard, on the session clock.
777	//
778	// words.json is the server's own answer, kept as it came (pipeline.go): one
779	// entry per token with its sample range, at sampleRate. Tokens are pieces of
780	// words -- "wa", "lle", "t" -- and a leading space is what starts a new one, so
781	// they are glued back together here. Punctuation-only tokens carry no sound of
782	// their own and are attached to the word before them without moving its end:
783	// left in, a comma's stamp lands in the silence after the sentence and makes
784	// every last word of a sentence look a second longer than it is.
785	func (a *App) sessionWords(paths []string) []srcWord {
786		// on the SESSION clock, like everything the marks are measured in.
787		// sourceStart is a wall clock -- seconds since the epoch -- and the one
788		// place that difference shows up is here, where a word at 1.789e9 and a
789		// mark at 99.1 simply never meet: nothing matched, nothing was verified,
790		// and every mark came through exactly as the model wrote it.
791		at, zero := srcClock(paths)
792		var out []srcWord
793		for _, p := range paths {
794			base := baseName(p)
795			dir := filepath.Join(a.inputsDir(), base)
796			mine := glueWords(wordTimes(dir), at[p]-zero)
797			dressWords(mine, readFileString(filepath.Join(dir, "transcript.txt")))
798			for _, w := range mine {
799				w.src = base
800				if w.raw == "" {
801					w.raw = w.w
802				}
803				out = append(out, w)
804			}
805		}
806		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].s < out[j].s })
807		// ...and then the spelling the transcript pass settled on, which is where
808		// the session context reaches the subtitles (subwords.go). The raw
809		// transcript above is what the ALIGNER was handed and is the only thing
810		// its bare words can be walked against; this is what the editor asked the
811		// line to say. Unshifted rows on purpose: the words here carry no shift
812		// either, and matching two clocks that have moved differently matches
813		// nothing.
814		fixWords(out, loadTSVRows(filepath.Join(a.transcriptDir(), "session.tsv")))
815		return out
816	}
817	
818	// dressWords gives each word its spelling back: case and punctuation, off the
819	// transcript the aligner was handed.
820	//
821	// The aligner answers in bare lowercase -- it is matching sound to text and
822	// hands back what it matched rather than what it was given -- so the times are
823	// right and the writing is gone: "welcome back this is a weekly summary" for a
824	// transcript that reads "Welcome back. This is a weekly summary". The
825	// subtitles are built from these words (wordCues), and a subtitle is read.
826	//
827	// The transcript IS what the aligner was given, word for word and in order, so
828	// the two are walked together. A word the walk cannot place keeps the bare
829	// form: a caption missing a capital is a smaller fault than one missing a word.
830	func dressWords(words []srcWord, text string) {
831		fields := strings.Fields(text)
832		j := 0
833		for i := range words {
834			for k := j; k < len(fields) && k-j < dressReach; k++ {
835				if bareWord(fields[k]) == words[i].w {
836					words[i].raw = fields[k]
837					j = k + 1
838					break
839				}
840			}
841		}
842	}
843	
844	// dressReach is how far ahead in the transcript a word is looked for: the
845	// aligner drops one here and there, and past a few the walk has lost its place
846	// and every word after it would be dressed in the wrong one.
847	const dressReach = 8
848	
849	// asrToken is one entry of the server's words list.
850	type asrToken struct {
851		Word  string `json:"word"`
852		Start int64  `json:"start_sample"`
853		End   int64  `json:"end_sample"`
854	}
855	
856	// glueWords turns a model's tokens into words at off seconds.
857	//
858	// Two conventions are in play and they cannot be told apart token by token.
859	// Nemotron answers in PIECES with a leading space on the first of each word --
860	// " wa", "lle", "t" -- and a token of nothing but space where a word begins;
861	// drop that space without remembering it and the word glues onto the one
862	// before. Qwen and the aligner answer in whole words with no leading space
863	// anywhere, and the same rule welds a whole take into a single word: the first
864	// two measurements of this taken by hand came out as "1 word", which is what
865	// sent me looking.
866	//
867	// So the stream says which it is. A leading space anywhere means pieces; none
868	// means every token is a word.
869	func glueWords(toks []asrToken, off float64) []srcWord {
870		pieces := false
871		for _, w := range toks {
872			if strings.HasPrefix(w.Word, " ") {
873				pieces = true
874				break
875			}
876		}
877		var out []srcWord
878		brk := true
879		for _, w := range toks {
880			bare := bareWord(w.Word)
881			raw := strings.TrimSpace(w.Word)
882			t0, t1 := off+float64(w.Start)/sampleRate, off+float64(w.End)/sampleRate
883			if bare == "" {

885				// text: it belongs to the word in front of it, which is what the

887				if raw != "" && len(out) > 0 && !brk {

892			}
893			if !pieces || strings.HasPrefix(w.Word, " ") || brk || len(out) == 0 {
894				out = append(out, srcWord{s: t0, e: t1, w: bare, raw: raw})
895				brk = false
896				continue
897			}
898			out[len(out)-1].e = t1
899			out[len(out)-1].w += bare
900			out[len(out)-1].raw += raw

902		return out

905	// edgeLookup is the envelope under a session second, loaded once per source:
906	// which recording is under t is the timeline's to say (srcOf), and the
907	// recording's envelope is read or built on the first ask (loadEdges).
908	func (a *App) edgeLookup(paths []string, spoken []tsvRow) func(t float64) *edges {
909		at, zero := srcClock(paths)
910		byBase := map[string]string{}
911		for _, p := range paths {
912			byBase[baseName(p)] = p
913		}
914		env := map[string]*edges{}
915		return func(t float64) *edges {
916			base := srcOf(spoken, t)
917			p, ok := byBase[base]
918			if !ok {
919				return nil
920			}
921			if e, ok := env[p]; ok {
922				return e
923			}
924			env[p] = a.loadEdges(p, at[p]-zero)
925			return env[p]
926		}
927	}
928	
929	// goesWith is how much of the session this mark actually takes out, which is
930	// not the same as how long the abandoned words are.
931	//
932	// A false start is often ONE word -- "...for Android, which" -- and then the
933	// camera stops and eighteen seconds of nothing follow before the retake says
934	// "which seems to have". Measured on the words that is a tenth of a second and
935	// refused as too small to cut cleanly; measured on what goes it is eighteen
936	// seconds of a man sitting in silence, and the tenth of a second is the least
937	// of what the cut is for. So the floor is applied to the removal, which runs
938	// to the retake's onset wherever there is nothing said in between.
939	func goesWith(m retake, spoken []tsvRow) float64 {
940		if m.Again > m.E && !wordsBetween(spoken, m.E, m.Again) {
941			return m.Again - m.S
942		}
943		return m.E - m.S
944	}
945	
946	// lastWord is the last word that ends at or before t.
947	func lastWord(words []srcWord, t float64) (srcWord, bool) {
948		var out srcWord
949		ok := false
950		for _, w := range words {
951			if w.e <= t+0.01 && (!ok || w.e > out.e) {
952				out, ok = w, true
953			}
954		}
955		return out, ok
956	}
957	
958	// wordAt is the word that starts at t, if one does.
959	func wordAt(words []srcWord, t float64) (srcWord, bool) {
960		for _, w := range words {
961			if math.Abs(w.s-t) < 0.01 {
962				return w, true
963			}
964		}
965		return srcWord{}, false
966	}
967	
968	// lastWordEnd is where the last word that ends at or before t ends, or 0 when
969	// there is none. The floor under an edge: what is before it was said once and
970	// stays, and an edge that crosses it takes a word out of the video with it.
971	func lastWordEnd(words []srcWord, t float64) float64 {
972		out := 0.0
973		for _, w := range words {
974			if w.e <= t+0.01 && w.e > out {
975				out = w.e
976			}
977		}
978		return out
979	}
980	
981	// srcOf is which recording a session second falls in, by the lines around it,
982	// and where that recording starts. "" when no line is near.
983	func srcOf(spoken []tsvRow, t float64) string {
984		best, d := "", 1e9
985		for _, r := range spoken {
986			if r.s <= t && t <= r.e {
987				return r.src
988			}
989			if x := math.Min(math.Abs(r.s-t), math.Abs(r.e-t)); x < d {
990				best, d = r.src, x
991			}
992		}
993		if d > 30 {
994			return ""
995		}
996		return best
997	}

999	// placeEdges moves every mark's two edges onto the sound (retake_edge.go): the
1000	// removal starts where the last kept sound ends, and -- when there is a retake
1001	// and nothing else was said before it -- ends where the retake's sound begins.
1002	func (a *App) placeEdges(marks []retake, paths []string, spoken []tsvRow, words []srcWord) ([]retake, []string) {
1003		edgeOf := a.edgeLookup(paths, spoken)
1004		var notes []string
1005		for i := range marks {
1006			m := &marks[i]
1007			if len(words) > 0 {
1008				// The WORDS fence both edges, and the sound chooses inside the
1009				// fence (endAfter, startBefore).
1010				//
1011				// The envelope alone used to place them, for ASR stamps that ran
1012				// half a second late -- and it cannot tell a breath from a word.
1013				// A breath is sound: asked where the sound before the abandoned
1014				// word stops it answered "after the breath", and the breath was
1015				// kept; that was every deep breath heard at a join. Now the
1016				// aligner's edges say which words the cut may touch -- none --
1017				// and between the last word that stays and the first that was
1018				// abandoned the sound only says where the quietest moment is,
1019				// with the word's own tail followed first so a trailing s is not
1020				// shaved. Everything between the two edges goes.
1021				if w, ok := lastWord(words, m.S); ok && w.e < m.S {
1022					s := math.Min(m.S, w.e+wordPad)
1023					if e := edgeOf(w.e); e != nil {
1024						s = e.endAfter(w, m.S)
1025					}
1026					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s: the cut ends %.2fs earlier, after the last word that stays", mmss(m.S), m.S-s))
1027					m.S = s
1028				}
1029				if m.Again > m.E && len(wordsIn(words, m.E, m.Again)) == 0 {
1030					// nothing said between: it all goes, up to the retake's own
1031					// first word
1032					to := math.Max(m.E, m.Again-wordPad)
1033					if w, ok := wordAt(words, m.Again); ok {
1034						if e := edgeOf(m.Again); e != nil {
1035							to = e.startBefore(w, m.E)
1036						}
1037					}
1038					if to > m.To {
1039						notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s: the cut resumes at %s, just before the retake's first word", mmss(m.S), mmss(to)))
1040						m.To = to
1041					}
1042				}
1043				continue
1044			}
1045			// no word times: the sound is all there is to place an edge by
1046			if e := edgeOf(m.S); e != nil {
1047				if s := e.endBefore(m.S); s != m.S {
1048					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s: the cut ends %.2fs earlier, where the sound before it stops", mmss(m.S), m.S-s))
1049					m.S = s
1050				}
1051			}
1052			if m.Again > 0 && !wordsBetween(spoken, m.E, m.Again) {
1053				to := m.Again
1054				if e := edgeOf(m.Again); e != nil {
1055					to = math.Min(math.Max(e.startAt(m.Again), m.E), m.Again)
1056				}
1057				if to > m.To {
1058					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s: the cut resumes at %s, where the retake starts to sound", mmss(m.S), mmss(to)))
1059					m.To = to
1060				}
1061			}
1062		}
1063		return marks, notes
1064	}
1065	
1066	// reHear asks the audio server about the two attempts alone, and applies the
1067	// marks it can then verify.
1068	//
1069	// The transcript was taken off a whole recording, and one word heard
1070	// differently in the two attempts -- "stay safe" against "stay unsafe" -- is
1071	// enough for the word check to refuse a real retake. A clip of a few seconds
1072	// holding just the one attempt gives the model nothing to segment across, and
1073	// it usually comes back as the same words both times. Only the refused marks
1074	// are asked about, and only when there is a retake to compare against; a few
1075	// short calls, not a second transcription.
1076	func (a *App) reHear(refused []retake, paths []string, spoken []tsvRow) ([]retake, []string) {
1077		var out []retake
1078		var notes []string
1079		if err := a.ensureAudioServer(); err != nil {
1080			return nil, []string{fmt.Sprintf("no second hearing: %v", err)}
1081		}
1082		at, zero := srcClock(paths)
1083		byBase := map[string]string{}
1084		for _, p := range paths {
1085			byBase[baseName(p)] = p
1086		}
1087		tmp, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "naivepost-rehear-*")
1088		if err != nil {
1089			return nil, []string{fmt.Sprintf("no second hearing: %v", err)}
1090		}
1091		defer os.RemoveAll(tmp)
1092		hear := func(t0, t1 float64, name string) []srcWord {
1093			p, ok := byBase[srcOf(spoken, t0)]
1094			if !ok {
1095				return nil
1096			}
1097			off := at[p] - zero
1098			wav := filepath.Join(tmp, name+".wav")
1099			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-ss", fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", t0-off),
1100				"-t", fmt.Sprintf("%.2f", t1-t0), "-i", p, "-vn", "-ac", "1", "-ar", "16000",
1101				"-c:a", "pcm_s16le", wav); err != nil {
1102				return nil
1103			}
1104			body, _, err := a.asrJSON(wav)
1105			if err != nil {
1106				return nil
1107			}
1108			var doc struct {
1109				Words []asrToken `json:"words"`
1110			}
1111			if json.Unmarshal(body, &doc) != nil {
1112				return nil
1113			}
1114			return glueWords(doc.Words, t0)
1115		}
1116		for i, m := range refused {
1117			if m.Again <= 0 {
1118				continue
1119			}
1120			said := hear(m.S-0.3, m.E+0.3, fmt.Sprintf("said%d", i))
1121			again := hear(m.Again-0.3, m.Again+againReach, fmt.Sprintf("again%d", i))
1122			if len(said) == 0 || len(again) == 0 {
1123				notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s heard again: nothing came back -- left in", mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E)))
1124				continue
1125			}
1126			k := repeatFrom(said, again)
1127			if k < 0 {
1128				notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s heard again as %q, still not said again -- left in",
1129					mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E), shortWords(said)))
1130				continue
1131			}
1132			if said[k].s > m.S {
1133				m.S = said[k].s
1134			}
1135			if m.E-m.S < retakeMin {
1136				continue
1137			}
1138			notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s-%s heard again: %q is said again after all -- cut",
1139				mmss(m.S), mmss(m.E), shortWords(said[k:])))
1140			out = append(out, m)
1141		}
1142		return out, notes
1143	}

301			k := baseName(it.path)
302			if p, ok := seen[k]; ok {
303				return p, it.path
304			}
305			seen[k] = it.path
306		}
307		return "", ""
308	}
309	
310	func (s *sourceList) paths() []string {
311		out := make([]string, len(s.items))
312		for i, it := range s.items {
313			out[i] = it.path
314		}
315		return out
316	}
317	
318	// prune drops rows whose file is gone and names them, for the log. A source
319	// that quietly stopped being in the list is how a render comes out missing a
320	// camera angle nobody can account for.
321	func (s *sourceList) prune() []string {
322		var gone []string
323		var kept []sourceItem
324		for _, it := range s.items {
325			if exists(it.path) {
326				kept = append(kept, it)
327				continue
328			}
329			gone = append(gone, it.path)
330		}
331		if len(gone) == 0 {
332			return nil
333		}
334		s.items = kept
335		s.autoTag()
336		s.changed()
337		return gone
338	}
339	
340	// load replaces the list wholesale -- a project being opened. Roles come from
341	// the project as stored: a list with nobody in slot 1 is one the user untagged,
342	// and it must come back untagged. autoTag runs only when a broken tag had to
343	// be stripped -- filling the one kind of gap load itself leaves.
344	func (s *sourceList) load(items []sourceItem) {
345		s.items = nil
346		stripped := false
347		for _, it := range items {
348			// a hand-edited project must not seat two people in one slot,
349			// or promise frames out of a file that has none
350			if it.narrator != 0 && (it.narrator < 1 || it.narrator > narratorSlots || s.slotHolder(it.narrator) >= 0) {
351				it.narrator = 0
352				stripped = true
353			}
354			it.footage = it.footage && isVideo(it.path)
355			s.items = append(s.items, it)
356		}
357		if stripped {
358			s.autoTag()
359		}
360		s.changed()
361	}
362	
363	func (s *sourceList) changed() {
364		// before anything reads the list: placing a file is the first thing every
365		// step does with one, and it has to place it where this list says
366		s.render()
367		if s.onChange != nil {
368			s.onChange()
369		}
370	}
371	
372	// srcRowKey is the key to a row's four symbols, appended to each of their
373	// tooltips: a word each, opening with the symbol (Unicode, since a tooltip is
374	// text), so the three the pointer is NOT on are explained where the eye is.
375	const srcRowKey = "\n\nThe symbols on every row, in order:\n" +
376		"🎥 footage — frames come out of it, and the cut is made of it\n" +
377		"🎤 narrator — which of the voices this is; 1 speaks the narration\n" +
378		"✂ split the voice off — ▶ separates it into the voice and the rest\n" +
379		"🗑 remove — off this list; the file itself is left alone"
380	
381	// ---- the rows ---------------------------------------------------------------
382	
383	func (s *sourceList) render() {
384		if s.box == nil {
385			return // headless, in tests
386		}
387		for {
388			row := s.box.RowAtIndex(0)
389			if row == nil {
390				break
391			}
392			s.box.Remove(row)
393		}
394		for i := range s.items {
395			s.box.Append(s.row(i))
396		}
397	}
398	
399	func (s *sourceList) row(i int) *gtk.Box {
400		it := s.items[i]
401	
402		// footage: what frames are taken from, and what the cut and the render are
403		// made of. On by default for a video file, off for a recording, and a
404		// toggle either way -- a capture wanted only for its sound is a video with
405		// this off, which is the case that used to need a second copy of the file
406		// in the other folder.
407		foot := gtk.NewToggleButton()
408		foot.SetIconName("camera-video-symbolic")
409		foot.AddCSSClass("flat")
410		foot.SetActive(it.footage)
411		// only a video can be footage, so on an audio file the toggle is dead
412		// rather than a button that silently never sticks
413		foot.SetSensitive(isVideo(it.path))
414		foot.SetTooltipText("Footage — frames come out of this file and it can be cut.\n" +
415			"Off: it is only listened to, which is what a video kept for its audio wants." + srcRowKey)
416		foot.ConnectToggled(func() { s.setFootage(i, foot.Active()) })
417	
418		// the narrator slot: a microphone, and the slot number once it holds one --
419		// which of the four voices this recording is. Untagged is the mic alone,
420		// dimmed; a placeholder dash was just one more thing to decode. Click cycles.
421		narr := gtk.NewButton()
422		narr.AddCSSClass("flat")
423		nb := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 2)
424		nb.Append(gtk.NewImageFromIconName("audio-input-microphone-symbolic"))
425		// the slot number, and the room for one whether or not there is a number
426		// to put in it: the label is always there and always a character wide, so
427		// an untagged row is exactly as wide as a tagged one. Built the other way
428		// -- the label appended only when there is a slot -- the button was two
429		// sizes, and every file name in the list started at whichever x its own
430		// row happened to give it.
431		slot := gtk.NewLabel("")
432		slot.SetWidthChars(1)
433		if it.narrator > 0 {
434			slot.SetText(strconv.Itoa(it.narrator))
435		} else {
436			nb.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
437		}
438		nb.Append(slot)
439		narr.SetChild(nb)
440		if it.narrator == 1 {
441			narr.AddCSSClass("suggested-action") // the voice the narration is spoken in
442		}
443		narr.SetTooltipText("Narrator — click to cycle through the free slots and back to none.\n" +
444			"1 is the voice the narration is spoken in; 2–4 are the rest of the group." + srcRowKey)
445		narr.ConnectClicked(func() { s.cycleNarrator(i) })
446	
447		// an ellipsizing label: a recorder filename is 50 characters, and a row
448		// that insists on all of them sets a floor under the whole window
449		lbl := gtk.NewLabel(it.name())
450		lbl.SetXAlign(0)
451		lbl.SetHExpand(true)
452		lbl.SetEllipsize(pango.EllipsizeMiddle)
453		lbl.SetTooltipText(it.path) // sources come from anywhere; the name alone can repeat
454	
455		// split the voice off: the recording becomes two rows -- itself without the
456		// voice, and the voice on its own. A flag, because the separation is a
457		// model on the server and minutes of it, so the press that starts work is
458		// ▶ like every other minute this page spends. Toggled on it is loud, so a
459		// row waiting for it is visible from across the list.
460		sep := gtk.NewToggleButton()
461		sep.SetIconName("edit-cut-symbolic")
462		sep.AddCSSClass("flat")
463		sep.SetActive(it.sepVoice)
464		sep.SetTooltipText("Split the voice off — on ▶ this recording is separated into the\n" +
465			"voice and everything else. This row keeps everything else; the voice\n" +
466			"is added as a track of its own, so it can be cut and mixed apart." + srcRowKey)
467		sep.ConnectToggled(func() { s.setSepVoice(i, sep.Active()) })
468		// a row that IS a half of a split has no voice left to take off a voice,
469		// so its scissors are dead -- greyed rather than gone. Removed from the
470		// row entirely they took their column with them, and in a list where some
471		// rows are split products and some are not, the trash beside them sat at
472		// two different x.
473		sep.SetSensitive(!splitProduct(it.path))
474	
475		del := flatIcon("user-trash-symbolic", "Remove from this session — the file itself is left alone"+srcRowKey, func() { s.remove(i) })
476	
477		row := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 4)
478		row.SetMarginStart(6)
479		row.SetMarginEnd(2)
480		row.Append(foot)
481		row.Append(narr)
482		row.Append(lbl)
483		// only for a file that holds more than one audio track: an ordinary
484		// recording has nothing to choose and gets no button (trackButton)
485		if tb := s.trackButton(i); tb != nil {
486			row.Append(tb)
487		}
488		// sources align on the wall clock, and the clock comes out of the name --
489		// a file without one is stacked at the session's start and has to be lined
490		// up by hand. That deserves a flag on the row, not a failed run.
491		if _, ok := nameStamp(it.name()); !ok {
492			warn := gtk.NewImageFromIconName("dialog-warning-symbolic")
493			warn.AddCSSClass("stamp-warn")
494			warn.SetTooltipText("No timestamp in the file name — this file starts where the\n" +
495				"session does, which is only right if it was rolling from the start.\n" +
496				"Rename it with when the recording STARTED, like\n" +
497				"clip_2026-08-08_19-55-15.mkv — most recorders already do — or drag it\n" +
498				"into place with the right mouse button on the Cut page.")
499			row.Append(warn)
500		}
501		row.Append(sep)
502		row.Append(del)
503		return row
504	}

908	// frameChangeScores diffs consecutive frames at postage-stamp size; local
909	// maxima are scene-change candidates.
910	//
911	// The decoding is Go's own and not GdkPixbuf's, deliberately: this runs on a
912	// worker goroutine (a long recording is hundreds of frames and the caller must
913	// not stall the window), and every pixbuf is a GObject whose reference
914	// bookkeeping gotk4 finishes back on the main loop. Making and dropping
915	// hundreds of them off the main thread raced that bookkeeping and corrupted the
916	// heap -- GLib said so by the hundred lines (g_atomic_rc_box_release_full:
917	// assertion 'real_box->magic == G_BOX_MAGIC' failed) before the abort landed in
918	// an unrelated finalizer. image/jpeg touches nothing but Go memory, so it is
919	// safe anywhere. Thumbnails on screen (ed.thumb) stay on pixbufs: those are
920	// made on the main thread, where they belong.
921	func frameChangeScores(frames []string) []float64 {
922		out := make([]float64, len(frames))
923		var prev []byte
924		for i, f := range frames {
925			px := framePostage(f)
926			if px == nil {
927				continue
928			}
929			if prev != nil && len(prev) == len(px) {
930				sum := 0
931				for j := 0; j < len(px); j++ {
932					d := int(px[j]) - int(prev[j])
933					if d < 0 {
934						d = -d
935					}
936					sum += d
937				}
938				out[i] = float64(sum) / float64(len(px))
939			}
940			prev = append(prev[:0], px...)
941		}
942		return out
943	}
944	
945	// postage size: what a scene change has to survive being shrunk to before we
946	// call it one. Small enough that camera noise and a wobbling hand average out,
947	// big enough that a person walking through the shot moves a box or two.
948	const postW, postH = 24, 14
949	
950	// framePostage reads one frame down to a postW x postH grid of brightness,
951	// each cell the average of the whole box of source pixels under it, so a moved
952	// edge changes a cell instead of falling between two sampled points. It returns
953	// nil for anything it cannot read -- a half-written frame, a format the
954	// stdlib does not know -- and the caller then leaves that frame's score at zero.
955	func framePostage(file string) []byte {
956		f, err := os.Open(file)
957		if err != nil {
958			return nil
959		}
960		defer f.Close()
961		img, _, err := image.Decode(f)
962		if err != nil {
963			return nil
964		}
965		b := img.Bounds()
966		if b.Dx() <= 0 || b.Dy() <= 0 {
967			return nil
968		}
969		sum := make([]int, postW*postH)
970		cnt := make([]int, postW*postH)
971		// jpeg decodes to YCbCr, whose Y plane already is the brightness -- reading
972		// it straight is worth it here, where the loop runs over every pixel of
973		// every frame of the recording
974		yc, _ := img.(*image.YCbCr)
975		for y := b.Min.Y; y < b.Max.Y; y++ {
976			row := (y - b.Min.Y) * postH / b.Dy() * postW
977			for x := b.Min.X; x < b.Max.X; x++ {
978				k := row + (x-b.Min.X)*postW/b.Dx()
979				if yc != nil {
980					sum[k] += int(yc.Y[yc.YOffset(x, y)])
981				} else {
982					r, g, bl, _ := img.At(x, y).RGBA()
983					sum[k] += int((r + 2*g + bl) / 4 >> 8)
984				}
985				cnt[k]++
986			}
987		}
988		px := make([]byte, postW*postH)
989		for k := range px {
990			if cnt[k] > 0 {
991				px[k] = byte(sum[k] / cnt[k])
992			}
993		}
994		return px
995	}
996	
997	// ---- geometry --------------------------------------------------------------
998	
999	// tlSpan is one filmed stretch of the session and where it is drawn. The axis
1000	// is TIME, not the recordings laid end to end: two cameras rolling through the
1001	// same minute share one x. Unfilmed time collapses to nothing.
1002	type tlSpan struct {
1003		t0, t1 float64 // the session seconds this run covers
1004		px     float64 // where t0 is on the timeline
1005		// this stretch is FOLDED: drawn at no width at all however long it is, so
1006		// the footage either side of it meets (cut_fold.go). A filmed run is cut

1011	// dur is the run's length in seconds.
1012	func (s tlSpan) dur() float64 { return s.t1 - s.t0 }

1014	// timeSpans is that union: the filmed runs, in order, none touching.
1015	func timeSpans(vids []tlVideo) []tlSpan {
1016		raw := make([]tlSpan, 0, len(vids))
1017		for _, v := range vids {
1018			if v.dur > 0 {
1019				raw = append(raw, tlSpan{t0: v.start, t1: v.start + v.dur})
1020			}
1021		}
1022		// ed.vids is sorted by start, but a lane shifted in time by hand is not,
1023		// and the merge below is only right on a sorted list
1024		sort.Slice(raw, func(i, j int) bool { return raw[i].t0 < raw[j].t0 })
1025		var out []tlSpan
1026		for _, r := range raw {
1027			if n := len(out); n > 0 && r.t0 <= out[n-1].t1 {
1028				out[n-1].t1 = math.Max(out[n-1].t1, r.t1)
1029				continue // this one carries on where the run so far had got to
1030			}
1031			out = append(out, r)
1032		}
1033		return out
1034	}

1036	// runs is the filmed stretches, laid out or not. relayout caches them with
1037	// their pixel origins, and everything that draws reads that cache; anything
1038	// that only wants the TIMES -- what got dropped, what a selection can cover --
1039	// asks here instead, so it still answers on an editor that has no widgets and
1040	// has never been laid out.
1041	func (ed *cutEditor) runs() []tlSpan {

1043			return ed.filmed
1044		}
1045		return timeSpans(ed.vids)

1048	// assignLanes is which row each recording is drawn on: one camera's files share
1049	// a row, a camera rolling through another gets its own. Greedy interval
1050	// colouring in start order. pin (cutFile.Rows) holds rows chosen by hand, so a
1051	// drag that ends an overlap does not collapse two cameras onto one row.
1052	func assignLanes(vids []tlVideo, pin map[string]int) int {
1053		ord := make([]int, len(vids))
1054		for i := range ord {
1055			ord[i] = i
1056		}
1057		// ed.vids is sorted by start on load, but a row shifted in time by hand is
1058		// not, and colouring out of order would stack two recordings that do not
1059		// overlap
1060		sort.SliceStable(ord, func(a, b int) bool { return vids[ord[a]].start < vids[ord[b]].start })
1061		var rows [][][2]float64 // per row: the stretches already on it
1062		grow := func(r int) {
1063			for len(rows) <= r {
1064				rows = append(rows, nil)
1065			}
1066		}
1067		free := func(r int, s, e float64) bool {
1068			for _, iv := range rows[r] {
1069				if s < iv[1]-1e-9 && e > iv[0]+1e-9 {
1070					return false
1071				}
1072			}
1073			return true
1074		}
1075		put := func(v *tlVideo, r int) {
1076			grow(r)
1077			v.lane = r
1078			rows[r] = append(rows[r], [2]float64{v.start, v.start + v.dur})
1079		}
1080		// the written-down rows first and in full, so the greedy pass below sees
1081		// every row they claim, whichever end of the session they claim it at
1082		for _, i := range ord {
1083			if r, ok := pin[vids[i].base]; ok && r >= 0 {
1084				put(&vids[i], r)
1085			}
1086		}
1087		for _, i := range ord {
1088			v := &vids[i]
1089			if r, ok := pin[v.base]; ok && r >= 0 {
1090				continue // already placed above
1091			}
1092			// the lowest row that is already finished by the time this one begins.
1093			// Greedy in start order is optimal for interval colouring, and on a
1094			// session with no pins and no shifts it puts one camera's files back
1095			// on one row exactly as it always did.
1096			lane := len(rows)
1097			for r := range rows {
1098				if free(r, v.start, v.start+v.dur) {
1099					lane = r
1100					break
1101				}
1102			}
1103			put(v, lane)
1104		}
1105		return max(1, len(rows))
1106	}

1108	func (ed *cutEditor) relayout() {

1344	// syncScroll points the scrollbar at the timeline as it now is. It is also

1627	// (narrate_fxview.go) so the two cannot drift. Returns the clock now and the
1628	// high-water mark to keep; the caller stores the mark.
1629	func liveClock(playhead, posT float64, posAt time.Time, liveMax, rate float64, playing bool) (now, mark float64) {
1630		if !playing || posAt.IsZero() {
1631			return playhead, playhead // nothing to smooth; re-arm on the line itself
1632		}
1633		d := time.Since(posAt).Seconds()
1634		if d < 0 {
1635			d = 0
1636		}
1637		span := float64(playTick) / 1000
1638		if d > span {
1639			d = span
1640		}
1641		if v := posT + d*rate; v > liveMax {
1642			liveMax = v
1643		}
1644		if hi := posT + span*rate; liveMax > hi {
1645			liveMax = hi // a whole tick of headroom, and not one second more
1646		}
1647		return liveMax, liveMax
1648	}

1673	func (ed *cutEditor) skipGap() bool {

1682		}
1683		switch {
1684		case next < 0:
1685			// past the last clip: the finished video has ended, and stopping here
1686			// is what that looks like

1696			// landed yet is not fought tick after tick, but a seek that can never
1697			// land is not a seek in flight. It happens when the clip starts where

1700			// this same gap again. Ask once more, from the first second there is

1702			//

1723	// playable is t, or the first second at or after it that a recording covers.
1724	// A cut may name a second nobody filmed -- the model chooses from a timeline
1725	// where unfilmed time is written down as plainly as the rest -- and the player
1726	// has nothing to seek to there.
1727	func (ed *cutEditor) playable(t float64) float64 {
1728		if ed.videoAt(t) != nil {
1729			return t
1730		}
1731		best := math.Inf(1)
1732		for i := range ed.vids {
1733			if v := &ed.vids[i]; v.start >= t && v.start < best {
1734				best = v.start
1735			}
1736		}
1737		if math.IsInf(best, 1) {
1738			return t
1739		}
1740		return best
1741	}

1743	// walkOn carries playback from the end of one recording to the next.
1744	//
1745	// A row is several files in a line and the timeline is one clock over all of
1746	// them, so the end of a file is not the end of anything the page shows: ▶ ran
1747	// out of stream and the line stopped in the hatched strip between two
1748	// recordings, with the rest of the session still to the right of it.
1749	//
1750	// The strip is not played through. Nobody filmed those minutes -- there is
1751	// nothing there to watch -- and the page does not even draw them to scale
1752	// (cut_fold.go), so the line lands on the next recording's first frame and
1753	// keeps going, which is what the same press already does when the cut runs onto
1754	// another camera (followPlayback).
1755	//
1756	// Only after an END. A pause is a decision and stays one, and a stream nobody
1757	// started has nowhere to walk on to.
1758	func (ed *cutEditor) walkOn() bool {
1759		if ed.player == nil || !ed.player.ended || ed.hold.on {
1760			return false
1761		}
1762		t, v, ok := ed.nextPlay()
1763		if !ok {
1764			return false // the last recording has played out: that IS the end
1765		}
1766		if v == ed.playVideo && t <= ed.playhead {
1767			return false // the same file at the same second is not somewhere to go
1768		}
1769		ed.jumped = -1
1770		ed.setPlayhead(t)
1771		ed.cutOnlySnap() // ▶✂ carries on at the next KEPT clip, not the next frame
1772		if !ed.player.playing {
1773			// setPlayhead cues the player where it finds it, and it found it
1774			// stopped: what ended was the file, not the press
1775			ed.player.Toggle()
1776		}
1777		return true
1778	}

1780	// nextPlay is where that is: the second the line is already on when another
1781	// camera is still rolling through it, and otherwise the first frame of the next

1783	//
1784	// The recording that just ended is never the answer, whatever the clock says.
1785	// Two files written back to back -- a camera stopped and started again, a
1786	// recorder splitting by size -- meet at one second, and asking which recording
1787	// that second belongs to has two answers; the one we have just played out is
1788	// not the one to play next.
1789	func (ed *cutEditor) nextPlay() (float64, *tlVideo, bool) {
1790		t := ed.playhead
1791		if v := ed.videoAt(t); v != nil && v != ed.playVideo {
1792			return t, v, true
1793		}
1794		var best *tlVideo
1795		for i := range ed.vids {
1796			v := &ed.vids[i]
1797			if v == ed.playVideo || v.start < t-0.01 {
1798				continue
1799			}
1800			if best == nil || v.start < best.start {
1801				best = v
1802			}
1803		}
1804		if best == nil {
1805			return 0, nil, false
1806		}
1807		return math.Max(best.start, t), best, true
1808	}

1823	// followPlayback keeps the red line on the player's clock while it runs;
1824	// on pause the queries stop and the line simply stays put.

1827	// track. Called as the line moves under playback -- a rate change with no seek
1828	// on the way to carry it, which is the one case SetRate deliberately leaves to
1829	// its caller. SetRateNow asks the running pipeline for an instant rate change
1830	// and falls back to a flushing seek-in-place only where that is refused
1831	// (player.go has the story), so a ramp's stairs no longer each cost a hitch.
1832	func (ed *cutEditor) followPlayback() bool {

1834		// follow: the footage is held and the card runs on the wall clock instead

1836			ed.tickHold()
1837			return true
1838		}

1840		// the line walks on to the next one rather than stopping in the strip
1841		// between two files (walkOn)

1850			was := ed.playhead
1851			ed.playhead = ed.playVideo.sessionAt(pos)   // off included: a cut lane's window starts partway in
1852			ed.posT, ed.posAt = ed.playhead, time.Now() // the camera's clock; see livePlayhead
1853			ed.noteLine()                               // once a second of this, not ten (cut_line.go)
1854			ed.syncFxHold()                             // ▶ walks the line off whatever was picked up
1855			ed.showTime()

1857			// into comes open and stays open (cut_fold.go). ▶✂ never enters one.
1858			if !ed.cutOnly {

1907	func (ed *cutEditor) xOf(t float64) float64 {
1908		for _, s := range ed.spans {
1909			if t <= s.t1 {
1910				if t < s.t0 {
1911					return s.px // in an unfilmed stretch: the next run's edge
1912				}
1913				if s.fold {
1914					return s.px // a folded cell has no width: every second in it is the seam
1915				}
1916				return s.px + (t-s.t0)*ed.pps
1917			}
1918		}
1919		return ed.totalW
1920	}
1921	
1922	func (ed *cutEditor) tAt(x float64) float64 {
1923		if len(ed.spans) == 0 {
1924			return 0 // nothing loaded: every x on an empty track is time zero
1925		}
1926		for _, s := range ed.spans {
1927			if x < s.px {
1928				return s.t0 // left of the first run: the gutter, which is not tape
1929			}
1930			w := ed.spanW(s)
1931			if s.fold && x <= s.px+w {
1932				// a seam is one x standing for the whole gap; a press on it is
1933				// its first second, which is where the footage stops being kept
1934				return s.t0
1935			}
1936			// half-open on the right, because unfilmed time takes no width: the x
1937			// where one recording stops is the x where the next one starts, and it
1938			// reads as the second the LATER one begins. A press there is a press
1939			// on the take you can see there.
1940			if x < s.px+w {
1941				return s.t0 + (x-s.px)/ed.pps
1942			}
1943		}
1944		return ed.spans[len(ed.spans)-1].t1
1945	}

1947	// ontoFilm is the nearest second to t that a recording covers, in the direction
1948	// the edge is facing: a start moves FORWARD to where the next take begins, an
1949	// end moves BACK to where the last one stopped, so an edge never crosses the
1950	// footage it belongs to on its way out of a hole.
1951	func (ed *cutEditor) ontoFilm(t float64, isStart bool) float64 {
1952		best, dist := t, math.Inf(1)
1953		for i := range ed.vids {
1954			v := &ed.vids[i]
1955			c := v.start
1956			if !isStart {
1957				c = v.start + v.dur
1958			}
1959			if isStart && c < t || !isStart && c > t {
1960				continue
1961			}
1962			if d := math.Abs(c - t); d < dist {
1963				best, dist = c, d
1964			}
1965		}
1966		if math.IsInf(dist, 1) {
1967			// nothing that way: the other way is better than a second of nothing
1968			for i := range ed.vids {
1969				v := &ed.vids[i]
1970				for _, c := range []float64{v.start, v.start + v.dur} {
1971					if d := math.Abs(c - t); d < dist {
1972						best, dist = c, d
1973					}
1974				}
1975			}
1976		}
1977		return best
1978	}

1984	// thumbStep is how many frames apart the thumbnails on a row stand: one

1986	//
1987	// The width is whatever shape this source is. Assuming 16:9 for every source
1988	// left the row striped on a 4:3 capture, on a phone held upright, on anything
1989	// else odd -- the step was measured for a picture wider than the one that got
1990	// drawn, and what showed through between two frames was the band's own ground.
1991	// A source that has not said what shape it is keeps the old assumption, which
1992	// is right for most cameras and no worse than what it replaced.
1993	//

1995	// step is a stripe, and only one of those can be seen.
1996	func (v *tlVideo) thumbStep(th, pps float64) int {

1998		if v.w > 0 && v.h > 0 {
1999			ar = float64(v.w) / float64(v.h)
2000		}
2001		if v.interval <= 0 || pps <= 0 {

package main

// Where a retake's edges actually are.
//
// The ASR stamps a word to 80 ms, and on the first word after a silence the
// stamp runs late -- half a second late, measured, on a take's opening "And".
// A boundary placed on the stamp therefore lands INSIDE the word it was meant
// to precede, and whatever came out before it -- the breath, the false start
// the ASR folded away -- is kept.
//
// The waveform envelope already exists for the timeline, at 10 ms (waveHz),
// and for placing a cut it is the right instrument: what matters at a join is
// where sound starts and stops, not what the sound was. So the two edges of a
// mark are moved onto it. The cut ends where the last kept sound ends, and
// resumes where the retake's sound begins -- everything between goes, whatever
// it was, which is what "said again" means.
//
// The envelopes are built once per source and kept under cache/edges, apart
// from the timeline's own cache: that one is built to the page's channel count
// and this one is mono, and a file written to one reading must not be read by
// the other.

import (
	"math"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
)

const (
	// how far an edge may be moved off its stamp. A stamp half a second late
	// is what was measured; a sound a whole second away is a different sound.
	edgeReach = 0.8
	// what is left of a sound at a cut: a few buckets, so the last consonant
	// is not shaved and the first is not clipped
	edgePad = 0.05
	// how far behind its sound a stamp may run and still be that sound's:
	// half a second was measured on a take's opening word
	lateStamp = 0.6

	// With ALIGNED words the envelope's job changes: the words fence the cut
	// and the sound only chooses where inside the fence it falls.
	//
	// how far below a word's own level its tail still counts as the word.
	// On the meter scale the envelope is drawn in (-70..0 dBFS over 0..255),
	// a breath sits 20 dB or more under the word it follows, and a trailing
	// consonant a few dB under; twelve tells them apart.
	edgeTailDB = 12.0
	// how far past the aligner's edge a word's own sound is followed. The
	// aligner is within a fiftieth on an onset and can be a touch early on
	// a trailing s or k; a quarter second is that, and not the breath after.
	edgeTailMax = 0.25
	// how far into the gap the quietest moment is looked for. Past the
	// word's own tail the gap is breath and room; the cut goes where that
	// is lowest, and a trough further off than this is a different gap.
	troughReach = 0.4
)

// endAfter is where the cut ends after a word that stays, given the word and
// how far the cut may go (the next word's start, which it never reaches):
// the word's own sound followed to where it drops (edgeTailMax), then the
// quietest moment after that (troughReach). The words fence it; the sound
// chooses inside the fence. Without an envelope, a hair after the word.
func (e *edges) endAfter(w srcWord, limit float64) float64 {
	if limit <= w.e {
		return w.e
	}
	i0, i1 := e.at(w.s), e.at(w.e)
	lim := e.at(limit)
	if e == nil || i0 < 0 || i1 < 0 {
		return math.Min(w.e+wordPad, limit)
	}
	if lim < 0 {
		lim = len(e.wf.chans[0]) - 1
	}
	thr := e.tailLevel(i0, i1)
	end := i1
	for stop := min(lim, i1+int(edgeTailMax*e.wf.hz)); end < stop && e.sound(end, thr); end++ {
	}
	best := end
	for k := end; k <= min(lim, end+int(troughReach*e.wf.hz)); k++ {
		if e.wf.chans[0][k] < e.wf.chans[0][best] {
			best = k
		}
	}
	return math.Min(limit, math.Max(w.e, e.off+float64(best)/e.wf.hz))
}

// startBefore is the same the other way: where the cut resumes before a word
// that starts again, given how far back it may go (the last dropped word's
// end, which it never reaches).
func (e *edges) startBefore(w srcWord, limit float64) float64 {
	if limit >= w.s {
		return w.s
	}
	i0, i1 := e.at(w.s), e.at(w.e)
	lim := e.at(limit)
	if e == nil || i0 < 0 || i1 < 0 {
		return math.Max(w.s-wordPad, limit)
	}

		lim = 0
	}

	}

		}
	}

}

// tailLevel is what still counts as the word between buckets i0 and i1: its
// own peak less edgeTailDB, and never under the room (floor).
func (e *edges) tailLevel(i0, i1 int) uint8 {
	peak := uint8(0)
	for k := i0; k <= i1 && k < len(e.wf.chans[0]); k++ {
		peak = max(peak, e.wf.chans[0][k])
	}
	thr := int(peak) - int(math.Round(edgeTailDB*255/70))
	return uint8(max(thr, int(e.floor(e.off+float64(i0)/e.wf.hz))))
}

// edges is the envelope of one source, mono, with the source's place in the
// session so a session second can be looked up in it.
type edges struct {
	wf  *waveform
	off float64 // session second the file's first sample lands on
}

// loadEdges reads or builds the envelope for a source.
func (a *App) loadEdges(path string, off float64) *edges {
	wf, err := loadWave(filepath.Join(a.outDir, "cache", "edges"),
		tlAudio{base: baseName(path), path: path, chans: 1})
	if err != nil || wf == nil || len(wf.chans) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return &edges{wf: wf, off: off}
}

// at is the bucket a session second falls in, or -1 outside the file.
func (e *edges) at(t float64) int {
	i := int((t - e.off) * e.wf.hz)
	if i < 0 || i >= len(e.wf.chans[0]) {
		return -1
	}
	return i
}

// floor is what counts as sound around a point: the quiet of that stretch of
// the recording, with room over it. Measured on the buckets around t rather
// than fixed, because a room, a microphone and a gain setting each put the
// silence somewhere else -- and taken from the quieter end of the window, so
// a window that is mostly talking still finds its floor.
func (e *edges) floor(t float64) uint8 {
	i := e.at(t)
	if i < 0 {
		return 255
	}
	lo, hi := max(0, i-400), min(len(e.wf.chans[0]), i+400) // ±4 s
	win := append([]uint8(nil), e.wf.chans[0][lo:hi]...)
	sort.Slice(win, func(a, b int) bool { return win[a] < win[b] })
	quiet := int(win[len(win)/5]) // the 20th percentile is the room
	return uint8(min(255, max(quiet*3, quiet+8)))
}

// sound is whether bucket i is above the floor.
func (e *edges) sound(i int, thr uint8) bool {
	return i >= 0 && i < len(e.wf.chans[0]) && e.wf.chans[0][i] >= thr
}

// endBefore is where the last sound before session second t ends: the cut
// ends there. t is the stamp of the first abandoned word, which may fall inside

	return max(e.off, e.off+float64(j)/e.wf.hz-edgePad)
}
package main

// The spelling the subtitles carry.
//
// The words a subtitle is built from come off the ALIGNER: it is handed the
// recogniser's transcript and answers where each word falls, to about 20 ms,
// which is the only source of times in the app accurate enough to caption with
// (wordCues). What it hands back is bare lowercase, so dressWords puts the
// case and punctuation back from the transcript it was given -- the raw one,
// straight off the speech model.
//
// And that is where the session context stopped. The transcript pass reads it
// ("use the script's spelling for names, companies and numbers I say aloud")
// and writes what it settled on into the session timeline; the subtitles never
// read that file, so they went on saying what the recogniser heard. One
// recogniser writes "rsa two hundred and sixty" where another writes "RSA-260"
// -- the same seconds of the same video, captioned two ways depending on which
// model was loaded that day, and the sentence in the user context asking for
// one of them had no effect on the subtitles at all.
//
// fixWords closes that: the words keep their times and take the transcript's
// spelling. It is a re-dressing and never a rewrite -- no word gains a time it
// did not have, and a stretch that cannot be matched keeps what the recogniser
// wrote rather than guessing.

import "strings"

// fixRunReach is how far apart the two spellings of one stretch may be before
// the walk gives up on it: "two hundred and sixty" against "RSA-260" is four
// words against one, and a window of six covers every rewrite of a number, a
// name or a company seen so far. Past it the walk has lost its place, and
// dressing the rest of the line from the wrong offset would put the right
// words on the wrong seconds.
const fixRunReach = 6

// fixWords re-dresses the aligned words with what the transcript pass wrote
// for the same seconds. rows are the merged timeline's (session.tsv): the
// fixed text, on the session clock, with the recording each line came off.
//
// Only .raw changes -- the word used for MATCHING (.w) stays the recogniser's,
// because every pass that reads the words reads that one, and only the
// subtitles read the other (wordCues).
func fixWords(words []srcWord, rows []tsvRow) {
	if len(words) == 0 || len(rows) == 0 {
		return
	}
	// a cursor per recording: the words and the rows are both in time order,
	// so each row picks up where the last one of its recording left off
	at := map[string]int{}
	idx := map[string][]int{}
	for i, w := range words {
		idx[w.src] = append(idx[w.src], i)
	}
	for _, r := range rows {
		if r.spk == "EVENT" || strings.TrimSpace(r.text) == "" {
			continue
		}
		in := idx[r.src]
		var mine []*srcWord
		k := at[r.src]
		for ; k < len(in); k++ {
			w := &words[in[k]]
			mid := (w.s + w.e) / 2
			if mid < r.s-0.01 {
				continue // said before this line: a word the row does not cover
			}
			if mid > r.e+0.01 {
				break
			}
			mine = append(mine, w)
		}
		at[r.src] = k
		redress(mine, strings.Fields(r.text))
	}
}

// redress walks one line's words against one line's fixed text and hands each
// word its spelling. Where the two spell a stretch differently, the whole of
// the fixed spelling goes on the FIRST word of the stretch and the rest are
// emptied: every word keeps its own seconds, so a cut through the middle of
// such a stretch loses the words rather than showing words the video does not
// play -- which is the one thing subtitles built from the aligner exist to
// prevent.
func redress(ws []*srcWord, fixed []string) {
	// A line with NOTHING in common is not a line that was respelled: it is a
	// line the walk should not be trusted with -- a row matched to the wrong
	// recording's words, a clock that moved under one of them. Left as it was
	// heard, it is one line captioned the way it always was; rewritten from a
	// text that shares no word with it, it is the wrong words on these
	// seconds. One word in common is enough to believe the pairing.
	if !anyShared(ws, fixed) {
		return
	}
	pending := "" // fixed words with no time of their own, waiting for one
	put := func(w *srcWord, s string) {
		w.raw = strings.TrimSpace(pending + s)
		pending = ""
	}
	i, j := 0, 0
	for i < len(ws) && j < len(fixed) {
		if bareWord(fixed[j]) == ws[i].w {
			put(ws[i], fixed[j])
			i, j = i+1, j+1
			continue
		}
		di, dj, ok := fixResync(ws, fixed, i, j)
		switch {
		case !ok:
			// nothing within reach spells the same: the walk takes them as
			// the same word anyway -- it is the same position in a line that
			// matched either side of here -- and the transcript's spelling
			// wins, which is the whole point. "RSA-1024" against a heard
			// "rsa" resyncs on neither and is the right word for that second.
			// The next word is matched normally, so a walk that really has
			// lost its place finds itself again rather than running on.
			put(ws[i], fixed[j])
			i, j = i+1, j+1
		case di == 0:
			// the transcript has words the recogniser never heard: they have
			// no seconds, so they ride on the next word that does
			pending += strings.Join(fixed[j:j+dj], " ") + " "
			j += dj
		default:
			put(ws[i], strings.Join(fixed[j:j+dj], " "))
			for k := i + 1; k < i+di; k++ {
				ws[k].raw = ""
			}
			i, j = i+di, j+dj
		}
	}
	// whatever the line ends with and the words do not: onto the last word
	// that has a time, for the same reason
	if j < len(fixed) && len(ws) > 0 {
		last := ws[min(i, len(ws))-1]
		last.raw = strings.TrimSpace(last.raw + " " + strings.Join(fixed[j:], " "))
	}
	// ...and the other way round -- words left over when the line has run out.
	// They are the tail of a stretch the transcript folded into fewer words
	// ("two hundred and fifty" into "RSA-250"), and the fold is already
	// printed on the first of them: kept, they would be said twice.
	for ; i < len(ws); i++ {
		ws[i].raw = ""
	}
}

// anyShared is whether the two spellings of a line have a single word in
// common, which is what makes the walk below a re-dressing rather than a
// guess.
func anyShared(ws []*srcWord, fixed []string) bool {
	have := make(map[string]bool, len(ws))
	for _, w := range ws {
		have[w.w] = true
	}
	for _, f := range fixed {
		if have[bareWord(f)] {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// fixResync is the shortest pair of runs that puts the walk back in step: how
// many words of the recogniser's and how many of the transcript's to skip
// before the two spell the same word again. Shortest by total length, so one
// word against four is found before two against five.
func fixResync(ws []*srcWord, fixed []string, i, j int) (int, int, bool) {
	for d := 1; d <= 2*fixRunReach; d++ {
		for di := 0; di <= d && di <= fixRunReach; di++ {
			dj := d - di
			if dj > fixRunReach || i+di >= len(ws) || j+dj >= len(fixed) {
				continue
			}
			if bareWord(fixed[j+dj]) == ws[i+di].w {
				return di, dj, true
			}
		}
	}
	return 0, 0, false
}

package main

// Text edit: the cut of a read to camera, made as a text edit.
//
// A session recorded off a script is the speech and nothing else -- every word
// goes into the video except the mistakes in the saying: an attempt said
// again, a false start, a fragment left hanging. So the finished video is a
// SUBSEQUENCE of what was spoken, and choosing it is choosing words, not
// seconds. The model is handed the words and answers with the words; it never
// sees a clock. The cut follows from the aligner's times for the words that
// survive, and every boundary is a word edge by construction.
//
// That replaces the retake pass for this kind of session (styleRead), and the
// picture is never described: nothing about which words survive is in the
// picture, and describing it was the longest part of Prepare.

import (
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"regexp"
	"strings"
)

// the video styles, as the project stores them. Blank is the ordinary answer
// and every project written before this reads as it.
const (
	styleMoments = ""     // a session: the cut picks the moments, with the picture described
	styleRead    = "read" // a read to camera: the words are the video
)

// the two, as the page names them: Lecture first, since it is the one this
// editor is mostly for. The stored words stay what they were (styleRead,
// styleMoments), so a project written before the rename still reads.
var styleLabels = []string{"Lecture", "Gaming"}

// styleOf is the stored style for a dropdown index, and styleIndex the other
// way: Lecture is the read to camera, Gaming the session whose moments are
// picked.
func styleOf(i uint) string {
	if i == 0 {
		return styleRead
	}
	return styleMoments
}

func styleIndex(name string) uint {
	if name == styleRead {
		return 0
	}
	return 1
}

309			a.logfIdle("!!! text edit: join %d: %s -- nothing removed there", k+1, why)
310			return seamCut{}, hit, nil
311		}
312		if !hit {
313			a.keepReply("textedit", ask, reply)
314		}
315		return cut, hit, nil
316	}
