318	// seamCutOf turns the joined text back into how much comes off each side, or
319	// says why it cannot be used. at is the index, within win, of the first word of
320	// AFTER.
321	//
322	// The match is against WHAT WAS PRINTED, and that is the whole of the lesson
323	// here. The model reads seamWords: the spelling the transcript pass settled on.
324	// The words themselves carry a second spelling, the bare one the aligner heard,
325	// and for a while the answer was matched against that instead. They are not the
326	// same: the transcript folds a heard "das über datum" into a written "das
327	// Über-Datum.", and one German lecture had sixty-four words folded that way.
328	// Every fold looked to the match like a word the model had deliberately
329	// dropped, so every answer read as several separate stretches and was refused
330	// whole -- twenty-nine joins of a session, nought marks, while the very same
331	// answers matched against the printed forms give ten clean cuts with not one
332	// invented word between them.
333	//
334	// So the answer can only take words away, and what it may take words away from
335	// is exactly the text it was shown.
336	func seamCutOf(win []srcWord, at int, joined string) (seamCut, string) {
337		toks, owner := shownTokens(win)
338		ans := textTokens(joined)
339		if len(ans) == 0 {
340			return seamCut{}, "the answer has no words in it"
341		}
342		// keepMask walks the answer backwards against the words, which is what
343		// prefers the LATER of two sayings -- the rule the whole pass runs on
344		shown := make([]srcWord, len(toks))
345		for i, t := range toks {
346			shown[i].w = t
347		}
348		keptTok, _ := keepMask(shown, ans)
349		// a word survives if any of what was printed for it did: the transcript
350		// spells some single words as two, and half a spelling is not a deletion
351		kept := make([]bool, len(win))
352		for i, ok := range keptTok {
353			if ok {
354				kept[owner[i]] = true
355			}
356		}
357		// what it left out, stretch by stretch. There should be exactly one and it
358		// should be at the join; a second one somewhere else is the model editing
359		// prose, and the whole answer is refused over it.
360		//
361		// Except where that second one is a word or two, which is usually not a
362		// deletion at all. The model respells as it writes -- "Ein interessantes
363		// Gebiet" for a transcript that reads "Ein Interessensgebiet" -- and a word
364		// it spelled its own way matches nothing and reads here exactly as if it
365		// had been removed on purpose. Measured over two runs of a 42-minute
366		// lecture: taking those as respellings rather than removals turns four
367		// refusals into two and five into two, and gets one more join exactly right
368		// each time. It was the only change of several that held up across both.
369		first, last, other := -1, -1, 0
370		for i := 0; i < len(win); {
371			if kept[i] {
372				i++
373				continue
374			}
375			j := i
376			for j < len(win) && !kept[j] {
377				j++
378			}
379			switch {
380			case i <= at+seamSnap && j-1 >= at-1-seamSnap:
381				first, last = i, j-1 // the one at the join, which is the repair
382			case j-i > seamNoise:
383				other++
384			}
385			i = j
386		}
387		switch {
388		case first < 0 && other == 0:
389			return seamCut{}, "" // nothing left out, which is a whole answer
390		case first < 0:
391			return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("the %s left out is not at the join",
392				plural(other, "stretch"))
393		case other > 0:
394			return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("%d separate stretches left out, not one at the join", other+1)
395		}
396		// ...and the stretch has to be AT the join, which is what tells a repair
397		// apart from the model editing prose: a hole in the middle of BEFORE is the
398		// removal that takes the object out of a sentence, leaving something that
399		// parses and means nothing.
400		//
401		// Coming within a word or two of the join counts as being at it, and the
402		// rest of the way is closed here. A model that names "Das heißt, hier habe
403		// ich jeweils das Über-Datum." and leaves "datum und" standing against the
404		// stop has found the abandoned attempt and stopped short of its last
405		// syllables; the words it left are the end of that same attempt, and they
406		// are on the side the pass spends first. Refusing the whole answer over
407		// them is how the join everybody could see kept coming back.
408		if d := at - 1 - last; d > 0 {
409			if d > seamSnap {
410				return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("the stretch left out (%q) stops %d words short of the join",
411					seamWords(win[first:last+1]), d)
412			}
413			last = at - 1
414		}
415		if d := first - at; d > 0 {
416			if d > seamSnap {
417				return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("the stretch left out (%q) starts %d words past the join",
418					seamWords(win[first:last+1]), d)
419			}
420			first = at
421		}
422		if n := last - first + 1; n > seamMaxWords || float64(n) > seamCeil*float64(len(win)) {
423			return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("%d of the %d words left out -- that is not a repair",
424				n, len(win))
425		}
426		return seamCut{Before: at - first, After: last + 1 - at}, ""
427	}
428	
429	// shownTokens is the window as the model reads it: one entry per word of what
430	// seamWords printed, each saying which of the window's words it came from.
431	//
432	// Usually one token per word. Not always: where the transcript has words the
433	// recogniser never heard, they ride on the next word that does have a time
434	// (redress), so one word can print as two or three. Those tokens all point back
435	// at the same word, and the word goes only if the whole of it went.
436	func shownTokens(win []srcWord) (toks []string, owner []int) {
437		for i, w := range win {
438			n := 0
439			for _, f := range strings.Fields(seamWord(w)) {
440				if b := bareWord(f); b != "" {
441					toks = append(toks, b)
442					owner = append(owner, i)
443					n++
444				}
445			}
446			if n == 0 {
447				// nothing printable at all: a token of its own so the walk keeps
448				// its place, and one the answer will never match
449				toks = append(toks, "")
450				owner = append(owner, i)
451			}
452		}
453		return toks, owner
454	}
455	
456	// seamWords is one side of a join as the model reads it: the words as they are
457	// WRITTEN -- the case and punctuation the transcript pass settled on -- because
458	// the question is whether the join reads as a sentence, and a lower-case stream
459	// with no stops in it has no sentences to read. The match that follows is on
460	// the bare forms either way (textTokens), so what is shown here changes nothing
461	// about how an answer is understood.
462	func seamWords(ws []srcWord) string {
463		var b []string
464		for _, w := range ws {
465			b = append(b, seamWord(w))
466		}
467		return strings.Join(b, " ")
468	}
469	
470	// seamWord is one word as it is shown and as it is written out: the spelling
471	// the transcript pass settled on, or the bare one it was heard as where the
472	// fold left it none. Never empty -- a word with nothing to print is still a
473	// word of the recording, and leaving it out would shift every number after it
474	// off the word it names (seamNumbered).
475	func seamWord(w srcWord) string {
476		if w.raw != "" {
477			return w.raw
478		}
479		return w.w
480	}
481	
482	// writeFinalText writes the finished text: the words that survive, as they are
483	// written. It is the edit, and a person can read it -- or change it and cut
484	// again (marksFromText), which is why it is punctuated rather than the bare
485	// stream the match works in.
486	//
487	// Every join is marked, because a join is the only place in the file where
488	// anything can be wrong. |cut 10| is a join where ten words went; |cut| is one
489	// where the recording stopped and nothing went, which is worth seeing too --
490	// a stumble the pass walked past looks exactly like ordinary prose otherwise.
491	// Reading 29 marks and the few words either side of each is the check; reading
492	// five thousand words of continuous text is not.
493	//
494	// The marks come back out again on the way in (textTokens), so this file can be
495	// edited by hand and cut from with them left in or taken out.
496	func (a *App) writeFinalText(words []srcWord, drop []bool) error {
497		return os.WriteFile(a.finalText(), []byte(a.finishedText(words, drop)+"\n"), 0o644)
498	}
499	
500	// finishedText is what it writes, apart from the file, so that the marking can
501	// be read without a project on disk.
502	func (a *App) finishedText(words []srcWord, drop []bool) string {
503		var b []string
504		last, gone := "", 0
505		for i, w := range words {
506			if drop != nil && drop[i] {
507				gone++
508				continue
509			}
510			if last != "" && w.src != last {
511				if gone > 0 {
512					b = append(b, fmt.Sprintf("|cut %d|", gone))
513				} else {
514					b = append(b, "|cut|")
515				}
516			}
517			last, gone = w.src, 0
518			// a word whose spelling was folded into the one in front of it
519			// (redress): it keeps its seconds and stays in the video, but it has
520			// nothing of its own to print. The subtitles skip it for the same
521			// reason. This file used to fall back to the bare heard form instead
522			// -- seamWord, which the prompt needs so that every word makes a token
523			// -- and printed "Public-Key-Pairs. key pairs", the one spelling twice.
524			if w.raw == "" {
525				continue
526			}
527			b = append(b, w.raw)
528		}
529		return strings.Join(b, " ")
530	}
531	
532	// finalText is where the edit lives: the words of the finished video.
533	func (a *App) finalText() string { return filepath.Join(a.transcriptDir(), "final.txt") }
534	
535	// marksOfText is the mechanical half of the pass: the text matched back to
536	// the words, checked, and the dropped runs made into marks with their edges
537	// placed. false when the text is refused as an edit.
538	func (a *App) marksOfText(text string, words []srcWord, rows []tsvRow, paths []string) ([]retake, bool) {
539		kept, extra := keepMask(words, textTokens(text))
540		// ...and "keep the later" once more, at every join: a word left dangling
541		// on one side of a cut that the other side begins with is the same word
542		// twice in the video -- "...existing project and | and the more..." --
543		// whatever the model meant by leaving it
544		for _, n := range dedupeJoins(words, kept) {
545			a.logfIdle(">>> text edit: %s", n)
546		}
547		if extra > 0 {
548			a.logfIdle("!!! text edit: %d word(s) in the text were never said -- left out, there is no sound for them", extra)
549		}
550		dropped := 0
551		for _, k := range kept {
552			if !k {
553				dropped++
554			}
555		}
556		if float64(dropped) > retakeCeil*float64(len(words)) {
557			a.logfIdle("!!! text edit: %d of %d words removed -- refused, that is not an edit, nothing is marked", dropped, len(words))
558			return nil, false
559		}
560		// the runs that went, then their edges: fenced by the words either side,
561		// placed by the sound between them (placeEdges)
562		marks, notes := a.placeEdges(marksFrom(words, kept), paths, rows, words)
563		for _, n := range notes {
564			a.logfIdle(">>> text edit: %s", n)
565		}
566		marks = mergeMarks(marks)
567		for _, m := range marks {
568			a.logfIdle(">>> text edit: %s-%s goes (%q)", mmss(m.S), mmss(m.To), m.Text)
569		}
570		a.logfIdle(">>> text edit: %d of %d words removed in %d stretch(es)", dropped, len(words), len(marks))
571		return marks, true
572	}
573	
574	// marksFromText rebuilds the marks from a final.txt edited BY HAND: when the
575	// text is newer than the marks, the words in it are the edit and the marks
576	// are remade from them, no model asked. Delete a word in the file, save, press
577	// Cut, and it is out of the video -- which is the whole point of the text
578	// being a file. false when there is nothing newer to read.
579	func (a *App) marksFromText() ([]retake, bool) {
580		ti, err := os.Stat(a.finalText())
581		if err != nil {
582			return nil, false
583		}
584		if mi, err := os.Stat(a.retakeFile()); err == nil && !ti.ModTime().After(mi.ModTime()) {
585			return nil, false
586		}
587		text, err := os.ReadFile(a.finalText())
588		if err != nil {
589			return nil, false
590		}
591		vids, auds := a.snapSources()
592		paths := append(vids, auds...)
593		words := a.spokenWords(paths)
594		if len(words) == 0 {
595			return nil, false
596		}
597		a.logf(">>> final.txt was edited after Prepare -- the marks are remade from it, no model asked")
598		marks, ok := a.marksOfText(string(text), words, a.sessionRows(), paths)
599		if !ok {
600			return nil, false
601		}
602		if err := a.writeRetakes(marks); err != nil {
603			a.logf("!!! could not write the marks: %v", err)
604		}
605		return marks, true
606	}

608	// spokenWords is the session's words that the video plays: everything but the
609	// narrator's own microphone, which the video never plays (tlLabel).
610	func (a *App) spokenWords(paths []string) []srcWord {
611		narr := a.narratorMic()
612		var out []srcWord
613		for _, w := range a.sessionWords(paths) {
614			if narr == "" || w.src != narr {
615				out = append(out, w)
616			}
617		}
618		return out
619	}
620	
621	// textTokens is the answer as words: whatever it was wrapped in, bare and
622	// lowercase like the words it was made from, with the markers left out.
623	func textTokens(reply string) []string {
624		var out []string
625		reply = pauseMark.ReplaceAllString(reply, " ")
626		for _, f := range strings.Fields(reply) {
627			// the join marks final.txt is written with, and the one the whole-text
628			// pass used to write. Never a word anyone said: a pipe does not occur
629			// in a transcript, so the test can be the character rather than the
630			// exact spelling, and a mark a hand has mangled still goes.
631			if f == "SEAM" || strings.Contains(f, "|") {
632				continue
633			}
634			if w := bareWord(f); w != "" {
635				out = append(out, w)
636			}
637		}
638		return out
639	}
640	
641	// pauseMark is the pause marker as the brief writes it, echoed or not.
642	var pauseMark = regexp.MustCompile(`\(pause [0-9.]+s\)`)
643	
644	// keepMask is which of the words the answer kept, and how many of the
645	// answer's words were never said.
646	//
647	// Matched from the END backwards, on purpose. The same words occur twice
648	// wherever there was a retake, and an answer that keeps them once could be
649	// matched to either; walked forwards it would take the earlier -- the
650	// abandoned attempt -- every time. Walked backwards it takes the later, which
651	// is the one that stays, and the rule "prefer the second" is not a request
652	// to the model but the shape of the match.
653	func keepMask(words []srcWord, out []string) ([]bool, int) {
654		kept := make([]bool, len(words))
655		extra := 0
656		i := len(words) - 1
657		for j := len(out) - 1; j >= 0; j-- {
658			k := i
659			for ; k >= 0 && i-k < keepReach && words[k].w != out[j]; k-- {
660			}
661			if k < 0 || i-k >= keepReach {
662				extra++ // nothing said matches this: it was not said
663				continue
664			}
665			kept[k] = true
666			i = k - 1
667		}
668		return kept, extra
669	}
670	
671	// keepReach is how many words back the match may look for the answer's next
672	// word: past it, the word was not said and the answer moves on. A dropped
673	// stretch is a sentence or two, and two hundred words is a minute of speech.
674	const keepReach = 200
675	
676	// dedupeJoins drops the kept words before a cut that the kept words after it
677	// begin with, up to joinReach of them, and says which. The later saying stays,
678	// exactly as the match prefers it (keepMask) -- the match cannot see this one
679	// because the model kept both.
680	func dedupeJoins(words []srcWord, kept []bool) []string {
681		var notes []string
682		for j := 1; j < len(words); j++ {
683			if kept[j] || !kept[j-1] {
684				continue // not the first dropped word of a run
685			}
686			k := j
687			for k < len(words) && !kept[k] {
688				k++
689			}
690			if k >= len(words) {
691				break
692			}
693			// the kept words before the run, and after it
694			var before, after []int
695			for i := j - 1; i >= 0 && kept[i] && len(before) < joinReach; i-- {
696				before = append([]int{i}, before...)
697			}
698			for i := k; i < len(words) && kept[i] && len(after) < joinReach; i++ {
699				after = append(after, i)
700			}
701			for n := min(len(before), len(after)); n > 0; n-- {
702				same := true
703				for x := 0; x < n && same; x++ {
704					same = sameWord(words[before[len(before)-n+x]].w, words[after[x]].w)
705				}
706				if same {
707					for _, i := range before[len(before)-n:] {
708						kept[i] = false
709					}
710					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q said again straight after the cut -- the earlier one goes",
711						mmss(words[before[len(before)-n]].s), shortWords(words[before[len(before)-n]:before[len(before)-1]+1])))
712					break
713				}
714			}
715		}
716		return notes
717	}
718	
719	// joinReach is how many words either side of a join are compared: a doubled
720	// word or two is a join's own stumble; a whole sentence twice is a retake, and
721	// the model's to find.
722	const joinReach = 3
723	
724	// marksFrom is the dropped stretches as marks: each a run of words that went,
725	// from the first to the last, with the word that resumes named. The edges
726	// themselves are placed afterwards, exactly as a retake's are (placeEdges).
727	func marksFrom(words []srcWord, kept []bool) []retake {
728		var out []retake
729		for i := 0; i < len(words); {
730			if kept[i] {
731				i++
732				continue
733			}
734			j := i
735			for j < len(words) && !kept[j] {
736				j++
737			}
738			m := retake{S: words[i].s, E: words[j-1].e, To: words[j-1].e, Text: shortWords(words[i:j])}
739			if j < len(words) {
740				m.Again = words[j].s
741			}
742			out = append(out, m)
743			i = j
744		}
745		return out
746	}
747	
748	// textCut is the cut of a read to camera: every filmed second, minus the
749	// marks, minus the dead air. No model -- the words decided, in Prepare.
750	//
751	// Only the arithmetic. What it is given is the editor's state as values --
752	// the inserts it already holds, the filmed runs, where the talking is -- and
753	// what it hands back is segments and two numbers for the log; putting them on
754	// the page is the page's job (applyTextCut). It used to reach into the editor
755	// itself, undo stack and status line included, which made a file about words
756	// the one logic file that drove a widget.
757	func (a *App) textCut(marks []retake, inserts []cutSeg, runs []tlSpan, talk [][2]float64) (segs []cutSeg, marked int, dead float64) {
758		segs = insertsOf(inserts)
759		// each filmed run trimmed to its words: a recording starts rolling
760		// before the first word and stops after the last, and neither stretch
761		// is the video. The same fenced placement a cut gets (endAfter,
762		// startBefore), with the run's own edge as the fence.
763		vids, auds := a.snapSources()
764		paths := append(vids, auds...)
765		words := a.spokenWords(paths)
766		edgeOf := a.edgeLookup(paths, a.sessionRows())
767		for _, r := range runs {
768			segs = append(segs, trimRunToWords(cutSeg{S: r.t0, E: r.t1}, words, edgeOf))
769		}
770		marked = dropMarked(&segs, marks)
771		dead = dropDeadAir(&segs, talk)
772		return segs, marked, dead
773	}
774	
775	// trimRunToWords is a filmed run cut down to its speech: from just before its
776	// first word to just after its last, placed by the sound within troughReach
777	// of each and never outside the run. A run with no words in it stands as it
778	// is -- footage with nothing said over it is still footage.
779	func trimRunToWords(seg cutSeg, words []srcWord, edgeOf func(float64) *edges) cutSeg {
780		var first, last *srcWord
781		for i := range words {
782			w := &words[i]
783			if w.s < seg.S-0.01 || w.e > seg.E+0.01 {
784				continue
785			}
786			if first == nil {
787				first = w
788			}
789			last = w
790		}
791		if first == nil {
792			return seg
793		}
794		s := math.Max(seg.S, first.s-wordPad)
795		if e := edgeOf(first.s); e != nil {
796			s = e.startBefore(*first, math.Max(seg.S, first.s-troughReach))
797		}
798		t := math.Min(seg.E, last.e+wordPad)
799		if e := edgeOf(last.e); e != nil {
800			t = e.endAfter(*last, math.Min(seg.E, last.e+troughReach))
801		}
802		return cutSeg{S: s, E: t}
803	}

2338	// camName is how a camera is referred to in a sentence: the row's first
2339	// recording, which is the name written on its own band. Falls back to the row
2340	// number when the row is empty, which is a session that has just lost a camera.
2341	func (ed *cutEditor) camName(lane int) string {
2342		for _, v := range ed.vids {
2343			if v.lane == lane {
2344				return v.base
2345			}
2346		}
2347		return fmt.Sprintf("row %d", lane+1)
2348	}
2349	
2350	// insDefault is how long an insert runs when nothing in the file says. A card
2351	// nobody reads in four seconds is a card that was too wordy to be a card.
2352	const insDefault = 4.0
2353	
2354	// addInsert drops a file onto the timeline at t. The cut is a sequence, so the
2355	// footage under it gives way: the segment is split around it, as Remove would,
2356	// and the insert takes the seconds between. Undoable. Landing in a gap between
2357	// recordings costs nothing.
2358	func (ed *cutEditor) addInsert(path string, t, dur float64, mute bool) {
2359		ed.layOver(cutSeg{S: t, E: t + dur, Ins: path, Mute: mute, Cam: ed.sel.lane})
2360	}
2361	
2362	// addSound lays a stretch of a sound file over the footage at t: for dur
2363	// seconds what is heard is the file from ss; the picture is untouched and the
2364	// video no longer. Returns how many stretches of footage it landed on (see
2365	// layOverSound).
2366	func (ed *cutEditor) addSound(path string, t, dur, ss float64, lane string) int {
2367		return ed.layOverSound(cutSeg{S: t, E: t + dur, Ins: path, Ss: ss, Lane: lane})
2368	}
2369	
2370	// layOver is the cut taking one insert over the footage, with the undo step
2371	// and the save both ways of arriving here owe. Two ways arrive: a file chosen
2372	// from disk and a stretch of a lane copied out of the session. What differs
2373	// between them is what is IN the segment, never what the cut does with it, so
2374	// the doing is written once.
2375	func (ed *cutEditor) layOver(s cutSeg) {
2376		if s.E-s.S < minSegLn {
2377			s.E = s.S + insDefault
2378		}
2379		ed.pushUndo()
2380		ed.removeSpan(s.S, s.E)
2381		ed.segs = append(ed.segs, s)
2382		ed.coalesce()
2383		ed.persist()
2384	}
2385	
2386	// under this a piece is not worth a segment of its own: the sound would be a
2387	// blink, and the footage either side of it would have been split for nothing.
2388	const sndMinLn = 0.05
2389	
2390	// layOverSound lays a sound over the footage without moving the picture. The
2391	// span is cut to what the cut already keeps and one sound goes over each piece
2392	// with its own offset, so it never puts dropped footage back or displaces a
2393	// card. Splits are exact (no minimum-scene guard). Returns how many pieces.
2394	func (ed *cutEditor) layOverSound(s cutSeg) int {
2395		if s.E-s.S < minSegLn {
2396			s.E = s.S + insDefault
2397		}
2398		out, n := make([]cutSeg, 0, len(ed.segs)+2), 0
2399		for _, f := range ed.segs {
2400			t0, t1 := math.Max(f.S, s.S), math.Min(f.E, s.E)
2401			if f.isInsert() || t1-t0 < sndMinLn {
2402				out = append(out, f)
2403				continue
2404			}
2405			if t0 > f.S {
2406				out = append(out, cutSeg{S: f.S, E: t0})
2407			}
2408			// Ss walks with the piece: the second of the file this piece begins at
2409			// is as far into it as the piece is into the span asked for, so two
2410			// pieces either side of a hole are two parts of one sound and not the
2411			// same opening seconds played twice. Lane does not walk -- every piece
2412			// stands in for the same recording, because the lane was named once
2413			// for the whole span and a hole in the footage is no reason to change
2414			// its mind.
2415			out = append(out, cutSeg{S: t0, E: t1, Ins: s.Ins, Ss: s.Ss + t0 - s.S, Lane: s.Lane})
2416			if t1 < f.E {
2417				out = append(out, cutSeg{S: t1, E: f.E})
2418			}
2419			n++
2420		}
2421		if n == 0 {
2422			return 0
2423		}
2424		ed.pushUndo()
2425		ed.segs = out
2426		ed.coalesce()
2427		ed.persist()
2428		return n
2429	}
2430	
2431	// addSplice drops a file BETWEEN the footage: the clip is cut open at t, the
2432	// card runs for dur, the footage picks up where it left off. It takes no
2433	// session time, so it is stored as a point (S == E) with its length in Dur.
2434	func (ed *cutEditor) addSplice(path string, t, dur float64, mute bool, cam int) {
2435		if dur < minSegLn {
2436			dur = insDefault
2437		}
2438		ed.pushUndo()
2439		ed.segs = append(ed.segs, cutSeg{S: t, E: t, Ins: path, Dur: dur, Mute: mute, Cam: cam})
2440		ed.coalesce()
2441		ed.persist()
2442	}
2443	
2444	// A copied selection is an insert whose "file" is the session itself:
2445	// copy:SECONDS, the footage second it plays from, length in Dur. It gets every
2446	// behaviour a card has and costs one case at render time (see produce). No file
2447	// can shadow the scheme: insert paths are project-relative and no admitted
2448	// suffix contains ":".
2449	const copyScheme = "copy:"
2450	
2451	// copySrc is the footage second a copy starts at, and whether ins is one.
2452	func copySrc(ins string) (float64, bool) {
2453		if !strings.HasPrefix(ins, copyScheme) {
2454			return 0, false
2455		}
2456		t, err := strconv.ParseFloat(ins[len(copyScheme):], 64)
2457		return t, err == nil && t >= 0
2458	}
2459	
2460	func (s cutSeg) isCopy() bool {
2461		_, ok := copySrc(s.Ins)
2462		return ok
2463	}
2464	
2465	// audioIns says this insert is sound alone: an audio file placed on the cut.
2466	// Its picture is the session's own, which is why its marker is drawn in the
2467	// audio lanes and not in the picture band.
2468	func (s cutSeg) audioIns() bool {
2469		return s.isInsert() && insKind(s.Ins) == "audio"
2470	}
2471	
2472	// The two readings of Mute, which is one flag because it is one sentence --
2473	// this insert brings no sound of its own -- and two behaviours because the mode
2474	// already says what is underneath it.
2475	//
2476	// keepsSoundUnder: the cut was NOT opened for it, so the footage it covers is
2477	// still there being heard. Only the picture is replaced, and the render takes
2478	// the sound from the recording instead of from the file (produce.go, the isInsert
2479	// case, which puts it in prodClip.snd exactly where an audio insert's file
2480	// would go).
2481	//
2482	// playsSilent: the cut WAS opened for it, so there is nothing underneath to
2483	// keep and no sound anywhere in the slot. clipInput reports the input as having
2484	// no audio and the silence comes from anullsrc, the same way a held frame's
2485	// does.
2486	func (s cutSeg) keepsSoundUnder() bool { return s.isInsert() && s.Mute && !s.spliced() }
2487	func (s cutSeg) playsSilent() bool     { return s.isInsert() && s.Mute && s.spliced() }
2488	
2489	// insName is what an insert is called on the track and in the status line: the
2490	// file's name, or, for a copy, the footage it plays again -- a copy has no file
2491	// to name, and the seconds are how the eye finds the original.
2492	func insName(s cutSeg) string {
2493		if from, ok := copySrc(s.Ins); ok {
2494			return "copy of " + mmss(from)
2495		}
2496		return insBase(s.Ins)
2497	}
2498	
2499	// applyInsert puts the Edit dialog's answer into the cut -- words, mode, length
2500	// -- as one undo step. Not a field assignment: going over the footage takes
2501	// seconds out of it, going between hands them back.
2502	func (ed *cutEditor) applyInsert(i int, ins string, m insMode) {
2503		if i < 0 || i >= len(ed.segs) || !ed.segs[i].isInsert() {
2504			return
2505		}
2506		if m.dur < minSegLn {
2507			m.dur = insDefault
2508		}
2509		ed.pushUndo()
2510		card := ed.segs[i]
2511		card.Ins = ins
2512		// the dialog asks this one whenever it is a live question (insMode.askMute);
2513		// otherwise m.mute came back exactly as the card handed it over
2514		card.Mute = m.mute
2515		if m.splice {
2516			if !card.spliced() {
2517				ed.returnFootage(i)
2518			}
2519			card.E, card.Dur = card.S, m.dur
2520			ed.segs[i] = card
2521		} else {
2522			card.E, card.Dur = card.S+m.dur, 0
2523			ed.putOver(i, card)
2524		}
2525		ed.coalesce()
2526		ed.persist()
2527		ed.reholdSeg(card)
2528	}
2529	
2530	// setSpliced switches a card between the modes and changes nothing else.
2531	func (ed *cutEditor) setSpliced(i int, on bool) {
2532		if i < 0 || i >= len(ed.segs) || ed.segs[i].spliced() == on {
2533			return
2534		}
2535		s := ed.segs[i]
2536		ed.applyInsert(i, s.Ins, insMode{splice: on, dur: s.length()})
2537	}
2538	
2539	// returnFootage gives the clip before card i the seconds the card was covering,
2540	// so that when it stops covering them the footage is whole again. The clip after
2541	// it then touches this one and coalesce makes them one clip, which is what they
2542	// were before the card was placed.
2543	//
2544	// A card that took nothing -- one dropped in the hole between two recordings --
2545	// finds no clip ending where it starts, and nothing is given back.
2546	func (ed *cutEditor) returnFootage(i int) {
2547		card := ed.segs[i]
2548		for j := range ed.segs {
2549			p := &ed.segs[j]
2550			if p.isInsert() || math.Abs(p.E-card.S) > 0.05 {
2551				continue
2552			}
2553			hi := card.E
2554			if v := ed.videoAt(p.S); v != nil {
2555				hi = math.Min(hi, v.start+v.dur) // never past the end of the file
2556			}
2557			if hi > p.E {
2558				p.E = hi
2559			}
2560			return
2561		}
2562	}
2563	
2564	// putOver seats card i over the footage in its own seconds: whatever is under it
2565	// gives way, the same surgery addInsert does. Written as a removal because that
2566	// is what it is -- the card is lifted out of the list first, or removeSpan would
2567	// drop it along with the footage, an insert being a file and not a span.
2568	func (ed *cutEditor) putOver(i int, card cutSeg) {
2569		rest := make([]cutSeg, 0, len(ed.segs))
2570		rest = append(rest, ed.segs[:i]...)
2571		ed.segs = append(rest, ed.segs[i+1:]...)
2572		ed.removeSpan(card.S, card.E)
2573		ed.segs = append(ed.segs, card)
2574	}
2575	
2576	// indexOfSeg finds a clip in the list again by what it is: an insert is its file
2577	// at its own start time, and nothing else in a cut is both.
2578	func (ed *cutEditor) indexOfSeg(want cutSeg) int {
2579		for i, s := range ed.segs {
2580			if s.Ins == want.Ins && math.Abs(s.S-want.S) < 0.001 {
2581				return i
2582			}
2583		}
2584		return -1
2585	}
2586	
2587	// reholdSeg takes hold of a clip again after the list has been rearranged under
2588	// it -- found by what it is, not by where it was, since coalesce sorts and
2589	// renumbers. An edit made from the toolbar should leave the thing being edited
2590	// still held, or the next edit needs the card picked up a second time.
2591	func (ed *cutEditor) reholdSeg(want cutSeg) {
2592		if i := ed.indexOfSeg(want); i >= 0 {
2593			ed.segOn, ed.segSel, ed.segDirty = true, i, false
2594		}
2595		ed.syncInsertBtn()
2596		ed.redrawTracks()
2597	}
2598	
2599	// removeSpan is removeRange without the bookkeeping -- the same surgery, so
2600	// that a caller doing several things at once pushes one undo and saves once.
2601	func (ed *cutEditor) removeSpan(t0, t1 float64) {
2602		var out []cutSeg
2603		for _, s := range ed.segs {
2604			if s.E <= t0 || s.S >= t1 { // untouched
2605				out = append(out, s)
2606				continue
2607			}
2608			if s.isInsert() {
2609				// an insert is a file, not a span: it is dropped whole or not at all.
2610				// Trimming one to a fraction of its length would leave a clip nobody
2611				// asked for, showing part of a card.
2612				continue
2613			}
2614			// the halves are the same scene shortened, not new ones: they keep
2615			// whatever it said about itself, and what it says now is which camera
2616			// it shows
2617			if s.S < t0 && t0-s.S >= minPieceLn {
2618				h := s
2619				h.E = t0
2620				out = append(out, h)
2621			}
2622			if s.E > t1 && s.E-t1 >= minPieceLn {
2623				h := s
2624				h.S = t1
2625				out = append(out, h)
2626			}
2627		}
2628		ed.segs = out
2629	}
2630	
2631	// stealSpan takes t0..t1 away from the scenes on every row BUT cam: the newer
2632	// green wins, which is how painting camera B over camera A's green switches
2633	// camera. Inserts are left alone -- an insert is not a camera.
2634	func (ed *cutEditor) stealSpan(t0, t1 float64, cam int) {
2635		var out []cutSeg
2636		for _, s := range ed.segs {
2637			if s.isInsert() || s.Cam == cam || s.E <= t0 || s.S >= t1 {
2638				out = append(out, s)
2639				continue
2640			}
2641			// the same floor a removal leaves: painting camera B over a moment of
2642			// camera A must not take a second of A with it (minPieceLn)
2643			if s.S < t0 && t0-s.S >= minPieceLn {
2644				h := s
2645				h.E = t0
2646				out = append(out, h)
2647			}
2648			if s.E > t1 && s.E-t1 >= minPieceLn {
2649				h := s
2650				h.S = t1
2651				out = append(out, h)
2652			}
2653		}
2654		ed.segs = out
2655	}
2656	
2657	func (ed *cutEditor) removeRange(t0, t1 float64) {
2658		if t1 < t0 {
2659			t0, t1 = t1, t0
2660		}
2661		ed.removeSpan(t0, t1)
2662		ed.coalesce()
2663		ed.persist()
2664	}
2665	
2666	// ---- moving a clip edge by hand ---------------------------------------------
2667	//
2668	// The green borders are handles: hovering highlights one, a press picks it up,
2669	// and ‹f/f› then move it a frame at a time instead of the playhead. Both put the
2670	// picture on the frame the edge cuts on.
2671	
2672	// edgeAt is the clip edge nearest a point of the timeline, within edgeGrab px:
2673	// the segment's index and which side of it. The waveform lanes answer to it as
2674	// the picture band does -- a cut point is a time, and every band is the same
2675	// timeline seen a different way.
2676	func (ed *cutEditor) edgeAt(px float64) (int, bool, bool) {
2677		// the borders on the press's own side first, then the rest. Folded, one clip's
2678		// end and the next one's start are the SAME x (cut_fold.go), so nearest-wins
2679		// could never take the right-hand start; the clip the press is inside is the
2680		// clip it means.
2681		for _, inside := range []bool{true, false} {
2682			seg, end, near := -1, false, edgeGrab
2683			for i, s := range ed.segs {
2684				// A spliced card has no borders to trim: it sits at one point of the
2685				// footage and its length is its own, typed in the dialog. Both its edges
2686				// are that one x -- the middle of the marker you press to take hold of
2687				// the card -- so answering with an edge here would hand you a border of a
2688				// clip with no length instead of the card you pressed, and the border
2689				// wins over the clip.
2690				if s.spliced() {
2691					continue
2692				}
2693				x0, x1 := ed.xOf(s.S), ed.xOf(s.E)
2694				if d := math.Abs(x0 - px); d < near && (!inside || px >= x0) {
2695					seg, end, near = i, false, d
2696				}
2697				if d := math.Abs(x1 - px); d < near && (!inside || px <= x1) {
2698					seg, end, near = i, true, d
2699				}
2700			}
2701			if seg >= 0 {
2702				return seg, end, true
2703			}
2704		}
2705		return -1, false, false
2706	}
2707	
2708	// grabEdge picks up the edge under a timeline x, and says whether it found one.
2709	func (ed *cutEditor) grabEdge(px float64) bool {
2710		seg, end, ok := ed.edgeAt(px)
2711		if !ok {
2712			return false
2713		}
2714		ed.edgeOn, ed.edgeSeg, ed.edgeEnd, ed.edgeDirty = true, seg, end, false
2715		ed.segOn, ed.fxOn = false, false // one thing is held at a time, and this is now it
2716		ed.syncInsertBtn()
2717		side := "start"
2718		if end {
2719			side = "end"
2720		}
2721		// what is in hand, and the one thing about it that cannot be seen: which
2722		// button moves it. The rest -- the frame keys, ⌦, that a click elsewhere
2723		// puts it down -- was a paragraph printed on every press, and a status bar
2724		// is one line wide (fxStatus).
2725		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("clip %d's %s picked up at %s — right-drag to trim",
2726			seg+1, side, fmtClock(ed.edgeTime())))
2727		ed.redrawTracks()
2728		return true
2729	}
2730	
2731	// edgeHeld is whether a clip border is in hand.
2732	func (ed *cutEditor) edgeHeld() bool { return ed.edgeOn && ed.edgeSeg < len(ed.segs) }
2733	
2734	// onHeldEdge says whether a timeline x is close enough to the held edge to take
2735	// hold of it. This is what makes a left drag mean "move this" rather than "start
2736	// a new selection": the press has to land on the bar, not merely somewhere on a
2737	// page that happens to have an edge held.
2738	func (ed *cutEditor) onHeldEdge(px float64) bool {
2739		if !ed.edgeHeld() {
2740			return false
2741		}
2742		return math.Abs(ed.xOf(ed.edgeTime())-px) <= edgeMove
2743	}
2744	
2745	func (ed *cutEditor) dropEdge() {
2746		if !ed.edgeOn {
2747			return
2748		}
2749		ed.edgeOn = false
2750		ed.redrawTracks()
2751	}
2752	
2753	// edgeTime is where the held edge is now, or 0 when nothing is held.
2754	func (ed *cutEditor) edgeTime() float64 {
2755		if !ed.edgeHeld() {
2756			return 0
2757		}
2758		if ed.edgeEnd {
2759			return ed.segs[ed.edgeSeg].E
2760		}
2761		return ed.segs[ed.edgeSeg].S
2762	}
2763	
2764	// clampEdge is how far an edge may travel: never so far that its own clip is
2765	// shorter than minSegLn, never onto the neighbouring clip, and never out of the
2766	// recording it was cut from (lo..hi). The cut is the input to every step after
2767	// this one, so this arithmetic sits on its own where it can be tested rather
2768	// than inside a mouse handler.
2769	func clampEdge(segs []cutSeg, i int, end bool, t, lo, hi float64) float64 {
2770		s := segs[i]
2771		if end {
2772			if i+1 < len(segs) {
2773				hi = math.Min(hi, segs[i+1].S)
2774			}
2775			return math.Min(math.Max(t, s.S+minSegLn), hi)
2776		}
2777		if i > 0 {
2778			lo = math.Max(lo, segs[i-1].E)
2779		}
2780		return math.Max(math.Min(t, s.E-minSegLn), lo)
2781	}
2782	
2783	// moveEdgeTo puts the held edge at a session time, as far as it may go. live
2784	// says the mouse is still down, and then the cut is only redrawn: writing
2785	// cut.json (and re-reading the folder it is in, and re-gating two tabs) on
2786	// every motion event is a lot of work for a version of the cut that exists for
2787	// sixteen milliseconds. The drag's end writes the one that matters.
2788	func (ed *cutEditor) moveEdgeTo(t float64, live bool) {
2789		if !ed.edgeHeld() {
2790			ed.edgeOn = false
2791			return
2792		}
2793		s := &ed.segs[ed.edgeSeg]
2794		lo, hi := math.Inf(-1), math.Inf(1)
2795		if v := ed.videoAt((s.S + s.E) / 2); v != nil {
2796			lo, hi = v.start, v.start+v.dur
2797		}
2798		t = clampEdge(ed.segs, ed.edgeSeg, ed.edgeEnd, t, lo, hi)
2799		if (ed.edgeEnd && t == s.E) || (!ed.edgeEnd && t == s.S) {
2800			return // against a stop: not an edit, and not worth an undo step
2801		}
2802		// one undo entry for the whole hold, not one per mouse move: a drag is a
2803		// single act, and fifty of them would be the entire history
2804		if !ed.edgeDirty {
2805			ed.pushUndo()
2806			ed.edgeDirty = true
2807		}
2808		if ed.edgeEnd {
2809			s.E = t
2810		} else {
2811			s.S = t
2812		}
2813		if live {
2814			ed.updateTotal()
2815			ed.redrawTracks()
2816			return
2817		}
2818		ed.persist()
2819	}
2820	
2821	// edgeFPS is the frame rate of the recording the held edge falls in, which is
2822	// what a "frame" means for it. 30 when there is nothing there to ask.
2823	func (ed *cutEditor) edgeFPS() float64 {
2824		if v := ed.videoAt(ed.edgeTime()); v != nil && v.fps > 0 {
2825			return v.fps
2826		}
2827		return 30
2828	}
2829	
2830	// edgeFrame is the frame the held edge is judged by. An end edge is a frame
2831	// short of itself: the boundary's own frame is the first one the cut does NOT
2832	// keep, and what you are looking at is the last one it does.
2833	func (ed *cutEditor) edgeFrame() float64 {
2834		t := ed.edgeTime()
2835		if ed.edgeEnd {
2836			t -= 1 / ed.edgeFPS()
2837		}
2838		return t
2839	}
2840	
2841	// showEdge puts the preview on that frame, so the edge is moved against the
2842	// picture rather than against a ruler. live is a drag still in progress, and
2843	// then it is thinned to scrubEvery -- the seeks would otherwise queue up behind
2844	// the mouse and the picture would arrive after the drag had ended.
2845	func (ed *cutEditor) showEdge(live bool) {
2846		if !ed.edgeHeld() {
2847			return
2848		}
2849		if live {
2850			if time.Since(ed.lastScrub) < scrubEvery {
2851				return
2852			}
2853			ed.lastScrub = time.Now()
2854		}
2855		ed.setPlayhead(ed.edgeFrame())
2856	}

2991	// clampSeg is where a clip may sit: inside the recording it was cut from, clear

2993	// are in timeline order, i is the clip moved; snap is seconds counting as
2994	// touching -- a px tolerance at the current zoom.
2995	func clampSeg(segs []cutSeg, i int, t, lo, hi, snap float64) float64 {
2996		s := segs[i]
2997		ln := s.E - s.S
2998		// the neighbours: the nearest clip before and after in time, which is what
2999		// "the next area" means to a hand that can see them
3000		before, after := math.Inf(-1), math.Inf(1)

3002			if j == i {
3003				continue
3004			}
3005			if o.E <= s.S && o.E > before {
3006				before = o.E
3007			}
3008			if o.S >= s.E && o.S < after {
3009				after = o.S
3010			}
3011		}
3012		lo, hi = math.Max(lo, before), math.Min(hi, after)
3013		if math.Abs(t-lo) <= snap {
3014			t = lo // flush against what comes before
3015		} else if math.Abs(t+ln-hi) <= snap {
3016			t = hi - ln // ...or against what comes after
3017		}
3018		if t+ln > hi {
3019			t = hi - ln
3020		}
3021		if t < lo {
3022			t = lo
3023		}
3024		return t
3025	}

3379			return false
3380		}
3381		for _, q := range a {
3382			if !laneQuiet(b, q) {
3383				return false
3384			}
3385		}
3386		return true
3387	}
3388	
3389	func sameState(a, b cutState) bool {
3390		if !sameCut(a.segs, b.segs) || a.aspect != b.aspect || len(a.fx) != len(b.fx) {
3391			return false
3392		}
3393		if !sameShift(a.shift, b.shift) || !sameCutLanes(a.lanes, b.lanes) {
3394			return false // a lane dragged into place, or put there, is worth Reverting
3395		}
3396		for i := range a.fx {
3397			if a.fx[i] != b.fx[i] {
3398				return false
3399			}
3400		}
3401		return true
3402	}
3403	
3404	func (ed *cutEditor) syncButtons() {
3405		if ed.undoBtn != nil {
3406			ed.undoBtn.SetSensitive(len(ed.undo) > 0)
3407		}
3408		if ed.redoBtn != nil {
3409			ed.redoBtn.SetSensitive(len(ed.redo) > 0)
3410		}
3411		if ed.revertBtn != nil {
3412			ed.revertBtn.SetSensitive(!sameState(ed.snapshot(), ed.base))
3413		}
3414		ed.syncInsertBtn()
3415		ed.syncPlayBtn()
3416	}
3417	
3418	// syncPlayBtn greys ▶✂ out when there is nothing it could honestly play: its
3419	// preview is the finished video, an empty cut IS an empty video, and with no
3420	// clips there are no gaps to skip either -- it would run the whole recording
3421	// against its face's one promise. Plain ▶ never greys: the recording is always
3422	// there to play. Synced from setCutOnly and from syncButtons, which every edit
3423	// passes through, so adding the first clip wakes the button up again.
3424	func (ed *cutEditor) syncPlayBtn() {
3425		if ed.cutPlayBtn == nil {
3426			return
3427		}
3428		ed.cutPlayBtn.SetSensitive(len(ed.segs) > 0)
3429		ed.syncReviewPlay() // and ▶✂✂ needs two clips, not one
3430	}
3431	
3432	// syncInsertBtn tells the Insert button which of its two jobs it is doing. Held
3433	// card: it opens that card, so it says Edit. Anything else: it puts a new one in
3434	// at the playhead.
3435	func (ed *cutEditor) syncInsertBtn() {
3436		if ed == nil || ed.insBtn == nil {
3437			return
3438		}
3439		// what the copy in hand would be put down as, on the button that puts it
3440		// there. Grey with nothing in hand, which is most of the time.
3441		if ed.pasteBtn != nil {
3442			ed.pasteBtn.SetSensitive(ed.copyOn)
3443			switch {
3444			case !ed.copyOn:
3445				ed.pasteBtn.SetTooltipText("put a copy down at the red line — ⧉ takes one first")
3446			case ed.copyAud != "":
3447				ed.pasteBtn.SetTooltipText(fmt.Sprintf("lay the copied sound (%.1f s of %s, %s – %s) "+
3448					"over the footage at the red line: the picture runs on and the video stays "+
3449					"exactly as long. Esc drops the copy",
3450					ed.copyLen, ed.copyAud, mmss(ed.copyFrom), mmss(ed.copyFrom+ed.copyLen)))
3451			default:
3452				ed.pasteBtn.SetTooltipText(fmt.Sprintf("splice the copied footage (%s – %s, %.1f s) into "+
3453					"the cut at the red line: the cut is opened there, those seconds play again, and "+
3454					"the video gets longer by them. Esc drops the copy",
3455					mmss(ed.copyFrom), mmss(ed.copyFrom+ed.copyLen), ed.copyLen))
3456			}
3457		}
3458		if ed.laneBtn != nil {
3459			// footage only: a copied SOUND has no picture to put on a row, and the
3460			// lane it stands in for is already chosen (cutSeg.Lane). Grey rather
3461			// than hidden, like the paste beside it: a button that comes and goes
3462			// moves every button after it, and a bar whose contents shift as you
3463			// work is one you cannot aim at.
3464			ed.laneBtn.SetSensitive(ed.copyOn && ed.copyAud == "")
3465			if !ed.copyOn {
3466				ed.laneBtn.SetTooltipText("put a copy on a row of its own — ⧉ takes one first")
3467			}
3468			if ed.copyOn {
3469				ed.laneBtn.SetTooltipText(fmt.Sprintf("put the copied footage (%s – %s, %.1f s) "+
3470					"on a row of its own starting at the red line, instead of splicing it into "+
3471					"the cut. Nothing is cut to it yet: select on the new row and press ＋ Add, "+
3472					"the same way you would cut to a second camera",
3473					mmss(ed.copyFrom), mmss(ed.copyFrom+ed.copyLen), ed.copyLen))
3474			}
3475		}
3476		if s := ed.heldSeg(); s != nil && s.isInsert() {
3477			ed.insBtn.SetIconName("document-edit-symbolic")
3478			ed.insBtn.SetTooltipText("change the held card — what it says, and whether it plays " +
3479				"over the footage (overwrite) or between it (insert)")
3480			return
3481		}
3482		if f := ed.heldFx(); f != nil {
3483			ed.insBtn.SetIconName("document-edit-symbolic")
3484			ed.insBtn.SetTooltipText("change the held effect — " + f.fxLabel())
3485			return
3486		}
3487		ed.insBtn.SetIconName("insert-object-symbolic")
3488		ed.insBtn.SetTooltipText("put a file in the cut at the playhead — a video sting, a still, " +
3489			"or an SVG that animates itself. A selected region gives it its length; " +
3490			"otherwise the file's own. With the selection drawn in a lane's own wave " +
3491			"it offers sounds instead, and lays one over those seconds without moving the " +
3492			"picture. A card (tier.svg, s.svg … in assets) or any SVG " +
3493			"with {{holes}} in it asks what to put on it first. Right-click a card on " +
3494			"the track to hold it, and this becomes Edit.")
3495	}
3496	
3497	// droppedSpans is the session time this cut throws away, as stretches: the
3498	// holes between kept clips plus what hangs off either end of each recording.
3499	// Built on demand for the cut preview's scrim. Inserts neither open nor close
3500	// a hole (a spliced card has S == E, an overwriting one sits in kept footage).
3501	func (ed *cutEditor) droppedSpans() [][2]float64 {
3502		var out [][2]float64
3503		for _, sp := range ed.runs() {
3504			t := sp.t0
3505			for _, s := range ed.segs {
3506				if s.isInsert() || s.E <= t || s.S >= sp.t1 {
3507					continue
3508				}
3509				if s.S > t {
3510					out = append(out, [2]float64{t, math.Min(s.S, sp.t1)})
3511				}
3512				t = math.Max(t, s.E)
3513			}
3514			if t < sp.t1 {
3515				out = append(out, [2]float64{t, sp.t1})
3516			}
3517		}
3518		return out
3519	}
3520	
3521	// segAt returns the index of the kept scene covering t, or -1.
3522	func (ed *cutEditor) segAt(t float64) int {
3523		for i, s := range ed.segs {
3524			if t >= s.S && t < s.E {
3525				return i
3526			}
3527		}
3528		return -1
3529	}
3530	
3531	func (ed *cutEditor) coalesce() {
3532		// this is where the segment list is rearranged wholesale -- sorted, merged,
3533		// renumbered -- so a held edge or a held clip, which are indexes into it, have
3534		// to let go
3535		ed.edgeOn, ed.segOn = false, false
3536		sort.Slice(ed.segs, func(i, j int) bool { return ed.segs[i].S < ed.segs[j].S })
3537		var out []cutSeg
3538		film := -1 // where the last stretch of footage went, which is what merges
3539		for _, s := range ed.segs {
3540			// An insert never merges (it is a file, not seconds); the merge is into
3541			// the last FOOTAGE, since a spliced card takes no session time. Scenes of
3542			// different cameras never merge -- the seam is the switch -- and a border
3543			// | Split made is kept until a drag rejoins the two (mergeDropped).
3544			if !s.isInsert() && !s.Split && film >= 0 && s.Cam == out[film].Cam &&
3545				s.S <= out[film].E+mergeTol && allSpliced(out[film+1:]) {
3546				if s.E > out[film].E {
3547					out[film].E = s.E
3548				}
3549				continue
3550			}
3551			if !s.isInsert() {
3552				film = len(out)
3553			}
3554			out = append(out, s)
3555		}
3556		ed.segs = out
3557	}
3558	
3559	// allSpliced is whether everything here takes no session time -- which is to
3560	// say, whether two clips either side of it are still next to each other.
3561	func allSpliced(segs []cutSeg) bool {
3562		for _, s := range segs {
3563			if !s.spliced() {
3564				return false
3565			}
3566		}
3567		return true
3568	}
3569	
3570	// inserts are the cut's non-footage items, kept aside while the footage is
3571	// replaced wholesale -- which is what a suggestion and an audit both do. They
3572	// were placed by hand and no model was told they exist, so a run that came back
3573	// without them has not decided against them, it never saw them.
3574	func insertsOf(segs []cutSeg) []cutSeg {
3575		var out []cutSeg
3576		for _, s := range segs {
3577			if s.isInsert() {
3578				out = append(out, s)
3579			}
3580		}
3581		return out
3582	}
3583	
3584	// splitSpliced is the cut as a sequence of clips to render: every spliced
3585	// insert cuts the footage it sits in and the halves come out either side. Not
3586	// what the timeline stores -- there the footage is one clip with a splice
3587	// point in it. Every step after this reads the cut through produceSegs.
3588	func splitSpliced(segs []cutSeg) []cutSeg {
3589		ordered := append([]cutSeg(nil), segs...)
3590		sort.SliceStable(ordered, func(i, j int) bool {
3591			if ordered[i].S != ordered[j].S {
3592				return ordered[i].S < ordered[j].S
3593			}
3594			// a splice at the very start of a clip goes before it, not after: the
3595			// card is what you meant to see first
3596			return ordered[i].spliced() && !ordered[j].spliced()
3597		})
3598		var out []cutSeg
3599		for _, s := range ordered {
3600			n := len(out)
3601			if !s.spliced() || n == 0 {
3602				out = append(out, s)
3603				continue
3604			}
3605			// the clip it lands in is the one before it, since the list is in
3606			// order -- and it only cuts anything if it lands strictly inside
3607			prev := out[n-1]
3608			if prev.isInsert() || s.S <= prev.S || s.S >= prev.E {
3609				out = append(out, s)
3610				continue
3611			}
3612			tail := prev
3613			out[n-1].E, tail.S = s.S, s.S
3614			out = append(out, s, tail)
3615		}
3616		return out
3617	}
3618	
3619	func filmedOf(segs []cutSeg) []cutSeg {
3620		var out []cutSeg
3621		for _, s := range segs {
3622			if !s.isInsert() {
3623				out = append(out, s)
3624			}
3625		}
3626		return out
3627	}
3628	
3629	func (ed *cutEditor) persist() {
3630		// keyed, because cutFile.Sound is read on load and never written: an old
3631		// project's whole-cut choice is migrated into the scenes once (migrateSound)
3632		// and the field goes out of the file on the very next save
3633		// what is stored is the gaps as they now are: a fold is matched to a gap
3634		// by overlap, and this is where that reading is written back (syncFolds)
3635		ed.syncFolds()
3636		b, _ := json.MarshalIndent(cutFile{Segs: ed.segs, Aspect: ed.aspect, Fx: ed.fx,
3637			Shift: ed.shift, Rows: ed.rows, Lanes: ed.cutLanes, NRows: ed.nRows,
3638			Folds: ed.folds}, "", "  ")
3639		os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(ed.a.cutPath()), 0o755)
3640		if err := os.WriteFile(ed.a.cutPath(), append(b, '\n'), 0o644); err != nil {
3641			ed.a.logf("save cut: %v", err)
3642		}
3643		ed.updateTotal()
3644		ed.updateOut() // the file on disk just changed size
3645		// Narrate and Produce are gated on cut.json existing, and this is the only
3646		// place it comes into existence. Without this the tabs stayed grey after a
3647		// perfectly good cut and woke up only on a rescan or a restart, which looks
3648		// exactly like the cut not having worked.
3649		ed.a.updateGates()
3650		ed.syncButtons() // every edit changes whether there is a delta to revert
3651		// an edit can put a card under the playhead or take one away -- dropping an
3652		// insert, removing it, undoing either -- and the preview says which of those
3653		// happened before the line is moved again
3654		ed.showInsert()
3655		ed.redrawTracks()
3656	}
3657	
3658	// rawLen is the same cut with the speed effects taken off: the footage kept as
3659	// filmed. "How much have I kept" and "how long is the video" are both asked.
3660	func (ed *cutEditor) rawLen() float64 {
3661		sum := 0.0
3662		for _, s := range ed.segs {
3663			if s.Dur > 0 {
3664				sum += s.Dur // a card runs for its own length, whatever is around it
3665				continue
3666			}
3667			sum += math.Max(0, s.E-s.S)
3668		}
3669		return sum
3670	}
3671	
3672	// cutLen is how long the finished video is: a spliced card's own length,
3673	// slowed footage as it plays, everything else the footage under it -- not the
3674	// timeline's span.
3675	func (ed *cutEditor) cutLen() float64 {
3676		sum := 0.0
3677		for _, s := range ed.fxSegs() {
3678			sum += s.length() // a spliced card takes no session time and still runs
3679		}
3680		return sum
3681	}
3682	
3683	// fxSegs is the cut as the render runs it: spliced cards cut out, every clip
3684	// carrying its rate (splitSpliced + applyFx, produceSegs' own pipe). Every
3685	// number this page prints about TIME goes through here -- a clip's session
3686	// seconds stopped being the answer when speed effects existed.
3687	func (ed *cutEditor) fxSegs() []cutSeg { return applyFx(splitSpliced(ed.segs), ed.fx) }
3688	
3689	// cutPos is where session time t falls on the finished video's clock, effects
3690	// and all. The reading the ▶✂ preview is asked for.
3691	func (ed *cutEditor) cutPos(t float64) float64 { return cutPos(ed.fxSegs(), t) }
3692	
3693	// runLen is how long session seconds t0..t1 run in the finished video (a
3694	// selection or a held clip). A stop runs at ×1 here, as the render treats it:
3695	// the footage under the still plays on, so a stop costs no time.
3696	func (ed *cutEditor) runLen(t0, t1 float64) float64 {
3697		if t1 <= t0 {
3698			return 0
3699		}
3700		out, at := 0.0, t0
3701		for _, st := range rateSpans(ed.fx) {
3702			lo, hi := math.Max(st.t0, t0), math.Min(st.t1, t1)
3703			if hi <= lo {
3704				continue
3705			}
3706			out += math.Max(0, lo-at) // seconds no effect covers run at ×1
3707			out += (hi - lo) / st.applied()
3708			at = hi
3709		}
3710		return out + math.Max(0, t1-at)
3711	}
3712	
3713	// spanSecs is how a stretch's length is written in a status line: its own
3714	// seconds, and what it comes to in the video when an effect makes those two
3715	// different. Both, because both are being asked about -- the first is the
3716	// footage you are pointing at, the second is what it costs the video -- and a
3717	// cut with no effects in it reads exactly as it always did.
3718	func (ed *cutEditor) spanSecs(t0, t1 float64) string {
3719		raw, run := t1-t0, ed.runLen(t0, t1)
3720		if math.Abs(raw-run) < 0.05 {
3721			return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f s", raw)
3722		}
3723		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f s, %.1f s in the video", raw, run)
3724	}
3725	
3726	// updateTotal fills the three readings at the foot of the quiet column: how
3727	// long the cut runs, how much footage it was cut from, and how many pieces it
3728	// is in. One line each, in the column the playhead and the selection are read
3729	// in -- they were one line of three facts separated by dots, which is a
3730	// sentence in a column of readings.
3731	func (ed *cutEditor) updateTotal() {
3732		if ed.total == nil {
3733			return
3734		}
3735		sum, src := ed.cutLen(), 0.0
3736		for _, v := range ed.vids {
3737			src += v.dur
3738		}
3739		ed.total.SetText(mmss(sum))
3740		ed.totalRaw.SetText(mmss(ed.rawLen()))
3741		ed.totalSrc.SetText(mmss(src))
3742		segs := strconv.Itoa(len(ed.segs))
3743		// counted separately because they are not segments of the session: two of
3744		// the "segments" being cards is the difference between a five-minute cut of
3745		// footage and a five-minute cut with a minute of graphics in it
3746		if n := len(insertsOf(ed.segs)); n > 0 {
3747			segs += fmt.Sprintf(", %d inserted", n)
3748		}
3749		ed.totalSegs.SetText(segs)
3750	}
3751	
3752	// updateInputs says what this page works from: the recordings on the tracks,
3753	// and the session timeline Suggest is sent -- every line anyone said, merged
3754	// with every recording's event log.
3755	func (ed *cutEditor) updateInputs() {
3756		if ed == nil || ed.inputs == nil {
3757			return
3758		}
3759		src := 0.0
3760		var names []string
3761		for _, v := range ed.vids {
3762			src += v.dur
3763			names = append(names, fmt.Sprintf("%s  %s", mmss(v.dur), v.base))
3764		}
3765		// short enough to read in one glance: each input is named and counted, and
3766		// what each one MEANS is the tooltip's (see narrate.go's own row)
3767		line := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s", plural(len(ed.vids), "video"), mmss(src))
3768		detail := strings.Join(names, "\n")
3769		if len(names) == 0 {
3770			line, detail = "nothing to cut — no source on Inputs is marked as footage", ""
3771		}
3772		// the separate recordings are not footage and are not part of the timeline's
3773		// geometry, but they are on the page, and a lane that starts in the middle
3774		// of the tracks and stops before the end is only explicable if this row says
3775		// why: each is placed by its own wall clock, and only the stretch that
3776		// overlaps the footage is drawn.
3777		if len(ed.auds) > 0 {
3778			sep := 0
3779			for _, au := range ed.auds {
3780				if !au.master {
3781					sep++
3782				}
3783			}
3784			line += " · +" + plural(sep, "recording")
3785			detail += "\n\nEvery sound in the session, placed by its own clock — only the part running while the footage ran is drawn, and all of it is what the preview plays:"
3786			for _, au := range ed.auds {
3787				kind := "mono"
3788				if au.chans >= 2 {
3789					// a stereo file with one signal in it is said as such: it is why
3790					// it is drawn on one lane, and the row is where that is explained
3791					kind = "L/R"
3792					if ed.lanes(au) < 2 {
3793						kind = "L=R"
3794					}
3795				}
3796				what := fmt.Sprintf("from %s into the session", mmss(au.start))
3797				if au.master {
3798					what = "the footage's own track"
3799				}
3800				detail += fmt.Sprintf("\n%s  %s  %s, %s", mmss(au.dur), au.base, kind, what)
3801			}
3802		}
3803	
3804		rows := loadTSVRows(filepath.Join(ed.a.transcriptDir(), "session.tsv"))
3805		switch {
3806		case len(rows) == 0:
3807			line += " · no timeline"
3808		default:
3809			speech, events := 0, 0
3810			for _, r := range rows {
3811				if r.spk == "EVENT" {
3812					events++
3813				} else {
3814					speech++
3815				}
3816			}
3817			// the COUNT is not information: nothing on this page is decided by 688
3818			// rather than 700. That the timeline is there at all is, so the row
3819			// speaks only when it is missing -- which is the state that stops
3820			// Suggest.
3821			detail += fmt.Sprintf("\n\n%d lines: %d spoken, %d what was on screen, all of it sent with Suggest",
3822				speech+events, speech, events)
3823			// the same string the request will carry, so the size is the real one
3824			detail += fmt.Sprintf("\n\nprepare/transcript/session.txt — %d kB, sent whole with the cut prompt",
3825				(len(sessionText(rows, ed.a.narratorMic(), ed.a.loadRetakes()))+512)/1024)
3826		}
3827		// the context rides along with every request this page makes -- in the
3828		// tooltip, not on the row: the box is on the page before this one and the
3829		// word "context" alone says nothing about what is in it.
3830		if c := ed.a.sessionCtx(); c != "" {
3831			detail += "\n\nSession context (Describe), sent with Suggest and the audit:\n" + c
3832		}
3833		ed.inputs.SetText(line)
3834		ed.inputs.SetTooltipText(strings.TrimSpace(detail))
3835	}
3836	
3837	// updateOut says what is on disk, which is not what ed.total says: the total is
3838	// the cut in the editor, and until it is persisted the two differ.
3839	func (ed *cutEditor) updateOut() {
3840		if ed == nil || ed.out == nil {
3841			return
3842		}
3843		ed.out.SetText(summarizeOutputs(ed.a.cutDir()))
3844	}
3845	
3846	// ---- drawing ---------------------------------------------------------------
3847	
3848	// srcEdgeMark paints one end of a recording ON its own pictures: a band of
3849	// amber diagonals with the border line down its outer side. dir is +1 for a
3850	// beginning and -1 for an end, so the band always lies inside the footage it
3851	// belongs to and never over the take next door.
3852	//
3853	// Striped and not a plain line, because a line only says WHERE. What happened
3854	// here is that the camera stopped, and the minutes it was off take no width on
3855	// this timeline at all -- so if the mark does not say it, nothing does. Two
3856	// takes that meet are two striped bands back to back, and that reads as a
3857	// break in the footage the way two plain lines never did.
3858	//
3859	// room is how much of this recording there is to draw on; a take narrower than
3860	// two bands gets what fits rather than a band over its neighbour.
3861	func srcEdgeMark(cr *cairo.Context, x, dir, top, h, room float64) {
3862		w := math.Min(srcEdgeW, math.Max(1, room/2))
3863		cr.Save()
3864		cr.Rectangle(math.Min(x, x+dir*w), top, w, h)
3865		cr.Clip()
3866		// through the stripes, because what is under them is the frame this take
3867		// begins on and covering it is a worse trade than a fainter mark
3868		cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.9, 0.7, 0.2, 0.7)
3869		cr.SetLineWidth(1.5)
3870		for dy := -w; dy < h; dy += 5 {
3871			cr.MoveTo(x, top+dy+w)
3872			cr.LineTo(x+dir*w, top+dy)
3873			cr.Stroke()

3886	// clipped to the band. Marks only and no ground of their own, because the one
3887	// thing they mark is already painted something -- the splice marker is violet
3888	// first, since it says two things at once, and hatching drawn under that
3889	// violet would be tinted by it until it was no longer the same marks.

3895		cr.SetSourceRGB(0.45, 0.4, 0.3)
3896		cr.SetLineWidth(1)
3897		// the stroke runs corner to corner, so its length is the diagonal; a fifth
3898		// of that, with as much again of gap, is the dash
3899		cr.SetDash([]float64{h * math.Sqrt2 / 5, h * math.Sqrt2 / 5}, 0)

3902			cr.LineTo(dx+h, top)
3903			cr.Stroke()
3904		}
3905	}

3907	// plateText draws a label on its own dark ground: no single ink is readable
3908	// over thumbnails, and DIFFERENCE fails on mid-grey.
3909	func plateText(cr *cairo.Context, x, y float64, s string) {

3914		cr.MoveTo(x, y)
3915		cr.ShowText(s)
3916	}

3918	// plateH is how tall a plate is, plateR how round its corners are. Rounded,
3919	// where bands stay square: a band is a MEASUREMENT aimed at by its ends and

3922		plateH = 14.0
3923		plateR = 3.0
3924	)

3926	// platePath lays the plate's outline and sets its ink, ready to be filled. The
3927	// radius gives way on a plate too small to hold it -- a two-pixel label with
3928	// three-pixel corners is a lozenge -- so what is drawn is always a plate.
3929	func platePath(cr *cairo.Context, x, y, w, h float64) {
3930		cr.SetSourceRGBA(0, 0, 0, 0.66)
3931		r := math.Min(plateR, math.Min(w, h)/2)
3932		cr.NewSubPath()
3933		cr.Arc(x+w-r, y+r, r, -math.Pi/2, 0)
3934		cr.Arc(x+w-r, y+h-r, r, 0, math.Pi/2)
3935		cr.Arc(x+r, y+h-r, r, math.Pi/2, math.Pi)
3936		cr.Arc(x+r, y+r, r, math.Pi, 3*math.Pi/2)
3937		cr.ClosePath()
3938	}
3939	
3940	// drawTrack paints the footage with the kept stretches tinted green. The widget
3941	// is the window onto the timeline, never the timeline (an hour at top zoom is
3942	// wider than a cairo surface can be): everything is in timeline coordinates
3943	// under a Translate, and every loop is culled to the view first.
3944	func (ed *cutEditor) drawTrack(cr *cairo.Context, w, h int) {
3945		th := float64(ed.thumbHt)
3946		top := ed.picTop()

3948		// CUT and not about one camera is drawn across all of it: one green band
3949		// down every row, not a separate one per row that could be read as saying
3950		// the cameras were kept separately.
3951		bandH := ed.picBottom() - top

3954		cr.Rectangle(0, 0, float64(w), float64(h))
3955		cr.Fill()
3956	
3957		// what is on screen, in timeline px. The margin is for the things that
3958		// start left of the edge and reach into view: a thumbnail, a tick's label.
3959		const margin = 80
3960		vx0, vx1 := ed.viewX-margin, ed.viewX+float64(w)
3961		cr.Save()
3962		cr.Translate(-ed.viewX, 0)
3963		defer cr.Restore()
3964	
3965		for _, v := range ed.vids {
3966			if v.pxOrigin > vx1 || v.pxOrigin+v.dur*ed.pps < vx0 {
3967				continue // this recording is off screen entirely
3968			}
3969			lt := ed.laneTop(v.lane)        // this camera's row
3970			step := v.thumbStep(th, ed.pps) // thumbnails, only the ones in view
3971			// per CELL, not per recording: a folded gap inside this row's footage
3972			// is 32 px standing for minutes, so the frames on either side of it
3973			// are two runs of pictures at two origins, and none at all belongs in
3974			// the middle (cut_fold.go). With nothing folded this is one cell and
3975			// one pass, exactly as before.
3976			for _, cell := range ed.cellsOf(v.start, v.start+v.dur) {
3977				cv := v
3978				// where this recording's frame nought WOULD be drawn if the cell
3979				// carried on backwards: the origin frameRange counts indices from
3980				cv.pxOrigin = cell.px - (cell.t0-v.start)*ed.pps
3981				cx0, cx1 := math.Max(vx0, cell.px), math.Min(vx1, cell.px+ed.spanW(cell))
3982				first, last := cv.frameRange(ed.pps, cx0, cx1, step)
3983				for i := first; i < last; i += step {

3985					// ready, or nothing: a frame that has not been read yet is asked
3986					// for and the band's own ground stands in for it until it lands
3987					// (cut_thumbs.go). Nothing is decoded from inside a draw.
3988					pic := ed.thumb(v.frames[i])
3989					if pic == nil || pic.surf == nil {
3990						continue
3991					}
3992					x := ed.xOf(t)
3993					// never wider than the row it belongs to, nor than the cell:
3994					// a lane's last thumbnail is a whole frame's worth of a file
3995					// the row stops partway through, and the last one before a
3996					// fold must not spill across the seam
3997					w := math.Min(pic.w, float64(step)*v.interval*ed.pps)
3998					w = math.Min(w, ed.xOf(v.start+v.dur)-x)
3999					w = math.Min(w, cell.px+ed.spanW(cell)-x)

func srtStamp(t float64) string {
	if t < 0 {
		t = 0
	}
	h := int(t) / 3600
	m := (int(t) % 3600) / 60
	s := int(t) % 60
	ms := int((t-math.Floor(t))*1000 + 0.5)
	return fmt.Sprintf("%02d:%02d:%02d,%03d", h, m, s, ms)
}

// Accepts the stamps recorders write: OBS 2026-08-08 19-55-15, Quest
// ...-20260808-195900-0, phone VID_20250814_213311, dashcam 20250814213311,
// ShadowPlay 2025.08.14 - 21.33.11.03, QuickTime "2026-08-08 at 7.55.15 PM",
// ISO 2026-08-08T19:55:15. Always year first (day/month order is a guess that
// misplaces by weeks); century pinned to 19/20; parseStamp rejects month 13
// and hour 25. A single-digit hour must bring its own separators.
var tsRe = regexp.MustCompile(`((?:19|20)\d{2})[-._]?(\d{2})[-._]?(\d{2})` +
	`(?:\s?[aA][tT]\s|[-_T. ]{0,3})` +
	`(?:(\d{2})[-.:_]?(\d{2})[-.:_]?(\d{2})|(\d)[-.:_](\d{2})[-.:_](\d{2}))` +
	`(?:\s?([aApP][mM]))?`)

// epochRe is the last resort: bare unix seconds, which is what an iPhone
// screen recording (RPReplay_Final1723456789.mp4) carries. Ten digits bounded
// by non-digits, pinned to 2017..2033 so an arbitrary number has to look like
// the present decade before it counts.
var epochRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?:\A|\D)(1[5-9]\d{8})(?:\D|\z)`)

func parseStamp(m []string) (float64, error) {
	h, mn, sc := m[4], m[5], m[6]
	if h == "" { // the single-digit-hour layout matched instead
		h, mn, sc = "0"+m[7], m[8], m[9]
	}
	t, err := time.ParseInLocation("20060102-150405",
		m[1]+m[2]+m[3]+"-"+h+mn+sc, time.Local)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	// a 12-hour stamp names its half of the day
	if ap := m[10]; ap != "" {
		switch hr := t.Hour(); {
		case (ap[0] == 'p' || ap[0] == 'P') && hr < 12:
			t = t.Add(12 * time.Hour)
		case (ap[0] == 'a' || ap[0] == 'A') && hr == 12:
			t = t.Add(-12 * time.Hour)
		}
	}
	return float64(t.Unix()), nil
}

// nameStamp reads the wall clock out of a file name, if it carries one. It is
// the whole of what this app knows about when a recording happened: the Inputs
// page asks it to warn about names that carry none, and srcClock asks it to
// place the file. Every candidate the pattern finds gets a chance, so a
// digit run that only resembles a date (a resolution, a serial) cannot mask a
// real stamp sitting after it.
func nameStamp(name string) (float64, bool) {
	for _, m := range tsRe.FindAllStringSubmatch(name, -1) {
		if t, err := parseStamp(m); err == nil {
			return t, true
		}
	}
	if m := epochRe.FindStringSubmatch(name); m != nil {
		if n, err := strconv.Atoi(m[1]); err == nil {
			return float64(n), true
		}
	}
	return 0, false
}

// stampFmt is the human half of what tsRe reads back, and it is what an output
// file naming a moment is called: 2026-08-08_19-59-00. Seconds are the whole
// resolution -- a frame every three seconds or thirty a second, the name says
// which second it belongs to and stampSeq separates the ones that share one.
const stampFmt = "2006-01-02_15-04-05"

// stampName renders a wall-clock instant, floored to the second it falls in.
// Local time, because that is what the recorders put in their own file names
// and what parseStamp reads them back as.
func stampName(unix float64) string {
	return time.Unix(int64(math.Floor(unix)), 0).Format(stampFmt)
}

// stampSeq names a series of instants, numbering the ones landing in the same
// second: 19-59-00, then 19-59-00-1, 19-59-00-2. The first frame of a second
// keeps the bare name, which plain string sort then gets backwards ('-' sorts
// before '.') -- read such a folder back with sortStamped, not sort.Strings.
type stampSeq struct{ used map[string]int }

func (s *stampSeq) name(unix float64, ext string) string {
	if s.used == nil {
		s.used = map[string]int{}
	}
	base := stampName(unix)
	n := s.used[base]
	s.used[base]++
	if n > 0 {
		base = fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d", base, n)
	}
	return base + ext
}

// readStamp is the inverse: the second a name claims, and which frame of that
// second it is. Names carrying no stamp -- f000001.jpg from before frames were
// timestamped, a stray file -- report !ok and are left to sort by name.
func readStamp(path string) (sec float64, sub int, ok bool) {
	base := filepath.Base(path)
	m := tsRe.FindStringSubmatch(base)
	loc := tsRe.FindStringIndex(base)
	if m == nil || loc == nil {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	t, err := parseStamp(m)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	rest := strings.TrimSuffix(base[loc[1]:], filepath.Ext(base))
	if rest == "" {
		return t, 0, true
	}
	n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(rest, "-"))
	if err != nil || !strings.HasPrefix(rest, "-") {
		return 0, 0, false
	}
	return t, n, true
}

// sortStamped puts timestamped output files back in the order they were made.
func sortStamped(paths []string) {
	sort.Slice(paths, func(i, j int) bool {
		as, an, aok := readStamp(paths[i])
		bs, bn, bok := readStamp(paths[j])
		switch {
		case !aok || !bok:
			return paths[i] < paths[j]
		case as != bs:
			return as < bs
		default:
			return an < bn
		}
	})
}

// srcClock puts sources on one wall clock and says where second nought falls.
// A file that NAMES a moment is placed at it. One that does not goes at the
// session's start -- not its mtime, which is when it was copied or exported --
// where the right drag can line it up by ear (cut_shift.go). Nothing named:
// all start together at 0:00. This is the only door for lanes, transcript,
// describe, frame names and render, and it is handed the WHOLE session, since
// a shorter list can put zero elsewhere. Names only, no stat or ffprobe.
func srcClock(paths []string) (map[string]float64, float64) {
	at := make(map[string]float64, len(paths))
	zero := math.Inf(1)
	for _, p := range paths {
		if t, ok := nameStamp(filepath.Base(p)); ok {
			at[p], zero = t, math.Min(zero, t)
		}
	}
	if math.IsInf(zero, 1) {
		zero = 0 // nothing named a moment: the session starts at 0:00
	}
	for _, p := range paths {
		if _, ok := at[p]; !ok {
			at[p] = zero
		}
	}
	return at, zero
}

// sourceStart is where one file sits on that same clock, for the steps that
// hold a path and not the list. It IS srcClock, asked about the whole session
// with this file in it -- so a file the session does not contain, a sting on a
// cut lane say, is placed by the same rule as one it does.
func (a *App) sourceStart(path string) float64 {
	vids, auds := a.snappedSources()
	all := append(append(append([]string{}, vids...), auds...), path)
	at, _ := srcClock(all)
	return at[path]
}

// one source with everything known about its place in the world
type src struct {
	path, base string
	start      float64 // wall clock, seconds since epoch
	dur        float64
	isVideo    bool
	rows       []seg4   // fixed transcript, its own timeline
	events     []tsvRow // videos only
}

// The fixer fixes every source's transcript and writes the merged session
// timeline. span is this job's share of the progress bar; see the describer.
func (a *App) fixTranscripts(videos, audios []string, span float64) error {

	if err := os.MkdirAll(trDir, 0o755); err != nil {
