4190			// and has no span of the timeline to be drawn across. What it has is a
4191			// POINT where the footage is cut open and a length of its own, and
4192			// spliceSpan is that length drawn at this zoom, STARTING at the point --
4193			// the card begins where the red line was when it was placed, and the
4194			// marker grows rightward with the zoom the way the card runs.
4195			x0, x1 := ed.segSpan(s)
4196			if x1 < vx0 || x0 > vx1 {
4197				continue
4198			}
4199			cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.55, 0.35, 0.9, 0.55)
4200			cr.Rectangle(x0, top, x1-x0, bandH)
4201			cr.Fill()
4202			if s.spliced() {
4203				// hatched over the violet, so the marker says both things at once: a
4204				// card goes in here, and the footage stops for it
4205				hatchStrokes(cr, x0, x1-x0, top, bandH)
4206			}
4207			cr.SetSourceRGB(0.75, 0.6, 1)
4208			cr.SetLineWidth(2)
4209			for _, x := range []float64{x0, x1} {
4210				cr.MoveTo(x, top)
4211				cr.LineTo(x, top+bandH)
4212				cr.Stroke()
4213			}
4214			cr.SetFontSize(10)
4215			switch {
4216			case s.spliced():
4217				// The length comes with the name here and nowhere else: a spliced card
4218				// does not stretch between two borders you can read off the ruler.
4219				// Beside the marker while the marker is a marker, inside it once the
4220				// zoom has made it wide enough to write in -- text that starts at the
4221				// same place either way, so it does not appear to jump as you zoom.
4222				tx := x1 + 4
4223				if x1-x0 > 90 {
4224					tx = x0 + 4
4225				}
4226				markPlate(cr, tx, top+th-2, "card", fmt.Sprintf("%s  %.1fs", insName(s), s.Dur))
4227			case x1-x0 > 24:
4228				// the file, not the parameters: a filled-in tier board's parameters
4229				// are longer than the clip they would be written across
4230				markPlate(cr, x0+4, top+th-2, "card", insName(s))
4231			}
4232		}
4233	
4234		// A sound-only insert is marked on the SOUND: the recorders' band below
4235		// when the session has one (drawAudio, which also says why the picture
4236		// band leaves these alone), and every row's wave strip here always --
4237		// with the cameras' waves paired under their pictures, a session with no
4238		// separate recorder has no other band to say "these seconds were placed".
4239		heldSnd := ed.heldSeg()
4240		for i := range ed.segs {
4241			s := ed.segs[i]
4242			if !s.audioIns() {
4243				continue
4244			}
4245			x0, x1 := ed.segSpan(s)
4246			if x1 < vx0 || x0 > vx1 {
4247				continue
4248			}
4249			named := false
4250			for r := 0; r < max(1, ed.laneN); r++ {
4251				ph := ed.pairH(r)
4252				if ph <= 0 {
4253					continue
4254				}
4255				// named once, on the first strip that can carry it: the same
4256				// mark on three rows saying the same file three times is noise
4257				ed.sndInsMark(cr, s, x0, x1, ed.laneTop(r)+ed.laneH(), ph, heldSnd == &ed.segs[i], !named)
4258				named = true
4259			}
4260		}
4261	
4262		// slowed or frozen stretches, tinted rose over the footage itself: the
4263		// effect belongs to the frames under it, and the lane below carries its
4264		// handle. The same hue as its lane marker, so the two read as one thing.
4265		for _, f := range ed.fx {
4266			if f.Kind != "speed" {
4267				continue
4268			}
4269			x0, x1 := ed.fxSpanPx(f)
4270			if x1 < vx0 || x0 > vx1 {
4271				continue
4272			}
4273			cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.92, 0.42, 0.6, 0.18)
4274			cr.Rectangle(x0, top, x1-x0, bandH)
4275			cr.Fill()
4276		}
4277	
4278		// What each scene does with the sound on its own camera, on the strips under
4279		// the pictures -- and which row it is shown from, on the rows (drawCamBadges).
4280		// After the green, not before: "silences its camera" has to be the answer
4281		// you see over "is in the video".
4282		ed.drawSilences(cr, ed.pairSilences(), vx0, vx1)
4283		ed.drawCamBadges(cr, vx0, vx1)
4284		ed.drawHearBadges(cr, ed.hearBadgesSrc(), vx0, vx1)
4285		// the ✕ that takes a whole row away, over everything else the picture band
4286		// draws: a control the inserts or the cut preview's dimming could paint
4287		// over would be a control that is there on some frames and not others.
4288		// The one that drops a scene is not here -- it is on the green bar in the
4289		// selection row (drawSelBand), which is drawn just below.
4290		ed.drawLaneKill(cr, vx0, vx1)
4291		// the black strip in front of second zero, drawn over the picture band and
4292		// under the two rows below -- nothing on the tape may reach into it, and
4293		// the switches above stand in it (cut_gutter.go). The bands get their own
4294		// pass because they are drawn after this one.
4295		ed.drawGutter(cr, top, bandH)
4296		ed.drawPairSwitches(cr)
4297		ed.drawRowKill(cr)
4298	
4299		// the two rows that speak for the whole cut, over the pictures rather than
4300		// under them now: the green bar under the clock and the effects lane under
4301		// it (cut_fx.go). Drawn after the band so the hairline that closes the
4302		// group lands on the pictures' own top edge rather than beneath it.
4303		ed.drawSelBand(cr, vx0, vx1)
4304		ed.drawFoldBadges(cr, vx0, vx1)
4305		ed.drawFxLane(cr, vx0, vx1)
4306		ed.drawFxKill(cr, vx0, vx1)
4307		// the same strip across the two bands, and the one control that belongs to
4308		// the whole page rather than to a row: fold every dropped stretch away, or
4309		// bring them all back (cut_gutter.go)
4310		ed.drawGutter(cr, float64(rulerH), ed.picTop()-float64(rulerH))
4311		ed.drawFoldAll(cr)
4312	
4313		// the clip a double click has picked up, outlined in white. The edge marker
4314		// below says which BORDER is about to move; this says which whole clip is,
4315		// and they are the same gesture at two scales, so they are the same ink.
4316		if s := ed.heldSeg(); s != nil && !s.audioIns() {
4317			// ...unless the held clip is a sound: its marker is in the lanes, and
4318			// the outline goes where the marker is (drawAudio)
4319			x0, x1 := ed.segSpan(*s)
4320			st := ed.segTop(*s)
4321			cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.9)
4322			cr.SetLineWidth(2)
4323			cr.Rectangle(x0+1, st+1, x1-x0-2, ed.laneH()-2)
4324			cr.Stroke()
4325		}
4326	
4327		// selection rubber band
4328		if ed.sel.active {
4329			a, b := ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1
4330			if b < a {
4331				a, b = b, a
4332			}
4333			x0, x1 := ed.xOf(a), ed.xOf(b)
4334			// on the row it was drawn on: the blue says which picture ＋ Add is
4335			// about to keep, so it has to be over that picture
4336			cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.3, 0.55, 0.9, 0.45)
4337			lt, lh := ed.laneTop(ed.sel.lane), ed.laneH()
4338			cr.Rectangle(x0, lt, x1-x0, lh)
4339			cr.Fill()
4340			// ...and its two ENDS drawn as ends, with a grip at mid-height: a
4341			// press on either takes that end from here exactly as it does from
4342			// the band, and a hand cannot aim at an edge that is only where a
4343			// wash stops. Lit while the pointer is on one (selHov), as the band
4344			// lights its own grips.
4345			cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.45, 0.7, 1, 0.95)
4346			cr.SetLineWidth(2)
4347			if ed.selHov {
4348				cr.SetLineWidth(3)
4349			}
4350			for _, x := range []float64{x0, x1} {
4351				cr.MoveTo(x, lt)
4352				cr.LineTo(x, lt+lh)
4353				cr.Stroke()
4354				cr.Rectangle(x-3, lt+lh/2-7, 6, 14)
4355				cr.Fill()
4356			}
4357		}
4358	
4359		// which sound is in hand, said on the wave itself: a selection drawn on a
4360		// row's own strip wears its second wash there, exactly as one drawn in a
4361		// separate recorder's lane wears it in the band below (drawAudio)
4362		if ed.sel.active && ed.selSnd() {
4363			for _, v := range ed.vids {
4364				if v.base != ed.sel.aud {
4365					continue
4366				}
4367				if au := ed.pairAud(v.base); au != nil {
4368					x0, x1 := ed.selSpanPx()
4369					sy, sh := ed.laneTop(v.lane)+ed.laneH(), float64(ed.lanes(*au))*waveLaneH
4370					cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.3, 0.55, 0.9, 0.34)
4371					cr.Rectangle(x0, sy, x1-x0, sh)
4372					cr.Fill()
4373					cr.SetSourceRGB(0.62, 0.82, 1)
4374					for _, x := range []float64{x0, x1} {
4375						cr.Rectangle(x-1.5, sy, 3, sh)
4376					}
4377					cr.Fill()
4378				}
4379			}
4380		}
4381	
4382		// the row the preview is watching (camAt), outlined across the pair --
4383		// the strip is the same footage. Dashed, so it cannot be read as the held
4384		// clip's solid white; gone the moment ▶ takes the preview back to the cut.
4385		if m := ed.watchRow(); m >= 0 {
4386			lt := ed.laneTop(m)
4387			cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.95, 0.95, 1, 0.6)
4388			cr.SetLineWidth(1.5)
4389			cr.SetDash([]float64{5, 4}, 0)
4390			cr.Rectangle(ed.viewX+1, lt+0.75, float64(w)-2, ed.laneH()+ed.pairH(m)-1.5)
4391			cr.Stroke()
4392			cr.SetDash(nil, 0)
4393		}
4394	
4395		// the border under the pointer: a soft white bar with a halo behind it, over
4396		// the green one it belongs to. Not the held marker's ink -- no heads, and
4397		// half the strength -- because it is an offer rather than a state: this is
4398		// the border the next press would take, and it goes away when the pointer
4399		// does. See hoverEdge.
4400		if ed.edgeHovOn {
4401			x := ed.xOf(ed.edgeHovT)
4402			cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.16)
4403			cr.SetLineWidth(9)
4404			cr.MoveTo(x, top)
4405			cr.LineTo(x, top+bandH)
4406			cr.Stroke()
4407			cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.6)
4408			cr.SetLineWidth(3)
4409			cr.MoveTo(x, top)
4410			cr.LineTo(x, top+bandH)
4411			cr.Stroke()
4412		}
4413	
4414		// the clip edge that is held: white, wider than the green border it sits on,
4415		// with a head each way to say that it moves. Drawn last, so nothing painted
4416		// over it can hide what is about to change under the next ‹f.
4417		if ed.edgeOn && ed.edgeSeg < len(ed.segs) {
4418			x := ed.xOf(ed.edgeTime())
4419			st, lh := ed.segTop(ed.segs[ed.edgeSeg]), ed.laneH()
4420			cr.SetSourceRGB(1, 1, 1)
4421			cr.SetLineWidth(3)
4422			cr.MoveTo(x, st)
4423			cr.LineTo(x, st+lh)
4424			cr.Stroke()
4425			for _, d := range []float64{-1, 1} {
4426				cr.MoveTo(x, st+lh/2-5)
4427				cr.LineTo(x+7*d, st+lh/2)
4428				cr.LineTo(x, st+lh/2+5)
4429				cr.ClosePath()
4430				cr.Fill()
4431			}
4432		}
4433	}
4434	
4435	func (ed *cutEditor) inCut(t float64) bool {
4436		for _, s := range ed.segs {
4437			if t >= s.S && t < s.E {
4438				return true
4439			}
4440		}
4441		return false
4442	}
4443	
4444	// tickStep is how far apart the ruler's marks stand, in seconds: the coarsest
4445	// step that still puts them about 70 px apart, so a window holds roughly twenty
4446	// of them at every zoom.
4447	//
4448	// Below a second at the top zooms, because that is what the zoom is FOR: at
4449	// 240 px/s a one-second ruler is four marks across the window, and a cut being
4450	// judged against a word edge wants to see the fifths of a second it is being
4451	// moved by. Those steps label with a decimal (tickLabel) -- two marks 400 ms
4452	// apart both reading 0:37 is worse than no mark at all.
4453	func tickStep(pps float64) float64 {
4454		for _, s := range []float64{0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60, 120, 300, 600} {
4455			if s*pps >= 70 {
4456				return s
4457			}
4458		}
4459		return 1200
4460	}
4461	
4462	// tickLabel is a ruler mark's time, with as much of a second as the step it
4463	// stands on needs.
4464	func tickLabel(t, step float64) string {
4465		if step >= 1 {
4466			return fmt.Sprintf("%d:%02d", int(t)/60, int(t)%60)
4467		}
4468		return fmt.Sprintf("%d:%04.1f", int(t)/60, math.Mod(t, 60))
4469	}
4470	
4471	// The run bar drives the preview through these; see transport in pipeline.go.
4472	func (ed *cutEditor) playing() bool { return ed.player != nil && ed.player.Playing() }
4473	func (ed *cutEditor) cued() bool    { return ed.player != nil && ed.player.Cued() }
4474	
4475	// playAs is both play buttons. Each one is ▶ for its own idea of what the
4476	// preview IS -- ▶ the recording, ▶✂ the cut -- so each press delivers exactly
4477	// what the face it landed on promises. Pressing the button whose preview is
4478	// already running pauses it; pressing the other one switches the preview over,
4479	// and if something was playing it plays on as the other thing rather than
4480	// stopping -- switching is why you pressed a play button and not ⏸.
4481	func (ed *cutEditor) playAs(cut bool) {
4482		if ed.cutOnly != cut {
4483			ed.setCutOnly(cut)
4484			if ed.playing() {
4485				return
4486			}
4487		} else if cut && ed.reviewOn {
4488			// ▶✂ pressed while the review runs: the same switch-over, from the
4489			// review to the plain cut. The review's own button is the one that
4490			// pauses it (playReview); this one's face said ▶, so it plays.
4491			ed.reviewOff()
4492			if ed.playing() {
4493				return
4494			}
4495		}
4496		ed.toggle()
4497	}
4498	
4499	// setCutOnly switches what the preview IS, with everything that follows from
4500	// that: the gap-skip guard, the dimming, the clock's meaning and the ▶✂ lamp.
4501	// The two play buttons are the only hands on it.
4502	func (ed *cutEditor) setCutOnly(cut bool) {
4503		if ed.cutOnly == cut {
4504			return
4505		}
4506		ed.cutOnly = cut
4507		ed.jumped = -1
4508		if !cut {
4509			ed.reviewOff() // the review is a cut preview; there is none to review the recording by
4510		}
4511		ed.syncPlayBtn() // an empty cut is nothing to play; see that function
4512		if cut {
4513			// the mode promises kept material, so it delivers some immediately
4514			// rather than at the next tick
4515			ed.cutOnlySnap()
4516			if len(ed.segs) == 0 {
4517				ed.a.setStatus("preview is the cut — and the cut is empty, so ▶✂ has " +
4518					"nothing to play until a clip is added")
4519			} else {
4520				ed.a.setStatus("preview is the cut — the clock reads the finished video")
4521			}
4522		} else {
4523			ed.a.setStatus("preview is the recording again — everything plays, cuts and all")
4524		}
4525		ed.showTime()
4526		ed.a.syncPlayIcons() // both ▶s redraw: whose preview this is just changed
4527		ed.redrawTracks()
4528	}
4529	
4530	// syncCutPlay draws the ▶✂ button: a pause face while its preview is the one
4531	// running, and lit for as long as the preview is the cut at all -- the lamp
4532	// the old toggle button's pressed state used to be.
4533	//
4534	// The play/pause half is the stock ICON, and the ✂ beside it is the label. It
4535	// was one label of two glyphs, "▶✂" and "⏸✂", because no stock icon says
4536	// "play, but the cut" -- and swapping those two glyphs moved the whole page.
4537	// ⏸ (U+23F8) is in a different font from ▶ (U+25B6) on an ordinary Linux
4538	// desktop: Pango falls back to the emoji face for it, which is taller, so the
4539	// button grew a few px on every press, the toolbar row grew with it, and the
4540	// timeline under it stepped down and back up as the preview started and
4541	// stopped. An icon is the same size in both states, and the ✂ never changes.
4542	func (ed *cutEditor) syncCutPlay() {
4543		if ed.cutPlayBtn == nil || ed.cutPlayIcon == nil {
4544			return
4545		}
4546		// ⏸ only while the plain cut runs: under a review the cut is running
4547		// too, but the review's button is the one that started it and the one
4548		// that wears the ⏸ (syncReviewPlay) -- one ⏸ per thing running
4549		if ed.playing() && ed.cutOnly && !ed.reviewOn {
4550			ed.cutPlayIcon.SetFromIconName("media-playback-pause-symbolic")
4551			ed.cutPlayBtn.SetTooltipText("pause the cut preview")
4552		} else {
4553			ed.cutPlayIcon.SetFromIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
4554			ed.cutPlayBtn.SetTooltipText("play the CUT instead of the recording: the removed " +
4555				"stretches are skipped, so this runs the finished video. The clock reads the " +
4556				"cut's own time while it does. Changes nothing that is saved.")
4557		}
4558		// lit while the preview is the cut and not the review of it: one lamp
4559		// across the three ▶s (lamp, cut_review.go)
4560		lamp(ed.cutPlayBtn, ed.cutOnly && !ed.reviewOn)
4561	}
4562	
4563	func (ed *cutEditor) toggle() {
4564		// ▶ is grey in this state (syncPlayBtn), but the button is not the only way
4565		// in -- a click on the picture and the run bar land here too, and every way
4566		// in has to refuse for the same reason
4567		if ed.cutOnly && len(ed.segs) == 0 {
4568			ed.a.setStatus("the cut is empty — add a clip to play it, or press ▶ " +
4569				"to play the recording instead")
4570			return
4571		}
4572		if ed.player == nil {
4573			return
4574		}
4575		if !ed.playing() {
4576			// ▶ plays the CUT: a preview that was watching one row on a click's
4577			// orders stops watching it. The scenes name their own cameras from
4578			// here (camAt), and the branches below must load the scene's file,
4579			// not the watched one's.
4580			ed.monRow = 0
4581			ed.redrawTracks() // the dashed outline goes with it
4582		}
4583		// ▶ starts where the red line is, both buttons, whatever is in hand. Under
4584		// ✂ only, a line in a dropped stretch moves to the next clip (cutOnlySnap).
4585		if !ed.playing() && ed.cutOnly {
4586			ed.cutOnlySnap()
4587		}
4588		// what this scene hears, settled before the transport moves rather than in
4589		// the showInsert below it: ▶ starts the recordings (syncMix), and a lane
4590		// this scene silences is one ▶ must not start at all
4591		ed.syncHush()
4592		if ed.playing() {
4593			ed.reviewOff() // a pause is a decision: the review does not resume from it
4594		}
4595		ed.player.Toggle()
4596		// the black "no footage on this row" frame comes and goes with the
4597		// standstill (showInsert), and pausing is a standstill nothing else
4598		// re-settles: playback's own ticks stop with it
4599		ed.showInsert()
4600		ed.started = ed.started || ed.player.Playing()
4601		ed.a.updateRunControls()
4602	}
4603	
4604	func (ed *cutEditor) stop() {
4605		ed.reviewOff()
4606		if ed.player != nil {
4607			ed.player.Stop()
4608		}
4609		ed.started = false // ⏹ hands ▶ back to the step's own job, suggesting
4610	}
4611	
4612	// ---- page ------------------------------------------------------------------
4613	
4614	func (a *App) buildCut() gtk.Widgetter {
4615		ed := &cutEditor{a: a, pps: 4, thumbHt: 64, jumped: -1, rowHov: -1, fxKillHov: -1,
4616			bandKillHov: -1, foldHov: -1, thumbs: map[string]*thumbPic{}}
4617		a.ed = ed
4618		if p, err := NewPlayer(); err == nil {
4619			ed.player = p // the preview above the tracks; independent of Review's
4620			p.OnState = a.updateRunControls
4621			p.OnError = a.playerErr("the cut preview")
4622			p.OnLog = func(s string) { a.logf("%s", s) }
4623			glib.TimeoutAdd(playTick, ed.followPlayback)
4624		} else {
4625			a.logf("cut preview player: %v", err)
4626		}
4627	
4628		// Suggesting is this page's long job, and every other page's long job is
4629		// the run bar's ▶. There is nothing here for it any more: the length it
4630		// aims at is a sentence in the user context on Prepare ("about 12 min"),
4631		// beside everything else the run is told.
4632		// Not the blue one. suggested-action is the page's primary verb, and this
4633		// is not it -- ▶ on the run bar is -- so the colour was saying "press this
4634		// first" about a button that cannot be pressed at all until seconds are
4635		// marked. The bar is a row of equal verbs, and which of them is live says
4636		// what to do next (syncSelBtns).
4637		// Icons, like the transport and the undo group either side of them. Five
4638		// words on five buttons is a third of the bar spent saying what a symbol
4639		// says -- and these five are the page's own verbs, pressed all session,
4640		// which is exactly the set a hand learns by position. What each one is
4641		// stays in the tooltip and in the status line the press writes.
4642		ed.addBtn = gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-add-symbolic")
4643		add := ed.addBtn
4644		add.ConnectClicked(func() { a.addSelClicked() })
4645		// the same selection, cut out of what it lies in rather than kept or
4646		// dropped: the third thing that can be done to a span (cut_split.go).
4647		ed.splitBtn = gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("edit-cut-symbolic")
4648		ed.splitBtn.ConnectClicked(func() { a.splitSelRange() })
4649		// the same selection, dropped instead of kept. Beside Add because they are
4650		// one pair, and greyed by the same rule -- see cut_selrm.go for why a
4651		// remove is back on the bar at all.
4652		ed.remBtn = gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-remove-symbolic")
4653		ed.remBtn.ConnectClicked(func() { a.removeSelRange() })

# Native AI Video Editor for Post Processing (Naivepost)

A desktop video editor for sessions you have already recorded, where the
tedious half of the work is done by models running on your own machine.

You give it the files a session left behind — camera footage, a separate
microphone recording, a screen capture — and it transcribes them, works out
what is on screen, proposes a cut, writes and speaks a narration over it,
renders the video, and writes the title, description, subtitles and thumbnail
you upload with. Every one of those is a proposal you can overrule; none of
them is a black box you have to accept whole.

It is a GTK4 application in Go (`gui/`, ~100k lines), talking to four local
HTTP servers over the network — nothing is compiled in, nothing calls out to a
cloud service unless you point it at one.

---

## What it actually does

Four tabs, left to right, in the order the work happens. Each has one **▶** that
runs that step; **▶▶** beside it runs several in a row. The thumbnail and the
upload text live on Produce, beside the render they belong to.

### Prepare

Add the session's files. Each row says what its file is *for*: a camera icon
means frames come out of it and it can be cut; a microphone tags who is
speaking, voice 1 being the one the narration is spoken in. One file can be
both.

Everything is placed on **one clock**, taken from the timestamp in the filename
or the file's own creation time and length. That is what puts a separate
recorder's words, waveform and sound where they belong against the footage. The
footage is the master: a recording is heard for exactly the part of it that was
running while the footage was.

Pressing ▶ then does, in order:

1. **Optional voice separation** — a source flagged for it is split into voice
====

3	// Effects a cut carries beyond which seconds it keeps: zoom (where the camera
4	// is; Stay keeps the framing until the next zoom), speed (the clock: a rate, or
5	// a held frame), text (words in a box, fxtext.go) and volume. None touch the
6	// segments; an effect whose seconds are cut out never fires (applyFx).
7	//
8	// A zoom's rectangle is stored normalized against the SOURCE frame with no
9	// width -- it is always the cut's aspect, so width = hf*sh*A. A text's box is
10	// normalized against the OUTPUT frame and keeps its width (fxtext.go).

26	// wrote.
27	type cutFx struct {
28		Kind string  `json:"kind"` // "zoom", "speed", "text", "svg" or "volume"
29		T    float64 `json:"t"`    // session time it happens at
30		// Every kind reads these two the same way: the seconds the effect fades
31		// in at its start and out at its end, both inside Dur. For a zoom that is
32		// the camera gliding to the region and back off it, for a speed the clock
33		// ramping to the rate and back, for a text and a stop the words and the
34		// still fading up and down. 0 either side is a hard cut.
35		Trans float64 `json:"trans,omitempty"`
36		Tout  float64 `json:"tout,omitempty"`
37		// The shape both fades travel in: "" is the straight ramp, which is the
38		// only shape anything here draws (fxEases). Stored by name rather than by
39		// number so a cut written by a version that knows a curve this one does
40		// not still reads back as the effect it was.
41		Ease string `json:"ease,omitempty"`
42		// How long the effect runs, its fades included -- the bar on the lane,
43		// for every kind. speed: the session seconds it covers, and for a stop
44		// (Rate 0) the seconds the still stands over footage that keeps running,
45		// so the cut is the same length with or without it.
46		Dur float64 `json:"dur,omitempty"`
47		// zoom: what the camera does when its seconds are up. false pulls back to
48		// where the camera was before it; true stays on the region until the next
49		// zoom says otherwise -- the reframing a vertical cut is made of.
50		Stay bool `json:"stay,omitempty"`
51		// zoom: the camera rectangle. Centre as a fraction of the source
52		// frame's width and height; Hf is rect height over source height. May
53		// reach past the edges (that is zooming OUT past the frame; the render
54		// pads with black), and may exceed 1 (wider shot than the frame is tall).
55		// text: the box the words are fitted into -- and these four are fractions
56		// of the OUTPUT frame instead, so the words stay put while the camera

58		Cx float64 `json:"cx,omitempty"`
59		Cy float64 `json:"cy,omitempty"`
60		Hf float64 `json:"hf,omitempty"`

62		// window's width is its height times the cut's aspect and is never stored.
63		Wf float64 `json:"wf,omitempty"`
64		// speed: 1 is the footage's own clock, 0.5 is half speed, 8 is eight
65		// times faster. 0 is the whole of the stop effect: the picture stands

97		// fxMaxRate is as fast as the clock goes. A hundred times is a minute of
98		// footage every 0.6 seconds -- past that a stretch worth marking at all
99		// comes out shorter than the frames it is made of.
100		fxMaxRate = 100.0
101		// fxMinRate is the other end: a twentieth, past which the sound stops
102		// being sound.
103		fxMinRate = 0.05
104		// fxMinPlay is how little of the finished video a speed may come out as.
105		// It is the render's own floor (minClipLn) rather than a number of its
106		// own: below it the clip is not a fast stretch, it is a stretch of footage
107		// that never reaches the video. It used to be less than the render's, so
108		// anything past about ×2 over a short band was dropped in silence.
109		fxMinPlay = minClipLn
110	)
111	
112	// clampSpeed keeps a speed inside what the render can make of it: a rate
113	// between fxMinRate and fxMaxRate, over a stretch that still lasts fxMinPlay
114	// on screen once the rate has had it. When those two fight it is the RATE that
115	// gives way -- the seconds are what the user marked and can see.
116	func clampSpeed(rate, dur float64) (float64, float64) {
117		dur = math.Max(minClipLn, dur)
118		rate = math.Max(fxMinRate, math.Min(fxMaxRate, rate))
119		if dur/rate < fxMinPlay {
120			rate = dur / fxMinPlay
121		}
122		return rate, dur
123	}
124	
125	// fxMaxGain is as loud as a volume effect goes: ten times what was recorded,
126	// which is 1000% on the form. The number is not arbitrary -- it is the ceiling
127	// of playbin's own volume property, so the preview can be as loud as the
128	// render and neither has to explain a limit the other does not have. Past it
129	// there is nothing left to recover anyway: a passage quiet enough to need more
130	// than ten times is a passage whose noise floor comes up with it.
131	const fxMaxGain = 10.0
132	
133	// clampGain holds a gain to what both ends of the app can make of it. Silence
134	// is a legitimate answer, so the floor is 0 and not some small number.
135	func clampGain(g float64) float64 { return math.Max(0, math.Min(fxMaxGain, g)) }
136	
137	// fxSpan is the stretch of session time an effect owns on the timeline, and it
138	// is the same stretch for every kind: T to T+Dur, fades included. The bar on
139	// the lane IS the seconds the effect is doing something -- the camera away
140	// from where it was, the clock off its own rate, the words or the still on
141	// screen -- which is what makes two 3 s effects the same width whatever their
142	// transitions.
143	func (f cutFx) fxSpan() (float64, float64) {
144		switch f.Kind {
145		case "zoom", "speed", "text", "svg", "volume", "label":
146			return f.T, f.T + math.Max(f.Dur, 0)
147		}
148		return f.T, f.T
149	}
150	
151	func (f cutFx) frozenFx() bool { return f.Kind == "speed" && f.Rate <= 0 }
152	
153	// fxLabel is how an effect introduces itself in the status line and the lane.
154	func (f cutFx) fxLabel() string {
155		switch f.Kind {
156		case "zoom":
157			var extra []string
158			if f.Trans > 0 {
159				extra = append(extra, fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs in", f.Trans))
160			}
161			if !f.Stay && f.Tout > 0 {
162				extra = append(extra, fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs out", f.Tout))
163			}
164			if f.Stay {
165				extra = append(extra, "stays")
166			}
167			if len(extra) > 0 {
168				return fmt.Sprintf("zoom at %s for %.1fs (%s)", mmss(f.T), f.Dur, strings.Join(extra, ", "))
169			}
170			return fmt.Sprintf("zoom at %s for %.1fs", mmss(f.T), f.Dur)
171		case "speed":
172			if f.frozenFx() {
173				var extra []string
174				if f.Trans > 0 || f.Tout > 0 {
175					extra = append(extra, fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs in", math.Max(f.Trans, 0)),
176						fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs out", math.Max(f.Tout, 0)))
177				}
178				if f.sound() == sndMute {
179					extra = append(extra, "silent")
180				}
181				if len(extra) > 0 {
182					return fmt.Sprintf("stop at %s for %.1fs (%s)",
183						mmss(f.T), f.Dur, strings.Join(extra, ", "))
184				}
185				return fmt.Sprintf("stop at %s for %.1fs", mmss(f.T), f.Dur)
186			}
187			verb := "slowed"
188			if f.Rate > 1 {
189				verb = "sped up"
190			}
191			ramp := ""
192			if f.Trans > 0 || f.Tout > 0 {
193				ramp = fmt.Sprintf(" (%.1fs in, %.1fs out)", math.Max(f.Trans, 0), math.Max(f.Tout, 0))
194			}
195			// and what the sound does, when it is not what it has always done
196			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s ×%s for %.1fs%s%s", mmss(f.T), verb, fxNum(f.Rate),
197				f.Dur, ramp, sndSuffix(f))
198		case "text":
199			return fmt.Sprintf("text %s at %s for %.1fs", quoteFirst(f.Text, 24), mmss(f.T), f.Dur)
200		case "svg":
201			return fmt.Sprintf("svg %s at %s for %.1fs", svgName(f), mmss(f.T), f.Dur)
202		case "label":
203			return fmt.Sprintf("label %s at %s", quoteFirst(f.Text, 24), mmss(f.T))
204		case "volume":
205			verb := "louder"
206			switch g := clampGain(f.Gain); {
207			case g == 0:
208				verb = "silent"
209			case g < 1:
210				verb = "quieter"
211			}
212			fade := ""
213			if f.Trans > 0 || f.Tout > 0 {
214				fade = fmt.Sprintf(" (%.1fs in, %.1fs out)", math.Max(f.Trans, 0), math.Max(f.Tout, 0))
215			}
216			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s at %s for %.1fs%s",
217				mmss(f.T), verb, gainPct(f.Gain), f.Dur, fade)
218		}
219		return "effect"
220	}
221	
222	// quoteFirst is the opening of a text effect, for a label that has to fit on a
223	// status line: one line of it, cut at n characters with an ellipsis, quoted so
224	// an empty one still reads as something rather than as a gap.
225	func quoteFirst(s string, n int) string {
226		s = strings.Join(strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\n", " ")), " ")
227		if r := []rune(s); len(r) > n {
228			s = strings.TrimSpace(string(r[:n])) + "…"
229		}
230		return "“" + s + "”"
231	}
232	
233	// ---- aspect -----------------------------------------------------------------
234	
235	// fxAspects is what the toolbar offers. "source" is the absence of a choice:
236	// the cut comes out the shape the footage is, which is what every cut did
237	// before this control existed.
238	var fxAspects = []string{"source", "9:16", "1:1", "4:5", "16:9"}
239	
240	// parseAspect turns "9:16" into 9.0/16, or 0 for "source"/"" -- 0 meaning "the
241	// footage's own", which nothing here needs a number for.
242	func parseAspect(s string) float64 {
243		var w, h float64
244		if n, _ := fmt.Sscanf(s, "%f:%f", &w, &h); n == 2 && w > 0 && h > 0 {
245			return w / h
246		}
247		return 0
248	}
249	
250	// ---- where the camera is ----------------------------------------------------
251	
252	// fxRect is a camera rectangle, normalized to the source frame (see cutFx).
253	type fxRect struct{ cx, cy, hf float64 }
254	
255	func lerpRect(a, b fxRect, k float64) fxRect {
256		k = math.Min(1, math.Max(0, k))
257		return fxRect{a.cx + (b.cx-a.cx)*k, a.cy + (b.cy-a.cy)*k, a.hf + (b.hf-a.hf)*k}
258	}
259	
260	// fullFill is the framing nobody has to place: the output frame carved out of
261	// the middle of the source at the footage's own scale.
262	// A portrait cut of widescreen footage gets the full height with the sides
263	// cropped; the other way round gets the full width with top and bottom
264	// cropped. NOT a letterbox -- the picture stays its own size and a zoom is
265	// how the user picks WHICH slice, not whether there is one. srcA and outA
266	// are width over height; the same shape in and out is the exact frame.
267	func fullFill(srcA, outA float64) fxRect {
268		if srcA <= 0 || outA <= 0 {
269			return fxRect{0.5, 0.5, 1}
270		}
271		return fxRect{0.5, 0.5, math.Min(1, srcA/outA)}
272	}
273	
274	func (r fxRect) rect() (cx, cy, hf float64) { return r.cx, r.cy, r.hf }
275	
276	// fxRectAt is where the camera is at session time t -- the one answer for the
277	// preview overlay and the render's camera path (produce_fx.go). Zooms chain:
278	// each glides from where the camera actually is at its T, holds, then returns
279	// to the framing it left or (Stay) becomes that framing. Nothing reaches
280	// backwards: an effect acts over its own seconds and after, never before.
281	func fxRectAt(fx []cutFx, t float64, srcA, outA float64) fxRect {
282		return camRectAt(zoomsOf(fx), t, srcA, outA)
283	}
284	
285	// camRectAt is fxRectAt over the camera effects alone, already in order.
286	func camRectAt(zooms []cutFx, t float64, srcA, outA float64) fxRect {
287		settled := fullFill(srcA, outA)
288		// the zoom being walked: where it goes, where it came from, where it goes
289		// back to, and its shape in time
290		to, from, back := settled, settled, settled
291		t0, trans, dur, tout, stay := math.Inf(-1), 0.0, 0.0, 0.0, true
292		at := func(tt float64) fxRect {
293			if trans > 0 && tt < t0+trans {
294				return lerpRect(from, to, (tt-t0)/trans) // still arriving
295			}
296			if !stay {
297				if tt >= t0+dur {
298					return back
299				}
300				// held for its seconds and now letting go: the same glide as the
301				// way in, run backwards to where the camera came from
302				if tout > 0 {
303					if u := (tt - (t0 + dur - tout)) / tout; u > 0 {
304						return lerpRect(to, back, u)
305					}
306				}
307			}
308			return to
309		}
310		for _, z := range zooms {
311			if z.T > t {
312				break
313			}
314			tin, tback := z.zoomGlides()
315			// at(z.T) and not `to`: a zoom placed while the one before it is
316			// still moving starts from where the camera actually is, so the two
317			// never fight over the same second
318			from, back = at(z.T), settled
319			to = fxRect{z.Cx, z.Cy, z.Hf}
320			t0, trans, dur, tout, stay = z.T, tin, math.Max(z.Dur, 0), tback, z.Stay
321			if stay {
322				settled = to
323			}
324		}
325		return at(t)
326	}
327	
328	// clampFades holds an effect's two fades inside its own band: neither below
329	// zero, and never together longer than the seconds they have to happen in.
330	// Asked for more than there is, both give way in proportion -- cutting one
331	// side back to nothing and leaving the other at its full length would turn a
332	// fade the hand drew as symmetric into a lopsided one, for a reason nothing
333	// on screen explains.
334	//
335	// This is the one fade rule, and every place that sets a fade goes through it:
336	// the three dialogs, the drag that resizes a band, and the pass that holds a
337	// suggestion to the final cut. That matters because zoomGlides, textFades and
338	// speedRamps all clamp again at render time -- so a number stored outside the
339	// band is a number the dialog shows you and the render quietly ignores.
340	func clampFades(f *cutFx) {
341		f.Trans = math.Max(f.Trans, 0)
342		f.Tout = math.Max(f.Tout, 0)
343		dur := math.Max(f.Dur, 0)
344		if sum := f.Trans + f.Tout; sum > dur {
345			if sum <= 0 {
346				return // both already zero: nothing to share out
347			}
348			k := dur / sum
349			f.Trans, f.Tout = f.Trans*k, f.Tout*k
350		}
351	}
352	
353	// trimFades is what a band cut shorter does to the two fades inside it, where
354	// was is the seconds it covered before: they shrink in proportion, so the
355	// effect keeps its shape. Held at their old lengths, six seconds cut to two
356	// left 2/2 fading -- the camera never once held the region.
357	func trimFades(f *cutFx, was float64) {
358		if was > 0 && f.Dur < was {
359			k := math.Max(f.Dur, 0) / was
360			f.Trans, f.Tout = f.Trans*k, f.Tout*k
361		}
362		clampFades(f)
363	}
364	
365	// zoomGlides is the in and out glide a zoom actually gets: each at least 0,
366	// together no longer than the zoom itself, the way in winning any overlap.
367	func (z cutFx) zoomGlides() (tin, tout float64) {
368		dur := math.Max(z.Dur, 0)
369		tin = math.Min(math.Max(z.Trans, 0), dur)
370		tout = math.Min(math.Max(z.Tout, 0), dur-tin)
371		return
372	}
373	
374	// zoomsOf is the cut's camera effects, in the order the camera obeys them.
375	func zoomsOf(fx []cutFx) []cutFx {
376		var out []cutFx
377		for _, f := range fx {
378			if f.Kind == "zoom" {
379				out = append(out, f)
380			}
381		}
382		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].T < out[j].T })
383		return out
384	}
385	
386	// hasStay is whether the cut has been given a lasting framing at all -- one
387	// zoom that stays on its region. Without one the finished video is the plain
388	// centred slice of the recording from beginning to end.
389	func (ed *cutEditor) hasStay() bool {
390		for _, f := range ed.fx {
391			if f.Kind == "zoom" && f.Stay {
392				return true
393			}
394		}
395		return false
396	}
397	
398	// migrateFx brings a cut.json written before the camera effects became one
399	// kind up to date. A "view" was a region the camera kept until the next one --
400	// a zoom that stays -- with its hold stored WITHOUT the glides; a view that
401	// glided back out to the whole frame was already a zoom that pulls back. The
402	// numbers move over so the finished video is frame for frame what it was.
403	func migrateFx(fx []cutFx) []cutFx {
404		for i := range fx {
405			f := &fx[i]
406			// the stop's old silence tick, which was a bool because a stop was the
407			// only rate with a question about its sound. Every rate has one now
408			// (sndOf), so the answer is a word rather than a flag.
409			if f.Mute {
410				f.Mute = false
411				if f.Snd == "" {
412					f.Snd = sndMute
413				}
414			}
415			if f.Kind != "view" {
416				continue
417			}
418			f.Kind = "zoom"
419			f.Dur = math.Max(f.Trans, 0) + math.Max(f.Dur, 0) + math.Max(f.Tout, 0)
420			f.Stay = f.Tout <= 0
421		}
422		return fx
423	}
424	
425	// fxHasCamera is whether anything would move or crop the picture: an aspect
426	// that is not the source's, or any zoom at all. It is the render's "is the
427	// whole camera machinery needed at all" question.
428	func fxHasCamera(aspect string, fx []cutFx) bool {
429		if parseAspect(aspect) > 0 {
430			return true
431		}
432		for _, f := range fx {
433			if f.Kind == "zoom" {
434				return true
435			}
436		}
437		return false
438	}
439	
440	// ---- the clock: speed effects on the segment list ---------------------------
441	
442	// applyFx rewrites a render sequence (splitSpliced's output) with the speed
443	// effects: footage under one gets its Rate. Only footage, only its clock --
444	// cards keep their own, a freeze is an overlay (freezeCues) and not here, and
445	// an effect whose moment is in no kept segment does nothing.
446	func applyFx(segs []cutSeg, fx []cutFx) []cutSeg {
447		out := segs
448		for _, st := range rateSpans(fx) {
449			if r := st.applied(); math.Abs(r-1) > 1e-9 {
450				out = rateSpan(out, st.t0, st.t1, r)
451			}
452		}
453		return out
454	}
455	
456	func speedsOf(fx []cutFx) []cutFx {
457		var out []cutFx
458		for _, f := range fx {
459			if f.Kind == "speed" {
460				out = append(out, f)
461			}
462		}
463		sort.SliceStable(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].T < out[j].T })
464		return out
465	}
466	
467	// rateStep is one constant-rate stretch of a speed effect.
468	type rateStep struct{ t0, t1, rate float64 }
469	
470	// rampStep is how long one stair of a ramp lasts IN THE FINISHED VIDEO, not in
471	// footage: at ×8 a stair reads eight seconds of footage to last one on screen.
472	// Measured in footage, every stair of a fast ramp fell under the render's floor
473	// and its seconds went missing. Finer stairs are clips too short to render.
474	const rampStep = 0.6
475	
476	// speedRamps is the seconds a speed effect actually spends ramping each way:
477	// under one stair rounds to none at all (see rampStep), and ramps asked to
478	// cover more than the effect does share it in proportion, the flat middle
479	// disappearing between them. The lane draws exactly these, so the triangles
480	// on the marker are the stairs the render makes and not the numbers as typed.
481	func (f cutFx) speedRamps() (in, out float64) {
482		in, out = f.rampAsk()
483		if in <= 0 && out <= 0 {
484			return 0, 0
485		}
486		// and the staircase they imply has to be one the render will keep whole.
487		// A dropped stair does not play at the wrong speed, it takes its footage
488		// out of the video -- so a staircase that cannot be built entirely is not
489		// built at all, and the effect falls back to the plain change of speed it
490		// would have been with no ramps, which clampSpeed has already made sure
491		// is long enough to render.
492		for _, st := range f.stairs(in, out) {
493			if (st.t1-st.t0)/st.rate < minClipLn-1e-9 {
494				return 0, 0
495			}
496		}
497		return in, out
498	}
499	
500	// rampAsk is the ramps as asked for, held to what a stair costs: the arithmetic
501	// before the staircase is checked.
502	func (f cutFx) rampAsk() (in, out float64) {
503		in, out = math.Max(f.Trans, 0), math.Max(f.Tout, 0)
504		// the footage one stair costs at this rate. A single stair of a ramp to
505		// ×R runs at √R -- the geometric middle of 1 and R -- so that is the rate
506		// the price is set at, and a ramp that cannot pay it gets none.
507		least := rampStep * math.Sqrt(math.Max(1, f.Rate))
508		if in < least {
509			in = 0
510		}
511		if out < least {
512			out = 0
513		}
514		if in+out > f.Dur {
515			k := f.Dur / (in + out)
516			in, out = in*k, out*k
517			// the share-out can leave a ramp under the price again
518			if in < least {
519				in = 0
520			}
521			if out < least {
522				out = 0
523			}
524			return
525		}
526		// a flat middle too short to render is worse than no flat middle at all:
527		// the ramps grow to meet where it was, rather than the render dropping it
528		// and the seconds between the two ramps going missing
529		if mid := f.Dur - in - out; mid > 0 && mid/f.Rate < minClipLn {
530			k := f.Dur / (in + out)
531			in, out = in*k, out*k
532		}
533		return
534	}
535	
536	// speedSteps turns a ramp into the constant-rate stairs ffmpeg can make (one
537	// setpts/atempo per clip). Rates climb geometrically, each stair at the rate
538	// of its own middle; the count is set by the fastest end, whose stair comes out
539	// shortest (rampStairs). At least one stair.
540	func speedSteps(f cutFx) []rateStep {
541		if f.Rate <= 0 || f.Dur <= 0 {
542			return nil
543		}
544		in, out := f.speedRamps()
545		if in <= 0 && out <= 0 {
546			return []rateStep{{f.T, f.T + f.Dur, f.Rate}}
547		}
548		return f.stairs(in, out)
549	}
550	
551	// stairs builds the staircase for ramps of exactly in and out seconds. It is
552	// split from speedSteps because speedRamps has to look at the stairs a pair of
553	// ramps would make before it can say whether those ramps happen at all, and a
554	// function that called speedRamps to answer that would be asking itself.
555	func (f cutFx) stairs(in, out float64) []rateStep {
556		var steps []rateStep
557		ramp := func(t0, d, from, to float64) {
558			n := rampStairs(d, from, to)
559			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
560				u := (float64(i) + 0.5) / float64(n)
561				steps = append(steps, rateStep{
562					t0: t0 + d*float64(i)/float64(n),
563					t1: t0 + d*float64(i+1)/float64(n),
564					// from·(to/from)^u: the geometric middle of the stair
565					rate: from * math.Pow(to/from, u),
566				})
567			}
568		}
569		if in > 0 {
570			ramp(f.T, in, 1, f.Rate)
571		}
572		if f.Dur-in-out > 1e-6 {
573			steps = append(steps, rateStep{f.T + in, f.T + f.Dur - out, f.Rate})
574		}
575		if out > 0 {
576			ramp(f.T+f.Dur-out, out, f.Rate, 1)
577		}
578		return steps
579	}
580	
581	// fxGainAt is how loud session second t is, as a linear gain: 1 with no volume
582	// effect, every covering effect MULTIPLIED (two gains are two things done to
583	// the same sound; rates average instead, rateSpans), capped at a single
584	// effect's ceiling. The one gain rule: the preview reads it per tick
585	// (syncPlayGain), the render per clip (gainCues).
586	func fxGainAt(fx []cutFx, t float64) float64 {
587		g := 1.0
588		for _, f := range fx {
589			if f.Kind != "volume" {
590				continue
591			}
592			// the fades are a title's fades, evaluated by a title's function: a
593			// volume effect's envelope is 0 outside its band, 1 across the middle
594			// and a straight ramp either side, which is exactly what textAlpha is.
595			// A band of no length needs no guard of its own -- textAlpha reads it
596			// as covering no second at all, so it changes nothing here
597			g *= 1 + (clampGain(f.Gain)-1)*textAlpha(f, t)
598		}
599		return clampGain(g)
600	}
601	
602	// gainPct is a gain written the way the form asks for it and the lane shows
603	// it: whole percent, because "180%" is how loud something is and "1.8" is a
604	// number that has to be converted before it means anything.
605	func gainPct(g float64) string {
606		return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f%%", clampGain(g)*100)
607	}
608	
609	// rampStairs is how many stairs a ramp gets: as many as the render keeps whole,
610	// judged at the fastest stair's OWN rate -- half a stair short of the top --
611	// not at the top, or an eight-second ramp to ×8 gets one stair where it can
612	// afford two.
613	func rampStairs(d, from, to float64) int {
614		n := 1
615		for rampFits(d, from, to, n+1) {
616			n++
617		}
618		return n
619	}
620	
621	// rampFits asks whether all n stairs of a ramp clear rampStep on screen, by
622	// measuring the fastest of them: the last stair going up, the first coming
623	// down, and the same rate either way.
624	func rampFits(d, from, to float64, n int) bool {
625		lo, hi := math.Min(from, to), math.Max(from, to)
626		if lo <= 0 || n < 1 {
627			return false
628		}
629		// lo·(hi/lo)^((n-½)/n): the middle of the stair that ends at hi
630		fast := lo * math.Pow(hi/lo, (float64(n)-0.5)/float64(n))
631		return (d/float64(n))/fast >= rampStep
632	}
633	
634	// fxPreviewRateAt is the rate the PREVIEW runs at t: the covering speed
635	// effect's rate flat across its seconds (the render follows the stairs). A
636	// rate change is a flushing seek on the GTK thread, and a ramp's stairs ten
637	// times a second hung the window. A stop reads as 1 (the still is an overlay);
638	// overlapping speeds take the first, where the render averages (rateSpans).
639	func fxPreviewRateAt(fx []cutFx, t float64) float64 {
640		for _, f := range speedsOf(fx) {
641			if f.frozenFx() || f.Dur <= 0 || t < f.T || t >= f.T+f.Dur {
642				continue
643			}
644			r, _ := clampSpeed(f.Rate, f.Dur)
645			return r
646		}
647		return 1
648	}
649	
650	// fxRateAt is the clock the footage at session time t runs on -- what the
651	// covering speed effects ask for, ramps included, or 1. Reads the same
652	// stretches applyFx applies. Frozen seconds come back as 1, not 0: the footage
653	// under a still runs on at full speed so the still can fade out onto it where
654	// the clock says. fxMeanRate keeps the 0.
655	func fxRateAt(fx []cutFx, t float64) float64 {
656		for _, st := range rateSpans(fx) {
657			if t >= st.t0 && t < st.t1 {
658				return st.applied()
659			}
660		}
661		return 1
662	}
663	
664	// rateSpan gives every piece of footage inside [t0, t1) the rate, splitting
665	// clips at the boundaries so the rest of them play at their own speed.
666	func rateSpan(segs []cutSeg, t0, t1, rate float64) []cutSeg {
667		var out []cutSeg
668		for _, s := range segs {
669			if s.isInsert() || s.Dur > 0 || s.E <= t0 || s.S >= t1 {
670				out = append(out, s)
671				continue
672			}
673			if s.S < t0 {
674				head := s
675				head.E = t0
676				out = append(out, head)
677			}
678			mid := s
679			mid.S, mid.E, mid.Rate = math.Max(s.S, t0), math.Min(s.E, t1), rate
680			out = append(out, mid)
681			if s.E > t1 {
682				tail := s
683				tail.S = t1
684				out = append(out, tail)
685			}
686		}
687		return out
688	}
689	
690	// ---- the effects on the page -------------------------------------------------
691	//
692	// The editor's half: the lane under the video track, the toolbar controls
693	// that create effects, and the forms that ask their numbers. The gestures are
694	// the timeline's own: press picks up, drag slides, ‹f/f› nudge, Del removes,
695	// Esc puts down, Insert reads ✎ Edit while one is held.
696	
697	// fxLaneH is the height of the effects lane drawn under the picture band.
698	// Always there, even empty: a lane that appears when the first effect does
699	// would move the audio lanes down at the moment you are aiming at them.
700	//
701	// It is deliberately generous. A short effect is a bar a few pixels wide, so
702	// height is the only dimension it has left to be aimed at with; a lane sized
703	// to the long bands alone makes the short ones fiddly.
704	const fxLaneH = 26
705	
706	// fxLaneTop is the lane's y: directly under the green bar, above the pictures,
707	// so the two bands that speak for the whole cut sit together and the lane's y
708	// does not move with the camera rows.
709	func (ed *cutEditor) fxLaneTop() float64 { return float64(rulerH) + float64(selBandH) }
710	
711	// fxHitLane is whether a press in the source-track area lands in the lane. It
712	// has a bottom now: with the lane under the pictures this was everything below
713	// its top, and the slack at the foot of the area went to it by default.
714	func (ed *cutEditor) fxHitLane(y float64) bool {
715		return y >= ed.fxLaneTop() && y < ed.picTop()
716	}
717	
718	// fxPackMin is the shortest span the packing gives width to. A very short
719	// effect is nearly a point in time, so two of them a frame apart would pack
720	// into the same row and draw through each other -- which is the thing rows
721	// exist to stop. A floor of a few tenths of a second makes "these are two effects, not
722	// one" a fact about the cut rather than about how far in you happen to be
723	// zoomed.
724	const fxPackMin = 0.4
725	
726	// fxRows assigns each effect a row: the first whose contents it does not
727	// overlap (first-fit in start order colours an interval graph optimally), so
728	// the lane is only as deep as the deepest pile. In seconds, not pixels, so
729	// rows do not reshuffle with the zoom.
730	func fxRows(fx []cutFx) ([]int, int) {
731		rows := make([]int, len(fx))
732		order := make([]int, len(fx))
733		for i := range order {
734			order[i] = i
735		}
736		sort.SliceStable(order, func(a, b int) bool {
737			ta, _ := fx[order[a]].fxSpan()
738			tb, _ := fx[order[b]].fxSpan()
739			return ta < tb
740		})
741		var ends []float64 // how far right each row reaches so far
742		for _, i := range order {
743			t0, t1 := fx[i].fxSpan()
744			t1 = math.Max(t1, t0+fxPackMin)
745			r := 0
746			for ; r < len(ends); r++ {
747				if ends[r] <= t0 {
748					break
749				}
750			}
751			if r == len(ends) {
752				ends = append(ends, 0)
753			}
754			ends[r], rows[i] = t1, r
755		}
756		return rows, max(1, len(ends))
757	}
758	
759	// fxLaneHeight is what the lane asks the page for: one row's worth even when
760	// there is nothing in it, because a lane that appeared with the first effect
761	// would move everything under it at the moment you were aiming there.
762	func (ed *cutEditor) fxLaneHeight() float64 {
763		_, n := fxRows(ed.fx)
764		return float64(n) * fxLaneH
765	}
766	
767	// fxSpanPx is where an effect is drawn and grabbed, in timeline px. Like
768	// spliceSpan: a thing with no width of its own still has to be a mouse
769	// target, so everything gets a floor.
770	func (ed *cutEditor) fxSpanPx(f cutFx) (float64, float64) {
771		t0, t1 := f.fxSpan()
772		x0, x1 := ed.xOf(t0), ed.xOf(t1)
773		return x0, math.Max(x1, x0+10)
774	}
775	
776	// fxBandSpan is the effect's band as DRAWN, in seconds -- fxSpan for every
777	// kind, now that a freeze's bar is the session seconds its still stands over.
778	func (ed *cutEditor) fxBandSpan(f cutFx) (float64, float64) {
779		return f.fxSpan()
780	}
781	
782	// which part of an effect's band a press has hold of.
783	const (
784		fxWhole = iota
785		fxStart
786		fxEnd
787	)
788	
789	// fxMinBand is how wide a bar must be drawn before its ends become handles.
790	// A short effect on a zoomed-out timeline is a sliver ten pixels across and is
791	// meant to be picked up and slid; if its ends were grips, every attempt to
792	// move one would stretch it instead. Ends are for things that are already
793	// bands on screen.
794	const fxMinBand = 30.0
795	
796	// fxMinDur is the shortest a band may be dragged down to. A zoom or a title of
797	// no length does nothing, cannot be grabbed again, and looks exactly like the
798	// effect having been deleted -- so the hand that overshoots gets a very short
799	// effect rather than an invisible one.
800	const fxMinDur = 0.1

961	// for saying "not quite there".

1341	// setAspect points the editor and its dropdown at an aspect without treating
1342	// it as an edit: reload, undo and revert come through here.
1343	func (ed *cutEditor) setAspect(s string) {
1344		if s == "source" {
1345			s = ""
1346		}
1347		ed.aspect = s
1348		if ed.aspectDD != nil {
1349			pos := 0
1350			for i, a := range fxAspects {
1351				if a == s {
1352					pos = i
1353				}
1354			}
1355			ed.aspectMu = true
1356			ed.aspectDD.SetSelected(uint(pos))
1357			ed.aspectMu = false
1358		}
1359		if ed.fxArea != nil {
1360			ed.fxArea.QueueDraw()
1361		}
1362	}
1363	
1364	// aspectChanged is the dropdown being used by hand: an edit like any other,
1365	// undoable and saved.
1366	// aspectStayLn is how long the framing an aspect places runs. A second: a
1367	// staying zoom holds until the next one whatever its length, so this is only
1368	// how much of the lane it takes up -- long enough to see, take hold of and
1369	// press the ✕ on, short enough not to look like a stretch of the video it has
1370	// an opinion about.
1371	const aspectStayLn = 1.0
1372	
1373	func (ed *cutEditor) aspectChanged(s string) {
1374		if s == "source" {
1375			s = ""
1376		}
1377		if s == ed.aspect {
1378			return
1379		}
1380		ed.pushUndo()
1381		ed.aspect = s
1382		// the framing this shape asks for goes in the SAME step: one press, one
1383		// undo, and the file on disk is written once with both in it
1384		placed := s != "" && !ed.hasStay()
1385		if placed {
1386			sw, sh := ed.fxSrcSize()
1387			r := fullFill(sw/sh, parseAspect(s))
1388			ed.fx = append(ed.fx, cutFx{Kind: "zoom", T: 0, Dur: aspectStayLn,
1389				Cx: r.cx, Cy: r.cy, Hf: r.hf, Stay: true})
1390		}
1391		ed.persist()
1392		if ed.fxArea != nil {
1393			ed.fxArea.QueueDraw()
1394		}
1395		if s == "" {
1396			ed.a.setStatus("aspect: the source's own — the video comes out the shape it was filmed")
1397			return
1398		}
1399		// A cut with an aspect of its own needs a framing; rather than a hidden
1400		// fallback, it is placed as a staying zoom at 0:00, centred, full-fill, one
1401		// second long -- visible on the lane, draggable, droppable. Only when no
1402		// staying zoom exists yet.
1403		if placed {
1404			ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("aspect %s — a ⊕ zoom at 0:00 holds the whole frame, centred", s))
1405			return
1406		}
1407		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("aspect %s — the zooms on the lane decide the framing", s))
1408	}

1410	// armFx puts the next drag on the video in charge of creating an effect.
1411	func (ed *cutEditor) armFx(kind string) {
1412		if ed.player == nil || ed.playVideo == nil || !ed.hasPlay {
1413			ed.a.setStatus("click a track first — the effect needs a moment to happen at")
1414			return
1415		}
1416		if ed.fxArm == kind {
1417			ed.disarmFx() // the button again is "never mind"
1418			return
1419		}
1420		ed.fxArm = kind
1421		ed.syncFxCursor()
1422		// arming a zoom drops the live layer (the box is drawn on
1423		// everything the camera could see); arming an overlay keeps it up (the
1424		// box is drawn on the finished frame). Either way the layer must follow
1425		// NOW, not at the next redraw.
1426		ed.syncPreviewZoom()
1427		ed.a.setStatus(ed.fxArmWords())
1428	}
1429	
1430	// disarmFx puts the armed drag down again, from Cancel or from picking the
1431	// same kind twice.
1432	func (ed *cutEditor) disarmFx() {
1433		if ed.fxArm == "" {
1434			return
1435		}
1436		ed.fxArm = ""

1438		ed.syncPreviewZoom()
1439		ed.a.setStatus("cancelled")
1440	}

1442	// fxArmWords is what an armed drag is waiting for, in one paragraph: the same
1443	// words the column shows and the status line says, so there is one wording to
1444	// keep true rather than two.
1445	func (ed *cutEditor) fxArmWords() string {
1446		when := "It starts at the red line and runs 3 s; the form that opens says how long."
1447		if t0, dur := ed.fxSpanNow(3); ed.fxMarked() {
1448			when = fmt.Sprintf("It covers the marked stretch — %s – %s, %.1f s — which the "+
1449				"form that opens can change.", mmss(t0), mmss(t0+dur), dur)
1450		}
1451		switch ed.fxArm {
1452		case "text":
1453			return "Drag the box the words go in — anywhere on the picture, any shape. " +
1454				"A click puts one across the lower third. " + when
1455		case "svg":
1456			return fmt.Sprintf("Drag the box %s goes in — anywhere on the picture, any "+
1457				"shape; the drawing keeps its own shape inside it. A click puts one "+
1458				"across the middle. %s", svgBase(ed.fxSrc), when)
1459		}
1460		return "Drag a box on the video: the picture zooms there and comes back out on " +
1461			"its own, or stays on it — the form that opens is where that is said. The " +
1462			"box keeps the cut's shape; let go near the full width or height to snap " +
1463			"to it. " + when
1464	}
1465	
1466	// fxSpanNow is where an effect placed now goes: the marked stretch if there is
1467	// one -- the rule ⏩ Speed already follows -- and def seconds from the red line
1468	// if there is not. Marking a stretch and then framing it is how the region a
1469	// zoom holds gets said without typing its length twice.
1470	func (ed *cutEditor) fxSpanNow(def float64) (float64, float64) {
1471		if t0, t1 := ed.selOrdered(); ed.fxMarked() {
1472			return t0, t1 - t0
1473		}
1474		return ed.playhead, def
1475	}
1476	
1477	// fxMarked is whether the band is worth placing an effect on. The same floor
1478	// ⏩ Speed uses: a band a fifth of a second wide is a click that shivered.
1479	func (ed *cutEditor) fxMarked() bool {
1480		t0, t1 := ed.selOrdered()
1481		return ed.sel.active && t1-t0 >= fxMinSel
1482	}
1483	
1484	// selOrdered is the band's ends the way round they are read, which is not the
1485	// way round they were drawn if the drag went right to left.
1486	func (ed *cutEditor) selOrdered() (float64, float64) {
1487		if ed.sel.t1 < ed.sel.t0 {
1488			return ed.sel.t1, ed.sel.t0
1489		}
1490		return ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1
1491	}
1492	
1493	// syncFxArm shows the armed drag in the column and takes the note away again:
1494	// arming otherwise changes only the cursor and the status line, which nobody
1495	// looks at. Called from syncFxCursor, which every arm and disarm path already
1496	// calls.
1497	func (ed *cutEditor) syncFxArm() {
1498		if ed.formBox == nil {
1499			return // headless, or a page with no column yet
1500		}
1501		if ed.fxArm == "" {
1502			if ed.formArm != "" {
1503				ed.hideForm()
1504			}
1505			return
1506		}
1507		if ed.formArm == ed.fxArm {
1508			return // already saying it
1509		}
1510		title := map[string]string{"zoom": "⊕ Zoom", "text": "❝ Text", "svg": "▨ SVG"}[ed.fxArm]
1511		words := gtk.NewLabel(ed.fxArmWords())
1512		words.SetXAlign(0)
1513		words.SetWrap(true)
1514		body := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 8)
1515		body.Append(words)
1516		cancel := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Cancel")
1517		cancel.SetTooltipText("put the drag down again — Esc does the same")
1518		cancel.ConnectClicked(func() { ed.disarmFx() })
1519		foot := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
1520		foot.SetHAlign(gtk.AlignEnd)
1521		foot.Append(cancel)
1522		// after the show, not before: showing takes the last form out, and if that
1523		// was this note its gone would clear the flag we had just set
1524		ed.showFormFoot(title, body, foot, func() { ed.formArm = "" })
1525		ed.formArm = ed.fxArm
1526	}
1527	
1528	// speedClicked is the ⏩ Speed entry: a stretch on a clock of its own,
1529	// including the one that does not run -- a stop is ×0, same dialog, same bar.
1530	// A marked stretch is the seconds it covers; with nothing marked, a couple of
1531	// seconds from the line.
1532	func (a *App) speedClicked() {
1533		ed := a.ed
1534		t0, t1 := ed.selOrdered()
1535		marked := ed.fxMarked()
1536		if !marked {
1537			if !ed.hasPlay {
1538				a.setStatus("click a track or mark a stretch first — speed needs seconds to work on")
1539				return
1540			}
1541			t0, t1 = ed.playhead, ed.playhead+2
1542		}
1543		f := cutFx{Kind: "speed", T: t0, Dur: t1 - t0, Rate: 0.5}
1544		if !marked {
1545			f.Rate, f.Trans, f.Tout = 0, 0.5, 0.5 // a stop, faded on and off
1546		}
1547		a.askSpeedParams(f, true, func(f cutFx) {
1548			ed.addFx(f)
1549			ed.sel.active = false
1550			what := "the footage plays at that rate there and the cut gets longer or shorter to match"
1551			if f.frozenFx() {
1552				what = "the picture stands still there while the clock runs"
1553			}
1554			a.setStatus(f.fxLabel() + " — " + what + "; ↶ Undo takes it back")
1555		})
1556	}
1557	
1558	// volumeClicked is the 🔊 Volume entry: a stretch of the session played louder or
1559	// quieter than it was recorded. The one effect here that changes nothing you
1560	// can see -- which is why it has no drag on the picture and no box: there is
1561	// nowhere on a frame to point at a sound.
1562	//
1563	// A marked stretch is the seconds it covers, and with nothing marked it takes
1564	// a couple of seconds from the line, exactly as a speed does.
1565	func (a *App) volumeClicked() {
1566		ed := a.ed
1567		t0, t1 := ed.selOrdered()
1568		marked := ed.fxMarked()
1569		if !marked {
1570			if !ed.hasPlay {
1571				a.setStatus("click a track or mark a stretch first — volume needs seconds to work on")
1572				return
1573			}
1574			t0, t1 = ed.playhead, ed.playhead+2
1575		}
1576		// twice as loud, and a quarter of a second of fade at each end. The fades
1577		// are not decoration: a gain that arrives on one sample is a click, and a
1578		// click is the one artefact a listener hears as a broken video rather than
1579		// as an edit. Typed to 0 by anyone who wants the hard step.
1580		f := cutFx{Kind: "volume", T: t0, Dur: t1 - t0, Gain: 2, Trans: 0.25, Tout: 0.25}
1581		a.askVolumeParams(f, true, func(f cutFx) {
1582			ed.addFx(f)
1583			ed.sel.active = false
1584			a.setStatus(f.fxLabel() + " — the picture is untouched")
1585		})
1586	}

1588	// labelClicked is the 🏷 Label entry: a name for a moment, in your own words.
1589	//
1590	// The one effect that changes nothing -- no picture, no sound, nothing in the
1591	// render at all. It exists to be READ: the narration writer is given a brief
1592	// per clip (what the frames showed, what was said) and neither of those can
1593	// contain "the reveal". This is the editor saying what they think is
1594	// happening, at the second they think it happens, in a line the user context
1595	// can point at.
1596	//
1597	// Placed like a volume: over the marked stretch, or a couple of seconds from
1598	// the red line. It is a moment rather than a span, but a bar with no width is
1599	// nothing to aim at afterwards, and a span says how long the moment lasts.
