1666				"same terms", f.Tout, live)
1667		eRow, ec := fxEaseRow(f, live)
1668		a.fxWin(fmt.Sprintf("Volume %s – %s", mmss(f.T), mmss(f.T+f.Dur)), isNew, live,
1669			[]gtk.Widgetter{fxLine(gRow, lRow), fxLine(iRow, oRow, eRow)}, func() {
1670				f.Gain = clampGain(fxNumOf(g, clampGain(f.Gain)*100) / 100)
1671				// no minClipLn here: a volume effect makes no clip, so the render's
1672				// floor is not its floor. A tenth of a second is the shortest thing
1673				// worth placing -- audible, and still a band the lane can draw.
1674				f.Dur = math.Max(0.1, fxNumOf(l, f.Dur))
1675				f.Trans, f.Tout = math.Max(0, fxNumOf(i, f.Trans)), math.Max(0, fxNumOf(o, f.Tout))
1676				f.Ease = fxEaseOf(ec.Selected())
1677				clampFades(&f)
1678				ok(f)
1679			})
1680	}
1681	
1682	// editFx reopens the held effect's numbers -- the ✎ Edit button's other job.
1683	func (a *App) editFx() {
1684		ed := a.ed
1685		f := ed.heldFx()
1686		if f == nil {
1687			return
1688		}
1689		// which effect this is, taken as a value: the form opens in the page's
1690		// column and not in a window over it (cut_form.go), so the timeline stays
1691		// live under it -- the hold can be moved to another effect, and an undo can
1692		// renumber the list, between opening the form and pressing Save.
1693		was := *f
1694		switch f.Kind {
1695		case "zoom":
1696			a.askZoomParams(was, false, func(nf cutFx) { ed.updateFx(was, nf) })
1697		case "speed":
1698			a.askSpeedParams(was, false, func(nf cutFx) { ed.updateFx(was, nf) })
1699		case "text":
1700			a.askTextParams(was, false, func(nf cutFx) { ed.updateFx(was, nf) })
1701		case "svg":
1702			a.askSvgParams(was, false, func(nf cutFx) { ed.updateFx(was, nf) })
1703		case "volume":
1704			a.askVolumeParams(was, false, func(nf cutFx) { ed.updateFx(was, nf) })
1705		case "label":
1706			a.askLabelParams(was, false, func(nf cutFx) { ed.updateFx(was, nf) })
1707		}
1708	}
1709	
1710	// indexOfFx finds an effect again by what it was, the way indexOfSeg finds a
1711	// segment. Same reason, too: the form is not a window and does not hold the
1712	// timeline still, so "the held one" at Save time may be a different effect
1713	// entirely -- and writing a zoom's numbers onto the caption somebody clicked
1714	// while the form was open is the one mistake here that cannot be seen happening.
1715	func (ed *cutEditor) indexOfFx(want cutFx) int {
1716		for i, f := range ed.fx {
1717			if f.Kind == want.Kind && math.Abs(f.T-want.T) < 0.001 {
1718				return i
1719			}
1720		}
1721		return -1
1722	}
1723	
1724	// updateFx is writeFx with a step in the history: the first answer a form gives
1725	// is the edit, and the ones behind it are the same edit still being typed
1726	// (fxLiveOk).
1727	func (ed *cutEditor) updateFx(was, nf cutFx) {
1728		if ed.indexOfFx(was) >= 0 {
1729			ed.pushUndo()
1730		}
1731		ed.writeFx(was, nf)
1732	}
1733	
1734	// writeFx writes a form's answer back onto the effect the form was opened for,
1735	// which is not necessarily the one held now.
1736	func (ed *cutEditor) writeFx(was, nf cutFx) {
1737		i := ed.indexOfFx(was)
1738		if i < 0 {
1739			ed.a.setStatus("that effect is no longer in the cut — nothing was changed")
1740			return
1741		}
1742		// the box belongs to the picture, not to the form. No dialog has a field
1743		// for it -- a camera window and a caption's rectangle are only ever set by
1744		// dragging them on the preview -- and the form sits in the page's column
1745		// with that preview live beside it. So a box dragged bigger while the
1746		// words were being typed is NEWER than the snapshot the form opened with,
1747		// and writing the snapshot back is what made it spring to its old size on
1748		// Save. Take those four from the effect as it stands now.
1749		nf.Cx, nf.Cy, nf.Wf, nf.Hf = ed.fx[i].Cx, ed.fx[i].Cy, ed.fx[i].Wf, ed.fx[i].Hf
1750		ed.fx[i] = nf
1751		ed.persist()
1752		ed.a.setStatus(nf.fxLabel())
1753	}
1754	
1755	// ---- dialogs ----------------------------------------------------------------
1756	
1757	// fxWin is the form every effect opens in the Cut page's column (cut_form.go):
1758	// the caller's rows and a line saying what is already true. No Save/Cancel --
1759	// every keystroke lands after a beat (fxLive) and Undo takes the visit back.
1760	// isNew places the effect as the form opens.
1761	func (a *App) fxWin(title string, isNew bool, live *fxLive, rows []gtk.Widgetter, apply func()) {
1762		form := a.cutForm()
1763		if form == nil {
1764			return // no page, so no column and no effect to be editing
1765		}
1766		// the form about to be replaced hands its last keystroke over first
1767		// (dropForm, from showFormFoot below) -- so this is set after the rows are
1768		// built and before anything is applied, and a stale timer from the old
1769		// form finds a live that is no longer the current one and does nothing.
1770		live.fire = func() {
1771			if form.fxLiveCur == live {
1772				apply()
1773			}
1774		}
1775		note := gtk.NewLabel("Kept as you type — ↶ Undo takes the whole edit back.")
1776		note.SetXAlign(0)
1777		note.SetWrap(true)
1778		note.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
1779	
1780		box := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 8)
1781		for _, r := range rows {
1782			box.Append(r)
1783		}
1784		form.showFormFoot(title, box, note, nil) // which drops whatever form was up
1785		form.fxLiveCur, form.fxLiveOn = live, nil
1786		if isNew {
1787			apply() // not the debounce: the effect exists from the press that asked for it
1788		}
1789	}
1790	
1791	// fxLive is the thread every control in a live form pulls when it changes: one
1792	// per form, handed to the rows as they are built, wired up after. The wait is
1793	// the page's debounce -- a burst of keystrokes is one edit.
1794	type fxLive struct {
1795		d    debounce
1796		fire func()
1797	}
1798	
1799	// touch is what a control calls. Safe before the form is wired: a widget that
1800	// fires while it is being built has nothing to apply yet.
1801	func (l *fxLive) touch() {
1802		if l == nil || l.fire == nil {
1803			return
1804		}
1805		f := l.fire
1806		l.d.call(f)
1807	}
1808	
1809	// fxLiveOk turns a form's stream of answers into "place it once, change it
1810	// after".
1811	//
1812	// A live form gives its answer over and over, and the first one is not the same
1813	// act as the rest: for a new effect it is the placement, for an edit it is the
1814	// first change, and either way it is the one that belongs in the undo history.
1815	// The ones after it write onto the same effect without pushing a step, so a
1816	// visit to a form is one thing to undo rather than one per burst of typing.
1817	//
1818	// The refusals stay with the caller (an svg with no file chosen is not placed),
1819	// which is why placement is detected rather than assumed: if the effect is not
1820	// in the cut after ok has had it, nothing was placed and the next answer is a
1821	// first answer again.
1822	func (a *App) fxLiveOk(ok func(cutFx)) func(cutFx) {
1823		return func(nf cutFx) {
1824			ed := a.ed
1825			if ed == nil {
1826				return
1827			}
1828			if ed.fxLiveOn == nil {
1829				ok(nf) // places it, or writes the first edit -- and pushes the undo
1830				if ed.indexOfFx(nf) < 0 {
1831					return // refused: the next answer is a first answer again
1832				}
1833				was := nf
1834				ed.fxLiveOn = &was
1835				return
1836			}
1837			ed.writeFx(*ed.fxLiveOn, nf)
1838		}
1839	}
1840	
1841	// fxField is one question in a form: the label and the control that answers
1842	// it, kept apart until the grid puts them in. Apart is the point -- a column
1843	// of labels lines up with the column beside it only if the grid can see the
1844	// labels themselves, and a label sealed inside a row box is a label the grid
1845	// cannot measure.
1846	type fxField struct {
1847		lbl *gtk.Label
1848		ctl gtk.Widgetter
1849	}
1850	
1851	// setSensitive greys the whole question, not half of it: a live label over a
1852	// dead entry reads as a field that is simply refusing to be typed in.
1853	func (f fxField) setSensitive(on bool) {
1854		f.lbl.SetSensitive(on)
1855		gtk.BaseWidget(f.ctl).SetSensitive(on)
1856	}
1857	
1858	// fxLine puts a form's questions on one line: label, control, label, control.
1859	// Line one is what the effect IS (rate/gain/sound, length), line two how it
1860	// arrives and leaves (the fades and their shape), the same in every dialog.
1861	func fxLine(fields ...fxField) *gtk.Box {
1862		b := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 6)
1863		for i, f := range fields {
1864			if i > 0 {
1865				f.lbl.SetMarginStart(12) // a gutter between one question and the next
1866			}
1867			f.lbl.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
1868			b.Append(f.lbl)
1869			b.Append(f.ctl)
1870		}
1871		return b
1872	}
1873	
1874	// fxRowLabel is a field's label, with the field's own words on both halves of
1875	// it: the explanation is wanted while the pointer is over either one.
1876	func fxRowLabel(text, tip string, ctl gtk.Widgetter) *gtk.Label {
1877		l := gtk.NewLabel(text)
1878		l.SetXAlign(0)
1879		if tip != "" {
1880			l.SetTooltipText(tip)
1881			gtk.BaseWidget(ctl).SetTooltipText(tip)
1882		}
1883		return l
1884	}
1885	
1886	// fxNumRow is a labelled number entry, the control these dialogs are mostly
1887	// made of. It asks for the width it will use and no more: every number in
1888	// these forms is seconds or a percent, "0.35" and "180" are the shape of them,
1889	// and an entry given the panel's slack was a hand's width of white for four
1890	// characters. The live form has no Enter to press -- what is typed is applied
1891	// a beat after the typing stops (fxLive).
1892	func fxNumRow(label, tip string, val float64, live *fxLive) (fxField, *gtk.Entry) {
1893		e := gtk.NewEntry()
1894		e.SetText(strings.TrimSuffix(fmt.Sprintf("%.1f", val), ".0"))
1895		e.SetWidthChars(fxNumChars)
1896		e.SetMaxWidthChars(fxNumChars)
1897		e.SetInputPurpose(gtk.InputPurposeNumber)
1898		e.ConnectChanged(live.touch)
1899		return fxField{fxRowLabel(label, tip, e), e}, e
1900	}
1901	
1902	// fxWordsRow is the label effect's words: a name for a moment, in the editor's
1903	// own words. Narrow, because it is a NAME -- "the reveal", "boss fight" -- and
1904	// a box the width of the panel invites a sentence, which is what the caption
1905	// effect is for. What is typed past the width still fits; the box scrolls.
1906	func fxWordsRow(f cutFx, live *fxLive) (fxField, *gtk.Entry) {
1907		e := gtk.NewEntry()
1908		e.SetText(f.Text)
1909		e.SetWidthChars(fxWordChars)
1910		e.SetMaxWidthChars(fxWordChars)
1911		e.ConnectChanged(live.touch)
1912		return fxField{fxRowLabel("Name",
1913			"what you call this moment -- \"the reveal\", \"boss fight\". It changes "+
1914				"nothing in the video: it is written into the brief the narration writer "+
1915				"is given, with the second it lands on, so your own notes on Prepare can "+
1916				"say what to do when it comes", e), e}, e
1917	}
1918	
1919	// fxWordChars is how wide that box is. A name, not a line.
1920	const fxWordChars = 10
1921	
1922	// fxNumChars is how wide a number field is: "100.5" is the longest thing any
1923	// of them holds.
1924	const fxNumChars = 5
1925	
1926	// fxEases are the shapes a fade can travel in, and there is one of them: every
1927	// fade in this app is a straight ramp, in the preview and in the render alike.
1928	// It is asked on the form regardless, because "what shape does it fade in" is
1929	// a question the form was answering on your behalf without saying so -- and a
1930	// curve added later appears in this list rather than quietly changing what
1931	// every effect already placed does.
1932	var fxEases = []string{"Linear"}
1933	
1934	// fxEaseOf is the name a picked shape is stored under. The straight ramp
1935	// stores as "", so a cut saved with this row on disk is byte for byte the cut
1936	// that was saved before the row existed.
1937	func fxEaseOf(i uint) string {
1938		if int(i) <= 0 || int(i) >= len(fxEases) {
1939			return ""
1940		}
1941		return strings.ToLower(fxEases[i])
1942	}
1943	
1944	func fxEaseIndex(name string) uint {
1945		for i, e := range fxEases {
1946			if strings.EqualFold(e, name) {
1947				return uint(i)
1948			}
1949		}
1950		return 0 // a shape this version has never heard of falls back to straight
1951	}
1952	
1953	// fxEaseRow is the fade-shape row, the same one in all four dialogs. It takes
1954	// the width of the one word in it: given the panel's slack, a dropdown holding
1955	// "Linear" was the widest thing on the form.
1956	func fxEaseRow(f cutFx, live *fxLive) (fxField, *gtk.DropDown) {
1957		dd := gtk.NewDropDownFromStrings(fxEases)
1958		dd.SetSelected(fxEaseIndex(f.Ease))
1959		dd.NotifyProperty("selected", live.touch)
1960		return fxField{fxRowLabel("Curve",
1961			"the shape both fades travel in. Straight is all there is so far: the "+
1962				"camera, the words or the clock move by the same amount every frame "+
1963				"of the fade, start to finish", dd), dd}, dd
1964	}
1965	
1966	// fxRates are the speeds worth having on a list. The two ends of the range are
1967	// what makes the list a list and not the whole answer: the useful slow rates
1968	// are a handful and sit close together, while the fast ones run from "trim the
1969	// dead air a bit" to a hundred, so anything not here is typed instead.
1970	var fxRates = []float64{0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.5, 2, 4, 8, 20, 100}
1971	
1972	func fxRateLabels() []string {
1973		out := make([]string, 0, len(fxRates)+1)
1974		for _, r := range fxRates {
1975			s := "×" + fxNum(r)
1976			switch r {
1977			case 0:
1978				s += " — stop"
1979			case 1:
1980				s += " — as filmed"
1981			}
1982			out = append(out, s)
1983		}
1984		return append(out, "Custom…")
1985	}
1986	
1987	func fxRateIndex(v float64) uint {
1988		for i, r := range fxRates {
1989			if math.Abs(r-v) < 1e-9 {
1990				return uint(i)
1991			}
1992		}
1993		return uint(len(fxRates)) // Custom…
1994	}
1995	
1996	// ratePick is the Speed × control: the rates off a list, and a typed box for
1997	// the ones that are not on it. The box is only there for Custom -- shown
1998	// beside every pick it would be a second answer to a question already
1999	// answered, and the two would have to be kept agreeing with each other.
2000	type ratePick struct {
2001		box *gtk.Box
2002		dd  *gtk.DropDown
2003		e   *gtk.Entry
2004	}
2005	
2006	func newRatePick(val float64, changed func()) *ratePick {
2007		p := &ratePick{
2008			box: gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 6),
2009			dd:  gtk.NewDropDownFromStrings(fxRateLabels()),
2010			e:   gtk.NewEntry(),
2011		}
2012		p.e.SetText(fxNum(val)) // a rate is finer than the other rows' one decimal
2013		p.e.SetInputPurpose(gtk.InputPurposeNumber)
2014		p.e.SetMaxWidthChars(fxNumChars)
2015		p.e.SetWidthChars(fxNumChars)
2016		// no HExpand on either: given the panel's slack, a dropdown holding "×8"
2017		// was the widest thing on the form, and what it offers is a list of four
2018		// characters (fxRateLabels)
2019		p.box.Append(p.dd)
2020		p.box.Append(p.e)
2021		p.dd.SetSelected(fxRateIndex(val))
2022		p.e.SetVisible(p.custom())
2023		p.dd.Connect("notify::selected", func() {
2024			if i := p.dd.Selected(); int(i) < len(fxRates) {
2025				// so that switching to Custom starts from the rate on screen
2026				// rather than from whatever was typed three picks ago
2027				p.e.SetText(fxNum(fxRates[i]))
2028			}
2029			p.e.SetVisible(p.custom())
2030			changed()
2031		})
2032		p.e.ConnectChanged(func() { changed() })
2033		return p
2034	}
2035	
2036	func (p *ratePick) custom() bool { return int(p.dd.Selected()) >= len(fxRates) }
2037	
2038	// rate is the number the control is showing, def for a Custom box with
2039	// nothing usable typed in it.
2040	func (p *ratePick) rate(def float64) float64 {
2041		if i := p.dd.Selected(); int(i) < len(fxRates) {
2042			return fxRates[i]
2043		}
2044		return fxNumOf(p.e, def)
2045	}
2046	
2047	// fxNum prints a number as short as it can without lying. The one decimal the
2048	// other fields are shown with is too coarse for a rate -- a quarter speed that
2049	// opens as 0.2 is a different effect from the one that was saved -- and %g
2050	// turns a hundred into "1e+02" on a lane label two characters wide.
2051	func fxNum(v float64) string {
2052		// FormatFloat always writes the point at this precision, so trimming
2053		// zeros can never eat the zeros of a round number like 100
2054		s := strings.TrimRight(strconv.FormatFloat(v, 'f', 2, 64), "0")
2055		return strings.TrimSuffix(s, ".")
2056	}
2057	
2058	func fxNumOf(e *gtk.Entry, def float64) float64 {
2059		if v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(e.Text()), 64); err == nil && v >= 0 {
2060			return v
2061		}
2062		return def
2063	}
2064	
2065	// askZoomParams asks a camera move's numbers: the fades, how long it lasts,
2066	// and whether the camera comes back off the region or stays. One effect,
2067	// because one gesture: draw a region, say how long.
2068	func (a *App) askZoomParams(f cutFx, isNew bool, ok func(cutFx)) {
2069		// the form applies as it is typed, and the first answer it gives places
2070		// the effect or opens the undo step (fxWin, fxLiveOk)
2071		ok = a.fxLiveOk(ok)
2072		live := &fxLive{}
2073		if f.Dur <= 0 {
2074			f.Dur = 3
2075		}
2076		gRow, g := fxNumRow("Fade in (s)",
2077			"how long the camera takes to arrive: 0 cuts straight to the region, "+
2078				"1 glides over a second", f.Trans, live)
2079		dRow, d := fxNumRow("Length (s)",
2080			"how long the camera move lasts altogether, fades included", f.Dur, live)
2081		oRow, o := fxNumRow("Fade out (s)",
2082			"how long it takes to come back off the region again: 0 cuts straight back", f.Tout, live)
2083		eRow, ec := fxEaseRow(f, live)
2084	
2085		// what happens when its seconds are up, as a question on the line rather
2086		// than as two sentences under it: the pair is one answer with two names,
2087		// and the names are two words each. Why you would want either is the
2088		// tooltip's job -- that is read once, and the labels are read every time.
2089		back := gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel("Pull back")
2090		stay := gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel("Stay on it")
2091		stay.SetGroup(back) // one group of two is a pair of radio buttons
2092		back.SetActive(!f.Stay)
2093		stay.SetActive(f.Stay)
2094		back.SetTooltipText("A passing close-up: the picture closes in, holds for its seconds " +
2095			"and opens back out on its own, leaving the rest of the video framed as it was.")
2096		stay.SetTooltipText("A reframing: from here on the finished video shows this region. " +
2097			"This is how a vertical short is made out of widescreen footage — say where the " +
2098			"action is, and say it again when it moves.")
2099		ends := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
2100		ends.Append(back)
2101		ends.Append(stay)
2102		eEnd := fxField{fxRowLabel("At the end",
2103			"whether the camera comes back out on its own when its seconds are up, or "+
2104				"holds this region until the next zoom says otherwise", ends), ends}
2105	
2106		// a camera that stays has no way back, so it has no fade out. That row
2107		// says so by going quiet, which is the answer to "why has this effect
2108		// only one of the two". The fade IN stays live whatever else is in the
2109		// cut: every staying zoom arrives from the framing that was on screen the
2110		// instant before it, and the earliest of them arrives from the plain
2111		// centred slice -- it is not special, because nothing reaches backwards
2112		// past its own T any more (camRectAt).
2113		note := gtk.NewLabel("")
2114		note.SetXAlign(0)
2115		note.SetWrap(true)
2116		note.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
2117		sync := func() {
2118			oRow.setSensitive(!stay.Active())
2119			msg := ""
2120			if stay.Active() {
2121				msg = "A camera that stays has no way back, so no fade out."
2122			}
2123			note.SetText(msg)
2124			note.SetVisible(msg != "")
2125		}
2126		sync()
2127		back.ConnectToggled(func() {
2128			sync()
2129			live.touch()
2130		})
2131	
2132		a.fxWin(fmt.Sprintf("Zoom at %s", mmss(f.T)), isNew, live,
2133			[]gtk.Widgetter{fxLine(dRow, eEnd), fxLine(gRow, oRow, eRow), note}, func() {
2134				f.Trans = fxNumOf(g, f.Trans)
2135				f.Tout = fxNumOf(o, f.Tout)
2136				f.Ease = fxEaseOf(ec.Selected())
2137				f.Dur = math.Max(0.4, fxNumOf(d, f.Dur))
2138				f.Stay = stay.Active()
2139				clampFades(&f)
2140				ok(f)
2141			})
2142	}
2143	
2144	// fxTextH is how deep the words box is: three lines of it. It was five, which
2145	// is two more than any caption anybody has typed into it and enough to push
2146	// the numbers under it off the bottom of the panel. It scrolls, so a longer
2147	// one is still typed -- three lines is what is shown at once.
2148	const fxTextH = 62
2149	
2150	// askTextParams asks a text effect's four things: the words, how long they
2151	// are on screen, and the two fades. The words get a real multi-line box --
2152	// newlines are content here (they break a line, and nothing else does), so a
2153	// single-line entry would quietly make them impossible to type.
2154	func (a *App) askTextParams(f cutFx, isNew bool, ok func(cutFx)) {
2155		// the form applies as it is typed, and the first answer it gives places
2156		// the effect or opens the undo step (fxWin, fxLiveOk)

6015		ed.pushUndo()
6016		stole := ed.addRange(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1)
6017		ed.sel.active = false
6018		ed.clearMarks()
6019		// with two cameras up, "added" is only half of what happened: the seconds
6020		// came off whatever camera had them, and a switch nobody was told about is
6021		// a switch that reads as footage going missing
6022		switch {
6023		case stole && ed.laneN > 1:
6024			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("added on %s, and taken off the other camera — "+
6025				"↶ Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes it back", ed.camName(ed.sel.lane)))
6026		case ed.laneN > 1:
6027			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("added on %s — ↶ Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes it back",
6028				ed.camName(ed.sel.lane)))
6029		default:
6030			a.setStatus("added — ↶ Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes it back")
6031		}
6032	}
6033	
6034	// copyClicked takes the selected stretch of footage in hand. Nothing happens
6035	// to the cut: the selection is measured, remembered, and the Insert button
6036	// turns into ⧉ Paste. The selection itself stays on the band -- taking a copy
6037	// is reading, not editing.
6038	func (a *App) copyClicked() {
6039		ed := a.ed
6040		if !ed.sel.active {
6041			a.setStatus("select a stretch of the pictures or of a lane first — " +
6042				"⧉ Copy takes the selection in hand")
6043			return
6044		}
6045		t0 := math.Min(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1)
6046		ln := math.Abs(ed.sel.t1 - ed.sel.t0)
6047		if ln < minSegLn {
6048			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("the selection is %.2f s — under %.0f s there is nothing worth copying", ln, minSegLn))
6049			return
6050		}
6051		ed.copyFrom, ed.copyLen, ed.copyOn = t0, ln, true
6052		// what was drawn on is what is copied: a lane's sound from a lane, footage
6053		// -- picture and what was filmed with it -- from the pictures. Silencing a
6054		// pasted stretch is the pasted clip's own question, asked of it by its form
6055		// (soundOpen), rather than a scope set before the copy was taken.
6056		ed.copyAud, ed.copyCam = ed.sel.aud, ed.sel.lane
6057		ed.syncInsertBtn()
6058		if ed.copyAud != "" {
6059			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("copied %.1f s of %s (%s – %s) — click where it goes, then ⧉ Paste",
6060				ln, ed.copyAud, mmss(t0), mmss(t0+ln)))
6061			return
6062		}
6063		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("copied %s – %s (%.1f s) — click where it goes, then ⧉ Paste",
6064			mmss(t0), mmss(t0+ln), ln))
6065	}
6066	
6067	// pasteCopy splices the copied footage into the cut at the red line, as a copy
6068	// segment (see copyScheme): the cut is opened at that point, the copied seconds
6069	// play again, and the footage carries on from the very next frame. Pasting
6070	// consumes the copy -- the button goes back to ⧉ Insert -- because a copy that
6071	// stayed in hand would leave the file chooser unreachable behind a label that
6072	// never changes back; the selection is still on the band, and ⧉ Copy takes it
6073	// again for another paste of the same seconds.
6074	func (a *App) pasteCopy() {
6075		ed := a.ed
6076		if !ed.hasPlay {
6077			a.setStatus("click the timeline where the copy goes first")
6078			return
6079		}
6080		if ed.copyAud != "" {
6081			a.pasteSound()
6082			return
6083		}
6084		was := ed.cutLen()
6085		ed.addSplice(fmt.Sprintf("%s%.3f", copyScheme, ed.copyFrom), ed.playhead, ed.copyLen,
6086			false, ed.copyCam)
6087		ed.copyOn = false
6088		ed.syncInsertBtn()
6089		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("pasted %.1f s from %s at %s — the cut is %s, was %s",
6090			ed.copyLen, mmss(ed.copyFrom), mmss(ed.playhead), mmss(ed.cutLen()), mmss(was)))
6091	}
6092	
6093	// pasteLane is the other place a copy can go: not back into the cut in
6094	// sequence, but onto a row of its own beside the cameras, so the green can
6095	// choose between the two (cut_lane.go).
6096	//
6097	// It is the same seconds of the same file either way. What differs is what the
6098	// timeline then says about them: spliced, they play after the footage they were
6099	// taken from and the video is longer by them; on a lane they play INSTEAD of
6100	// whatever else was rolling, and the video is exactly as long as it was. A
6101	// second angle on a session shot with one camera is this, and nothing else on
6102	// this page can say it.
6103	//
6104	// Nothing is cut to the new row. A lane that arrived already green would have
6105	// made the choice the lane exists to offer.
6106	func (a *App) pasteLane() {
6107		ed := a.ed
6108		if !ed.copyOn || ed.copyAud != "" {
6109			return // the button is only on the bar while footage is in hand
6110		}
6111		if !ed.hasPlay {
6112			a.setStatus("click the timeline where the new lane starts first")
6113			return
6114		}
6115		v := pickVideoOn(ed.vids, ed.copyCam, ed.copyFrom)
6116		if v == nil {
6117			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("nothing is rolling at %s any more", mmss(ed.copyFrom)))
6118			return
6119		}
6120		// the FILE second, which is what a lane is a window on: the copy was taken
6121		// at a session second, and the two differ by wherever that recording sits
6122		name := ed.addLane(v.path, v.at(ed.copyFrom), ed.playhead, ed.copyLen)
6123		if name == "" {
6124			a.setStatus("that copy is too short to be a lane of its own")
6125			return
6126		}
6127		ed.copyOn = false
6128		ed.syncInsertBtn()
6129		ed.sel.active = false
6130		ed.clearMarks()
6131		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%.1f s from %s is now the %s lane, starting at %s",
6132			ed.copyLen, mmss(ed.copyFrom), name, mmss(ed.playhead)))
6133		ed.redrawTracks()
6134	}
6135	
6136	// pasteSound lays the copied sound over the footage at the red line. Sound
6137	// alone, so the picture is left exactly as it was: those seconds keep their
6138	// frames, the video does not get longer by a single one, and the only thing
6139	// that changes is what is heard. That is the other half of ⧉ Paste -- a copy
6140	// of footage is spliced in and lengthens the video, a copy of sound is laid
6141	// over it and does not -- and which of the two this is was settled by the band
6142	// the selection was drawn on, not asked again here.
6143	func (a *App) pasteSound() {
6144		ed := a.ed
6145		au := ed.audByBase(ed.copyAud)
6146		if au == nil {
6147			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s is not in the session any more — the copied sound has "+
6148				"nowhere to come from", ed.copyAud))
6149			return
6150		}
6151		// where in the FILE those seconds are. A selection that began before the
6152		// recording did starts the sound where the LANE does -- the file's own
6153		// beginning for a recording, the window's for a cut lane: there is nothing
6154		// earlier on that lane to play, and refusing the paste over a second of
6155		// lead-in nobody selected on purpose would be the worse answer.
6156		ss := au.at(math.Max(ed.copyFrom, au.start))
6157		at := ed.playhead
6158		// the copy stays in hand when it had nowhere to go: the paste did not
6159		// fail so much as miss, and the answer to missing is to move the red line
6160		// and press again, not to go and copy the same seconds a second time
6161		n := ed.addSound(a.storePath(au.path), at, ed.copyLen, ss, ed.copyAud)
6162		if n == 0 {
6163			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("the cut keeps no footage at %s — a sound needs a picture under it", mmss(at)))
6164			return
6165		}
6166		ed.copyOn = false
6167		ed.syncInsertBtn()
6168		over := "the footage"
6169		if n > 1 {
6170			// it crossed a hole in the cut, and saying so is the difference between
6171			// a puzzling second marker in the lanes and an expected one
6172			over = fmt.Sprintf("%d stretches of footage", n)
6173		}
6174		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("laid %.1f s of %s over %s at %s", ed.copyLen, ed.copyAud, over, mmss(at)))
6175	}
6176	
6177	// audByBase is the recording with this base name, or nil when the session no
6178	// longer has it -- which a copy taken before a reload can find.
6179	func (ed *cutEditor) audByBase(base string) *tlAudio {
6180		for i := range ed.auds {
6181			if ed.auds[i].base == base {
6182				return &ed.auds[i]
6183			}
6184		}
6185		return nil
6186	}
6187	
6188	// syncSelBtns greys the verbs that have nothing to act on and says why in the
6189	// tooltip: a selection drawn on a wave is sound, and Add/Split/Remove act on
6190	// footage.
6191	func (ed *cutEditor) syncSelBtns() {
6192		if ed == nil {
6193			return
6194		}
6195		// A verb is live when it has something to act on, grey when not. snd is the
6196		// exception said in words: a selection on a WAVE is seconds of sound, and Add,
6197		// Split and Remove act on footage -- the tooltip says why the button is grey.
6198		snd := ed.sel.active && ed.sel.aud != ""
6199		on := ed.sel.active && ed.sel.aud == ""
6200		long := on && math.Abs(ed.sel.t1-ed.sel.t0) >= minSegLn
6201		if ed.copyBtn != nil {
6202			ed.copyBtn.SetSensitive(ed.sel.active && math.Abs(ed.sel.t1-ed.sel.t0) >= minSegLn)
6203		}
6204		if ed.addBtn != nil {
6205			// a scene has a floor: a selection under it adds nothing, and a button
6206			// that reports "nothing to add" is a button that should have been grey
6207			ed.addBtn.SetSensitive(long)
6208			tip := "keep the selected region (Undo takes it back)"
6209			switch {
6210			case snd:
6211				tip = "＋ Add keeps footage, and this selection is " + ed.sel.aud + "'s sound"
6212			case !ed.sel.active:
6213				tip = "drag a region on a track, then ＋ Add keeps it"
6214			case !long:
6215				tip = fmt.Sprintf("the selection is under %.0f s — too short to keep as a scene", minSegLn)
6216			}
6217			ed.addBtn.SetTooltipText(tip)
6218		}
6219		if ed.splitBtn != nil {
6220			// the one verb that works with nothing selected: it cuts at the red
6221			// line instead, so it needs a line or a selection and not both
6222			ed.splitBtn.SetSensitive(!snd && (on || ed.hasPlay))
6223			tip := "cut the selected region free: a border at each end, nothing removed, " +
6224				"so those seconds become a scene of their own. With nothing selected it " +
6225				"cuts once, at the red line (Undo takes it back)"
6226			switch {
6227			case snd:
6228				tip = "| Split cuts footage, and this selection is " + ed.sel.aud + "'s sound"
6229			case !on && !ed.hasPlay:
6230				tip = "click a track to put the red line somewhere, then | Split cuts there"
6231			}
6232			ed.splitBtn.SetTooltipText(tip)
6233		}
6234		if ed.remBtn != nil {
6235			ed.remBtn.SetSensitive(on)
6236			tip := "drop the selected region — through the middle of a scene it " +
6237				"leaves two, one either side (Undo takes it back)"
6238			switch {
6239			case snd:
6240				tip = "－ Remove drops footage, and this selection is " + ed.sel.aud + "'s sound"
6241			case !ed.sel.active:
6242				tip = "drag a region on a track, then － Remove drops it"
6243			}
6244			ed.remBtn.SetTooltipText(tip)
6245		}
6246	}
6247	
6248	// insertClicked drops a file into the cut at the playhead: a sting, a still,
6249	// a diagram, an animated tier list -- things a session does not contain. The
6250	// playhead, not the selection: an insert replaces footage rather than choosing
6251	// it. A selected region lends its length.
6252	func (a *App) insertClicked() {
6253		ed := a.ed
6254		// the same button opens a held card instead of choosing a new file. Holding
6255		// one is a statement about what you are working on, and "insert another card
6256		// at the playhead" is not what anyone means while holding one.
6257		if s := ed.heldSeg(); s != nil && s.isInsert() {
6258			a.editInsert()
6259			return
6260		}
6261		// and a held effect the same way: while one is held, the button is its Edit
6262		if ed.heldFx() != nil {
6263			a.editFx()
6264			return
6265		}
6266		if !ed.hasPlay && !ed.sel.active {
6267			a.setStatus("click the timeline where the insert goes first")
6268			return
6269		}
6270		at, want := ed.playhead, 0.0
6271		// the selection is read HERE and not in the callback, beside the seconds
6272		// and for the same reason: the chooser is a window the hand can reach
6273		// around, and the file that comes back has to be placed the way the
6274		// selection read when the button was pressed.
6275		lane := ""
6276		if ed.sel.active {
6277			at = math.Min(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1)
6278			want = math.Abs(ed.sel.t1 - ed.sel.t0)
6279			lane = ed.sel.aud
6280		}
6281	
6282		// what the chooser admits follows what the selection was drawn on. A
6283		// selection in a lane is about sound, and offering it a tier card there
6284		// would be offering to put a picture where the hand pointed at a waveform.
6285		// Footage, and no selection at all, are offered everything -- what an
6286		// insert does to the sound is the form's question now, asked of the file
6287		// that actually comes back (soundOpen).
6288		title, name, exts := "Insert a clip, image, animation or sound",
6289			"Video, image, SVG or audio", insExts
6290		if ed.sel.active && ed.selSnd() {
6291			title, name, exts = "Insert a sound over the selected seconds", "Audio", audExts
6292		}
6293		a.pickFile(title, a.insertDir(), extFilter(name, exts...), func(path string) {
6294			// Which mode a file arrives in follows the gesture that placed it, and
6295			// the button is called Insert: a card dropped at the playhead is put
6296			// BETWEEN the footage, so the video gets longer by it and nothing
6297			// filmed is lost. A card placed over a SELECTION is the other one --
6298			// marking seconds and then putting a card there is a sentence that
6299			// says what those seconds are for -- and it is the selection that gave
6300			// it its length, so the two answers stay together.
6301			m := insMode{dur: want, splice: want < minSegLn, lane: lane}
6302			if m.dur < minSegLn {
6303				m.dur = a.insertLength(path)
6304			}
6305			// what the tick opens on: a file with no sound of its own replaces no
6306			// sound, so the session carries on under it -- which is the rule the
6307			// page has always followed ("an insert replaces what it brings, and
6308			// nothing else"). A file that brought sound arrives bringing it.
6309			m.mute = !insHasSound(path)
6310			m.askMute = ed.soundOpen(path, at, m.dur, m)
6311			// a card is a picture with holes in it, and the holes are the whole
6312			// point of one: ask before placing it rather than dropping an empty
6313			// board on the timeline and leaving the filling to a path typed by hand.
6314			// A file with no holes is asked about too -- how it sits in the cut and
6315			// how long it runs are questions about a video sting as much as about a
6316			// card, and a sting placed without being asked is a sting that can only
6317			// ever overwrite.
6318			fields, _ := insFields(path)
6319			a.askInsertParams("Insert", path, fields, m, func(q svgQuery, m insMode) {
6320				a.placeInsert(path+q.suffix(), at, m)
6321			})
6322		})
6323	}
6324	
6325	// What the insert chooser admits. audExts is the sound half on its own,
6326	// because a selection drawn in a lane is offered only those. Both lists are
6327	// the extensions insKind sorts by, so what the chooser lets in is exactly what
6328	// the render knows how to ask ffmpeg for.
6329	var audExts = []string{"mp3", "wav", "ogg", "oga", "flac", "m4a", "aac", "opus"}
6330	
6331	// picExts is the picture half, offered on its own to a selection scoped to the
6332	// picture alone.
6333	var picExts = []string{"mp4", "mkv", "mov", "webm", "avi", "m4v",
6334		"png", "jpg", "jpeg", "webp", "bmp", "gif", "svg"}
6335	
6336	var insExts = append(append([]string{}, picExts...), audExts...)
6337	
6338	// insMode is how an insert sits in the cut: over the footage or between it, and
6339	// for how long. The two are asked for together because they are one decision --
6340	// a card that costs no footage has nothing to take its length from, so the
6341	// seconds have to be said rather than dragged.
6342	type insMode struct {
6343		splice bool
6344		dur    float64
6345		// whether it brings its own sound. The dialog's one tick, in whichever of
6346		// its two readings the mode is in (askInsertParams): silent when the
6347		// footage is cut open for it, the session carrying on underneath when it
6348		// is laid over. See cutSeg.Mute, which is the field it becomes.
6349		mute bool
6350		// which recording a sound is being put in place of: the lane the selection
6351		// was drawn in, read before the chooser opened. Not a dialog question --
6352		// the hand said it by pointing at that waveform. See cutSeg.Lane.
6353		lane string
6354		// a third way for it to sit in the cut, and the only one that adds a ROW
6355		// rather than a scene: the file goes on a band of its own and the cut
6356		// reaches it with the green, like a second camera nobody filmed with
6357		// (cut_lane.go). Video only -- a row is footage, and a still on one would
6358		// be a card wearing a camera's clothes.
6359		asLane bool
6360		// whether mute is a live question for this insert at all, which is what
6361		// decides if the dialog shows the tick: a picture insert that either
6362		// brings a sound of its own or lands over seconds that have one. Both
6363		// answers are then honest readings and only the hand knows which was
6364		// meant. See cutEditor.soundOpen, which is the whole of the condition.
6365		askMute bool
6366	}
6367	
6368	// placeInsert puts a chosen file in the cut. The path may carry a card's
6369	// parameters, which are kept with it: the file is made relative to the project
6370	// so it survives a move, and the parameters are not a path and are not touched.
6371	func (a *App) placeInsert(ins string, at float64, m insMode) {
6372		if m.dur < minSegLn {
6373			m.dur = a.insertLength(ins)
6374		}
6375		file, q := insSplit(ins)
6376		rel := a.storePath(file) + q.suffix()
6377		was := a.ed.cutLen()
6378		how := "over the footage — drag its edges to retime it"
6379		switch {
6380		case m.asLane:
6381			// a row, not a scene. Nothing is added to the cut here on purpose: the
6382			// point of a lane is that the green chooses between it and the cameras
6383			// beside it, and a lane that arrived already green would have taken
6384			// that choice (cut_lane.go)
6385			name := a.ed.addLane(file, 0, at, m.dur)
6386			if name == "" {
6387				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s is too short to be a lane of its own",
6388					filepath.Base(file)))
6389				return
6390			}
6391			how = fmt.Sprintf("on a lane of its own (%s) — select on that row and press ＋ Add "+
6392				"to cut to it; its ✕ takes the row away again", name)
6393		case m.splice:
6394			a.ed.addSplice(rel, at, m.dur, m.mute, a.ed.sel.lane)
6395			how = "between the footage, which is cut open for it"
6396			if m.mute {
6397				how = "between the footage, which is cut open for it, and silent — " +
6398					"the selection was scoped to the picture alone"
6399			}
6400		case insKind(file) == "audio":
6401			// a sound goes in through its own door, because it is the one insert
6402			// that must leave the picture exactly as it found it (layOverSound)
6403			n := a.ed.addSound(rel, at, m.dur, 0, m.lane)
6404			if n == 0 {
6405				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("the cut keeps no footage at %s — %s is a sound, and one needs a picture under it",
6406					mmss(at), filepath.Base(file)))
6407				return
6408			}
6409			how = "over the footage, which keeps its frames — drag its edges to retime it"
6410			if n > 1 {
6411				how = fmt.Sprintf("over %d stretches of footage, which keep their frames", n)
6412			}
6413		default:
6414			a.ed.addInsert(rel, at, m.dur, m.mute)
6415			if m.mute {
6416				how = "over the picture only, and what is heard under it runs on — " +
6417					"drag its edges to retime it"
6418			}
6419		}
6420		a.ed.sel.active = false
6421		a.ed.clearMarks()
6422		// The length of the finished video, said here because this is the one edit
6423		// whose effect on it cannot be read off the timeline: the timeline is the
6424		// session's clock and stays exactly as long as the recording, while a card
6425		// spliced into it makes the VIDEO longer by its own seconds.
6426		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s inserted at %s for %.1f s, %s — the cut is now %s (was %s) "+
6427			"— ↶ Undo takes it back", filepath.Base(file), mmss(at), m.dur, how,
6428			mmss(a.ed.cutLen()), mmss(was)))
6429	}
6430	
6431	// editInsert opens the held card: what is written on it, whether it plays over
6432	// the footage or between it, and how long it runs. It is the same dialog that
6433	// places one, because those are the same three questions -- and it opens even
6434	// for a card with nothing written on it, since a video sting still has a mode
6435	// and a length.
6436	func (a *App) editInsert() {
6437		ed := a.ed
6438		held := ed.heldSeg()
6439		if held == nil || !held.isInsert() {
6440			return
6441		}
6442		was := *held
6443		before := ed.cutLen()
6444		file, q := insSplit(was.Ins)
6445		path := a.loadPath(file) + q.suffix()
6446		if was.isCopy() {
6447			path = was.Ins // not a file: the dialog asks only its mode and seconds
6448		}
6449		fields, _ := insFields(path) // no fields is a dialog of mode and seconds
6450		em := insMode{splice: was.spliced(), dur: was.length(), mute: was.Mute, lane: was.Lane}
6451		em.askMute = ed.soundOpen(path, was.S, em.dur, em)
6452		a.askInsertParams("Save", path, fields, em,
6453			func(q svgQuery, m insMode) {
6454				// the card is found again rather than remembered: the dialog does
6455				// not hold the timeline still, and coalesce renumbers
6456				i := ed.indexOfSeg(was)
6457				if i < 0 {
6458					a.setStatus("that card is no longer in the cut")
6459					return
6460				}
6461				ed.applyInsert(i, file+q.suffix(), m)
6462				how := "over the footage"
6463				if m.splice {
6464					how = "between the footage, which is cut open for it"
6465				}
6466				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s — %.1f s, %s — the cut is now %s (was %s)",
6467					insBase(was.Ins), m.dur, how, mmss(ed.cutLen()), mmss(before)))
6468			})
6469	}
6470	
6471	// insertDir is where the insert chooser opens: an assets folder beside the
6472	// project, since a card reused across sessions lives with the project rather
6473	// than with any recording. Opening the chooser is also when the built-in cards
6474	// are put there -- there is no other moment where a card is what the user is

## What it needs

Four HTTP servers, all local by default — an empty Server box in Settings
means the loopback address below. Compose files for all of them are in
`../cpp/`; the writing model's default port is
[halogen-flash-server](https://github.com/peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server)'s own.

| what | default | serves |
|---|---|---|
| an OpenAI-compatible LLM | `http://127.0.0.1:8731` | every text and vision job |
| audio.cpp | `http://127.0.0.1:8765` | speech-to-text, alignment, diarization, separation, TTS |
| sd.cpp | `http://127.0.0.1:1234` | the thumbnail |
| ffmpeg / ffprobe | on `PATH` | every frame, cut and encode |

Settings are one bash-sourceable file, `~/.config/naivepost/llm.conf`: server
URLs, API keys, and which model id to ask each server for. Model *weights* are
never named here — that is the servers' business (`cpp/config-llamacpp.ini`,
`cpp/config-audiocpp.json`).

The vision model has to be able to read images, or Describe is the one job that
cannot run.

Which step calls which server, what waits for what, and what could overlap:
[SERVICES.md](SERVICES.md).

## Build and run

```sh
cd gui && go build && ./gui
```

Go 1.26, GTK4 via gotk4. No libadwaita.

To ship it, `./release.sh` tags the next version (v0.1, v0.2, ...) and pushes
the tag; GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) then runs the tests,
builds a Flatpak and an AppImage and attaches both to the release. The same
builds run locally with `./release.sh flatpak` (flatpak-builder needed, from
`ch.bocek.naivepost.yml`) and `./release.sh appimage` (docker or podman
needed, built in a Debian testing container); both land in `dist/`. Prefer the
Flatpak where Flatpak exists: the GNOME runtime already carries GTK4, the GTK4
video sink, GStreamer and an ffmpeg with h264, so nothing is bundled by hand
and ffmpeg is inside the sandbox. The four servers are not in either; the app
reaches them over HTTP wherever you run them. The AppImage also expects what
any desktop has: an icon theme, GL, the X11/Wayland and text libraries. Inside
Flatpak the app writes no desktop entry of its own and offers the model no web
search.

One package. The pipeline files -- transcribe, align, describe, fix, translate,
the LLM and image clients -- touch no widget, and `gui/seam.go` says exactly
what they may take from the application: an interface `*App` satisfies, plus
the handful of fields read directly. A test reads those files and fails on
anything past it, so a pipeline function that reaches for a page is a red test
rather than a race that happens to work.

## A project on disk

A project is a **folder** ending in `.naivepost`, holding everything the session
produced. It can be moved, copied or zipped whole.

```
<name>.naivepost/
  naivepost.json                    the project: sources, settings, context, prompts
  sources/                        the footage, if you asked for it to be copied in
  prepare/
    inputs/<source>/              voice16k.wav, transcript.{txt,tsv,srt},
                                  words.json, asrchunks.json,
                                  words.aligned.json, turns.json
    inputs/frames/<source>/       one JPEG per interval, named for its second
    describe/<source>/events.tsv  what was on screen, per few seconds
    transcript/
      <source>/transcript.fixed.tsv + subtitles.srt
      session.tsv / session.txt   everything on one clock — what the cut reads
      retakes.tsv                 the stretches that were said twice
      final.txt                   Lecture only: the words of the finished video
  cache/
    llm/<step>/                   model answers, keyed by the exact request
    waves/, edges/                waveform envelopes
  cut/cut.json                    the segments, in session seconds, plus effects
  narrate/narration.json          the lines, their voices and their placements
  produce/
    clips/                        per-clip encodes, the working .srt, translations
    final.<container>             the upload
  publish/
    thumbnail.png                 the picture with the words on it
    thumbnail-plain.png           the picture as drawn
    description.txt               the description
  llm/                            a readable transcript of every model call
```

`cache/llm` is keyed on the exact request, images included, so re-running a step
whose inputs have not changed costs nothing. Change a prompt and the cache for
that step misses, which is what you want.

## Design rules the code holds to

These are the decisions everything else follows from.

- **Models propose; the machine places.** A model is never asked for a
  timestamp it would have to compute. It answers in words, or line numbers, or
  clip-relative seconds — and the app turns that into a cut using the aligner's
  word times. Where a model was given the arithmetic, it got it wrong: one run
  read the marker `[01:45]` as 145 seconds instead of 105 and removed five
  seconds of good speech.
- **Every cut lands on a word edge.** The aligner is accurate to about 20 ms;
  the audio envelope is only ever allowed to choose *where between two known
  words* a splice falls, never which words it touches. An envelope cannot tell
  a breath from a word, and letting it try is what used to clip syllables.
- **Nothing is deleted, only marked.** A retake, a false start, a stretch the
  cut drops — the transcript keeps every word, and the marks are a file you can
  read and edit.
- **A step's output is its resume marker.** Every stage checks whether its own
  file exists before doing the work, so a run that was stopped, failed or ran
  out of memory resumes from where it stopped.
- **Failure is specific and local.** A pass that cannot run says so at the
  point it failed, naming the model and the reason, and the step carries on
  where it can. A language that fails to translate costs that language and
  nothing else.
- **One place per answer.** A thing you tell the editor is said once, in the
  context box, and reaches every job from there — rather than in a settings
  field that can quietly disagree with it.

## Tests

```sh
cd gui && go test ./...
```

About 24 seconds, no network, no GPU, no servers. Much of the suite pins
*reasons* rather than outputs — the wording a prompt has to contain, the order
=====
  it on a server configured to hold both.
- **sd.cpp** holds whatever model it was started with, for the one thumbnail.
- **ffmpeg** is CPU and memory-cheap, and is the one thing that can always
  overlap with a GPU job — which is what items 1 and 5 exploit, and what the
  two parallel tracks that already exist were built for.

The app unloads the audio models when a run ends (`freeAudioModels`, after the
chain's next step has started — the next step usually wants them back).

---

## What is skipped on a re-run

None of the above costs anything if the answer is already on disk. Re-running
is a resume:

| stage | skipped when |
|---|---|
| voice separation | both halves exist |
| frames | `.interval` marker matches the interval and scale |
| wav, ASR, alignment, diarization | `voice16k.wav`, `words.json`, `words.aligned.json`, `turns.json` exist |
| describe | the chunk is already in `events.tsv`; otherwise the request is looked up in `cache/llm/describe` |
| fix | per block, `cache/llm/transcript` |
| textedit / retake / translate | `cache/llm/<step>`, keyed on the whole request (retake also on the run number, so the pool stays a pool) |
| narration TTS | the wav is named after the text, emotion, voice and re-roll |
| upload text | `produce/publish/publish.json` exists |
| thumbnail | `thumbnail.stamp` matches the images, instruction and crop |
| the video | `<name>.stamp` matches the settings, cut, narration wavs and source files |

Two of those are **existence** checks and not input checks: change the ASR
model or the aligner in Settings and Prepare will not redo a recording that has
`words.json` / `words.aligned.json` already. Delete the file to re-run that
stage.

240		cr.SetFontSize(size)

244		left := func(ln string) float64 { return mid - cr.TextExtents(ln).XAdvance/2 }

246		cr.PushGroup()
247		cr.SetSourceRGB(0, 0, 0)
248		for i, ln := range lines {
249			if strings.TrimSpace(ln) == "" {
250				continue
251			}
252			x := left(ln)
253			for k := 0; k < fxEdgeSteps; k++ {
254				a := 2 * math.Pi * float64(k) / fxEdgeSteps

258		}
259		cr.PopGroupToSource()
260		cr.PaintWithAlpha(fxEdgeA * alpha)
261	
262		cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, alpha)
263		for i, ln := range lines {
264			if strings.TrimSpace(ln) == "" {

266			}

1	package main
2	
3	// What the sound does over a speed effect: five answers on every rate.
4	//
5	//	with the picture, voice held   the clock takes the sound too, pitch kept
6	//	with the picture, pitch and all the tape-speed version
7	//	at 1×, until the speed change ends
8	//	at 1×, until the scene ends
9	//	silent
10	//
11	// The two 1× answers let the picture's and the sound's read-heads come apart,
12	// and the GAP is closed where the hand chose: ×4 skips the sound never heard,
13	// ×0.5 repeats what was heard. The close is a splice, dipped rather than cut
14	// (sndDip): clips are joined with a stream copy, so nothing can cross the join
15	// -- one tail fades down, the next head fades up.
16	
17	import (
18		"fmt"
19		"math"
20	
21		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/cairo"
22	)
23	
24	// The five answers. Stored as words (cutFx.Snd) rather than a number, so a cut
25	// written by a version that knows an answer this one does not reads back as
26	// the effect it was rather than as whatever that number now means.
27	const (
28		sndWith  = ""      // the sound travels with the picture, pitch held
29		sndPitch = "pitch" // ...and with the pitch riding the rate
30		sndFx    = "own"   // 1×, back in sync when the speed change ends
31		sndScene = "scene" // 1×, back in sync when the scene ends
32		sndMute  = "mute"  // nothing is heard over these seconds
33	)
34	
35	// sndKinds is the order they are offered in and stored as; sndNames is what
36	// the dropdown says. The two lists are one list read twice -- an index into
37	// either is an index into the other.
38	var (
39		sndKinds = []string{sndWith, sndPitch, sndFx, sndScene, sndMute}
40		// short, because a dropdown is as wide as the longest thing in it and this
41		// one shares a line with two other questions. What each answer COSTS is
42		// the line under the box (sndNote), which is the part worth reading twice.
43		sndNames = []string{
44			"With the picture",
45			"With the picture, pitched",
46			"1× to the effect's end",
47			"1× to the scene's end",
48			"Silent",
49		}
50	)
51	
52	// sound is the effect's answer, normalised. An unmigrated stop's tick reads as
53	// silence (migrateFx does this once on load, and this is the same reading for
54	// anything that never went through it), and a word this version does not know
55	// reads as the default, which is what every cut did before there was a choice.
56	func (f cutFx) sound() string {
57		k := f.Snd
58		if k == "" && f.Mute {
59			k = sndMute
60		}
61		for _, w := range sndKinds {
62			if k == w {
63				return k
64			}
65		}
66		return sndWith
67	}
68	
69	// sndShifts is whether an answer lets the sound come away from the picture --
70	// the two the render has to plan for rather than filter (produce_snd.go).
71	func sndShifts(k string) bool { return k == sndFx || k == sndScene }
72	
73	// sndIndex is where an answer sits in the dropdown, and sndKindOf is the way
74	// back.
75	func sndIndex(k string) uint {
76		for i, w := range sndKinds {
77			if w == k {
78				return uint(i)
79			}
80		}
81		return 0
82	}
83	
84	func sndKindOf(i uint) string {
85		if int(i) >= len(sndKinds) {
86			return sndWith
87		}
88		return sndKinds[i]
89	}
90	
91	// sndAt is the sound answer in force at session second t, and which effect
92	// gave it. Rates average (cut_speedmix.go); sound answers do not -- the
93	// EARLIER effect's holds, since its sound is already running.
94	func sndAt(fx []cutFx, t float64) (string, cutFx, bool) {
95		for _, f := range speedsOf(fx) { // sorted by T
96			if f.Dur > 0 && t >= f.T-1e-9 && t < f.T+f.Dur-1e-9 {
97				return f.sound(), f, true
98			}
99		}
100		return sndWith, cutFx{}, false
101	}
102	
103	// sndDebt is how far apart the two read-heads are by the end of an effect that
104	// keeps its sound at 1×, in seconds of the recording. Positive is sound behind
105	// the picture (a fast stretch), negative is sound ahead (slow motion).
106	//
107	// The picture eats the effect's whole span; the sound eats only as many
108	// seconds as the effect LASTS on screen, because it is reading at 1× and the
109	// screen is all the time it has.
110	func sndDebt(f cutFx) float64 {
111		if f.Kind != "speed" || f.Dur <= 0 {
112			return 0
113		}
114		out := 0.0
115		for _, st := range speedSteps(f) {
116			out += st.outLn()
117		}
118		if out <= 0 {
119			return 0
120		}
121		return f.Dur - out
122	}
123	
124	// sndTail is the stretch of the timeline where an effect's sound is still out
125	// of step with the picture AFTER the effect's own seconds are over, and by how
126	// much. Only "until the scene ends" has one -- the other answer closes the gap
127	// on the effect's own last frame -- and it is what the lane draws past the end
128	// of the band (cut_fx.go), because this is the one effect on the page whose
129	// reach is not its own bar.
130	func (ed *cutEditor) sndTail(f cutFx) (float64, float64, float64, bool) {
131		if f.Kind != "speed" || f.sound() != sndScene {
132			return 0, 0, 0, false
133		}
134		debt := sndDebt(f)
135		if math.Abs(debt) < 0.05 {
136			return 0, 0, 0, false // ×1 with a choice on it: nothing comes apart
137		}
138		end := f.T + f.Dur
139		i := ed.segAt(end - 1e-6)
140		if i < 0 {
141			if i = ed.segAt(f.T); i < 0 {
142				return 0, 0, 0, false // the effect is over footage the cut drops
143			}
144		}
145		if ed.segs[i].E <= end+0.05 {
146			return 0, 0, 0, false // the scene ends with the effect: nothing to run on into
147		}
148		return end, ed.segs[i].E, debt, true
149	}
150	
151	// sndDip is how long the sound takes to fade down into a close and back up out
152	// of it. Short enough not to be heard as a fade, long enough not to click.
153	const sndDip = 0.15
154	
155	// sndNote is the line under the dropdown: what the answer in the box costs at
156	// the rate in the box. The arithmetic is the whole of what makes these five
157	// answers different from each other, and it is arithmetic nobody should be
158	// asked to do while deciding.
159	func sndNote(kind string, rate, dur float64) string {
160		if rate <= 0 {
161			if kind == sndMute {
162				return ""
163			}
164			// applied(): the footage under a still runs at 1× whatever the rate
165			// says, so the picture is the only thing standing still
166			return "A stop's footage runs on at 1× under the held frame, so every answer " +
167				"but Silent sounds the same here."
168		}
169		if !sndShifts(kind) || dur <= 0 {
170			return ""
171		}
172		debt := dur - dur/rate
173		switch {
174		case math.Abs(debt) < 0.05:
175			return ""
176		case debt > 0:
177			return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s on screen: the sound ends %.0f s behind the picture, "+
178				"and going back in sync skips those seconds.", dur/rate, debt)
179		default:
180			return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s on screen: the sound runs %.0f s ahead of the picture, "+
181				"and going back in sync plays those seconds again.", dur/rate, -debt)
182		}
183	}
184	
185	// drawSndTail marks how far past its own bar an effect's sound reaches: "at 1×
186	// until the scene ends" runs over the clips that follow, out of step by a fixed
187	// number of seconds, so the bar grows a thin tail to the second the sound goes
188	// back in sync, labelled with the gap. Drawn inside drawFxLane's translation.
189	func (ed *cutEditor) drawSndTail(cr *cairo.Context, f cutFx, y float64) {
190		t0, t1, debt, ok := ed.sndTail(f)
191		if !ok {
192			return
193		}
194		x0, x1 := ed.xOf(t0), ed.xOf(t1)
195		if x1-x0 < 2 {
196			return
197		}
198		mid := y + fxLaneH/2
199		cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.92, 0.42, 0.6, 0.75)
200		cr.SetLineWidth(1)
201		cr.SetDash([]float64{3, 3}, 0)
202		cr.MoveTo(x0, mid)
203		cr.LineTo(x1, mid)
204		cr.Stroke()
205		cr.SetDash(nil, 0)
206		// a stop at the far end, where the sound goes back in sync: the tail has
207		// an end and the end is the point of it
208		cr.MoveTo(x1-0.5, y+3)
209		cr.LineTo(x1-0.5, y+fxLaneH-3)
210		cr.Stroke()
211		if x1-x0 < 60 {
212			return // no room for the number; the line still says how far
213		}
214		word := fmt.Sprintf("sound %.0fs behind", debt)
215		if debt < 0 {
216			word = fmt.Sprintf("sound %.0fs ahead", -debt)
217		}
218		markPlate(cr, x0+4, y+fxLaneH-4, "snd", word)
219	}
220

```
### Prepare

Add the session's files. Each row says what its file is *for*: a camera icon
means frames come out of it and it can be cut; a microphone tags who is
speaking, voice 1 being the one the narration is spoken in. One file can be
both.

Everything is placed on **one clock**, taken from the timestamp in the filename
or the file's own creation time and length. That is what puts a separate
recorder's words, waveform and sound where they belong against the footage. The
footage is the master: a recording is heard for exactly the part of it that was
running while the footage was.

Pressing ▶ then does, in order:

1. **Optional voice separation** — a source flagged for it is split into voice
   and everything else, and the two halves replace it for everything below.
2. **Audio extraction and frames** — 16 kHz mono wav per source, and a JPEG out
   of the footage every *n* seconds (the Freq control; 1 s is typical).
3. **Speech to text** — every source transcribed, with word-level times. A file
   under two seconds — a recorder opened and closed again — is written up as
   silence without asking any server, and a video shorter than the frame
   interval keeps its one frame.
4. **Forced alignment** — a second pass that times each word to within about
   20 ms. This matters more than it sounds: the best transcriber here returns no
   word times at all, ASR timestamps elsewhere run a third of a second late, and
   every cut point in the app is placed on a word edge. The aligner is given the
   recording one piece at a time, and each piece carries the words the ASR heard
   in exactly those seconds (`asrchunks.json`) — never a guess at how many words
   a stretch of audio ought to hold. A forced aligner cannot decline the text it
   is handed, so a guess that runs high compresses real speech and leaves the
   rest of the recording with no words over it, which the cut then deletes as
   footage where nobody spoke.
5. **Diarization** — who spoke when, merged into the transcript. The window it
   asks for shrinks until the server can hold it (90 s, then 45, then 25): the
   model permits 90 s, but the buffer grows with the window and a machine with
   an LLM's weights pinned beside it may have no 2.9 GB hole to put one in.
6. **Describe** — the frames go to a vision model in small batches, each batch
   carrying the words heard in those seconds and a rolling summary of what has
   happened so far, so the answer is *what is happening* rather than *what is in
   this picture*. Output is one EVENT line per frame, stamped on that frame's
   second; a frame in which nothing changed says only `same` and is folded
   into the line before it when the log is read, so a change is dated to the
   second it happened and a brief still reads one line per thing that happened.
7. **Fix** — the raw transcripts are cleaned into publishable text, grounded in
   the event log and in what other microphones heard at the same moment. Times
   and speaker labels pass through byte-identical, enforced.
8. **Merge** — everything above becomes one session timeline: every spoken line
   and every EVENT line on one clock.
9. **Mark what was said twice** — see *Video style* below.

Every stage is skipped if its output is already on disk, so a re-run resumes
rather than starting over. ⏸ parks the run between requests; ⏹ ends it.

The right-hand pane is **every prompt the app will send**, one menu row at a
time. The first row is not a prompt: it is what you want the editor to know
about this session — who is in it, how names are spelled, what has to end up in
the video, how long it should be — and every request this project makes carries
it. Behind it, in pipeline order, are all twelve system prompts. A ✎ beside a
name means yours differs from the shipped one; Reset restores it.

### Video style

A dropdown on Prepare that chooses **which pipeline runs**, not which wording is
used:

**Lecture** — a read to camera, where the speech *is* the video. Everything you
said goes in; only the mistakes in the saying come out. You stop the recording
when you stumble and say it again, so the mistakes are at the **joins**, and
that is what the model is asked about: one join at a time, the last words of
the take that was interrupted and the first words of the take that follows, as
they are written. It answers with two numbers — how many words come off each
side so the two run on as one sentence — and *nothing* else. Nought and nought
is a whole answer: a recording stopped to change a slide is not a stumble. The
side **before** the join is cut first and as far back as the repetition goes,
because what was said last is what you meant to keep.

Each removal becomes a cut whose edges are fenced by the surviving words on
either side: the cut can never touch a word that stays, and within that fence
the audio envelope picks the quietest moment to splice at. What survives is
written to `prepare/transcript/final.txt`, punctuated and readable — delete a
word there by hand, press Cut, and it is out of the video, with no model asked.

**Gaming** — a session where the interesting moments have to be *chosen*. The
cut model reads the whole session timeline and answers with the segments worth
keeping, to a target length if the context names one.

Both styles describe the frames, because the thumbnail is picked by what is on
one.

### Cut

The session on a timeline: thumbnails per camera row, a waveform lane per sound
below, everything the cut keeps tinted green. Time nobody filmed takes no width
at all, so two recordings meet with a striped amber border each.
```

// setting on this machine (llm.conf) and is now a field on the project, for the
// reason setup.go's header gives: the stack is the same every night, the
// footage is not.
const defLanguage = "en"

// projectLanguage is the box's text as the project file stores it: what was
// typed, trimmed, and "" when nothing was -- an empty box means the default,
// and writing "en" into every project would freeze today's default into files
// that never asked for it (same rule as an unedited prompt).
func (a *App) projectLanguage() string {
	a.promptMu.Lock()
	defer a.promptMu.Unlock()
	return strings.TrimSpace(a.langTxt)
}

// asrLanguage is the same value with the default filled in: what Prepare puts in
// the request. Callable from a runner's goroutine, which is the whole reason
// the string is cached beside the widget rather than read off it -- the box is
// the GUI thread's (same rule as sessionCtx).
func (a *App) asrLanguage() string {
	if s := a.projectLanguage(); s != "" {
		return s
	}
	return defLanguage
}

func (a *App) setLanguage(s string) {
	a.promptMu.Lock()
	a.langTxt = s
	a.promptMu.Unlock()
	// the subtitle translations are offered in every language but this one,
	// and this is where it changes (syncLangs)
	a.syncSubLangs()
}

// applyLanguage loads a project's language into the box as well as the cache.
// GUI thread only, like applySessionCtx and for the same reason.
func (a *App) applyLanguage(s string) {
	a.setLanguage(s)
	if a.langEntry != nil {
		a.langEntry.SetText(s)
	}
}

func (a *App) frameInterval() float64 { return frameStops[a.interval.i] }

func (a *App) setFrameInterval(v float64) { a.interval.set(nearestStop(v)) }

// nearestStop maps seconds onto the stop table -- a project may store a value
// from a build whose table was different, and typing is free-form.
func nearestStop(v float64) int {
	best, bd := 4, math.MaxFloat64 // default 1 s
	for i, s := range frameStops {
		if d := math.Abs(s - v); d < bd {
			best, bd = i, d
		}
	}
	return best
}

// freqPick is the frame-frequency stepper: one stop visible at a time, - / +
// walking the table, and the text editable by hand. Hand-rolled rather than a
// GtkSpinButton because the spin button re-reads its own display as a plain
// number before every step -- and "each" and "1s" are not numbers, so every
// click first corrupted the value it was about to step.
type freqPick struct {
	box   *gtk.Box
	entry *gtk.Entry
	i     int
}

func newFreqPick() *freqPick {
	f := &freqPick{}
	f.entry = gtk.NewEntry()
	f.entry.SetWidthChars(4)
	f.entry.SetMaxWidthChars(4)
	f.entry.SetAlignment(0.5)
	f.entry.SetTooltipText("Seconds between frames — type 0.1 to 5, or 'each' for every frame")
	f.entry.ConnectActivate(f.parse)
	// clicking elsewhere commits like Enter does: a half-typed value silently
	// kept on screen would not be the value a run then uses
	fc := gtk.NewEventControllerFocus()
	fc.ConnectLeave(f.parse)
	f.entry.AddController(fc)

	minus := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-remove-symbolic")
	minus.ConnectClicked(func() { f.set(f.i - 1) })
	plus := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-add-symbolic")
	plus.ConnectClicked(func() { f.set(f.i + 1) })

	f.box = gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 0)
	f.box.AddCSSClass("linked") // one control, three parts
	f.box.Append(f.entry)
	f.box.Append(minus)
	f.box.Append(plus)
	f.set(defFrameStop)
	return f
}

// set clamps to the table -- past either end the buttons simply stop moving.
func (f *freqPick) set(i int) {
	if i < 0 {
		i = 0
	}
	if i >= len(frameStops) {
		i = len(frameStops) - 1
	}
	f.i = i
	f.entry.SetText(frameStopLabels[i])
}

// parse commits a typed value: seconds with or without the s, or "each"/"0"
// for every frame, landing on the nearest stop. Anything unreadable snaps the
// display back to the value still in force.
func (f *freqPick) parse() {
	t := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.entry.Text())), "s")
	if t == "each" {
		f.set(0)
		return
	}
	v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(t, 64)
	if err != nil || v < 0 {
		f.set(f.i)
		return
	}
	f.set(nearestStop(v))
}

// snapSources caches the session's sources for background runners, which must
// never touch the list widget. Split by role: the footage, then everything
// else; every source is in exactly one of the two.
func (a *App) snapSources() (vids, auds []string) {
	if a.srcList == nil {
		return a.snappedSources()
	}
	return a.snapItems(append([]sourceItem(nil), a.srcList.items...))
}

// snapItems takes one list of sources as the run's snapshot and hands back the
// two path lists the pipeline works from. It goes through a sourceList of its
// own rather than reading the fields: what counts as footage and who holds a
// narrator slot are that type's rules, and the run must not answer either
// question differently from the page.
func (a *App) snapItems(items []sourceItem) (vids, auds []string) {
	l := sourceList{items: items} // the rules, without the widget
	vids, auds = l.split()
	var narr [narratorSlots]string
	for n := 1; n <= narratorSlots; n++ {
		narr[n-1] = l.narratorPath(n)
	}
	// only the rows that answered, so the map is empty for every session that
	// has no multi-track file in it and nothing downstream has to tell "the
	// first track" from "no answer" a second time
	tracks := map[string][]int{}
	for _, it := range items {
		if len(it.tracks) > 0 {
			tracks[it.path] = append([]int(nil), it.tracks...)
		}
	}
	a.srcMu.Lock()
	a.selItems, a.selVid, a.selAud, a.selNarr, a.selTracks = items, vids, auds, narr, tracks
	a.srcMu.Unlock()
	return
}

// snappedTracks is the per-file track choice from the run's snapshot, for the
// background work that must not touch the list widget. Nil before any snapshot
// has been taken, which reads as "nobody chose anything" and is the truth.
func (a *App) snappedTracks() map[string][]int {
	a.srcMu.Lock()
	defer a.srcMu.Unlock()
	return a.selTracks
}

func (a *App) snappedSources() (vids, auds []string) {
	a.srcMu.Lock()
	defer a.srcMu.Unlock()
	return a.selVid, a.selAud
}

// snappedItems is the whole snapshot, for the one thing that rewrites it.
func (a *App) snappedItems() []sourceItem {
	a.srcMu.Lock()
	defer a.srcMu.Unlock()
	return append([]sourceItem(nil), a.selItems...)
}

// sepWanted is every source still waiting for its voice to be lifted off, from
// the snapshot -- so the runner can ask without touching a widget.
func (a *App) sepWanted() []string {
	a.srcMu.Lock()
	defer a.srcMu.Unlock()
	l := sourceList{items: a.selItems}
	return l.sepVoiceWanted()
}

146:### Narrate
147-
148-An editable line per clip: what is said over it, in which voice, with what
149-emotion. ▶ writes the lines the cut does not have and speaks the ones not
150-already in the cache. A clip grows, or the speech speeds up, when a line does
151-not quite fit — both are logged. Turn the narration off entirely and everything
152-that exists to carry one disappears from the page.
153-
154-### Produce
155-
156-Renders the video. Every clip is encoded once from its own recording, joined by
157-stream copy, loudness-normalized over the whole thing so the joins do not pump.
158-Container, codec, quality, resolution, frame rate, audio bitrate, mono, frame
159-edges — all here.
160-
161-**Subtitles** come from Prepare's aligned words, not from a second transcription
162-and not from reading the finished video back: the words that survive the cut,
163-in each clip's own seconds, spelled the way the **fixed** transcript spells
164-them — so the sentence in your context asking for the script's spelling of a
165-name or a number reaches the subtitles too, whichever speech model heard it. An `.srt` **and** a `.vtt` are written beside the video on every
166-render, one pair per language, whatever else you asked for — the video itself
167-can carry them burned into the picture, as a track inside the file, or not at
168-all. The `.vtt` is there because a browser reads no other subtitle format and
169-ignores the tracks muxed into the file; a `<video>` tag pointing at the poster
170-and every track is written out beside them, ready to paste into a page. **Translate**
171-takes the same cues into other languages — one call per language for the whole track, read back by line number
172-so a dropped line can never shift the rest onto the wrong seconds.
173-
174-The **thumbnail** is either drawn by an image model from real frames of your
175-video, or — where your context asks for a picture the video already contains
176-("use the frame that shows the title slide") — the frame itself, cropped, with
177-the title printed on it locally. The title, the description and the thumbnail
178-instruction come from one model call that reads your context.
179-
180----
181-
182-## What it needs
183-
184-Four HTTP servers, all local by default — an empty Server box in Settings
185-means the loopback address below. Compose files for all of them are in
186-`../cpp/`; the writing model's default port is
187-[halogen-flash-server](https://github.com/peonist-ai/halogen-flash-server)'s own.
188-
189-| what | default | serves |
190-|---|---|---|
191-| an OpenAI-compatible LLM | `http://127.0.0.1:8731` | every text and vision job |
192-| audio.cpp | `http://127.0.0.1:8765` | speech-to-text, alignment, diarization, separation, TTS |
193-| sd.cpp | `http://127.0.0.1:1234` | the thumbnail |
194-| ffmpeg / ffprobe | on `PATH` | every frame, cut and encode |
195-
196-Settings are one bash-sourceable file, `~/.config/naivepost/llm.conf`: server
197-URLs, API keys, and which model id to ask each server for. Model *weights* are
198-never named here — that is the servers' business (`cpp/config-llamacpp.ini`,
199-`cpp/config-audiocpp.json`).
200-
201-The vision model has to be able to read images, or Describe is the one job that
202-cannot run.
203-
204-Which step calls which server, what waits for what, and what could overlap:
205-[SERVICES.md](SERVICES.md).
206-
207-## Build and run
208-
209-```sh
210-cd gui && go build && ./gui
211-```
212-
213-Go 1.26, GTK4 via gotk4. No libadwaita.
214-
215-To ship it, `./release.sh` tags the next version (v0.1, v0.2, ...) and pushes
216-the tag; GitHub Actions (`.github/workflows/release.yml`) then runs the tests,
217-builds a Flatpak and an AppImage and attaches both to the release. The same
218-builds run locally with `./release.sh flatpak` (flatpak-builder needed, from
219-`ch.bocek.naivepost.yml`) and `./release.sh appimage` (docker or podman
220-needed, built in a Debian testing container); both land in `dist/`. Prefer the
221-Flatpak where Flatpak exists: the GNOME runtime already carries GTK4, the GTK4
222-video sink, GStreamer and an ffmpeg with h264, so nothing is bundled by hand
223-and ffmpeg is inside the sandbox. The four servers are not in either; the app
224-reaches them over HTTP wherever you run them. The AppImage also expects what
225-any desktop has: an icon theme, GL, the X11/Wayland and text libraries. Inside
226-Flatpak the app writes no desktop entry of its own and offers the model no web

30		if ed.fxScreen.page == nil {
31			ed.fxScreen.page = ed
32		}
33		return &ed.fxScreen
34	}

48	}
