50	// fxSrcSize falls back to the first recording, then to plain HD, so the
51	// overlay never divides by zero.
52	func (ed *cutEditor) fxSrcSize() (float64, float64) {
53		v := ed.playVideo
54		if v == nil && len(ed.vids) > 0 {
55			v = &ed.vids[0]
56		}
57		if v != nil && v.w > 0 && v.h > 0 {
58			return float64(v.w), float64(v.h)
59		}
60		return 1920, 1080
61	}
62	
63	// fxCamOK takes the camera layer down while a zoom is aimed by hand (you must
64	// see everything the camera could see) or a text's bar is held (its box is
65	// only editable on the layer with a grab). An armed TEXT keeps the layer up:
66	// its box lives on the OUTPUT frame.
67	func (ed *cutEditor) fxCamOK() bool {
68		return ed.hasPlay && (ed.fxArm == "" || ed.fxOverArm()) &&
69			ed.fxRectHeld() == nil && ed.fxHeldBox() == nil
70	}
71	
72	// fxRectHeld is the held effect if it is one with a camera rectangle.
73	func (ed *cutEditor) fxRectHeld() *cutFx {
74		if f := ed.heldFx(); f != nil && f.Kind == "zoom" {
75			return f
76		}
77		return nil
78	}
79	
80	// camInForce is the zoom whose OWN rectangle the picture is framed by at
81	// session time t. nil when the framing at t belongs to no single effect.
82	func (ed *cutEditor) camInForce(t float64) *cutFx {
83		if i := ed.camIndexInForce(t); i >= 0 {
84			return &ed.fx[i]
85		}
86		return nil
87	}
88	
89	// camIndexInForce is camInForce as a position in ed.fx (holdFx takes an index;
90	// a pointer into a slice undo replaces is not one). A zoom whose band covers t
91	// wins, latest first; otherwise the staying zoom in force; -1 when neither --
92	// the camera parked on the whole frame, which no effect can be edited by.
93	func (ed *cutEditor) camIndexInForce(t float64) int {
94		band, stay := -1, -1
95		for i := range ed.fx {
96			f := &ed.fx[i]
97			if f.Kind != "zoom" {
98				continue
99			}
100			if f.T <= t+1e-9 && t < f.T+math.Max(f.Dur, 0) && (band < 0 || f.T >= ed.fx[band].T) {
101				band = i
102			}
103			if f.Stay && f.T <= t+1e-9 && (stay < 0 || f.T >= ed.fx[stay].T) {
104				stay = i
105			}
106		}
107		if band >= 0 {
108			return band
109		}
110		return stay
111	}
112	
113	// camMoving is whether the camera is MID-MOVE at t -- inside some zoom's fade
114	// in or fade out, on its way between two framings.
115	//
116	// Every fade in counts, the cut's first included: it travels from the plain
117	// centred slice the video opens on, which is a journey like any other now that
118	// no zoom reaches back before its own T (camRectAt).
119	func camMoving(fx []cutFx, t float64) bool {
120		for _, z := range zoomsOf(fx) {
121			tin, tout := z.zoomGlides()
122			if tin > 0 && t >= z.T && t < z.T+tin {
123				return true
124			}
125			if !z.Stay && tout > 0 && t >= z.T+math.Max(z.Dur, 0)-tout && t < z.T+math.Max(z.Dur, 0) {
126				return true
127			}
128		}
129		return false
130	}
131	
132	// fxCamSettled is whether the camera is STANDING STILL at t -- parked on one
133	// zoom's rectangle, no fade half done -- which is the condition for offering
134	// the rectangle to the hand. Mid-move it belongs to no single effect.
135	func fxCamSettled(fx []cutFx, t float64) bool {
136		return len(zoomsOf(fx)) > 0 && !camMoving(fx, t)
137	}
138	
139	// fxDragTarget is the effect a drag on the picture edits when nothing is held:
140	// the zoom the picture is framed by right now. Deliberately narrow: nothing
141	// while playing (the camera layer uses a different mapping, syncPreviewZoom),
142	// nothing while the camera moves, nothing before the first zoom.
143	func (ed *cutEditor) fxDragTarget() *cutFx {
144		if f := ed.fxRectHeld(); f != nil {
145			return f
146		}
147		if !ed.hasPlay || ed.livePreview() || !fxCamSettled(ed.fx, ed.playhead) {
148			return nil
149		}
150		return ed.camInForce(ed.playhead)
151	}
152	
153	// fxHeldBox is the held effect if it is one of the two laid over the picture
154	// -- a text or a drawing (overFx) -- which are the other kind of rectangle the
155	// picture offers, and the only one not bound to the cut's aspect.
156	func (ed *cutEditor) fxHeldBox() *cutFx {
157		if f := ed.heldFx(); f != nil && overFx(*f) {
158			return f
159		}
160		return nil
161	}
162	
163	// fxOverArm is whether the next drag on the picture draws an overlay's box
164	// rather than a camera window. The two kinds are armed apart -- a text needs
165	// words typed, a drawing needs a file chosen -- and treated alike from the
166	// drag on, because a box is a box.
167	func (ed *cutEditor) fxOverArm() bool {
168		return ed.fxArm == "text" || ed.fxArm == "svg"
169	}

171	// fxEdges says what a point at (x, y) has hold of on the rectangle r: which
172	// borders it is within reach of, and whether it is inside at all. Both edges
173	// at once is a corner, which is why these come back as two independent axes.
174	func fxEdges(x, y, rx, ry, rw, rh float64) (horiz, vert, left, top, inside bool) {
175		inX := x >= rx-fxGrab && x <= rx+rw+fxGrab
176		inY := y >= ry-fxGrab && y <= ry+rh+fxGrab
177		nearL, nearR := math.Abs(x-rx) <= fxGrab, math.Abs(x-(rx+rw)) <= fxGrab
178		nearT, nearB := math.Abs(y-ry) <= fxGrab, math.Abs(y-(ry+rh)) <= fxGrab
179		horiz, vert = (nearL || nearR) && inY, (nearT || nearB) && inX
180		inside = x >= rx && x <= rx+rw && y >= ry && y <= ry+rh
181		return horiz, vert, nearL, nearT, inside
182	}
183	
184	// fxCursorName is the pointer over a rectangle: the resize arrows on the
185	// borders and the corners, the move hand inside. Naming what a border does
186	// before it is pressed is the whole of how anyone finds out it resizes.
187	func fxCursorName(horiz, vert, left, top, inside bool) string {
188		switch {
189		case horiz && vert:
190			if left == top {
191				return "nwse-resize"
192			}
193			return "nesw-resize"
194		case horiz:
195			return "ew-resize"
196		case vert:
197			return "ns-resize"
198		case inside:
199			return "move"
200		}
201		return "default"
202	}
203	
204	// resizeRect is a border drag in widget pixels: the hand at (x, y), the fixed
205	// far edge/corner at (ax, ay), pxA the cut's aspect in those pixels;
206	// horiz/vert say which borders were grabbed, left/top which side. ONE number
207	// is dragged -- the height -- and the width follows the aspect; a corner takes
208	// the axis the hand moved further. Returns the new centre and height.
209	func resizeRect(x, y, ax, ay, pxA float64, horiz, vert, left, top bool) (cx, cy, h float64) {
210		switch {
211		case horiz && vert:
212			h = math.Max(math.Abs(x-ax)/pxA, math.Abs(y-ay))
213		case horiz:
214			h = math.Abs(x-ax) / pxA
215		default:
216			h = math.Abs(y - ay)
217		}
218		h = math.Max(h, 12) // a rectangle smaller than this is a slip, not an edit
219		w := h * pxA
220		cx, cy = ax, ay
221		if horiz {
222			cx = ax + w/2
223			if left {
224				cx = ax - w/2
225			}
226		}
227		if vert {
228			cy = ay + h/2
229			if top {
230				cy = ay - h/2
231			}
232		}
233		return cx, cy, h
234	}
235	
236	// resizeFree is a border drag on a rectangle that owes nothing to the cut's
237	// aspect -- a text box, which is whatever shape the words want. The two axes
238	// are independent: a side moves one edge, a corner moves two, and an edge that
239	// was not grabbed does not move at all. x0,y0,w0,h0 is the rectangle as it was;
240	// ax,ay the edges being kept still. min is the smallest it may become, so a
241	// box cannot be collapsed into something the hand can no longer find.
242	func resizeFree(x, y, ax, ay, x0, y0, w0, h0, min float64,
243		horiz, vert, left, top bool) (nx, ny, nw, nh float64) {
244		nx, ny, nw, nh = x0, y0, w0, h0
245		if horiz {
246			if left {
247				nx = math.Min(x, ax-min)
248				nw = ax - nx
249			} else {
250				nw = math.Max(x-ax, min)
251				nx = ax
252			}
253		}
254		if vert {
255			if top {
256				ny = math.Min(y, ay-min)
257				nh = ay - ny
258			} else {
259				nh = math.Max(y-ay, min)
260				ny = ay
261			}
262		}
263		return nx, ny, nw, nh
264	}
265	
266	// fxGrab is how near the rectangle's edge a press counts as taking hold of
267	// that edge rather than of the whole rectangle. A 1.5 px line is not a mouse
268	// target; this is, on either side of it.
269	const fxGrab = 9.0
270	
271	// syncFxCursor decides whether the overlay owns the pointer. Only while a
272	// drag would mean something: armed, or holding a view/zoom to re-frame. The
273	// rest of the time it must not take the click that toggles playback.
274	func (ed *cutEditor) syncFxCursor() {
275		ed.syncFxArm() // the same state, said in the column where it can be read
276		if ed.fxArea == nil {
277			return
278		}
279		armed := ed.fxArm != ""
280		held := ed.fxRectHeld() != nil || ed.fxHeldBox() != nil
281		// the overlay also takes the pointer when there is simply something on the
282		// picture to grab -- a view framing it, a text showing on it -- so that a
283		// box can be moved and resized where it is seen. That swallows the click
284		// that toggles playback, so every press that turns out not to be a drag is
285		// handed back to it (see the drag's end).
286		ed.fxArea.SetCanTarget(armed || held || ed.fxDragTarget() != nil ||
287			len(textsAt(ed.fx, ed.playhead)) > 0)
288		if armed {
289			// nothing is under the pointer yet; the motion controller takes over
290			// as soon as it moves. Its cache is set here too, or the first move
291			// after arming would decide the crosshair is already up and leave the
292			// resize arrow the last hover put there.
293			ed.fxCursor = "crosshair"
294			ed.fxArea.SetCursor(gdk.NewCursorFromName("crosshair", nil))
295		} else if ed.fxCursor == "crosshair" {
296			ed.fxCursor = "default"
297			ed.fxArea.SetCursor(gdk.NewCursorFromName("default", nil))
298		}
299	}

301	// fxDisp is where the video's picture actually is inside the overlay widget:
302	// GtkPicture keeps the frame's aspect (contain), so there are bars either
303	// side or above, and the maths here has to match or the rectangle is drawn on
304	// the bars.
305	func fxDisp(w, h, srcA float64) (ox, oy, dw, dh float64) {
306		if w <= 0 || h <= 0 || srcA <= 0 {
307			return 0, 0, w, h
308		}
309		dw = w
310		dh = w / srcA
311		if dh > h {
312			dh = h
313			dw = h * srcA
314		}
315		return (w - dw) / 2, (h - dh) / 2, dw, dh
316	}
317	
318	// snapRectPos pulls a sliding camera rectangle onto the frame's edges when it
319	// comes close: cx,cy is the centre, wf,hf the rectangle's size, all fractions
320	// of the source frame; tx,ty how close counts, in the same units. The axes
321	// snap independently, so corners come for free.
322	func snapRectPos(cx, cy, wf, hf, tx, ty float64) (float64, float64) {
323		switch {
324		case math.Abs(cx-wf/2) < tx:
325			cx = wf / 2 // left edge on the frame's left
326		case math.Abs(cx-(1-wf/2)) < tx:
327			cx = 1 - wf/2 // right edge on the frame's right
328		}
329		switch {
330		case math.Abs(cy-hf/2) < ty:
331			cy = hf / 2 // top on top
332		case math.Abs(cy-(1-hf/2)) < ty:
333			cy = 1 - hf/2 // bottom on bottom
334		}
335		return cx, cy
336	}
337	
338	// fxSnapPx is how near a line has to come, in widget pixels, before a
339	// rectangle on the picture is put exactly on it. The same reach the timeline's
340	// own snapping uses, measured on the screen rather than in seconds.
341	const fxSnapPx = 10.0
342	
343	// snapPointPx pulls a dragged edge onto one of the frame's own lines when the
344	// hand brings it within tol pixels -- the nearest one wins, and a hand nowhere
345	// near any of them is left exactly where it is. This is the resize half of the
346	// snapping: what moves under the hand IS the edge, so putting the pointer on
347	// the line puts the edge on it.
348	func snapPointPx(v, tol float64, lines ...float64) float64 {
349		best, d := v, tol
350		for _, l := range lines {
351			if e := math.Abs(v - l); e < d {
352				best, d = l, e
353			}
354		}
355		return best
356	}
357	
358	// snapEdgePx is the move half: a whole rectangle is sliding, so any of its
359	// three lines on this axis -- near edge, middle, far edge -- may be the one
360	// that lands. v is the near edge and ln the length; whichever of the three
361	// comes closest to one of the frame's lines is put on it and the rectangle
362	// carried with it. Nothing within reach leaves v alone.
363	func snapEdgePx(v, ln, tol float64, lines ...float64) float64 {
364		best, d := v, tol
365		for _, mine := range []float64{v, v + ln/2, v + ln} {
366			for _, l := range lines {
367				if e := math.Abs(mine - l); e < d {
368					best, d = v+(l-mine), e
369				}
370			}
371		}
372		return best
373	}
374	
375	// fxZoomDrag reports that the drag in flight belongs to a zoom -- armed, or
376	// re-framing a held one. A zoom's rectangle is not bound by the cut's aspect.
377	func (ed *cutEditor) fxZoomDrag() bool {
378		if ed.fxArm != "" {
379			return ed.fxArm == "zoom"
380		}
381		f := ed.fxRectHeld()
382		return f != nil && f.Kind == "zoom"
383	}
384	
385	// fxFreeDrag reports that the rectangle being drawn is a free shape rather
386	// than one locked to the cut's aspect: a zoom's window (which the render fits
387	// the output box into) and a text's box (which is a shape on the finished
388	// frame, not a frame of its own).
389	func (ed *cutEditor) fxFreeDrag() bool {
390		return ed.fxOverArm() || ed.fxZoomDrag()
391	}
392	
393	// fxClampRect keeps a camera rectangle somewhere a person can find it again.
394	// The limits are deliberately loose -- a pull-back well past the frame's edge
395	// is a real shot, and so is a tight crop -- they only rule out the rectangles
396	// that are no longer a picture: a hair-thin sliver, something a thousand
397	// frames wide, a centre dragged into the void off the side of the recording.
398	func fxClampRect(f *cutFx) {
399		if f == nil {
400			return
401		}
402		f.Hf = math.Min(math.Max(f.Hf, 0.02), 12)
403		f.Cx = math.Min(math.Max(f.Cx, -2), 3)
404		f.Cy = math.Min(math.Max(f.Cy, -2), 3)
405	}
406	
407	// liveZoom is the transform that puts the camera on the playing preview: the
408	// scale s and offset tx,ty that map the picture, drawn 1:1 at sw×sh, so the
409	// camera rect r fills the output-shaped box centred in a W×H widget.
410	func liveZoom(W, H, sw, sh, outA float64, r fxRect) (s, tx, ty float64) {
411		bx, by, bw, bh := fxDisp(W, H, outA)
412		s = bh / (r.hf * sh)
413		tx = bx + bw/2 - r.cx*sw*s
414		ty = by + bh/2 - r.cy*sh*s
415		return
416	}
417	
418	// stillFit is that mapping, source pixels to widget pixels, as one scale and
419	// one offset. Live, it is the camera's own -- the SAME numbers the footage
420	// under the still is on, which is the point: the two layers move together or
421	// the frozen frame is a picture the camera cannot reach. Not live, it is the
422	// plain contain fit GtkPicture would do, which is what the raw frame beneath
423	// is on.
424	func stillFit(W, H, sw, sh, outA float64, live bool, r fxRect) (s, tx, ty float64) {
425		if live {
426			return liveZoom(W, H, sw, sh, outA, r)
427		}
428		s = math.Min(W/sw, H/sh)
429		return s, (W - sw*s) / 2, (H - sh*s) / 2
430	}
431	
432	// zoomTransform builds translate(tx,ty)·scale(s) as ONE matrix from a nil
433	// transform. Chaining gsk_transform_* calls consumes each transform while the
434	// Go value keeps a finalizer that unrefs it again -- a double free on every
435	// tick. The result goes to SetChildTransform (transfer-none), so its one
436	// finalizer balances.
437	func zoomTransform(s, tx, ty float64) *gsk.Transform {
438		var identity *gsk.Transform
439		return identity.Matrix2D(float32(s), 0, 0, float32(s), float32(tx), float32(ty))
440	}
441	
442	// buildFxOverlay wraps the preview picture with the framing overlay and wires
443	// its gestures. Everything the drag knows lives in the closure; what it emits
444	// goes through the same addFx/updateFx as every other edit.
445	func (ed *cutEditor) buildFxOverlay() *gtk.Overlay {
446		// the three layers themselves are the shared ones (cut_fxscreen.go), so
447		// this page and Narrate's are the same picture; what is added here is
448		// everything only an editor has, starting with the gestures
449		over := ed.screen().buildLayers(ed, ed.player.Picture, ed.player.video)
450		// the wheel over the picture steps frames -- the preview is where you look
451		// while hunting for one, so it answers the scrub gesture itself
452		over.AddController(ed.wheelFrames())
453		area := ed.fxArea
454	
455		// The camera's own clock: the 100ms timer is right for a red line and wrong
456		// for a glide, and the render (zoompan per frame) has no steps. The frame
457		// clock costs nothing while the layer is down; the timeline keeps its 100ms.
458		area.AddTickCallback(func(_ gtk.Widgetter, _ gdk.FrameClocker) bool {
459			if ed.livePreview() && ed.player != nil && ed.player.playing {
460				ed.syncPreviewZoom()
461				area.QueueDraw() // the mask and the titles move with the camera
462			}
463			return true
464		})
465	
466		// ---- geometry ---------------------------------------------------------
467		//
468		// Three nested rectangles: dispPx is where the video's picture is in the
469		// widget (GtkPicture letterboxes), camPx the camera's window on it -- what
470		// the finished video shows -- and a text box is a fraction of THAT (fxtext.go).
471	
472		dispPx := func() (ox, oy, dw, dh float64) {
473			aw, ah := float64(area.AllocatedWidth()), float64(area.AllocatedHeight())
474			sw, sh := ed.srcSize()
475			return fxDisp(aw, ah, sw/sh)
476		}
477	
478		// pxAspect is the cut's aspect measured in widget pixels: dh widget px are
479		// sh source px, so a rectangle's width is its height times this.
480		pxAspect := func() float64 {
481			sw, sh := ed.srcSize()
482			_, _, dw, dh := dispPx()
483			if dw <= 0 || dh <= 0 || sw <= 0 || sh <= 0 {
484				return ed.outAspect()
485			}
486			return ed.outAspect() * (dw / sw) * (sh / dh)
487		}
488	
489		// rectPx puts a normalized camera rectangle on the widget.
490		rectPx := func(r fxRect) (rx, ry, rw, rh float64) {
491			ox, oy, dw, dh := dispPx()
492			rh = r.hf * dh
493			rw = rh * pxAspect()
494			return ox + r.cx*dw - rw/2, oy + r.cy*dh - rh/2, rw, rh
495		}
496	
497		// camPx is the camera rectangle the overlay is showing: the held view or
498		// zoom's own, or -- with nothing held -- where the camera is at the
499		// playhead. Not ok when nothing frames the picture at all.
500		camPx := func() (rx, ry, rw, rh float64, ok bool) {
501			if f := ed.fxRectHeld(); f != nil {
502				rx, ry, rw, rh = rectPx(fxRect{f.Cx, f.Cy, f.Hf})
503				return rx, ry, rw, rh, true
504			}
505			if !ed.hasPlay || !fxHasCamera(ed.aspect, ed.fx) {
506				return
507			}
508			sw, sh := ed.srcSize()
509			rx, ry, rw, rh = rectPx(fxRectAt(ed.fx, ed.playhead, sw/sh, ed.outAspect()))
510			return rx, ry, rw, rh, true
511		}
512	
513		// outFramePx is the finished frame on screen -- the rectangle a text box
514		// is a fraction of. That is the camera's window when there is a camera,
515		// the whole picture when there is not, and while the preview is playing
516		// the output box the live layer is drawn into.
517		outFramePx := func() (x, y, w, h float64) {
518			if ed.livePreview() {
519				aw, ah := float64(area.AllocatedWidth()), float64(area.AllocatedHeight())
520				return fxDisp(aw, ah, ed.outAspect())
521			}
522			if rx, ry, rw, rh, ok := camPx(); ok {
523				return rx, ry, rw, rh
524			}
525			return dispPx()
526		}
527	
528		textPx := func(f cutFx) (x, y, w, h float64) {
529			ox, oy, ow, oh := outFramePx()
530			return fxOverPx(f, ox, oy, ow, oh)
531		}
532	
533		// setTextPx is the way back: a rectangle on the widget written onto the
534		// effect as fractions of the finished frame, clamped so a box can never be
535		// dragged off the video and lost.
536		setTextPx := func(f *cutFx, x, y, w, h float64) {
537			ox, oy, ow, oh := outFramePx()
538			if ow <= 0 || oh <= 0 {
539				return
540			}
541			b := fxBox{cx: (x + w/2 - ox) / ow, cy: (y + h/2 - oy) / oh, wf: w / ow, hf: h / oh}.clamp()
542			f.Cx, f.Cy, f.Wf, f.Hf = b.cx, b.cy, b.wf, b.hf
543		}
544	
545		// ---- what a press takes hold of ----------------------------------------
546	
547		// fxGrabbed is one rectangle offered to the hand: the effect behind it,
548		// where it is on the widget, and which of its borders the pointer has.
549		type fxGrabbed struct {
550			f                              *cutFx
551			text                           bool
552			x, y, w, h                     float64
553			horiz, vert, left, top, inside bool
554		}
555		// grabAt is the whole hit test, and its ORDER is the rule the picture
556		// follows: whatever is held answers first (you are working on it), then
557		// the texts on screen from the top down (they sit inside the camera
558		// rectangle, so they have to be asked before it), and last the view that
559		// frames the picture. Nothing while an effect is armed -- that drag is
560		// drawing a new box -- and nothing while the preview plays.
561		grabAt := func(x, y float64) *fxGrabbed {
562			try := func(f *cutFx, text bool, rx, ry, rw, rh float64) *fxGrabbed {
563				g := &fxGrabbed{f: f, text: text, x: rx, y: ry, w: rw, h: rh}
564				g.horiz, g.vert, g.left, g.top, g.inside = fxEdges(x, y, rx, ry, rw, rh)
565				if !g.horiz && !g.vert && !g.inside {
566					return nil
567				}
568				return g
569			}
570			if ed.fxArm != "" || ed.livePreview() {
571				return nil
572			}
573			if f := ed.fxHeldBox(); f != nil {
574				tx, ty, tw, th := textPx(*f)
575				return try(f, true, tx, ty, tw, th)
576			}
577			if f := ed.fxRectHeld(); f != nil {
578				if rx, ry, rw, rh, ok := camPx(); ok {
579					return try(f, false, rx, ry, rw, rh)
580				}
581				return nil
582			}
583			vis := textsAt(ed.fx, ed.playhead)
584			for i := len(vis) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
585				f := &ed.fx[vis[i]]
586				tx, ty, tw, th := textPx(*f)
587				if g := try(f, true, tx, ty, tw, th); g != nil {
588					return g
589				}
590			}
591			if f := ed.fxDragTarget(); f != nil {
592				if rx, ry, rw, rh, ok := camPx(); ok {
593					return try(f, false, rx, ry, rw, rh)
594				}
595			}
596			return nil
597		}
598	
599		// The drag in flight, in widget px. Its kind is settled at the press and
600		// never changes under the hand:
601		//
602		//	""     grabbed nothing -- the press is the preview's own click
603		//	draw   a fresh rectangle, dragged corner to corner
604		//	move   slides what was grabbed
605		//	size   scales it about the border opposite the one taken hold of
606		var drag struct {
607			on             bool
608			kind           string
609			x0, y0, x1, y1 float64
610			moved          bool
611			g              fxGrabbed
612			cx0, cy0       float64 // a camera rectangle's centre when the press landed
613			ax, ay         float64 // the point a resize keeps still
614		}
615	
616		// dragRect is the rectangle the current drag means, in widget px:
617		// anchored at the press, following the pointer, locked to the cut's aspect
618		// and snapped to the frame's full width or height when it comes within
619		// reach -- unless it is a free one (a zoom's window, a text's box), which
620		// is simply the two corners.
621		dragRect := func() (x, y, w, h float64) {
622			_, _, dw, dh := dispPx()
623			pxA := pxAspect()
624			dx, dy := drag.x1-drag.x0, drag.y1-drag.y0
625			if ed.fxFreeDrag() {
626				return math.Min(drag.x0, drag.x1), math.Min(drag.y0, drag.y1),
627					math.Abs(dx), math.Abs(dy)
628			}
629			h = math.Max(math.Abs(dy), math.Abs(dx)/pxA)
630			// snap: close to the whole frame in either direction is the whole frame
631			if math.Abs(h*pxA-dw) < dw*0.05 {
632				h = dw / pxA
633			} else if math.Abs(h-dh) < dh*0.05 {
634				h = dh
635			}
636			w = h * pxA
637			x, y = drag.x0, drag.y0
638			if dx < 0 {
639				x -= w
640			}
641			if dy < 0 {
642				y -= h
643			}
644			return x, y, w, h
645		}
646	
647		// drawOver is either kind of overlay put on the picture the way the render
648		// will put it, and the way the OTHER preview puts it: Narrate draws the
649		// same titles over the same finished frame (cut_fxpaint.go), so the words,
650		// the font fitting and the fades are shared and only the box is local.
651		drawOver := func(cr *cairo.Context, f cutFx, alpha float64) {
652			ox, oy, ow, oh := outFramePx()
653			ed.drawFxOver(cr, f, alpha, ox, oy, ow, oh)
654		}
655	
656		// boxOutline is the dashed violet frame around a text box, drawn only for
657		// the one being worked on: a title with a rectangle permanently round it
658		// would not look like the title the render makes.
659		boxOutline := func(cr *cairo.Context, x, y, w, h float64) {
660			cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.6, 0.55, 0.95, 0.9)
661			cr.SetLineWidth(1.5)
662			cr.SetDash([]float64{4, 3}, 0)
663			cr.Rectangle(x, y, w, h)
664			cr.Stroke()
665			cr.SetDash(nil, 0)
666		}
667	
668		area.SetDrawFunc(func(_ *gtk.DrawingArea, cr *cairo.Context, w, h int) {
669			if ed.player == nil || ed.player.still {
670				return // a card is on screen; the camera talks about footage
671			}
672			if ed.livePreview() {
673				// the camera is live on the picture underneath (syncPreviewZoom),
674				// so the mask and the titles are the shared painting the Narrate
675				// preview also does (fxScreen.paintLive) and nothing else -- the
676				// outline waits for the pause
677				if !ed.paintLive(cr, w, h) {
678					return
679				}
680				// an overlay's box being drawn by hand: the one arm that keeps
681				// this layer up (syncPreviewZoom), because the box is a fraction
682				// of the OUTPUT frame and this is the output frame on screen
683				if drag.on && drag.kind == "draw" && ed.fxOverArm() {
684					x, y, ww, hh := dragRect()
685					boxOutline(cr, x, y, ww, hh)
686				}
687				return
688			}
689			// 1. the camera rectangle, or the one being drawn in its place
690			var rx, ry, rw, rh float64
691			haveCam := false
692			label := ed.aspect
693			drawingCam := drag.on && drag.kind == "draw" && !ed.fxOverArm()
694			switch {
695			case drawingCam:
696				rx, ry, rw, rh = dragRect()
697				haveCam = true
698			default:
699				if x, y, ww, hh, ok := camPx(); ok {
700					rx, ry, rw, rh, haveCam = x, y, ww, hh, true
701					if f := ed.fxRectHeld(); f != nil {
702						label = f.fxLabel()
703					}
704				}
705			}
706			if haveCam {
707				// dim what the finished video does not show
708				cr.SetSourceRGBA(0, 0, 0, 0.45)
709				cr.Rectangle(0, 0, float64(w), float64(h))
710				cr.NewSubPath()
711				cr.Rectangle(rx, ry, rw, rh)
712				cr.SetFillRule(cairo.FillRuleEvenOdd)
713				cr.Fill()
714				cr.SetFillRule(cairo.FillRuleWinding)
715				col := [3]float64{1, 1, 1}
716				if drawingCam || ed.fxRectHeld() != nil {
717					// the lane's own two camera colours, so the box on the
718					// picture and the bar under it are plainly the same effect:
719					// the close-up that comes back out, and the reframing that
720					// stays on the region
721					col = [3]float64{0.25, 0.72, 0.82}
722					if f := ed.fxRectHeld(); f != nil && f.Stay {
723						col = [3]float64{0.95, 0.62, 0.15}
724					}
725				}
726				cr.SetSourceRGB(col[0], col[1], col[2])
727				cr.SetLineWidth(1.5)
728				cr.Rectangle(rx, ry, rw, rh)
729				cr.Stroke()
730				if label != "" {
731					cr.SetFontSize(10)
732					plateText(cr, rx+4, ry+13, label)
733				}
734			}
735			// 2. the words on the finished frame, faded as the render will fade
736			// them -- and the held one always, wherever the playhead is, because
737			// something being edited has to be visible to be edited
738			held := ed.fxHeldBox()
739			for _, i := range textsAt(ed.fx, ed.playhead) {
740				if f := &ed.fx[i]; f != held {
741					drawOver(cr, *f, textAlpha(*f, ed.playhead))
742				}
743			}
744			if held != nil {
745				drawOver(cr, *held, 1)
746				tx, ty, tw, th := textPx(*held)
747				boxOutline(cr, tx, ty, tw, th)
748			}
749			// 3. a text box being drawn by hand, or one under the pointer that a
750			// press would take hold of
751			switch {
752			case drag.on && drag.kind == "draw" && ed.fxOverArm():
753				x, y, ww, hh := dragRect()
754				boxOutline(cr, x, y, ww, hh)
755			case drag.on && drag.g.text && drag.g.f != nil && drag.g.f != held:
756				tx, ty, tw, th := textPx(*drag.g.f)
757				boxOutline(cr, tx, ty, tw, th)
758			}
759		})
760	
761		g := gtk.NewGestureDrag()
762		g.ConnectDragBegin(func(x, y float64) {
763			drag.kind, drag.moved, drag.g = "", false, fxGrabbed{}
764			drag.on = true
765			drag.x0, drag.y0, drag.x1, drag.y1 = x, y, x, y
766			defer area.QueueDraw()
767			if ed.fxArm != "" {
768				drag.kind = "draw" // an armed button always means a fresh box
769				return
770			}
771			gr := grabAt(x, y)
772			if gr == nil {
773				// clear of everything: with a camera rectangle held a drag draws a new one
774				// for it; otherwise the press is the picture's, which answers a click with
775				// play/pause (ConnectDragEnd). Nothing is offered while the framed layer is
776				// up: framing starts by taking the effect off the lane.
777				if ed.fxRectHeld() != nil {
778					drag.kind = "draw"
779				}
780				return
781			}
782			drag.g = *gr
783			drag.cx0, drag.cy0 = gr.f.Cx, gr.f.Cy
784			if gr.horiz || gr.vert {
785				// an edge grabbed square-on keeps the middle of the opposite one,
786				// so the rectangle grows along that axis alone; a corner keeps the
787				// far corner, which is what every resize handle everywhere does
788				drag.kind = "size"
789				drag.ax, drag.ay = gr.x+gr.w/2, gr.y+gr.h/2
790				if gr.horiz {
791					drag.ax = gr.x
792					if gr.left {
793						drag.ax = gr.x + gr.w
794					}
795				}
796				if gr.vert {
797					drag.ay = gr.y
798					if gr.top {
799						drag.ay = gr.y + gr.h
800					}
801				}
802				return
803			}
804			drag.kind = "move"
805		})
806		g.ConnectDragUpdate(func(dx, dy float64) {
807			if !drag.on {
808				return
809			}
810			drag.x1, drag.y1 = drag.x0+dx, drag.y0+dy
811			editing := drag.kind == "move" || drag.kind == "size"
812			if !drag.moved && math.Hypot(dx, dy) > 2 {
813				drag.moved = true
814				if editing {
815					ed.pushUndo() // once, before anything shifts: one Undo per drag
816				}
817			}
818			if editing && drag.moved {
819				f := drag.g.f
820				ox, oy, dw, dh := dispPx()

3	// Text on the picture: the layout and the SVG the render draws it from.
4	//
5	// A text box is a fraction of the OUTPUT frame (Cx, Cy, Wf, Hf), composited
6	// after the camera chain, so it stays put while the camera glides; views and
7	// zooms are fractions of the SOURCE and have no Wf (a camera window is always
8	// the cut's aspect). fitText is the ONLY text measurement either side makes --
9	// cairo could measure, librsvg will not -- an estimate over an average advance
10	// (fitFont in svgcards.go) that errs small.
11	
12	import (
13		"fmt"
14		"math"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	const (
19		// textAdvance is the average width of a character as a fraction of the
20		// font size. Sans-serif faces sit a little over half an em; this is the
21		// number svgcards.go has always fitted chip labels with.
22		textAdvance = 0.58
23		// textLine is the distance between baselines, font sizes.
24		textLine = 1.25
25		// textAscent is how far the first baseline sits below the top of the
26		// block, font sizes.
27		textAscent = 0.95
28		// textMinPt is as small as fitting is allowed to go. Past this the words
29		// are not readable at video sizes, so the box overflows instead -- which
30		// is visible, and a visible mistake can be fixed.
31		textMinPt = 7.0
32		// textMaxLines is the most lines a box is broken into. A box asked to hold
33		// a paragraph would otherwise shrink until it was a grey smudge; this
34		// stops at a size that still reads and lets the rest run out of the box.
35		textMaxLines = 12
36	)
37	
38	// fxTextDefault is the box a text effect gets when it is placed without one
39	// being drawn: the lower third, most of the width, which is where a caption
40	// goes unless somebody says otherwise.
41	var fxTextDefault = fxBox{cx: 0.5, cy: 0.78, wf: 0.8, hf: 0.16}
42	
43	// fxBox is a rectangle on the output frame, all four numbers fractions of it.
44	// The text effect's own box; view and zoom use fxRect, which is a fraction of
45	// the SOURCE and carries no width.
46	type fxBox struct{ cx, cy, wf, hf float64 }
47	
48	// textBox is f's box, with anything unset filled in. A text effect written by
49	// an older build -- or by hand -- has no box at all, and no box means the
50	// default one rather than a zero-sized rectangle nobody can see or grab. A
51	// drawing gets its own default, in the middle rather than the lower third
52	// (fxsvg.go): the two are put on the picture for different reasons.
53	func (f cutFx) textBox() fxBox {
54		b := fxBox{f.Cx, f.Cy, f.Wf, f.Hf}
55		if b.wf <= 0 || b.hf <= 0 {
56			if f.Kind == "svg" {
57				return fxSvgDefault
58			}
59			return fxTextDefault
60		}
61		return b.clamp()
62	}
63	
64	// clamp keeps a text box on the frame: big enough to hold a word and to be
65	// grabbed, and never dragged so far that it cannot be found again. Both edges
66	// are allowed to sit exactly on the frame's, and no further.
67	func (b fxBox) clamp() fxBox {
68		b.wf = math.Min(math.Max(b.wf, 0.04), 1)
69		b.hf = math.Min(math.Max(b.hf, 0.03), 1)
70		b.cx = math.Min(math.Max(b.cx, b.wf/2), 1-b.wf/2)
71		b.cy = math.Min(math.Max(b.cy, b.hf/2), 1-b.hf/2)
72		return b
73	}
74	
75	// px is the box in the pixels of a w×h frame: corner, width and height.
76	func (b fxBox) px(w, h float64) (x, y, bw, bh float64) {
77		bw, bh = b.wf*w, b.hf*h
78		return b.cx*w - bw/2, b.cy*h - bh/2, bw, bh
79	}
80	
81	// textLines is the words as the layout will break them: explicit newlines
82	// always break, and anything longer than the width is wrapped between words.
83	// A single word too long for the box is split rather than left to run out of
84	// it -- one over-long word is a URL or a hashtag, not a mistake to preserve.
85	func textLines(text string, width, size float64) []string {
86		adv := math.Max(size*textAdvance, 1e-6)
87		max := int(width / adv) // characters that fit on a line
88		if max < 1 {
89			max = 1
90		}
91		var out []string
92		for _, para := range strings.Split(strings.ReplaceAll(text, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
93			words := strings.Fields(para)
94			if len(words) == 0 {
95				out = append(out, "") // a blank line was typed on purpose
96				continue
97			}
98			line := ""
99			for _, w := range words {
100				for len([]rune(w)) > max { // an over-long word, split at the edge
101					if line != "" {
102						out = append(out, line)
103						line = ""
104					}
105					r := []rune(w)
106					out = append(out, string(r[:max]))
107					w = string(r[max:])
108				}
109				switch {
110				case line == "":
111					line = w
112				case len([]rune(line))+1+len([]rune(w)) <= max:
113					line += " " + w
114				default:
115					out = append(out, line)
116					line = w
117				}
118			}
119			if line != "" {
120				out = append(out, line)
121			}
122		}
123		return out
124	}
125	
126	// fitText is the whole of the layout: the largest font size at which the words
127	// fit the box, and the lines at that size, in the box's own units. Binary
128	// search, because preview and render must agree to the last decimal.
129	func fitText(text string, boxW, boxH float64) (size float64, lines []string) {
130		if strings.TrimSpace(text) == "" || boxW <= 0 || boxH <= 0 {
131			return 0, nil
132		}
133		fits := func(s float64) ([]string, bool) {
134			ls := textLines(text, boxW, s)
135			if len(ls) > textMaxLines {
136				return ls, false
137			}
138			return ls, float64(len(ls))*s*textLine <= boxH
139		}
140		// one line as tall as the box is the ceiling; nothing bigger can fit
141		hi := boxH / textLine
142		if ls, ok := fits(hi); ok {
143			return hi, ls
144		}
145		lo := textMinPt
146		if hi <= lo {
147			ls, _ := fits(lo)
148			return lo, ls
149		}
150		for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
151			mid := (lo + hi) / 2
152			if _, ok := fits(mid); ok {
153				lo = mid
154			} else {
155				hi = mid
156			}
157		}
158		lines, _ = fits(lo)
159		return lo, lines
160	}
161	
162	// textBaselines is where each line's baseline sits, given the box in pixels
163	// and the size fitText chose. The block is centred in the box vertically; each
164	// line is centred horizontally, so the x is the box's middle for all of them.
165	func textBaselines(y, boxH, size float64, n int) []float64 {
166		if n <= 0 {
167			return nil
168		}
169		block := float64(n) * size * textLine
170		top := y + math.Max(0, (boxH-block)/2)
171		out := make([]float64, n)
172		for i := range out {
173			out[i] = top + float64(i)*size*textLine + size*textAscent
174		}
175		return out
176	}

178	// ---- the SVG the render draws ------------------------------------------------
179	
180	// textSVG is one text effect as a transparent document the size of the output
181	// frame (a plain 0,0 composite, see textChain): white words with a dark
182	// outline, the outline a stroke-only copy of every line drawn underneath.
183	func textSVG(f cutFx, outW, outH int) []byte {
184		w, h := float64(outW), float64(outH)
185		x, y, bw, bh := f.textBox().px(w, h)
186		size, lines := fitText(f.Text, bw, bh)
187		var b strings.Builder
188		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>`+"\n"+
189			`<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="%d" height="%d" `+
190			`viewBox="0 0 %d %d">`+"\n", outW, outH, outW, outH)
191		if size > 0 {
192			mid := x + bw/2
193			base := textBaselines(y, bh, size, len(lines))
194			fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<g font-family="sans-serif" font-weight="bold" font-size="%s" `+
195				`text-anchor="middle">`+"\n", trimNum(size))
196			// the outline first, the fill over it: one pass each, so a descender
197			// of one line is never drawn over the outline of the next
198			for _, pass := range [2]string{
199				// twice the radius: a stroke straddles the outline, so half of it
200				// is inside the glyph and half is the edge the preview dilates by
201				// (fxEdgeR). One number for both, or the thumbnail and the video
202				// wear different edges and only a screenshot says so.
203				fmt.Sprintf(`fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="%s" stroke-linejoin="round" opacity="%s"`,
204					trimNum(size*fxEdgeR*2), trimNum(fxEdgeA)),
205				`fill="#ffffff"`,
206			} {
207				for i, ln := range lines {
208					if strings.TrimSpace(ln) == "" {
209						continue
210					}
211					// attrEscaper, not svgEscape: svgEscape is the percent
212					// escaping an insert's "?" parameters need, and the words
213					// here are XML content -- an unescaped & or < is a document
214					// librsvg refuses, which would lose the whole overlay
215					fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<text x="%s" y="%s" %s>%s</text>`+"\n",
216						trimNum(mid), trimNum(base[i]), pass, attrEscaper.Replace(ln))
217				}
218			}
219			b.WriteString("</g>\n")
220		}
221		b.WriteString("</svg>\n")
222		return []byte(b.String())
223	}

225	// ---- when a text is on screen ------------------------------------------------
226	
227	// textCue is one text effect inside one clip, in that clip's own output
228	// seconds: when it comes up, when it goes, and how long each fade takes.
229	type textCue struct {
230		fx        cutFx
231		s, e      float64
232		fin, fout float64
233		// idx is the effect's place in the cut's list, so the file written for it
234		// can be named after something stable across a re-render.
235		idx int
236	}
237	
238	// overFx is whether an effect is laid OVER the running picture: text or a
239	// drawing (svg, fxsvg.go). Cues, filter graph and preview treat both as one
240	// thing; only what is drawn differs. An empty one (no words, no file) is not
241	// an effect -- it would be an input ffmpeg cannot open.
242	func overFx(f cutFx) bool {
243		switch f.Kind {
244		case "text":
245			return strings.TrimSpace(f.Text) != ""
246		case "svg":
247			return strings.TrimSpace(f.Src) != ""
248		}
249		return false
250	}
251	
252	// textsOf is the overlay effects of a cut, earliest first, skipping the ones
253	// that would show nothing: nothing to draw, or no time to draw it in.
254	func textsOf(fx []cutFx) []cutFx {
255		var out []cutFx
256		for _, f := range fx {
257			if overFx(f) && f.Dur > 0 {
258				out = append(out, f)
259			}
260		}
261		return out
262	}
263	
264	// textsAt is the places in fx of the text effects visible at session time t,
265	// in the order they were placed -- so the last one is the one drawn on top and
266	// the first one a press should find. Indices rather than copies because the
267	// preview both draws these and lets them be dragged, and a drag needs the
268	// effect itself. The render walks textCues instead: it needs the clip's own
269	// clock rather than the session's.
270	func textsAt(fx []cutFx, t float64) []int {
271		var out []int
272		for i, f := range fx {
273			if !overFx(f) || f.Dur <= 0 {
274				continue
275			}
276			if t >= f.T && t < f.T+f.Dur {
277				out = append(out, i)
278			}
279		}
280		return out
281	}
282	
283	// textAlpha is how opaque a text is at session time t: the fades, evaluated
284	// the same way the render's fade filters will. The preview draws with it so a
285	// half-faded title looks half-faded.
286	func textAlpha(f cutFx, t float64) float64 {
287		if t < f.T || t >= f.T+f.Dur {
288			return 0
289		}
290		fin, fout := f.textFades()
291		a := 1.0
292		if fin > 0 && t < f.T+fin {
293			a = (t - f.T) / fin
294		}
295		if fout > 0 && t > f.T+f.Dur-fout {
296			a = math.Min(a, (f.T+f.Dur-t)/fout)
297		}
298		return math.Min(1, math.Max(0, a))
299	}
300	
301	// textFades is the fades a text actually gets: each at least 0, together no
302	// longer than the text is on screen, the way in winning any overlap. Exactly
303	// the bargain zoomGlides strikes for a zoom's two glides.
304	func (f cutFx) textFades() (fin, fout float64) {
305		fin = math.Min(math.Max(f.Trans, 0), f.Dur)
306		fout = math.Min(math.Max(f.Tout, 0), f.Dur-fin)
307		return
308	}
309	
310	// textCues maps the cut's text effects onto one clip. sessS is the session
311	// time the clip starts at, span the session seconds it covers (0 for a freeze
312	// or a spliced card, which are one session moment held for a while), rate its
313	// playback rate and length its output seconds -- the same five numbers
314	// buildCam is given, and mapped the same way, so a text and a camera move
315	// together under a speed effect instead of drifting apart.
316	func textCues(fx []cutFx, sessS, span, rate, length float64) []textCue {
317		if length <= 0 {
318			return nil
319		}
320		var out []textCue
321		for i, f := range fx {
322			if !overFx(f) || f.Dur <= 0 {
323				continue
324			}
325			fin, fout := f.textFades()
326			var s, e float64
327			if span <= 0 {
328				// one session moment stretched over the whole clip: either the
329				// text covers that moment or it has nothing to appear over
330				if sessS < f.T || sessS >= f.T+f.Dur {
331					continue
332				}
333				s, e = 0, length
334				fin, fout = 0, 0 // there is no time inside a held frame to fade over
335			} else {
336				var ok bool
337				s, e, fin, fout, ok = cueClip(f.T, f.Dur, fin, fout, sessS, rate, length)
338				if !ok {
339					continue
340				}
341			}
342			// the two fades cannot together outlast the appearance
343			if fin+fout > e-s {
344				fin = math.Min(fin, e-s)
345				fout = math.Max(0, e-s-fin)
346			}
347			out = append(out, textCue{fx: f, s: s, e: e, fin: fin, fout: fout, idx: i})
348		}
349		return out
350	}
351	
352	// cueClip maps a session stretch [T, T+dur] with its fades onto one clip that
353	// starts at sessS, plays at rate and runs length output seconds: the piece
354	// inside the clip, in the clip's own seconds. An overlay that starts before
355	// the clip is already fully up when the clip begins, so the fade it keeps is
356	// the part still owing -- and the same at the far end. ok is false when
357	// nothing of it worth a frame lands in the clip.
358	func cueClip(T, dur, fin, fout, sessS, rate, length float64) (s, e, cin, cout float64, ok bool) {
359		if rate <= 0 {
360			rate = 1
361		}
362		s = (T - sessS) / rate
363		e = (T + dur - sessS) / rate
364		if e <= 0 || s >= length {
365			return 0, 0, 0, 0, false
366		}
367		if s < 0 {
368			cin = math.Max(0, fin/rate+s)
369			s = 0
370		} else {
371			cin = fin / rate
372		}
373		if e > length {
374			cout = math.Max(0, fout/rate-(e-length))
375			e = length
376		} else {
377			cout = fout / rate
378		}
379		if e-s < 0.04 { // shorter than a frame: nothing to see
380			return 0, 0, 0, 0, false
381		}
382		return s, e, cin, cout, true
383	}
384	
385	// freezeCues maps the cut's stop effects onto one clip on textCues' terms --
386	// same five numbers -- so a still and a title at the same second come and go
387	// together. A held clip (span 0) gets none. A stop stands over frozenSpans'
388	// seconds, not its whole bar: a crossing speed effect dilutes its ×0
389	// (cut_speedmix.go), and an edge made by a crossing is hard.
390	func freezeCues(fx []cutFx, sessS, span, rate, length float64) []textCue {
391		if length <= 0 || span <= 0 {
392			return nil
393		}
394		var out []textCue
395		for i, f := range fx {
396			fin, fout := f.textFades()
397			for _, fs := range frozenSpans(fx, f) {
398				in, off := 0.0, 0.0
399				if math.Abs(fs[0]-f.T) < 1e-9 {
400					in = fin
401				}
402				if math.Abs(fs[1]-(f.T+f.Dur)) < 1e-9 {
403					off = fout
404				}
405				s, e, cin, cout, ok := cueClip(fs[0], fs[1]-fs[0], in, off, sessS, rate, length)
406				if !ok {
407					continue
408				}
409				if cin+cout > e-s {
410					cin = math.Min(cin, e-s)
411					cout = math.Max(0, e-s-cin)
412				}
413				out = append(out, textCue{fx: f, s: s, e: e, fin: cin, fout: cout, idx: i})
414			}
415		}
416		return out
417	}
418	
419	// textChain is the filter graph that puts the cues on the picture: each its
420	// own input, faded on its own alpha, enabled for exactly its seconds. in is
421	// the incoming label, base the input index of the first overlay file,
422	// boxW/boxH the frame size; the outgoing label comes back. A title's file is
423	// already frame-sized (textSVG) and goes on at the origin; a drawing is fitted
424	// into its box here using ffmpeg's own w/h. Commas inside enable= are escaped
425	// as pieceExpr does for zoompan.
426	func textChain(cues []textCue, in string, base, boxW, boxH int) (string, string) {
427		var b strings.Builder
428		cur := in
429		for k, c := range cues {
430			b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("[%d:v]format=rgba", base+k))
431			pos := "x=0:y=0"
432			if c.fx.Kind == "svg" {
433				if x, y, bw, bh, ok := svgFitPx(c.fx, boxW, boxH); ok {
434					b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(",scale=%d:%d:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease", bw, bh))
435					pos = fmt.Sprintf("x=%d+(%d-w)/2:y=%d+(%d-h)/2", x, bw, y, bh)
436				} else {
437					pos = "x=(W-w)/2:y=(H-h)/2" // no frame size to fit against
438				}
439			}
440			if c.fin > 0 {
441				b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(",fade=t=in:st=%.3f:d=%.3f:alpha=1", c.s, c.fin))
442			}
443			if c.fout > 0 {
444				b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf(",fade=t=out:st=%.3f:d=%.3f:alpha=1", c.e-c.fout, c.fout))
445			}
446			b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("[tx%d];", k))
447			out := fmt.Sprintf("vtx%d", k)
448			b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("[%s][tx%d]overlay=%s:eof_action=pass:"+
449				"enable=between(t\\,%.3f\\,%.3f)[%s];", cur, k, pos, c.s, c.e, out))
450			cur = out
451		}
452		return b.String(), cur
453	}

275	// posTag says whether a tag word names a caption placement, and which one it
276	// stores as. The spelled-out default comes back as the empty string it is
277	// saved as -- "[bottom]" is an answer, not an emotion.
278	func posTag(s string) (string, bool) {
279		switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(s)) {
280		case "top":
281			return "top", true
282		case "center", "centre", "middle":
283			return "center", true
284		case "bottom":
285			return "", true
286		}
287		return "", false
288	}
