290	func lineParts(s string) (emotion string, at float64, hasAt bool, text string) {
291		s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
292		if strings.HasPrefix(s, "[") {
293			if i := strings.Index(s, "]"); i > 0 {
294				tag := strings.TrimSpace(s[1:i])
295				if m := lineAtRe.FindStringSubmatch(tag); m != nil {
296					at, _ = strconv.ParseFloat(m[1], 64)
297					hasAt = true
298					tag = strings.TrimSpace(tag[:len(tag)-len(m[0])])
299				}
300				return tag, at, hasAt, strings.TrimSpace(s[i+1:])
301			}
302		}
303		return "", 0, false, s
304	}
305	
306	// lineText is the inverse: what the box shows for an entry. The placement is
307	// NOT rendered back -- the row's time field owns it now, and two editable
308	// spellings of one number is how they drift apart. @N typed into the box still
309	// works (lineParts), it just moves the line and then lives in the time field.
310	func lineText(e narrEntry) string {
311		if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) == "" {
312			return "" // a silent clip is an empty box; an emotion alone says nothing
313		}
314		tag := e.Emotion
315		if tag == "" {
316			tag = e.Pos // a caption has no delivery; its placement is the tag
317		}
318		if tag == "" {
319			return e.Text
320		}
321		return "[" + tag + "] " + e.Text
322	}
323	
324	func (a *App) narrPath() string { return filepath.Join(a.narrateDir(), "narration.json") }
325	
326	// keepPrevNarration copies the narration aside before a run overwrites it and
327	// hands back where -- one generation deep, for "I did not mean that". Nothing
328	// here fails the run.
329	func keepPrevNarration(path string) (string, error) {
330		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
331		if err != nil {
332			return "", err // no narration yet: nothing to keep, and not a problem
333		}
334		prev := strings.TrimSuffix(path, ".json") + ".prev.json"
335		if err := os.WriteFile(prev, b, 0o644); err != nil {
336			return "", err
337		}
338		return prev, nil
339	}
340	
341	// ---- persistence ------------------------------------------------------------
342	
343	// has is whether i names a line.
344	func (n *narrator) has(i int) bool { return i >= 0 && i < len(n.entries) }
345	
346	func (n *narrator) load() {
347		n.entries, n.silent = nil, nil
348		if b, err := os.ReadFile(n.a.narrPath()); err == nil {
349			var f struct {
350				Entries []narrEntry
351				Silent  []cutSeg
352			}
353			if json.Unmarshal(b, &f) == nil {
354				n.entries, n.silent = f.Entries, f.Silent
355			}
356		}
357		// in placement order, whatever the file says. Every reader downstream walks
358		// the list in order -- staleFor decides from it whether ▶ must rewrite the
359		// narration, entryAt gives a line the window up to the next one -- and the
360		// file can be written mid-edit, between a line moving clips and the rows
361		// being rebuilt around it.
362		n.sortEntries()
363	}
364	
365	// saveSoon is save once the typing stops. Everything that edits a line as it is
366	// typed goes through here; everything that is a decision -- a row added, a take
367	// picked, a line silenced -- still calls save outright, because a decision you
368	// watched happen must be on disk before you can doubt it.
369	func (n *narrator) saveSoon() { n.saveQ.call(n.save) }
370	
371	// flushSave settles what typing owes before something else looks at the file.
372	// Nil-safe, so the page that is not built yet costs its callers no guard.
373	func (n *narrator) flushSave() {
374		if n != nil {
375			n.saveQ.flush()
376		}
377	}
378	
379	func (n *narrator) save() {
380		n.silent = pruneSilent(n.silent, n.entries)
381		b, _ := json.MarshalIndent(struct {
382			Entries []narrEntry `json:"entries"`
383			Silent  []cutSeg    `json:"silent,omitempty"`
384		}{n.entries, n.silent}, "", "  ")
385		os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(n.a.narrPath()), 0o755)
386		if err := os.WriteFile(n.a.narrPath(), append(b, '\n'), 0o644); err != nil {
387			n.a.logf("save narration: %v", err)
388		}
389		n.updateOut()
390	}
391	
392	// pullRows copies the editable widgets back into the model.
393	func (n *narrator) pullRows() {
394		if n.building {
395			return
396		}
397		for i, r := range n.rows {
398			if i >= len(n.entries) {
399				break
400			}
401			buf := r.text.Buffer()
402			emo, at, hasAt, text := lineParts(buf.Text(buf.StartIter(), buf.EndIter(), false))
403			n.entries[i].Text = text
404			if text == "" {
405				continue // an emptied box silences the line; its old emotion stays
406			}
407			if p, ok := posTag(emo); ok {
408				// the tag word is a placement, not a delivery: "[top]" moves the
409				// caption and leaves nothing for the TTS to act
410				n.entries[i].Pos = p
411				n.entries[i].Emotion = ""
412			} else {
413				n.entries[i].Emotion = emo
414			}
415			if hasAt {
416				e := &n.entries[i]
417				e.At = math.Min(math.Max(0, at), math.Max(0, e.E-e.S-1))
418			}
419		}
420	}
421	
422	// ---- page ------------------------------------------------------------------
423	
424	func (a *App) buildNarrate() gtk.Widgetter {
425		n := &narrator{a: a, playSeg: -1, jumped: -1, speaking: -1, solo: -1, liveRow: -1,
426			synthFail: map[string]bool{}, durCache: map[string]float64{},
427			durProbe: map[string]bool{}}
428		a.narr = n
429		if p, err := NewPlayer(); err == nil {
430			n.player = p
431			// the picture is what "playing" means here; the narration track follows
432			// it, so only this one draws the run bar's button -- and the transport's
433			p.OnState = func() {
434				a.updateRunControls()
435				if n.playBtn != nil {
436					setPlayIcon(n.playBtn, p.playing,
437						"play the cut with its narration", "pause")
438				}
439			}
440			p.OnError = a.playerErr("the narrate preview")
441			p.OnLog = func(s string) { a.logf("%s", s) }
442		}
443		if p, err := NewPlayer(); err == nil {
444			n.voice = p
445			// not the run bar's business -- this one speaks single lines -- but the
446			// line's own button has to go back to ▶ when the line ends
447			p.OnState = a.syncPlayIcons
448			p.OnError = a.playerErr("the narration line")
449		}
450	
451		n.list = gtk.NewListBox()
452		n.list.SetSelectionMode(gtk.SelectionSingle)
453		n.list.ConnectRowSelected(func(row *gtk.ListBoxRow) {
454			if row == nil || n.building {
455				return
456			}
457			i := row.Index()
458			if i >= 0 && i < len(n.entries) {
459				// to the LINE, not its clip, with the row's own leadIn of run-in. This is
460				// the ONLY place the preview jumps of its own accord: the tick that follows
461				// playback selects rows too, and selectRow holds n.building across it.
462				n.seekTo(n.leadIn(i))
463			}
464		})
465		left := gtk.NewScrolledWindow()
466		n.listScroll = left
467		left.SetChild(n.list)
468		left.SetVExpand(true)
469		// The rows wrap; they do not scroll sideways. Left on the default the
470		// column scrolled horizontally instead, which is not a narrower column at
471		// all: the rows keep the width their longest line wants, the text boxes
472		// stay exactly as wide as they were, and a scrollbar appears under them --
473		// so making the window smaller hid the words rather than re-wrapping them.
474		// Every other scrolling column in the app says this (cut_form.go,
475		// publish.go); this one had been the exception.
476		left.SetPolicy(gtk.PolicyNever, gtk.PolicyAutomatic)
477		// a floor, not the width: the divider opens this column at 790, which is
478		// wide enough that a narration line wraps into about three. As a minimum
479		// 780 was the widest thing in the app, and every other page inherited it --
480		// the cost of asking for a comfortable size instead of setting one.
481		left.SetSizeRequest(360, -1)
482	
483		// right side: video + controls + the prompt, top to bottom of the page
484		vframe := videoFrame(nil)
485		vframe.SetTooltipText("click the picture to play the cut with its narration, " +
486			"and again to pause — ⏹ below hands ▶ back to writing and speaking the narration")
487		if n.player != nil {
488			n.player.Picture.SetVExpand(true)
489			// the picture goes in wrapped: what this page is for is judging a line
490			// against the moment it lands on, and the moment is the FINISHED frame
491			// -- cropped, zoomed, frozen where a stop freezes it, with its titles
492			// on (narrate_fxview.go)
493			vframe.SetChild(n.buildNarrFx())
494			click := gtk.NewGestureClick()
495			// held goes with it: a pause the user asked for is theirs to undo, and a
496			// synthesis finishing must not start the video back up behind them
497			click.ConnectReleased(func(cnt int, x, y float64) { n.toggle() })
498			n.player.Picture.AddController(click)
499			glib.TimeoutAdd(100, n.followPlayback)
500		}
501		// Top and bottom only: the column's own margins (on right, below) give the
502		// video the same left and right edge as the button and the prompt under it.
503		// It had none on the left at all, so the picture ran into the divider and
504		// the frame around it stopped being a frame on that side.
505		vframe.SetMarginTop(10)
506		vframe.SetMarginBottom(6)
507	
508		// The transport: play/pause, a seek slider over the cut, the playhead's
509		// clock, a line at the playhead, and voicing what changed. ±3 s in session
510		// time on the cut: a jump into a removed stretch carries on to the
511		// neighbouring clip, as the slider and wheel do.
512		back := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("media-seek-backward-symbolic")
513		back.SetTooltipText("back 3 seconds")
514		back.ConnectClicked(func() { n.seekTo(snapToCut(n.clips(), n.pos, n.pos-3, cutEdge)) })
515		n.playBtn = gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
516		n.playBtn.SetTooltipText("play the cut with its narration")
517		n.playBtn.ConnectClicked(func() { n.toggle() })
518		fwd := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("media-seek-forward-symbolic")
519		fwd.SetTooltipText("forward 3 seconds")
520		fwd.ConnectClicked(func() { n.seekTo(snapToCut(n.clips(), n.pos, n.pos+3, cutEdge)) })
521		n.slider = gtk.NewScale(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, nil)
522		n.slider.SetHExpand(true)
523		n.slider.SetDrawValue(false)
524		n.slider.SetTooltipText("the cut, end to end — what the edit removed is not on this bar, so every " +
525			"point on it is video you keep. Drag to seek; paused, the wheel steps a frame at a time")
526		// The wheel over the slider steps frames, and only while the picture is
527		// stopped: scrolling a playing preview fights the tick, which is writing the
528		// slider's value ten times a second, and the seeks land behind where the
529		// video has already got to. Capture phase and a true return take the wheel
530		// off GtkRange, whose own handling would jump the value by a page.
531		wheel := gtk.NewEventControllerScroll(gtk.EventControllerScrollVertical |
532			gtk.EventControllerScrollDiscrete)
533		wheel.SetPropagationPhase(gtk.PhaseCapture)
534		wheel.ConnectScroll(func(dx, dy float64) bool {
535			if n.player == nil || n.player.Playing() {
536				return true // swallowed: a scrub during playback is not a scrub
537			}
538			if dy != 0 {
539				n.frameStep(int(math.Round(dy))) // wheel down runs forward, as everywhere
540			}
541			return true
542		})
543		n.slider.AddController(wheel)
544		n.slider.ConnectValueChanged(func() {
545			if n.sliding {
546				return
547			}
548			// The handle is on the CUT, so there is nothing to snap; it only has to be
549			// read back into session time. Spanning the gaps made most of the bar dead
550			// space and every drag a fight with the snap.
551			n.seekWant = cutAt(n.clips(), n.slider.Value())
552			// one seek per 120 ms, not one per pixel of the drag: a seek that
553			// lands in a different recording reloads the pipeline
554			if n.seekArmed {
555				return
556			}
557			n.seekArmed = true
558			glib.TimeoutAdd(120, func() bool {
559				n.seekArmed = false
560				n.seekTo(n.seekWant)
561				return false
562			})
563		})
564		n.timeLbl = gtk.NewLabel("00:00")
565		n.timeLbl.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
566		// ＋ is the same ＋ every row carries: a new line here, at the playhead. It is
567		// also the only way in ABOVE a line -- a row's ＋ adds below itself.
568		addBtn := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-add-symbolic")
569		addBtn.SetTooltipText("start a new narration line at this second — it runs until the clip's " +
570			"next line, or the clip's end. Pause where the video has nothing to say and press this.")
571		addBtn.ConnectClicked(func() { a.addLineClicked() })
572	
573		transport := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 6)
574		transport.Append(back)
575		transport.Append(n.playBtn)
576		transport.Append(fwd)
577		transport.Append(addBtn)
578		transport.Append(n.slider)
579		transport.Append(n.timeLbl)
580		// and how loud it is, beside the button that plays it: this page is where
581		// a narration line is judged against the sound under it, which is a
582		// judgement made with a hand on the volume
583		transport.Append(volumeCtl())
584	
585		preview := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 8)
586		preview.Append(vframe)
587		preview.Append(transport)
588		// the picture takes this column's spare height -- on the FRAME as well as the
589		// box, or with no player built the box grew and its children did not, leaving
590		// a hand's width of nothing above the voice picker.
591		vframe.SetVExpand(true)
592		preview.SetVExpand(true)
593	
594		// The voice picker sits under the video, where it is read alongside the
595		// sample it plays; the lines have their whole column, because sentences want
596		// width. The prompt is on Prepare (prepedit.go).
597		voice := a.buildVoicePicker()
598	
599		// Whether this video is narrated at all, at the top right of the page.
600		// Some videos want none -- the speakers carry them, or the words go on
601		// screen instead -- and there was no way to say so: the nearest was the
602		// captions voice, which still writes lines and still asks Produce to carry
603		// them. Off means off, and Produce loses what only a narration needs
604		// (produce.go).
605		n.onBox = gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel("Narration")
606		n.onBox.SetActive(!a.narrOff)
607		n.onBox.SetTooltipText("Whether this video has a narration. Unticked, ▶ writes none, " +
608			"the lines already written are left alone, and Produce drops the game-volume " +
609			"slider and the subtitle choices -- all three exist to carry a voice-over.")
610		n.onBox.ConnectToggled(func() { a.setNarrOff(!n.onBox.Active()) })
611	
612		// the picture and the voice it is played in, in one column, under the one
613		// tick that is about the narration as a whole rather than about any line
614		// of it -- top left, where a page's first question goes
615		head := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 6)
616		head.SetHAlign(gtk.AlignStart)
617		head.Append(n.onBox)
618		top := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 6)
619		top.Append(head)
620		top.Append(preview)
621		// the handle under it is a control, not a rule: pressed against the
622		// transport's buttons it reads as part of them, and the hand aiming at the
623		// last button lands on the drag instead
624		top.SetMarginBottom(6)
625	
626		// ...and a handle between the two, so the column can be traded: a bigger
627		// picture while the cut is being watched, a bigger waveform while the
628		// seconds to clone are being picked. It was a fixed split, and the video
629		// took whatever was left over -- which is the wrong way round twice a
630		// session and cannot be argued with either time.
631		shown := gtk.NewPaned(gtk.OrientationVertical)
632		shown.SetMarginStart(12) // the window's edge
633		shown.SetMarginEnd(6)    // ...and the handle's, which the lines match
634		shown.SetMarginTop(8)
635		shown.SetMarginBottom(8)
636		shown.SetStartChild(top)
637		shown.SetEndChild(voice)
638		shown.SetPosition(420)
639		shown.SetResizeStartChild(true)
640		shown.SetResizeEndChild(false)
641		shown.SetShrinkStartChild(false)
642		shown.SetShrinkEndChild(false)
643	
644		// ...and the lines beside them
645		written := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
646		margins(written, 8, 8, 6, 12)
647		written.Append(left)
648		// everything on this page except the tick itself: with no narration there
649		// is nothing here to do, and a page of live controls over a video that has
650		// none is a page that invites the work the tick just said not to do. The
651		// tick stays alive, because turning it back on is the one thing still
652		// worth pressing.
653		n.body = []gtk.Widgetter{left, preview, voice}
654	
655		// Picture left, words right -- the shape Cut and Produce have. The lines take
656		// the window's extra width; the picture keeps what it was dragged to.
657		split := gtk.NewPaned(gtk.OrientationHorizontal)
658		split.SetStartChild(shown)
659		split.SetEndChild(written)
660		split.SetPosition(560)
661		split.SetVExpand(true)
662		split.SetShrinkStartChild(false)
663		split.SetResizeStartChild(false)
664		split.SetResizeEndChild(true)
665	
666		// What this step reads, on the shared bottom bar beside what it has
667		// written (inputsLabel, outStack)
668		n.inputs = inputsLabel()
669		a.inStack.AddNamed(n.inputs, "narrate")
670	
671		openOut := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("folder-open-symbolic")
672		openOut.SetTooltipText("narrate/ — narration.json, the voice reference and the synthesis cache")
673		openOut.ConnectClicked(func() { a.openFolder(a.narrateDir()) })
674		n.out = gtk.NewLabel("")
675		outRow := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
676		outRow.Append(openOut)
677		outRow.Append(n.out)
678		a.outStack.AddNamed(outRow, "narrate")
679	
680		page := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
681		page.Append(split)
682	
683		n.load()
684		n.rebuildRows()
685		n.updateInputs()
686		n.updateOut()
687		return page
688	}
689	
690	// textBoxHeight is how tall a row's box has to be to hold that many lines of
691	// words: the lines themselves, the view's own margins (2 above, 2 below), the
692	// frame's 1px border, and two pixels of slack. The error is not symmetric -- a
693	// box two pixels too tall is invisible, a box two pixels too short is a
694	// scrollbar -- so the slack rounds up.
695	func textBoxHeight(lineH, lines int) int { return lines*lineH + 8 }
696	
697	// queueRebuild is rebuildRows for a caller inside a row's own signal handler:
698	// GTK is still standing on that widget, so the rebuild runs on the next idle,
699	// coalesced (Enter commits, then the focus leaves the box).
700	func (n *narrator) queueRebuild() {
701		if n.list == nil || n.rebuildQ {
702			return // headless (tests), or one is already on its way
703		}
704		n.rebuildQ = true
705		glib.IdleAdd(func() {
706			n.rebuildQ = false
707			n.rebuildRows()
708		})
709	}
710	
711	func (n *narrator) rebuildRows() {
712		if n.list == nil {
713			return // headless (tests): the entries are the model, the rows a view of it
714		}
715		// Where the reader was: a rebuild throws every row away, and a fresh list is
716		// scrolled to the top. The OFFSET is restored, not the focus -- a rebuild is
717		// usually raised by focus leaving a box (queueRebuild); focusLine asks by
718		// name.
719		at, sel := n.listOffset(), -1
720		if r := n.list.SelectedRow(); r != nil {
721			sel = r.Index()
722		}
723		n.building = true
724		for {
725			row := n.list.RowAtIndex(0)
726			if row == nil {
727				break
728			}
729			n.list.Remove(row)
730		}
731		n.rows = nil
732		n.speaking, n.solo = -1, -1 // the buttons that knew about it are gone
733		n.sortEntries()             // a hand-edited time may have reordered the list
734		// A line's height in pixels, measured in the BOX's font (monospace, a few px
735		// taller than the list's) -- sized from the list, a full three-line box came
736		// up ten pixels short with a scrollbar that travelled that far.
737		lineH := 20
738		probe := gtk.NewTextView()
739		probe.SetMonospace(true)
740		if lay := probe.CreatePangoLayout("Ay"); lay != nil {
741			if _, h := lay.PixelSize(); h > 0 {
742				lineH = h
743			}
744		}
745		oneLine, threeLines := textBoxHeight(lineH, 1), textBoxHeight(lineH, 3)
746		for i := range n.entries {
747			e := &n.entries[i]
748			i := i
749	
750			head := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 6)
751			// the line's start, on the session clock, editable: the "at" is
752			// derived from it (clamped to the line's clip), so timing is corrected
753			// where it is judged -- against the video -- not by arithmetic on
754			// offsets. The list re-sorts when the edit is done (activate/rebuild),
755			// not per keystroke, or the box would jump out from under the cursor.
756			when := gtk.NewEntry()
757			// A clock is eight characters wide and never more, so say so twice: an
758			// entry with no max-width-chars asks for a natural width far past what
759			// it will ever hold, and took most of the row with "10:25.0" in it --
760			// pushing the end-time label off the edge.
761			when.SetWidthChars(8)
762			when.SetMaxWidthChars(8)
763			when.SetHExpand(false)
764			when.SetText(fmtClock(e.S + e.At))
765			when.SetTooltipText("when this line's audio starts (mm:ss.s on the session clock) — after the dash is " +
766				"when it stops speaking. A time inside another clip moves the line there; one outside the cut is " +
767				"refused and the box goes back to where the line really is")
768			tl := gtk.NewLabel("")
769			tl.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
770			// ...and never a floor under the window, the way the Inputs line is
771			// not one. Now that the column no longer scrolls sideways, a label's
772			// minimum width IS the row's, and this one holds sentences: "⚠ this
773			// clip's lines run 3.4 s past it — the render will have them moved
774			// earlier and sped up" is half a screen that nothing could shrink
775			// past. It is a summary of what the row below already says.
776			tl.SetEllipsize(pango.EllipsizeEnd)
777			// an empty box is now an answer and not a failure -- the narration is
778			// asked to leave clips alone -- so the row says which it is, or a page
779			// with three blank lines on it reads as a run that half worked
780			stamp := func() {
781				warn, s := false, ""
782				if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) == "" {
783					s = "(no line — this clip plays on its own audio)"
784				} else if n.a.captionsOnly() {
785					// nothing below applies with no voice: no wav, no spoken
786					// length, no overrun to warn about. The line stays on screen
787					// until the next one, so there is no end time to print either.
788					s = "(caption — the viewer reads it; never spoken)"
789				} else {
790					// the end is when the AUDIO stops: start plus the spoken
791					// length, measured off the wav when it exists and estimated
792					// (~, from how fast the spoken lines came out) until it does.
793					// The gap to the next line
794					// is just the game playing -- it belongs to nobody's row.
795					dur := n.speechDur(*e)
796					s = "– " + fmtClock(e.S+e.At+dur)
797					if !exists(n.a.ttsWav(*e)) {
798						s += " (~)" // estimated: the line has not been spoken yet
799					}
800					// the corner the mix can only paper over: more speech than the
801					// slot holds gets slid earlier and then sped up. Say so here,
802					// while the words are still being chosen.
803					if win := n.lineWindow(i); dur > win {
804						edge := "the clip ends"
805						if n.lineEnd(i) < e.E-0.05 {
806							edge = "the next line"
807						}
808						s += fmt.Sprintf("  ⚠ ~%.0f s of speech, %.0f s before %s", dur, win, edge)
809						warn = true
810					}
811					// ...and the clip's whole schedule, on the row it hangs off.
812					// The line above is about one line's room; this is about all
813					// of them stacked up, which is the thing the render moves
814					// (clipOverrun).
815					if n.clipTop(i) {
816						if over := n.clipOverrun(i); over > 0.05 {
817							how := "moved earlier"
818							if over > n.clipSlack(i) {
819								how = "moved earlier and sped up"
820							}
821							s += fmt.Sprintf("  ⚠ this clip's lines run %.1f s past it — the render will have them %s",
822								over, how)
823							warn = true
824						}
825					}
826				}
827				if warn {
828					tl.AddCSSClass("error")
829				} else {
830					tl.RemoveCSSClass("error")
831				}
832				tl.SetText(s)
833			}
834			stamp()
835			tl.SetHExpand(true)
836			tl.SetXAlign(0)
837			when.ConnectChanged(func() {
838				if n.building {
839					return
840				}
841				// only what a clock can contain gets to stay: a stray letter is
842				// removed as it is typed, not complained about after
843				if c := cleanClock(when.Text()); c != when.Text() {
844					p := when.Position()
845					when.SetText(c) // re-enters this handler; the clean text passes
846					when.SetPosition(p - 1)
847					return
848				}
849				t, ok := parseClock(when.Text())
850				if !ok {
851					when.AddCSSClass("error") // half-typed reads as such, not as applied
852					return
853				}
854				when.RemoveCSSClass("error")
855				// live, while typing, the line only moves INSIDE its own clip: a
856				// half-typed "1" on its way to "12:42" must not re-home the line to
857				// the clip at one second and back again on the next keystroke.
858				// Landing somewhere else is a decision, and decisions are committed.
859				e.At = math.Min(math.Max(0, t-e.S), math.Max(0, e.E-e.S-1))
860				n.saveSoon()
861				n.restamp(i)
862			})
863			// commit is what a finished edit means: the typed time is placed for
864			// real -- another clip included -- and then WRITTEN BACK, so the box
865			// shows where the line is rather than where it was asked to go. That
866			// write-back is the fix for a row reading "12:42 – 11:07.5".
867			commit := func() bool {
868				if n.building {
869					return false
870				}
871				t, ok := parseClock(when.Text())
872				if !ok {
873					// a half-typed time abandoned snaps back to the last applied
874					// one -- an "error" box left behind would read as a placement
875					// that somehow took
876					when.RemoveCSSClass("error")
877					when.SetText(fmtClock(e.S + e.At))
878					return false
879				}
880				moved := n.moveLine(i, t)
881				when.SetText(fmtClock(e.S + e.At))
882				n.restamp(i)
883				return moved
884			}
885			// Enter commits the edit: the list re-sorts around the new time
886			when.ConnectActivate(func() {
887				commit()
888				if !n.building {
889					n.queueRebuild()
890				}
891			})
892			wf := gtk.NewEventControllerFocus()
893			wf.ConnectLeave(func() {
894				// a line that changed clips has moved in the list as well, so the
895				// order has to be redone; one nudged within its clip has not, and
896				// rebuilding under a click that is on its way to another widget
897				// would pull that widget out from under it
898				if commit() {
899					n.queueRebuild()
900				}
901			})
902			when.AddController(wf)
903			// ▶ per line rather than a 🔊: it is a play button and, while its line is
904			// sounding, the ⏸ for it (syncSpeakIcons draws that)
905			speak := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
906			if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) == "" {
907				// no line to lead into: this ▶ plays the clip itself (syncSpeakIcons
908				// keeps the wording right as the words come and go)
909				speak.SetTooltipText("play this clip — it has no line, so you hear the game")
910			} else {
911				speak.SetTooltipText("play this line — from a few seconds ahead of it where those seconds are its own, " +
912					"from the line itself where the line above is still speaking; the preview then carries on down the cut")
913			}
914			speak.ConnectClicked(func() { n.a.speakEntry(i) })
915			roll := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("view-refresh-symbolic")
916			roll.SetTooltipText("re-roll: speak this line again as a different take — same words, same delivery, new draw")
917			roll.ConnectClicked(func() { n.a.rerollEntry(i) })
918			// One ＋, and it adds BELOW. A second one for the other direction was a
919			// third button on a row that already carries five, to reach a place the
920			// transport's own ＋ reaches better: that one adds at the playhead, so
921			// the way to put a line above the first of a clip is to pause where it
922			// should speak and press the ＋ next to ▶ -- which is also how you place
923			// every other line, against the picture rather than against a row.
924			add := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("＋")
925			add.SetTooltipText("add a line below this one, starting where its audio ends — " +
926				"for one above it, pause there and use the ＋ beside the play button")
927			add.ConnectClicked(func() {
928				n.pullRows()
929				n.focusLine(n.addLineAfter(i))
930			})
931			del := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("user-trash-symbolic")
932			del.SetTooltipText("remove this line — the video plays its own audio here instead")
933			del.ConnectClicked(func() { n.deleteLine(i) })
934			head.Append(when)
935			head.Append(tl)
936			head.Append(speak)
937			head.Append(roll)
938			head.Append(add)
939			head.Append(del)
940	
941			text := gtk.NewTextView()
942			text.SetWrapMode(gtk.WrapWord)
943			text.SetMonospace(true) // every editable box in the app is this font
944			text.SetTopMargin(2)
945			text.SetBottomMargin(2) // the last line needs its descender, same as the first
946			text.SetLeftMargin(6)
947			text.SetTooltipText(`"[emotion] words" — the emotion is sent to the TTS as the delivery, never spoken; the field on the left is when the line starts.
948	Words are read by a judge: "angry", "surprised, happy". Add weights to skip it and set the mix exactly: "[angry=1]", "[happy=0.8, surprised=0.4]", "[excited=1]".
949	The eight it mixes: happy, angry, sad, afraid, disgusted, melancholic, surprised, calm — plus named mixes of them (excited, awed, alarmed, frustrated, tender, ... see the ⓘ).`)
950			text.Buffer().SetText(lineText(*e))
951			tScroll := gtk.NewScrolledWindow()
952			tScroll.SetChild(text)
953			tScroll.SetPropagateNaturalHeight(true)
954			// the words wrap, so nothing ever runs off the side: a horizontal
955			// scrollbar could only take height away from the lines
956			tScroll.SetPolicy(gtk.PolicyNever, gtk.PolicyAutomatic)
957			// The box is as tall as what is in it, between one line and three: with
958			// propagate-natural-height set, the scrolled window asks for the view's
959			// own height and these two clamp it. A one-line row is one line tall --
960			// a page of them used to be a page of mostly empty boxes -- and the
961			// fourth line is where the scrollbar starts, with three lines of context
962			// above it rather than a few pixels of travel.
963			tScroll.SetMinContentHeight(oneLine)
964			tScroll.SetMaxContentHeight(threeLines)
965			tScroll.AddCSSClass("frame")
966	
967			change := func() {
968				if !n.building {
969					n.pullRows()
970					n.saveSoon() // a file write per keystroke, otherwise
971					n.restamp(i) // pullRows has just put what is in the box into e
972				}
973			}
974			text.Buffer().ConnectChanged(change)
975	
976			box := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
977			box.SetMarginTop(6)
978			box.SetMarginBottom(6)
979			box.SetMarginStart(8)
980			box.SetMarginEnd(8)
981			box.Append(head)
982			box.Append(tScroll)
983			n.list.Append(box)
984			n.rows = append(n.rows, &narrRow{text: text, speak: speak, stamp: stamp})
985		}
986		n.building = false
987		n.restoreOffset(at, sel)
988	}
989	
990	// listOffset is how far down the narration list the reader has scrolled, or 0
991	// where there is no scroller to ask (a test's page).
992	func (n *narrator) listOffset() float64 {
993		if n.listScroll == nil {
994			return 0
995		}
996		if adj := n.listScroll.VAdjustment(); adj != nil {
997			return adj.Value()
998		}
999		return 0
1000	}
1001	
1002	// restoreOffset puts the list back where it was after a rebuild, and re-selects
1003	// the row that was selected.
1004	//
1005	// On the idle rather than now: the rows have just been appended and have no
1006	// height yet, so the adjustment has no range to hold the value and setting it
1007	// here would clamp it to nought -- which is the very jump this exists to stop.
1008	// Clamped to what the new list can actually show, because the rebuild may have
1009	// left fewer rows than the offset was measured against (a line deleted, another
1010	// project loaded).
1011	//
1012	// The selection goes back through selectRow, which holds n.building across it:
1013	// picking a row seeks the preview, and a row that was already picked being put
1014	// back is not a hand asking for anything.
1015	func (n *narrator) restoreOffset(at float64, sel int) {
1016		if n.listScroll == nil || (at <= 0 && sel < 0) {
1017			return
1018		}
1019		glib.IdleAdd(func() {
1020			if n.listScroll == nil {
1021				return
1022			}
1023			if adj := n.listScroll.VAdjustment(); adj != nil && at > 0 {
1024				adj.SetValue(math.Max(0, math.Min(at, adj.Upper()-adj.PageSize())))
1025			}
1026			if sel >= 0 && sel < len(n.rows) {
1027				n.selectRow(sel)
1028			}
1029		})
1030	}
1031	
1032	// restamp redraws the times on a row and on the row above it, and the second
1033	// half is the point. A line's slot runs to where the NEXT line on the clip
1034	// starts (lineEnd, lineWindow), so a typed time -- or a box emptied, which
1035	// hands the seconds back to the clip -- changes two rows and only the edited
1036	// one was ever redrawn. The row above went on printing an end that had moved
1037	// and a ⚠ measured against a slot that was no longer that size, until some
1038	// unrelated rebuild happened to correct it.
1039	func (n *narrator) restamp(i int) {
1040		for _, j := range []int{i - 1, i} {
1041			if j >= 0 && j < len(n.rows) && n.rows[j].stamp != nil {
1042				n.rows[j].stamp()
1043			}
1044		}
1045	}
1046	
1047	// seekTo cues the preview at a session time, preserving play state.
1048	func (n *narrator) seekTo(t float64) { n.cue(t, n.player != nil && n.player.playing) }
1049	
1050	// cue is seekTo with the play state named rather than carried over, for the
1051	// one caller that has nothing to carry: a preview started from a cold page,
1052	// where the file has to be loaded and played in one go. Handing PlaySegment
1053	// play=false and calling Toggle after it would race the preroll -- the seek
1054	// only lands when the bus says AsyncDone, and pendPlay is how it is told.
1055	func (n *narrator) cue(t float64, play bool) {
1056		ed := n.a.ed
1057		if ed == nil || n.player == nil {
1058			return
1059		}
1060		// cutVideoAt, not videoAt: this page previews the FINISHED VIDEO, so the
1061		// picture is the one the scene at t names. videoAt starts from the row the
1062		// Cut page was last asked to watch, which is a thing you do while editing
1063		// there -- and it followed the preview here, so a click on the second
1064		// camera's thumbnails in Cut made Narrate play the second camera for the
1065		// whole session, whatever the cut says. Nil in a gap; there is no finished
1066		// video there, and followPlayback skips them anyway.
1067		v := ed.cutVideoAt(t)
1068		if v == nil {
1069			return
1070		}
1071		n.setPlayhead(t)
1072		n.playSeg = -1 // re-trigger the voice on the next tick
1073		// Already in this file: seek inside it. Reloading the uri tears the pipeline
1074		// down and builds it again for a jump of a few seconds, and playback only
1075		// picks up when the fresh preroll reports back on the bus -- a seek just
1076		// keeps playing, which is what skipping a gap should feel like.
1077		if n.player.loaded == v.path {
1078			// before the seek, never after: a rate only takes hold at a seek, and
1079			// this is the seek
1080			n.player.SetRate(fxPreviewRateAt(ed.fx, t))
1081			n.player.SeekTo(t - v.start)
1082			// the seek cleared ended, so this starts at the new position rather
1083			// than replaying whatever the stream stopped on
1084			if play && !n.player.playing {
1085				n.player.Toggle()
1086			}
1087			return
1088		}
1089		// which recordings are heard under THIS footage: the render mixes them
1090		// (clipMixes) and so must the page that judges whether a line fits between
1091		// them -- a scene shown from one camera and heard from another's
1092		// microphone was silent here until this
1093		n.player.SetMix(ed.mixUnder(v))
1094		n.player.SetRate(fxPreviewRateAt(ed.fx, t))
1095		n.player.PlaySegment(v.path, t-v.start, -1, play)
1096		n.playVideoStart = v.start
1097		n.syncFxSound() // the mix is new, so its hush is owed again
1098	}
1099	
1100	// setPlayhead records where the preview is and shows it on the slider, without
1101	// the slider's own handler mistaking the update for a drag. The blue row comes
1102	// with it: every way the preview moves -- the tick, a seek, a drag, ⏪ and ⏩ --
1103	// arrives here, so this is the one place that keeps the list pointing at what
1104	// is on screen.
1105	func (n *narrator) setPlayhead(t float64) {
1106		n.pos = t
1107		// the effects follow the line, always: this is the one funnel every mover
1108		// of the playhead goes through, so hanging them here is what makes a seek
1109		// into a zoom show the zoom and a seek into a stop show the frozen frame
1110		n.syncFx(t)
1111		n.syncFxSound()
1112		// ...but only while the picture is rolling. Paused, the blue row is the
1113		// user's: they clicked it to work on it, and a click seeks five seconds
1114		// ahead of the line so the moment can be watched arriving -- following the
1115		// playhead there would move the selection off the row that was just picked.
1116		if n.player != nil && n.player.playing {
1117			n.selectRow(n.nearestEntry(t))
1118		}
1119		if n.slider == nil || n.sliding {
1120			return
1121		}
1122		segs := n.clips()
1123		n.sliding = true
1124		n.slider.SetValue(cutPos(segs, t)) // the bar is the cut's clock, this is the session's
1125		n.sliding = false
1126		if n.timeLbl != nil {
1127			// both clocks, because the page needs both: the session time is what the
1128			// rows, the Cut page and every warning are written in, and the cut time
1129			// is how far into the finished video this is -- which is the question a
1130			// bar measuring the cut invites, and the one nothing here answered
1131			n.timeLbl.SetText(fmt.Sprintf("%02d:%02d · %s/%s", int(t)/60, int(t)%60,
1132				mmss(cutPos(segs, t)), mmss(cutLen(segs))))
1133		}
1134	}
1135	
1136	// gameGain is the level the footage plays at, at t: the volume effect there,
1137	// times GameVol on any clip with a line on it -- the render ducks the WHOLE
1138	// clip, not the words (encodeClip), and the page has to sound the same way.
1139	func (n *narrator) gameGain(t float64) float64 {
1140		g := 1.0
1141		if n.a != nil && n.a.ed != nil {
1142			g = fxGainAt(n.a.ed.fx, t)
1143		}
1144		if n.clipSpeaks(t) {
1145			g *= n.a.gameVol()
1146		}
1147		return g
1148	}
1149	
1150	// clipSpeaks is whether the clip at session second t has anything written on
1151	// it. The render's own question, asked the render's way -- the whole clip, not
1152	// the seconds a line covers -- so that the level does not step up and down
1153	// inside a clip here while the video holds it flat.
1154	func (n *narrator) clipSpeaks(t float64) bool {
1155		for _, e := range n.entries {
1156			if t >= e.S && t < e.E && strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) != "" {
1157				return true
1158			}
1159		}
1160		return false
1161	}
1162	
1163	// syncFxSound puts the preview's sound where the finished video's is: the
1164	// lanes the scene hears, the volume effects, silence where a stop cuts seconds
1165	// out. All three settle on the playhead (setPlayhead), no seek needed. The
1166	// picture's half is fxPage (formerly narrate_fxview.go).
1167	func (n *narrator) syncFxSound() {
1168		ed, p := n.a.ed, n.player
1169		if ed == nil || p == nil {
1170			return
1171		}
1172		p.SetFxGain(n.gameGain(n.pos))
1173		s := n.heardScene(n.pos)
1174		// Two silences this page owes: fxHush (a speed effect that silenced its
1175		// seconds) and cardHush (a card over the footage, unless it was for the
1176		// picture alone, keepsSoundUnder). The preview cannot load a card, so the
1177		// picture is a known hole; the SOUND being wrong is not survivable here.
1178		p.SetMuted(fxHush(ed.fx, n.pos) || cardHush(overInsert(ed.segs, n.pos)))
1179		base, until := "", 0.0
1180		if v := ed.cutVideoAt(n.pos); v != nil {
1181			base = v.base
1182			// the answer holds to the end of this clip, or to the next clip's
1183			// start, in the file's own seconds: a lane started now stops there
1184			// by itself (auxAudio.stopAt), the way the Cut page's does
1185			if s != nil {
1186				until = v.at(s.E)
1187			} else if _, next := gapAt(ed.segs, n.pos); next >= 0 {
1188				until = v.at(ed.segs[next].S)
1189			}
1190		} else if p.loaded != "" {
1191			base = baseName(p.loaded) // past a clip's end: the file still running
1192		}
1193		own, quiet := hushOf(s, base)
1194		p.Hush(own, quiet, until)
1195	}
1196	
1197	// overInsert is the card the cut lays over the footage at t. Spliced cards are
1198	// deliberately not here: those own no session time at all (S == E, see
1199	// cutSeg.spliced) -- they are a point the footage is cut open at -- so a
1200	// playhead running down the session never sits inside one.
1201	func overInsert(segs []cutSeg, t float64) *cutSeg {
1202		for i := range segs {
1203			if s := &segs[i]; s.isInsert() && !s.spliced() && t >= s.S && t < s.E {
1204				return s
1205			}
1206		}
1207		return nil
1208	}
1209	
1210	// needsReload is the tick's one question about the file under the picture: is
1211	// the preview on the recording the CUT names at t. Split out of followPlayback
1212	// because the tick is GStreamer and this is arithmetic, and because the case it
1213	// was missing is invisible from inside the tick -- two scenes that touch, taken
1214	// on different lanes. Nothing moves, no gap is jumped, and the answer changes.
1215	func needsReload(segs []cutSeg, vids []tlVideo, loaded string, t float64) bool {
1216		v := cutVideoOn(segs, vids, t)
1217		return v != nil && loaded != v.path
1218	}
1219	
1220	// heardScene is the clip whose lane answers the preview is under: the clip
1221	// being played OUT of, or before the first one the clip being played INTO. Not
1222	// "the clip under the playhead" -- this page spends real time outside clips
1223	// (holding past an end, skipping a gap) and must not play lanes those scenes
1224	// silence.
1225	func (n *narrator) heardScene(t float64) *cutSeg {
1226		ed := n.a.ed
1227		if ed == nil {
1228			return nil
1229		}
1230		if i := ed.segAt(t); i >= 0 {
1231			return &ed.segs[i]
1232		}
1233		prev, next := -1, -1
1234		for i := range ed.segs {
1235			if ed.segs[i].E <= t && (prev < 0 || ed.segs[i].E > ed.segs[prev].E) {
1236				prev = i
1237			}
1238			if ed.segs[i].S > t && (next < 0 || ed.segs[i].S < ed.segs[next].S) {
1239				next = i
1240			}
1241		}
1242		switch {
1243		case prev >= 0:
1244			return &ed.segs[prev]
1245		case next >= 0:
1246			return &ed.segs[next]
1247		}
1248		return nil
1249	}
1250	
1251	// syncPlayRate is the one that does: a speed effect only takes hold at a seek,
1252	// so crossing into or out of one while the picture runs has to seek to where
1253	// the stream already is. The same bargain Cut makes -- a small hitch at each
1254	// boundary, in exchange for a preview that is actually the speed it claims.
1255	func (n *narrator) syncPlayRate() {
1256		if n.player != nil && n.a.ed != nil {
1257			n.player.SetRateNow(fxPreviewRateAt(n.a.ed.fx, n.pos))
1258		}
1259	}
1260	
1261	// frameStep nudges the preview by whole frames, the way Cut's playhead
1262	// moves. It is what the wheel over the slider does: ⏪ and ⏩ jump three seconds
1263	// to find a moment, and this lands on it -- "the chest is on screen HERE" is a
1264	// frame, and a line's placement is only as good as the frame it was judged
1265	// against.
1266	//
1267	// Frames, not seconds, so the source's own rate decides the step: a 60 fps
1268	// capture nudges half as far as a 30 fps one, which is what a frame means.
1269	// Inside the cut only. The slider shows the cut and its gaps snap over, so a
1270	// step that would land in removed material lands on the near edge of the
1271	// neighbouring clip instead -- the same rule the preview follows when it plays
1272	// through one.
1273	func (n *narrator) frameStep(frames int) {
1274		segs := n.clips()
1275		if n.a.ed == nil || n.player == nil || len(segs) == 0 || frames == 0 {
1276			return
1277		}
1278		fps := 30.0 // no video under the playhead: a plausible rate beats no step
1279		if v := n.a.ed.cutVideoAt(n.pos); v != nil && v.fps > 0 {
1280			fps = v.fps
1281		}
1282		n.seekTo(frameTarget(segs, n.pos, fps, frames))
1283	}
1284	
1285	// frameTarget is where that step lands: the arithmetic, with the cut's gaps
1286	// closed up. Split out because it is the part that can be wrong.
1287	func frameTarget(segs []cutSeg, pos, fps float64, frames int) float64 {
1288		return snapToCut(segs, pos, pos+float64(frames)/fps, 1/fps)
1289	}
1290	
1291	// cutEdge is how far inside a clip a scrub lands when it snaps back onto its
1292	// tail. The clip's end is already the gap after it, so landing exactly there

52	// for the words. ok is false when the frame's size is not known, which is the
53	// only case there is nothing to fit against.
54	func svgFitPx(f cutFx, w, h int) (x, y, bw, bh int, ok bool) {
55		if w <= 0 || h <= 0 {

68	// needs and a frame of footage does not: the librsvg options that set the size
69	// the vector is rendered at, and an output kept in rgba so a transparent
70	// background stays transparent instead of coming out black.
71	func svgRaster(path string, w, h int) ([]byte, error) {
72		args := []string{"-v", "error", "-nostdin"}
73		if w > 0 && h > 0 {
74			args = append(args, "-width", fmt.Sprint(w), "-height", fmt.Sprint(h), "-keep_ar", "1")
75		}
76		args = append(args, "-i", path, "-frames:v", "1",
77			"-pix_fmt", "rgba", "-f", "image2", "-c:v", "png", "-")
78		cmd := exec.Command(ffTool("ffmpeg"), args...)
79		var out, errb bytes.Buffer
80		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &out, &errb
81		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
82			tail := strings.TrimSpace(errb.String())
83			if len(tail) > 200 {
84				tail = tail[len(tail)-200:]
85			}
86			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ffmpeg: %w: %s", err, tail)
87		}
88		if out.Len() == 0 {
89			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ffmpeg drew nothing")
90		}
91		return out.Bytes(), nil
92	}

107	func (ed *cutEditor) svgSurface(path string) *cairo.Surface {

120			return c.surf

123		a := ed.a

127			if err == nil {

130			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
131				c.busy = false
132				if err != nil {

134					if a != nil {

136					}
137					return
138				}
139				c.surf = cairo.CreateSurfaceFromImage(img)
140				if ed.fxArea != nil {
141					ed.fxArea.QueueDraw()
142				}
143			})
144		}()
145		return nil
146	}

149	// exactly as textChain fits it in the render: scaled to sit inside, its own
150	// shape kept, centred on the axis the fit left short.
151	func (ed *cutEditor) drawSVG(cr *cairo.Context, f cutFx, x, y, w, h, alpha float64) {
152		if alpha <= 0.01 || w <= 0 || h <= 0 {
153			return
154		}
155		surf := ed.svgSurface(f.Src)
156		if surf == nil {
157			return
158		}
159		sw, sh := float64(surf.Width()), float64(surf.Height())
160		if sw <= 0 || sh <= 0 {
161			return
162		}
163		s := math.Min(w/sw, h/sh)
164		cr.Save()
165		cr.Translate(x+(w-sw*s)/2, y+(h-sh*s)/2)
166		cr.Scale(s, s)
167		cr.SetSourceSurface(surf, 0, 0)
168		cr.PaintWithAlpha(alpha)
169		cr.Restore()
170	}

package main

// Answers kept, so the same question is not paid for twice.
//
// Describing an hour of footage is the longest thing this app does: one vision
// call per few frames, seven seconds each, hundreds of them. The step already
// resumes -- a chunk in the event log is not described again -- but a ⏹ that
// lands in the middle arms a fresh start (undFreshStart), and a fresh start on
// unchanged footage used to mean paying the whole twenty minutes again for
// answers that could only come back the same.
//
// So the answer is filed under the question. The key is the WHOLE request: the
// system prompt, the user text -- the rolling state, the speech, the context --
// and the frames themselves, which ride inside it as data URLs. Nothing that
// decides the answer is outside the key, which is the only way a cache like
// this can be safe: change the wording, the interval, the scale or a word of
// the context and every affected chunk is asked again, because the question is
// not the same question.
//
// It lives under the project's cache/ beside the waveforms, which is the folder
// for things that can be thrown away and made again. Deleting it costs time and
// nothing else.

import (
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
)

// llmCacheDir is where a step's answers are kept.
func (a *App) llmCacheDir(step string) string {
	return filepath.Join(a.outDir, "cache", "llm", step)
}

// askKey digests a request into the name of the file its answer belongs in.
// Everything the model is sent goes in, in order; JSON is the spelling, so the
// key is exactly as stable as the request the server would receive.
func askKey(parts ...any) string {
	h := sha256.New()
	for _, p := range parts {
		b, err := json.Marshal(p)
		if err != nil {
			// unmarshalable means unsendable: a key that cannot be computed
			// must not collide with one that can
			return ""
		}
		h.Write(b)
		h.Write([]byte{0})
	}
	return hex.EncodeToString(h.Sum(nil))
}

// cachedReply is the answer to this exact request, if it has been asked before.
func (a *App) cachedReply(step, key string) (string, bool) {
	if key == "" || a.outDir == "" {
		return "", false
	}
	b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(a.llmCacheDir(step), key))
	if err != nil || len(b) == 0 {
		return "", false
	}
	return string(b), true
}

// keepReply files one. Best-effort: a cache that cannot be written is a step
// that runs at its ordinary speed, which is what it did before there was one.
func (a *App) keepReply(step, key, reply string) {
	if key == "" || a.outDir == "" || reply == "" {
		return
	}
	dir := a.llmCacheDir(step)
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return
	}
	os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, key), []byte(reply), 0o644)
}

1	package main
2	
3	// The render's half of the effects (cut_fx.go): per-clip ffmpeg filter chains
4	// for aspect, views and zooms, plus the audio arithmetic a clip off its own
5	// speed needs. Every clip must come out at the same frame size (outBox)
6	// because the join is a stream copy:
7	//
8	//	pad  -> room around the frame, when a rectangle reaches past its edges
9	//	crop -> the fixed box the whole camera journey happens inside
10	//	zoompan -> the moving window, piecewise-linear expressions of in_time --
11	//	           or a plain crop and scale when the camera never moves
12	//
13	// The camera path comes from fxRectAt, the same function the preview draws,
14	// sampled at every moment anything starts or stops moving.
15	
16	import (
17		"fmt"
18		"math"
19		"strings"
20	)
21	
22	// camPath is the camera over one clip, in the clip's own output time. ts is
23	// ascending, starts at 0 and ends at the clip's length; r[i] is where the
24	// camera is at ts[i], and between breakpoints it travels straight -- which is
25	// exact, because everything fxRectAt does between its own breakpoints is a
26	// straight lerp too.
27	type camPath struct {
28		ts []float64
29		r  []fxRect
30		// the pixel plan, fixed for the whole clip (see buildCam)
31		sw, sh     int // source frame
32		outW, outH int // the frame every clip comes out at
33		padL, padT int // room added around the source
34		padW, padH int
35		boxX, boxY int // the fixed crop inside the padded frame
36		boxW, boxH int
37		fps        float64 // the grid zoompan runs on
38	}
39	
40	// static is whether the camera never moves in this clip.
41	func (p *camPath) static() bool {
42		for _, r := range p.r[1:] {
43			if r != p.r[0] {
44				return false
45			}
46		}
47		return true
48	}
49	
50	// buildCam samples the camera over one clip. sessS is the session time the
51	// clip starts at, span the session seconds it covers (0 for a freeze), rate
52	// its playback rate (1 = normal), length its output seconds, out the frame
53	// size, fps the grid an animated camera runs on.
54	func buildCam(fx []cutFx, aspect string, sw, sh int, sessS, span, rate, length float64,
55		outW, outH int, fps float64) *camPath {
56		if sw <= 0 || sh <= 0 || outW <= 0 || outH <= 0 || length <= 0 {
57			return nil
58		}
59		if rate <= 0 {
60			rate = 1
61		}
62		srcA, outA := float64(sw)/float64(sh), float64(outW)/float64(outH)
63		// every session moment the camera starts or stops moving inside this clip
64		sessTs := []float64{sessS, sessS + span}
65		for _, f := range fx {
66			if f.Kind != "zoom" {
67				continue
68			}
69			// every moment the camera changes what it is DOING: arriving, parked,
70			// letting go, gone. The path travels straight between samples, so a
71			// hold and a fade out that are not sampled are not rendered -- the
72			// camera would leave its rectangle the instant it reached it and
73			// drift across the rest of the clip instead of standing still for its
74			// seconds and then letting go. A staying zoom needs no end samples:
75			// it is parked on its rectangle from the moment it arrives.
76			tin, tout := f.zoomGlides()
77			sessTs = append(sessTs, f.T, f.T+tin)
78			if !f.Stay {
79				sessTs = append(sessTs, f.T+math.Max(f.Dur, 0)-tout, f.T+math.Max(f.Dur, 0))
80			}
81		}
82		p := &camPath{sw: sw, sh: sh, outW: outW, outH: outH, fps: fps}
83		seen := map[int64]bool{}
84		for _, st := range sessTs {
85			if st < sessS-1e-6 || st > sessS+span+1e-6 {
86				continue
87			}
88			t := 0.0
89			if span > 0 {
90				t = (st - sessS) / rate
91			}
92			t = math.Min(math.Max(0, t), length)
93			key := int64(math.Round(t * 1000))
94			if seen[key] {
95				continue
96			}
97			seen[key] = true
98			p.ts = append(p.ts, t)
99			p.r = append(p.r, fxRectAt(fx, st, srcA, outA))
100		}
101		// a freeze (span 0) collapses to one sample; give the path its two ends
102		if len(p.ts) == 1 {
103			p.ts = append(p.ts, length)
104			p.r = append(p.r, p.r[0])
105		}
106		sortCam(p)
107		p.plan(outA)
108		return p
109	}
110	
111	// gainCues maps the cut's volume effects onto one clip on textCues' terms --
112	// same five numbers -- so a title and a gain at the same second come and go
113	// together, and a gain under a speed effect stretches with its sound. A clip
114	// that is one held moment (span 0) gets none.
115	func gainCues(fx []cutFx, sessS, span, rate, length float64) []textCue {
116		if length <= 0 || span <= 0 {
117			return nil
118		}
119		var out []textCue
120		for i, f := range fx {
121			if f.Kind != "volume" {
122				continue
123			}
124			// no guard against a band of no length: cueClip turns down anything
125			// shorter than a frame, which is the same answer for a better reason
126			fin, fout := f.textFades()
127			s, e, cin, cout, ok := cueClip(f.T, f.Dur, fin, fout, sessS, rate, length)
128			if !ok {
129				continue
130			}
131			if cin+cout > e-s {
132				cin = math.Min(cin, e-s)
133				cout = math.Max(0, e-s-cin)
134			}
135			out = append(out, textCue{fx: f, s: s, e: e, fin: cin, fout: cout, idx: i})
136		}
137		return out
138	}
139	
140	// gainExpr is one volume cue as an ffmpeg volume expression in the clip's own
141	// seconds: the gain across the band, 1 elsewhere, a straight ramp over each
142	// fade. One expression, since volume's eval=frame re-reads it anyway. The
143	// multiplier is written with an explicit sign (1-0.5000*... not 1+-0.5000*...).
144	func gainExpr(c textCue) string {
145		g := clampGain(c.fx.Gain)
146		var ramps []string
147		if c.fin > 0 {
148			ramps = append(ramps, fmt.Sprintf("(t-%.3f)/%.3f", c.s, c.fin))
149		}
150		if c.fout > 0 {
151			ramps = append(ramps, fmt.Sprintf("(%.3f-t)/%.3f", c.e, c.fout))
152		}
153		val := fmt.Sprintf("%.4f", g)
154		switch len(ramps) {
155		case 1:
156			val = fmt.Sprintf("1%+.4f*min(1,%s)", g-1, ramps[0])
157		case 2:
158			val = fmt.Sprintf("1%+.4f*min(1,min(%s,%s))", g-1, ramps[0], ramps[1])
159		}
160		return fmt.Sprintf("if(between(t,%.3f,%.3f),%s,1)", c.s, c.e, val)
161	}

163	// gainChain is every volume cue of one clip, applied in turn to the label the
164	// sound arrives on; it returns the filter text and the label it leaves on. In
165	// turn, so two overlapping effects multiply -- which is exactly what fxGainAt
166	// tells the preview they do.
167	func gainChain(cues []textCue, in string) (string, string) {
168		fc := ""
169		for k, c := range cues {
170			out := fmt.Sprintf("gv%d", k)
171			fc += fmt.Sprintf("[%s]volume=volume='%s':eval=frame[%s];", in, gainExpr(c), out)
172			in = out
173		}
174		return fc, in
175	}

177	func sortCam(p *camPath) {
178		for i := 1; i < len(p.ts); i++ {
179			for j := i; j > 0 && p.ts[j] < p.ts[j-1]; j-- {
180				p.ts[j], p.ts[j-1] = p.ts[j-1], p.ts[j]
181				p.r[j], p.r[j-1] = p.r[j-1], p.r[j]
182			}
183		}
184	}
185	
186	// rectPx is a camera rectangle in source pixels: hf of the source height
187	// tall, exactly the output aspect wide.
188	func (p *camPath) rectPx(r fxRect, outA float64) (x, y, w, h float64) {
189		h = r.hf * float64(p.sh)
190		w = h * outA
191		return r.cx*float64(p.sw) - w/2, r.cy*float64(p.sh) - h/2, w, h
192	}
193	
194	// plan fixes the pixel geometry: how much black to pad around the source so
195	// no rectangle falls off it, and the one crop box -- output-shaped, covering
196	// the whole journey -- the moving window works inside.
197	func (p *camPath) plan(outA float64) {
198		minX, minY := math.Inf(1), math.Inf(1)
199		maxX, maxY := math.Inf(-1), math.Inf(-1)
200		for _, r := range p.r {
201			x, y, w, h := p.rectPx(r, outA)
202			minX, minY = math.Min(minX, x), math.Min(minY, y)
203			maxX, maxY = math.Max(maxX, x+w), math.Max(maxY, y+h)
204		}
205		p.padL = int(math.Ceil(math.Max(0, -minX)))
206		p.padT = int(math.Ceil(math.Max(0, -minY)))
207		padR := int(math.Ceil(math.Max(0, maxX-float64(p.sw))))
208		padB := int(math.Ceil(math.Max(0, maxY-float64(p.sh))))
209		even := func(n int) int { return n + n%2 }
210		p.padW = even(p.sw + p.padL + padR)
211		p.padH = even(p.sh + p.padT + padB)
212		// the box: the union of every rectangle, grown to the output's aspect so
213		// the moving window inside it never distorts
214		bx, by := minX+float64(p.padL), minY+float64(p.padT)
215		bw, bh := maxX-minX, maxY-minY
216		if bw/bh < outA {
217			grow := bh*outA - bw
218			bx -= grow / 2
219			bw += grow
220		} else if bw/outA > bh {
221			grow := bw/outA - bh
222			by -= grow / 2
223			bh += grow
224		}
225		p.boxW, p.boxH = even(int(math.Ceil(bw))), even(int(math.Ceil(bh)))
226		p.boxX = int(math.Round(bx))
227		p.boxY = int(math.Round(by))
228		// the grown box may poke out of the padded frame; slide it back in, and
229		// pad more if it is simply bigger
230		if p.boxW > p.padW {
231			p.padW = even(p.boxW)
232		}
233		if p.boxH > p.padH {
234			p.padH = even(p.boxH)
235		}
236		p.boxX = int(math.Max(0, math.Min(float64(p.boxX), float64(p.padW-p.boxW))))
237		p.boxY = int(math.Max(0, math.Min(float64(p.boxY), float64(p.padH-p.boxH))))
238	}
239	
240	// pieceExpr is a piecewise-linear function of in_time as an ffmpeg
241	// expression: nested ifs, one segment per interval, clamped flat past either
242	// end. vs[i] is the value at ts[i].
243	func pieceExpr(ts, vs []float64) string {
244		if len(ts) == 0 {
245			return "0"
246		}
247		expr := fmt.Sprintf("%.4f", vs[len(vs)-1]) // past the end: the last value
248		for i := len(ts) - 2; i >= 0; i-- {
249			t0, t1, v0, v1 := ts[i], ts[i+1], vs[i], vs[i+1]
250			var seg string
251			if t1-t0 < 1e-4 || v0 == v1 {
252				seg = fmt.Sprintf("%.4f", v1)
253			} else {
254				seg = fmt.Sprintf("%.4f+%.4f*clip((it-%.4f)/%.4f\\,0\\,1)",
255					v0, v1-v0, t0, t1-t0)
256			}
257			expr = fmt.Sprintf("if(lt(it\\,%.4f)\\,%s\\,%s)", t1, seg, expr)
258		}
259		return expr
260	}
261	
262	// padBox is the border the camera needs around the recording: the padded
263	// frame's size and where the recording sits in it. encodeClip fills it
264	// (bdrop); every crop and zoompan expression below is measured on the padded
265	// frame. ok is false when the camera never looks past the edge.
266	func (p *camPath) padBox() (w, h, l, t int, ok bool) {
267		if p.padW == p.sw && p.padH == p.sh {
268			return 0, 0, 0, 0, false
269		}
270		return p.padW, p.padH, p.padL, p.padT, true
271	}
272	
273	// chain is the filter steps that realize the camera: pad and crop (skipped
274	// when no-ops), then a plain scale for a still camera or zoompan with the
275	// journey in its expressions. padded says the caller already put the recording
276	// on a padded frame (encodeClip, for the blurred border).
277	func (p *camPath) chain() []string { return p.chainOn(false) }
278	
279	func (p *camPath) chainOn(padded bool) []string {
280		outA := float64(p.outW) / float64(p.outH)
281		var vf []string
282		if _, _, _, _, ok := p.padBox(); ok && !padded {
283			vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("pad=%d:%d:%d:%d:color=black",
284				p.padW, p.padH, p.padL, p.padT))
285		}
286		if p.static() {
287			// one rectangle for the whole clip: crop it and scale it, exactly
288			x, y, w, h := p.rectPx(p.r[0], outA)
289			even := func(v float64) int { n := int(math.Round(v)); return n - n%2 }
290			cw, ch := even(w), even(h)
291			cx := int(math.Round(x)) + p.padL
292			cy := int(math.Round(y)) + p.padT
293			cx = int(math.Max(0, math.Min(float64(cx), float64(p.padW-cw))))
294			cy = int(math.Max(0, math.Min(float64(cy), float64(p.padH-ch))))
295			vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("crop=%d:%d:%d:%d", cw, ch, cx, cy),
296				fmt.Sprintf("scale=%d:%d", p.outW, p.outH))
297			return vf
298		}
299		if p.boxW != p.padW || p.boxH != p.padH {
300			vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("crop=%d:%d:%d:%d", p.boxW, p.boxH, p.boxX, p.boxY))
301		}
302		// the moving window: zoom is how many times the box's height the window
303		// is, position is the rectangle's corner. All three are driven by the
304		// same piecewise-linear samples, so what the window does between two
305		// breakpoints is precisely what the preview overlay drew.
306		n := len(p.ts)
307		hs, xs, ys := make([]float64, n), make([]float64, n), make([]float64, n)
308		for i, r := range p.r {
309			x, y, w, h := p.rectPx(r, outA)
310			_ = w
311			hs[i] = h
312			xs[i] = x + float64(p.padL) - float64(p.boxX)
313			ys[i] = y + float64(p.padT) - float64(p.boxY)
314		}
315		fps := p.fps
316		if fps <= 0 {
317			fps = 30
318		}
319		vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf(
320			"zoompan=z='%d/(%s)':x='%s':y='%s':d=1:s=%dx%d:fps=%g",
321			p.boxH, pieceExpr(p.ts, hs), pieceExpr(p.ts, xs), pieceExpr(p.ts, ys),
322			p.outW, p.outH, fps))
323		return vf
324	}
325	
326	// maxZoom is the deepest the moving window goes, box heights per window
327	// height. zoompan clamps at 10; past that the render comes out shallower
328	// than the preview promised, which is worth a line in the log.
329	func (p *camPath) maxZoom() float64 {
330		z := 1.0
331		for _, r := range p.r {
332			if h := r.hf * float64(p.sh); h > 0 {
333				z = math.Max(z, float64(p.boxH)/h)
334			}
335		}
336		return z
337	}

339	// outBox is the frame size every clip comes out at: the footage's own shape
340	// (clipBox) until an aspect is chosen, and then the settings' tier -- or the
341	// footage's own height -- inside that aspect (tierBox).
342	func outBox(clips []prodClip, st prodSettings, aspect string) (int, int) {
343		a := parseAspect(aspect)
344		if a <= 0 {
345			return clipBox(clips, st)
346		}
347		h0 := 0
348		if st.Height <= 0 {
349			for _, c := range clips {
350				if c.video == nil {
351					continue
352				}
353				if _, fh, err := ffprobeSize(c.video.path); err == nil {
354					h0 = fh
355					break
356				}
357			}
358		}
359		return tierBox(a, h0, st.Height)
360	}
361	
362	// tierBox is the frame a chosen aspect comes out at. The tier names the SHORT
363	// side: "1080p" on a 9:16 cut is 1080×1920. With no tier the footage's height
364	// names the frame's. Both sides rounded even for yuv420. Pure, so the Produce
365	// info line can say the frame without opening a file.
366	func tierBox(a float64, h0, height int) (int, int) {
367		if a < 1 && height > 0 {
368			w := height - height%2
369			return w, int(math.Round(float64(w)/a/2)) * 2
370		}
371		h := height
372		if h <= 0 {
373			h = h0
374		}
375		if h <= 0 {
376			h = 1080
377		}
378		h -= h % 2
379		return int(math.Round(float64(h)*a/2)) * 2, h
380	}
381	
382	// atempoChain is the audio counterpart of footage off its own clock: atempo
383	// holds the pitch, and the rates one instance of it will not take are reached
384	// by chaining. It refuses anything below 0.5, and old builds refuse above 2 --
385	// so both ends are walked in halves and doublings, which every build takes.
386	func atempoChain(rate float64) string {
387		if rate <= 0 || rate == 1 {
388			return ""
389		}
390		var parts []string
391		for rate < 0.5 {
392			parts = append(parts, "atempo=0.5")
393			rate *= 2
394		}
395		for rate > 2 {
396			parts = append(parts, "atempo=2")
397			rate /= 2
398		}
399		if rate != 1 {
400			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("atempo=%g", rate))
401		}
402		return "," + strings.Join(parts, ",")
403	}

1325	// cutLen, cutPos and cutAt are the session clock, the cut's own clock (only
1326	// what is kept -- the clock of the video that will be produced) and the
1327	// conversion between them. The seek bar is on the cut's clock, so the gaps
1328	// are simply not on it.
1329	func cutLen(segs []cutSeg) float64 {
1330		tot := 0.0
1331		for _, s := range segs {
1332			tot += math.Max(0, s.length())
1333		}
1334		return tot
1335	}
1336	
1337	// cutPos is a session time on the cut's clock: how much kept material comes
1338	// before it. A time in a gap -- the preview passes through them, briefly, on its
1339	// way to the next clip -- reads as the boundary it is about to reach, so the
1340	// handle waits at the join instead of jumping ahead of the picture.
1341	func cutPos(segs []cutSeg, t float64) float64 {
1342		acc := 0.0
1343		for _, s := range segs {
1344			if t <= s.S {
1345				return acc
1346			}
1347			if t < s.E {
1348				off := t - s.S
1349				if s.Rate > 0 {
1350					off /= s.Rate // slowed footage: a session second is 1/rate cut seconds
1351				}
1352				return acc + off
1353			}
1354			acc += math.Max(0, s.length())
1355		}
1356		return acc
1357	}
1358	
1359	// cutAt is the way back: a place on the cut's clock as a session time. Every
1360	// value the slider can hold maps into a clip, which is the point of the whole
1361	// exercise -- there is no such thing as dropping the handle on removed footage.
1362	func cutAt(segs []cutSeg, x float64) float64 {
1363		if len(segs) == 0 {
1364			return x
1365		}
1366		acc := 0.0
1367		for _, s := range segs {
1368			d := math.Max(0, s.length())
1369			if x < acc+d {
1370				if s.Dur > 0 {
1371					// a card runs for d, but it happens AT a point of the session:
1372					// there is no session time inside it to land on, only the
1373					// moment the footage is cut open for it
1374					return s.S
1375				}
1376				if s.Rate > 0 {
1377					// slowed footage: the bar's seconds cover 1/rate of the session's
1378					return s.S + math.Max(0, x-acc)*s.Rate
1379				}
1380				return s.S + math.Max(0, x-acc)
1381			}
1382			acc += d
1383		}
1384		// the far end of the bar is the cut's last frame, not the instant after it:
1385		// e.E is already the gap that follows, the same edge snapToCut backs off
1386		last := segs[len(segs)-1]
1387		return math.Max(last.S, last.E-cutEdge)
1388	}
