1570				d = t - end
1571			}
1572			// ties go to the later row: two lines on one clip meet at a shared
1573			// instant -- where the first one's stretch ends is where the second's
1574			// begins -- and at that instant the one about to be heard is the answer,
1575			// the same way entryAt hands the second its own window there.
1576			if d <= bestD {
1577				best, bestD = i, d
1578			}
1579		}
1580		return best
1581	}
1582	
1583	// voiceBusy reports that a narration line is sounding right now -- the state
1584	// the preview must not cut mid-word.
1585	func (n *narrator) voiceBusy() bool {
1586		return n.voice != nil && n.voice.playing && n.speaking >= 0
1587	}
1588	
1589	// selectRow moves the blue row to the line the playback is on, so the list
1590	// follows the sound. Selecting a row by hand seeks the preview -- that is what
1591	// clicking one is for -- so this programmatic move rides the building flag,
1592	// the same guard every rebuild-driven signal uses. No focus grab: the user may
1593	// be typing in another row's box, and the highlight must not steal the cursor.
1594	func (n *narrator) selectRow(i int) {
1595		if n.list == nil || i < 0 {
1596			return
1597		}
1598		row := n.list.RowAtIndex(i)
1599		if row == nil || row == n.list.SelectedRow() {
1600			return
1601		}
1602		was := n.building
1603		n.building = true
1604		n.list.SelectRow(row)
1605		n.building = was
1606	}
1607	
1608	// addLineAt inserts a line at a session time, the way a subtitle editor's
1609	// "add cue at playhead" does. The line belongs to the cut segment under t --
1610	// the cut is Cut's and stays respected: between clips there is nothing to
1611	// narrate, so the button reports that instead of inventing an interval. A clip
1612	// whose one entry is the empty "leave it alone" marker is not given a second
1613	// row; that entry IS the clip's line the moment it gets a placement and words.
1614	// Returns the index of the row to edit, or -1 with the reason set as status.
1615	func (n *narrator) addLineAt(t float64) int {
1616		segs := n.clips()
1617		si := -1
1618		for i, s := range segs {
1619			if t >= s.S && t < s.E {
1620				si = i
1621				break
1622			}
1623		}
1624		if si < 0 {
1625			n.a.setStatus("the playhead is between clips — the cut has nothing to narrate here")
1626			return -1
1627		}
1628		s := segs[si]
1629		at := math.Min(math.Max(0, t-s.S), math.Max(0, s.length()-1))
1630		// the clip's own entries, if any
1631		lo, hi := -1, -1
1632		for i, e := range n.entries {
1633			if math.Abs(e.S-s.S) <= 0.05 && math.Abs(e.E-s.E) <= 0.05 {
1634				if lo < 0 {
1635					lo = i
1636				}
1637				hi = i
1638			}
1639		}
1640		// a second can only hold one line. Where one already starts, the + is a
1641		// jump to it, not a duplicate; where one is still SPEAKING, there is no
1642		// room and the honest answer is where the room begins.
1643		for i := lo; lo >= 0 && i <= hi; i++ {
1644			e := n.entries[i]
1645			if math.Abs(e.At-at) < 1 {
1646				n.a.setStatus("a line already starts here — edit it, or move the playhead")
1647				return i
1648			}
1649			if end := e.At + n.speechDur(e); strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) != "" &&
1650				at > e.At && at < end+0.3 {
1651				n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("a line is speaking here until %s — add after it",
1652					fmtClock(s.S+end)))
1653				return -1
1654			}
1655		}
1656		if lo >= 0 && lo == hi && strings.TrimSpace(n.entries[lo].Text) == "" {
1657			n.entries[lo].At = at // the silent marker becomes the line
1658			n.save()
1659			n.rebuildRows()
1660			return lo
1661		}
1662		// insert in placement order among the clip's entries; a clip with none yet
1663		// gets its first, placed after whichever earlier clip's entries exist
1664		ins := len(n.entries)
1665		if lo >= 0 {
1666			ins = hi + 1
1667			for i := lo; i <= hi; i++ {
1668				if at < n.entries[i].At {
1669					ins = i
1670					break
1671				}
1672			}
1673		} else {
1674			for i, e := range n.entries {
1675				if e.S > s.S+0.05 {
1676					ins = i
1677					break
1678				}
1679			}
1680		}
1681		e := narrEntry{S: s.S, E: s.E, At: at}
1682		n.entries = append(n.entries[:ins], append([]narrEntry{e}, n.entries[ins:]...)...)
1683		n.save()
1684		n.rebuildRows()
1685		return ins
1686	}
1687	
1688	// addLineAfter is the row's own +: a line starting where this one's audio ends
1689	// plus a beat, which is the first second the playhead rule would allow anyway.
1690	func (n *narrator) addLineAfter(i int) int {
1691		if !n.has(i) {
1692			return -1
1693		}
1694		e := n.entries[i]
1695		at := e.At + 1.2 // a marker's "audio" is nothing: right after its start
1696		if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) != "" {
1697			at = e.At + n.speechDur(e) + 0.5
1698		}
1699		if at >= e.E-e.S-1 {
1700			n.a.setStatus("no room after this line — the clip ends first")
1701			return -1
1702		}
1703		return n.addLineAt(e.S + at)
1704	}
1705	
1706	// moveLine puts line i where the row's time field says. A time in another
1707	// clip is a move (the wav is keyed by words and delivery, so it costs
1708	// nothing); a time in a gap is clamped and said so. Returns true when the
1709	// line changed clips, so the caller re-sorts.
1710	func (n *narrator) moveLine(i int, t float64) bool {
1711		if !n.has(i) {
1712			return false
1713		}
1714		e := &n.entries[i]
1715		segs := n.clips()
1716		ci, _ := gapAt(segs, t)
1717		if ci < 0 {
1718			// keep it where it is, and name the clip it may live in -- "that time is
1719			// not in this line's clip" is the one thing the old silent clamp never
1720			// managed to say
1721			e.At = math.Min(math.Max(0, t-e.S), math.Max(0, e.E-e.S-1))
1722			n.save()
1723			n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s is outside the cut — this line stays in its clip (%s–%s), at %s",
1724				fmtClock(t), fmtClock(e.S), fmtClock(e.E), fmtClock(e.S+e.At)))
1725			return false
1726		}
1727		s := segs[ci]
1728		from := cutSeg{S: e.S, E: e.E} // the clip it may be leaving, for the note below
1729		moved := math.Abs(s.S-e.S) > 0.05 || math.Abs(s.E-e.E) > 0.05
1730		e.S, e.E = s.S, s.E
1731		// a line still may not start in the last second of its clip: there is no
1732		// room to speak, and everything downstream (lineWindow, the ⚠, the render's
1733		// spill) is written against that rule
1734		e.At = math.Min(math.Max(0, t-s.S), math.Max(0, s.length()-1))
1735		at := e.At // read before the caller's rebuild can move the entry
1736		// The clip the line just left is now empty and has to say so (silentFor), or
1737		// staleFor reads the hole as a clip the cut moved. Only when it was the last
1738		// line there, and only for a clip really in the cut -- an orphan (refitEntries)
1739		// leaves nothing.
1740		if moved && clipIndex(segs, from) >= 0 && !clipHasEntry(n.entries, from, i) {
1741			n.silent = markSilent(n.silent, from)
1742		}
1743		n.save()
1744		if moved {
1745			n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("moved this line to the clip at %s — it now starts at %s",
1746				fmtClock(s.S), fmtClock(s.S+at)))
1747		}
1748		return moved
1749	}
1750	
1751	// onClip, clipIndex and clipHasEntry are "the same clip" asked three ways. The
1752	// bounds are compared with a twentieth of a second of slack, the tolerance the
1753	// whole page uses for a line sitting on a clip: the numbers make the round trip
1754	// through JSON and through the cut editor's own arithmetic, and a line is on the
1755	// clip it was written for or it is not.
1756	func onClip(s cutSeg, S, E float64) bool {
1757		return math.Abs(s.S-S) <= 0.05 && math.Abs(s.E-E) <= 0.05
1758	}
1759	
1760	func clipIndex(segs []cutSeg, s cutSeg) int {
1761		for i, c := range segs {
1762			if onClip(c, s.S, s.E) {
1763				return i
1764			}
1765		}
1766		return -1
1767	}
1768	
1769	// silentFor, markSilent and pruneSilent record a clip emptied on purpose, so
1770	// staleFor (which reads coverage) does not have ▶ fill it back in. Kept by
1771	// bounds, not index: a clip that moves in Cut counts as uncovered again.
1772	func silentFor(silent []cutSeg, s cutSeg) bool {
1773		for _, q := range silent {
1774			if onClip(s, q.S, q.E) {
1775				return true
1776			}
1777		}
1778		return false
1779	}
1780	
1781	func markSilent(silent []cutSeg, s cutSeg) []cutSeg {
1782		if silentFor(silent, s) {
1783			return silent
1784		}
1785		return append(silent, cutSeg{S: s.S, E: s.E})
1786	}
1787	
1788	// pruneSilent drops the records for clips that have a line again, so a clip
1789	// re-narrated by hand is not carrying a note saying it is quiet.
1790	func pruneSilent(silent []cutSeg, entries []narrEntry) []cutSeg {
1791		out := silent[:0]
1792		for _, q := range silent {
1793			if !clipHasEntry(entries, q, -1) {
1794				out = append(out, q)
1795			}
1796		}
1797		if len(out) == 0 {
1798			return nil
1799		}
1800		return out
1801	}
1802	
1803	// clipHasEntry is "does this clip still have a line on it", skipping one row --
1804	// the one being moved or deleted, which is on its way off the clip.
1805	func clipHasEntry(entries []narrEntry, s cutSeg, skip int) bool {
1806		for j, o := range entries {
1807			if j != skip && onClip(s, o.S, o.E) {
1808				return true
1809			}
1810		}
1811		return false
1812	}
1813	
1814	// focusLine puts a row under the user's fingers: selected, cursor in the box.
1815	func (n *narrator) focusLine(i int) {
1816		if i < 0 {
1817			return
1818		}
1819		n.selectRow(i)
1820		if i < len(n.rows) {
1821			n.rows[i].text.GrabFocus()
1822		}
1823	}
1824	
1825	// addLineClicked is the button behind addLineAt: pause, place, select, and put
1826	// the cursor in the new box so the next thing typed is the line's words.
1827	func (a *App) addLineClicked() {
1828		n := a.narr
1829		if n == nil {
1830			return
1831		}
1832		if n.player != nil && n.player.playing {
1833			n.player.Pause() // a line is placed on a moment, not on a moving target
1834			if n.voice != nil {
1835				n.voice.Pause()
1836			}
1837		}
1838		n.pullRows()
1839		i := n.addLineAt(n.pos)
1840		n.focusLine(i)
1841	}
1842	
1843	// deleteLine removes a row -- all of it, including the last one on a clip.
1844	//
1845	// It used to turn that last one into the empty "this clip plays its own audio"
1846	// marker instead, so the trash on such a row cleared the words and left the row
1847	// sitting there, and pressing it again did nothing at all. A button that does
1848	// not remove the thing it is pointed at is worse than no button. What the
1849	// marker was protecting is staleFor, which read a clip with no entry as a clip
1850	// that had MOVED and made the next run rewrite narration nobody touched; that
1851	// is fixed where it belongs, in staleFor.
1852	//
1853	// The clip then has no row on the page. That is what removing its only line
1854	// means, and the status says how to get one back.
1855	func (n *narrator) deleteLine(i int) {
1856		if !n.has(i) {
1857			return
1858		}
1859		// the indices the playback state holds are about to shift; the picture may
1860		// keep rolling, but a voice mid-line might be the very line being deleted
1861		if n.voice != nil && n.voice.playing {
1862			n.voice.Pause()
1863		}
1864		n.playSeg, n.speaking, n.solo = -1, -1, -1
1865		e := n.entries[i]
1866		clip := cutSeg{S: e.S, E: e.E}
1867		n.entries = append(n.entries[:i], n.entries[i+1:]...)
1868		if clipHasEntry(n.entries, clip, -1) {
1869			n.a.setStatus("line removed")
1870		} else {
1871			n.silent = markSilent(n.silent, clip)
1872			n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("line removed — the clip at %s plays its own audio", fmtClock(e.S)))
1873		}
1874		n.save()
1875		n.rebuildRows()
1876		n.updateOut()
1877	}
1878	
1879	// fmtClock and parseClock are the row's time field: session seconds as
1880	// "mm:ss.d" out, and back in as "mm:ss", "mm:ss.5", "h:mm:ss" or plain
1881	// seconds -- whatever the user reaches for.
1882	func fmtClock(t float64) string {
1883		if t < 0 {
1884			t = 0
1885		}
1886		return fmt.Sprintf("%02d:%04.1f", int(t)/60, t-float64(int(t)/60*60))
1887	}
1888	
1889	// cleanClock strips everything a clock cannot contain, so the field corrects
1890	// itself as it is typed instead of complaining afterwards.
1891	func cleanClock(s string) string {
1892		var b strings.Builder
1893		for _, r := range s {
1894			if (r >= '0' && r <= '9') || r == ':' || r == '.' {
1895				b.WriteRune(r)
1896			}
1897		}
1898		return b.String()
1899	}
1900	
1901	func parseClock(s string) (float64, bool) {
1902		parts := strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(s), ":")
1903		if len(parts) > 3 {
1904			return 0, false
1905		}
1906		t := 0.0
1907		for _, p := range parts {
1908			v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(p), 64)
1909			if err != nil || v < 0 {
1910				return 0, false
1911			}
1912			t = t*60 + v
1913		}
1914		return t, true
1915	}
1916	
1917	// sortEntries keeps the list in playing order -- by clip, then by placement --
1918	// which everything downstream leans on: entryAt bounds a line's window by the
1919	// NEXT entry, lineWindow reads its sibling at i+1, and the rows read top to
1920	// bottom the way the video plays. A hand-edited time can break the order; a
1921	// rebuild restores it.
1922	func (n *narrator) sortEntries() {
1923		sort.SliceStable(n.entries, func(a, b int) bool {
1924			if n.entries[a].S != n.entries[b].S {
1925				return n.entries[a].S < n.entries[b].S
1926			}
1927			return n.entries[a].At < n.entries[b].At
1928		})
1929	}
1930	
1931	// nextSpoken is the line whose arrival ends line i's time:
1932	// the next on the same clip with words, using onClip's slack rather than
1933	// exact equality, so entryAt and lineEnd cannot disagree.
1934	func (n *narrator) nextSpoken(i int) int {
1935		if i+1 < len(n.entries) && math.Abs(n.entries[i+1].S-n.entries[i].S) <= 0.05 &&
1936			strings.TrimSpace(n.entries[i+1].Text) != "" {
1937			return i + 1
1938		}
1939		return -1
1940	}
1941	
1942	// lineEnd is where line i's slot closes on the session clock: the same clip's
1943	// next line, or the clip's end -- without the render's growth, which is the
1944	// mix's spill room.
1945	func (n *narrator) lineEnd(i int) float64 {
1946		if j := n.nextSpoken(i); j >= 0 {
1947			return n.entries[i].S + n.entries[j].At
1948		}
1949		return n.entries[i].E
1950	}
1951	
1952	// clipTop is whether row i is the first line written for its clip -- the row
1953	// the whole clip's schedule hangs off, and the one a warning about the clip
1954	// belongs on.
1955	func (n *narrator) clipTop(i int) bool {
1956		return i == 0 || math.Abs(n.entries[i].S-n.entries[i-1].S) > 0.05
1957	}
1958	
1959	// clipLines is a clip's rows in the shape the render packs them: every line
1960	// written for the same stretch, at the moment it was placed and as long as it
1961	// takes to say. Wordless rows are left out for the same reason the render
1962	// leaves them out -- there is nothing to speak, so there is nothing to fit.
1963	func (n *narrator) clipLines(top int) []prodLine {
1964		var out []prodLine
1965		for i := top; i < len(n.entries) && (i == top || !n.clipTop(i)); i++ {
1966			if e := n.entries[i]; strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) != "" {
1967				out = append(out, prodLine{at: e.At, dur: n.speechDur(e)})
1968			}
1969		}
1970		return out
1971	}
1972	
1973	// clipOverrun is how far a clip's narration runs past its end after packLines
1974	// and maxExtend -- the render's own arithmetic, asked here. Cumulative: a long
1975	// first line pushes every later one, and it is the last that falls off. The
1976	// footage bound is deliberately not applied (a fact about the file).
1977	func (n *narrator) clipOverrun(top int) float64 {
1978		lines := n.clipLines(top)
1979		if len(lines) == 0 {
1980			return 0
1981		}
1982		e := n.entries[top]
1983		return math.Max(0, narrRun(lines, 1)-(e.E-e.S)-maxExtend)
1984	}
1985	
1986	// clipSlack is how much earlier the render may slide a clip's whole schedule
1987	// before it has to start speeding the words up instead: the first line's
1988	// placement, down to the lead-in, and no further.
1989	func (n *narrator) clipSlack(top int) float64 {
1990		lines := n.clipLines(top)
1991		if len(lines) == 0 {
1992			return 0
1993		}
1994		packLines(lines, 1)
1995		return math.Max(0, lines[0].delay-narrLead)
1996	}
1997	
1998	// lineWindow is how long line i may speak: until the same clip's next line
1999	// starts, or -- for a clip's last line -- to the clip's end plus the growth
2000	// the render allows it (maxExtend). It is the number the ⚠ compares against.
2001	func (n *narrator) lineWindow(i int) float64 {
2002		e := n.entries[i]
2003		if j := n.nextSpoken(i); j >= 0 {
2004			return n.entries[j].At - e.At
2005		}
2006		return (e.E - e.S) - e.At + maxExtend
2007	}
2008	
2009	// speechRate is how much text this TTS gets through in a second, counted in
2010	// characters. Words are the wrong unit: "a second a word" -- what this used to
2011	// guess -- read a ten-word line as ten seconds when it speaks in three, which
2012	// is not a near miss but a ⚠ on a line that fits fine. Characters take word
2013	// length and punctuation with them, and 15 a second is the 2.5 words a second
2014	// narrBudget already hands out, so the estimate and the budget finally agree.
2015	const speechRate = 15.0
2016	
2017	// rateBounds is how far a measured rate is allowed to move the estimate. A
2018	// wav that failed halfway, or one line of "Go!" padded with silence, would
2019	// otherwise teach the page a speaking rate nobody speaks at.
2020	const (
2021		rateMin = 8.0
2022		rateMax = 28.0
2023	)
2024	
2025	// measured is the take's real length, or 0 if not yet measured. Probed once
2026	// per wav, off the GTK thread (this is asked on every rebuild and tick, and an
2027	// ffprobe is a process); speechDur stands in until the answer lands and
2028	// rebuilds the rows.
2029	func (n *narrator) measured(e narrEntry) float64 {
2030		wav := n.a.ttsWav(e)
2031		if d, ok := n.durCache[wav]; ok {
2032			return d
2033		}
2034		// headless (tests) has no idle loop for the answer to land on; a probe
2035		// already in flight needs no second one; a take not yet spoken has
2036		// nothing to measure. A probe that failed is none of these: it stays
2037		// unmarked and is simply tried again when next asked, exactly as the
2038		// synchronous version retried -- the wav may still have been being
2039		// written when the first probe read it.
2040		if n.durCache == nil || n.durProbe == nil || n.durProbe[wav] || !exists(wav) {
2041			return 0
2042		}
2043		n.durProbe[wav] = true
2044		go func() {
2045			d, err := ffprobeDur(wav)
2046			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
2047				delete(n.durProbe, wav)
2048				if err != nil {
2049					return
2050				}
2051				n.durCache[wav] = d
2052				n.queueRebuild() // the (~) rows re-measure against the real length
2053			})
2054		}()
2055		return 0
2056	}
2057	
2058	// spokenRate is speechRate corrected by this narration's own takes. Every
2059	// voice, language and emotion speaks at its own pace, and the lines already in
2060	// the cache measure it exactly -- so once a few are spoken, the lines that are
2061	// not stop being estimated against a stranger's rate.
2062	func (n *narrator) spokenRate() float64 {
2063		chars, secs := 0, 0.0
2064		for _, e := range n.entries {
2065			t := strings.TrimSpace(e.Text)
2066			if t == "" {
2067				continue
2068			}
2069			if d := n.measured(e); d > 0 {
2070				chars += len([]rune(t))
2071				secs += d
2072			}
2073		}
2074		if secs < 3 || chars < 60 { // too little spoken to learn anything from
2075			return speechRate
2076		}
2077		return math.Min(rateMax, math.Max(rateMin, float64(chars)/secs))
2078	}
2079	
2080	// speechDur is how long the line takes to say: the synthesized wav when there
2081	// is one, and the text divided by the rate until then.
2082	func (n *narrator) speechDur(e narrEntry) float64 {
2083		if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) == "" {
2084			return 0
2085		}
2086		if d := n.measured(e); d > 0 {
2087			return d
2088		}
2089		return float64(len([]rune(strings.TrimSpace(e.Text)))) / n.spokenRate()
2090	}
2091	
2092	// updateInputs is the row this page now opens with, the same question Inputs,
2093	// Describe and Cut answer at the top of theirs: what is the narration run
2094	// actually sent? Every one of these comes from somewhere else -- the clips from
2095	// Cut, the words from Describe's transcript, the context box from Describe.
2096	// A narration written against a cut you have since changed reads exactly
2097	// like one written against the current cut, and this line is the difference.
2098	func (n *narrator) updateInputs() {

36		type line struct {

38			Text string

// ---- run --------------------------------------------------------------------

// prepRun validates the sources and starts the whole step: transcripts and
// frames, then describing and fixing, in one press. No describe-only or
// fix-only run: describe resumes per chunk, and half of what the fixer is for
// is the events the describer just wrote.
func (a *App) prepRun() {
	if a.running {
		return
	}
	// one source is enough: a session can be a single screen recording that is
	// both the footage and every voice on it, and it can equally be a recording
	// with no footage at all
	vids, auds := a.snapSources()
	if len(vids)+len(auds) == 0 {
		a.setStatus("add at least one source")
		return
	}
	// two sources of the same name would write into one folder under inputs/,
	// and the second would quietly overwrite the first's transcript
	if x, y := a.srcList.clash(); x != "" {
		a.logf("!!! %s and %s are both inputs/%s -- rename one", x, y, baseName(x))
		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s and %s have the same name — rename one",
			filepath.Base(x), filepath.Base(y)))
		return
	}
	// The working copy always reflects what actually ran -- and so does the
	// named project, since saveProjectNow writes every target. It used to be
	// saveProjectTo(project.json), which also RENAMED the open project to the
	// working copy: running the step quietly stopped the autosave following the
	// file you had opened, and the header bar changed under you to say so.
	a.saveProjectNow()
	// ⏹ then ▶ is "do it again", not "carry on" -- and this is the moment to
	// act on that rather than the stop itself: pressing ⏹ has to be safe to do
	// at the end of the day, with the half-run still on disk in the morning.
	// It is the press that starts the work over that throws the work away.
	if err := a.undFreshStart(); err != nil {
		// nothing here is worth refusing to run over: say what could not be
		// cleared, and let the run pick up from what is still on disk
		a.logf(">>> could not clear the last run (%v) -- resuming it", err)
	}
	scaleName, scaleVF := a.frameScale()
	a.startPrep(vids, auds, a.frameInterval(), scaleName, scaleVF)
}

// undFreshStart is the difference between ⏸ and ⏹: paused resumes, stopped
// restarts the describing from the beginning, dropping the event logs it
// resumes from. Transcripts and frames are per-file on disk and untouched; the
// fixer never resumed anyway. Only armed by a ⏹ that had reached the
// describing.
func (a *App) undFreshStart() error {
	if !a.undRestart {
		return nil
	}
	a.undRestart = false
	return a.resetDescribe()
}

func (a *App) startPrep(videos, audios []string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF string) {
	a.startRun()
	a.prog(trackSTT, 0, "preparing")
	a.logExp.SetExpanded(true)
	// what went in, by name -- the page has room for a count and nothing more
	a.logf(">>> prepare: %d input files", len(videos)+len(audios))
====
// prepSepShare is the slice of that first third the voice splitting takes when
// there is any to do. A third of it: the separation is one model pass over the
// audio and the transcripts are two, over the same audio, plus every frame.
const prepSepShare = 0.1

// prepare is the whole press: the transcripts and the frames, then the
// describing and the fixing. It reports whether the second half had begun,
// which is what a ⏹ needs to know -- that is the half a restart throws away.
//
// Neither half knows the other exists: each still divides its own work into two
// tracks that add up to a whole bar. qPhase is what puts each of them in its
// own slice of it, so the needle crosses the middle once and never goes back.
func (a *App) prepare(videos, audios []string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF string) (bool, error) {
	// the models are the server's to load, but that it HAS them is worth
	// finding out now rather than after the frame extraction -- and before the
	// separation too, since that is the phase this step now opens with and the
	// one asking for the model a server is least likely to have.
	sep := len(a.sepWanted()) > 0
	if err := a.ensureAudioModels(sep); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	// the splitting goes first, because it changes what the rest of this is OF:
	// a recording being split is not the file the frames come out of or the
	// transcript is of -- the two files it becomes are. With nothing flagged
	// this phase costs nothing and the two below are the two there always were.
	sepAt := 0.0
	if sep {
		a.qPhase(0, prepSepShare)
		var err error
		if videos, audios, err = a.separateVoices(videos, audios); err != nil {
			return false, err
		}
		sepAt = prepSepShare
	}
	a.qPhase(sepAt, prepInputsShare-sepAt)
	if err := a.ingest(videos, audios, interval, scaleName, scaleVF); err != nil {
		return false, err
	}
	a.qPhase(prepInputsShare, 1-prepInputsShare)
	return true, a.understand(videos, audios)
}

8		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/cairo"
9	)
10	
11	// Clear empties the cut -- kept stretches and effects, including proposed ones
12	// -- and leaves the session alone: sources, rows, clock corrections, cut lanes.
13	// One undo step for the lot.
14	
15	// clearCut empties the cut. Nothing at all to clear is not an edit and says so
16	// rather than leaving an undo step that undoes nothing.
17	func (ed *cutEditor) clearCut() {
18		if len(ed.segs) == 0 && len(ed.fx) == 0 {
19			ed.a.setStatus("nothing to clear — the timeline holds no cut yet")
20			return
21		}
22		segs, fx := len(ed.segs), len(ed.fx)
23		ed.pushUndo()
24		ed.segs, ed.fx = nil, nil
25		// every hold is an index into a list that is now empty, and the selection
26		// is a span over footage the cut no longer keeps
27		ed.dropSeg()
28		ed.dropEdge()
29		ed.dropFx()
30		ed.dropSel()
31		ed.sel.active = false
32		ed.clearMarks()
33		ed.persist()
34		ed.syncSelBtns()
35		ed.redrawTracks()
36		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("cleared %s and %s", plural(segs, "scene"), plural(fx, "effect")))
37	}
38	
39	// － Remove is the SELECTION's verb and nothing else's: it cuts a hole in a kept
40	// scene, which the ✕ on a bar cannot (there is no scene to press for a span that
41	// makes two). No selection, a sound-scoped selection, or nothing kept under it:
42	// it says so instead of guessing. Greyed under the same rule as ＋ Add.
43	
44	// spanTouches reports whether removing t0..t1 would change the cut at all.
45	//
46	// It is the same test removeSpan makes on each segment, asked ahead of time:
47	// anything with a positive overlap is trimmed, split or (an insert) dropped
48	// whole, and anything else is copied across untouched. So a false here means
49	// the press would be a no-op, which is the one thing the status line must not
50	// call a removal.
51	func (ed *cutEditor) spanTouches(t0, t1 float64) bool {
52		if t1 < t0 {
53			t0, t1 = t1, t0
54		}
55		for _, s := range ed.segs {
56			if s.E > t0 && s.S < t1 {
57				return true
58			}
59		}
60		return false
61	}
62	
63	// removeSelRange is － Remove: the selected stretch comes out of the cut.
64	func (a *App) removeSelRange() {
65		ed := a.ed
66		// the band, not its numbers: sel.t0/t1 keep whatever the last drag left in
67		// them after the band comes down, so a press with nothing selected would
68		// otherwise cut a hole where a selection USED to be. (＋ Add asks for
69		// footage as well as a band; this one does not need to -- it edits the cut,
70		// and a cut with scenes in it is one there is something to remove from.)
71		if !ed.sel.active {
72			a.setStatus("drag a region on a track first")
73			return
74		}
75		// the mirror of ＋ Add's guard, in the same words: both buttons act on
76		// footage, and a selection pointed at a waveform is not about footage. The
77		// button is greyed for this; the guard is for every other way in.
78		if ed.sel.aud != "" {
79			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("－ Remove drops footage — the selection is %s's sound", ed.sel.aud))
80			return
81		}
82		if !ed.spanTouches(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1) {
83			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("nothing to remove: the cut keeps nothing between %s and %s",
84				mmss(math.Min(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1)), mmss(math.Max(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1))))
85			return
86		}
87		// measured on the finished video's clock, not on the session's: a stretch
88		// under a ×2 is half as many seconds of video as it is of footage, and
89		// "removed 20 s" over a video that got 10 s shorter is the number nobody
90		// can check against the total under the tracks (cutLen).
91		before, was := len(ed.segs), ed.cutLen()
92		ed.pushUndo()
93		ed.removeRange(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1)
94		ed.sel.active = false
95		ed.clearMarks()
96		a.setStatus(removedMsg(was-ed.cutLen(), before, len(ed.segs)))
97	}
98	
99	// removedMsg is what the line says afterwards.
100	//
101	// The scene count going UP is the whole point of this button and reads as a
102	// mistake unless it is named -- "2 scenes, was 1" over a press that REMOVED
103	// something is a sentence that has to be worked out. So the split says what
104	// happened in words, and everything else says the count.
105	func removedMsg(gone float64, before, after int) string {
106		if after > before {
107			return fmt.Sprintf("removed %.1f s — the scene it went through is two now "+
108				"(↶ Undo takes it back)", gone)
109		}
110		return fmt.Sprintf("removed %.1f s — %d scene(s), was %d (↶ Undo takes it back)",
111			gone, after, before)
112	}
113	
114	// Dropping a scene: the ✕ on the green bar in the selection row (bandKillAt),
115	// which stands for the clip in hand or under the red line. ⌦ still removes
116	// whatever is in hand. drawKillBadge is the one recipe every ✕ on the page
117	// wears -- bar, cut lane, emptied row, effect.
118	
119	const (
120		segKillR   = 4.0  // the arms of the ✕, from its centre
121		segKillPad = 3.0  // the plate's edge, beyond the arms
122		segKillHit = 10.0 // and the target, which is bigger than either
123		segKillTop = 11.0 // its centre, down from the top of the picture band
124		// ...and in from the edge it sits against, ONE number for every ✕. Every such
125		// edge can be grabbed within edgeGrab px, so the badge's target begins exactly
126		// where the grab stops -- otherwise "a bit shorter" finds "gone". Same rule as
127		// the speaker badges (hearIn).
128		killIn = edgeGrab + segKillHit
129		// ...for a badge drawn against an edge. Plated ✕ sit in the MIDDLE of what
130		// they remove (drawSelBand, fxKillCentre) since the ends are grips; killMin is
131		// the floor under which there is no middle to spare and no ✕ is drawn.
132		killMin = 2 * killIn
133	)
134	
135	// drawKillBadge paints one ✕ centred on cx,cy: a plate, then the arms.
136	//
137	// A plate under the mark, always: two white strokes laid straight onto a
138	// thumbnail are legible over a dark frame and invisible over a bright one, and
139	// a control that disappears on half the footage is not a control. Red only
140	// under the pointer -- a row of red buttons standing open over the cut reads
141	// as damage already done.
142	func drawKillBadge(cr *cairo.Context, cx, cy float64, hot bool) {
143		if hot {
144			plate(cr, cx, cy, segKillR+segKillPad, 0.85, 0.24, 0.28, 0.95)
145		} else {
146			plate(cr, cx, cy, segKillR+segKillPad, 0.06, 0.06, 0.07, 0.55)
147		}
148		cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.9)
149		cr.SetLineWidth(1.6)
150		for _, d := range [][2]float64{{-1, -1}, {-1, 1}} {
151			cr.MoveTo(cx+segKillR*d[0], cy+segKillR*d[1])
152			cr.LineTo(cx-segKillR*d[0], cy-segKillR*d[1])
153		}
154		cr.Stroke()
155	}
156	
157	// killSeg drops scene i. It is removeSelClicked's own arithmetic with the
158	// guessing taken out: the scene is named by the press, so there is no held
159	// clip and no playhead to consult.
160	func (ed *cutEditor) killSeg(i int) {
161		if i < 0 || i >= len(ed.segs) {
162			return
163		}
164		s := ed.segs[i]
165		ed.pushUndo()
166		ed.segs = append(ed.segs[:i], ed.segs[i+1:]...)
167		// whatever was in hand was holding an index, and the indices have moved
168		ed.dropSeg()
169		ed.dropEdge()
170		ed.bandKillHov = -1 // the indices moved; whatever was lit is not that clip now
171		ed.persist()
172		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("removed the scene at %s (%s) — ↶ Undo takes it back",
173			mmss(s.S), ed.spanSecs(s.S, s.E)))
174		ed.redrawTracks()
175	}
176	
177	// | Split cuts the span free of the scene it lies in: nothing is removed,
178	// nothing moves, the render shows the same frames. The border is DELIBERATE and
179	// stored (cutSeg.Split), because coalesce would otherwise merge two touching
180	// clips of one camera on the next edit. Only mergeDropped clears it.
181	
182	// splitSelRange is the button: a border at each end of the selection. Same
183	// guards as － Remove, plus its own no-op case: a selection in a gap, or whose
184	// ends fall on existing borders, says why nothing changed.
185	func (a *App) splitSelRange() {
186		ed := a.ed
187		if !ed.sel.active {
188			// no band drawn: the red line is the border. A clip in hand and a
189			// press on Split is a razor, which is what the button looks like it
190			// is -- and refusing because no REGION was drawn is the page insisting
191			// on a gesture for a cut that needs one number, not two.
192			a.splitAtLine()
193			return
194		}
195		if ed.sel.aud != "" {
196			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("| Split cuts footage — the selection is %s's sound", ed.sel.aud))
197			return
198		}
199		t0, t1 := math.Min(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1), math.Max(ed.sel.t0, ed.sel.t1)
200		if !ed.spanTouches(t0, t1) {
201			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("nothing to split: the cut keeps nothing between %s and %s",
202				mmss(t0), mmss(t1)))
203			return
204		}
205		// asked before the undo entry is pushed: a press that draws no border must
206		// not leave a step in the history that undoes nothing
207		if ed.splitIdx(t0) < 0 && ed.splitIdx(t1) < 0 {
208			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("nothing to split at %s – %s", mmss(t0), mmss(t1)))
209			return
210		}
211		before := len(ed.segs)
212		ed.pushUndo()
213		// the LATER border first: splitting at t0 renumbers everything after it,
214		// and a search for t1 that runs before any of that happens is one fewer
215		// thing to be right about.
216		//
217		// The borders that were actually drawn are what the status names, and a
218		// selection with one end already on a border draws one: "split at 1:20 and
219		// 1:45" over a single cut is a sentence the page can be caught out on.
220		var at []string
221		if ed.splitBorder(t1) {
222			at = append(at, mmss(t1))
223		}
224		if ed.splitBorder(t0) {
225			at = append([]string{mmss(t0)}, at...)
226		}
227		ed.persist()
228		ed.redrawTracks()
229		// the selection stays up. It is exactly the scene that was just made, and
230		// the reason for making one is nearly always the next press -- ⧉ Copy, a
231		// camera, a lane switched off -- which wants that span still in hand.
232		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("split at %s — %d scenes, was %d", strings.Join(at, " and "), len(ed.segs), before))
233		ed.syncSelBtns()
234	}
235	
236	// splitAtLine is | Split with nothing selected: one border, where the red line
237	// is. The selection's version draws two because a region has two ends; this
238	// draws the one the line names, which is how a razor works everywhere else and
239	// what a hand that has just put the line somewhere is asking for.
240	func (a *App) splitAtLine() {
241		ed := a.ed
242		if !ed.hasPlay {
243			a.setStatus("| Split cuts at the red line — click a track to put it somewhere")
244			return
245		}
246		t := ed.playhead
247		if ed.splitIdx(t) < 0 {
248			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("nothing to split at %s", mmss(t)))
249			return
250		}
251		before := len(ed.segs)
252		ed.pushUndo()
253		ed.splitBorder(t)
254		ed.persist()
255		ed.redrawTracks()
256		// the right-hand half in hand, outlined: two scenes that touch are one
257		// stretch of green with one more line drawn on it, and the white outline
258		// is what says a press just made a scene rather than doing nothing
259		if i := ed.segAt(t); i >= 0 {
260			ed.segOn, ed.segSel, ed.segDirty = true, i, false
261			ed.edgeOn, ed.fxOn = false, false
262		}
263		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("split at %s — %d scenes, was %d", mmss(t), len(ed.segs), before))
264		ed.syncSelBtns()
265	}
266	
267	// splitBorder cuts the footage at t in two and says whether it did. Only
268	// inside a clip and only where both halves clear minPieceLn; inserts are passed
269	// over. The right-hand half carries the flag: it is the clip whose START is
270	// the new border (coalesce).
271	func (ed *cutEditor) splitBorder(t float64) bool {
272		i := ed.splitIdx(t)
273		if i < 0 {
274			return false
275		}
276		right := ed.segs[i] // every other field goes to both halves: same camera,
277		right.S = t         // same silenced lanes -- it is the same footage
278		right.Split = true
279		ed.segs[i].E = t
280		ed.segs = append(ed.segs, cutSeg{})
281		copy(ed.segs[i+2:], ed.segs[i+1:]) // memmove: the tail shifts right by one
282		ed.segs[i+1] = right
283		// the halves are new items in the list, and whatever was held is an index
284		// into the old one
285		ed.dropSeg()
286		ed.dropEdge()
287		return true
288	}
289	
290	// splitIdx is the clip a border at t would cut, or -1: the question splitBorder
291	// acts on and splitSelRange asks first, so the refusal and the edit cannot
292	// drift apart.
293	func (ed *cutEditor) splitIdx(t float64) int {
294		for i := range ed.segs {
295			s := ed.segs[i]
296			// the same floor a removal leaves (minPieceLn), not the second it takes
297			// to be worth SUGGESTING a scene: cutting a border half a second into a
298			// clip is a thing a hand means, and refusing it silently is not an answer
299			if !s.isInsert() && t > s.S+minPieceLn && t < s.E-minPieceLn {
300				return i
301			}
302		}
303		return -1
304	}
305	
306	// mergeDropped joins the dropped clip to the neighbour it was dragged against
307	// and reports whether it did. It is | Split's inverse and the only thing that
308	// clears a deliberate border -- on this pair only. Same-camera, touching
309	// neighbours only (coalesce's rule).
310	func (ed *cutEditor) mergeDropped() bool {
311		if !ed.segOn {
312			return false
313		}
314		return ed.mergeTouching(ed.segSel)
315	}
316	
317	// mergeTouching is the same join asked about a clip by index: dragging a
318	// clip's BORDER out to meet the next clip is the commoner way to close a gap,
319	// and both drops end here.
320	func (ed *cutEditor) mergeTouching(held int) bool {
321		if held < 0 || held >= len(ed.segs) {
322			return false
323		}
324		s := &ed.segs[held]
325		if s.isInsert() {
326			return false
327		}
328		for i := range ed.segs {
329			n := &ed.segs[i]
330			if i == held || n.isInsert() || n.Cam != s.Cam {
331				continue
332			}
333			switch {
334			case math.Abs(s.S-n.E) <= mergeTol:
335				s.Split = false // this drag is the join, whatever put the border there
336			case math.Abs(n.S-s.E) <= mergeTol:
337				n.Split = false
338			default:
339				continue
340			}
341			a, b := math.Min(s.S, n.S), math.Max(s.E, n.E)
342			ed.coalesce() // which is where two touching clips of one camera become one
343			ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("joined into one scene, %s – %s (%s) — "+
344				"↶ Undo puts the border back", mmss(a), mmss(b), ed.spanSecs(a, b)))
345			ed.redrawTracks()
346			return true
347		}
348		return false
349	}
350	
351	// mergeTol is how close two ends have to be to count as touching. coalesce's
352	// own number, named here because a drag has to ask the question before the
353	// merge rather than discover the answer afterwards: clampSeg snaps a dragged
354	// clip against its neighbour, so the everyday case is exactly 0 apart, and the
355	// tolerance is for the frame or two a hand-placed one lands out by.
356	//
357	// A frame or two is what it says, and for a long time it was a quarter of a
358	// second -- seven frames, and wider than plenty of things worth cutting out. A
359	// hole removed from the middle of a scene was two clips a fifth of a second
360	// apart, which this then read as a pair that had failed to meet and closed
361	// again: the removal undid itself and the status line said "removed 0.0 s".
362	// Anything a hand can see at the top zoom (maxPps) is wider than this.
363	const mergeTol = 0.04
364

18	// The playhead's own layer. GTK4 has no partial invalidation, so the cheap
19	// repaint has to be a cheap WIDGET: a transparent layer over both bands with
20	// nothing but the line, repainted ten times a second while the bands underneath
21	// repaint only on edits and scrolls (redrawTracks).
22	
23	// lineOver lays the line's layer over the two bands. Transparent to the
24	// pointer as well as the eye: every hover, click and drag on the timeline
25	// belongs to the bands underneath, and a layer that could be a target would
26	// swallow all of them.
27	func (ed *cutEditor) lineOver(band gtk.Widgetter) *gtk.Overlay {
28		ed.lineArea = gtk.NewDrawingArea()
29		ed.lineArea.SetCanTarget(false)
30		ed.lineArea.SetDrawFunc(func(_ *gtk.DrawingArea, cr *cairo.Context, _, h int) {
31			ed.drawPlayline(cr, h)
32		})
33		over := gtk.NewOverlay()
34		over.SetChild(band)
35		over.AddOverlay(ed.lineArea)
36		return over
37	}
38	
39	// drawPlayline is the line itself, through both bands and the gap between
40	// them. The bands draw translated by the scroll; this layer does not scroll,
41	// so the view offset is subtracted here instead.
42	func (ed *cutEditor) drawPlayline(cr *cairo.Context, h int) {
43		if !ed.hasPlay {
44			return
45		}
46		x := ed.xOf(ed.playhead) - ed.viewX
47		cr.SetSourceRGB(0.9, 0.15, 0.15)
48		cr.SetLineWidth(2)
49		cr.MoveTo(x, 0)
50		cr.LineTo(x, float64(h))
51		cr.Stroke()
52	}
53	
54	// redrawLine repaints what the running clock alone moves: the line's layer and
55	// the framing overlay on the preview, cursor and camera with it -- the same
56	// trio redrawTracks settles, minus the bands. This is the playback tick's
57	// repaint; redrawTracks stays the answer for anything that changes what the
58	// bands show.
59	func (ed *cutEditor) redrawLine() {
60		if ed.lineArea != nil {
61			ed.lineArea.QueueDraw()
62		}
63		if ed.fxArea != nil {
64			ed.fxArea.QueueDraw()
65			ed.syncFxCursor()
66			ed.syncPreviewZoom()
67		}
68	}

70	// Timeline marks are drawn as paths, not text: cairo's toy text API does no
71	// font fallback and no stock font has all of ⏸ ⧉ ⊕ ▭ ❝ ♪, so they came out as
72	// boxes. Each mark is a few lines and arcs in a small square, in the current colour.
73	
74	// fxMarkW is the square a mark is drawn in. Nine pixels beside a ten pixel
75	// font: the mark reads as a sibling of the words rather than as a picture
76	// stuck in front of them.
77	const fxMarkW = 9.0
78	
79	// markPlate is plateText with a mark in front of the words -- the dark plate
80	// covering both, so a band's label stays legible over whatever the band's own
81	// fill is doing under it.
82	func markPlate(cr *cairo.Context, x, y float64, kind, s string) {
83		e := cr.TextExtents(s)
84		platePath(cr, x-3, y-11, fxMarkW+4+e.Width+6, plateH)
85		cr.Fill()
86		cr.SetSourceRGB(1, 1, 1)
87		drawMark(cr, kind, x, y-10)
88		cr.MoveTo(x+fxMarkW+4, y)
89		cr.ShowText(s)
90	}
91	
92	// drawMark paints one mark in the fxMarkW square whose top left corner is
93	// (x, y), in the colour and on the path state the caller has set up. An
94	// unknown kind draws nothing rather than a placeholder: a mark nobody
95	// recognises is worse than a label with no mark.
96	func drawMark(cr *cairo.Context, kind string, x, y float64) {
97		m := fxMarkW
98		cx, cy := x+m/2, y+m/2
99		cr.SetLineWidth(1.2)

101		case "zoom":
102			// a circle closing on a point: the camera moving in and back out
103			cr.NewSubPath()

105			cr.Stroke()
106			cr.MoveTo(cx-m/4, cy)
107			cr.LineTo(cx+m/4, cy)
108			cr.MoveTo(cx, cy-m/4)
109			cr.LineTo(cx, cy+m/4)
110			cr.Stroke()
111		case "stay":
112			// a frame that is put somewhere and left there
113			cr.Rectangle(x+0.7, y+1.7, m-1.4, m-3.4)
114			cr.Stroke()
115		case "stop":
116			// the two bars every pause button in the world wears
117			cr.Rectangle(x+1.2, y+1, 2.3, m-2)
118			cr.Rectangle(x+m-3.5, y+1, 2.3, m-2)
119			cr.Fill()
120		case "hush":
121			// a stop that takes its sound with it: the same two bars, struck out
122			drawMark(cr, "stop", x, y)
123			cr.SetLineWidth(1.2)
124			cr.MoveTo(x-0.4, y+m+0.4)
125			cr.LineTo(x+m+0.4, y-0.4)
126			cr.Stroke()
127		case "speed":
128			// two chevrons, the way every fast-forward points
129			for _, dx := range []float64{0.6, 4.2} {
130				cr.MoveTo(x+dx, y+1.4)
131				cr.LineTo(x+dx+3, cy)
132				cr.LineTo(x+dx, y+m-1.4)
133			}

135		case "text":

137			cr.MoveTo(x+0.8, y+1.7)
138			cr.LineTo(x+m-0.8, y+1.7)
139			cr.MoveTo(cx, y+1.7)
140			cr.LineTo(cx, y+m-1)
141			cr.Stroke()
142		case "svg":

144			cr.Rectangle(x+0.7, y+1.2, m-1.4, m-2.4)

146			cr.MoveTo(x+1.6, y+m-2)
147			cr.LineTo(cx, cy-0.4)
148			cr.LineTo(x+m-1.6, y+m-2)

150			cr.Fill()
151		case "card":
152			// two sheets, one laid over the other: something spliced in
153			cr.Rectangle(x+0.7, y+2.6, m-3.3, m-3.9)
154			cr.Stroke()
155			cr.Rectangle(x+2.6, y+0.7, m-3.3, m-3.9)
156			cr.Stroke()
157		case "vol":
158			// a speaker: a cone opening to the right, with a wave off it
159			cr.MoveTo(x+0.8, y+2.4)
160			cr.LineTo(x+0.8, y+m-2.4)
161			cr.LineTo(x+2.6, y+m-2.4)
162			cr.LineTo(x+4.6, y+m-0.8)
163			cr.LineTo(x+4.6, y+0.8)
164			cr.LineTo(x+2.6, y+2.4)
165			cr.ClosePath()
166			cr.Fill()
167			cr.NewSubPath()
168			cr.Arc(x+4.6, cy, 2.2, -1.0, 1.0)
169			cr.Stroke()
170		case "sound":
171			// a note
172			cr.NewSubPath()
173			cr.Arc(x+2.4, y+m-2.2, 1.7, 0, 2*math.Pi)
174			cr.Fill()
175			cr.MoveTo(x+4.1, y+m-2.2)
176			cr.LineTo(x+4.1, y+0.9)
177			cr.LineTo(x+m-0.7, y+2.1)
178			cr.Stroke()
179		}
180	}

182	// sndSuffix is the tail on a speed's label: nothing for the default answer,
183	// a word or two for the four worth knowing without opening the form.
184	func sndSuffix(f cutFx) string {
185		switch f.sound() {
186		case sndPitch:
187			return " pitched"
188		case sndFx:
189			return " · sound 1×"
190		case sndScene:
191			return " · sound 1× to the scene's end"
192		case sndMute:
193			return " silent"
194		}
195		return ""
196	}
197	
198	// laneLabel is what one band on the effect lane says: a mark naming the kind
199	// and a few words of detail. The words go through cairo's toy text API (one
200	// font face, no fallback), so a label may only use characters every face has;
201	// anything a mark can say instead, a mark says. chars is the room in
202	// characters; only a title uses it.
203	func laneLabel(f cutFx, chars int) (mark, label string) {
204		switch f.Kind {
205		case "label":
206			// the name IS the effect: there is nothing else about it to say, and
207			// what it is called is what the hand is looking for on the lane
208			return "label", laneWords(f.Text, chars)
209		case "zoom":
210			if f.Stay {
211				return "stay", fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs", f.Dur)
212			}
213			return "zoom", fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs", f.Dur)
214		case "speed":
215			if f.frozenFx() {
216				if f.sound() == sndMute {
217					return "hush", fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs", f.Dur) // silent seconds
218				}
219				return "stop", fmt.Sprintf("%.1fs", f.Dur)
220			}
221			// the rate, and what the sound does when that is not the plain answer:
222			// a ×4 whose sound is silent or off on its own clock is a different
223			// effect to hear, and the bar is where that is read (cut_fxsound.go)
224			return "speed", "×" + fxNum(f.Rate) + sndSuffix(f)
225		case "text":
226			return "text", laneWords(f.Text, chars)
227		case "svg":
228			return "svg", laneWords(svgName(f), chars)
229		case "volume":
230			// the percent, which is the whole of what this one does. No "%" in the
231			// words: the mark beside them is a speaker, so the number can only be
232			// a loudness, and every character costs room on a narrow band
233			return "vol", gainPct(f.Gain)
234		}
235		return "", ""
236	}

238	// Thumbnails on the video rows: one frame every thumbStep frames, from the
239	// files Prepare extracted.
240	//
241	// Nothing is decoded inside a draw. A zoom changes which files are needed (the
242	// step is th*aspect/(pps*interval)), so a wheel notch used to stall on a
243	// screenful of JPEG decodes. A miss paints nothing and queues the file; a worker
244	// decodes the batch, hands it back on the GTK thread, and asks for one more
245	// draw. The cache holds cairo SURFACES: gdk_cairo_set_source_pixbuf converts on
246	// every paint; converted once on arrival, a paint is a memcpy.
247	
248	// thumbPic is one frame, ready to paint: the surface and its width, which is
249	// whatever shape the source is at the row's height.
250	//
251	// A nil surface is a file that could not be read. It is kept in the cache
252	// exactly so it is not read again -- every draw would otherwise ask for it
253	// again, which is a decode attempt per frame per missing file.
254	type thumbPic struct {
255		surf *cairo.Surface
256		w    float64
257	}
258	
259	// thumb is what drawTrack asks for. It never reads a file: the answer is
260	// either a picture that is ready or nothing at all, and asking for one that is
261	// not ready puts it on the list the loader drains.
262	func (ed *cutEditor) thumb(path string) *thumbPic {
263		if p, ok := ed.thumbs[path]; ok {
264			return p
265		}
266		if ed.thumbWant == nil {
267			ed.thumbWant = map[string]bool{}
268		}
269		if !ed.thumbWant[path] {
270			ed.thumbWant[path] = true
271			ed.loadThumbs()
272		}
273		return nil
274	}
275	
276	// thumbBatch is how many files one round of the loader hands back at a time.
277	// The whole point is that the page keeps moving, so a long list arrives in
278	// pieces: a screenful of pictures appears while the rest are still being read.
279	const thumbBatch = 6
280	
281	// loadThumbs arms the worker, on an idle rather than here.
282	//
283	// On an idle because this is called from inside a draw: starting a goroutine
284	// is cheap, but the map it reads is the GTK thread's and the draw is not
285	// finished with it. One armed loader at a time -- what arrives while it runs
286	// is asked for again by the next draw, which is the same list one frame later.
287	func (ed *cutEditor) loadThumbs() {
288		if ed.thumbBusy {
289			return
290		}
291		ed.thumbBusy = true
292		glib.IdleAdd(func() { ed.runThumbs() })
293	}
294	
295	// runThumbs takes the list, reads the files off the GTK thread, and hands the
296	// pictures back to it.
297	//
298	// gen is the row height the batch was asked at. It travels with the work
299	// because setThumbH empties the cache and asks for everything again at another
300	// size, and a picture decoded for the old height would otherwise land in the
301	// new cache and be drawn at the wrong scale.
302	func (ed *cutEditor) runThumbs() {
303		want := make([]string, 0, len(ed.thumbWant))
304		for p := range ed.thumbWant {
305			want = append(want, p)
306		}
307		ed.thumbWant = map[string]bool{}
308		if len(want) == 0 {
309			ed.thumbBusy = false
310			return
311		}
312		h, gen := ed.thumbHt, ed.thumbGen
313		go func() {
314			done := make(map[string]*gdkpixbuf.Pixbuf, thumbBatch)
315			flush := func() {
316				if len(done) == 0 {
317					return
318				}
319				batch := done
320				done = make(map[string]*gdkpixbuf.Pixbuf, thumbBatch)
321				glib.IdleAdd(func() { ed.tookThumbs(batch, gen) })
322			}
323			for _, p := range want {
324				// the read, the decode and the scale, all of it here: this is the
325				// work that used to happen inside drawTrack
326				pb, err := gdkpixbuf.NewPixbufFromFileAtScale(p, -1, h, true)
327				if err != nil {
328					pb = nil // remembered as unreadable rather than tried again
329				}
330				done[p] = pb
331				if len(done) >= thumbBatch {
332					flush()
333				}
334			}
335			flush()
336			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
337				ed.thumbBusy = false
338				if len(ed.thumbWant) > 0 {
339					ed.loadThumbs() // more was asked for while this ran
340				}
341			})
342		}()
343	}
344	
345	// tookThumbs puts a batch in the cache and asks for one draw for the lot.
346	//
347	// The pixbuf becomes a cairo surface here, on the GTK thread with the rest of
348	// the drawing machinery, and is not kept: what the band paints from is the
349	// surface, and holding both would be two copies of every frame in memory for
350	// no reader.
351	func (ed *cutEditor) tookThumbs(batch map[string]*gdkpixbuf.Pixbuf, gen int) {
352		if gen != ed.thumbGen {
353			return // asked for at a row height nobody is drawing any more
354		}
355		if ed.thumbs == nil {
356			ed.thumbs = map[string]*thumbPic{}
357		}
358		for p, pb := range batch {
359			ed.thumbs[p] = thumbSurface(pb)
360		}
361		ed.queueTracks()
362	}
363	
364	// thumbSurface paints a pixbuf onto an image surface once, so that every draw
365	// after it is a copy rather than a conversion. A pixbuf that could not be read
366	// comes back as a picture with no surface, which is how the cache remembers
367	// that the file is not worth asking about again.
368	func thumbSurface(pb *gdkpixbuf.Pixbuf) *thumbPic {
369		if pb == nil {
370			return &thumbPic{}
371		}
372		w, h := pb.Width(), pb.Height()
373		if w <= 0 || h <= 0 {
374			return &thumbPic{}
375		}
376		surf := cairo.CreateImageSurface(cairo.FormatARGB32, w, h)
377		cr := cairo.Create(surf)
378		gdk.CairoSetSourcePixbuf(cr, pb, 0, 0)
379		cr.Paint()
380		surf.Flush()
381		return &thumbPic{surf: surf, w: float64(w)}
382	}

384	// A file with several audio tracks (OBS desktop+mic, game+headset) gives one
385	// lane per chosen track, on the file's clock, indistinguishable downstream from
386	// a separate recorder. Which tracks are used is chosen on the Prepare row -- a
387	// fact about the FILE. Default is the first track alone, so old projects open
388	// unchanged.
389	
390	// audTrack is one audio stream of a file as ffprobe lists them. The POSITION in
391	// the slice is the a:N index everything below uses -- ffprobe lists them in that
392	// order and ffmpeg counts them the same way, so no absolute stream index has to
393	// be carried around and no file's video streams can shift the numbering.
394	type audTrack struct {
395		chans int    // 1 or 2, downmixed like ffprobeChannels: see lanes
396		title string // the recorder's own name for it ("Mic/Aux"), or ""
397	}
398	
399	// ffprobeTracks is every audio stream in a file, in a:0..a:N-1 order.
400	//
401	// Empty means the file has no sound, which is a real answer: a silent screen
402	// capture gets no lane rather than a strip of ground and a decode that can only
403	// fail. A probe that would not RUN is not that answer -- it is no answer -- and
404	// reports one mono track, which is the same guess this made when it was called
405	// ffprobeChannels and keeps a file the probe stumbled over in the session.
406	func ffprobeTracks(path string) []audTrack {
407		// a file ffprobe could not open is the only one that gets a guess: a
408		// silent capture answers with no audio streams, and that is a real answer
409		// -- it has no lane (TestASilentVideoHasNoLane)
410		if info := ffprobeInfo(path); info.ok {
411			return info.tracks
412		}
413		return []audTrack{{chans: 1}}
414	}
415	
416	// parseTracks reads that listing, one track per line. Split out from the probe
417	// so the answers it gives to a line it did not expect can be asked for directly
418	// -- the file that would produce one is a file nobody can conveniently write.
419	func parseTracks(out string) []audTrack {
420		var tr []audTrack
421		for _, ln := range strings.Split(out, "\n") {
422			if ln = strings.TrimSpace(ln); ln == "" {
423				continue
424			}
425			// "2" for a track with no name, "2,Desktop Audio" for one with. The
426			// title is cut off LAST because it is the field that can hold a comma,
427			// and a recorder's own name for a track is exactly where one turns up.
428			num, title, _ := strings.Cut(ln, ",")
429			n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(num))
430			if err != nil || n < 1 {
431				n = 1 // a stream ffprobe would not count is still a stream
432			}
433			tr = append(tr, audTrack{chans: min(2, n), title: strings.TrimSpace(title)})
434		}
435		return tr
436	}
437	
438	// ffprobeChannels is how many lanes a recording gets: the first track's channel
439	// count, and zero when there is no audio at all. Kept as its own name because
440	// that is the question a separately recorded file asks -- one file, one track,
441	// how deep is its lane -- and asking it through the list is the same probe.
442	func ffprobeChannels(path string) int {
443		tr := ffprobeTracks(path)
444		if len(tr) == 0 {
445			return 0
446		}
447		return tr[0].chans
448	}
449	
450	// trackName: the file's own name for the first track, name + track number for
451	// the rest. The first stays BARE because lane names key cutSeg.Quiet,
452	// cutFile.Shift, cutFile.Rows and the waveform cache. Positional numbers, not
453	// the recorder's titles: titles can repeat, and a repeat is two lanes on one key.
454	func trackName(base string, n int) string {
455		if n <= 0 {
456			return base
457		}
458		return fmt.Sprintf("%s #%d", base, n+1) // 1-based, the way recorders count them
459	}
460	
461	// wantTracks is which of a file's audio streams this session uses: the choice
462	// on its Prepare row, made safe against the file. Empty means the first track
463	// alone (what every older project means, so nothing migrates). Sorted,
464	// deduplicated, and dropped where it names a track the file has not got.
465	func wantTracks(sel []int, have int) []int {
466		if have <= 0 {
467			return nil
468		}
469		if len(sel) == 0 {
470			return []int{0}
471		}
472		seen := map[int]bool{}
473		var out []int
474		for _, n := range sel {
475			if n >= 0 && n < have && !seen[n] {
476				seen[n] = true
477				out = append(out, n)
478			}
479		}
480		sort.Ints(out)
481		return out
482	}
483	
484	// srcLanes: the footage's own sound as lanes, one per chosen track. The FIRST
485	// track is the master (the preview's sound, drawn as a strip under the pictures,
486	// taken by the render off the footage input); every other one is a lane in the
487	// recorders' band. No sound, or first track not chosen: no master strip.
488	// want is the per-file choice keyed on path; unlisted files use track one.
489	func srcLanes(vids []tlVideo, want map[string][]int) []tlAudio {
490		var out []tlAudio
491		for _, v := range vids {
492			tr := ffprobeTracks(v.path)
493			for _, n := range wantTracks(want[v.path], len(tr)) {
494				out = append(out, tlAudio{base: trackName(v.base, n), path: v.path,
495					start: v.start, off: v.off, dur: v.dur, track: n,
496					chans: tr[n].chans, master: n == 0})
497			}
498		}
499		return out
500	}
501	
502	// ownTrack says whether a video's own first track is one of this session's
503	// lanes -- the only thing a clip's base audio can come from ([0:a] in
504	// encodeClip). A row that asked for the second track and not the first gets
505	// it as a lane in the mix instead. True for a file nobody said anything about.
506	func ownTrack(want map[string][]int, path string) bool {
507		sel := want[path]
508		if len(sel) == 0 {
509			return true
510		}
511		for _, n := range sel {
512			if n == 0 {
513				return true
514			}
515		}
516		return false
517	}
518	
519	// trackOf is a chosen track as ffmpeg names it in a filtergraph or -map: bare
520	// for the first, indexed for the rest. Bare and not "a:0" so a render nobody
521	// chose anything for logs the identical command it always did.
522	func trackOf(input int, track int) string {
523		if track <= 0 {
524			return fmt.Sprintf("%d:a", input)
525		}
526		return fmt.Sprintf("%d:a:%d", input, track)
527	}
528	
529	// ---- the choice, on the Prepare row -----------------------------------------
530	
531	// srcTracks is one source's audio streams, probed once per session and path:
532	// the list is rebuilt whole on every change, and an ffprobe per row per rebuild
533	// stalls the page. The one thing that changes a row's audio hands it a new
534	// path (separate.go), which is a new key.
535	func (s *sourceList) srcTracks(path string) []audTrack {
536		if s.probed == nil {
537			s.probed = map[string][]audTrack{}
538		}
539		tr, ok := s.probed[path]
540		if !ok {
541			tr = ffprobeTracks(path)
542			s.probed[path] = tr
543		}
544		return tr
545	}
546	
547	// setTrack turns one of a file's audio tracks on or off for this session. The
548	// last one on cannot be turned off: "this file, none of it" is the ✕ at the
549	// end of the row, and the stored form keeps one meaning -- what is listed is
550	// used, nothing listed is the first track (wantTracks).
551	func (s *sourceList) setTrack(i, n int, on bool) {
552		if i < 0 || i >= len(s.items) {
553			return
554		}
555		it := s.items[i]
556		var next []int
557		for _, t := range wantTracks(it.tracks, len(s.srcTracks(it.path))) {
558			if t != n {
559				next = append(next, t)
560			}
561		}
562		if on {
563			next = append(next, n)
564			sort.Ints(next)
565		}
566		if len(next) == 0 {
567			return // the last one standing; see above
568		}
569		s.items[i].tracks = next
570		s.changed()
571	}
572	
573	// trackLabel names one track the way the row shows it: its number, and the name
574	// the recorder gave it when it gave one -- OBS writes "Desktop Audio" and "Mic/
575	// Aux" into the container, and those are the words the person choosing is
576	// thinking in. The number is always there because the title is the part that
577	// can be missing, wrong, or the same on two tracks.
578	func trackLabel(n int, t audTrack) string {
579		name := fmt.Sprintf("Track %d", n+1)
580		if t.title != "" {
581			name += " — " + t.title
582		}
583		if t.chans > 1 {
584			return name + " (stereo)"
585		}
586		return name + " (mono)"
587	}
588	
589	// trackButton is the row's control for a multi-track file: a menu holding one
590	// check per audio stream, and nil for the ordinary file with one, which has
591	// nothing to choose and would only get a button that cannot be wrong.
592	//
593	// It says how many are on over how many there are, because that is the fact a
594	// glance up the list is after -- which of these files is only half in the
595	// session -- and it is the fact the rest of the app is about to act on.
596	func (s *sourceList) trackButton(i int) *gtk.MenuButton {
597		it := s.items[i]
598		tr := s.srcTracks(it.path)
599		if len(tr) < 2 {
600			return nil
601		}
602		on := wantTracks(it.tracks, len(tr))
603		box := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 2)
604		margins(box, 6, 6, 6, 6)
605		head := headLabel("Audio tracks in this file")
606		box.Append(head)
607		for n := range tr {
608			n := n
609			c := gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel(trackLabel(n, tr[n]))
610			c.SetActive(slices.Contains(on, n))
611			c.ConnectToggled(func() { s.setTrack(i, n, c.Active()) })
612			box.Append(c)
613		}
614		why := gtk.NewLabel("Each track chosen gets a lane of its own in Cut, and is mixed\n" +
615			"into the render like a separate recording. Untick one to leave it\n" +
616			"out of the session entirely.")
617		why.SetXAlign(0)
618		why.SetMarginTop(4)
619		why.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
620		box.Append(why)
621		pop := gtk.NewPopover()
622		pop.SetChild(box)
623	
624		b := gtk.NewMenuButton()
625		b.AddCSSClass("flat")
626		b.SetPopover(pop)
627		inner := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 2)
628		inner.Append(gtk.NewImageFromIconName("media-playlist-consecutive-symbolic"))
629		inner.Append(gtk.NewLabel(fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", len(on), len(tr))))
630		b.SetChild(inner)
631		if len(on) < len(tr) {
632			b.AddCSSClass("dim-label") // some of this file is not in the session
633		}
634		b.SetTooltipText(fmt.Sprintf("Audio tracks — this file holds %d, and %d of them are in\n"+
635			"the session. Each one is a lane of its own in Cut and is mixed like a\n"+
636			"separate recording.", len(tr), len(on)))
637		return b
638	}
