2277			n.selectRow(ei)
2278			n.syncSpeakIcons()
2279		case n.synthFail[wav]:
2280			n.playSeg = ei // the server already refused this line; run the clip mute
2281			// ...but say so every time it comes around: a sticky silent failure
2282			// reads as "the TTS stopped working", not as a line that failed once
2283			n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("line %d failed to synthesize — see log; its ▶ retries", ei+1))
2284		default:
2285			n.holdForSynth(ei) // playSeg stays put: the voice starts when we resume
2286		}
2287		return true
2288	}
2289	
2290	// holdForSynth stops the preview on a line that has not been spoken yet, speaks
2291	// it, and picks the video up where it stopped. Running the clip mute and
2292	// catching the voice on some later pass would preview a cut nobody is going to
2293	// watch; a few seconds of waiting is the honest version.
2294	func (n *narrator) holdForSynth(i int) {
2295		n.player.Pause()
2296		if n.voice != nil {
2297			// Stop, not Pause: whatever wav is in there is a line that no longer
2298			// exists (the edit changed the cache key, which is why we are here).
2299			// Left merely paused, any later resume could replay a syllable of the
2300			// old voice before the tick catches up.
2301			n.voice.Stop()
2302		}
2303		n.playSeg = -1 // the resume must re-decide the voice, never assume it
2304		n.held = true
2305		if n.synthing {
2306			return // already on it; this tick only caught us still paused
2307		}
2308		n.pullRows() // speak what is in the box, not what was last saved
2309		if i >= len(n.entries) {
2310			return
2311		}
2312		e := n.entries[i]
2313		wav := n.a.ttsWav(e)
2314		n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("synthesizing line %d", i+1))
2315		n.synthWait(i, e, wav)
2316	}
2317	
2318	// synthWait does the waiting part off the GUI thread: the tick that got us here
2319	// only knows the line is missing, and the server call that fills it in would
2320	// otherwise stutter the picture from inside the tick.
2321	func (n *narrator) synthWait(i int, e narrEntry, wav string) {
2322		n.synthing = true
2323		n.syncSpeakIcons() // the wait is part of the audition; its row says so
2324		n.a.snapSources()
2325		go func() {
2326			err := n.a.synthesize(e)
2327			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
2328				n.synthing = false
2329				n.syncSpeakIcons()
2330				if err != nil {
2331					n.synthFail[wav] = true
2332					n.a.logf("synthesis failed: %v", err)
2333					n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("line %d failed -- see log; playing on without it", i+1))
2334				} else {
2335					n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("line %d ready", i+1))
2336				}
2337				// only if the pause was ours: a pause the user asked for stays.
2338				// The resume goes back to the LINE'S start, not to wherever the
2339				// picture froze: the hold can land mid-line (an edited line is
2340				// re-synthesized where its old audio used to be), and resuming
2341				// there would start the new wav at a stale offset -- past its end
2342				// if the new line is shorter, which is a video with no voice.
2343				if n.held && n.player != nil && !n.player.playing {
2344					n.held = false
2345					if err == nil {
2346						n.cue(math.Max(e.S, e.S+e.At), true)
2347					} else {
2348						n.player.Toggle() // no new line to land on; just carry on
2349					}
2350				}
2351			})
2352		}()
2353	}
2354	
2355	// sessionZero is the session's own second nought on the wall clock: the
2356	// earliest moment any source names. It always answers -- a session where no
2357	// file names a moment starts at 0:00 -- so callers subtract it without asking
2358	// whether the sources could be placed at all.
2359	func (a *App) sessionZero() float64 {
2360		vids, auds := a.snappedSources()
2361		_, zero := srcClock(append(append([]string{}, vids...), auds...))
2362		return zero
2363	}
2364	
2365	// ---- generation -------------------------------------------------------------
2366	
2367	// staleFor is why the narration would have to be written again, or "" when it
2368	// answers this cut. The times are the test: an entry's start IS its clip's
2369	// start, so a mismatch means the cut moved underneath. Edited text is NOT here
2370	// -- a rewritten line is the line you want.
2371	func (n *narrator) staleFor(segs []cutSeg) string {
2372		if len(n.entries) == 0 {
2373			return "there is no narration yet"
2374		}
2375		// a clip may carry several entries, so the test is coverage, not count:
2376		// every entry sits exactly on a clip, and every clip either has one or is
2377		// on the silent list -- emptied by hand, which is an answer and not a hole
2378		ei := 0
2379		for i := range segs {
2380			on := 0
2381			for ei < len(n.entries) && onClip(segs[i], n.entries[ei].S, n.entries[ei].E) {
2382				on++
2383				ei++
2384			}
2385			if on == 0 && !silentFor(n.silent, segs[i]) {
2386				return fmt.Sprintf("clip %d has no narration — it is new, or the cut moved under it", i+1)
2387			}
2388		}
2389		if ei != len(n.entries) {
2390			return "the narration has lines for clips the cut no longer has"
2391		}
2392		return ""
2393	}
2394	
2395	// staleCounts is what the ⚠ says: clips with no line on them, and lines
2396	// sitting on footage the cut no longer keeps. staleFor answers WHETHER the
2397	// narration is off the cut, in a sentence for the tooltip; this answers how
2398	// far off, which is the part worth a row.
2399	func (n *narrator) staleCounts(segs []cutSeg) (missing, orphan int) {
2400		if len(n.entries) == 0 {
2401			return 0, 0
2402		}
2403		ei := 0
2404		for i := range segs {
2405			on := 0
2406			for ei < len(n.entries) && onClip(segs[i], n.entries[ei].S, n.entries[ei].E) {
2407				on++
2408				ei++
2409			}
2410			if on == 0 && !silentFor(n.silent, segs[i]) {
2411				missing++
2412			}
2413		}
2414		return missing, len(n.entries) - ei
2415	}
2416	
2417	// refitEntries moves the lines onto the cut as it is now without asking the
2418	// model: the words are kept, the times follow. A line keeps its place against
2419	// the VIDEO, not its offset into the clip. Lines whose clip is gone are left
2420	// alone and counted (orphan) for staleFor.
2421	func refitEntries(segs []cutSeg, entries []narrEntry) (moved, orphan int) {
2422		for i := range entries {
2423			e := &entries[i]
2424			j := clipFor(segs, *e)
2425			if j < 0 {
2426				orphan++
2427				continue
2428			}
2429			if math.Abs(segs[j].S-e.S) <= 0.05 && math.Abs(segs[j].E-e.E) <= 0.05 {
2430				continue
2431			}
2432			at := e.S + e.At - segs[j].S
2433			e.S, e.E = segs[j].S, segs[j].E
2434			e.At = math.Min(math.Max(0, at), math.Max(0, e.E-e.S-1))
2435			moved++
2436		}
2437		return moved, orphan
2438	}
2439	
2440	// clipFor is the clip a line belongs to once the cut has moved: the one it
2441	// shares the most video with. Overlap rather than "the clip holding its start",
2442	// because a clip trimmed at the front leaves that start outside the very clip
2443	// the rest of the line plainly sits in.
2444	func clipFor(segs []cutSeg, e narrEntry) int {
2445		if e.E <= e.S {
2446			// a line written on a card has no span to share: its clip is the
2447			// zero-span seg still sitting at the same moment, if any
2448			for i, s := range segs {
2449				if s.E <= s.S && math.Abs(s.S-e.S) <= 0.05 {
2450					return i
2451				}
2452			}
2453			return -1
2454		}
2455		best, most := -1, 0.0
2456		for i, s := range segs {
2457			if o := math.Min(e.E, s.E) - math.Max(e.S, s.S); o > most {
2458				best, most = i, o
2459			}
2460		}
2461		return best
2462	}
2463	
2464	// refit is refitEntries on the page: called when Narrate is opened, which is
2465	// the only moment the cut can have changed under it. The boxes are pulled in
2466	// first because the rebuild reads the entries and would drop an edit still
2467	// sitting in one, and the rebuild itself only happens when something moved.
2468	func (n *narrator) refit() {
2469		segs := n.a.produceSegs()
2470		if len(segs) == 0 || len(n.entries) == 0 {
2471			return
2472		}
2473		n.pullRows()
2474		moved, orphan := refitEntries(segs, n.entries)
2475		if moved == 0 {
2476			return
2477		}
2478		n.sortEntries()
2479		n.save()
2480		n.rebuildRows()
2481		if orphan > 0 {
2482			n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("the cut moved — %d line(s) followed their clips, %d sit on video the cut no longer has", moved, orphan))
2483			return
2484		}
2485		n.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("the cut moved — %d line(s) followed their clips", moved))
2486	}
2487	
2488	// unspoken counts the lines with no wav in the cache for the CURRENT voice --
2489	// which is what makes switching voice, nudging the pitch or editing a line all
2490	// show up as work for ▶ to do, without any of them being tracked as such.
2491	func (n *narrator) unspoken() int {
2492		if n.a.captionsOnly() {
2493			return 0 // no voice: a written line is a finished line
2494		}
2495		miss := 0
2496		for _, e := range n.entries {
2497			if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) != "" && !exists(n.a.ttsWav(e)) {
2498				miss++
2499			}
2500		}
2501		return miss
2502	}
2503	
2504	// narrateRun is ▶: write the narration, then speak whatever is not cached, as
2505	// one run. It writes EVERY time -- keepPrevNarration copies the previous
2506	// narration.json aside first -- because a narration that already covers the
2507	// cut could otherwise never be redone. staleFor only names why, in the log and
2508	// on the inputs row.
2509	func (a *App) narrateRun() {
2510		if a.busy() {
2511			return
2512		}
2513		n := a.narr
2514		if n == nil {
2515			return
2516		}
2517		segs := a.produceSegs()
2518		if len(segs) == 0 {
2519			a.setStatus("no cut yet — build one on the Cut step first")
2520			return
2521		}
2522		if a.narrOff {
2523			a.setStatus("this video has no narration — tick Narration at the top of this page to write one")
2524			return
2525		}
2526		n.pullRows() // an edit still sitting in a text box is part of this run
2527		// why is the reason for the log, not the decision: ▶ writes either way
2528		why := n.staleFor(segs)
2529		if why == "" {
2530			why = "rewriting every line"
2531		}
2532		if !exists(filepath.Join(a.transcriptDir(), "session.tsv")) {
2533			a.setStatus("run Transcript first — no session timeline")
2534			return
2535		}
2536		// the lines to speak are the ones the model is about to write, below: ▶
2537		// always writes first, so there is nothing here worth copying out
2538		var speak []narrEntry
2539		a.saveProjectNow() // the run is a moment worth a file, whatever the ticker is doing
2540	
2541		a.startRun()
2542		// True only while the model is writing. The pulse used to stop when the run
2543		// did, which is the wrong end of it: the writing is one call with nothing to
2544		// measure, but the speaking that follows it is n lines and counts them, and
2545		// a bar still pulsing over that reading turned a real "speaking 4/9" into a
2546		// block sliding back and forth. It is read and written on the GUI thread
2547		// only -- the timeout below and the idle callback that clears it.
2548		writing := true
2549		// what the bar calls the two halves. Writing is one call and cannot be
2550		// queued -- the model decides how many lines there are -- so it is a job
2551		// with no tasks under it; the speaking below queues one task per line.
2552		a.qJob(trackSTT, "narration", 1, 2)
2553		a.logf(">>> narrate: %s — writing %d clip(s), one LLM call, then speaking them",
2554			why, len(segs))
2555		a.prog(trackSTT, 0, "thinking about it")
2556		glib.TimeoutAdd(150, func() bool {
2557			if !a.running || !writing {
2558				return false
2559			}
2560			// the reply is streamed, so the moment the first clip closes there is
2561			// something real to show and the pulse has to get out of its way --
2562			// Pulse and SetFraction are the same needle
2563			a.progMu.Lock()
2564			counted := a.progParts[trackSTT] > 0
2565			a.progMu.Unlock()
2566			if counted {
2567				return false
2568			}
2569			a.progress.Pulse()
2570			return true
2571		})
2572	
2573		// the writing is always the run's first half now, so the speaking is
2574		// always the second
2575		speakBase, speakSpan := narrWriteShare, 1-narrWriteShare
2576	
2577		go func() {
2578			{
2579				a.logCtx("narration")
2580				entries, err := a.writeNarration(segs)
2581				if err != nil {
2582					a.narrateDone(err, "narration")
2583					return
2584				}
2585				speak = entries
2586				// the written lines have to be on the page before they are spoken:
2587				// the run bar's ⏹ mid-synthesis must not leave the text nowhere
2588				// whatever the streamed count reached, the writing is now finished:
2589				// the bar starts the speaking half from a full half, not from
2590				// wherever a clip that closed oddly left it
2591				a.qDone(trackSTT, narrWriteShare)
2592				done := make(chan struct{})
2593				glib.IdleAdd(func() {
2594					writing = false // hands the bar to the count below
2595					// the old lines are on their way out; keep them where a hand
2596					// that wanted one back can reach it (see narrateRun's header)
2597					if prev, err := keepPrevNarration(a.narrPath()); err == nil && prev != "" {
2598						a.logf("    the narration it replaced is kept at %s", prev)
2599					}
2600					n.entries, n.silent = entries, nil
2601					n.save()
2602					n.rebuildRows()
2603					a.logf(">>> narration written for %d clips", len(entries))
2604					a.setStatus("narration written — speaking it")
2605					close(done)
2606				})
2607				<-done
2608			}
2609			if a.captionsOnly() {
2610				// no voice: a written line is a finished line. The speaking job
2611				// still opens and closes so the bar reaches the end it promised.
2612				a.qJob(trackSTT, "speaking", 2, 2)
2613				a.logfIdle("    narrate: captions only — %d line(s) written, none spoken", len(speak))
2614				a.narrateDone(nil, "narration")
2615				return
2616			}
2617			var failed error
2618			// the speaking half, which CAN be queued: one task per line, cached or
2619			// not. It is always the run's second job, because the writing above is
2620			// always the first.
2621			a.qJob(trackSTT, "speaking", 2, 2)
2622			a.qPush(trackSTT, len(speak), "line")
2623			spoke, cached := 0, 0
2624			for i, e := range speak {
2625				// ▶ started this and is the ⏸ for it, so the pause has to be real:
2626				// between lines, like every other run's (checkpoint in pipeline.go)
2627				if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
2628					failed = err
2629					break
2630				}
2631				// before the cache check, not after: a line already spoken is a line
2632				// this run is done with, and skipping the reading for it left the bar
2633				// sitting at whatever the last synthesized line put there while the
2634				// loop ran through the rest of a cached narration.
2635				a.qTake(trackSTT)
2636				a.prog(trackSTT, speakBase+speakSpan*float64(i)/float64(len(speak)), "")
2637				if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) == "" || exists(a.ttsWav(e)) {
2638					cached++
2639					continue
2640				}
2641				if err := a.synthesize(e); err != nil {
2642					failed = err
2643					break
2644				}
2645				spoke++
2646			}
2647			if failed == nil {
2648				a.logfIdle("    narrate: %d line(s) spoken, %d already in the cache", spoke, cached)
2649			}
2650			a.narrateDone(failed, "synthesis")
2651		}()
2652	}
2653	
2654	// narrateDone ends the run from whichever stage stopped it, on the GUI thread.
2655	func (a *App) narrateDone(err error, stage string) {
2656		glib.IdleAdd(func() {
2657			a.endRun()
2658			if n := a.narr; n != nil {
2659				n.updateInputs()
2660				n.updateOut()
2661			}
2662			if err != nil {
2663				if !errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
2664					a.logf("%s FAILED: %v", stage, err)
2665					a.progress.SetText(stage + " failed — see log")
2666					return
2667				}
2668				a.progress.SetText(stage + " stopped")
2669				return
2670			}
2671			a.progress.SetFraction(1)
2672			if a.captionsOnly() {
2673				a.progress.SetText("narration ready — captions only, nothing spoken")
2674				return
2675			}
2676			a.progress.SetText("narration ready and spoken — ▶ the preview hears it in place")
2677		})
2678	}
2679	
2680	// narratorMic names the one recording the finished video
2681	// never plays -- the narration's to quote; blank when the voice is cut from
2682	// the footage.
2683	func (a *App) narratorMic() string {
2684		slot := narratorSlot(a.voiceID())
2685		if slot == 0 {
2686			slot = 1 // a stock voice still narrates for whoever holds slot 1
2687		}
2688		p := a.narratorSource(slot)
2689		if p == "" {
2690			return ""
2691		}
2692		vids, _ := a.snappedSources()
2693		for _, v := range vids {
2694			if v == p {
2695				return ""
2696			}
2697		}
2698		return baseName(p)
2699	}
2700	
2701	// narrBudget is how many words a clip is allowed: under a third of speaking
2702	// rate, so there is room for the thought AND its punchline and the words run
2703	// out early in every clip; the cap binds past 40 s so a two-minute clip does
2704	// not get two minutes of talking.
2705	func narrBudget(dur float64) int {
2706		n := int(dur * 0.75)
2707		switch {
2708		case n < 8:
2709			return 8 // even a five-second clip can take a short one
2710		case n > 30:
2711			return 30
2712		}
2713		return n
2714	}
2715	
2716	// clipBriefs writes each clip's block. narr is narratorMic: lines off that
2717	// recording are the narrator's own and get his name, every other line is one
2718	// the video plays out loud. Blank means nobody is exempt, which is the
2719	// assumption that cannot embarrass the narration.
2720	func clipBriefs(segs []cutSeg, rows []tsvRow, fx []cutFx, narr string) string {
2721		return clipBriefsWith(segs, rows, fx, narr, func(i int, s cutSeg) string {
2722			return fmt.Sprintf("CLIP %d: %.1f–%.1f (%s, at most %d words -- fewer is better, none is fine)",
2723				i+1, s.S, s.E, clipPlays(s), narrBudget(s.length()))
2724		})
2725	}
2726	
2727	// clipPlays is how long a clip is on screen, and at what speed -- the two
2728	// facts every brief's heading needs and only one of which is its length.
2729	//
2730	// A clip at 4 runs a quarter of the session seconds its lines are stamped in:
2731	// a line at [+40s] of it arrives ten seconds into what the viewer watches. The
2732	// briefs stamp lines in session seconds because that is what the transcript
2733	// has, so the heading is where the rate has to be said.
2734	func clipPlays(s cutSeg) string {
2735		if s.Rate > 0 && s.Rate != 1 {
2736			return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s of footage at %gx, %.0f s on screen", s.E-s.S, s.Rate, s.length())
2737		}
2738		return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s", s.length())
2739	}
2740	
2741	// clipBriefsWith is the same blocks under headings of the caller's own. The
2742	// narration's carry the word budget; the upload text's carry where the clip
2743	// falls in the finished video, which is the only clock its chapter list may
2744	// use. A heading is read as an instruction as much as a label -- "at most 30
2745	// words" over a clip in the upload brief is a limit a small model will obey on
2746	// the description -- so each job writes its own.
2747	func clipBriefsWith(segs []cutSeg, rows []tsvRow, fx []cutFx, narr string, head func(i int, s cutSeg) string) string {
2748		var b strings.Builder
2749		for i, s := range segs {
2750			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n%s\n", head(i, s))
2751			// An insert has no footage under it and no transcript over it, so the
2752			// lines around it would be a description of whatever it covered -- which
2753			// is the one thing the viewer will not be looking at. Say what it is
2754			// instead: a card that says "a few moments later" wants no narration, and
2755			// a ranking graphic wants the ranking read out, and the file's name is
2756			// the only thing here that tells them apart.
2757			if s.isInsert() {
2758				// deliberately the whole thing, parameters and all: "tier.svg" says
2759				// nothing about what is on the card and "tier.svg?S=Dust II,Mirage"
2760				// says all of it, which is exactly what a narrator needs to read
2761				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  (not footage: a graphic or clip inserted here, %q. "+
2762					"Narrate what is ON it, or say nothing -- there is nothing from the "+
2763					"session to describe, and inventing one would caption the wrong picture)\n",
2764					filepath.Base(s.Ins))
2765				continue
2766			}
2767			n := 0
2768			for _, r := range rows {
2769				if r.e <= s.S-4 || r.s >= s.E+4 {
2770					continue
2771				}
2772				// seconds from the clip's own start, so the narration can follow the
2773				// clip instead of arriving at it; a line just outside the clip goes
2774				// negative or past the end, which is exactly what it is
2775				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  [%+.0fs] %s: %s\n", r.s-s.S, tlLabel(r, narr), r.text)
2776				n++
2777			}
2778			if n == 0 {
2779				// neutral: three passes read this brief, and "say something
2780				// general" is an instruction to one of them (the narration says
2781				// it in its own wording). To the speed pass the same clip is a
2782				// stretch where nothing was said and nothing changed on screen,
2783				// which is the plainest description of dull there is.
2784				b.WriteString("  (no lines over this clip: nothing said, nothing described)\n")
2785			}
2786			// and the moments somebody marked. A label effect changes nothing in

2926	// the job rather than one exercising taste. A clip with no entry at all is

2928	func bindEntries(segs []cutSeg, raw []rawEntry) ([]narrEntry, string) {
2929		var entries []narrEntry

2934			// rejects entries out of order instead of silently reordering them.

2940				}
2941			}
2942			if j < 0 {

2945			if j > last+1 {

2947				return nil, fmt.Sprintf("clip %d (%.1f-%.1f) got no entry", last+2, segs[last+1].S, segs[last+1].E)
2948			}
2949			ci = j
2950			if strings.TrimSpace(r.Text) != "" {

2952			}
2953			last = j
2954			// the placement is clamped here so everything downstream can trust

2956			at := math.Min(math.Max(0, r.At), math.Max(0, segs[j].length()-1))

2958			// else the model invents is the bottom, same as saying nothing
2959			pos, _ := posTag(r.Pos)

2961				S: segs[j].S, E: segs[j].E, At: at, Text: strings.TrimSpace(r.Text),

2967		if said == 0 {
2968			return nil, "every clip came back with no line at all"
2969		}
2970		// two lines in one clip play in time order whatever order they arrived in
2971		sort.SliceStable(entries, func(a, b int) bool {
2972			if entries[a].S != entries[b].S {
2973				return entries[a].S < entries[b].S
2974			}
2975			return entries[a].At < entries[b].At
2976		})

3	// Two speed effects over the same seconds: the rate is the MEAN of what they
4	// ask for. A stop is ×0 in that arithmetic, so the picture freezes only where
5	// the mean is nought -- a stop with nothing over it -- and a stop under a ×2

13	// applied is the rate the render actually runs a stretch at. A frozen stretch
14	// has no observable rate -- the still covers it -- and ×0 is not a clip any
15	// encoder can build, so the footage under it runs at ×1, which is what it has
16	// always done (see cut_fxstill.go).
17	func (st rateStep) applied() float64 {
18		if st.rate <= 0 {
19			return 1
20		}
21		return st.rate
22	}
23	
24	// outLn is how long a stretch comes out on screen, which is the length the
25	// render measures it by.
26	func (st rateStep) outLn() float64 { return (st.t1 - st.t0) / st.applied() }
27	
28	// rateSpans is the whole cut's speed as flat stretches: every boundary any
29	// speed effect draws, and between two boundaries the rate they agree on.
30	// Seconds no effect covers are not in the list at all -- they run at ×1 by
31	// simply being left alone.
32	func rateSpans(fx []cutFx) []rateStep {
33		var all []rateStep
34		for _, f := range speedsOf(fx) {
35			if f.Dur <= 0 {
36				continue
37			}
38			if f.frozenFx() {
39				// a stop is one flat ×0 over its band; it has no stairs, because
40				// there is no ramping into and out of standing still
41				all = append(all, rateStep{f.T, f.T + f.Dur, 0})
42				continue
43			}
44			all = append(all, speedSteps(f)...)
45		}
46		if len(all) == 0 {
47			return nil
48		}
49		cuts := make([]float64, 0, 2*len(all))
50		for _, st := range all {
51			cuts = append(cuts, st.t0, st.t1)
52		}
53		sort.Float64s(cuts)
54		var out []rateStep
55		for i := 1; i < len(cuts); i++ {
56			t0, t1 := cuts[i-1], cuts[i]
57			if t1-t0 < 1e-9 {
58				continue
59			}
60			mid := (t0 + t1) / 2
61			sum, n := 0.0, 0
62			for _, st := range all {

65				}
66			}

75	// joinSpans folds together neighbours that ask for the same thing, so a
76	// boundary two effects happen to share does not become a cut in the video.
77	func joinSpans(sp []rateStep) []rateStep {

96		for pass := 0; pass < len(sp)+1 && len(sp) > 0; pass++ {
97			k := -1

104				}

108			}

114	// spanCuts is whether a stretch is a cut in the finished video at all. One
115	// that runs at the same speed as both its neighbours -- and the footage
116	// outside the list runs at ×1 -- makes no clip of its own, so it has no length
117	// for the render to find too short. This is what keeps a very short stop from
118	// being healed away: on its own it splits nothing.
119	func spanCuts(sp []rateStep, i int) bool {
120		left, right := 1.0, 1.0
121		if i > 0 {
122			left = sp[i-1].applied()
123		}
124		if i < len(sp)-1 {
125			right = sp[i+1].applied()
126		}
127		a := sp[i].applied()
128		return math.Abs(a-left) > 1e-9 || math.Abs(a-right) > 1e-9
129	}

131	// absorbSpan hands stretch k's seconds to a neighbour -- the longer one, which
132	// is the one least changed by taking them -- or drops it when it stands alone.
133	func absorbSpan(sp []rateStep, k int) []rateStep {
134		switch {
135		case len(sp) == 1:
136			return nil
137		case k == 0:
138			sp[1].t0 = sp[0].t0
139			return joinSpans(sp[1:])
140		case k == len(sp)-1:
141			sp[k-1].t1 = sp[k].t1
142			return joinSpans(sp[:k])
143		}
144		if sp[k-1].outLn() >= sp[k+1].outLn() {
145			sp[k-1].t1 = sp[k].t1
146		} else {
147			sp[k+1].t0 = sp[k].t0
148		}
149		return joinSpans(append(sp[:k:k], sp[k+1:]...))
150	}

func (a *App) narrateRun() {
	if a.busy() {
		return
	}
	n := a.narr
	if n == nil {
		return
	}
	segs := a.produceSegs()
	if len(segs) == 0 {
		a.setStatus("no cut yet — build one on the Cut step first")
		return
	}
	if a.narrOff {
		a.setStatus("this video has no narration — tick Narration at the top of this page to write one")
		return
	}
	n.pullRows() // an edit still sitting in a text box is part of this run
	// why is the reason for the log, not the decision: ▶ writes either way
	why := n.staleFor(segs)
	if why == "" {
		why = "rewriting every line"
	}
	if !exists(filepath.Join(a.transcriptDir(), "session.tsv")) {
		a.setStatus("run Transcript first — no session timeline")
		return
	}
	// the lines to speak are the ones the model is about to write, below: ▶
	// always writes first, so there is nothing here worth copying out
	var speak []narrEntry
	a.saveProjectNow() // the run is a moment worth a file, whatever the ticker is doing

	a.startRun()
	// True only while the model is writing. The pulse used to stop when the run

func (a *App) produceClicked() {
	if !a.renderWanted() {
		a.produceRun(true)
		return
	}
	a.askOverwrite(func() { a.produceRun(true) })
}

func (a *App) transcodeClicked() { a.askOverwrite(func() { a.produceRun(false) }) }

// renderWanted is renderStale with the page's own inputs read for it, for the
// two callers that have not gathered them yet.
func (a *App) renderWanted() bool {
	if a.prod == nil {
		return false
	}
	vids, auds := a.snapSources()
	return a.renderStale(a.produceSegs(), a.produceEntries(), a.prodSettings(), vids, auds)
}

func (a *App) askOverwrite(run func()) {
	p := a.prod
	if p == nil || !exists(p.outFile) {
		run()
		return
	}
	fi, err := os.Stat(p.outFile)
	detail := p.outFile
	if err == nil {
		detail = fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s, %s", p.outFile, humanSize(fi.Size()), humanAgo(fi.ModTime()))
	}
	a.confirm("Overwrite "+filepath.Base(p.outFile)+"?",
		detail+"\n\nThe encode takes minutes and there is no undo for it.", "Overwrite", run)
}

	if a.busy() {
		return
	}
	if a.pub == nil {
		return
	}
	segs := a.produceSegs()
	if len(segs) == 0 {
		a.setStatus("no cut yet — build one on the Cut step first")

	entries := a.produceEntries()
	st := a.prodSettings()
	vids, auds := a.snapSources()

429	func (ed *cutEditor) hoverEdge(x float64, cut bool) {
430		on, t := false, 0.0
431		if cut {
432			if seg, end, ok := ed.edgeAt(x + ed.viewX); ok {
433				on = true
434				if t = ed.segs[seg].S; end {
435					t = ed.segs[seg].E
436				}
437			}
438		}
439		if on == ed.edgeHovOn && t == ed.edgeHovT {
440			return // nothing the bands draw has changed
441		}
442		ed.edgeHovOn, ed.edgeHovT = on, t
443		// the two bands that draw the marker, and not redrawTracks: a hover happens
444		// on the way past and must not drag the overlay's pointer-grabbing and the
445		// track's height along behind it
446		if ed.srcArea != nil {
447			ed.srcArea.QueueDraw()
448		}
449		if ed.audArea != nil {
450			ed.audArea.QueueDraw()
451		}
452	}
453	
454	// wantCursor is what a press at this point would do, said in the pointer: the
455	// three things the selection row does live in the same sixteen pixels, and a
456	// resize cursor over an end and an open hand over a middle tell them apart
457	// before anything is committed. The effects lane answers the same way.
458	func (ed *cutEditor) wantCursor(x, y float64) string {
459		if x < 0 {
460			return ""
461		}
462		// the gutter's controls stand in front of second zero, where nothing on
463		// the tape reaches (cut_gutter.go)
464		if ed.foldAllAt(x+ed.viewX, y) || ed.pairSwitchAt(x+ed.viewX, y) != nil ||
465			ed.rowKillAt(x+ed.viewX, y) >= 0 {
466			return "pointer"
467		}
468		switch {
469		case ed.hitSelBand(y):
470			// the fold's own badge first, and for the reason every badge is asked
471			// first: it sits between two bars, where a press would otherwise be
472			// read as one of their ends (cut_fold.go)
473			if ed.foldBadgeAt(x+ed.viewX, y) >= 0 {
474				return "pointer"
475			}
476			switch ed.selPartAt(x + ed.viewX) {
477			case selStart, selEnd:
478				return "ew-resize"
479			case selWhole:
480				return "grab"
481			case selKill:
482				return "pointer"
483			}
484			// clear of the blue, the green bar answers with the same cursors: its
485			// ends trim the clip's borders, its middle moves the clip, its ✕
486			// removes it
487			switch _, part := ed.bandClipPartAt(x + ed.viewX); part {
488			case selStart, selEnd:
489				return "ew-resize"
490			case selWhole:
491				return "grab"
492			case selKill:
493				return "pointer"
494			}
495		case ed.fxHitLane(y):
496			// the band's own ✕ first, exactly as the press asks it first
497			// (cut_fxkill.go): it sits ON the band, so without this the pointer
498			// over a button that removes the effect was the open hand that means
499			// "this whole thing moves" -- the one promise it must not make
500			if ed.fxKillAt(x+ed.viewX, y) >= 0 {
501				return "pointer"
502			}
503			i := ed.fxIndexAt(x+ed.viewX, y)
504			if i < 0 {
505				return ""
506			}
507			if p := ed.fxPartAt(i, x+ed.viewX); p == fxStart || p == fxEnd {
508				return "ew-resize"
509			}
510			return "grab"
511		case ed.hitPics(y):
512			// a lane's ✕ first, for the reason the press asks it first: it can
513			// overlap a clip border, and a resize arrow over a button is a lie
514			if ed.laneKillAt(x+ed.viewX, y) != "" {
515				return "pointer"
516			}
517			// ...and an emptied row's, which the press asks in the same breath
518			if ed.rowKillAt(x+ed.viewX, y) >= 0 {
519				return "pointer"
520			}
521			if _, _, ok := ed.edgeAt(x + ed.viewX); ok {
522				return "ew-resize"
523			}
524			// ...and the blue selection's own ends, which the press takes from
525			// here exactly as the selection row does; the hand has to be able
526			// to see that before it reaches
527			if p := ed.selPartNear(x+ed.viewX, selGripPicsPx); p == selStart || p == selEnd {
528				return "ew-resize"
529			}
530		}
531		return ""
532	}
533	
534	// setCursor points a band's pointer at name, or back to the page's own for "".
535	// One slot per band, remembered, because SetCursorFromName on every motion
536	// event is a call into the display server for a cursor it already has.
537	func (ed *cutEditor) setCursor(area *gtk.DrawingArea, name string) {
538		if area == nil {
539			return
540		}
541		last := &ed.selCur
542		if area == ed.audArea {
543			last = &ed.audCur
544		}
545		if *last == name {
546			return
547		}
548		*last = name
549		if name == "" {
550			area.SetCursor(nil)
551			return
552		}
553		area.SetCursorFromName(name)
554	}
555	
556	// ---- drawing ----------------------------------------------------------------
557	
558	// drawSelBand paints the band. Called from drawTrack inside its translation, so
559	// x here is timeline px like everything drawn around it.
560	func (ed *cutEditor) drawSelBand(cr *cairo.Context, vx0, vx1 float64) {
561		y := ed.selBandTop()
562		// the row itself, as wide as the recordings, so that an empty band is
563		// visibly a place a selection could go rather than a gap in the page
564		cr.SetSourceRGB(bandGround, bandGround, bandGround+0.01)
565		for _, v := range ed.vids {
566			cr.Rectangle(v.pxOrigin, y, v.dur*ed.pps, selBandH)
567		}
568		cr.Fill()
569		// Every kept scene as a bar, always: the green tint over dark footage is
570		// invisible, the band's flat ground answers "what does the cut keep" at a
571		// glance. The clip under the red line is drawn brighter with end handles (it
572		// is what the arrows and toolbar act on); the rest dimmer, a pixel short of
573		// their right edge so touching scenes read as two. Drawn first so a selection
574		// lands on top.
575		cur := ed.bandClipIdx()
576		// A pixel short of its own right edge so touching clips read as two, deep
577		// enough to hold a badge. Every bar wears END HANDLES, because every bar
578		// answers the hand (bandClipPartAt) -- as the picture band draws every kept
579		// stretch's borders.
580		for _, i := range ed.bandBars() {
581			s := ed.segs[i]
582			gx0, gx1 := ed.xOf(s.S), ed.xOf(s.E)
583			if gx1 < vx0 || gx0 > vx1 {
584				continue
585			}
586			// the bar in reach is a shade stronger and a touch deeper: it is the
587			// one the arrow keys and the toolbar are about, and the row still says
588			// which that is
589			if i == cur {
590				cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.2, 0.8, 0.3, 0.5)
591				cr.Rectangle(gx0, y+2, gx1-gx0, selBandH-4)
592			} else {
593				cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.2, 0.8, 0.3, 0.4)
594				cr.Rectangle(gx0, y+4, math.Max(1, gx1-gx0-1), selBandH-8)
595			}
596			cr.Fill()
597			cr.SetSourceRGB(0.5, 0.92, 0.58)
598			for _, hx := range []float64{gx0, gx1} {
599				cr.Rectangle(hx-1.5, y, 3, selBandH)
600			}
601			cr.Fill()
602			// the ✕, the same badge on every bar and red under the pointer,
603			// because this is the page's one "remove that" and it says so the
604			// same way everywhere (drawKillBadge). Not the blue's flat mark --
605			// the blue's ✕ throws away a selection and leaves the footage alone.
606			if gx1-gx0 >= killMin {
607				drawKillBadge(cr, (gx0+gx1)/2, y+selBandH/2, ed.bandKillHov == i)
608			}
609			if i != cur {
610				continue
611			}
612			switch {
613			case (ed.segOn && ed.segSel == i) || (ed.edgeOn && ed.edgeSeg == i):
614				cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.9)
615				cr.SetLineWidth(2)
616				cr.Rectangle(gx0-1, y+1, gx1-gx0+2, selBandH-2)
617				cr.Stroke()
618			case ed.bandHov:
619				cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.4)
620				cr.SetLineWidth(1.5)
621				cr.Rectangle(gx0-1, y+1.25, gx1-gx0+2, selBandH-2.5)
622				cr.Stroke()
623			}
624		}
625		if !ed.sel.active {
626			return
627		}
628		x0, x1 := ed.selSpanPx()
629		if x1 < vx0 || x0 > vx1 {
630			return
631		}
632		a, b := ed.selSpan()
633	
634		cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.3, 0.55, 0.9, 0.75)
635		cr.Rectangle(x0, y+2, x1-x0, selBandH-4)
636		cr.Fill()
637		// the ends, drawn as the handles they are: a bar the full height of the
638		// row, brighter than the fill, on both sides of the border rather than
639		// inside it, so that what is grabbable looks grabbable
640		cr.SetSourceRGB(0.62, 0.82, 1)
641		for _, x := range []float64{x0, x1} {
642			cr.Rectangle(x-1.5, y, 3, selBandH)
643		}
644		cr.Fill()
645	
646		cr.SetFontSize(9)
647		if x1-x0 >= selMinBand {
648			// the ✕, inboard of the right handle and in the same column as every
649			// other one on the page
650			kx := x1 - killIn
651			cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.85)
652			cr.SetLineWidth(1.6)
653			for _, d := range [][2]float64{{-1, -1}, {-1, 1}} {
654				cr.MoveTo(kx+3*d[0], y+selBandH/2+3*d[1])
655				cr.LineTo(kx-3*d[0], y+selBandH/2-3*d[1])
656			}
657			cr.Stroke()
658		}
659		// how long it is, which is the number a selection is usually being adjusted
660		// towards. Plain white on the blue rather than the plated text the rest of
661		// the page uses: a plate is for words that land on thumbnails and have to
662		// survive whatever is under them, and putting one here would black out most
663		// of the band it is labelling. Drawn only when it fits clear of the ✕ --
664		// truncated to "0:20 – 0:5" it would say nothing and cost the band its
665		// colour.
666		lbl := fmt.Sprintf("%s – %s  %.1fs", mmss(a), mmss(b), b-a)
667		if e := cr.TextExtents(lbl); x0+6+e.Width < x1-killIn-selKillW/2-4 {
668			cr.SetSourceRGB(1, 1, 1)
669			cr.MoveTo(x0+6, y+selBandH-5)
670			cr.ShowText(lbl)
671		}
672		// held is a solid white ring, the same two weights the effects lane uses
673		switch {
674		case ed.selOn:
675			cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.9)
676			cr.SetLineWidth(2)
677			cr.Rectangle(x0-1, y+1, x1-x0+2, selBandH-2)
678			cr.Stroke()
679		case ed.selHov:
680			cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.4)
681			cr.SetLineWidth(1.5)
682			cr.Rectangle(x0-1, y+1.25, x1-x0+2, selBandH-2.5)
683			cr.Stroke()
684		}
685	}

10	// Folding dropped stretches, IDE-style: a folded gap is drawn with no width
11	// (foldPx), so its clips meet border to border; everything follows because
12	// xOf/tAt walk the cells (layoutPx). A fold is a view, not an edit -- no undo
13	// step -- but is kept with the cut (cutFile.Folds).
14	//
15	// Drags open it: a press that can MOVE something opens the folds around it
16	// while the button is down (foldOpen/foldShut), so the drag runs on the
17	// ordinary timeline and the merge at its end is the usual one. The view is
18	// anchored on the pressed second across both, as the wheel zoom anchors on the
19	// cursor.
20	
21	const (
22		// foldPx: a folded stretch has NO width; the two clips meet border to
23		// border. A press on the seam opens it (foldOpen); which border it means is
24		// the side it lands on (bandClipPartAt).
25		foldPx = 0.0
26		// a gap with no room to draw the − in is not offered one: the badge would
27		// be wider than the thing it folds, and would sit on both its neighbours.
28		foldMin = 2 * segKillHit
29	)
30	
31	// foldGap is one dropped stretch and whether it is folded: what the − and +
32	// are drawn on, and what a press on one toggles.
33	type foldGap struct {
34		t0, t1 float64
35		on     bool
36	}
37	
38	// foldGaps is every stretch the cut drops, in order, each saying whether it is
39	// folded. The head of a run before its first clip and the tail after its last
40	// are dropped stretches like any other and fold like any other.
41	func (ed *cutEditor) foldGaps() []foldGap {
42		var out []foldGap
43		for _, g := range ed.droppedSpans() {
44			out = append(out, foldGap{g[0], g[1], ed.foldedGap(g[0], g[1])})
45		}
46		return out
47	}
48	
49	// foldedGap is whether a stretch is folded: a stored fold that OVERLAPS it,
50	// rather than one that matches its ends.
51	//
52	// Trimming a clip moves the edge of the gap beside it, splitting one moves a
53	// gap's whole middle, and a fold matched by its ends would be lost to both. It
54	// is the gap between these two clips that is folded, and overlap is how that
55	// survives the cut being worked on.
56	func (ed *cutEditor) foldedGap(t0, t1 float64) bool {
57		for _, f := range ed.folds {
58			if f[1] > t0 && f[0] < t1 {
59				return true
60			}
61		}
62		return false
63	}
64	
65	// syncFolds rewrites the stored list to the gaps as they now are: one entry
66	// per folded gap, at that gap's own bounds, and nothing for a gap that no
67	// longer exists. Called wherever the cut changes shape, so what is stored
68	// cannot drift away from what is drawn.
69	func (ed *cutEditor) syncFolds() {
70		if len(ed.folds) == 0 {
71			return
72		}
73		var out [][2]float64
74		for _, g := range ed.foldGaps() {
75			if g.on && !ed.wholeRun(g.t0, g.t1) {
76				out = append(out, [2]float64{g.t0, g.t1})
77			}
78		}
79		ed.folds = out
80	}
81	
82	// wholeRun is whether a gap has swallowed an entire recording: nothing kept
83	// before or after it. A fold is remembered by overlap, which would otherwise
84	// carry it through the cut being emptied and collapse the whole page to one
85	// strip. A fold is a gap BETWEEN scenes; with none either side it is not one.
86	func (ed *cutEditor) wholeRun(t0, t1 float64) bool {
87		for _, r := range ed.runs() {
88			if t0 <= r.t0+0.01 && t1 >= r.t1-0.01 {
89				return true
90			}
91		}
92		return false
93	}
94	
95	// cells is the filmed runs cut into the pieces the page lays out: a run with a
96	// folded gap in it becomes the stretch before, the fold, and the stretch
97	// after. Only folds are cut on -- an unfolded gap is drawn to scale like the
98	// footage around it, and cutting there would be a boundary nothing needs.
99	func (ed *cutEditor) cells() []tlSpan {
100		var out []tlSpan
101		for _, run := range ed.runs() {
102			at := run.t0
103			for _, g := range ed.foldGaps() {
104				if !g.on || g.t1 <= at || g.t0 >= run.t1 {
105					continue
106				}
107				t0, t1 := math.Max(g.t0, at), math.Min(g.t1, run.t1)
108				if t0 > at {
109					out = append(out, tlSpan{t0: at, t1: t0})
110				}
111				out = append(out, tlSpan{t0: t0, t1: t1, fold: true})
112				at = t1
113			}
114			// at == run.t0 is "nothing folded here": the run is one cell, and it is
115			// emitted even if it has no length at all
116			if at < run.t1 || at == run.t0 {
117				out = append(out, tlSpan{t0: at, t1: run.t1})
118			}
119		}
120		return out
121	}
122	
123	// spanW is how wide a cell is drawn: its seconds at the current zoom, or the
124	// one fixed width when it is folded.
125	func (ed *cutEditor) spanW(s tlSpan) float64 {
126		if s.fold {
127			return foldPx
128		}
129		return s.dur() * ed.pps
130	}

132	// foldAt is the folded cell covering a session second, or nil.
133	func (ed *cutEditor) foldAt(t float64) *tlSpan {
134		for i := range ed.spans {
135			if s := &ed.spans[i]; s.fold && t >= s.t0 && t < s.t1 {
136				return s
137			}
138		}
139		return nil
140	}

142	// cellsOf is the cells a stretch of session time is drawn across: one for a
143	// stretch with no fold in it, and the pieces either side of every fold that
144	// cuts through it. What is drawn IN each is the caller's own business -- the
145	// pictures skip the folded ones, the waveforms skip them, and both walk the
146	// rest at that cell's own origin, because px is only linear in time inside a
147	// cell (xOf).
148	func (ed *cutEditor) cellsOf(t0, t1 float64) []tlSpan {
149		var out []tlSpan
150		for _, s := range ed.spans {
151			if s.fold || s.t1 <= t0 || s.t0 >= t1 {
152				continue
153			}
154			out = append(out, s)
155		}
156		return out
157	}

159	// ---- the − and the + ---------------------------------------------------------
160	
161	// foldBadge is one gap's control: where it is drawn, and which way it goes.
162	// The + of a folded gap sits on the seam itself -- the two bars either side
163	// meet at one x, and that x is the only mark on the page saying the footage
164	// between them is still there; the − of an unfolded one sits in the middle of
165	// the gap, where there is nothing else to press.
166	type foldBadge struct {
167		gap    foldGap
168		cx, cy float64 // timeline x, and the middle of the selection band
169	}
170	
171	// foldBadges is one per gap worth offering: a gap with no room for the badge
172	// itself gets none (foldMin).
173	func (ed *cutEditor) foldBadges() []foldBadge {
174		var out []foldBadge
175		cy := ed.selBandTop() + selBandH/2
176		for _, g := range ed.foldGaps() {
177			x0, x1 := ed.xOf(g.t0), ed.xOf(g.t1)
178			if !g.on && x1-x0 < foldMin {
179				continue
180			}
181			out = append(out, foldBadge{g, ed.foldBadgeX(g, x0, x1), cy})
182		}
183		return out
184	}

186	// foldBadgeX: the badge sits in the middle of the gap it folds, wherever that
187	// gap is. Its ends are grips, and its middle is the one part of it a press can
188	// only mean one thing on.
189	//
190	// Two gaps do not get that: the one that opens the tape and the one that closes
191	// it. Their middle is an arbitrary point in the void -- they are the longest
192	// gaps on the page -- and their far end IS the edge of the page, where a badge
193	// floats in black with nothing to say which timeline it is on. So those go just
194	// INSIDE the clip they run up against, killIn from the border and never past
195	// that clip's middle, which is its ✕. A gap with no room for the badge at all,
196	// a folded one drawn as a seam (foldPx), goes the same way.
197	//
198	// EVERY head and tail used to take that fallback, on the grounds that a gap at
199	// a recording's own edge is "not between anything". Between two recordings it
200	// is: the tail of one take and the head of the next are two separate foldable
201	// stretches with the unfilmed border between them, and pinning both badges to
202	// the inner ends of the bars drew them as one gap wearing a control at each
203	// end. They are two gaps, and each one now says so by wearing its own.
204	func (ed *cutEditor) foldBadgeX(g foldGap, x0, x1 float64) float64 {
205		mid := (x0 + x1) / 2
206		opens, closes := ed.endsOfTape(g)
207		if x1-x0 < foldMin || opens || closes {
208			head, tail := ed.headTail(g)
209			switch {
210			case head:
211				mid = ed.insideBar(g.t1, true)
212			case tail:
213				mid = ed.insideBar(g.t0, false)
214			}
215		}
216		const plate = segKillR + segKillPad
217		return math.Max(plate, math.Min(mid, ed.totalW-plate))
218	}

220	// endsOfTape says whether a gap is the one that opens the whole tape or the one
221	// that closes it -- the two whose far end is the edge of the page. Asked of the
222	// filmed runs, not of the clock: a session begins when the first camera started
223	// rolling, and the hours before that are not a gap anyone can see.
224	func (ed *cutEditor) endsOfTape(g foldGap) (opens, closes bool) {
225		runs := ed.runs()
226		if len(runs) == 0 {
227			return false, false
228		}
229		first, last := runs[0].t0, runs[0].t1
230		for _, r := range runs[1:] {
231			first = math.Min(first, r.t0)
232			last = math.Max(last, r.t1)
233		}
234		return g.t0 <= first+0.01, g.t1 >= last-0.01
235	}

237	// insideBar is a point killIn inside the kept clip that starts (or ends) at
238	// second t, and no further in than that clip's own middle. With no clip there
239	// -- an empty cut is one gap and no bars -- it is the border itself.
240	func (ed *cutEditor) insideBar(t float64, start bool) float64 {
241		for _, s := range ed.segs {
242			if s.isInsert() {
243				continue
244			}
245			if start && math.Abs(s.S-t) < 0.01 {
246				x0, x1 := ed.xOf(s.S), ed.xOf(s.E)
247				return math.Min(x0+killIn, (x0+x1)/2)
248			}
249			if !start && math.Abs(s.E-t) < 0.01 {
250				x0, x1 := ed.xOf(s.S), ed.xOf(s.E)
251				return math.Max(x1-killIn, (x0+x1)/2)
252			}
253		}
254		return ed.xOf(t)
255	}

257	// headTail says whether a gap opens a filmed run or closes one: the stretch
258	// before that recording's first kept clip, and the one after its last.
259	func (ed *cutEditor) headTail(g foldGap) (head, tail bool) {
260		for _, r := range ed.runs() {
261			if math.Abs(g.t0-r.t0) < 0.01 {
262				head = true
263			}
264			if math.Abs(g.t1-r.t1) < 0.01 {
265				tail = true
266			}
267		}
268		return head, tail
269	}

271	// foldBadgeAt is the gap whose badge is under a press at timeline-x px, or -1
272	// into foldBadges.
273	func (ed *cutEditor) foldBadgeAt(px, y float64) int {
274		for i, b := range ed.foldBadges() {

283	// pointer under the pointer: everything right of the gap moves, so anchor

288			return

290		g := badges[i].gap
291		t := ed.tAt(anchor)
292		if g.on {
293			ed.unfold(g.t0, g.t1)
294		} else {
295			ed.folds = append(ed.folds, [2]float64{g.t0, g.t1})
296		}
297		ed.foldLayout(t, anchor)
298		ed.persist()

300			ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("unfolded %s – %s (%s)", mmss(g.t0), mmss(g.t1), ed.spanSecs(g.t0, g.t1)))
301			return
302		}
303		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("folded %s – %s (%s)", mmss(g.t0), mmss(g.t1), ed.spanSecs(g.t0, g.t1)))
304	}

306	// unfold drops every stored fold overlapping a stretch.
307	func (ed *cutEditor) unfold(t0, t1 float64) {
308		var out [][2]float64
309		for _, f := range ed.folds {
310			if f[1] > t0 && f[0] < t1 {
311				continue
312			}
313			out = append(out, f)
314		}
315		ed.folds = out
316	}

318	// foldLayout re-lays the timeline out and puts session second t back at
319	// timeline x, which is the same trick the wheel zooms about the cursor with
320	// (zoomAt). Everything right of a fold moves when it opens or closes; this is
321	// what keeps the thing being pressed from moving with it.
322	func (ed *cutEditor) foldLayout(t, x float64) {
323		ed.layoutPx()
324		ed.syncScroll()
325		ed.setOff(ed.xOf(t) - (x - ed.viewX))
326		ed.redrawTracks()

329	// drawFoldBadges paints the − and the + on the selection band, over the bars.
330	func (ed *cutEditor) drawFoldBadges(cr *cairo.Context, vx0, vx1 float64) {
331		for i, b := range ed.foldBadges() {
332			if b.cx < vx0-segKillHit || b.cx > vx1+segKillHit {
333				continue
334			}
335			mark := "−"
336			if b.gap.on {
337				mark = "+"
338			}
339			foldPlate(cr, b.cx, b.cy, mark, ed.foldHov == i)
340		}

343	// foldPlate is the badge itself: the plate every control on this page wears
344	// (drawKillBadge), with a bar or a cross on it rather than the ✕. Lit under
345	// the pointer like the rest of them, and not red -- folding takes nothing
346	// away.
347	func foldPlate(cr *cairo.Context, cx, cy float64, mark string, hot bool) {
348		if hot {
349			hotPlate(cr, cx, cy, segKillR+segKillPad)
350		} else {
351			plate(cr, cx, cy, segKillR+segKillPad, 0.06, 0.06, 0.07, 0.55)
352		}
353		cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.92)
354		cr.SetLineWidth(1.6)
355		cr.MoveTo(cx-segKillR, cy)
356		cr.LineTo(cx+segKillR, cy)
357		if mark == "+" {
358			cr.MoveTo(cx, cy-segKillR)
359			cr.LineTo(cx, cy+segKillR)
360		}
361		cr.Stroke()
362	}

367		i := -1

369			i = ed.foldBadgeAt(x+ed.viewX, y)

381	// walkFold opens the fold the line has walked into: ▶ plays the footage,
382	// dropped stretches included, and a seam shown while the line is inside it
383	// lies about where the line is. ▶✂ never enters one. It stays open afterwards
384	// -- refolding under a running line would pull the page sideways.
385	func (ed *cutEditor) walkFold() {
386		s := ed.foldAt(ed.playhead)
387		if s == nil {
388			return
389		}
390		t0, t1 := s.t0, s.t1
391		x := ed.xOf(ed.playhead)
392		ed.unfold(t0, t1)
393		ed.foldLayout(ed.playhead, x)
394		ed.persist()
395		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("unfolded %s — ▶ ran into it", mmss(t0)))

398	// foldOpen opens the folds a press could drag something into or out of -- the
399	// one under it and either side of what it grabbed -- for as long as the button
400	// is down, and returns what foldShut needs to put them back.
401	func (ed *cutEditor) foldOpen(a, b, px float64) []foldGap {
402		reach := foldReach / math.Max(ed.pps, 0.001)
403		var shut []foldGap
404		for _, g := range ed.foldGaps() {
405			if g.on && g.t1 >= a-reach && g.t0 <= b+reach {
406				shut = append(shut, g)
407			}
408		}
409		if len(shut) == 0 {
410			return nil
411		}
412		t := ed.tAt(px)
413		for _, g := range shut {
414			ed.unfold(g.t0, g.t1)
415		}
416		ed.foldLayout(t, px)
417		return shut
418	}

420	// foldReach is how far past what is held a fold still counts as reachable, in
421	// px: the grab itself, so the seam AT the end of a clip being dragged opens
422	// with it and the next one along does not.
423	const foldReach = edgeGrab
424	
425	// foldShut folds back what foldOpen opened, once the button is up, anchored on
426	// the second under the pointer so the page does not jump out from under the
427	// hand that just let go.
428	//
429	// A gap the drag CLOSED -- a clip grown across it, two clips merged -- is gone,
430	// and folding it back would fold whatever gap now overlaps where it was. So
431	// each one is only put back if it is still a dropped stretch of its own.
432	func (ed *cutEditor) foldShut(shut []foldGap, px float64) {
433		if len(shut) == 0 {
434			return
435		}
436		t := ed.tAt(px)
437		gaps := ed.foldGaps()
438		for _, g := range shut {
439			for _, now := range gaps {
440				if now.t0 < g.t1 && now.t1 > g.t0 && now.t1-now.t0 > 0.05 {
441					ed.folds = append(ed.folds, [2]float64{now.t0, now.t1})
442					break
443				}
444			}
445		}
446		ed.syncFolds()
447		ed.foldLayout(t, px)
448		ed.persist()
449	}

451	// The gutter: the timeline starts gutterPx in, and the black strip before it
452	// holds the permanent controls (whole-lane sound switches, row ✕, fold-all) so
453	// they never sit on footage. It is content, not a pinned column: the first
454	// gutterPx of timeline coordinate space (layoutPx), so controls are placed and
455	// pressed in timeline px and scroll away with the tape.
456	
457	const (
458		// gutterPx is how much black stands in front of second zero, and
459		// gutterMid is where a control in it is centred. Wide enough for the
460		// plates the switches wear (hearPlate, foldPlate) with a px or two either
461		// side, and no wider: it is space taken off the width the footage has.
462		gutterPx  = 30.0
463		gutterMid = gutterPx / 2
464	)
465	
466	// drawGutter fills the strip. Black rather than the band's own dark grey: the
467	// bands say "footage" and this is the one part of the page that is not, and at
468	// the zoom floor -- where the whole session is on screen and the strip is the
469	// only thing to the left of it -- a shade of the same grey would read as more
470	// timeline with nothing on it.
471	func (ed *cutEditor) drawGutter(cr *cairo.Context, top, h float64) {
472		cr.SetSourceRGB(0, 0, 0)
473		cr.Rectangle(0, top, gutterPx, h)
474		cr.Fill()
475	}
476	
477	// ---- fold the lot -----------------------------------------------------------
478	
479	// foldAllY is where the fold-all control sits: the selection band's own line,
480	// under the clock, because folding is about the gaps between the green bars
481	// that band draws.
482	func (ed *cutEditor) foldAllY() float64 { return ed.selBandTop() + selBandH/2 }
483	
484	// foldAllOn is what pressing it would do: with anything folded it opens
485	// everything, and only with nothing folded does it fold. One press to get the
486	// page back is worth more than one press to fold the last gap -- and a control
487	// that reads "+" while half the page is folded and half is not would be lying
488	// about the half it is not.
489	func (ed *cutEditor) foldAllOn() bool { return len(ed.folds) > 0 }
490	
491	// foldAllAt is whether a press in the gutter is on it.
492	func (ed *cutEditor) foldAllAt(px, y float64) bool {
493		return len(ed.foldGaps()) > 0 &&
494			math.Abs(px-gutterMid) <= segKillHit && math.Abs(y-ed.foldAllY()) <= segKillHit
495	}
496	
497	// toggleFoldAll folds every dropped stretch away, or brings them all back.
498	//
499	// The view is anchored the way one gap's own badge anchors it (toggleFold):
500	// the second at the left of the page stays at the left of the page, so folding
501	// the lot pulls the timeline in around what you were looking at rather than
502	// throwing it somewhere else entirely.
503	func (ed *cutEditor) toggleFoldAll() {
504		gaps := ed.foldGaps()
505		if len(gaps) == 0 {
506			return
507		}
508		t := ed.tAt(ed.viewX + gutterPx)
509		on := ed.foldAllOn()
510		n := 0
511		if on {
512			ed.folds = nil
513			n = len(gaps)
514		} else {
515			for _, g := range gaps {
516				ed.folds = append(ed.folds, [2]float64{g.t0, g.t1})
517				n++
518			}
519			ed.syncFolds() // a gap that is a whole recording is not one to fold (wholeRun)
520			n = len(ed.folds)
521		}
522		ed.foldLayout(t, ed.xOf(t))
523		ed.persist()
524		if on {
525			ed.a.setStatus("unfolded " + plural(n, "seam"))
526			return
527		}
528		ed.a.setStatus("folded " + plural(n, "seam"))
529	}
530	
531	// drawFoldAll paints it: the same − and + a single gap's badge wears, because
532	// it is the same verb over all of them.
533	func (ed *cutEditor) drawFoldAll(cr *cairo.Context) {
534		if len(ed.foldGaps()) == 0 {
535			return
536		}
537		mark := "−"
538		if ed.foldAllOn() {
539			mark = "+"
540		}
541		foldPlate(cr, gutterMid, ed.foldAllY(), mark, ed.foldAllHov)
542	}
543	
544	// gutterCtl is whether a press landed on a control in the strip: the fold-all
545	// badge, a lane's sound switch, a row strip's switch, an emptied row's ✕.
546	// Every second in the gutter is second zero, so a press on a control must not
547	// also cue the line there; only the black between them is a place for the line.
548	func (ed *cutEditor) gutterCtl(px, y float64) bool {
549		if px > gutterPx {
550			return false
551		}
552		return ed.foldAllAt(px, y) || ed.laneSwitchAt(px, y) != "" ||
553			ed.pairSwitchAt(px, y) != nil || ed.rowKillAt(px, y) >= 0
554	}
555	
556	// hoverFoldAll lights it under the pointer, like every other badge here.
557	func (ed *cutEditor) hoverFoldAll(x, y float64) {
558		on := x >= 0 && ed.foldAllAt(x+ed.viewX, y)
559		if on != ed.foldAllHov {
560			ed.foldAllHov = on
561			if ed.srcArea != nil {
562				ed.srcArea.QueueDraw()
563			}
564		}
565	}

205	// keepFilmed drops what cannot be shown: a segment with no recording at either

208	func (a *App) keepFilmed(segs []cutSeg) []cutSeg {

213			if !s.isInsert() && a.ed.videoAt(s.S) == nil && a.ed.videoAt(s.E) == nil {

224	// rejecting a two-segment answer to a 25 s target burns attempts on a rule
225	// the target itself contradicts.
226	func minSuggestSegs(target float64) int {

3	// One written line into a spoken wav: the page's only path off this machine.
4	// The wav is named after everything that went into it (ttsKey), so the same
5	// line comes back the same and a take on disk is the answer; rerolling changes
6	// the seed. The emotion tag (emoTerm..emoOpts) maps a word, or two with
7	// weights, onto the server's eight-axis vector, forgiving: an unknown tag is
8	// spoken plainly rather than refused.

12		"crypto/sha1"
13		"encoding/binary"

27	//
28	// The server itself lives in audiocpp.go: it does the listening for Prepare too,
29	// and the parts below are only what speaking adds to it.
30	
31	// ttsModelID is the model the narration is spoken through: the id set in
32	// Settings (default index-tts2), verified once per session against the
33	// server's catalog -- a guessed or stale id would otherwise come back as an
34	// error that reads like a broken model.
35	func (a *App) ttsModelID() (string, error) {
36		if a.ttsModel != "" {
37			return a.ttsModel, nil
38		}
39		c := a.readConf()
40		cat, err := audioCatalog(a.audioURL(), c.TTSKey)
41		if err != nil {
42			return "", err
43		}
44		want := c.TTSModel
45		m, ok := cat[want]
46		if !ok {
47			return "", fmt.Errorf("the audio.cpp server at %s serves %s, but not %q -- "+
48				"the TTS model set in Settings", a.audioURL(), catalogIDs(cat), want)
49		}
50		// only a cloning model: that server also serves the ASR and diarization
51		// models, and either would take the job and fail at it
52		if m.Task != "" && m.Task != "clon" && m.Family != "index_tts2" {
53			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q on %s is declared task %q -- it cannot clone a voice",
54				want, a.audioURL(), m.Task)
55		}
56		a.ttsModel = want
57		return want, nil
58	}
