60	// ttsKey names one take: everything that decides how this line comes back.
61	// The voice, pitch included, is part of it -- changing either must not serve
62	// the old speaker from cache, and must not throw the old speaker's lines away
63	// either; switch back and they are all still there. So is the emotion blend
64	// (emoAlpha): a stronger blend is a different performance of the same words,
65	// and serving the tamer one would make the constant a lie. So is Roll, which
66	// is the user saying "same line, different draw".
67	func (a *App) ttsKey(e narrEntry) string {
68		// A weighted tag is keyed by the mix it resolves to, not its spelling: the
69		// mapping moves ("excited" changed), and "angry=1" and "furious=1" are one
70		// take. Unweighted tags keep their old key -- they go to the judge as words.
71		emo := e.Emotion
72		if vec, ok := emoVector(emo); ok {
73			emo = vec
74		}
75		// the default voice keeps the key it had before the voice picker existed, so a project
76		// narrated back then does not re-speak every line the first time it opens
77		key := e.Text + "|" + emo
78		if v := a.voiceKey(); v != ownVoice {
79			key = v + "|" + key
80		}
81		if e.Roll > 0 { // a line never re-rolled keeps the key it already has
82			key = strconv.Itoa(e.Roll) + "#" + key
83		}
84		// "25e" says which performer and what reached it: 2.5 weights, with the
85		// emotion actually delivered. Everything before this prefix is either the
86		// 2.0 voice or a flat read from the era when the request carried the
87		// emotion in a field the server ignored -- neither may be served as the
88		// current take.
89		return "25e" + emoAlpha + "|" + key
90	}
91	
92	// ttsWav is where that take lives.
93	func (a *App) ttsWav(e narrEntry) string {
94		h := sha1.Sum([]byte(a.ttsKey(e)))
95		return filepath.Join(a.narrateDir(), "tts", fmt.Sprintf("%x.wav", h[:8]))
96	}
97	
98	// ttsSeed is the take's random seed, cut from the same digest as its filename:
99	// one filename, one seed, and only what moves the filename (words, emotion,
100	// voice, re-roll) moves it. Left alone, the engine draws a fresh seed per
101	// request.
102	func ttsSeed(key string) uint32 {
103		h := sha1.Sum([]byte(key))
104		return binary.BigEndian.Uint32(h[8:12])
105	}
106	
107	// synthesize speaks one entry through the resident server into the cache.
108	func (a *App) synthesize(e narrEntry) error {
109		k := a.ttsKey(e)
110		return a.speak(e.Text, e.Emotion, ttsSeed(k), a.ttsWav(e))
111	}
112	
113	// The eight bases the engine mixes, in the order it wants them. Everything a
114	// line can ask for is a point in this space; the names below are only the doors
115	// into it. The kin lists are deliberately generous -- someone writing "furious"
116	// or "deadpan" means one of these eight, and refusing them would send the line
117	// down the slower path for a spelling.
118	var emoBases = [8][]string{
119		{"happy", "happiness", "joy", "joyful", "cheerful", "glad", "delighted", "upbeat", "pleased"},
120		{"angry", "anger", "mad", "furious", "fury", "rage", "annoyed", "irritated", "indignant"},
121		{"sad", "sadness", "unhappy", "sorrow", "sorrowful", "hurt", "crying", "tearful"},
122		{"afraid", "fear", "fearful", "scared", "frightened", "terrified", "nervous", "anxious", "panicked"},
123		{"disgusted", "disgust", "revolted", "repulsed", "grossed"},
124		{"melancholic", "melancholy", "low", "gloomy", "down", "depressed", "depression", "wistful", "weary"},
125		{"surprised", "surprise", "shocked", "amazed", "astonished", "startled", "stunned"},
126		{"natural", "neutral", "calm", "deadpan", "flat", "plain", "even", "relaxed", "matter-of-fact"},
127	}
128	
129	// emoTerm resolves one word to its base, -1 if it is none of them.
130	func emoTerm(w string) int {
131		w = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(w))
132		for i, kin := range emoBases {
133			for _, k := range kin {
134				if w == k {
135					return i
136				}
137			}
138		}
139		return -1
140	}
141	
142	// The blends: mixes over the eight bases that no single base reaches --
143	// "excited" is happy plus surprise, not a kin of happy. Recipes, not synonyms;
144	// every recipe peaks at 1 so a weight means the same as on a base. Nothing
145	// outside the eight axes can be invented (smug, sarcastic, whispered stay on
146	// the judge's side).
147	var emoBlends = []struct {
148		Kin []string
149		V   [8]float64 // happy, angry, sad, afraid, disgusted, melancholic, surprised, calm
150	}{
151		{[]string{"excited", "thrilled", "exhilarated", "eager", "enthusiastic"}, [8]float64{0: 1, 6: 0.55}},
152		{[]string{"ecstatic", "overjoyed", "elated", "jubilant"}, [8]float64{0: 1, 6: 0.8}},
153		{[]string{"playful", "amused", "teasing", "cheeky"}, [8]float64{0: 1, 6: 0.3, 7: 0.35}},
154		{[]string{"proud", "triumphant", "victorious"}, [8]float64{0: 1, 7: 0.4}},
155		{[]string{"relieved", "reassured"}, [8]float64{0: 0.6, 7: 1}},
156		{[]string{"hopeful", "encouraging", "optimistic"}, [8]float64{0: 0.7, 7: 1}},
157		{[]string{"tender", "warm", "affectionate", "gentle", "fond"}, [8]float64{0: 0.5, 7: 1}},
158		{[]string{"nostalgic", "bittersweet", "reminiscent"}, [8]float64{0: 0.4, 5: 1}},
159		{[]string{"solemn", "grave", "reverent", "serious"}, [8]float64{1: 0.3, 5: 0.45, 7: 1}},
160		{[]string{"awed", "awestruck", "breathless", "wonder"}, [8]float64{0: 0.5, 3: 0.25, 6: 1}},
161		{[]string{"alarmed", "urgent", "frantic"}, [8]float64{3: 0.85, 6: 1}},
162		{[]string{"horrified", "appalled", "aghast"}, [8]float64{3: 1, 4: 0.7, 6: 0.5}},
163		{[]string{"desperate", "pleading", "begging"}, [8]float64{2: 0.7, 3: 1}},
164		{[]string{"confused", "puzzled", "baffled", "bewildered", "perplexed"}, [8]float64{3: 0.3, 6: 1, 7: 0.4}},
165		{[]string{"frustrated", "exasperated"}, [8]float64{1: 1, 4: 0.35, 5: 0.5}},
166		{[]string{"bitter", "resentful", "sullen"}, [8]float64{1: 0.7, 4: 0.4, 5: 1}},
167		{[]string{"contemptuous", "scornful", "sneering", "dismissive"}, [8]float64{1: 0.6, 4: 1}},
168		{[]string{"dismayed", "crestfallen", "disappointed"}, [8]float64{2: 1, 6: 0.5}},
169		{[]string{"heartbroken", "devastated", "grief", "anguished"}, [8]float64{2: 1, 5: 0.8}},
170		{[]string{"ominous", "foreboding", "menacing"}, [8]float64{1: 0.3, 3: 0.5, 7: 1}},
171		{[]string{"tense", "suspenseful", "wary"}, [8]float64{3: 0.7, 6: 0.35, 7: 1}},
172	}
173	
174	// emoBlend resolves one word to its recipe, ok false if it names none.
175	func emoBlend(w string) ([8]float64, bool) {
176		w = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(w))
177		for _, b := range emoBlends {
178			for _, k := range b.Kin {
179				if w == k {
180					return b.V, true
181				}
182			}
183		}
184		return [8]float64{}, false
185	}
186	
187	// emoWeights splits a tag into its name=weight pairs. weighted says whether any
188	// weight was actually written -- "[angry]" and "[angry=1]" name the same point,
189	// but only the second one asked for it, and only the second one skips the judge.
190	func emoWeights(tag string) (parts []struct {
191		Name string
192		W    float64
193	}, weighted bool) {
194		for _, f := range strings.Split(tag, ",") {
195			f = strings.TrimSpace(f)
196			if f == "" {
197				continue
198			}
199			name, w := f, 1.0
200			if i := strings.IndexByte(f, '='); i >= 0 {
201				v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(f[i+1:]), 64)
202				if err != nil || math.IsNaN(v) || math.IsInf(v, 0) {
203					return nil, false // a weight that is not a number is not a weight
204				}
205				name, w, weighted = strings.TrimSpace(f[:i]), math.Max(0, math.Min(1, v)), true
206			}
207			parts = append(parts, struct {
208				Name string
209				W    float64
210			}{name, w})
211		}
212		return parts, weighted
213	}
214	
215	// emoVector turns a weighted tag into the eight floats the engine takes
216	// directly. emotion_text goes through a small judge model (a guess, diluted by
217	// every non-emotion word); a vector is exact and repeatable. Weights are the
218	// opt-in: a bare "[angry]" still goes through the judge. Bases, kin and blends
219	// reach a vector; anything else falls back to the text path.
220	func emoVector(tag string) (string, bool) {
221		parts, weighted := emoWeights(tag)
222		if !weighted || len(parts) == 0 {
223			return "", false
224		}
225		var v [8]float64
226		sum := 0.0
227		for _, p := range parts {
228			if i := emoTerm(p.Name); i >= 0 {
229				v[i] = math.Max(v[i], p.W) // named twice: the louder ask wins
230				sum += p.W
231				continue
232			}
233			// not one of the eight, but possibly a mix of them: a blend spends its
234			// weight across several axes at once, scaled so "=0.5" is the same
235			// recipe read half as hard
236			mix, ok := emoBlend(p.Name)
237			if !ok {
238				return "", false
239			}
240			for i, f := range mix {
241				v[i] = math.Max(v[i], f*p.W)
242				sum += f * p.W
243			}
244		}
245		if sum <= 0 {
246			return "", false // "[angry=0]" asks for nothing; let the judge read the line
247		}
248		out := make([]string, 8)
249		for i, f := range v {
250			// three decimals: a blend scaled by a weight lands on numbers like
251			// 0.16499999999999998, and this string is both what the engine reads
252			// and part of the take's name (ttsKey) -- neither wants the tail
253			out[i] = strconv.FormatFloat(math.Round(f*1000)/1000, 'g', -1, 64)
254		}
255		return strings.Join(out, ","), true
256	}
257	
258	// emoText is what the judge sees: the same tag with the weights taken off, so a
259	// tag that named an axis this client does not know ("[wistful=1, smug=0.3]")
260	// still arrives as words it can score.
261	func emoText(tag string) string {
262		parts, weighted := emoWeights(tag)
263		if !weighted {
264			return tag
265		}
266		names := make([]string, 0, len(parts))
267		for _, p := range parts {
268			names = append(names, p.Name)
269		}
270		return strings.Join(names, ", ")
271	}
272	
273	// emoOpts is the request's options block. The emotion belongs HERE: the speech
274	// endpoint drops unknown top-level fields (a top-level "emotion" was silently
275	// ignored for a long time). emotion_text needs use_emotion_text; emotion_vector
276	// needs no switch; the engine tests use_emotion_text FIRST, so exactly one
277	// branch is sent.
278	func emoOpts(emotion string) map[string]any {
279		opts := map[string]any{"emotion_alpha": emoAlpha}
280		tag := strings.TrimSpace(emotion)
281		if tag == "" {
282			return opts
283		}
284		if vec, ok := emoVector(tag); ok {
285			// alpha is a multiplier over the weights, not a separate dial: the
286			// engine scales every value by it and fills the remainder with the
287			// speaker's own reading. At 0.85 a written "angry=1" would arrive as
288			// 0.85 anger and 0.15 of whatever the sample sounds like, which is the
289			// one thing an exact weight is written to prevent. So the weighted path
290			// sends 1 and lets the number mean itself; "=0.85" is then the same
291			// intensity a plain word gets.
292			opts["emotion_vector"] = vec
293			opts["emotion_alpha"] = "1"
294			return opts
295		}
296		opts["use_emotion_text"] = "true"
297		opts["emotion_text"] = emoText(tag)
298		return opts
299	}
300	
301	// speak is the one call that reaches the model: text in, wav at out. The voice
302	// sample at the top of this page and the narration lines below it go through it
303	// identically, so a sample is a true preview -- same server, same reference,
304	// same settings.
305	func (a *App) speak(text, emotion string, seed uint32, out string) error {
306		if err := a.ensureVoiceRef(); err != nil {
307			return err
308		}
309		if err := a.ensureAudioServer(); err != nil {
310			return err
311		}
312		model, err := a.ttsModelID()
313		if err != nil {
314			return err
315		}
316		opts := emoOpts(emotion)
317		opts["seed"] = strconv.FormatUint(uint64(seed), 10)
318		// the reference goes up like any other file the server has to open -- it is
319		// the same wav on every line, but see serverFile on why it is not remembered
320		ref, err := a.serverFile(a.refPath())
321		if err != nil {
322			return err
323		}
324		body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
325			"model":     model,
326			"input":     text,
327			"voice_ref": ref,
328			"language":  "en",
329			"options":   opts,
330		})
331		req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", a.audioURL()+"/v1/audio/speech", bytes.NewReader(body))
332		if err != nil {
333			return err
334		}
335		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
336		bearer(req, a.readConf().TTSKey)
337		resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
338		if err != nil {
339			return err
340		}
341		defer resp.Body.Close()
342		data, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
343		if resp.StatusCode != 200 || len(data) < 1000 {
344			return fmt.Errorf("tts (%s): %.300s", resp.Status, string(data))
345		}
346		os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(out), 0o755)
347		return os.WriteFile(out, data, 0o644)
348	}
349	
350	// syncSpeakIcons draws the per-line buttons: the running row shows ⏸, every
351	// other ▶. Running is three states: the voice sounding on that row; the row
352	// auditioning with its picture rolling before any sound (the audio pipeline
353	// reports playing only after preroll); or the audition waiting for a line
354	// never spoken.
355	func (n *narrator) syncSpeakIcons() {
356		live := n.livePlayRow()
357		n.liveRow = live
358		rolling := n.soloPic && n.player != nil && n.player.Playing()
359		for i, r := range n.rows {
360			// a clip with no line plays too, on its own audio -- so its ▶ says that
361			// rather than promising a line that is not there
362			tip := "play this clip with its line spoken over it"
363			if i < len(n.entries) && strings.TrimSpace(n.entries[i].Text) == "" {
364				tip = "play this clip — it has no line, so you hear the game"
365			}
366			setPlayIcon(r.speak, i == live || (i == n.solo && (rolling || n.synthing)), tip, "pause this clip")
367		}
368	}
369	
370	// livePlayRow is the row the ⏸ belongs on: the row under the playhead while
371	// the picture rolls, not the row whose wav is on the voice player -- the two
372	// differ between lines, where the ⏸ used to stick. A wordless row counts,
373	// since it plays like any other (speakEntry).
374	func (n *narrator) livePlayRow() int {
375		i := -1
376		switch {
377		case n.player != nil && n.player.Playing():
378			i = n.nearestEntry(n.pos)
379		case n.voice != nil && n.voice.Playing():
380			i = n.speaking // a line spoken over a still frame: no picture to follow
381		}
382		if !n.has(i) {
383			return -1
384		}
385		return i
386	}
387	
388	// rerollEntry asks for another take of a line whose words are right: it moves
389	// the seed (and so the key) and lets the audition speak it through the normal
390	// path. The old take stays on disk -- a re-roll can come back worse or fail.
391	func (a *App) rerollEntry(i int) {
392		n := a.narr
393		n.pullRows()
394		if !n.has(i) {
395			return
396		}
397		if strings.TrimSpace(n.entries[i].Text) == "" {
398			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("clip %d has no line to re-roll", i+1))
399			return
400		}
401		if a.captionsOnly() {
402			a.setStatus("no audio is chosen — a caption has no take to re-roll")
403			return
404		}
405		n.entries[i].Roll++
406		n.save()
407		n.rebuildRows() // the end time is an estimate again until the new take exists
408		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("line %d: new take, speaking it", i+1))
409		a.speakEntry(i)
410	}
411	
412	// pausePress is whether pressing row i's button means "pause it" -- the same
413	// question syncSpeakIcons draws the face from, asked in one place. Only the
414	// picture, not the voice: a line over a still frame is voice.Toggle's.
415	func (n *narrator) pausePress(i int) bool {
416		return n.player != nil && n.player.Playing() && n.livePlayRow() == i
417	}
418	
419	// speakEntry auditions one line: the clip it was written for, played with the
420	// line spoken over it, and stopping at the end of that clip. A line read over a
421	// frozen frame is not what it was written against -- half of judging a line is
422	// whether it lands on what is happening -- and this button used to give you
423	// exactly that. Clicked again it pauses, and again resumes, the picture and the
424	// voice together. Another line's button interrupts it, which is what a list of
425	// lines to audition wants: one click, not stop-then-play.
426	func (a *App) speakEntry(i int) {
427		n := a.narr
428		n.pullRows()
429		if !n.has(i) {
430			return
431		}
432		// The ⏸ a row is showing means that row, whatever is written on it. Only
433		// the wordless branch below ever asked, so pressing ⏸ on a LINE that was
434		// playing fell through to the audition at the bottom and re-cued it from
435		// its lead-in -- which starts the picture again -- and it took a second
436		// press, with solo now set, to actually pause. Ahead of every branch
437		// because every kind of row can be the one under the playhead: a line, a
438		// caption, a clip with nothing written on it.
439		if n.pausePress(i) {
440			n.player.Pause()
441			if n.voice != nil {
442				n.voice.Pause()
443			}
444			n.syncSpeakIcons()
445			a.updateRunControls()
446			return
447		}
448		e := n.entries[i]
449		if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) == "" {
450			// A clip the narration left alone is still a clip of the video, and this
451			// button is "play from here" first: the picture rolls from the top of the
452			// clip and the preview carries on down the cut. No synthesis (saying nothing
453			// costs a call) and no solo -- this is a seek into the cut that plays.
454			if ed := a.ed; ed != nil && n.player != nil && ed.videoAt(e.S) != nil {
455				n.claimVoice()
456				n.playSeg, n.jumped = -1, -1
457				n.cue(e.S, true)
458				n.selectRow(i)
459				n.syncSpeakIcons()
460				a.updateRunControls()
461				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("clip %d has no line — playing it on its own audio", i+1))
462				return
463			}
464			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("clip %d has no line, and no recording covers it", i+1))
465			return
466		}
467		if a.captionsOnly() {
468			// no voice to audition: the ▶ is a seek to the line's moment, and the
469			// caption itself is judged where it is burned in -- Produce
470			if ed := a.ed; ed != nil && n.player != nil && ed.videoAt(e.S) != nil {
471				n.claimVoice()
472				n.playSeg, n.jumped = -1, -1
473				n.cue(n.leadIn(i), true)
474				n.selectRow(i)
475				n.syncSpeakIcons()
476				a.updateRunControls()
477				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("line %d is a caption — read, never spoken; playing its moment", i+1))
478				return
479			}
480			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("line %d is a caption, and no recording covers its clip", i+1))
481			return
482		}
483		// a failed line stays mute in the ticking preview so one bad request does
484		// not stall every pass -- but this ▶ is the user asking for THIS line, and
485		// that is an explicit retry
486		delete(n.synthFail, a.ttsWav(e))
487		// this line has never been spoken and the server is on it: with the picture
488		// the video is stopped waiting, without it there is nothing to play yet.
489		// Either way a second click can only start the same synthesis twice.
490		if n.solo == i && n.synthing {
491			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("still speaking line %d for the first time — ⏹ gives up on it", i+1))
492			return
493		}
494		if n.solo == i && n.soloPic && n.player != nil {
495			if n.player.Playing() {
496				n.player.Pause()
497				if n.voice != nil {
498					n.voice.Pause()
499				}
500			} else {
501				// playSeg back to -1, or the tick would see a line it has already
502				// played and run the rest of the clip mute
503				n.playSeg = -1
504				n.player.Toggle()
505			}
506			n.syncSpeakIcons()
507			a.updateRunControls()
508			return
509		}
510		// spoken over a still frame, and clicked again: pause, resume, or -- if it
511		// ran to its end -- play it again, all of which Toggle knows how to do
512		if n.voice != nil && n.solo == i && !n.soloPic && (n.voice.Playing() || n.voice.Cued()) {
513			n.voice.Toggle()
514			n.syncSpeakIcons()
515			return
516		}
517		n.claimVoice() // whatever else was sounding, this button takes over from it
518		// A seek into the preview, landing just ahead of this line. The tick does the
519		// speaking from here: it is the one thing that knows where the picture has
520		// got to, and it already knows how to wait for a line that has never been
521		// spoken (holdForSynth). What it no longer does is stop or hop when the line
522		// is over -- past its own line this is simply the preview, playing the cut.
523		if ed := a.ed; ed != nil && n.player != nil && ed.videoAt(e.S) != nil {
524			n.playSeg, n.jumped = -1, -1
525			n.solo, n.soloPic = i, true
526			// a few seconds ahead of the line, not the head of the clip: the line
527			// may sit a minute in ("at"), and a ▶ that answers with silence for a
528			// minute reads as a line that is not there. The run-in is what the
529			// audition is FOR -- seeing the moment the line was placed on arrive --
530			// and leadIn is where it may start without waking the line above
531			n.cue(n.leadIn(i), true)
532			n.selectRow(i) // the ▶ is inside the row but does not select it on its own
533			a.updateRunControls()
534			return
535		}
536		a.speakAlone(i, e)
537	}
538	
539	// speakAlone is the audition for a clip no recording covers -- a source not on
540	// this machine, or one taken off the Inputs step since the cut was made. The
541	// line is spoken over whatever the picture is showing, because that is all
542	// there is, and this path does its own synthesis: with the picture rolling that
543	// is the tick's job, and it stops the video to wait rather than speaking late.
544	func (a *App) speakAlone(i int, e narrEntry) {
545		n := a.narr
546		// claimed before the request goes out, not after it comes back: the row is
547		// this button's from the click, and the wait for a first synthesis is the
548		// part of it the user is most likely to press again
549		n.speaking, n.solo, n.soloPic, n.synthing = i, i, false, true
550		n.selectRow(i)
551		n.syncSpeakIcons()
552		a.snapSources()
553		go func() {
554			wav := a.ttsWav(e)
555			if !exists(wav) {
556				glib.IdleAdd(func() { a.setStatus("synthesizing… (first line after a cold start also loads the model)") })
557				if err := a.synthesize(e); err != nil {
558					a.logfIdle("synthesis failed: %v", err)
559					glib.IdleAdd(func() {
560						n.synthing, n.solo = false, -1
561						n.syncSpeakIcons()
562						a.setStatus("synthesis failed — see log")
563					})
564					return
565				}
566			}
567			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
568				n.synthing = false
569				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("entry %d — no recording covers this clip, so the line plays on its own", i+1))
570				if n.voice != nil {
571					n.voice.PlaySegment(wav, 0, -1, true)
572				}
573				n.syncSpeakIcons()
574			})
575		}()
576	}

3	// The audio lanes under the cut: one pair for the footage's own sound, one per
4	// separate recording. The footage is the master; a recording is placed by the
5	// wall clock (srcClock) and only the part overlapping the footage is drawn, on
6	// its own lighter ground. The footage's own track is drawn too, so a laugh in
7	// two lanes either lines up or does not. Left and right are separate lanes
8	// (one player per side is common). Blue, because every other ink here means
9	// something else.
10	
11	import (
12		"bufio"
13		"encoding/binary"
14		"fmt"
15		"io"
16		"math"
17		"os"
18		"os/exec"
19		"path/filepath"
20		"sort"
21		"strconv"
22		"strings"
23	
24		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/cairo"
25		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/glib/v2"
26	)
27	
28	const (
29		// The envelope's resolution: a hair under one pixel at the top zoom
30		// (maxPps), so the drawing never runs out of detail, and an hour of stereo
31		// is 1.4 MB of it -- small enough to keep in memory and to cache on disk
32		// without thinking about it.
33		//
34		// Every cached envelope carries the rate it was built at in its own header
35		// (waveHead.Hz) and is drawn by that, so raising this does not spoil the
36		// caches a project already has: they go on drawing correctly at 100 Hz and
37		// are rebuilt at this rate the next time their recording changes.
38		waveHz = 200.0
39		// What the decode asks ffmpeg for. Peaks of a downsampled signal are a
40		// little lower than the true ones, which does not matter for a picture, and
41		// 8 kHz is a tenth of the bytes to push through the pipe.
42		waveRate  = 8000
43		waveLaneH = 30.0 // one channel's lane
44		waveGap   = 4.0  // between one recording's lanes and the next's
45		wavePad   = 3.0  // above and below the lanes as a whole
46	)
47	
48	// tlAudio is a recording placed on the session timeline, as tlVideo is, minus
49	// the pictures. Not part of the timeline's geometry: relayout lays out the
50	// videos and the audio is drawn against that. The footage's own track is one
51	// too, master set -- side by side with it, the same shout is visibly in both
52	// lanes at the same x, which is what makes a lane readable.
53	type tlAudio struct {
54		base   string
55		path   string
56		start  float64 // session time of the lane's first second
57		off    float64 // the second of the FILE that lands there; see at
58		dur    float64
59		chans  int  // 1 or 2 lanes; more than two is downmixed to a stereo picture
60		master bool // the footage's own track: heard by the preview already
61		// which of the file's audio streams this lane is, a:N. Nought for a
62		// recording, which is one file with one track, and for the first track of a
63		// video; above nought for the rest of a multi-track capture, where the same
64		// path is on several lanes and only this tells them apart (cut_tracks.go).
65		track int
66	}
67	
68	// at is the second of the file heard at session second t (tlVideo.at for
69	// sound). off is nought for a recording; a cut lane is a WINDOW partway into a
70	// file (cut_lane.go) and its sound is that same window.
71	func (au tlAudio) at(t float64) float64 { return t - au.start + au.off }
72	
73	// soundAt says whether anything is audible at these seconds -- the capture's own
74	// track or a separate recording running under it. ed.auds is the right list to
75	// ask because it is both: masterLanes puts the footage's track in it, and only
76	// when the file actually has one.
77	func (ed *cutEditor) soundAt(t, dur float64) bool {
78		for _, au := range ed.auds {
79			if t < au.start+au.dur && t+dur > au.start {
80				return true
81			}
82		}
83		return false
84	}
85	
86	// soundOpen is whether the insert form asks what this insert does to the
87	// sound: only for a picture insert (a sound insert IS the sound). Spliced
88	// between the footage the question is own sound or silent; laid over it, own
89	// sound or the session's carrying on. A copied stretch counts as having sound.
90	func (ed *cutEditor) soundOpen(path string, at, dur float64, m insMode) bool {
91		if ed == nil || m.lane != "" || insKind(path) == "audio" {
92			return false
93		}
94		if m.splice {
95			return insHasSound(path)
96		}
97		return insHasSound(path) || ed.soundAt(at, dur)
98	}
99	
100	// insHasSound is whether the insert brings a sound of its own to decide about.
101	func insHasSound(path string) bool {
102		if _, ok := copySrc(path); ok {
103			return true // a stretch of the session: picture and what was filmed with it
104		}
105		file, _ := insSplit(path)
106		return hasAudioStream(file)
107	}
108	
109	// loadWaves fetches an envelope for every lane without one, one goroutine
110	// each; a lane draws its ground until its wave lands. Asked whenever the lanes
111	// change (setLanes). Keyed by lane name: a copied shot is one file on two lanes.
112	func (ed *cutEditor) loadWaves() {
113		if ed.audArea == nil {
114			return // no band to draw them in: an editor built for a test
115		}
116		if ed.waves == nil {
117			ed.waves = map[string]*waveform{}
118		}
119		a := ed.a
120		for _, au := range ed.auds {
121			if _, ok := ed.waves[au.base]; ok {
122				continue
123			}
124			au := au
125			go func() {
126				wf, err := loadWave(a.waveCache(), au)
127				glib.IdleAdd(func() {
128					if err != nil {
129						a.logf("no waveform for %s: %v", au.base, err)
130						return
131					}
132					ed.waves[au.base] = wf
133					ed.fitAudio()     // it may have come back on fewer lanes than the probe promised
134					ed.fitSrc()       // ...and a master's collapse is a shallower ROW: the strip under
135					ed.redrawTracks() // its pictures is row geometry now, not the band's
136				})
137			}()
138		}
139	}
140	
141	// sortLanes is the order the lanes are read in: the footage's own first
142	// whatever the clock says, because it is the thing every other lane is being
143	// compared to, then the rest by when they started. A master that sorted itself
144	// into the middle of the recordings would be one more lane to find first.
145	func sortLanes(auds []tlAudio) {
146		sort.SliceStable(auds, func(i, j int) bool {
147			if auds[i].master != auds[j].master {
148				return auds[i].master
149			}
150			return auds[i].start < auds[j].start
151		})
152	}
153	
154	// waveform is the peak envelope: one byte per bucket per channel, the loudest
155	// sample in that bucket. Peak rather than RMS because what a cut is aimed at is
156	// where someone starts talking, and RMS rounds an onset off.
157	type waveform struct {
158		hz    float64
159		chans [][]uint8
160	}
161	
162	// ---- how loud is drawn ------------------------------------------------------
163	//
164	// The height is a meter reading on the IEC 60268-18 scale (-70..0 dBFS), not
165	// an amplitude: linear puts everything but the loudest few dB on the floor.
166	// The envelope is a peak per 10 ms bucket, so a lane is filled from the
167	// bottom, not mirrored -- a level has no negative side.
168	
169	// iecRaw is the standard's own curve: linear amplitude in, meter deflection
170	// out, with the knots exactly where IEC 60268-18 puts them.
171	func iecRaw(amp float64) float64 {
172		if amp <= 0 {
173			return 0
174		}
175		db := 20 * math.Log10(amp)
176		switch {
177		case db < -70:
178			return 0
179		case db < -60:
180			return (db + 70) * 0.0025
181		case db < -50:
182			return (db+60)*0.005 + 0.025
183		case db < -40:
184			return (db+50)*0.0075 + 0.075
185		case db < -30:
186			return (db+40)*0.015 + 0.15
187		case db < -20:
188			return (db+30)*0.02 + 0.3
189		}
190		return math.Min(1, (db+20)*0.025+0.5)
191	}
192	
193	// iecFloor is where the curve stands when the envelope holds the quietest
194	// thing it can hold. A bucket is one byte, so the smallest sound that is not
195	// silence is 1/255 of full scale -- about -48 dBFS -- while the curve's own
196	// bottom is -70. Left alone, the 22 dB between them would be a band of the
197	// lane no signal could ever land in, and a noise floor hovering around the
198	// byte's own floor would draw as a picket fence: nothing, then a fourteenth of
199	// the lane, then nothing.
200	var iecFloor = iecRaw(1.0 / 255)
201	
202	// iecScale is the curve as this page uses it: the quietest bucket the envelope
203	// can hold sits on the floor of the lane, full scale reaches the top, and
204	// everything between is the meter curve stretched across that range.
205	func iecScale(amp float64) float64 {
206		v := (iecRaw(amp) - iecFloor) / (1 - iecFloor)
207		return math.Max(0, math.Min(1, v))
208	}
209	
210	// peak is the loudest thing between two file-local times, 0..1. A drawn column
211	// covers many buckets when zoomed out and a fraction of one when zoomed in, and
212	// both have to answer: the first by taking the loudest of them (a peak envelope
213	// that averaged would fade out as you zoomed out), the second by taking the one
214	// it lands in.
215	func (wf *waveform) peak(ch int, from, to float64) float64 {
216		if wf == nil || ch >= len(wf.chans) {
217			return 0
218		}
219		buf := wf.chans[ch]
220		i := int(from * wf.hz)
221		j := int(math.Ceil(to * wf.hz))
222		if j <= i {
223			j = i + 1
224		}
225		if i < 0 {
226			i = 0
227		}
228		if j > len(buf) {
229			j = len(buf)
230		}
231		top := uint8(0)
232		for ; i < j; i++ {
233			if buf[i] > top {
234				top = buf[i]
235			}
236		}
237		return float64(top) / 255
238	}
239	
240	// ---- getting one ------------------------------------------------------------
241	
242	// waveCache is where the envelopes live between runs. Not under cut/, which
243	// is the cut's own folder and whose file count is reported to the user as what
244	// this step produced: an envelope is not an output, it is a picture of an input
245	// that would otherwise be decoded again on every start.
246	func (a *App) waveCache() string { return filepath.Join(a.outDir, "cache", "waves") }
247	
248	// waveMagic changes when the format does, so an old cache is simply not read
249	// rather than read as something it is not. It has now changed twice without the
250	// layout changing, for the same reason both times: a stereo file whose two
251	// sides are the same signal is one channel (AWV3), and so is one whose two
252	// sides merely DRAW the same (AWV4, see sameLanes). A cache written before
253	// either would go on drawing the second lane forever, since it is keyed by the
254	// recording and the recording has not changed.
255	const waveMagic = "AWV4"
256	
257	// loadWave is the cache in front of buildWave, keyed by the source's size and
258	// mtime (a re-recording under the same name is a different recording) and by
259	// the LANE's name, not the file's: two tracks of one .mkv share size and
260	// mtime, and a file-named cache would hand the second lane the first's
261	// envelope.
262	func loadWave(dir string, au tlAudio) (*waveform, error) {
263		fi, err := os.Stat(au.path)
264		if err != nil {
265			return nil, err
266		}
267		cf := filepath.Join(dir, au.base+".wave")
268		if wf, ok := readWave(cf, fi.Size(), fi.ModTime().Unix()); ok {
269			return wf, nil
270		}
271		wf, err := buildWave(au.path, au.track, au.chans)
272		if err != nil {
273			return nil, err
274		}
275		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err == nil {
276			writeWave(cf, wf, fi.Size(), fi.ModTime().Unix())
277		}
278		return wf, nil
279	}
280	
281	// header: magic, channels, hz, buckets, and the source's size and mtime
282	type waveHead struct {
283		Chans uint8
284		Hz    uint16
285		Count uint32
286		Size  int64
287		Mtime int64
288	}
289	
290	func readWave(file string, size, mtime int64) (*waveform, bool) {
291		f, err := os.Open(file)
292		if err != nil {
293			return nil, false
294		}
295		defer f.Close()
296		r := bufio.NewReader(f)
297		magic := make([]byte, len(waveMagic))
298		if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, magic); err != nil || string(magic) != waveMagic {
299			return nil, false
300		}
301		var h waveHead
302		if binary.Read(r, binary.LittleEndian, &h) != nil {
303			return nil, false
304		}
305		if h.Size != size || h.Mtime != mtime || h.Chans == 0 || h.Chans > 2 || h.Hz == 0 {
306			return nil, false // a different recording, or a format we do not read
307		}
308		wf := &waveform{hz: float64(h.Hz)}
309		for c := 0; c < int(h.Chans); c++ {
310			buf := make([]uint8, h.Count)
311			if _, err := io.ReadFull(r, buf); err != nil {
312				return nil, false
313			}
314			wf.chans = append(wf.chans, buf)
315		}
316		return wf, true
317	}
318	
319	func writeWave(file string, wf *waveform, size, mtime int64) error {
320		f, err := os.Create(file)
321		if err != nil {
322			return err
323		}
324		defer f.Close()
325		w := bufio.NewWriter(f)
326		w.WriteString(waveMagic)
327		n := 0
328		if len(wf.chans) > 0 {
329			n = len(wf.chans[0])
330		}
331		if err := binary.Write(w, binary.LittleEndian, waveHead{
332			Chans: uint8(len(wf.chans)), Hz: uint16(wf.hz), Count: uint32(n),
333			Size: size, Mtime: mtime,
334		}); err != nil {
335			return err
336		}
337		for _, c := range wf.chans {
338			w.Write(c)
339		}
340		return w.Flush()
341	}
342	
343	// buildWave decodes the recording and keeps the loudest sample of every bucket.
344	// Nothing is held but the envelope: the samples go past in a pipe, which is why
345	// this can be pointed at an hour of 48 kHz stereo without asking what it costs.
346	func buildWave(path string, track, chans int) (*waveform, error) {
347		if chans < 1 {
348			chans = 1
349		}
350		if chans > 2 {
351			chans = 2
352		}
353		args := []string{"-v", "error", "-i", path, "-vn"}
354		// only for a track past the first: -vn already leaves ffmpeg picking the
355		// best audio stream, which for every single-track file in the world is the
356		// one meant, and adding a -map that says the same thing would change the
357		// command every existing .wave in the cache was built by.
358		if track > 0 {
359			args = append(args, "-map", fmt.Sprintf("0:a:%d", track))
360		}
361		args = append(args, "-ac", strconv.Itoa(chans), "-ar", strconv.Itoa(waveRate),
362			"-f", "s16le", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", "-")
363		cmd := exec.Command(ffTool("ffmpeg"), args...)
364		out, err := cmd.StdoutPipe()
365		if err != nil {
366			return nil, err
367		}
368		var errBuf strings.Builder
369		cmd.Stderr = &errBuf
370		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
371			return nil, err
372		}
373		wf := &waveform{hz: waveHz, chans: make([][]uint8, chans)}
374		per := int(waveRate / waveHz) // samples per bucket per channel
375		r := bufio.NewReaderSize(out, 1<<16)
376		buf := make([]byte, 2*chans*per)
377		loudest, apart := 0, 0 // the peak of the whole file, and how far the sides get from each other
378		for {
379			n, err := io.ReadFull(r, buf)
380			if n >= 2*chans {
381				frames := n / (2 * chans)
382				for c := 0; c < chans; c++ {
383					top := 0
384					for f := 0; f < frames; f++ {
385						if v := abs16(s16(buf, f*chans+c)); v > top {
386							top = v
387						}
388					}
389					if top > loudest {
390						loudest = top
391					}
392					// 32767 would put a full-scale peak one short of the top byte
393					wf.chans[c] = append(wf.chans[c], uint8(min(255, top*255/32767)))
394				}
395				for f := 0; chans == 2 && f < frames; f++ {
396					if d := abs16(s16(buf, 2*f) - s16(buf, 2*f+1)); d > apart {
397						apart = d
398					}
399				}
400			}
401			if err != nil {
402				break
403			}
404		}
405		if err := cmd.Wait(); err != nil {
406			tail := errBuf.String()
407			if len(tail) > 200 {
408				tail = tail[len(tail)-200:]
409			}
410			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ffmpeg: %w\n%s", err, tail)
411		}
412		if len(wf.chans[0]) == 0 {
413			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: no audio came out of it", filepath.Base(path))
414		}
415		// Two sides carrying the same signal are one signal (a mono mic in a stereo
416		// container). Not sample-exact: an encoder adds noise between the sides, so
417		// the test is whether they ever differ by more than a hundredth of the file's
418		// peak -- 40 dB down, invisible in a 30 px lane. A silent stereo file
419		// collapses too.
420		if chans == 2 && (apart*dualMonoRatio <= loudest || sameLanes(wf.chans[0], wf.chans[1])) {
421			wf.chans = wf.chans[:1]
422		}
423		return wf, nil
424	}
425	
426	// dualMonoRatio is how much quieter the difference between two channels has to
427	// be than the recording itself before they count as one signal.
428	const dualMonoRatio = 100
429	
430	// sameLanes asks whether two envelopes draw the same PICTURE: mean difference
431	// within a byte, with a ceiling on any single bucket so one hard pan still
432	// counts as stereo. Looser than the sample test (which fails on one lossy
433	// transient) and an order of magnitude away from a mismatched mic pair.
434	const (
435		laneSameAvg = 1.0 // bytes of envelope, meaned over the recording
436		laneSameMax = 8   // ...and the most any one bucket may be out
437	)
438	
439	func sameLanes(a, b []uint8) bool {
440		if len(a) == 0 || len(a) != len(b) {
441			return false
442		}
443		sum := 0
444		for i := range a {
445			d := int(a[i]) - int(b[i])
446			if d < 0 {
447				d = -d
448			}
449			if d > laneSameMax {
450				return false
451			}
452			sum += d
453		}
454		return float64(sum)/float64(len(a)) < laneSameAvg
455	}
456	
457	// s16 is sample i of an interleaved little-endian s16 buffer.
458	func s16(b []byte, i int) int { return int(int16(uint16(b[2*i]) | uint16(b[2*i+1])<<8)) }
459	
460	func abs16(v int) int {
461		if v < 0 {
462			return -v
463		}
464		return v
465	}
466	
467	// ---- drawing ----------------------------------------------------------------
468	
469	// lanes is how many lanes one recording draws.
470	//
471	// The envelope decides, not the probe: a stereo file whose two sides are the
472	// same signal is one lane, and that is not something ffprobe can be asked --
473	// only the decode knows it. Until the envelope lands the probe is what there
474	// is, so a stereo recording briefly takes two lanes and settles into one when
475	// its wave arrives, which is also when the area is re-fitted around it.
476	func (ed *cutEditor) lanes(au tlAudio) int {
477		if wf := ed.waves[au.base]; wf != nil && len(wf.chans) > 0 {
478			return len(wf.chans)
479		}
480		return max(1, au.chans)
481	}
482	
483	// sepAuds is what the band under the timeline holds: the separate recordings,
484	// the sound nobody filmed. A master -- some row's own track -- is drawn under
485	// that row's pictures instead (drawPairStrip), so every question about the
486	// band's own layout is a question about this list and not about ed.auds.
487	func (ed *cutEditor) sepAuds() []tlAudio {
488		var out []tlAudio
489		for _, au := range ed.auds {
490			if !au.master {
491				out = append(out, au)
492			}
493		}
494		return out
495	}
496	
497	// audioHeight is the widget's height, and 0 when there is nothing to show --
498	// which hides the area entirely rather than leaving an empty black strip under
499	// the cut saying nothing. With the masters paired under their rows that is the
500	// everyday state, not the odd one: a cameras-only session has no band at all.
501	func (ed *cutEditor) audioHeight() int {
502		n := ed.audioLanes()
503		if n == 0 {
504			return 0
505		}
506		return int(float64(n)*waveLaneH + float64(len(ed.sepAuds())-1)*waveGap + 2*wavePad)
507	}
508	
509	// audioLanes is how many waveform lanes the band holds: the separate
510	// recordings' channels, and only theirs -- a master's wave lives under its
511	// own row of pictures now, not down here.
512	func (ed *cutEditor) audioLanes() int {
513		n := 0
514		for _, au := range ed.sepAuds() {
515			n += ed.lanes(au)
516		}
517		return n
518	}
519	
520	// audAtY is the recording whose lanes sit at y in the audio area, by base name,
521	// or "" with none at all. Total, deliberately: a press on the pad above a lane
522	// or the hair between two must not quietly mean "the pictures".
523	func (ed *cutEditor) audAtY(y float64) string {
524		auds := ed.sepAuds()
525		if len(auds) == 0 {
526			return ""
527		}
528		top := wavePad
529		for _, au := range auds {
530			if top += float64(ed.lanes(au)) * waveLaneH; y < top {
531				return au.base
532			}
533			top += waveGap
534		}
535		return auds[len(auds)-1].base
536	}
537	
538	// audLaneSpan is the top and bottom of one recording's lanes, and whether it
539	// has any -- the other half of audAtY, for drawing on the recording a
540	// selection is of rather than across all of them.
541	func (ed *cutEditor) audLaneSpan(base string) (float64, float64, bool) {
542		top := wavePad
543		for _, au := range ed.sepAuds() {
544			h := float64(ed.lanes(au)) * waveLaneH
545			if au.base == base {
546				return top, top + h, true
547			}
548			top += h + waveGap
549		}
550		return 0, 0, false
551	}
552	
553	// drawAudio paints every lane. Same discipline as drawTrack: timeline
554	// coordinates with the view translated under them, and every loop cut down to
555	// the columns actually on screen first, so an afternoon of recording costs the
556	// same per frame as a minute of it.
557	func (ed *cutEditor) drawAudio(cr *cairo.Context, w, h int) {
558		fh := float64(h)
559		cr.SetSourceRGB(0.13, 0.13, 0.13)
560		cr.Rectangle(0, 0, float64(w), fh)
561		cr.Fill()
562		auds := ed.sepAuds()
563		if len(auds) == 0 || len(ed.vids) == 0 {
564			return
565		}
566		vx0, vx1 := ed.viewX, ed.viewX+float64(w)
567	
568		cr.Save()
569		cr.Translate(-ed.viewX, 0)
570		y := wavePad
571		for _, au := range auds {
572			wf := ed.waves[au.base]
573			for ch := 0; ch < ed.lanes(au); ch++ {

778		}
779		if !named {

781		}
782		// named at the bottom of the strip: the plates own the top left
783		cr.SetFontSize(10)

799	// the session, and two sources sharing a row each bring the stretch under

801	func (ed *cutEditor) drawPairStrip(cr *cairo.Context, v tlVideo, au tlAudio, y, vx0, vx1 float64) {
802		wf := ed.waves[au.base]
803		for ch := 0; ch < ed.lanes(au); ch++ {
804			ed.drawWaveSpan(cr, au, v, wf, ch, y, vx0, vx1, true)

809	// drawWaveSpan paints the stretch of one channel of one recording that
810	// overlaps one piece of footage. dim is the paired strip's voice: the same
811	// wave turned down, plateless, edge to edge under the thumbnails, so it reads
812	// as the row's shadow rather than a row of its own.
813	func (ed *cutEditor) drawWaveSpan(cr *cairo.Context, au tlAudio, v tlVideo, wf *waveform, ch int, y, vx0, vx1 float64, dim bool) {
814		// the overlap of this recording with this piece of footage, in session
815		// time
816		t0 := math.Max(au.start, v.start)
817		t1 := math.Min(au.start+au.dur, v.start+v.dur)
818		if t1 <= t0 {
819			return // this recording was not running while this one was
820		}
821		// ...then in px, one CELL at a time: a folded gap inside the overlap is
822		// 32 px standing for minutes, so the wave either side of it is two pieces
823		// at two origins and there is none to draw in between (cut_fold.go). With
824		// nothing folded this is one cell and one pass, as it always was.
825		for _, cell := range ed.cellsOf(t0, t1) {
826			cv := v
827			cv.pxOrigin = cell.px - (cell.t0-v.start)*ed.pps
828			ct0, ct1 := math.Max(t0, cell.t0), math.Min(t1, cell.t1)
829			ed.drawWaveCell(cr, au, cv, wf, ch, y, ct0, ct1,
830				math.Max(vx0, cell.px), math.Min(vx1, cell.px+ed.spanW(cell)), dim)
831		}
832	}
833	
834	// drawWaveCell is that painter for one cell: the stretch [t0,t1] of one
835	// channel of one recording, clipped to the px window, at an origin px is
836	// linear from.
837	func (ed *cutEditor) drawWaveCell(cr *cairo.Context, au tlAudio, v tlVideo, wf *waveform, ch int,
838		y, t0, t1, vx0, vx1 float64, dim bool) {
839	
840		bot := y + waveLaneH - 1 // the meter's zero, a hair inside the lane
841		full := waveLaneH - 2    // and how far up full scale reaches
842		alpha := 1.0
843		if dim {
844			alpha = 0.55
845		}
846		x0 := math.Max(v.pxOrigin+(t0-v.start)*ed.pps, vx0)
847		x1 := math.Min(v.pxOrigin+(t1-v.start)*ed.pps, vx1)
848		if x1 <= x0 {
849			return // off screen
850		}
851		// the ground says where the recording IS, which is the other half of
852		// only drawing the relevant part: an empty lane and a lane of silence
853		// are different things and have to look different
854		cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.16, 0.17, 0.2, alpha)
855		cr.Rectangle(x0, y, x1-x0, waveLaneH)
856		cr.Fill()
857		// the baseline sits under the fill rather than through it: it is the
858		// meter's zero, and on a silent stretch it is the only thing saying the
859		// recorder was still running
860		cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.35, 0.6, 1, 0.35*alpha)
861		cr.SetLineWidth(1)
862		cr.MoveTo(x0, math.Round(bot)+0.5)
863		cr.LineTo(x1, math.Round(bot)+0.5)
864		cr.Stroke()
865		if wf == nil {
866			return // still being decoded; the ground already says it is here
867		}
868		// one filled column per pixel, standing up from the baseline
869		spp := 1 / ed.pps // seconds per pixel
870		hgts := make([]float64, 0, int(x1-math.Floor(x0))+1)
871		cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.29, 0.62, 1, alpha)
872		for x := math.Floor(x0); x < x1; x++ {
873			at := au.timeAt(v, ed.pps, x)
874			// the envelope is a linear peak and the lane is a meter: iecScale
875			// is the whole difference between a row of spikes over a flat line
876			// and a picture of where the sound is
877			p := iecScale(wf.peak(ch, at, at+spp))
878			h := 0.0
879			if p > 0 {
880				h = math.Max(1, p*full)
881				cr.Rectangle(x, bot-h, 1, h)
882			}
883			hgts = append(hgts, h)
884		}
885		cr.Fill()
886		// and a darker cap along the top of the fill. A column is one pixel
887		// wide, so at any zoom worth looking at the lane is a solid block of
888		// blue whose only shape is its skyline; drawn in the same ink as the
889		// block it sits on, that skyline is exactly where the eye stops being
890		// able to see it.
891		cr.SetSourceRGBA(0.09, 0.27, 0.52, alpha)
892		for i, h := range hgts {
893			if h >= 3 { // below that the cap would eat the column it caps
894				cr.Rectangle(math.Floor(x0)+float64(i), bot-h, 1, 1)
895			}
896		}
897		cr.Fill()
898	}
899	
900	// timeAt is the recording's own time at a timeline x, through the video that x
901	// belongs to. The audio's clock and the footage's clock differ by exactly where
902	// each of them started, which is what start holds and what makes this a
903	// subtraction rather than an alignment problem.
904	func (au tlAudio) timeAt(v tlVideo, pps, x float64) float64 {
905		return au.at(v.start + (x-v.pxOrigin)/pps)
906	}

908	// selSnd is the selection scoped to one recording's sound -- drawn in a lane,
909	// or on the wave strip under a row's pictures, which is the only place that
910	// choice is made now (the press that starts the drag says it, cut.go). The
911	// strip that used to be able to change it afterwards is gone: what a
912	// selection is OF is what it was drawn on, and which rows a SCENE is made of
913	// is said on the scene itself (cut_cam.go, cut_hear.go).
914	func (ed *cutEditor) selSnd() bool { return ed.sel.aud != "" }
915	
916	// fitSelAud keeps the selection's scope pointing at things the session still
917	// has: the lanes are rebuilt from what is on disk, a recording can go away
918	// between one reload and the next, and a selection pointing at one nobody has
919	// is a selection whose every verb would miss. So it comes back to the footage.
920	func (ed *cutEditor) fitSelAud() {
921		if ed.sel.aud != "" && ed.audByBase(ed.sel.aud) == nil {
922			ed.sel.aud = ""
923			ed.syncSelBtns()
924		}
925	}

359	// fxFromReply turns proposed effects into cutFx: the model chooses WHEN and
360	// WHICH KIND, the app's own defaults decide HOW. Nonsense entries are dropped,
361	// not fatal. svg cannot be asked for (a file on this machine).
362	// fxMaxProposed caps a reply's effects at the wording's rate over a cut longer
363	// than anyone makes.
364	const fxMaxProposed = 1000 // effectively none: how many effects a cut carries is the prompt's call, not this file's
365	
366	func fxFromReply(in []sugFx) []cutFx { return fxFrom(in, fxMaxProposed) }
367	
368	// fxFrom is fxFromReply with the cap as an argument: the reply's own effects
369	// are decorations and are held to fxMaxProposed; the speeds a cut is built
370	// from are not decorations and are held to nothing, or a cut of sixty
371	// sped-up stretches has thirty-six of them quietly running at 1.
372	func fxFrom(in []sugFx, cap int) []cutFx {
373		var out []cutFx
374		for _, f := range in {
375			if cap > 0 && len(out) == cap {
376				break
377			}
378			d := f.End - f.Start
379			switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.Kind)) {
380			case "zoom":
381				if d <= 0 {
382					continue
383				}
384				g := math.Min(1, d/3) // the dialog's second of glide, shrunk to fit a short zoom
385				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "zoom", T: f.Start, Dur: d,
386					Cx: 0.5, Cy: 0.5, Hf: 0.6, Trans: g, Tout: g})
387			case "speed":
388				if d <= 0 {
389					continue
390				}
391				rate := f.Rate
392				if rate <= 0 {
393					rate = 0.5 // an unnamed rate means slow-mo; 0 would be a freeze nobody asked for
394				}
395				rate, d = clampSpeed(rate, d)
396				// the same fades a suggested zoom and caption get, on the same
397				// terms: a second either side where the stretch is long enough to
398				// spend it, and nothing where the render could not build the
399				// stairs anyway -- which at a fast rate wants more footage than a
400				// second, because a stair is measured on the finished video
401				ramp := math.Min(1, d/4)
402				if ramp < rampStep*math.Max(1, rate) {
403					ramp = 0
404				}
405				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "speed", T: f.Start, Dur: d, Rate: rate,
406					Trans: ramp, Tout: ramp})
407			case "stop":
408				// the held frame: the picture stands still at f.Start while the
409				// footage runs on under it, which is a speed of 0 (frozenFx). It
410				// is a kind of its own in the reply because a rate cannot say it
411				// -- an omitted rate and a rate of 0 are the same JSON number,
412				// and reading that as a freeze would hand a still to every reply
413				// that forgot to name a speed
414				if d <= 0 {
415					d = 2 // long enough to read as a hold, short enough not to strand the viewer
416				}
417				fade := math.Min(0.3, d/4)
418				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "speed", T: f.Start, Dur: d, Rate: 0,
419					Trans: fade, Tout: fade})
420			case "volume":
421				if d <= 0 {
422					continue
423				}
424				// a gain nobody named is a field left out, and there is nothing
425				// to do about it; 1 is dropped for the plainer reason that it
426				// does nothing. An explicit 0 is kept -- that is a stretch the
427				// session wanted silent.
428				if f.Gain == nil || *f.Gain == 1 {
429					continue
430				}
431				// the same second either way that a suggested zoom and caption get
432				ramp := math.Min(1, d/4)
433				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "volume", T: f.Start, Dur: d,
434					Gain: clampGain(*f.Gain), Trans: ramp, Tout: ramp})
435			case "text":
436				txt := strings.TrimSpace(f.Text)
437				if txt == "" {
438					continue // a caption with no words is nothing to draw
439				}
440				if d <= 0 {
441					d = 3 // the dialog's own opening duration
442				}
443				fade := math.Min(0.3, d/4)
444				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "text", T: f.Start, Dur: d,
445					Trans: fade, Tout: fade, Text: txt})
446			}
447		}
448		return out
449	}

451	func (a *App) suggestCut(session string, target, span float64) ([]cutSeg, []cutFx, error) {
452		system := a.sysPrompt("cut")
453		// With a target: the range, not just the number. Told "300 seconds" alone, a
454		// model spends the call adding and dropping segments to hit it exactly and
455		// runs out of room for the answer (once: 85 kB of arithmetic, no JSON). From
456		// the same function the validator uses, so prompt and gate cannot drift.
457		//
458		// With none: say there is none. A length nobody asked for is not a weaker
459		// instruction than a real one -- it is the instruction, and the model obeys
460		// it by leaving out material the person wanted in.
461		length := "NO TARGET LENGTH. The user context names none, so there is none: keep every " +
462			"moment worth keeping and the video is as long as that comes to. Nothing is dropped to " +
463			"reach a length, and nothing is kept to fill one."
464		if target > 0 {
465			lo, hi := a.footageWindow(target)

3	// Hand-picked seconds of a narrator's recording for the voice reference,
4	// overruling narrate_ref.go's automatic pick (which cannot hear clipping, fans
5	// or a reading voice). Drag on the wave, ＋, and those seconds are the
6	// reference, taken whole -- not re-ranked, trimmed to refWant or capped at

8	// not hand them to someone else. Part of voiceKey: change a take and every
9	// line is respoken.

14		"fmt"
15		"math"
16		"os"
17		"path/filepath"
18		"sort"

20	
21	// voiceTake is one stretch of a recording, in that file's own seconds.
22	type voiceTake struct {
23		S float64 `json:"s"`
24		E float64 `json:"e"`
25	}
26	
27	func (t voiceTake) dur() float64 { return t.E - t.S }
28	
29	// takeMin is the shortest stretch ＋ will accept. Not refMinLen (five seconds,
30	// what an automatic pick has to clear): somebody adding a third piece to two
31	// good ones knows what they are doing, and a floor there would be this file
32	// arguing with the ear it exists to defer to. It is here at all because a
33	// click that moved two pixels is a click, and a 30 ms take in the list is a
34	// mistake nothing else would report.
35	const takeMin = 0.4
36	
37	// takesFile is where they live -- beside voice.txt and pitch.txt, the project's
38	// other answers about who speaks.
39	func (a *App) takesFile() string { return filepath.Join(a.narrateDir(), "takes.json") }
40	
41	// takesRead1 reads the file once into the map. The caller holds voiceMu: the
42	// map itself never leaves this lock, which is the point. It used to be handed
43	// back to be indexed by the caller, and the two threads that ask -- the GUI
44	// after a ＋, and whatever worker is about to speak a line (voiceKey) -- would
45	// then read it while a ＋ on the other one was writing it. A Go map does not
46	// merely give a stale answer to that; it stops the program.
47	func (a *App) takesRead1() {
48		if a.takesRead {
49			return
50		}
51		a.takesRead, a.takesMap = true, map[string][]voiceTake{}
52		if b, err := os.ReadFile(a.takesFile()); err == nil {
53			var m map[string][]voiceTake
54			if json.Unmarshal(b, &m) == nil {
55				for k, v := range m {
56					if ts := cleanTakes(v); len(ts) > 0 {
57						a.takesMap[k] = ts
58					}
59				}
60			}
61		}
62	}
63	
64	// takesFor is one recording's hand-picked takes, in order. Asked for on every
65	// cache key, which is once per narration line, so the file is read once and the
66	// answer is a lookup after that.
67	func (a *App) takesFor(base string) []voiceTake {
68		a.voiceMu.Lock()
69		defer a.voiceMu.Unlock()
70		a.takesRead1()
71		return a.takesMap[base]
72	}

74	// setTakesFor writes them and drops the reference built from the old ones, so
75	// the next thing spoken cuts a fresh one -- the same move setVoice makes, for
76	// the same reason: the file on disk is an answer to a question that has
77	// changed. Safe off the GUI thread.
78	func (a *App) setTakesFor(base string, ts []voiceTake) error {
79		if base == "" {
80			return fmt.Errorf("no recording to pick takes from")
81		}
82		a.voiceMu.Lock()
83		a.takesRead1() // the file first, or writing one recording's takes drops the rest
84		if ts = cleanTakes(ts); len(ts) == 0 {
85			delete(a.takesMap, base)
86		} else {
87			a.takesMap[base] = ts
88		}
89		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(a.takesMap, "", "  ")

92			return err
93		}

95			return err
96		}

99		}

101		os.Remove(a.refPath())

105	// takeSource is the recording the chosen voice is cut from, or "" when there
106	// is nothing to pick from: a wav out of the voices folder is used whole, and
107	// "no audio" is not a voice.
108	func (a *App) takeSource() string {

131	func cleanTakes(ts []voiceTake) []voiceTake {
132		var in []voiceTake
133		for _, t := range ts {

136			}

175	}

177	// takesTotal is how much reference the set adds up to -- what the status line
178	// says after every ＋ and －, because "is that enough" is the one question the
179	// picture cannot answer.
180	func takesTotal(ts []voiceTake) float64 {
181		sum := 0.0
182		for _, t := range ts {
183			sum += t.dur()
184		}
185		return sum
186	}
187	
188	// sameTakes asks whether two sets are the same seconds, which is what a ＋ or
189	// － needs to know before it says anything happened. Counting them and adding
190	// them up is not that question -- two sets can agree on both and still be
191	// different takes -- and the answer to the real one is this cheap.
192	func sameTakes(a, b []voiceTake) bool {
193		if len(a) != len(b) {
194			return false
195		}
196		for i := range a {
197			if a[i] != b[i] {
198				return false
199			}
200		}
201		return true
202	}
203	
204	// takesKey is the set as a cache key: empty for a voice nobody has hand-picked,
205	// so every project that has never touched this keeps the key it already has and
206	// nothing already spoken is orphaned by the feature existing. Rounded to the
207	// millisecond, which is finer than any edge anyone can drag and coarse enough
208	// that float noise cannot invent a new voice.
209	func takesKey(ts []voiceTake) string {
210		if len(ts) == 0 {
211			return ""
212		}
213		h := sha1.New()
214		for _, t := range ts {
215			fmt.Fprintf(h, "%.3f-%.3f;", t.S, t.E)
216		}
217		return fmt.Sprintf("%x", h.Sum(nil)[:4])
218	}
219	
220	// handPicks turns the set into what ensureVoiceBase cuts from. The word count
221	// is nought and stays nought: it is what refCuts RANKS by, and a hand-picked
222	// set is not ranked.
223	func handPicks(ts []voiceTake) []refTake {
224		out := make([]refTake, 0, len(ts))
225		for _, t := range ts {
226			out = append(out, refTake{s: t.S, e: t.E})
227		}
228		return out
229	}

12	// Which lanes a scene is heard on: per scene, on the lanes. Take a scene in
13	// hand and every audio lane shows green/grey with a badge that toggles it; two
14	// lanes on are summed at their recorded levels with a limiter on the clip
15	// (clipCeil, produce.go). The badge sits at the LEFT of the held scene only --
16	// the rest of the scene is the press that moves the line or takes it in hand.
17	// Both the camera's own strip and the recorders' band wear one.
18	
19	const (
20		hearR   = 4.5  // the speaker cone, from its centre
21		hearPad = 3.5  // the plate's edge, beyond it
22		hearHit = 10.0 // and the target, bigger than either
23		// its centre, in from the held scene's LEFT border -- far enough that the
24		// badge's TARGET begins where the border's grab ends (edgeGrab), the same
25		// clearance the bar's ✕ keeps from the grip at the other end. Closer in,
26		// the two shared pixels: a press meant for the border switched a lane,
27		// and the badge looked like part of the handle it was sitting on.
28		hearIn = edgeGrab + hearHit
29		// under this a scene has no room to wear one, by killMin's rule: the
30		// target reaches hearIn+hearHit in from the left border, and a scene
31		// narrower than twice that has its MIDDLE inside the badge -- so a press
32		// meant to put the line on the clip would switch a lane instead.
33		hearMin = 2*(hearIn+hearHit) + 6
34	)

36	// hearBadge is one lane's answer for the held scene, and where it is drawn.
37	//
38	// h is the whole RECORDING's depth and not one channel's: a stereo microphone
39	// is two waveforms and one answer, and a wash that covered only the first would
40	// say the second is a lane of its own that nobody has decided about yet.
41	type hearBadge struct {
42		base   string
43		cx, cy float64 // timeline x, and the middle of the lane in area y
44		h      float64 // how deep the lane is, all its channels together
45		on     bool    // this scene hears this lane
46	}

48	// hearScene is the scene the badges are about: the one in hand, else the one
49	// under the line -- which is the scene the preview's hush follows (syncHush),
50	// so the badge shown is the thing you hear.
51	func (ed *cutEditor) hearScene() *cutSeg {
52		if s := ed.heldSeg(); s != nil {
53			return s
54		}
55		if i := ed.segAt(ed.playhead); i >= 0 {
56			return &ed.segs[i]
57		}
58		return nil

61	// hearX is where the badges for the scene go, and whether it is wide enough
62	// to wear any. Timeline px, like everything else drawn in a translated area.
63	func (ed *cutEditor) hearX() (float64, bool) {
64		s := ed.hearScene()
65		if s == nil || s.isInsert() {
66			// an insert brings its own sound or replaces the lane it was laid in
67			// (dropLane), and neither is a question about which lanes are heard
68			return 0, false
69		}
70		x0, x1 := ed.xOf(s.S), ed.xOf(s.E)
71		if x1-x0 < hearMin {
72			return 0, false
73		}
74		return x0 + hearIn, true
75	}

252	// toggleLanesAll is that press for a switch standing for several recordings --
253	// a camera row (pairSwitches). name is what the status calls them. Off if ANY

255	func (ed *cutEditor) toggleLanesAll(bases []string, name string) {
256		if len(bases) == 0 {
257			return
258		}
259		if len(ed.segs) == 0 {
260			ed.a.setStatus(name + " is in no scene yet — cut something first")
261			return

269		ed.pushUndo()
270		n := 0
271		for i := range ed.segs {
272			s := &ed.segs[i]
273			if s.isInsert() {

275			}
276			var next []string

278				if !slices.Contains(bases, q) {
279					next = append(next, q)
280				}
281			}
282			if !on {
283				next = append(next, bases...)
284			}
285			if len(next) != len(s.Quiet) {

287			}
288			s.Quiet = next
289		}
290		ed.persist()
291		ed.redrawTracks()
292		if on {
293			ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s is on for the whole cut — every scene hears it (%d changed)", name, n))
294			return
295		}
296		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s off for the whole cut — %d scene(s) changed", name, n))

561	// migrateSound reads a cut from when sound was one lane for the whole project
562	// (cutFile.Sound) and writes the same thing per scene: every scene silences
563	// every lane but that one. Runs once -- nothing writes Sound any more; scenes
564	// that already name silenced lanes are left alone. The old choice could put
565	// camera A's sound under camera B's picture; those scenes keep their OWN camera
566	// (audible and correctable beats silent), and the note counts them.
567	func migrateSound(segs []cutSeg, snd string, vids []tlVideo, auds []tlAudio) ([]cutSeg, string) {
568		if strings.TrimSpace(snd) == "" || len(segs) == 0 {
569			return segs, ""
570		}
571		// the chosen name read as a camera ROW and not as one file: a camera
572		// stopped and started again is several recordings in a line, and the old
573		// choice carried across them exactly as the picture does. Below zero means
574		// it named a separately recorded lane instead, which is one file and needs
575		// none of this.
576		row := -1
577		for _, v := range vids {
578			if v.base == snd {
579				row = v.lane
580			}
581		}
582		out := append([]cutSeg(nil), segs...)

584		for i := range out {
585			if len(out[i].Quiet) > 0 {
586				continue
587			}
588			keep := snd
589			if row >= 0 {
590				switch v := pickVideoOn(vids, out[i].Cam, out[i].S); {
591				case v == nil:
592					keep = ""
593				case v.lane != row:
594					keep, crossed = v.base, crossed+1
595				default:
596					keep = v.base
597				}
598			}
599			var quiet []string
600			for _, au := range auds {
601				if au.base != keep {
602					quiet = append(quiet, au.base)
603				}
604			}
605			out[i].Quiet = quiet
606		}
607		note := fmt.Sprintf("this cut was heard on %s from end to end; that is now said scene "+
608			"by scene, and every scene has been set to silence the other lanes", snd)
609		if crossed > 0 {
610			were := "scenes are"
611			if crossed == 1 {
612				were = "scene is"
613			}
614			note += fmt.Sprintf(" — except %d, which %s shown from another camera and left "+
615				"hearing their own sound: one camera's sound under another's picture is no "+
616				"longer something the render can do", crossed, were)

618		return out, note

621	// syncHush tells the preview what the scene under the playhead hears, from
622	// showInsert -- every path that moves the line -- so a badge press is audible
623	// at once and playback picks the new answer up at the boundary. Off the ends
624	// of the cut and in gaps everything is heard.
625	func (ed *cutEditor) syncHush() {
626		if ed.player == nil {
627			return
628		}

630		if i := ed.segAt(ed.playhead); i >= 0 {
631			s = &ed.segs[i]
632		}
633		var base string
634		if ed.playVideo != nil {
635			base = ed.playVideo.base
636		}
637		// and how long the answer holds: to the end of this scene, or, in a gap,
638		// to the start of the next -- in the master's own seconds, which is the
639		// clock the lanes are placed on. A lane started now stops there by
640		// itself (auxAudio.stopAt), which is what keeps the first sound of the
641		// next scene from being a tick's worth of the lane it silences.
642		until := 0.0
643		if ed.playVideo != nil {
644			if s != nil {
645				until = ed.playVideo.at(s.E)
646			} else if _, next := gapAt(ed.segs, ed.playhead); next >= 0 {
647				until = ed.playVideo.at(ed.segs[next].S)
648			}
649		}

651		ed.player.Hush(own, quiet, until)

654	// hushOf is what a scene does not hear, in the two pieces the preview keeps
655	// its sound in: whether the recording the picture comes from is silenced, and
656	// the scene's own list of silenced lanes. No scene, no answer: gaps and the
657	// ends of the cut are heard whole.
658	func hushOf(s *cutSeg, base string) (bool, []string) {
659		if s == nil {
660			return false, nil
661		}
662		return base != "" && laneQuiet(s.Quiet, base), s.Quiet
663	}

665	// Which camera a scene is shown from (cutSeg.Cam), said on the rows: a held
666	// scene wears a lens badge on every row that was rolling, lit on the row shown,
667	// at the same x as the speaker badges. A lens is a radio (one picture, never
668	// none) where a speaker is a checkbox. Rows filming nothing at those seconds
669	// get none: the render would fall back anyway (pickVideoOn).
670	
671	// camBadge is one row's answer for the scene the badges are about: where it is
672	// drawn, in timeline x and area y, and whether the scene is shown from there.
673	type camBadge struct {
674		row    int
675		cx, cy float64

679	// camBadges is one per row that could show this scene: the rows that have
680	// footage under it. Empty when there is no scene in hand, when the scene is too
681	// narrow to wear a mark, or when one row is all there is -- a badge that is the
682	// only badge answers a question nobody can ask.

685	// at the scene's left edge and read as one question asked of every row.
686	func (ed *cutEditor) camBadges() []camBadge {
687		cx, ok := ed.hearX()

690		}
691		s := ed.hearScene()

695				continue // that camera was not rolling here
696			}
697			out = append(out, camBadge{r, cx, ed.laneTop(r) + ed.laneH()/2, r == s.Cam})
698		}
699		if len(out) < 2 {

701		}

703	}

706	func (ed *cutEditor) camBadgeAt(px, y float64) int {

708			if math.Abs(px-b.cx) <= hearHit && math.Abs(y-b.cy) <= hearHit {
709				return b.row
710			}
711		}
712		return -1
713	}

715	// setSegCam shows the scene from row r; seconds, silenced lanes and effects
716	// stay. It does not coalesce -- rearranging the list under a hand still on a
717	// badge is how a press becomes "what happened to my clip"; the next edit joins

719	func (ed *cutEditor) setSegCam(r int) {
720		s := ed.hearScene()

722			return
723		}
724		ed.pushUndo()
725		s.Cam = r
726		ed.persist()
727		ed.showInsert() // the preview is standing on a frame that came from the old row
728		ed.redrawTracks()
729		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("the scene at %s is shown from %s now", mmss(s.S), ed.camName(r)))

735	func (ed *cutEditor) drawCamBadges(cr *cairo.Context, vx0, vx1 float64) {
736		badges := ed.camBadges()
737		if len(badges) == 0 {
738			return
739		}
740		s := ed.hearScene()
741		x0, x1 := ed.xOf(s.S), ed.xOf(s.E)

744				continue

758	// camPlate is the round plate a lens is drawn on: lit on the row the scene is
759	// shown from, dark on the rows it could be shown from instead. The plate is the
760	// speaker's, because both marks answer "is this row in this scene" and the page

763	func camPlate(cr *cairo.Context, cx, cy float64, on, hot bool) {

770	// like every other mark on this page.
771	func drawLens(cr *cairo.Context, cx, cy float64, on bool) {

773		cr.SetLineWidth(1.4)

778		}
779		cr.Arc(cx, cy, hearR*0.4, 0, 2*math.Pi)

783	// ---- the badge under the pointer ---------------------------------------------
784	//
785	// Every speaker and every lens lights under the pointer, like the rest of the
786	// plated controls on this page. One id rather than a field per control, and one
787	// hit test asking the press's own questions in the press's own order (cut.go):
788	// a hover that answered differently would light a badge the press does not act
789	// on.
790	type badgeID struct {
791		kind int
792		base string // the recording a speaker is about
793		row  int    // the row a lens is about
794	}
795	
796	const (
797		badgeNone   = iota
798		badgeSwitch // a recording's whole-lane switch, in the band's gutter
799		badgePair   // a camera row's, in the picture band's
800		badgeHear   // one lane's badge on the scene the badges are about
801		badgeCam    // the lens that says which camera a scene is shown from
802	)
803	
804	// badgeAt is the badge under a point in timeline px, or none. src says which
805	// band: the two carry different controls at the same x.
806	func (ed *cutEditor) badgeAt(px, y float64, src bool) badgeID {
807		if src {
808			if bases := ed.pairSwitchAt(px, y); len(bases) > 0 {
809				return badgeID{kind: badgePair, base: bases[0]}
810			}
811		} else if base := ed.laneSwitchAt(px, y); base != "" {
812			return badgeID{kind: badgeSwitch, base: base}
813		}
814		if base := ed.hearAt(px, y, src); base != "" {
815			return badgeID{kind: badgeHear, base: base}
816		}
817		if src {
818			if r := ed.camBadgeAt(px, y); r >= 0 {
819				return badgeID{kind: badgeCam, row: r}
820			}
821		}
822		return badgeID{}
823	}
824	
825	// badgeHot is whether b is the badge under the pointer.
826	func (ed *cutEditor) badgeHot(b badgeID) bool { return ed.badgeHov == b }
827	
828	// hoverBadges lights the one under the pointer. x below zero means the pointer
829	// has left the band, which puts them all out: the two bands share the field
830	// because only one of them has the pointer.
831	func (ed *cutEditor) hoverBadges(x, y float64, src bool) {
832		var b badgeID
833		if x >= 0 {

835		}
836		if b == ed.badgeHov {
837			return
838		}
839		ed.badgeHov = b
840		if ed.srcArea != nil {
841			ed.srcArea.QueueDraw()
842		}
843		if ed.audArea != nil {
844			ed.audArea.QueueDraw()
845		}
846	}
