3	// The spelling the subtitles carry.
4	//
5	// The words a subtitle is built from come off the ALIGNER: it is handed the
6	// recogniser's transcript and answers where each word falls, to about 20 ms,
7	// which is the only source of times in the app accurate enough to caption with
8	// (wordCues). What it hands back is bare lowercase, so dressWords puts the
9	// case and punctuation back from the transcript it was given -- the raw one,
10	// straight off the speech model.
11	//
12	// And that is where the session context stopped. The transcript pass reads it
13	// ("use the script's spelling for names, companies and numbers I say aloud")
14	// and writes what it settled on into the session timeline; the subtitles never
15	// read that file, so they went on saying what the recogniser heard. One
16	// recogniser writes "rsa two hundred and sixty" where another writes "RSA-260"
17	// -- the same seconds of the same video, captioned two ways depending on which
18	// model was loaded that day, and the sentence in the user context asking for
19	// one of them had no effect on the subtitles at all.
20	//
21	// fixWords closes that: the words keep their times and take the transcript's
22	// spelling. It is a re-dressing and never a rewrite -- no word gains a time it
23	// did not have, and a stretch that cannot be matched keeps what the recogniser
24	// wrote rather than guessing.
25	
26	import "strings"
27	
28	// fixRunReach is how far apart the two spellings of one stretch may be before
29	// the walk gives up on it: "two hundred and sixty" against "RSA-260" is four
30	// words against one, and a window of six covers every rewrite of a number, a
31	// name or a company seen so far. Past it the walk has lost its place, and
32	// dressing the rest of the line from the wrong offset would put the right
33	// words on the wrong seconds.
34	const fixRunReach = 6
35	
36	// fixWords re-dresses the aligned words with what the transcript pass wrote
37	// for the same seconds. rows are the merged timeline's (session.tsv): the
38	// fixed text, on the session clock, with the recording each line came off.
39	//
40	// Only .raw changes -- the word used for MATCHING (.w) stays the recogniser's,
41	// because every pass that reads the words reads that one, and only the
42	// subtitles read the other (wordCues).
43	func fixWords(words []srcWord, rows []tsvRow) {
44		if len(words) == 0 || len(rows) == 0 {
45			return
46		}
47		// a cursor per recording: the words and the rows are both in time order,
48		// so each row picks up where the last one of its recording left off
49		at := map[string]int{}
50		idx := map[string][]int{}
51		for i, w := range words {
52			idx[w.src] = append(idx[w.src], i)
53		}
54		for _, r := range rows {
55			if r.spk == "EVENT" || strings.TrimSpace(r.text) == "" {
56				continue
57			}
58			in := idx[r.src]
59			var mine []*srcWord
60			k := at[r.src]
61			for ; k < len(in); k++ {
62				w := &words[in[k]]
63				mid := (w.s + w.e) / 2
64				if mid < r.s-0.01 {
65					continue // said before this line: a word the row does not cover
66				}
67				if mid > r.e+0.01 {
68					break
69				}
70				mine = append(mine, w)
71			}
72			at[r.src] = k
73			redress(mine, strings.Fields(r.text))
74		}
75	}
76	
77	// redress walks one line's words against one line's fixed text and hands each
78	// word its spelling. Where the two spell a stretch differently, the whole of
79	// the fixed spelling goes on the FIRST word of the stretch and the rest are
80	// emptied: every word keeps its own seconds, so a cut through the middle of
81	// such a stretch loses the words rather than showing words the video does not
82	// play -- which is the one thing subtitles built from the aligner exist to
83	// prevent.
84	func redress(ws []*srcWord, fixed []string) {
85		// A line with NOTHING in common is not a line that was respelled: it is a
86		// line the walk should not be trusted with -- a row matched to the wrong
87		// recording's words, a clock that moved under one of them. Left as it was
88		// heard, it is one line captioned the way it always was; rewritten from a
89		// text that shares no word with it, it is the wrong words on these
90		// seconds. One word in common is enough to believe the pairing.
91		if !anyShared(ws, fixed) {
92			return
93		}
94		pending := "" // fixed words with no time of their own, waiting for one
95		put := func(w *srcWord, s string) {
96			w.raw = strings.TrimSpace(pending + s)
97			pending = ""
98		}
99		i, j := 0, 0
100		for i < len(ws) && j < len(fixed) {
101			if bareWord(fixed[j]) == ws[i].w {
102				put(ws[i], fixed[j])
103				i, j = i+1, j+1
104				continue
105			}
106			di, dj, ok := fixResync(ws, fixed, i, j)
107			switch {
108			case !ok:
109				// nothing within reach spells the same: the walk takes them as
110				// the same word anyway -- it is the same position in a line that
111				// matched either side of here -- and the transcript's spelling
112				// wins, which is the whole point. "RSA-1024" against a heard
113				// "rsa" resyncs on neither and is the right word for that second.
114				// The next word is matched normally, so a walk that really has
115				// lost its place finds itself again rather than running on.
116				put(ws[i], fixed[j])
117				i, j = i+1, j+1
118			case di == 0:
119				// the transcript has words the recogniser never heard: they have
120				// no seconds, so they ride on the next word that does
121				pending += strings.Join(fixed[j:j+dj], " ") + " "
122				j += dj
123			default:
124				put(ws[i], strings.Join(fixed[j:j+dj], " "))
125				for k := i + 1; k < i+di; k++ {
126					ws[k].raw = ""
127				}
128				i, j = i+di, j+dj
129			}
130		}
131		// whatever the line ends with and the words do not: onto the last word
132		// that has a time, for the same reason
133		if j < len(fixed) && len(ws) > 0 {
134			last := ws[min(i, len(ws))-1]
135			last.raw = strings.TrimSpace(last.raw + " " + strings.Join(fixed[j:], " "))
136		}
137		// ...and the other way round -- words left over when the line has run out.
138		// They are the tail of a stretch the transcript folded into fewer words
139		// ("two hundred and fifty" into "RSA-250"), and the fold is already
140		// printed on the first of them: kept, they would be said twice.
141		for ; i < len(ws); i++ {
142			ws[i].raw = ""
143		}
144	}
145	
146	// anyShared is whether the two spellings of a line have a single word in
147	// common, which is what makes the walk below a re-dressing rather than a
148	// guess.
149	func anyShared(ws []*srcWord, fixed []string) bool {
150		have := make(map[string]bool, len(ws))
151		for _, w := range ws {
152			have[w.w] = true
153		}
154		for _, f := range fixed {
155			if have[bareWord(f)] {
156				return true
157			}
158		}
159		return false
160	}
161	
162	// fixResync is the shortest pair of runs that puts the walk back in step: how
163	// many words of the recogniser's and how many of the transcript's to skip
164	// before the two spell the same word again. Shortest by total length, so one
165	// word against four is found before two against five.
166	func fixResync(ws []*srcWord, fixed []string, i, j int) (int, int, bool) {
167		for d := 1; d <= 2*fixRunReach; d++ {
168			for di := 0; di <= d && di <= fixRunReach; di++ {
169				dj := d - di
170				if dj > fixRunReach || i+di >= len(ws) || j+dj >= len(fixed) {
171					continue
172				}
173				if bareWord(fixed[j+dj]) == ws[i+di].w {
174					return di, dj, true
175				}
176			}
177		}
178		return 0, 0, false
179	}

// volumeCtl is the preview volume control: a speaker and a slider, built fresh
// for each place a video can be played from. Built rather than shared because
// a GTK widget has one parent, and the alternative to one per transport is
// re-parenting it on every tab switch.
func volumeCtl() *gtk.Box {
	icon := gtk.NewImageFromIconName("audio-volume-high-symbolic")
	sc := gtk.NewScaleWithRange(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 0, 100, 1)
	sc.SetValue(previewVol * 100)
	sc.SetSizeRequest(120, -1)
	tip := "preview volume — the players only; nothing that is rendered, and the " +
		"same setting wherever it is shown"
	icon.SetTooltipText(tip)
	sc.SetTooltipText(tip)
	sc.ConnectValueChanged(func() {
		if volSyncing {

3	// ---- a lane the cut put there -----------------------------------------------
4	//
5	// A cut lane is a shot copied from elsewhere in the session, or a video that
6	// was never a source, on a row of its own. Cut-only: it lives in cut.json,
7	// nothing transcribes or describes it; reload builds the sources and lays these
8	// over. It gets a waveform lane from the same window (Off, Dur) as its
9	// pictures. A row is a window on a file -- tlVideo.at maps session seconds to
10	// file seconds; a recording is the same with the window wide open. Its row is
11	// pinned (cut_shift.go): cutSeg.Cam is a row NUMBER.
12	
13	import (
14		"fmt"
15		"math"
16		"path/filepath"
17		"sort"
18	
19		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/cairo"

21	
22	type cutLane struct {
23		Name string  `json:"name"`          // the row's name, and its key everywhere else
24		Src  string  `json:"src"`           // the file it shows, project-relative
25		At   float64 `json:"at"`            // the session second the row starts at
26		Off  float64 `json:"off,omitempty"` // the second of the file that lands there
27		Dur  float64 `json:"dur"`           // and how long it runs
28	}
29	
30	// laneVideos turns the saved lanes into rows of the picture band.
31	//
32	// The thumbnails come from the source's own frame folder when the file IS a
33	// source: a copied shot is one recording seen twice, and its frames were
34	// extracted the first time round. A file from outside the session has none, and
35	// its row draws its name and no pictures -- extracting frames for it would be
36	// exactly the Prepare pass this lane exists to do without.
37	func (a *App) laneVideos(lanes []cutLane, vids []tlVideo) []tlVideo {
38		// the wall clock of session second nought, for a lane whose file has no
39		// stamp of its own to read. Only the output clips are named off this.
40		//
41		// Read off the recording that STARTS earliest rather than the first in the
42		// list: a corrected clock makes the two different answers, and the render
43		// hands its sources over in the order they were chosen while the page holds
44		// them in timeline order. Same lanes, same seconds, two names for the clip.
45		zeroWall, first := 0.0, math.Inf(1)
46		for _, v := range vids {
47			if v.start < first {
48				zeroWall, first = v.wall-v.start, v.start
49			}
50		}
51		var out []tlVideo
52		for _, l := range lanes {
53			if l.Dur < minSegLn || l.Name == "" || l.Src == "" {
54				// a row of no seconds is a row nobody can see or press, and one
55				// with no file behind it would resolve to the project folder
56				continue
57			}
58			path := a.loadPath(l.Src)
59			v := tlVideo{base: l.Name, path: path, start: l.At, off: l.Off, dur: l.Dur,
60				wall: zeroWall + l.At - l.Off, fps: 30}
61			if src := videoByPath(vids, path); src != nil {
62				v.wall, v.fps, v.w, v.h = src.wall, src.fps, src.w, src.h
63				v.interval, v.frames = src.interval, src.frames
64			} else {
65				// what the file itself says it is, when it says anything. wall is
66				// the wall clock of the file's own second NOUGHT (produce names the
67				// output clips off it), which is what a stamp in the name is -- so
68				// off does not come into it, and a file naming no moment keeps the
69				// place the row was put at instead.
70				if st, ok := nameStamp(filepath.Base(path)); ok {
71					v.wall = st
72				}
73				v.fps = ffprobeFPS(path)
74				v.w, v.h, _ = ffprobeSize(path)
75			}
76			out = append(out, v)
77		}
78		return out
79	}
80	
81	// laneAudios is the sound of cut lanes: the file's track windowed as the row's
82	// pictures are. Not masterLanes (whose window is the whole file): one file on
83	// the band twice is two lanes with two offs. Files without a track get none.
84	// Channel count comes off the source's own lane when the file is a source
85	// (src: the non-cut lanes).
86	func laneAudios(rows []tlVideo, src []tlAudio) []tlAudio {
87		var out []tlAudio
88		for _, v := range rows {
89			ch, known := 0, false
90			for _, au := range src {
91				// the MASTER lane of that file, because that is the sound a copied
92				// shot carries: the file's first track, the one the render takes
93				// off the footage input. A further track of a multi-track capture is
94				// on the same path and is not it (cut_tracks.go).
95				if au.path == v.path && au.master {
96					ch, known = au.chans, true
97					break
98				}
99			}
100			// and a source whose first track this session was told to leave out is
101			// a source with nothing to copy: only a file that is not in the session
102			// at all -- an insert from outside it -- is worth a probe of its own
103			if !known {
104				if inSession(src, v.path) {
105					continue
106				}
107				ch = ffprobeChannels(v.path)
108			}
109			if ch < 1 {
110				continue
111			}
112			out = append(out, tlAudio{base: v.base, path: v.path, start: v.start,
113				off: v.off, dur: v.dur, chans: ch, master: true})
114		}
115		return out
116	}
117	
118	// inSession says whether a file is one the session's own lanes were built from,
119	// which is how "this source has no first track" is told apart from "this file
120	// was never a source": the first has an answer already and the second has none.
121	func inSession(src []tlAudio, path string) bool {
122		for _, au := range src {
123			if au.path == path {
124				return true
125			}
126		}
127		return false
128	}
129	
130	// videoByPath is the recording a lane is a second look at, or nil when the file
131	// came from outside the session.
132	func videoByPath(vids []tlVideo, path string) *tlVideo {
133		for i := range vids {
134			if vids[i].path == path {
135				return &vids[i]
136			}
137		}
138		return nil
139	}
140	
141	// cutLaneName is what to call a new row: the file's name, and the file's name with
142	// a number after it when the session already has one. Names are the key the
143	// pinned rows and the hand-made corrections are held under, so two rows sharing
144	// one would move together and be drawn on top of each other.
145	func cutLaneName(vids []tlVideo, want string) string {
146		taken := func(s string) bool {
147			for _, v := range vids {
148				if v.base == s {
149					return true
150				}
151			}
152			return false
153		}
154		if !taken(want) {
155			return want
156		}
157		for n := 2; ; n++ {
158			try := fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d", want, n)
159			if !taken(try) {
160				return try
161			}
162		}
163	}
164	
165	// addLane puts a stretch of a file on a row of its own and returns the row's
166	// name. src is absolute; off is the file second the row starts at, at where
167	// that lands in the session, dur how long it runs. Rows are frozen first
168	// (setShift's reason): a row number is what a scene carries.
169	func (ed *cutEditor) addLane(src string, off, at, dur float64) string {
170		off, at = math.Max(0, off), math.Max(0, at)
171		// a window can only be as long as there is file left past off. Zero dur
172		// means "as much as there is", which is what choosing a file rather than
173		// copying a stretch asks for; anything longer than that is a row drawing
174		// band the green can be laid on over footage that stops partway.
175		if d := ed.srcDur(src); d > off {
176			if dur < minSegLn {
177				dur = d - off
178			}
179			dur = math.Min(dur, d-off)
180		}
181		if dur < minSegLn {
182			return ""
183		}
184		ed.pushUndo()
185		ed.freezeRows()
186		name := cutLaneName(ed.vids, baseName(src))
187		ed.cutLanes = append(ed.cutLanes, cutLane{Name: name, Src: ed.a.storePath(src),
188			At: at, Off: off, Dur: dur})
189		// its own row, under everything already there -- read off the rows in use
190		// rather than off laneN, which is floored at one and would leave an empty
191		// row above the first lane on a project with no footage of its own yet
192		row := 0
193		for _, v := range ed.vids {
194			row = max(row, v.lane+1)
195		}
196		ed.rows[name] = row
197		ed.setLanes(ed.cutLanes)
198		ed.relayout()
199		ed.persist()
200		return name
201	}
202	
203	// srcDur is how long the file behind a lane runs, or zero when nobody knows.
204	// A recording on the band already answers it -- the row IS that file, whole --
205	// and shelling out for a number the page is drawing would be an ffprobe per
206	// press for nothing. Cut lanes are skipped: one of those is a WINDOW on a file
207	// and its dur is the window, which would clamp the next lane to the last one.
208	func (ed *cutEditor) srcDur(path string) float64 {
209		for i := range ed.vids {
210			if v := &ed.vids[i]; v.path == path && v.dur > 0 && !ed.isCutLane(v.base) {
211				return v.dur
212			}
213		}
214		if d, err := ffprobeDur(path); err == nil {
215			return d
216		}
217		return 0
218	}
219	
220	// killLane takes a row away again, with whatever the cut had put on it. The
221	// scenes go with it: they are frames of a file that is no longer on the page,
222	// and a scene left pointing at a row that is not there falls back to whatever
223	// was rolling at that second (pickVideoOn) -- which is a different picture
224	// arriving in the render for a reason nobody could see on this page.
225	//
226	// The rows below it come up one, and every scene on them comes with them.
227	func (ed *cutEditor) killLane(name string) {
228		i := cutLaneIdx(ed.cutLanes, name)
229		if i < 0 {
230			return
231		}
232		// the row it is actually DRAWN on, which is what every scene's Cam is
233		// measured against. The pin says the same thing whenever there is one, but
234		// only the band is sure -- and a lane in cut.json that never made it onto
235		// the band has no scenes to take with it and no rows to bring up, so
236		// reading a missing pin as row nought would take the first camera's cut.
237		row := -1
238		for i := range ed.vids {
239			if ed.vids[i].base == name {
240				row = ed.vids[i].lane
241				break
242			}
243		}
244		ed.pushUndo()
245		ed.cutLanes = append(ed.cutLanes[:i], ed.cutLanes[i+1:]...)
246		delete(ed.rows, name)
247		delete(ed.shift, name)
248		var vids []tlVideo
249		for _, v := range ed.vids {
250			if v.base != name {
251				vids = append(vids, v)
252			}
253		}
254		ed.vids = vids
255		// and its sound, which came with its pictures (laneAudios) and has no more
256		// reason than they had to stay on a band the row has left. Taken off here
257		// rather than by rebuilding through setLanes, because the rows below have
258		// to come up one first and that is this function's own work.
259		var auds []tlAudio
260		for _, au := range ed.auds {
261			if au.base != name {
262				auds = append(auds, au)
263			}
264		}
265		ed.auds = auds
266		ed.fitAudio()
267		ed.fitSelAud()
268		if row < 0 {
269			ed.relayout()
270			ed.persist()
271			return
272		}
273		ed.closeRow(row)
274		ed.relayout()
275		ed.persist()
276		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("removed the %s lane", name))
277		ed.redrawTracks()
278	}

280	func cutLaneIdx(lanes []cutLane, name string) int {
281		for i, l := range lanes {
282			if l.Name == name {
283				return i
284			}
285		}
286		return -1
287	}
288	
289	// isCutLane says this row was put there by the cut rather than by Prepare.
290	func (ed *cutEditor) isCutLane(base string) bool { return cutLaneIdx(ed.cutLanes, base) >= 0 }
291	
292	// ---- the ✕ that takes one away ----------------------------------------------
293	//
294	// A recording is removed on Prepare; a cut lane was made by a press here and is
295	// unmade by one: drawKillBadge at the row's left edge beside its name, asked
296	// before the clip border it can sit on (cut.go).
297	
298	// laneKillCentre is where the ✕ for a cut lane sits: timeline x, area y.
299	func (ed *cutEditor) laneKillCentre(v *tlVideo) (float64, float64) {
300		return v.pxOrigin + killIn, ed.laneTop(v.lane) + segKillTop
301	}
302	
303	// laneKillAt is the cut lane whose ✕ is under a press, or "".
304	func (ed *cutEditor) laneKillAt(px, y float64) string {
305		for i := range ed.vids {
306			v := &ed.vids[i]
307			if !ed.isCutLane(v.base) {
308				continue
309			}
310			cx, cy := ed.laneKillCentre(v)
311			if math.Abs(px-cx) <= segKillHit && math.Abs(y-cy) <= segKillHit {
312				return v.base
313			}
314		}
315		return ""
316	}
317	
318	// hoverLaneKill lights the badge under the pointer. x below zero means the
319	// pointer has left the band.
320	func (ed *cutEditor) hoverLaneKill(x, y float64) {
321		name, row := "", -1
322		if x >= 0 && ed.hitPics(y) {
323			name = ed.laneKillAt(x+ed.viewX, y)
324			row = ed.rowKillAt(x+ed.viewX, y)
325		}
326		if name != ed.laneHov || row != ed.rowHov {
327			ed.laneHov, ed.rowHov = name, row
328			if ed.srcArea != nil {
329				ed.srcArea.QueueDraw()
330			}
331		}
332	}
333	
334	// drawLaneKill paints them, in drawTrack's own translation so x is timeline px.
335	func (ed *cutEditor) drawLaneKill(cr *cairo.Context, vx0, vx1 float64) {
336		for i := range ed.vids {
337			v := &ed.vids[i]
338			if !ed.isCutLane(v.base) {
339				continue
340			}
341			cx, cy := ed.laneKillCentre(v)
342			if cx < vx0-segKillHit || cx > vx1+segKillHit {
343				continue
344			}
345			drawKillBadge(cr, cx, cy, ed.laneHov == v.base)
346		}
347	}
348	
349	// closeRow brings the rows above `row` down one and renumbers everything that
350	// names a row: pins, scenes, selection, a copy in hand, the watch. Shared by
351	// killLane and killRow. Every source is pinned first -- an unpinned one is
352	// re-coloured at the next relayout and could land in the closed gap.
353	func (ed *cutEditor) closeRow(row int) {
354		if ed.rows == nil {
355			ed.rows = map[string]int{}
356		}
357		for _, v := range ed.vids {
358			if _, ok := ed.rows[v.base]; !ok {
359				ed.rows[v.base] = v.lane
360			}
361		}
362		for b, r := range ed.rows {
363			if r > row {
364				ed.rows[b] = r - 1
365			}
366		}
367		var segs []cutSeg
368		for _, s := range ed.segs {
369			switch {
370			case s.Cam == row:
371				continue // it showed that row, and that row has gone
372			case s.Cam > row:
373				s.Cam--
374			}
375			segs = append(segs, s)
376		}
377		// the live row numbers that are not written in the cut. A selection, a copy
378		// in hand and the watch each name a ROW, and a row number that quietly came
379		// to mean the camera below is the same silent repointing the pins exist to
380		// prevent -- except here it would put the green, the next paste, or the
381		// preview on footage nobody chose. What named the row that has gone lets go
382		// instead.
383		switch {
384		case ed.sel.lane == row:
385			ed.sel.active = false
386		case ed.sel.lane > row:
387			ed.sel.lane--
388		}
389		switch {
390		case !ed.copyOn || ed.copyAud != "": // a copied SOUND names a lane, not a row
391		case ed.copyCam == row:
392			ed.copyOn = false
393		case ed.copyCam > row:
394			ed.copyCam--
395		}
396		switch {
397		case ed.monRow-1 == row: // monRow is 1-based, 0 for off
398			ed.monRow = 0
399		case ed.monRow-1 > row:
400			ed.monRow--
401		}
402		if ed.nRows > 0 {
403			ed.nRows-- // one row fewer is one row less of floor to hold
404		}
405		ed.laneHov, ed.rowHov = "", -1 // the badge under the pointer went with it
406		ed.segs = segs
407		ed.dropSeg()
408		ed.dropEdge()
409		ed.syncSelBtns()
410		ed.syncInsertBtn() // ⇲ Lane goes off the bar with the copy it would have used
411	}
412	
413	// ---- the ✕ on a row with nothing on it ---------------------------------------
414	//
415	// moveRow leaves an emptied row standing (closing it would renumber scenes as
416	// a side effect of a drag). It wears the same ✕ a cut lane does, at the edge
417	// of the VIEW since there is no footage to put it beside.
418	
419	// rowEmpty says nothing is drawn on row r.
420	func (ed *cutEditor) rowEmpty(r int) bool {
421		for i := range ed.vids {
422			if ed.vids[i].lane == r {
423				return false
424			}
425		}
426		return true
427	}
428	
429	// rowKillAt is the empty row whose ✕ is under a press, or -1. Timeline px, so
430	// the centre is the view's left edge plus the badge's inset. Not offered on the
431	// last row standing: with no footage at all the one row IS the band, and an ✕
432	// there would remove nothing.
433	func (ed *cutEditor) rowKillAt(px, y float64) int {
434		if ed.laneN <= 1 {
435			return -1
436		}
437		for r := 0; r < ed.laneN; r++ {
438			if !ed.rowEmpty(r) {
439				continue
440			}
441			cx, cy := gutterMid, ed.laneTop(r)+segKillTop
442			if math.Abs(px-cx) <= segKillHit && math.Abs(y-cy) <= segKillHit {
443				return r
444			}
445		}
446		return -1
447	}

449	// drawRowKill paints them, in drawTrack's own translation like drawLaneKill.
450	// They stand in the gutter at the head of the tape (cut_gutter.go), which is
451	// where every permanent control on this page is: an empty row has no footage
452	// to be drawn over, but it has neighbours that do, and one rule for the lot is
453	// worth more than one exception.
454	func (ed *cutEditor) drawRowKill(cr *cairo.Context) {
455		if ed.laneN <= 1 {
456			return
457		}
458		for r := 0; r < ed.laneN; r++ {

460				continue
461			}
462			drawKillBadge(cr, gutterMid, ed.laneTop(r)+segKillTop, ed.rowHov == r)
463		}
464	}

466	// killRow takes an empty row away: the rows below come up one and every scene
467	// keeps the camera it was showing. Only an EMPTY row -- a row with footage has
468	// its own ways off the band (a cut lane's ✕, Prepare) and each of those
469	// says what happens to the footage, which this deliberately has no answer for.
470	func (ed *cutEditor) killRow(row int) {
471		if row < 0 || row >= ed.laneN || ed.laneN <= 1 || !ed.rowEmpty(row) {
472			return
473		}
474		ed.pushUndo()
475		ed.closeRow(row)
476		ed.relayout()
477		ed.persist()
478		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("removed the empty row %d", row+1))
479		ed.redrawTracks()
480	}
481	
482	// setLanes puts the cut's own rows on the band, replacing whatever was there.
483	// Rebuilt rather than patched: a load is putting them there for the first time,
484	// and an undo may be putting one back, taking one away, or doing both at once.
485	//
486	// They land where the corrections say, not where cut.json says: a lane can be
487	// right-dragged like any other row (cut_shift.go), and its correction is held in
488	// the same map under the same key as a recording's.
489	func (ed *cutEditor) setLanes(lanes []cutLane) {
490		// what is on the band because Prepare put it there, picture and
491		// sound. Asked before ed.cutLanes is replaced, so a lane being TAKEN away
492		// is still known to be one: read after, its name is in neither list and it
493		// would survive as a row of a file nothing on the page mentions.
494		var vids []tlVideo
495		for _, v := range ed.vids {
496			if !ed.isCutLane(v.base) {
497				vids = append(vids, v)
498			}
499		}
500		var auds []tlAudio
501		for _, au := range ed.auds {
502			if !ed.isCutLane(au.base) {
503				auds = append(auds, au)
504			}
505		}
506		ed.cutLanes = append([]cutLane(nil), lanes...)
507		rows := ed.a.laneVideos(ed.cutLanes, vids)
508		for i := range rows {
509			rows[i].start += ed.shift[rows[i].base]
510		}
511		ed.vids = append(vids, rows...)
512		ed.sortVids()
513		// and their sound with them, from the rows as they now stand so a lane
514		// dragged in time takes its waveform along
515		ed.auds = append(auds, laneAudios(rows, auds)...)
516		sortLanes(ed.auds)
517		ed.loadWaves() // a row added now would otherwise draw ground until a reload
518		ed.fitAudio()  // one more lane to make room for, or one fewer
519		ed.fitSelAud() // and a selection that was on a lane just taken away
520	}
521	
522	// sortVids puts the picture band back in timeline order. Stable, so two rows
523	// starting on the same second keep the order the list already had rather than
524	// swapping places on every redraw.
525	func (ed *cutEditor) sortVids() {
526		sort.SliceStable(ed.vids, func(i, j int) bool { return ed.vids[i].start < ed.vids[j].start })
527	}
528	
529	// sameCutLanes compares two lists of the cut's own rows, in order: reordering them
530	// changes which row each is drawn on, which is an edit like any other.
531	func sameCutLanes(a, b []cutLane) bool {
532		if len(a) != len(b) {
533			return false
534		}
535		for i := range a {
536			if a[i] != b[i] {
537				return false
538			}
539		}
540		return true
541	}

449	// came off, so the correction is one addition per line.

458			rows[i].s, rows[i].e = rows[i].s+d, rows[i].e+d
459		}
460		sort.SliceStable(rows, func(i, j int) bool { return rows[i].s < rows[j].s })

23		// (waveLaneH): that band is one of a dozen rows sharing a page, and this
24		// is the only picture in its own half of the column -- the seconds worth
25		// cloning are picked by looking at it, and a 30 px strip is a strip you
26		// squint at.
27		takeLaneH  = 56.0
28		takeMaxPps = 200.0
29		// a press that travels less than this is a click, not a drag: it clears
30		// the selection instead of making a nought-length one
31		takeClickPx = 3.0
32	)
33	
34	// what ▶ says when it is a ▶. Named because the button wears two faces and the
35	// other one has to be able to put this back (syncPlayBtn).
36	const takePlayTip = "Play from the red bar: the takes, one after another — " +
37		"exactly what the model is cloned from"
38	
39	type takeBand struct {
40		vp    *voicePicker
41		area  *gtk.DrawingArea
42		frame *gtk.Frame
43		// ＋, －, ▶ takes. Kept because they are greyed as a set: with no
44		// recording behind the band there is nothing any of them could do.
45		addBtn, delBtn, playBtn *gtk.Button
46	
47		// the way back to the rest of the recording once the wheel has zoomed past
48		// it. Ours rather than a scrolled window's, for the reason the Cut page's is
49		// (cut.go): a scrolled window would want a child as wide as the whole file.
50		bar *gtk.Scrollbar
51		adj *gtk.Adjustment
52	
53		src  string // the recording drawn, "" when this voice has none
54		base string
55		dur  float64
56		wf   *waveform
57	
58		pps   float64 // px per second; fitPps when the whole file is shown
59		viewX float64 // px of it scrolled off the left
60		lastX float64 // where the pointer is, so the wheel zooms around it
61		w     float64 // the area's width, learned at the last resize
62	
63		// where ▶ starts, in the file's own seconds; < 0 for "at the first take".
64		// A click puts it there, and until the click there is nowhere in a
65		// recording nobody has listened to that is a better guess than its takes.
66		at float64
67		// and the same bar under the pointer, drawn faint: a click is about to put
68		// it there, and a band that says so before the click is one you can aim
69		hoverX float64
70		hover  bool
71	
72		takes []voiceTake
73		// the live selection in the file's own seconds; sel1 <= sel0 is none.
74		// It is not a take: ＋ is what makes it one, so a drag can be re-aimed
75		// as many times as it takes without touching what the model gets.
76		sel0, sel1 float64
77	
78		// ▶: the takes queued back to back, and which one is sounding. The
79		// player's own end-of-segment is what advances it (chainOn).
80		queue []voiceTake
81		qAt   int
82	}
83	
84	func (b *takeBand) sel() (float64, float64, bool) {
85		if b.sel1 <= b.sel0 {
86			return 0, 0, false
87		}
88		return b.sel0, b.sel1, true
89	}
90	
91	// ---- geometry ---------------------------------------------------------------
92	
93	// fitPps is the zoom at which the whole recording is on screen, and the zoom
94	// this will not go below: there is nothing to the left of a file's first second
95	// or to the right of its last, so scrolling past either is scrolling into
96	// nothing.
97	func (b *takeBand) fitPps() float64 {
98		if b.dur <= 0 || b.w <= 0 {
99			return 1
100		}
101		return b.w / b.dur
102	}
103	
104	func (b *takeBand) xOf(t float64) float64 { return t*b.pps - b.viewX }
105	func (b *takeBand) tAt(x float64) float64 { return (x + b.viewX) / b.pps }
106	
107	// clampView keeps the zoom and the offset in range together, since neither is
108	// valid on its own: zooming out past the fit and then scrolling is how a band
109	// ends up drawing a file that starts three hundred pixels in.
110	func (b *takeBand) clampView() {
111		b.pps = math.Max(b.fitPps(), math.Min(takeMaxPps, b.pps))
112		b.viewX = math.Max(0, math.Min(math.Max(0, b.dur*b.pps-b.w), b.viewX))
113	}
114	
115	// zoomAt multiplies the zoom and leaves the second under the cursor where it
116	// was, which is the only zoom that does not lose your place.
117	func (b *takeBand) zoomAt(x, factor float64) {
118		at := b.tAt(x)
119		b.pps *= factor
120		b.clampView()
121		b.viewX = at*b.pps - x
122		b.clampView()
123		b.syncScroll()
124		b.redraw()
125	}
126	
127	// syncScroll points the scrollbar at the recording as it is now shown, and is
128	// also where the bar disappears. The adjustment holds the offset in the same
129	// pixels viewX is in, and its clamping is the one that counts: setting the
130	// value against the new upper is what pulls a view back onto the file after a
131	// zoom out, so viewX is read back from it rather than trusted.
132	func (b *takeBand) syncScroll() {
133		if b.adj == nil {
134			return
135		}
136		b.adj.SetUpper(b.dur * b.pps)
137		b.adj.SetPageSize(b.w)
138		b.adj.SetStepIncrement(b.w / 8)
139		b.adj.SetPageIncrement(b.w * 0.9)
140		b.adj.SetValue(b.viewX)
141		b.viewX = b.adj.Value()
142		b.bar.SetVisible(b.dur*b.pps > b.w+0.5)
143	}
144	
145	func (b *takeBand) redraw() {
146		if b.area != nil {
147			b.area.QueueDraw()
148		}
149	}
150	
151	// laneCount is how many lanes the envelope draws, before it has arrived as well
152	// as after: one, until the decode says two.
153	func (b *takeBand) laneCount() int {
154		if b.wf != nil && len(b.wf.chans) > 0 {
155			return len(b.wf.chans)
156		}
157		return 1
158	}
159	
160	func (b *takeBand) height() int {
161		return int(takeRulerH + float64(b.laneCount())*takeLaneH + 2*wavePad)
162	}
163	
164	// ---- building ---------------------------------------------------------------
165	
166	// buildTakeBand makes the band and the three buttons that work on it. The
167	// buttons are returned separately because they belong on the dropdown's row --
168	// the choice of voice and the choice of seconds within it are one decision, and
169	// splitting them over two rows put a slider between them.
170	func (vp *voicePicker) buildTakeBand() (*gtk.Frame, *gtk.Box) {
171		b := &takeBand{vp: vp, pps: 1, at: -1}
172		vp.band = b
173	
174		b.area = gtk.NewDrawingArea()
175		b.area.SetDrawFunc(b.draw)
176		b.area.SetContentHeight(b.height())
177		b.area.SetHExpand(true)
178		b.area.SetTooltipText("The recording this voice is cloned from. Drag to select, " +
179			"＋ to make that a take, click to put the red bar where ▶ starts, wheel to " +
180			"zoom, Shift+wheel to pan. With no takes the seconds are chosen for you.")
181	
182		// the width is the view, and it is learned here rather than at the draw:
183		// the scrollbar has to be told about it, and showing or hiding a widget
184		// from inside a draw is how you get a resize loop (fitSrc says the same)
185		b.area.ConnectResize(func(w, _ int) {
186			b.w = float64(w)
187			b.clampView()
188			b.syncScroll()
189			b.redraw()
190		})
191	
192		motion := gtk.NewEventControllerMotion()
193		motion.ConnectMotion(func(x, _ float64) {
194			b.lastX, b.hoverX, b.hover = x, x, true
195			b.redraw()
196		})
197		motion.ConnectLeave(func() {
198			b.hover = false
199			b.redraw()
200		})
201		b.area.AddController(motion)
202	
203		// the Cut page's wheel, to the letter (cut.go): plain wheel zooms around
204		// the cursor, Shift -- and a trackpad's sideways swipe -- pans
205		scroll := gtk.NewEventControllerScroll(gtk.EventControllerScrollBothAxes)
206		scroll.ConnectScroll(func(dx, dy float64) bool {
207			if scroll.CurrentEventState()&gdk.ShiftMask != 0 {
208				dx, dy = dy, 0
209			}
210			if dx != 0 {
211				b.viewX += dx * b.w / 8
212				b.clampView()
213				b.syncScroll()
214				b.redraw()
215			}
216			if dy != 0 {
217				b.zoomAt(b.lastX, math.Pow(1.25, -dy))
218			}
219			return true
220		})
221		b.area.AddController(scroll)
222	
223		drag := gtk.NewGestureDrag()
224		var fromX float64
225		drag.ConnectDragBegin(func(x, _ float64) { fromX = x })
226		drag.ConnectDragUpdate(func(dx, _ float64) { b.dragTo(fromX, fromX+dx) })
227		drag.ConnectDragEnd(func(dx, _ float64) {
228			if math.Abs(dx) < takeClickPx {
229				// a click is "never mind, start here": it puts the selection away
230				// rather than leaving a hairline one that ＋ would then refuse, and
231				// it moves the bar ▶ picks up from
232				b.sel0, b.sel1 = 0, 0
233				if b.dur > 0 {
234					b.at = math.Max(0, math.Min(b.dur, b.tAt(fromX)))
235				}
236				b.redraw()
237				return
238			}
239			b.dragTo(fromX, fromX+dx)
240		})
241		b.area.AddController(drag)
242	
243		// the playhead is only worth a redraw while something is running through
244		// the takes; the rest of the time this band is a still picture
245		b.area.AddTickCallback(func(_ gtk.Widgetter, _ gdk.FrameClocker) bool {
246			if len(b.queue) > 0 && vp.playing() {
247				b.redraw()
248			}
249			return true
250		})
251	
252		// Hidden while the whole file is on screen: a bar at the zoom floor says
253		// there is more recording off to the right when there is not.
254		b.adj = gtk.NewAdjustment(0, 0, 0, 1, 1, 0)
255		b.adj.ConnectValueChanged(func() {
256			b.viewX = b.adj.Value()
257			b.redraw()
258		})
259		b.bar = gtk.NewScrollbar(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, b.adj)
260		b.bar.SetVisible(false)
261	
262		inner := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 0)
263		inner.Append(b.area)
264		inner.Append(b.bar)
265		b.frame = gtk.NewFrame("")
266		b.frame.SetLabelWidget(nil)
267		b.frame.SetChild(inner)
268	
269		b.addBtn = gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-add-symbolic")
270		b.addBtn.SetTooltipText("Use the selected seconds as a voice-clone take")
271		b.addBtn.ConnectClicked(b.addClicked)
272		b.delBtn = gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-remove-symbolic")
273		b.delBtn.SetTooltipText("Take the selected seconds back out of the takes")
274		b.delBtn.ConnectClicked(b.delClicked)
275		b.playBtn = gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
276		b.playBtn.SetTooltipText(takePlayTip)
277		b.playBtn.ConnectClicked(b.playClicked)
278	
279		btns := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 4)
280		btns.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
281		btns.Append(b.addBtn)
282		btns.Append(b.delBtn)
283		btns.Append(b.playBtn)
284		return b.frame, btns
285	}
286	
287	// dragTo sets the selection from two x's, either way round, clipped to the
288	// file: dragging off the left end means "from the start", not a negative
289	// second the reference would then be cut at.
290	func (b *takeBand) dragTo(x0, x1 float64) {
291		t0, t1 := b.tAt(math.Min(x0, x1)), b.tAt(math.Max(x0, x1))
292		b.sel0 = math.Max(0, t0)
293		b.sel1 = math.Min(b.dur, t1)
294		b.redraw()
295	}
296	
297	// ---- what it is showing -----------------------------------------------------
298	
299	// forget aims the band at a new recording, which means putting away every
300	// number that was a second in the old one: the picked stretch, the red bar ▶
301	// starts from, the zoom and how far along it we had scrolled, and the queue a
302	// ▶ already pressed was walking. None of them mean anything in the next file,
303	// and one left behind aims at a place that is not on screen any more.
304	func (b *takeBand) forget(src string) {
305		b.src, b.base = src, baseName(src)
306		b.wf, b.dur = nil, 0
307		b.sel0, b.sel1 = 0, 0
308		b.viewX, b.pps = 0, 1
309		b.at = -1
310		b.hover = false
311		b.queue, b.qAt = nil, 0
312	}
313	
314	// sync points the band at whatever the chosen voice is cut from, and is the
315	// one way in: it is called when the page is built, when the voice changes, and
316	// when the Prepare page re-tags who is who. Cheap when nothing moved, because
317	// the answer is usually the same recording it was already drawing.
318	func (b *takeBand) sync() {
319		if b == nil {
320			return
321		}
322		a := b.vp.a
323		src := a.takeSource()
324		show := src != ""
325		b.frame.SetVisible(show)
326		for _, btn := range []*gtk.Button{b.addBtn, b.delBtn, b.playBtn} {
327			btn.SetSensitive(show)
328		}
329		defer b.syncPlayBtn() // forget() may end a walk; the ⏹ goes back to ▶
330		if src == b.src {
331			b.takes = a.voiceTakes() // the file may have been edited under us
332			b.redraw()
333			return
334		}
335		b.forget(src)
336		if !show {
337			b.redraw()
338			return
339		}
340		b.takes = a.voiceTakes()
341		b.load()
342	}
343	
344	// load decodes the envelope and probes the length off the GUI thread -- both
345	// shell out, and a recording nobody has drawn yet is an ffmpeg pass over the
346	// whole file. The band draws its ground and says so in the meantime.
347	func (b *takeBand) load() {
348		a, src, base := b.vp.a, b.src, b.base
349		go func() {
350			dur, _ := ffprobeDur(src)
351			au := tlAudio{base: base, path: src, dur: dur, chans: ffprobeChannels(src)}
352			wf, err := loadWave(a.waveCache(), au)
353			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
354				if b.src != src {
355					return // the voice changed while this was decoding
356				}
357				if err != nil {
358					a.logf("no waveform for %s: %v", base, err)
359				}
360				b.wf, b.dur = wf, dur
361				b.pps = 0 // below fit, so clampView lands exactly on the whole file
362				b.clampView()
363				b.syncScroll()
364				b.area.SetContentHeight(b.height())
365				b.redraw()
366			})
367		}()
368	}
369	
370	// ---- the three buttons -------------------------------------------------------
371	
372	func (b *takeBand) addClicked() {
373		s, e, ok := b.sel()
374		if !ok {
375			b.vp.a.setStatus("drag across the wave first — ＋ makes the selection a take")
376			return
377		}
378		if e-s < takeMin {
379			b.vp.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("that is %.2f s — a take has to be at least %.1f s", e-s, takeMin))
380			return
381		}
382		b.commit(addTake(b.takes, s, e), fmt.Sprintf("take added: %s–%s", mmss(s), mmss(e)))
383	}
384	
385	func (b *takeBand) delClicked() {
386		s, e, ok := b.sel()
387		if !ok {
388			b.vp.a.setStatus("drag across the takes you want gone — － removes those seconds")
389			return
390		}
391		next := dropTakes(b.takes, s, e)
392		if sameTakes(next, b.takes) {
393			b.vp.a.setStatus("nothing is picked in those seconds")
394			return
395		}
396		b.commit(next, "takes removed")
397	}
398	
399	// commit stores the new set and says what it means. The write and the ffmpeg
400	// the write triggers go off the GUI thread; the band is redrawn straight away,
401	// because the set is what the band draws and it has already changed.
402	func (b *takeBand) commit(ts []voiceTake, what string) {
403		a, base := b.vp.a, b.base
404		b.takes = ts
405		b.sel0, b.sel1 = 0, 0
406		b.redraw()
407		total := takesTotal(ts)
408		go func() {
409			if err := a.setTakesFor(base, ts); err != nil {
410				a.logfIdle("takes: %v", err)
411				glib.IdleAdd(func() { a.setStatus("could not save the takes — see log") })
412				return
413			}
414			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
415				if len(ts) == 0 {
416					a.setStatus("no takes left — the seconds are chosen for you again on the next line spoken")
417					return
418				}
419				// the total, because it is the number that decides whether this is
420				// a voice: refWant is what the automatic pick aims for and is a
421				// fair mark to be judged against
422				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s — %d take(s), %.1f s of reference (%.0f s is plenty). "+
423					"Re-cut on the next line spoken.", what, len(ts), total, refWant))
424			})
425		}()
426	}
427	
428	// playClicked plays what takeQueue says, from the red bar. Not the reference
429	// file, which does not exist until something has been spoken and is levelled
430	// and pitch-shifted besides: this is the seconds themselves, in the recording
431	// they came from, which is the thing being judged.
432	func (b *takeBand) playClicked() {
433		if len(b.queue) > 0 {
434			b.stopWalk()
435			return
436		}
437		q, takes := takeQueue(b.takes, b.at, b.dur)
438		if len(q) == 0 {
439			b.vp.a.setStatus("no takes yet — drag across the wave and press ＋")
440			return
441		}
442		if b.vp.player == nil {
443			b.vp.a.setStatus("no player available — see log")
444			return
445		}
446		b.queue, b.qAt = q, 0
447		b.syncPlayBtn() // ⏹ now, not when the first segment prerolls
448		// the player is the sample's as well, and it is holding the recording now:
449		// leaving the old sample's key behind would have ▶ beside the sample
450		// "resume" a wav that is no longer in it
451		b.vp.spoken = ""
452		b.cue()
453		if !takes {
454			b.vp.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("playing the recording from %s — nothing is picked after it", mmss(q[0].S)))
455			return
456		}
457		b.vp.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("playing %d take(s), %.1f s from %s",
458			len(q), takesTotal(q), mmss(q[0].S)))
459	}
460	
461	// stopWalk ends the walk on purpose, which is the other thing that button can
462	// mean. The queue is emptied FIRST: stopping the player lands straight back
463	// here through OnState, and chainOn finding nothing queued is what makes that
464	// re-entry a no-op rather than a second "takes played".
465	func (b *takeBand) stopWalk() {
466		b.queue, b.qAt = nil, 0
467		if b.vp.player != nil {
468			b.vp.player.Stop()
469		}
470		b.syncPlayBtn()
471		b.vp.a.setStatus("stopped playing the takes")
472		b.redraw()
473	}
474	
475	// syncPlayBtn draws the button's two faces: ⏹, not ⏸, since a walk cues each
476	// take from its own start and a second press can only mean "enough". It reads
477	// the QUEUE, not the player, which pauses at every join.
478	func (b *takeBand) syncPlayBtn() {
479		if b == nil || b.playBtn == nil {
480			return
481		}
482		if len(b.queue) > 0 {
483			b.playBtn.SetIconName("media-playback-stop-symbolic")
484			b.playBtn.SetTooltipText("Stop playing the takes")
485			return
486		}
487		b.playBtn.SetIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
488		b.playBtn.SetTooltipText(takePlayTip)
489	}
490	
491	// takeQueue is what ▶ plays: the takes from the red bar onward, the one the bar
492	// lands inside trimmed to begin there; all of them with no bar. The bool says
493	// whether those ARE takes -- a bar past the last, or no takes at all, means
494	// play the recording from there, which is how takes get found.
495	func takeQueue(ts []voiceTake, at, dur float64) ([]voiceTake, bool) {
496		var out []voiceTake
497		for _, t := range ts {
498			if at >= 0 {
499				if t.E <= at {
500					continue
501				}
502				t.S = math.Max(t.S, at)
503			}
504			out = append(out, t)
505		}
506		if len(out) > 0 {
507			return out, true
508		}
509		if at < 0 || at >= dur {
510			return nil, false
511		}
512		return []voiceTake{{S: at, E: dur}}, false
513	}
514	
515	func (b *takeBand) cue() {
516		t := b.queue[b.qAt]
517		b.vp.player.PlaySegment(b.src, t.S, t.E, true)
518	}
519	
520	// chainOn hangs on the player's OnState, where a segment's end arrives (the
521	// bus watch pauses on EOS). It drops the chain whenever the player holds
522	// anything but this recording, so playing a sample cancels it.
523	func (b *takeBand) chainOn() {
524		if b == nil || len(b.queue) == 0 {
525			return
526		}
527		p := b.vp.player
528		if p == nil {
529			return
530		}
531		next := takeNext(p.loaded, b.src, p.ended, b.qAt, len(b.queue))
532		switch {
533		case next == b.qAt: // a start, a pause, anything that is not an end
534		case next < 0:
535			// the walk is over, either because the last take finished or because
536			// something else took the player. Only the first is worth saying.
537			done := p.loaded == b.src
538			b.queue = nil
539			if done {
540				b.vp.a.setStatus("takes played")
541			}
542		default:
543			b.qAt = next
544			b.cue()
545		}
546	}
547	
548	// takeNext is the whole of that decision, split out from the pipeline it is
549	// made about: the player is GStreamer and stays out of a unit test, exactly as
550	// Player.hushes is split from applyMute. It answers with the take to cue next,
551	// the one already sounding for "nothing has happened", or -1 for "stop".
552	func takeNext(loaded, src string, ended bool, at, n int) int {
553		if loaded != src {
554			return -1 // the player is holding something else: the sample took it
555		}
556		if !ended {
557			return at
558		}
559		if at+1 >= n {
560			return -1
561		}
562		return at + 1
563	}
564	
565	// ---- drawing ----------------------------------------------------------------
566	
567	func (b *takeBand) draw(_ *gtk.DrawingArea, cr *cairo.Context, w, h int) {
568		if b.pps <= 0 || b.pps < b.fitPps() {
569			b.clampView() // the first draw, and every one after a window resize
570		}
571		cr.SetSourceRGB(0.11, 0.11, 0.12)
572		cr.Rectangle(0, 0, float64(w), float64(h))
573		cr.Fill()
574		if b.src == "" {
575			return
576		}
577		top := takeRulerH + wavePad
578		lanes := b.laneCount()
579		laneH := float64(lanes) * takeLaneH
580		x0 := math.Max(0, b.xOf(0))
581		x1 := math.Min(float64(w), b.xOf(b.dur))
582		if b.dur <= 0 {
583			x0, x1 = 0, float64(w) // length not probed yet; the ground is the whole band
584		}
585	
586		// the ground says the recording is here, exactly as a Cut lane's does, and

710		}
711		spp := 1 / b.pps
712		hgts := make([]float64, 0, int(x1-math.Floor(x0))+1)
713		cr.SetSourceRGB(0.29, 0.62, 1)
714		for x := math.Floor(x0); x < x1; x++ {
715			at := b.tAt(x)

717			if p := iecScale(b.wf.peak(ch, at, at+spp)); p > 0 {
718				h = math.Max(1, p*full)
719				cr.Rectangle(x, bot-h, 1, h)
720			}
721			hgts = append(hgts, h)
722		}
723		cr.Fill()
724		cr.SetSourceRGB(0.09, 0.27, 0.52)
725		for i, h := range hgts {
726			if h >= 3 {
727				cr.Rectangle(math.Floor(x0)+float64(i), bot-h, 1, 1)
728			}
729		}
730		cr.Fill()

31		// 1920-wide card decoded ten times a second is memory spent on pixels that
32		// are thrown away in the scale to the widget.
33		insPreviewW = 960

35		// eight a second would otherwise be half a gigabyte of pictures nobody is
36		// looking at any more; dropping all of them costs the next pass through the

41	// insFilm is one insert's pictures, rendered as the playhead asks for them.
42	//
43	// Rendering happens off the GTK thread and the result comes back through an
44	// idle, so a card that takes 80 ms to draw slows the card down and nothing else.
45	// One frame is in flight at a time: the playhead moves ten times a second and
46	// the renderer is slower than that, and a queue of frames for moments already
47	// gone by is how a preview ends up lagging further behind the longer it runs.
48	type insFilm struct {
49		ins    string // the insert path these belong to, parameters and all
50		fps    float64
51		tex    map[int]*gdk.Texture
52		busy   bool
53		shown  int  // frame currently on the picture, -1 for none
54		failed bool // it cannot be drawn; said once, then left alone
55	}

57	// insertAt is the insert session time t falls inside, and how far into the
58	// card's own time that is; nil on footage. A spliced card owns no session time,
59	// so its marker (spliceSpan) is what the playhead sweeps -- the same picture
60	// the eye reads, 1:1 at a zoom where the marker is the card's own length.
61	func (ed *cutEditor) insertAt(t float64) (*cutSeg, float64) {
62		for i := range ed.segs {
63			s := &ed.segs[i]
64			switch {
65			case !s.isInsert():
66			case s.spliced():
67				x0, x1 := ed.spliceSpan(*s)
68				w := (x1 - x0) / math.Max(ed.pps, 0.001)
69				if t >= s.S && t < s.S+w {
70					return s, (t - s.S) / w * s.Dur
71				}
72			case t >= s.S && t < s.E:
73				return s, t - s.S
74			}
75		}
76		return nil, 0
77	}

80	//
81	// A spliced card owns no session time -- it is a point where the footage is cut
82	// open -- so there is no stretch of the stream for it to play "during". What
83	// there is instead is this: the player paused where the cut is, a card running
84	// on the wall clock for as long as it was given, and then the footage let go
85	// again at the same frame. Watched end to end that is what the render makes.
86	type insHold struct {

89		start time.Time

91		// marker is still under the playhead and insertAt still answers with the

100	// counts, so a seek past a card does not play it.
101	func (ed *cutEditor) splicedCrossed(from, to float64) *cutSeg {
102		if to <= from || to-from > 1.0 {
103			return nil
104		}

119	// says for the next few seconds, the page is not idle: the card is playing, and

121	func (ed *cutEditor) startHold(s *cutSeg) {

134	// the card has run its length. Called from the same timer that follows playback,
135	// because while the hold is on there is no playback to follow.
136	func (ed *cutEditor) tickHold() {
137		switch {
138		case !ed.hold.on:
139		case ed.player == nil || ed.player.playing:
140			// somebody pressed ▶ while the card was up; the footage has taken itself
141			// back and the card is over
142			ed.endHold(false)
143		case ed.holdInto(time.Now()) >= ed.hold.seg.Dur:
144			ed.endHold(true)

151	// never past its end -- the last frame is the one it finishes on.

153		return math.Min(now.Sub(ed.hold.start).Seconds(), ed.hold.seg.Dur)

296			// back), and black is what is true. Only at a standstill -- in playback the
297			// running pipeline is the clock.
298			if !ed.player.playing && ed.videoShown(ed.playhead) == nil {
299				ed.player.ShowStill(blackStill())
300			} else {
301				ed.player.ShowVideo()
302			}
303			if ed.film != nil {
304				ed.film.shown = -1 // whatever it was showing is off the picture now
305			}

307		}
308		if ed.film == nil || ed.film.ins != s.Ins {
309			ed.film = ed.a.newFilm(s.Ins)
310		}
311		f := ed.film
312		if f.failed {
313			return
314		}
315		i := 0
316		if f.fps > 0 {
317			i = max(0, int(into*f.fps))
318		}
319		if tex := f.tex[i]; tex != nil {
320			if f.shown != i || !ed.player.still {
321				ed.player.ShowStill(tex)
322				f.shown = i
323			}
324			return
325		}
326		// The frame for this instant is not drawn yet. Showing nothing here is not
327		// neutral: it leaves the paused FOOTAGE on screen, and an animated card
328		// whose rendering runs slower than its own clock -- which is the usual case,
329		// a frame takes longer to draw than 1/8th of a second -- then never catches
330		// up with the playhead and never appears at all. So the nearest frame that
331		// IS drawn goes up while this one is asked for: a card a little behind its
332		// clock, rather than no card.
333		if j, tex := f.nearest(i); tex != nil {
334			if f.shown != j || !ed.player.still {
335				ed.player.ShowStill(tex)

337			}
338		}

342	// blackTex is built once and kept: the "nothing here" frame never changes, and
343	// showInsert puts it up on every playhead move across an empty stretch.
344	var blackTex *gdk.Texture
345	
346	// blackStill is the picture for a row with no footage under the line: plain
347	// black, in the video's shape so the letterboxing does not jump when real
348	// footage comes back. 16x9 pixels is enough -- every pixel is the same one.
349	func blackStill() *gdk.Texture {
350		if blackTex == nil {
351			pb := gdkpixbuf.NewPixbuf(gdkpixbuf.ColorspaceRGB, false, 8, 16, 9)
352			pb.Fill(0x000000ff)
353			blackTex = gdk.NewTextureForPixbuf(pb)
354		}
355		return blackTex
356	}
357	
358	// nearest is the rendered frame closest to i, preferring the one behind it: a
359	// card seen slightly earlier in its run reads as the card arriving, one seen
360	// ahead of its run is a jump backwards when the real frame lands.
361	func (f *insFilm) nearest(i int) (int, *gdk.Texture) {
362		best, d := -1, 0
363		for j := range f.tex {
364			dj := i - j
365			if dj < 0 {
366				dj = (j - i) * 2 // ahead of the clock costs double
367			}
368			if best < 0 || dj < d {
369				best, d = j, dj
370			}
371		}
372		if best < 0 {
373			return -1, nil
374		}
375		return best, f.tex[best]
376	}
377	
378	// newFilm decides how an insert moves, which is the only thing about it this
379	// page needs to know in advance: a still and a card that does not animate are
380	// one picture held for the whole slot, everything else is a frame per moment.
381	func (a *App) newFilm(ins string) *insFilm {
382		f := &insFilm{ins: ins, tex: map[int]*gdk.Texture{}, shown: -1}
383		if _, ok := copySrc(ins); ok {
384			f.fps = insPreviewFPS // footage moves; drawn at the card rate like a sting
385			return f
386		}
387		switch insKind(ins) {
388		case "video":
389			f.fps = insPreviewFPS
390		case "svg":
391			file, q := insSplit(ins)
392			if src, _, err := insSVG(a.loadPath(file) + q.suffix()); err == nil && svgAnimated(src) {
393				f.fps = insPreviewFPS
394			}
395		}
396		return f
397	}
398	
399	// renderFrame draws one frame in the background and puts it up when it arrives
400	// -- by asking showInsert again rather than by showing it directly, because by
401	// then the playhead may be somewhere else entirely and the frame that was asked
402	// for is no longer the frame that belongs on screen.
403	func (ed *cutEditor) renderFrame(f *insFilm, i int) {
404		if f.busy {
405			return
406		}
407		f.busy = true
408		a, ins := ed.a, f.ins
409		at := 0.0
410		if f.fps > 0 {
411			at = float64(i) / f.fps
412		}
413		go func() {
414			png, file, err := a.insPNG(ins, at)
415			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
416				f.busy = false
417				if ed.film != f {
418					return // a different insert is on the playhead now
419				}
420				tex, terr := insTexture(png, file)
421				if err == nil {
422					err = terr
423				}
424				if err != nil {
425					f.failed = true
426					a.logf(">>> %s cannot be shown in the preview: %v", insBase(ins), err)
427					return
428				}
429				if len(f.tex) >= insFilmMax {
430					f.tex = map[int]*gdk.Texture{}
431					f.shown = -1
432				}
433				f.tex[i] = tex
434				ed.showInsert()
435			})
436		}()
437	}

439	// insTexture turns what the renderer produced into something GtkPicture can
440	// draw: the PNG it rendered, or -- for a file that is already a picture -- the
441	// file itself, which lets GTK's own loaders deal with a webp or a gif rather
442	// than this decoding one to re-encode it as the other.
443	func insTexture(png []byte, file string) (*gdk.Texture, error) {
444		if len(png) > 0 {
445			return gdk.NewTextureFromBytes(glib.NewBytes(png))
446		}
447		if file == "" {
448			return nil, fmt.Errorf("nothing came out of the renderer")
449		}
450		return gdk.NewTextureFromFilename(file)
451	}
452	
453	// insPNG renders an insert at one moment of its own time. It returns either the
454	// picture, or the path of a file the caller should open directly.
455	//
456	// at is seconds into the insert, and it is what makes a preview of an animated
457	// card worth having: the same document, evaluated at the same moment svganim
458	// would bake it at, so a wipe that has not finished by the time the slot ends is
459	// visible here rather than in the finished video.
460	func (a *App) insPNG(ins string, at float64) (png []byte, file string, err error) {
461		// a copy has no file of its own: its frames are its recording's, at the
462		// copied seconds -- the same cut the render makes, one frame at a time
463		if from, ok := copySrc(ins); ok {
464			v := a.ed.videoAt(from + at)
465			if v == nil {
466				return nil, "", fmt.Errorf("the copied footage falls in no recording")
467			}
468			out, err := ffmpegPNG("-ss", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", v.at(from+at)), "-i", v.path)
469			return out, "", err
470		}
471		src, q := insSplit(ins)
472		path := a.loadPath(src)
473		switch insKind(ins) {
474		case "still":
475			return nil, path, nil
476	
477		case "video":
478			out, err := ffmpegPNG("-ss", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", at), "-i", path)
479			return out, "", err
480		}
481	
482		// an svg: the card with its parameters applied, and, if it moves, at the
483		// moment the playhead is inside it. Same two calls Produce makes (insSVG,
484		// renderAt), so the preview cannot disagree with the render about what the
485		// card says.
486		doc, _, err := insSVG(path + q.suffix())
487		if err != nil {
488			return nil, "", err
489		}
490		if svgAnimated(doc) {
491			root, err := parseSVG(doc)
492			if err != nil {
493				return nil, "", err
494			}
495			var b strings.Builder
496			b.WriteString(`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>` + "\n")
497			root.renderAt(&b, at)
498			doc = []byte(b.String())
499		}
500		// through a file rather than a pipe: ffmpeg's svg decoder wants to seek in
501		// what it is reading, and a card is a few kilobytes
502		tmp, err := os.CreateTemp("", "naivepost-card-*.svg")
503		if err != nil {
504			return nil, "", err
505		}
506		defer os.Remove(tmp.Name())
507		if _, err := tmp.Write(doc); err != nil {
508			tmp.Close()
509			return nil, "", err
510		}
511		if err := tmp.Close(); err != nil {
512			return nil, "", err
513		}
514		out, err := ffmpegPNG("-i", tmp.Name())
515		return out, "", err
516	}
517	
518	// ffmpegPNG is one frame of whatever the input arguments name, as PNG bytes on
519	// stdout. Scaled down but never up: a card is drawn at 1920 and a still may be
520	// anything, and blowing a small picture up here would only make the widget scale
521	// it back down with fewer pixels to work from.
522	func ffmpegPNG(in ...string) ([]byte, error) {
523		args := append([]string{"-v", "error", "-nostdin"}, in...)
524		args = append(args, "-frames:v", "1",
525			"-vf", fmt.Sprintf("scale='min(iw,%d)':-2", insPreviewW),
526			"-f", "image2", "-c:v", "png", "-")
527		cmd := exec.Command(ffTool("ffmpeg"), args...)
528		var out, errb bytes.Buffer
529		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = &out, &errb
530		if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
531			tail := strings.TrimSpace(errb.String())
532			if len(tail) > 200 {
533				tail = tail[len(tail)-200:]
534			}
535			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ffmpeg: %w: %s", err, tail)
536		}
537		if out.Len() == 0 {
538			return nil, fmt.Errorf("ffmpeg drew nothing")
539		}
540		return out.Bytes(), nil
541	}

211	// and above 48 kHz ffmpeg writes WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE (tag 0xFFFE), which
212	// the audio server refuses ("unsupported WAV encoding"). 48 kHz keeps the
213	// header plain and is at or above anything we clone from.

216	// wavPlain asks the question the server asks: is this a wav whose samples it
217	// knows how to read. The format tag is the whole answer -- 1 for integer PCM,
218	// 3 for float, and 0xFFFE for the WAVE_FORMAT_EXTENSIBLE header ffmpeg writes
219	// above refRate, which is the one it refuses. The chunk's length is not the
220	// test: a plain float wav carries 18 bytes rather than 16. Only the head of the
221	// file is read -- fmt comes before the samples, and the samples are megabytes.
222	func wavPlain(p string) bool {
223		f, err := os.Open(p)
224		if err != nil {
225			return false
226		}
227		defer f.Close()
228		b := make([]byte, 512)
229		n, _ := io.ReadFull(f, b)
230		if n < 12 || string(b[:4]) != "RIFF" || string(b[8:12]) != "WAVE" {
231			return false
232		}
233		// walk only as far as a whole fmt chunk head plus its tag can have been
234		// read. A file that ends inside its own fmt chunk never reaches the tag,
235		// and unread is not readable: it is refused with everything else.
236		for i := 12; i+10 <= n; {
237			size := int(binary.LittleEndian.Uint32(b[i+4 : i+8]))
238			if string(b[i:i+4]) == "fmt " {
239				if size < 16 {
240					return false
241				}
242				tag := binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[i+8 : i+10])
243				return tag == 1 || tag == 3
244			}
245			i += 8 + size + size%2
246		}
247		return false
248	}

251	// out as levelled mono PCM. Three things write a reference -- a picked wav
252	// chosen, the same wav healed on another machine, and a narrator's own takes
253	// concatenated -- and a level rule that only two of them followed would be a
254	// voice that changed loudness when the project moved.
255	func (a *App) levelRef(dst string, in ...string) error {
256		args := append([]string{"-v", "error", "-y"}, in...)
257		args = append(args, "-af", refLoud, "-ac", "1", "-ar", refRate, "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", dst)
258		return a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), args...)
259	}
260	
261	// refBase is the chosen recording as it was picked, refPath the shifted copy
262	// the server is handed. Keeping them apart is what makes the slider cheap: the
263	// base is cut or converted once, the shift is redone from it.
264	// The base is also where the rate is decided (refRate): every writer of it goes
265	// through levelRef, and shifting does not resample, so pinning it once covers
266	// the file the server actually reads.
267	func (a *App) refBase() string { return filepath.Join(a.narrateDir(), "voice_ref_base.wav") }
268	func (a *App) refPath() string { return filepath.Join(a.narrateDir(), "voice_ref.wav") }
269	
270	// setVoice installs the reference the model clones from. A narrator slot just
271	// removes the files, so ensureVoiceRef cuts a fresh one from that recording the
272	// next time anything speaks -- which is also how a project built under an older
273	// rule for choosing those seconds gets a reference under the current one.
274	// Anything else is converted to the mono PCM the model wants.
275	// Safe off the GUI thread -- it only runs ffmpeg and writes files.
276	func (a *App) setVoice(v voiceOpt) error {
277		dir := a.narrateDir()
278		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
279			return err
280		}
281		// the shifted copy belongs to the old voice; drop it either way and let
282		// ensureVoiceRef rebuild it from whatever base we end up with. "No audio"
283		// needs no reference at all -- nothing will ever be synthesized from it.
284		os.Remove(a.refPath())
285		if v.id == captionsVoice || narratorSlot(v.id) > 0 {
286			os.Remove(a.refBase())
287		} else if err := a.levelRef(a.refBase(), "-i", v.path); err != nil {
288			return err
289		}
290		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "voice.txt"), []byte(v.id), 0o644); err != nil {
291			return err
292		}
293		a.voiceMu.Lock()
294		a.voiceSel = v.id
295		a.voiceMu.Unlock()
296		return nil
297	}
298	
299	// importVoice adds a recording to the voices folder as the mono PCM wav the
300	// model wants -- so any audio file works, not just the ones already in the
301	// right format. It lands beside the built-in voices rather than in the project
302	// because the id the caches and voice.txt use is the file's base name, which
303	// only keeps resolving while the file stays somewhere the list looks; a voice
304	// added here is therefore available to every project, and to the WebUI.
305	// Safe off the GUI thread -- ffmpeg and files only.
306	func (a *App) importVoice(src string) (voiceOpt, error) {
307		dir := a.voicesDir()
308		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
309			return voiceOpt{}, fmt.Errorf("%s is not writable: %w", dir, err)
310		}
311		base := sanitizeVoiceID(strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(src), filepath.Ext(src)))
312		id, dst := base, filepath.Join(dir, base+".wav")
313		// never overwrite: a name already taken belongs to another voice, and every
314		// project pointing at it would start speaking in this one instead
315		for i := 2; exists(dst); i++ {
316			id = fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d", base, i)
317			dst = filepath.Join(dir, id+".wav")
318		}
319		if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", src,
320			"-ac", "1", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", dst); err != nil {
321			return voiceOpt{}, err
322		}
323		return voiceOpt{id: id, name: filepath.Base(dst), path: dst}, nil
324	}
325	
326	// A folder import used to live here: pick a folder, convert every recording
327	// directly in it, skip what is there already. It went with the row that drove
328	// it. Voices arrive one at a time -- you hear a sample, you want THAT speaker
329	// -- and a button that installs thirty at once was answering a question about
330	// stocking a library, which is a file manager's job and not this page's.
331	
332	// sanitizeVoiceID keeps the id usable as a file name: it is pasted into the
333	// sample cache's names and read back out of voice.txt, so a slash in it would
334	// write somewhere else entirely.
335	func sanitizeVoiceID(s string) string {
336		s = strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
337			switch {
338			case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z', r >= '0' && r <= '9':
339				return r
340			case r == '-', r == '_', r == '.':
341				return r
342			}
343			return '-'
344		}, s)
345		if s = strings.Trim(s, "-._"); s == "" {
346			return "voice"
347		}
348		return s
349	}

351	// ---- the reference pitch ----------------------------------------------------
352	
353	// pitchST is how far the reference is moved, in semitones, remembered in the
354	// output folder next to the voice it belongs to.
355	func (a *App) pitchST() float64 {
356		// under voiceMu with the voice id and the takes, and for the same reason:
357		// voiceKey asks all three, and it is asked by whichever worker is about to
358		// speak a line as well as by the GUI thread that moved the slider
359		a.voiceMu.Lock()
360		defer a.voiceMu.Unlock()
361		if a.pitchRead {
362			return a.pitchSel
363		}
364		a.pitchRead, a.pitchSel = true, 0
365		if b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(a.narrateDir(), "pitch.txt")); err == nil {
366			if f, err := strconv.ParseFloat(strings.TrimSpace(string(b)), 64); err == nil {
367				a.pitchSel = clampPitch(f)
368			}
369		}
370		return a.pitchSel
371	}
372	
373	func clampPitch(st float64) float64 {
374		return math.Max(-pitchRange, math.Min(pitchRange, st))
375	}
376	
377	// setPitchST remembers the shift and drops the shifted reference so it is built
378	// again. When there is no base yet -- "own voice" before Prepare has run -- that
379	// is all there is to do; the next line spoken cuts one and shifts it then.
380	// Safe off the GUI thread.
381	func (a *App) setPitchST(st float64) error {
382		st = clampPitch(st)
383		dir := a.narrateDir()
384		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
385			return err
386		}
387		if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "pitch.txt"),
388			[]byte(strconv.FormatFloat(st, 'f', 1, 64)), 0o644); err != nil {
389			return err
390		}
391		a.voiceMu.Lock()
392		a.pitchRead, a.pitchSel = true, st
393		a.voiceMu.Unlock() // before shiftRef: it asks pitchST back
394		os.Remove(a.refPath())
395		if !exists(a.refBase()) {
396			return nil
397		}
398		return a.shiftRef()
399	}
400	
401	// shiftRef writes the file the server actually clones: the base moved by the
402	// slider. formant=preserved moves the pitch and leaves the vowels where a
403	// human's are, so the reference still sounds like someone worth cloning
404	// instead of like a sped-up tape -- the model reproduces artifacts as
405	// faithfully as it reproduces the voice.
406	func (a *App) shiftRef() error {
407		if st := a.pitchST(); st != 0 {
408			return a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y", "-i", a.refBase(),
409				"-af", fmt.Sprintf("rubberband=pitch=%.4f:formant=preserved:pitchq=quality",
410					math.Pow(2, st/12)),
411				"-ac", "1", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", a.refPath())
412		}
413		// unshifted: the server still reads one fixed path, so hand it a copy
414		// rather than teaching every caller which of the two files to use
415		b, err := os.ReadFile(a.refBase())
416		if err != nil {
417			return err
418		}
419		return os.WriteFile(a.refPath(), b, 0o644)
420	}
421	
422	// ensureVoiceRef makes sure the file the server clones from is on disk and
423	// matches the voice above: a base recording, moved by the pitch slider.
424	func (a *App) ensureVoiceRef() error {
425		if err := a.ensureVoiceBase(); err != nil {
426			return err
427		}
428		// on disk is not enough: it has to be one the server will read. shiftRef
429		// overwrites, so a copy that fails goes back through it.
430		if exists(a.refPath()) && wavPlain(a.refPath()) {
431			return nil
432		}
433		return a.shiftRef()
434	}

436	// ensureVoiceBase builds the unshifted reference. For a picked voice that is a
437	// copy of the wav it names -- rebuilt here so a project folder carried to
438	// another machine heals itself. For one of the session's own voices it is cut
439	// from that recording's best stretches -- solo, clear of everyone else, and
440	// with the most actually said in them (refCuts, narrate_ref.go) -- taken from
441	// the ORIGINAL file for fidelity.
442	func (a *App) ensureVoiceBase() error {
443		ref := a.refBase()
444		// before the pitch slider there was one file and it was never shifted, so
445		// an existing voice_ref.wav is exactly the base this now keeps apart
446		if !exists(ref) && exists(a.refPath()) {
447			if err := os.Rename(a.refPath(), ref); err != nil {
448				return err
449			}
450		}
451		if exists(ref) && wavPlain(ref) {
452			return nil
453		}
454		// A reference is built once and then kept, which means a bad one is kept
455		// too: every project that had a reference before refRate was pinned holds a
456		// 192 kHz file the server refuses, and nothing would ever cut it again --
457		// the voice would simply never speak. So what is on disk is judged by the
458		// header rather than by existing, and one this build would not have written
459		// is cut afresh over the top of it.
460		if exists(ref) {
461			a.logf("voice reference %s is not a wav the server reads -- cutting it again", filepath.Base(ref))
462		}
463		id := a.voiceID()
464		slot := narratorSlot(id)
465		if slot == 0 {
466			src := filepath.Join(a.voicesDir(), id+".wav")
467			if !exists(src) {
468				return fmt.Errorf("voice %q is no longer in %s -- pick another at the top of this step", id, a.voicesDir())
469			}
470			os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(ref), 0o755)
471			return a.levelRef(ref, "-i", src)
472		}
473		aud := a.narratorSource(slot)
474		if aud == "" {
475			return fmt.Errorf("nothing is tagged as narrator %d on the Prepare step", slot)
476		}
477		base := baseName(aud)
478		// Hand-picked takes are the whole answer when there are any (narrate_take.go):
479		// they were chosen by ear, on this recording, usually against a clone that
480		// was wrong -- so nothing here re-ranks them, and the caps that keep a guess
481		// honest do not apply. They also need no diarization, which is what lets a
482		// recording nobody has run Prepare over still be cloned from.
483		hand := a.takesFor(base)
484		picks := handPicks(hand)
485		if len(picks) == 0 {
486			turns, err := loadSpans(filepath.Join(a.inputsDir(), base, "turns.json"))
487			if err != nil {
488				return fmt.Errorf("no diarization for %s -- run Prepare, or pick the seconds by hand under the video", base)
489			}
490			// the transcript of the same recording, on the same clock: what refCuts
491			// weighs the stretches by. Missing is allowed and means unweighed.
492			rows := loadSeg4(filepath.Join(a.inputsDir(), base, "transcript.tsv"))
493			if picks = refCuts(turns, rows); len(picks) == 0 {
494				return fmt.Errorf("no clean solo stretch found for the voice reference")
495			}
496		}
497		dir := a.narrateDir()
498		os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755)
499		// the pieces and the list that names them are scaffolding for one concat.
500		// They were left in narrate/ afterwards, where a later build with fewer takes
501		// leaves the extra ones lying beside the reference looking like part of it.
502		var tmp []string
503		defer func() {
504			for _, f := range tmp {
505				os.Remove(f)
506			}
507		}()
508		var list strings.Builder
509		total, words := 0.0, 0
510		for i, t := range picks {
511			if len(hand) == 0 && (total >= refWant || i >= refTakeMax) {
512				break
513			}
514			d := t.dur()
515			if len(hand) == 0 {
516				d = math.Min(d, refWant-total)
517			}
518			f := filepath.Join(dir, fmt.Sprintf(".ref%d.wav", i))
519			tmp = append(tmp, f)
520			if err := a.runCmd(ffTool("ffmpeg"), "-v", "error", "-y",
521				"-ss", fmt.Sprint(t.s), "-t", fmt.Sprint(d),
522				"-i", aud, "-ac", "1", f); err != nil {
523				return err
524			}
525			list.WriteString(concatLine(f))
526			total, words = total+d, words+t.words
527		}
528		lf := filepath.Join(dir, ".ref.list")
529		tmp = append(tmp, lf)
530		if err := os.WriteFile(lf, []byte(list.String()), 0o644); err != nil {
531			return err
532		}
533		if err := a.levelRef(ref, "-f", "concat", "-safe", "0", "-i", lf); err != nil {
534			return err
535		}
536		// which of the two it was, because they fail differently: an automatic
537		// reference that sounds wrong is a ranking to overrule by hand, and a
538		// hand-picked one that sounds wrong is seconds to re-pick.
539		how := fmt.Sprintf("%d words", words)
540		if len(hand) > 0 {
541			how = fmt.Sprintf("%d hand-picked take(s)", len(hand))
542		}
543		a.logfIdle(">>> voice reference built: %.1f s, %s from %s", total, how, base)
544		return nil
545	}

547	// voiceKey is the voice as the caches see it. Pitch 0 and no takes keep the
548	// key older projects had, so nothing already spoken is orphaned. Both parts
549	// change who is speaking -- a reference cut from different seconds is a
550	// different clone (sampleNeedsSpeaking).
551	func (a *App) voiceKey() string {
552		k := a.voiceID()
553		if st := a.pitchST(); st != 0 {
554			k = fmt.Sprintf("%s@%+.1f", k, st)
555		}
556		if h := takesKey(a.voiceTakes()); h != "" {
557			k += "#" + h
558		}
559		return k
560	}
561	
562	// sampleKey is what ▶ would speak if it were pressed now: which voice, shifted
563	// by how much, saying which words, on which draw. Everything the sample can be
564	// is in here, which is what lets the button tell "play that again" from "that
565	// is not what I asked for any more".
566	func (vp *voicePicker) sampleKey(text string) string {
567		k := vp.a.voiceKey() + "|" + strings.TrimSpace(text)
568		if vp.roll > 0 { // a sample nobody re-rolled keeps the key it already has
569			k = strconv.Itoa(vp.roll) + "#" + k
570		}
571		return k
572	}
573	
574	// sampleNeedsSpeaking is what ▶ does: resume the sample in the player, or make
575	// a new one. The player holds a file, not a question, and the file stops being
576	// the answer when the voice, pitch or words change -- resuming then played the
577	// old setting.
578	func sampleNeedsSpeaking(sounding bool, loaded, now string) bool {
579		return !sounding || loaded != now
580	}
581	
582	// sampleWav caches one voice's reading of one sample text, so hearing a voice
583	// again is instant and comparing two is a click each. id is the readable half
584	// of the name; key is what decides the file.
585	func (a *App) sampleWav(id, key string) string {
586		h := sha1.Sum([]byte(key))
587		return filepath.Join(a.narrateDir(), "samples", fmt.Sprintf("%s_%x.wav", id, h[:6]))
588	}
