590	// ---- the page ---------------------------------------------------------------
591	
592	// buildVoicePicker is the top of the Narrate step: who speaks. It was a step of
593	// its own, which put the choice of voice and the lines it would speak on
594	// different screens -- and made the run bar's ▶ mean "play a sample" here and
595	// "run this step" everywhere else. Sharing the page, the sample gets its own ▶
596	// and the run bar keeps one meaning.
597	//
598	// Two rows. This was a scrolling list, a filter box over it, two import
599	// buttons, an editable folder path and three explanatory labels, stacked in a
600	// divider -- a third of a column for a choice made once per project. Every one
601	// of those parts was answering a question the dropdown's own row text answers:
602	// the list is picked from and then closed, so it is a dropdown; the filter went
603	// with the list; and the "Voice: …" label read back what the closed dropdown is
604	// already showing. What is left is the choice, and the way to hear it.
605	func (a *App) buildVoicePicker() gtk.Widgetter {
606		vp := &voicePicker{a: a}
607		a.voicePick = vp
608		if p, err := NewPlayer(); err == nil {
609			vp.player = p
610			// one player, two things that use it: the sample, and ▶ walking the
611			// takes. A segment reaching its end arrives here, which is what moves
612			// the walk on to the next take (chainOn).
613			p.OnState = func() {
614				vp.band.chainOn()
615				a.updateRunControls()
616			}
617			p.OnError = a.playerErr("the voice sample")
618		}
619		vp.voices = a.listVoices()
620	
621		vp.names = gtk.NewStringList(voiceNames(vp.voices))
622		vp.pick = gtk.NewDropDown(vp.names, nil)
623		vp.pick.SetHExpand(true)
624		// what the paragraph under this used to say, moved to where it is read at
625		// the moment the choice is being made rather than on every look at the page
626		vp.pick.SetTooltipText("Who speaks the narration. Every line is spoken by cloning the " +
627			"selected recording; switching voices keeps what you already synthesized")
628		// picking IS choosing: this is the step whose whole job is that choice, and
629		// switching costs nothing now that the cache knows about voices.
630		vp.pick.NotifyProperty("selected", func() {
631			if vp.syncing {
632				return
633			}
634			vp.choose(int(vp.pick.Selected()))
635		})
636	
637		// one recording at a time. The folder import that stood beside this is gone
638		// with the folder row: you hear a sample and want THAT speaker, and the
639		// voices folder is set in llm.conf for the audio server anyway.
640		add := flexButton("Add file…", "Copy one recording into the voices folder and use it")

1	package main

3	// The third ▶: review the cuts.
4	//
5	// ▶ plays the recording and ▶✂ plays the finished video, and neither is the
6	// way to check a cut. What you want to know about a cut is whether the JOIN
7	// works -- does the sentence run on, is the splice in a silence, did the model
8	// take one word too many -- and that is a few seconds either side of each
9	// seam, not the minutes of kept material between them. So ▶✂✂ plays exactly
10	// that: for every join, reviewPad seconds of the cut before it and reviewPad
11	// after, one join after the other, and stops when the last one has been heard.
12	//
13	// It is the ▶✂ preview underneath -- the removed stretch is jumped by the same
14	// skipGap, the clock reads the cut's own time -- with one more hand on the
15	// line: reviewTick, which notices when the seconds after a join have played
16	// out and moves the line to the run-up of the next. A join whose run-up is
17	// already under the line (two cuts close together) is simply played into,
18	// so a stretch of short clips is heard once, in order, and not rewound for
19	// every seam in it.
20	//
21	// Nothing about it is saved; pressing anything else that moves the line ends
22	// the review, and pausing does too.
23	
24	import (
25		"fmt"
26		"math"
27	
28		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gtk/v4"
29	)
30	
31	// reviewPad is how much of the cut is heard on each side of a join, in
32	// seconds of the finished video.
33	const reviewPad = 10.0
34	
35	// reviewMove is what the review does on a tick.
36	type reviewMove int
37	
38	const (
39		reviewStay reviewMove = iota // the join under review is still being heard
40		reviewSeek                   // the next join's run-up is ahead: seek to it
41		reviewDone                   // the last join has been heard
42		reviewLost                   // the line is nowhere near the join: somebody moved it
43	)
44	
45	// reviewWindow is seam i's stretch of the cut: the join is where segs[i]
46	// ends and segs[i+1] begins. from is reviewPad before it, but never before
47	// the earlier clip's own start -- what lies before that is a removed stretch,
48	// not the cut -- and to is reviewPad after it, but never past the later clip's
49	// end, for the same reason the other way round.
50	func reviewWindow(segs []cutSeg, i int) (from, to float64) {
51		from = math.Max(segs[i].S, segs[i].E-reviewPad)
52		to = math.Min(segs[i+1].E, segs[i+1].S+reviewPad)
53		return from, to
54	}
55	
56	// reviewStep is the review's whole decision, pure so it can be checked
57	// without a player: seam i is being heard and the line is at session time t.
58	// It answers which seam is under review after this tick and what the line
59	// has to do about it. A seam whose run-up begins at or before t is not sought
60	// but played on into (see the top of the file).
61	//
62	// armed says the line has already been seen inside this seam's window. A
63	// line found BEFORE the window is then a hand's doing and the review is
64	// over; unarmed it is the review's own seek not yet landed -- the player
65	// answers the old position for a tick or two after a flushing seek, and 0
66	// for the first tick on a freshly cued file -- and the answer is to wait.
67	func reviewStep(segs []cutSeg, i int, t float64, armed bool) (int, reviewMove) {
68		last := len(segs) - 2 // the last seam: there are len-1 of them
69		if i > last {
70			return i, reviewDone
71		}
72		from, to := reviewWindow(segs, i)
73		if t < from {
74			if armed {
75				return i, reviewLost
76			}
77			return i, reviewStay
78		}
79		if t < to {
80			return i, reviewStay
81		}
82		for i < last {
83			i++
84			from, to = reviewWindow(segs, i)
85			if from > t {
86				return i, reviewSeek
87			}
88			if t < to {
89				return i, reviewStay
90			}
91		}
92		return i, reviewDone
93	}
94	
95	// reviewSeamAt is where a review pressed with the line at t begins: the seam
96	// whose window the line is already in, played on from the line itself, or
97	// else the next seam ahead, sought to its run-up. Past the last window it
98	// wraps to the first join -- there is nothing ahead to hear, and a review
99	// that refuses to start is worse than one that starts over.
100	func reviewSeamAt(segs []cutSeg, t float64) (i int, seek bool) {
101		for i := 0; i < len(segs)-1; i++ {
102			from, to := reviewWindow(segs, i)
103			if t < from {
104				return i, true
105			}
106			if t < to {
107				return i, false
108			}
109		}
110		return 0, true
111	}
112	
113	// reviewSeams is how many joins the cut has to review: one fewer than its
114	// clips. A cut of one clip has nothing to hear.
115	func (ed *cutEditor) reviewSeams() int { return max(len(ed.segs)-1, 0) }
116	
117	// playReview is the ▶✂✂ button. Pressed while it is the one running, it
118	// pauses, and the review is over -- a resume would be ▶✂ from wherever the
119	// line stands, which is what that button is for. Otherwise it starts from the
120	// first join, whatever was playing and whichever preview it was.
121	//
122	// The three ▶s are one rule: each wears ⏸ only while ITS thing runs, pressing
123	// that one pauses it, and pressing another switches the preview over to that
124	// button's thing without stopping. ▶ during a review plays the recording on
125	// from the line; ▶✂ during a review plays the cut on from the line; either
126	// ends the review (setCutOnly, playAs).
127	func (ed *cutEditor) playReview() {
128		if ed.reviewOn && ed.playing() {
129			ed.toggle() // pauses, and the pause ends the review (see toggle)
130			return
131		}
132		if ed.reviewSeams() == 0 {
133			ed.a.setStatus("nothing to review — a cut needs two clips to have a join between them")
134			return
135		}
136		ed.setCutOnly(true) // the review IS the cut preview, with one more hand on the line
137		// from the red line, not from the top: a review paused to look at a join
138		// resumes at that join, and a line parked between two joins goes to the
139		// next one. The first join only when there is none ahead.
140		i, seek := reviewSeamAt(ed.segs, ed.playhead)
141		ed.reviewOn, ed.review, ed.reviewArmed = true, i, !seek
142		ed.jumped = -1
143		if seek {
144			from, _ := reviewWindow(ed.segs, i)
145			ed.setPlayhead(ed.playable(from))
146		} else {
147			ed.setPlayhead(ed.playhead) // where it stands: cues the player there
148		}
149		if !ed.playing() {
150			ed.toggle()
151		}
152		ed.sayReview()
153		ed.syncFaces()
154	}
155	
156	// reviewTick is the review's hand on the line, from followPlayback: once the
157	// seconds after the join under review have played, the line goes to the next
158	// join's run-up, or stops after the last one. true when it moved or stopped
159	// the line, in which case the tick is done (setPlayhead did the rest).
160	func (ed *cutEditor) reviewTick() bool {
161		if !ed.reviewOn {
162			return false
163		}
164		if !ed.cutOnly || ed.reviewSeams() == 0 {
165			ed.reviewOff() // the preview was switched under it, or the cut was edited away
166			return false
167		}
168		i, move := reviewStep(ed.segs, ed.review, ed.playhead, ed.reviewArmed)
169		if i != ed.review {
170			ed.reviewArmed = false // a new seam: its window has not been seen yet
171		}
172		ed.review = i
173		if from, _ := reviewWindow(ed.segs, i); ed.playhead >= from {
174			ed.reviewArmed = true
175		}
176		switch move {
177		case reviewSeek:
178			ed.jumped = -1
179			ed.reviewArmed = false
180			from, _ := reviewWindow(ed.segs, i)
181			ed.setPlayhead(ed.playable(from))
182			ed.sayReview()
183			return true
184		case reviewDone:
185			n := ed.reviewSeams()
186			ed.reviewOff()
187			if ed.player != nil {
188				ed.player.Pause()
189			}
190			ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("reviewed all %d cuts", n))
191			ed.a.updateRunControls()
192			return true
193		case reviewLost:
194			ed.reviewOff()
195			ed.a.setStatus("the line was moved — the cut review is over; ▶✂✂ starts it again")
196		}
197		return false
198	}
199	
200	// reviewOff ends the review without touching the transport: whatever is
201	// playing plays on as the plain ▶✂ preview.
202	func (ed *cutEditor) reviewOff() {
203		if !ed.reviewOn {
204			return
205		}
206		ed.reviewOn = false
207		ed.syncFaces()
208	}
209	
210	// syncFaces redraws all three ▶s. The review starting or ending changes what
211	// ▶✂ says as much as what ▶✂✂ says -- the ⏸ and the lamp move from one to
212	// the other -- and when the cut was already playing there is no transport
213	// change to redraw them for: a review started over a running cut left ▶✂
214	// wearing ⏸ and lit beside a ▶✂✂ wearing the same, which is the one state
215	// the three-button rule exists to rule out.
216	func (ed *cutEditor) syncFaces() {
217		if ed.a != nil {
218			ed.a.syncPlayIcons()
219			return
220		}
221		ed.syncReviewPlay()
222	}
223	
224	func (ed *cutEditor) sayReview() {
225		ed.a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("reviewing cut %d of %d — %.0f s before and after the join at %s",
226			ed.review+1, ed.reviewSeams(), reviewPad, mmss(ed.segs[ed.review].E)))
227	}
228	
229	// syncReviewPlay draws the ▶✂✂ button: a pause face while the review is what
230	// is running, lit while a review is on at all, and grey when the cut has no
231	// join to review. The face is built the way ▶✂'s is -- a stock icon and a
232	// label beside it -- for the reason given at syncCutPlay.
233	func (ed *cutEditor) syncReviewPlay() {
234		if ed.reviewBtn == nil || ed.reviewIcon == nil {
235			return
236		}
237		ed.reviewBtn.SetSensitive(ed.reviewSeams() > 0)
238		if ed.reviewOn && ed.playing() {
239			ed.reviewIcon.SetFromIconName("media-playback-pause-symbolic")
240			ed.reviewBtn.SetTooltipText("pause the cut review")
241		} else {
242			ed.reviewIcon.SetFromIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
243			ed.reviewBtn.SetTooltipText(fmt.Sprintf("review every cut in one go: plays %.0f s of the "+
244				"finished video before each join and %.0f s after it, one join after the other, "+
245				"and stops after the last. The removed stretches are skipped as under ▶✂. "+
246				"Changes nothing that is saved.", reviewPad, reviewPad))
247		}
248		lamp(ed.reviewBtn, ed.reviewOn) // one of the three is lit: see syncPlayIcons
249	}
250	
251	// lamp lights a button, or puts it out. The three ▶s on the Cut page share
252	// one lamp between them: the lit face is the one whose preview the page is
253	// in right now -- the recording, the cut, or the review of the cut -- so the
254	// page always says which of the three a ⏸, the clock and the dimming belong
255	// to. Never two at once and never none.
256	func lamp(b *gtk.Button, on bool) {
257		if b == nil {
258			return
259		}
260		if on {
261			b.AddCSSClass("suggested-action")
262		} else {
263			b.RemoveCSSClass("suggested-action")
264		}
265	}
266	
267	// buildReviewBtn is the button itself, for the transport group in buildCut.
268	func (ed *cutEditor) buildReviewBtn() *gtk.Button {
269		ed.reviewIcon = gtk.NewImageFromIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
270		face := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 2)
271		face.Append(ed.reviewIcon)
272		face.Append(gtk.NewLabel("✂✂"))
273		ed.reviewBtn = gtk.NewButton()
274		ed.reviewBtn.SetChild(face)
275		ed.reviewBtn.ConnectClicked(ed.playReview)
276		ed.syncReviewPlay()
277		return ed.reviewBtn
278	}

3	// Produce: every clip cut from its own recording, narration over ducked game
4	// audio, joined by stream copy, loudness-normalized. A clip grows (maxExtend)
5	// or the narration speeds up (maxTempo) when a line does not fit; both are
6	// logged. Encoding happens once, per clip -- burned subtitles go into that
7	// encode.
8	//
9	// produce/clips/c000.<ext>   per-clip encodes
10	// produce/clips/final.srt    subtitles on the produced timeline (scratch)
11	// produce/final.<container>  the upload
12	
13	import (
14		"encoding/json"
15		"errors"
16		"fmt"

30	const (
31		narrLead  = 0.3  // the earliest a line may start into its clip (writer's "at" 0 lands here)
32		narrGap   = 0.3  // ...and the breath left between two lines on the same clip
33		narrTail  = 0.2  // ...and after the last one, before the clip is over
34		maxExtend = 4.0  // seconds a clip may grow to fit its line
35		maxTempo  = 1.25 // ... and how much the line may be sped up after that
36		// The final mix, and the gap filling in front of it.
37		//
38		// Every clip is encoded on its own, and AAC frames are 1024 samples: a
39		// clip's audio therefore ends on a frame boundary that does not land
40		// exactly where its video does, and the concat leaves a HOLE at every
41		// join. Measured on a 14-clip lecture: 13 holes of 15-86 ms, 511 ms in
42		// total, written into the file as stretched frame durations.
43		//
44		// A player that reads each frame's own duration (VLC, mpv) plays the holes
45		// as the silences they are and stays in sync. One that decodes AAC as the
46		// continuous 1024-samples-a-frame stream it usually is -- which is what a
47		// browser does -- runs the sound ahead of the picture by the accumulated
48		// hole: 28 ms after the first join, half a second by the end. That is the
49		// "slightly out of sync, and worse as it goes on" that VLC will never show
50		// you. aresample fills them, and the same measurement afterwards is one
51		// hole of 60 ms instead of thirteen.
52		//
53		// In front of loudnorm rather than after it, so the loudness pass sees the
54		// continuous stream it is measuring.
55		loudFlt = "aresample=async=1:first_pts=0,loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11"
56		// clipCeil limits every clip's audio before its AAC encode: lanes are mixed
57		// at their recorded levels (normalize=0), so two lanes are louder than one,
58		// and the loudnorm pass over the joined file comes too late to undo a
59		// clipped encode. level=disabled keeps alimiter from scaling back up to 0
60		// dBFS. On every clip, not only mixed ones: the join is a copy, so a filter
61		// some clips went through is a seam.
62		clipCeil = "alimiter=limit=0.891:level=disabled" // -1 dBFS
63	)
64	
65	// audFmt is the shape every clip's audio is forced into. Every clip the same,
66	// or the concat copy produces a file whose second half is silent on half the
67	// players -- which is also why the stereo/mono choice has to reach in here
68	// rather than sit on the encoder at the end: the clips are joined by copying,
69	// so a layout decided per clip IS the layout of the video.
70	func audFmt(st prodSettings) string {
71		return "aformat=sample_fmts=fltp:sample_rates=48000:channel_layouts=" + audLayout(st)
72	}
73	
74	// audLayout is that choice by its ffmpeg name. Mono halves the audio bitrate's
75	// work for a screen recording whose two sides were the same signal all along --
76	// which is most of them, and is exactly what the timeline says when it draws
77	// such a recording on one lane (see sameLanes).
78	func audLayout(st prodSettings) string {
79		if st.Mono {
80			return "mono"
81		}
82		return "stereo"
83	}

96		// Bare leaves the parts of the frame the picture does not reach black,
97		// instead of filling them with a blurred blow-up of the picture itself.

100		// getting it.
101		Bare bool `json:"bare,omitempty"`
102		// what the VIDEO carries: burn | mux | none. The .srt beside it is written
103		// for all three ("sidecar", which used to be the third, is migrated to
104		// "none" -- see UnmarshalJSON).

106		// the languages the subtitles are also written in (translate.go). The

110		SubLangs []string `json:"sub_langs,omitempty"`
111		OutFile  string   `json:"out_file"`
112		// There was a second subtitle setting here: what the track CARRIES -- the
113		// narration, or the transcript of what the people in the recording said.
114		// It is gone, and the track is the narration.
115		//
116		// The transcript half was a second answer to a question the app already
117		// answers twice: the Cut page's captions put chosen lines on screen as
118		// text effects, and the user context is where "put what I say on screen"
119		// is asked for. A dropdown offering a third path -- every spoken line,
120		// automatically, in a subtitle track -- is a setting whose result nothing
121		// on the pages before it can show you. Old projects that stored subs_from

126	// captionLines is what the subtitle track carries for one clip: the narration
127	// lines the writer put on it.
128	// captionLines is what the subtitle track carries for a clip: the narration's
129	// lines where there is a narration, and otherwise what was SAID in the clip,
130	// off the transcript (transcriptSubs). The track used to be the voice-over's
131	// alone, so a session with nobody narrating -- a read to camera, where the
132	// speech IS the video -- asked for a track in the file and got a file with no
133	// track in it, and nothing said why.
134	func captionLines(c prodClip) []prodLine {
135		if len(c.lines) > 0 {
136			return c.lines
137		}
138		return c.subs
139	}
140	
141	// transcriptSubs puts each footage clip's own speech on it as caption-only
142	// lines, in the clip's output seconds. Rows are the session timeline's
143	// (sessionRows): a row overlapping the clip is clipped to it, and a row on the
144	// narrator's own microphone is not a subtitle, since the video does not play
145	// that microphone (tlLabel).
146	func transcriptSubs(clips []prodClip, words []srcWord, narr string) {
147		for i := range clips {
148			c := &clips[i]
149			if c.video == nil || c.ins != "" || c.freeze {
150				continue
151			}
152			s0, s1 := c.sessS, c.sessS+c.length*c.speed()
153			var mine []srcWord
154			for _, w := range words {
155				if w.s >= s0-0.01 && w.e <= s1+0.01 && (narr == "" || w.src != narr) {
156					mine = append(mine, w)
157				}
158			}
159			c.subs = wordCues(mine, s0, c.speed(), c.length)
160		}
161	}
162	
163	// wordCues groups one clip's words into caption lines, in the clip's own
164	// output seconds.
165	//
166	// Per WORD and not per transcript line, because a transcript line is not what
167	// the video says. The lines come off Prepare, before the cut, and the cut
168	// removes stretches inside them: a line clipped to the clip kept its whole
169	// text, so the join at 1:45 read "…public state of the art, and the whole run
170	// took roughly 13" over footage that says "…public state of the art" -- words
171	// that are not in the video, and are read AGAIN when the retake plays. Eleven
172	// of that session's eighty-one lines were cut into. Built from the words that
173	// survive, the subtitles say what the video says, and there is nothing left
174	// for them to be wrong about.
175	//
176	// A cue ends at a breath (subBreak), or when it has as much on it as two rows
177	// hold, or after subCueMax seconds -- a player wraps what it is given at its
178	// own font size, so a cue longer than two rows is one it will break into four.
179	func wordCues(words []srcWord, s0, speed, length float64) []prodLine {
180		var out []prodLine
181		var cur []srcWord
182		flush := func() {
183			if len(cur) == 0 {
184				return
185			}
186			var txt []string
187			for _, w := range cur {
188				// a word whose spelling was folded into the one in front of it
189				// (fixWords): it holds its seconds and says nothing of its own
190				if w.raw == "" {
191					continue
192				}
193				txt = append(txt, w.raw)
194			}
195			at := math.Max(0, (cur[0].s-s0)/speed)
196			end := math.Min(length, (cur[len(cur)-1].e-s0)/speed)
197			cur = nil
198			if end <= at {
199				return
200			}
201			// Every word here was folded into one in the cue BEFORE (fixWords):
202			// "RSA-1024" is printed on the first word of "one thousand twenty
203			// four" and the rest say nothing, and when that stretch crosses a cue
204			// boundary the second cue is left with no words of its own. It is not
205			// a blank subtitle -- the phrase is on screen already, and what these
206			// seconds want is for it to STAY there. A cue with nothing in it went
207			// into the .srt as an empty caption and out to the translator as an
208			// empty line, which came back empty twice and was reported as a line
209			// the model had lost.
210			if len(txt) == 0 {
211				if len(out) > 0 {
212					last := &out[len(out)-1]
213					last.dur = math.Min(math.Max(last.dur, end-last.at), subCueMax)
214				}
215				return
216			}
217			out = append(out, prodLine{text: strings.Join(txt, " "), at: at, delay: at, dur: end - at})
218		}
219		n := 0
220		for i, w := range words {
221			if len(cur) > 0 {
222				long := n+1+len(w.raw) > 2*subRowChars
223				if w.s-cur[len(cur)-1].e >= subBreak || long || (w.e-cur[0].s)/speed >= subCueMax {
224					flush()
225					n = 0
226				}
227			}
228			cur = append(cur, w)
229			n += len(w.raw) + 1
230			_ = i
231		}
232		flush()
233		return out
234	}

240		subBreak = 0.6
241		// how many characters a row of a caption holds (wrapSub wraps at this),
242		// and how long one may stay up before the next takes over
243		subRowChars = 42
244		subCueMax   = 6.0
245	)

312	// syncNarrOff shows or hides what only a narration needs. Called when the tick
313	// on the Narrate page changes and when a project's answer arrives, and safe
314	// before the page exists -- a project can load before Produce is built.
315	func (a *App) syncNarrOff() {
316		p := a.prod
317		if p == nil || p.subs == nil {
318			return
319		}
320		// the game-volume slider only: the subtitles are no longer the
321		// narration's alone (captionLines), so their choice stays whatever the
322		// narration does
323		on := !a.narrOff
324		for _, w := range []interface{ SetVisible(bool) }{
325			p.gvol, p.gvolLbl,
326		} {

333	// defaultProdSettings is the render a project gets before anyone touches the
334	// Produce page: h264 in mp4 at the quality this pipeline was tuned on. Named
335	// because two places need it -- the page before it is built, and a new project,
336	// which has to come back to these rather than to zeroes (a 0 CRF is lossless
337	// and a 0 fps is not a video at all).
338	func defaultProdSettings() prodSettings {
339		return prodSettings{Container: "mp4", Codec: "h264", CRF: 24, Preset: "veryslow",
340			Height: 1080, FPS: 30, AudioKbps: 128, GameVol: 0.22, Subs: "none"}
341	}

343	// UnmarshalJSON seeds the defaults before decoding so an ABSENT game_vol (an
344	// older project: keep 0.22) and a stored 0 (a deliberate pick: silence the
345	// game) stop meaning the same thing. Only GameVol: CRF's slider starts at 14,
346	// so its 0 guard cannot be wrong.
347	func (s *prodSettings) UnmarshalJSON(b []byte) error {
348		type raw prodSettings // a defined type carries no methods, so no recursion
349		v := raw{GameVol: defaultProdSettings().GameVol}
350		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &v); err != nil {
351			return err
352		}
353		*s = prodSettings(v)
354		// "sidecar" was "the .srt beside the video, nothing in it". The file is
355		// written for every choice now, so what is left of that answer is the
356		// half about the video: nothing in it.
357		if s.Subs == "sidecar" {
358			s.Subs = "none"
359		}
360		return nil
361	}

363	// gameVol is the level the render plays the game at under a narration line.
364	// Asked on its own because the Narrate preview has to duck to it on the
365	// playback tick, and reading a page of widgets ten times a second to get one
366	// number is not what that tick is for.
367	func (a *App) gameVol() float64 {
368		if a == nil || a.prod == nil || a.prod.gvol == nil {
369			return defaultProdSettings().GameVol
370		}
371		return a.prod.gvol.Value()
372	}

313	type sugFx struct {
314		Kind       string
315		Start, End float64
316		Rate       float64
317		// a pointer because 0 is a gain somebody can mean. Silence is the whole
318		// reason a session says "do not use this audio", and as a plain float64
319		// that instruction and a volume effect with no gain field at all arrive
320		// here as the same 0 -- so obeying one meant obeying the other, and the
321		// parser chose to obey neither. Absent is nil; explicit is a number.
322		Gain *float64

328	// apart -- a one-second island of normal speed between two fast ones, which
329	// on screen is a hiccup and on the lane is two badges jammed together. Under
330	// this many seconds of ordinary footage between them, the island goes too.
331	const speedGapMin = 4.0

333	// joinSpeeds folds speed effects at one rate that run into each other, or
334	// nearly, into one. The rest of the list is untouched and the order is kept.
335	func joinSpeeds(fx []cutFx) []cutFx {
336		var speeds, rest []cutFx
337		for _, f := range fx {
338			if f.Kind == "speed" && f.Rate > 0 {
339				speeds = append(speeds, f)
340			} else {

342			}
343		}

56		// the two disagreed for a week of runs, the box quietly winning while the
57		// sentence beside it read 12 minutes. One place, and it is the one the
58		// person writes in. Nothing named, and the default stands.
59		// 0 is "no target", and it is the ordinary answer: a session whose context
60		// names no length has no length, not a secret default one. It used to fall
61		// back to 300 s and the request then told the model that 300 was "the
62		// length named in the user context" -- which nobody had named. A script
63		// read out in full came back cut to a third of itself, with the rest left
64		// for a speed pass the same context had forbidden.
65		target := 0.0
66		if want, ok := ctxLength(a.sessionCtx()); ok {
67			target = want
68		} else {
69			a.logf(">>> suggest: the user context names no length — everything worth keeping goes in")
70		}
71		// how long the session runs, which is the denominator the choosing half of
72		// the bar counts against (see suggestCut)
73		span := 0.0
74		for _, r := range rows {
75			span = math.Max(span, r.e)
76		}
77	
78		a.startRun()
79		a.saveProjectNow() // the run is a moment worth a file
80		if target > 0 {
81			a.logf(">>> suggest: target %.0f s — three calls: the cut, its captions, its effects", target)
82		} else {
83			a.logf(">>> suggest: no target length — three calls: the cut, its captions, its effects")
84		}
85		// Both calls are streamed, but the model thinks for minutes before the first
86		// segment, so the bar pulses until the first finished segment's own fraction
87		// stops it (same shape as publish). The queue's first word, not the bar's:
88		// anything the queue says later would wipe it (showProg runs on an idle).
89		a.qJob(trackSTT, "suggest", 1, 4)
90		a.prog(trackSTT, 0, "thinking over the whole session")
91		glib.TimeoutAdd(150, func() bool {
92			if !a.running {
93				return false
94			}
95			a.progMu.Lock()
96			moving := a.progParts[trackSTT] > 0
97			a.progMu.Unlock()
98			if moving {
99				return false
100			}
101			a.progress.Pulse()
102			return true
103		})
104		go func() {
105			a.logCtx("suggest")
106			segs, fx, err := a.suggestCut(session, target, span)
107			if err == nil {
108				// the cut stands. Now what goes ON it, clip by clip: the captions,
109				// then the decorations. Each pass sees the kept clips and nothing
110				// else, answers in the clip's own seconds, and can fail on its own
111				// without taking the cut with it.
112				a.qJob(trackSTT, "suggest", 2, 4)
113				caps := a.captionCut(segs, rows)
114				// the speeds come after the captions and know about them: a
115				// caption over a stretch at 4 is gone before it is read, and
116				// which lines are captioned is the pass above's decision
117				a.qJob(trackSTT, "suggest", 3, 4)
118				a.prog(trackSTT, 0.85, "how fast each clip plays")
119				fx = append(fx, caps...)
120				fx = append(fx, a.speedCut(segs, caps, rows)...)
121				a.qJob(trackSTT, "suggest", 4, 4)
122				a.prog(trackSTT, 0.93, "the zooms and stops")
123				fx = append(fx, a.decorateCut(segs, rows, fx)...)
124			}
125			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
126				a.endRun()
127				if err != nil {
128					if !errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
129						a.logf("suggest FAILED: %v", err)
130					}
131					a.progress.SetFraction(0)
132					a.setStatus("suggest failed — see log")
133					return
134				}
135				a.ed.pushUndo() // a suggestion is a proposal; Undo clears it again
136				// A re-suggest replaces the old cut, never stacks on it -- but only
137				// the footage half of it. The inserts were placed by hand, the model
138				// was never told they exist, and an answer that does not mention them
139				// is not an answer that dropped them.
140				a.ed.segs = insertsOf(a.ed.segs)
141				segs = joinSeams(segs, rows)
142				for _, s := range segs {
143					a.ed.segs = append(a.ed.segs, cutSeg{
144						S: a.ed.snapEdge(s.S, true), E: a.ed.snapEdge(s.E, false)})
145				}
146				// ...and then the marks, last and over the top of the snapping.
147				//
148				// Hiding a stretch from the brief is not the same as keeping it out
149				// of the cut: the model answers in RANGES, and a range that spans a
150				// folded stretch keeps every second of it. One run came back with
151				// 39.28-108.44 and 113.28-164.00 either side of a mark at
152				// 106.16-111.36 -- it had clearly aimed at the seam and missed it by
153				// two seconds, which is the whole of the doubled sentence.
154				//
155				// After the snap and not before it, because snapEdge moves an end
156				// outward by up to five seconds to find a silence, and outward from
157				// the border of a marked stretch is INTO it.
158				if n := dropMarked(&a.ed.segs, marks); n > 0 {
159					a.logf(">>> %d marked stretch(es) taken out of the cut — said twice, kept once", n)
160				}
161				// ...and the stretches where nothing was said at all, which are
162				// nobody else's job (dropDeadAir)
163				if gone := dropDeadAir(&a.ed.segs, a.ed.talk); gone > 0 {
164					a.logf(">>> %s of silence taken out of the cut — nothing was said in it", mmss(gone))
165				}
166				a.ed.coalesce()
167				// snapEdge and coalesce just moved the boundaries the effects
168				// were placed against. The clamp is the guarantee -- whichever
169				// pass proposed an effect, it lands inside the cut as applied,
170				// or not at all.
171				if len(fx) > 0 {
172					kept := clampFxToSegs(fx, a.ed.segs)
173					if n := len(fx) - len(kept); n > 0 {
174						a.logf(">>> %d effect(s) pointed at footage the final cut does not keep — dropped", n)
175					}
176					fx = kept
177				}
178				// the effects the style proposed, on the page as if drawn by
179				// hand. They REPLACE what was there: the moments they decorate
180				// are the new suggestion's, and effects pinned to the old choice
181				// would decorate stretches no longer in the video. A reply that
182				// proposed none changes nothing here, and the pushUndo above
183				// takes segments and effects back as one.
184				if len(fx) > 0 {
185					a.ed.fx = fx
186					a.ed.dropFx()
187				}
188				a.ed.persist()
189				a.ed.setBase() // from here on, Revert comes back to this suggestion
190				a.progress.SetFraction(1)
191				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("suggested %d segments", len(segs)))
192				// the length of the VIDEO this makes, effects included, which is
193				// what the target was a target for: read straight off the
194				// segments it would over-report every speed-up in the answer
195				total := a.ed.cutLen()
196				a.logf(">>> suggested %d segments, %d:%02d total",
197					len(segs), int(total)/60, int(total)%60)
198				if len(fx) > 0 {
199					a.logf(">>> ...and %d effect(s): the speeds, the captions and the decorations", len(fx))
200				}
201			})
202		}()
203	}
204	
205	// keepFilmed drops what cannot be shown: a segment with no recording at either
206	// end is time nobody has footage of. The suggestion goes
207	// through it, so neither can put a hole in the video.
208	func (a *App) keepFilmed(segs []cutSeg) []cutSeg {
209		var out []cutSeg
210		for _, s := range segs {
211			// an insert brings its own picture, which is the entire point of it --
212			// "no recording under it" is its normal state, not a fault
213			if !s.isInsert() && a.ed.videoAt(s.S) == nil && a.ed.videoAt(s.E) == nil {
214				continue
215			}
216			out = append(out, s)
217		}
218		return out
219	}
220	
221	// minSuggestSegs is how few segments a suggestion may come back with before it
222	// is arithmetic nonsense rather than a choice. Four made sense when every cut
223	// was minutes long; a Short's count is however many beats its notes name, and
224	// rejecting a two-segment answer to a 25 s target burns attempts on a rule
225	// the target itself contradicts.
226	func minSuggestSegs(target float64) int {
227		if n := 1 + int(target/30); n < 4 {
228			return n
229		}
230		return 4
231	}
232	
233	// maxSuggestSegs is the other end of the same question, and it exists because
234	// of one failure: an answer of 548 segments, the first five real moments and
235	// the rest a mechanical march of 24-second blocks every 32 seconds, running
236	// eleven times past the end of the session until the token ceiling chopped it
237	// mid-number. Nothing rejected it for its SHAPE -- the segments past the end
238	// were dropped for having no footage, the total then failed the length gate,
239	// and the reason the model was told was arithmetic when the reason was that it
240	// had stopped cutting and started counting.
241	//
242	// Generous: the wordings ask for about one segment per 20 seconds of target,
243	// and this is four times that with a floor, so a cut that really is made of
244	// many short moments is not refused. What it catches is the runaway, which
245	// misses by an order of magnitude and not by a few.
246	func maxSuggestSegs(target float64) int {
247		if n := int(target / 5); n > 40 {
248			return n
249		}
250		return 40
251	}
252	
253	// ctxLength is a length the user context names for the finished video, in
254	// seconds, and whether it names one at all. "12min", "~15 min", "5 minutes",
255	// "90 s", "90 seconds": a number with a unit of time on it. A bare number is
256	// not a length -- "500 wins" and "level 2" are not durations -- and the first
257	// one with a unit is taken, because a context that names two is a context
258	// whose author knows which one they meant.
259	func ctxLength(ctx string) (float64, bool) {
260		m := ctxLenRe.FindStringSubmatch(ctx)
261		if m == nil {
262			return 0, false
263		}
264		n, err := strconv.ParseFloat(m[1], 64)
265		if err != nil || n <= 0 {
266			return 0, false
267		}
268		if strings.HasPrefix(strings.ToLower(m[2]), "m") {
269			n *= 60
270		}
271		return n, true
272	}
273	
274	var ctxLenRe = regexp.MustCompile(`(?i)~?\b(\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*(min(?:ute)?s?|m|s|sec(?:ond)?s?)\b`)
275	
276	// footageWindow is how much SESSION the cut may keep. The floor is the
277	// finished video's own -- footage under it cannot fill the target at any rate
278	// -- and the ceiling is what the speed pass could squeeze into the target at
279	// the fastest rate it uses, so a cut inside it is one the arithmetic can still
280	// land. Wide on purpose: which of those seconds are worth keeping is the cut's
281	// judgement, and how many of them run fast is a later call's.
282	func (a *App) footageWindow(target float64) (lo, hi float64) {
283		lo, hi = a.suggestWindow(target)
284		return lo, hi * maxSpeedRate
285	}
286	
287	// maxSpeedRate is the fastest rate the speed pass is expected to use, and
288	// therefore how much footage a target can swallow. 4 and not 8: eight is for a
289	// minute of loading screen, not for a whole video, and a ceiling built on it
290	// would accept cuts nothing could make watchable.
291	const maxSpeedRate = 4.0
292	
293	// suggestWindow is how far a suggestion's total may drift from the target. A
294	// long cut is a wish (half over is fine); under a minute it is a promise, so
295	// the ceiling is a fifth over -- a 25-second target must not ship as 37. The
296	// floor is shared.
297	func (a *App) suggestWindow(target float64) (lo, hi float64) {
298		if target <= shortTarget {
299			return target * 0.6, target * 1.2
300		}
301		return target * 0.6, target * 1.5
302	}
303	
304	// shortTarget is where a target stops being a wish and becomes a format. Under
305	// a minute is a Short, a teaser, a clip for a post: a length somebody promised
306	// somewhere, and 45 seconds of "30 second" video is a different thing from
307	// what was asked for. Minutes-long cuts land where the material lets them.
308	const shortTarget = 60.0
309	
310	// sugFx is one effect as a cut style's reply spells it: a kind, the stretch of
311	// session seconds it covers, and the one number that kind needs. Every style
312	// asks for these; a reply without the list parses to none.
313	type sugFx struct {
314		Kind       string
315		Start, End float64
316		Rate       float64
317		// a pointer because 0 is a gain somebody can mean. Silence is the whole
318		// reason a session says "do not use this audio", and as a plain float64
319		// that instruction and a volume effect with no gain field at all arrive
320		// here as the same 0 -- so obeying one meant obeying the other, and the
321		// parser chose to obey neither. Absent is nil; explicit is a number.
322		Gain *float64
323		Text string
324	}
325	
326	// speedGapMin is how close two speed stretches at the same rate may come
327	// before they are one stretch. A cut once came back with two ×4 runs a second
328	// apart -- a one-second island of normal speed between two fast ones, which
329	// on screen is a hiccup and on the lane is two badges jammed together. Under
330	// this many seconds of ordinary footage between them, the island goes too.
331	const speedGapMin = 4.0
332	
333	// joinSpeeds folds speed effects at one rate that run into each other, or
334	// nearly, into one. The rest of the list is untouched and the order is kept.
335	func joinSpeeds(fx []cutFx) []cutFx {
336		var speeds, rest []cutFx
337		for _, f := range fx {
338			if f.Kind == "speed" && f.Rate > 0 {
339				speeds = append(speeds, f)
340			} else {
341				rest = append(rest, f)
342			}
343		}
344		sort.SliceStable(speeds, func(i, j int) bool { return speeds[i].T < speeds[j].T })
345		var out []cutFx
346		for _, f := range speeds {
347			if n := len(out); n > 0 && out[n-1].Rate == f.Rate &&
348				f.T-(out[n-1].T+out[n-1].Dur) < speedGapMin {
349				end := math.Max(out[n-1].T+out[n-1].Dur, f.T+f.Dur)
350				out[n-1].Dur = end - out[n-1].T
351				out[n-1].Tout = f.Tout // the fade out is the later stretch's
352				continue
353			}
354			out = append(out, f)
355		}
356		return append(out, rest...)
357	}
358	
359	// fxFromReply turns proposed effects into cutFx: the model chooses WHEN and
360	// WHICH KIND, the app's own defaults decide HOW. Nonsense entries are dropped,
361	// not fatal. svg cannot be asked for (a file on this machine).
362	// fxMaxProposed caps a reply's effects at the wording's rate over a cut longer
363	// than anyone makes.
364	const fxMaxProposed = 1000 // effectively none: how many effects a cut carries is the prompt's call, not this file's
365	
366	func fxFromReply(in []sugFx) []cutFx { return fxFrom(in, fxMaxProposed) }
367	
368	// fxFrom is fxFromReply with the cap as an argument: the reply's own effects
369	// are decorations and are held to fxMaxProposed; the speeds a cut is built
370	// from are not decorations and are held to nothing, or a cut of sixty
371	// sped-up stretches has thirty-six of them quietly running at 1.
372	func fxFrom(in []sugFx, cap int) []cutFx {
373		var out []cutFx
374		for _, f := range in {
375			if cap > 0 && len(out) == cap {
376				break
377			}
378			d := f.End - f.Start
379			switch strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.Kind)) {
380			case "zoom":
381				if d <= 0 {
382					continue
383				}
384				g := math.Min(1, d/3) // the dialog's second of glide, shrunk to fit a short zoom
385				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "zoom", T: f.Start, Dur: d,
386					Cx: 0.5, Cy: 0.5, Hf: 0.6, Trans: g, Tout: g})
387			case "speed":
388				if d <= 0 {
389					continue
390				}
391				rate := f.Rate
392				if rate <= 0 {
393					rate = 0.5 // an unnamed rate means slow-mo; 0 would be a freeze nobody asked for
394				}
395				rate, d = clampSpeed(rate, d)
396				// the same fades a suggested zoom and caption get, on the same
397				// terms: a second either side where the stretch is long enough to
398				// spend it, and nothing where the render could not build the
399				// stairs anyway -- which at a fast rate wants more footage than a
400				// second, because a stair is measured on the finished video
401				ramp := math.Min(1, d/4)
402				if ramp < rampStep*math.Max(1, rate) {
403					ramp = 0
404				}
405				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "speed", T: f.Start, Dur: d, Rate: rate,
406					Trans: ramp, Tout: ramp})
407			case "stop":
408				// the held frame: the picture stands still at f.Start while the
409				// footage runs on under it, which is a speed of 0 (frozenFx). It
410				// is a kind of its own in the reply because a rate cannot say it
411				// -- an omitted rate and a rate of 0 are the same JSON number,
412				// and reading that as a freeze would hand a still to every reply
413				// that forgot to name a speed
414				if d <= 0 {
415					d = 2 // long enough to read as a hold, short enough not to strand the viewer
416				}
417				fade := math.Min(0.3, d/4)
418				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "speed", T: f.Start, Dur: d, Rate: 0,
419					Trans: fade, Tout: fade})
420			case "volume":
421				if d <= 0 {
422					continue
423				}
424				// a gain nobody named is a field left out, and there is nothing
425				// to do about it; 1 is dropped for the plainer reason that it
426				// does nothing. An explicit 0 is kept -- that is a stretch the
427				// session wanted silent.
428				if f.Gain == nil || *f.Gain == 1 {
429					continue
430				}
431				// the same second either way that a suggested zoom and caption get
432				ramp := math.Min(1, d/4)
433				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "volume", T: f.Start, Dur: d,
434					Gain: clampGain(*f.Gain), Trans: ramp, Tout: ramp})
435			case "text":
436				txt := strings.TrimSpace(f.Text)
437				if txt == "" {
438					continue // a caption with no words is nothing to draw
439				}
440				if d <= 0 {
441					d = 3 // the dialog's own opening duration
442				}
443				fade := math.Min(0.3, d/4)
444				out = append(out, cutFx{Kind: "text", T: f.Start, Dur: d,
445					Trans: fade, Tout: fade, Text: txt})
446			}
447		}
448		return out
449	}
450	
451	func (a *App) suggestCut(session string, target, span float64) ([]cutSeg, []cutFx, error) {
452		system := a.sysPrompt("cut")
453		// With a target: the range, not just the number. Told "300 seconds" alone, a
454		// model spends the call adding and dropping segments to hit it exactly and
455		// runs out of room for the answer (once: 85 kB of arithmetic, no JSON). From
456		// the same function the validator uses, so prompt and gate cannot drift.
457		//
458		// With none: say there is none. A length nobody asked for is not a weaker
459		// instruction than a real one -- it is the instruction, and the model obeys
460		// it by leaving out material the person wanted in.
461		length := "NO TARGET LENGTH. The user context names none, so there is none: keep every " +
462			"moment worth keeping and the video is as long as that comes to. Nothing is dropped to " +
463			"reach a length, and nothing is kept to fill one."
464		if target > 0 {
465			lo, hi := a.footageWindow(target)
466			length = fmt.Sprintf("TARGET LENGTH: %.0f seconds of finished video, which is the length "+
467				"named in the user context. The dull stretches are played fast afterwards, so KEEP "+
468				"between %.0f and %.0f seconds of footage, in at most %d segments. Stop at the "+
469				"first set of moments that lands in that range.", target, lo, hi, maxSuggestSegs(target))
470		}
471		// ...and how long the session it is choosing from actually runs. Nothing
472		// used to state where the session ENDS: three attempts in a row once came
473		// back with segments marching to 28999 -- eight hours of a 28-minute
474		// recording -- because a model that has lost its place has nothing in the
475		// request to lose its place against. Both spellings here as on every
476		// timeline line (stamp), since a clock read as a count of seconds is where
477		// a run of plausible numbers turns into nonsense.
478		user := a.ctxBlockFor("cut") + fmt.Sprintf("SESSION LENGTH: %.0f seconds, which the timeline "+
479			"writes as %s. Every start and end you give is a number of SECONDS between 0 and "+
480			"%.0f.\n\n%s\n\nSESSION TIMELINE:\n%s", span, mmss(span), span, length, session)
481		msgs := []map[string]any{msg("system", system), msg("user", user)}
482		// the web, for a caption that names a thing the timeline does not explain
483		tools, ffx := a.webToolsFor("suggest")
484		// The bar, while a call that takes minutes runs: segments counted as they
485		// close, placed by where in the session they land (see jsonItemsDone).
486		// Only ever forward -- a rejected attempt starts the count again, and a bar
487		// that fell back to the first minute would read as work being undone rather
488		// than redone.
489		best := 0.0
490		onText := func(s string) {
491			n, through := jsonItemsDone(s, "segments")
492			if n == 0 {
493				return // still thinking, and the pulse says that better than a 0 does
494			}
495			f := float64(n) / suggestMaxSegs // no timeline to place them on: count
496			if span > 0 && through > 0 {
497				f = through / span
498			}
499			// never quite 0: a first segment two minutes into a two-hour session is
500			// news, and reporting it as nothing would leave the pulse running
501			f = math.Max(0.02, math.Min(1, f))
502			if f <= best {
503				return
504			}
505			best = f
506			if span > 0 {
507				a.prog(trackSTT, suggestChooseShare*f, "%d moments, at %s of %s",
508					n, mmss(through), mmss(span))
509			} else {
510				a.prog(trackSTT, suggestChooseShare*f, "%d moments", n)
511			}
512		}
513		// Thinking first, execute mode only after an attempt comes back empty
514		// (thinkAgain): thinking calls answered in about ten minutes over three days
515		// of runs; execute-mode ones answered in two and worse.
516		think := true
517		for try := 0; try < 3; try++ {
518			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
519				return nil, nil, err
520			}
521			reply, err := a.llmChatRetryTools("suggest", msgs, think, tools, a.webRunner("suggest", ffx), onText)
522			if err != nil {
523				return nil, nil, err
524			}
525			segs, fx, problem := a.checkCutReply(reply, target, span, try+1)
526			if problem == "" {
527				return segs, fx, nil
528			}
529			a.logfIdle(">>> suggest attempt %d rejected: %s", try+1, problem)
530			// the search goes with the first refusal. The tools are there for a
531			// caption that names something the timeline does not explain, which is
532			// a detail of an answer -- and a model that has just failed to write
533			// the answer spends the retry searching instead: one run went eight
534			// rounds deep into a wiki and ran out of rounds without ever proposing
535			// a segment. Everything the cut needs is in the timeline it was given.
536			if tools != nil {
537				a.logfIdle(">>> suggest: asking again without the web tools")
538				tools = nil
539			}
540			if next := thinkAgain(think, reply); next != think {
541				think = next
542				a.logfIdle(">>> suggest: the model spent the whole call thinking and wrote " +
543					"nothing — asking again with thinking off")
544			}
545			msgs = retryTurn(msgs, reply, problem)
546		}
547		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("no valid cut after 3 attempts")
548	}
549	
550	// checkCutReply reads one answer to the cut and says everything wrong with it
551	// -- one fault per sentence, worst first -- or hands back the cut. Everything,
552	// not the first thing: there are only three attempts, and an answer with three
553	// faults gets one round to fix them all.
554	func (a *App) checkCutReply(reply string, target, span float64, attempt int) ([]cutSeg, []cutFx, string) {
555		var out struct {
556			// speed and rate on a SEGMENT are the same thing said where a model
557			// keeps saying it: a stretch that runs at 4 is one segment with one
558			// number on it, which is exactly what the wording asks for and not
559			// quite the shape the reply names. It is read as the speed effect it
560			// means rather than thrown away -- thrown away, the arithmetic the
561			// model did with it was right and the total it was told was wrong.
562			Segments []struct{ Start, End, Speed, Rate float64 } `json:"segments"`
563			Fx       []sugFx                                     `json:"fx"`
564		}
565		if problem := jsonReply(reply, &out); problem != "" {
566			return nil, nil, problem
567		}
568		// a rate on a segment: 1 is the ordinary rate and says nothing, and any
569		// other is a speed effect over the whole segment. They are kept APART from
570		// the reply's own effects -- they are how the cut is built, not decoration
571		// on it, so they are neither counted against the effect ceiling nor cut
572		// off by fxMaxProposed, which once dropped every one of sixty and had the
573		// total counted at the footage's own length
574		var segSpeeds []sugFx
575		for _, s := range out.Segments {
576			if r := math.Max(s.Speed, s.Rate); r > 0 && math.Abs(r-1) > 1e-9 {
577				segSpeeds = append(segSpeeds, sugFx{Kind: "speed", Start: s.Start, End: s.End, Rate: r})
578			}
579		}
580		var probs []string
581	
582		// timestamps past the end of the recording, segments and effects alike.
583		// Said first, because it is the fault underneath the others: a cut whose
584		// seconds run past the end fails the length gate too, and being told the
585		// total sends the next attempt to rebalance an answer whose real problem
586		// is that it read the timeline's stamps as decimals. That is what these
587		// numbers are, every time -- 2804 for the line stamped [28:04] -- so the
588		// message does the one conversion the model got wrong, on its own number.
589		past, first := 0, 0.0
590		for _, s := range out.Segments {
591			if span > 0 && s.Start >= span {
592				if past == 0 {
593					first = s.Start
594				}
595				past++
596			}
597		}
598		for _, f := range append(append([]sugFx(nil), out.Fx...), segSpeeds...) {
599			if span > 0 && f.Start >= span {
600				if past == 0 {
601					first = f.Start
602				}
603				past++
604			}
605		}
606		if past > 0 {
607			probs = append(probs, fmt.Sprintf("%d of your timestamps lie after the session ends at %.0f s%s",
608				past, span, mmssHint(first, span)))
609		}
610	
611		if len(out.Segments) < minSuggestSegs(target) {
612			probs = append(probs, fmt.Sprintf("fewer than %d segments", minSuggestSegs(target)))
613		} else if n := maxSuggestSegs(target); len(out.Segments) > n {
614			// said as a shape problem, because that is what it is: an answer
615			// this long is a model that stopped choosing moments
616			probs = append(probs, fmt.Sprintf("%d segments, which is not a cut -- keep it under %d, "+
617				"and use a speed effect over one long segment where a stretch has to be "+
618				"shown but not watched", len(out.Segments), n))
619		}
620	
621		var segs []cutSeg
622		for _, s := range out.Segments {
623			if s.End <= s.Start {
624				probs = append(probs, "a segment ends before it starts")
625				break
626			}
627			segs = append(segs, cutSeg{S: s.Start, E: s.End})
628		}
629		// only video-backed time counts, and it is counted after the drop: a
630		// suggestion that spent half its length on stretches nobody filmed is
631		// short, and being told the number it actually landed on is what makes
632		// the next attempt aim elsewhere
633		asked := len(segs)
634		segs = a.keepFilmed(segs)
635		if n := asked - len(segs); n > 0 {
636			a.logfIdle(">>> suggest attempt %d: %d segment(s) dropped for having no footage", attempt, n)
637		}
638		// on FOOTAGE, not on finished length: how fast it plays is the speed
639		// pass's answer and does not exist yet. The ceiling is what that pass
640		// could compress into the target at the fastest ordinary rate, so a cut
641		// this side of it is one the arithmetic can still land.
642		fx := joinSpeeds(append(fxFrom(segSpeeds, 0), fxFromReply(out.Fx)...))
643		raw := 0.0
644		for _, s := range segs {
645			raw += s.E - s.S
646		}
647		// only against a target the user named: with none there is no range, and a
648		// cut that keeps the whole of a script is the right answer rather than an
649		// answer that missed one
650		if lo, hi := a.footageWindow(target); target > 0 && (raw < lo || raw > hi) {
651			probs = append(probs, fmt.Sprintf("%.0f s of footage, where %.0f to %.0f is accepted "+
652				"(the dull stretches are played fast afterwards, which is what makes the "+
653				"upper end reachable)", raw, lo, hi))
654		}
655		if len(probs) > 0 {
656			return nil, nil, strings.Join(probs, "; ")
657		}
658		return segs, fx, ""
659	}
660	
661	// mmssHint is the conversion a stamp-read-as-a-decimal got wrong, done on the
662	// model's own number: 2804 came from [28:04], which is 28*60+4. Empty when the
663	// number does not read as a stamp at all, rather than a hint that is itself a
664	// guess.
665	func mmssHint(n, span float64) string {
666		mm, ss := int(n)/100, int(n)%100
667		if ss >= 60 || mm <= 0 {
668			return ""
669		}
670		secs := mm*60 + ss
671		if float64(secs) > span {
672			return ""
673		}
674		return fmt.Sprintf(" -- %.0f is not a second: a stamp [%02d:%02d] is mm*60+ss, %d",
675			n, mm, ss, secs)
676	}
677	
678	// clampFxToSegs holds a proposed effect to the cut as it will actually play:
679	// inside a footage segment, or gone. It has to run against the segments AS
680	// APPLIED -- after snapEdge, after coalesce -- because every
681	// one of those moves boundaries after the effects were chosen, and a rule
682	// enforced any earlier is enforced against a cut that no longer exists.
683	// Inserts do not count as home: they bring their own picture, and an effect
684	// proposed off the timeline was never about one.
685	func clampFxToSegs(fx []cutFx, segs []cutSeg) []cutFx {
686		var out []cutFx
687		for _, f := range fx {
688			t0, t1 := f.fxSpan()
689			// a point -- a bare view -- has no width to overlap with; being
690			// inside a segment is the whole question
691			if t1 <= t0 {
692				for _, s := range segs {
693					if !s.isInsert() && s.S <= t0 && t0 <= s.E {
694						out = append(out, f)
695						break
696					}
697				}
698				continue
699			}
700			// the footage segment this effect shares the most time with
701			best, overlap := -1, 0.0
702			for i, s := range segs {
703				if s.isInsert() {
704					continue
705				}
706				if o := math.Min(t1, s.E) - math.Max(t0, s.S); o > overlap {
707					best, overlap = i, o
708				}
709			}
710			if best < 0 {
711				continue // no kept footage under it at all
712			}
713			s := segs[best]
714			if t0 >= s.S && t1 <= s.E {
715				out = append(out, f) // already inside: exactly as proposed
716				continue
717			}
718			was := t1 - t0 // the band before the cut took a piece off it
719			nt0, nt1 := math.Max(t0, s.S), math.Min(t1, s.E)
720			if nt1-nt0 < 1 {
721				// under a second left is not the effect that was meant: most of
722				// the moment it decorated is not in the video
723				continue
724			}
725			f.T, f.Dur = nt0, nt1-nt0
726			switch f.Kind {
727			case "zoom", "text", "svg", "volume":
728				// nothing kind-specific: the band is the band, and the fades
729				// inside it are shrunk with it below
730			case "speed":
731				// a rate has to stay playable over the band it was trimmed to.
732				// A stop is not a rate and gets none: clampSpeed would hand the
733				// frozen frame one, which is a stop that quietly became slow
734				// motion because the cut moved under it.
735				if !f.frozenFx() {
736					f.Rate, f.Dur = clampSpeed(f.Rate, f.Dur)
737				}
738			default:
739				continue // a kind with no span to trim
740			}
741			trimFades(&f, was)
742			out = append(out, f)
743		}
744		return out
745	}
746	
747	// ---- the passes after the cut ----------------------------------------------
748	//
749	// Cut first, then captions, speed and effects over the kept clips in the clips'
750	// own seconds (offsets from the clip's start, never session stamps). One reply
751	// for all of it ran out of tokens or wrote nothing.
752	
753	// captionBatch is how many clips one captions request carries. Five is a few
754	// paragraphs in and a few dozen lines out -- small enough that a bad answer
755	// costs a minute, not a run.
756	const captionBatch = 5
757	
758	// captionCut is the captions pass: every spoken line over the kept clips as a
759	// text effect, batch by batch. A batch that fails twice is skipped and said
760	// so; the cut stands either way.
761	func (a *App) captionCut(segs []cutSeg, rows []tsvRow) []cutFx {
762		var out []cutFx
763		narr := a.narratorMic()
764		system := a.sysPrompt("captions")
765		batches := (len(segs) + captionBatch - 1) / captionBatch
766		for b := 0; b*captionBatch < len(segs); b++ {
767			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
768				return out
769			}
770			lo, hi := b*captionBatch, min(len(segs), (b+1)*captionBatch)
771			batch := segs[lo:hi]
772			a.prog(trackSTT, 0.7+0.2*float64(b)/float64(batches), "captions, clips %d–%d of %d", lo+1, hi, len(segs))
773			brief := clipBriefsWith(batch, rows, nil, narr, func(i int, s cutSeg) string {
774				return fmt.Sprintf("CLIP %d: %.0f s long", lo+i+1, s.E-s.S)
775			})
776			user := a.ctxBlockFor("captions") + "THE CLIPS, AND WHAT WAS SAID OVER EACH:\n" + brief
777			msgs := []map[string]any{msg("system", system), msg("user", user)}
778			for try := 0; try < 2; try++ {
779				reply, err := a.llmChatRetryOn("captions", msgs, false, nil)
780				if err != nil {
781					a.logfIdle("!!! captions: clips %d–%d: %v", lo+1, hi, err)
782					break
783				}
784				fx, problem := captionsFromReply(batch, lo, reply)
785				if problem == "" {
786					out = append(out, fx...)
787					a.logfIdle(">>> captions: clips %d–%d: %d caption(s)", lo+1, hi, len(fx))
788					break
789				}
790				a.logfIdle(">>> captions: clips %d–%d rejected: %s", lo+1, hi, problem)
791				if try == 1 {
792					a.logfIdle("!!! captions: clips %d–%d skipped -- the cut stands without them", lo+1, hi)
793				}
794				msgs = retryTurn(msgs, reply, problem)
795			}
796		}
797		return out
798	}
799	
800	// captionsFromReply reads one batch's answer into text effects on the session
801	// clock. Clip numbers are as the brief gave them (first is number first+1);
802	// seconds are offsets from the clip's start and are held inside the clip. A
803	// clip the reply does not mention has no captions, which is an answer.
804	func captionsFromReply(batch []cutSeg, first int, reply string) ([]cutFx, string) {
805		var out struct {
806			Clips []struct {
807				I  int `json:"i"`
808				Fx []struct {
809					Start, End float64
810					Text       string
811				} `json:"fx"`
812			} `json:"clips"`
813		}
814		if p := jsonReply(reply, &out); p != "" {
815			return nil, p
816		}
817		var fx []cutFx
818		for _, c := range out.Clips {
819			k := c.I - first - 1
820			if k < 0 || k >= len(batch) {
821				return nil, fmt.Sprintf("clip %d is not one of the clips given (%d to %d)", c.I, first+1, first+len(batch))
822			}
823			seg := batch[k]
824			for _, e := range c.Fx {
825				txt := strings.TrimSpace(e.Text)
826				if txt == "" {
827					continue
828				}
829				st, en := math.Max(0, e.Start), math.Min(seg.E-seg.S, e.End)
830				if en-st < 0.3 {
831					continue // a caption nobody could read, or one entirely past the clip
832				}
833				d := en - st
834				fade := math.Min(0.3, d/4)
835				fx = append(fx, cutFx{Kind: "text", T: seg.S + st, Dur: d, Trans: fade, Tout: fade, Text: txt})
836			}
837		}
838		return fx, ""
839	}
840	
841	// decorateCut is the effects pass: zooms, stops and volume in one request over
842	// every kept clip; a failed answer leaves the cut plain. It is told the
843	// captions (CAPTION lines) and each clip's rate, since both change the answer.
844	func (a *App) decorateCut(segs []cutSeg, rows []tsvRow, done []cutFx) []cutFx {
845		if len(segs) == 0 {
846			return nil
847		}
848		if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
849			return nil
850		}
851		rate := make([]float64, len(segs))
852		for _, f := range done {
853			if f.Kind != "speed" || f.Rate <= 0 {
854				continue
855			}
856			t0, t1 := f.fxSpan()
857			for i, s := range segs {
858				if t1 > s.S && t0 < s.E {
859					rate[i] = f.Rate
860				}
861			}
862		}
863		brief := clipBriefsWith(segs, rows, done, a.narratorMic(), func(i int, s cutSeg) string {
864			h := fmt.Sprintf("CLIP %d: %.0f s long", i+1, s.E-s.S)
865			if rate[i] > 0 && rate[i] != 1 {
866				h += fmt.Sprintf(", plays at %gx", rate[i])
867			}
868			return h
869		})
870		user := a.ctxBlockFor("effects") + "THE CLIPS, AND WHAT WAS SAID AND SHOWN OVER EACH:\n" + brief
871		msgs := []map[string]any{msg("system", a.sysPrompt("effects")), msg("user", user)}
872		for try := 0; try < 2; try++ {
873			reply, err := a.llmChatRetryOn("effects", msgs, false, nil)
874			if err != nil {
875				a.logfIdle("!!! effects: %v", err)
876				return nil
877			}
878			fx, problem := decorationsFromReply(segs, reply)
879			if problem == "" {
880				a.logfIdle(">>> effects: %d decoration(s)", len(fx))
881				return fx
882			}
883			a.logfIdle(">>> effects rejected: %s", problem)
884			msgs = retryTurn(msgs, reply, problem)
885		}
886		a.logfIdle("!!! effects: no usable answer -- the cut stands without them")
887		return nil
888	}
889	
890	// decorationsFromReply reads the effects pass: each named to a clip, offsets
891	// from that clip's start, held inside it. The kinds the pass owns and no
892	// others -- a speed or a caption here is written elsewhere and is dropped.
893	func decorationsFromReply(segs []cutSeg, reply string) ([]cutFx, string) {
894		var out struct {
895			Fx []struct {
896				Clip       int
897				Kind       string
898				Start, End float64
899				Gain       *float64
900			} `json:"fx"`
901		}
902		if p := jsonReply(reply, &out); p != "" {
903			return nil, p
904		}
905		var in []sugFx
906		for _, e := range out.Fx {
907			k := e.Clip - 1
908			if k < 0 || k >= len(segs) {
909				return nil, fmt.Sprintf("clip %d is not one of the clips given (1 to %d)", e.Clip, len(segs))
910			}
911			kind := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(e.Kind))
912			if kind != "zoom" && kind != "stop" && kind != "volume" {
913				continue
914			}
915			seg := segs[k]
916			st, en := math.Max(0, e.Start), math.Min(seg.E-seg.S, e.End)
917			if en <= st {
918				continue
919			}
920			in = append(in, sugFx{Kind: kind, Start: seg.S + st, End: seg.S + en, Gain: e.Gain})
921		}
922		return fxFrom(in, 0), ""
923	}
924	
925	// ---- the speed pass ---------------------------------------------------------
926	//
927	// A rate per clip, asked once the cut and its captions stand: a rate on a
928	// captioned clip is dropped here (words at 4 are unreadable). It is handed no
929	// target -- how much to speed up is the user context's to say (speedSystem);
930	// the cut's length is the cut pass's gate (footageWindow).
931	
932	// speedCut asks for a rate per clip and returns the speed effects. A failure
933	// leaves the cut at 1 throughout, which is a longer video and a whole one.
934	func (a *App) speedCut(segs []cutSeg, caps []cutFx, rows []tsvRow) []cutFx {
935		if len(segs) == 0 {
936			return nil
937		}
938		if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
939			return nil
940		}
941		capped := make([]int, len(segs)) // how many captions each clip carries
942		for _, f := range caps {
943			for i, s := range segs {
944				if f.T >= s.S && f.T < s.E {
945					capped[i]++
946				}
947			}
948		}
949		// ...and the clip's own lines: what was said and shown, at the seconds they
950		// happened. Two counts (lines spoken, captions) could not tell a silent walk
951		// back from a silent final approach; the lines can.
952		raw := 0.0
953		for _, s := range segs {
954			raw += s.E - s.S
955		}
956		brief := clipBriefsWith(segs, rows, caps, a.narratorMic(), func(i int, s cutSeg) string {
957			h := fmt.Sprintf("CLIP %d: %.0f s long", i+1, s.E-s.S)
958			if capped[i] > 0 {
959				h += fmt.Sprintf(", %d caption(s) -- runs at 1", capped[i])
960			}
961			return h
962		})
963		user := a.ctxBlockFor("speed") + fmt.Sprintf("FOOTAGE: %.0f seconds over %d clips.\n\n"+
964			"THE CLIPS, AND WHAT WAS SAID AND SHOWN OVER EACH:\n%s", raw, len(segs), brief)
965		msgs := []map[string]any{msg("system", a.sysPrompt("speed")), msg("user", user)}
966		for try := 0; try < 2; try++ {
967			reply, err := a.llmChatRetryOn("speed", msgs, false, nil)
968			if err != nil {
969				a.logfIdle("!!! speed: %v", err)
970				return nil
971			}
972			fx, problem := speedsFromReply(segs, capped, reply)
973			if problem == "" {
974				// no length gate: "no clip runs fast" is a right answer to a cut
975				// with nothing dull in it, and the length is the cut pass's
976				a.logfIdle(">>> speed: %d clip(s) run fast — %s of video from %s of footage",
977					len(fx), mmss(cutLen(applyFx(segs, fx))), mmss(raw))
978				return fx
979			}
980			a.logfIdle(">>> speed rejected: %s", problem)
981			msgs = retryTurn(msgs, reply, problem)
982		}
983		a.logfIdle("!!! speed: no usable answer — every clip plays at 1")
984		return nil
985	}
986	
987	// speedsFromReply reads a rate per clip into speed effects over whole clips.
988	//
989	// A rate ABOVE 1 on a captioned clip is dropped: the words on it would be
990	// unreadable, and that rule is not the model's to weigh against the
991	// arithmetic. Below 1 is slow motion and is kept -- it costs the target
992	// seconds rather than saving them, which is the arithmetic's problem and is
993	// caught by the length gate, and a caption over a slowed clip is on screen
994	// longer rather than shorter.
995	//
996	// What is SAID over a clip is not enforced here, only asked for (speedSystem):
997	// the user context can ask for more speed than the silent clips can give, and
998	// the wording says what to take then.
999	func speedsFromReply(segs []cutSeg, capped []int, reply string) ([]cutFx, string) {
1000		var out struct {
1001			Speeds []struct {
1002				Clip int
1003				Rate float64
1004			} `json:"speeds"`
1005		}
1006		if p := jsonReply(reply, &out); p != "" {
1007			return nil, p
1008		}
1009		var in []sugFx
1010		for _, sp := range out.Speeds {
1011			i := sp.Clip - 1
1012			if i < 0 || i >= len(segs) {
1013				return nil, fmt.Sprintf("clip %d is not one of the clips given (1 to %d)", sp.Clip, len(segs))
1014			}
1015			if sp.Rate <= 0 || math.Abs(sp.Rate-1) < 0.01 {
1016				continue // 1 is the footage's own speed and says nothing
1017			}
1018			if sp.Rate > 1 && capped[i] > 0 {
1019				// words on screen: this clip runs at 1, whatever was asked for.
1020				// Only the fast half of the rule -- a caption over a clip in slow
1021				// motion is on screen longer, not shorter.
1022				continue
1023			}
1024			in = append(in, sugFx{Kind: "speed", Start: segs[i].S, End: segs[i].E, Rate: sp.Rate})
1025		}
1026		return joinSpeeds(fxFrom(in, 0)), ""
1027	}
1028	
1029	// seamMax is the widest hole that can be a rounding artifact rather than an
1030	// edit. The timeline is stamped in whole seconds, so the finest cut a reply can
1031	// express is one -- and "this stretch carries on" comes out as ...86], [87...
1032	// with whatever fell in that second falling out of the video.
1033	const seamMax = 1.5
1034	
1035	// joinSeams closes the holes a reply did not mean to open.
1036	//
1037	// One run asked for 21 holes. Eleven were exactly one second, and eight of
1038	// those had a WORD in them -- "new algorithms.", "deprecated.", "once,",
1039	// "that wallet", "global North" -- each of them the middle of a sentence the
1040	// cut kept both sides of. They are not edits; they are the model saying the
1041	// stretch continues in the only vocabulary it has.
1042	//
1043	// Ten of the eleven were closed anyway, by luck: both edges usually snap to the
1044	// same pause and coalesce joins what touches. The one where they did not lost
1045	// the word "once". This is that repair done on purpose, before the snapping
1046	// rather than as a side effect of it.
1047	//
1048	// A short hole with nothing but silence in it is left alone: that one may well
1049	// be a trim, and the seconds it drops are seconds nobody spoke in.
1050	func joinSeams(segs []cutSeg, rows []tsvRow) []cutSeg {
1051		if len(segs) < 2 {
1052			return segs
1053		}
1054		out := []cutSeg{segs[0]}
1055		for _, s := range segs[1:] {
1056			last := &out[len(out)-1]
1057			if s.S-last.E > 0 && s.S-last.E <= seamMax && wordsBetween(rows, last.E, s.S) {
1058				last.E = s.E
1059				continue
1060			}
1061			out = append(out, s)
1062		}
1063		return out
1064	}
1065	
1066	// wordsBetween is whether anybody was talking between two seconds of the
1067	// session -- the EVENT lines are the picture and say nothing about that.
1068	func wordsBetween(rows []tsvRow, t0, t1 float64) bool {
1069		for _, r := range rows {

3	// Filling a card in: the drawing lives in the file, the numbers come from
4	// here. Holes in the document:
5	//
6	//	{{name}}                     filled in, or nothing
7	//	{{name|what it says instead}} filled in, or that
8	//
9	// The holes are a place's contents, the fitted name size, and every
10	// animation's values and keyTimes. Everything else is in the file only.
11	
12	import (
13		"bytes"
14		"regexp"
15		"strings"
16	)
17	
18	// svgScope is what the card has to say about a document: hole name (lower case)
19	// to value. The value is escaped on the way in, so a title with an ampersand in
20	// it is a title and not a broken document.
21	type svgScope map[string]string
22	
23	// svgFillScope answers the holes the card has a value for and leaves the rest as
24	// they are, defaults and all -- those are the parameters' turn, and after them
25	// their own defaults. A place the card said nothing about is a place the file
26	// itself calls empty.
27	func svgFillScope(src []byte, vals svgScope) []byte {
28		if len(vals) == 0 {
29			return src
30		}
31		return outsideComments(src, func(b []byte) []byte {
32			return svgHole.ReplaceAllFunc(b, func(m []byte) []byte {
33				g := svgHole.FindSubmatch(m)
34				v, ok := vals[strings.ToLower(string(g[1]))]
35				if !ok {
36					return m
37				}
38				return []byte(escapeText(v))
39			})
40		})
41	}
42	
43	// A comment is not part of the picture, and neither is a hole written in one:
44	// the file explains itself in comments, and the example it uses to explain what
45	// a {{hole}} is must not turn into a box in the dialog, be quietly answered by a
46	// path, or be filled in by the card and stop explaining anything. So everything
47	// that fills a document in steps over its comments.
48	var reComment = regexp.MustCompile(`(?s)<!--.*?-->`)
49	
50	func outsideComments(src []byte, f func([]byte) []byte) []byte {
51		var out bytes.Buffer
52		pos := 0
53		for _, c := range reComment.FindAllIndex(src, -1) {
54			out.Write(f(src[pos:c[0]]))
55			out.Write(src[c[0]:c[1]])
56			pos = c[1]
57		}
58		out.Write(f(src[pos:]))
59		return out.Bytes()
60	}
61	
62	// stampArgs writes the parameters a card was drawn with back into its root
63	// element, so the finished document is the same complete statement of itself the
64	// drawn cards always were: what drew it, and what with.
65	func stampArgs(src []byte, q svgQuery) []byte {
66		return reStampArgs.ReplaceAll(src, []byte(`data-naivepost-args="`+attrEsc(q.args())+`"`))
67	}

69	var reStampArgs = regexp.MustCompile(`data-naivepost-args="[^"]*"`)

982		// it: splitSpliced opens scenes for cards and applyFx cuts them again at
983		// every rate boundary, and both copy the segment whole, so the stamp
984		// travels with the pieces (cutSeg.Scene).
985		segs := splitSpliced(c.Segs)

987			segs[i].Scene = i
988		}
989		return applyFx(segs, c.Fx)

992	// produceCut is the whole cut file the render works from: the live editor when
993	// it has one, what is saved otherwise; everything above the segment level reads
994	// it here so it cannot disagree with produceSegs. The editor counts as having a
995	// cut when it has segments, a timeline correction or a row of its own.
996	func (a *App) produceCut() cutFile {
997		if ed := a.ed; ed != nil && (len(ed.segs) > 0 || len(ed.shift) > 0 || len(ed.cutLanes) > 0) {
998			return cutFile{Segs: ed.segs, Aspect: ed.aspect, Fx: ed.fx, Shift: ed.shift,
999				Rows: ed.rows, Lanes: ed.cutLanes, NRows: ed.nRows}
1000		}
1001		b, err := os.ReadFile(a.cutPath())
1002		if err != nil {
1003			return cutFile{}
1004		}
1005		var c cutFile
1006		if json.Unmarshal(b, &c) != nil {
1007			return cutFile{}
1008		}
1009		c.Fx = migrateFx(c.Fx)
1010		return c
1011	}

1015		// the render behaves as if it were not there -- nothing spoken, nothing
1016		// laid over a clip, no subtitle track (narrate.go's own tick). Read here
1017		// rather than at each of the four places that use these entries, because
1018		// this is the one seam every one of them comes through.

1020			return nil
1021		}
1022		if a.narr != nil {
1023			a.narr.pullRows()
1024			if len(a.narr.entries) > 0 {
1025				return append([]narrEntry(nil), a.narr.entries...)
1026			}
1027		}
1028		a.narr.flushSave() // a line typed a moment ago belongs in this render
1029		b, err := os.ReadFile(a.narrPath())
1030		if err != nil {
1031			return nil
1032		}
1033		var f struct{ Entries []narrEntry }
