1040	// sessionTracks is the same placement for both kinds at once: the footage on
1041	// the timeline, and the separate recordings beside it on the same clock. The
1042	// render needs the second list for the same reason the cut page draws lanes
1043	// from it -- a recording that was running while a clip was running is part of
1044	// that clip's sound, and the only thing that says which stretch of it that is
1045	// is where both of them sit on this one clock.
1046	func (a *App) sessionTracks(vids, auds []string) ([]tlVideo, []tlAudio, error) {
1047		if len(vids) == 0 {
1048			return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("no videos selected")
1049		}
1050		type st struct {
1051			path  string
1052			start float64
1053		}
1054		// same zero convention as session.tsv: the earliest moment any source
1055		// names, and 0:00 when none of them names one (srcClock)
1056		var all []st
1057		paths := append(append([]string{}, vids...), auds...)
1058		at, zero := srcClock(paths)
1059		for _, p := range paths {
1060			all = append(all, st{p, at[p]})
1061		}
1062		var out []tlVideo
1063		for _, s := range all[:len(vids)] { // the videos are the leading entries
1064			dur, err := ffprobeDur(s.path)
1065			if err != nil {
1066				return nil, nil, err
1067			}
1068			out = append(out, tlVideo{base: baseName(s.path), path: s.path,
1069				start: s.start - zero, wall: s.start, dur: dur, fps: ffprobeFPS(s.path)})
1070		}
1071	
1072		var rec []tlAudio
1073		for _, s := range all[len(vids):] {
1074			dur, err := ffprobeDur(s.path)
1075			if err != nil || dur <= 0 {
1076				continue // not something with sound in it; the lanes skip it too
1077			}
1078			rec = append(rec, tlAudio{base: baseName(s.path), path: s.path,
1079				start: s.start - zero, dur: dur})
1080		}
1081		// the corrections the cut page made to these clocks, put on before anything
1082		// is sorted or coloured. The render places its own tracks and would
1083		// otherwise place them off the raw timestamps -- the ones the hand was
1084		// dragging to correct in the first place.
1085		c := a.produceCut()
1086		for i := range out {
1087			out[i].start += c.Shift[out[i].base]
1088		}
1089		for i := range rec {
1090			rec[i].start += c.Shift[rec[i].base]
1091		}
1092		// the further tracks of a multi-track capture, which are recordings in every
1093		// way that matters here: a lane each, on the file's own clock, mixed under
1094		// the clips they were running through. They are built from the videos AFTER
1095		// those were corrected, so a row dragged to fix its clock takes its own
1096		// second track with it, and their own name is still a name a further drag
1097		// can be stored under (slideSrc, cut_shift.go).
1098		for _, au := range srcLanes(out, a.snappedTracks()) {
1099			if au.master {
1100				continue // that one is the footage's own sound, taken off its input
1101			}
1102			au.start += c.Shift[au.base]
1103			rec = append(rec, au)
1104		}
1105		// and the rows the cut put on the band itself, which are in cut.json and in
1106		// no source list -- the render has to be told about them or every scene cut
1107		// to one would resolve to whatever recording was rolling at that second
1108		// (cut_lane.go). They are placed by laneVideos and corrected here, exactly
1109		// as the editor does it.
1110		lanes := a.laneVideos(c.Lanes, out)
1111		for i := range lanes {
1112			lanes[i].start += c.Shift[lanes[i].base]
1113		}
1114		out = append(out, lanes...)
1115		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].start < out[j].start })
1116		sort.Slice(rec, func(i, j int) bool { return rec[i].start < rec[j].start })
1117		// the rows, worked out the same way the cut page works them out, because a
1118		// scene says which ROW its picture comes from (cutSeg.Cam) and the number
1119		// has to mean the same thing on both sides. Without this every scene would
1120		// resolve against row nought and a two-camera cut would render as one.
1121		assignLanes(out, c.Rows)
1122		return out, rec, nil
1123	}

1300	//
1301	// Everything upstream that decides how long a clip will COME OUT measures
1302	// itself against this number rather than one of its own -- the speed clamp and
1303	// the ramp stairs both do -- because a floor here and a different floor there
1304	// is how footage goes missing between the timeline and the video.

1307	// blurSigma is how far the backdrop is smeared, as a fraction of the finished
1308	// frame's height. Enough that no detail survives to be read as a second
1309	// picture, not so much that a bright scene turns into one flat colour.
1310	const blurSigma = 0.02
1311	
1312	// chain is the sub-graph that lays the picture on a blurred blow-up of itself:
1313	// one split, the copy scaled to COVER the frame and blurred, the picture laid
1314	// back over it. in is the label it reads, k a number that keeps its own labels
1315	// apart from every other one in the graph; it returns the filter_complex text
1316	// and the label it wrote.
1317	func (b bdrop) chain(in string, k int) (string, string) {
1318		out := fmt.Sprintf("bd%d", k)
1319		if b.bare {
1320			// black, and one filter to say it: pad puts the picture on a bigger
1321			// frame at the corner it belongs at, and the fitted case scales it
1322			// down first because an insert brings its own shape
1323			if b.fit {
1324				return fmt.Sprintf("[%s]scale=%d:%d:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease,"+
1325					"pad=%d:%d:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=black[%s];",
1326					in, b.w, b.h, b.w, b.h, out), out
1327			}
1328			return fmt.Sprintf("[%s]pad=%d:%d:%d:%d:color=black[%s];",
1329				in, b.w, b.h, b.x, b.y, out), out
1330		}
1331		sig := math.Max(4, float64(b.h)*blurSigma)
1332		fg := fmt.Sprintf("bdf%d", k)
1333		bg := fmt.Sprintf("bdb%d", k)
1334		fc := fmt.Sprintf("[%s]split=2[%s][%s];", in, bg, fg)
1335		// increase then crop is "cover": the copy is blown up until it is at
1336		// least the frame in both directions, and the excess is cut off centred
1337		fc += fmt.Sprintf("[%s]scale=%d:%d:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,"+
1338			"crop=%d:%d,gblur=sigma=%.2f,setsar=1[%s];", bg, b.w, b.h, b.w, b.h, sig, bg)
1339		if b.fit {
1340			fc += fmt.Sprintf("[%s]scale=%d:%d:force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease[%s];",
1341				fg, b.w, b.h, fg)
1342			fc += fmt.Sprintf("[%s][%s]overlay=(W-w)/2:(H-h)/2[%s];", bg, fg, out)
1343			return fc, out
1344		}
1345		fc += fmt.Sprintf("[%s][%s]overlay=%d:%d[%s];", bg, fg, b.x, b.y, out)
1346		return fc, out
1347	}

1355	// joinMismatch is what to say about clips that will break the join: the concat

1357	// decoder comes apart on it and the video smears from there. Every branch of
1358	// encodeClip pins its size, so a mismatch means one stopped. Measured against
1359	// the FIRST clip, reported by name.
1360	func joinMismatch(made []clipSize) []string {
1361		var out []string
1362		for i, c := range made {
1363			if i == 0 || (c.w == made[0].w && c.h == made[0].h) {
1364				continue
1365			}
1366			out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf(
1367				"%s came out %d×%d where %s is %d×%d — the join is a stream copy and cannot mix sizes, so the video breaks at this clip",
1368				c.name, c.w, c.h, made[0].name, made[0].w, made[0].h))
1369		}
1370		return out

14	const cardGuide = `# Writing a card
15	
16	This folder holds *cards*: SVG files that can be dropped into a cut as an
17	insert. The footage stops, the card is on screen for a few seconds, the footage
18	carries on.
19	
20	Naivepost renders SVG itself -- no browser is involved anywhere. A card that
21	animates is evaluated and written out as one static SVG per frame, and those
22	frames are handed to ffmpeg as an image sequence. A card that does not animate
23	is one still held for the length of the insert.
24	
25	This note is the whole contract. If you are a model being asked to write a new
26	card for this folder, everything you need is below, and the files beside it are
27	worked examples of it.
28	
29	## The canvas
30	
31	    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1920" height="1080"
32	         viewBox="0 0 1920 1080">
33	
34	* Always 1920x1080. The card is scaled to the footage's frame at render time,
35	  so the numbers below are the only ones you have to think in.
36	* Draw an opaque background first -- a full-size rect, dark (#14171c is what
37	  the built-in cards use). A card replaces the picture; it does not sit over it.
38	* The file must be self-contained. Frames are written to a temporary folder and
39	  read from there, so a relative href resolves against nothing and an absolute
40	  one is refused. Put images in the document: href="data:image/png;base64,...".
41	* Fonts are the ones installed on the machine, named as a family list --
42	  "DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif". No @font-face
43	  with a URL, no webfont.
44	* Nothing can measure text before it is drawn. Err small: a heading a size too
45	  modest still reads, one that runs off the edge does not. About 0.58em of
46	  advance per character is a safe estimate for these faces.
47	
48	## Filling one in
49	
50	A card is worth more than a picture when the same file can say something
51	different every time it is used. Put placeholders in it:
52	
53	    <text ...>{{title}}</text>
54	    <text ...>{{caption|Nobody said}}</text>
55	
56	* {{name}} is empty when nobody says otherwise; {{name|words}} falls back to
57	  those words. A placeholder is never left in the picture as literal text.
58	* They work in attributes as well as in content: fill="{{colour|#ff7f7f}}".
59	* The insert carries the values on the end of its path, as a URL does:
60	  card.svg?title=Best maps&caption=Nuke. Inside a value, only % & = ? are
61	  escaped (%25 %26 %3D %3F); spaces, commas and colons are written as they are.
62	* Whatever is substituted is XML-escaped, so a title with an & in it is safe.
63	
64	## Saying what the placeholders are
65	
66	The insert dialog builds itself out of the file. By default it asks for each
67	{{name}} under its bare name and says nothing about it, which is enough for a
68	card with one hole and thin for a card with six. Declare them instead:
69	
70	    <!-- Input: title | Title | over the card, empty for none -->
71	    <!-- Input: logo[logo] | Logo | a picture file, from anywhere in the project -->
72	    <!-- Input: colour | Colour | #rrggbb -->
73	
74	The key, then what the box is called, then what it says under the box. The key
75	matches the placeholder. Everything after the second bar is the hint, bars and
76	all, so a hint may contain a bar.
77	
78	The square brackets are flags, space separated, all optional:
79	
80	    keep    the value is written out even when it is left empty
81	    logo    the box is a comma-separated list that may hold image files, and
82	            the dialog offers a file picker for it
83	
84	Declare some and the rest are still asked for -- a declaration adds words to a
85	box, it does not hide the others. The order of the comments is the order of the
86	dialog.
87	
88	A {{name}} written inside a comment is not a parameter: comments are where a
89	card explains itself, and an example in one is never asked for and never filled
90	in from a path. The one exception is the Input line itself, which is read.
91	
92	## Room for more than one thing
93	
94	A card that ranks things needs somewhere to put them, and a file cannot invent
95	places to put them in. So write the places out -- all of them, with their own
96	coordinates -- and switch off the ones nobody filled in:
97	
98	    <g display="{{s1.show|none}}">
99	      <rect x="338" y="188" width="230" height="108" rx="10" fill="#2b313b"/>
100	      <text x="453" y="282" font-size="{{s1.name.size|27}}">{{s1.name}}</text>
101	    </g>
102	
103	* display="{{...|none}}" is how an empty place stays empty: the fallback is off,
104	  and the card switches on the ones it has something for.
105	* The same trick works for anything optional -- a picture element with no
106	  picture, a caption nobody wrote.
107	* It costs nothing to read: a place nobody used is a group with display:none in
108	  it, and the file still opens as the finished card in any viewer.
109	
110	tier.svg is written exactly this way: six tiers, six places in each, all thirty
111	six written out, and one Input line per tier beside the tier it belongs to.
112	
113	## Animating it
114	
115	**Every animation begins at 0 and does its waiting inside keyTimes.** Not a
116	style rule. Before an animation begins, SVG says the static attribute stands, so
117	an element parked off-screen by a static transform is off-screen for anything
118	that does not animate -- the file manager's thumbnail, the insert chooser's
119	preview, an SVG editor, and this app's own fallback when a document turns out
120	not to bake. With the delay written into the animation, the static document is
121	the *finished* card, which is what all of those should show.
122	
123	So, a group that is invisible for the first 1.2 seconds of a 3.4 second card and
124	fades in over the next 0.4:
125	
126	    <g>
127	      <animate attributeName="opacity" dur="3.4s" fill="freeze"
128	               values="0;0;1;1" keyTimes="0;0.353;0.471;1"/>
129	      <animate attributeName="transform" type="translate" dur="3.4s" ... />
130	    </g>
131	
132	Note the shape of it: one animation per attribute, running the card's whole
133	length, with the moments as fractions of it, and fill="freeze". Every card in
134	this folder is written that way.
135	
136	What is read:
137	
138	* SMIL -- <animate>, <set>, <animateTransform> -- on numbers, number lists,
139	  lengths with units, and hex or rgb() colours. from/to/by, values with
140	  keyTimes, dur, begin, repeatCount, fill="freeze". calcMode discrete steps;
141	  paced and spline are treated as linear.
142	* CSS @keyframes in a <style> block, which is what a drawing tool exports:
143	  opacity, transform and fill; translate, scale and rotate in px and deg; one
144	  compound selector per rule (#id, .class, tag, and combinations -- no
145	  descendant selectors, no attribute selectors, no pseudo-classes); animation
146	  and its longhands; linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out and
147	  cubic-bezier() easing.
148	* An animation element must sit inside the element it animates. A begin that
149	  chains off another animation or off an event is not read.
150	
151	Anything outside that renders statically, which is the finished card, which is
152	never wrong -- only less alive than it could be.
153	
154	The card's own length is offered as the length of the insert: the last moment
155	anything is still moving. Leave about two seconds of stillness at the end, so
156	the card is read after it has arrived rather than while it is arriving.
157	
158	## The cards this app draws itself
159	
160	tier.svg and the single letters carry data-naivepost="tier" or "badge" and the
161	parameters they were drawn with. They are *drawn*, not just filled in: the app
162	works out which places on the board are used, how big a name has to be to fit,
163	which one is the thing that just arrived and when everything moves, and puts
164	those numbers into the file.
165	
166	tier.svg is the file the board is drawn FROM. The whole picture is in it -- the
167	six rows, the six places in each, every coordinate -- and the holes are only
168	what the app has to say: what is in a place, what it is called, and every
169	animation's own values and keyTimes. Restyle it and the boards drawn from it
170	come out restyled; that is what it is there for. Rename a box in one of its
171	Input comments and the dialog calls it that. The single letters are drawn flat:
172	a badge is one letter and one caption, so editing their shapes does nothing --
173	they are redrawn from the letter every time.
174	
175	To write your own card, do not copy the stamp. A document without one, with
176	{{placeholders}} in it, is filled in exactly as written and is yours.
177	
178	## A complete example
179	
180	    <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
181	    <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="1920" height="1080"
182	         viewBox="0 0 1920 1080">
183	      <!-- Input: line | Headline | the one thing this card says -->
184	      <!-- Input: sub | Under it | smaller, arrives second -->
185	      <rect width="1920" height="1080" fill="#14171c"/>
186	      <g>
187	        <animate attributeName="transform" type="translate" dur="3.2s"
188	                 fill="freeze" values="1920 0;1920 0;0 0;0 0"
189	                 keyTimes="0;0.06;0.28;1"/>
190	        <text x="960" y="520" font-family="DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif"
191	              font-size="96" font-weight="700" fill="#e6e9ef"
192	              text-anchor="middle">{{line|Chapter one}}</text>
193	      </g>
194	      <g>
195	        <animate attributeName="opacity" dur="3.2s" fill="freeze"
196	                 values="0;0;1;1" keyTimes="0;0.31;0.44;1"/>
197	        <text x="960" y="620" font-family="DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, sans-serif"
198	              font-size="48" fill="#e6e9ef" text-anchor="middle">{{sub}}</text>
199	      </g>
200	    </svg>
201	
202	## Before you call it done
203	
204	* Open it in anything that renders SVG. What you see is the card as it ends,
205	  with the places nobody has filled in yet showing what they are.
206	* No external file is referenced, and no placeholder is left visible.
207	* Everything is inside 1920x1080, including text at its longest plausible value.
208	* Every animation begins at 0, runs the same total, and freezes.
209	* The last movement ends about two seconds before the card does.
210	`
211

1100	// Diarization alone finds where somebody held the floor, which can be a laugh
1101	// and a long think. With no transcript the fallback is longest turns first.
1102	
1103	const (
1104		// refMinLen is the shortest take worth having. Under about five seconds
1105		// there is not enough of a voice in it to be one.
1106		refMinLen = 5.0
1107		// refPad is how far another speaker must stay from a take on either side.
1108		// Diarization edges are approximate, and a syllable of the wrong person
1109		// bleeding into the reference is a syllable the clone learns.
1110		refPad = 2.0
1111		// refWant is how much reference the model is given, and refTakeMax how
1112		// many pieces it may be assembled from. More than this stops helping;
1113		// fewer, longer pieces are steadier than many short ones.
1114		refWant    = 14.0
1115		refTakeMax = 3
1116		// refMinRate is how much speech a take has to hold to count as speech:
1117		// words per second. Ordinary talk runs near 2.5, so this admits somebody
1118		// speaking slowly or leaving pauses and turns away the stretch that is
1119		// mostly not talking -- including the credits ASR invents over silence,
1120		// which are a handful of words spread over a long quiet.
1121		refMinRate = 1.5
1122	)

1124	// refTake is one stretch worth cloning: the seconds it covers, and how much
1125	// was said in them.
1126	type refTake struct {
1127		s, e  float64
1128		words int
1129	}
1130	
1131	func (t refTake) dur() float64 { return t.e - t.s }
1132	
1133	// domSpeaker is whoever did most of the talking, by total time. A voice
1134	// recording is one person plus whatever the room leaked into it, so this is
1135	// the person, and everyone else is the leak.
1136	func domSpeaker(turns []span) string {
1137		by := map[string]float64{}
1138		for _, t := range turns {
1139			by[t.slot] += t.e - t.s
1140		}
1141		dom, best := "", 0.0
1142		for s, d := range by {
1143			if d > best {
1144				dom, best = s, d
1145			}
1146		}
1147		return dom
1148	}
1149	
1150	// refCuts ranks the stretches of a recording a reference should be cut from,
1151	// best first. turns is the diarization, rows the transcript of the same
1152	// recording on the same clock; rows may be empty.
1153	func refCuts(turns []span, rows []seg4) []refTake {
1154		dom := domSpeaker(turns)
1155		if dom == "" {
1156			return nil
1157		}
1158		var cand []refTake
1159		for _, t := range turns {
1160			if t.slot != dom || !soloTurn(turns, t, dom) {
1161				continue
1162			}
1163			// no length test on the turn itself: spokenIn only ever narrows it,
1164			// so the take being long enough says the turn was
1165			if c := spokenIn(t, rows); c.dur() >= refMinLen {
1166				cand = append(cand, c)
1167			}
1168		}
1169		// The takes somebody is speaking through. With no transcript none of them
1170		// qualifies and the whole set stays, ranked below by length alone -- and
1171		// the same happens for a speaker so slow that nothing clears the bar,
1172		// which is a thin reference but a better one than none.
1173		var spoke []refTake
1174		for _, c := range cand {
1175			if float64(c.words) >= refMinRate*c.dur() {
1176				spoke = append(spoke, c)
1177			}
1178		}
1179		if len(spoke) > 0 {
1180			cand = spoke
1181		}
1182		// most said first, and length breaks the tie the no-transcript case makes
1183		// of every comparison
1184		sort.SliceStable(cand, func(i, j int) bool {
1185			if cand[i].words != cand[j].words {
1186				return cand[i].words > cand[j].words
1187			}
1188			return cand[i].dur() > cand[j].dur()
1189		})

1191	}

1193	// soloTurn is whether a turn has the recording to itself, refPad included.
1194	func soloTurn(turns []span, t span, dom string) bool {
1195		for _, o := range turns {
1196			if o.slot != dom && o.e > t.s-refPad && o.s < t.e+refPad {
1197				return false
1198			}
1199		}
1200		return true
1201	}

1203	// spokenIn narrows a turn to the words inside it and counts them. A row counts
1204	// when its middle is in the turn: diarization edges are approximate, and a row
1205	// across the boundary belongs to the side holding most of it. Speakers are not
1206	// checked -- the turn is already this speaker's alone.
1207	func spokenIn(t span, rows []seg4) refTake {
1208		out := refTake{s: t.s, e: t.e}
1209		first, last := 0.0, 0.0
1210		for _, r := range rows {
1211			if mid := (r.s + r.e) / 2; mid < t.s || mid >= t.e {
1212				continue
1213			}
1214			// a row with no words in it is not the end of the speech: letting it
1215			// through would stretch the take out over the silence it stands for
1216			n := len(strings.Fields(r.text))
1217			if n == 0 {
1218				continue
1219			}

1221			// the turn or end after it, and the seconds outside are the pad
1222			if out.words == 0 {
1223				first = max(r.s, t.s)
1224			}
1225			last = min(r.e, t.e)
1226			out.words += n
1227		}
1228		if out.words > 0 {
1229			out.s, out.e = first, last
1230		}
1231		return out
1232	}

// trackLabel names one track the way the row shows it: its number, and the name
// the recorder gave it when it gave one -- OBS writes "Desktop Audio" and "Mic/
// Aux" into the container, and those are the words the person choosing is
// thinking in. The number is always there because the title is the part that
// can be missing, wrong, or the same on two tracks.
func trackLabel(n int, t audTrack) string {
	name := fmt.Sprintf("Track %d", n+1)
	if t.title != "" {
		name += " — " + t.title
	}
	if t.chans > 1 {
		return name + " (stereo)"
	}
	return name + " (mono)"
}

// trackButton is the row's control for a multi-track file: a menu holding one
// check per audio stream, and nil for the ordinary file with one, which has
// nothing to choose and would only get a button that cannot be wrong.
//
// It says how many are on over how many there are, because that is the fact a
// glance up the list is after -- which of these files is only half in the
// session -- and it is the fact the rest of the app is about to act on.
func (s *sourceList) trackButton(i int) *gtk.MenuButton {
	it := s.items[i]
	tr := s.srcTracks(it.path)
	if len(tr) < 2 {
		return nil
	}
	on := wantTracks(it.tracks, len(tr))
	box := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 2)
	margins(box, 6, 6, 6, 6)
	head := headLabel("Audio tracks in this file")
	box.Append(head)
	for n := range tr {
		n := n
		c := gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel(trackLabel(n, tr[n]))
		c.SetActive(slices.Contains(on, n))
		c.ConnectToggled(func() { s.setTrack(i, n, c.Active()) })
		box.Append(c)
	}
	why := gtk.NewLabel("Each track chosen gets a lane of its own in Cut, and is mixed\n" +
		"into the render like a separate recording. Untick one to leave it\n" +
		"out of the session entirely.")
	why.SetXAlign(0)
	why.SetMarginTop(4)
	why.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
	box.Append(why)
	pop := gtk.NewPopover()
	pop.SetChild(box)

	b := gtk.NewMenuButton()
	b.AddCSSClass("flat")
	b.SetPopover(pop)
	inner := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 2)
	inner.Append(gtk.NewImageFromIconName("media-playlist-consecutive-symbolic"))
	inner.Append(gtk.NewLabel(fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", len(on), len(tr))))
	b.SetChild(inner)
	if len(on) < len(tr) {
		b.AddCSSClass("dim-label") // some of this file is not in the session
	}
	b.SetTooltipText(fmt.Sprintf("Audio tracks — this file holds %d, and %d of them are in\n"+
		"the session. Each one is a lane of its own in Cut and is mixed like a\n"+
		"separate recording.", len(tr), len(on)))
	return b
}

1498			detail = fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s, %s", p.outFile, humanSize(fi.Size()), humanAgo(fi.ModTime()))
1499		}
1500		a.confirm("Overwrite "+filepath.Base(p.outFile)+"?",
1501			detail+"\n\nThe encode takes minutes and there is no undo for it.", "Overwrite", run)
1502	}
1503	
1504	func (a *App) produceRun(words bool) {
1505		if a.busy() {
1506			return
1507		}
1508		if a.pub == nil {
1509			return
1510		}
1511		segs := a.produceSegs()
1512		if len(segs) == 0 {
1513			a.setStatus("no cut yet — build one on the Cut step first")
1514			return
1515		}
1516		entries := a.produceEntries()
1517		st := a.prodSettings()
1518		vids, auds := a.snapSources()
1519		// the drawing half's inputs, read on this thread like everything above:
1520		// the goroutine below must not go reading widgets or the editor
1521		pst := a.pub.snapshot()
1522		aspect := a.produceCut().Aspect
1523		written := a.publishRecorded()
1524		a.saveProjectNow() // the run is a moment worth a file, whatever the ticker is doing
1525	
1526		a.startRun()
1527		// ▶ leaves an up-to-date video alone; ↻ Transcode is the press that means
1528		// "encode it anyway", so it never asks this question.
1529		encode := !words || a.renderStale(segs, entries, st, vids, auds)
1530		if !encode {
1531			a.logf(">>> the video is already what this page describes — not encoding it again " +
1532				"(↻ beside Transcode encodes anyway)")
1533		}
1534		switch {
1535		case !encode:
1536		case !words:
1537			a.logf(">>> transcoding %s: %d clips at %s/%s crf %d — the thumbnail and the upload text are left as they are",
1538				filepath.Base(st.OutFile), len(segs), st.Container, st.Codec, st.CRF)
1539		case written:
1540			a.logf(">>> producing %s: %d clips at %s/%s crf %d, and the thumbnail redrawn beside them",
1541				filepath.Base(st.OutFile), len(segs), st.Container, st.Codec, st.CRF)
1542		default:
1543			a.logf(">>> producing %s: %d clips at %s/%s crf %d, and the upload text and thumbnail written beside them",
1544				filepath.Base(st.OutFile), len(segs), st.Container, st.Codec, st.CRF)
1545		}
1546		// two halves, side by side. The render owns the fraction -- it is minutes
1547		// where the other is seconds, so the needle IS the render's progress --
1548		// and the words-and-picture half owns the second line of the bar, which
1549		// is what it has to say for itself.
1550		a.qJob(trackSTT, "render", 0, 0)
1551		a.prog(trackSTT, 0, "preparing")
1552		if words {
1553			a.qJob(trackFrames, "publish", 0, 0)
1554			a.prog(trackFrames, 0, "thinking")
1555		}
1556		a.pulseUntilCounted()
1557	
1558		go func() {
1559			// The two halves do not touch. The upload text and the thumbnail are
1560			// written from the cut and the narration and read their frames out of
1561			// inputs/; the render reads the same cut and narration and writes
1562			// produce/ and the video. Neither reads a file the other writes, and
1563			// the render never reads the publish record -- so there was nothing
1564			// for the render to wait for, and it waited anyway: a minute of an
1565			// idle encoder while a model thought about a title, and then the
1566			// thumbnail drawing on the GPU while the CPU had nothing to do.
1567			//
1568			// A failure in the words does not throw the render away any more.
1569			// They are separate deliverables, the expensive one is the video, and
1570			// an sd.cpp that is down is not a reason to spend the encode again.
1571			var wg sync.WaitGroup
1572			var pubErr error
1573			if words {
1574				wg.Add(1)
1575				go func() {
1576					defer wg.Done()
1577					pubErr = a.publishStage(trackFrames, pst, aspect, segs, entries, !written, written, false, false)
1578					a.qDone(trackFrames, 0) // its own line goes quiet; the needle was never its
1579					glib.IdleAdd(func() {
1580						if p := a.pub; p != nil {
1581							p.refresh() // whatever landed, up as soon as it is written
1582						}
1583					})
1584					if pubErr != nil && !errors.Is(pubErr, errStopped) {
1585						a.logfIdle("!!! the upload text and thumbnail failed: %v -- the render carries on", pubErr)
1586					}
1587				}()
1588			}
1589			var err error
1590			if encode {
1591				if err = a.produce(segs, entries, st, vids, auds); err == nil {
1592					a.markRendered(segs, entries, st, vids, auds)
1593				}
1594			}
1595			wg.Wait()
1596			// Both halves are in, so the deliverables can be described: the
1597			// <video> tag, with the poster the words half just drew and the .vtt
1598			// tracks the render half just wrote (produce_embed.go). Here and not
1599			// at the end of either half -- the tag needs both, and it is rewritten
1600			// even on a press that skipped the encode, because the files beside
1601			// the video are then the ones the render before left.
1602			a.writeEmbed(st.OutFile, st.Codec)
1603			// the render's word is the run's: it is what the press was for, and a
1604			// title that did not get written is a line in the log, not a failure
1605			// to show for a video that rendered
1606			if err == nil && pubErr != nil {
1607				err = pubErr
1608			}
1609			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
1610				a.endRun()
1611				a.updateGates()
1612				if err != nil {
1613					if !errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
1614						a.logf("produce FAILED: %v", err)
1615					}
1616					if errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
1617						a.setStatus("production stopped")
1618					} else {
1619						a.setStatus("production failed — see log")
1620					}
1621					return
1622				}
1623				a.progress.SetFraction(1)
1624				a.setStatus("done")
1625				// the bar carries the outcome; filled in below, once the file has
1626				// been measured
1627				dur, _ := ffprobeDur(st.OutFile)
1628				fi, _ := os.Stat(st.OutFile)
1629				size := int64(0)
1630				if fi != nil {
1631					size = fi.Size()
1632				}
1633				a.logf(">>> %s  (%.1f s, %s)", st.OutFile, dur, humanSize(size))
1634				a.progress.SetText(fmt.Sprintf("produced %s — %.1f s, %s",
1635					filepath.Base(st.OutFile), dur, humanSize(size)))
1636				a.updateProduceInfo()
1637			})
1638		}()
1639	}
1640	
1641	func (a *App) produce(segs []cutSeg, entries []narrEntry, st prodSettings, srcVid, srcAud []string) error {
1642		vids, recs, err := a.sessionTracks(srcVid, srcAud)
1643		if err != nil {
1644			return err
1645		}
1646		dir := a.produceDir()
1647		clipDir := filepath.Join(dir, "clips")
1648		if err := os.RemoveAll(clipDir); err != nil {
1649			return err
1650		}
1651		if err := os.MkdirAll(clipDir, 0o755); err != nil {
1652			return err
1653		}
1654	
1655		// 1. speak whatever is still missing, so a render never silently drops a line
1656		// -- unless nothing is ever spoken: captions only renders every line as a
1657		// caption with no wav, which the planning below already knows how to lay out
1658		var todo []narrEntry
1659		if !a.captionsOnly() {
1660			for _, e := range entries {
1661				if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) != "" && !exists(a.ttsWav(e)) {
1662					todo = append(todo, e)
1663				}
1664			}
1665		} else if len(entries) > 0 && st.Subs == "none" {
1666			a.logfIdle(">>> captions only and nothing in the video — the lines are in the .srt beside it")
1667		}
1668		if len(todo) > 0 {
1669			// a render that has to speak first is two jobs, and the bar says so;
1670			// when everything is already spoken there is only ever the one
1671			a.qJob(trackSTT, "speaking", 1, 2)
1672			a.qPush(trackSTT, len(todo), "line")
1673		}
1674		for i, e := range todo {
1675			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
1676				return err
1677			}
1678			a.qTake(trackSTT)
1679			a.prog(trackSTT, 0.2*float64(i)/float64(len(todo)), "")
1680			if err := a.synthesize(e); err != nil {
1681				return fmt.Errorf("synthesis for %.0fs: %w", e.S, err)
1682			}
1683		}
1684		base := 0.0
1685		if len(todo) > 0 {
1686			base = 0.2
1687			a.qJob(trackSTT, "render", 2, 2)
1688			a.prog(trackSTT, base, "planning the clips")
1689		}
1690	
1691		// 2. plan every clip: which recording, how long, which voice file, and
1692		// which lanes the scene was told not to hear (cutSeg.Quiet, cut_hear.go)
1693		var clips []prodClip
1694		for i, s := range segs {
1695			var c prodClip
1696			switch {
1697			case s.isCopy():
1698				// a copied stretch: not a file to stretch into a slot but footage
1699				// to cut from its recording, exactly as the segment it was copied
1700				// from would be cut
1701				from, _ := copySrc(s.Ins)
1702				v := pickVideoOn(vids, s.Cam, from)
1703				if v == nil {
1704					a.logfIdle("clip %d copies footage at %.0f s that falls in no recording — skipped", i+1, from)
1705					continue
1706				}
1707				c = copyClip(i, s, from, v)
1708				if end := v.start + v.dur; from+c.length > end {
1709					c.length = end - from
1710					a.logfIdle("clip %d copies past the end of %s — shortened to %.1f s", i+1, v.base, c.length)
1711				}
1712			case s.audioIns():
1713				// sound alone: the picture is the session's own -- held on one
1714				// frame when the file is spliced in, kept running when it covers a
1715				// selection -- and the file replaces the session's sound for the
1716				// slot (encodeClip routes snd where the capture's sound was)
1717				file, _ := insSplit(s.Ins)
1718				path := a.loadPath(file)
1719				if !exists(path) {
1720					a.logfIdle("clip %d: %s is not there any more — skipped", i+1, file)
1721					continue
1722				}
1723				v := pickVideoOn(vids, s.Cam, s.S)
1724				if v == nil {
1725					a.logfIdle("clip %d at %.0f s falls in no recording — its sound has no picture, skipped", i+1, s.S)
1726					continue
1727				}
1728				c = sndClip(i, s, path, v, recs)
1729				if end := v.start + v.dur; !c.freeze && s.E > end {
1730					c.length = end - s.S
1731					a.logfIdle("clip %d runs past the end of %s — shortened to %.1f s", i+1, v.base, c.length)
1732				}
1733			case s.isInsert():
1734				// an insert is its own picture, so there is nothing to look up and
1735				// nothing to run past the end of: the slot is exactly as long as the
1736				// cut says, and assetClip stretches or trims the file to fill it
1737				// the file is resolved and the card's parameters ride along with it:
1738				// what is on disk is a picture the parameters are applied TO, and
1739				// only the part before the "?" is a path at all
1740				file, q := insSplit(s.Ins)
1741				path := a.loadPath(file)
1742				if !exists(path) {
1743					a.logfIdle("clip %d: %s is not there any more — skipped", i+1, file)
1744					continue
1745				}
1746				var note string
1747				c, note = insClip(i, s, path+q.suffix(), vids)
1748				if note != "" {
1749					a.logfIdle("clip %d %s", i+1, note)
1750				}
1751			default:
1752				v := pickVideoOn(vids, s.Cam, s.S)
1753				if v == nil {
1754					a.logfIdle("clip %d at %.0f s falls in no recording — skipped", i+1, s.S)
1755					continue
1756				}
1757				c = prodClip{idx: i, video: v, local: v.at(s.S), tempo: 1, rate: 1,
1758					length: s.length()}
1759				if s.Rate > 0 {
1760					c.rate = s.Rate
1761				}
1762				// the clamp is in session seconds -- what the recording has left --
1763				// and the slot in output seconds, which under slow motion is longer
1764				if end := v.start + v.dur; s.E > end {
1765					c.length = (end - s.S) / c.speed()
1766					a.logfIdle("clip %d runs past the end of %s — shortened to %.1f s", i+1, v.base, c.length)
1767				}
1768			}
1769			if c.length < minClipLn {
1770				// under half a second there is nothing to encode, but a piece
1771				// vanishing out of the middle of the cut in silence reads as a
1772				// render bug. It is nearly always an effect boundary landing just
1773				// short of a cut, which is a thing the hand can move.
1774				a.logfIdle("clip %d at %s is %.2f s — too short to render, dropped%s",
1775					i+1, mmss(s.S), c.length, spokenHere(entries, s))
1776				continue
1777			}
1778			c.sessS = s.S
1779			c.scene = s.Scene // which scene of the cut this piece is part of
1780			c.quiet = s.Quiet // every clip kind, so one scene answers one way
1781			if from, ok := copySrc(s.Ins); ok {
1782				// its text cues are the copied footage's, not the paste point's:
1783				// a name plate over the original belongs over the copy too
1784				c.sessS = from
1785			}
1786			matched := matchEntries(entries, s)
1787			for _, e := range matched {
1788				text := strings.TrimSpace(e.Text)
1789				if text == "" {
1790					continue
1791				}
1792				// at is an offset into the clip the line was WRITTEN against, and
1793				// matchEntries deliberately accepts a clip that has moved since --
1794				// so it has to be re-based onto the clip actually being rendered. A
1795				// border dragged 20 s to the left and the line kept its old offset,
1796				// which is 20 s early: near the head of the clip, over whatever the
1797				// line before it was saying. Identical arithmetic to Narrate's
1798				// refit, and a no-op for a clip that has not moved.
1799				at := (e.S + e.At - s.S) / c.speed() // under slow motion the moment lands later in the clip
1800				ln := prodLine{text: text, pos: e.Pos,
1801					at: math.Min(math.Max(0, at), math.Max(0, c.length-1))}
1802				ln.delay = math.Max(narrLead, ln.at)
1803				wav := a.ttsWav(*e)
1804				if !exists(wav) {
1805					if !a.captionsOnly() { // with no voice chosen, this is every line
1806						a.logfIdle("clip %d: no synthesis for a line — it is captioned only", i+1)
1807					}
1808				} else {
1809					ln.wav = wav
1810					ln.dur, _ = ffprobeDur(wav)
1811				}
1812				c.lines = append(c.lines, ln)
1813			}
1814			if len(c.lines) == 0 && len(entries) > 0 && len(matched) == 0 && s.E > s.S {
1815				a.logfIdle("clip %d at %.0f s has no narration entry — it keeps its own audio", i+1, s.S)
1816			}
1817			// make the lines fit where the writer put them: each starts no earlier
1818			// than the one before it ended, the slot grows first (the placement
1819			// survives whole -- a sign-off at the end stays at the end), then the
1820			// schedule slides earlier as one piece, and only as the last resort
1821			// are the lines distorted
1822			if len(c.lines) > 0 {
1823				pack := func() float64 { return narrRun(c.lines, c.tempo) }
1824				need := pack()
1825				if need > c.length {
1826					c.length += math.Min(need-c.length, maxExtend)
1827					// footage runs out; an insert does not -- a still or a loop is
1828					// as long as the slot asks for
1829					if v := c.video; v != nil {
1830						if end := v.start + v.dur; s.S+c.length*c.speed() > end {
1831							c.length = (end - s.S) / c.speed()
1832						}
1833					}
1834				}
1835				if over := need - c.length; over > 0 {
1836					shift := math.Min(over, c.lines[0].delay-narrLead)
1837					for k := range c.lines {
1838						c.lines[k].delay -= shift
1839					}
1840					need -= shift
1841					a.logfIdle("clip %d: the narration does not fit where it was placed — moved %.1f s earlier",
1842						i+1, shift)
1843				}
1844				if need > c.length {
1845					var talk float64
1846					for _, ln := range c.lines {
1847						talk += ln.dur
1848					}
1849					avail := c.length - narrLead - 0.2 - 0.3*float64(len(c.lines)-1)
1850					c.tempo = math.Min(talk/math.Max(0.1, avail), maxTempo)
1851					// repack with the sped-up lines, then slide once more: the
1852					// placements are re-derived from at, so the schedule is the
1853					// writer's shape at the new speed
1854					need = pack()
1855					if over := need - c.length; over > 0 {
1856						shift := math.Min(over, c.lines[0].delay-narrLead)
1857						for k := range c.lines {
1858							c.lines[k].delay -= shift
1859						}
1860					}
1861					a.logfIdle("clip %d: narration %.1f s does not fit %.1f s — sped up %.2fx",
1862						i+1, talk, c.length, c.tempo)
1863				}
1864			}
1865			clips = append(clips, c)
1866		}
1867		if len(clips) == 0 {
1868			return fmt.Errorf("no clip could be placed on a recording")
1869		}
1870		// what the sound does, before the recordings are placed: a clip whose
1871		// sound has come away from the picture hears the lanes from the same
1872		// second the capture is read from, and clipMixes below asks it
1873		// (laneOverlap). After the lengths are settled, because the sound
1874		// advances by however long the clip is on SCREEN -- a slot grown for its
1875		// narration is more seconds of sound too.
1876		audioPlan(clips, a.produceCut().Fx)
1877		// the separate recordings, now that every clip's length is settled: growing
1878		// a slot for its narration lengthens what was heard under it too
1879		for i := range clips {
1880			clips[i].mix = clipMixes(clips[i], recs)
1881		}
1882		if len(recs) > 0 {
1883			for _, line := range laneReport(clips, recs) {
1884				a.logfIdle("%s", line)
1885			}
1886		}
1887		// every insert is fitted into the size the footage comes out at, which can
1888		// only be known once it is settled which recordings are in (clipBox) --
1889		// and when the cut names an aspect, that size is the aspect's own frame
1890		// instead, for footage and inserts alike (outBox)
1891		cf := a.produceCut()
1892		fx, aspect := cf.Fx, cf.Aspect
1893		boxW, boxH := outBox(clips, st, aspect)
1894		if boxW > 0 {
1895			// on every clip, not only the inserts that are fitted into it: a text
1896			// overlay is drawn at the finished frame's size too, and it has to be
1897			// the same size for footage as for a card or the words land elsewhere
1898			for i := range clips {
1899				clips[i].boxW, clips[i].boxH = boxW, boxH
1900			}
1901		}
1902		// the camera: with an aspect, a view or a zoom in play, every footage clip
1903		// is taken through fxRectAt -- the same function the preview overlay draws
1904		// -- sampled at every moment anything starts or stops moving (buildCam)
1905		if fxHasCamera(aspect, fx) && boxW > 0 {
1906			camFps := st.FPS
1907			if camFps <= 0 {
1908				camFps = 30
1909			}
1910			for i := range clips {
1911				c := &clips[i]
1912				if c.video == nil {
1913					continue
1914				}
1915				sw, sh, err := ffprobeSize(c.video.path)
1916				if err != nil {
1917					return fmt.Errorf("%s: the camera needs the source frame size: %w", c.video.base, err)
1918				}
1919				span := c.length * c.speed()
1920				if c.freeze {
1921					span = 0 // a freeze is one session moment, not a stretch of it
1922				}
1923				c.cam = buildCam(fx, aspect, sw, sh, c.video.sessionAt(c.local), span,
1924					c.speed(), c.length, boxW, boxH, camFps)
1925				if c.cam != nil && c.cam.maxZoom() > 10 {
1926					a.logfIdle("clip %d: the zoom goes deeper than ffmpeg's 10× — it is rendered at 10×", i+1)
1927				}
1928			}
1929		}
1930	
1931		// the words: the same session-to-clip mapping the camera just used, so a
1932		// title and a camera move placed at the same second happen at the same
1933		// second in the render. An insert or a freeze is one session moment held
1934		// for a while (span 0), exactly as buildCam treats it.
1935		if boxW > 0 {
1936			for i := range clips {
1937				c := &clips[i]
1938				span := c.length * c.speed()
1939				if c.freeze || c.ins != "" {
1940					span = 0
1941				}
1942				c.texts = textCues(fx, c.sessS, span, c.speed(), c.length)
1943			}
1944		}
1945	
1946		// the volume effects: the same mapping a third time, and outside the boxW
1947		// guard above because a gain needs no frame size -- a clip with no picture
1948		// to put a title on still has sound to turn up.
1949		for i := range clips {
1950			c := &clips[i]
1951			span := c.length * c.speed()
1952			if c.freeze || c.ins != "" {
1953				span = 0
1954			}
1955			c.gains = gainCues(fx, c.sessS, span, c.speed(), c.length)
1956		}
1957	
1958		// the seconds nothing is heard over: a speed effect whose sound is Silent,
1959		// at any rate. Mapped exactly as the volume effects above are, and for the
1960		// same reason -- a stop and a ×1 leave the segment list alone, so their
1961		// bands lie inside a clip rather than being one.
1962		for i := range clips {
1963			c := &clips[i]
1964			span := c.length * c.speed()
1965			if c.freeze || c.ins != "" {
1966				span = 0
1967			}
1968			c.hushes = hushCues(fx, c.sessS, span, c.speed(), c.length)
1969		}
1970	
1971		// the stop effects: the same mapping once more, but the overlay is a frame
1972		// of a recording rather than a drawn card, resolved here where the
1973		// recordings are known -- a stop's bar can hang into a clip cut from a
1974		// different recording than the one its frame is in
1975		for i := range clips {
1976			c := &clips[i]
1977			if c.video == nil || c.ins != "" || c.freeze {
1978				continue // no footage runs under a card or a held frame
1979			}
1980			for _, cue := range freezeCues(fx, c.sessS, c.length*c.speed(), c.speed(), c.length) {
1981				// the scene's own camera (cutVideoOn), not whichever recording
1982				// happened to be rolling: on a session shot on two cameras,

3	// The audio.cpp server: one endpoint for listening (ASR, diarization) and
4	// speaking (TTS). Paths in requests are the SERVER's -- it runs in a container
5	// -- so files go up via serverFile first. A model id names family, task,
6	// weights and session options (config-audiocpp.json), never per-request flags.
7	
8	import (
9		"bytes"
10		"context"
11		"encoding/json"
12		"fmt"
13		"io"
14		"net/http"
15		"os"
16		"path/filepath"
17		"sort"
18		"strings"
19		"time"
20	)
21	
22	// audioURL is where an audio.cpp server is expected. AUDIOCPP_SERVER is
23	// audio.cpp's own variable -- the WebUI reads it to talk to an already-running
24	// server instead of managing one -- so setting it once points both frontends at
25	// the same server. NAIVEPOST_TTS_URL overrides it when only naivepost should move.
26	// The settings dialog wins over the environment: it is the one of the two a
27	// user can see and clear, and a stale export in the launching shell should not
28	// quietly outrank what the dialog says.
29	func (a *App) audioURL() string {
30		if u := a.configuredAudio(); u != "" {
31			return u
32		}
33		return fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d", ttsPort)
34	}
35	
36	// configuredAudio is the server the user pointed us at, from the settings file
37	// or the environment; "" means the compose default on the loopback port.
38	func (a *App) configuredAudio() string {
39		if u := serverURL(a.readConf().TTS); u != "" {
40			return u
41		}
42		for _, k := range []string{"NAIVEPOST_TTS_URL", "AUDIOCPP_SERVER"} {
43			if u := serverURL(os.Getenv(k)); u != "" {
44				return u
45			}
46		}
47		return ""
48	}
49	
50	// bearer puts an API key on a request, and a blank key nowhere. It is the only
51	// place this header is built -- the audio server, the LLM and both Settings
52	// probes all come through here -- because the rule is easy to forget one client
53	// at a time: the local stack has no auth, and sending "Bearer " with nothing
54	// after it is a header that means nothing at best and a 401 from a strict proxy
55	// at worst. An empty key is "this server wants none", not "the key is empty".
56	func bearer(req *http.Request, key string) {
57		if k := strings.TrimSpace(key); k != "" {
58			req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+k)
59		}
60	}
61	
62	// serverFile uploads a local file (POST /v1/ui/upload) and returns the
63	// server-side path every request must name: the server only sees its own
64	// container. Uploaded every time -- a remembered path dies with a restart.
65	func (a *App) serverFile(path string) (string, error) {
66		// before the file, not after: this is now the first request of any job, so
67		// "nothing is listening" has to be answered here or it arrives as a bare
68		// dial error from a POST nobody was expecting to be the first one
69		if err := a.ensureAudioServer(); err != nil {
70			return "", err
71		}
72		f, err := os.Open(path)
73		if err != nil {
74			return "", err
75		}
76		defer f.Close()
77		fi, err := f.Stat()
78		if err != nil {
79			return "", err
80		}
81		ctx := a.runCtx
82		if ctx == nil {
83			ctx = context.Background()
84		}
85		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST", a.audioURL()+"/v1/ui/upload", f)
86		if err != nil {
87			return "", err
88		}
89		// the body is the file itself, not a form. Setting the length keeps Go from
90		// chunking it, which the server's own HTTP parser does not read.
91		req.ContentLength = fi.Size()
92		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/octet-stream")
93		req.Header.Set("X-Audiocpp-Filename", filepath.Base(path))
94		bearer(req, a.readConf().TTSKey)
95		resp, err := (&http.Client{}).Do(req)
96		if err != nil {
97			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
98				return "", errStopped
99			}
100			return "", err
101		}
102		defer resp.Body.Close()
103		out, _ := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
104		if resp.StatusCode == 403 {
105			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s will not take uploads, so it can only read files it "+
106				"already has: start it with --ui-management (cpp/docker-compose.yml, the "+
107				"audio service's command), or mount %s into the container at that same path",
108				a.audioURL(), filepath.Dir(path))
109		}
110		if resp.StatusCode != 200 {
111			return "", fmt.Errorf("uploading %s to %s answered %s: %.400s",
112				filepath.Base(path), a.audioURL(), resp.Status, strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
113		}
114		var got struct {
115			Path string `json:"path"`
116		}
117		if err := json.Unmarshal(out, &got); err != nil || got.Path == "" {
118			return "", fmt.Errorf("%s took %s but did not say where it put it: %.200s",
119				a.audioURL(), filepath.Base(path), strings.TrimSpace(string(out)))
120		}
121		return got.Path, nil
122	}
123	
124	// ensureAudioServer checks that something is listening, and says so when
125	// nothing is. Naivepost never starts a server: one GPU, started by whoever owns
126	// the stack. The compose "audio" service runs audiocpp_server and points the
127	// WebUI at it, so bringing that up is what makes narration -- and now the
128	// transcripts -- work.
129	func (a *App) ensureAudioServer() error {
130		url := a.audioURL()
131		req, err := http.NewRequest("GET", url+"/health", nil)
132		if err != nil {
133			return err
134		}
135		bearer(req, a.readConf().TTSKey)
136		r, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
137		if err != nil {
138			return fmt.Errorf("no audio.cpp server answering at %s -- start it "+
139				"(in the stack's compose folder: docker compose up -d audio), or point "+
140				"Settings at where one runs", url)
141		}
142		r.Body.Close()
143		if a.audioNoted != url {
144			a.audioNoted, a.ttsModel = url, "" // a different server, a different catalog
145			a.logfIdle(">>> using the audio.cpp server on %s", url)
146		}
147		return nil
148	}
149	
150	// audioModel is one entry of the server's catalog: the id we ask for, and what
151	// it turns out to be.
152	type audioModel struct {
153		ID     string `json:"id"`
154		Family string `json:"family"`
155		Task   string `json:"task"`
156	}
157	
158	// audioCatalog is what the server serves right now, by id.
159	func audioCatalog(url, key string) (map[string]audioModel, error) {
160		req, err := http.NewRequest("GET", strings.TrimRight(url, "/")+"/v1/models", nil)
161		if err != nil {
162			return nil, err
163		}
164		bearer(req, key)
165		r, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
166		if err != nil {
167			return nil, err
168		}
169		defer r.Body.Close()
170		var out struct {
171			Data []audioModel `json:"data"`
172		}
173		if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&out); err != nil {
174			return nil, fmt.Errorf("model list from %s: %w", url, err)
175		}
176		got := map[string]audioModel{}
177		for _, m := range out.Data {
178			got[m.ID] = m
179		}
180		return got, nil
181	}

183	// sortedKeys is a map read in an order that does not change between runs --
184	// for an error message that must not reshuffle itself, and for a config file
185	// that must not (rememberedBody).
186	func sortedKeys[V any](m map[string]V) []string {
187		ids := make([]string, 0, len(m))
188		for id := range m {
189			ids = append(ids, id)
190		}
191		sort.Strings(ids)
192		return ids
193	}
194	
195	// catalogIDs names the catalog for an error message: what a server offers is
196	// half of why the model you asked for is not there.
197	func catalogIDs(cat map[string]audioModel) string {
198		if len(cat) == 0 {
199			return "nothing"
200		}
201		return strings.Join(sortedKeys(cat), ", ")
202	}

204	// freeAudioModels asks the audio server to let go of everything it is holding.

208	// resident afterwards -- gigabytes of a shared GPU held for work that finished
209	// -- and the next thing that needs room competes with models nobody is going

212	//
213	// Quiet on purpose, and it never starts a server to say this. A run that used

215	// holding nothing: both are the same silence.
216	func (a *App) freeAudioModels() {
217		req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", a.audioURL()+"/v1/tasks/unload_all_models", nil)
218		if err != nil {

231	// audioRun posts one job and hands back the answer verbatim. Verbatim matters:

238	func (a *App) audioRun(model string, req map[string]any) ([]byte, error) {

28		// thread: every state change here happens either on it or on the bus watch,

34		// is nowhere at all: a wav the decoder refused looked exactly like a wav
35		// playing silently, and the transport button sat there claiming ⏸. Also on
