49		// when the last flushing seek-for-a-rate went out (SetRateNow)
50		rateSeekAt time.Time
51		// the sink's own paintable, kept so that a picture put over the video (an
52		// insert; see ShowStill) can be taken away again
53		video   gdk.Paintabler
54		still   bool
55		loaded  string // file currently cued, so a caller can seek instead of reload
56		playing bool
57		// the separate recordings heard under this file, each its own pipeline
58		// (SetMix). Empty for every player but the cut editor's.
59		mix []*auxAudio
60		// the session's sound is off: the picture is not the session's. Set while a
61		// card is on the preview, where hearing the footage carry on underneath is
62		// how an insert ends up sounding exactly like the overwrite it is not.
63		muted bool
64		// the lanes the scene under the playhead does not hear (Hush): hushOwn for
65		// the footage's own sound, and a name for each recording mixed under it.
66		// Separate from muted because they answer different questions -- muted is
67		// "none of this is the session", hush is "this much of the session" -- and
68		// a scene can silence the camera while still hearing the microphone.
69		hushOwn bool
70		hush    map[string]bool
71		// what was last written to each pipeline's mute property, so the ten calls
72		// a second this is asked from settle into nothing when nothing changed
73		ownMute bool
74		// an inserted video's own sound, its own pipeline for the same reason the
75		// recordings have theirs. Empty unless a video insert is on screen.
76		card     *auxAudio
77		cardFile string
78		// the stream ran to its end and is sitting on its last frame. Resuming
79		// there plays nothing, so ▶ starts the same segment over instead.
80		ended               bool
81		lastStart, lastStop float64
82		// pending segment, applied once the new uri has prerolled
83		pendStart, pendStop int64 // nanoseconds; pendStart < 0 = nothing pending
84		pendPlay            bool  // false = preroll only, show the first frame paused
85		// a second pipeline prerolled at wherever the line is about to be put
86		// next, so a cut is a swap and not a reload (Preload, player_spare.go).
87		// Built on the first Preload, so a player that never jumps -- Narrate's,
88		// the voice sample's -- never carries one.
89		spare *spare
90		// the clock the stream runs on: 1 is the footage's own, and a cut with
91		// speed effects in it moves this as the line crosses them (SetRate). Every
92		// seek in this file carries it, the separate recordings' seeks included,
93		// or the sound would walk away from the picture at the first slow stretch.
94		rate float64
95		// the rate the master pipeline is ACTUALLY running at, which is whatever
96		// the last seek carried. A rate set while paused does not reach the
97		// pipeline until something seeks, and ▶ on its own does not seek -- so
98		// resuming has to notice the two have drifted apart and put that right.
99		seekRate float64
100		// the volume effects' say over this pipeline: the gain the cut asks for at
101		// the second under the playhead (fxGainAt), 1 where no volume effect
102		// covers it. Kept per player because it is a property of what that player
103		// is showing, unlike previewVol below, which is a property of the room.
104		// The two are multiplied together at every write (applyVol).
105		fxGain float64
106	}
107	
108	func NewPlayer() (*Player, error) {
109		gst.Init()
110	
111		pb, gain, paintable, err := videoPipe("main")
112		if err != nil {
113			return nil, err
114		}
115	
116		pic := gtk.NewPicture()
117		pic.SetPaintable(paintable)
118		pic.SetContentFit(gtk.ContentFitContain)
119	
120		p := &Player{pb: pb, gain: gain, Picture: pic, video: paintable, pendStart: -1, pendStop: -1,
121			rate: 1, seekRate: 1, fxGain: 1}
122		// born at the volume the sliders say, like every pipeline in the app --
123		// and on the roll it visits when one of them moves
124		p.applyVol()
125		allPlayers = append(allPlayers, p)
126		p.watch(pb)
127		return p, nil
128	}
129	
130	// videoPipe builds one video pipeline: playbin3 into a gtk4paintablesink,
131	// with the app's own volume element in its audio path. Its paintable is what
132	// a GtkPicture shows. Built twice per player that jumps -- the one playing
133	// and the spare prerolling the next cut -- and once for every other.
134	func videoPipe(name string) (pb, gain gst.Element, paintable gdk.Paintabler, err error) {
135		pb = gst.ElementFactoryMake("playbin3", name)
136		if pb == nil {
137			return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("playbin3 not available (gst-plugins-base)")
138		}
139		sink := gst.ElementFactoryMake("gtk4paintablesink", name+"sink")
140		if sink == nil {
141			return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("gtk4paintablesink not available (pacman -S gst-plugin-gtk4)")
142		}
143		pb.SetObjectProperty("video-sink", sink)
144	
145		pv := sink.ObjectProperty("paintable")
146		gobj, ok := pv.(gobject.Object)
147		if !ok {
148			return nil, nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("paintable property is %T, expected a gobject.Object", pv)
149		}
150		// ToGlibNone hands out the pointer without a transfer; Take refs it into
151		// gotk4's world, so both wrappers legitimately co-own the C object.
152		paintable = &gdk.Paintable{Object: coreglib.Take(gobject.UnsafeObjectToGlibNone(gobj))}
153	
154		filter, gain := audioFilter(name)
155		pb.SetObjectProperty("audio-filter", filter)
156		resetStreamVolume(pb)
157		return pb, gain, paintable, nil
158	}
159	
160	// watch puts the bus watch on one of this player's video pipelines. The
161	// signal watch dispatches on the default main context, i.e. the GTK loop.
162	// One handler for both pipelines, because which of them is the one playing
163	// changes at every swap (PlaySegment): the message is read for whichever
164	// role its pipeline has NOW.
165	func (p *Player) watch(pb gst.Element) {
166		bus := pb.GetBus()
167		bus.AddSignalWatch()
168		bus.ConnectMessage(func(_ gst.Bus, msg *gst.Message) {
169			if p.pb == pb {
170				p.mainMsg(msg)
171			} else if s := p.spare; s != nil && s.pb == pb {
172				s.msg(msg)
173			}
174		})
175	}
176	
177	// mainMsg is the playing pipeline's bus.
178	func (p *Player) mainMsg(msg *gst.Message) {
179		switch msg.Type() {
180		case gst.MessageAsyncDone:
181			if p.pendStart >= 0 {
182				start, stop := p.pendStart, p.pendStop
183				p.pendStart, p.pendStop = -1, -1
184				p.seekRate = p.rate
185				if stop > 0 {
186					p.pb.Seek(p.rate, gst.FormatTime,
187						gst.SeekFlagFlush|gst.SeekFlagAccurate,
188						gst.SeekTypeSet, start, gst.SeekTypeSet, stop)
189				} else {
190					p.pb.Seek(p.rate, gst.FormatTime,
191						gst.SeekFlagFlush|gst.SeekFlagAccurate,
192						gst.SeekTypeSet, start, gst.SeekTypeNone, 0)
193				}
194				if p.pendPlay {
195					p.pb.SetState(gst.StatePlaying)
196					p.setPlaying(true)
197				}
198			}
199		case gst.MessageEOS:
200			// freeze on the last frame instead of tearing the stream down
201			p.pb.SetState(gst.StatePaused)
202			p.ended = true
203			p.setPlaying(false)
204		case gst.MessageError:
205			errMsg, _ := msg.ParseError()
206			// the pipeline is done for; say so, and stop drawing ⏸ over a
207			// stream that has stopped
208			p.setPlaying(false)
209			if p.OnError != nil {
210				p.OnError(fmt.Sprint(errMsg))
211				return
212			}
213			fmt.Println("gst error:", errMsg)
214		}
215	}
216	
217	// audioFilter is every pipeline's audio path: scaletempo (a rate other than 1
218	// without a pitch change, as atempo does in the render) then a volume element
219	// of our own. Gain and mute go on that element, not on playbin's properties:
220	// those are the sound server's per-application stream volume, which it
221	// REMEMBERS -- one 0 written there muted every later stream across restarts.
222	// A missing plugin degrades the preview rather than killing it.
223	func audioFilter(name string) (filter, gain gst.Element) {
224		gain = gst.ElementFactoryMake("volume", name+"gain")
225		tempo := gst.ElementFactoryMake("scaletempo", name+"tempo")
226		bin, ok := gst.NewBin(name + "afilter").(gst.Bin)
227		if !ok || gain == nil {
228			return tempo, nil
229		}
230		var first, last gst.Element
231		if tempo != nil {
232			bin.Add(tempo)
233			bin.Add(gain)
234			tempo.Link(gain)
235			first, last = tempo, gain
236		} else {
237			bin.Add(gain)
238			first, last = gain, gain
239		}
240		sink := gst.NewGhostPad("sink", first.GetStaticPad("sink"))
241		src := gst.NewGhostPad("src", last.GetStaticPad("src"))
242		sink.SetActive(true)
243		src.SetActive(true)
244		bin.AddPad(sink)
245		bin.AddPad(src)
246		return bin, gain
247	}
248	
249	// resetStreamVolume is the one write to playbin's own volume and mute, made
250	// once when the pipeline is built: full and unmuted, which the sound server
251	// stores in place of whatever it had remembered for this app (audioFilter).
252	func resetStreamVolume(pb gst.Element) {
253		pb.SetObjectProperty("volume", 1.0)
254		pb.SetObjectProperty("mute", false)
255	}
256	
257	// setGain writes a gain, or a mute, onto our own volume element -- or, on a
258	// machine with no volume plugin, onto playbin's, which is the old behaviour
259	// and the old fault, kept over silence.
260	func setGain(gain, pb gst.Element, vol float64, mute bool) {
261		el := gain
262		if el == nil {
263			el = pb
264		}
265		el.SetObjectProperty("volume", vol)
266		el.SetObjectProperty("mute", mute)
267	}
268	
269	// fileURI is how a path is handed to playbin, and it is not "file://"+path --
270	// which is what this was, and what a file could be lost behind. A path is
271	// bytes; a uri is text with punctuation, and the two disagree about '#'.
272	// Everything after a '#' in a uri is a fragment, dropped before the file is
273	// ever opened, so a voice sample named for hand-picked takes
274	// (own@-0.5#3a1f2b_9c2b1e4d.wav) reached filesrc as ".../own@-0.5" and failed
275	// with "No such file" -- a name the app itself had written. '?' would cut the
276	// same way and a '%' in a name would be read as an escape of whatever came
277	// after it.
278	//
279	// So every byte outside the unreserved set is percent-escaped, which GStreamer
280	// undoes on the way back to a filename. '/' is the exception: it is the one
281	// piece of punctuation that means the same thing on both sides.
282	func fileURI(path string) string {
283		var b strings.Builder
284		b.WriteString("file://")
285		for i := 0; i < len(path); i++ {
286			switch c := path[i]; {
287			case c >= 'a' && c <= 'z', c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z', c >= '0' && c <= '9',
288				c == '-', c == '_', c == '.', c == '~', c == '/':
289				b.WriteByte(c)
290			default:
291				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%%%02X", c)
292			}
293		}
294		return b.String()
295	}
296	
297	// PlaySegment cues [start, stop) seconds of file; stop < 0 means to the end.
298	// play=false prerolls only: the first frame shows, paused, until Toggle.
299	func (p *Player) PlaySegment(file string, start, stop float64, play bool) {
300		if p.swapIn(file, start, stop, play) {
301			return // the spare had it prerolled: no reload, and no wait
302		}
303		p.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
304		p.pb.SetObjectProperty("uri", fileURI(file))
305		p.loaded = file
306		p.pendStart = int64(start * 1e9)
307		p.pendStop = -1
308		if stop > 0 {
309			p.pendStop = int64(stop * 1e9)
310		}
311		p.pendPlay = play
312		p.ended = false
313		p.lastStart, p.lastStop = start, stop
314		// preroll paused; the bus watch seeks (and maybe plays) on AsyncDone
315		p.pb.SetState(gst.StatePaused)
316		p.setPlaying(false)
317		for _, a := range p.mix {
318			a.cue(start, play, p.rate, p.stopFor(a))
319		}
320	}
321	
322	// ---- a picture in front of the video ----------------------------------------
323	
324	// ShowStill puts a picture where the video was -- the card an insert plays --
325	// without touching the stream underneath, which the timeline scrolls against
326	// and the clock is read from. The swap is the paintable, not a widget over the
327	// picture.
328	func (p *Player) ShowStill(tex gdk.Paintabler) {
329		if tex == nil {
330			return
331		}
332		p.Picture.SetPaintable(tex)
333		p.still = true
334	}
335	
336	// ShowVideo takes that picture away again. Cheap to call on every tick: it is
337	// the playhead leaving an insert that has to reach it, and the playhead does not
338	// know when that was.
339	func (p *Player) ShowVideo() {
340		if !p.still {
341			return
342		}
343		p.Picture.SetPaintable(p.video)
344		p.still = false
345	}
346	
347	// ---- the separate recordings ------------------------------------------------
348	
349	// What the cut plays is the session at that moment, not the file with the
350	// pictures: each separate recording is its own audio-only pipeline, seeked to
351	// its own second of the same instant and driven by the same transport. A
352	// monitor mix; the render does its own arithmetic (clipMixes).
353	type auxAudio struct {
354		pb   gst.Element
355		gain gst.Element // our volume element inside pb's audio path (audioFilter)
356		// the lane's name, which is how a scene names the lanes it does not hear
357		// (cutSeg.Quiet). Empty for a card's own sound, which no scene silences.
358		base string
359		// the file's seconds this lane covers: a recording is its whole file, a
360		// cut lane is a window into one (tlAudio.off), and a further track of the
361		// capture is the capture's own span. A seek outside [lo, hi] is silence,
362		// not the wrong minute played quietly under the picture.
363		lo, hi float64
364		// the scene under the playhead does not hear this lane. Not merely
365		// turned down: a hushed lane is never cued, never seeked and never set
366		// to PLAYING (audible), so there is no sample of it to be heard early.
367		// See applyMute.
368		mute bool
369		// what to add to a time in the master's file to get the same instant in
370		// this one: (master's session start) - (this recording's session start).
371		delta float64
372		pend  int64 // nanoseconds; < 0 = nothing pending
373		play  bool
374		// live is a pipeline that has prerolled and not been sent below PAUSED
375		// since: one that can be seeked in place. A lane in READY or NULL has to
376		// preroll first and seek when that lands (cue, landed).
377		live bool
378		// stopAt is the second of this file the running seek stops at -- the end
379		// of the scene under the line, in this lane's clock (Player.until) -- or
380		// 0 for no stop. The stop is GStreamer's, sample-accurate, which is what
381		// a timer-driven hush could never be: the lane fell silent up to a tick
382		// after the boundary, and a tick is a tenth of a second of the next
383		// scene's sound.
384		stopAt float64
385		// the master's rate, copied here at every seek: this pipeline's deferred
386		// seek fires from a bus callback that has no player to ask
387		rate float64
388	}
389	
390	// mixTrack is one recording to be heard under the footage, as the cut editor
391	// knows it: where the file is, and how the two clocks differ.
392	type mixTrack struct {
393		base  string
394		path  string
395		delta float64
396		// the window of the file this lane is: the seconds of it between lo and
397		// hi are what session time maps onto (tlAudio.off, tlAudio.dur)
398		lo, hi float64
399		// which audio stream of the file, a:N. Above nought this lane is a further
400		// track of a multi-track capture, sharing its path with the footage that
401		// is already playing -- and is the one kind of lane the preview used to
402		// leave out entirely, which is what a badge lit green over silence was.
403		track int
404	}
405	
406	// SetMix replaces the recordings heard under whatever this player shows. The
407	// pipelines are rebuilt rather than reused: the set changes when the session's
408	// sources do, which is rare, and a stale uri playing under the wrong footage is
409	// the one failure that would be hard to notice.
410	func (p *Player) SetMix(tracks []mixTrack) {
411		for _, a := range p.mix {
412			a.pb.SetState(gst.StateNull)
413		}
414		p.mix = nil
415		var names []string
416		for i, t := range tracks {
417			a := newAux(fmt.Sprintf("mix%d", i), t, p.vol(), p.laneErr(t.base))
418			if a == nil {
419				// one lane GStreamer would not build is one lane, not the rest of
420				// the mix and not the hush below it
421				p.say("!!! preview: could not build a pipeline for " + t.base)
422				continue
423			}
424			p.mix = append(p.mix, a)
425			names = append(names, t.base)
426			p.say(fmt.Sprintf(">>> preview: lane %s is file seconds %.1f-%.1f, master second + %.1f, track %d",
427				t.base, t.lo, t.hi, t.delta, t.track))
428		}
429		// said once per file, because a lane that is missing from this line is
430		// the answer to "why can I not hear it" and there is no other way to see
431		// which recordings the preview is mixing
432		if len(names) > 0 {
433			p.say(">>> preview: mixing " + strings.Join(names, ", ") + " under the footage")
434		}
435		// after the loop, so a lane the scene already silences is born silent
436		// rather than saying its first ten milliseconds out loud
437		p.applyMute()
438	}
439	
440	// say puts a line in the app's log, when there is one to put it in. The
441	// player is built before the window is, so the hook is optional.
442	func (p *Player) say(s string) {
443		if p.OnLog != nil {
444			p.OnLog(s)
445		}
446	}
447	
448	// laneErr is what a mix lane's pipeline does with an error: name the lane and
449	// say it. A lane whose file will not decode, or whose sink cannot open the
450	// device a second time, used to fail without a word -- indistinguishable, on
451	// the page, from a lane that was playing.
452	func (p *Player) laneErr(base string) func(string) {
453		return func(m string) { p.say("!!! preview: " + base + " will not play — " + m) }
454	}
455	
456	// newAux builds one audio-only pipeline for a file and the bus watch that does
457	// its seeking. nil when GStreamer will not give us a playbin, which is the one
458	// failure a caller can do nothing about.
459	func newAux(name string, t mixTrack, vol float64, onErr func(string)) *auxAudio {
460		// playbin, not playbin3: a lane may be the second track of the capture,
461		// and playbin's current-audio is the one property that picks a track by
462		// number. playbin3 selects streams by id, which is a query and a callback
463		// for what is one integer here. With no video sink of its own it would put
464		// up a window; a fake one is how "audio only" is spelled without flags.
465		pb := gst.ElementFactoryMake("playbin", name)
466		if pb == nil {
467			return nil
468		}
469		if fake := gst.ElementFactoryMake("fakesink", name+"novideo"); fake != nil {
470			pb.SetObjectProperty("video-sink", fake)
471		}
472		pb.SetObjectProperty("uri", fileURI(t.path))
473		if t.track > 0 {
474			pb.SetObjectProperty("current-audio", t.track)
475		}
476		filter, gain := audioFilter(name)
477		pb.SetObjectProperty("audio-filter", filter)
478		resetStreamVolume(pb)
479		a := &auxAudio{pb: pb, gain: gain, base: t.base, delta: t.delta, lo: t.lo, hi: t.hi, pend: -1, rate: 1}
480		// born at the loudness its player is already running at, which is the
481		// slider and any volume effect under the playhead together (Player.vol)
482		setGain(a.gain, pb, vol, false)
483		bus := pb.GetBus()
484		bus.AddSignalWatch()
485		bus.ConnectMessage(func(_ gst.Bus, msg *gst.Message) {
486			switch msg.Type() {
487			case gst.MessageError:
488				e, _ := msg.ParseError()
489				a.pend, a.live = -1, false
490				if onErr != nil {
491					onErr(fmt.Sprint(e))
492				}
493			case gst.MessageAsyncDone:
494				a.landed()
495			}
496		})
497		return a
498	}
499	
500	// landed is the deferred seek: the preroll a cue asked for has finished, so
501	// the lane can be put at its second and, if the transport is running and the
502	// scene hears it, let go. From the bus after an AsyncDone, and from cue itself
503	// when the state change was not asynchronous at all -- a pipeline already in
504	// PAUSED answers a request for PAUSED at once and posts no AsyncDone, and a
505	// cue that waited for one there waited forever, with the lane standing silent
506	// at its old second under a picture that had moved on.
507	func (a *auxAudio) landed() {
508		if a.pend < 0 {
509			return
510		}
511		at := a.pend
512		a.pend, a.live = -1, true
513		a.seekTo(float64(at) / 1e9)
514		// the hush may have landed while this preroll was in flight, and
515		// this callback is the one thing that would start the lane after it
516		if a.play && !a.mute {
517			a.pb.SetState(gst.StatePlaying)
518		}
519	}
520	
521	// The preview's loudness, one number for the whole app. Package state rather
522	// than a Player field because it is how loud the ROOM is, and the room does
523	// not change when a tab does -- there is a slider on the run bar and one
524	// beside each transport that can play video (volumeCtl), and all of them are
525	// hands on this one number. 1 is the footage as recorded; playbin treats it as
526	// a plain linear gain.
527	var previewVol = 1.0
528	
529	// every player ever built, so a volume set on any of the sliders reaches
530	// pipelines that already exist. Players are made once per page at startup and
531	// never torn down, so the roll only ever holds those few.
532	var allPlayers []*Player
533	
534	// SetPreviewVolume turns the whole preview up or down: every player, and inside
535	// each one the footage, the separate recordings mixed under it and an insert's
536	// own sound alike. One gain for all of them, because the slider's promise is
537	// "quieter", not "rebalanced".
538	func SetPreviewVolume(v float64) {
539		previewVol = math.Max(0, math.Min(1, v))
540		for _, p := range allPlayers {
541			p.applyVol()
542		}
543	}
544	
545	// every volume slider on screen. There is one wherever a video can be played
546	// -- the run bar, the Cut transport, the Narrate transport -- and they are
547	// hands on the one number, so a slider pulled down on Cut has to be found
548	// pulled down on Narrate. Otherwise the second page would show 100% while
549	// playing at 40, which is a control lying about the state it is in.
550	var volScales []*gtk.Scale
551	
552	// volSyncing is up while one slider is writing the others, so their own
553	// value-changed handlers know not to write back. GtkAdjustment stays quiet
554	// when the value does not actually change, so the loop would end anyway; the
555	// flag is here because "would end anyway" is a thing to have to work out, and
556	// the rounding through 0..100 and back is exactly where it would stop being
557	// true.
558	var volSyncing bool
559	
560	// formSlider is what a slider with a number on it looks like everywhere: its
561	// own width, its value beside the trough (above, GTK's default, makes the row
562	// a line and a half tall), centred in its row.
563	func formSlider(sc *gtk.Scale, tip string) {
564		sc.SetDrawValue(true)
565		sc.SetValuePos(gtk.PosRight)
566		sc.SetSizeRequest(150, -1)
567		sc.SetHAlign(gtk.AlignStart)
568		sc.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
569		sc.SetTooltipText(tip)
570	}
571	
572	// volumeCtl is the preview volume control: a speaker and a slider, built fresh
573	// for each place a video can be played from. Built rather than shared because
574	// a GTK widget has one parent, and the alternative to one per transport is
575	// re-parenting it on every tab switch.
576	func volumeCtl() *gtk.Box {
577		icon := gtk.NewImageFromIconName("audio-volume-high-symbolic")
578		sc := gtk.NewScaleWithRange(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 0, 100, 1)
579		sc.SetValue(previewVol * 100)
580		sc.SetSizeRequest(120, -1)
581		tip := "preview volume — the players only; nothing that is rendered, and the " +
582			"same setting wherever it is shown"
583		icon.SetTooltipText(tip)
584		sc.SetTooltipText(tip)
585		sc.ConnectValueChanged(func() {
586			if volSyncing {
587				return
588			}
589			SetPreviewVolume(sc.Value() / 100)
590			volSyncing = true
591			for _, o := range volScales {
592				if o != sc {
593					o.SetValue(previewVol * 100)
594				}
595			}
596			volSyncing = false
597		})
598		volScales = append(volScales, sc)
599		box := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 4)
600		box.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
601		box.Append(icon)
602		box.Append(sc)
603		return box
604	}
605	
606	// SetFxGain is the volume effect under the playhead, which the preview obeys
607	// as it obeys a speed effect's rate. Multiplied with the slider, so turning
608	// the preview down still turns a boosted stretch down. Nothing is written when
609	// the gain has not moved -- this runs ten times a second.
610	func (p *Player) SetFxGain(g float64) {
611		g = math.Max(0, math.Min(fxMaxGain, g))
612		if math.Abs(p.fxGain-g) < 1e-6 {
613			return
614		}
615		p.fxGain = g
616		p.applyVol()
617	}
618	
619	// vol is the one loudness every pipeline this player owns runs at: the room's
620	// setting (previewVol) and the cut's own say over the seconds under the
621	// playhead (fxGain), multiplied and held to what the property will take. One
622	// function, because a pipeline built later must start at the same number the
623	// ones built earlier are already at.
624	func (p *Player) vol() float64 {
625		return math.Max(0, math.Min(fxMaxGain, previewVol*p.fxGain))
626	}
627	
628	// applyVol writes the two gains, multiplied, onto every pipeline this player
629	// owns -- the footage, the separate recordings heard under it, and an insert's
630	// own sound. playbin's volume runs to 10, which is exactly as far as a volume
631	// effect goes (fxMaxGain), so a boosted stretch played at the slider's full
632	// travel still lands inside what the property will take.
633	func (p *Player) applyVol() {
634		v := p.vol()
635		if (v == 0) != p.volZero {
636			p.volZero = v == 0
637			if p.volZero {
638				p.say(fmt.Sprintf(">>> preview: silent -- the slider is at %.2f and the volume effect under the line at %.2f", previewVol, p.fxGain))
639			} else {
640				p.say(">>> preview: sound is back")
641			}
642		}
643		setGain(p.gain, p.pb, v, p.ownMute)
644		for _, a := range p.mix {
645			setGain(a.gain, a.pb, v, a.mute)
646		}
647		if p.card != nil {
648			setGain(p.card.gain, p.card.pb, v, false)
649		}
650	}
651	
652	// SetMuted cuts the session's sound -- footage and every recording under it --
653	// without stopping anything; the clock runs on. The preview's half of an
654	// insert: the render never puts session audio under a card (clipMixes).
655	func (p *Player) SetMuted(v bool) {
656		p.muted = v
657		p.applyMute()
658	}
659	
660	// Hush silences what the scene under the playhead does not hear (cutSeg.Quiet):
661	// only mute properties move, never the pipelines, since the answer changes
662	// every tick. until is the master-file second the answer expires at (0 =
663	// never); a lane started under it is seeked with a stop there (stopFor) so it
664	// falls silent on the boundary, and the tick re-places it (applyMute).
665	func (p *Player) Hush(own bool, quiet []string, until float64) {
666		p.hushOwn, p.hush, p.until = own, hushSet(quiet), until
667		p.applyMute()
668	}
669	
670	// stopFor is where a lane's running seek stops, in the lane's own clock, or
671	// 0 for no stop.
672	func (p *Player) stopFor(a *auxAudio) float64 {
673		if p.until <= 0 {
674			return 0
675		}
676		return p.until + a.delta
677	}
678	
679	// hushSet turns the scene's list into what the pipelines are checked against.
680	// nil for a scene that hears everything, which is most of them: the absence of
681	// the map IS that answer, so the common case costs nothing and a scene that
682	// stops silencing a lane cannot leave the old set standing behind it.
683	func hushSet(quiet []string) map[string]bool {
684		if len(quiet) == 0 {
685			return nil
686		}
687		m := make(map[string]bool, len(quiet))
688		for _, q := range quiet {
689			m[q] = true
690		}
691		return m
692	}
693	
694	// hushes is the whole decision about one pipeline's sound, split out from the
695	// writing of it so it can be asked directly -- the pipelines are GStreamer and
696	// stay out of a unit test. own marks the footage's own sound, which is a lane
697	// the scene can silence like any other and is not one of p.mix.
698	func (p *Player) hushes(base string, own bool) bool {
699		if p.muted {
700			return true // not the session's picture at all, so none of its sound
701		}
702		if own {
703			return p.hushOwn
704		}
705		return p.hush[base]
706	}
707	
708	// applyMute writes that answer onto every pipeline, and only where it changed:
709	// this runs from the playback tick, and a property written ten times a second
710	// with the value it already holds is ten notifications a second for nothing.
711	//
712	// The footage's own sound is the video's pipeline and cannot be stopped -- the
713	// picture comes out of it -- so for that one the answer is the mute property.
714	// A separate recording is its own pipeline with nothing but sound in it, and
715	// there the answer is to stop it: muting it still starts it, and a pipeline
716	// that is started can be heard for the moment between the first buffer and the
717	// mute reaching the sink, which is exactly the "I can hear the lane I switched
718	// off, briefly" this exists to prevent. The property is written too, so the
719	// sound stops at once rather than when the state change lands.
720	func (p *Player) applyMute() {
721		if m := p.hushes("", true); m != p.ownMute {
722			p.ownMute = m
723			setGain(p.gain, p.pb, p.vol(), m)
724			switch {
725			case !m:
726				p.say(">>> preview: the footage's own sound is heard again")
727			case p.muted:
728				p.say(">>> preview: the footage's own sound is muted -- a card or a stop stands over the picture")
729			default:
730				p.say(">>> preview: the footage's own sound is muted -- the scene under the line does not hear it")
731			}
732		}
733		// the master's second, asked once and only when a lane needs it -- a
734		// player with no pipeline (a test's) is never asked
735		pos, havePos, asked := 0.0, false, false
736		where := func() (float64, bool) {
737			if !asked {
738				asked = true
739				if p.pb != nil {
740					pos, havePos = p.Position()
741				}
742			}
743			return pos, havePos
744		}
745		for _, a := range p.mix {
746			m := p.hushes(a.base, false)
747			if m == a.mute {
748				// a lane whose running seek has reached its stop stands silent at the
749				// boundary; once the scene under the line has moved on and still hears it,
750				// it is placed again with the next stop. Not before: a seek whose stop is
751				// already behind it has no stop, and the lane would bleed past the boundary.
752				if !m && a.live && a.stopAt > 0 && p.stopFor(a) > a.stopAt {
753					if pos, ok := where(); ok && pos+a.delta >= a.stopAt-0.05 {
754						p.place(a, pos, p.playing)
755					}
756				}
757				continue
758			}
759			a.mute = m
760			setGain(a.gain, a.pb, p.vol(), m)
761			if m {
762				p.say(">>> preview: " + a.base + " silent -- the scene under the line does not hear it")
763			} else {
764				p.say(">>> preview: " + a.base + " heard again")
765			}
766			if m {
767				// READY, not PAUSED: a paused lane still holds a stream at the
768				// sound server, corked, and sits in the system mixer as a second
769				// "naivepost-gui" at whatever level -- which is a thing to wonder
770				// about. A lane nobody hears has no stream.
771				a.pend, a.live = -1, false
772				a.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
773				continue
774			}
775			// heard again: it has been sitting still wherever it was stopped, so
776			// it is put back on the master's clock before it is let go
777			if pos, ok := where(); ok {
778				p.place(a, pos, p.playing)
779			}
780		}
781	}
782	
783	// CardSound plays an inserted video's own audio, at seconds into it; an empty
784	// file takes it away. Its own pipeline, unmuted by SetMuted: it is the
785	// insert's sound, not the session's. A card with no audio track plays nothing.
786	func (p *Player) CardSound(file string, at float64, play bool) {
787		if file != p.cardFile {
788			p.dropCard()
789			if file == "" {
790				return
791			}
792			a := newAux("cardsound", mixTrack{path: file}, p.vol(), p.laneErr("the card's sound"))
793			if a == nil {
794				return
795			}
796			p.card, p.cardFile = a, file
797		}
798		if p.card == nil {
799			return
800		}
801		p.card.cue(at, play, p.rate, 0)
802	}
803	
804	// dropCard tears the insert's audio pipeline down. Not merely paused: the next
805	// card is a different file, and a uri cannot be changed under a live pipeline.
806	func (p *Player) dropCard() {
807		if p.card != nil {
808			p.card.pb.SetState(gst.StateNull)
809		}
810		p.card, p.cardFile = nil, ""
811	}
812	
813	// cue puts this recording at the master's time t and either holds it there or
814	// lets it run. A time this recording was not running at is silence, and silence
815	// is a pipeline taken to READY -- no stream at all -- rather than one seeked to
816	// its own edge, which would play the wrong minute quietly under the picture.
817	//
818	// stop is the second of this file to stop at, or 0 (Player.stopFor).
819	//
820	// A lane that is live -- prerolled, in PAUSED or PLAYING -- is seeked in
821	// place and set going: no state change on the way, because a PLAYING lane
822	// asked for PAUSED answers asynchronously and needs a fresh buffer to
823	// preroll on before it says so, and the seek that waited for that came late
824	// or not at all -- scene 3 played silent until a badge was pressed twice. A
825	// lane below PAUSED has no choice: it prerolls, and seeks when that lands.
826	func (a *auxAudio) cue(t float64, play bool, rate float64, stop float64) {
827		at := t + a.delta
828		a.rate = rate // the deferred seek fires with no player in reach
829		if !a.audible(t) {
830			a.pend, a.live = -1, false
831			a.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
832			return
833		}
834		a.play, a.stopAt = play, stop
835		if a.live {
836			a.pend = -1
837			a.seekTo(at)
838			if play {
839				a.pb.SetState(gst.StatePlaying)
840			} else {
841				a.pb.SetState(gst.StatePaused)
842			}
843			return
844		}
845		a.pend = int64(at * 1e9)
846		// a synchronous answer is a pipeline that was already there: no bus
847		// message is coming, so the seek is made now (see landed)
848		if a.pb.SetState(gst.StatePaused) == gst.StateChangeSuccess {
849			a.landed()
850		}
851	}
852	
853	// seekTo is the lane's flushing seek to its own second, with the stop the
854	// scene asked for when there is one ahead of it.
855	func (a *auxAudio) seekTo(at float64) {
856		if a.stopAt > at {
857			a.pb.Seek(a.rate, gst.FormatTime, gst.SeekFlagFlush|gst.SeekFlagAccurate,
858				gst.SeekTypeSet, int64(at*1e9), gst.SeekTypeSet, int64(a.stopAt*1e9))
859			return
860		}
861		a.pb.Seek(a.rate, gst.FormatTime, gst.SeekFlagFlush|gst.SeekFlagAccurate,
862			gst.SeekTypeSet, int64(at*1e9), gst.SeekTypeNone, 0)
863	}
864	
865	// running says whether this one has something to play at the master's time t,
866	// which is what keeps a resume from starting a recording that had already
867	// stopped when this second happened.
868	func (a *auxAudio) running(t float64) bool {
869		at := t + a.delta
870		return at >= a.lo && (a.hi <= a.lo || at <= a.hi)
871	}
872	
873	// audible is whether this lane is to be running at all: it has something at
874	// this second AND the scene under the playhead hears it. Every path that
875	// starts a recording asks this one question, because "silenced" has to mean
876	// the same thing as "nothing recorded here" -- a pipeline that is not started
877	// cannot be heard for the moment before the mute lands.
878	func (a *auxAudio) audible(t float64) bool {
879		return !a.mute && a.running(t)
880	}
881	
882	// setPlaying records the state and tells whoever is drawing a transport button
883	// that it changed. Nothing else may write p.playing.
884	func (p *Player) setPlaying(v bool) {
885		if p.playing == v {
886			return
887		}
888		p.playing = v
889		if p.OnState != nil {
890			p.OnState()
891		}
892	}
893	
894	// Playing reports whether the stream is running right now; Cued reports that
895	// something is loaded and paused, i.e. that ▶ should resume it rather than
896	// start whatever the page does when idle.
897	func (p *Player) Playing() bool { return p.playing }
898	func (p *Player) Cued() bool    { return p.loaded != "" && !p.playing }
899	
900	// Loaded is whether this player has been pointed at a file at all, playing or
901	// not. The question an overlay asks before it draws anything on the picture:
902	// there is no framing to show over a player that has never been given footage.
903	func (p *Player) Loaded() bool { return p.loaded != "" }
904	
905	// Toggle is what every play button in the app does: pause what is running,
906	// resume what is paused -- and, on a stream that has run to its end, play it
907	// again from the top. Resuming at the last frame is silence and a still
908	// picture, i.e. a play button that looks broken.
909	func (p *Player) Toggle() {
910		switch {
911		case p.playing:
912			p.pb.SetState(gst.StatePaused)
913			p.syncMix(false)
914			p.cardState(gst.StatePaused)
915			p.setPlaying(false)
916		case p.ended && p.loaded != "":
917			p.PlaySegment(p.loaded, p.lastStart, p.lastStop, true)
918		default:
919			// a rate chosen while paused has not reached the pipeline yet, and
920			// syncMix below is about to seek the recordings at it: without this
921			// the picture would run at the old clock and the sound at the new one
922			if math.Abs(p.rate-p.seekRate) > 1e-6 {
923				if pos, ok := p.Position(); ok {
924					p.SeekTo(pos)
925				}
926			}
927			p.pb.SetState(gst.StatePlaying)
928			p.syncMix(true)
929			// an insert's sound stops and starts with the transport like everything
930			// else on the page; where it is in the card is where it was left
931			p.cardState(gst.StatePlaying)
932			p.setPlaying(true)
933		}
934	}
935	
936	// syncMix puts every recording back on the master's clock. It is called on
937	// every transport change rather than only on the first one: two pipelines
938	// started a minute apart agree to the millisecond and then drift as slowly as
939	// their clocks differ, and a resync that costs a seek nobody hears is cheaper
940	// than reasoning about how long that takes to be audible.
941	func (p *Player) syncMix(play bool) {
942		if len(p.mix) == 0 {
943			return
944		}
945		pos, ok := p.Position()
946		if !ok {
947			return
948		}
949		for _, a := range p.mix {
950			p.place(a, pos, play)
951		}
952	}
953	
954	// place puts one recording at the master's time t and lets it run or holds it.
955	// The one place a mix pipeline is started, so it knows that a lane with nothing
956	// to play and a lane the scene does not hear are the same thing (audible):
957	// READY. Through cue, not a bare seek: a hushed lane is in READY with no
958	// stream (applyMute), and a seek on that is a start from the file's first
959	// second.
960	func (p *Player) place(a *auxAudio, t float64, play bool) {
961		if !a.audible(t) {
962			a.pend, a.live = -1, false
963			a.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
964			if !a.mute {
965				p.say(fmt.Sprintf(">>> preview: %s has nothing at the master's second %.1f (its file second %.1f is outside %.1f-%.1f)",
966					a.base, t, t+a.delta, a.lo, a.hi))
967			}
968			return
969		}
970		if play {
971			p.say(fmt.Sprintf(">>> preview: %s playing from its second %.1f", a.base, t+a.delta))
972		}
973		a.cue(t, play, p.rate, p.stopFor(a))
974	}
975	
976	// Stop tears the stream down and forgets the file, so the next ▶ is a fresh
977	// start rather than a resume of something the user already ended.
978	func (p *Player) Stop() {
979		p.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
980		for _, a := range p.mix {
981			a.pend, a.live = -1, false
982			a.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
983		}
984		p.loaded = ""
985		p.ended = false
986		p.dropSpare() // ⏹ is a fresh start for the next ▶, and that includes what was prerolled for it
987		p.dropCard()
988		p.SetMuted(false) // whatever was covering the sound is over with the stream
989		p.setPlaying(false)
990	}
991	
992	func (p *Player) Pause() {
993		p.pb.SetState(gst.StatePaused)
994		for _, a := range p.mix {
995			a.pb.SetState(gst.StatePaused)
996		}
997		p.cardState(gst.StatePaused)
998		p.setPlaying(false)
999	}
1000	
1001	// cardState moves the insert's audio pipeline, if there is one, and is silence
1002	// about it when there is not.
1003	func (p *Player) cardState(s gst.State) {
1004		if p.card != nil {
1005			p.card.pb.SetState(s)
1006		}
1007	}
1008	
1009	// SeekTo jumps within the currently loaded file; while paused the new frame
1010	// still renders, which is what frame-stepping relies on.
1011	func (p *Player) SeekTo(t float64) {
1012		p.ended = false // wherever we land, there is stream ahead of it again
1013		p.seekRate = p.rate
1014		p.pb.Seek(p.rate, gst.FormatTime,
1015			gst.SeekFlagFlush|gst.SeekFlagAccurate,
1016			gst.SeekTypeSet, int64(t*1e9), gst.SeekTypeNone, 0)
1017		// the recordings land on the same instant, told in their own seconds --
1018		// asking the master where it is would ask before this seek has taken
1019		for _, a := range p.mix {
1020			p.place(a, t, p.playing)
1021		}
1022	}
1023	
1024	// Rate is the clock the picture is actually running on -- the last seek's, not
1025	// one asked for and not yet taken hold.
1026	func (p *Player) Rate() float64 {
1027		if p.seekRate <= 0 {
1028			return 1
1029		}
1030		return p.seekRate
1031	}
1032	
1033	// SetRate stores the clock the stream is to run on and says whether that is a
1034	// change. It does NOT seek: a rate only takes effect at a seek and every caller
1035	// is about to make one. Changing the rate mid-playback is the editor's job
1036	// (syncPlayRate).
1037	func (p *Player) SetRate(r float64) bool {
1038		if r <= 0 || math.IsNaN(r) || math.IsInf(r, 0) {
1039			r = 1
1040		}
1041		if math.Abs(r-p.rate) < 1e-6 {
1042			return false
1043		}
1044		p.rate = r
1045		return true
1046	}
1047	
1048	// SetRateNow changes the rate under a running preview with a flushing seek to
1049	// the current position -- a small stumble. INSTANT_RATE_CHANGE does not return
1050	// on this stack (playbin3, scaletempo, gtk4paintablesink). Held to one seek
1051	// per rateSeekGap; inside the gap the rate is put back so the next tick asks
1052	// again.
1053	func (p *Player) SetRateNow(r float64) {
1054		was := p.rate
1055		if !p.SetRate(r) {
1056			return
1057		}
1058		if !p.playing {
1059			return // parked: whatever seek starts the stream again carries it
1060		}
1061		if time.Since(p.rateSeekAt) < rateSeekGap {
1062			p.rate = was
1063			return
1064		}
1065		p.rateSeekAt = time.Now()
1066		if pos, ok := p.Position(); ok {
1067			p.SeekTo(pos)
1068		}
1069	}
1070	
1071	// rateSeekGap is the least time between two flushing seeks made only to
1072	// change the rate under a running preview.
1073	const rateSeekGap = 250 * time.Millisecond
1074	
1075	// Position reports the current playback position in seconds.
1076	func (p *Player) Position() (float64, bool) {
1077		ns, ok := p.pb.QueryPosition(gst.FormatTime)
1078		if !ok || ns < 0 {
1079			return 0, false
1080		}
1081		return float64(ns) / 1e9, true
1082	}
1083	
1084	// videoFrame is the box a preview sits in, and all three pages that show video
1085	// use it so they cannot drift apart.
1086	//
1087	// gtk.NewFrame("") is a frame WITH a label: the empty string still builds a
1088	// GtkLabel, and an empty label is a whole line of text high. Measured, not
1089	// guessed -- 640x361 frame, child allocated at y=26 with a height of 333 and
1090	// the top 26 pixels gone. Every video in the app was sitting under an invisible
1091	// caption. A frame with no label widget hands its child the whole inside.
1092	//
1093	// The dark fill is the other half of the same complaint. A picture keeps the
1094	// video's aspect, so whatever the frame has spare turns into bars beside it.
1095	// In the window's own background those bars read as an over-wide border; in
1096	// black they read as letterboxing, which is what they are.
1097	func videoFrame(child gtk.Widgetter) *gtk.Frame {
1098		f := gtk.NewFrame("")
1099		f.SetLabelWidget(nil)
1100		f.AddCSSClass("videoframe")
1101		if child != nil {
1102			f.SetChild(child)
1103		}
1104		return f
1105	}
1106	
1107	// playerErr is what every player's OnError is set to. Named, because there are
1108	// five of them and "playback failed" in a log shared by the whole pipeline
1109	// answers none of the questions you have at that point. The status line gets it
1110	// too: a failure the log records and the window does not mention is a failure

// Cards: the pictures the app draws itself. An insert path may carry
// parameters after a "?", as a URL does:
//
//	assets/tier.svg?S=Dust II,Mirage|logos/mirage.png&A=Nuke&title=Best maps
//	assets/s.svg?label=S&item=Dust II
//
// The part before "?" must exist. A document with {{name}} placeholders has
// them filled in; one stamped data-naivepost="tier" is drawn again by that card
// from the parameters, the file saying where every place is. The stamp also
// carries the parameters it was drawn with (data-naivepost-args), overridden key
// by key by the "?". Animation is SMIL, baked per frame by svganim.go.

// than a map because the order is content here: the tier rows come out in the
// order they were written, and a map would rank the maps alphabetically.
type svgParam struct{ Key, Val string }

type svgQuery []svgParam

// insSplit takes an insert path apart into the file and its parameters. Every
// place that opens, probes or names an insert goes through this: a path with a
// "?" left on it is a file that does not exist, and the symptom is a card that

func insSplit(p string) (string, svgQuery) {
	i := strings.IndexByte(p, '?')
	if i < 0 {

	}
	return p[:i], parseSVGQuery(p[i+1:])
}

// insBase is what an insert is called on screen and in the log: the file's name
// without the parameters, which are usually longer than the rest of the row.
func insBase(p string) string {
	file, _ := insSplit(p)
	return filepath.Base(file)
}

		}

}

// coordinates written out. This file supplies what a document cannot: what is
// in a place, how big its name must be to fit, which place just arrived, and
// when everything moves.

import (

// The board as tier.svg draws it. These numbers are in two places on purpose --
// there and here -- because two things need them that a document cannot do:
// fitting a name to the width of a place, and knowing how far off the right edge
// a chip flies in from. Move something in the file and move it here.
const (
	tierSlots  = 6     // places in a tier, and the whole of what a tier holds
	tierTop    = 180.0 // the first row's top edge
	tierRowH   = 140.0 // and one row to the next
	tierBoxH   = 124.0 // how tall the row itself is, the gap taken off
	tierChipX  = 338.0 // the first place in a row
	tierChipDX = 244.0 // and one place to the next
	tierChipW  = 230.0
	tierChipH  = 108.0
	tierPad    = 14.0 // inside a place, around the picture and under the name
)

// The six tiers, in the order they are written down the side of the board, with
// the colour each letter has always had. E is missing because a tier list is
// read as S to F and nobody has ever put an E in the middle of one.

	tierLetters = []string{"S", "A", "B", "C", "D", "F"}
	tierColors  = []string{"#ff7f7f", "#ffbf7f", "#ffdf7f", "#ffff7f", "#bfff7f", "#7fffff"}

func tierPlaceY(i int) float64    { return tierRowY(i) + 8 }
func tierNameY(i int) float64     { return tierPlaceY(i) + tierChipH - tierPad }

func tierSlotKey(i, j int) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%s%d", tierPrefix(i), j+1) }

package main

// CSS animation, baked the way SMIL is: @keyframes rules become svgAnims for
// svganim.go, which interpolates, freezes, repeats and writes the frame.
//
// Subset:
//
//	properties   opacity, transform, fill
//	transform    translate(X/Y), scale(X/Y), rotate, none -- px and deg
//	selectors    one compound selector: #id, .class, tag, *, combinations
//	             ("rect.row"); no combinators, attributes or pseudo-classes
//	timing       animation and its longhands: name, duration, delay,
//	             timing-function, iteration-count, fill-mode
//	easing       linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out, cubic-bezier();
//	             steps() read as linear
//
// Anything outside it stays in the document and renders statically. Widen via
// cssAnimProps and cssTransform.
//
// Baked frames drop the @keyframes blocks, the animation declarations and the
// declarations of the animated properties: a stylesheet outranks a
// presentation attribute, so "opacity: 0" left in a rule would hide the baked
// value. Cost: a rule that animates one element and statically styles another
// loses that property for both.

import (
	"math"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// cssAnimProps is the allowlist, and each base is the property's value on an
// element that never set it -- the underlying value a keyframe list that starts
// at 50%, or ends at 80%, interpolates from and back to. A slice rather than a
// map so two runs of the baker over one document write the same file.
var cssAnimProps = []struct{ prop, base string }{
	{"opacity", "1"},
	{"transform", ""}, // no useful initial: an identity shaped like the other end
	{"fill", "#000000"},
}

func cssBaseOf(prop string) (string, bool) {
	for _, p := range cssAnimProps {
		if p.prop == prop {
			return p.base, true
		}
	}
	return "", false
}

// svgCSSAnimated is the cheap textual test for a document worth parsing:
// keyframes to read AND something that runs them. Either alone animates nothing.
func svgCSSAnimated(b []byte) bool {
	s := string(b)
	return strings.Contains(s, "@keyframes") && strings.Contains(s, "animation")
}

// ---- the little bit of CSS this reads ----------------------------------------

type cssDecl struct{ prop, val string }

// cssRule is one plain rule. used and baked are filled while the elements are
// walked: an animation is not a property of a rule but of an element, since the
// name can come from one rule and the delay from another -- which is how a tier
// list staggers its rows (.row for the animation, .r2 .r3 for the delays).
type cssRule struct {
	sels  []string
	decls []cssDecl
	used  bool            // contributed to an animation that was baked
	baked map[string]bool // ...and the properties that were baked from it
}

// cssItem keeps the stylesheet's order for writing it back: a plain rule, a
// @keyframes block (kept until it is known to have been consumed), or anything
// else (@font-face, @media, a stray line) held verbatim.
type cssItem struct {
	raw  string
	kf   string // the name, for a @keyframes block
	rule *cssRule
}

package main

// Animated SVG, without a browser. Nothing in the render path plays SMIL
// (librsvg, Inkscape and resvg all render t=0), so it is EVALUATED: read the
// animation elements, compute every animated attribute at t, write a static
// document with those values baked in, once per frame; ffmpeg reads the
// sequence as stills.
//
// Supported: <animate>, <set>, <animateTransform> on numbers, number lists,
// lengths with units, hex/rgb() colours; from/to/by, values with keyTimes,
// dur, begin, repeatCount (number or indefinite), fill="freeze"; calcMode
// discrete steps, paced and spline read as linear. CSS @keyframes is folded in
// by svgcss.go. Not read: begin chained off another animation or an event, and
// elements targeting something other than their parent -- both render static.

import (
	"encoding/xml"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"math"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
)

// svgFPS is the rate an insert's baked sequence is rendered at when the render
// settings do not name one. Animation is the only reason a still becomes a
// sequence at all, so this only has to be smooth, not to match a camera.
const svgFPS = 25

// svgNode is the document as read, with the animation elements pulled out of
// the children and hung on the element they animate. Attrs keeps the original
// order and spelling: what comes out of here has to be the same document with
// different numbers in it, not a normalized rewrite of it.
type svgNode struct {
	name  string
	attrs []xml.Attr
	kids  []*svgNode
	text  string // character data; only leaves have any that matters
	anims []*svgAnim
	// self-closing in the source. Preserved because an empty <rect/> written as
	// <rect></rect> is the same document, but a reader diffing two baked frames
	// against the original should see only the numbers move.
	empty bool
}

// svgAnim is one animation element, already parsed into the four things
// evaluating it needs: what it animates, what the values are, when it runs, and
// whether it holds its last value afterwards.
type svgAnim struct {
	attr      string   // attributeName
	transform string   // animateTransform's type; empty for a plain animate
	values    []string // at least two once from/to/by has been folded in
	keyTimes  []float64
	begin     float64
	dur       float64
	repeat    float64 // how many times; math.Inf(1) for indefinite
	freeze    bool
	discrete  bool
	additive  bool // additive="sum": the value adds to the static attribute
	// the two CSS brought with it (svgcss.go). SMIL leaves both zero: an
	// animation with no easing is linear, and one that has not begun yet leaves
	// the static value alone.
	backfill bool     // fill-mode backwards: hold the first value before it begins
	ease     *cssEase // nil is linear, which is every SMIL animation
}

// svgAnimated reports whether a document has anything to bake. Cheap and
// deliberately textual: the caller uses it to decide whether an insert is a
// still or a sequence, and a document with no SMIL in it should not be parsed
// twice to find that out.
func svgAnimated(b []byte) bool {
	s := string(b)
	for _, tag := range []string{"<animate", "<set", "<animateTransform", "<animateMotion"} {
		if strings.Contains(s, tag) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return svgCSSAnimated(b)

2322					if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(file), 0o755); err != nil {
2323						return nil, false, err
2324					}
2325					if err := os.WriteFile(file, src, 0o644); err != nil {
2326						return nil, false, err
2327					}
2328				}
2329				break
2330			}
2331			// baked beside the clips rather than next to the asset: this is derived
2332			// from the cut's slot length, so it belongs to the render and goes when
2333			// the render does
2334			dir := filepath.Join(a.produceDir(), "clips",
2335				fmt.Sprintf("c%03d_%s.frames", c.idx, safeStem(c.ins)))
2336			pat, n, err := bakeSVG(src, dir, rate, c.length)
2337			if err != nil {
2338				return nil, false, fmt.Errorf("animating %s: %w", insBase(c.ins), err)
2339			}
2340			a.logfIdle("%s: %d frames baked at %g fps", insBase(c.ins), n, rate)
2341			return []string{"-framerate", fmt.Sprintf("%g", rate), "-i", pat}, false, nil
2342		}
2343		// a still, and a static SVG that fell through to here: one frame held for
2344		// the whole slot. -framerate on the input rather than -r, so the held frames
2345		// are generated at the output's rate instead of one frame being stretched
2346		// into a stream nothing downstream can cut at.
2347		return []string{"-loop", "1", "-framerate", fmt.Sprintf("%g", rate),
2348			"-t", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", c.length), "-i", file}, false, nil
2349	}
2350	
2351	// safeStem is a file's name reduced to what a clip folder can be named after:
2352	// no separators, no spaces, no surprises for a shell that never sees it anyway.
2353	func safeStem(path string) string {
2354		file, _ := insSplit(path) // a card's parameters are not part of its name
2355		base := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(file), filepath.Ext(file))
2356		var b strings.Builder
2357		for _, r := range base {
2358			switch {
2359			case r >= 'a' && r <= 'z', r >= 'A' && r <= 'Z', r >= '0' && r <= '9', r == '-', r == '_':
2360				b.WriteRune(r)
2361			default:
2362				b.WriteByte('-')
2363			}
2364		}
2365		s := strings.Trim(b.String(), "-")
2366		if s == "" {
2367			return "insert"
2368		}
2369		if len(s) > 40 {
2370			s = s[:40]
2371		}
2372		return s
2373	}
2374	
2375	// clipBox is the frame every insert has to fill: the size the footage clips
2376	// come out at (the join is a stream copy), from the first recording used
2377	// rather than the settings, which only name a height. A cut of nothing but
2378	// inserts falls back to the output height at 16:9.
2379	func clipBox(clips []prodClip, st prodSettings) (int, int) {
2380		for _, c := range clips {
2381			if c.video == nil {
2382				continue
2383			}
2384			w0, h0, err := ffprobeSize(c.video.path)
2385			if err != nil {
2386				continue
2387			}
2388			return outSize(w0, h0, st.Height)
2389		}
2390		return outSize(0, 0, st.Height)
2391	}
2392	
2393	// outSize is the frame the render comes out at, given the footage's own size
2394	// and the tier that was asked for. The tier names the SHORT side of the frame:
2395	// the height of a wide video -- which is all "1080p" has ever meant there --
2396	// and the width of a tall one, where 1080p is 1080×1920, the size a Short is
2397	// uploaded at, not a 608-wide strip. "original" (0) keeps the footage's own
2398	// frame. Both sides rounded even -- an insert one pixel off is a clip a
2399	// concat will not take.
2400	//
2401	// Its own function, over sizes that are already known, so the Produce page can
2402	// say the frame in pixels without opening a file. "original" on a 4K screen
2403	// capture reads like a setting and lands as a 700 MB upload, and the only
2404	// moment that is worth knowing is before the encode, not after it.
2405	func outSize(w0, h0, height int) (int, int) {
2406		if w0 <= 0 || h0 <= 0 {
2407			h := height
2408			if h <= 0 {
2409				h = 1080 // nothing probed and nothing chosen
2410			}
2411			return int(math.Round(float64(h)*16/9/2)) * 2, h - h%2
2412		}
2413		k := 1.0 // original: the footage's own frame
2414		if height > 0 {
2415			k = float64(height) / float64(min(w0, h0))
2416		}
2417		return int(math.Round(float64(w0)*k/2)) * 2, int(math.Round(float64(h0)*k/2)) * 2
2418	}
2419	
2420	// clipMixes is the stretch of every separate recording running while this
2421	// clip was, in the clip's own time; a recording not running at all is absent.
2422	// Inserts and freezes get none (added time, nothing was recorded under them).
2423	// On a slowed clip the session span is the length through the rate, the
2424	// placement is divided by it, and dur stays in file seconds (the stretch
2425	// happens in the graph, atempo).
2426	func clipMixes(c prodClip, recs []tlAudio) []prodMix {
2427		var out []prodMix
2428		if c.dropLane != "" && c.snd != "" {
2429			// the inserted sound goes in the mix where the recording it replaced
2430			// would have been, rather than in the capture's slot: that is the whole
2431			// difference between "these seconds sound like the file" and "this one
2432			// recording sounds like the file". at is 0 because a sound laid over
2433			// footage starts where the footage does, by construction.
2434			out = append(out, prodMix{base: baseName(c.snd), path: c.snd,
2435				at: 0, ss: c.sndAt, dur: c.length})
2436		}
2437		if len(recs) == 0 {
2438			return out
2439		}
2440		for _, au := range recs {
2441			if au.base == c.dropLane {
2442				continue // this one is what the inserted sound was put in place of
2443			}
2444			if laneQuiet(c.quiet, au.base) {
2445				continue // and this one the scene was told not to hear
2446			}
2447			t0, t1 := laneOverlap(c, au)
2448			if t1-t0 < laneMinMix { // nothing worth an input, and a 0 s one ffmpeg refuses
2449				continue
2450			}
2451			at := (t0 - c.sessS) / c.speed()
2452			if c.audOwn {
2453				at = t0 - c.audSess // 1x, from the second the sound starts at
2454			}
2455			out = append(out, prodMix{base: au.base, path: au.path, track: au.track,
2456				at: at, ss: t0 - au.start, dur: t1 - t0})
2457		}
2458		return out
2459	}
2460	
2461	// laneMinMix is the shortest overlap worth an ffmpeg input -- and a zero-length
2462	// one it refuses outright.
2463	const laneMinMix = 0.1
2464	
2465	// laneReport says per recording whether it reached the render and, if not,
2466	// which of the two reasons: not running while any clip was (a placement to
2467	// look at), or silenced by the scenes (the cut doing what it was told). It
2468	// reads clipMixes' decision rather than re-deciding.
2469	func laneReport(clips []prodClip, recs []tlAudio) []string {
2470		var out []string
2471		for _, au := range recs {
2472			under, past := 0, 0
2473			for i := range clips {
2474				mixed := false
2475				for _, m := range clips[i].mix {
2476					mixed = mixed || m.base == au.base
2477				}
2478				// three ways for a clip to stand to a recording, and every clip
2479				// is exactly one of them. The overlap is read off the same
2480				// function the mix is built from, so the count and the mix
2481				// cannot disagree about which clips a track was running under.
2482				if t0, t1 := laneOverlap(clips[i], au); mixed {
2483					under++
2484				} else if t1-t0 >= laneMinMix {
2485					past++
2486				}
2487			}
2488			switch {
2489			case under > 0:
2490				out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s is mixed into %d of the %d clips",
2491					au.base, under, len(clips)))
2492			case past > 0:
2493				out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s runs under %d clip(s) and every one of them leaves it out — it is not in the render",
2494					au.base, past))
2495			default:
2496				out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf("%s was not running while any clip was — it is not in the render",
2497					au.base))
2498			}
2499		}
2500		return out
2501	}
2502	
2503	// laneOverlap is the session stretch a clip and a recording were both running
2504	// in, empty when they were not; shared by the mix and the run's report so the
2505	// two cannot disagree. A freeze and a card overlap nothing: they are time
2506	// ADDED to the session.
2507	func laneOverlap(c prodClip, au tlAudio) (float64, float64) {
2508		if c.freeze || c.noLanes {
2509			return 0, 0
2510		}
2511		s0 := c.sessS
2512		s1 := s0 + c.length*c.speed()
2513		if c.audOwn {
2514			// the sound is off the picture's clock: the lanes are the same moment
2515			// as the capture's own track and are read from the same second, at 1x
2516			// for exactly as long as the clip is on screen (cut_fxsound.go)
2517			s0 = c.audSess
2518			s1 = s0 + c.length
2519		}
2520		return math.Max(s0, au.start), math.Min(s1, au.start+au.dur)
2521	}
2522	
2523	// narrRun is the slot a clip's narration asks for: where the last line stops,
2524	// plus the moment of air the render leaves after it. It is the number every
2525	// decision about a clip's length is made against.
2526	func narrRun(lines []prodLine, tempo float64) float64 {
2527		return packLines(lines, tempo) + narrTail
2528	}
2529	
2530	// packLines lays a clip's lines out in its slot and answers where the last one
2531	// stops. Each starts where the writer placed it, but never before the line
2532	// above has finished and a breath has passed -- so an overlong line pushes
2533	// everything under it later, and it is the LAST line that falls off the end of
2534	// the clip. The delays are written back into the slice, because that schedule
2535	// is what the render feeds adelay.
2536	//
2537	// A function rather than the closure it used to be, because the Narrate page
2538	// has to be able to ask the same question. Its own per-line ⚠ answers a
2539	// different one -- "has THIS line room before the next" -- and cannot see the
2540	// pushing, which is exactly what the render's "does not fit where it was
2541	// placed" is complaining about (clipOverrun, narrate.go).
2542	func packLines(lines []prodLine, tempo float64) float64 {
2543		if tempo <= 0 {
2544			tempo = 1 // a clip built by hand, and every arithmetic here divides
2545		}
2546		prev := 0.0
2547		for k := range lines {
2548			d := math.Max(narrLead, lines[k].at)
2549			if d < prev {
2550				d = prev
2551			}
2552			lines[k].delay = d
2553			prev = d + lines[k].dur/tempo + narrGap
2554		}
2555		return prev - narrGap
2556	}
2557	
2558	// delayMS is a line's start in the units adelay actually reads: whole
2559	// milliseconds, never below the lead-in. Rounded rather than truncated, so a
2560	// placement is out by at most half a millisecond either way.
2561	func delayMS(delay float64) int {
2562		return int(math.Round(math.Max(narrLead, delay) * 1000))
2563	}
2564	
2565	// encodeClip cuts one slot out of its recording -- or renders an insert into
2566	// one -- and mixes the narration in.
2567	func (a *App) encodeClip(c prodClip, out, cueFile string, st prodSettings) error {
2568		src, srcSound, err := a.clipInput(c, st)
2569		if err != nil {
2570			return err
2571		}
2572		args := append([]string{"-v", "error", "-y"}, src...)
2573		game := "0:a"
2574		switch {
2575		case c.snd != "" && c.dropLane == "":
2576			// the inserted sound goes exactly where the silence would: input 1,
2577			// which keeps every index downstream where it was. The recording's own
2578			// sound is simply never mapped -- overwriting is replacing, not mixing.
2579			//
2580			// A copied stretch of a lane starts inside its file rather than at the
2581			// top of it, and -ss before -i is how that is asked: the trim is the
2582			// input's, so -t below still measures the slot and not the file.
2583			if c.sndAt > 0 {
2584				args = append(args, "-ss", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", c.sndAt))
2585			}
2586			// the trim is in SOURCE seconds and the slot is in output ones, so a
2587			// clip played fast eats more of the file than it is long: without the
2588			// speed the sound would run out partway and apad would finish the slot
2589			// in silence. Slower than 1 takes less and the extra is simply
2590			// decoded and dropped, which costs nothing worth a branch.
2591			args = append(args, "-t", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", c.length*math.Max(1, c.speed())),
2592				"-i", c.snd)
2593			game = "1:a"
2594		case c.audOwn && srcSound:
2595			// the sound has come away from the picture (cut_fxsound.go): it is a
2596			// second read of the same recording, from the second the plan says
2597			// and at 1×, for exactly as long as this clip is on screen. -ss
2598			// before -i, like every other seek here: the trim is the input's, so
2599			// this decodes the seconds it uses rather than the file.
2600			args = append(args, "-ss", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", math.Max(0, c.audAt)),
2601				"-t", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", c.length), "-i", c.audPath)
2602			game = "1:a"
2603		case !srcSound:
2604			args = append(args, "-f", "lavfi", "-t", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", c.length),
2605				"-i", "anullsrc=channel_layout="+audLayout(st)+":sample_rate=48000")
2606			game = "1:a"
2607		}
2608		// every spoken line is its own input, mixed over the ducked game together
2609		var spoken []prodLine
2610		for _, ln := range c.lines {
2611			if ln.wav != "" {
2612				spoken = append(spoken, ln)
2613				args = append(args, "-i", ln.wav)
2614			}
2615		}
2616		voiceBase := 1
2617		if game == "1:a" {
2618			voiceBase = 2
2619		}
2620		// the separate recordings last, so adding one cannot move a voice input out
2621		// from under the index the narration filters were written against. Seeked
2622		// and trimmed on the input rather than in the graph: this is one stretch of
2623		// a file that may be an hour long, and decoding all of it to throw away the
2624		// rest is the difference between a render and an afternoon.
2625		mixBase := voiceBase + len(spoken)
2626		for _, m := range c.mix {
2627			args = append(args, "-ss", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", math.Max(0, m.ss)),
2628				"-t", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", m.dur), "-i", m.path)
2629		}
2630		// the overlays, last, for the same reason the recordings are last: a new
2631		// one must not move an index an earlier filter was written against. A
2632		// title is a still SVG the size of the finished frame, written here
2633		// (fxtext.go); a drawing is the user's own file (fxsvg.go). Either way an
2634		// SVG looped for the clip's length -- ffmpeg reads SVG already, it is how
2635		// the cards get in.
2636		txtBase := mixBase + len(c.mix)
2637		svgFps := st.FPS
2638		if svgFps <= 0 {
2639			svgFps = 30
2640		}
2641		for _, cue := range c.texts {
2642			file := cue.fx.Src
2643			if cue.fx.Kind != "svg" {
2644				file = fmt.Sprintf("%s_t%02d.svg", strings.TrimSuffix(out, filepath.Ext(out)), cue.idx)
2645				if err := os.WriteFile(file, textSVG(cue.fx, c.boxW, c.boxH), 0o644); err != nil {
2646					return err
2647				}
2648			}
2649			// a hair longer than the slot, so the last frame of the clip still has
2650			// something to composite; the overlay's eof_action=pass covers the rest
2651			args = append(args, "-loop", "1", "-framerate", fmt.Sprintf("%g", svgFps))
2652			if cue.fx.Kind == "svg" {
2653				// a vector rendered at the size it is used at rather than at the
2654				// size its document happens to declare (fxsvg.go); a title's file
2655				// is already written the frame's size and wants none of this
2656				if _, _, bw, bh, ok := svgFitPx(cue.fx, c.boxW, c.boxH); ok {
2657					args = append(args, "-width", strconv.Itoa(bw), "-height", strconv.Itoa(bh),
2658						"-keep_ar", "1")
2659				}
2660			}
2661			args = append(args, "-t", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", c.length+0.2), "-i", file)
2662		}
2663		// the stop stills, after everything else for the same index-stability
2664		// reason: each is one decoded frame of its recording, cut at the stop's own
2665		// second. The half-second input window is all trim=end_frame=1 below needs,
2666		// and it spares decoding the hour of recording behind it.
2667		stillBase := txtBase + len(c.texts)
2668		for _, sc := range c.stills {
2669			args = append(args, "-ss", fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", sc.at), "-t", "0.5", "-i", sc.path)
2670		}
2671	
2672		var vf []string
2673		// the clock first: setpts stretches or squeezes the timestamps, and
2674		// everything after it -- the fps grid, the camera -- works in that time,
2675		// which is the clip's own output time
2676		if c.ins == "" && !c.freeze && c.speed() != 1 {
2677			vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("setpts=PTS/%g", c.speed()))
2678		}
2679		if c.freeze {
2680			// one decoded frame, held: everything after the first frame is cut and
2681			// the frame is cloned out a hair past the slot (the output -t below is
2682			// what makes the length exact)
2683			vf = append(vf, "trim=end_frame=1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS",
2684				fmt.Sprintf("tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=%.3f", c.length+0.2))
2685		}
2686		// the fps FILTER is what pins a stream to a rate: it duplicates and drops
2687		// frames until they land on that grid, whether the source was faster or
2688		// slower. Under VFR the rate is a ceiling instead, which is the encoder's
2689		// job and not a filter's (see fpsArgs).
2690		if st.FPS > 0 && !st.VFR {
2691			vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("fps=%g", st.FPS))
2692		} else if c.cam != nil && !c.cam.static() {
2693			// zoompan places its window per frame, so a moving camera needs a grid
2694			// even when the output is VFR; this clip gets one at the camera's rate
2695			vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("fps=%g", c.cam.fps))
2696			a.logfIdle("%s: the moving camera needs a fixed frame rate — this clip is %g fps",
2697				c.name(), c.cam.fps)
2698		}
2699		// the stop stills go on between here and the camera: in the clip's own
2700		// time but in the SOURCE frame, so a zoom or a view crops the still
2701		// exactly as it crops the footage running under it (the chain is spliced
2702		// in where fc is assembled below, at this point of the filter list)
2703		clock := len(vf)
2704		// what the bare parts of the frame get instead of black. Emitted below,
2705		// at the same point in the graph the pad it replaces sat at: after the
2706		// stop stills (a still is the recording's own frame and is padded with
2707		// it) and before the crop the camera does.
2708		var bd bdrop
2709		switch {
2710		case c.ins != "":
2711			// An insert has to come out at exactly the frame size the footage clips
2712			// do, because the join is a stream copy: the concat demuxer refuses a
2713			// clip whose dimensions differ from the ones before it, and there is no
2714			// re-encode later to paper over it. So it is fitted rather than scaled --
2715			// scaled down until it fits, then centred on a black frame, which keeps a
2716			// square diagram square and a 4:3 card 4:3 inside a 16:9 video.
2717			if c.boxW > 0 && c.boxH > 0 {
2718				bd = bdrop{w: c.boxW, h: c.boxH, fit: true}
2719			}
2720			// a video insert shorter than its slot would end the clip early and take
2721			// the narration written over it with it; the last frame is held instead
2722			vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=%.3f", c.length))
2723		case c.cam != nil:
2724			// the camera looking past the edge of the recording: the same padded
2725			// frame it always measured itself on, with the border filled in
2726			if pw, ph, pl, pt, ok := c.cam.padBox(); ok {
2727				bd = bdrop{w: pw, h: ph, x: pl, y: pt}
2728			}
2729			vf = append(vf, c.cam.chainOn(bd.on())...)
2730		case c.boxW > 0 && c.boxH > 0:
2731			// Plain footage comes out at the finished frame: the join is a stream
2732			// copy, so every clip must match. Fitted onto a backdrop, not stretched
2733			// (a 4:3 webcam keeps its shape); footage already the frame's shape takes
2734			// the plain scale, since the backdrop would be fully covered.
2735			if fitsFrame(c.video, c.boxW, c.boxH) {
2736				vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("scale=%d:%d", c.boxW, c.boxH))
2737			} else {
2738				bd = bdrop{w: c.boxW, h: c.boxH, fit: true}
2739			}
2740		case st.Height > 0:
2741			// no box was worked out for this clip -- which the render always does
2742			// (clipBox), so this is a clip built by hand -- and the height that was
2743			// asked for is then the best answer available
2744			vf = append(vf, fmt.Sprintf("scale=-2:%d", st.Height))
2745		}
2746		bd.bare = st.Bare // black edges or a blurred blow-up: the region is the same
2747		vf = append(vf, "setsar=1")
2748		if cueFile != "" {
2749			vf = append(vf, "subtitles="+ffEscape(cueFile))
2750		}
2751		vlab := "v"
2752		head := "[0:v]"
2753		fc := ""
2754		if len(c.stills) > 0 || bd.on() {
2755			// the clock and the fps grid run on their own, so that the stills and
2756			// the backdrop can be spliced in between them and the camera
2757			pre := strings.Join(vf[:clock], ",")
2758			if pre == "" {
2759				pre = "null"
2760			}
2761			fc = head + pre + "[vpre];"
2762			head = "[vpre]"
2763			vf = vf[clock:]
2764		}
2765		if len(c.stills) > 0 {
2766			// each still is the same one-frame hold an audio insert's picture uses,
2767			// on an overlay input: cut to its first frame, cloned out past the
2768			// slot, faded on its alpha exactly as a title is (textChain), and laid
2769			// over the running footage only while its bar says so
2770			cur := strings.Trim(head, "[]")
2771			for k, sc := range c.stills {
2772				fc += fmt.Sprintf("[%d:v]trim=end_frame=1,setpts=PTS-STARTPTS,"+
2773					"tpad=stop_mode=clone:stop_duration=%.3f,format=rgba",
2774					stillBase+k, c.length+0.2)
2775				if sc.w > 0 && sc.h > 0 {
2776					// fitted and centred rather than stretched, and padded with
2777					// transparency (#00000000, not a black the toggle would owe an
