package main

// The run queue: what one press of ▶ turned into, in order. A job fills it as
// work is found, the runner picks tasks off the front, and the bar says one
// short line: which job, which of the run's jobs, what the head task is doing,
// how far down the queue. Filenames belong in the log. The bar's FRACTION is
// not the queue's length -- the queue grows as it is opened, and a total that
// grows under a fraction drags the bar backwards -- but the weighted tracks
// (prog).

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"math"
	"strings"

	"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/glib/v2"
)

// The two tracks are the two halves of the bar. They are concurrent in Prepare
// (speech recognition on the GPU, frame extraction on the CPU) and sequential
// on Describe + Transcript, but the arithmetic is the same either way: each
// track reports its own absolute contribution and the bar shows the sum.
// Letting either write a raw fraction would make the bar bounce between them.
const (
	trackSTT    = 0
	trackFrames = 1
	// the same two tracks under the names the Describe + Transcript step uses
	// them for: its two jobs run one after the other, but each still owns half
	// the bar and its own line
	trackDescribe = trackSTT
	trackFix      = trackFrames
)

// qTrack is one half of the bar: the job on it, the work it has left, and what
// the task at the head of the queue is doing this second.
type qTrack struct {
	job        string // "describe", "speech", "narrate" — what this half is
	phase, of  int    // ...and which of the run's jobs it is, when there are two
	queued     int    // tasks known about, including the ones already taken
	taken      int    // how many have been picked up: the head's position
	what       string // what the head is doing, in two or three words
	kind       string // what a task of this queue is, when nothing else is said
	doneJob    bool   // the job finished; the other track may still be going
	everFilled bool   // a queue that was filled and emptied is not an unfilled one
}

// line is a track's whole contribution to the bar:
//
//	describe 1/2: chunk 4/12
//	transcript 2/2: fixing block 3/7
//	speech: recognising 2/3
//
// Every piece is dropped when it has nothing to say, so a job with one task and
// no phases is simply "thumbnail: drawing".
func (t qTrack) line() string {
	if t.doneJob {
		if t.job == "" {
			return ""
		}
	a.progMu.Lock()
	a.progParts = [2]float64{}
	a.progQ = [2]qTrack{}
	a.progBase, a.progShare = 0, 0
	a.progMu.Unlock()
	a.showProg()
}

// qPhase says where in the bar the jobs that come next are drawn (base, share)
// and clears the queue for them. A single-step press never calls it; Prepare's
// ▶ is two steps back to back, each reporting its own whole bar, and the
// scaling happens here rather than in every place that moves the needle. A
// phase that has reported nothing stands where the one before it finished.
func (a *App) qPhase(base, share float64) {
	a.progMu.Lock()
	a.progBase, a.progShare = base, share
	a.progQ = [2]qTrack{}
	a.progParts = [2]float64{base / 2, base / 2}
	a.progMu.Unlock()
	a.showProg()
}

// scaled maps a track's own fraction into the phase's slice of the bar. Share 0
// means no phase was set, which is the whole bar -- that is every step but
// Prepare, and it is also the headless App the tests build. Called with
// progMu held.
func (a *App) scaled(f float64) float64 {
	if a.progShare == 0 {
		return f
	}
	return a.progBase/2 + f*a.progShare
}

// qJob says which job now owns a track, and which of the run's jobs it is --
// "describe 1/2", then "transcript 2/2". Pass of = 0 for a run that is one job,
// or whose jobs are concurrent and named rather than numbered.
func (a *App) qJob(track int, job string, phase, of int) {
	a.progMu.Lock()
	a.progQ[track] = qTrack{job: job, phase: phase, of: of}
	a.progMu.Unlock()
	a.showProg()
}

// qPush queues n more tasks of one kind. Called again whenever more work is
// found: a run that could count all of its work in advance would not need a
// queue.
func (a *App) qPush(track, n int, kind string) {
	if n <= 0 {
		return
	}
	a.progMu.Lock()
	t := &a.progQ[track]
	t.queued += n
	t.everFilled = true
	if kind != "" {
		t.kind = kind
	}
	a.progMu.Unlock()
	a.showProg()
}

// qTake picks the next task up. It is called once per task whatever becomes of
// it -- work already on disk from an earlier run is a task this run is done
// with, and a queue that skipped those would stall at the position where the
// resume started.
func (a *App) qTake(track int) {
	a.progMu.Lock()
	t := &a.progQ[track]
	t.taken++
	t.what = ""
	a.progMu.Unlock()
	a.showProg()
}

// qDone ends a track's job: it keeps the half of the bar it earned and stops
// saying anything but its name, so the line belongs to whatever is still
// running.
func (a *App) qDone(track int, f float64) {
	a.progMu.Lock()
	a.progParts[track] = a.scaled(f)
	a.progQ[track].doneJob = true
	a.progMu.Unlock()
	a.showProg()
}

// busy says whether a run is already active, and tells the status line so.
func (a *App) busy() bool {
	if a.running {
		a.setStatus("a run is already active — stop it first (⏹)")
	}
	return a.running
}

// startRun flips the app into a run: the flags, a fresh context, an empty
// queue, the controls, the log open. Every ▶ and ↻ goes through it.
func (a *App) startRun() {
	a.running = true
	a.stopFlag.Store(false)
	a.pauseFlag.Store(false)
	a.runCtx, a.runCancel = context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	a.qReset()
	a.updateRunControls()
	a.logExp.SetExpanded(true)
}

// endRun is the GUI-thread half of a run finishing.
func (a *App) endRun() {
	a.running = false
	a.updateRunControls()
	// ...and the next step of a chain, if one is under way (runchain.go).
	// Before the model unload below, which is housekeeping: the next step
	// usually wants the same models back.
	defer a.chainDone()
	// ...and the machine's half: whatever the run left loaded on the audio
	// server is memory nothing is waiting on any more (freeAudioModels). Off
	// the GUI thread, because it is a request over the network and the window
	// has to come back to life now, not when the server answers.
	go a.freeAudioModels()
}

// prog is how far this track has got and what its task is doing: the fraction
// is the track's absolute contribution; the text is two or three words, no
// filename, no count (the queue counts, the log names). An empty format falls
// back to the task's kind ("chunk 4/12").
func (a *App) prog(track int, f float64, format string, args ...any) {
	txt := fmt.Sprintf(format, args...)

}

// pulseUntilCounted keeps the bar moving while a model thinks. The LLM calls
// have nothing countable in them, so the bar pulses until something with real

func (a *App) pulseUntilCounted() {

1	package main
2	
3	// The spare: a second video pipeline, prerolled at the next cut.
4	//
5	// A cut in the preview is a jump of the line to somewhere else -- the next
6	// clip after a removed stretch, the next join in a review, the next recording
7	// when this one runs out -- and until now every jump onto another file was
8	// PlaySegment: the pipeline to READY, a new uri, a preroll, a seek, and only
9	// then PLAYING, some three hundred milliseconds in which the picture froze
10	// and the sound stopped. A jump within the file was a flushing seek, which is
11	// quicker but still a stumble. That is what a cut looked like, and it is not
12	// what the render makes.
13	//
14	// So the editor says where the line is going a few seconds before it goes
15	// there (cut_preload.go), and this pipeline is taken to PAUSED at exactly
16	// that file and second -- decoded, prerolled, first frame ready, sound
17	// buffered. When the jump comes, PlaySegment finds it ready and SWAPS: the
18	// spare becomes the pipeline playing and the old one becomes the spare, the
19	// picture is pointed at the new paintable, and PLAYING on a prerolled
20	// pipeline is immediate. The join plays through like the join it will be.
21	//
22	// One spare, not one per row: the line goes one place next. Built on the
23	// first Preload, so only the player that jumps -- the cut editor's -- ever
24	// has one.
25	
26	import (
27		"math"
28	
29		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gdk/v4"
30		"github.com/go-gst/go-gst/pkg/gst"
31	)
32	
33	// preloadTol is how close the prerolled second has to be to the one asked
34	// for. The editor computes both from the same numbers, so this is float
35	// slack, not a search radius.
36	const preloadTol = 0.01
37	
38	type spare struct {
39		pb, gain gst.Element
40		video    gdk.Paintabler
41		loaded   string  // the file it holds, or "" for nothing
42		at       float64 // the file second it was asked to preroll at
43		pend     int64   // the seek still to make once the uri has prerolled, ns; <0 none
44		ready    bool    // prerolled AT at: the seek has landed
45		seekRate float64 // the rate that seek carried
46	}
47	
48	// Preload asks for the spare to be prerolled at a second of a file. Cheap to
49	// ask on every tick: already there, or on its way there, is nothing to do.
50	func (p *Player) Preload(file string, start float64) {
51		if p.spare == nil {
52			pb, gain, video, err := videoPipe("spare")
53			if err != nil {
54				return // no spare: every cut is a reload, as it was
55			}
56			p.spare = &spare{pb: pb, gain: gain, video: video, pend: -1}
57			p.watch(pb)
58		}
59		s := p.spare
60		if s.loaded == file && math.Abs(s.at-start) < preloadTol {
61			return
62		}
63		s.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
64		s.pb.SetObjectProperty("uri", fileURI(file))
65		s.loaded, s.at, s.ready = file, start, false
66		s.pend = int64(start * 1e9)
67		s.seekRate = p.rate
68		// silent while it waits: a paused pipeline makes no sound, but the
69		// moment it is swapped in it must be at the player's loudness, and that
70		// is written on the way in (swapIn)
71		s.pb.SetState(gst.StatePaused)
72	}
73	
74	// Preloaded is whether a PlaySegment for this file and second would be a
75	// swap rather than a reload -- what setPlayhead asks before choosing an
76	// in-place seek, which the swap beats.
77	func (p *Player) Preloaded(file string, start float64) bool {
78		s := p.spare
79		return s != nil && s.ready && s.loaded == file && math.Abs(s.at-start) < preloadTol
80	}
81	
82	// swapIn is PlaySegment's first question: is the spare sitting at exactly
83	// this? If so the two pipelines change places and the answer is yes. A
84	// segment with a stop is never swapped in -- the spare prerolls with none,
85	// and the cut editor never asks for one.
86	func (p *Player) swapIn(file string, start, stop float64, play bool) bool {
87		s := p.spare
88		if stop > 0 || !p.Preloaded(file, start) {
89			return false
90		}
91		p.pb, s.pb = s.pb, p.pb
92		p.gain, s.gain = s.gain, p.gain
93		p.video, s.video = s.video, p.video
94		// the old pipeline is the spare now: parked, holding nothing
95		s.loaded, s.ready, s.pend = "", false, -1
96		s.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
97		p.loaded = file
98		p.pendStart, p.pendStop, p.pendPlay = -1, -1, false
99		p.ended = false
100		p.lastStart, p.lastStop = start, stop
101		p.seekRate = s.seekRate
102		if !p.still {
103			p.Picture.SetPaintable(p.video) // a card over the picture stays; ShowVideo finds the new one
104		}
105		setGain(p.gain, p.pb, p.vol(), p.ownMute)
106		if math.Abs(p.rate-p.seekRate) > 1e-6 {
107			p.SeekTo(start) // prerolled at the old clock: one seek in place puts it on the new
108		}
109		if play {
110			p.pb.SetState(gst.StatePlaying)
111			p.setPlaying(true)
112		} else {
113			p.setPlaying(false)
114		}
115		for _, a := range p.mix {
116			a.cue(start, play, p.rate, p.stopFor(a))
117		}
118		return true
119	}
120	
121	// dropSpare forgets what the spare holds. The pipeline stays: it is reused by
122	// the next Preload.
123	func (p *Player) dropSpare() {
124		if s := p.spare; s != nil {
125			s.loaded, s.ready, s.pend = "", false, -1
126			s.pb.SetState(gst.StateReady)
127		}
128	}
129	
130	// msg is the spare's bus: the uri has prerolled, so the seek is made; the
131	// seek has prerolled, so it is ready. An error is a spare that holds nothing
132	// -- the cut will be a reload, which will then say what is wrong with the
133	// file in the usual place.
134	func (s *spare) msg(msg *gst.Message) {
135		switch msg.Type() {
136		case gst.MessageAsyncDone:
137			if s.pend >= 0 {
138				at := s.pend
139				s.pend = -1
140				s.pb.Seek(s.seekRate, gst.FormatTime,
141					gst.SeekFlagFlush|gst.SeekFlagAccurate,
142					gst.SeekTypeSet, at, gst.SeekTypeNone, 0)
143				return
144			}
145			if s.loaded != "" {
146				s.ready = true
147			}
148		case gst.MessageError:
149			s.loaded, s.ready, s.pend = "", false, -1
150		}
151	}

3	// Where the line is going next, said to the player ahead of time.
4	//
5	// The transport moves the line without being asked in three places: the gap
6	// skip (a clip ends, the next begins), the review (a join's seconds are
7	// heard, the next join's run-up is sought) and the walk-on (a recording ends,
8	// the next begins). Each of those is a jump the tick will make, and each is
9	// known seconds before it is made. This tells the player's spare pipeline
10	// (player_spare.go) so the jump is a swap and not a reload.
11	
12	import "math"
13	
14	// preloadLead is how far ahead of a jump the spare is asked for it. A
15	// preroll is a few hundred milliseconds on a local file; three seconds is
16	// that with room for a slow disk, and short enough that a hand moving the
17	// line does not have a stale preroll waiting for long.
18	const preloadLead = 3.0
19	
20	// jumpAhead is the cut's own jumps, pure: the session second the line will
21	// be put at next (to) and when (at), if that is within lead seconds of t.
22	// Under ▶✂ a clip's end is a jump to the next clip; under a review a seam's
23	// window closing is a jump to the next seam's run-up, unless that run-up is
24	// already behind the line and is simply played into. The earlier of the two
25	// is the answer, since it comes first.
26	func jumpAhead(segs []cutSeg, t float64, cutOnly, review bool, seam int, lead float64) (at, to float64, ok bool) {
27		at = math.Inf(1)
28		if cutOnly {
29			if cur, _ := gapAt(segs, t); cur >= 0 && cur+1 < len(segs) && segs[cur].E-t < lead {
30				at, to, ok = segs[cur].E, segs[cur+1].S, true
31			}
32		}
33		if review && seam >= 0 && seam+1 < len(segs)-1 {
34			_, end := reviewWindow(segs, seam)
35			from, _ := reviewWindow(segs, seam+1)
36			if from > end && end-t < lead && end < at {
37				at, to, ok = end, from, true
38			}
39		}
40		return at, to, ok
41	}
42	
43	// preloadAhead is the tick's call: whichever jump comes first -- the cut's
44	// own (jumpAhead) or the recording under the line running out -- the spare
45	// is pointed at where it lands. Nothing to do while nothing is coming.
46	func (ed *cutEditor) preloadAhead() {
47		v := ed.playVideo
48		if ed.player == nil || v == nil {
49			return
50		}
51		t := ed.playhead
52		at, to, ok := jumpAhead(ed.segs, t, ed.cutOnly, ed.reviewOn, ed.review, preloadLead)
53		// the file's end is a jump in every mode (walkOn): to the next recording
54		if end := v.start + v.dur; end-t < preloadLead && end < at {
55			if nt, ok2 := ed.recordingAfter(end); ok2 {
56				at, to, ok = end, nt, true
57			}
58		}
59		if !ok {
60			return
61		}
62		to = ed.playable(to)
63		if nv := ed.videoAt(to); nv != nil {
64			ed.player.Preload(nv.path, nv.at(to))
65		}
66	}

68	// recordingAfter is the first second of the first recording that starts at
69	// or after t, other than the one playing -- where walkOn will go.
70	func (ed *cutEditor) recordingAfter(t float64) (float64, bool) {
71		best := math.Inf(1)
72		for i := range ed.vids {
73			if v := &ed.vids[i]; v != ed.playVideo && v.start >= t-0.01 && v.start < best {
74				best = v.start
75			}
76		}
77		if math.IsInf(best, 1) {
78			return 0, false
79		}
80		return best, true
81	}

2916	// fpsArgs decides the output's frame timing, explicitly in every direction.
2917	// Left to itself ffmpeg decides per container and per whether a rate was named,
2918	// so the same checkbox would have meant different things depending on a
2919	// dropdown three rows up.
2920	//
2921	// A ceiling and pure passthrough cannot be asked for together: -fpsmax next to
2922	// an explicit -fps_mode vfr is refused as contradictory ("One of -r/-fpsmax was
2923	// specified together a non-CFR -fps_mode"). So a rate under VFR goes in as
2924	// -fpsmax, which is a ceiling rather than a target -- footage slower than it
2925	// keeps its own rate instead of being duplicated up onto the grid, and footage
2926	// faster is dropped down to it. That is what a headset capture wants: 72 is the
2927	// peak it reaches, not the rate it holds. With no rate named there is nothing
2928	// to clamp, and every source timestamp goes through as it came.
2929	func fpsArgs(st prodSettings) []string {

2931		case !st.VFR:

2933		case st.FPS > 0:
2934			return []string{"-fpsmax", fmt.Sprintf("%g", st.FPS)}
2935		default:
2936			return []string{"-fps_mode", "vfr"}
2937		}
2938	}

2944			return []string{"-c:v", "libx265", "-preset", st.Preset,
2945				"-crf", strconv.Itoa(st.CRF), "-tag:v", "hvc1", "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p"}
2946		case "vp9":
2947			return []string{"-c:v", "libvpx-vp9", "-crf", strconv.Itoa(st.CRF), "-b:v", "0",
2948				"-row-mt", "1", "-cpu-used", vp9Speed(st.Preset), "-pix_fmt", "yuv420p"}
2949		default:

2952			// the file plays in software and tears on every GPU. Four keeps the

3074	// spokenHere is what to add to a dropped-clip message when narration lines
3075	// were written on it; empty for a clip nobody wrote on.
3076	func spokenHere(entries []narrEntry, s cutSeg) string {
3077		n := 0
3078		for _, e := range matchEntries(entries, s) {
3079			if strings.TrimSpace(e.Text) != "" {
3080				n++
3081			}
3082		}
3083		switch n {
3084		case 0:
3085			return ""
3086		case 1:
3087			return " — the narration line written on it is dropped with it"
3088		default:
3089			return fmt.Sprintf(" — the %d narration lines written on it are dropped with it", n)
3090		}

3093	// matchEntries finds the narration written for a segment, every line of it in
3094	// placement order. Real overlap is enough, merely touching is not: a cut
3095	// edited after narrating can shift, and a line silently dropped is the worst
3096	// failure here.
3097	func matchEntries(entries []narrEntry, s cutSeg) []*narrEntry {
3098		var out []*narrEntry
3099		for i := range entries {
3100			e := &entries[i]
3101			if s.E <= s.S {
3102				// a card or a freeze occupies no span of the session, so overlap
3103				// cannot find its lines: they are the entries written exactly on it
3104				if math.Abs(e.S-s.S) <= 0.05 && math.Abs(e.E-s.E) <= 0.05 {
3105					out = append(out, e)
3106				}
3107				continue
3108			}
3109			ov := math.Min(e.E, s.E) - math.Max(e.S, s.S)
3110			shorter := math.Min(e.E-e.S, s.E-s.S)
3111			if ov > 0 && (shorter <= 0 || ov >= shorter/2) {
3112				out = append(out, e)
3113			}
3114		}
3115		sort.SliceStable(out, func(a, b int) bool { return out[a].At < out[b].At })
3116		return out
3117	}

3125	}

3127	// wrapSub breaks a line into at most two subtitle rows of readable width.
3128	func wrapSub(s string) string {
3129		words := strings.Fields(s)
3130		var rows []string
3131		cur := ""
3132		for _, w := range words {
3133			if cur == "" {
3134				cur = w
3135			} else if len(cur)+1+len(w) <= 42 {
3136				cur += " " + w
3137			} else {
3138				rows = append(rows, cur)
3139				cur = w
3140			}
3141		}
3142		if cur != "" {
3143			rows = append(rows, cur)
3144		}
3145		if len(rows) > 2 { // rebalance rather than drop text off the screen
3146			joined := strings.Join(rows, " ")
3147			half := len(joined) / 2
3148			cut := strings.LastIndex(joined[:half], " ")
3149			if cut < 0 {
3150				cut = half
3151			}
3152			rows = []string{joined[:cut], joined[cut+1:]}
3153		}
3154		return strings.Join(rows, "\n")
3155	}

3164	func subText(ln prodLine) string {

3170		}

3174	// ffEscape quotes a path for use inside a filtergraph argument, where ':' and
3175	// ',' separate options and '\' escapes.
3176	func ffEscape(p string) string {

3178			`\`, `\\`, `:`, `\:`, `'`, `\'`, `[`, `\[`, `]`, `\]`, `,`, `\,`,
3179		).Replace(p)

3182	// subCue is one line of the subtitle track on the produced timeline.
3183	type subCue struct {
3184		s, e float64
3185		text string
3186	}

3188	// tidyCues makes the track watchable: it holds each line until the next one
3189	// begins, drops the ones too short to read, and never lets two overlap.
3190	//
3191	// The cues come off the transcript one line each, and the gap between two
3192	// lines of the same sentence is the breath between them -- five, twenty,
3193	// eighty milliseconds. At thirty frames a second every one of those is the
3194	// text blanking for a frame and coming back, and a sentence of six lines
3195	// flickers six times. Nobody means those gaps to be seen: a subtitle that
3196	// disappears between two words is a fault of the clock, not a choice. So a
3197	// gap under subHold is closed by holding the line that is already up.
3198	//
3199	// A line's own length is left alone where the gap is a real pause -- a held
3200	// caption over silence is what an editor would do anyway -- except at the very
3201	// end, where nothing follows to hold it against.
3202	func tidyCues(in []subCue) []subCue {
3203		var out []subCue
3204		for _, c := range in {
3205			if c.e < c.s {
3206				c.e = c.s
3207			}
3208			if n := len(out); n > 0 {
3209				p := &out[n-1]
3210				if c.s < p.e {
3211					p.e = c.s // no two on screen at once, whatever the clocks said
3212				}
3213				if c.s-p.e < subHold {
3214					p.e = c.s // the breath between two lines is not a blank screen
3215				}
3216				if p.e-p.s < subMin {
3217					// too short to read even after the hold: fold its words into
3218					// the line that follows rather than flashing them
3219					c.s, c.text = p.s, p.text+"\n"+c.text
3220					out = out[:n-1]
3221				}
3222			}
3223			out = append(out, c)
3224		}
3225		// ...and the last line has nothing to hold against, so it is given the
3226		// time a reader needs rather than the time it was spoken in
3227		if n := len(out); n > 0 && out[n-1].e-out[n-1].s < subMin {
3228			out[n-1].e = out[n-1].s + subMin
3229		}
3230		return out
3231	}
3232	
3233	const (
3234		// a gap between two lines shorter than this is a breath, not a blank
3235		// screen: the line already up is held across it
3236		subHold = 1.2
3237		// ...and no line is on screen for less than this, however briefly it was
3238		// said: under it a reader sees a flash rather than a word
3239		subMin = 0.8
3240	)

3242	// pickedLangs is the languages ticked, in the order the menu lists them. The
3243	// language the session is SPOKEN in is never among them, whatever a tick says:
3244	// its track is written anyway, and translating a language into itself is a

3246	func (p *producer) pickedLangs() []string {
3247		// asrLanguage and not projectLanguage: the box on the Prepare page is
3248		// EMPTY by default and shows "en" as a placeholder, so the project's own
3249		// answer is "" until somebody types in it -- and "" matches no language,
3250		// which is why English stayed in the menu of an English session.
3251		own := p.a.asrLanguage()

3258				out = append(out, l.code)

3268	func (p *producer) syncLangs() {

3281				names = append(names, n)

3283		}
3284		if len(names) == 0 {
3285			p.langs.SetLabel("none")

3288		p.langs.SetLabel(strings.Join(names, ", "))

3	// The scrollbar's thumb, geared down.
4	//
5	// The bar under the tracks is a stock GtkScrollbar over the page's own
6	// adjustment, and a stock scrollbar maps the thumb onto the whole range: one
7	// pixel of thumb is totalW/troughW pixels of timeline. Zoomed right in on a
8	// session of any length that is a couple of hundred timeline pixels -- a good
9	// part of what is on screen -- per pixel of drag, so the pictures whip past
10	// faster than they can be read, and the thumb is useless for the one thing it
11	// was picked up for, which was to look along the session.
12	//
13	// So the drag is geared: once a pixel of thumb would move the view by more
14	// than a fortieth of itself, it moves it by exactly that instead. The thumb
15	// then no longer stays under the pointer -- it cannot, the range is what it
16	// is -- but the view scrolls at a speed the eye can follow, and a screenful
17	// is always the same forty pixels of drag whatever the zoom. Below that ratio
18	// the bar is left entirely to GTK, thumb under pointer, as it always was: the
19	// gearing exists for the zoomed-in case and is not felt anywhere else. A
20	// click in the trough is GTK's too.
21	
22	import (
23		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gtk/v4"
24	)
25	
26	// gearPx is the drag, in pixels, that scrolls one screenful once the thumb
27	// is geared.
28	const gearPx = 40.0
29	
30	// scrollGear is how many timeline pixels one pixel of thumb drag moves:
31	// linear is what the stock bar would do, and the answer is that, held to a
32	// fortieth of the view.
33	func scrollGear(linear, viewW float64) float64 {
34		if lim := viewW / gearPx; linear > lim {
35			return lim
36		}
37		return linear
38	}
39	
40	// gearScrollbar puts the geared drag on the bar. A capture-phase gesture, so
41	// it sees the press before the scrollbar's own does; it claims the sequence
42	// only when the drag is geared, and denies it -- hands it to GTK untouched --
43	// for every press that is not on the thumb, or is on it at a zoom the stock
44	// bar serves fine.
45	func (ed *cutEditor) gearScrollbar() {
46		if ed.hbar == nil {
47			return
48		}
49		drag := gtk.NewGestureDrag()
50		drag.SetPropagationPhase(gtk.PhaseCapture)
51		var v0, gear float64
52		drag.ConnectDragBegin(func(x, _ float64) {
53			gear = 0
54			slider := cssChild(ed.hbar, "slider")
55			if slider == nil {
56				drag.SetState(gtk.EventSequenceDenied)
57				return
58			}
59			sb, ok := slider.ComputeBounds(ed.hbar)
60			if !ok || x < float64(sb.X()) || x > float64(sb.X()+sb.Width()) {
61				drag.SetState(gtk.EventSequenceDenied) // the trough: GTK pages
62				return
63			}
64			trough := slider.Parent()
65			if trough == nil {
66				drag.SetState(gtk.EventSequenceDenied)
67				return
68			}
69			tb, ok := gtk.BaseWidget(trough).ComputeBounds(ed.hbar)
70			if !ok || tb.Width()-sb.Width() <= 0 {
71				drag.SetState(gtk.EventSequenceDenied)
72				return
73			}
74			linear := (ed.hadj.Upper() - ed.hadj.PageSize()) / float64(tb.Width()-sb.Width())
75			g := scrollGear(linear, ed.viewW)
76			if g >= linear {
77				drag.SetState(gtk.EventSequenceDenied) // not geared: the stock drag
78				return
79			}
80			drag.SetState(gtk.EventSequenceClaimed)
81			v0, gear = ed.hadj.Value(), g
82		})
83		drag.ConnectDragUpdate(func(dx, _ float64) {
84			if gear > 0 {
85				ed.setOff(v0 + dx*gear)
86			}
87		})
88		drag.ConnectDragEnd(func(_, _ float64) { gear = 0 })
89		ed.hbar.AddController(drag)
90	}
91	
92	// cssChild is the first descendant of w with that CSS node name -- how a
93	// stock widget's parts are found, since a scrollbar hands out no handle to
94	// its slider.
95	func cssChild(w gtk.Widgetter, name string) *gtk.Widget {
96		for c := gtk.BaseWidget(w).FirstChild(); c != nil; c = gtk.BaseWidget(c).NextSibling() {
97			cw := gtk.BaseWidget(c)
98			if cw.CSSName() == name {
99				return cw
100			}
101			if d := cssChild(cw, name); d != nil {
102				return d
103			}
104		}
105		return nil
106	}

3	// The red line, remembered.
4	//
5	// Where the line stood is the one thing about a session the page forgot
6	// between openings: the cut came back, the effects came back, and the line
7	// stood at the top of the timeline, so the first thing every reopening
8	// started with was finding the place again. Now the second the line is on
9	// is written to a file of its own beside the cut and read back on the next
10	// reload, and the line is put there -- cued, so the picture is the frame it
11	// was, and scrolled into view.
12	//
13	// Its own file, not cut.json: cut.json coming into existence is what wakes
14	// Narrate and Produce up (persist), and a line moved over a project with no
15	// cut yet is not a cut. And not the project file, which is written by a
16	// comparing autosave and would find itself different ten times a second.
17	//
18	// Written once a second at most while the line moves, since playback moves
19	// it ten times a second and a file write per tick is a file write for
20	// nothing; the second's last position is what lands. Flushed when the window
21	// closes, so the position you closed on is the one you open on.

26		"path/filepath"

31	// lineSaveMs is the least time between two writes of the line.
32	const lineSaveMs = 1000
33	
34	type lineFile struct {
35		T float64 `json:"t"` // session second
36	}
37	
38	func (a *App) linePath() string { return filepath.Join(a.cutDir(), "line.json") }
39	
40	// noteLine is every hand on the line -- a click, a step, the tick -- saying
41	// it moved. The first says arms a write a second out; the ones that follow
42	// inside that second say nothing, and the write takes whatever the line is
43	// on when it fires.
44	func (ed *cutEditor) noteLine() {
45		if ed.a == nil || ed.a.outDir == "" || !ed.hasPlay || ed.lineArmed {
46			return
47		}
48		ed.lineArmed = true
49		arm := ed.lineArm
50		if arm == nil {
51			arm = func(ms uint, fn func() bool) { glib.TimeoutAdd(ms, fn) }
52		}
53		arm(lineSaveMs, func() bool {
54			ed.flushLine()
55			return false
56		})
57	}
58	
59	// flushLine writes the line now, if a write is owed. On the window closing,
60	// and from the timer noteLine armed.
61	func (ed *cutEditor) flushLine() {
62		if !ed.lineArmed {
63			return
64		}
65		ed.lineArmed = false
66		ed.saveLine()
67	}
68	
69	func (ed *cutEditor) saveLine() {
70		if ed.a == nil || ed.a.outDir == "" || !ed.hasPlay {
71			return
72		}
73		b, _ := json.Marshal(lineFile{T: ed.playhead})
74		os.MkdirAll(ed.a.cutDir(), 0o755)
75		if err := os.WriteFile(ed.a.linePath(), append(b, '\n'), 0o644); err != nil {
76			ed.a.logf("save line: %v", err)
77		}
78	}

80	// restoreLine puts the line where the last session left it, once per
81	// project: reload runs again whenever a run rewrites what the page shows,
82	// and a line you have since moved is not to be moved back. A second no
83	// recording covers -- the sources changed -- is left alone, and so is a
84	// project that never had a line.
85	func (ed *cutEditor) restoreLine() {
86		if ed.a == nil || ed.a.outDir == "" || ed.lineOf == ed.a.outDir {
87			return
88		}
89		ed.lineOf = ed.a.outDir
90		b, err := os.ReadFile(ed.a.linePath())

92			return
93		}

96			return
97		}
98		ed.setPlayhead(l.T)
99		ed.revealPlayhead()

// plus the moment of air the render leaves after it. It is the number every
// decision about a clip's length is made against.
func narrRun(lines []prodLine, tempo float64) float64 {

}

// packLines lays a clip's lines out in its slot and answers where the last one
// stops. Each starts where the writer placed it, but never before the line
// above has finished and a breath has passed -- so an overlong line pushes
// everything under it later, and it is the LAST line that falls off the end of
// the clip. The delays are written back into the slice, because that schedule
// is what the render feeds adelay.
//

// has to be able to ask the same question. Its own per-line ⚠ answers a
// different one -- "has THIS line room before the next" -- and cannot see the
// pushing, which is exactly what the render's "does not fit where it was
// placed" is complaining about (clipOverrun, narrate.go).
func packLines(lines []prodLine, tempo float64) float64 {
	if tempo <= 0 {
		tempo = 1 // a clip built by hand, and every arithmetic here divides
	}
	prev := 0.0
	for k := range lines {
		d := math.Max(narrLead, lines[k].at)
		if d < prev {
			d = prev
		}
		lines[k].delay = d
		prev = d + lines[k].dur/tempo + narrGap
	}
	return prev - narrGap
}

// milliseconds, never below the lead-in. Rounded rather than truncated, so a
// placement is out by at most half a millisecond either way.
func delayMS(delay float64) int {
	return int(math.Round(math.Max(narrLead, delay) * 1000))
}

}

// countOutputs is the same walk with the two halves kept apart. Prepare
// shows three of these at once and puts the age on hover: three sentences of
// the form above, side by side, is a paragraph across the bottom of a page.
func countOutputs(dir string) (n int, newest time.Time, size int64) {
	filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(_ string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
		if err != nil || d.IsDir() {
			return nil // an unreadable subtree is not worth a whole error line here
		}
		n++
		if fi, err := d.Info(); err == nil {
			size += fi.Size()
			if fi.ModTime().After(newest) {
				newest = fi.ModTime()
			}
		}
		return nil
	})
	return n, newest, size
}

func humanAgo(t time.Time) string {
	d := time.Since(t)
	switch {
	case d < time.Minute:
		return "just now"
	case d < time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d min ago", int(d.Minutes()))
	case d < 24*time.Hour:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d h ago", int(d.Hours()))
	case d < 48*time.Hour:
		return "yesterday"
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d days ago", int(d.Hours()/24))
	}
}

// logListMax is how many files a directory gets to name before it becomes a
// count. Prepare writes one frame per second of footage; a log carrying four
// thousand f000123.jpg lines is a log nobody scrolls, and the run's own
// messages would be buried in it.
const logListMax = 12

// logOutputs names what a step actually wrote, in the log, and returns the file
// count for the status line. The page shows the count; the names live here,
// because that is the place you can scroll back through after a run.
// GUI thread only -- callers are completion handlers.
func (a *App) logOutputs(label, dir string) int {
	n := a.logTree(dir, label) // label leads every path, so the log says which step
	if n == 0 {
		a.logf("    %s/: nothing written", label)
	}
	return n
}

func (a *App) logTree(dir, rel string) int {
	ents, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
	if err != nil {
		return 0
	}
	n := 0
	var files []os.DirEntry
	for _, e := range ents {
		if e.IsDir() {
			n += a.logTree(filepath.Join(dir, e.Name()), filepath.Join(rel, e.Name()))
			continue
		}
		files = append(files, e)
	}
	if len(files) > logListMax {
		a.logf("    %s/ — %d files (%s … %s)", rel, len(files),
			files[0].Name(), files[len(files)-1].Name())
	} else {
		for _, e := range files {
			size := ""
			if fi, err := e.Info(); err == nil {
				size = "  (" + humanSize(fi.Size()) + ")"
			}
			a.logf("    %s%s", filepath.Join(rel, e.Name()), size)
		}
	}
	return n + len(files)
}

func humanSize(n int64) string {
	switch {
	case n > 1<<20:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.1f MB", float64(n)/(1<<20))
	case n > 1<<10:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.0f kB", float64(n)/(1<<10))
	default:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d B", n)
	}
}

1	package main

3	// The Cut page's form column: the right half of the top row, where insert and
4	// effect forms live instead of modal dialogs, so the timeline and preview stay
5	// live while a question about the footage is answered. Showing a second form
6	// takes the first down and calls its gone, so a waiting dialog learns it will
7	// get no answer.
8	
9	import (
10		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gtk/v4"
11		"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/pango"
12	)
13	
14	// buildForm makes the column; with no form in it, it holds the view controls
15	// and the totals (formIdle). Three pieces, only the middle scrolls: the
16	// heading is pinned to the top and the buttons to the bottom, so a form taller
17	// than the column keeps its Place button on screen.
18	func (ed *cutEditor) buildForm() *gtk.Box {
19		ed.formTitle = gtk.NewLabel("")
20		ed.formTitle.SetXAlign(0)
21		ed.formTitle.SetHExpand(true)
22		ed.formTitle.AddCSSClass("heading")
23		ed.formTitle.SetEllipsize(pango.EllipsizeEnd)
24	
25		shut := flatIcon("window-close-symbolic", "close this form — nothing is lost that was not already saved", func() { ed.hideForm() })
26	
27		ed.formHead = gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 6)
28		ed.formHead.Append(ed.formTitle)
29		ed.formHead.Append(shut)
30	
31		// What the column holds when no form is open: the zoom and the thumbnail
32		// size, and what the cut comes to (filled in by buildCut). Set-once controls
33		// that do not belong on the bar of verbs, in a column that is otherwise empty
34		// exactly when nobody is zooming.
35		ed.formIdle = gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 6)
36		ed.formIdle.SetVExpand(true)
37	
38		ed.formBox = gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 8)
39		ed.formBox.Append(ed.formIdle)
40	
41		// one scrollbar for the column, and it is around the questions only.
42		//
43		// Not an overlay scrollbar, though it is the default: an overlay is drawn on
44		// top of whatever is under it, and what is under it here is the right-hand
45		// border of a framed box. A slider sitting on a box's own border, and with
46		// no border of its own, is what a column of these looks wrong as. Given its
47		// own gutter it is beside the boxes instead of on them.
48		pane := gtk.NewScrolledWindow()
49		pane.SetChild(ed.formBox)
50		pane.SetPolicy(gtk.PolicyNever, gtk.PolicyAutomatic)
51		pane.SetOverlayScrolling(false)
52		pane.SetVExpand(true)
53	
54		ed.formFoot = gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 0)
55	
56		col := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 8)
57		col.SetMarginTop(8)
58		col.SetMarginBottom(8)
59		col.SetMarginStart(6) // the handle's side; the preview beside it matches
60		col.SetMarginEnd(12)  // ...and the window's
61		col.Append(ed.formHead)
62		col.Append(pane)
63		col.Append(ed.formFoot)
64		ed.hideForm() // the heading belongs to a form, and there is none yet
65		return col
66	}
67	
68	// idleRow is one line of the quiet column: what it is, then the thing itself.
69	// Every line is named, including the ones whose "reading" is a control -- a
70	// row with no name in a column of named rows is the row you have to work out.
71	func idleRow(name string, w gtk.Widgetter) *gtk.Box {
72		l := dimLabel(name + ":")
73		l.SetWidthChars(13) // one column for the names, whatever the readings measure
74		l.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
75		row := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 6)
76		row.Append(l)
77		row.Append(w)
78		return row
79	}
80	
81	// idleRead is one of that column's readings: left-aligned, dim, and in the
82	// numeric face the clock uses, so a column of them lines up digit under digit.
83	func idleRead() *gtk.Label {
84		l := dimLabel("")
85		l.AddCSSClass("numeric")
86		return l
87	}
88	
89	// showFormFoot puts a form in the column, in place of whatever was there, with
90	// foot pinned under the scrolling part of it. Pass a nil foot for a form whose
91	// buttons are its own business.
92	func (ed *cutEditor) showFormFoot(title string, body, foot gtk.Widgetter, gone func()) {
93		if ed.formBox == nil {
94			return // headless: no page was built
95		}
96		ed.dropForm()
97		ed.formTitle.SetText(title)
98		ed.formHead.SetVisible(true)
99		ed.formIdle.SetVisible(false)
100		ed.formCur, ed.formGone = body, gone
101		ed.formBox.Append(body)
102		if foot != nil {
103			ed.formFootCur = foot
104			ed.formFoot.Append(foot)
105		}
106	}
107	
108	// hideForm empties the column and puts its own words back.
109	func (ed *cutEditor) hideForm() {
110		if ed.formBox == nil {
111			return
112		}
113		ed.dropForm()
114		ed.formTitle.SetText("")
115		ed.formHead.SetVisible(false)
116		ed.formIdle.SetVisible(true)
117	}
118	
119	// dropForm takes the current form out and tells its owner, in that order: gone
120	// is where widgets are let go of, and letting go of a widget that is still in
121	// the box is how a dropdown ends up pointing at a text view nobody can see.
122	func (ed *cutEditor) dropForm() {
123		// a live form's last burst of typing, before the form it belongs to is
124		// taken out from under it: the debounce is a few hundred ms, and closing
125		// the panel a moment after the last letter must not be how that letter is
126		// lost. flush is a no-op when nothing is owed (debounce.go).
127		if l := ed.fxLiveCur; l != nil {
128			l.d.flush()
129			ed.fxLiveCur, ed.fxLiveOn = nil, nil
130		}
131		if ed.formFootCur != nil {
132			ed.formFoot.Remove(ed.formFootCur)
133			ed.formFootCur = nil
134		}
135		if ed.formCur != nil {
136			ed.formBox.Remove(ed.formCur)
137			ed.formCur = nil
138		}
139		if g := ed.formGone; g != nil {
140			ed.formGone = nil
141			g()
142		}
143	}
144	
145	// cutForm is where a Cut-page dialog puts itself. Nil before the page is built,
146	// which is every headless test and nowhere else -- a form with nowhere to go is
147	// not shown at all rather than opened in a window, because everything that asks
148	// for one is a button on this page and cannot be pressed until it exists.
149	func (a *App) cutForm() *cutEditor {
150		if a.ed == nil || a.ed.formBox == nil {
151			return nil
152		}
153		return a.ed
154	}

1	package main

3	// Two speed effects over the same seconds: the rate is the MEAN of what they
4	// ask for. A stop is ×0 in that arithmetic, so the picture freezes only where
5	// the mean is nought -- a stop with nothing over it -- and a stop under a ×2
6	// comes out ×1.
7	
8	import (
9		"math"
10		"sort"
11	)
12	
13	// applied is the rate the render actually runs a stretch at. A frozen stretch
14	// has no observable rate -- the still covers it -- and ×0 is not a clip any
15	// encoder can build, so the footage under it runs at ×1, which is what it has
16	// always done (see cut_fxstill.go).
17	func (st rateStep) applied() float64 {
18		if st.rate <= 0 {
19			return 1
20		}
21		return st.rate
22	}
23	
24	// outLn is how long a stretch comes out on screen, which is the length the
25	// render measures it by.
26	func (st rateStep) outLn() float64 { return (st.t1 - st.t0) / st.applied() }
27	
28	// rateSpans is the whole cut's speed as flat stretches: every boundary any
29	// speed effect draws, and between two boundaries the rate they agree on.
30	// Seconds no effect covers are not in the list at all -- they run at ×1 by
31	// simply being left alone.
32	func rateSpans(fx []cutFx) []rateStep {
33		var all []rateStep
34		for _, f := range speedsOf(fx) {
35			if f.Dur <= 0 {
36				continue
37			}
38			if f.frozenFx() {
39				// a stop is one flat ×0 over its band; it has no stairs, because
40				// there is no ramping into and out of standing still
41				all = append(all, rateStep{f.T, f.T + f.Dur, 0})
42				continue
43			}
44			all = append(all, speedSteps(f)...)
45		}
46		if len(all) == 0 {
47			return nil
48		}
49		cuts := make([]float64, 0, 2*len(all))
50		for _, st := range all {
51			cuts = append(cuts, st.t0, st.t1)
52		}
53		sort.Float64s(cuts)
54		var out []rateStep
55		for i := 1; i < len(cuts); i++ {
56			t0, t1 := cuts[i-1], cuts[i]
57			if t1-t0 < 1e-9 {
58				continue
59			}
60			mid := (t0 + t1) / 2
61			sum, n := 0.0, 0
62			for _, st := range all {
63				if mid >= st.t0 && mid < st.t1 {
64					sum, n = sum+st.rate, n+1
65				}
66			}
67			if n == 0 {
68				continue // plain footage between two effects
69			}
70			out = append(out, rateStep{t0, t1, sum / float64(n)})
71		}
72		return healSpans(joinSpans(out))
73	}
74	
75	// joinSpans folds together neighbours that ask for the same thing, so a
76	// boundary two effects happen to share does not become a cut in the video.
77	func joinSpans(sp []rateStep) []rateStep {
78		var out []rateStep
79		for _, st := range sp {
80			if n := len(out); n > 0 && math.Abs(out[n-1].t1-st.t0) < 1e-9 &&
81				math.Abs(out[n-1].rate-st.rate) < 1e-9 {
82				out[n-1].t1 = st.t1
83				continue
84			}
85			out = append(out, st)
86		}
87		return out
88	}

91	// overlapping by a tenth of a second slice a sliver under minClipLn out of
92	// each other, and such a clip is not encoded (planClips). The sliver goes to
93	// a neighbour -- slightly the wrong speed for a tenth of a second beats
94	// footage going missing.
95	func healSpans(sp []rateStep) []rateStep {
96		for pass := 0; pass < len(sp)+1 && len(sp) > 0; pass++ {
97			k := -1
98			for i, st := range sp {
99				if st.outLn() >= minClipLn-1e-9 || !spanCuts(sp, i) {
100					continue
101				}
102				if k < 0 || st.outLn() < sp[k].outLn() {
103					k = i // the thinnest one first; the rest may heal with it
104				}
105			}
106			if k < 0 {
107				return sp
108			}
109			sp = absorbSpan(sp, k)
110		}
111		return sp

114	// spanCuts is whether a stretch is a cut in the finished video at all. One
115	// that runs at the same speed as both its neighbours -- and the footage
116	// outside the list runs at ×1 -- makes no clip of its own, so it has no length
117	// for the render to find too short. This is what keeps a very short stop from
118	// being healed away: on its own it splits nothing.
119	func spanCuts(sp []rateStep, i int) bool {
120		left, right := 1.0, 1.0
121		if i > 0 {
122			left = sp[i-1].applied()
123		}
124		if i < len(sp)-1 {
125			right = sp[i+1].applied()
126		}
127		a := sp[i].applied()
128		return math.Abs(a-left) > 1e-9 || math.Abs(a-right) > 1e-9
129	}

131	// absorbSpan hands stretch k's seconds to a neighbour -- the longer one, which

133	func absorbSpan(sp []rateStep, k int) []rateStep {
134		switch {
135		case len(sp) == 1:
136			return nil
137		case k == 0:

139			return joinSpans(sp[1:])

143		}
144		if sp[k-1].outLn() >= sp[k+1].outLn() {
145			sp[k-1].t1 = sp[k].t1
146		} else {
147			sp[k+1].t0 = sp[k].t0
148		}
149		return joinSpans(append(sp[:k:k], sp[k+1:]...))
150	}
151	
152	// fxMeanRate is what the effects covering session time t ask for between them,
153	// ×0 included: nought where the picture is frozen, ×1 where nothing covers t.
154	func fxMeanRate(fx []cutFx, t float64) float64 {
155		for _, st := range rateSpans(fx) {
156			if t >= st.t0 && t < st.t1 {
157				return st.rate
158			}
159		}
160		return 1
161	}

163	// frozenSpans is the session seconds a stop effect actually stands over: the
164	// stretches of its own band where the mean is nought. With nothing else over
165	// it that is the whole band, which is the ordinary case; where a ×2 crosses it
166	// the mean there is ×1 and the footage runs, so the still steps aside for

168	func frozenSpans(fx []cutFx, f cutFx) [][2]float64 {
169		if !f.frozenFx() || f.Dur <= 0 {
170			return nil
171		}
172		t0, t1 := f.T, f.T+f.Dur
173		var out [][2]float64
174		for _, st := range rateSpans(fx) {
175			if st.rate > 0 || st.t1 <= t0 || st.t0 >= t1 {
176				continue
177			}
178			s, e := math.Max(st.t0, t0), math.Min(st.t1, t1)
179			if e-s < 1e-9 {
180				continue
181			}
182			if n := len(out); n > 0 && math.Abs(out[n-1][1]-s) < 1e-9 {
183				out[n-1][1] = e
184				continue
185			}
186			out = append(out, [2]float64{s, e})
187		}
188		return out
189	}

3	// The <video> tag, written beside the video.
4	//
5	// A browser plays none of the subtitle tracks muxed into the mp4 -- in-band
6	// text is not something Firefox or Chrome offer at all -- and <track> parses
7	// WebVTT alone, so the .srt that VLC reads is the wrong file for a page. What
8	// a page needs is the .vtt files the render writes beside the video and a tag
9	// pointing at them, and getting that tag right is five minutes of somebody's
10	// afternoon, every time. So it is written out with the video: open it to check
11	// the result, or paste the four lines into the page they belong in.
12	
13	import (
14		"fmt"
15		"html"
16		"image/jpeg"
17		"os"
18		"path/filepath"
19		"sort"
20		"strings"
21	)
22	
23	// embedFile is where the tag goes: beside the video, named after it.
24	func embedFile(out string) string {
25		return strings.TrimSuffix(out, filepath.Ext(out)) + ".html"
26	}
27	
28	// posterFile is the still a <video> shows before it is played: the thumbnail,
29	// as a jpeg beside the video. A .jpg and not the thumbnail.png it comes from,
30	// because a poster is one frame of decoration on a page that already carries
31	// the video, and 200 kB of PNG is not worth it.
32	func posterFile(out string) string {
33		return strings.TrimSuffix(out, filepath.Ext(out)) + ".jpg"
34	}
35	
36	// webUnplayable says why a browser will not play this file, or "". The tag is
37	// written for every render, and a page is the one place where the container
38	// and codec chosen for a desktop player quietly stop working -- it is cheaper
39	// to read it in the log than to wonder at a black rectangle.
40	func webUnplayable(out, codec string) string {
41		switch {
42		case strings.EqualFold(filepath.Ext(out), ".mkv"):
43			return "no browser plays Matroska — render to mp4 or webm for a page"
44		case codec == "h265":
45			return "Firefox plays no h265 at all, and the others only where the machine " +
46				"decodes it in hardware — h264 is the one that plays everywhere"
47		}
48		return ""
49	}
50	
51	// writeEmbed writes the poster and the tag. Called when the whole run is over,
52	// not at the end of the render: the thumbnail is drawn by the other half of
53	// that run (produceRun), and a tag written before it landed would have no
54	// poster in it. Never an error worth failing a render for -- the video and the
55	// subtitles are on disk either way.
56	func (a *App) writeEmbed(out, codec string) {
57		if out == "" || !exists(out) {
58			return
59		}
60		poster := ""
61		if err := a.writePoster(out); err != nil {
62			a.logfIdle("    produce: no poster for the <video> tag (%v)", err)
63		} else {
64			poster = filepath.Base(posterFile(out))
65		}
66		tracks := a.embedTracks(out)
67		body := embedHTML(filepath.Base(out), poster, tracks)
68		if err := os.WriteFile(embedFile(out), []byte(body), 0o644); err != nil {
69			a.logfIdle("    produce: could not write %s (%v)", filepath.Base(embedFile(out)), err)
70			return
71		}
72		a.logfIdle(">>> the <video> tag for it: %s", embedFile(out))
73		if why := webUnplayable(out, codec); why != "" {
74			a.logfIdle("    (this video is not one a page can play: %s)", why)
75		}
76		if len(tracks) > 0 {
77			// the one that costs an afternoon: a <track> is fetched under the
78			// same-origin rule, and file:// counts as a different origin for
79			// every file. Opened from disk the video plays and the subtitles are
80			// simply absent, with nothing on screen to say why.
81			a.logfIdle("    (subtitles need it served over http -- opened as a file:// page " +
82				"the browser refuses every <track>)")
83		}
84	}
85	
86	// writePoster is the thumbnail as a jpeg beside the video.
87	func (a *App) writePoster(out string) error {
88		src := a.thumbFile()
89		if !exists(src) {
90			return fmt.Errorf("no thumbnail has been drawn yet")
91		}
92		img, err := pubDecode(src) // the thumbnail is a PNG; pubDecode takes any of them
93		if err != nil {
94			return err
95		}
96		f, err := os.Create(posterFile(out))
97		if err != nil {
98			return err
99		}
100		defer f.Close()
101		return jpeg.Encode(f, img, &jpeg.Options{Quality: 90})
102	}
103	
104	// embedTracks is the .vtt files that are actually beside the video, in the
105	// order a player should offer them: the video's own language first, the
106	// translations after it by name.
107	//
108	// Read off the DISK rather than taken from the render, because this runs after
109	// a press that may have skipped the encode entirely -- the subtitles from the
110	// render before are the subtitles this video has.
111	func (a *App) embedTracks(out string) []subTrack {
112		stem := strings.TrimSuffix(out, filepath.Ext(out))
113		own := a.asrLanguage()
114		var rest []subTrack
115		var first []subTrack
116		for _, p := range subSideFiles(out) {
117			if !strings.HasSuffix(p, ".vtt") || !exists(p) {
118				continue
119			}
120			// "<stem>.vtt" is the video's own language; "<stem>.de.vtt" names its
121			// own between two dots
122			code := own
123			if tail := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimPrefix(p, stem), ".vtt"); tail != "" {
124				code = strings.TrimPrefix(tail, ".")
125			}
126			t := subTrack{code: code, name: strings.ToUpper(code), path: p}
127			if _, n, ok := subLangOf(code); ok {
128				t.name = n
129			}
130			if p == stem+".vtt" {
131				first = append(first, t)
132				continue
133			}
134			rest = append(rest, t)
135		}
136		sort.Slice(rest, func(i, j int) bool { return rest[i].name < rest[j].name })
137		return append(first, rest...)
138	}
139	
140	// embedHTML is the tag itself. Bare -- no document around it, no styling --
141	// because it is written to be pasted into a page that has both, and it still
142	// opens in a browser on its own.
143	func embedHTML(video, poster string, tracks []subTrack) string {
144		var b strings.Builder
145		b.WriteString("<video")
146		if poster != "" {
147			fmt.Fprintf(&b, " poster=%q", html.EscapeString(poster))
148		}
149		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " controls src=%q preload=\"none\">\n", html.EscapeString(video))
150		for i, t := range tracks {
151			// default on the first alone: two default tracks is two sets of
152			// subtitles drawn over each other in some players
153			def := ""
154			if i == 0 {
155				def = " default"
156			}
157			fmt.Fprintf(&b, " <track label=%q kind=\"subtitles\" srclang=%q src=%q%s />\n",
158				html.EscapeString(t.name), html.EscapeString(t.code),
159				html.EscapeString(filepath.Base(t.path)), def)
160		}
161		b.WriteString("</video>\n")
162		return b.String()
163	}

3	// The render's half of the sound over a speed effect. Three answers are a
4	// filter (atempoChain, asetrateChain, hushCues); the two 1× answers are a
5	// plan: clip by clip, which second of which recording is read and for how
6	// long. Possible because a speed effect cuts the segment list at its edges
7	// (applyFx), so "off the picture's clock" is always about whole clips. No
8	// crossfade at the seam: half a dip at each side of the stream-copy join
9	// (sndDip).
10	
11	import (
12		"fmt"
13		"math"
14	)
15	
16	// hushCues is the seconds of one clip a speed effect asks to be silent, in the
17	// clip's output seconds, mapped as a volume band is (gainCues). A window, not
18	// a property of the clip: ×1 and a stop do not cut the segment list, so their
19	// bands lie INSIDE a clip.
20	func hushCues(fx []cutFx, sessS, span, rate, length float64) []textCue {
21		if length <= 0 || span <= 0 {
22			return nil
23		}
24		var out []textCue
25		for i, f := range fx {
26			if f.Kind != "speed" || f.sound() != sndMute {
27				continue
28			}
29			s, e, _, _, ok := cueClip(f.T, f.Dur, 0, 0, sessS, rate, length)
30			if !ok {
31				continue
32			}
33			out = append(out, textCue{fx: f, s: s, e: e, idx: i})
34		}
35		return out
36	}
37	
38	// hushExpr is every silent window of a clip as one enable expression, in the
39	// clip's own seconds -- the shape stillMute already builds for a stop, which
40	// this is the general case of. Empty when nothing is silenced.
41	func hushExpr(hushes []textCue, stills []stillCue) string {
42		expr := stillMute(stills)
43		for _, h := range hushes {
44			if h.e <= h.s {
45				continue
46			}
47			if expr != "" {
48				expr += "+"
49			}
50			expr += fmt.Sprintf("between(t,%.3f,%.3f)", h.s, h.e)
51		}
52		return expr
53	}
54	
55	// asetrateChain is the sound going with the picture by tape speed: the samples
56	// are simply declared to arrive faster, so the pitch rides the rate -- the
57	// fast-forward everybody knows the sound of. aresample puts the rate back
58	// afterwards, because everything downstream of here is 48 kHz.
59	//
60	// atempoChain is the other half of the same question and needs a chain of
61	// filters to get past its own limits; this one has no limits to get past.
62	func asetrateChain(rate float64) string {
63		if rate <= 0 || rate == 1 {
64			return ""
65		}
66		return fmt.Sprintf(",asetrate=48000*%g,aresample=48000", rate)
67	}
68	
69	// audioPlan marks the clips whose sound has come away from the picture: where
70	// it reads from, how far the run reaches, where the closing splice falls. One
71	// running read-head opens in sync where a 1×-sound effect starts and advances
72	// by each clip's SCREEN length; the picture advances by footage covered, and
73	// the difference is the gap.
74	//
75	//	sndFx     the run is that effect's clips and no more
76	//	sndScene  it runs to the end of the scene the effect is in
77	//
78	// A card, a held frame or a clip on no recording closes a run wherever it
79	// falls.
80	func audioPlan(clips []prodClip, fx []cutFx) {
81		run, open := 0, false
82		var mode, path string
83		var fxT, at, sess float64
84		var scene int
85		for i := range clips {
86			c := &clips[i]
87			playable := c.ins == "" && !c.freeze && c.video != nil
88			// what the effect covering this clip says. The clip's own middle, so
89			// a band that starts exactly where the clip does and one that ends
90			// there are both read as this clip's rather than the neighbour's.
91			mid := c.sessS + c.length*c.speed()/2
92			kind, f, has := sndAt(fx, mid)
93			if open {
94				switch {
95				case !playable:
96					open = false
97				case mode == sndFx:
98					open = has && math.Abs(f.T-fxT) < 1e-9
99				default:
100					open = c.scene == scene
101				}
102			}
103			if !open && playable && sndShifts(kind) && math.Abs(sndDebt(f)) >= 0.05 {
104				// a ×1 with one of these answers on it has nothing to come apart,
105				// and a run that opens with no gap is a run that only complicates
106				// the graph
107				open, mode, fxT, scene = true, kind, f.T, c.scene
108				path, at, sess = c.video.path, c.video.at(c.sessS), c.sessS
109				run++
110			}
111			if !open {
112				continue
113			}
114			c.audOwn, c.audRun, c.audPath, c.audAt, c.audSess = true, run, path, at, sess
115			c.audPitch = false // it is at 1×: there is no rate for a pitch to ride
116			at += c.length     // the sound reads on at its own speed
117			sess += c.length
118		}
119		// the pitch answer, which is a filter and not a plan -- and the splices,
120		// which are where a run stops being true
121		for i := range clips {
122			c := &clips[i]
123			if !c.audOwn {
124				if k, _, has := sndAt(fx, c.sessS+c.length*c.speed()/2); has && k == sndPitch {
125					c.audPitch = true
126				}
127				continue
128			}
129			if i+1 < len(clips) && clips[i+1].audRun == c.audRun {
130				continue // the run carries on: no seam here
131			}
132			// the sound jumps at this clip's end -- forward over what it never
133			// reached, or back over what it has already played -- so it fades out
134			// here and the clip that follows fades in
135			c.audOut = true
136			if i+1 < len(clips) {
137				clips[i+1].audIn = true
138			}
139		}
140	}
141	
142	// audDipChain is the two half-fades, in the clip's own seconds. in is the
143	// label the bed arrives on and the label it leaves on comes back, so a clip
144	// with no seam at either end costs nothing at all.
145	func audDipChain(c prodClip, in string) (string, string) {
146		var parts []string
147		if c.audIn {
148			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("afade=t=in:st=0:d=%.3f", sndDip))
149		}
150		if c.audOut && c.length > sndDip {
151			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("afade=t=out:st=%.3f:d=%.3f", c.length-sndDip, sndDip))
152		}
153		if len(parts) == 0 {
154			return "", in
155		}
156		out := "dip"
157		fc := "[" + in + "]" + parts[0]
158		for _, p := range parts[1:] {
159			fc += "," + p
160		}
161		return fc + "[" + out + "];", out
162	}
163

// ---- the cards themselves ----------------------------------------------------

// svgField is one thing to ask for: a parameter, what to call it, and what it
// says at the moment.
type svgField struct {
	Key   string
	Label string
	Hint  string
	Val   string
	// written out even when it is left empty. A tier row is: an empty D tier is
	// a board with a D on it and nothing in it, which is a thing people mean.
	Keep bool
	// a list that can hold image files, so the dialog offers to go and find them
	// rather than leaving a path to be typed by hand.
	Logo bool
}

// insFields is what an insert can be asked for before it is placed, and whether
// there is anything to ask at all. A card knows its own parameters; any other
// SVG answers with what it declares, and failing that with what its
// {{placeholders}} name; everything else -- a video, a still, an SVG that is
// just a picture -- has nothing to fill in.
func insFields(path string) ([]svgField, bool) {
	if insKind(path) != "svg" {
		return nil, false
	}
	file, q := insSplit(path)
	if f, ok := insForm(path, q); ok {
		return f, true
	}
	src, err := os.ReadFile(file)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, false
	}
	if h := svgHoles(src); len(h) > 0 {
		return h, true
	}
	return nil, false
}

// insForm is the same question insFields asks, of a card as the dialog has been
// editing it: the card is asked what it wants asked, so what the boxes are is
// the card's business and not the dialog's. A document that is not a card
// answers with what it declares, which is the same list every time -- but the
// values in it are the ones on screen.
func insForm(path string, q svgQuery) ([]svgField, bool) {
	file, _ := insSplit(path)
	src, err := os.ReadFile(file)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, false
	}
	if card, def := svgStamp(src); card != nil {
		return card.form(def.merge(q), src), true
	}
	if f := declaredFields(src, q); len(f) > 0 {
		return f, true
	}
	return nil, false
}

// svgCard is a picture the app draws. draw gets the file's parameters with the
// path's laid over them, the card's folder (what a logo is relative to) and
// the document itself, so a restyled board stays restyled. tmpl is the
// document as shipped. form is what to ask for, handed the document because
// labels and hints are written in it.
type svgCard struct {
	name string
	what string
	tmpl string
	draw func(q svgQuery, dir string, src []byte) []byte
	form func(q svgQuery, src []byte) []svgField
	// note is what a path asked for that the card cannot show, for the log. A
	// card has a fixed amount of room in it, and something typed into a board
	// that has no room left for it is otherwise a change nobody sees.
	note func(q svgQuery) string
}

var svgCardKinds = map[string]*svgCard{
	"tier": {
		name: "tier",

		tmpl: tierTemplate,
		draw: tierSVG,
		form: tierForm,
		note: tierNote,
	},
	"badge": {
		name: "badge",
		what: "one big tier letter that flies in, with a caption under it",
		draw: badgeSVG,
		form: badgeForm,
	},
}

// svgSeeds are the cards written into a project's assets folder, so the insert
// chooser has something to pick and a plain SVG viewer has something to show.
// The parameters here are the file's defaults: they are stamped into it, and
// what a path's "?" overrides.
// The badges come first and the board last, and that order is load-bearing: the
// board's own defaults put two of them on it, and a logo is embedded from the
// file, so a board drawn before a.svg exists is a board with the letter missing.
var svgSeeds = []struct {
	file string
	card string
	def  svgQuery
}{
	{"s.svg", "badge", svgQuery{{"label", "S"}}},
	{"a.svg", "badge", svgQuery{{"label", "A"}}},
	{"b.svg", "badge", svgQuery{{"label", "B"}}},
	{"c.svg", "badge", svgQuery{{"label", "C"}}},
	{"d.svg", "badge", svgQuery{{"label", "D"}}},
	{"f.svg", "badge", svgQuery{{"label", "F"}}},
	// the board arrives empty except for two chips that are not there at the
	// start and fly into it a second in -- which is the one thing about these
	// cards that a still cannot show, and is what the Just added line does
	{"tier.svg", "tier", svgQuery{{"new", "A[1.2s]: a.svg, B[1.8s]: b.svg"}}},
}

// writeSVGCards puts the built-in cards in dir, and never over one that is
// already there: these are starting points, and a card the user has edited is
// theirs. Returns the ones it actually wrote, for the log.
func writeSVGCards(dir string) ([]string, error) {
	if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var wrote []string
	for _, s := range svgSeeds {
		path := filepath.Join(dir, s.file)
		if exists(path) {
			continue
		}
		card := svgCardKinds[s.card]
		if card == nil {
			continue
		}
		// a card with a template is written as its template, holes and all: that
		// is the file people edit, and it opens as a board either way, since the
		// holes in it are the contents and not the picture. The parameters go
		// into the stamp, so the file still says what it is a picture of. A card
		// without a template is written drawn, as the finished picture it is.
		doc := stampArgs([]byte(card.tmpl), s.def)
		if card.tmpl == "" {

			return wrote, err
		}
		wrote = append(wrote, s.file)
	}

	if guide := filepath.Join(dir, cardGuideFile); !exists(guide) {
		if err := os.WriteFile(guide, []byte(cardGuide), 0o644); err != nil {
			return wrote, err
		}
		wrote = append(wrote, cardGuideFile)
	}
	return wrote, nil
}

// svgStamp reads what drew a document and what with, from the root element. A
// file nothing here drew has no stamp, which is the same answer as "not a card".
func svgStamp(src []byte) (*svgCard, svgQuery) {
	dec := xml.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(string(src)))
	dec.Strict = false
	for {
		tok, err := dec.Token()
		if err != nil {
			return nil, nil
		}
		t, ok := tok.(xml.StartElement)
		if !ok {
			continue
		}
		var card *svgCard
		var def svgQuery
		for _, a := range t.Attr {
			switch xmlName(a.Name) {
			case "data-naivepost":
				card = svgCardKinds[a.Value]
			case "data-naivepost-args":
				def = parseSVGQuery(a.Value)
			}
		}
		return card, def
	}
}

// insSVG is the picture an insert path names: the file, with its parameters
// applied. The note is how it was arrived at, for the log -- a path that asks
// for something the file cannot do has to say so rather than render the file
// unchanged and let the user find out in the video.
func insSVG(path string) (out []byte, note string, err error) {
	file, q := insSplit(path)
	src, err := os.ReadFile(file)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, "", err
	}
	// a card first, parameters or none: the file is a template, and what makes it
	// a picture is being drawn. Handing back the file itself would put {{row.label}}
	// in the video.
	if card, def := svgStamp(src); card != nil {
		q = def.merge(q)
		note := "drawn by the built-in " + card.name + " card"
		if card.note != nil {
			if n := card.note(q); n != "" {
				note += ", except that " + n
			}
		}
		return card.draw(q, filepath.Dir(file), src), note, nil
	}
	if len(q) == 0 {
		return src, "", nil
	}
	if len(svgHoles(src)) > 0 {
		return svgFill(src, q), "filled in", nil
	}
	return src, "has no {{placeholders}} and was not drawn by a card, so its parameters " +
		"were ignored", nil
}

// ---- drawing -----------------------------------------------------------------

// A card is drawn at 1920x1080 whatever the video is: it is scaled to fit the
// footage's frame at render time (clipBox), and an SVG scales without loss.
const (
	cardW    = 1920.0
	cardH    = 1080.0
	cardBG   = "#14171c"
	cardFG   = "#e6e9ef"
	cardInk  = "#16181d" // text on a tier colour, which is always a light one
	cardFont = "DejaVu Sans, Liberation Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif"
	cardHold = 2.2 // seconds the finished card stands still before the slot ends
)

// How a tier board that has something new on it spends its time: the board so
// far is replayed at tierCatchUp of its own pace, and then the new item gets
// more time on its own than any of it had. A third is about as fast as the
// recap can go and still be followed; below that the rows land on top of each
// other and it reads as a flash rather than as a board being rebuilt.
const (
	tierCatchUp = 0.35 // of its usual pace, for what was already on the board
	tierNewBeat = 0.25 // the board stands still this long before the new item
	tierNewStep = 0.45 // between two new items, on the rare board that has two
	tierNewFly  = 0.6  // the new item's own flight, slower than any of the recap

60	const youtubeSystem = `You write the upload text for a finished video on YouTube: its title, and the description that sits under it.
61	
62	You are given what the video is made of -- its clips, what was seen and said in each, and the narration that was written over it. That is the video.
63	
64	What the user context singles out is what the description should lead with. Answer in the upload text's shape.
65	
66	The title.
67	
68	- Four to seven words. It is the YouTube title, and it is also printed across the upper part of the thumbnail afterwards, read at the size of a phone's sidebar -- every extra word costs one that mattered.
69	- Say the specific thing that happens in THIS video: the moment, the mistake, the win, the thing nobody expected. A title that would fit any session like it is a wasted title.
70	- Plain words people say out loud. No colons splitting a subtitle off, no clickbait punctuation, no ALL CAPS -- it is drawn in large letters already.
71	- Never promise something the clips do not contain: a title is a claim about the video, and this one is the claim most people will only ever read.
72	
73	The thumbnail.
74	
75	There are two ways to answer for it, and the user context decides which.
76	
77	- Where the context asks for a picture the video ALREADY CONTAINS -- a slide, a title card, a particular moment, anything phrased as "use the frame that shows ...", "pick one", "do not generate" -- the thumbnail line is a frame line: answer it as "THUMBNAIL: frame: clip <n> +<seconds>", naming the clip whose block that picture is described in and the offset stamped on the EVENT line that describes it -- both copied off the brief, neither worked out -- and write no instruction anywhere. The editor takes that frame as it is and prints the title onto it. This is the better answer whenever the context offers it: a frame out of the video cannot promise something the video does not contain.
78	- Otherwise the thumbnail line is the instruction below, and no second is named.
79	
80	The thumbnail instruction.
81	
82	- One or two sentences telling the image model how to compose ONE picture out of the frames: what this video is about, and the moment it shows.
83	- It is an instruction, not a description. Anything you do not mention is left alone, so describing the whole scene gets a picture of something else instead of the moment that was filmed. Say what to combine, brighten, push forward, or clear out of the way.
84	- Name only things the clips contain. "Add the dragon" to a video with no dragon in it is a thumbnail that lies about the video.
85	
86	The description.
87	
88	- Open with one or two sentences that say what happens in this video, in plain language, and make someone want to watch it. This first line is the only part shown before "...more", so it has to work alone.
89	- Then a short paragraph, three or four sentences, on what the session actually was: where it is set, who is in it, what went right and wrong.
90	- Then a chapter list if the video has distinct beats -- one line per beat, "0:00 What this is", at the time the clip list gives for that clip ("at 1:23 in the video"), never a session time. Only if the beats are real; a made-up timestamp is worse than no chapter list.
91	- Finish with a line of five to eight hashtags, lower case, naming what this is, where it is set and the kind of moment. No hashtag salad.
92	
93	Voice.
94	
95	- The voice of someone who was there and is telling a friend about it, not a press release. Contractions are fine.
96	- No emoji walls, no "smash that like button", no promises about upload schedules, no links to things you were not told exist.`

170		cx, cy := 0.5, 0.5

188	// a radio saying which was the base -- up to the list. The radio's answer is
189	// applied by moving that frame to the front, where the answer now lives.
190	func (st pubSettings) migrate() pubSettings {
191		st.Frames = moveToFront(append([]string(nil), st.Frames...), st.Base)
192		st.Base = 0
193		// a project from when the picture printed the entry's words: it was
194		// printing them unless title_off said otherwise, and either way that
195		// question has been answered once already

206		// model as the description of a picture -- which is how a run came back
207		// generation_failed with no thumbnail at all. One line only: a real
208		// instruction does not fit on one and start with the label.
209		if p := strings.TrimSpace(st.Prompt); !strings.Contains(p, "\n") {
210			if _, _, ok := peelLabel(p, "frame:"); ok {

217	// moveToFront makes fs[i] the base. Out-of-range is a no-op rather than an
218	// error: i comes from a project file and from a model's reply, and neither is
219	// trustworthy enough to panic on.
220	func moveToFront(fs []string, i int) []string {
221		if i <= 0 || i >= len(fs) {
222			return fs
223		}
224		out := append([]string{fs[i]}, fs[:i]...)
225		return append(out, fs[i+1:]...)
226	}
