425		// words from then on (pubSettings.ThumbTitle): rewording the upload's
426		// title is not an instruction to redraw the words on a picture that may
427		// have been cropped, moved and reworded around them.
428	
429		p.desc, descBox = p.textBox(8, "The text under the video on the YouTube page. Written by the "+
430			"prompt above, and yours to rewrite.")
431	
432		// ↻ sits on the Title heading because the title is the first thing it
433		// rewrites -- it is one call and it writes all three, the instruction on the
434		// other side of the page included -- and it is the only thing that rewrites
435		// them: ▶ writes them once and then never touches them again
436		p.suggest = gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("view-refresh-symbolic")
437		p.suggest.AddCSSClass("flat")
438		p.suggest.SetTooltipText("Ask the model for a fresh title, thumbnail instruction and " +
439			"description — the only thing that does. ▶ never rewrites text that has already been " +
440			"written, and nothing here redraws the picture; ▶ does that")
441		p.suggest.ConnectClicked(func() { a.publishSuggest() })
442	
443		wrote := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 6)
444		// no margins of its own: the words and the encoder settings under them are
445		// two rows of one column, and the column carries the margins for both
446		// (buildProduce). Its own pair put the words 12 further in than the
447		// settings, so the two halves of one column had two right edges.
448		wrote.Append(p.a.heading("Title", "The YouTube title, printed across the top of the thumbnail",
449			p.suggest))
450		wrote.Append(p.title)
451		wrote.Append(p.a.heading("YouTube description", "The text under the video on the upload page"))
452		wrote.Append(descBox)
453		descBox.SetVExpand(true)
454		wrote.SetVExpand(true)
455	
456		// no Outputs row of its own: the thumbnail and the words are written
457		// under produce/ with the video, and the page has one Outputs group
458		// (producer.updateOut)
459		p.refresh()
460		return drawScroll, wrote
461	}
462	
463	// heading is the one-line label above each field, with anything the caller
464	// wants on its right. It joins the same size group every prompt box's heading
465	// row is in, so the fields on this side of the divider line up with the prompts
466	// on the other.
467	func (a *App) heading(title, tip string, extra ...gtk.Widgetter) *gtk.Box {
468		l := gtk.NewLabel(title)
469		l.SetXAlign(0)
470		l.SetHExpand(true)
471		l.SetEllipsize(pango.EllipsizeEnd)
472		l.AddCSSClass("heading")
473		l.SetTooltipText(tip)
474		row := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
475		row.Append(l)
476		for _, w := range extra {
477			row.Append(w)
478		}
479		if a.headGroup == nil {
480			a.headGroup = gtk.NewSizeGroup(gtk.SizeGroupVertical)
481		}
482		a.headGroup.AddWidget(row)
483		return row
484	}
485	
486	// textBox is one of the editable result fields, floored at lines of text.
487	// Monospace, like every editable box in the app, and the floor is measured in
488	// monospace lines (a few px taller than the proportional font).
489	func (p *publisher) textBox(lines int, tip string) (*gtk.TextView, *gtk.ScrolledWindow) {
490		tv := gtk.NewTextView()
491		tv.SetMonospace(true)
492		tv.SetWrapMode(gtk.WrapWord)
493		tv.SetTopMargin(4)
494		tv.SetBottomMargin(4)
495		tv.SetLeftMargin(6)
496		tv.SetRightMargin(6)
497		tv.SetTooltipText(tip)
498		sc := gtk.NewScrolledWindow()
499		sc.SetChild(tv)
500		sc.SetPolicy(gtk.PolicyNever, gtk.PolicyAutomatic)
501		sc.SetSizeRequest(-1, lines*monoLineH+8)
502		sc.AddCSSClass("frame")
503		return tv, sc
504	}
505	
506	// monoLineH is a monospace line's height at the app's font size, near enough
507	// for a size REQUEST: the box scrolls, so being a pixel out costs nothing, and
508	// measuring it properly means building a widget to ask (narrate.go does, for a
509	// number that has to be exact).
510	const monoLineH = 20
511	
512	// setFrames replaces the row. Everything that changes the list goes through
513	// here -- a user gesture and apply alike -- so one place keeps the widgets,
514	// the cap and the Inputs line in step. Nothing flags the edit beyond that:
515	// the project is bytes-compared by the autosave. The cap lives here rather
516	// than on the Add button so that it also holds for a hand-edited project
517	// file: the row is what gets attached to the vision call, and twenty images
518	// is a call that costs a fortune and answers worse.
519	func (p *publisher) setFrames(fs []string) {
520		p.frames = append([]string(nil), fs...)
521		if len(p.frames) > maxPubFrames {
522			p.frames = p.frames[:maxPubFrames]
523		}
524		p.rebuildFrames()
525		p.a.updateProduceInfo() // the page's Inputs row counts these images
526	}
527	
528	// rebuildFrames throws the row away and builds it again from p.frames. Cheaper
529	// to reason about than editing it in place: a row whose length changes has to
530	// renumber every slot after the one that moved anyway, and "Ref 3" left over
531	// beside the second image is the kind of wrong that is never noticed.
532	func (p *publisher) rebuildFrames() {
533		if p.framesBox == nil {
534			return
535		}
536		for c := p.framesBox.FirstChild(); c != nil; c = p.framesBox.FirstChild() {
537			p.framesBox.Remove(c)
538		}
539		if len(p.frames) == 0 {
540			// an empty row is a legitimate state, not an error, so it says what it
541			// will do rather than looking like something failed to load
542			empty := gtk.NewLabel("No image — the thumbnail will be drawn from the instruction alone.\n" +
543				"Add image… to edit one of your own frames instead.")
544			empty.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
545			empty.SetJustify(gtk.JustifyCenter)
546			empty.SetVExpand(true)
547			p.framesBox.Append(empty)
548		}
549		for i, f := range p.frames {
550			s := &pubSlot{p: p, i: i, path: f}
551			p.framesBox.Append(s.build())
552		}
553		if p.addFrame != nil {
554			p.addFrame.SetSensitive(len(p.frames) < maxPubFrames)
555		}
556	}
557	
558	// addImage appends one. New images go to the END, never the front: appending
559	// cannot silently change which picture is being edited, and promoting is one
560	// click away for when that is what was meant.
561	func (p *publisher) addImage() {
562		if len(p.frames) >= maxPubFrames {
563			return
564		}
565		start := ""
566		if n := len(p.frames); n > 0 {
567			start = filepath.Dir(p.frames[n-1])
568		}
569		p.pickImage(fmt.Sprintf("Image %d", len(p.frames)+1), start, func(path string) {
570			p.setFrames(append(p.frames, path))
571		})
572	}
573	
574	// useAsThumbnail makes this picture the thumbnail without drawing anything:
575	// it is written as the plain copy and the words are printed onto it, which is
576	// the same last step a drawn one gets (recomposite).
577	//
578	// It exists because a session often already contains the picture. The frame
579	// where the tower is lit and centred is a better thumbnail than anything a
580	// model will invent from it, and until now the only way to get it there was
581	// to make it the base and ask sd.cpp to change as little as possible -- a GPU
582	// run to approximate a file that was already on disk.
583	//
584	// Cropped like the base is (pubCropRect): a thumbnail is the video's shape,
585	// and a widescreen frame dropped whole into a vertical thumbnail would be
586	// letterboxed by whatever showed it.
587	func (s *pubSlot) useAsThumbnail() {
588		p := s.p
589		if p.a.busy() {
590			return
591		}
592		dir := p.a.publishDir()
593		if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o755); err != nil {
594			p.a.logf("thumbnail: %v", err)
595			return
596		}
597		w, h := pubBox(p.a.produceCut().Aspect)
598		srcA, outA := imageAspect(s.path), float64(w)/float64(h)
599		if err := pubWriteCropped(s.path, p.snapshot().cropRect(srcA, outA), srcA, outA, w, h,
600			p.a.thumbPlain()); err != nil {
601			p.a.logf("thumbnail: %v", err)
602			p.a.setStatus("could not use that image — see log")
603			return
604		}
605		// the choice, remembered: ▶ prints the words onto it and draws nothing,
606		// until ↻ over the thumbnail says otherwise
607		st := p.snapshot()
608		st.Own = true
609		p.apply(st)
610		p.seedThumbTitle() // the first picture to exist takes the title as its line
611		p.a.logf(">>> publish: %s is the thumbnail, as it is — no model, no GPU, and ▶ will not redraw it",
612			filepath.Base(s.path))
613		p.recomposite() // the title and the marked words go on, as on a drawn one
614		p.a.updateGates()
615		p.a.setStatus("thumbnail taken from " + filepath.Base(s.path) +
616			" — the words are printed on it; ↻ draws over it")
617	}
618	
619	func (s *pubSlot) build() gtk.Widgetter {
620		pic := gtk.NewPicture()
621		pic.SetCanShrink(true)
622		// Big enough to judge by. At thumbnail size every frame of a session looks
623		// like every other one, which is exactly the mistake the choice is
624		// supposed to avoid.
625		pic.SetSizeRequest(-1, 200)
626		pic.SetFilename(s.path)
627		// the base wears the thumbnail's own frame, draggable (publish_crop.go)
628		pf := videoFrame(s.cropOverlay(pic))
629	
630		// Which file it is, on the row of buttons under the picture rather than on a
631		// heading over it; the role word ("Base", "Ref 2") is the tooltip's -- the
632		// row already shows it (the base has no "Make base" button).
633		name := gtk.NewLabel(strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(s.path), filepath.Ext(s.path)))
634		name.SetXAlign(0)
635		name.SetHExpand(true)
636		name.SetEllipsize(pango.EllipsizeMiddle)
637		name.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
638		name.SetTooltipText(s.path + "\n\nThe picture being edited — the instruction changes this one")
639		if s.i > 0 {
640			name.SetTooltipText(fmt.Sprintf("%s\n\nA reference: unchanged, and there to be named. "+
641				"The instruction calls this one \"the %s image\"", s.path, ordinal(s.i+1)))
642		}
643	
644		row := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 4)
645		row.Append(name)
646		if s.i > 0 {
647			mk := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Make base")
648			mk.AddCSSClass("flat")
649			mk.SetTooltipText("Edit this one instead, and demote the current base to a reference")
650			mk.ConnectClicked(func() { s.p.setFrames(moveToFront(s.p.frames, s.i)) })
651			row.Append(mk)
652		}
653		use := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Set Thumbnail")
654		use.AddCSSClass("flat")
655		use.SetTooltipText("Put this picture on the thumbnail as it is -- cropped to the video's " +
656			"shape, no model and no GPU. The title and any marked words are printed onto it, and " +
657			"↻ over the thumbnail draws over it again whenever you want the model back.")
658		use.ConnectClicked(func() { s.useAsThumbnail() })
659		row.Append(use)
660	
661		change := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Change…")
662		change.AddCSSClass("flat")
663		change.SetTooltipText("Swap this image for another, keeping its place in the row")
664		change.ConnectClicked(func() { s.choose() })
665		row.Append(change)
666	
667		drop := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-remove-symbolic")
668		drop.AddCSSClass("flat")
669		drop.SetTooltipText("Remove this image from the row")
670		drop.SetHAlign(gtk.AlignEnd)
671		drop.ConnectClicked(func() {
672			s.p.setFrames(append(append([]string(nil), s.p.frames[:s.i]...), s.p.frames[s.i+1:]...))
673		})
674		row.Append(drop)
675	
676		box := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 2)
677		box.Append(pf)
678		box.Append(row)
679		return box
680	}
681	
682	// ordinal is for the tooltip that tells the user what to call an image in the
683	// instruction. Only ever asked for small numbers -- the row holds maxPubFrames.
684	func ordinal(n int) string {
685		names := []string{"", "first", "second", "third", "fourth", "fifth", "sixth", "seventh", "eighth"}
686		if n < len(names) {
687			return names[n]
688		}
689		return fmt.Sprintf("%dth", n)
690	}
691	
692	// choose swaps this slot's image, keeping its position -- so changing the base
693	// leaves it the base, and changing a reference does not renumber the others.
694	func (s *pubSlot) choose() {
695		s.p.pickImage(fmt.Sprintf("Image %d", s.i+1), filepath.Dir(s.path), func(path string) {
696			fs := append([]string(nil), s.p.frames...)
697			if s.i < len(fs) {
698				fs[s.i] = path
699			}
700			s.p.setFrames(fs)
701		})
702	}
703	
704	// pickImage opens the file chooser. An empty start folder means the one Prepare
705	// extracted frames into, which is the only place worth opening on by default.
706	func (p *publisher) pickImage(title, start string, done func(string)) {
707		a := p.a
708		if start == "" || !exists(start) {
709			start = filepath.Join(a.inputsDir(), "frames")
710			if vids, _ := a.snappedSources(); len(vids) > 0 {
711				if d := filepath.Join(start, baseName(vids[0])); exists(d) {
712					start = d
713				}
714			}
715		}
716		a.pickFile(title, start, extFilter("Images", "jpg", "jpeg", "png", "webp"), done)
717	}
718	
719	// ---- reading and writing the page ------------------------------------------------
720	
721	// snapshot is the page as a runner will see it, taken on the GUI thread. Same
722	// rule as snapSources: a goroutine never touches a widget, and a value copied
723	// out before the run is a value the run cannot see change under it.
724	func (p *publisher) snapshot() pubSettings {
725		st := pubSettings{Frames: append([]string(nil), p.frames...), Crop: p.crop,
726			Own: p.own, TitleBox: p.titleBox, ThumbTitle: p.thumbTitle,
727			TitleSeeded: p.titleSeeded, Texts: append([]pubText(nil), p.texts...)}
728		st.Title = strings.TrimSpace(p.title.Text())
729		st.Prompt = strings.TrimSpace(viewText(p.prompt))
730		st.Negative = strings.TrimSpace(viewText(p.neg))
731		st.Desc = strings.TrimSpace(viewText(p.desc))
732		return st
733	}
734	
735	// apply is snapshot's inverse: what a run wrote, or what a project holds, put
736	// back on the page.
737	func (p *publisher) apply(st pubSettings) {
738		p.crop, p.own, p.titleBox = st.Crop, st.Own, st.TitleBox
739		p.thumbTitle, p.titleSeeded = st.ThumbTitle, st.TitleSeeded
740		p.setFrames(st.Frames)
741		// quiet: the title entry re-prints the words when TYPED in, and this is
742		// not typing -- a run or a project load is putting back words that are
743		// already on the picture (or about to be printed by the run itself)
744		p.quiet = true
745		p.title.SetText(st.Title)
746		p.quiet = false
747		p.texts = append([]pubText(nil), st.Texts...)
748		if p.shotOver != nil {
749			p.shotOver.QueueDraw()
750		}
751		setViewText(p.prompt, st.Prompt)
752		setViewText(p.neg, st.Negative)
753		setViewText(p.desc, st.Desc)
754	}
755	
756	func viewText(tv *gtk.TextView) string {
757		b := tv.Buffer()
758		return b.Text(b.StartIter(), b.EndIter(), false)
759	}
760	
761	func setViewText(tv *gtk.TextView, s string) { tv.Buffer().SetText(s) }
762	
763	// currentPublish is what the project stores, with the frames made relative to
764	// root so a moved naivepost folder keeps its thumbnail.
765	func (a *App) currentPublish() *pubSettings {
766		if a.pub == nil {
767			return nil
768		}
769		st := a.pub.snapshot()
770		for i, f := range st.Frames {
771			st.Frames[i] = a.storePath(f)
772		}
773		// nothing chosen and nothing written is not worth a key in the file
774		if len(st.Frames) == 0 && st.Crop == nil && len(st.Texts) == 0 && !st.Own &&
775			st.TitleBox == nil && st.Title == "" && st.Prompt == "" && st.Desc == "" {
776			return nil
777		}
778		return &st
779	}
780	
781	func (a *App) applyPublish(st *pubSettings) {
782		if a.pub == nil {
783			return
784		}
785		if st == nil {
786			a.pub.apply(pubSettings{})
787			a.pub.showShot()
788			return
789		}
790		// migrate first, then resolve: an old project's base index points into the
791		// order it was saved in, so rotating has to happen before anything else
792		// touches the list
793		c := st.migrate()
794		for i, f := range c.Frames {
795			c.Frames[i] = a.loadPath(f)
796		}
797		a.pub.apply(c)
798		a.pub.showShot()
799	}
800	
801	// refresh redraws both rows and the picture -- called when the page is entered,
802	// because everything it reads (the cut, the narration, the output folder) is
803	// made somewhere else.
804	func (p *publisher) refresh() {
805		if p == nil {
806			return
807		}
808		p.reread()
809		// the row is rebuilt, not just re-read: the base wears a crop box of the
810		// CUT's shape, and the cut is the thing most likely to have been reshaped
811		// since this page was last looked at
812		p.rebuildFrames()
813		p.updateOut()
814		p.showShot()
815	}
816	
817	// showShot puts the last thumbnail back in the picture. The file on disk is the
818	// state, not something remembered in the struct: it survives a restart, and a
819	// project whose folder was reopened shows what was drawn for it last time.
820	func (p *publisher) showShot() {
821		if p == nil || p.shot == nil {
822			return
823		}
824		// the finished one first, then the plain copy: the plain one is what a
825		// run interrupted between the two writes leaves behind, and a picture
826		// without its words is still the thumbnail
827		for _, f := range []string{p.a.thumbFile(), p.a.thumbPlain()} {
828			if exists(f) {
829				// the TEXTURE, not the filename. GtkPicture compares the GFile it
830				// is given against the one it holds and returns early when they
831				// are equal -- so re-printing the words writes thumbnail.png and
832				// then shows the copy already decoded, and the box you had just
833				// typed into came up empty. Every path here rewrites the same two
834				// names, so the name is exactly what cannot be used to notice a
835				// change.
836				if tex, err := gdk.NewTextureFromFilename(f); err == nil {
837					p.shot.SetPaintable(tex)
838				} else {
839					p.a.logf("thumbnail: %v", err)
840					p.shot.SetFilename(f)
841				}
842				p.shot.SetTooltipText("publish/" + filepath.Base(f))
843				// cached for the marking layer: its draw handler and its drag
844				// both need to know where the picture is, per pointer move
845				p.shotPath = f
846				p.shotA = imageAspect(f)
847				if p.shotOver != nil {
848					p.shotOver.QueueDraw()
849				}
850				return
851			}
852		}
853		p.shotPath, p.shotA = "", 0
854		p.shot.SetPaintable(nil)
855		p.shot.SetTooltipText("nothing drawn yet — ▶ below draws it")
856		if p.shotOver != nil {
857			p.shotOver.QueueDraw()
858		}
859	}
860	
861	// reread reloads the cut's aspect off disk -- the one thing the drawing side
862	// still reads from another step's file. Only on arrival and after a run, never
863	// per frame: the crop box is redrawn on every pointer move.
864	func (p *publisher) reread() {
865		p.aspect = p.a.produceCut().Aspect
866	}
867	
868	// updateOut passes the news to the page's one Outputs group: what this half
869	// writes lands in the same folder the video does.
870	func (p *publisher) updateOut() {
871		if p == nil {
872			return
873		}
874		p.a.prod.updateOut()
875	}
876	
877	// ---- choosing the candidate frames -------------------------------------------
878	
879	// pubShot is one extracted frame and where it falls on the session clock.
880	type pubShot struct {
881		path string
882		t    float64
883	}
884	
885	// publishShots is every frame Prepare extracted, on the session's clock. The
886	// times come from the frame's own filename when it has a stamp -- which is
887	// what they are named for -- and from the video's start plus the interval when
888	// it does not, which is how folders extracted before the renaming look.
889	//
890	// Runner-side: it reads a frame folder per source, so it is not something to
891	// call from a page refresh.
892	func (a *App) publishShots() []pubShot {
893		vids, _ := a.snappedSources()
894		if len(vids) == 0 {
895			return nil
896		}
897		zero := a.sessionZero()
898		var out []pubShot
899		for _, v := range vids {
900			plan, err := a.planVideo(v, a.describeDir())
901			if err != nil {
902				a.logfIdle("    publish: no frames for %s (%v)", baseName(v), err)
903				continue
904			}
905			start := a.sourceStart(v) // its own stamp, or the session's start
906			for i, f := range plan.frames {
907				t := start - zero + float64(i)*plan.interval
908				if s, _, ok := readStamp(f); ok {
909					t = s - zero
910				}
911				out = append(out, pubShot{path: f, t: t})
912			}
913		}
914		return out
915	}
916	
917	// pickShots chooses n candidate frames: frames the cut kept first (a thumbnail
918	// of an edited-out moment promises a video that does not exist), spread evenly
919	// as the middles of n equal bands -- the first frame is usually a loading
920	// screen, the last a fade.
921	func pickShots(shots []pubShot, segs []cutSeg, n int) []string {
922		if n <= 0 || len(shots) == 0 {
923			return nil
924		}
925		pool := shots
926		if len(segs) > 0 {
927			var kept []pubShot
928			for _, s := range shots {
929				for _, c := range segs {
930					// an insert covers session seconds without showing them, so a
931					// frame under one is not in the video at all -- picking a
932					// thumbnail from it would offer a shot no viewer ever sees
933					if !c.isInsert() && s.t >= c.S && s.t <= c.E {
934						kept = append(kept, s)
935						break
936					}
937				}
938			}
939			// only if the cut actually leaves enough to choose between: a cut
940			// whose clips fall between two frames would otherwise reduce the
941			// candidates to the same one repeated
942			if len(kept) >= n {
943				pool = kept
944			}
945		}
946		var out []string
947		for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
948			j := int(float64(len(pool)) * (float64(i) + 0.5) / float64(n))
949			if j >= len(pool) {
950				j = len(pool) - 1
951			}
952			out = append(out, pool[j].path)
953		}
954		return out
955	}
956	
957	// ---- what the model is told about the video -------------------------------------
958	
959	// publishBrief is the video as a paragraph of facts: how long it is, what its

// animStop is one value and the moment the card reaches it.

// cardAnim writes one animation element: stops in seconds, turned into values
// and keyTimes over the card's whole length. Held before the first stop and
// after the last, so a row waits its turn and then stays where it landed.
func cardAnim(b *strings.Builder, pad, attr, kind string, total float64, stops ...animStop) {
	vals, times := animPair(total, stops...)
	if vals == "" {
		return
	}
	el, extra := "animate", ""
	if kind != "" {
		el, extra = "animateTransform", fmt.Sprintf(" type=%q", kind)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(b, "\n%s<%s attributeName=%q%s values=%q keyTimes=%q dur=%q fill=\"freeze\"/>",

// animPair is that same schedule as the two strings an <animate> is made of.
// A card written as a template holds the element and gets these handed to it,
// which is what puts a moment somebody typed -- D[1.1s] -- into the document as
// a number instead of leaving it in a printf in here.
func animPair(total float64, stops ...animStop) (values, keyTimes string) {
	if total <= 0 || len(stops) == 0 {
		return "", ""
	}
	full := stops
	if full[0].at > 0 {
		full = append([]animStop{{0, full[0].val}}, full...)
	}
	if last := full[len(full)-1]; last.at < total {
		full = append(append([]animStop{}, full...), animStop{total, last.val})
	}
	vs := make([]string, len(full))
	ts := make([]string, len(full))
	for i, st := range full {
		vs[i] = st.val
		ts[i] = trimNum(math.Min(1, math.Max(0, st.at/total)))
	}
	return strings.Join(vs, ";"), strings.Join(ts, ";")
}

		return "image/bmp"
	case bytes.HasPrefix(b, []byte("RIFF")) && len(b) > 12 && bytes.Equal(b[8:12], []byte("WEBP")):
		return "image/webp"
	case bytes.Contains(b[:min(len(b), 1024)], []byte("<svg")):
		return "image/svg+xml"
	}
	return logoExt[strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(path))]
}

// ---- drawing -----------------------------------------------------------------

// badgeInputs is the badge's form, and what a badge file says about itself: one
// letter and one caption, however it is filled in.
var badgeInputs = []svgField{
	{Key: "label", Label: "Letter", Hint: "the big letter on the card"},
	{Key: "item", Label: "Caption", Hint: "what earned it — under the badge"},
	{Key: "color", Label: "Colour", Hint: "#rrggbb; empty follows the letter"},
}

func badgeForm(q svgQuery, src []byte) []svgField {
	var f []svgField
	for _, in := range cardInputs(src, badgeInputs) {
		in.Val = q.get(in.Key)
		f = append(f, in)
	}
	return f
}

var hexColor = regexp.MustCompile(`^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}$`)

// badgeSVG is the single-letter card: one tier's badge flying in from the left,
// overshooting and settling, with the caption arriving after it has landed. It
// is the card for calling a verdict out one at a time -- s.svg, a.svg and the
// rest are this one card with the letter stamped into them.
func badgeSVG(q svgQuery, _ string, _ []byte) []byte {
	label := strings.TrimSpace(q.get("label"))
	item := strings.TrimSpace(q.get("item"))
	col := strings.TrimSpace(q.get("color"))
	if !hexColor.MatchString(col) {
		col = tierColor(label, 0)
	}

	boxW, boxH := 440.0, 440.0
	cx, cy := cardW/2, cardH/2
	if item != "" {
		cy -= 90 // room under it for the caption
	}
	total := 0.75
	if item != "" {
		total = 0.97
	}
	total += cardHold

	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("\n  <g>")
	flyIn(&b, "    ", total, 0.1, 0.65, -(cardW/2 + boxW))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n    <rect x=\"%s\" y=\"%s\" width=\"%s\" height=\"%s\" rx=\"52\" fill=%q/>",
		trimNum(cx-boxW/2), trimNum(cy-boxH/2), trimNum(boxW), trimNum(boxH), col)
	fs := fitFont(label, boxW-80, 300)
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n    <text x=\"%s\" y=\"%s\" font-family=%q font-size=\"%s\" font-weight=\"700\""+
		" fill=%q text-anchor=\"middle\">%s</text>\n  </g>",
		trimNum(cx), trimNum(cy+fs*0.35), cardFont, trimNum(fs), cardInk, escapeText(label))

	if item != "" {
		cfs := fitFont(item, cardW-240, 96)
		b.WriteString("\n  <g>")
		cardAnim(&b, "    ", "opacity", "", total, animStop{0.62, "0"}, animStop{0.97, "1"})
		cardAnim(&b, "    ", "transform", "translate", total,
			animStop{0.62, "0 48"}, animStop{0.97, "0 0"})
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n    <text x=\"%s\" y=\"%s\" font-family=%q font-size=\"%s\" font-weight=\"600\""+
			" fill=%q text-anchor=\"middle\">%s</text>\n  </g>",
			trimNum(cx), trimNum(cy+boxH/2+140), cardFont, trimNum(cfs), cardFG, escapeText(item))
	}
	return cardDoc("badge", q, badgeInputs, b.String())
}

// cardDoc wraps a card's body in the document every card has: frame,
// background, the stamp saying what drew it and with what (insSVG reads it
// back), and the card's form as Input comments, which the dialog is built
// from. Comments, so no renderer sees them and the baker drops them.
func cardDoc(name string, args svgQuery, inputs []svgField, body string) []byte {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(`<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>` + "\n")
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="%s" height="%s" viewBox="0 0 %s %s"`+
		" data-naivepost=%q data-naivepost-args=\"%s\">",
		trimNum(cardW), trimNum(cardH), trimNum(cardW), trimNum(cardH), name, attrEsc(args.args()))
	for _, in := range inputs {
		b.WriteString("\n  " + inputDecl(in))
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n  <rect width=\"%s\" height=\"%s\" fill=%q/>", trimNum(cardW), trimNum(cardH), cardBG)
	b.WriteString(body)
	b.WriteString("\n</svg>\n")
	return []byte(b.String())
}

// trimNum writes a coordinate the short way: SVG takes "120" and "120.4" and
// not "1.204e+02", and a card is several hundred numbers.
func trimNum(f float64) string {
	s := strconv.FormatFloat(f, 'f', 2, 64)
	s = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimRight(s, "0"), ".")
	if s == "" || s == "-" {
		return "0"
	}
	return s
}

// fitFont is a font size that keeps s inside w. SVG cannot measure text without
// a renderer, so this uses the one number that holds across sans-serif faces --
// an average advance of a bit over half an em -- and errs small: a card whose
// text is a size too modest still reads, and one whose text runs off the chip
// does not.
func fitFont(s string, w, max float64) float64 {
	n := float64(len([]rune(strings.TrimSpace(s))))
	if n == 0 {
		return max
	}
	if f := w / (0.58 * n); f < max {
		return math.Max(f, 12)
	}
	return max
}

// secStr writes a SMIL clock value without an exponent or a trailing run of
// zeroes -- "0.15s", not "1.5e-01s", which clockValue would refuse.
func secStr(f float64) string {
	return strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimRight(fmt.Sprintf("%.3f", f), "0"), ".") + "s"
}

var attrEscaper = strings.NewReplacer("&", "&amp;", "<", "&lt;", ">", "&gt;", `"`, "&quot;")

func attrEsc(s string) string { return attrEscaper.Replace(s) }

// the lookup can fail) counts as open rather than as locked: refusing to show a
// page is the worse mistake.
func (a *App) stepLocked(i int) bool {
	if i < 0 || i >= len(steps) {
		return false
	}
	switch steps[i].name {
	case "cut":
		return a.cutLocked
	case "narrate":
		// choosing a voice lives on this tab and therefore waits for a cut,
		// which it does not need. That is deliberate: it belongs beside the lines
		// it will speak, and hearing a sample before there is anything to narrate
		// decides nothing you cannot decide again afterwards.
		return a.narrateLocked
	case "produce":
		return a.produceLocked
	}
	return false
}

func stepIndex(name string) int {
	for i, s := range steps {
		if s.name == name {
			return i
		}
	}
	return -1
}

// showStep moves to a page without going through the tab's click handler --
// for the bounce off a locked tab, and for sending a page whose prerequisites
// vanished back to the start.
func (a *App) showStep(name string) {
	// whatever was half-typed on the page being left is on disk before it is
	// left: the narration boxes write on a beat after the typing stops, and
	// clicking a tab is exactly the moment that beat has not come yet
	a.narr.flushSave()
	a.tabGuard = true
	for i, s := range steps {
		a.tabs[i].SetActive(s.name == name)
	}
	a.tabGuard = false
	a.stack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
	// the two groups on the shared bar are this page's
	a.inStack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
	a.outStack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
	a.updateRunControls() // ▶ ⏹ belong to the new page's playback now
	a.syncHelp()          // and so does the ⓘ
	// ...and so does ▶ itself, when the ticks beside it name one step: the tab
	// you walk to is the step you mean (followChainTick)
	a.followChainTick(name)
	// Cut's Inputs row lists what Suggest will be sent, and one of those things
	// is the context box on Describe -- the page you have usually just come
	// from. Refreshed on arrival rather than on every keystroke over there,
	// which would re-read the session timeline as you type.
	// ...and the tracks themselves, when the last run (or another project) moved
	// what they are drawn from. Only then: a rebuild probes every recording and
	// drops the undo history, which is not what a tab click should cost.
	if name == "cut" && a.ed != nil {
		if a.ed.stale || len(a.ed.vids) == 0 {
			a.updateCutInfo() // which does updateInputs itself
		} else {
			a.ed.updateInputs()
		}
	}
	// Narrate's row says the same thing about the narration, and one of the
	// things it counts is the cut -- which is the page you have just come from
	// and the one thing most likely to have changed under it.
	if name == "narrate" && a.narr != nil {
		a.narr.refit() // a clip dragged wider over there moves its line's slot here
		a.narr.updateInputs()
		a.narr.updateOut()
	}
	// ...and Produce reads both of those, plus the synthesis cache and the file
	// it wrote last time. It is the end of the chain, so everything upstream is
	// something that may have moved since it was last looked at.
	if name == "produce" {
		a.updateProduceInfo()
		// ...and the thumbnail half reads the folder it wrote into last time,
		// since the picture on the page is the file on disk rather than
	a.updateProduceInfo()
	a.setStatus("rescanned")
}

// updateNarrateInfo re-reads the narration from disk. It was the one step a
// rescan skipped: delete narrate/ and the page went on showing the narration it
// had in memory and an Outputs line counting files that were no longer there.
// Nothing is lost by re-reading -- every edit on that page is written as it is
// typed -- and after a rescan the folder is the answer, including when the
// answer is that there is nothing in it.
func (a *App) updateNarrateInfo() {
	n := a.narr
	if n == nil || n.list == nil {
		return // page not built yet
	}
	n.load()
	n.rebuildRows()
	n.updateInputs()
	n.updateOut()
}

30	// footage's own shape is not known here, and 16:9 is what a recording is.
31	// Both sides are even, because half the image models quietly round and the
32	// half that do not refuse.
33	func pubBox(aspect string) (int, int) {
34		a := parseAspect(aspect)
35		if a <= 0 {

37		}

39		if a >= 1 {

49	// inside the frame. hf and the width it implies are fractions of the SOURCE

51	func pubCropAt(srcA, outA, cx, cy float64) fxRect {

53		wf := pubCropW(r.hf, srcA, outA)
54		// An axis with no slack needs no separate case: fullFill never returns
55		// more than the whole frame, so when the box fills one the clamp's two
56		// bounds meet at the middle and the drag on that axis simply does nothing.
57		r.cx = math.Min(math.Max(cx, wf/2), 1-wf/2)
58		r.cy = math.Min(math.Max(cy, r.hf/2), 1-r.hf/2)

140	// shape right. A chosen frame and a drawn one must be the same size -- a 3840
141	// wide capture frame is a 14 MB PNG YouTube refuses. Area average (always a
142	// downscale, often 3-4×); smaller images are returned as they are.
143	func pubFit(src image.Image, w, h int) image.Image {
144		b := src.Bounds()
145		if w <= 0 || h <= 0 || b.Dx() <= w || b.Dy() <= h {
146			return src
147		}
148		dst := image.NewRGBA(image.Rect(0, 0, w, h))
149		for y := 0; y < h; y++ {
150			y0 := b.Min.Y + y*b.Dy()/h
151			y1 := b.Min.Y + (y+1)*b.Dy()/h
152			for x := 0; x < w; x++ {
153				x0 := b.Min.X + x*b.Dx()/w
154				x1 := b.Min.X + (x+1)*b.Dx()/w
155				var rs, gs, bs, as, n uint64
156				for sy := y0; sy < y1; sy++ {
157					for sx := x0; sx < x1; sx++ {
158						cr, cg, cb, ca := src.At(sx, sy).RGBA()
159						rs, gs, bs, as, n = rs+uint64(cr), gs+uint64(cg), bs+uint64(cb), as+uint64(ca), n+1
160					}
161				}
162				if n == 0 {
163					continue
164				}
165				dst.Set(x, y, color.RGBA64{uint16(rs / n), uint16(gs / n), uint16(bs / n), uint16(as / n)})
166			}
167		}
168		return dst
169	}
170	
171	// pubDecode is one image file, whatever it is encoded as.
172	func pubDecode(path string) (image.Image, error) {
173		f, err := os.Open(path)
174		if err != nil {
175			return nil, err
176		}
177		defer f.Close()
178		img, _, err := image.Decode(f)
179		return img, err
180	}
181	
182	// pubCropImage is the crop itself: the part of the file the box keeps, or nil
183	// where the whole frame is kept and the caller should use the file as it is.
184	func pubCropImage(path string, r fxRect, srcA, outA float64) (image.Image, error) {
185		if srcA <= 0 || outA <= 0 || pubWholeFrame(r, srcA, outA) {
186			return nil, nil
187		}
188		f, err := os.Open(path)
189		if err != nil {
190			return nil, err
191		}
192		defer f.Close()
193		src, _, err := image.Decode(f)
194		if err != nil {
195			return nil, err
196		}
197		b := src.Bounds()
198		wf := pubCropW(r.hf, srcA, outA)
199		x0 := b.Min.X + int(math.Round((r.cx-wf/2)*float64(b.Dx())))
200		y0 := b.Min.Y + int(math.Round((r.cy-r.hf/2)*float64(b.Dy())))
201		x1 := x0 + int(math.Round(wf*float64(b.Dx())))
202		y1 := y0 + int(math.Round(r.hf*float64(b.Dy())))
203		cut := image.Rect(x0, y0, x1, y1).Intersect(b)
204		if cut.Empty() {
205			return nil, fmt.Errorf("the crop box keeps none of %s", path)
206		}
207		// SubImage is what every std image type offers and none of them promise;
208		// the type assertion is the check, and a decoder that does not have it
209		// falls back to the whole frame rather than to an error nobody can act on.
210		sub, ok := src.(interface {
211			SubImage(image.Rectangle) image.Image
212		})
213		if !ok {
214			return nil, nil
215		}
216		return sub.SubImage(cut), nil
217	}
218	
219	// ---- the box on the picture -------------------------------------------------
220	
221	// cropOverlay is the base image with its crop box laid over it, draggable.
222	// A reference, or a base whose shape already matches, comes back plain -- a
223	// control that cannot change anything invites the question of what it does.
224	// The box is drawn by dimming everything OUTSIDE it.
225	func (s *pubSlot) cropOverlay(pic *gtk.Picture) gtk.Widgetter {
226		p := s.p
227		outA := 0.0
228		if w, h := pubBox(p.aspect); h > 0 {
229			outA = float64(w) / float64(h)
230		}
231		// read once per rebuild, not once per frame: this opens the file
232		srcA := imageAspect(s.path)
233		if s.i != 0 || srcA <= 0 || outA <= 0 || pubWholeFrame(pubCropAt(srcA, outA, 0.5, 0.5), srcA, outA) {
234			return pic
235		}
236		// through pubSettings so the "never dragged means the middle" default is
237		// written down once, in the place the project file reads it from
238		rect := func() fxRect { return pubSettings{Crop: p.crop}.cropRect(srcA, outA) }
239	
240		area := gtk.NewDrawingArea()
241		area.SetTooltipText("The part of this frame the thumbnail keeps — the video's own shape. " +
242			"Drag it over what matters; everything dimmed is cut away before the image model " +
243			"is given the picture.")
244		area.SetDrawFunc(func(_ *gtk.DrawingArea, cr *cairo.Context, w, h int) {
245			ox, oy, dw, dh := fxDisp(float64(w), float64(h), srcA)
246			if dw <= 0 || dh <= 0 {
247				return
248			}
249			r := rect()
250			wf := pubCropW(r.hf, srcA, outA)
251			bx, by := ox+(r.cx-wf/2)*dw, oy+(r.cy-r.hf/2)*dh
252			bw, bh := wf*dw, r.hf*dh
253			// the surround, as one path with the box cut out of it: filled even-odd
254			// so the hole is a hole and not a second dark rectangle over the first
255			cr.SetSourceRGBA(0, 0, 0, 0.55)
256			cr.SetFillRule(cairo.FillRuleEvenOdd)
257			cr.Rectangle(ox, oy, dw, dh)
258			cr.Rectangle(bx, by, bw, bh)
259			cr.Fill()
260			cr.SetFillRule(cairo.FillRuleWinding)
261			// and a hairline on the box itself, because a dimmed surround alone
262			// disappears over footage that is already dark
263			cr.SetSourceRGBA(1, 1, 1, 0.9)
264			cr.SetLineWidth(1.5)
265			cr.Rectangle(bx+0.75, by+0.75, bw-1.5, bh-1.5)
266			cr.Stroke()
267		})
268	
269		// the drag. The centre is taken at the press and moved by the pointer's
270		// travel, not set to where the pointer is: grabbing the box near its edge
271		// and having it jump so its middle is under the finger is the one thing
272		// that makes a box like this feel broken.
273		g := gtk.NewGestureDrag()
274		var cx0, cy0 float64
275		g.ConnectDragBegin(func(float64, float64) { r := rect(); cx0, cy0 = r.cx, r.cy })
276		g.ConnectDragUpdate(func(dx, dy float64) {
277			_, _, dw, dh := fxDisp(float64(area.AllocatedWidth()), float64(area.AllocatedHeight()), srcA)
278			if dw <= 0 || dh <= 0 {
279				return
280			}
281			r := pubCropAt(srcA, outA, cx0+dx/dw, cy0+dy/dh)
282			p.crop = &pubPoint{X: r.cx, Y: r.cy}
283			area.QueueDraw()
284		})
285		area.AddController(g)
286	
287		ov := gtk.NewOverlay()
288		ov.SetChild(pic)
289		ov.AddOverlay(area)
290		return ov
291	}
292

441	func drawPencil(cr *cairo.Context, cx, cy, size float64) {
442		cr.Save()
443		cr.Translate(cx, cy)
444		cr.Rotate(-math.Pi / 4)

453		cr.Fill()

458		cr.Stroke()
459		cr.Restore()
460	}

// textCut is the cut of a read to camera: every filmed second, minus the
// marks, minus the dead air. No model -- the words decided, in Prepare.
//
// Only the arithmetic. What it is given is the editor's state as values --
// the inserts it already holds, the filmed runs, where the talking is -- and
// what it hands back is segments and two numbers for the log; putting them on
// the page is the page's job (applyTextCut). It used to reach into the editor
// itself, undo stack and status line included, which made a file about words
// the one logic file that drove a widget.
func (a *App) textCut(marks []retake, inserts []cutSeg, runs []tlSpan, talk [][2]float64) (segs []cutSeg, marked int, dead float64) {
	segs = insertsOf(inserts)
	// each filmed run trimmed to its words: a recording starts rolling
	// before the first word and stops after the last, and neither stretch
	// is the video. The same fenced placement a cut gets (endAfter,
	// startBefore), with the run's own edge as the fence.
	vids, auds := a.snapSources()
	paths := append(vids, auds...)
	words := a.spokenWords(paths)
	edgeOf := a.edgeLookup(paths, a.sessionRows())
	for _, r := range runs {
		segs = append(segs, trimRunToWords(cutSeg{S: r.t0, E: r.t1}, words, edgeOf))
	}
	marked = dropMarked(&segs, marks)
	dead = dropDeadAir(&segs, talk)
	return segs, marked, dead
}

// trimRunToWords is a filmed run cut down to its speech: from just before its
// first word to just after its last, placed by the sound within troughReach
// of each and never outside the run. A run with no words in it stands as it
// is -- footage with nothing said over it is still footage.
func trimRunToWords(seg cutSeg, words []srcWord, edgeOf func(float64) *edges) cutSeg {
	var first, last *srcWord
	for i := range words {
		w := &words[i]
		if w.s < seg.S-0.01 || w.e > seg.E+0.01 {
			continue
		}
		if first == nil {
			first = w
		}
		last = w
	}
	if first == nil {
		return seg
	}
	s := math.Max(seg.S, first.s-wordPad)
	if e := edgeOf(first.s); e != nil {
		s = e.startBefore(*first, math.Max(seg.S, first.s-troughReach))
	}
	t := math.Min(seg.E, last.e+wordPad)
	if e := edgeOf(last.e); e != nil {
		t = e.endAfter(*last, math.Min(seg.E, last.e+troughReach))
	}
	return cutSeg{S: s, E: t}
}

// cutLen, cutPos and cutAt are the session clock, the cut's own clock (only
// what is kept -- the clock of the video that will be produced) and the
// conversion between them. The seek bar is on the cut's clock, so the gaps
// are simply not on it.
func cutLen(segs []cutSeg) float64 {
	tot := 0.0
	for _, s := range segs {
		tot += math.Max(0, s.length())
	}
	return tot
}

// cutPos is a session time on the cut's clock: how much kept material comes
// before it. A time in a gap -- the preview passes through them, briefly, on its
// way to the next clip -- reads as the boundary it is about to reach, so the
// handle waits at the join instead of jumping ahead of the picture.
func cutPos(segs []cutSeg, t float64) float64 {
	acc := 0.0
	for _, s := range segs {
		if t <= s.S {
			return acc
		}
		if t < s.E {
			off := t - s.S
			if s.Rate > 0 {
				off /= s.Rate // slowed footage: a session second is 1/rate cut seconds
			}
			return acc + off
		}
		acc += math.Max(0, s.length())
	}
	return acc
}

// cutAt is the way back: a place on the cut's clock as a session time. Every
// value the slider can hold maps into a clip, which is the point of the whole
	segs := make([]cutSeg, len(n.entries))
	for i, e := range n.entries {
		segs[i] = cutSeg{S: e.S, E: e.E}
	}
	return segs
}

// gapAt places a session time against the cut: the clip covering t, and the
// first clip starting after it. cur < 0 with next >= 0 is a hole the edit
// removed; both < 0 is past the end of the cut.
func gapAt(segs []cutSeg, t float64) (cur, next int) {
	next = -1
	for i, s := range segs {
		if t >= s.S && t < s.E {
			return i, -1
		}
		if s.S > t {
			return -1, i
		}
	}
	return -1, next
}

// leadIn is where a row's ▶ drops the preview: a few seconds ahead of the
// line, but never back inside the line before it on the same clip -- entryAt
// decides who owns those seconds.
func (n *narrator) leadIn(i int) float64 {
	e := n.entries[i]
	t := math.Max(e.S, e.S+e.At-narrRunIn) // not before the clip: no video there
	if n.entryAt(t) >= 0 {
		return e.S + e.At // a line is speaking there; start on this one instead
	n.rebuildRows()
	n.updateOut()
}

// fmtClock and parseClock are the row's time field: session seconds as
// "mm:ss.d" out, and back in as "mm:ss", "mm:ss.5", "h:mm:ss" or plain
// seconds -- whatever the user reaches for.
func fmtClock(t float64) string {
	if t < 0 {
		t = 0
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%02d:%04.1f", int(t)/60, t-float64(int(t)/60*60))
}

# Prompt: system

Shipped default, verbatim from the prototype.

```
You are called by an automated video editor, one job per call.

THE ANSWER
Read by a machine, not a person: exactly what the job asks for and nothing around it -- no markdown, no code fence, no preamble, no report of what you did. Where a job asks for JSON, strict JSON is the whole answer; where it asks for lines or columns, their number and order are part of it.

THE MATERIAL
One session -- pictures and microphones, all on one clock -- written as stamped lines:

  [724s | 12:04] EVENT: what the picture showed in those seconds, and whether it was hectic or calm
  [727s | 12:07] SPEAKER_01: something said out loud, which the video plays
  [731s | 12:11] NARRATOR: something said on a microphone the video does not play, so only a job that uses it is heard

A clip's block may also carry MARKED: the editor's own name for a moment in it -- not something said and not something the picture showed, but what they call it.

THE CLOCKS
Every line is stamped, and the request says which clock. Answer on the same one.

  [724s | 12:04] session time, the same instant written twice: the seconds, then mm:ss from the session start with minutes counting past 59. Times you return on this clock are the SECONDS, and you take them off the line -- never work them out from the mm:ss, and never answer with an mm:ss.
  [+2.0s] an offset from the start of what the request is about -- these frames, this clip. Negative is before it.
  A bare number in a column is seconds on one recording's own timeline: copied, never recomputed.

THE FOUR STEPS
  Prepare writes those lines: frames described into EVENT lines, microphones transcribed into SPEAKER and NARRATOR lines. No later step sees the footage -- from here the lines ARE the session.
  Cut picks the segments the video is made of. What is captioned over each, how fast each plays and what is drawn on each are asked for after it, clip by clip.
  Narrate writes the voice-over over those segments. Each clip keeps its own sound underneath.
  Produce writes the upload text, draws the thumbnail, renders the video.

The finished video is those segments played one after another, so it has a clock of its own: a time in the video is not a time in the session.

THE CUT
A segment is a stretch of session seconds: chronological, never overlapping, each boundary in the gap between two lines, and not all the same length -- what is on screen decides, never an average.

The segments are chosen first and are not changed afterwards. What is written over each clip, how fast it plays and what is drawn on it are three later jobs, each given the clips and answering in the clip's own seconds. An effect belongs to one clip; one outside every clip is thrown away.

WHAT EACH JOB IS GIVEN, AND WHAT IT ANSWERS WITH -- nothing around the answer:

  describe: a few frames, each after a line "[+2.0s] FRAME 3 of 4" on the same clock as the speech around them; the running STATE from the chunk before; the last EVENT lines. Answers two lines:
    EVENT: Calm; the tower fires into the crowd and a health bar empties.
    STATE: On the second map, defending the left lane with the new tower.
  transcript: a context block, then N lines of TSV -- start, end, speaker, text. Answers exactly those N lines in order, start, end and speaker copied character for character and only the text changed. No line merged, split, dropped, added or emptied; no tabs in the text; no line numbers. Any difference in count, order, times or speakers discards the block.
  retake: every spoken line of the session, numbered, each with its own seconds, the pause in front of it and the seams between recordings. Answers ABANDONED, strict JSON and nothing else:
    {"abandoned":[{"from":<n>,"to":<n>,"again":<n>}]}
    <n> is a line number exactly as the request gave it. "from" to "to" is the stretch that was abandoned, inclusive; "again" is the line where the attempt that was kept begins, or 0 when it was broken off and never picked up. Nothing to mark is a whole answer: {"abandoned":[]}.
  translate: the numbered lines of one video's subtitle track. Answers exactly those lines, in order, translated -- one line out for every line in, each beginning with its own number and a tab.
  textedit: ONE join -- the last words of the take that was interrupted, then the first words of the take that follows. Answers strict JSON and nothing else:
    {"joined":"<the two parts run on as one, with the stumble left out>"}
    Every word of the answer must be a word the request gave, spelled and ordered as it gave it; the only thing you may do is leave words out, and what you leave out must be one stretch at the join. Leaving nothing out is a whole answer: a recording that stopped between two thoughts is not a stumble.
  cut: the footage range and the session timeline. Answers SEGMENTS, strict JSON and nothing else:
    {"segments":[{"start":<sec>,"end":<sec>}]}
    <sec> is session seconds, a number. Segments in order, never overlapping, and inside the range the request gives.
  captions: a few clips, "CLIP n" with its length, then the lines said over it stamped as offsets from that clip's start. Answers CAPTIONS, strict JSON and nothing else:
    {"clips":[{"i":<n>,"fx":[{"start":<sec>,"end":<sec>,"text":"<words>"}]}]}
    <n> is the clip's number exactly as the request gave it; <sec> is seconds from that clip's start, inside the clip. A clip with nothing to caption is left out, and {"clips":[]} is a whole answer.
  speed: the clips with their lengths, what is spoken over each and which carry captions, the footage they come to, the target and the range. Answers SPEEDS, strict JSON and nothing else:
    {"speeds":[{"clip":<n>,"rate":<x>}]}
    <x> is the playback rate: 1 is the footage's own speed, above 1 runs fast, below 1 is slow motion. A clip left out plays at 1.
  effects: every clip of the cut, "CLIP n" with its length, then what was said and shown over it stamped as offsets from that clip's start. Answers EFFECTS, strict JSON and nothing else:
    {"fx":[{"clip":<n>,"kind":"zoom"|"stop"|"volume","start":<sec>,"end":<sec>,"gain":<x>}]}
    <sec> is seconds from that clip's start, inside the clip. "gain" belongs to volume alone: 1 as recorded, 0 silent.
  narrate: one block per clip -- "CLIP n" with its start, end, length and word ceiling, then what happened over it stamped as offsets from that clip's start. Answers ENTRIES, strict JSON and nothing else:
    {"entries":[{"start":<sec>,"end":<sec>,"at":<sec>,"text":"<words>","emotion":"<name>=<0..1>"}]}
    "start" and "end" are the clip's own, copied from the request; "at" is seconds from that clip's start.
    emotion is how the TTS reads it: a base -- happy, angry, sad, afraid, disgusted, melancholic, surprised, calm -- or close kin, weighted 0 to 1 ("angry=1", "happy=0.8, surprised=0.4"); named mixes (excited, awed, alarmed, confused, frustrated, desperate, tender, proud, dismayed, horrified, ominous) take a weight the same way. Loud or fast is not an emotion.
  upload text: the clips, each with where it starts in the finished video, what was seen and said in each, and the narration over it. Answers three parts with a blank line between them -- the title on one line prefixed exactly "TITLE: ", the thumbnail on one line prefixed exactly "THUMBNAIL: ", then the description as prose. No JSON. The thumbnail line is one of two things, and the job says which to answer: an instruction, or "frame: clip <n> +<seconds>" naming a moment of the video to be taken as it is -- the clip and the offset inside it as the request stamps them, both copied -- in which case the line reads exactly "THUMBNAIL: frame: clip 3 +12" and nothing is drawn. An instruction goes to an image model that edits the first frame it is given, the others as references named by position ("the ship from the second image"); the title is printed onto the finished picture afterwards, so ask for no text, no lettering and no logo, and for the part it lands in to stay calm and uncluttered.

TOOLS
Some jobs are offered web_search and web_read. They are for a fact about a named thing you are about to WRITE DOWN and would otherwise guess -- what a tower does, what an item costs, how a name is spelled -- and only when the material does not contain it. Not to understand the session, not to confirm what the material already tells you, and never on a job whose answer is numbers rather than words: a search costs minutes, and the reasoning that led to it is done again from the start with the results in hand. A fact you write is one the material shows or one you looked up; with no tool offered, a fact you do not have is one you do not write.

NEVER INVENT
Only what the material shows. Never invent a time, a name, a score, a moment or an outcome -- not even one the user context leads you to expect: a stretch the lines do not cover did not happen, and only stretches with EVENT lines have footage behind them.

# Prompt: cut

Shipped default, verbatim from the prototype.

```
You choose the moments a video is cut from. The recording is a session of something happening -- a game, a build, a lesson, a conversation, a drive -- and the USER CONTEXT says which, when it says anything at all.

Work in this order.

1. Work out what this session is before you choose anything. The user context usually says it in its first sentence; with none, the first minutes of the timeline do -- what the speakers say they are doing, and what the EVENT lines keep showing. Cut for THAT, not for what a session like it usually contains. This is for you, not for the answer: the answer is segments and nothing else.

2. List what the user context names: every thing, moment, person or part. Each one gets a segment where it happens on the timeline. Find the place by the speech and the EVENT lines around it, and take the whole beat -- the setup, the thing itself, and what came of it, even when they are minutes apart. These come first and are never dropped for length.

3. Fill the rest of the target with what would be missed if it were gone: the thing working, the thing failing, the point being made, the answer to a question asked earlier. What people responded to outranks a competent stretch nobody said anything about. Take something from every part of the session, not only the start.

4. Shape the whole. The first segment establishes what this is: wherever the speakers say what they are doing or what they are after. Set busy stretches (EVENT says hectic) against calm ones. Finish on something that reads as an ending -- the result, the verdict, the last word.

Each segment starts a beat before the first word you want and ends after the reaction to it. About one segment per 20 seconds of target length, never fewer than two.

Every line is stamped with the seconds it STARTS and the seconds it ENDS: [733s-745s | 12:13] runs from 733 to 745. A SPEAKER line is a sentence or a phrase being said for the whole of that range, so a boundary inside it cuts a sentence in half -- the stretch you drop begins after a line's end and finishes before the next line's start, never between the two numbers of one line. The EVENT lines describe the picture and say nothing reliable about when speech stops: where an EVENT line and a SPEAKER line disagree about whether someone is talking, the SPEAKER line is right.

A line reading (abandoned attempt ...) has ALREADY been taken out of the video for you, to the word. Read it as though it were not there: the line before it and the line after it are one continuous sentence.

This does not change your job. You still choose which stretches the video keeps and which it drops, here as everywhere else, and a session with no target length still has silences, dead ends and stretches worth nothing in it that it is YOUR job to leave out. Answering with segments that run end to end over the whole session is not a cut. All the marker means is that you never have to aim a boundary at one: that particular cut is already made, more exactly than a boundary of yours can be.

A segment ends on the payoff, never just before it, and a moment that only makes sense because of an earlier one takes that one too or neither. Segments run from about 8 seconds to a minute, longer where a stretch has to be shown but not watched -- keep such a stretch whole, as ONE segment: it is played fast afterwards, not cut into pieces with the dull seconds left out.

Answer with SEGMENTS, and nothing else in the reply. How fast each plays, what is captioned over it and what is drawn on it are asked for afterwards, clip by clip, once the cut stands.

Check before you answer: every segment has an EVENT line inside it, every start is later than the end before it, everything the user context names is in, and -- if you were given a range -- the footage they come to, end minus start added up, lands in it. Anywhere inside it is right; do not trim towards its middle. Given no range, there is nothing to add up: keep what is worth keeping and stop.

321	func srtText(cues []subCue) string {
322		var b strings.Builder
323		for i, c := range cues {
324			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%d\n%s --> %s\n%s\n\n", i+1, srtTime(c.s), srtTime(c.e), c.text)

333	// point it at an .srt and Firefox fetches the file, fails to parse it and
334	// shows nothing -- and the tracks muxed INTO the mp4 are not offered by any
335	// browser at all, whatever VLC does with them. Two files for the same cues,
336	// because the player on the desk and the player on the page do not read the
337	// same one.
338	//
339	// The difference is a header, a full stop instead of a comma, and the three
340	// characters WebVTT treats as markup.
341	func vttText(cues []subCue) string {
342		var b strings.Builder
343		b.WriteString("WEBVTT\n\n")
344		for i, c := range cues {
345			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%d\n%s --> %s\n%s\n\n", i+1, vttTime(c.s), vttTime(c.e), vttEscape(c.text))
346		}
347		return b.String()

350	// vttTime is an .srt stamp with the decimal point WebVTT wants.
351	func vttTime(t float64) string { return strings.Replace(srtTime(t), ",", ".", 1) }

353	// vttEscape keeps a cue's text from being read as markup: WebVTT allows
354	// <b>, <i> and &amp; inside a cue, so a spoken "R&D" or a "<" out of a
355	// transcript would be swallowed or break the cue.
356	func vttEscape(s string) string {
357		s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "&", "&amp;")
358		s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "<", "&lt;")
359		return strings.ReplaceAll(s, ">", "&gt;")
360	}

198				// the tell for a model going in circles: the identical call again,
199				// which is what eight rounds of one wiki page looked like from the
200				// outside -- nothing, until the step failed
201				a.logfIdle(">>> %s: round %d of %d asks for the same thing again — %s",
202					step, round+1, toolRounds, asked)
203			} else {
204				a.logfIdle(">>> %s: round %d of %d — the model asked for %s",
205					step, round+1, toolRounds, asked)
206			}
207			last = asked
208			msgs = append(msgs, map[string]any{"role": "assistant", "content": rep.Content, "tool_calls": rep.Calls})
209			for _, c := range rep.Calls {
210				msgs = append(msgs, map[string]any{"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": c.ID,
211					"content": run(c.Function.Name, json.RawMessage(c.Function.Arguments))})
212			}
213		}
214		a.logfIdle("!!! %s: still calling tools after %d rounds — the step gets no answer from this call",
215			step, toolRounds)
216		return "", fmt.Errorf("the model was still calling tools after %d rounds", toolRounds)
217	}
218	
219	// chatRound is one request and its recorded exchange.
220	func (a *App) chatRound(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool,
221		tools []map[string]any, onText func(string)) (chatReply, error) {
222		rec := a.recordChatStart(step, thinking, msgs)
223		// tee an existing stream through the live page; a caller with no callback
224		// stays unstreamed (wrapping nil would flip the wire request to streaming)
225		if onText != nil {
226			user := onText
227			onText = func(s string) { rec.stream(s); user(s) }
228		}
229		t0 := time.Now()
230		rep, err := a.llmChatPost(step, msgs, thinking, tools, onText)
231		rec.done(rep.recorded(), rep.Stop, time.Since(t0), err)
232		return rep, err
233	}
234	
235	// recorded is the reply as the exchange log shows it: thinking, words, then
236	// the calls. Reasoning is wrapped in <think> tags -- how an inlining model
237	// arrives anyway, and what chatHTML folds away -- so the page has one spelling.
238	func (r chatReply) recorded() string {
239		body := r.Content
240		if strings.TrimSpace(r.Think) != "" && !strings.Contains(body, "</think>") {
241			body = "<think>" + r.Think + "</think>" + body
242		}
243		if len(r.Calls) == 0 {
244			return body
245		}
246		var b strings.Builder
247		b.WriteString(body)
248		for _, c := range r.Calls {
249			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n[tool call %s(%s)]", c.Function.Name, c.Function.Arguments)
250		}
251		return b.String()
252	}
253	
254	// thinkSwitch says whether the model may reason before it answers, in BOTH
255	// spellings the local servers take. llama.cpp renders the chat template itself
256	// and reads chat_template_kwargs; halogen-flash-server takes the same two
257	// names at the top level -- /health lists "enable_thinking" and
258	// "preserve_thinking" under "supported" -- and ignores keys it does not know.
259	// Sending both is what lets one settings file point at either.
260	//
261	// It is not decoration. With the nested spelling alone, halogen never saw the
262	// switch: asked for one word inside a 16-token budget it spent all 16 on
263	// reasoning and answered with empty content (finish_reason "length"), which
264	// the Settings Test reported as a fault of the model. The same request with
265	// the switch at the top level answers in two tokens, and its prompt is 40
266	// tokens shorter -- the thinking scaffold comes out of the template too.
267	func thinkSwitch(body map[string]any, on bool) {
268		body["enable_thinking"] = on
269		// the reasoning is kept in the reply either way: the log records what the
270		// model thought (chatReply.recorded), and a job that did not ask to think
271		// has nothing to keep
272		body["preserve_thinking"] = true
273		body["chat_template_kwargs"] = map[string]any{
274			"enable_thinking": on, "preserve_thinking": true,
275		}
276	}
277	
278	// llmChatPost is the wire call itself: build the body, post it, read the answer.
279	// step names the caller so the watch can say whose call is running (llmstall.go).
280	func (a *App) llmChatPost(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool,
281		tools []map[string]any, onText func(string)) (chatReply, error) {
282		c := a.readConf()
283		// the server has a default and the model cannot: the id has to match what
284		// this server actually serves, and Fetch models is how it is found
285		if c.Model == "" {
286			return chatReply{}, fmt.Errorf("no LLM model configured -- use the gear button")
287		}
288		body := map[string]any{
289			"model":            c.Model,
290			"messages":         msgs,
291			"top_p":            0.95,
292			"top_k":            20,
293			"min_p":            0.0,
294			"presence_penalty": 0.0,
295		}
296		if thinking {
297			body["temperature"] = 1.0
298			body["max_tokens"] = thinkTokens
299		} else {
300			body["temperature"] = 0.6
301			body["max_tokens"] = plainTokens
302		}
303		thinkSwitch(body, thinking)
304		if len(tools) > 0 {
305			body["tools"] = tools
306		}
307		if onText != nil {
308			body["stream"] = true
309		}
310		buf, err := json.Marshal(body)
311		if err != nil {
312			return chatReply{}, err
313		}
314		ctx := a.runCtx
315		if ctx == nil {
316			ctx = context.Background()
317		}
318		// one request on the wire at a time (llmgate.go): the queue is waited
319		// out before the watch below starts, so the wait is not read as a stall
320		if err := a.takeLLM(ctx, step); err != nil {
321			return chatReply{}, err
322		}
323		defer a.giveLLM()
324		// the watch holds the call to a silence rule and says every minute what is
325		// arriving; a call nobody streams has no silence to measure, so it keeps a
326		// whole-call ceiling on the client instead
327		w := a.watchChat(step, onText != nil)
328		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
329		defer cancel()
330		stop := w.guard(cancel)
331		defer stop()
332		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST",
333			llmServer(c)+"/v1/chat/completions", bytes.NewReader(buf))
334		if err != nil {
335			return chatReply{}, err
336		}
337		bearer(req, c.Key)
338		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
339		client := &http.Client{}
340		if onText == nil {
341			client.Timeout = llmWhole
342		}
343		resp, err := client.Do(req)
344		if err != nil {
345			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
346				return chatReply{}, errStopped
347			}
348			return chatReply{}, w.blame(err)
349		}
350		defer resp.Body.Close()
351		// only if the server actually streamed: one that ignores the flag, or that
352		// answers an error as plain JSON, falls through to the decode below
353		if onText != nil && strings.Contains(resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"), "text/event-stream") {
354			rep, err := a.readChatStream(w.wrap(resp.Body), onText, w)
355			return rep, w.blame(err)
356		}
357		var out struct {
358			Choices []struct {
359				Message struct {
360					Content string `json:"content"`
361					// the same out-of-band thinking readChatStream reads, for a
362					// call nobody streamed: kept for the record and nothing else
363					Reasoning string     `json:"reasoning_content"`
364					ToolCalls []toolCall `json:"tool_calls"`
365				} `json:"message"`
366				FinishReason string `json:"finish_reason"`
367			} `json:"choices"`
368			Error any `json:"error"`
369		}
370		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out); err != nil {
371			return chatReply{}, fmt.Errorf("bad response (%s): %w", resp.Status, err)
372		}
373		if len(out.Choices) == 0 {
374			return chatReply{}, fmt.Errorf("no choices (%s): %v", resp.Status, out.Error)
375		}
376		return chatReply{Content: out.Choices[0].Message.Content,
377			Think: out.Choices[0].Message.Reasoning, Calls: out.Choices[0].Message.ToolCalls,
378			Stop: out.Choices[0].FinishReason}, nil
379	}
380	
381	// readChatStream assembles a server-sent-event reply, handing the caller the
382	// text so far as each piece lands. bufio.Reader, not Scanner: one event can be
383	// a line of any length. A tool call arrives in pieces stamped with its index
384	// and is reassembled by it.
385	func (a *App) readChatStream(r io.Reader, onText func(string), w *chatWatch) (chatReply, error) {
386		br := bufio.NewReader(r)
387		var b, think strings.Builder
388		var calls []toolCall
389		stop := "" // the reason the LAST chunk gives for stopping; see chatReply.Stop
390		for {
391			line, err := br.ReadString('\n')
392			if s := strings.TrimSpace(line); strings.HasPrefix(s, "data:") {
393				payload := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(s, "data:"))
394				if payload == "[DONE]" {
395					return chatReply{Content: b.String(), Think: think.String(), Calls: calls, Stop: stop}, nil
396				}
397				var ch struct {
398					Choices []struct {
399						Delta struct {
400							Content string `json:"content"`
401							// the model's reasoning. This server keeps it out of content, so a call
402							// thinking hard used to look hung; it is counted and shown (onText feeds the
403							// bar and the recorded page) and goes nowhere near the reply.
404							Reasoning string `json:"reasoning_content"`
405							ToolCalls []struct {
406								Index    int    `json:"index"`
407								ID       string `json:"id"`
408								Type     string `json:"type"`
409								Function struct {
410									Name      string `json:"name"`
411									Arguments string `json:"arguments"`
412								} `json:"function"`
413							} `json:"tool_calls"`
414						} `json:"delta"`
415						FinishReason string `json:"finish_reason"`
416					} `json:"choices"`
417				}
418				// a chunk that will not parse is a chunk, not the reply: keep reading
419				if json.Unmarshal([]byte(payload), &ch) == nil && len(ch.Choices) > 0 {
420					if r := ch.Choices[0].FinishReason; r != "" {
421						stop = r
422					}
423					d := ch.Choices[0].Delta
424					if d.Reasoning != "" {
425						w.wrote(d.Reasoning, true)
426						think.WriteString(d.Reasoning) // for the record, not for the reply
427					}
428					if d.Content != "" {
429						w.wrote(d.Content, false)
430						b.WriteString(d.Content)
431						onText(b.String())
432					}
433					for _, tc := range d.ToolCalls {
434						for len(calls) <= tc.Index {
435							calls = append(calls, toolCall{})
436						}
437						c := &calls[tc.Index]
438						if tc.ID != "" {
439							c.ID = tc.ID
440						}
441						if tc.Type != "" {
442							c.Type = tc.Type
443						}
444						if tc.Function.Name != "" {
445							c.Function.Name += tc.Function.Name
446						}
447						c.Function.Arguments += tc.Function.Arguments
448						w.wrote(tc.Function.Arguments, true)
449					}
450				}
451			}
452			if err != nil {
453				if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
454					// a stream that ends without [DONE] still said what it said
455					return chatReply{Content: b.String(), Think: think.String(), Calls: calls, Stop: stop}, nil
456				}
457				if a.stopFlag.Load() {
458					return chatReply{}, errStopped
459				}
460				return chatReply{}, err // a half-written JSON reply is worth less than the error
461			}
462		}
463	}
464	
465	// jsonItemsDone reads a reply still arriving: how many objects have closed
466	// inside the LAST "<key>": [ (everything before is thinking, which may mention
467	// the key), and the "end" of the last closed one for shapes that carry it.
468	// Only complete items count. The end time is the bar's denominator-free
469	// progress: the model walks the session from the front.
470	func jsonItemsDone(s, key string) (done int, through float64) {
471		q := `"` + key + `"`
472		i := -1
473		for at := 0; ; {
474			j := strings.Index(s[at:], q)
475			if j < 0 {
476				break
477			}
478			j += at
479			at = j + 1
480			rest := strings.TrimLeft(s[j+len(q):], " \t\r\n")
481			if !strings.HasPrefix(rest, ":") {
482				continue
483			}
484			if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimLeft(rest[1:], " \t\r\n"), "[") {
485				i = j
486			}
487		}
488		if i < 0 {
489			return 0, 0
490		}
491		tail := s[i:]
492		depth, from := 0, 0
493		inStr, esc := false, false
494		for k, r := range tail {
495			switch {
496			case esc:
497				esc = false
498			case inStr && r == '\\':
499				esc = true
500			case r == '"':
501				inStr = !inStr
502			case inStr: // braces inside a line of narration are just text
503			case r == '{':
504				if depth == 0 {
505					from = k
506				}
507				depth++
508			case r == '}':
509				if depth--; depth == 0 {
510					done++
511					if e, ok := jsonEnd(tail[from : k+1]); ok && e > through {
512						through = e
513					}
514				}
515			}
516		}
517		return done, through
518	}
519	
520	// jsonEnd reads the "end" out of one finished object. A shape without one -- a
521	// narration clip, say -- simply has no answer here, and its caller falls back
522	// to counting.
523	func jsonEnd(obj string) (float64, bool) {
524		var o struct {
525			End *float64 `json:"end"`
526		}
527		if json.Unmarshal([]byte(obj), &o) != nil || o.End == nil {
528			return 0, false
529		}
530		return *o.End, true
531	}
532	
533	// llmChatRetry absorbs one transport hiccup, which a multi-hour pass will hit
534	// -- but never retries a user stop.
535	// ---- what a rejected answer does to the conversation -------------------------
536	
537	// noAnswer names the failure a JSON parser cannot: a reply with no answer in
538	// it at all -- the thinking budget spent and not a word written (reasoning is
539	// kept out of the reply, readChatStream), which json would report as
540	// "unexpected end of JSON input".
541	func noAnswer(reply string) string {
542		if _, answer := splitThink(reply); strings.TrimSpace(answer) != "" {
543			return ""
544		}
545		return "you returned no answer at all -- the whole reply was reasoning. " +
546			"Think briefly, then write the complete JSON: every segment and every effect, not a sample"
547	}
548	
549	// thinkAgain: whether the NEXT attempt may still think. An EMPTY answer means
550	// the thinking budget was spent with no words -- the same question asked the
551	// same way answers the same -- so the retry sends enable_thinking false with
552	// the shorter ceiling (llmChatPost). Bad JSON or the wrong shape keeps
553	// thinking: that model is writing and getting it wrong.
554	func thinkAgain(think bool, reply string) bool { return think && noAnswer(reply) == "" }
555	
556	// cutOff names the other failure a JSON parser cannot: an answer that stopped
557	// at the token ceiling. json says "unexpected end of JSON input" either way,
558	// and the two want opposite fixes -- a malformed answer wants care, a
559	// truncated one wants a SHORTER answer.
560	func cutOff(reply string, err error) string {
561		if strings.TrimSpace(reply) == "" || err == nil {
562			return ""
563		}
564		if !errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) &&
565			!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unexpected end of JSON input") {
566			return ""
567		}
568		return "your answer stopped in the middle -- it was too long to finish. " +
569			"Answer again with far fewer items"
570	}
571	
572	// retryTurn puts a rejected answer and its correction into the history.
573	//
574	// An empty answer is not echoed back. There is nothing to show the model, and
575	// an empty assistant turn is one the next round has to make sense of -- some
576	// servers refuse a conversation containing one outright, and the rest are
577	// being told "you said:" followed by nothing. The correction carries the whole
578	// message in that case, which is what noAnswer is for.
579	func retryTurn(msgs []map[string]any, reply, problem string) []map[string]any {
580		if strings.TrimSpace(reply) != "" {
581			msgs = append(msgs, msg("assistant", reply))
582		}
583		return append(msgs, msg("user",
584			"Your answer failed validation: "+problem+". Return corrected strict JSON only."))
585	}
586	
587	// jsonReply reads a model's answer into out: the JSON object after any
588	// preamble, code fences stripped. The problem string is the correction to send
589	// back, "" when it parsed.
590	func jsonReply(reply string, out any) string {
591		problem := noAnswer(reply)
592		if problem != "" {
593			return problem
594		}
595		clean := strings.TrimSpace(reply)
596		if i := strings.Index(clean, "{"); i >= 0 {
597			clean = clean[i:]
598		}
599		clean = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(clean), "```")
600		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(clean), out); err != nil {
601			if problem = cutOff(reply, err); problem == "" {
602				problem = "not valid JSON: " + err.Error()
603			}
604		}
605		return problem
606	}
607	
608	func (a *App) llmChatRetry(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool) (string, error) {
609		return a.llmChatRetryOn(step, msgs, thinking, nil)
610	}
611	
612	func (a *App) llmChatRetryOn(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool, onText func(string)) (string, error) {
613		return a.llmChatRetryTools(step, msgs, thinking, nil, nil, onText)
614	}
615	
616	// llmChatRetryTools is the retrying call with tools on the table; with none
617	// it is llmChatRetryOn exactly.
618	//
619	// Two kinds of failure, and they deserve different patience. An answer this app
620	// cannot use -- a 400, a refusal, a reply that will not parse -- is the same
621	// answer in two seconds, so it gets the one short retry it always had. A call
622	// that died IN TRANSIT is a different thing: the server went away mid-answer
623	// and is coming back. On this stack that is its own watchdog taking the
624	// container down after 180 s of engine silence, for the restart policy to pick
625	// up, and the restart is minutes of loading weights. Waiting through it is the
626	// difference between a run that carries on and a Prepare that starts over --
627	// so the waits climb past the restart rather than giving up inside it.
628	func (a *App) llmChatRetryTools(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool,
629		tools []map[string]any, run toolRunner, onText func(string)) (string, error) {
630		reply, err := a.llmChatTools(step, msgs, thinking, tools, run, onText)
631		for try := 0; err != nil && !errors.Is(err, errStopped); try++ {
632			wait, again := llmWait(err, try)
633			if !again {
634				break
635			}
636			if llmGone(err) {
637				a.logfIdle("!!! %s: the server went away mid-call (%v) -- waiting %s and asking again (%d of %d)",
638					step, err, durOf(wait), try+1, len(llmBackoff))
639			}
640			if !a.nap(wait) {
641				return "", errStopped
642			}
643			reply, err = a.llmChatTools(step, msgs, thinking, tools, run, onText)
644		}
645		return reply, err
646	}
647	
648	// llmBackoff is how long to wait before each attempt at a call that died in
649	// transit. Past the restart, not inside it: the container has to stop, come
650	// back and read tens of gigabytes of weights before it answers anything, and
651	// an attempt made while that is happening is a connection refused that costs
652	// one of the tries. Roughly eight minutes of patience in five attempts, all of
653	// it interruptible.
654	var llmBackoff = []time.Duration{5 * time.Second, 20 * time.Second, time.Minute,
655		2 * time.Minute, 4 * time.Minute}
656	
657	// llmWait is how long to wait before trying again, and whether to try at all.
658	func llmWait(err error, try int) (time.Duration, bool) {
659		if llmGone(err) {
660			if try < len(llmBackoff) {
661				return llmBackoff[try], true
662			}
663			return 0, false
664		}
665		// anything else: the one short retry, and only on the first failure
666		if try == 0 {
667			return 2 * time.Second, true
668		}
669		return 0, false
670	}
671	
672	// llmGone is whether the error means the server went away rather than answered
673	// something unusable: the connection closed mid-reply (EOF), was reset, was
674	// refused, or the stream stopped short of its end. Every one of those is a
675	// server that is down or restarting, and none of them says anything about the
676	// request -- which is what makes asking the same question again worth doing.
677	//
678	// A status code is deliberately not in here. A 500 is the server answering,
679	// and answering the same way in four minutes.
680	func llmGone(err error) bool {
681		if err == nil || errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
682			return false
683		}
684		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) || errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) ||
685			errors.Is(err, syscall.ECONNRESET) || errors.Is(err, syscall.ECONNREFUSED) ||
686			errors.Is(err, syscall.EPIPE) || errors.Is(err, syscall.ENETUNREACH) {
687			return true
688		}
689		// ...and by the words, for the ones that arrive as a bare string: net/http
690		// and the h2 transport both report a server closing on us that way. Whole
691		// words, so a model's own prose in an error message cannot read as one.
692		return goneWords.MatchString(strings.ToLower(err.Error()))
693	}
694	
695	var goneWords = regexp.MustCompile(`\b(eof|connection reset|connection refused|` +
696		`broken pipe|server closed|no such host|transport is closing)\b`)
697	
698	// nap waits, and answers false when the run was stopped instead. Sleeping
699	// through a restart is only tolerable if ⏹ still ends it: eight minutes of
700	// time.Sleep is eight minutes of a button that does nothing.
701	func (a *App) nap(d time.Duration) bool {
702		ctx := a.runCtx
703		if ctx == nil {
704			ctx = context.Background()
705		}
706		t := time.NewTimer(d)
707		defer t.Stop()
708		select {
709		case <-t.C:
710			return !a.stopFlag.Load()
711		case <-ctx.Done():
712			return false
713		}
714	}
