82	
83	The prototype asks the model for a whole answer as strict JSON, parses it, validates it, and on failure sends "Your answer failed validation: … Return corrected strict JSON only." The rewrite MUST instead offer each job a small set of **tools** and let the model finish the flow by calling them. The app validates inside the tool and returns the problem as the tool result, so correction happens in the same conversation, one item at a time, and a partial answer is never lost when the model runs out of tokens.
84	
85	Design rules for tools:
86	
87	- Every job has a `finish` tool (or a named terminal tool such as `finish_cut`) that ends the flow; a job that stops calling tools without finishing is asked once to finish, then treated as done with what it produced.
88	- Reading tools give the model the material in pieces (`get_lines(from, to)`, `get_frames(clip)`) so a 64-minute session is not one 450 kB prompt (`09-llm-and-tools.md` §5 on context budgets).
89	- Writing tools carry the same validation the prototype's parsers did; the result is either `ok` plus the normalised item, or a one-sentence problem the model can act on.
90	- Tools never take a time the model would have to compute: they take line numbers, clip numbers, frame numbers and offsets "as stamped on the request".
91	- The final walk-back onto the timeline (rule 2.6) still runs after `finish`: tools validate items; the walk-back reconciles the whole.
92	- The exchange log records every tool call and result.
93	- A server that refuses a `tools` field gets the prototype's fallback: the same job as one JSON answer (kept as a documented degraded mode, not the design).
94	
95	`02-services.md` §3 lists the tool catalogue per job; each tab chapter names which tools its flows use.
96	
97	## 5. Generalisations proposed (REVIEW)
98	
99	- **Styles** become a list of named pipelines, not two hard-coded names: each style says which marking pass runs (joins / retakes / none), whether the cut is text-derived or model-chosen, and which policy defaults apply. Lecture and Gaming are the shipped two.
100	- **Languages** for subtitles become a list in the settings (code, ISO-639-2 tag, name) instead of three constants.
101	- **Cards** (SVG inserts) stay a folder of files with a declared-inputs convention; the two built-ins are shipped files, not code.
102	- **Narrator slots** stay four but the number is a policy default.
103	- **Frame-interval stops, scale presets, encoder option lists** stay shipped lists but live in one table the settings can extend.
104	
105	## 6. Glossary
106	
107	- **Session**: all recordings of one sitting, on one clock (the *session clock*, seconds from the earliest timestamped file).
108	- **Source**: one file in the session; it may be *footage* (frames come out of it, it can be cut) and/or a *recording* (heard); one source may hold *narrator slot* 1–4.
109	- **Row / camera**: a horizontal band of the timeline holding recordings that do not overlap; a scene names the row its picture comes from.
110	- **Lane**: a waveform of one audio track (a recording, or a further track of a capture).
111	- **Scene / clip / segment**: a kept stretch `[s, e)` of session time on one row; a *spliced insert* is a card with `s == e` and its own duration; an *overwriting insert* replaces footage seconds.
112	- **Cut**: the list of scenes plus effects, aspect, corrections and lanes (`cut/cut.json`).
113	- **Join / seam**: where one kept scene ends and the next begins; in a lecture, also where one recording stopped and the next started.
114	- **Retake / mark**: a stretch that was said, broken off and said again; marked, never deleted.
115	- **Effect**: zoom, speed (incl. stop), text, svg, volume, label; spans `[t, t+dur)` of session time.
116	- **Line**: one narration entry over one clip (`narrate/narration.json`).
117	- **Policy**: the project's editing parameters (§3).
118	- **Run**: one press of ▶: a chain of steps with one progress bar, one log page, one cancel.
119	# 01 — The project on disk
120	
121	A project is a folder ending in `.naivepost`. The folder **is** the output folder: nothing stores where work goes, so nothing can disagree. Every file inside is readable.
122	
123	## 1. Layout
124	
125	```
126	<name>.naivepost/
127	  naivepost.json                     the project (§2)
128	  sources/                           copies of added files (when "copy into project" is on)
129	  stems/                             voice-separation products: <base>.split-voice.wav, <base>.split-novoice.wav|.mkv
130	  assets/                            SVG cards and other inserts; CARDS.md guide; built-ins written on first use
131	  prepare/
132	    inputs/meta.env                  VIDEO_FILE, VIDEO_BASE, AUDIO_FILE, AUDIO_BASE, INTERVAL, SCALE
133	    inputs/<source>/                 voice16k.wav, transcript.txt, transcript.tsv, transcript.srt,
134	                                     words.json, asrchunks.json, words.aligned.json, turns.json
135	                                     (asr/, diar/ scratch while running)
136	    inputs/frames/<source>/          <YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS[-n]>.jpg per interval, .interval marker
137	    describe/<source>/events.tsv     one row per frame; state.txt; .llmframes/ (scaled frames)
138	    transcript/<source>/             transcript.fixed.tsv | commentary.fixed.tsv, subtitles.srt
139	    transcript/session.tsv           the merged timeline (machine copy)
140	    transcript/session.txt           the timeline as sent to the cut model
141	    transcript/offsets.tsv           video, audio, offset seconds
142	    transcript/retakes.tsv           the marks
143	    transcript/final.txt             the words of the finished video (lecture style)
144	  cache/llm/<step>/<sha256>          cached model replies
145	  cache/waves/<lane>.wave            waveform envelopes
146	  cache/edges/                       mono envelopes for edge placement
147	  cut/cut.json                       the cut (§3)
148	  cut/line.json                      {"t": <session second>} — the red line
149	  narrate/narration.json             the lines (§4); narration.prev.json (one generation back)
150	  narrate/voice.txt, pitch.txt, takes.json, voice_ref_base.wav, voice_ref.wav
151	  narrate/tts/<16 hex>.wav           spoken lines; samples/<voice>_<12 hex>.wav
152	  produce/clips/                     per-clip encodes, final.srt, final.<code>.srt, concat.txt
153	  produce/final.<container>          the video; final.stamp; final[.<code>].srt/.vtt; final.jpg; final.html
154	  produce/publish/publish.json       the upload text and thumbnail state (§5)
155	  produce/publish/thumbnail.png, thumbnail-plain.png, thumbnail.stamp, description.txt
156	  llm/<MMDD-HHMMSS>-<step>.html      one readable page per run
157	```
158	
159	Directories are created 0755, files 0644, except prompts and the settings file on the machine (0700 / 0600).
160	
161	Paths written into any project file go through one rule: inside the project → `project:<slash-relative>`; under the application root → root-relative; else absolute. One reader resolves them.
162	
163	## 2. naivepost.json
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "sources": [{"path": "project:sources/a.mkv", "footage": true, "narrator": 1, "sepvoice": false, "tracks": [0, 1]}],
168	  "interval": 1.0,
169	  "frame_scale": "original",
170	  "style": "read",
171	  "run_steps": ["prep", "cut"],
172	  "language": "en",
173	  "no_narration": false,
174	  "reference_sources": false,
175	  "vid_dir": "…", "aud_dir": "…",
176	  "context": "The weekly blockchain lecture …",
177	  "policy": { … },
178	  "produce": { … },
179	  "publish": { … }
180	}
181	```
182	
183	| key | meaning | default |
184	|---|---|---|
185	| sources | in order; `footage` only on video; `narrator` 1..N (exclusive); `sepvoice` is a wish cleared when granted; `tracks` = audio stream indices in the session (empty = first) | [] |
186	| interval | seconds between frames; 0 = every frame; always written | 1.0 |
187	| frame_scale | preset name (original, 896w (LLM), 480p, 720p, 1080p) | original |
188	| style | a style name from the style table (`00-principles.md` §5); prototype: "read" or "" | "" |
189	| run_steps | ticked chain pages | ["prep"] |
190	| language | ASR language code | en |
191	| no_narration | narration off | false |
192	| reference_sources | inverted on purpose: absent = copy sources in | false |
193	| vid_dir / aud_dir | last chooser folders | root/input_video, root/input_audio |
194	| context | the User Context, verbatim | "" |
195	| policy | the editing policy (`10-parameters.md` §2) with a `source` per field (user / model / default) | defaults |
196	| produce | encoder settings (`08-produce.md` §2); `out_file` is never stored | defaults |
197	| publish | upload text and thumbnail state (§5) | absent |
198	
199	Legacy keys read and migrated once, never written: `videos`, `audios` (first recording → narrator 1), `in_dir`, `out_dir`, `*_hints` (folded into the prompts with their historical lead-ins), `prompts` (adopted where the machine has none), `pitch`.
200	
201	Autosave: the project is marshalled every 2 s and written only when the bytes differ from the last write. Also flushed on window close. There is no "unsaved changes" prompt.
202	
203	## 3. cut/cut.json
204	
205	```json
206	{
207	  "segs": [{"s": 1.5, "e": 34.7, "cam": 0, "quiet": ["mic"]},
208	           {"s": 40.0, "e": 40.0, "ins": "project:assets/tier.svg?S=Dust II", "dur": 4.0, "mute": true},
209	           {"s": 60.0, "e": 65.0, "ins": "project:assets/sting.wav", "ss": 2.0, "lane": "mic"}],
210	  "aspect": "9:16",
211	  "fx": [{"kind": "zoom", "t": 12.0, "dur": 3.0, "trans": 1, "tout": 1, "cx": 0.5, "cy": 0.5, "hf": 0.6}],
212	  "shift": {"cam2": -1.25},
213	  "rows": {"cam2": 1},
214	  "lanes": [{"name": "cam-2", "src": "project:sources/cam.mkv", "at": 100.0, "off": 30.0, "dur": 20.0}],
215	  "nrows": 2,
216	  "folds": [[34.7, 40.0]]
217	}
218	```
219	
220	Segment fields: `s`, `e` session seconds (`s == e` with `dur > 0` = spliced insert); `ins` asset path (project-relative; may carry `?key=value&…`; `copy:<seconds>` = a pasted stretch of the session); `dur` (spliced length); `rate` (written only by the render planner); `ss` (start inside an inserted sound); `mute` (spliced: silent; overwriting: the footage's sound stays); `cam` (picture row); `lane` (which recording an overlaid sound replaces; "" = everything audible); `quiet` (lanes this scene does not hear); `split` (starts at a Split border; never merged automatically).
221	
222	Effects: see `06-effects.md` §1. `shift`/`rows`: hand corrections of where a recording sits and on which row. `lanes`: windows of a file given a row of their own. `nrows`: floor under the row count. `folds`: view only, ignored by the render. Legacy `sound` (whole-cut hearing) is migrated into per-scene `quiet` on first save.
223	
224	`cut.json` existing is what unlocks the Narrate and Produce steps' ▶ (the tabs themselves are always openable). It is written by exactly one function.
225	
226	## 4. narrate/narration.json
227	
228	```json
229	{"entries": [{"s": 1.5, "e": 34.7, "at": 2.0, "text": "We start with …", "emotion": "calm", "pos": "", "roll": 0}],
230	 "silent": [{"S": 40.0, "E": 65.0}]}
231	```
232	`s`/`e` are the clip's bounds copied verbatim from the cut; `at` seconds from the clip's start; `text` "" = deliberately silent; `emotion` a delivery tag; `pos` caption placement top/center/"" (bottom); `roll` re-roll count (salts the TTS cache). `silent` = clips whose last line was deleted on purpose, kept by bounds. Entries are always sorted by (s, at).
233	
234	TTS cache key (kept stable across versions on purpose): `25e<alpha>|[<roll>#][<voiceKey>|]<text>|<emotion or 8-float vector>`; file = first 8 bytes of SHA-1 as hex; seed = bytes 8..11.
235	
236	## 5. produce/publish/publish.json
237	
238	```json
239	{"frames": ["project:prepare/inputs/frames/a/2026-09-16_17-25-30.jpg"], "crop": {"x": 0.5, "y": 0.5}, "own": false,
240	 "title_box": {"cx": 0.5, "cy": 0.25, "wf": 1, "hf": 0.4}, "thumb_title": "…", "title_seeded": true,
241	 "texts": [{"cx": 0.3, "cy": 0.8, "wf": 0.4, "hf": 0.1, "text": "…"}],
242	 "title": "…", "prompt": "…", "negative": "…", "description": "…"}
243	```
244	The first frame is the base the image model edits; the rest are references. `own` = the thumbnail is a chosen frame, not drawn. `publish.json` existing means the upload text has been written; deleting the folder starts the text over.
245	
246	## 6. Text formats
247	
248	- `transcript.tsv` / `*.fixed.tsv`: `start\tend\tspeaker\ttext`, times `%.2f`.
249	- `session.tsv`: `start\tend\tsource\tspeaker|EVENT\ttext` on the session clock.
250	- `events.tsv`: `start\tend\ttext` per frame; a `same` row extends the previous row when read.
251	- `retakes.tsv`: `S\tE\tAgain\tTo\tText` (3-, 4- and 5-column files accepted).
252	- `final.txt`: the surviving words as written, `|cut N|` or `|cut|` at every join.
253	- `meta.env`: `KEY=VALUE` lines; its existence says the sources have been read.
254	- `words.json`: the ASR server's own document (`{"text", "words":[{word,start_sample,end_sample}]}`); `words.aligned.json`: `{"words":[…]}` from the aligner; `turns.json`: `[{start_sample,end_sample,speaker_id}]`.
255	- `.interval`: `<interval>|<scale name>`.
256	- `cache/waves/*.wave`: magic `AWV4`, header {chans u8, hz u16, count u32, size i64, mtime i64}, then peak bytes.
257	
258	## 7. Machine files
259	
260	- `~/.config/naivepost/llm.conf` (0600): bash-sourceable `KEY="value"`; keys in `03-shell.md` §6.
261	- `~/.config/naivepost/prompts/<key>.txt`: a prompt edited on this machine (only when it differs from the shipped text).
262	- `~/.config/naivepost/hang-*.txt`: watchdog dumps.
263	- `~/.local/share/applications/ch.bocek.naivepost.desktop` and the mime XML for `*.naivepost` (installed when the app is not run from a build cache or a Flatpak).
264	
265	## 8. Session clock
266	
267	Every source is placed by the timestamp in its file name; the earliest is zero. Accepted spellings (year first, century 19/20): `2026-08-08 19-55-15`, `…-20260808-195900-0`, `VID_20250814_213311`, `20250814213311`, `2025.08.14 - 21.33.11.03`, `2026-08-08 at 7.55.15 PM`, `2026-08-08T19:55:15`, and bare unix seconds 2017–2033. A file with no stamp sits at the session start (never at its mtime) and its row shows a warning. Nothing stamped → everything starts at 0:00. The clock is always computed over the whole session; a subset would move zero. Frames are named from the frame number (`start + (n−1)·interval`), never from a sorted position.
268	# 02 — Services and the tool catalogue
269	
270	## 1. The four servers
271	
272	| what | default | serves | API |
273	|---|---|---|---|
274	| OpenAI-compatible LLM | `http://127.0.0.1:8731` | every text and vision job | `POST /v1/chat/completions` (streaming, tools), `GET /v1/models` |
275	| audio.cpp | `http://127.0.0.1:8765` | speech to text, alignment, diarization, voice separation, text to speech | `GET /health`, `GET /v1/models` (id, family, task), `POST /v1/ui/upload` (raw body, `X-Audiocpp-Filename`), `POST /v1/tasks/run` `{"model","request"}`, `POST /v1/audio/speech`, `POST /v1/tasks/unload_all_models` |
276	| sd.cpp (sd-server) | `http://127.0.0.1:1234` | the thumbnail when one is drawn | `GET /sdcpp/v1/capabilities`, `POST /sdcpp/v1/img_gen` → job id, `GET /sdcpp/v1/jobs/{id}`, `POST /sdcpp/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` |
277	| ffmpeg / ffprobe | on PATH (or a configured path; ffprobe from the same folder) | frames, waveforms, cuts, encodes | subprocesses |
278	
279	A server box left empty means the loopback default. A box with a host and no scheme is read as `https://host`. Keys are sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` only when non-empty. `readConf` is re-read per step so a settings change takes effect on the next step.
280	
281	Audio model ids (settings, with defaults): ASR `nemotron-asr`, diarization `sortformer-diar`, TTS `index-tts2`, separation `bs-roformer`, aligner: none by default (any model declared task `align`, preferring `qwen3-aligner`). A missing model is reported with the server's own install hint. Nothing is compiled in; no call leaves the machine unless a box points elsewhere.
282	
283	Every request rides the run's cancel context, so ⏹ aborts it. Audio task calls have no client timeout (an hour of audio is an hour of work). LLM calls have a silence rule (streamed) or a whole-call ceiling (`09-llm-and-tools.md` §4).
284	
285	## 2. Model roles (which job asks which server)
286	
287	| job | model | thinking | answers with |
288	|---|---|---|---|
289	| speech to text | ASR (audio.cpp) | – | text per chunk (≤ 60 s for qwen3-family, else ≤ 300 s) |
290	| word times | aligner (audio.cpp) | – | start/end per word, the chunk's own words in hand |
291	| who spoke when | diarization (audio.cpp) | – | speaker turns per window (90 → 45 → 25 s ladder) |
292	| voice split | separation (audio.cpp) | – | voice and rest stems |
293	| what is on screen | LLM with vision | off | one EVENT per frame + a running STATE, four frames a call |
294	| clean transcript | LLM | off | the same lines respelled; times and speakers unchanged, enforced |
295	| lecture joins | LLM | on | the two takes run on as one; only deletions accepted |
296	| retakes (gaming) | LLM | off | line numbers of abandoned stretches, three runs pooled |
297	| gaming cut | LLM (+ web tools) | on | segments in session seconds copied off the timeline |
298	| captions, speed, effects | LLM | off | per clip, in the clip's own seconds |
299	| narration | LLM (+ web tools) → TTS | on | a line per clip with an emotion; spoken in the cloned voice |
300	| upload text | LLM (+ web tools) | on | title, thumbnail (frame or instruction), description |
301	| thumbnail | sd.cpp | – | an image edited from real frames; only when an instruction exists and no frame was named |
302	| subtitles in other languages | LLM | off | numbered lines translated, one call per language |
303	
304	## 3. Tool catalogue (rewrite directive B)
305	
306	Tools are offered per job. Each tool's result is a short JSON object; problems come back as `{"error": "<one sentence the model can act on>"}` and never end the flow. Numbers the model must not compute are always identifiers from the request (line, clip, frame numbers; offsets as stamped).
307	
308	### 3.1 Shared
309	
310	| tool | args | result |
311	|---|---|---|
312	| `get_context` | – | the User Context and the policy fields relevant to this job |
313	| `get_lines` | `from`, `to` (line numbers of the session timeline) | the stamped lines |
314	| `get_events` | `from`, `to` (session seconds) | EVENT lines in the range |
315	| `web_search` | `broad`, `medium`, `narrow` | up to 8 hits with snippets (offered only where the prototype offered it: cut, narrate, upload text) |
316	| `web_read` | `url` | page text (≤ 6000 chars) |
317	| `finish` | – | ends the job |
318	
319	### 3.2 Describe (per chunk of frames)
320	| tool | args | result |
321	|---|---|---|
322	| `record_event` | `frame` (1..n as stamped), `text`, `calm` (bool) | ok; a frame recorded twice replaces |
323	| `set_state` | `text` | ok |
324	`finish` validates that every frame has an event (missing frames become "same"; the first frame of a batch with no history must not be "same").
325	
326	### 3.3 Fix (per block of transcript lines)
327	| tool | args | result |
328	|---|---|---|
329	| `fix_line` | `n` (line number in the block), `text` | ok, or error when `text` contains a tab |
330	Times and speakers are not arguments: the tool cannot change them, which is the enforcement the prototype did by comparison.
331	
332	### 3.4 Retake marking (gaming)
333	| tool | args | result |
334	|---|---|---|
335	| `mark_abandoned` | `from`, `to`, `again` (line numbers; `again` 0 = never picked up) | ok, or the prototype's refusal ("lines a-b say they are said again at line c, which is inside them -- not a mark", out of range, too far (> policy.retakeReach)) |
336	| `unmark` | `from`, `to` | ok |
337	
338	### 3.5 Text edit (lecture, per join)
339	| tool | args | result |
340	|---|---|---|
341	| `drop_words` | `side` (before/after), `count` | ok with the words that would go; error when the join would lose more than policy.seamMaxWords / policy.seamCeil |
342	| `keep_join` | – | nothing removed here (a whole answer) |
343	Prototype: the model returned the joined text and the app derived the counts by matching backwards. With tools the counts are stated directly, and the app still re-derives the deleted stretch to check it is one stretch at the join.
344	
345	### 3.6 Cut (gaming)
346	| tool | args | result |
347	|---|---|---|
348	| `add_segment` | `start`, `end` (session seconds copied off lines), `why` | ok with the snapped segment, or error (past the end with the mm:ss hint; ends before start; no EVENT line inside; overlaps an existing segment) |
349	| `remove_segment` | `start` | ok |
350	| `set_speed` | `start`, `rate` | ok (a rate over a whole segment) |
351	| `finish_cut` | – | runs the prototype's whole-cut checks (count within [min,max], footage within the target window) and returns the problem list or ok |
352	
353	### 3.7 Captions / speed / decorations (per clip)
354	| tool | args | result |
355	|---|---|---|
356	| `add_caption` | `clip`, `start`, `end` (offsets), `text` | ok or error (clip not given; under policy.captionMin) |
357	| `set_clip_speed` | `clip`, `rate` | ok or error (rate > 1 on a captioned clip) |
358	| `add_effect` | `clip`, `kind` (zoom/stop/volume), `start`, `end`, `gain?` | ok or error (kind not one of the three) |
359	
360	### 3.8 Narration
361	| tool | args | result |
362	|---|---|---|
363	| `write_line` | `clip`, `at` (offset), `text`, `emotion`, `pos?` | ok (at clamped inside the clip, never its last second; word ceiling reported), or error |
364	| `leave_silent` | `clip` | ok |
365	`finish` reports clips with no answer.
366	
367	### 3.9 Upload text and thumbnail
368	| tool | args | result |
369	|---|---|---|
370	| `set_title` | `text` | ok (warns over seven words) |
371	| `set_description` | `text` | ok |
372	| `pick_frame` | `clip`, `offset` | ok with the frame taken as the thumbnail (no drawing) |
373	| `set_thumbnail_instruction` | `text`, `negative?` | ok (an image model will draw) |
374	`finish` requires a title and a description.
375	
376	### 3.10 Translate (per batch of numbered lines)
377	| tool | args | result |
378	|---|---|---|
379	| `translate_line` | `n`, `text` | ok or error (empty) |
380	`finish` lists the numbers still missing; the app re-asks once for those.
381	
382	### 3.11 Policy derivation (once per project, F0.7)
383	| tool | args | result |
384	|---|---|---|
385	| `set_policy` | `field`, `value`, `because` | ok or error (unknown field, out of range) |
386	The model reads the User Context and sets only the fields the context speaks to ("clips under 2 s", "about 12 minutes", "keep the swearing"). Every other field keeps its default. The form shows the `because`.
387	
388	## 4. Degraded modes
389	- No aligner: cut points come off the waveform ("clean wherever there is a silence to cut in, and unable to cut between two words of one breath").
390	- No firefox or inside Flatpak: no web tools offered; the model writes only what the material says.
391	- sd.cpp down: the render completes; the thumbnail half fails and is logged.
392	- An LLM server that refuses `tools`: the job runs as one JSON answer with the prototype's parsers and retry turns.
393	- A model whose reply is cut off at the token limit: with tools, everything already called stands; without, the prototype's "answer again with far fewer items" retry.
394

29	## 2. Flows
30	
31	### F1.1 ▶ Prepare
32	S1 Ignore when running. No sources → "add at least one source". Two sources with one base name → refuse (log "!!! A and B are both inputs/<base> -- rename one"). S2 Save the project. S3 If the last run was stopped inside Describe → remove every `events.tsv`/`state.txt` (">>> stopped last time — describing from the start again: … (scaled frames kept)"). S4 startRun; log ">>> prepare: N input files", each file, the inputs summary, and ">>> prepare: sending the session context from Prepare (N characters)". S5 Check the audio server and that the ASR and diarization models (and separation when asked) are served. S6 Phases with their share of the bar: voice separation (F1.2) 0–10 % when asked; ingest (F1.3 + F1.6 in parallel) to 30 %; understand = describe (F1.7) then fix (F1.8) then marking (F1.9/F1.10) 30–100 %. S7 On success: fraction 1, ">>> prepare wrote:" + a tree of the three folders, status "prepared — N files"; stopped → "stopped — finished work is kept"; failed → "prepare FAILED: …" / "prepare failed — see log". S8 Refresh the page, the gates and the Cut page; unload audio models.
33	
34	```
35	 ▶ ──► preflight ──► [separate] ──► ingest ┬─ speech: per source F1.3 ──┐
36	                                            └─ frames: per video  F1.6 ──┴──► describe F1.7 ──► fix F1.8 ──► mark F1.9|F1.10 ──► done
37	```
38	
39	### F1.2 Voice separation (rows with ✂)
40	S1 Decode to 44.1 kHz stereo pcm. S2 Chunk at P.sep.chunkMax (300 s) on silences. S3 Per chunk: upload, run the separation model, take the `vocals|voice` stem as the voice and the `instrumental` stem (or every other stem mixed with amix normalize=0) as the rest. S4 Join the parts; a video's rest is muxed as mkv with the picture copied. S5 Write `stems/<base>.split-voice.wav` and `<base>.split-novoice.wav|.mkv` (names keep the timestamp). S6 Log ">>> [base] split into A and B" and a loudness report; warn when the rest sits ≥ 10 dB under the mix. S7 The source row becomes two rows: the rest keeps footage, the voice takes the narrator slot; the wish is cleared; project saved. Skip when both halves exist.
41	
42	### F1.3 Per source: audio → text → word times → speakers → segments
43	S1 `voice16k.wav` (mono 16 kHz) unless present; log ">>> [base] X s of audio". S2 **Short take**: shorter than P.policy.minTakeSeconds (2.0) → written up as silence, no server asked (">>> [base] X s long -- a start/stop, not a take: written up as silence"). S3 ASR (F1.4) unless `words.json` exists. S4 Alignment (F1.5) when an aligner is served and `words.aligned.json` is absent; failure is a warning when the ASR gave word times, a hard error when it did not. S5 Diarization unless `turns.json` exists (fatal after the window ladder). S6 Segments: words from the aligned or ASR times; speaker by greatest turn overlap, else nearest turn within 1 s, else SPEAKER_00 when there are no turns, else "?"; a word's end clamped to start + 2 s; a segment breaks on speaker change, a gap > 0.7 s, or 12 s; write `transcript.tsv` and `transcript.srt`; log ">>> [base] N segments".
44	
45	### F1.4 ASR in chunks
46	S1 Chunk limit 60 s for a qwen3-family model, else 300 s; on an out-of-memory error halve down to 20 s and retry (log). S2 One request when the file fits; else cut at silence midpoints into even pieces (seek ≤ 20 s, capped at limit/6 and step/3); scratch in `asr/`, removed on success. S3 Per chunk: checkpoint, progress "recognising speech i/n", cut with -ss before -i, upload, run the ASR model with `{audio, language}`. S4 Stitch `{text, words}` with sample offsets shifted; write `transcript.txt`, `asrchunks.json`, then `words.json` last. Empty text is a real case (">>> [base] no speech found -- an empty transcript").
47	
48	### F1.5 Forced alignment
49	S1 Aligner = the configured id, else every model declared task align, preferring qwen3-aligner; the first that answers is used for the rest of the run. S2 Pieces = the ASR's own chunks when word counts agree, else 60 s windows cut at silences with the words shared by voiced seconds. S3 Each window trimmed to where sound is (0.25 s pad); over the limit and > 15 s → split at the quietest moment nearest the middle (inside the middle three quarters); on out-of-memory halve to ≥ 15 s. S4 Request `{audio, text, language}`; reply words from `words|alignment|segments|result.*`, times from samples → ms → seconds. S5 Write `words.aligned.json` whole at the end. S6 Warn "!!! align: N s of the M s spoken has no word over it -- the times are wrong, and the cut will drop that footage" when bare voiced seconds ≥ 10 s and ≥ 8 %.
50	
51	### F1.6 Frames per video
52	S1 Marker `.interval` = "<interval>|<scale>" matches → only rename legacy numbered frames; skip (">>> [base] frames already extracted (Xs, scale), skipping"). S2 Else clear the folder; log the plan; filter `fps=1/interval` + the scale (a take shorter than one interval takes its first frame alone). S3 Parallel chunks of whole intervals (workers clamp(CPU/4, 2, 8); 1 for tiny or every-frame jobs); progress from ffmpeg's `-progress`. S4 Rename `f000001.jpg…` to `<start + (n−1)·interval>` stamps (-1, -2 within one second). S5 Write the marker; log ">>> [base] N frames extracted".
53	
54	### F1.7 Describe (per footage source, chunks of P.describe.framesPerReq = 4)
55	S1 Frames sorted by stamp; scaled once to 896 wide into `.llmframes/` unless the preset already is. S2 Resume: chunks whose start is already in `events.tsv` are skipped; the last 3 rows seed the rolling window; `state.txt` seeds the STATE ("Recording just started."). S3 Message: User Context; "STATE so far: …"; "Frames cover t=As to t=Bs, X s apart."; "Just before this:" + the last events; the speech block (three sections always present: context before, spoken during, context after; before/after within 10 s, at most 2 per source); then per frame "[+N.Ns] FRAME i of n" and the image. S4 Cache on the whole content (images inline). S5 **Tools** (`02-services.md` §3.2): `record_event(frame, text, calm)`, `set_state(text)`, `finish`. Prototype: one "EVENT [+Ns]: …" line per frame plus "STATE: …", parsed leniently. S6 Write one `events.tsv` row per frame (a frame without an event is "same"; the first frame of a batch with no history must not be "same"); `state.txt` after every chunk. S7 Log ">>> [base] event log complete (N chunks, M answered from the cache)".
56	
57	### F1.8 Fix the transcripts (blocks of P.fix.block = 25 lines)
58	S1 Place every source on the session clock; load transcripts and event logs. S2 Per block: checkpoint; context ±5 s from every other source (its events and lines) and the source's own events; message "Context around these lines:\n…\nTranscript lines to clean (N lines, return exactly N):\n…". S3 **Tools**: `fix_line(n, text)` per line; `finish`. Prototype: N TSV lines back, discarded unless count, times (±0.01) and speakers are identical; two tries; the originals kept on failure. Only a valid block is cached. S4 Write `<source>/transcript.fixed.tsv` (+ `subtitles.srt`) or `commentary.fixed.tsv`; `offsets.tsv`. S5 Merge into `session.tsv` (rows sorted by start; events labelled EVENT); log ">>> session timeline: N rows across M source(s)". S6 Run the marking pass of the style (F1.9 or F1.10); a failure leaves the timeline unmarked ("!!! retakes: … -- the timeline stands unmarked"). S7 Write `session.txt` exactly as the cut model will see it (marked stretches folded into one line each: "<stamp> (abandoned attempt to <stamp>, said again at <stamp> -- already removed, read straight past it)").
59	
60	### F1.9 Mark retakes (Gaming style)
61	S1 Spoken lines (< 4 → empty `retakes.tsv`). S2 Brief: every spoken line numbered with "(N.Ns pause)" at gaps ≥ P.policy.retakePause (1.5 s) and "--- the recording stops here; the next one begins ---" at source changes. S3 P.policy.retakeRuns (3) identical calls (thinking off), each its own cache slot, answers pooled and deduped. **Tools**: `mark_abandoned(from, to, again)`, `unmark`, `finish` (validation in the tool: range, `again` inside the stretch, beyond the timeline, farther than P.policy.retakeReach 180 s). S4 Verify against the words: removal shorter than P.policy.retakeMin (0.3 s) dropped; `again = 0` accepted only for a whole take; the repeated tail found by a fuzzy match (≥ 70 % run, ≤ 3 skips; words equal, prefix ≥ 3 bytes, or one edit) and the mark trimmed to it; a rephrase trimmed to the broken-off tail (fragments ≤ 6 s); refused marks re-heard by a second ASR pass on both attempts. S5 Place the edges (F1.11), merge marks. S6 Refuse everything when more than P.policy.retakeCeil (40 %) of the speech would go. S7 Write `retakes.tsv` (empty on purpose when none); log ">>> retakes: N abandoned stretch(es), m:ss of speech, kept out of the cut".
62	
63	### F1.10 Repair the joins (Lecture style)
64	S1 Words of every recording except the narrator mic (< 4 → empty). S2 Seams = source changes; none → ">>> text edit: one recording, no seam to repair -- every word stands". S3 Per seam (thinking ON): "JOIN k of n." + "BEFORE (the end of the take that was interrupted):" + the last P.policy.seamReach (140) words + "AFTER (the beginning of the take that follows):" + the first 140 words. **Tools**: `drop_words(side, count)`, `keep_join`, `finish`. Prototype: `{"joined": "…"}` matched back backwards (preferring the later saying); the dropped stretch must be one stretch at the join (snap 3 words; other stretches ≤ 2 words are respellings); refusals logged "!!! text edit: join k: <reason> -- nothing removed there" (no words; not at the join; several stretches; > P.policy.seamMaxWords 40 or > P.policy.seamCeil 60 %). Cached only when usable. S4 Deduplicate words repeated straight across a cut (3 words either side; the earlier goes). S5 Marks from the dropped runs; edges (F1.11); merge. S6 Write `final.txt` (surviving words as written; `|cut N|` / `|cut|` at every join) and `retakes.tsv` together; log ">>> text edit: N of M words removed in K stretch(es)".
65	
66	### F1.11 Place the edges of a mark
67	With word times: the cut ends after the last surviving word (within 0.08 s, refined to the quietest moment within 0.4 s after following the word's own sound up to 0.25 s) and resumes just before the retake's first word when nothing was said in between. Without: the mono envelope alone (reach 0.8 s, pad 0.05 s, late stamp 0.6 s). Envelope floor = 20th percentile of ±4 s raised to max(3×, +8); tail level = peak − 12 dB.
68	
69	### F1.12 Hand-edit the text (Lecture)
70	S1 The user edits `prepare/transcript/final.txt` (delete words; the join marks may stay or go). S2 On the next Cut ▶, if its mtime is after `retakes.tsv`'s: the marks are remade from the text with no model (">>> final.txt was edited after Prepare -- the marks are remade from it, no model asked"); words never said are dropped with a warning; more than 40 % removed is refused. REVIEW: a rewrite SHOULD also offer this file in an editor on the Prepare page, with the join marks as clickable seams.
71	
72	## 3. Data written
73	See `01-project-and-files.md` §1 (prepare/…).
74	
75	## 4. Parameters used
76	P.policy: minTakeSeconds, retakePause, retakeRuns, retakeReach, retakeMin, retakeCeil, retakeFrag, againReach, seamReach, seamMaxWords, seamCeil, seamSnap, seamNoise, describeFramesPerReq, describeRecentEvents, describeCtxSegs, describeCtxWindow, fixBlock. P.audio: chunk sizes, silence threshold, diarization windows and anchor sizes, merge gap/length. Engineering: frame workers, quality, scratch handling. Full list in `10-parameters.md`.
77	
78	## 5. Rules
79	- Every stage skips when its output exists; resume markers are written last and whole; scratch dirs survive failure and go on success.
80	- The server's own documents are never rewritten; derived files live beside them.
81	- Only usable answers are cached; the fix pass changes text only; the retake pass answers in line numbers; the join pass can only delete; "prefer the later saying" is the direction of the match, not a request to the model.
82	- Marks are markings, never deletions; an empty marks file means "asked, none".
83	- No aligner is a working setup; no ASR word times and no aligner is a hard failure named plainly; diarization failure is fatal after the ladder; no speech is a real case at every layer.
84	- ⏸ resumes; ⏹ restarts only the describing, and only on the next ▶.
85

32	
33	## 2. Flows
34	
35	### F4.1 ▶ Write and speak
36	S1 Refuse: busy; no cut ("no cut yet — build one on the Cut step first"); narration off ("this video has no narration — tick Narration at the top of this page to write one"); no session timeline ("run Transcript first — no session timeline"). S2 Pull half-typed rows; keep the previous file as `narration.prev.json`. S3 Job "narration" 1/2, "thinking about it"; one model call (F4.2). S4 Replace every line (REVIEW: the prototype always rewrites; the Readme promised only missing lines — the rewrite SHOULD rewrite only clips with no entry unless the user asks for all, via a choice on the ▶ or the policy); the silent list is cleared; save; rebuild; ">>> narration written for N clips"; "narration written — speaking it". S5 Captions-only voice → done ("narrate: captions only — N line(s) written, none spoken"). S6 Job "speaking" 2/2, one task per line: checkpoint; skip blank text or a cached wav; else synthesize (F4.4). ">>> narrate: N line(s) spoken, M already in the cache". S7 Done: "narration ready and spoken — ▶ the preview hears it in place" / "narration ready — captions only, nothing spoken" / "<stage> stopped" / "<stage> failed — see log".
37	
38	### F4.2 The narration call
39	System = house rules + the "narrate" prompt (+ the speech addendum when the clips play what people said out loud: "THIS VIDEO PLAYS WHAT PEOPLE SAID OUT LOUD… never say one back: set it up before it lands, or react after it"; + the captions addendum for a captions-only voice: write for the eye, emotion "", every entry has a placement). User = User Context (+ the speech rule) + "THE CLIPS AND WHAT IS KNOWN ABOUT EACH:" + per clip "CLIP n: a–b (X s[ of footage at Rx, Y s on screen], at most W words -- fewer is better, none is fine)" with its lines within ±4 s as "[+Ns] LABEL: text" (the narrator's mic as NARRATOR; "(no lines over this clip: nothing said, nothing described)"), inserts described ("not footage: a graphic or clip inserted here … Narrate what is ON it, or say nothing"), and effects as "[+Ns] MARKED: name" / "[+Ns] CAPTION: text". Word ceiling per clip = clamp(0.75 · seconds, P.policy.narrationMinWords 8, P.policy.narrationMaxWords 30). Thinking on; web tools offered. **Tools**: `write_line(clip, at, text, emotion, pos?)`, `leave_silent(clip)`, `finish` (`02-services.md` §3.8). Validation in the tool: the clip must be one given; `at` clamped inside the clip and never its last second; `pos` normalised. Prototype: `{"entries":[{start,end,at,text,emotion}]}` matched to clips by echoed bounds within 0.5 s scanning forward, three attempts, thinking turned off after a call that wrote nothing. Streaming progress = written clips / clips. Not served from the reply cache (the TTS cache is the cache).
40	
41	### F4.3 Fit a line to its clip (the render's rule, mirrored by the row warnings)
42	Lines pack in order from max(P.policy.narrationLead 0.3, at), never before the previous line's end + P.policy.narrationGap (0.3); need = packed end + P.policy.narrationTail (0.2). Over the clip: grow the clip by up to P.policy.narrationMaxExtend (4 s), never past the footage; still over: slide every line earlier down to the lead; still over: speed the speech up to P.policy.narrationMaxTempo (1.25×). Each is logged ("clip N: the narration does not fit where it was placed — moved X s earlier" / "clip N: narration X s does not fit Y s — sped up Zx"). Speech length = the wav's duration when it exists, else characters / the narration's own measured rate (default 15 chars/s, clamped 8..28).
43	
44	### F4.4 Speak a line (TTS)
45	S1 Reference on disk (F4.6). S2 Audio server health; the TTS model served and able to clone. S3 Upload the reference (every line; a server path dies with a restart). S4 POST /v1/audio/speech `{model, input: text, voice_ref: <server path>, language: "en", options: {emotion_alpha "0.85", seed, and either emotion_vector "<8 floats>" with emotion_alpha "1" (a weighted tag whose names are all known) or use_emotion_text "true" + emotion_text "<names>" (the judge)}}`. REVIEW: the language is hard-coded "en" in the prototype; it SHOULD follow the project language or a policy field. S5 A reply under 1000 bytes or non-200 is a failure; else write `narrate/tts/<hash>.wav`. S6 Emotion vocabulary: eight bases (happy, angry, sad, afraid, disgusted, melancholic, surprised, calm) with kin words, 21 named blends as recipes over the bases; weights 0..1; unknown names go to the judge as words; never an error.
46	
47	### F4.5 Preview the cut with narration
48	S1 Click the picture or ▶: play from the line (or from the cut's start; "nothing to preview yet — cut some clips first"). The red playhead is a 2 px line on its own layer across both bands. The timeline has no tooltips by design; the status line and cursor shapes say what a press would do.

**Toolbar groups** (left to right): transport (▶ recording, ▶✂ cut, ▶✂✂ review, frame steps; the wheel over the bar steps frames, Shift = 5); preview volume; verbs (＋ Add, | Split, － Remove, ⧉ Copy, ⧉ Paste, Insert/Edit, ⇲ Lane); the effects dropdown (✚ Effect: ⊕ Zoom, ❝ Text, ▨ SVG, ⏩ Speed, 🔊 Volume, 🏷 Label); history (Undo Ctrl+Z, Redo Ctrl+Shift+Z, Revert, ✗ Clear); zoom (−, +). **Form column**: idle readings (thumbnail size, aspect, playhead clock, selection, cut length, cut at 1×, source length, segments) or the form of whatever is being placed or edited (an insert, an effect); forms are live (kept as you type; one Undo takes the whole edit back) with a pinned heading (✕ closes) and a pinned footer for buttons.

**Tracks**: gutter (fold-all badge, per-lane and per-row sound switches, empty-row ✕), ruler, selection band (green bar per kept scene with its ✕ and draggable ends; the blue selection with its ✕ and ends; fold −/+ badges), effects lane (one row per overlapping group), picture rows (thumbnails; amber striped edges where a recording starts/ends; each row's own first audio track as a strip below it; camera and speaker badges on the scene under the line or held), the separate recordings' lanes below, then the scrollbar (hidden when everything fits; its thumb is geared at high zoom so one screenful is always 40 px of drag).

## 2. Model (summary; full schema in `01-project-and-files.md` §3)
Session clock; rows by greedy interval colouring with pins; filmed runs and cells; folds have zero width; x↔time through the cells (half-open on the right); zoom 4 px/s at open, floor = fit the filmed length, ceiling 240 px/s; scenes `[s,e)` on a row with inserts, lanes, quiet lists; effects; undo snapshots (segments, effects, aspect, shift, rows, lanes, nrows), depth 50; base = the last suggestion or what the page opened with.

## 3. Transport flows

### F2.1 Play the recording (▶)
S1 If the preview is the cut → switch it to the recording ("preview is the recording again — everything plays, cuts and all"); if already playing, carry on and stop here. S2 Else toggle: pause when playing; play from the red line otherwise. S3 While playing every second plays, cuts and all; playback into a folded seam opens it ("unfolded m:ss — ▶ ran into it"); at the end of a recording the line walks on to the next one (or a camera still rolling at that second). S4 The clock shows session time; the line follows the player ten times a second with a smoothed live clock in between.

### F2.2 Play the cut (▶✂)
S1 Greyed with no clips. S2 If the preview is the recording → switch to the cut (the line snaps onto kept material; "preview is the cut — the clock reads the finished video"); if playing, carry on. S3 If a review is running → end the review and carry on as the plain cut. S4 Else toggle. S5 While playing: removed stretches are skipped (the line jumps to the next clip's first playable second; past the last clip playback pauses); the next jump is preloaded three seconds ahead in a spare pipeline so the join plays without a freeze (P.preview.preloadLead); speed effects run at their flat rate; stops show their still; volume effects apply; the clock reads the cut's own time. S6 The dropped stretches are dimmed on the tracks.

### F2.3 Review every cut (▶✂✂)
S1 Greyed with fewer than two clips ("nothing to review — a cut needs two clips to have a join between them"). S2 Start from the red line: inside a join's window (P.policy.reviewPad = 10 s before the join to 10 s after it, clamped to the clips) → play on; between windows → seek to the next join's run-up; past the last → the first join. S3 Play as the cut; when the seconds after a join have played, seek to the next join's run-up unless it is already behind the line, in which case play on into it. S4 Status "reviewing cut N of M — 10 s before and after the join at m:ss"; after the last: pause, "reviewed all N cuts". S5 Pressing ▶✂✂ while it runs pauses and ends the review; ▶ or ▶✂ switch over without stopping; moving the line by hand ends it ("the line was moved — the cut review is over; ▶✂✂ starts it again").

**One rule for the three buttons**: each wears ⏸ only while its own thing runs; pressing that one pauses; pressing another switches the preview over without stopping; exactly one of the three is lit (▶ recording, ▶✂ cut, ▶✂✂ review).

### F2.4 Place and step the line
S1 A click on a track puts the red line there, clears the selection, watches that row, and takes the scene under the click in hand. S2 ‹f f› step one frame (Shift/‹‹f f›› five) of the recording under the line and pause; with an edge, clip or effect held they nudge that instead. S3 ←/→ do the same only while something is held; Space toggles play. S4 The line's position is remembered in `cut/line.json` (written at most once a second while it moves, flushed on close) and restored on the next open when a recording still covers it.

### F2.5 Hush and mix (what the preview hears)
The separate recordings overlapping the footage play as their own pipelines in sync; a lane the scene under the line silences is never started; the footage's own sound is muted by property when silenced; a lane started under a scene boundary is seeked with a stop at it. Rate and gain follow the effects under the line. The preview volume is one number shared by every preview.

## 4. Editing flows

### F2.6 Select
S1 Left-drag on a picture row, a wave strip or a lane draws a selection scoped to what it was drawn on (footage of that row, or one recording's sound). S2 The band's ends resize it, its middle moves it, its ✕ clears it; ends snap to clip borders, recording ends, effect ends and the playhead within 8 px. S3 In/out marks and the Selection readout follow the band. S4 A sound selection greys Add/Split/Remove and re-aims Copy and Insert at sound.

### F2.7 Add, Split, Remove, ⌦
- **Add**: keep the selection as scenes (one per filmed run; under P.policy.minSceneSeconds = 1 s refused: "nothing to add: X s selected, a scene is 1 s or more"); both ends snap to word edges, silences, line edges and visual cuts within 5 s; the span is taken off every other row ("added on <cam>, and taken off the other camera — ↶ Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes it back").
- **Split**: a border at each end of the selection, nothing removed (halves ≥ 0.04 s; the right half is marked so coalescing does not undo it); with no selection, one border at the red line and the right half taken in hand.
- **Remove**: drop exactly the selection ("removed X s — the scene it went through is two now (↶ Undo takes it back)"); remainders ≥ 0.04 s survive.
- **⌦ / Delete**: in order: a held effect; a held clip (the only way to remove a spliced card); a selection; the scene under the line; else "nothing selected — click a kept scene, or drag a region on a track".
- **✕ badges**: on a green bar (drop that scene), on the selection, on a cut lane, on an empty row, on an effect.

### F2.8 Trim and move
S1 Wherever the pointer shows a resize arrow (within 6 px of a clip border on the pictures or the green bar), a drag with either button trims that border: an end may not go below start + 1 s, past the next clip or the recording's end; a start not above end − 1 s, below the previous clip or the recording's start; the picture scrubs live (throttled); on release touching neighbours merge and the picture lands on the edge ("clip N: a – b (X s)"). S2 The right button moves: a green bar's middle or a clip on the green slides the scene along its recording (keeping its length, clear of neighbours, snapping flush within 8 px); a press elsewhere on a row slides the whole camera row along the clock (the shift correction), a lane or a strip slides that one recording, and a selection of footage slides the selected scenes; a row change happens when the recording fits; folds near the grab open for the drag and refold after; one Undo per gesture; status "<what> moved +1.23 s". S3 An unmoved press is a click; a right click never moves the line.

### F2.9 Copy, Paste, Lane
S1 Copy takes the selection in hand (≥ 1 s; "copied m:ss – m:ss (X s) — click where it goes, then ⧉ Paste"); the selection survives. S2 Paste at the red line: footage → a spliced insert `copy:<seconds>` (the cut is opened there, those seconds play again, the video gets longer); a sound → laid over the kept footage at the line, one piece per kept stretch, replacing the recording it was copied from ("laid X s of <base> over the footage at m:ss"; refused when no footage is kept there). Pasting consumes the copy; Esc drops it. S3 ⇲ Lane puts a footage copy on a row of its own (a cut lane windowing the file), nothing cut yet ("X s from a is now the <name> lane, starting at b").

### F2.10 Cameras and hearing
S1 The lens badge on a scene chooses which row its picture comes from ("the scene at m:ss is shown from <cam> now"). S2 The speaker badges on each lane of the held/current scene toggle whether that scene hears that lane ("<base> is silent in the scene at m:ss"); the gutter switch toggles a lane for the whole cut. S3 A click on a row watches it in the preview until ▶ takes the preview back to the cut.

### F2.11 Folds and rows
S1 The − badge in a gap folds the unfilmed time to a seam; + on the seam unfolds; the gutter badge folds or unfolds all. Folds are a view, never an edit, and never used to measure a drag. S2 An emptied bottom row stays until its ✕; a cut lane's ✕ removes the lane, its pins, shift, pictures and sound.

S1 Needs a line or a selection ("click the timeline where the insert goes first"). S2 Chooser "Insert a clip, image, animation or sound" (or "Insert a sound over the selected seconds" for a sound-scoped selection), opening in `assets/`, where the built-in SVG cards and `CARDS.md` are written on first use. S3 Defaults: a selection gives the length and means overwrite; none means splice with the file's own length (video/audio duration, an SVG's animation length, else P.policy.insertDefaultSeconds = 4). S4 Form in the column: one entry per declared card field (a Logo… picker for logo fields); radios Insert BETWEEN the footage / Play OVER the footage / Put it on a LANE of its own (video only); the sound tick ("Play it SILENT — the insert's own sound is not used" when spliced; "Keep the sound running under it — only the picture is replaced" when over); Seconds. S5 Placed: a spliced insert `s == e` with `dur`; an overwriting one replaces those seconds; a sound lays over kept footage; a lane adds a row. Status "<file> inserted at m:ss for X s, <how> — the cut is now a (was b) — ↶ Undo takes it back". S6 Right-click a card on the track to hold it; Insert becomes Edit and re-opens the form; switching modes returns or takes footage.
S7 Preview: cards render at 8 fps (one frame for stills) through ffmpeg, the nearest rendered frame shown; a spliced card holds the footage while it plays on the wall clock; card sound is its own pipeline.

### F2.13 Undo, Redo, Revert, Clear
Undo/Redo walk the snapshots ("undone — N segment(s) left"); Revert restores the base ("reverted to the N segment(s) of the last suggestion (↶ Undo brings your edits back)"); Clear takes every scene and effect off in one step ("cleared N scene(s) and M effect(s)"; sources, rows, shifts and lanes stay).

## 5. Suggest (▶ on the run bar while the preview is not started)

### F2.14 Suggest a cut
S1 Guards: busy; hand edits ("you have hand edits — press Revert first for a fresh suggestion"); no session timeline ("run Describe first — the suggestion reads the session timeline, and there is none").
S2a **Text-derived styles (Lecture)**: no model. Marks from `retakes.tsv`, or remade from `final.txt` when it was edited later (F1.12). Cut = hand-placed inserts + every filmed run trimmed to its words (from just before the first to just after the last, placed by the sound within 0.4 s, never outside the run) → marked stretches removed → dead air removed (silences longer than P.policy.deadAirMaxSeconds = 8 inside a clip are cut out leaving P.policy.deadAirKeepSeconds = 0.5) → coalesce → persist → base. Status "cut by the words: N segments"; log ">>> cut by the words: N stretch(es) taken out, m:ss of silence, N segments, M:SS total".
S2b **Model-chosen styles (Gaming)**: four jobs on the bar. (1) The cut: target length from P.policy.targetLengthSeconds (derived from the context by F0.7; prototype: a regex over the context); message = User Context + "SESSION LENGTH: N seconds…" + the target block ("KEEP between A and B seconds of footage, in at most K segments…" or "NO TARGET LENGTH…") + "SESSION TIMELINE:" + `session.txt`; thinking on; web tools offered (dropped after a first rejection). **Tools**: `add_segment`, `remove_segment`, `set_speed`, `finish_cut` (`02-services.md` §3.6); the checks the prototype ran on the whole reply (timestamps past the end with the mm:ss hint; fewer than min(1 + target/30, 4) segments; more than max(target/5, 40); footage outside target × [0.6, 1.2 | 1.5] × [1, 4]) become `finish_cut`'s answer. Up to P.llm.attempts = 3 rounds of correction; "no valid cut after 3 attempts". Streaming progress counts segments. (2) Captions, (3) speeds, (4) decorations: `06-effects.md` F3.9–F3.11.
S3 Apply: one Undo; hand-placed inserts kept; holes ≤ P.policy.seamMaxSeconds (1.5) closed only when somebody talked in them; both edges of every segment snapped (silence midpoint 0.8, word edge 0.9, line edge 0.95, visual cut where nobody talks; within 5 s; outward preferred); marked stretches removed; dead air removed; coalesce; effects clamped to the footage kept and replaced as a list; persist; base. Log ">>> suggested N segments, M:SS total" and ">>> …and N effect(s): the speeds, the captions and the decorations".

```
 ▶ (Cut) ─► guards ─► style?
   Lecture: marks ─► words fence the cut ─► drop marked ─► drop dead air ─► coalesce ─► done (no model)
   Gaming:  cut (LLM, tools) ─► captions (LLM) ─► speeds (LLM) ─► decorations (LLM) ─► walk-back ─► done
```

## 6. Parameters used
P.policy: minSceneSeconds (1.0), minPieceSeconds (0.04), snapToleranceSeconds (5.0), talkPadSeconds (0.2), deadAirMaxSeconds (8), deadAirKeepSeconds (0.5), seamMaxSeconds (1.5), reviewPadSeconds (10), targetLengthSeconds (0 = none), suggestMinSegments/maxSegments formulas, footageWindow factors, maxSpeedRate (4), insertDefaultSeconds (4), captionBatch (5). P.preview: playTick 100 ms, preloadLead 3 s, rateSeekGap 250 ms, thumb batch 6, card fps 8. Engineering: pixel reaches (6, 8, 10, 12 px), band heights, colours, zoom limits, undo depth, waveform cache format.

## 7. Rules
- One thing held at a time; picking up is not an edit; one Undo per drag; an unmoved press is a click.
- A border belongs to both buttons; moving is the right button's own verb; a selection is of what it was drawn on.
- Unfilmed time has no width; the seam second belongs to the later take; preview and render agree on half-open ranges.
- Inserts are files: never trimmed, merged, dropped by a re-suggest or given a hearing answer; a spliced insert costs no session time.
- A clip may not leave its recording; clips never overlap; Remove takes exactly the selection.
- Suggest replaces the footage half and the effects, keeps inserts, and sets the base; every model reply is walked back onto the timeline.
- `cut.json` is written by one function and its existence unlocks Narrate and Produce.
- Nothing decodes inside a draw; the tracks are a window drawn under a translate; the page is rebuilt only when Prepare's output changed.

1	# 01 — The project on disk
2	
3	A project is a folder ending in `.naivepost`. The folder **is** the output folder: nothing stores where work goes, so nothing can disagree. Every file inside is readable.
4	
5	## 1. Layout
6	
7	```
8	<name>.naivepost/
9	  naivepost.json                     the project (§2)
10	  sources/                           copies of added files (when "copy into project" is on)
11	  stems/                             voice-separation products: <base>.split-voice.wav, <base>.split-novoice.wav|.mkv
12	  assets/                            SVG cards and other inserts; CARDS.md guide; built-ins written on first use
13	  prepare/
14	    inputs/meta.env                  VIDEO_FILE, VIDEO_BASE, AUDIO_FILE, AUDIO_BASE, INTERVAL, SCALE
15	    inputs/<source>/                 voice16k.wav, transcript.txt, transcript.tsv, transcript.srt,
16	                                     words.json, asrchunks.json, words.aligned.json, turns.json
17	                                     (asr/, diar/ scratch while running)
18	    inputs/frames/<source>/          <YYYY-MM-DD_HH-MM-SS[-n]>.jpg per interval, .interval marker
19	    describe/<source>/events.tsv     one row per frame; state.txt; .llmframes/ (scaled frames)
20	    transcript/<source>/             transcript.fixed.tsv | commentary.fixed.tsv, subtitles.srt
21	    transcript/session.tsv           the merged timeline (machine copy)
22	    transcript/session.txt           the timeline as sent to the cut model
23	    transcript/offsets.tsv           video, audio, offset seconds
24	    transcript/retakes.tsv           the marks
25	    transcript/final.txt             the words of the finished video (lecture style)
26	  cache/llm/<step>/<sha256>          cached model replies
27	  cache/waves/<lane>.wave            waveform envelopes
28	  cache/edges/                       mono envelopes for edge placement
29	  cut/cut.json                       the cut (§3)
30	  cut/line.json                      {"t": <session second>} — the red line
31	  narrate/narration.json             the lines (§4); narration.prev.json (one generation back)
32	  narrate/voice.txt, pitch.txt, takes.json, voice_ref_base.wav, voice_ref.wav
33	  narrate/tts/<16 hex>.wav           spoken lines; samples/<voice>_<12 hex>.wav
34	  produce/clips/                     per-clip encodes, final.srt, final.<code>.srt, concat.txt
35	  produce/final.<container>          the video; final.stamp; final[.<code>].srt/.vtt; final.jpg; final.html
36	  produce/publish/publish.json       the upload text and thumbnail state (§5)
37	  produce/publish/thumbnail.png, thumbnail-plain.png, thumbnail.stamp, description.txt
38	  llm/<MMDD-HHMMSS>-<step>.html      one readable page per run
39	```
40	
41	Directories are created 0755, files 0644, except prompts and the settings file on the machine (0700 / 0600).
42	
43	Paths written into any project file go through one rule: inside the project → `project:<slash-relative>`; under the application root → root-relative; else absolute. One reader resolves them.
44	
45	## 2. naivepost.json
46	
47	```json
48	{
49	  "sources": [{"path": "project:sources/a.mkv", "footage": true, "narrator": 1, "sepvoice": false, "tracks": [0, 1]}],
50	  "interval": 1.0,
51	  "frame_scale": "original",
52	  "style": "read",
53	  "run_steps": ["prep", "cut"],
54	  "language": "en",
55	  "no_narration": false,
56	  "reference_sources": false,
57	  "vid_dir": "…", "aud_dir": "…",
58	  "context": "The weekly blockchain lecture …",
59	  "policy": { … },
60	  "produce": { … },
61	  "publish": { … }
62	}
63	```
64	
65	| key | meaning | default |
66	|---|---|---|
67	| sources | in order; `footage` only on video; `narrator` 1..N (exclusive); `sepvoice` is a wish cleared when granted; `tracks` = audio stream indices in the session (empty = first) | [] |
68	| interval | seconds between frames; 0 = every frame; always written | 1.0 |
69	| frame_scale | preset name (original, 896w (LLM), 480p, 720p, 1080p) | original |
70	| style | a style name from the style table (`00-principles.md` §5); prototype: "read" or "" | "" |
71	| run_steps | ticked chain pages | ["prep"] |
72	| language | ASR language code | en |
73	| no_narration | narration off | false |
74	| reference_sources | inverted on purpose: absent = copy sources in | false |
75	| vid_dir / aud_dir | last chooser folders | root/input_video, root/input_audio |
76	| context | the User Context, verbatim | "" |
77	| policy | the editing policy (`10-parameters.md` §2) with a `source` per field (user / model / default) | defaults |
78	| produce | encoder settings (`08-produce.md` §2); `out_file` is never stored | defaults |
79	| publish | upload text and thumbnail state (§5) | absent |
80	
81	Legacy keys read and migrated once, never written: `videos`, `audios` (first recording → narrator 1), `in_dir`, `out_dir`, `*_hints` (folded into the prompts with their historical lead-ins), `prompts` (adopted where the machine has none), `pitch`.
82	
83	Autosave: the project is marshalled every 2 s and written only when the bytes differ from the last write. Also flushed on window close. There is no "unsaved changes" prompt.
84	
85	## 3. cut/cut.json
86	
87	```json
88	{
89	  "segs": [{"s": 1.5, "e": 34.7, "cam": 0, "quiet": ["mic"]},
90	           {"s": 40.0, "e": 40.0, "ins": "project:assets/tier.svg?S=Dust II", "dur": 4.0, "mute": true},
91	           {"s": 60.0, "e": 65.0, "ins": "project:assets/sting.wav", "ss": 2.0, "lane": "mic"}],
92	  "aspect": "9:16",
93	  "fx": [{"kind": "zoom", "t": 12.0, "dur": 3.0, "trans": 1, "tout": 1, "cx": 0.5, "cy": 0.5, "hf": 0.6}],
94	  "shift": {"cam2": -1.25},
95	  "rows": {"cam2": 1},
96	  "lanes": [{"name": "cam-2", "src": "project:sources/cam.mkv", "at": 100.0, "off": 30.0, "dur": 20.0}],
97	  "nrows": 2,
98	  "folds": [[34.7, 40.0]]
99	}
100	```
101	
102	Segment fields: `s`, `e` session seconds (`s == e` with `dur > 0` = spliced insert); `ins` asset path (project-relative; may carry `?key=value&…`; `copy:<seconds>` = a pasted stretch of the session); `dur` (spliced length); `rate` (written only by the render planner); `ss` (start inside an inserted sound); `mute` (spliced: silent; overwriting: the footage's sound stays); `cam` (picture row); `lane` (which recording an overlaid sound replaces; "" = everything audible); `quiet` (lanes this scene does not hear); `split` (starts at a Split border; never merged automatically).
103	
104	Effects: see `06-effects.md` §1. `shift`/`rows`: hand corrections of where a recording sits and on which row. `lanes`: windows of a file given a row of their own. `nrows`: floor under the row count. `folds`: view only, ignored by the render. Legacy `sound` (whole-cut hearing) is migrated into per-scene `quiet` on first save.
105	
106	`cut.json` existing is what unlocks the Narrate and Produce steps' ▶ (the tabs themselves are always openable). It is written by exactly one function.
107	
108	## 4. narrate/narration.json
109	
110	```json
111	{"entries": [{"s": 1.5, "e": 34.7, "at": 2.0, "text": "We start with …", "emotion": "calm", "pos": "", "roll": 0}],
112	 "silent": [{"S": 40.0, "E": 65.0}]}
113	```
114	`s`/`e` are the clip's bounds copied verbatim from the cut; `at` seconds from the clip's start; `text` "" = deliberately silent; `emotion` a delivery tag; `pos` caption placement top/center/"" (bottom); `roll` re-roll count (salts the TTS cache). `silent` = clips whose last line was deleted on purpose, kept by bounds. Entries are always sorted by (s, at).
115	
116	TTS cache key (kept stable across versions on purpose): `25e<alpha>|[<roll>#][<voiceKey>|]<text>|<emotion or 8-float vector>`; file = first 8 bytes of SHA-1 as hex; seed = bytes 8..11.
117	
118	## 5. produce/publish/publish.json
119	
120	```json
121	{"frames": ["project:prepare/inputs/frames/a/2026-09-16_17-25-30.jpg"], "crop": {"x": 0.5, "y": 0.5}, "own": false,
122	 "title_box": {"cx": 0.5, "cy": 0.25, "wf": 1, "hf": 0.4}, "thumb_title": "…", "title_seeded": true,
123	 "texts": [{"cx": 0.3, "cy": 0.8, "wf": 0.4, "hf": 0.1, "text": "…"}],
124	 "title": "…", "prompt": "…", "negative": "…", "description": "…"}
125	```
126	The first frame is the base the image model edits; the rest are references. `own` = the thumbnail is a chosen frame, not drawn. `publish.json` existing means the upload text has been written; deleting the folder starts the text over.
127	
128	## 6. Text formats
129	
130	- `transcript.tsv` / `*.fixed.tsv`: `start\tend\tspeaker\ttext`, times `%.2f`.
131	- `session.tsv`: `start\tend\tsource\tspeaker|EVENT\ttext` on the session clock.
132	- `events.tsv`: `start\tend\ttext` per frame; a `same` row extends the previous row when read.
133	- `retakes.tsv`: `S\tE\tAgain\tTo\tText` (3-, 4- and 5-column files accepted).
134	- `final.txt`: the surviving words as written, `|cut N|` or `|cut|` at every join.
135	- `meta.env`: `KEY=VALUE` lines; its existence says the sources have been read.
136	- `words.json`: the ASR server's own document (`{"text", "words":[{word,start_sample,end_sample}]}`); `words.aligned.json`: `{"words":[…]}` from the aligner; `turns.json`: `[{start_sample,end_sample,speaker_id}]`.
137	- `.interval`: `<interval>|<scale name>`.
138	- `cache/waves/*.wave`: magic `AWV4`, header {chans u8, hz u16, count u32, size i64, mtime i64}, then peak bytes.
139	
140	## 7. Machine files
141	
142	- `~/.config/naivepost/llm.conf` (0600): bash-sourceable `KEY="value"`; keys in `03-shell.md` §6.
143	- `~/.config/naivepost/prompts/<key>.txt`: a prompt edited on this machine (only when it differs from the shipped text).
144	- `~/.config/naivepost/hang-*.txt`: watchdog dumps.
145	- `~/.local/share/applications/ch.bocek.naivepost.desktop` and the mime XML for `*.naivepost` (installed when the app is not run from a build cache or a Flatpak).
146	
147	## 8. Session clock
148	
149	Every source is placed by the timestamp in its file name; the earliest is zero. Accepted spellings (year first, century 19/20): `2026-08-08 19-55-15`, `…-20260808-195900-0`, `VID_20250814_213311`, `20250814213311`, `2025.08.14 - 21.33.11.03`, `2026-08-08 at 7.55.15 PM`, `2026-08-08T19:55:15`, and bare unix seconds 2017–2033. A file with no stamp sits at the session start (never at its mtime) and its row shows a warning. Nothing stamped → everything starts at 0:00. The clock is always computed over the whole session; a subset would move zero. Frames are named from the frame number (`start + (n−1)·interval`), never from a sorted position.
150	
```

1	# 02 — Services and the tool catalogue
2	
3	## 1. The four servers
4	
5	| what | default | serves | API |
6	|---|---|---|---|
7	| OpenAI-compatible LLM | `http://127.0.0.1:8731` | every text and vision job | `POST /v1/chat/completions` (streaming, tools), `GET /v1/models` |
8	| audio.cpp | `http://127.0.0.1:8765` | speech to text, alignment, diarization, voice separation, text to speech | `GET /health`, `GET /v1/models` (id, family, task), `POST /v1/ui/upload` (raw body, `X-Audiocpp-Filename`), `POST /v1/tasks/run` `{"model","request"}`, `POST /v1/audio/speech`, `POST /v1/tasks/unload_all_models` |
9	| sd.cpp (sd-server) | `http://127.0.0.1:1234` | the thumbnail when one is drawn | `GET /sdcpp/v1/capabilities`, `POST /sdcpp/v1/img_gen` → job id, `GET /sdcpp/v1/jobs/{id}`, `POST /sdcpp/v1/jobs/{id}/cancel` |
10	| ffmpeg / ffprobe | on PATH (or a configured path; ffprobe from the same folder) | frames, waveforms, cuts, encodes | subprocesses |
11	
12	A server box left empty means the loopback default. A box with a host and no scheme is read as `https://host`. Keys are sent as `Authorization: Bearer …` only when non-empty. `readConf` is re-read per step so a settings change takes effect on the next step.
13	
14	Audio model ids (settings, with defaults): ASR `nemotron-asr`, diarization `sortformer-diar`, TTS `index-tts2`, separation `bs-roformer`, aligner: none by default (any model declared task `align`, preferring `qwen3-aligner`). A missing model is reported with the server's own install hint. Nothing is compiled in; no call leaves the machine unless a box points elsewhere.
15	
16	Every request rides the run's cancel context, so ⏹ aborts it. Audio task calls have no client timeout (an hour of audio is an hour of work). LLM calls have a silence rule (streamed) or a whole-call ceiling (`09-llm-and-tools.md` §4).
17	
18	## 2. Model roles (which job asks which server)
19	
20	| job | model | thinking | answers with |
21	|---|---|---|---|
22	| speech to text | ASR (audio.cpp) | – | text per chunk (≤ 60 s for qwen3-family, else ≤ 300 s) |
23	| word times | aligner (audio.cpp) | – | start/end per word, the chunk's own words in hand |
24	| who spoke when | diarization (audio.cpp) | – | speaker turns per window (90 → 45 → 25 s ladder) |
25	| voice split | separation (audio.cpp) | – | voice and rest stems |
26	| what is on screen | LLM with vision | off | one EVENT per frame + a running STATE, four frames a call |
27	| clean transcript | LLM | off | the same lines respelled; times and speakers unchanged, enforced |
28	| lecture joins | LLM | on | the two takes run on as one; only deletions accepted |
29	| retakes (gaming) | LLM | off | line numbers of abandoned stretches, three runs pooled |
30	| gaming cut | LLM (+ web tools) | on | segments in session seconds copied off the timeline |
31	| captions, speed, effects | LLM | off | per clip, in the clip's own seconds |
32	| narration | LLM (+ web tools) → TTS | on | a line per clip with an emotion; spoken in the cloned voice |
33	| upload text | LLM (+ web tools) | on | title, thumbnail (frame or instruction), description |
34	| thumbnail | sd.cpp | – | an image edited from real frames; only when an instruction exists and no frame was named |
35	| subtitles in other languages | LLM | off | numbered lines translated, one call per language |
36	
37	## 3. Tool catalogue (rewrite directive B)
38	
39	Tools are offered per job. Each tool's result is a short JSON object; problems come back as `{"error": "<one sentence the model can act on>"}` and never end the flow. Numbers the model must not compute are always identifiers from the request (line, clip, frame numbers; offsets as stamped).
40	
41	### 3.1 Shared
42	
43	| tool | args | result |
44	|---|---|---|
45	| `get_context` | – | the User Context and the policy fields relevant to this job |
46	| `get_lines` | `from`, `to` (line numbers of the session timeline) | the stamped lines |
47	| `get_events` | `from`, `to` (session seconds) | EVENT lines in the range |
48	| `web_search` | `broad`, `medium`, `narrow` | up to 8 hits with snippets (offered only where the prototype offered it: cut, narrate, upload text) |
49	| `web_read` | `url` | page text (≤ 6000 chars) |
50	| `finish` | – | ends the job |
51	
52	### 3.2 Describe (per chunk of frames)
53	| tool | args | result |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| `record_event` | `frame` (1..n as stamped), `text`, `calm` (bool) | ok; a frame recorded twice replaces |
56	| `set_state` | `text` | ok |
57	`finish` validates that every frame has an event (missing frames become "same"; the first frame of a batch with no history must not be "same").
58	
59	### 3.3 Fix (per block of transcript lines)
60	| tool | args | result |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| `fix_line` | `n` (line number in the block), `text` | ok, or error when `text` contains a tab |
63	Times and speakers are not arguments: the tool cannot change them, which is the enforcement the prototype did by comparison.
64	
65	### 3.4 Retake marking (gaming)
66	| tool | args | result |
67	|---|---|---|
68	| `mark_abandoned` | `from`, `to`, `again` (line numbers; `again` 0 = never picked up) | ok, or the prototype's refusal ("lines a-b say they are said again at line c, which is inside them -- not a mark", out of range, too far (> policy.retakeReach)) |
69	| `unmark` | `from`, `to` | ok |
70	
71	### 3.5 Text edit (lecture, per join)
72	| tool | args | result |
73	|---|---|---|
74	| `drop_words` | `side` (before/after), `count` | ok with the words that would go; error when the join would lose more than policy.seamMaxWords / policy.seamCeil |
75	| `keep_join` | – | nothing removed here (a whole answer) |
76	Prototype: the model returned the joined text and the app derived the counts by matching backwards. With tools the counts are stated directly, and the app still re-derives the deleted stretch to check it is one stretch at the join.
77	
78	### 3.6 Cut (gaming)
79	| tool | args | result |
80	|---|---|---|
81	| `add_segment` | `start`, `end` (session seconds copied off lines), `why` | ok with the snapped segment, or error (past the end with the mm:ss hint; ends before start; no EVENT line inside; overlaps an existing segment) |
82	| `remove_segment` | `start` | ok |
83	| `set_speed` | `start`, `rate` | ok (a rate over a whole segment) |
84	| `finish_cut` | – | runs the prototype's whole-cut checks (count within [min,max], footage within the target window) and returns the problem list or ok |
85	
86	### 3.7 Captions / speed / decorations (per clip)
87	| tool | args | result |
88	|---|---|---|
89	| `add_caption` | `clip`, `start`, `end` (offsets), `text` | ok or error (clip not given; under policy.captionMin) |
90	| `set_clip_speed` | `clip`, `rate` | ok or error (rate > 1 on a captioned clip) |
91	| `add_effect` | `clip`, `kind` (zoom/stop/volume), `start`, `end`, `gain?` | ok or error (kind not one of the three) |
92	
93	### 3.8 Narration
94	| tool | args | result |
95	|---|---|---|
96	| `write_line` | `clip`, `at` (offset), `text`, `emotion`, `pos?` | ok (at clamped inside the clip, never its last second; word ceiling reported), or error |
97	| `leave_silent` | `clip` | ok |
98	`finish` reports clips with no answer.
99	
100	### 3.9 Upload text and thumbnail
101	| tool | args | result |
102	|---|---|---|
103	| `set_title` | `text` | ok (warns over seven words) |
104	| `set_description` | `text` | ok |
105	| `pick_frame` | `clip`, `offset` | ok with the frame taken as the thumbnail (no drawing) |
106	| `set_thumbnail_instruction` | `text`, `negative?` | ok (an image model will draw) |
107	`finish` requires a title and a description.
108	
109	### 3.10 Translate (per batch of numbered lines)
110	| tool | args | result |
111	|---|---|---|
112	| `translate_line` | `n`, `text` | ok or error (empty) |
113	`finish` lists the numbers still missing; the app re-asks once for those.
114	
115	### 3.11 Policy derivation (once per project, F0.7)
116	| tool | args | result |
117	|---|---|---|
118	| `set_policy` | `field`, `value`, `because` | ok or error (unknown field, out of range) |
119	The model reads the User Context and sets only the fields the context speaks to ("clips under 2 s", "about 12 minutes", "keep the swearing"). Every other field keeps its default. The form shows the `because`.
120	
121	## 4. Degraded modes
122	- No aligner: cut points come off the waveform ("clean wherever there is a silence to cut in, and unable to cut between two words of one breath").
123	- No firefox or inside Flatpak: no web tools offered; the model writes only what the material says.
124	- sd.cpp down: the render completes; the thumbnail half fails and is logged.
125	- An LLM server that refuses `tools`: the job runs as one JSON answer with the prototype's parsers and retry turns.
126	- A model whose reply is cut off at the token limit: with tools, everything already called stands; without, the prototype's "answer again with far fewer items" retry.
127	
```
