1	# 06 — Effects
2	
3	Zoom, speed (including stop), text, SVG drawing, volume and label. Each is one record in `cut.json`'s `fx` list, drawn as a bar on the effects lane, placed by hand on the preview or the lane, or proposed by the model after the cut. The preview and the render share the functions that turn an effect into a camera path, a fitted title, a fade or a gain.
4	
5	## 1. Record
6	
7	| field | zoom | speed/stop | text | svg | volume | label |
8	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
9	| t, dur | session second; total length incl. fades (the bar) | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ |
10	| trans, tout, ease | glide in/out | ramp in/out (or the still's fades) | fade in/out | fade in/out | ramp in/out | – |
11	| cx, cy, hf | rect centre + height as fractions of the SOURCE frame (width follows the aspect) | – | box centre + height as fractions of the OUTPUT frame | same | – | – |
12	| wf | – | – | box width / output width | same | – | – |
13	| stay | pull back (false) or reframe until the next zoom (true) | – | – | – | – | – |
14	| rate, snd | – | rate (1 own clock; 0 = stop); sound answer "" / pitch / own / scene / mute | – | – | – | – |
15	| gain | – | – | – | – | linear gain, 0 = silence | – |
16	| text / src | – | – | the words | the file | – | the name |
17	
18	Legacy: `view` → zoom; `mute` → `snd: "mute"`. `ease` stores "" for linear so old files stay byte-identical.
19	
20	## 2. The lane and the preview
21	
22	```
23	 effects lane   ⊕ 3.0s ████████╲     ❝ “Welcome to…” ▓▓▓▓▓▓   ⏩ ×4 · sound 1× ▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒╌╌╌╌|   🏷 “boss fight” ┆╌╌╌╌
24	                (envelope = the glides/ramps/fades the render will make; ✕ in the middle when ≥ 32 px; grips at the ends when ≥ 30 px)
25	```
26	
27	Colours: zoom (0.25,0.72,0.82), staying zoom (0.95,0.62,0.15), speed/stop (0.92,0.42,0.6), text (0.6,0.55,0.95), svg (0.4,0.8,0.5), volume (0.95,0.85,0.2), label grey-white. Rows: first-fit by seconds (span floor 0.4 s); the lane is one row deep even when empty.
28	
29	Preview (paused): everything outside the camera rect dimmed black 0.45, the rect stroked white with a plate; visible overlays at their real alpha, the held one at full with a dashed violet outline; a box being drawn dashed. Playing: only the black mask over what the finished frame does not show, and the titles; the camera layer runs on the smoothed live clock. A stop's still is rendered from the scene's own camera and fitted on the same transform as the footage.
30	
31	Preview vs render, deliberately different: the preview runs a speed effect at one flat rate (a rate change is a flushing seek); the render follows the ramps and averages overlaps; the two 1× sound answers cannot be previewed (the lane's dashed tail shows the debt).
32	
33	## 3. Flows
34	
35	### F3.1 Zoom by hand
36	S1 ✚ Effect ▾ → ⊕ Zoom arms a drag (refuses without a line: "click a track first — the effect needs a moment to happen at"; the same entry again disarms). Status/panel text: "Drag a box on the video: the picture zooms there and comes back out on its own, or stays on it — the form that opens is where that is said. The box keeps the cut's shape; let go near the full width or height to snap to it. It starts at the red line and runs 3 s…" (or "It covers the marked stretch — a – b, X s"). The camera layer goes down so the whole source is visible. S2 Drag a box on the preview (< 12 px is ignored; the smallest output-shaped window containing the box is taken; near-full width/height snaps). S3 Defaults: glide 1 s in and out, length 3 s (or the marked stretch); `stay` when an aspect is set and no staying zoom exists yet (then no glides). S4 Form "Zoom at m:ss": Length (s); At the end: Pull back / Stay on it; Fade in (s); Fade out (s) (greyed when staying: "A camera that stays has no way back, so no fade out."); Curve (Linear). Live; length ≥ 0.4. S5 Status "<label> — ↶ Undo takes it back" (or "… — the video shows this region from here on…").
37	Camera path: from the centred full-fill slice; each zoom glides from where the camera is at its start to its rect, holds, and (unless staying) glides back; a staying zoom becomes the new settled frame; nothing reaches backwards; fade-in wins overlaps. Rect clamp hf ∈ [0.02, 12], centre ∈ [−2, 3].
38	
39	### F3.2 Aspect ratio
40	Dropdown source / 9:16 / 1:1 / 4:5 / 16:9 in the form column ("the shape of the finished video — source is the footage's own, 9:16 is a vertical short. The whole frame fits inside it (bars either side) until ▭ View frames a region; the outline on the preview is what the finished video shows"). Choosing a non-source aspect with no staying zoom appends a staying zoom at 0:00 holding the whole frame for 1 s, in the same Undo step ("aspect 9:16 — a ⊕ zoom at 0:00 holds the whole frame, centred").
41	
42	### F3.3 Speed and stop by hand
43	S1 ⏩ Speed: with a selection → t/dur from it, rate 0.5; with only a line → a stop at the line for 2 s with 0.5 s fades; neither → "click a track or mark a stretch first — speed needs seconds to work on". S2 Form "Speed a – b": Speed × (×0 — stop, ×0.25, ×0.5, ×0.75, ×1 — as filmed, ×1.5, ×2, ×4, ×8, ×20, ×100, Custom…); Sound (With the picture / With the picture, pitched / 1× to the effect's end / 1× to the scene's end / Silent); Length (s); Fade in (s) ("…A ramp needs about 0.6s of footage for every × of the rate…"); Fade out (s); Curve; a cost note ("N s on screen: the sound ends N s behind the picture, and going back in sync skips those seconds."). S3 Rate 0 → a stop with length ≥ 0.5 and no clamp; else clampSpeed: rate ∈ [P.policy.minRate 0.05, P.policy.maxRate 100] and on-screen length ≥ P.policy.minClipSeconds (0.5), the rate giving way. S4 Status "… — the footage plays at that rate there and the cut gets longer or shorter to match; ↶ Undo takes it back" / "… — the picture stands still there while the clock runs…".
44	Arithmetic: overlapping rates average per span; spans that would render under 0.5 s are healed into the longer neighbour; ramps are geometric staircases with each stair ≥ P.policy.rampStepSeconds (0.6) on screen, built whole or not at all; footage under a still runs at 1×.
45	
46	### F3.4 Text (caption) by hand
47	S1 ❝ Text arms: "Drag the box the words go in — anywhere on the picture, any shape. A click puts one across the lower third." The camera layer stays up (the box is on the output frame). S2 Drag or click (default box: the lower third {0.5, 0.78, 0.8, 0.16}); t/dur from the line (3 s) or the selection; fades 0.3. S3 Form "Text at m:ss": the words (3-line box; Enter starts a new line), Length, Fade in, Fade out, Curve; length ≥ 0.3. Empty words are not placed ("type the words and they go on the picture — the form applies as you type it"). S4 Fitting: the largest size where ≤ 12 lines of 0.58 em per character fit the box (min 7 pt); bold sans-serif, white with a dark dilated edge; the same function for preview and render. S5 On the preview a box moves (snapping to the frame's thirds within 10 px) and resizes (independent axes, 16 px floor); a press without travel toggles play/pause.
48	
49	### F3.5 SVG drawing by hand
50	▨ SVG asks for the file first ("Choose a drawing to lay over the video", from `assets/`), then arms ("Drag the box <file> goes in — … the drawing keeps its own shape inside it. A click puts one across the middle."). Default box the middle {0.5, 0.5, 0.6, 0.6}. Form "SVG at m:ss": file + Choose…, Length, fades, Curve. Preview raster via ffmpeg at 512 px with transparency, cached per file. An svg with no file is not placed.
51	
52	### F3.6 Volume by hand
53	🔊 Volume: selection or line..+2 s ("click a track or mark a stretch first — volume needs seconds to work on"); defaults gain 200 %, ramps 0.25 s. Form "Volume a – b": Volume % (0..1000; "…up to 1000 for a passage recorded too quietly to hear — though a passage lifted that far brings its hiss up with it"), Length (≥ 0.1), Fade in ("0 is the hard step, which on a big change is audible as a click"), Fade out, Curve. Overlapping gains multiply; the preview applies the gain even while paused. Status "… — the picture is untouched".
54	
55	### F3.7 Label by hand
56	🏷 Label: selection or line..+2 s; Form "Label at m:ss": Name ("what you call this moment -- "the reveal", "boss fight". It changes nothing in the video: it is written into the brief the narration writer is given…"), Length (the stretch a clip must overlap). Empty name not placed. Drawn as a tag; never rendered; the narration brief lists it as MARKED.
57	
58	### F3.8 Hold, move, resize, edit, remove
59	S1 A press on a band picks it up (the line moves to its start; status "<label> picked up"; Insert becomes ✎ Edit); ends are grips when the band is ≥ 30 px; a press under 4 px of travel is a click and opens the form. S2 Drag moves the whole band (clamped inside the timeline; both ends offered to snap marks: segment ends and other effects' ends, 8 px) or an end (length ≥ 0.1 s). Frame steps and ←/→ nudge a held effect unsnapped. The hold drops when the line walks more than 1/24 s off the band. S3 The ✕ in the band's middle (≥ 32 px) or ⌦ removes it ("removed <label> — ↶ Undo takes it back"). Esc drops the hold and disarms. S4 Edit re-finds the effect by kind and start (|Δt| < 1 ms; "that effect is no longer in the cut — nothing was changed") and always takes the box from the live effect, never from the form's snapshot. S5 Forms are live: the first answer pushes Undo; every keystroke lands after a debounce; "Kept as you type — ↶ Undo takes the whole edit back."
60	
61	### F3.9 Captions proposed by the model (after the cut)
62	Batches of P.policy.captionBatch (5) clips; message = User Context + "THE CLIPS, AND WHAT WAS SAID OVER EACH:" + "CLIP n: X s long" + the lines as offsets. **Tools**: `add_caption(clip, start, end, text)`, `finish` (`02-services.md` §3.7). Validation in the tool: the clip must be one given; end−start ≥ P.policy.captionMinSeconds (0.3). Prompt rules: captions only if the context asks; clean like a subtitler (no ehm, no stutters, sentence case, swearing kept, never a paraphrase); never caption an aside to the editor. Fades min(0.3, d/4). A failed batch is skipped ("!!! captions: clips a–b skipped -- the cut stands without them").
63	
64	### F3.10 Speeds proposed by the model
65	One call; briefs note captions ("…, N caption(s) -- runs at 1") and the footage total. **Tools**: `set_clip_speed(clip, rate)` (rate > 1 on a captioned clip refused; rate ≈ 1 ignored), `finish`. Prompt rules: the longer the dull stretch the higher the rate; a clip with speech plays at 1 unless the context asks for more; slow motion only on a short clip the video is about; one rate per clip. Same-rate stretches nearer than P.policy.speedGapSeconds (4) are merged. Log ">>> speed: N clip(s) run fast — a of video from b of footage". No length gate.
66	
67	### F3.11 Decorations proposed by the model
68	One call over every clip, told the captions and speeds. **Tools**: `add_effect(clip, kind zoom|stop|volume, start, end, gain?)`, `finish`. Prompt: few and deliberate (about three or four per five minutes unless the context says otherwise); zoom 2–4 s; one stop per video; volume for level, ducking or muting; never zoom past captions. Defaults the app applies: zoom centre 60 % height with glides min(1, d/3); stop default 2 s with fades min(0.3, d/4); volume ramps min(1, d/4); a gain of 1 or none ignored, 0 kept.
69	
70	### F3.12 Clamp to the cut as applied
71	After snapping, dead-air and mark removal and coalescing: a point effect needs a footage clip under it; a band is trimmed to the clip it overlaps most and dropped under P.policy.effectMinSurvivingSeconds (1.0); a speed is re-clamped unless it is a stop; fades shrink proportionally; ">>> N effect(s) pointed at footage the final cut does not keep — dropped". Suggested effects replace the list, in the same Undo step as the segments.
72	
73	## 4. Render (how each effect becomes ffmpeg)
74	- **Speed** is the only effect that changes the clip list: clips are split at rate boundaries and the middle carries the rate (`setpts=PTS/rate`; sound by an atempo chain, or asetrate when pitched, or a mute expression when silent, or a planned 1× read head with 0.15 s dips at run ends for the own/scene answers). Inserts and spliced cards keep their own clock.
75	- **Stop**: a still of the frame at t (from the scene's own camera) overlaid with alpha fades for the frozen spans while the footage runs on at 1×.
76	- **Zoom**: sampled at clip ends and every zoom's breakpoints, straight lines between; static → crop + scale; moving → pad black as needed, crop to the union box, `zoompan` with piecewise-linear expressions at a fixed fps (default 30); more than 10× is capped and logged.
77	- **Text/SVG**: composited after the camera and the burned subtitles, each from a looped input (a title as a generated transparent SVG the frame's size: black round-joined stroke then white fill; an svg effect from the user's file scaled into its box), with alpha fades and an enable window.
78	- **Volume**: one `volume=<expr>:eval=frame` per cue applied in turn after the lane mix and before the narration.
79	- **Label**: nothing.
80	Frame box for every clip: no aspect → the footage's own; with an aspect the resolution tier names the short side (1080p on 9:16 = 1080×1920), even sides.
81	
82	## 5. Cards (SVG inserts)
83	An insert path may carry `?key=value&…` (order matters; escapes `% & = ?` only). Documents declare inputs as `<!-- Input: key[flags] | Label | hint -->` (flags `keep`, `logo`) and holes as `{{name}}` / `{{name|fallback}}` (outside comments). Two shipped cards: **tier** (a board of rows S A B C D F with items "Name|logo.png" and a `new` list of arrivals with per-item timing) and **badge** (one big letter with a caption); seeds `s a b c d f .svg` and `tier.svg` plus `CARDS.md` are written into `assets/` on first use, never overwriting. Canvas 1920×1080, dark background, 2.2 s of stillness at the end. Every animation starts at 0 and waits inside `keyTimes`, so the static file is the finished card. The render bakes SMIL (animate/set/animateTransform on numbers, lengths, colours; values/keyTimes; repeat; freeze; additive) and a CSS subset (opacity, transform, fill; simple selectors; animation longhands; standard easings) to a frame sequence at the render fps (default 25). A card's own length = the last moving moment, offered as the insert's length.
84	
85	## 6. Parameters used
86	P.policy: minRate, maxRate, minClipSeconds, rampStepSeconds, maxGain (10), speedGapSeconds, captionBatch, captionMinSeconds, effectMinSurvivingSeconds, default lengths (zoom/text/svg 3 s; label/speed/volume 2 s), default fades (text/svg 0.3; volume 0.25; stop 0.5; zoom 1), default gain 2, default rate 0.5, suggested zoom hf 0.6, decorations density (prompt). Engineering: lane height 26, grip/kill widths, snap 8/10 px, text metrics (0.58, 1.25, 0.95, 7 pt, 12 lines), edge dilation, svg preview 512 px, card constants, bake fps.
87	
88	## 7. Rules
89	One list, one owner; nothing reaches backwards; dur is the bar for every kind; one fade rule (both fades ≥ 0, together ≤ dur, trimmed proportionally); rates average, gains multiply, sound answers do not merge; a stop is not a rate; staircases are built whole or not at all; slivers are healed, not dropped; only speed touches the clip list; camera windows have no width, overlay boxes do; the box belongs to the picture not the form; forms find effects by value; one Undo per visit, drag or hold; empty effects are never placed; a click is not a drag; framing is done paused; hit order on the picture: held box → held camera → texts top-down → the framing zoom; snapping is pixel-constant and nudging unsnapped; effects cannot leave the timeline; the lane draws what the render does; static card files are finished pictures; a path with `?` is not a file; suggested effects are clamped against the cut as applied.
90	# 08 — Produce
91	
92	Renders the video, writes the subtitles in each language, and writes the title, description and thumbnail. The words half and the render half run side by side; neither reads the other's files.
93	
94	## 1. Screen
95	
96	```
97	┌ Produce ────────────────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
98	│ Images ⓘ                              [Add image…]  │ Title ⓘ                                   [↻] │
99	│ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐                     │ [Blockchain Basics: Keys and Signatures      ] │
100	│ │ base   │ │ ref 2  │ │ ref 3  │                     │ YouTube description ⓘ                          │
101	│ │ ┌crop┐ │ │        │ │        │                     │ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
102	│ │ └────┘ │ │        │ │        │                     │ │ In this lecture we …                       │ │
103	│ └────────┘ └────────┘ └────────┘                     │ │ 0:00 What this is                          │ │
104	│ 17-25-30   [Make base][Set Thumbnail][Change…][−]     │ │ #blockchain #lecture …                     │ │
105	│ Edit instruction ⓘ                                   │ └────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
106	│ [blur the background, keep the lecturer sharp …    ] ├────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
107	│ Negative prompt ⓘ                                    │ Transcode ⓘ                          [↻] [⤓] │
108	│ [watermarks, lettering                              ] │ Container: [mp4 ▾]  Codec: [h264 ▾]  Preset: [veryslow ▾] │
109	│ Thumbnail ⓘ                              [⤓] [↻]     │ Resolution: [1080p ▾] Frame rate: [30 ▾] Audio: [128 ▾] │
110	│ ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐   │ Subtitles: [none in the video ▾] Translate: [none ▾] │
111	│ │        (thumbnail; drag a box to add words)    │   │ Game audio: ━━━●━━━━━━━ 0.22                    │
112	│ │   ✎ Blockchain Basics                           │   │ Quality (CRF): ━━━━━━●━━━ 24   Frame timing: ☐ peak rate (VFR) │
113	│ └────────────────────────────────────────────────┘   │ Channels: ☐ mono              Frame edges: ☑ blurred │
114	└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
115	 Inputs: 57 clips · 11:52 · 3 to speak · no upload text      Outputs: [📁] produce/: 61 files, 220 MB
116	```
117	
118	- **Encoder settings** (labels, options, defaults and tooltips in `inventory/produce.md` §A, normative): Container mp4/mkv/webm; Codec h264/h265/vp9; Preset ultrafast…veryslow (default veryslow — REVIEW: `medium` or `slow` is a better default for hour-long sessions); Resolution 720p/1080p/original (names the short side; the cut's aspect sets the shape); Frame rate source/60/30/24; Audio 128/192/256/320 kbit/s; Subtitles burned in / track in file / none in the video (an .srt and .vtt are written beside the video either way); Translate (ticks per language in the settings list; the session's own language is never offered); Game audio 0..1 (hidden when narration is off); Quality CRF 14..34 (mark at 24); Frame timing "peak rate (VFR)"; Channels "mono"; Frame edges "blurred" (on). webm forces vp9 and turns "track in file" into "none". Output = `produce/final.<container>`, not a question. ↻ Transcode ("Encode the video again from the cut and these settings — no model call…"); ⤓ Save video (a copy elsewhere).
119	- **Images row**: up to 8; the first is the base the image model edits, the others references it can name ("the ship from the second image"); the base wears a crop box when its shape differs from the video's; per slot: Make base, Set Thumbnail (take this picture as it is, no model), Change…, remove; empty state "No image — the thumbnail will be drawn from the instruction alone." **Edit instruction** and **Negative prompt** boxes; **Thumbnail** with ⤓ export (JPEG under 2 MB) and ↻ redraw; the picture is a text-overlay editor: drag a box to add words printed to fill it, drag borders/middle to resize/move, ✎ to reword or remove; the title band is a box of its own.
120	- **Title** entry (also printed across the thumbnail the first time; after that the two are separate) with ↻ suggest (a fresh title, instruction and description; the only thing that rewrites text); **YouTube description** box.
121	- Inputs: "N clip(s) · mm:ss[ · no narration | · N to speak][ · no upload text]"; the tooltip explains what will be spoken first, which recordings are mixed, the voice, and whether `publish.json` exists. Outputs: "produce/ — the finished video, the per-clip encodes, the thumbnail and the upload text".
122	
123	## 2. Flows
124	
125	### F5.1 ▶ Produce
126	S1 Refuse when busy; no cut → "no cut yet — build one on the Cut step first". S2 If the render is up to date (F5.3 stamp) the encode is skipped (">>> the video is already what this page describes — not encoding it again (↻ beside Transcode encodes anyway)"); otherwise, if the video exists, confirm "Overwrite <base>?" ("<path> — size, age\n\nThe encode takes minutes and there is no undo for it."). S3 Snapshot everything on the GUI thread (cut, lines, settings, sources, publish state, aspect). S4 startRun; two halves in parallel: **words** (F5.6, its own progress line; a failure is logged "!!! the upload text and thumbnail failed: … -- the render carries on") and **render** (F5.2). S5 After both: write the `<video>` tag page (F5.5). S6 The render's error is the run's verdict; done → "produced <file> — X s, size".
127	
128	```
129	 ▶ ──┬── words: brief ─► LLM (tools) ─► frames row ─► publish.json ─► [draw sd.cpp] ─► print words ─► thumbnail.png
130	     └── render: speak missing ─► plan clips ─► subtitles ─► encode clips ─► join ─► translate ─► loudness+mux ─► sidecars
131	                                                                                                        └─► <video> tag
132	```
133	
134	### F5.2 The render
135	S1 Clear `produce/clips/`. S2 Speak every line that has no wav (job "speaking" 1/2). S3 Plan one clip per cut segment (after speed effects split them): footage (rate, clamped to the recording), copies (`copy:<s>`), inserts (missing file → "clip N: <file> is not there any more — skipped"), sounds over footage; clips shorter than P.policy.minClipSeconds (0.5) are dropped with a log line naming any narration lost with them. Narration lines matched to clips (overlap ≥ half the shorter span) and fitted (F4.3). Sound plan for own-clock runs; lane mixes per clip (overlaps ≥ 0.1 s; a per-lane report "<lane> is mixed into N of the M clips"); frame box for every clip; camera paths; text, gain, hush and still cues. S4 Subtitles on the produced clock (F5.4) → `clips/final.srt`; stale sidecars beside the video deleted by exact name. S5 Encode each clip (job "clip": stems `c000_<stamp>`; -ss before -i; the filter graph of `06-effects.md` §4 plus burned subtitles; audio: speed → hush → lane bed → gains → seam dips → narration mix at P.policy.gameVolume → limiter −1 dBFS → 48 kHz format; codec args by codec/preset/CRF; every command logged). A size mismatch against clip 0 is logged (the join is a stream copy). S6 Join by stream copy ("joining"). S7 Translate the cues into the ticked languages (F5.4; after the encodes so the encoder never idles behind the LLM gate). S8 Loudness + mux: `aresample=async=1:first_pts=0,loudnorm=I=-14:TP=-1.5:LRA=11`, 48 kHz, the audio codec, subtitle tracks when "track in file" (mov_text in mp4, srt in mkv; never webm), mp4 faststart flags. S9 Sidecars `<stem>[.code].srt` and `.vtt` per language; log each. S10 Write the stamp (F5.3). Checkpoints between every subprocess.
136	
137	### F5.3 What "up to date" means
138	The stamp = a hash of the encoder settings (without the output path), the segments, the lines (bounds, text, wav size and mtime), the sources (path, size, mtime), the aspect, the voice and the narration flag, kept as `<stem>.stamp` beside the video. Title, description, thumbnail and the upload record are not in it. The upload text is "written" when `produce/publish/publish.json` exists; deleting `publish/` starts the text over.
139	
140	### F5.4 Subtitles
141	S1 Cues per clip: the narration lines where a clip has them, else the clip's own speech from the aligned words (narrator mic excluded), respelled from the fixed transcript; per word: a new cue at a gap ≥ P.policy.subtitleBreakSeconds (0.6), over 2 × P.policy.subtitleRowChars (42) characters, or ≥ P.policy.subtitleMaxSeconds (6); an empty cue extends the previous one. S2 On the produced clock: no overlaps; gaps under 1.2 s held; cues under 0.8 s folded into the next; wrapped at 42 chars into ≤ 2 rows; placement tags `{\an8}`/`{\an5}` for top/centre. S3 Translation per ticked language: batches of P.policy.translateBatch lines (REVIEW: new; prototype sent all lines at once and repaired gaps), numbered; message "TRANSLATE THESE N LINES INTO X. Answer with N lines, numbered as they are here:"; thinking off; **Tools**: `translate_line(n, text)`, `finish` (`02-services.md` §3.10); missing numbers re-asked once with their original numbers; still missing keep the original text with a warning; cached only when complete. The session's own language is track 0 and never translated.
142	
143	### F5.5 The `<video>` tag
144	Poster `<stem>.jpg` (JPEG 90) from the thumbnail; tracks = the `.vtt` files on disk, the video's own language first and default; `<stem>.html` holding a bare `<video poster controls src preload="none">` with one `<track>` per language. Notes logged when the container or codec is not web-playable and that subtitles need http, not file://.
145	
146	### F5.6 Upload text and thumbnail
147	S1 Brief: "THE FINISHED VIDEO: N clips, m:ss long." + per clip "CLIP n (at m:ss in the video, X s): session a–b" with what was seen and said, + the narration at its time in the video (or "(no narration has been written for this video)"). REVIEW: for long sessions the brief MUST be bounded (P.llm.briefMaxChars, default ~120 kB) by folding each clip to its first lines and events, and the model MAY read more with `get_lines`. S2 System = the "youtube" prompt; thinking on; web tools offered. **Tools**: `set_title`, `set_description`, `pick_frame(clip, offset)`, `set_thumbnail_instruction(text, negative?)`, `finish` (`02-services.md` §3.9). Prototype: "TITLE: …", "THUMBNAIL: <instruction | frame: clip n +s>", then the description, peeled from prose. S3 A picked frame: the nearest extracted frame, cropped to the video's shape, becomes the thumbnail as it is (no model, no GPU); the row holds that frame only; `own` = true. S4 First run with no images and no chosen frame: 3 frames evenly spread over the kept footage fill the row. S5 Write `publish.json` and `description.txt` before drawing (a failed draw keeps the thinking); the title is printed onto the picture the first time it exists. S6 Drawing (unless `own`, or the thumbnail is already drawn from these images and this instruction per its own stamp): instruction + "Do not write any words, letters, titles, logos or captions into the picture. Keep the <upper|middle|lower> part of the picture calm and uncluttered: a title will be printed across it afterwards."; frame = the video's aspect at long side 1280; base cropped, references raw; sd.cpp request {prompt, negative_prompt, width, height, seed −1, ref_images, auto_resize_ref_image, png} (steps/cfg left to the server); poll every second with "drawing (<status>)"; result → `thumbnail-plain.png`. S7 Print the marked texts then the title onto `thumbnail.png`; write `thumbnail.stamp`. S8 Missing title/instruction leave the previous value; the description is always replaced.
148	
149	### F5.7 Page runs
150	- ↻ over the thumbnail: redraw from the images and instruction as they stand (clears "own"; always draws; "thumbnail drawn — ▶ renders the video").
151	- ↻ beside Title: rewrite title, instruction and description only ("title, instruction and description rewritten — ▶ renders the video").
152	- Set Thumbnail on an image: take it as it is, cropped; "thumbnail taken from <file> — the words are printed on it; ↻ draws over it".
153	- Words on the thumbnail: drag a box → dialog "Words on the thumbnail" (Remove / Cancel / Save); boxes snap to the picture's and each other's edges and middles; re-printing costs a decode, never a GPU run.
154	- ⤓ export: JPEG at the first of qualities 92, 85, 75, 60, 40 under 2 MiB.
155	- ⤓ Save video: a copy to a chosen path; ↻ Transcode: encode again without asking the model.
156	
157	## 3. Data
158	`produce/clips/` (encodes, final.srt, final.<code>.srt, concat.txt), `produce/final.<ext>` + `.stamp` + sidecars + `.jpg` + `.html`, `produce/publish/` (`01-project-and-files.md` §5).
159	
160	## 4. Parameters used
161	P.policy: minClipSeconds, gameVolume (0.22), subtitle break/row chars/max/hold/min, translateBatch, narration fitting (F4.3), loudness target (−14 LUFS, −1.5 dBTP, LRA 11), limiter (−1 dBFS), thumbnail long side (1280), title band, publish frames (3, max 8), briefMaxChars. Project: encoder settings. Engineering: input ordering, faststart flags, sd.cpp timeouts, poster quality, export ladder.
162	
163	## 5. Rules
164	- The join is a stream copy: every clip must come out at one frame size and audio layout; -ss before -i; -t on the output for inserts, sounds, freezes and rated clips; adelay in whole milliseconds; input indices append-only; 0.5 s is the single clip floor; a dropped clip is always logged.
165	- Cues are built for every subtitle mode; sidecars always written and stale ones deleted first; never an empty cue; translations read back by number; gaps re-asked once then left in the original; the own language is never translated; webm carries no subtitle track.
166	- ▶ leaves an up-to-date video alone; the upload text is written once per project; `publish.json` is laid down before drawing; the thumbnail has its own stamp; ↻ over it always redraws; a chosen frame survives ▶; the title is seeded onto the picture once; re-printing words never costs a GPU run.
167	- The two halves touch no common file; every widget read happens before the goroutine; the `<video>` tag is rewritten even when the encode was skipped.
168	# 09 — The LLM client, tools, gate, cache, log
169	
170	## 1. Request contract
171	- `POST <server>/v1/chat/completions`, bearer key when set; model id required ("no LLM model configured -- use the gear button").
172	- Body: `model`, `messages` (text parts and `image_url` data URLs), sampling `top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0, presence_penalty 0`; thinking mode `temperature 1.0, max_tokens 65536, enable_thinking true`; execute mode `temperature 0.6, max_tokens 8192, enable_thinking false`; the thinking switch sent both top-level and in `chat_template_kwargs` (llama.cpp reads one, other servers the other), `preserve_thinking true`; `tools` when offered; `stream true` when the caller streams.
173	- Response: `choices[0].message.{content, reasoning_content, tool_calls}` and `finish_reason`. Streaming only when the response is `text/event-stream`: `data:` chunks, `[DONE]`, tool calls reassembled by index; reasoning kept apart and never returned as the answer; EOF without `[DONE]` keeps what arrived.
174	- Every request rides the run's cancel context.
175	
176	## 2. Tool protocol
177	S1 Offer the job's tools (`02-services.md` §3) with their JSON schemas; descriptions are the instructions. S2 Loop up to P.llm.toolRounds (8): a round with calls appends the assistant turn and one `tool` message per call with the tool's result; log ">>> <step>: round i of 8 — the model asked for name(args…)" (or "…asks for the same thing again — …" when identical, the tell for a loop). S3 A round without calls: if the job's `finish` was called, the flow is complete; else ask once "Call finish when you are done, or continue with the tools." and then treat it as finished with what was produced. S4 Exhausted rounds → "!!! <step>: still calling tools after 8 rounds — the step gets no answer from this call". S5 An error on round 0 that is not a stop is read as a server refusing a `tools` field → the same job as one JSON answer with the prototype's parsers and "Your answer failed validation: … Return corrected strict JSON only." turns (degraded mode). S6 Tool errors are returned as text to the model, never failing the job. S7 Every call and result is written to the exchange page.
178	Web tools (where offered): `web_search(broad, medium, narrow)` runs three queries through a headless Firefox and answers with the narrowest that found anything (8 hits); `web_read(url)` returns up to 6000 characters; bot walls detected; 45 s per call; none inside Flatpak or with firefox "off".
179	
180	## 3. Retries
181	- Transport death (EOF, reset, refused, broken pipe, unreachable, or the words eof/connection reset/connection refused/broken pipe/server closed/no such host/transport is closing): wait 5 s, 20 s, 1 min, 2 min, 4 min (past a container restart and weight load), each cancellable by ⏹; log "!!! <step>: the server went away mid-call (…) -- waiting T and asking again (i of 5)".
182	- Anything else (a 4xx/5xx, an unusable answer): one retry after 2 s on the first failure only. A status code is never "the server went away". REVIEW: a 5xx whose body names a device or memory failure SHOULD back off like a transport death rather than resend at once.
183	- Content repair in degraded (JSON) mode: `noAnswer` (the whole reply was reasoning), `cutOff` (unexpected end of JSON → "answer again with far fewer items"), `thinkAgain` (an empty answer turns thinking off for the retry), `retryTurn`. With tools these become tool results.
184	
185	## 4. Liveness
186	- A streamed call is given up after P.llm.stallMinutes (5) without a byte; an unstreamed call after P.llm.wholeMinutes (10). Every minute a heartbeat line: ">>> <step>: nothing yet, T in" or ">>> <step>: X thinking, Y reply, T in — “…the tail…”" (the tail is the answer when there is one, else the reasoning). A cancel by the guard is reported as "nothing arrived in 5m0s" / "stopped answering after T".
187	- The **gate**: one chat request on the wire per application, taken before the watch starts and released after the reply; a queued step logs once ">>> <step>: waited for the LLM -- it was busy with <other>; one request at a time". The wait is cancellable by ⏹. Produce runs its translation after the encodes so the encoder never idles behind the gate.
188	
189	## 5. Context budgets (REVIEW — new)
190	The prototype sent whole sessions (a 64-minute lecture made a 451 kB upload brief and a 778-line translation call, and the server lost its GPU). The rewrite MUST bound every prompt: P.llm.promptMaxChars (default 120 000) per request; jobs over it read the rest through `get_lines`/`get_events` tools or run in batches (captions 5 clips; translation P.policy.translateBatch lines; the cut brief folded per clip). The exchange log records the size sent.
191	
192	## 6. Cache
193	`<project>/cache/llm/<step>/<sha256 of the JSON-encoded parts joined by NUL>`; the key holds everything that decides the answer (system prompt, user text, rolling state, speech, context, image data URLs, the run index for pooled calls). Only usable answers are stored (a fix block that failed validation, a join not at the seam, an incomplete translation are not). Used by describe, transcript, textedit, retake, translate; not by the cut, narration or upload text. With tools, the cached unit is the finished item list of a job with identical inputs.
194	
195	## 7. Exchange log
196	`<project>/llm/<MMDD-HHMMSS>-<first step>.html`, one page per run (a run = the calls between two queue resets; a call outside a run gets its own page). Sections: "N. step", a meta line (time, model, thinking/execute, duration), every message (text in `pre`, images inline), tool calls and results, the reply with reasoning in a `details` block, notes for cut-off and empty answers. App log: sizes sent, the verdict and the first 110 characters of the reply, and once per run the clickable page link. Recording never fails the call.
197	
198	## 8. Prompt assembly
199	System message = the "system" prompt cut to the job's sections by heading (THE ANSWER, THE MATERIAL, THE CLOCKS, WHAT EACH JOB IS GIVEN with only this job's line and example, TOOLS, NEVER INVENT; an unknown heading goes to every job) + "\n\n" + the job's prompt + (when the User Context is non-empty) the precedence rule. User message = the User Context block (+ the speech rule for cut and narrate) + the job's material. The twelve prompts are in `prompts/`; the policy-derivation prompt (F0.7) is new.
200	
201	## 9. Model list and tests
202	`GET /v1/models` (15 s) fills the Settings dropdown. The Settings tests send one completion and one red-square vision probe (`03-shell.md` F0.13).
203	
```

267				"nothing moves the picture but you. Picking a line — clicking its row, or " +
268				"its ▶ — starts three seconds before that line so you can watch it land, " +
269				"and then the preview simply carries on down the cut. A clip the narration " +
270				"left alone keeps its row and its ▶ too: that one plays the clip from the " +
271				"top on its own audio, which is how you decide whether it wants a line. " +
272				"A line whose time you retype into another clip leaves that row behind it, " +
273				"empty. ⏪ and ⏩ " +
274				"jump three seconds; stopped, the wheel over the slider steps one frame " +
275				"at a time, which is the resolution a line's placement is judged at. The " +
276				"playhead only lands on material the cut kept: dropped into a gap it " +
277				"carries on the way it was going, to the head of the next clip or back " +
278				"to the tail of the one behind.\n\nA take " +
279				"is stable: the same words, delivery and voice always come back as the " +
280				"same performance, so nothing you have approved changes behind you. " +
281				"When a delivery is wrong rather than the words, the row's ↻ re-rolls " +
282				"it — same line, a new draw — and plays the result.\n\nThe TTS blends eight base emotions — " +
283				"happy, angry, sad, afraid, disgusted, melancholic, surprised, calm — " +
284				"and maps whatever is in the [brackets] onto them. One or two of those " +
285				"words work best; \"loud\" or \"fast\" is not an emotion and only dilutes " +
286				"the match (anger already shouts, calm is already slow). Length lives in " +
287				"the words themselves: more short exclamations, not stretched letters, " +
288				"which get spelled out.\n\nPlain words are read by a small judge model, " +
289				"which is forgiving but approximate. Write a weight and it is skipped, " +
290				"the mix going to the engine exactly as asked: \"[angry=1]\" is pure " +
291				"anger at full force, \"[happy=0.8, surprised=0.4]\" a blend you chose. " +
292				"Weights run 0 to 1, and the difference is audible: \"[surprised]\" " +
293				"is the judge's reading of the word, \"[surprised=1]\" the axis " +
294				"itself at full force.\n\nBeside the eight there are named mixes of " +
295				"them, which take a weight the same way: excited, ecstatic, playful, " +
296				"proud, relieved, hopeful, tender, nostalgic, solemn, awed, alarmed, " +
297				"horrified, desperate, confused, frustrated, bitter, contemptuous, " +
298				"dismayed, heartbroken, ominous, tense. \"[excited=1]\" is happiness " +
299				"with surprise mixed into it, which is what excitement sounds like " +
300				"and what plain happiness does not. Any name none of these knows sends the " +
301				"line back to the judge rather than guessing at an axis."},
302		{"produce", "Produce", "applications-multimedia-symbolic", "Write the upload text, draw the thumbnail and render the video",
303			"Finish Cut first — there is no cut to produce a video from",
304			"Everything the upload needs, from one ▶: the first press writes the " +
305				"title, the thumbnail instruction and the description; every press " +
306				"draws the thumbnail; and then the final video is rendered — every " +
307				"clip cut from its own recording, the narration laid over ducked game " +
308				"audio, the whole thing loudness-normalized to -14 LUFS for YouTube. " +
309				"Lines that have not been synthesized yet are spoken first.\n\nThe " +
310				"model is not asked for the text again after the first run, however " +
311				"much you edit the boxes: rewording the edit instruction or swapping " +
312				"the images costs GPU time and no thinking. Deleting the publish folder " +
313				"is what starts the text over; Suggest again, beside the title, " +
314				"rewrites it without redrawing or rendering.\n\nThe thumbnail is " +
315				"usually an edit of one of your own frames, which is what keeps it " +
316				"recognizably this video rather than a stock illustration of the " +
317				"genre. The first image in the row is the picture being edited; the " +
318				"others are references the instruction can name by position — \"put " +
319				"the ship from the second image behind them\" — and Make base " +
320				"promotes one to the front. Empty the row and it is drawn from the " +
321				"instruction alone. Write the instruction as instructions, not as a " +
322				"description of a picture: say what to change, and everything you do " +
323				"not mention stays as it is. The title is lettered into the picture " +
324				"by the image model — four or five words survive being shrunk to a " +
325				"phone's sidebar, and an empty title means no lettering.\n\nA " +
326				"session's separate recordings are in the sound as well as in the " +
327				"picture: whatever was running while a clip was running is mixed into " +
328				"it, from the second of that recording the clip actually falls on — " +
329				"the same placement the blue lanes on Cut are drawn from, with the " +
330				"footage as the master. It joins the game audio rather than the " +
331				"narration, so \"Game audio under voice\" ducks both together and " +
332				"the spoken lines still sit on top. Cards are left silent: a card is " +
333				"time added to the cut, not a moment of the session, so there is " +
334				"nothing that was said under it."},
335	}

337	// stepLocked reports whether a tab's prerequisites are missing. Prepare
338	// never is -- it is where the sources are added, so a project with nothing in
339	// it still has to be able to open it -- and an unknown name (there is none, but
340	// the lookup can fail) counts as open rather than as locked: refusing to show a
341	// page is the worse mistake.
342	func (a *App) stepLocked(i int) bool {
343		if i < 0 || i >= len(steps) {
344			return false
345		}
346		switch steps[i].name {
347		case "cut":
348			return a.cutLocked
349		case "narrate":
350			// choosing a voice lives on this tab and therefore waits for a cut,
351			// which it does not need. That is deliberate: it belongs beside the lines
352			// it will speak, and hearing a sample before there is anything to narrate
353			// decides nothing you cannot decide again afterwards.
354			return a.narrateLocked
355		case "produce":
356			return a.produceLocked
357		}
358		return false
359	}
360	
361	func stepIndex(name string) int {
362		for i, s := range steps {
363			if s.name == name {
364				return i
365			}
366		}
367		return -1
368	}
369	
370	// showStep moves to a page without going through the tab's click handler --
371	// for the bounce off a locked tab, and for sending a page whose prerequisites
372	// vanished back to the start.
373	func (a *App) showStep(name string) {
374		// whatever was half-typed on the page being left is on disk before it is
375		// left: the narration boxes write on a beat after the typing stops, and
376		// clicking a tab is exactly the moment that beat has not come yet
377		a.narr.flushSave()
378		a.tabGuard = true
379		for i, s := range steps {
380			a.tabs[i].SetActive(s.name == name)
381		}
382		a.tabGuard = false
383		a.stack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
384		// the two groups on the shared bar are this page's
385		a.inStack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
386		a.outStack.SetVisibleChildName(name)
387		a.updateRunControls() // ▶ ⏹ belong to the new page's playback now
388		a.syncHelp()          // and so does the ⓘ
389		// ...and so does ▶ itself, when the ticks beside it name one step: the tab
390		// you walk to is the step you mean (followChainTick)
391		a.followChainTick(name)
392		// Cut's Inputs row lists what Suggest will be sent, and one of those things
393		// is the context box on Describe -- the page you have usually just come
394		// from. Refreshed on arrival rather than on every keystroke over there,
395		// which would re-read the session timeline as you type.
396		// ...and the tracks themselves, when the last run (or another project) moved
397		// what they are drawn from. Only then: a rebuild probes every recording and
398		// drops the undo history, which is not what a tab click should cost.
399		if name == "cut" && a.ed != nil {
400			if a.ed.stale || len(a.ed.vids) == 0 {
401				a.updateCutInfo() // which does updateInputs itself
402			} else {
403				a.ed.updateInputs()
404			}
405		}
406		// Narrate's row says the same thing about the narration, and one of the
407		// things it counts is the cut -- which is the page you have just come from
408		// and the one thing most likely to have changed under it.
409		if name == "narrate" && a.narr != nil {
410			a.narr.refit() // a clip dragged wider over there moves its line's slot here
411			a.narr.updateInputs()
412			a.narr.updateOut()
413		}
414		// ...and Produce reads both of those, plus the synthesis cache and the file
415		// it wrote last time. It is the end of the chain, so everything upstream is
416		// something that may have moved since it was last looked at.
417		if name == "produce" {
418			a.updateProduceInfo()
419			// ...and the thumbnail half reads the folder it wrote into last time,
420			// since the picture on the page is the file on disk rather than
421			// something remembered
422			if a.pub != nil {
423				a.pub.refresh()
424			}
425		}
426	}
427	
428	// syncHelp points the header ⓘ tooltip at the open page's help. Called from
429	// showStep, including the bounce off a locked tab.
430	func (a *App) syncHelp() {
431		if a.helpInfo == nil {
432			return
433		}
434		i := stepIndex(a.stack.VisibleChildName())
435		if i < 0 {
436			return
437		}
438		a.helpInfo.SetTooltipText(steps[i].label + "\n\n" + steps[i].help)
439	}

445		outDir string // where step outputs go; default root, project-settable

453		narrateLocked bool          // no cut yet -- nothing to narrate
454		produceLocked bool          // no cut yet -- nothing to produce

459		linkPaths     map[string]string // what a tagged path displays -> where it really is
460		llmMu         sync.Mutex        // guards llmSeq; describe calls from worker goroutines
461		gate          *llmGate          // one chat request on the wire at a time (llmgate.go)
462		gateMu        sync.Mutex
463		llmSeq        int // per-run counter naming the llm/ exchange files
464		// whether this video has a narration at all. The Narrate page's own
465		// checkbox writes it, the run refuses when it is set, and Produce hides
466		// what only a narration needs (narrate.go, produce.go).
467		narrOff bool
468		// sources are referenced in place rather than copied into the project
469		// (Project.RefSources); copyTick is the tick on Prepare that says so

472		copyTick   *gtk.CheckButton
473		// the run's own page: its file name, the finished calls' HTML in order, and
474		// how many there have been. One page per run rather than one per call --

476		// is not a thread (llmlog.go).
477		runName    string
478		runSecs    []string
479		runN       int

481		running    bool

483		ttsModel   string // the model id that server serves, asked for once
484		// which aligner answered. A catalog entry is a claim rather than a working
485		// model (alignModels) -- a server lists one whose family the engine it is
486		// running was not built with -- so the run remembers the one that worked
487		// instead of spending a failed request per source to learn it again.
488		alignPick string
489	
490		// The Prepare page's own controls -- the settings a run reads off it,
491		// which is everything on that page a runner needs and nothing it draws.
492		srcList   *sourceList // the session's files, and what each one is for
493		interval  *freqPick
494		scalePick *gtk.DropDown
495		// which pipeline this session runs through (textedit.go): the page's
496		// dropdown, and the project's word for it before the page exists
497		// the steps ▶ runs one after another (runchain.go)
498		chainPick  *gtk.MenuButton

500		chain      []string // what is left of the chain under way
501		chainSteps []string // ...and a project's answer, before the ticks exist
502		// how long it is all taking: when the press was, when the step under way
503		// started, which step that is, and what each finished one cost
504		chainFrom  time.Time
505		chainAt    time.Time
506		chainStep  string
507		chainRan   []string
508		chainQuiet bool
509		// set while the CHAIN is moving the pages itself (chainNext), so that the
510		// move is not read as the hand walking to a tab (followChainTick)
511		chainMoving bool
512	
513		stylePick  *gtk.DropDown
514		videoStyle string     // which pipeline this session runs through; guarded by promptMu, like langTxt
515		styleQuiet bool       // applyStyle is setting the dropdown, not the hand
516		langEntry  *gtk.Entry // what the ASR is told this session is spoken in
517	
518		// One controller per page, in tab order (steps). Each is nil until its page
519		// has been built, which is what every headless test is and also what the
520		// first seconds of a session are -- so every reader checks.
521		prep *preproc
522		ed   *cutEditor
523		narr *narrator
524		prod *producer
525		pub  *publisher

527		// The Narrate page's voice picker, and the choice it holds. The id is
528		// cached from narrate/voice.txt and guarded: since the narrator's name became
529		// part of every step's input (tlLabel), it is read by the describe and
530		// transcript workers as well as by the GUI thread.
531		voicePick *voicePicker
532		voiceMu   sync.Mutex
533		voiceSel  string
534		pitchSel  float64 // semitones the reference is shifted by, from narrate/pitch.txt
535		pitchRead bool    // ...and whether that file has been read yet (0 is a real value)
536		// the hand-picked voice-clone takes, by recording (narrate_take.go), under
537		// the same lock and for the same reason: they are part of the cache key, so
538		// they are read by whatever thread is about to speak a line.
539		takesMap  map[string][]voiceTake
540		takesRead bool

542		progress *gtk.ProgressBar

546		// own by step name. The two live side by side at the right of the shared
547		// bottom bar: what the step reads, then what it has written.
548		inStack  *gtk.Stack
549		outStack *gtk.Stack

551		// pipeline control: pause parks the runners at the next checkpoint, stop
552		// kills the in-flight subprocesses; finished stages stay on disk either
553		// way. STT and frame extraction run as parallel tracks (GPU vs CPU), so
554		// several subprocesses can be live at once.
555		ctlMu     sync.Mutex
556		curCmds   map[*exec.Cmd]bool
557		stopFlag  atomic.Bool
558		pauseFlag atomic.Bool
559		runCtx    context.Context // canceled by stop -- aborts in-flight LLM calls
560		runCancel context.CancelFunc
561		// ⏸ parks a run, ⏹ abandons one, and the difference has to be visible on
562		// the next ▶: resume where it stopped, or start over. Only the describer
563		// can tell them apart at all -- it is the one job that resumes per chunk --
564		// so a stopped Describe + Transcript sets this, and the next run of that
565		// step throws its half-written event logs away first. See resetDescribe.
566		undRestart bool
567	
568		srcMu sync.Mutex
569		// snapshot of the session's sources, taken on the GUI thread when a run
570		// starts. selItems is the whole of it and the other three are what the
571		// pipeline actually asks for, derived from it: the footage, then the rest,
572		// and who was tagged as which narrator. They are kept together because a
573		// run can rewrite the session -- splitting a voice off a recording turns
574		// one row into two -- and every one of them has to say so at once.
575		selItems []sourceItem
576		selVid   []string
577		selAud   []string
578		selNarr  [narratorSlots]string
579		// which audio tracks of each source the session uses, keyed on path. A path
580		// this says nothing about uses its first track alone, so an ordinary
581		// session's map is empty and every reader of it is a no-op (cut_tracks.go).
582		selTracks map[string][]int
583	
584		// the editable system prompts. The views are the GUI thread's; promptTxt is
585		// the copy a runner reads, kept current by the buffers' changed handler --
586		// same rule as selVid/selAud, for the same reason.
587		promptMu    sync.Mutex
588		promptTxt   map[string]string
589		promptViews map[string]*gtk.TextView
590		// promptTxt is empty for a job whose shipped wording is what the model
591		// reads; what is in it is this machine's own. promptDisk is what the
592		// prompt folder is believed to hold, so the flush that mirrors one onto
593		// the other writes only what changed (promptstore.go) -- GUI thread only,
594		// like the views: it is written from the autosave tick.
595		promptDisk map[string]string
596		// the row above each box -- the "edited" mark and the Reset beside it --
597		// and the flag that stops filling a box from reading as the user typing in
598		// it. GUI thread only, so no lock (showPrompt).
599		promptRows  map[string]promptRow
600		promptQuiet bool
601		// redraws the ✎ marks on the bench's menu when a project load or an edit
602		// changes what the project is holding (prepedit.go)
603		prepSync func()
604		// every text box's heading row, so a row with a Reset button and a row with
605		// a bare label are the same height and the boxes under them line up
606		// (editorBody). GUI thread only, like the views.
607		headGroup *gtk.SizeGroup

609		// for the same reason
610		langTxt string

612		// every step (context.go). Under promptMu for the same reason as the
613		// prompts: the box belongs to the GUI thread, the string is what a runner
614		// reads. Not in promptTxt -- it is not a prompt and it is stored in full,
615		// whereas a prompt is stored only when it differs from the built-in.
616		ctxTxt string
617		// the bench's box while it is showing the context row, and nil while it is
618		// showing a prompt (prepedit.go). Nil is normal, not a "page not built
619		// yet": a project loaded while a prompt is on screen writes the cache
620		// only, and the box rereads it on the next switch.
621		ctxView *gtk.TextView
622

638		// tabWordsOn says which of the two states the row is in, because the row's

641		head       *gtk.HeaderBar
642		headBtns   []gtk.Widgetter
643		tabRow     *gtk.Box
644		tabWords   []*gtk.Label
645		tabWordsOn bool

647		headWatch  bool

651		progMu    sync.Mutex
652		progParts [2]float64

655		progBase, progShare float64

659	// The frame slider snaps to these stops; a linear 0.1..5 s scale would cram
660	// all the useful low end into the first pixel. Index 0 keeps every frame.
661	var frameStops = []float64{0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
662	var frameStopLabels = []string{"each", "0.1", "0.2", "0.5", "1s", "2s", "3s", "4s", "5s"}
663	
664	// where a session with nobody's opinion on it starts: one frame a second. Named
665	// rather than typed twice, since a new project has to land on the same stop the
666	// stepper builds itself at -- and index 0 is not it (that is every frame, which
667	// is gigabytes).
668	const defFrameStop = 4
669	
670	// Frame size presets, no-resize first because that is the default and picking a
671	// size is the exception. Name is the identity and Label is only what the drop
672	// down shows: the name goes into the project file AND into the stamp that
673	// decides whether frames must be extracted again, so it has to stay put even
674	// when the wording moves. 896w is the width the vision model gets fed.
675	var scalePresets = []struct{ Name, Label, VF string }{
676		// the label said "Resize", which on the closed button read as the
677		// control's caption and in the open list as a nonsense first choice
678		{"original", "Original", ""},
679		{"896w (LLM)", "896w (LLM)", "scale=896:-2"},
680		{"480p", "480p", "scale=-2:480"},
681		{"720p", "720p", "scale=-2:720"},
682		{"1080p", "1080p", "scale=-2:1080"},
683	}
684	
685	func (a *App) frameScale() (name, vf string) {
686		i := int(a.scalePick.Selected())
687		if i < 0 || i >= len(scalePresets) {
688			i = 0
689		}
690		return scalePresets[i].Name, scalePresets[i].VF
691	}
692	
693	func (a *App) setFrameScale(name string) {
694		for i, p := range scalePresets {
695			if p.Name == name || p.Label == name {
696				a.scalePick.SetSelected(uint(i))
697				return
698			}
699		}
700	}
701	
702	// defLanguage is what a session is assumed to be in when nobody says. It was a
703	// setting on this machine (llm.conf) and is now a field on the project, for the
704	// reason setup.go's header gives: the stack is the same every night, the
705	// footage is not.
706	const defLanguage = "en"
707	
708	// projectLanguage is the box's text as the project file stores it: what was
709	// typed, trimmed, and "" when nothing was -- an empty box means the default,
710	// and writing "en" into every project would freeze today's default into files
711	// that never asked for it (same rule as an unedited prompt).
712	func (a *App) projectLanguage() string {
713		a.promptMu.Lock()
714		defer a.promptMu.Unlock()
715		return strings.TrimSpace(a.langTxt)
716	}
717	
718	// asrLanguage is the same value with the default filled in: what Prepare puts in
719	// the request. Callable from a runner's goroutine, which is the whole reason
720	// the string is cached beside the widget rather than read off it -- the box is
721	// the GUI thread's (same rule as sessionCtx).
722	func (a *App) asrLanguage() string {
723		if s := a.projectLanguage(); s != "" {
724			return s
725		}
726		return defLanguage
727	}
728	
729	func (a *App) setLanguage(s string) {
730		a.promptMu.Lock()
731		a.langTxt = s
732		a.promptMu.Unlock()
733		// the subtitle translations are offered in every language but this one,
734		// and this is where it changes (syncLangs)
735		a.syncSubLangs()
736	}
737	
738	// applyLanguage loads a project's language into the box as well as the cache.
739	// GUI thread only, like applySessionCtx and for the same reason.
740	func (a *App) applyLanguage(s string) {
741		a.setLanguage(s)
742		if a.langEntry != nil {

751	// nearestStop maps seconds onto the stop table -- a project may store a value
752	// from a build whose table was different, and typing is free-form.
753	func nearestStop(v float64) int {
754		best, bd := 4, math.MaxFloat64 // default 1 s
755		for i, s := range frameStops {
756			if d := math.Abs(s - v); d < bd {
757				best, bd = i, d
758			}
759		}
760		return best
761	}

763	// freqPick is the frame-frequency stepper: one stop visible at a time, - / +
764	// walking the table, and the text editable by hand. Hand-rolled rather than a
765	// GtkSpinButton because the spin button re-reads its own display as a plain
766	// number before every step -- and "each" and "1s" are not numbers, so every
767	// click first corrupted the value it was about to step.
768	type freqPick struct {
769		box   *gtk.Box
770		entry *gtk.Entry
771		i     int
772	}
773	
774	func newFreqPick() *freqPick {
775		f := &freqPick{}
776		f.entry = gtk.NewEntry()
777		f.entry.SetWidthChars(4)
778		f.entry.SetMaxWidthChars(4)
779		f.entry.SetAlignment(0.5)
780		f.entry.SetTooltipText("Seconds between frames — type 0.1 to 5, or 'each' for every frame")
781		f.entry.ConnectActivate(f.parse)
782		// clicking elsewhere commits like Enter does: a half-typed value silently
783		// kept on screen would not be the value a run then uses
784		fc := gtk.NewEventControllerFocus()
785		fc.ConnectLeave(f.parse)
786		f.entry.AddController(fc)
787	
788		minus := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-remove-symbolic")
789		minus.ConnectClicked(func() { f.set(f.i - 1) })
790		plus := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("list-add-symbolic")
791		plus.ConnectClicked(func() { f.set(f.i + 1) })
792	
793		f.box = gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 0)
794		f.box.AddCSSClass("linked") // one control, three parts
795		f.box.Append(f.entry)
796		f.box.Append(minus)
797		f.box.Append(plus)
798		f.set(defFrameStop)
799		return f
800	}
801	
802	// set clamps to the table -- past either end the buttons simply stop moving.
803	func (f *freqPick) set(i int) {
804		if i < 0 {
805			i = 0
806		}
807		if i >= len(frameStops) {
808			i = len(frameStops) - 1
809		}

814	// parse commits a typed value: seconds with or without the s, or "each"/"0"
815	// for every frame, landing on the nearest stop. Anything unreadable snaps the
816	// display back to the value still in force.
817	func (f *freqPick) parse() {
818		t := strings.TrimSuffix(strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(f.entry.Text())), "s")
819		if t == "each" {
820			f.set(0)
821			return
822		}
823		v, err := strconv.ParseFloat(t, 64)
824		if err != nil || v < 0 {
825			f.set(f.i)
826			return
827		}
828		f.set(nearestStop(v))
829	}

948	// snapItems takes one list of sources as the run's snapshot and hands back the

953	func (a *App) snapItems(items []sourceItem) (vids, auds []string) {
954		l := sourceList{items: items} // the rules, without the widget
955		vids, auds = l.split()

1462	func (a *App) logf(format string, args ...any) {

1464		if a.log == nil {

1466		}

1470		mark := buf.CreateMark("", buf.EndIter(), false)
1471		a.log.ScrollToMark(mark, 0, false, 0, 1)
1472		buf.DeleteMark(mark)
1473	}

1479	// A watchdog for the GTK thread: a heartbeat on the main loop, watched by its
1480	// own goroutine. When the beat is hangStall late, every goroutine's stack goes
1481	// to hang-<time>.txt beside the settings and to stderr -- the Go frames above
1482	// the blocked C call say which seek or state change never came back. One dump
1483	// per hang.
1484	
1485	const (
1486		hangBeat  = 200 * time.Millisecond // how often the main loop says it is alive
1487		hangStall = 3 * time.Second        // how late a beat has to be to count as a hang
1488	)
1489	
1490	// startHangWatch installs the heartbeat and the watcher. Called once the main
1491	// loop exists; harmless before the window does.
1492	func (a *App) startHangWatch() {
1493		var last atomic.Int64
1494		last.Store(time.Now().UnixNano())
1495		glib.TimeoutAdd(uint(hangBeat/time.Millisecond), func() bool {
1496			last.Store(time.Now().UnixNano())
1497			return true
1498		})
1499		go func() {
1500			dumped := false
1501			for range time.Tick(hangBeat) {
1502				late := time.Since(time.Unix(0, last.Load()))
1503				if late < hangStall {
1504					dumped = false
1505					continue
1506				}
1507				if dumped {
1508					continue
1509				}
1510				dumped = true
1511				a.dumpHang(late)
1512			}
1513		}()
1514	}
1515	
1516	// dumpHang writes every goroutine's stack. Not through the log: the log is a
1517	// widget on the thread that is stuck.
1518	func (a *App) dumpHang(late time.Duration) {
1519		buf := make([]byte, 1<<20)
1520		n := runtime.Stack(buf, true)
1521		head := fmt.Sprintf("naivepost: the GTK thread has not answered for %s -- every goroutine's stack follows\n\n", late.Round(100*time.Millisecond))
1522		fmt.Fprint(os.Stderr, head)
1523		os.Stderr.Write(buf[:n])
1524		dir := configDir()
1525		if dir == "" {
1526			return
1527		}
1528		p := filepath.Join(dir, "hang-"+time.Now().Format("0102-150405")+".txt")
1529		os.WriteFile(p, append([]byte(head), buf[:n]...), 0o600)
1530		fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "\nnaivepost: written to %s\n", p)
1531	}

The clock reads the cut's own time while it does. Changes nothing that is saved."; sensitive when segs > 0; lit while cutOnly and no review. ▶✂✂ (icon + "✂✂"): sensitive with ≥2 clips; "review every cut in one go: plays 10 s of the finished video before each join and 10 s after it, one join after the other, and stops after the last. The removed stretches are skipped as under ▶✂. Changes nothing that is saved." / "pause the cut review"; lit while reviewing. Frame buttons: "back 5 frames (pauses) — or whatever is held, 5 frames" etc.

118	3. separator.
119	4. linked(＋ Add, | Split, － Remove, ⧉ Copy, ⧉ Paste, Insert/Edit, ⇲ Lane) with state-dependent tooltips (Add: "keep the selected region (Undo takes it back)" / "＋ Add keeps footage, and this selection is <base>'s sound" / "drag a region on a track, then ＋ Add keeps it" / "the selection is under 1 s — too short to keep as a scene"; Split: "cut the selected region free: a border at each end, nothing removed, so those seconds become a scene of their own. With nothing selected it cuts once, at the red line (Undo takes it back)"; Remove: "drop the selected region — through the middle of a scene it leaves two, one either side (Undo takes it back)"; Paste: footage/sound variants naming the seconds, "Esc drops the copy"; Insert: "put a file in the cut at the playhead — a video sting, a still, or an SVG that animates itself. A selected region gives it its length; otherwise the file's own. With the selection drawn in a lane's own wave it offers sounds instead… Right-click a card on the track to hold it, and this becomes Edit."; held card → "change the held card — what it says, and whether it plays over the footage (overwrite) or between it (insert)"; held effect → "change the held effect — <label>"; Lane: "put a copy on a row of its own — ⧉ takes one first" / long variant ending "select on the new row and press ＋ Add, the same way you would cut to a second camera").
