128	## B. Timeline model
129	Session clock from srcClock over the snapshot; tlVideo{base, path, start, wall, dur, interval, fps (default 30), frames, w, h, lane, off}; at(t)=t−start+off; sessionAt(local)=start+local−off. tlAudio{base, path, start, off, dur, chans, master, track}.
130	Rows = greedy interval colouring of recordings in start order, pins (cut.json rows) applied first; nRows floor keeps an emptied bottom row until its ✕. Filmed runs = merged recording spans; cells = runs cut at folded gaps; spans carry pixel origins (gutter first; a folded cell has zero width).
131	x↔time: xOf walks spans (folded cell → its seam x; past the end → totalW); tAt is the inverse, half-open on the right (the seam second belongs to the later take); left of the first run → its start.
132	Folds are a view, not an edit: persisted as [t0,t1] pairs matched to gaps by overlap, rewritten on save, never over a whole recording; badge − in the gap middle (or inside the adjoining bar for the first/last/folded gap), + on the seam; fold-all badge in the gutter; statuses "folded N seam(s)", "unfolded m:ss – m:ss (X s)"; ▶ playing into a fold opens it ("unfolded m:ss — ▶ ran into it"); ▶✂ never enters one; a right-drag opens folds within 6 px of what it holds and refolds on release.
133	Shift corrections: shift map base→seconds and rows map base→row in cut.json and in every undo snapshot; applied on load; sliding moves the video, every lane of the base and every further track, and the speech-gap points; clamped to ±(60 + Σ durations); rows are frozen (pinned) on the first drag because segments carry a row number; copies follow a moved row.
134	Cut lanes: {name, src, at, off, dur} windows of a file on a row of their own; built from the source's metadata or probed; name, name-2 …; killing a lane removes its pins, shift, pictures and sound and closes the row.
135	Zoom: pps starts at 4; floor fits the filmed duration into the view minus the gutter; ceiling 240 px/s; zoomAt keeps the second under the anchor; wheel deltas banked and applied once per idle as 1.25^−dy; buttons zoom about the view centre.
136	Scroll: adjustment upper=totalW, page=viewW, step viewW/8; Shift+wheel pans by dx·viewW/8; revealPlayhead recentres when the line leaves the view.
137	Thumbnails: step = max(1, thumbHt·aspect/(pps·interval)); decoded in a worker in batches of 6 at the row height, converted once to cairo surfaces, generation-checked; unreadable files cached as empty; clipped to picture width, row end and cell end.
138	Visual-change scores per recording in the background from 24×14 brightness postages of consecutive frames.
139	
140	## C. Cut model
141	cutSeg: s, e (session seconds; s==e with dur>0 = spliced insert), ins (asset path, project-relative, or "copy:SECONDS"), dur (spliced insert length), rate (written only by produceSegs), ss (start inside an inserted sound), mute (spliced: silent; overwriting: footage sound kept), cam (picture row), lane (which recording an overlaid sound replaces; "" = everything), quiet (lanes this scene does not hear), split (starts at a Split border; blocks coalesce). length() = dur if spliced, else (e−s)/rate.
142	cut.json: {segs, aspect, fx, sound (legacy read-only), shift, rows, lanes, nrows, folds}; beside it cut/line.json {"t"}.
143	Edits: rangePieces (snap both ends, one piece per filmed run, drop < 1 s, cam = selection row); addRange (steal the span off other rows, append, coalesce, persist); removeSpan (inserts dropped whole or kept whole; remainders ≥ 0.04 s); stealSpan; layOver; layOverSound (one sound per kept piece, ss walking; floor 0.05 s); addSplice; splitBorder (strictly inside a footage clip, halves ≥ 0.04; the right half carries split); mergeTouching/mergeDropped (same-camera neighbours within 0.04 s; clears split); coalesce (sort by s; merge non-insert same-camera clips touching within 0.04 s unless split, across spliced cards); splitSpliced (render view: a spliced card inside a clip cuts it in two).
144	Undo: snapshot {segs, fx, aspect, shift, rows, lanes, nRows}, deep copies; depth 50; pushUndo clears redo; restore re-slides sources only when corrections differ, rebuilds lanes, relayouts; statuses "undone — N segment(s) left", "redone — N segment(s)", "nothing to undo/redo". Base set on load and after every suggestion; Revert restores it ("nothing to revert — the cut is as it was" / "reverted — N hand-made segment(s) gone, the cut is empty" / "reverted to the N segment(s) of the last suggestion (↶ Undo brings your edits back)"). Clear: one undo step, segs=fx=nil ("cleared N scene(s) and M effect(s)"; refuses "nothing to clear — the timeline holds no cut yet").
145	persist: syncFolds → write cut.json → totals → outputs → updateGates (the only place cut.json comes into existence) → buttons → showInsert → redraw.
146	Lengths: cutLen = Σ length of applyFx(splitSpliced(segs), fx); "%.1f s" or "%.1f s, %.1f s in the video" when they differ ≥ 0.05.
147	
148	## D. Transport
149	Three ▶ rule: each wears ⏸ only while its thing runs; pressing it pauses; pressing another switches over without stopping; exactly one lit. setCutOnly statuses: "preview is the cut — and the cut is empty, so ▶✂ has nothing to play until a clip is added" / "preview is the cut — the clock reads the finished video" / "preview is the recording again — everything plays, cuts and all". toggle refuses an empty cut in ✂ mode ("the cut is empty — add a clip to play it, or press ▶ to play the recording instead"), clears the watched row, snaps onto kept material, hushes before moving, ends a review on pause. stop = review off, player stop, started=false.
150	setPlayhead: set, re-base the live clock, hasPlay, cancel card hold, sync held effect, clock, note line, buttons, gain; if a recording covers t: rate before seek, mix on file change, hush, in-place seek (unless the spare holds the target) else PlaySegment; then showInsert, redraw.
151	Clock: "mm:ss.d"; "--:--.-" with no playhead; under ▶✂ the cut's own clock with tooltip "X into the cut, of Y — the finished video's own clock (the ▶✂ preview), the speed effects included. Session time here is Z."; else "The red line: X s into the session — <file> at mm:ss.d, frame N — kept|cut away here" or "in the gap between recordings".
152	Tick 100 ms; liveClock extrapolates ≤ one tick at the current rate, monotone; bands repaint only when the clip under the line changes.
153	followPlayback order: held card → tickHold; walkOn; not playing → return; position → playhead, noteLine, held effect, clock; walkFold unless cutOnly; reviewTick; spliced card crossed → hold, else showInsert; skipGap; camera change → re-cue; preloadAhead; rate; gain; reveal; repaint.
154	Gap skip (cutOnly): past last clip → pause; new gap → seek to playable(next.S); same gap again → re-ask only if the player is not on the target's file; no recording → pause.
155	Walk-on after a file ends: another camera rolling at this second, else the next recording start; re-cue, snap, toggle.
156	Review: pad 10 s; window [max(S_i, E_i−10), min(E_{i+1}, S_{i+1}+10)]; stay/seek/done/lost with an armed flag (lost only once the line was seen inside the window); run-ups already behind the line are played into; starts from the red line (inside a window → play on; between → next seam; past all → first); statuses "reviewing cut N of M — 10 s before and after the join at m:ss", "reviewed all N cuts", "the line was moved — the cut review is over; ▶✂✂ starts it again", "nothing to review — a cut needs two clips to have a join between them".
157	Preload: 3 s ahead of the next jump (clip end → next clip; seam window close → next run-up if ahead; recording end → next recording) the spare pipeline prerolls at the target; PlaySegment swaps it in when it matches within 0.01 s; a stop drops the spare.
158	Frame step: held edge → nudge edge; held clip → nudge clip; held effect → nudge effect; else pause and seek by n/fps (default 30); "click a track first to place the playhead".
159	Hush/mix: mixUnder(v) = every non-master lane overlapping v with delta/lo/hi/track; hush = the scene's quiet list + whether the picture's own sound is silenced + until (the scene's end in file seconds); a hushed lane is never started (READY), the footage's own sound uses the mute property; lanes under an until are seeked with a stop at the boundary. Rate changes under playback = flushing seek throttled to one per 250 ms; gain = fxGainAt × previewVol, clamped to 10.
160	Remembered line: cut/line.json written at most once per second, flushed on close, restored once per project when a recording covers it.
161	
162	## E. Editing flows
163	Left press order: gutter fold-all; selection band (fold badge, selection ✕, selection ends/middle, green-bar ✕, green-bar ends → trim, else drop selection); effects lane (✕, hold/part, else drop); selection ends on the pictures within 10 px; lane/row sound switches; speaker badge; camera badge; cut-lane ✕; empty-row ✕; trim grab on a clip border (6 px) → trimming; else drop holds and start a new selection (scope = the lane or row it was drawn on).
164	Drag: trim after 4 px slop; effect drag; selection move/resize; new selection. Drag end: trim drop (merge touching, persist, land on the edge, status "clip N: a – b (X s[, Y s in the video])"); effect persist/status/click opens its form; real drag (≥5 px) keeps the selection; click → clear selection and marks, set watched row when on a row, set playhead, hold the scene under the click.
165	Double click: pick up an edge within 12 px (held) or 6 px, or a clip.
166	Right button = moving: a lane recording; a row strip's recording; the selected scenes; a green bar end (trim) or middle (move); a clip on the green; else the whole camera row. Read in pixels over the zoom (folds have no width), snapped to marks within 8 px, row change when it fits, one undo per gesture; statuses "<what> moved +1.23 s" / "<what> is back where it started" / "<what> moved to row N — its kept scenes came along". Unmoved right press = "this one" (status only). Folds opened around the grab and refolded on release.
167	Trim: edges within 6 px (own side first), cards skipped; clamp: end ≥ S+1 s, ≤ next.S, ≤ recording end; start ≤ E−1 s, ≥ prev.E, ≥ recording start; live scrub throttled 90 ms; the end edge shows the frame before the boundary; status "clip N's start|end picked up at mm:ss.d — right-drag to trim".
168	Move clip: keeps length, inside its recording, clear of neighbours, snapped flush within 8 px; inserts may go anywhere the neighbours allow.
169	Selection band: ends (6 px; 10 on pictures), ✕ (only when ≥50 px wide), middle; snaps to clip borders, recording ends, effect ends, playhead; min 0.04 s; marks (green in / red out flags) follow the band; readout "mm:ss.d – mm:ss.d".
170	Verbs and statuses: Add ("added — ↶ Undo (Ctrl+Z) takes it back", "…on <cam>…", "…and taken off the other camera…"; refusals "drag a region on a track first", "＋ Add keeps footage — the selection is <base>'s sound", "nothing to add: X s selected, a scene is 1 s or more"); Remove ("removed X s — the scene it went through is two now (↶ Undo takes it back)" / "removed X s — N scene(s), was M"; "nothing to remove: the cut keeps nothing between…"); Split ("split at m:ss[ and m:ss] — N scenes, was M"; keeps the selection); Copy ("copied m:ss – m:ss (X s) — click where it goes, then ⧉ Paste"; refuses under 1 s); Paste ("pasted X s from a at b — the cut is c, was d"; "click the timeline where the copy goes first"); Lane ("X s from a is now the <name> lane, starting at b"); pasteSound ("laid X s of <base> over the footage|N stretches of footage at m:ss"; "the cut keeps no footage at m:ss — a sound needs a picture under it"); ⌦ order: held effect, held clip (the only way to remove a card), sound selection refused, selection, scene under the line, else "nothing selected — click a kept scene, or drag a region on a track"; ✕ badges: scene ("removed the scene at m:ss (X s) — ↶ Undo takes it back"), selection, lane ("removed the <name> lane"), empty row ("removed the empty row N"), effect; camera badge ("the scene at m:ss is shown from <cam> now"); speaker badge ("<base> is silent in|heard in the scene at m:ss"); whole-lane switch ("<name> off for the whole cut — N scene(s) changed" / "<name> is on for the whole cut — every scene hears it" / "<name> is in no scene yet — cut something first").
171	Keys: Space play/pause; Ctrl+Z undo; Ctrl+Shift+Z / Ctrl+Y redo; Delete/BackSpace ⌦; ←/→ frame step (Shift 5) only while something is held; Esc drops edge, clip, effect, selection, copy and arm.
172	Cursors: pointer over badges/switches/✕; ew-resize over borders and selection ends; grab over band middles/effect bodies; crosshair while an effect is armed.
173	
174	## F. Suggest (▶)
175	Guards: busy; hand edits → "you have hand edits — press Revert first for a fresh suggestion"; no session timeline → "run Describe first — the suggestion reads the session timeline, and there is none".
176	Read style: no model. marks = retakes.tsv, or remade from final.txt when it was edited later; textCut = inserts + each filmed run trimmed to its words (placed by sound within 0.4 s, never outside the run) → dropMarked → dropDeadAir; one undo, coalesce, persist, base; "cut by the words: N segments"; log ">>> cut by the words: N stretch(es) taken out, m:ss of silence, N segments, M:SS total".
177	Gaming style: 4 queue jobs: suggest (LLM "cut"), captions, speed, decorations (see fx inventory). Target length only from the context text (regex "N min|m|s|sec"; a bare number is never a length); none → ">>> suggest: the user context names no length — everything worth keeping goes in". suggestCut: system prompt "cut"; user = context block + "SESSION LENGTH: N seconds, which the timeline writes as mm:ss. Every start and end you give is a number of SECONDS between 0 and N." + target block ("TARGET LENGTH: N seconds … KEEP between A and B seconds of footage, in at most K segments. Stop at the first set of moments that lands in that range." | "NO TARGET LENGTH. …") + "SESSION TIMELINE:" + session.txt. Web tools offered, dropped after the first rejection. Streaming progress counts closed segments. Thinking on; off after a call that wrote nothing. 3 attempts with retryTurn; "no valid cut after 3 attempts".
178	Reply {"segments":[{start,end[,speed|rate]}],"fx":[…]}. checkCutReply faults: timestamps past the end (+ mm:ss hint); fewer than min(1+target/30, 4) segments; more than max(target/5, 40); a segment ends before it starts; footage length outside target×[0.6,1.2 (≤60 s) | 0.6,1.5]×[1,4] after keepFilmed (segments with no recording at either end dropped).
179	Apply: undo; keep hand-placed inserts; joinSeams (close holes ≤ 1.5 s only if somebody talked in them); snap edges; dropMarked (">>> N marked stretch(es) taken out of the cut — said twice, kept once"); dropDeadAir (silences > 8 s inside a clip cut out leaving 0.5 s; ">>> m:ss of silence taken out"); coalesce; clampFxToSegs; fx replaced; persist; base; "suggested N segments".
180	snapEdge scoring within 5 s: baseline 0.35, distance penalty −0.4·d/5, outward +0.3; silence midpoint 0.8, word edge 0.9, line start/end 0.95, visual peak min(1, score/(4·mean)) only where nobody is talking (±0.2 s).
181	
182	## G. Inserts
183	Insert needs a line or a selection ("click the timeline where the insert goes first"); chooser "Insert a clip, image, animation or sound" (sound-scoped selection: "Insert a sound over the selected seconds"), starting in <project>/assets where the built-in SVG cards are written on first open. Extensions: audio mp3 wav ogg oga flac m4a aac opus; picture mp4 mkv mov webm avi m4v png jpg jpeg webp bmp gif svg. insKind by extension: video|svg|audio|still.
184	Mode: a selection gives the length and means overwrite; no selection means splice with the file's own length (video/audio duration; SVG animation length; else 4 s). mute default = file has no sound; the sound question is asked only when relevant.
185	Form in the column (askInsertParams): one entry per declared card field (Logo… picker for logo fields); radios "Insert BETWEEN the footage — the video gets longer by the card, nothing filmed is lost" / "Play OVER the footage — the card replaces those seconds (the same as Remove)" / "Put it on a LANE of its own — a row of the band to cut to, and nothing is cut yet" (video only); tick "Play it SILENT — the insert's own sound is not used" (spliced) or "Keep the sound running under it — only the picture is replaced" (over); Seconds entry ("how long the card runs…"); Cancel + Insert/Save. Status "<file> inserted at m:ss for X s, <how> — the cut is now a (was b) — ↶ Undo takes it back".
186	Edit re-opens with current answers, re-finds the card by identity ("that card is no longer in the cut"); switching splice↔over returns or takes footage.
187	Preview of cards: 8 fps for video/animated SVG, one frame for stills; nearest rendered frame shown; 48-texture cap; rendered via ffmpeg at ≤960 px; a spliced card holds the footage while it plays on the wall clock ("<card> — the footage is held while it plays"); card sound is its own pipeline cued once.
188	Black frame when paused on a row with no footage.
189	
190	## H. Audio
191	Envelopes: 200 buckets/s from an 8 kHz decode, peak bytes, cached as cache/waves/<lane>.wave (magic AWV4, header chans/hz/count/size/mtime). Dual mono collapsed when channel difference ≤ 1/100 of peak or the two envelopes match (mean diff < 1, max 8): "L=R"; "mono"; "L"/"R".
192	Drawing: 1 px columns from the baseline, IEC 60268-18 meter scale stretched so −48 dBFS sits on the floor; a ground shows where the recording is; paired strips dimmed.
193	Lanes vs strips: a row's own first track is the master strip under its pictures; further tracks and separate recordings are lanes ("<base> #N"). Selection scope is the lane/row it was drawn on; a sound selection greys Add/Split/Remove and aims Copy/Insert at sound.
194	Cut lanes' sound: the source's master track windowed. Audio inserts drawn violet on the sound only (hatched when spliced), footage tint kept.
195	Per-scene hearing: speaker badges per lane on the held/current scene; green wash where heard, grey where silenced; whole-lane switch in the gutter; legacy whole-cut sound migrated once with a log line.

200	## J. Invariants
201	1. One thing held at a time; holds are indices and are dropped on renumbering; things picked from the toolbar are re-found by identity.
202	2. Picking up is not an edit; one undo per drag.
203	3. An unmoved press is a click; a right click never moves the line.
204	4. A border belongs to both buttons; the right button's own verb is moving.
205	5. A selection is of what it was drawn on.
206	6. Unfilmed time has no width; seams belong to the later take; preview and render agree on half-open ranges.
207	7. Folds are views, never edits, never used to measure drags.
208	8. Inserts are files: never trimmed, merged, dropped by re-suggest, or given a quiet answer; a spliced insert costs no session time and is removed only via ⌦ on a held card.
209	9. length()/cutLen are the only truth about video length; only produceSegs writes rate.
210	10. quiet lists silent lanes; compared as a set; fresh slices per toggle.
211	11. Rows are pinned once anything is dragged; nRows holds an emptied bottom row.
212	12. A clip may not leave its recording; clips never overlap.
213	13. Remove takes exactly the selection (floor 0.04 s); 1 s is only for proposing/copying.
214	14. A Split border survives coalesce until merged by a drag.
215	15. Suggest replaces footage and effects, keeps inserts, sets the base.
216	16. Every model reply is walked back onto the timeline before the page sees it.
217	17. Rates take hold at a seek; hushed lanes are never started; nothing decodes inside a draw; the tracks are a window drawn under a translate.
218	18. cut.json existing gates Narrate and Produce; persist is its only writer.
219	19. Exactly one ▶ lit; the page is a snapshot rebuilt only when Prepare's output changed.

153	## E. LLM client
154	Endpoint: POST <server>/v1/chat/completions, bearer key; server from the box (https:// added when no scheme) or http://127.0.0.1:8731; model required ("no LLM model configured -- use the gear button"). Models: GET /v1/models (15 s).
155	Body: model, messages, top_p 0.95, top_k 20, min_p 0, presence_penalty 0; thinking: temperature 1.0, max_tokens 65536, enable_thinking true; execute: temperature 0.6, max_tokens 8192, enable_thinking false; the thinking switch sent both top-level and in chat_template_kwargs, preserve_thinking true; tools when offered; stream true when a text callback is given. Content parts text / image_url data URLs.
156	Response: choices[0].message.{content, reasoning_content, tool_calls}, finish_reason; streaming only when the response is text/event-stream (data: chunks, [DONE], tool calls reassembled by index; reasoning kept apart, never returned as the answer); EOF without [DONE] keeps what arrived; stopFlag → errStopped.
157	Tools: up to 8 rounds; a round with calls appends the assistant turn and one tool message per call; logs ">>> <step>: round i of 8 — the model asked for name(args…)" (or "…asks for the same thing again"); exhausted → "!!! <step>: still calling tools after 8 rounds — the step gets no answer from this call"; an error on round 0 is read as "the server refused the request with tools" and the call is retried without them. Tools: web_search(broad, medium, narrow) and web_read(url) driven through headless Firefox (per-call timeout 45 s, boot 15 s, render 15 s, 8 hits, 6000 chars per page, bot-wall detection); tool errors are returned as text to the model.
158	Retries: transport death (EOF, reset, refused, pipe, unreachable, or gone-words) → 5 s, 20 s, 1, 2, 4 min, each cancellable; anything else → one 2 s retry; status codes are answers. Helpers: noAnswer, cutOff, thinkAgain (empty answer → thinking off), retryTurn ("Your answer failed validation: <problem>. Return corrected strict JSON only."), jsonReply (peel preamble/fence).
159	Stall watch: streamed calls given up after 5 min of silence; unstreamed calls capped at 10 min; heartbeat every minute (">>> <step>: nothing yet, T in" / "X thinking, Y reply, T in — “…tail”"); blame rewrites cancellations into "nothing arrived in 5m0s" / "stopped answering after T".
160	Gate: one request on the wire per app, taken before the watch, released after the call; ">>> <step>: waited for the LLM -- it was busy with <other>; one request at a time".
161	Cache: <project>/cache/llm/<step>/<sha256 of the JSON parts>; used by describe, transcript, retake, textedit, translate; only usable replies stored.

167	## G. Invariants
168	1. The join is a stream copy: every clip must come out at the same frame size and audio layout (box on every clip, format on every branch, limiter on every clip); aresample before loudnorm; -t on the output for inserts/sounds/freezes/rated clips; adelay in whole ms; input indices append-only; -ss before -i; 0.5 s is the single clip floor; a dropped clip is always logged; mp4 faststart flags; outSize names the short side.
169	2. Cues are built for every subtitle mode; sidecars always written, stale ones deleted by exact name first; never an empty cue; translations read back by number; gaps re-asked once then left in the original; cached only when complete; own language never translated; webm cannot carry srt; placement tags written into the srt.
170	3. ▶ leaves an up-to-date video alone; the stamp excludes the upload text; the text is written once per project (publish.json gates it; delete publish/ to start over); publish.json is laid down before drawing; the thumbnail has its own stamp; ↻ over the picture always redraws; Own survives ▶; the title is seeded onto the picture once; re-printing words never costs a GPU run; plain bytes copied through when nothing to print.
171	4. The two halves touch no common file; the render's error is the run's verdict; every widget read happens on the GUI thread first; landPublish blocks until applied; the gate serialises requests per app; checkpoints only between subprocesses; writeEmbed runs even when the encode was skipped.
172	5. Reasoning is never the reply; empty assistant turns are not echoed; a round-0 tools error retries plainly; status codes are never "went away"; every wait is cancellable; observability never breaks the work; the cache key contains everything that decides the answer.

51	func serverURL(s string) string {

110		// down as a blank page, which is the one case the pages are read for.
111		Think string
112		Calls []toolCall
113		// why the server stopped writing, as it says it: "stop" for an answer that
114		// ended, "length" for one that ran into the token ceiling and was cut off
115		// mid-word. The difference is invisible in the text -- a truncated JSON
116		// reply is just a parse error, and "unexpected end of JSON input" sends
117		// the reader looking for a bug in an answer that was never finished.
118		Stop string
119	}
120	
121	// callSummary is a round's calls as one short phrase for the log: the tool and
122	// what it was pointed at, so two rounds asking the same thing read the same and
123	// two asking different things do not.
124	func callSummary(calls []toolCall) string {
125		var out []string
126		for _, c := range calls {
127			arg := strings.TrimSpace(c.Function.Arguments)
128			if len(arg) > 60 {
129				arg = arg[:60] + "…"
130			}
131			out = append(out, c.Function.Name+arg)
132		}
133		return strings.Join(out, ", ")
134	}
135	
136	// toolRunner answers one call by name; what it returns is what the model
137	// reads as the tool's result.
138	type toolRunner func(name string, args json.RawMessage) string
139	
140	// the most rounds of tool calls one question may take. A model that has not
141	// found its words after this many has found a loop instead.
142	const toolRounds = 8
143	
144	// llmChat posts a chat completion; thinking selects the parameter set. step
145	// names the caller -- "suggest", "describe" -- and is what the recorded
146	// exchange is filed and logged under (recordChatStart in llmlog.go).
147	func (a *App) llmChat(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool) (string, error) {
148		return a.llmChatOn(step, msgs, thinking, nil)
149	}
150	
151	// llmChatOn is llmChat with the reply readable as it arrives: onText gets
152	// everything received so far on every chunk, on the calling goroutine; nil
153	// means the old single-response call. Streaming is what lets the bar count
154	// narration clips as they close (narrEntriesDone). Every call is recorded as
155	// an HTML page under llm/ (request first, reply folded in) with a preview in
156	// the log.
157	func (a *App) llmChatOn(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool, onText func(string)) (string, error) {
158		rep, err := a.chatRound(step, msgs, thinking, nil, onText)
159		return rep.Content, err
160	}
161	
162	// llmChatTools is llmChatOn with tools on the table. The loop is here and
163	// nowhere else: a round that comes back with calls is answered -- the
164	// assistant turn echoed with its calls, then one tool message per call, in
165	// order -- and the question is put again with all of it in the history, until
166	// a round comes back with words alone. Those words are the reply; the rounds
167	// before them are in the recorded exchanges.
168	func (a *App) llmChatTools(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool,
169		tools []map[string]any, run toolRunner, onText func(string)) (string, error) {
170		if len(tools) == 0 || run == nil {
171			return a.llmChatOn(step, msgs, thinking, onText)
172		}
173		msgs = append([]map[string]any(nil), msgs...)
174		last := "" // what the round before asked for, to catch a model going in circles
175		for round := 0; round < toolRounds; round++ {
176			rep, err := a.chatRound(step, msgs, thinking, tools, onText)
177			if err != nil && round == 0 && !errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
178				// a server that will not take a tools field answers the first
179				// round with an error and nothing else; the job is worth more
180				// than the search, so it is asked again plainly
181				a.logfIdle(">>> %s: the server refused the request with tools (%v) -- asked again without them", step, err)
182				return a.llmChatOn(step, msgs, thinking, onText)
183			}
184			if err != nil {
185				return "", err
186			}
187			if len(rep.Calls) == 0 {
188				return rep.Content, nil
189			}
190			// the round itself, in the log. The tools log what they DID -- what was
191			// searched, what was read -- and that was the whole of it: a step six
192			// minutes into a tool loop showed a handful of search lines with
193			// nothing tying them to the call they belong to, no count of how many
194			// rounds were left, and no sign at all when the loop ran out. The
195			// round is the fact; the searches under it are the detail.
196			asked := callSummary(rep.Calls)
197			if asked == last {
198				// the tell for a model going in circles: the identical call again,
199				// which is what eight rounds of one wiki page looked like from the
200				// outside -- nothing, until the step failed
201				a.logfIdle(">>> %s: round %d of %d asks for the same thing again — %s",
202					step, round+1, toolRounds, asked)
203			} else {
204				a.logfIdle(">>> %s: round %d of %d — the model asked for %s",
205					step, round+1, toolRounds, asked)
206			}
207			last = asked
208			msgs = append(msgs, map[string]any{"role": "assistant", "content": rep.Content, "tool_calls": rep.Calls})
209			for _, c := range rep.Calls {
210				msgs = append(msgs, map[string]any{"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": c.ID,
211					"content": run(c.Function.Name, json.RawMessage(c.Function.Arguments))})
212			}
213		}
214		a.logfIdle("!!! %s: still calling tools after %d rounds — the step gets no answer from this call",
215			step, toolRounds)
216		return "", fmt.Errorf("the model was still calling tools after %d rounds", toolRounds)
217	}
218	
219	// chatRound is one request and its recorded exchange.
220	func (a *App) chatRound(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool,
221		tools []map[string]any, onText func(string)) (chatReply, error) {
222		rec := a.recordChatStart(step, thinking, msgs)
223		// tee an existing stream through the live page; a caller with no callback
224		// stays unstreamed (wrapping nil would flip the wire request to streaming)
225		if onText != nil {
226			user := onText
227			onText = func(s string) { rec.stream(s); user(s) }
228		}
229		t0 := time.Now()
230		rep, err := a.llmChatPost(step, msgs, thinking, tools, onText)
231		rec.done(rep.recorded(), rep.Stop, time.Since(t0), err)
232		return rep, err
233	}
234	
235	// recorded is the reply as the exchange log shows it: thinking, words, then
236	// the calls. Reasoning is wrapped in <think> tags -- how an inlining model
237	// arrives anyway, and what chatHTML folds away -- so the page has one spelling.
238	func (r chatReply) recorded() string {
239		body := r.Content
240		if strings.TrimSpace(r.Think) != "" && !strings.Contains(body, "</think>") {
241			body = "<think>" + r.Think + "</think>" + body
242		}
243		if len(r.Calls) == 0 {
244			return body
245		}
246		var b strings.Builder
247		b.WriteString(body)
248		for _, c := range r.Calls {
249			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "\n[tool call %s(%s)]", c.Function.Name, c.Function.Arguments)
250		}
251		return b.String()
252	}
253	
254	// thinkSwitch says whether the model may reason before it answers, in BOTH
255	// spellings the local servers take. llama.cpp renders the chat template itself
256	// and reads chat_template_kwargs; halogen-flash-server takes the same two
257	// names at the top level -- /health lists "enable_thinking" and
258	// "preserve_thinking" under "supported" -- and ignores keys it does not know.
259	// Sending both is what lets one settings file point at either.
260	//
261	// It is not decoration. With the nested spelling alone, halogen never saw the
262	// switch: asked for one word inside a 16-token budget it spent all 16 on
263	// reasoning and answered with empty content (finish_reason "length"), which
264	// the Settings Test reported as a fault of the model. The same request with
265	// the switch at the top level answers in two tokens, and its prompt is 40
266	// tokens shorter -- the thinking scaffold comes out of the template too.
267	func thinkSwitch(body map[string]any, on bool) {
268		body["enable_thinking"] = on
269		// the reasoning is kept in the reply either way: the log records what the
270		// model thought (chatReply.recorded), and a job that did not ask to think
271		// has nothing to keep
272		body["preserve_thinking"] = true
273		body["chat_template_kwargs"] = map[string]any{
274			"enable_thinking": on, "preserve_thinking": true,
275		}
276	}
277	
278	// llmChatPost is the wire call itself: build the body, post it, read the answer.
279	// step names the caller so the watch can say whose call is running (llmstall.go).
280	func (a *App) llmChatPost(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool,
281		tools []map[string]any, onText func(string)) (chatReply, error) {
282		c := a.readConf()
283		// the server has a default and the model cannot: the id has to match what
284		// this server actually serves, and Fetch models is how it is found
285		if c.Model == "" {
286			return chatReply{}, fmt.Errorf("no LLM model configured -- use the gear button")
287		}
288		body := map[string]any{
289			"model":            c.Model,
290			"messages":         msgs,
291			"top_p":            0.95,
292			"top_k":            20,
293			"min_p":            0.0,
294			"presence_penalty": 0.0,
295		}
296		if thinking {
297			body["temperature"] = 1.0
298			body["max_tokens"] = thinkTokens
299		} else {
300			body["temperature"] = 0.6
301			body["max_tokens"] = plainTokens
302		}
303		thinkSwitch(body, thinking)
304		if len(tools) > 0 {
305			body["tools"] = tools
306		}
307		if onText != nil {
308			body["stream"] = true
309		}
310		buf, err := json.Marshal(body)
311		if err != nil {
312			return chatReply{}, err
313		}
314		ctx := a.runCtx
315		if ctx == nil {
316			ctx = context.Background()
317		}
318		// one request on the wire at a time (llmgate.go): the queue is waited
319		// out before the watch below starts, so the wait is not read as a stall
320		if err := a.takeLLM(ctx, step); err != nil {
321			return chatReply{}, err
322		}
323		defer a.giveLLM()
324		// the watch holds the call to a silence rule and says every minute what is
325		// arriving; a call nobody streams has no silence to measure, so it keeps a
326		// whole-call ceiling on the client instead
327		w := a.watchChat(step, onText != nil)
328		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
329		defer cancel()
330		stop := w.guard(cancel)
331		defer stop()
332		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "POST",
333			llmServer(c)+"/v1/chat/completions", bytes.NewReader(buf))
334		if err != nil {
335			return chatReply{}, err
336		}
337		bearer(req, c.Key)
338		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
339		client := &http.Client{}
340		if onText == nil {
341			client.Timeout = llmWhole
342		}
343		resp, err := client.Do(req)
344		if err != nil {
345			if a.stopFlag.Load() {
346				return chatReply{}, errStopped
347			}
348			return chatReply{}, w.blame(err)
349		}
350		defer resp.Body.Close()
351		// only if the server actually streamed: one that ignores the flag, or that
352		// answers an error as plain JSON, falls through to the decode below
353		if onText != nil && strings.Contains(resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"), "text/event-stream") {
354			rep, err := a.readChatStream(w.wrap(resp.Body), onText, w)
355			return rep, w.blame(err)
356		}
357		var out struct {
358			Choices []struct {
359				Message struct {
360					Content string `json:"content"`
361					// the same out-of-band thinking readChatStream reads, for a
362					// call nobody streamed: kept for the record and nothing else
363					Reasoning string     `json:"reasoning_content"`
364					ToolCalls []toolCall `json:"tool_calls"`
365				} `json:"message"`
366				FinishReason string `json:"finish_reason"`
367			} `json:"choices"`
368			Error any `json:"error"`
369		}
370		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&out); err != nil {
371			return chatReply{}, fmt.Errorf("bad response (%s): %w", resp.Status, err)
372		}
373		if len(out.Choices) == 0 {
374			return chatReply{}, fmt.Errorf("no choices (%s): %v", resp.Status, out.Error)
375		}
376		return chatReply{Content: out.Choices[0].Message.Content,
377			Think: out.Choices[0].Message.Reasoning, Calls: out.Choices[0].Message.ToolCalls,
378			Stop: out.Choices[0].FinishReason}, nil
379	}
380	
381	// readChatStream assembles a server-sent-event reply, handing the caller the
382	// text so far as each piece lands. bufio.Reader, not Scanner: one event can be
383	// a line of any length. A tool call arrives in pieces stamped with its index
384	// and is reassembled by it.
385	func (a *App) readChatStream(r io.Reader, onText func(string), w *chatWatch) (chatReply, error) {
386		br := bufio.NewReader(r)
387		var b, think strings.Builder
388		var calls []toolCall
389		stop := "" // the reason the LAST chunk gives for stopping; see chatReply.Stop
390		for {
391			line, err := br.ReadString('\n')
392			if s := strings.TrimSpace(line); strings.HasPrefix(s, "data:") {
393				payload := strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(s, "data:"))
394				if payload == "[DONE]" {
395					return chatReply{Content: b.String(), Think: think.String(), Calls: calls, Stop: stop}, nil
396				}
397				var ch struct {
398					Choices []struct {
399						Delta struct {
400							Content string `json:"content"`
401							// the model's reasoning. This server keeps it out of content, so a call
402							// thinking hard used to look hung; it is counted and shown (onText feeds the
403							// bar and the recorded page) and goes nowhere near the reply.
404							Reasoning string `json:"reasoning_content"`
405							ToolCalls []struct {
406								Index    int    `json:"index"`
407								ID       string `json:"id"`
408								Type     string `json:"type"`
409								Function struct {
410									Name      string `json:"name"`
411									Arguments string `json:"arguments"`
412								} `json:"function"`
413							} `json:"tool_calls"`
414						} `json:"delta"`
415						FinishReason string `json:"finish_reason"`
416					} `json:"choices"`
417				}
418				// a chunk that will not parse is a chunk, not the reply: keep reading
419				if json.Unmarshal([]byte(payload), &ch) == nil && len(ch.Choices) > 0 {
420					if r := ch.Choices[0].FinishReason; r != "" {
421						stop = r
422					}
423					d := ch.Choices[0].Delta
424					if d.Reasoning != "" {
425						w.wrote(d.Reasoning, true)
426						think.WriteString(d.Reasoning) // for the record, not for the reply
427					}
428					if d.Content != "" {
429						w.wrote(d.Content, false)
430						b.WriteString(d.Content)
431						onText(b.String())
432					}
433					for _, tc := range d.ToolCalls {
434						for len(calls) <= tc.Index {
435							calls = append(calls, toolCall{})
436						}
437						c := &calls[tc.Index]
438						if tc.ID != "" {
439							c.ID = tc.ID
440						}
441						if tc.Type != "" {
442							c.Type = tc.Type
443						}
444						if tc.Function.Name != "" {
445							c.Function.Name += tc.Function.Name
446						}
447						c.Function.Arguments += tc.Function.Arguments
448						w.wrote(tc.Function.Arguments, true)
449					}
450				}
451			}
452			if err != nil {
453				if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
454					// a stream that ends without [DONE] still said what it said
455					return chatReply{Content: b.String(), Think: think.String(), Calls: calls, Stop: stop}, nil
456				}
457				if a.stopFlag.Load() {
458					return chatReply{}, errStopped
459				}
460				return chatReply{}, err // a half-written JSON reply is worth less than the error
461			}
462		}
463	}
464	
465	// jsonItemsDone reads a reply still arriving: how many objects have closed
466	// inside the LAST "<key>": [ (everything before is thinking, which may mention
467	// the key), and the "end" of the last closed one for shapes that carry it.
468	// Only complete items count. The end time is the bar's denominator-free
469	// progress: the model walks the session from the front.
470	func jsonItemsDone(s, key string) (done int, through float64) {
471		q := `"` + key + `"`
472		i := -1
473		for at := 0; ; {
474			j := strings.Index(s[at:], q)
475			if j < 0 {
476				break
477			}
478			j += at
479			at = j + 1
480			rest := strings.TrimLeft(s[j+len(q):], " \t\r\n")
481			if !strings.HasPrefix(rest, ":") {
482				continue
483			}
484			if strings.HasPrefix(strings.TrimLeft(rest[1:], " \t\r\n"), "[") {
485				i = j
486			}
487		}
488		if i < 0 {
489			return 0, 0
490		}
491		tail := s[i:]
492		depth, from := 0, 0
493		inStr, esc := false, false
494		for k, r := range tail {
495			switch {
496			case esc:
497				esc = false
498			case inStr && r == '\\':
499				esc = true
500			case r == '"':
501				inStr = !inStr
502			case inStr: // braces inside a line of narration are just text
503			case r == '{':
504				if depth == 0 {
505					from = k
506				}
507				depth++
508			case r == '}':
509				if depth--; depth == 0 {
510					done++
511					if e, ok := jsonEnd(tail[from : k+1]); ok && e > through {
512						through = e
513					}
514				}
515			}
516		}
517		return done, through
518	}
519	
520	// jsonEnd reads the "end" out of one finished object. A shape without one -- a
521	// narration clip, say -- simply has no answer here, and its caller falls back
522	// to counting.
523	func jsonEnd(obj string) (float64, bool) {
524		var o struct {
525			End *float64 `json:"end"`
526		}
527		if json.Unmarshal([]byte(obj), &o) != nil || o.End == nil {
528			return 0, false
529		}
530		return *o.End, true
531	}
532	
533	// llmChatRetry absorbs one transport hiccup, which a multi-hour pass will hit
534	// -- but never retries a user stop.
535	// ---- what a rejected answer does to the conversation -------------------------
536	
537	// noAnswer names the failure a JSON parser cannot: a reply with no answer in
538	// it at all -- the thinking budget spent and not a word written (reasoning is
539	// kept out of the reply, readChatStream), which json would report as
540	// "unexpected end of JSON input".
541	func noAnswer(reply string) string {
542		if _, answer := splitThink(reply); strings.TrimSpace(answer) != "" {
543			return ""
544		}
545		return "you returned no answer at all -- the whole reply was reasoning. " +
546			"Think briefly, then write the complete JSON: every segment and every effect, not a sample"
547	}
548	
549	// thinkAgain: whether the NEXT attempt may still think. An EMPTY answer means
550	// the thinking budget was spent with no words -- the same question asked the
551	// same way answers the same -- so the retry sends enable_thinking false with
552	// the shorter ceiling (llmChatPost). Bad JSON or the wrong shape keeps
553	// thinking: that model is writing and getting it wrong.
554	func thinkAgain(think bool, reply string) bool { return think && noAnswer(reply) == "" }
555	
556	// cutOff names the other failure a JSON parser cannot: an answer that stopped
557	// at the token ceiling. json says "unexpected end of JSON input" either way,
558	// and the two want opposite fixes -- a malformed answer wants care, a
559	// truncated one wants a SHORTER answer.
560	func cutOff(reply string, err error) string {
561		if strings.TrimSpace(reply) == "" || err == nil {
562			return ""
563		}
564		if !errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) &&
565			!strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unexpected end of JSON input") {
566			return ""
567		}
568		return "your answer stopped in the middle -- it was too long to finish. " +
569			"Answer again with far fewer items"
570	}
571	
572	// retryTurn puts a rejected answer and its correction into the history.
573	//
574	// An empty answer is not echoed back. There is nothing to show the model, and
575	// an empty assistant turn is one the next round has to make sense of -- some
576	// servers refuse a conversation containing one outright, and the rest are
577	// being told "you said:" followed by nothing. The correction carries the whole
578	// message in that case, which is what noAnswer is for.
579	func retryTurn(msgs []map[string]any, reply, problem string) []map[string]any {
580		if strings.TrimSpace(reply) != "" {
581			msgs = append(msgs, msg("assistant", reply))
582		}
583		return append(msgs, msg("user",
584			"Your answer failed validation: "+problem+". Return corrected strict JSON only."))
585	}
586	
587	// jsonReply reads a model's answer into out: the JSON object after any
588	// preamble, code fences stripped. The problem string is the correction to send
589	// back, "" when it parsed.
590	func jsonReply(reply string, out any) string {
591		problem := noAnswer(reply)
592		if problem != "" {
593			return problem
594		}
595		clean := strings.TrimSpace(reply)
596		if i := strings.Index(clean, "{"); i >= 0 {
597			clean = clean[i:]
598		}
599		clean = strings.TrimSuffix(strings.TrimSpace(clean), "```")
600		if err := json.Unmarshal([]byte(clean), out); err != nil {
601			if problem = cutOff(reply, err); problem == "" {
602				problem = "not valid JSON: " + err.Error()
603			}
604		}
605		return problem
606	}
607	
608	func (a *App) llmChatRetry(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool) (string, error) {
609		return a.llmChatRetryOn(step, msgs, thinking, nil)
610	}
611	
612	func (a *App) llmChatRetryOn(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool, onText func(string)) (string, error) {
613		return a.llmChatRetryTools(step, msgs, thinking, nil, nil, onText)
614	}
615	
616	// llmChatRetryTools is the retrying call with tools on the table; with none
617	// it is llmChatRetryOn exactly.
618	//
619	// Two kinds of failure, and they deserve different patience. An answer this app
620	// cannot use -- a 400, a refusal, a reply that will not parse -- is the same
621	// answer in two seconds, so it gets the one short retry it always had. A call
622	// that died IN TRANSIT is a different thing: the server went away mid-answer
623	// and is coming back. On this stack that is its own watchdog taking the
624	// container down after 180 s of engine silence, for the restart policy to pick
625	// up, and the restart is minutes of loading weights. Waiting through it is the
626	// difference between a run that carries on and a Prepare that starts over --
627	// so the waits climb past the restart rather than giving up inside it.
628	func (a *App) llmChatRetryTools(step string, msgs []map[string]any, thinking bool,
629		tools []map[string]any, run toolRunner, onText func(string)) (string, error) {
630		reply, err := a.llmChatTools(step, msgs, thinking, tools, run, onText)
631		for try := 0; err != nil && !errors.Is(err, errStopped); try++ {
632			wait, again := llmWait(err, try)
633			if !again {
634				break
635			}
636			if llmGone(err) {
637				a.logfIdle("!!! %s: the server went away mid-call (%v) -- waiting %s and asking again (%d of %d)",
638					step, err, durOf(wait), try+1, len(llmBackoff))
639			}
640			if !a.nap(wait) {
641				return "", errStopped
642			}
643			reply, err = a.llmChatTools(step, msgs, thinking, tools, run, onText)
644		}
645		return reply, err
646	}
647	
648	// llmBackoff is how long to wait before each attempt at a call that died in
649	// transit. Past the restart, not inside it: the container has to stop, come
650	// back and read tens of gigabytes of weights before it answers anything, and
651	// an attempt made while that is happening is a connection refused that costs
652	// one of the tries. Roughly eight minutes of patience in five attempts, all of
653	// it interruptible.
654	var llmBackoff = []time.Duration{5 * time.Second, 20 * time.Second, time.Minute,
655		2 * time.Minute, 4 * time.Minute}
656	
657	// llmWait is how long to wait before trying again, and whether to try at all.
658	func llmWait(err error, try int) (time.Duration, bool) {
659		if llmGone(err) {
660			if try < len(llmBackoff) {
661				return llmBackoff[try], true
662			}
663			return 0, false
664		}
665		// anything else: the one short retry, and only on the first failure
666		if try == 0 {
667			return 2 * time.Second, true
668		}
669		return 0, false
670	}
671	
672	// llmGone is whether the error means the server went away rather than answered
673	// something unusable: the connection closed mid-reply (EOF), was reset, was
674	// refused, or the stream stopped short of its end. Every one of those is a
675	// server that is down or restarting, and none of them says anything about the
676	// request -- which is what makes asking the same question again worth doing.
677	//
678	// A status code is deliberately not in here. A 500 is the server answering,
679	// and answering the same way in four minutes.
680	func llmGone(err error) bool {
681		if err == nil || errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
682			return false
683		}
684		if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) || errors.Is(err, io.ErrUnexpectedEOF) ||
685			errors.Is(err, syscall.ECONNRESET) || errors.Is(err, syscall.ECONNREFUSED) ||
686			errors.Is(err, syscall.EPIPE) || errors.Is(err, syscall.ENETUNREACH) {
687			return true
688		}
689		// ...and by the words, for the ones that arrive as a bare string: net/http
690		// and the h2 transport both report a server closing on us that way. Whole
691		// words, so a model's own prose in an error message cannot read as one.
692		return goneWords.MatchString(strings.ToLower(err.Error()))
693	}
694	
695	var goneWords = regexp.MustCompile(`\b(eof|connection reset|connection refused|` +
696		`broken pipe|server closed|no such host|transport is closing)\b`)
697	
698	// nap waits, and answers false when the run was stopped instead. Sleeping
699	// through a restart is only tolerable if ⏹ still ends it: eight minutes of
700	// time.Sleep is eight minutes of a button that does nothing.
701	func (a *App) nap(d time.Duration) bool {
702		ctx := a.runCtx
703		if ctx == nil {
704			ctx = context.Background()
705		}
706		t := time.NewTimer(d)
707		defer t.Stop()
708		select {
709		case <-t.C:
710			return !a.stopFlag.Load()
711		case <-ctx.Done():
712			return false
713		}
714	}
715

package main

// The run bar: one ▶ and one ⏹ for every page, meaning the same thing on each
// -- start, pause and resume what the page does; end it. Moved out of
// pipeline.go, which is the steps and their subprocesses, because this is the
// one thing in that file that touched a widget, and a file that runs ffmpeg
// should not need GTK to compile.

import (
	"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gtk/v4"
)

// The tracks the two halves of the bar are reported on, and prog itself, live
// in runqueue.go with the work queue they feed.

// transport is what a page offers the run bar when it plays media rather than
// running a pipeline. With it, ▶ and ⏹ mean the same thing on every step: ▶
// starts what the page does and then pauses and resumes it, ⏹ ends it. Without
// it a page's playback was reachable only through the page's own buttons --
// which is why ⏸ and ⏹ sat there doing nothing while a voice sample played.
type transport interface {
	playing() bool // running right now
	cued() bool    // loaded but paused, so ▶ means resume rather than start over
	toggle()
	stop()
}

// pageTransport is the visible page's playback, if that page has any.
func (a *App) pageTransport() transport {
	switch a.stack.VisibleChildName() {
	case "cut":
		// ▶ here suggests a cut, the page's long job, and it stays that way
		// until the preview is actually running. The player is loaded the
		// moment you click the timeline -- that cues a frame to look at, it is
		// not playback, and it used to mean ▶ played the video on a page whose
		// cut was still empty. Once the preview HAS been started, the run bar
		// is its transport until ⏹.
		if a.ed != nil && (a.ed.playing() || a.ed.started) {
			return a.ed
		}
	case "narrate":
		// ▶ here is the step itself -- write the narration, then speak it -- and
		// it stays that way until the preview is actually running: the voice
		// sample has its own two buttons beside it, and a clip merely cued by
		// clicking a line to look at it is not playback. Once the preview HAS
		// been started, the run bar is its transport until ⏹ -- otherwise ⏸
		// would have nothing to pause and ⏹ nothing to end.
		if a.narr != nil && (a.narr.playing() || a.narr.started) {
			return a.narr
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// playClicked runs whatever step is on screen, pauses it, or resumes it.
func (a *App) playClicked() {
	if a.running {
		// while a run is under way ▶ is the pause button, and says so
		if a.pauseFlag.Load() {
			a.pauseFlag.Store(false)
			a.setStatus("resumed")
		} else {
			a.pauseFlag.Store(true)
			a.setStatus("pausing after the current stage…")
		}
		a.updateRunControls()
		return
	}
	// playback beats the page's action: once something is playing, the button
	// belongs to it until it is stopped or reaches the end
	if t := a.pageTransport(); t != nil && (t.playing() || t.cued()) {
		t.toggle()
		a.updateRunControls()
		return
	}
	// ▶ runs the steps ticked beside it (runchain.go), which is one step on a
	// fresh project and as many as you like after that. It used to run
	// whichever page was showing, which made the button mean a different
	// thing on each of four pages and gave the run bar two ▶s -- one for this
	// page, one for several -- where there is only ever one thing to press.
	a.snapSources()
	a.chainRun()
}

// runPageNow is one step, the same call that page's ▶ used to make on its own.
func (a *App) runPageNow(page string) {
	switch page {
	case "prep":
		// one press for the whole step: the transcripts and the frames, then
		// the describing and the fixing. They were two tabs and two buttons,
		// and the second could not be pressed before the first had finished.
		a.prepRun()
	case "cut":
		// ▶ is this step's job, suggesting, as on every other page; adding a
		// selection is ＋ Add. Suggesting over hand edits still refuses in
		// suggestClicked and says to Revert first.
		if a.ed != nil {
			a.suggestClicked()
		}
	case "narrate":
		// the whole step in one press: write the narration if the cut has no
		// narration or has moved under the one it has, then speak every line
		// that is not already in the cache (narrateRun). It used to be only the
		// speaking half, with the writing on a button beside the video.
		a.narrateRun()
	case "produce":
		// the whole end of the pipeline in one press: the upload text once,
		// the thumbnail, then the render -- whatever of it is still missing is
		// made, and what is already written is never rewritten (produceClicked)
		a.produceClicked()
	}
}

func (a *App) stopClicked() {
	if t := a.pageTransport(); t != nil && (t.playing() || t.cued()) {
		t.stop()
		a.setStatus("playback stopped")
		a.updateRunControls()
	}
	if !a.running {
		return
	}
	a.stopFlag.Store(true)
	a.pauseFlag.Store(false)
	if a.runCancel != nil {
		a.runCancel() // aborts LLM requests, which are not subprocesses
	}
	a.ctlMu.Lock()
	for cmd := range a.curCmds {
		if cmd.Process != nil {
			_ = cmd.Process.Kill()
		}
	}
	a.ctlMu.Unlock()
	a.setStatus("stopping…")
}

// updateRunControls draws the two buttons from whatever is actually under way:
// a run, this page's playback, or nothing. ▶ is a toggle rather than a separate
// pair, because a dedicated ⏸ was dead on every page whose ▶ is not a run.
func (a *App) updateRunControls() {
	t := a.pageTransport()
	busy := (a.running && !a.pauseFlag.Load()) || (t != nil && t.playing())
	if busy {
		a.playBtn.SetIconName("media-playback-pause-symbolic")
		a.playBtn.SetTooltipText("Pause")
	} else {
		a.playBtn.SetIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
		a.playBtn.SetTooltipText("Run this step — or resume what is paused")
	}
	a.stopBtn.SetSensitive(a.running || busy || (t != nil && t.cued()))
	a.syncPlayIcons()
}

// setPlayIcon draws one transport button from what its player is doing. Every
// play button in the app is this one button in two states -- a ▶ that has
// already started something is a lie, and a separate ⏸ beside it is a button
// that is dead more often than not.
func setPlayIcon(b *gtk.Button, playing bool, playTip, pauseTip string) {
	if b == nil {
		return
	}
	if playing {
		b.SetIconName("media-playback-pause-symbolic")
		b.SetTooltipText(pauseTip)
	} else {
		b.SetIconName("media-playback-start-symbolic")
		b.SetTooltipText(playTip)
	}
}

// syncPlayIcons redraws the pages' own play buttons. They hang off four
// different players, all of which report here through Player.OnState, so this
// runs on every start, pause and end-of-stream -- including the ones nobody
// clicked for, like a clip simply finishing.
func (a *App) syncPlayIcons() {
	if a.ed != nil {
		// two ▶s on that page, each pausing only what IT plays: plain ▶ wears
		// ⏸ only while the RECORDING runs, and ▶✂ (its own two-glyph face,
		// synced beside this) only while the cut does -- one ⏸ across both
		// would pause something its button never claimed to have started
		setPlayIcon(a.ed.playBtn, a.ed.playing() && !a.ed.cutOnly,
			"play the recording from the playhead — every second of it, removed "+
				"stretches included", "pause the preview")
		// and its lamp: lit while the preview is the recording, as ▶✂ is lit
		// while it is the cut and ▶✂✂ while it is the review (lamp)
		lamp(a.ed.playBtn, !a.ed.cutOnly)
		a.ed.syncCutPlay()
		a.ed.syncReviewPlay() // and the third, whose ⏸ is only the review's
	}
	if n := a.narr; n != nil {
		// the preview has no button of its own any more: the picture is its
		// play/pause, and the run bar is the rest of its transport
		n.syncSpeakIcons()
	}
	if vp := a.voicePick; vp != nil {
		// vp.spoken is what the player is holding: while the band walks the
		// takes it is "" and the player is on the RECORDING, so a face drawn
		// from playing() alone offered to pause a sample that is not there --
		// and pressing it synthesized one instead
		setPlayIcon(vp.playBtn, vp.playing() && vp.spoken != "",
			"Speak the sample in the selected voice", "pause the sample")
		if vp.stopBtn != nil {
			// nothing loaded is nothing to stop: the sample's ⏹ is the one
			// button on this page that the run bar's ⏹ no longer covers
			vp.stopBtn.SetSensitive(vp.playing() || vp.cued())
		}
		// and the band's ▶ beside the dropdown, which wears ⏹ rather than ⏸
		// while it walks the takes -- this is where a walk that simply ran out
		// puts it back (narrate_takeband.go)
		vp.band.syncPlayBtn()
	}
	// Produce is not here: it has no play button of its own. A finished run cues
	// its result into the picture and the run bar is that video's transport from
	// there, which is one ▶ for the page instead of the two it used to have.
}

package main

// Running the whole pipeline in one press.
//
// Each step is its own goroutine that ends on the GUI thread through endRun,
// so a chain is a LIST that endRun advances: the step that finished says what
// became of it, and the next is started or the chain is abandoned. Nothing
// about a step has to know it is in one.
//
// The steps are the pages, in the order the pipeline runs them, because that
// is the only order that makes sense: the cut reads what Prepare wrote, the
// narration is written over the cut, and the render needs both.

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/diamondburned/gotk4/pkg/gtk/v4"
)

// the steps a chain can hold, in pipeline order: the page each runs on, and
// what to call it in the menu.
var chainSteps = []struct{ page, name string }{
	{"prep", "Prepare"},
	{"cut", "Cut"},
	{"narrate", "Narrate"},
	{"produce", "Produce"},
}

// chainRun starts a chain: the ticked steps, in order, from the first one on.
func (a *App) chainRun() {
	if a.busy() {
		return
	}
	want := a.chainPicked()
	if len(want) == 0 {
		a.setStatus("nothing ticked beside ▶ — tick the steps to run")
		return
	}
	a.chain = want
	a.chainFrom, a.chainAt = time.Now(), time.Now()
	a.chainRan = nil
	a.logf(">>> run: %s", strings.Join(a.chainNames(want), " → "))
	a.chainNext()
}

// chainTime is a stretch of a run said the way a person would: under a minute
// in seconds, over it in minutes and seconds. Not mmss -- "3:04" beside a step
// name reads as a timestamp in the session rather than as how long the step
// took, and this is the one number on the page that is a duration.
func chainTime(d time.Duration) string {
	s := d.Seconds()
	if s < 60 {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%.0fs", s)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%dm %02ds", int(s)/60, int(s)%60)
}

// chainNext takes the next step off the chain and runs it, on the page it
// belongs to: a step's own ▶ works on the widgets of its page, and a page that
// was never shown has none.
func (a *App) chainNext() {
	for len(a.chain) > 0 {
		page := a.chain[0]
		a.chain = a.chain[1:]
		if page == "narrate" && a.narrOff {
			a.logf(">>> run: Narrate skipped — this video has no narration")
			continue
		}
		// Cut refuses over hand edits, and in a chain that refusal would be a
		// halt nobody asked for: the edits are the answer, so the step has
		// nothing to do and the rest of the chain still does.
		if page == "cut" && a.ed != nil && len(a.ed.segs) > 0 && !sameCut(a.ed.segs, a.ed.base.segs) {
			a.logf(">>> run: Cut skipped — the cut has hand edits, which are kept")
			continue
		}
		// showStep, not the stack: moving a page is more than showing it. It
		// swaps the tab row and the two bars, and -- the half that matters
		// here -- it REBUILDS the cut's tracks when a run has moved what they
		// are drawn from, synchronously, before anything presses that page's
		// button. Setting the stack's child alone left the cut asking about a
		// session it had not loaded: Prepare finished, the chain reached Cut
		// with an editor that still had no recordings in it, and the step
		// came to nothing.
		a.chainMoving = true
		a.showStep(page)
		a.chainMoving = false
		a.logf(">>> run: %s", a.pageName(page))
		a.chainStep, a.chainAt = page, time.Now()
		a.runPageNow(page)
		if !a.running {
			// the step declined -- nothing to do, or it refused -- so the
			// chain has to carry itself rather than wait for an endRun that
			// is not coming. Its clock goes with it: a step that never ran
			// has no duration, and leaving the marker set would put the next
			// press on a page of its own into this chain's tally.
			a.chainStep = ""
			continue
		}
		return
	}
	a.chainEnd("done")
}

// chainDone is endRun's half: the step that just finished either hands the
// chain on or ends it. Stopped or failed, the rest is abandoned -- a chain
// exists to save presses, not to carry on past the answer going wrong.
func (a *App) chainDone() {
	if a.chainStep == "" {
		return // no chain under way: a step pressed on its own page
	}
	// how long that step took, kept for the line at the end. Timed here rather
	// than by each step, because what a chain is about is the WAIT -- the
	// whole press, not the part of it any one page is responsible for.
	a.chainRan = append(a.chainRan, fmt.Sprintf("%s %s",
		a.pageName(a.chainStep), chainTime(time.Since(a.chainAt))))
	a.chainStep = ""
	if a.stopFlag.Load() {
		a.chainEnd("stopped")
		return
	}
	if len(a.chain) == 0 {
		a.chainEnd("done")
		return
	}
	a.chainNext()
}

// chainEnd says what the whole press cost, and what it did not get to. Only
// worth a line for a chain of more than one: a single step already says what
// it did, and "Prepare 9m 12s — total 9m 12s" is the same number twice.
func (a *App) chainEnd(how string) {
	left := len(a.chain)
	a.chain, a.chainStep = nil, ""
	if len(a.chainRan) == 0 {
		return
	}
	total := chainTime(time.Since(a.chainFrom))
	if len(a.chainRan) == 1 && left == 0 {
		a.chainRan = nil
		return
	}
	switch {
	case how == "stopped":
		a.logf(">>> run: stopped after %s — %s — %d step(s) left undone",
			total, strings.Join(a.chainRan, ", "), left)
		a.setStatus("stopped after " + total)
	case left > 0:
		a.logf(">>> run: %s — %s — %d step(s) left undone",
			total, strings.Join(a.chainRan, ", "), left)
		a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("ran %s, %d left undone", total, left))
	default:
		a.logf(">>> run: all done in %s — %s", total, strings.Join(a.chainRan, ", "))
		a.setStatus("all done in " + total)
	}
	a.chainRan = nil
}

func (a *App) pageName(page string) string {
	for _, s := range chainSteps {
		if s.page == page {
			return s.name
		}
	}
	return page
}

func (a *App) chainNames(pages []string) []string {
	var out []string
	for _, p := range pages {
		out = append(out, a.pageName(p))
	}
	return out
}

// chainPicked is the steps ticked, in pipeline order.
func (a *App) chainPicked() []string {
	var out []string
	for _, s := range chainSteps {
		if t := a.chainTicks[s.page]; t != nil && t.Active() {
			out = append(out, s.page)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// buildChainMenu is the ticks beside ▶ and the button that runs them. A menu
// rather than a second ▶: which steps is a standing answer, not a choice made
// on every press, and the button says which are on with the menu shut.
func (a *App) buildChainMenu() *gtk.Box {
	pop := gtk.NewPopover()
	list := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
	list.SetMarginTop(6)
	list.SetMarginBottom(6)
	list.SetMarginStart(10)
	list.SetMarginEnd(10)
	a.chainTicks = map[string]*gtk.CheckButton{}
	for _, s := range chainSteps {
		s := s
		c := gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel(s.name)
		// Prepare alone to begin with: it is the one step a fresh project can
		// run, and the only one whose inputs are on disk before anything else
		// has happened. The rest are a tick away, and the answer is kept with
		// the project.
		c.SetActive(s.page == chainSteps[0].page)
		c.ConnectToggled(func() {
			a.syncChain()
			if !a.chainQuiet {
				a.saveProjectNow()
			}
		})
		a.chainTicks[s.page] = c
		list.Append(c)
	}
	pop.SetChild(list)

	a.chainPick = gtk.NewMenuButton()
	a.chainPick.SetPopover(pop)
	a.chainPick.SetTooltipText("Which steps ▶ runs, in this order. Narrate skips itself " +
		"when the video has no narration, and Cut skips itself when the cut has hand edits.")
	// one control in two halves, the split button's shape: press ▶ for the
	// thing, press the arrow for which thing. GTK4 has no AdwSplitButton
	// without libadwaita, and does not need one -- a linked box of a button
	// and a menu button IS that control, and is what the tab row and the
	// stepper on this window are already made of (widgets.go).
	//
	// ▶ itself is the left half: there is one thing to press on this bar, and
	// two play buttons beside each other -- one for this page, one for
	// several -- was one too many.
	box := linked(a.playBtn, a.chainPick)
	a.syncChain()
	return box
}

// followChainTick moves a lone tick to the page just opened.
//
// The ticks are a standing answer -- which steps ▶ runs -- and most of the time
// there is exactly one, the step being worked on. Walking to another tab is
// then the whole of "I am working on that one now", and having to open the menu
// to say it again is a second answer to the same question: press ▶ on Cut with
// Prepare ticked and Prepare runs, which is never what the press meant.
//
// Only when exactly ONE is ticked. Several ticked is a chain somebody built on
// purpose -- Prepare → Cut → Produce -- and a tab click must not rewrite it.
//
// A run does not stop it. It used to: the chain moves the pages itself
// (chainNext), and switching this off for the whole run was the blunt way of
// keeping it from retargeting the ticks as the chain walked them. The cost was
// that walking to another tab while a step ran did nothing, which is exactly
// when you do it -- Prepare takes an hour and you go and look at Cut. So the
// guard is now the chain's own move rather than the run: chainMoving is set
// only around the page changes chainNext makes.
func (a *App) followChainTick(page string) {
	if a.chainTicks == nil || a.chainMoving {
		return
	}
	if a.chainTicks[page] == nil {
		return // a page the chain has no step for
	}
	picked := a.chainPicked()
	if len(picked) != 1 || picked[0] == page {
		return
	}
	// quietly, then one save: two toggles through the handler would be two
	// writes of the project for one gesture
	a.chainQuiet = true
	a.chainTicks[picked[0]].SetActive(false)
	a.chainTicks[page].SetActive(true)
	a.chainQuiet = false
	a.syncChain()
	a.saveProjectNow()
}

// syncChain puts the answer on the button.
func (a *App) syncChain() {
	if a.chainPick == nil {
		return
	}
	n := len(a.chainPicked())
	switch n {
	case 0:
		a.chainPick.SetLabel("none")
	case len(chainSteps):
		a.chainPick.SetLabel("all")
	default:
		a.chainPick.SetLabel(fmt.Sprintf("%d steps", n))
	}
}

// applyChain is a project's answer, put on the ticks without saving it back. A
// project written before this has none, and gets the first step alone -- the
// same as a new one.
func (a *App) applyChain(pages []string) {
	if a.chainTicks == nil {
		a.chainSteps = pages
		return
	}
	a.chainQuiet = true
	if pages == nil {
		for page, t := range a.chainTicks {
			t.SetActive(page == chainSteps[0].page)
		}
	} else {
		on := map[string]bool{}
		for _, p := range pages {
			on[p] = true
		}
		for page, t := range a.chainTicks {
			t.SetActive(on[page])
		}
	}
	a.chainQuiet = false
	a.syncChain()
}
