218	}
219	
220	// numberedLines reads the answer back onto the line numbers it was given, and
221	// says how many never came. By NUMBER and not by position: a model that drops a
222	// blank line or wraps one in two would otherwise shift every line after it onto
223	// the wrong seconds, which is the one mistake here that cannot be seen.
224	func numberedLines(reply string, n int) ([]string, int) {
225		out := make([]string, n)
226		for _, ln := range strings.Split(reply, "\n") {
227			num, text, ok := strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(ln), "\t")
228			if !ok {
229				// a model that answered "3. text" or "3 text" instead
230				num, text, ok = strings.Cut(strings.TrimSpace(ln), " ")
231				if !ok {
232					continue
233				}
234			}
235			i := 0
236			if _, err := fmt.Sscanf(strings.TrimRight(num, ".:"), "%d", &i); err != nil {
237				continue
238			}
239			if i >= 1 && i <= n && out[i-1] == "" {
240				out[i-1] = strings.TrimSpace(text)
241			}
242		}
243		miss := 0
244		for _, s := range out {
245			if s == "" {
246				miss++
247			}
248		}
249		return out, miss
250	}
251	
252	// subTrack is one finished subtitle file: the language it is in, and where it
253	// was written.
254	type subTrack struct {
255		code, tag, name string
256		path            string
257		// the cues themselves, because the file is not the only thing written
258		// from them: the same track goes out as WebVTT beside the video (vttText),
259		// and re-reading the .srt to get them back would be a parser nobody needs.
260		cues []subCue
261	}
262	
263	// subTracks writes the track and its translations, and says what it wrote. The
264	// first is always the session's own language, whatever the list says: the words
265	// the video actually speaks are not a translation of anything.
266	func (a *App) subTracks(cues []subCue, dir string, want []string) []subTrack {
267		if len(cues) == 0 {
268			return nil
269		}
270		// the language the video is SPOKEN in, default filled in (asrLanguage):
271		// the first track is not a translation of anything and carries it
272		own := a.asrLanguage()
273		tag, name, ok := subLangOf(own)
274		if !ok {
275			tag, name = "und", strings.ToUpper(own)
276		}
277		out := []subTrack{{code: own, tag: tag, name: name,
278			path: filepath.Join(dir, "final.srt"), cues: cues}}
279		for _, code := range want {
280			if code == own {
281				continue // already the track above, and not a translation of it
282			}
283			t, n, ok := subLangOf(code)
284			if !ok {
285				continue
286			}
287			a.prog(trackSTT, 0.94, "translating the subtitles")
288			a.logfIdle(">>> subtitles: translating %d lines into %s", len(cues), n)
289			done := a.translateCues(cues, code)
290			if len(done) == 0 {
291				continue
292			}
293			out = append(out, subTrack{code: code, tag: t, name: n,
294				path: filepath.Join(dir, "final."+code+".srt"), cues: done})
295			if err := os.WriteFile(out[len(out)-1].path, []byte(srtText(done)), 0o644); err != nil {
296				a.logfIdle("!!! subtitles: %s: %v", n, err)
297				out = out[:len(out)-1]
298			}
299		}
300		return out
301	}
302	
303	// subSideFiles is every path this video's subtitles can occupy beside it: the
304	// spoken language under the video's own name, and one pair per language the
305	// app can translate into.
306	//
307	// Named exactly, never globbed. "final*.srt" beside a final.mp4 also matches
308	// the final2.srt of the render before it -- a different video, in the folder
309	// people actually keep these in -- and this list is used to DELETE the stale
310	// ones as well as to find them.
311	func subSideFiles(out string) []string {
312		stem := strings.TrimSuffix(out, filepath.Ext(out))
313		files := []string{stem + ".srt", stem + ".vtt"}
314		for _, l := range subLangs {
315			files = append(files, stem+"."+l.code+".srt", stem+"."+l.code+".vtt")
316		}
317		return files
318	}
319	
320	// srtText is the cues as an .srt.
321	func srtText(cues []subCue) string {
322		var b strings.Builder
323		for i, c := range cues {
324			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%d\n%s --> %s\n%s\n\n", i+1, srtTime(c.s), srtTime(c.e), c.text)
325		}
326		return b.String()
327	}
328	
329	// vttText is the same cues as WebVTT, which is the only subtitle format a
330	// browser reads.
331	//
332	// A <video> tag needs this and not the .srt: <track> parses WebVTT alone --
333	// point it at an .srt and Firefox fetches the file, fails to parse it and
334	// shows nothing -- and the tracks muxed INTO the mp4 are not offered by any
335	// browser at all, whatever VLC does with them. Two files for the same cues,
336	// because the player on the desk and the player on the page do not read the
337	// same one.
338	//
339	// The difference is a header, a full stop instead of a comma, and the three
340	// characters WebVTT treats as markup.
341	func vttText(cues []subCue) string {
342		var b strings.Builder
343		b.WriteString("WEBVTT\n\n")
344		for i, c := range cues {
345			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%d\n%s --> %s\n%s\n\n", i+1, vttTime(c.s), vttTime(c.e), vttEscape(c.text))
346		}
347		return b.String()
348	}
349	
350	// vttTime is an .srt stamp with the decimal point WebVTT wants.
351	func vttTime(t float64) string { return strings.Replace(srtTime(t), ",", ".", 1) }
352	
353	// vttEscape keeps a cue's text from being read as markup: WebVTT allows
354	// <b>, <i> and &amp; inside a cue, so a spoken "R&D" or a "<" out of a
355	// transcript would be swallowed or break the cue.
356	func vttEscape(s string) string {
357		s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "&", "&amp;")
358		s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "<", "&lt;")
359		return strings.ReplaceAll(s, ">", "&gt;")
360	}

3	// The sd.cpp server (leejet/stable-diffusion.cpp sd-server, the compose file's
4	// "sd" service), talked to over HTTP like audio.cpp. Of its three API families
5	// this uses the native /sdcpp/v1: the only one that takes an init_image, and
6	// the thumbnail starts from a frame of the video. It is asynchronous -- POST
7	// img_gen answers 202 with a job id, GET jobs/{id} carries the picture when
8	// "completed" -- because a diffusion job outlives a proxy's read timeout. ONE
9	// model, chosen at server start: the Settings name is a check, not a choice.

13		"context"
14		"encoding/base64"

17		"io"

23	
24	// sdPort is where the compose "sd" service listens. Same convention as
25	// ttsPort: a blank endpoint in Settings means this, on the loopback.
26	const sdPort = 1234
27	
28	// sdURL is the server the thumbnail is drawn by. The settings file wins over
29	// the environment, for the same reason it does for audio.cpp: it is the one of
30	// the two the user can see and clear.
31	func (a *App) sdURL() string {
32		if u := serverURL(a.readConf().SD); u != "" {
33			return u
34		}
35		if u := serverURL(os.Getenv("SD_SERVER")); u != "" {
36			return u
37		}
38		return fmt.Sprintf("http://127.0.0.1:%d", sdPort)
39	}
40	
41	// sdCaps is what /sdcpp/v1/capabilities says about the running server. Only
42	// the parts naivepost can act on are decoded: which weights are loaded, and
43	// whether this build can generate an image at all -- a server started on a
44	// video model answers happily and then fails every img_gen.
45	type sdCaps struct {
46		Model struct {
47			Name string `json:"name"`
48			Stem string `json:"stem"`
49			Path string `json:"path"`
50		} `json:"model"`
51		Modes []string `json:"supported_modes"`
52	}
53	
54	// modelName is the loaded model as a human would name it: the file's stem when
55	// the server reports one, since that is what the Settings box is filled with.
56	func (c sdCaps) modelName() string {
57		if s := strings.TrimSpace(c.Model.Stem); s != "" {
58			return s
59		}
60		return strings.TrimSpace(c.Model.Name)
61	}
62	
63	func (c sdCaps) canImage() bool {
64		for _, m := range c.Modes {
65			if m == "img_gen" {
66				return true
67			}
68		}
69		// an older build that does not report modes is not a broken one: assume it
70		// can draw, and let the job say otherwise
71		return len(c.Modes) == 0
72	}
73	
74	func sdCapabilities(ctx context.Context, url, key string) (sdCaps, error) {
75		var caps sdCaps
76		req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, "GET",
77			strings.TrimRight(url, "/")+"/sdcpp/v1/capabilities", nil)
78		if err != nil {
79			return caps, err
80		}
81		bearer(req, key)
82		resp, err := (&http.Client{Timeout: 15 * time.Second}).Do(req)
83		if err != nil {
84			return caps, fmt.Errorf("nothing answering: %w", err)
85		}
86		defer resp.Body.Close()
87		if resp.StatusCode != 200 {
88			return caps, fmt.Errorf("%s does not look like an sd.cpp server: it answered %s",
89				url, resp.Status)
90		}
91		if err := json.NewDecoder(resp.Body).Decode(&caps); err != nil {
92			return caps, fmt.Errorf("%s answered something that is not sd.cpp capabilities: %w", url, err)
93		}
94		return caps, nil
95	}

98	// of the JSON entirely, so the server applies the defaults it was STARTED with
99	// -- and those matter, because steps, cfg-scale, sampler and flow-shift belong
100	// to the checkpoint and are passed to sd-server on its command line (see

102	// override the value the loaded model actually wants.
103	type sdRequest struct {
104		Prompt   string `json:"prompt"`

106		Width    int    `json:"width,omitempty"`
107		Height   int    `json:"height,omitempty"`

112		// renoises everything, and no strength survives it.
113		RefImages []string `json:"ref_images,omitempty"`

121	// sdRefImage reads a frame into the field above. Any image field takes a raw
122	// base64 string or a data URL; the data URL is used because it carries the
123	// type, and the frames are jpeg while the output is png.
124	func sdRefImage(path string) (string, error) {
125		b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
126		if err != nil {
127			return "", err
128		}
129		kind := "jpeg"
130		if strings.HasSuffix(strings.ToLower(path), ".png") {
131			kind = "png"
132		}
133		return "data:image/" + kind + ";base64," + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(b), nil

136	// sdJob is a job as the server reports it, at submission and at every poll.
137	type sdJob struct {
138		ID     string `json:"id"`
139		Status string `json:"status"`
140		Queue  int    `json:"queue_position"`
141		Result *struct {
142			Images []struct {
143				B64 string `json:"b64_json"`
144			} `json:"images"`
145		} `json:"result"`

147			Code    string `json:"code"`
148			Message string `json:"message"`
149		} `json:"error"`

152	// sdGenerate submits one image job and waits for the picture. onWait (may be
153	// nil) gets a human sentence per poll. The context is the run's, so ⏹ ends
154	// the wait, and the job is then cancelled on the server -- it would otherwise
155	// hold the card ahead of the next ▶.
156	func (a *App) sdGenerate(ctx context.Context, req sdRequest, onWait func(string)) ([]byte, error) {
157		url := a.sdURL()
158		key := a.readConf().SDKey // read once; the same key rides every request of the job
159		body, err := json.Marshal(req)
160		if err != nil {
161			return nil, err

171		// 202, in the polling loop below.
172		resp, err := (&http.Client{Timeout: 60 * time.Second}).Do(post)

181		}

183			return nil, fmt.Errorf("sd.cpp refused the job (%s): %s", resp.Status, sdJobError(job, raw))
184		}

188			select {

193			}

196			if err != nil {

198			}
199			bearer(get, key)

205				if ctx.Err() != nil {

210			}
211			raw, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)

220			}
221			switch st.Status {

233			default:

235					where := st.Status

245	// sdPollEvery is how often a running job is asked about. A thumbnail on this
246	// stack takes ten to thirty seconds, so a second is fine-grained enough to make

248	//
249	// A var rather than a const only so the tests can shrink it: they drive a fake
250	// server through the same loop, and at a second a poll the offline suite spends
251	// most of its runtime asleep.
252	var sdPollEvery = 1 * time.Second
253	
254	// sdCancel gives the card back. Best effort by design -- it runs when the user
255	// has already pressed ⏹, and there is nothing useful to tell them if the
256	// server has forgotten the job by the time we ask.
257	func (a *App) sdCancel(url, id string) {
258		req, err := http.NewRequest("POST", url+"/sdcpp/v1/jobs/"+id+"/cancel", nil)
259		if err != nil {
260			return
261		}
262		bearer(req, a.readConf().SDKey)
263		if resp, err := (&http.Client{Timeout: 10 * time.Second}).Do(req); err == nil {
264			resp.Body.Close()
265		}
266	}
267	
268	// sdJobError is the server's own words about a failure, falling back to the
269	// raw body: an error naivepost cannot name is still an error worth reading.
270	func sdJobError(job sdJob, raw []byte) string {
271		if job.Error != nil && strings.TrimSpace(job.Error.Message) != "" {
272			if job.Error.Code != "" {
273				return job.Error.Code + ": " + job.Error.Message
274			}
275			return job.Error.Message
276		}
277		return sdSnippet(raw)
278	}
279	
280	// sdSnippet trims a response body down to something that fits in the log. An
281	// HTML error page from a proxy in front of the server is the usual case, and
282	// the first line of it is the part that identifies the proxy.
283	func sdSnippet(raw []byte) string {
284		s := strings.TrimSpace(string(raw))
285		if s == "" {
286			return "(empty body)"
287		}
288		if i := strings.IndexByte(s, '\n'); i >= 0 {
289			s = s[:i]
290		}
291		if r := []rune(s); len(r) > 160 {
292			s = string(r[:160]) + "…"
293		}
294		return s
295	}
296	
297	// testSD is the Settings button: something answers, it answers like sd.cpp, it
298	// can draw, and these are the weights loaded (chosen in SD_ARGS, cpp/run.sh,
299	// not here). When capabilities fails, /v1/models is tried so the usual tenant
300	// of port 1234 (an OpenAI-shaped server) can at least be named in the verdict.
301	func testSD(url, key string) (string, error) {
302		caps, err := sdCapabilities(context.Background(), url, key)
303		if err != nil {
304			if ids, e2 := fetchModels(url, key); e2 == nil {
305				return "", fmt.Errorf("%s answers /v1/models with %s, but not /sdcpp/v1/capabilities -- "+
306					"that is an OpenAI-shaped server, not sd.cpp's sd-server, and the thumbnail needs "+
307					"sd-server's native API", url, strings.Join(ids, ", "))
308			}
309			return "", err
310		}
311		got := caps.modelName()
312		if got == "" {
313			return "", fmt.Errorf("answering, but reporting no loaded model -- was it started without weights?")
314		}
315		if !caps.canImage() {
316			return "", fmt.Errorf("%q is loaded, but this server does not offer img_gen (modes: %s)",
317				got, strings.Join(caps.Modes, ", "))
318		}
319		return fmt.Sprintf("%q is loaded and can draw (%s)", got, caps.Model.Path), nil
320	}

35		// Outputs group (inputsLabel): what the step reads, left of what it has
36		// written. The names and the per-source arithmetic go to the log when the
37		// run starts -- that is scrollable and this is not.
38		p.inputs = inputsLabel()
39		a.inStack.AddNamed(p.inputs, "prep")
40	
41		// Files left, context and prompts right (prepedit.go), a handle between
42		// opening at the middle; both sides resize with the window and stand six
43		// off the handle like every other divider in the app.
44		bench := a.prepEditor()
45		gtk.BaseWidget(bench).SetMarginStart(6)
46		sources := a.buildSources()
47		sources.SetMarginEnd(6)
48	
49		outer := gtk.NewPaned(gtk.OrientationHorizontal)
50		outer.SetStartChild(sources)
51		outer.SetEndChild(bench)
52		outer.SetResizeStartChild(true)
53		outer.SetResizeEndChild(true)
54		openAtHalf(outer)
55		// Shrink off on both ends: shrink means a child may be allocated less than
56		// it needs, and what these two need includes a heading row and a button
57		// row. With it off, GtkPaned clamps the handle to what both children need,
58		// so a shorter window moves the handle instead of hiding half a column.
59		outer.SetShrinkStartChild(false)
60		outer.SetShrinkEndChild(false)
61		outer.SetVExpand(true)
62		// 12 from the window's edges, like the columns on Cut and Narrate, so the
63		// boxes line up with the Inputs row above them and with the same boxes one
64		// tab over.
65		outer.SetMarginStart(12)
66		outer.SetMarginEnd(12)
67		// and 8 off the tabs above and the shared bar below, so the Freq row and
68		// the editor frame do not sit on the transport buttons -- the breathing
69		// room every other edge of every page has
70		outer.SetMarginTop(8)
71		outer.SetMarginBottom(8)
72	
73		// One open-folder button for prepare/ with how much is in it; the three
74		// subfolders are the folder's business. Rides the shared bottom bar
75		// (outStack in main.go).
76		outRow := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
77		outBtn := gtk.NewButtonFromIconName("folder-open-symbolic")
78		outBtn.SetTooltipText("prepare/ — this step's three folders:\n" +
79			"inputs/ — the frames, the per-source transcripts and who spoke when\n" +
80			"describe/ — the event logs, one per video\n" +
81			"transcript/ — the fixed transcripts, the subtitles and the session timeline")
82		outBtn.ConnectClicked(func() { a.openFolder(a.prepareDir()) })
83		p.prepOut = gtk.NewLabel("")
84		outRow.Append(outBtn)
85		outRow.Append(gtk.NewLabel("Prepare:"))
86		outRow.Append(p.prepOut)
87		a.outStack.AddNamed(outRow, "prep")
88	
89		// The work, and nothing above it -- no prompt row at the bottom any more,
90		// because this page's prompts live in the right-hand box now, behind its
91		// menu, and no Inputs row at the top: what this step reads and what it has
92		// written are the two groups on the shared bar below all of it.
93		page := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
94		page.Append(outer)
95	
96		p.refresh()
97		return page
98	}
99	
100	func (a *App) buildSources() *gtk.Box {
101		// every edit to the list changes what a run would see and who the narration
102		// would be spoken by, so the snapshot and the voice picker are refreshed
103		// from here rather than from each of the six things that can edit a row
104		a.srcList = newSourceList(func() {
105			a.snapSources()
106			if a.voicePick != nil {
107				a.voicePick.refreshNarrators()
108			}
109			a.prep.refresh()
110			a.refreshCut() // the tracks ARE this list: a row added or unmarked changes them
111		})
112	
113		// the frame controls: how often, then how big. A stepper over the same
114		// discrete stops the slider had, each..5s, typable by hand.
115		a.interval = newFreqPick()
116	
117		labels := make([]string, len(scalePresets))
118		for i, p := range scalePresets {
119			labels[i] = p.Label
120		}
121		a.scalePick = gtk.NewDropDownFromStrings(labels)
122		a.scalePick.SetTooltipText("Frame size — Original keeps the video's own size")
123		a.setFrameScale("original")
124		a.scalePick.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
125	
126		// The language, on the page whose run listens -- in Settings it was a property
127		// of the machine, three tabs from the sources it was wrong about. Free text:
128		// the code is the server's to interpret.
129		a.langEntry = gtk.NewEntry()
130		a.langEntry.SetWidthChars(4)
131		a.langEntry.SetMaxWidthChars(6)
132		a.langEntry.SetPlaceholderText(defLanguage)
133		a.langEntry.SetTooltipText("Language of this session's speech, as the ASR model spells it (en, de, …) — " +
134			"the wrong one transcribes into gibberish. Empty means " + defLanguage)
135		a.langEntry.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
136		// the cache follows every keystroke rather than a commit: unlike the frame
137		// stepper there is nothing to parse, and a value that only counts once you
138		// tab away is a value the next run silently disagrees with
139		a.langEntry.ConnectChanged(func() { a.setLanguage(a.langEntry.Text()) })
140	
141		// One list, the width of the page; each row says what its file is for. The
142		// buttons say "source" so the list needs no heading.
143		addBtn := gtk.NewButtonWithLabel("Add source files…")
144		addBtn.SetTooltipText("Add recordings or footage — several at once")
145		addBtn.ConnectClicked(a.addFilesDialog)
146		// "Add source folder…" was beside it. Nobody used it -- a session's
147		// recordings are picked by name -- and files picked by name are the one
148		// shape that works everywhere, a Flatpak's portal file chooser included,
149		// where a folder handed over whole is a different and weaker grant.
150		// The legend was here: the four row icons with their words, once, along
151		// the top of the list. It cost a line of the page permanently to answer a
152		// question asked twice -- and it answered it a hand's width away from the
153		// buttons it was about, which is the one place the eye is not while it is
154		// deciding what a symbol does. The words are on the buttons themselves
155		// now: every one of them ends its tooltip with the whole row (srcRowKey),
156		// so hovering any symbol says what all four are.
157	
158		// Where an added file goes, decided once and remembered with the project
159		// rather than asked on every Add: into the project folder, or left where
160		// it is. Copy is the default -- a project is one folder that can be moved
161		// or zipped, and a session whose footage is on the card it was recorded on
162		// is not one thing -- and the tick comes off for the machine that recorded
163		// the footage, where 20 GB of capture does not want a twin.
164		a.copyTick = gtk.NewCheckButtonWithLabel("copy into project")
165		a.copyTick.SetActive(true)
166		a.copyTick.SetTooltipText("Ticked, an added file is copied into the project's sources/ folder, " +
167			"so the project holds everything it needs. Unticked, the file is referenced where it is: " +
168			"nothing is duplicated, and the session breaks if it moves.")
169		a.copyTick.ConnectToggled(func() {
170			if a.refQuiet {
171				return
172			}
173			a.refSources = !a.copyTick.Active()
174			a.saveProjectNow()
175		})
176	
177		addRow := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
178		addRow.Append(addBtn)
179		addRow.Append(a.copyTick)
180	
181		listScroll := gtk.NewScrolledWindow()
182		listScroll.SetChild(a.srcList.box)
183		listScroll.SetVExpand(true)
184		// what the heading used to say, kept on the thing it was about
185		listScroll.SetTooltipText("Every file here is transcribed, and placed on the session clock by the timestamp in its name")
186		// this row is this side's heading, and it joins the size group every
187		// editor's heading is in (editorBody): the two sides of the divider are
188		// read against each other, so a button row a few px taller than the label
189		// row opposite it starts the list a few px above the box it is beside.
190		// The same group is why the Publish page's fields line up with the prompts
191		// (publisher.heading).
192		if a.headGroup == nil {
193			a.headGroup = gtk.NewSizeGroup(gtk.SizeGroupVertical)
194		}
195		a.headGroup.AddWidget(addRow)
196	
197		sources := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)
198		sources.SetVExpand(true)
199		// the same 4 px the editor's own box stands off the top with, so the two
200		// frames begin on one line (editorFrame)
201		sources.SetMarginTop(4)
202		sources.Append(addRow)
203		sources.Append(listScroll)
204	
205		// The bottom line, one line: how the frames are taken, and what language
206		// they are spoken in. Where it all lands used to be chosen here too; it is
207		// the project file's own folder now (project.go), so there is nothing to
208		// choose, and what has been written into it is counted along the bottom of
209		// the page where the other two folders this step writes are.
210		bottom := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 8)
211		bottom.Append(gtk.NewLabel("Freq:"))
212		bottom.Append(a.interval.box)
213		bottom.Append(a.scalePick)
214		bottom.Append(gtk.NewLabel("Language:"))
215		bottom.Append(a.langEntry)
216		// What kind of video this is, mechanically: a read to camera is edited as
217		// text and its picture is never described; a session is described and
218		// its moments picked. Not a wording -- the old Style dropdown below was
219		// one, and went to the context box -- but which PIPELINE runs, and that
220		// is this page's to say, since it is this page's ▶ that runs it.
221		a.stylePick = gtk.NewDropDownFromStrings(styleLabels)
222		a.stylePick.SetTooltipText("Lecture: a read to camera -- the speech is the video, cut by removing " +
223			"the words said twice and the false starts. Gaming: a session -- the cut picks the " +
224			"moments worth keeping. Both describe the picture; only what the cut is chosen from differs.")
225		a.stylePick.SetVAlign(gtk.AlignCenter)
226		a.stylePick.NotifyProperty("selected", func() {
227			// the cache first, then the save: the runner reads the cache, and a
228			// project written from the widget would be one from the OLD cache
229			a.setVideoStyle(styleOf(a.stylePick.Selected()))
230			if !a.styleQuiet {
231				a.saveProjectNow()
232			}
233		})
234		bottom.Append(gtk.NewLabel("Style:"))
235		bottom.Append(a.stylePick)
236		// The Style dropdown was here, after Language: which kind of video ▶
237		// Suggest built -- highlights, a rating, a Short -- turning every prompt
238		// at once to a wording of that name. It is gone. What kind of video this
239		// is, is a fact about the session like everything else on this page, and
240		// the box beside these controls is where the session's facts go: said
241		// there it reaches every step, it outranks the wordings (ctxRule), and
242		// there is one place to say it instead of two that can disagree.
243	
244		// No margins of its own: it is one side of the page's divider now, and the
245		// page keeps its columns 12 from the window's edges as Cut and Narrate do.
246		box := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 12)
247		box.SetVExpand(true)
248		box.Append(sources)
249		box.Append(bottom) // how the frames are taken, under the list they come from
250		return box
251	}
252	
253	// ---- what will be sent -------------------------------------------------------
254	
255	// refresh re-reads everything on the page that is derived from the sources or
256	// from the output folder: what a run would send, and how much of it is already
257	// there. Safe on a page that has not been built -- it is called from the
258	// project loader and from the rescan, both of which can run first.
259	func (p *preproc) refresh() {
260		if p == nil || p.inputs == nil {
261			return
262		}
263		line, detail := p.a.inputsSummary()
264		p.inputs.SetText(line)
265		p.inputs.SetTooltipText(detail) // the per-file arithmetic, on hover
266		setOutCount(p.prepOut, p.a.prepareDir())
267	
268	}
269	
270	// setOutCount fills one of the three output readings: how many files on the
271	// row, when the newest was written on hover. Three of the one-line form side by
272	// side is a paragraph across the bottom of the page, and the question the row
273	// is asked is how much is there.
274	func setOutCount(l *gtk.Label, dir string) {
275		if l == nil {
276			return
277		}
278		n, newest, size := countOutputs(dir)
279		if n == 0 {
280			l.SetText("nothing yet")
281			l.SetTooltipText("")
282			return
283		}
284		l.SetText(fmt.Sprintf("%d files, %s", n, humanSize(size)))
285		l.SetTooltipText("newest " + humanAgo(newest))
286	}
287	
288	// inputsSummary walks the session's sources once: line is what the page shows
289	// (files in, requests they become), detail the same per file for the tooltip
290	// and the log. One walk, because it reads every video's frame directory on
291	// every edit. framesPerReq and fixBlock are visible only here.
292	func (a *App) inputsSummary() (line, detail string) {
293		if a.srcList == nil {
294			return "", ""
295		}
296		vids, auds := a.srcList.split()
297		if len(vids)+len(auds) == 0 {
298			return "no input files — add some above", "(no sources)"
299		}
300		var b strings.Builder
301		frames, vision, lines, fixes := 0, 0, 0, 0
302		descDir := a.describeDir()
303		count := func(base string) {
304			n := len(loadSeg4(a.transcriptPath(base)))
305			lines += n
306			fixes += (n + fixBlock - 1) / fixBlock
307		}
308		for _, v := range vids {
309			base := baseName(v)
310			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n", base)
311			if p, err := a.planVideo(v, descDir); err != nil {
312				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  frames: %v\n", err)
313			} else {
314				scale := p.scale
315				if scale == "" {
316					scale = "original"
317				}
318				frames += len(p.frames)
319				vision += p.chunks
320				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "  %d frames @ %gs (%s)  ->  %d vision requests\n",
321					len(p.frames), p.interval, scale, p.chunks)
322			}
323			count(base)
324			b.WriteString(fixerLine(a.transcriptPath(base)))
325		}
326		for _, aud := range auds {
327			base := baseName(aud)
328			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n", base)
329			count(base)
330			b.WriteString(fixerLine(a.transcriptPath(base)))
331		}
332		// Names and counts, nothing else: the per-file arithmetic is the detail
333		// beside this line -- the tooltip ON it (refresh), and the log when ▶
334		// starts (prepRun) -- and a row that spells out what each number is FOR is
335		// a paragraph wearing a row's clothes. Nobody reads it twice.
336		// no count of the files: the list of them is directly under this row, with
337		// what each one is for on its own button (srcRowKey). A row that counts
338		// what the page below it shows is a row saying nothing.
339		line = fmt.Sprintf("%d frames → %d vision · %d lines → %d fixer", frames, vision, lines, fixes)
340		return line, strings.TrimRight(b.String(), "\n")
341	}
342	
343	// inputsLabel is the line every step wears on the shared bottom bar: what the
344	// step reads, whole on hover. Ellipsized and capped so it cannot push the run
345	// bar's controls off the window.
346	func inputsLabel() *gtk.Label {
347		l := gtk.NewLabel("")
348		l.SetXAlign(0)
349		l.SetEllipsize(pango.EllipsizeEnd)
350		l.SetMaxWidthChars(60)
351		return l
352	}
353	
354	// plural is "1 clip" and "2 clips": the Inputs rows are read at a glance and
355	// "1 clip(s)" is a word nobody says out loud. Only the plural-by-s cases are
356	// on those rows, so this is the whole of the grammar needed.
357	func plural(n int, one string) string {
358		if n == 1 {
359			return fmt.Sprintf("%d %s", n, one)
360		}
361		return fmt.Sprintf("%d %ss", n, one)
362	}
363	
364	func (a *App) transcriptPath(base string) string {
365		return filepath.Join(a.inputsDir(), base, "transcript.tsv")
366	}
367	
368	func fixerLine(path string) string {
369		if !exists(path) {
370			return "  transcript.tsv: missing -- not transcribed yet\n"
371		}
372		n := len(loadSeg4(path))
373		return fmt.Sprintf("  transcript.tsv, %d lines  ->  %d fixer requests\n",
374			n, (n+fixBlock-1)/fixBlock)
375	}
376	
377	// ---- run --------------------------------------------------------------------
378	
379	// prepRun validates the sources and starts the whole step: transcripts and
380	// frames, then describing and fixing, in one press. No describe-only or
381	// fix-only run: describe resumes per chunk, and half of what the fixer is for
382	// is the events the describer just wrote.
383	func (a *App) prepRun() {
384		if a.running {
385			return
386		}
387		// one source is enough: a session can be a single screen recording that is
388		// both the footage and every voice on it, and it can equally be a recording
389		// with no footage at all
390		vids, auds := a.snapSources()
391		if len(vids)+len(auds) == 0 {
392			a.setStatus("add at least one source")
393			return
394		}
395		// two sources of the same name would write into one folder under inputs/,
396		// and the second would quietly overwrite the first's transcript
397		if x, y := a.srcList.clash(); x != "" {
398			a.logf("!!! %s and %s are both inputs/%s -- rename one", x, y, baseName(x))
399			a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("%s and %s have the same name — rename one",
400				filepath.Base(x), filepath.Base(y)))
401			return
402		}
403		// The working copy always reflects what actually ran -- and so does the
404		// named project, since saveProjectNow writes every target. It used to be
405		// saveProjectTo(project.json), which also RENAMED the open project to the
406		// working copy: running the step quietly stopped the autosave following the
407		// file you had opened, and the header bar changed under you to say so.
408		a.saveProjectNow()
409		// ⏹ then ▶ is "do it again", not "carry on" -- and this is the moment to
410		// act on that rather than the stop itself: pressing ⏹ has to be safe to do
411		// at the end of the day, with the half-run still on disk in the morning.
412		// It is the press that starts the work over that throws the work away.
413		if err := a.undFreshStart(); err != nil {
414			// nothing here is worth refusing to run over: say what could not be
415			// cleared, and let the run pick up from what is still on disk
416			a.logf(">>> could not clear the last run (%v) -- resuming it", err)
417		}
418		scaleName, scaleVF := a.frameScale()
419		a.startPrep(vids, auds, a.frameInterval(), scaleName, scaleVF)
420	}
421	
422	// undFreshStart is the difference between ⏸ and ⏹: paused resumes, stopped
423	// restarts the describing from the beginning, dropping the event logs it
424	// resumes from. Transcripts and frames are per-file on disk and untouched; the
425	// fixer never resumed anyway. Only armed by a ⏹ that had reached the
426	// describing.
427	func (a *App) undFreshStart() error {
428		if !a.undRestart {
429			return nil
430		}
431		a.undRestart = false
432		return a.resetDescribe()
433	}
434	
435	func (a *App) startPrep(videos, audios []string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF string) {
436		a.startRun()
437		a.prog(trackSTT, 0, "preparing")
438		a.logExp.SetExpanded(true)
439		// what went in, by name -- the page has room for a count and nothing more
440		a.logf(">>> prepare: %d input files", len(videos)+len(audios))
441		for _, f := range append(append([]string{}, videos...), audios...) {
442			a.logf("    %s", f)
443		}
444		if _, detail := a.inputsSummary(); detail != "" {
445			a.logf("%s", detail)
446		}
447		a.logCtx("prepare")
448		go func() {
449			described, err := a.prepare(videos, audios, interval, scaleName, scaleVF)
450			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
451				a.endRun()
452				switch {
453				case errors.Is(err, errStopped):
454					// the work stays on disk until the next ▶, which is the press
455					// that decides it was not wanted (undFreshStart) -- and only
456					// the describing is thrown away, so a stop during the
457					// transcribing arms nothing
458					a.undRestart = described
459					a.setStatus("stopped — finished work is kept")
460				case err != nil:
461					a.logf("prepare FAILED: %v", err)
462					a.setStatus("prepare failed — see log")
463				default:
464					a.progress.SetFraction(1)
465					a.logf(">>> prepare wrote:")
466					n := a.logOutputs("inputs", a.inputsDir()) +
467						a.logOutputs("describe", a.describeDir()) +
468						a.logOutputs("transcript", a.transcriptDir())
469					a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("prepared — %d files", n))
470				}
471				a.prep.refresh()
472				a.updateGates()
473				// the frames and the session timeline the Cut page draws are what
474				// this run just wrote -- including the first time, where the tab it
475				// unlocks would otherwise open on nothing
476				a.refreshCut()
477			})
478		}()
479	}
480	
481	// prepInputsShare is how much of the progress bar the first half gets. The two
482	// halves are weighted by how long they TAKE, as the tracks inside each of them
483	// are: transcribing an hour of audio and pulling a frame out of it every couple
484	// of seconds is minutes, and describing those frames is a model call per
485	// handful of them and is the longest wait in the app. A third to the front is
486	// a rule of thumb from real sessions, and being roughly right is the whole
487	// requirement -- what a progress bar owes you is a direction, not an ETA.
488	const prepInputsShare = 0.3
489	
490	// prepSepShare is the slice of that first third the voice splitting takes when
491	// there is any to do. A third of it: the separation is one model pass over the
492	// audio and the transcripts are two, over the same audio, plus every frame.
493	const prepSepShare = 0.1
494	
495	// prepare is the whole press: the transcripts and the frames, then the
496	// describing and the fixing. It reports whether the second half had begun,
497	// which is what a ⏹ needs to know -- that is the half a restart throws away.
498	//
499	// Neither half knows the other exists: each still divides its own work into two
500	// tracks that add up to a whole bar. qPhase is what puts each of them in its
501	// own slice of it, so the needle crosses the middle once and never goes back.
502	func (a *App) prepare(videos, audios []string, interval float64, scaleName, scaleVF string) (bool, error) {
503		// the models are the server's to load, but that it HAS them is worth
504		// finding out now rather than after the frame extraction -- and before the
505		// separation too, since that is the phase this step now opens with and the
506		// one asking for the model a server is least likely to have.
507		sep := len(a.sepWanted()) > 0
508		if err := a.ensureAudioModels(sep); err != nil {
509			return false, err
510		}
511		// the splitting goes first, because it changes what the rest of this is OF:
512		// a recording being split is not the file the frames come out of or the
513		// transcript is of -- the two files it becomes are. With nothing flagged
514		// this phase costs nothing and the two below are the two there always were.
515		sepAt := 0.0
516		if sep {
517			a.qPhase(0, prepSepShare)
518			var err error
519			if videos, audios, err = a.separateVoices(videos, audios); err != nil {
520				return false, err
521			}
522			sepAt = prepSepShare
523		}
524		a.qPhase(sepAt, prepInputsShare-sepAt)
525		if err := a.ingest(videos, audios, interval, scaleName, scaleVF); err != nil {
526			return false, err
527		}
528		a.qPhase(prepInputsShare, 1-prepInputsShare)
529		return true, a.understand(videos, audios)
530	}
531	
532	func (a *App) understand(videos, audios []string) error {
533		// Every style is described, Lecture included. Its CUT does not need the
534		// picture -- the words are the video (textedit.go) -- and this step used
535		// to skip it on that ground, which was half the story: Publish picks the
536		// thumbnail by what is ON a frame, and a frame nobody described is a
537		// frame nothing can find. A lecture's title slide is the thumbnail.
538		//
539		// two jobs, one after the other, and the bar says which of the two it is
540		// on: this page's ▶ is the longest press in the app, and "1/2" is the
541		// difference between halfway through and nearly done.
542		a.qJob(trackDescribe, "describe", 1, 2)
543		if err := a.describeAll(videos, audios, 0.5); err != nil {
544			return err
545		}
546		a.qJob(trackFix, "transcript", 2, 2)
547		return a.fixTranscripts(videos, audios, 0.5)
548	}
549	
550	// openAtHalf opens a pane's handle at the middle of the window (unset, a
551	// GtkPaned gives each child what its widest content wants). It waits for the
552	// widget to be measured; Map fires on every show, hence the once guard, and
553	// after the first placement the handle is the user's.
554	func openAtHalf(p *gtk.Paned) {
555		split := false
556		p.ConnectMap(func() {
557			if split {
558				return
559			}
560			split = true
561			glib.IdleAdd(func() { p.SetPosition(p.AllocatedWidth() / 2) })
562		})
563	}
564	
565	// videoStyleName is the style, callable from a runner's goroutine.
566	//
567	// A cached string and not the dropdown, for the same reason sessionCtx and
568	// asrLanguage are: the widget belongs to the GUI thread, and this is read by
569	// findMarks in the middle of Prepare -- which is a runner. It used to read
570	// stylePick.Selected() directly, a GTK call off the main thread that happened
571	// to work. The dropdown writes the cache on every change (prep.go) and the
572	// project writes it on load (applyStyle), so the two never disagree.
573	func (a *App) videoStyleName() string {
574		a.promptMu.Lock()
575		defer a.promptMu.Unlock()
576		return a.videoStyle
577	}
578	
579	func (a *App) setVideoStyle(name string) {
580		a.promptMu.Lock()
581		a.videoStyle = name
582		a.promptMu.Unlock()
583	}
584	
585	// applyStyle is the project's answer, put on the page without saving it back.
586	func (a *App) applyStyle(name string) {
587		a.setVideoStyle(name)
588		if a.stylePick == nil {
589			return
590		}
591		a.styleQuiet = true
592		a.stylePick.SetSelected(styleIndex(name))
593		a.styleQuiet = false
594	}

10	// queries. A search is THREE queries, broad to narrow, answered with the

15	import (
16		"context"
17		"encoding/json"
18		"errors"

33	const (
34		searchHits      = 8                // results handed back per query
35		searchPageChars = 6000             // of a page's text; enough for a fact, not an article
36		searchRender    = 15 * time.Second // how long a result page may take to draw its anchors
37		searchTimeout   = 45 * time.Second // the whole of one tool call
38		searchBoot      = 15 * time.Second // firefox's port coming up
39	)
40	
41	// firefoxOff is what the settings box says when the tools are not wanted.
42	const firefoxOff = "off"
43	
44	// firefoxBin resolves the settings box to a binary: the path it names, or the
45	// firefox on PATH, or the usual places. "" with an error means there is none,
46	// and the tools are simply not offered -- a model that cannot search writes
47	// only what the material shows, which is the rule anyway.
48	func firefoxBin(conf string) (string, error) {
49		conf = strings.TrimSpace(conf)
50		if strings.EqualFold(conf, firefoxOff) {
51			return "", errors.New("web search is off")
52		}
53		if conf != "" {
54			if _, err := os.Stat(conf); err != nil {
55				return "", fmt.Errorf("firefox: %w", err)
56			}
57			return conf, nil
58		}
59		for _, n := range []string{"firefox", "firefox-esr", "firefox-bin"} {
60			if p, err := exec.LookPath(n); err == nil {
61				return p, nil
62			}
63		}
64		for _, p := range []string{"/usr/bin/firefox", "/usr/bin/firefox-esr", "/snap/bin/firefox",
65			"/Applications/Firefox.app/Contents/MacOS/firefox"} {
66			if _, err := os.Stat(p); err == nil {
67				return p, nil
68			}
69		}
70		return "", errors.New("no firefox found -- name one in the settings, or set it to off")
71	}
72	
73	// webHit is one search result as the model reads it.
74	type webHit struct {
75		Title, URL, Snippet string
76	}
77	
78	// ---- the browser ------------------------------------------------------------
79	
80	// browser is one headless Firefox and the WebSocket it is driven over. One per
81	// tool call, closed when the call is answered: a browser kept warm between
82	// calls is a process to leak, and a search is seconds anyway.
83	type browser struct {
84		cmd     *exec.Cmd
85		conn    *websocket.Conn
86		profile string
87		tab     string // the one browsing context, from browsingContext.getTree
88	
89		mu      sync.Mutex
90		pending map[int64]chan json.RawMessage
91		next    atomic.Int64
92		done    chan struct{}
93	}
94	
95	// ports are handed out in turn so two calls in flight -- the narration and a
96	// retry of the cut, say -- do not fight over one debugging port.
97	var browserPort atomic.Int64
98	
99	func init() { browserPort.Store(9222) }
100	
101	// startBrowser launches firefox on a fresh profile, waits for its debugging
102	// port, opens the BiDi session and finds the tab. The first page is navigated
103	// to afterwards rather than passed on the command line, because a URL on the
104	// command line gives no signal for when it has loaded.
105	func (a *App) startBrowser(ctx context.Context, bin string) (*browser, error) {
106		profile, err := os.MkdirTemp("", "naivepost-firefox-*")
107		if err != nil {
108			return nil, err
109		}
110		port := browserPort.Add(1)
111		cmd := exec.Command(bin, "-headless", "--private-window", "--no-remote", "--new-instance",
112			"--profile", profile, fmt.Sprintf("--remote-debugging-port=%d", port), "about:blank")
113		cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "MOZ_HEADLESS=1")
114		cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = io.Discard, io.Discard
115		b := &browser{cmd: cmd, profile: profile, pending: map[int64]chan json.RawMessage{}, done: make(chan struct{})}
116		// on the roll ⏹ kills, like ffmpeg (runCmd)
117		a.ctlMu.Lock()
118		a.curCmds[cmd] = true
119		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
120		if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
121			b.close(a)
122			return nil, fmt.Errorf("start firefox: %w", err)
123		}
124		addr := fmt.Sprintf("127.0.0.1:%d", port)
125		up := false
126		for t0 := time.Now(); time.Since(t0) < searchBoot; {
127			if c, err := net.DialTimeout("tcp", addr, 500*time.Millisecond); err == nil {
128				c.Close()
129				up = true
130				break
131			}
132			select {
133			case <-ctx.Done():
134				b.close(a)
135				return nil, ctx.Err()
136			case <-time.After(300 * time.Millisecond):
137			}
138		}
139		if !up {
140			b.close(a)
141			return nil, fmt.Errorf("firefox did not open port %d within %s", port, searchBoot)
142		}
143		conn, _, err := websocket.Dial(ctx, "ws://"+addr+"/session", nil)
144		if err != nil {
145			b.close(a)
146			return nil, fmt.Errorf("firefox bidi: %w", err)
147		}
148		conn.SetReadLimit(16 << 20)
149		b.conn = conn
150		go b.readLoop()
151		if _, err := b.send(ctx, "session.new", map[string]any{"capabilities": map[string]any{}}); err != nil {
152			b.close(a)
153			return nil, err
154		}
155		tree, err := b.send(ctx, "browsingContext.getTree", map[string]any{})
156		if err != nil {
157			b.close(a)
158			return nil, err
159		}
160		var got struct {
161			Contexts []struct {
162				Context string `json:"context"`
163			} `json:"contexts"`
164		}
165		if json.Unmarshal(tree, &got) != nil || len(got.Contexts) == 0 {
166			b.close(a)
167			return nil, errors.New("firefox bidi: no browsing context")
168		}
169		b.tab = got.Contexts[0].Context
170		return b, nil
171	}
172	
173	// readLoop hands every answer to the call waiting for it. Events -- messages
174	// with no id -- are nobody's and are dropped.
175	func (b *browser) readLoop() {
176		defer close(b.done)
177		for {
178			_, data, err := b.conn.Read(context.Background())
179			if err != nil {
180				b.mu.Lock()
181				for id, ch := range b.pending {
182					close(ch)
183					delete(b.pending, id)
184				}
185				b.mu.Unlock()
186				return
187			}
188			var r struct {
189				ID     int64           `json:"id"`
190				Type   string          `json:"type"`
191				Result json.RawMessage `json:"result"`
192				Error  string          `json:"error"`
193				Msg    string          `json:"message"`
194			}
195			if json.Unmarshal(data, &r) != nil || r.ID == 0 {
196				continue
197			}
198			b.mu.Lock()
199			ch := b.pending[r.ID]
200			delete(b.pending, r.ID)
201			b.mu.Unlock()
202			if ch == nil {
203				continue
204			}
205			if r.Type == "error" {
206				e, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]string{"bidiError": r.Error + ": " + r.Msg})
207				ch <- e
208			} else {
209				ch <- r.Result
210			}
211		}
212	}
213	
214	// send is one BiDi command and its answer.
215	func (b *browser) send(ctx context.Context, method string, params any) (json.RawMessage, error) {
216		id := b.next.Add(1)
217		ch := make(chan json.RawMessage, 1)
218		b.mu.Lock()
219		b.pending[id] = ch
220		b.mu.Unlock()
221		req, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"id": id, "method": method, "params": params})
222		if err := b.conn.Write(ctx, websocket.MessageText, req); err != nil {
223			return nil, err
224		}
225		select {
226		case <-ctx.Done():
227			return nil, ctx.Err()
228		case res, ok := <-ch:
229			if !ok {
230				return nil, errors.New("firefox closed the connection")
231			}
232			var e struct {
233				Err string `json:"bidiError"`
234			}
235			if json.Unmarshal(res, &e) == nil && e.Err != "" {
236				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", method, e.Err)
237			}
238			return res, nil
239		}
240	}

242	// navigate loads a page and waits for it to finish -- or for the deadline,
243	// after which whatever has arrived is what gets read.
244	func (b *browser) navigate(ctx context.Context, u string) error {
245		_, err := b.send(ctx, "browsingContext.navigate",
246			map[string]any{"context": b.tab, "url": u, "wait": "complete"})
247		return err
248	}
249	
250	// eval runs a script in the page and returns its string result.
251	func (b *browser) eval(ctx context.Context, js string) (string, error) {
252		res, err := b.send(ctx, "script.evaluate", map[string]any{
253			"expression": js, "target": map[string]any{"context": b.tab}, "awaitPromise": false})
254		if err != nil {
255			return "", err
256		}
257		var out struct {
258			Result struct {
259				Value string `json:"value"`
260			} `json:"result"`
261		}
262		if err := json.Unmarshal(res, &out); err != nil {
263			return "", err
264		}
265		return out.Result.Value, nil
266	}
267	
268	// close ends the browser and forgets the profile. Kill rather than a polite
269	// quit: it is a private window on a throwaway profile, and nothing in it is
270	// worth the seconds a shutdown takes.
271	func (b *browser) close(a *App) {
272		if b.conn != nil {
273			b.conn.CloseNow()
274		}
275		if b.cmd.Process != nil {
276			b.cmd.Process.Kill()
277			b.cmd.Wait()
278		}
279		a.ctlMu.Lock()
280		delete(a.curCmds, b.cmd)
281		a.ctlMu.Unlock()
282		os.RemoveAll(b.profile)
283	}

285	// ---- the two things it does -------------------------------------------------
286	
287	// ddgExtract reads the result anchors off a rendered DuckDuckGo page. The
288	// page repeats an anchor in its carousels, so the reader dedupes by URL.
289	const ddgExtract = `JSON.stringify(Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a[data-testid="result-title-a"]')).map(a => {
290	  const root = a.closest('article') || a.closest('[data-testid="result"]') || a.parentElement;
291	  const snip = root && (root.querySelector('[data-result="snippet"]') || root.querySelector('span[data-testid="result-snippet"]') || root.querySelector('.result__snippet'));
292	  return {title: (a.innerText || "").trim(), url: a.href, snippet: snip ? (snip.innerText || "").trim() : ""};
293	}).filter(r => r.url.startsWith('http')))`
294	
295	// webSearch is one query on a browser of its own: the settings dialog's
296	// Test. A job's searches share one (runWebTool), since a ladder is up to
297	// three and a browser takes seconds to come up.
298	func (a *App) webSearch(ctx context.Context, bin, query string) ([]webHit, error) {
299		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, searchTimeout)
300		defer cancel()
301		b, err := a.startBrowser(ctx, bin)
302		if err != nil {
303			return nil, err
304		}
305		defer b.close(a)
306		return b.search(ctx, query)
307	}
308	
309	// search is one query on this browser: the result page, the anchors off it.
310	func (b *browser) search(ctx context.Context, query string) ([]webHit, error) {
311		nav, cancelNav := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 10*time.Second)
312		b.navigate(nav, "https://duckduckgo.com/?q="+url.QueryEscape(query)) // a slow page is read as it stands
313		cancelNav()
314		var hits []webHit
315		for t0 := time.Now(); time.Since(t0) < searchRender; {
316			raw, err := b.eval(ctx, ddgExtract)
317			if err != nil {
318				return nil, err
319			}
320			var got []struct{ Title, URL, Snippet string }
321			if json.Unmarshal([]byte(raw), &got) == nil && len(got) > 0 {
322				seen := map[string]bool{}
323				for _, g := range got {
324					if seen[g.URL] {
325						continue
326					}
327					seen[g.URL] = true
328					hits = append(hits, webHit{Title: g.Title, URL: g.URL, Snippet: g.Snippet})
329					if len(hits) == searchHits {
330						break
331					}
332				}
333				break
334			}
335			select {
336			case <-ctx.Done():
337				return nil, ctx.Err()
338			case <-time.After(500 * time.Millisecond):
339			}
340		}
341		return hits, nil
342	}
343	
344	// webRead is one page's text, as a reader would see it, cut to what a fact
345	// needs. A wall -- a captcha, a "verify you are human" -- is reported as one
346	// rather than handed to the model as the page.
347	func (a *App) webRead(ctx context.Context, bin, u string) (string, error) {
348		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, searchTimeout)
349		defer cancel()
350		b, err := a.startBrowser(ctx, bin)
351		if err != nil {
352			return "", err
353		}
354		defer b.close(a)
355		nav, cancelNav := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 15*time.Second)
356		b.navigate(nav, u)
357		cancelNav()
358		text, err := b.eval(ctx, "document.body ? document.body.innerText : ''")
359		if err != nil {
360			return "", err
361		}
362		if issue := pageIssue(text); issue != "" {
363			return "", errors.New(issue)
364		}
365		return clipRunes(strings.TrimSpace(text), searchPageChars), nil
366	}
367	
368	// botWalls is what a page says instead of its content when it would rather
369	// not be read by a program.
370	var botWalls = []string{"just a moment", "checking your browser", "verify you are human",
371		"verifying you are human", "are you human", "press and hold", "please enable javascript and cookies",
372		"attention required", "access denied", "403 forbidden", "too many requests"}
373	
374	func pageIssue(text string) string {
375		t := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(text))
376		if t == "" {
377			return "the page had no text"
378		}
379		for _, w := range botWalls {
380			if strings.Contains(t, w) {
381				return "the page is behind a bot wall (" + w + ")"
382			}
383		}
384		if len(t) < 200 {
385			return "the page had almost no text (blocked, or not loaded)"
386		}
387		return ""
388	}
389	
390	func clipRunes(s string, n int) string {
391		if len(s) <= n {
392			return s
393		}
394		c := s[:n]
395		for len(c) > 0 && !isRuneStart(c[len(c)-1]) {
396			c = c[:len(c)-1]
397		}
398		return c + " …"
399	}
400	
401	func isRuneStart(b byte) bool { return b&0xC0 != 0x80 }
402	
403	// ---- the ladder -------------------------------------------------------------
404	
405	// searcher is webSearch with the browser chosen, so the ladder can be tested
406	// against a table rather than a Firefox.
407	type searcher func(ctx context.Context, query string) ([]webHit, error)
408	
409	// searchLadder runs the three queries from the broadest and keeps climbing
410	// while the web still answers: the narrowest query with results is the one
411	// whose results are about the thing asked for. A narrower query that finds
412	// nothing is a name the web does not know in that spelling, and the step
413	// below it is the answer. Nothing at any step is reported as nothing.
414	func searchLadder(ctx context.Context, search searcher, broad, medium, narrow string) (string, []webHit, error) {
415		var bestQ string
416		var best []webHit
417		var lastErr error
418		for _, q := range []string{broad, medium, narrow} {
419			q = strings.TrimSpace(q)
420			if q == "" {
421				continue
422			}
423			hits, err := search(ctx, q)
424			if err != nil {
425				lastErr = err
426				if ctx.Err() != nil {
427					return bestQ, best, err
428				}
429				continue
430			}
431			if len(hits) == 0 {
432				if best != nil {
433					break // the web stopped answering: the step below is the answer
434				}
435				continue
436			}
437			bestQ, best = q, hits
438		}
439		if best == nil && lastErr != nil {
440			return "", nil, lastErr
441		}
442		return bestQ, best, nil
443	}
444	
445	// formatHits is what the model reads back: numbered, the URL on its own line
446	// so a web_read can quote it exactly.
447	func formatHits(query string, hits []webHit) string {
448		if len(hits) == 0 {
449			return "No results for any of the three queries."
450		}
451		var b strings.Builder
452		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Results for %q:\n", query)
453		for i, h := range hits {
454			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%d. %s\n   %s\n", i+1, h.Title, h.URL)
455			if h.Snippet != "" {
456				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "   %s\n", h.Snippet)
457			}
458		}
459		return b.String()
460	}
461	
462	// ---- as the model sees it ---------------------------------------------------
463	
464	// webTools is the two tools in the shape the chat API takes. The descriptions
465	// are the instructions: when to reach for one, and that the three queries are
466	// one call.
467	func webTools() []map[string]any {
468		return []map[string]any{
469			{"type": "function", "function": map[string]any{
470				"name":        "web_search",
471				"description": "Look up a fact you are about to write into the video and would otherwise guess: what a named thing is, does or costs, a name's spelling, a number. Only for something the material does not contain, and only when the user context asks for a detail you do not have -- not to understand the session, not to check what you have already been told. Give three queries at once, from broad to narrow -- the game, the game and the thing, the thing's exact name -- and you get the narrowest one that found anything.",
472				"parameters": map[string]any{"type": "object", "properties": map[string]any{
473					"broad":  map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": "the general subject, e.g. the game"},
474					"medium": map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": "the subject and the thing"},
475					"narrow": map[string]any{"type": "string", "description": "the thing's exact name, as the user context spells it"},
476				}, "required": []string{"broad", "medium", "narrow"}}}},
477			{"type": "function", "function": map[string]any{
478				"name":        "web_read",
479				"description": "Read one page from a web_search result, by its URL, when the snippet did not say enough. Returns the page's text, shortened.",
480				"parameters": map[string]any{"type": "object", "properties": map[string]any{
481					"url": map[string]any{"type": "string"}}, "required": []string{"url"}}}},
482		}
483	}
484	
485	// webToolsFor is what a job is offered: the two tools when a firefox is at
486	// hand and the settings do not say off, nothing otherwise -- and the reason,
487	// once, in the log, so a run with no searches in it says why.
488	func (a *App) webToolsFor(step string) ([]map[string]any, string) {
489		// a sandbox has no host browser to launch; the model writes only what the
490		// material shows, which is the rule anyway
491		if inFlatpak() {
492			a.logfIdle(">>> %s: no web search inside Flatpak", step)
493			return nil, ""
494		}
495		bin, err := firefoxBin(a.readConf().Firefox)
496		if err != nil {
497			a.logfIdle(">>> %s: no web search (%v)", step, err)
498			return nil, ""
499		}
500		return webTools(), bin
501	}
502	
503	// webRunner is the tool runner a job hands the chat loop: one browser per
504	// call, on the run's own context so ⏹ ends a search with the run.
505	func (a *App) webRunner(step, bin string) toolRunner {
506		return func(name string, args json.RawMessage) string {
507			ctx := a.runCtx
508			if ctx == nil {
509				ctx = context.Background()
510			}
511			return a.runWebTool(ctx, bin, step, name, args)
512		}
513	}
514	
515	// runWebTool answers one call. Errors go back to the model as text: a tool
516	// that failed is something it can work around by writing less, and an error
517	// that ended the whole job would be a caption's worth of fact costing a cut.
518	func (a *App) runWebTool(ctx context.Context, bin, step, name string, args json.RawMessage) string {
519		switch name {
520		case "web_search":
521			var q struct{ Broad, Medium, Narrow string }
522			if err := json.Unmarshal(args, &q); err != nil {
523				return "web_search: could not read the arguments: " + err.Error()
524			}
525			ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, searchTimeout)
526			defer cancel()
527			b, err := a.startBrowser(ctx, bin)
528			if err != nil {
529				a.logfIdle("!!! %s: web search failed: %v", step, err)
530				return "web_search failed: " + err.Error()
531			}
532			defer b.close(a)
533			used, hits, err := searchLadder(ctx, b.search, q.Broad, q.Medium, q.Narrow)
534			if err != nil {
535				a.logfIdle("!!! %s: web search failed: %v", step, err)
536				return "web_search failed: " + err.Error()
537			}
538			a.logfIdle(">>> %s: searched %q / %q / %q -- %d result(s) for %q", step, q.Broad, q.Medium, q.Narrow, len(hits), used)
539			return formatHits(used, hits)
540		case "web_read":
541			var p struct{ URL string }
542			if err := json.Unmarshal(args, &p); err != nil || strings.TrimSpace(p.URL) == "" {
543				return "web_read: no url given"
544			}
545			text, err := a.webRead(ctx, bin, p.URL)
546			if err != nil {
547				a.logfIdle("!!! %s: could not read %s: %v", step, p.URL, err)
548				return "web_read failed: " + err.Error()
549			}
550			a.logfIdle(">>> %s: read %s (%d characters)", step, p.URL, len(text))
551			return text
552		}
553		return "unknown tool " + name
554	}

32	// one silently drops what a user wrote under the old name.

85	func (a *App) prompt(key string) string {

95	// setPrompt records what is in the box. Kept per machine and written to disk

98	func (a *App) setPrompt(key, text string) {

112	func (a *App) promptOwned(key string) bool {

115		a.promptMu.Unlock()

121	func (a *App) resetPrompt(key string) {

124		a.promptMu.Unlock()
125		a.showPrompt(key)

135	func (a *App) showPrompt(key string) {

255		// vexpand is what makes a taller window a taller box. Without it the box
256		// stops at the height of its text and the window's extra height piles up as
257		// blank page below it -- growing the window then bought nothing on the one
258		// page whose whole content is text. It propagates up through what this
259		// returns, so a page only has to put the box somewhere that can grow.

268		body := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationVertical, 4)

270		body.Append(head)
271		body.Append(scroll)

217		if err != nil {
218			return 0, 0, false
219		}
220		rest := strings.TrimSuffix(base[loc[1]:], filepath.Ext(base))
221		if rest == "" {
222			return t, 0, true
223		}
224		n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimPrefix(rest, "-"))
225		if err != nil || !strings.HasPrefix(rest, "-") {
226			return 0, 0, false
227		}
228		return t, n, true
229	}

231	// sortStamped puts timestamped output files back in the order they were made.
232	func sortStamped(paths []string) {
233		sort.Slice(paths, func(i, j int) bool {
234			as, an, aok := readStamp(paths[i])
235			bs, bn, bok := readStamp(paths[j])
236			switch {
237			case !aok || !bok:
238				return paths[i] < paths[j]
239			case as != bs:
240				return as < bs
241			default:
242				return an < bn
243			}
244		})
245	}
246	
247	// srcClock puts sources on one wall clock and says where second nought falls.
248	// A file that NAMES a moment is placed at it. One that does not goes at the
249	// session's start -- not its mtime, which is when it was copied or exported --
250	// where the right drag can line it up by ear (cut_shift.go). Nothing named:
251	// all start together at 0:00. This is the only door for lanes, transcript,
252	// describe, frame names and render, and it is handed the WHOLE session, since
253	// a shorter list can put zero elsewhere. Names only, no stat or ffprobe.
254	func srcClock(paths []string) (map[string]float64, float64) {
255		at := make(map[string]float64, len(paths))
256		zero := math.Inf(1)
257		for _, p := range paths {
258			if t, ok := nameStamp(filepath.Base(p)); ok {
259				at[p], zero = t, math.Min(zero, t)
260			}
261		}
262		if math.IsInf(zero, 1) {
263			zero = 0 // nothing named a moment: the session starts at 0:00
264		}
265		for _, p := range paths {
266			if _, ok := at[p]; !ok {
267				at[p] = zero
268			}
269		}
270		return at, zero
271	}

273	// sourceStart is where one file sits on that same clock, for the steps that
274	// hold a path and not the list. It IS srcClock, asked about the whole session
275	// with this file in it -- so a file the session does not contain, a sting on a
276	// cut lane say, is placed by the same rule as one it does.
277	func (a *App) sourceStart(path string) float64 {
278		vids, auds := a.snappedSources()
279		all := append(append(append([]string{}, vids...), auds...), path)
280		at, _ := srcClock(all)
281		return at[path]
282	}

429		// recording each line came off. session.txt is the readable one, and it is

431		// so what you read is what it reads.
432		var stv strings.Builder
433		var tl []tsvRow

436			tl = append(tl, tsvRow{s: r.g, e: r.ge, src: r.src, spk: r.spk, text: r.text})

450			}

454		}

459			return err

463	}

474	// fixRows runs one source's lines through the LLM in blocks. Validation is
475	// strict: same line count, byte-identical start/end/speaker; a block failing
476	// twice keeps its original lines, loudly.
477	func (a *App) fixRows(s *src, ctxFor func(*src, float64, float64) string,
478		done *int, total int, span float64) ([]seg4, error) {
479		cached := 0
480	
481		system := a.sysPrompt("fix")
482		var out []seg4
483		nblocks := (len(s.rows) + fixBlock - 1) / fixBlock
484		for b := 0; b < nblocks; b++ {
485			if err := a.checkpoint(); err != nil {
486				return nil, err
487			}
488			a.qTake(trackFix)
489			a.prog(trackFix, span*float64(*done)/float64(total), "")
490			*done++
491	
492			lo := b * fixBlock
493			hi := min(lo+fixBlock, len(s.rows))
494			blk := s.rows[lo:hi]
495			var lines []string
496			for _, r := range blk {
497				lines = append(lines, fmt.Sprintf("%.2f\t%.2f\t%s\t%s", r.s, r.e, r.spk, r.text))
498			}
499			user := a.ctxBlockFor("fix") + fmt.Sprintf(`Context around these lines:
500	%s
501	Transcript lines to clean (%d lines, return exactly %d):
502	%s`, ctxFor(s, blk[0].s, blk[len(blk)-1].e), len(blk), len(blk), strings.Join(lines, "\n"))
503	
504			ok := false
505			for try := 0; try < 2 && !ok; try++ {
506				// the same block, the same context, the same wording: the same
507				// answer (llmcache.go). Only the first attempt is cached -- a
508				// second attempt is asked BECAUSE the first came back unusable, and
509				// serving it from the file would repeat the failure for ever.
510				ask := ""
511				var reply string
512				if try == 0 {
513					ask = askKey(system, user)
514					if r, hit := a.cachedReply("transcript", ask); hit {
515						reply, cached = r, cached+1
516					}
517				}
518				var err error
519				if reply == "" {
520					reply, err = a.llmChatRetry("transcript", []map[string]any{
521						msg("system", system), msg("user", user),
522					}, false)
523				}
524				if err != nil {
525					if errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
526						return nil, errStopped
527					}
528					return nil, fmt.Errorf("fix %s block %d: %w", s.base, b+1, err)
529				}
530				var got []seg4
531				for _, l := range strings.Split(reply, "\n") {
532					f := strings.Split(l, "\t")
533					if len(f) < 4 {
534						continue
535					}
536					var r seg4
537					fmt.Sscanf(f[0], "%f", &r.s)
538					fmt.Sscanf(f[1], "%f", &r.e)
539					r.spk = f[2]
540					r.text = strings.Join(f[3:], " ")
541					got = append(got, r)
542				}
543				if len(got) == len(blk) {
544					match := true
545					for i := range got {
546						if math.Abs(got[i].s-blk[i].s) > 0.01 || math.Abs(got[i].e-blk[i].e) > 0.01 ||
547							got[i].spk != blk[i].spk {
548							match = false
549							break
550						}
551					}
552					if match {
553						// kept only when it passed: a block whose answer was
554						// refused is one the next run has to ask about again
555						if ask != "" {
556							a.keepReply("transcript", ask, reply)
557						}
558						out = append(out, got...)
559						ok = true
560					}
561				}
562			}
563			if !ok {
564				a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] block %d/%d failed validation, keeping original lines", s.base, b+1, nblocks)
565				out = append(out, blk...)
566			}
567		}
568		if cached > 0 {
569			a.logfIdle(">>> [%s] %d block(s) answered from the cache", s.base, cached)
570		}
571		return out, nil
572	}
573	
574	// findMarks is the pass that says which seconds go, by style: a read to camera
575	// is edited as text (textedit.go), a session has its retakes found (retake.go).
576	func (a *App) findMarks(tl []tsvRow) ([]retake, error) {
577		if a.videoStyleName() == styleRead {
578			return a.findTextEdit(tl)
579		}
580		return a.findRetakes(tl)

package main

// The thumbnail half of Produce: a picture and the words under it.
//
// The picture is an EDIT of real frames through sd.cpp's native API (sdcpp.go):
// ref_images keep it recognizably this video, and an edit model changes only
// what the instruction names (img2img renoised everything). The row of images
// is the user's; the first is the base, the rest are references named by
// position; an empty row draws from the instruction alone. No words come from
// the model: the title and marked texts are printed locally (publish_text.go),
// and the instruction asks for no lettering. One model job writes the title,
// the edit instruction and the description in one reply (prompt on Prepare).
//
// publish/thumbnail.png        the upload: the picture with the words printed on
// publish/thumbnail-plain.png  the picture as drawn, no words -- what re-prints start from
// publish/description.txt      the YouTube description
// publish/publish.json         all of it as data

// ---- the prompts --------------------------------------------------------------

// One paragraph or bullet per line, unwrapped: see describeSystem.

const youtubeSystem = `You write the upload text for a finished video on YouTube: its title, and the description that sits under it.

You are given what the video is made of -- its clips, what was seen and said in each, and the narration that was written over it. That is the video.

What the user context singles out is what the description should lead with. Answer in the upload text's shape.

The title.

- Four to seven words. It is the YouTube title, and it is also printed across the upper part of the thumbnail afterwards, read at the size of a phone's sidebar -- every extra word costs one that mattered.
- Say the specific thing that happens in THIS video: the moment, the mistake, the win, the thing nobody expected. A title that would fit any session like it is a wasted title.
- Plain words people say out loud. No colons splitting a subtitle off, no clickbait punctuation, no ALL CAPS -- it is drawn in large letters already.
- Never promise something the clips do not contain: a title is a claim about the video, and this one is the claim most people will only ever read.

The thumbnail.

There are two ways to answer for it, and the user context decides which.

- Where the context asks for a picture the video ALREADY CONTAINS -- a slide, a title card, a particular moment, anything phrased as "use the frame that shows ...", "pick one", "do not generate" -- the thumbnail line is a frame line: answer it as "THUMBNAIL: frame: clip <n> +<seconds>", naming the clip whose block that picture is described in and the offset stamped on the EVENT line that describes it -- both copied off the brief, neither worked out -- and write no instruction anywhere. The editor takes that frame as it is and prints the title onto it. This is the better answer whenever the context offers it: a frame out of the video cannot promise something the video does not contain.
- Otherwise the thumbnail line is the instruction below, and no second is named.

The thumbnail instruction.

- One or two sentences telling the image model how to compose ONE picture out of the frames: what this video is about, and the moment it shows.
- It is an instruction, not a description. Anything you do not mention is left alone, so describing the whole scene gets a picture of something else instead of the moment that was filmed. Say what to combine, brighten, push forward, or clear out of the way.
- Name only things the clips contain. "Add the dragon" to a video with no dragon in it is a thumbnail that lies about the video.

The description.

- Open with one or two sentences that say what happens in this video, in plain language, and make someone want to watch it. This first line is the only part shown before "...more", so it has to work alone.
- Then a short paragraph, three or four sentences, on what the session actually was: where it is set, who is in it, what went right and wrong.
- Then a chapter list if the video has distinct beats -- one line per beat, "0:00 What this is", at the time the clip list gives for that clip ("at 1:23 in the video"), never a session time. Only if the beats are real; a made-up timestamp is worse than no chapter list.
- Finish with a line of five to eight hashtags, lower case, naming what this is, where it is set and the kind of moment. No hashtag salad.

Voice.

- The voice of someone who was there and is telling a friend about it, not a press release. Contractions are fine.
- No emoji walls, no "smash that like button", no promises about upload schedules, no links to things you were not told exist.`

// cropRect is the crop box this project asks for on a base image of aspect
// srcA, for a thumbnail of aspect outA. Everything about its size comes from
// the two aspects; only the centre is the user's.
func (st pubSettings) cropRect(srcA, outA float64) fxRect {
	cx, cy := 0.5, 0.5
	if st.Crop != nil {
		cx, cy = st.Crop.X, st.Crop.Y
	}
	return pubCropAt(srcA, outA, cx, cy)

	return st.Frames[0]
}
