318	// seamCutOf turns the joined text back into how much comes off each side, or
319	// says why it cannot be used. at is the index, within win, of the first word of
320	// AFTER.
321	//
322	// The match is against WHAT WAS PRINTED, and that is the whole of the lesson
323	// here. The model reads seamWords: the spelling the transcript pass settled on.
324	// The words themselves carry a second spelling, the bare one the aligner heard,
325	// and for a while the answer was matched against that instead. They are not the
326	// same: the transcript folds a heard "das über datum" into a written "das
327	// Über-Datum.", and one German lecture had sixty-four words folded that way.
328	// Every fold looked to the match like a word the model had deliberately
329	// dropped, so every answer read as several separate stretches and was refused
330	// whole -- twenty-nine joins of a session, nought marks, while the very same
331	// answers matched against the printed forms give ten clean cuts with not one
332	// invented word between them.
333	//
334	// So the answer can only take words away, and what it may take words away from
335	// is exactly the text it was shown.
336	func seamCutOf(win []srcWord, at int, joined string) (seamCut, string) {
337		toks, owner := shownTokens(win)
338		ans := textTokens(joined)
339		if len(ans) == 0 {
340			return seamCut{}, "the answer has no words in it"
341		}
342		// keepMask walks the answer backwards against the words, which is what
343		// prefers the LATER of two sayings -- the rule the whole pass runs on
344		shown := make([]srcWord, len(toks))
345		for i, t := range toks {
346			shown[i].w = t
347		}
348		keptTok, _ := keepMask(shown, ans)
349		// a word survives if any of what was printed for it did: the transcript
350		// spells some single words as two, and half a spelling is not a deletion
351		kept := make([]bool, len(win))
352		for i, ok := range keptTok {
353			if ok {
354				kept[owner[i]] = true
355			}
356		}
357		// what it left out, stretch by stretch. There should be exactly one and it
358		// should be at the join; a second one somewhere else is the model editing
359		// prose, and the whole answer is refused over it.
360		//
361		// Except where that second one is a word or two, which is usually not a
362		// deletion at all. The model respells as it writes -- "Ein interessantes
363		// Gebiet" for a transcript that reads "Ein Interessensgebiet" -- and a word
364		// it spelled its own way matches nothing and reads here exactly as if it
365		// had been removed on purpose. Measured over two runs of a 42-minute
366		// lecture: taking those as respellings rather than removals turns four
367		// refusals into two and five into two, and gets one more join exactly right
368		// each time. It was the only change of several that held up across both.
369		first, last, other := -1, -1, 0
370		for i := 0; i < len(win); {
371			if kept[i] {
372				i++
373				continue
374			}
375			j := i
376			for j < len(win) && !kept[j] {
377				j++
378			}
379			switch {
380			case i <= at+seamSnap && j-1 >= at-1-seamSnap:
381				first, last = i, j-1 // the one at the join, which is the repair
382			case j-i > seamNoise:
383				other++
384			}
385			i = j
386		}
387		switch {
388		case first < 0 && other == 0:
389			return seamCut{}, "" // nothing left out, which is a whole answer
390		case first < 0:
391			return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("the %s left out is not at the join",
392				plural(other, "stretch"))
393		case other > 0:
394			return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("%d separate stretches left out, not one at the join", other+1)
395		}
396		// ...and the stretch has to be AT the join, which is what tells a repair
397		// apart from the model editing prose: a hole in the middle of BEFORE is the
398		// removal that takes the object out of a sentence, leaving something that
399		// parses and means nothing.
400		//
401		// Coming within a word or two of the join counts as being at it, and the
402		// rest of the way is closed here. A model that names "Das heißt, hier habe
403		// ich jeweils das Über-Datum." and leaves "datum und" standing against the
404		// stop has found the abandoned attempt and stopped short of its last
405		// syllables; the words it left are the end of that same attempt, and they
406		// are on the side the pass spends first. Refusing the whole answer over
407		// them is how the join everybody could see kept coming back.
408		if d := at - 1 - last; d > 0 {
409			if d > seamSnap {
410				return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("the stretch left out (%q) stops %d words short of the join",
411					seamWords(win[first:last+1]), d)
412			}
413			last = at - 1
414		}
415		if d := first - at; d > 0 {
416			if d > seamSnap {
417				return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("the stretch left out (%q) starts %d words past the join",
418					seamWords(win[first:last+1]), d)
419			}
420			first = at
421		}
422		if n := last - first + 1; n > seamMaxWords || float64(n) > seamCeil*float64(len(win)) {
423			return seamCut{}, fmt.Sprintf("%d of the %d words left out -- that is not a repair",
424				n, len(win))
425		}
426		return seamCut{Before: at - first, After: last + 1 - at}, ""
427	}
428	
429	// shownTokens is the window as the model reads it: one entry per word of what
430	// seamWords printed, each saying which of the window's words it came from.
431	//
432	// Usually one token per word. Not always: where the transcript has words the
433	// recogniser never heard, they ride on the next word that does have a time
434	// (redress), so one word can print as two or three. Those tokens all point back
435	// at the same word, and the word goes only if the whole of it went.
436	func shownTokens(win []srcWord) (toks []string, owner []int) {
437		for i, w := range win {
438			n := 0
439			for _, f := range strings.Fields(seamWord(w)) {
440				if b := bareWord(f); b != "" {
441					toks = append(toks, b)
442					owner = append(owner, i)
443					n++
444				}
445			}
446			if n == 0 {
447				// nothing printable at all: a token of its own so the walk keeps
448				// its place, and one the answer will never match
449				toks = append(toks, "")
450				owner = append(owner, i)
451			}
452		}
453		return toks, owner
454	}
455	
456	// seamWords is one side of a join as the model reads it: the words as they are
457	// WRITTEN -- the case and punctuation the transcript pass settled on -- because
458	// the question is whether the join reads as a sentence, and a lower-case stream
459	// with no stops in it has no sentences to read. The match that follows is on
460	// the bare forms either way (textTokens), so what is shown here changes nothing
461	// about how an answer is understood.
462	func seamWords(ws []srcWord) string {
463		var b []string
464		for _, w := range ws {
465			b = append(b, seamWord(w))
466		}
467		return strings.Join(b, " ")
468	}
469	
470	// seamWord is one word as it is shown and as it is written out: the spelling
471	// the transcript pass settled on, or the bare one it was heard as where the
472	// fold left it none. Never empty -- a word with nothing to print is still a
473	// word of the recording, and leaving it out would shift every number after it
474	// off the word it names (seamNumbered).
475	func seamWord(w srcWord) string {
476		if w.raw != "" {
477			return w.raw
478		}
479		return w.w
480	}
481	
482	// writeFinalText writes the finished text: the words that survive, as they are
483	// written. It is the edit, and a person can read it -- or change it and cut
484	// again (marksFromText), which is why it is punctuated rather than the bare
485	// stream the match works in.
486	//
487	// Every join is marked, because a join is the only place in the file where
488	// anything can be wrong. |cut 10| is a join where ten words went; |cut| is one
489	// where the recording stopped and nothing went, which is worth seeing too --
490	// a stumble the pass walked past looks exactly like ordinary prose otherwise.
491	// Reading 29 marks and the few words either side of each is the check; reading
492	// five thousand words of continuous text is not.
493	//
494	// The marks come back out again on the way in (textTokens), so this file can be
495	// edited by hand and cut from with them left in or taken out.
496	func (a *App) writeFinalText(words []srcWord, drop []bool) error {
497		return os.WriteFile(a.finalText(), []byte(a.finishedText(words, drop)+"\n"), 0o644)
498	}
499	
500	// finishedText is what it writes, apart from the file, so that the marking can
501	// be read without a project on disk.
502	func (a *App) finishedText(words []srcWord, drop []bool) string {
503		var b []string
504		last, gone := "", 0
505		for i, w := range words {
506			if drop != nil && drop[i] {
507				gone++
508				continue
509			}
510			if last != "" && w.src != last {
511				if gone > 0 {
512					b = append(b, fmt.Sprintf("|cut %d|", gone))
513				} else {
514					b = append(b, "|cut|")
515				}
516			}
517			last, gone = w.src, 0
518			// a word whose spelling was folded into the one in front of it
519			// (redress): it keeps its seconds and stays in the video, but it has
520			// nothing of its own to print. The subtitles skip it for the same
521			// reason. This file used to fall back to the bare heard form instead
522			// -- seamWord, which the prompt needs so that every word makes a token
523			// -- and printed "Public-Key-Pairs. key pairs", the one spelling twice.
524			if w.raw == "" {
525				continue
526			}
527			b = append(b, w.raw)
528		}
529		return strings.Join(b, " ")
530	}
531	
532	// finalText is where the edit lives: the words of the finished video.
533	func (a *App) finalText() string { return filepath.Join(a.transcriptDir(), "final.txt") }
534	
535	// marksOfText is the mechanical half of the pass: the text matched back to
536	// the words, checked, and the dropped runs made into marks with their edges
537	// placed. false when the text is refused as an edit.
538	func (a *App) marksOfText(text string, words []srcWord, rows []tsvRow, paths []string) ([]retake, bool) {
539		kept, extra := keepMask(words, textTokens(text))
540		// ...and "keep the later" once more, at every join: a word left dangling
541		// on one side of a cut that the other side begins with is the same word
542		// twice in the video -- "...existing project and | and the more..." --
543		// whatever the model meant by leaving it
544		for _, n := range dedupeJoins(words, kept) {
545			a.logfIdle(">>> text edit: %s", n)
546		}
547		if extra > 0 {
548			a.logfIdle("!!! text edit: %d word(s) in the text were never said -- left out, there is no sound for them", extra)
549		}
550		dropped := 0
551		for _, k := range kept {
552			if !k {
553				dropped++
554			}
555		}
556		if float64(dropped) > retakeCeil*float64(len(words)) {
557			a.logfIdle("!!! text edit: %d of %d words removed -- refused, that is not an edit, nothing is marked", dropped, len(words))
558			return nil, false
559		}
560		// the runs that went, then their edges: fenced by the words either side,
561		// placed by the sound between them (placeEdges)
562		marks, notes := a.placeEdges(marksFrom(words, kept), paths, rows, words)
563		for _, n := range notes {
564			a.logfIdle(">>> text edit: %s", n)
565		}
566		marks = mergeMarks(marks)
567		for _, m := range marks {
568			a.logfIdle(">>> text edit: %s-%s goes (%q)", mmss(m.S), mmss(m.To), m.Text)
569		}
570		a.logfIdle(">>> text edit: %d of %d words removed in %d stretch(es)", dropped, len(words), len(marks))
571		return marks, true
572	}
573	
574	// marksFromText rebuilds the marks from a final.txt edited BY HAND: when the
575	// text is newer than the marks, the words in it are the edit and the marks
576	// are remade from them, no model asked. Delete a word in the file, save, press
577	// Cut, and it is out of the video -- which is the whole point of the text
578	// being a file. false when there is nothing newer to read.
579	func (a *App) marksFromText() ([]retake, bool) {
580		ti, err := os.Stat(a.finalText())
581		if err != nil {
582			return nil, false
583		}
584		if mi, err := os.Stat(a.retakeFile()); err == nil && !ti.ModTime().After(mi.ModTime()) {
585			return nil, false
586		}
587		text, err := os.ReadFile(a.finalText())
588		if err != nil {
589			return nil, false
590		}
591		vids, auds := a.snapSources()
592		paths := append(vids, auds...)
593		words := a.spokenWords(paths)
594		if len(words) == 0 {
595			return nil, false
596		}
597		a.logf(">>> final.txt was edited after Prepare -- the marks are remade from it, no model asked")
598		marks, ok := a.marksOfText(string(text), words, a.sessionRows(), paths)
599		if !ok {
600			return nil, false
601		}
602		if err := a.writeRetakes(marks); err != nil {
603			a.logf("!!! could not write the marks: %v", err)
604		}
605		return marks, true
606	}

608	// spokenWords is the session's words that the video plays: everything but the
609	// narrator's own microphone, which the video never plays (tlLabel).
610	func (a *App) spokenWords(paths []string) []srcWord {
611		narr := a.narratorMic()
612		var out []srcWord
613		for _, w := range a.sessionWords(paths) {
614			if narr == "" || w.src != narr {
615				out = append(out, w)
616			}
617		}
618		return out
619	}
620	
621	// textTokens is the answer as words: whatever it was wrapped in, bare and
622	// lowercase like the words it was made from, with the markers left out.
623	func textTokens(reply string) []string {
624		var out []string
625		reply = pauseMark.ReplaceAllString(reply, " ")
626		for _, f := range strings.Fields(reply) {
627			// the join marks final.txt is written with, and the one the whole-text
628			// pass used to write. Never a word anyone said: a pipe does not occur
629			// in a transcript, so the test can be the character rather than the
630			// exact spelling, and a mark a hand has mangled still goes.
631			if f == "SEAM" || strings.Contains(f, "|") {
632				continue
633			}
634			if w := bareWord(f); w != "" {
635				out = append(out, w)
636			}
637		}
638		return out
639	}
640	
641	// pauseMark is the pause marker as the brief writes it, echoed or not.
642	var pauseMark = regexp.MustCompile(`\(pause [0-9.]+s\)`)
643	
644	// keepMask is which of the words the answer kept, and how many of the
645	// answer's words were never said.
646	//
647	// Matched from the END backwards, on purpose. The same words occur twice
648	// wherever there was a retake, and an answer that keeps them once could be
649	// matched to either; walked forwards it would take the earlier -- the
650	// abandoned attempt -- every time. Walked backwards it takes the later, which
651	// is the one that stays, and the rule "prefer the second" is not a request
652	// to the model but the shape of the match.
653	func keepMask(words []srcWord, out []string) ([]bool, int) {
654		kept := make([]bool, len(words))
655		extra := 0
656		i := len(words) - 1
657		for j := len(out) - 1; j >= 0; j-- {
658			k := i
659			for ; k >= 0 && i-k < keepReach && words[k].w != out[j]; k-- {
660			}
661			if k < 0 || i-k >= keepReach {
662				extra++ // nothing said matches this: it was not said
663				continue
664			}
665			kept[k] = true
666			i = k - 1
667		}
668		return kept, extra
669	}
670	
671	// keepReach is how many words back the match may look for the answer's next
672	// word: past it, the word was not said and the answer moves on. A dropped
673	// stretch is a sentence or two, and two hundred words is a minute of speech.
674	const keepReach = 200
675	
676	// dedupeJoins drops the kept words before a cut that the kept words after it
677	// begin with, up to joinReach of them, and says which. The later saying stays,
678	// exactly as the match prefers it (keepMask) -- the match cannot see this one
679	// because the model kept both.
680	func dedupeJoins(words []srcWord, kept []bool) []string {
681		var notes []string
682		for j := 1; j < len(words); j++ {
683			if kept[j] || !kept[j-1] {
684				continue // not the first dropped word of a run
685			}
686			k := j
687			for k < len(words) && !kept[k] {
688				k++
689			}
690			if k >= len(words) {
691				break
692			}
693			// the kept words before the run, and after it
694			var before, after []int
695			for i := j - 1; i >= 0 && kept[i] && len(before) < joinReach; i-- {
696				before = append([]int{i}, before...)
697			}
698			for i := k; i < len(words) && kept[i] && len(after) < joinReach; i++ {
699				after = append(after, i)
700			}
701			for n := min(len(before), len(after)); n > 0; n-- {
702				same := true
703				for x := 0; x < n && same; x++ {
704					same = sameWord(words[before[len(before)-n+x]].w, words[after[x]].w)
705				}
706				if same {
707					for _, i := range before[len(before)-n:] {
708						kept[i] = false
709					}
710					notes = append(notes, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %q said again straight after the cut -- the earlier one goes",
711						mmss(words[before[len(before)-n]].s), shortWords(words[before[len(before)-n]:before[len(before)-1]+1])))
712					break
713				}
714			}
715		}
716		return notes
717	}
718	
719	// joinReach is how many words either side of a join are compared: a doubled
720	// word or two is a join's own stumble; a whole sentence twice is a retake, and
721	// the model's to find.
722	const joinReach = 3
723	
724	// marksFrom is the dropped stretches as marks: each a run of words that went,
725	// from the first to the last, with the word that resumes named. The edges
726	// themselves are placed afterwards, exactly as a retake's are (placeEdges).
727	func marksFrom(words []srcWord, kept []bool) []retake {
728		var out []retake
729		for i := 0; i < len(words); {
730			if kept[i] {
731				i++
732				continue
733			}
734			j := i
735			for j < len(words) && !kept[j] {
736				j++
737			}
738			m := retake{S: words[i].s, E: words[j-1].e, To: words[j-1].e, Text: shortWords(words[i:j])}
739			if j < len(words) {
740				m.Again = words[j].s
741			}
742			out = append(out, m)
743			i = j
744		}
745		return out
746	}
747	
748	// textCut is the cut of a read to camera: every filmed second, minus the
749	// marks, minus the dead air. No model -- the words decided, in Prepare.
750	//
751	// Only the arithmetic. What it is given is the editor's state as values --
752	// the inserts it already holds, the filmed runs, where the talking is -- and
753	// what it hands back is segments and two numbers for the log; putting them on
754	// the page is the page's job (applyTextCut). It used to reach into the editor
755	// itself, undo stack and status line included, which made a file about words
756	// the one logic file that drove a widget.
757	func (a *App) textCut(marks []retake, inserts []cutSeg, runs []tlSpan, talk [][2]float64) (segs []cutSeg, marked int, dead float64) {
758		segs = insertsOf(inserts)
759		// each filmed run trimmed to its words: a recording starts rolling
760		// before the first word and stops after the last, and neither stretch
761		// is the video. The same fenced placement a cut gets (endAfter,
762		// startBefore), with the run's own edge as the fence.
763		vids, auds := a.snapSources()
764		paths := append(vids, auds...)
765		words := a.spokenWords(paths)
766		edgeOf := a.edgeLookup(paths, a.sessionRows())
767		for _, r := range runs {
768			segs = append(segs, trimRunToWords(cutSeg{S: r.t0, E: r.t1}, words, edgeOf))
769		}
770		marked = dropMarked(&segs, marks)
771		dead = dropDeadAir(&segs, talk)
772		return segs, marked, dead
773	}
774	
775	// trimRunToWords is a filmed run cut down to its speech: from just before its
776	// first word to just after its last, placed by the sound within troughReach
777	// of each and never outside the run. A run with no words in it stands as it
778	// is -- footage with nothing said over it is still footage.
779	func trimRunToWords(seg cutSeg, words []srcWord, edgeOf func(float64) *edges) cutSeg {
780		var first, last *srcWord
781		for i := range words {
782			w := &words[i]
783			if w.s < seg.S-0.01 || w.e > seg.E+0.01 {
784				continue
785			}
786			if first == nil {
787				first = w
788			}
789			last = w
790		}
791		if first == nil {
792			return seg
793		}
794		s := math.Max(seg.S, first.s-wordPad)
795		if e := edgeOf(first.s); e != nil {
796			s = e.startBefore(*first, math.Max(seg.S, first.s-troughReach))
797		}
798		t := math.Min(seg.E, last.e+wordPad)
799		if e := edgeOf(last.e); e != nil {
800			t = e.endAfter(*last, math.Min(seg.E, last.e+troughReach))
801		}
802		return cutSeg{S: s, E: t}
803	}

		a.setStatus("nothing to save yet — ▶ renders the video first")
		return
	}
	// named for the project rather than "final": the folder it came out of
	// says which project it is, and the copy is leaving that folder
	name := strings.TrimSuffix(filepath.Base(a.projPath), filepath.Ext(a.projPath)) + filepath.Ext(p.outFile)
	a.saveAs("Save the video", filepath.Dir(a.projPath), name, nil, func(out string) {
		src := p.outFile
		a.setStatus("saving " + filepath.Base(out) + "…")
		go func() {
			err := copyFile(src, out)
			glib.IdleAdd(func() {
				if err != nil {
					a.logf("!!! save video: %v", err)
					a.setStatus("could not save the video — see log")
					return
				}
				fi, _ := os.Stat(out)
				a.logf(">>> saved %s", out)
				a.setStatus(fmt.Sprintf("saved %s — %s", filepath.Base(out), humanSize(fi.Size())))
			})
		}()
	})
}

// updateProduceInfo redraws both rows: what the render reads and what it has
// written. Everything that changes either comes through here -- a cut edited
// next door, a finished run, a project load.
func (a *App) updateProduceInfo() {
	p := a.prod
	if p == nil {
		return
	}
	p.updateInputs()
	p.updateOut()
}

// updateInputs is the row Cut and Narrate open with, asking the same question
// of this page: what is actually going into the render? Three things, and not
// one of them is made here -- the clips come from Cut, the lines and their
// recordings from Narrate, and a line whose wav is missing is spoken before any
// video is encoded, which is minutes this row is the only warning of.
func (p *producer) updateInputs() {
	if p == nil || p.inputs == nil {
		return
	}
	a := p.a
	segs := a.produceSegs()
	entries := a.produceEntries()
	total := 0.0
	for _, s := range segs {
		total += s.length()
	}
	line := fmt.Sprintf("%s · %s", plural(len(segs), "clip"), mmss(total))
	detail := fmt.Sprintf("cut/cut.json — %d clips, %s of video (the produced file grows a little where the narration needs room)",
		len(segs), mmss(total))
	if len(segs) == 0 {
		line, detail = "no cut yet — build one on the Cut step", ""
	}
	spoken := 0
	for _, e := range entries {
		if exists(a.ttsWav(e)) {
			spoken++
		}
	}
	// What the run will DO, and nothing it will merely use. How many lines
	// there are, which voice speaks them, how many recordings are mixed in and
	// how many candidate thumbnails are on the page are all either said by
	// another page or shown by this one; what is worth a row here is the work
	// still owed -- lines with no wav yet, and an upload text nobody has
	// written -- because that is what the next ▶ spends its minutes on.
	switch {
	case len(entries) == 0:
		line += " · no narration"
	case spoken < len(entries):
		line += fmt.Sprintf(" · %d to speak", len(entries)-spoken)
		detail += fmt.Sprintf("\n\nnarrate/narration.json — %d lines, %d already in narrate/tts; the other %d are spoken first, before any video is encoded",
			len(entries), spoken, len(entries)-spoken)
	default:
		detail += fmt.Sprintf("\n\nnarrate/narration.json — %d lines, all of them already in narrate/tts", len(entries))
	}
	if _, auds := a.snappedSources(); len(auds) > 0 {
		detail += "\n\nMixed into each clip's own audio, for the stretch of it that was running while that clip was:"
		for _, p := range auds {
			detail += "\n" + baseName(p)
		}
	}
	if vp := a.voicePick; vp != nil && len(entries) > 0 {
		if v, ok := vp.current(); ok {
			detail += "\n\nSpoken by " + v.name + " (narrate/voice_ref.wav)"
		}
	}
	if a.pub != nil {
		if a.publishRecorded() {
			detail += "\n\npublish/publish.json — the upload text is written; ▶ redraws and re-renders without asking the model again (deleting publish/ starts the text over)"
		} else {
			line += " · no upload text"
			detail += "\n\nNo publish/publish.json yet — the first ▶ writes the title, the thumbnail instruction and the description before drawing anything"
		}
	}
	p.inputs.SetText(line)
	p.inputs.SetTooltipText(strings.TrimSpace(detail))
}

// updateOut is the line every step ends on: one folder, how many files, how
// big. Everything this step writes is under produce/ (produceDir, publishDir).
func (p *producer) updateOut() {
	if p == nil || p.out == nil {
		return
	}
	p.out.SetText(summarizeOutputs(p.a.produceDir()))
	tip := p.a.produceDir()
	if fi, err := os.Stat(p.outFile); err == nil {
		tip = fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s, %s\n\n%s", p.outFile,
			humanSize(fi.Size()), humanAgo(fi.ModTime()), p.a.produceDir())
	}
	p.out.SetTooltipText(tip)
}

// subsIndex is the label for a stored subtitle mode, rather than panicking on
// a project written by a later version. A mode this build does not know falls
// back to the one that changes nothing about the picture -- the first entry is
// "burned in", and defaulting an unknown answer to lettering somebody's video
// is the wrong way round.
func subsIndex(key string) int {
	for i, k := range prodSubsKey {
		if k == key {
			return i
		}
	}
	return len(prodSubsKey) - 1
}

// ---- inputs -----------------------------------------------------------------

// produceSegs prefers the live editor, so an unsaved tweak still renders.
//
// It is the cut as a SEQUENCE, which is not quite the cut as the timeline holds
// it: a spliced insert cuts the clip it sits in, and here it comes out as two
// clips with the card between them (splitSpliced). Every step after this one
// reads the cut through here, so they all see the same running order -- the one
// the narration is written against and the one that gets rendered.
func (a *App) produceSegs() []cutSeg {
	c := a.produceCut()
	// every piece remembers the scene it was cut from, before anything cuts
	// it: splitSpliced opens scenes for cards and applyFx cuts them again at
	// every rate boundary, and both copy the segment whole, so the stamp
	// travels with the pieces (cutSeg.Scene).
	segs := splitSpliced(c.Segs)
	for i := range segs {
		segs[i].Scene = i
	}
	return applyFx(segs, c.Fx)
}

// produceCut is the whole cut file the render works from: the live editor when
// it has one, what is saved otherwise; everything above the segment level reads
// it here so it cannot disagree with produceSegs. The editor counts as having a
// cut when it has segments, a timeline correction or a row of its own.
func (a *App) produceCut() cutFile {
	if ed := a.ed; ed != nil && (len(ed.segs) > 0 || len(ed.shift) > 0 || len(ed.cutLanes) > 0) {
		return cutFile{Segs: ed.segs, Aspect: ed.aspect, Fx: ed.fx, Shift: ed.shift,
			Rows: ed.rows, Lanes: ed.cutLanes, NRows: ed.nRows}
	}
	b, err := os.ReadFile(a.cutPath())
	if err != nil {
		return cutFile{}
	}
	var c cutFile
	if json.Unmarshal(b, &c) != nil {
		return cutFile{}
	}
	c.Fx = migrateFx(c.Fx)
	return c
}

func (a *App) produceEntries() []narrEntry {
	// no narration at all: whatever is written stays on the Narrate page, and
	// the render behaves as if it were not there -- nothing spoken, nothing
	// laid over a clip, no subtitle track (narrate.go's own tick). Read here
	// rather than at each of the four places that use these entries, because
	// this is the one seam every one of them comes through.
	if a.narrOff {
		return nil
	}
	if a.narr != nil {
		a.narr.pullRows()
		if len(a.narr.entries) > 0 {
			return append([]narrEntry(nil), a.narr.entries...)
		}
	}
	a.narr.flushSave() // a line typed a moment ago belongs in this render
	b, err := os.ReadFile(a.narrPath())
	if err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	var f struct{ Entries []narrEntry }
	if json.Unmarshal(b, &f) != nil {
		return nil
	}
	return f.Entries
}

// sessionTracks is the same placement for both kinds at once: the footage on
// the timeline, and the separate recordings beside it on the same clock. The
// render needs the second list for the same reason the cut page draws lanes
// from it -- a recording that was running while a clip was running is part of
// that clip's sound, and the only thing that says which stretch of it that is
// is where both of them sit on this one clock.
func (a *App) sessionTracks(vids, auds []string) ([]tlVideo, []tlAudio, error) {
	if len(vids) == 0 {
		return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("no videos selected")
	}
	type st struct {
		path  string
		start float64
	}
	// same zero convention as session.tsv: the earliest moment any source
	// names, and 0:00 when none of them names one (srcClock)
	var all []st
	paths := append(append([]string{}, vids...), auds...)
	at, zero := srcClock(paths)
	for _, p := range paths {
		all = append(all, st{p, at[p]})
	}
	var out []tlVideo
	for _, s := range all[:len(vids)] { // the videos are the leading entries
		dur, err := ffprobeDur(s.path)
		if err != nil {
			return nil, nil, err
		}
		out = append(out, tlVideo{base: baseName(s.path), path: s.path,
			start: s.start - zero, wall: s.start, dur: dur, fps: ffprobeFPS(s.path)})
	}

	var rec []tlAudio
	for _, s := range all[len(vids):] {
		dur, err := ffprobeDur(s.path)
		if err != nil || dur <= 0 {
			continue // not something with sound in it; the lanes skip it too
		}
		rec = append(rec, tlAudio{base: baseName(s.path), path: s.path,
			start: s.start - zero, dur: dur})
	}
	// the corrections the cut page made to these clocks, put on before anything
	// is sorted or coloured. The render places its own tracks and would
	// otherwise place them off the raw timestamps -- the ones the hand was
	// dragging to correct in the first place.
	c := a.produceCut()
	for i := range out {
		out[i].start += c.Shift[out[i].base]
	}
	for i := range rec {
		rec[i].start += c.Shift[rec[i].base]
	}
	// the further tracks of a multi-track capture, which are recordings in every
	// way that matters here: a lane each, on the file's own clock, mixed under
	// the clips they were running through. They are built from the videos AFTER
	// those were corrected, so a row dragged to fix its clock takes its own
	// second track with it, and their own name is still a name a further drag
	// can be stored under (slideSrc, cut_shift.go).
	for _, au := range srcLanes(out, a.snappedTracks()) {
		if au.master {
			continue // that one is the footage's own sound, taken off its input
		}
		au.start += c.Shift[au.base]
		rec = append(rec, au)
	}
	// and the rows the cut put on the band itself, which are in cut.json and in
	// no source list -- the render has to be told about them or every scene cut
	// to one would resolve to whatever recording was rolling at that second
	// (cut_lane.go). They are placed by laneVideos and corrected here, exactly
	// as the editor does it.
	lanes := a.laneVideos(c.Lanes, out)
	for i := range lanes {
		lanes[i].start += c.Shift[lanes[i].base]
	}
	out = append(out, lanes...)
	sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].start < out[j].start })
	sort.Slice(rec, func(i, j int) bool { return rec[i].start < rec[j].start })
	// the rows, worked out the same way the cut page works them out, because a
	// scene says which ROW its picture comes from (cutSeg.Cam) and the number
	// has to mean the same thing on both sides. Without this every scene would
	// resolve against row nought and a two-camera cut would render as one.
	assignLanes(out, c.Rows)
	return out, rec, nil
}

func hasAudioStream(path string) bool {
	out, err := exec.Command(ffTool("ffprobe"), "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "a:0",
		"-show_entries", "stream=codec_type", "-of", "csv=p=0", path).Output()
	return err == nil && strings.Contains(string(out), "audio")
}

func (b bdrop) on() bool { return b.w > 0 && b.h > 0 }

const blurSigma = 0.02

// chain is the sub-graph that lays the picture on a blurred blow-up of itself:
// one split, the copy scaled to COVER the frame and blurred, the picture laid
// back over it. in is the label it reads, k a number that keeps its own labels
// apart from every other one in the graph; it returns the filter_complex text
// and the label it wrote.
func (b bdrop) chain(in string, k int) (string, string) {
	out := fmt.Sprintf("bd%d", k)
	if b.bare {
		// black, and one filter to say it: pad puts the picture on a bigger
		// frame at the corner it belongs at, and the fitted case scales it
		// down first because an insert brings its own shape
		if b.fit {

				"pad=%d:%d:(ow-iw)/2:(oh-ih)/2:color=black[%s];",

			in, b.w, b.h, b.x, b.y, out), out

			fg, b.w, b.h, fg)

// demuxer stream-copies and does not refuse a clip of another size -- the
// decoder comes apart on it and the video smears from there. Every branch of
// encodeClip pins its size, so a mismatch means one stopped. Measured against
// the FIRST clip, reported by name.
func joinMismatch(made []clipSize) []string {
	var out []string
	for i, c := range made {
		if i == 0 || (c.w == made[0].w && c.h == made[0].h) {
			continue
		}
		out = append(out, fmt.Sprintf(
			"%s came out %d×%d where %s is %d×%d — the join is a stream copy and cannot mix sizes, so the video breaks at this clip",
			c.name, c.w, c.h, made[0].name, made[0].w, made[0].h))
	}
	return out
}

// fitsFrame is whether this recording, scaled down until it fits the finished
// frame, then covers it -- so that the edges need nothing filling in. Asked of
// the source size the Prepare page probed; a recording nobody measured answers
// no, because a wrong yes here is footage pulled out of shape.
func fitsFrame(v *tlVideo, w, h int) bool {
	if v == nil || v.w <= 0 || v.h <= 0 || w <= 0 || h <= 0 {
		return false
	}
	// what force_original_aspect_ratio=decrease would come out at: the smaller
	// of the two scales, so the picture never overshoots the frame and the
	// only question left is what it falls SHORT of. Within a pixel on both
	// axes is covered -- 1366x768 into 1920x1080 is not 16:9 to the last
	// decimal, and a one-pixel seam of blur is not worth a filter chain
	k := math.Min(float64(w)/float64(v.w), float64(h)/float64(v.h))
	return float64(w)-float64(v.w)*k < 2 && float64(h)-float64(v.h)*k < 2
}

// whose sizes were never probed -- a made-up size would be worse than none.
func stillSize(from, over *tlVideo) (int, int) {
	if from == nil || over == nil {
		return 0, 0
	}
	if from.w <= 0 || from.h <= 0 || over.w <= 0 || over.h <= 0 {
		return 0, 0
	}
	if from.w == over.w && from.h == over.h {
		return 0, 0
	}
	return over.w, over.h
}

// stillMute is the ffmpeg enable expression for the seconds this clip's stops
// asked to have taken out of its sound: one between() per still, added
// together the way ffmpeg spells "or". Empty when every stop keeps its sound,
// which is the ordinary case and leaves the graph exactly as it was.
func stillMute(stills []stillCue) string {
	var parts []string
	for _, sc := range stills {
		if sc.mute && sc.e > sc.s {
			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("between(t,%.3f,%.3f)", sc.s, sc.e))
		}
	}
	return strings.Join(parts, "+")
}

// prodMix is a separate recording playing under one clip: a headset recorder, a
// mic on the table, OBS's second track. The picture's own sound is the game and
// whatever the capture card happened to hear; this is the rest of what was said
// while it was recorded, and it is mixed into the same bed rather than over the
// narration -- so "Game audio under voice" ducks both together and the AI voice

//
// The three numbers are the whole placement: at is where in the clip it comes

// the recording the clip starts, and dur is how much of it is used. They come

func (a *App) transcodeClicked() { a.askOverwrite(func() { a.produceRun(false) }) }

// renderWanted is renderStale with the page's own inputs read for it, for the
// two callers that have not gathered them yet.
func (a *App) renderWanted() bool {
	if a.prod == nil {
		return false
	}
	vids, auds := a.snapSources()
	return a.renderStale(a.produceSegs(), a.produceEntries(), a.prodSettings(), vids, auds)
}

func (a *App) askOverwrite(run func()) {
	p := a.prod
	if p == nil || !exists(p.outFile) {
		run()
		return
	}
	fi, err := os.Stat(p.outFile)
	detail := p.outFile
	if err == nil {
		detail = fmt.Sprintf("%s — %s, %s", p.outFile, humanSize(fi.Size()), humanAgo(fi.ModTime()))
	}
	a.confirm("Overwrite "+filepath.Base(p.outFile)+"?",
		detail+"\n\nThe encode takes minutes and there is no undo for it.", "Overwrite", run)
}

func (a *App) produceRun(words bool) {
	if a.busy() {
		return
	}
	if a.pub == nil {
		return
	}
	segs := a.produceSegs()
	if len(segs) == 0 {
		a.setStatus("no cut yet — build one on the Cut step first")
		return
	}
	entries := a.produceEntries()
	st := a.prodSettings()
	vids, auds := a.snapSources()

	// the goroutine below must not go reading widgets or the editor
	pst := a.pub.snapshot()
	aspect := a.produceCut().Aspect
	written := a.publishRecorded()
	a.saveProjectNow() // the run is a moment worth a file, whatever the ticker is doing

	a.startRun()
	// ▶ leaves an up-to-date video alone; ↻ Transcode is the press that means
	// "encode it anyway", so it never asks this question.
	encode := !words || a.renderStale(segs, entries, st, vids, auds)
	if !encode {
		a.logf(">>> the video is already what this page describes — not encoding it again " +
			"(↻ beside Transcode encodes anyway)")
	}
	switch {
	case !encode:
	case !words:
		a.logf(">>> transcoding %s: %d clips at %s/%s crf %d — the thumbnail and the upload text are left as they are",
			filepath.Base(st.OutFile), len(segs), st.Container, st.Codec, st.CRF)
	case written:
		a.logf(">>> producing %s: %d clips at %s/%s crf %d, and the thumbnail redrawn beside them",
			filepath.Base(st.OutFile), len(segs), st.Container, st.Codec, st.CRF)
	default:
		a.logf(">>> producing %s: %d clips at %s/%s crf %d, and the upload text and thumbnail written beside them",
			filepath.Base(st.OutFile), len(segs), st.Container, st.Codec, st.CRF)
	}
	// two halves, side by side. The render owns the fraction -- it is minutes
	// where the other is seconds, so the needle IS the render's progress --
	// and the words-and-picture half owns the second line of the bar, which
	// is what it has to say for itself.
	a.qJob(trackSTT, "render", 0, 0)
	a.prog(trackSTT, 0, "preparing")
	if words {
		a.qJob(trackFrames, "publish", 0, 0)
		a.prog(trackFrames, 0, "thinking")
	}
	a.pulseUntilCounted()

	go func() {
		// The two halves do not touch. The upload text and the thumbnail are
		// written from the cut and the narration and read their frames out of
		// inputs/; the render reads the same cut and narration and writes
		// produce/ and the video. Neither reads a file the other writes, and
		// the render never reads the publish record -- so there was nothing
		// for the render to wait for, and it waited anyway: a minute of an
		// idle encoder while a model thought about a title, and then the
		// thumbnail drawing on the GPU while the CPU had nothing to do.
		//
		// A failure in the words does not throw the render away any more.
		// They are separate deliverables, the expensive one is the video, and
		// an sd.cpp that is down is not a reason to spend the encode again.
		var wg sync.WaitGroup
		var pubErr error
		if words {
			wg.Add(1)
			go func() {
				defer wg.Done()
				pubErr = a.publishStage(trackFrames, pst, aspect, segs, entries, !written, written, false, false)
				a.qDone(trackFrames, 0) // its own line goes quiet; the needle was never its
				glib.IdleAdd(func() {
					if p := a.pub; p != nil {
						p.refresh() // whatever landed, up as soon as it is written
					}
				})
				if pubErr != nil && !errors.Is(pubErr, errStopped) {
					a.logfIdle("!!! the upload text and thumbnail failed: %v -- the render carries on", pubErr)
				}
			}()
		}
		var err error
		if encode {
			if err = a.produce(segs, entries, st, vids, auds); err == nil {
				a.markRendered(segs, entries, st, vids, auds)
			}
		}
		wg.Wait()
		// Both halves are in, so the deliverables can be described: the
		// <video> tag, with the poster the words half just drew and the .vtt
		// tracks the render half just wrote (produce_embed.go). Here and not
		// at the end of either half -- the tag needs both, and it is rewritten
		// even on a press that skipped the encode, because the files beside
		// the video are then the ones the render before left.
		a.writeEmbed(st.OutFile, st.Codec)
		// the render's word is the run's: it is what the press was for, and a
		// title that did not get written is a line in the log, not a failure
		// to show for a video that rendered
		if err == nil && pubErr != nil {
			err = pubErr
		}
		glib.IdleAdd(func() {
			a.endRun()
			a.updateGates()
			if err != nil {
				if !errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
					a.logf("produce FAILED: %v", err)
				}
				if errors.Is(err, errStopped) {
					a.setStatus("production stopped")
				} else {
					a.setStatus("production failed — see log")
				}
				return
			}
			a.progress.SetFraction(1)
			a.setStatus("done")
			// the bar carries the outcome; filled in below, once the file has
			// been measured
			dur, _ := ffprobeDur(st.OutFile)
			fi, _ := os.Stat(st.OutFile)
			size := int64(0)
			if fi != nil {
				size = fi.Size()
			}
			a.logf(">>> %s  (%.1f s, %s)", st.OutFile, dur, humanSize(size))
			a.progress.SetText(fmt.Sprintf("produced %s — %.1f s, %s",
				filepath.Base(st.OutFile), dur, humanSize(size)))
			a.updateProduceInfo()
		})
	}()
}

package main

// Where a retake's edges actually are.
//
// The ASR stamps a word to 80 ms, and on the first word after a silence the
// stamp runs late -- half a second late, measured, on a take's opening "And".
// A boundary placed on the stamp therefore lands INSIDE the word it was meant
// to precede, and whatever came out before it -- the breath, the false start
// the ASR folded away -- is kept.
//
// The waveform envelope already exists for the timeline, at 10 ms (waveHz),
// and for placing a cut it is the right instrument: what matters at a join is
// where sound starts and stops, not what the sound was. So the two edges of a
// mark are moved onto it. The cut ends where the last kept sound ends, and
// resumes where the retake's sound begins -- everything between goes, whatever
// it was, which is what "said again" means.
//
// The envelopes are built once per source and kept under cache/edges, apart
// from the timeline's own cache: that one is built to the page's channel count
// and this one is mono, and a file written to one reading must not be read by
// the other.

import (
	"math"
	"path/filepath"
	"sort"
)

const (
	// how far an edge may be moved off its stamp. A stamp half a second late
	// is what was measured; a sound a whole second away is a different sound.
	edgeReach = 0.8
	// what is left of a sound at a cut: a few buckets, so the last consonant
	// is not shaved and the first is not clipped
	edgePad = 0.05
	// how far behind its sound a stamp may run and still be that sound's:
	// half a second was measured on a take's opening word
	lateStamp = 0.6

	// With ALIGNED words the envelope's job changes: the words fence the cut
	// and the sound only chooses where inside the fence it falls.
	//
	// how far below a word's own level its tail still counts as the word.
	// On the meter scale the envelope is drawn in (-70..0 dBFS over 0..255),
	// a breath sits 20 dB or more under the word it follows, and a trailing
	// consonant a few dB under; twelve tells them apart.
	edgeTailDB = 12.0
	// how far past the aligner's edge a word's own sound is followed. The
	// aligner is within a fiftieth on an onset and can be a touch early on
	// a trailing s or k; a quarter second is that, and not the breath after.
	edgeTailMax = 0.25
	// how far into the gap the quietest moment is looked for. Past the
	// word's own tail the gap is breath and room; the cut goes where that
	// is lowest, and a trough further off than this is a different gap.
	troughReach = 0.4
)

// endAfter is where the cut ends after a word that stays, given the word and
// how far the cut may go (the next word's start, which it never reaches):
// the word's own sound followed to where it drops (edgeTailMax), then the
// quietest moment after that (troughReach). The words fence it; the sound
// chooses inside the fence. Without an envelope, a hair after the word.
func (e *edges) endAfter(w srcWord, limit float64) float64 {
	if limit <= w.e {
		return w.e
	}
	i0, i1 := e.at(w.s), e.at(w.e)
	lim := e.at(limit)
	if e == nil || i0 < 0 || i1 < 0 {
		return math.Min(w.e+wordPad, limit)
	}
	if lim < 0 {
		lim = len(e.wf.chans[0]) - 1
	}
	thr := e.tailLevel(i0, i1)
	end := i1
	for stop := min(lim, i1+int(edgeTailMax*e.wf.hz)); end < stop && e.sound(end, thr); end++ {
	}
	best := end
	for k := end; k <= min(lim, end+int(troughReach*e.wf.hz)); k++ {
		if e.wf.chans[0][k] < e.wf.chans[0][best] {
			best = k
		}
	}
	return math.Min(limit, math.Max(w.e, e.off+float64(best)/e.wf.hz))
}

// startBefore is the same the other way: where the cut resumes before a word
// that starts again, given how far back it may go (the last dropped word's
// end, which it never reaches).
func (e *edges) startBefore(w srcWord, limit float64) float64 {
	if limit >= w.s {
		return w.s
	}
	i0, i1 := e.at(w.s), e.at(w.e)
	lim := e.at(limit)
	if e == nil || i0 < 0 || i1 < 0 {
		return math.Max(w.s-wordPad, limit)
	}
	if lim < 0 {
		lim = 0
	}
	thr := e.tailLevel(i0, i1)
	start := i0
	for stop := max(lim, i0-int(edgeTailMax*e.wf.hz)); start > stop && e.sound(start-1, thr); start-- {
	}
	best := start
	for k := start; k >= max(lim, start-int(troughReach*e.wf.hz)); k-- {
		if e.wf.chans[0][k] < e.wf.chans[0][best] {
			best = k
		}
	}
	return math.Max(limit, math.Min(w.s, e.off+float64(best)/e.wf.hz))
}

// tailLevel is what still counts as the word between buckets i0 and i1: its
// own peak less edgeTailDB, and never under the room (floor).
func (e *edges) tailLevel(i0, i1 int) uint8 {
	peak := uint8(0)
	for k := i0; k <= i1 && k < len(e.wf.chans[0]); k++ {
		peak = max(peak, e.wf.chans[0][k])
	}
	thr := int(peak) - int(math.Round(edgeTailDB*255/70))
	return uint8(max(thr, int(e.floor(e.off+float64(i0)/e.wf.hz))))
}

// edges is the envelope of one source, mono, with the source's place in the
// session so a session second can be looked up in it.
type edges struct {
	wf  *waveform
	off float64 // session second the file's first sample lands on
}

// loadEdges reads or builds the envelope for a source.
func (a *App) loadEdges(path string, off float64) *edges {
	wf, err := loadWave(filepath.Join(a.outDir, "cache", "edges"),
		tlAudio{base: baseName(path), path: path, chans: 1})
	if err != nil || wf == nil || len(wf.chans) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return &edges{wf: wf, off: off}
}

// at is the bucket a session second falls in, or -1 outside the file.
func (e *edges) at(t float64) int {
	i := int((t - e.off) * e.wf.hz)
	if i < 0 || i >= len(e.wf.chans[0]) {
		return -1
	}
	return i
}

// floor is what counts as sound around a point: the quiet of that stretch of
// the recording, with room over it. Measured on the buckets around t rather
// than fixed, because a room, a microphone and a gain setting each put the
// silence somewhere else -- and taken from the quieter end of the window, so
// a window that is mostly talking still finds its floor.
func (e *edges) floor(t float64) uint8 {
	i := e.at(t)
	if i < 0 {
		return 255
	}
	lo, hi := max(0, i-400), min(len(e.wf.chans[0]), i+400) // ±4 s
	win := append([]uint8(nil), e.wf.chans[0][lo:hi]...)
	sort.Slice(win, func(a, b int) bool { return win[a] < win[b] })
	quiet := int(win[len(win)/5]) // the 20th percentile is the room
	return uint8(min(255, max(quiet*3, quiet+8)))
}

// sound is whether bucket i is above the floor.
func (e *edges) sound(i int, thr uint8) bool {
	return i >= 0 && i < len(e.wf.chans[0]) && e.wf.chans[0][i] >= thr
}

// endBefore is where the last sound before session second t ends: the cut
// ends there. t is the stamp of the first abandoned word, which may fall inside
// that word or just before it; either way the sound run it belongs to is
// stepped out of first, then the quiet before it, and the sound before THAT is
// what the cut keeps. Unchanged when no such edge is within reach -- speech
// with no gap in it is cut where the stamp says.
func (e *edges) endBefore(t float64) float64 {
	i := e.at(t)
	if i < 0 {
		return t
	}
	thr := e.floor(t)
	limit := int(edgeReach * e.wf.hz)
	j := i
	for ; j >= 0 && i-j <= limit && e.sound(j, thr); j-- {
	}
	for ; j >= 0 && i-j <= limit && !e.sound(j, thr); j-- {
	}
	if j < 0 || i-j > limit {
		return t
	}
	return e.off + float64(j+1)/e.wf.hz + edgePad
}

// startAt is where the retake's sound begins: the cut resumes there. t is the
// stamp of its first word, and a stamp runs LATE -- never early -- so the word
// is the sound run the stamp falls in, or the one that ended just before it.
// Its onset is where the cut resumes. A stamp with quiet for a while before it
// is a stamp the sound has not reached yet, and it stands as it is: moving
// forward to the next sound would clip the very word it names.
func (e *edges) startAt(t float64) float64 {
	i := e.at(t)
	if i < 0 {
		return t
	}
	thr := e.floor(t)
	limit := int(edgeReach * e.wf.hz)
	j := i
	if !e.sound(i, thr) {
		// back over the quiet to the run before it, if the quiet is short
		// enough to be the tail of a late stamp
		for ; j > 0 && i-j <= int(lateStamp*e.wf.hz) && !e.sound(j-1, thr); j-- {
		}
		if j == 0 || !e.sound(j-1, thr) {
			return t
		}
	}
	for ; j > 0 && i-j <= limit && e.sound(j-1, thr); j-- {
	}
	if i-j > limit {
		return t
	}
	return max(e.off, e.off+float64(j)/e.wf.hz-edgePad)
}

69	// sourceItem is one file and what it is for. The path is absolute: sources come
70	// from wherever the capture put them now, so there is no folder left for a name
71	// to be relative to.
72	type sourceItem struct {
73		path     string
74		footage  bool
75		narrator int // 0 = untagged, 1..narratorSlots
76		// sepVoice asks for the voice to be split off this recording. It is a
77		// WISH, not a state: nothing has happened until Prepare runs, and once it
78		// has, the wish is spent -- the row then points at the voiceless file and
79		// the voice is a row of its own, so there is nothing left to ask for.
80		sepVoice bool
81		// which of the file's audio tracks the session uses, as a:N indices. Empty
82		// is the first alone, which is what an ordinary file means and what every
83		// project written before the choice existed means (wantTracks). Only a file
84		// with more than one track can be given a different answer, and only from
85		// the menu on its row -- see trackButton (cut_tracks.go).
86		tracks []int
87	}
88	
89	func (it sourceItem) name() string { return filepath.Base(it.path) }
90	
91	// sameSource is == for a struct holding a slice. Every field is spelled out,
92	// and TestEverySourceFieldCountsAsAChange fails on any field this forgets.
93	// Tracks compare in ORDER: they are the stored form of a sorted, deduplicated
94	// answer (wantTracks).
95	func sameSource(a, b sourceItem) bool {
96		if a.path != b.path || a.footage != b.footage || a.narrator != b.narrator ||
97			a.sepVoice != b.sepVoice || len(a.tracks) != len(b.tracks) {
98			return false
99		}
100		for i := range a.tracks {
101			if a.tracks[i] != b.tracks[i] {
102				return false
103			}
104		}
105		return true
106	}
107	
108	// sourceList is the session's sources. The order is arrival order and nothing
109	// hangs on it: sources are placed on the wall clock by the timestamp in their
110	// name (sourceStart), which is why a row whose name has no stamp gets a
111	// warning rather than a pair of reorder arrows. The whole list is rebuilt from
112	// the slice on every change -- at a handful of files that is simpler and safer
113	// than in-place row surgery.
114	type sourceList struct {
115		items    []sourceItem
116		box      *gtk.ListBox
117		onChange func()
118		// how many audio tracks each file holds, so the rows can be rebuilt without
119		// an ffprobe apiece every time one of them is touched (srcTracks)
120		probed map[string][]audTrack
121	}
122	
123	func newSourceList(onChange func()) *sourceList {
124		s := &sourceList{onChange: onChange}
125		s.box = gtk.NewListBox()
126		s.box.SetSelectionMode(gtk.SelectionNone)
127		s.box.AddCSSClass("boxed-list")
128		return s
129	}
130	
131	// add appends the files it does not already hold and returns how many that was.
132	// Adding the same file twice is a no-op rather than an error: the two ways in
133	// -- a folder and a file chooser -- overlap, and the pipeline transcribes one
134	// row once.
135	func (s *sourceList) add(paths ...string) int {
136		have := map[string]bool{}
137		for _, it := range s.items {
138			have[it.path] = true
139		}
140		n := 0
141		for _, p := range paths {
142			if abs, err := filepath.Abs(p); err == nil {
143				p = abs
144			}
145			if have[p] || !isMedia(p) {
146				continue
147			}
148			have[p] = true
149			s.items = append(s.items, sourceItem{path: p, footage: isVideo(p)})
150			n++
151		}
152		if n > 0 {
153			s.autoTag()
154			s.changed()
155		}
156		return n
157	}
158	
159	// addDir adds every media file in a folder, by name. This is how a session
160	// arrives: a card is dumped somewhere and all of it is the session.
161	func (s *sourceList) addDir(dir string) int {
162		var paths []string
163		for _, n := range listMedia(dir) {
164			paths = append(paths, filepath.Join(dir, n))
165		}
166		return s.add(paths...)
167	}

169	// autoTag gives narrator 1 away when nobody holds it. Somebody has to be the
170	// narrator -- it is the voice Narrate speaks in -- and a first session should
171	// not have to be told that the one recording in it is the one to clone.
172	// Recordings come before footage: a screen capture holds everyone at once, so
173	// a dedicated mic track is the better guess at "you".
174	func (s *sourceList) autoTag() {
175		for _, it := range s.items {
176			if it.narrator == 1 {
177				return
178			}
179		}
180		// only an untagged row: a row that already holds a slot is somebody the user
181		// named, and moving them to slot 1 would both re-cast the narration and
182		// silently free the slot they were in
183		for _, want := range []bool{false, true} { // recordings first, then footage
184			for i := range s.items {
185				if s.items[i].footage == want && s.items[i].narrator == 0 {
186					s.items[i].narrator = 1
187					return
188				}
189			}
190		}
191	}
192	
193	// remove throws a row out of the session. The file is not touched: this list is
194	// what a project is made of, and a project is not a folder.
195	func (s *sourceList) remove(i int) {
196		if i < 0 || i >= len(s.items) {
197			return
198		}
199		s.items = append(s.items[:i], s.items[i+1:]...)
200		s.autoTag() // the narrator may have just left
201		s.changed()
202	}
203	
204	// setFootage turns the frames on or off for one row. Only a video can be on:
205	// footage means frames come out of it, and an audio file has none to give --
206	// the toggle exists for the one direction that is a choice, a video kept only
207	// for its sound.
208	func (s *sourceList) setFootage(i int, on bool) {
209		if i < 0 || i >= len(s.items) || s.items[i].footage == on {
210			return
211		}
212		if on && !isVideo(s.items[i].path) {
213			return
214		}
215		s.items[i].footage = on
216		s.changed()
217	}
218	
219	// setSepVoice flags a row for voice separation, or unflags it. Only the wish
220	// is stored: the models are the server's and the work is minutes long, so the
221	// button cannot do it -- ▶ does, and until then this is reversible with a
222	// second click, which is the whole reason it is a flag and not an action.
223	func (s *sourceList) setSepVoice(i int, on bool) {
224		if i < 0 || i >= len(s.items) || s.items[i].sepVoice == on {
225			return
226		}
227		s.items[i].sepVoice = on
228		s.changed()
229	}
230	
231	// sepVoiceWanted is the list as the separator reads it: every path still
232	// waiting for its voice to be lifted off.
233	func (s *sourceList) sepVoiceWanted() []string {
234		var out []string
235		for _, it := range s.items {
236			if it.sepVoice {
237				out = append(out, it.path)
238			}
239		}
240		return out
241	}
242	
243	// cycleNarrator is what the microphone button does: step to the next free slot,
244	// and off the end back to untagged. Slots are exclusive -- a slot is a person,
245	// and two rows claiming to be narrator 1 would leave Narrate picking one of them
246	// silently -- so the ones other rows hold are stepped over rather than stolen.
247	func (s *sourceList) cycleNarrator(i int) {
248		if i < 0 || i >= len(s.items) {
249			return
250		}
251		next := 0
252		for n := s.items[i].narrator + 1; n <= narratorSlots; n++ {
253			if s.slotHolder(n) < 0 {
254				next = n
255				break
256			}
257		}
258		s.items[i].narrator = next
259		s.changed()
260	}
261	
262	// slotHolder is the row holding slot n, or -1.
263	func (s *sourceList) slotHolder(n int) int {
264		for i, it := range s.items {
265			if it.narrator == n {
266				return i
267			}
268		}
269		return -1
270	}
271	
272	// narratorPath is the recording tagged with slot n, or "".
273	func (s *sourceList) narratorPath(n int) string {
274		if i := s.slotHolder(n); i >= 0 {
275			return s.items[i].path
276		}
277		return ""
278	}
279	
280	// split is the list as the pipeline reads it: the footage, then everything
281	// else, each in list order. Every source appears in exactly one of the two, so
282	// appending them is the whole session and nothing is transcribed twice.
283	func (s *sourceList) split() (footage, rest []string) {
284		for _, it := range s.items {
285			if it.footage {
286				footage = append(footage, it.path)
287			} else {
288				rest = append(rest, it.path)
289			}
290		}
291		return
292	}
293	
294	// clash names two sources that would be written to the same place: every step
295	// keys output on the file name without extension, so clip.mkv and clip.flac
296	// are both inputs/clip and the second run would find the first's words.json.
297	// "" when the session is clean.
298	func (s *sourceList) clash() (a, b string) {
299		seen := map[string]string{}
300		for _, it := range s.items {
301			k := baseName(it.path)
302			if p, ok := seen[k]; ok {
303				return p, it.path
304			}
305			seen[k] = it.path
306		}
307		return "", ""
308	}
309	
310	func (s *sourceList) paths() []string {
311		out := make([]string, len(s.items))
312		for i, it := range s.items {
313			out[i] = it.path
314		}
315		return out
316	}

318	// prune drops rows whose file is gone and names them, for the log. A source
319	// that quietly stopped being in the list is how a render comes out missing a
320	// camera angle nobody can account for.
321	func (s *sourceList) prune() []string {
322		var gone []string
323		var kept []sourceItem
324		for _, it := range s.items {
325			if exists(it.path) {
326				kept = append(kept, it)
327				continue
328			}
329			gone = append(gone, it.path)
330		}
331		if len(gone) == 0 {
332			return nil
333		}
334		s.items = kept
335		s.autoTag()
336		s.changed()
337		return gone
338	}
339	
340	// load replaces the list wholesale -- a project being opened. Roles come from
341	// the project as stored: a list with nobody in slot 1 is one the user untagged,
342	// and it must come back untagged. autoTag runs only when a broken tag had to
343	// be stripped -- filling the one kind of gap load itself leaves.
344	func (s *sourceList) load(items []sourceItem) {
345		s.items = nil
346		stripped := false
347		for _, it := range items {
348			// a hand-edited project must not seat two people in one slot,
349			// or promise frames out of a file that has none
350			if it.narrator != 0 && (it.narrator < 1 || it.narrator > narratorSlots || s.slotHolder(it.narrator) >= 0) {
351				it.narrator = 0
352				stripped = true
353			}
354			it.footage = it.footage && isVideo(it.path)
355			s.items = append(s.items, it)
356		}
357		if stripped {
358			s.autoTag()
359		}
360		s.changed()
361	}
362	
363	func (s *sourceList) changed() {
364		// before anything reads the list: placing a file is the first thing every
365		// step does with one, and it has to place it where this list says
366		s.render()
367		if s.onChange != nil {
368			s.onChange()
369		}
370	}
371	
372	// srcRowKey is the key to a row's four symbols, appended to each of their
373	// tooltips: a word each, opening with the symbol (Unicode, since a tooltip is
374	// text), so the three the pointer is NOT on are explained where the eye is.
375	const srcRowKey = "\n\nThe symbols on every row, in order:\n" +
376		"🎥 footage — frames come out of it, and the cut is made of it\n" +
377		"🎤 narrator — which of the voices this is; 1 speaks the narration\n" +
378		"✂ split the voice off — ▶ separates it into the voice and the rest\n" +
379		"🗑 remove — off this list; the file itself is left alone"
380	
381	// ---- the rows ---------------------------------------------------------------
382	
383	func (s *sourceList) render() {
384		if s.box == nil {
385			return // headless, in tests
386		}
387		for {
388			row := s.box.RowAtIndex(0)
389			if row == nil {
390				break
391			}
392			s.box.Remove(row)
393		}
394		for i := range s.items {
395			s.box.Append(s.row(i))
396		}
397	}
398	
399	func (s *sourceList) row(i int) *gtk.Box {
400		it := s.items[i]
401	
402		// footage: what frames are taken from, and what the cut and the render are
403		// made of. On by default for a video file, off for a recording, and a
404		// toggle either way -- a capture wanted only for its sound is a video with
405		// this off, which is the case that used to need a second copy of the file
406		// in the other folder.
407		foot := gtk.NewToggleButton()
408		foot.SetIconName("camera-video-symbolic")
409		foot.AddCSSClass("flat")
410		foot.SetActive(it.footage)
411		// only a video can be footage, so on an audio file the toggle is dead
412		// rather than a button that silently never sticks
413		foot.SetSensitive(isVideo(it.path))
414		foot.SetTooltipText("Footage — frames come out of this file and it can be cut.\n" +
415			"Off: it is only listened to, which is what a video kept for its audio wants." + srcRowKey)
416		foot.ConnectToggled(func() { s.setFootage(i, foot.Active()) })
417	
418		// the narrator slot: a microphone, and the slot number once it holds one --
419		// which of the four voices this recording is. Untagged is the mic alone,
420		// dimmed; a placeholder dash was just one more thing to decode. Click cycles.
421		narr := gtk.NewButton()
422		narr.AddCSSClass("flat")
423		nb := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 2)
424		nb.Append(gtk.NewImageFromIconName("audio-input-microphone-symbolic"))
425		// the slot number, and the room for one whether or not there is a number
426		// to put in it: the label is always there and always a character wide, so
427		// an untagged row is exactly as wide as a tagged one. Built the other way
428		// -- the label appended only when there is a slot -- the button was two
429		// sizes, and every file name in the list started at whichever x its own
430		// row happened to give it.
431		slot := gtk.NewLabel("")
432		slot.SetWidthChars(1)
433		if it.narrator > 0 {
434			slot.SetText(strconv.Itoa(it.narrator))
435		} else {
436			nb.AddCSSClass("dim-label")
437		}
438		nb.Append(slot)
439		narr.SetChild(nb)
440		if it.narrator == 1 {
441			narr.AddCSSClass("suggested-action") // the voice the narration is spoken in
442		}
443		narr.SetTooltipText("Narrator — click to cycle through the free slots and back to none.\n" +
444			"1 is the voice the narration is spoken in; 2–4 are the rest of the group." + srcRowKey)
445		narr.ConnectClicked(func() { s.cycleNarrator(i) })
446	
447		// an ellipsizing label: a recorder filename is 50 characters, and a row
448		// that insists on all of them sets a floor under the whole window
449		lbl := gtk.NewLabel(it.name())
450		lbl.SetXAlign(0)
451		lbl.SetHExpand(true)
452		lbl.SetEllipsize(pango.EllipsizeMiddle)
453		lbl.SetTooltipText(it.path) // sources come from anywhere; the name alone can repeat
454	
455		// split the voice off: the recording becomes two rows -- itself without the
456		// voice, and the voice on its own. A flag, because the separation is a
457		// model on the server and minutes of it, so the press that starts work is
458		// ▶ like every other minute this page spends. Toggled on it is loud, so a
459		// row waiting for it is visible from across the list.
460		sep := gtk.NewToggleButton()
461		sep.SetIconName("edit-cut-symbolic")
462		sep.AddCSSClass("flat")
463		sep.SetActive(it.sepVoice)
464		sep.SetTooltipText("Split the voice off — on ▶ this recording is separated into the\n" +
465			"voice and everything else. This row keeps everything else; the voice\n" +
466			"is added as a track of its own, so it can be cut and mixed apart." + srcRowKey)
467		sep.ConnectToggled(func() { s.setSepVoice(i, sep.Active()) })
468		// a row that IS a half of a split has no voice left to take off a voice,
469		// so its scissors are dead -- greyed rather than gone. Removed from the
470		// row entirely they took their column with them, and in a list where some
471		// rows are split products and some are not, the trash beside them sat at
472		// two different x.
473		sep.SetSensitive(!splitProduct(it.path))
474	
475		del := flatIcon("user-trash-symbolic", "Remove from this session — the file itself is left alone"+srcRowKey, func() { s.remove(i) })
476	
477		row := gtk.NewBox(gtk.OrientationHorizontal, 4)
478		row.SetMarginStart(6)
479		row.SetMarginEnd(2)
480		row.Append(foot)
481		row.Append(narr)
482		row.Append(lbl)
483		// only for a file that holds more than one audio track: an ordinary
484		// recording has nothing to choose and gets no button (trackButton)
485		if tb := s.trackButton(i); tb != nil {
486			row.Append(tb)
487		}
488		// sources align on the wall clock, and the clock comes out of the name --
489		// a file without one is stacked at the session's start and has to be lined
490		// up by hand. That deserves a flag on the row, not a failed run.
491		if _, ok := nameStamp(it.name()); !ok {
492			warn := gtk.NewImageFromIconName("dialog-warning-symbolic")
493			warn.AddCSSClass("stamp-warn")
494			warn.SetTooltipText("No timestamp in the file name — this file starts where the\n" +
495				"session does, which is only right if it was rolling from the start.\n" +
496				"Rename it with when the recording STARTED, like\n" +
497				"clip_2026-08-08_19-55-15.mkv — most recorders already do — or drag it\n" +
498				"into place with the right mouse button on the Cut page.")
499			row.Append(warn)
500		}
501		row.Append(sep)
502		row.Append(del)
503		return row
504	}

	// instead, for footage and inserts alike (outBox)
	cf := a.produceCut()
	fx, aspect := cf.Fx, cf.Aspect

	if boxW > 0 {
		// on every clip, not only the inserts that are fitted into it: a text
		// overlay is drawn at the finished frame's size too, and it has to be

		for i := range clips {

	// is taken through fxRectAt -- the same function the preview overlay draws
	// -- sampled at every moment anything starts or stops moving (buildCam)
	if fxHasCamera(aspect, fx) && boxW > 0 {

		if camFps <= 0 {

		}

			}
			span := c.length * c.speed()
			if c.freeze {
				span = 0 // a freeze is one session moment, not a stretch of it
			}
			c.cam = buildCam(fx, aspect, sw, sh, c.video.sessionAt(c.local), span,
				c.speed(), c.length, boxW, boxH, camFps)
			if c.cam != nil && c.cam.maxZoom() > 10 {

	// title and a camera move placed at the same second happen at the same
	// second in the render. An insert or a freeze is one session moment held
	// for a while (span 0), exactly as buildCam treats it.
	if boxW > 0 {
		for i := range clips {
			c := &clips[i]
			span := c.length * c.speed()
			if c.freeze || c.ins != "" {
				span = 0
			}
			c.texts = textCues(fx, c.sessS, span, c.speed(), c.length)
		}
	}

	// guard above because a gain needs no frame size -- a clip with no picture
	// to put a title on still has sound to turn up.
	for i := range clips {
		c := &clips[i]
		span := c.length * c.speed()
		if c.freeze || c.ins != "" {
			span = 0
		}
		c.gains = gainCues(fx, c.sessS, span, c.speed(), c.length)

	// at any rate. Mapped exactly as the volume effects above are, and for the
	// same reason -- a stop and a ×1 leave the segment list alone, so their
	// bands lie inside a clip rather than being one.
	for i := range clips {
		c := &clips[i]
		span := c.length * c.speed()

			span = 0
		}

	// of a recording rather than a drawn card, resolved here where the
	// recordings are known -- a stop's bar can hang into a clip cut from a
	// different recording than the one its frame is in
	for i := range clips {
		c := &clips[i]
		if c.video == nil || c.ins != "" || c.freeze {
			continue // no footage runs under a card or a held frame
		}
		for _, cue := range freezeCues(fx, c.sessS, c.length*c.speed(), c.speed(), c.length) {
			// the scene's own camera (cutVideoOn), not whichever recording
			// happened to be rolling: on a session shot on two cameras,
			// pickVideo froze camera 1's frame over a scene showing camera 2 --
			// a still of something the clip around it never shows
			v := cutVideoOn(segs, vids, cue.fx.T)
			if v == nil {
				a.logfIdle("a stop at %.0f s falls in no recording — its still is skipped", cue.fx.T)
				continue
			}
			sc := stillCue{s: cue.s, e: cue.e, fin: cue.fin,
				fout: cue.fout, path: v.path, at: v.at(cue.fx.T),
				mute: cue.fx.sound() == sndMute}
			sc.w, sc.h = stillSize(v, c.video)
			c.stills = append(c.stills, sc)
		}
	}

	// 3. subtitles, on the produced timeline: the narration's lines where
	// there is a narration, and what was said in the clips where there is
	// not (captionLines)

// insKind says what an insert file is, which is the only thing that decides how
// ffmpeg has to be asked for it. By extension, deliberately: the alternative is
// probing every asset on every render, and an .svg that ffprobe calls a png
// stream is not more true than the name the user gave it.
func insKind(path string) string {
	file, _ := insSplit(path)
	switch strings.ToLower(filepath.Ext(file)) {
	case ".mp4", ".mkv", ".mov", ".webm", ".avi", ".m4v", ".mpg", ".mpeg", ".ts":
		return "video"
	case ".svg", ".svgz":
		return "svg"
	case ".mp3", ".wav", ".ogg", ".oga", ".flac", ".m4a", ".aac", ".opus":
		return "audio"
